4.  Let `baseURL` be `environment`'s <a href="#document-base-url"
    id="resolving-urls:document-base-url-2">base URL</a>, if
    `environment` is a [`Document`](#document) object; otherwise
    `environment`'s
    <a href="#api-base-url" id="resolving-urls:api-base-url-2">API base
    URL</a>.

5.  Return the result of applying the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
    id="resolving-urls:url-parser-3" data-x-internal="url-parser">URL
    parser</a> to `url`, with `baseURL` and `encoding`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
class="dfn">encoding-parse-and-serialize a URL</span>, given a string
`url`, relative to a [`Document`](#document) object or
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="resolving-urls:environment-settings-object-3">environment settings
object</a> `environment`, run these steps. They return failure or a
string.

1.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
    id="resolving-urls:encoding-parsing-a-url-2">encoding-parsing a URL</a>
    given `url`, relative to `environment`.

2.  If `url` is failure, then return failure.

3.  Return the result of applying the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="resolving-urls:concept-url-serializer"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">URL serializer</a> to
    `url`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.4.3</span> Document base URLs<a href="#document-base-urls" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="document-base-url" class="dfn" export="">document base
URL</span> of a [`Document`](#document) `document` is the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="document-base-urls:url-record" data-x-internal="url-record">URL
record</a> obtained by running these steps:

1.  If `document` has no
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="document-base-urls:descendant"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a>
    [`base`](#the-base-element) element that has an
    [`href`](#attr-base-href) attribute, then return `document`'s
    <a href="#fallback-base-url"
    id="document-base-urls:fallback-base-url">fallback base URL</a>.

2.  Otherwise, return the <a href="#frozen-base-url"
    id="document-base-urls:frozen-base-url">frozen base URL</a> of the
    first [`base`](#the-base-element) element in `document` that has an
    [`href`](#attr-base-href) attribute, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="document-base-urls:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="fallback-base-url" class="dfn">fallback base URL</span> of
a [`Document`](#document) object `document` is the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="document-base-urls:url-record-2" data-x-internal="url-record">URL
record</a> obtained by running these steps:

1.  If `document` is <a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
    id="document-base-urls:an-iframe-srcdoc-document">an <code>iframe</code>
    <code>srcdoc</code> document</a>:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="document-base-urls:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `document`'s <a href="#concept-document-about-base-url"
        id="document-base-urls:concept-document-about-base-url">about base
        URL</a> is non-null.

    2.  Return `document`'s <a href="#concept-document-about-base-url"
        id="document-base-urls:concept-document-about-base-url-2">about base
        URL</a>.

2.  If `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="document-base-urls:the-document&#39;s-address"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>
    <a href="#matches-about:blank"
    id="document-base-urls:matches-about:blank">matches
    <code>about:blank</code></a> and `document`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-about-base-url"
    id="document-base-urls:concept-document-about-base-url-3">about base
    URL</a> is non-null, then return `document`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-about-base-url"
    id="document-base-urls:concept-document-about-base-url-4">about base
    URL</a>.

3.  Return `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="document-base-urls:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="set-the-url" class="dfn">set the URL</span> for a
[`Document`](#document) `document` to a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="document-base-urls:url-record-3" data-x-internal="url-record">URL
record</a> `url`:

1.  Set `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="document-base-urls:the-document&#39;s-address-3"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> to `url`.

2.  <a href="#respond-to-base-url-changes"
    id="document-base-urls:respond-to-base-url-changes">Respond to base URL
    changes</a> given `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="respond-to-base-url-changes" class="dfn">respond to base
URL changes</span> for a [`Document`](#document) `document`:

1.  The user agent should update any user interface elements which are
    displaying affected URLs, or data derived from such URLs, to the
    user. Examples of such user interface elements would be a status bar
    that displays a
    <a href="#hyperlink" id="document-base-urls:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="document-base-urls:concept-hyperlink-url">url</a>, or some user
    interface which displays the URL specified by a
    [`q`](#the-q-element), [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element),
    [`ins`](#the-ins-element), or [`del`](#the-del-element) element's
    `cite` attribute.

2.  Ensure that the CSS
    [`:link`](#selector-link)/[`:visited`](#selector-visited)/etc.
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class"
    id="document-base-urls:pseudo-class"
    data-x-internal="pseudo-class">pseudo-classes</a> are updated
    appropriately.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="document-base-urls:list-iterate" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `descendant` of `document`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-descendant"
    id="document-base-urls:shadow-including-descendant"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-descendant">shadow-including
    descendants</a>:

    1.  If `descendant` is a [`script`](#the-script-element) element
        whose <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="document-base-urls:concept-script-result">result</a> is a
        <a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
        id="document-base-urls:speculation-rules-parse-result">speculation rules
        parse result</a>, then:

        1.  Let `oldResult` be `element`'s
            <a href="#concept-script-result"
            id="document-base-urls:concept-script-result-2">result</a>.

        2.  Let `newResult` be the result of
            <a href="#create-a-speculation-rules-parse-result"
            id="document-base-urls:create-a-speculation-rules-parse-result">creating
            a speculation rules parse result</a> given `element`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
            id="document-base-urls:child-text-content"
            data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>
            and `element`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
            id="document-base-urls:node-document"
            data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

        3.  <a href="#update-speculation-rules"
            id="document-base-urls:update-speculation-rules">Update speculation
            rules</a> given `element`'s
            <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
            id="document-base-urls:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
            object</a>, `oldResult`, and `newResult`.

4.  <a href="#consider-speculative-loads"
    id="document-base-urls:consider-speculative-loads">Consider speculative
    loads</a> given `document`.

</div>

<a href="#example-base-url-change-img-unaffected" class="self-link"></a>This
means that changing the base URL doesn't affect, for example, the image
displayed by [`img`](#the-img-element) elements. Thus, subsequent
accesses of the [`src`](#dom-img-src) IDL attribute from script will
return a new <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="document-base-urls:absolute-url"
data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute URL</a> that might no longer
correspond to the image being shown.

### <span class="secno">2.5</span> Fetching resources<a href="#fetching-resources" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.1</span> Terminology<a href="#terminology-3" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="terminology-3:concept-response"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> whose
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-type"
id="terminology-3:concept-response-type"
data-x-internal="concept-response-type">type</a> is "`basic`", "`cors`",
or "`default`" is <span id="cors-same-origin" class="dfn"
export="">CORS-same-origin</span>. [\[FETCH\]](#refsFETCH)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="terminology-3:concept-response-2"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> whose
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-type"
id="terminology-3:concept-response-type-2"
data-x-internal="concept-response-type">type</a> is "`opaque`" or
"`opaqueredirect`" is <span id="cors-cross-origin"
class="dfn">CORS-cross-origin</span>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="terminology-3:concept-response-3"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a>'s
<span id="unsafe-response" class="dfn" export="">unsafe response</span>
is its
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-internal-response"
id="terminology-3:concept-internal-response"
data-x-internal="concept-internal-response">internal response</a> if it
has one, and the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="terminology-3:concept-response-4"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> itself otherwise.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="create-a-potential-cors-request" class="dfn">create a
potential-CORS request</span>, given a `url`, `destination`,
`corsAttributeState`, and an optional *same-origin fallback flag*, run
these steps:

1.  Let `mode` be "`no-cors`" if `corsAttributeState` is
    <a href="#attr-crossorigin-none"
    id="terminology-3:attr-crossorigin-none">No CORS</a>, and "`cors`"
    otherwise.

2.  If *same-origin fallback flag* is set and `mode` is "`no-cors`", set
    `mode` to "`same-origin`".

3.  Let `credentialsMode` be "`include`".

4.  If `corsAttributeState` is <a href="#attr-crossorigin-anonymous"
    id="terminology-3:attr-crossorigin-anonymous">Anonymous</a>, set
    `credentialsMode` to "`same-origin`".

5.  Return a new
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
    id="terminology-3:concept-request"
    data-x-internal="concept-request">request</a> whose
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url"
    id="terminology-3:concept-request-url"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-url">URL</a> is `url`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
    id="terminology-3:concept-request-destination"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a> is
    `destination`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode"
    id="terminology-3:concept-request-mode"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-mode">mode</a> is `mode`, <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
    id="terminology-3:concept-request-credentials-mode"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
    is `credentialsMode`, and whose <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag"
    id="terminology-3:use-url-credentials-flag"
    data-x-internal="use-url-credentials-flag">use-URL-credentials flag</a>
    is set.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.2</span> Determining the type of a resource<a href="#content-type-sniffing" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="content-type" class="dfn">Content-Type metadata</span> of
a resource must be obtained and interpreted in a manner consistent with
the requirements of MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#refsMIMESNIFF)

The <span id="content-type-sniffing-2" class="dfn">[computed MIME
type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type)</span> of a
resource must be found in a manner consistent with the requirements
given in MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#refsMIMESNIFF)

The <span id="content-type-sniffing:-image" class="dfn">[rules for
sniffing images
specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically)</span>,
the <span id="content-type-sniffing:-text-or-binary" class="dfn">[rules
for distinguishing if a resource is text or
binary](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-text-or-binary)</span>,
and the <span id="content-type-sniffing:-video" class="dfn">[rules for
sniffing audio and video
specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-audio-and-video-specifically)</span>
are also defined in MIME Sniffing. These rules return a
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="content-type-sniffing:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
type</a> as their result. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#refsMIMESNIFF)

It is imperative that the rules in MIME Sniffing be followed exactly.
When a user agent uses different heuristics for content type detection
than the server expects, security problems can occur. For more details,
see MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#refsMIMESNIFF)

#### <span class="secno">2.5.3</span> Extracting character encodings from [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements<a href="#extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements"
class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

The
<span id="algorithm-for-extracting-a-character-encoding-from-a-meta-element"
class="dfn">algorithm for extracting a character encoding from a `meta`
element</span>, given a string `s`, is as follows. It returns either a
character encoding or nothing.

1.  Let `position` be a pointer into `s`, initially pointing at the
    start of the string.

2.  *Loop*: Find the first seven characters in `s` after `position` that
    are an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:ascii-case-insensitive"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for the word "`charset`". If no such match is found, return
    nothing.

3.  Skip any <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:space-characters"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> that
    immediately follow the word "`charset`" (there might not be any).

4.  If the next character is not a U+003D EQUALS SIGN (=), then move
    `position` to point just before that next character, and jump back
    to the step labeled *loop*.

5.  Skip any <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:space-characters-2"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> that
    immediately follow the equals sign (there might not be any).

6.  Process the next character as follows:

    If it is a U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (") and there is a later U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (") in `s`  
    If it is a U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (') and there is a later U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (') in `s`  
    Return the result of
    <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:getting-an-encoding"
    data-x-internal="getting-an-encoding">getting an encoding</a> from
    the substring that is between this character and the next earliest
    occurrence of this character.

    If it is an unmatched U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (")  
    If it is an unmatched U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (')  
    If there is no next character  
    Return nothing.

    Otherwise  
    Return the result of
    <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:getting-an-encoding-2"
    data-x-internal="getting-an-encoding">getting an encoding</a> from
    the substring that consists of this character up to but not
    including the first
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements:space-characters-3"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> or U+003B
    SEMICOLON character (;), or the end of `s`, whichever comes first.

</div>

This algorithm is distinct from those in the HTTP specifications (for
example, HTTP doesn't allow the use of single quotes and requires
supporting a backslash-escape mechanism that is not supported by this
algorithm). While the algorithm is used in contexts that, historically,
were related to HTTP, the syntax as supported by implementations
diverged some time ago. [\[HTTP\]](#refsHTTP)

#### <span class="secno">2.5.4</span> CORS settings attributes<a href="#cors-settings-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/crossorigin](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/crossorigin "The crossorigin attribute, valid on the <audio>, <img>, <link>, <script>, and <video> elements, provides support for CORS, defining how the element handles cross-origin requests, thereby enabling the configuration of the CORS requests for the element's fetched data. Depending on the element, the attribute can be a CORS settings attribute.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox8+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari6+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome13+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

A <span id="cors-settings-attribute" class="dfn">CORS settings
attribute</span> is an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="cors-settings-attributes:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-crossorigin-anonymous-keyword" class="dfn" dfn-for="audio/crossorigin,video/crossorigin,img/crossorigin,link/crossorigin,script/crossorigin" dfn-type="attr-value">`anonymous`</span> | <span id="attr-crossorigin-anonymous" class="dfn">Anonymous</span> | <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request"
data-x-internal="concept-request">Requests</a> for the element will have their <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-mode"
data-x-internal="concept-request-mode">mode</a> set to "`cors`" and their <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-credentials-mode"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a> set to "`same-origin`". |
| <span id="attr-crossorigin-use-credentials-keyword" class="dfn" dfn-for="audio/crossorigin,video/crossorigin,img/crossorigin,link/crossorigin,script/crossorigin" dfn-type="attr-value">`use-credentials`</span> | <span id="attr-crossorigin-use-credentials" class="dfn">Use Credentials</span> | <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request">Requests</a> for the element will have their <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-mode-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request-mode">mode</a> set to "`cors`" and their <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-credentials-mode-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a> set to "`include`". |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* is the
<span id="attr-crossorigin-none" class="dfn">No CORS</span> state, and
its *[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* and *[empty value
default](#empty-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-crossorigin-anonymous"
id="cors-settings-attributes:attr-crossorigin-anonymous">Anonymous</a>
state.

</div>

The majority of fetches governed by <a href="#cors-settings-attribute"
id="cors-settings-attributes:cors-settings-attribute">CORS settings
attributes</a> will be done via the
<a href="#create-a-potential-cors-request"
id="cors-settings-attributes:create-a-potential-cors-request">create a
potential-CORS request</a> algorithm.

<div algorithm="">

For more modern features, where the request's
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-mode-3"
data-x-internal="concept-request-mode">mode</a> is always "`cors`",
certain <a href="#cors-settings-attribute"
id="cors-settings-attributes:cors-settings-attribute-2">CORS settings
attributes</a> have been repurposed to have a slightly different
meaning, wherein they only impact the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-3"
data-x-internal="concept-request">request</a>'s <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="cors-settings-attributes:concept-request-credentials-mode-3"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>.
To perform this translation, we define the
<span id="cors-settings-attribute-credentials-mode" class="dfn"
export="">CORS settings attribute credentials mode</span> for a given
<a href="#cors-settings-attribute"
id="cors-settings-attributes:cors-settings-attribute-3">CORS settings
attribute</a> to be determined by switching on the attribute's state:

<a href="#attr-crossorigin-none"
id="cors-settings-attributes:attr-crossorigin-none">No CORS</a>  
<a href="#attr-crossorigin-anonymous"
id="cors-settings-attributes:attr-crossorigin-anonymous-2">Anonymous</a>  
"`same-origin`"

<a href="#attr-crossorigin-none"
id="cors-settings-attributes:attr-crossorigin-none-2">Use
Credentials</a>  
"`include`"

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.5</span> Referrer policy attributes<a href="#referrer-policy-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="referrer-policy-attribute" class="dfn" export="">referrer
policy attribute</span> is an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="referrer-policy-attributes:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a>. Each <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="referrer-policy-attributes:referrer-policy"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a>, including the
empty string, is a keyword for this attribute, mapping to a state of the
same name.

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the empty
string state.

</div>

The impact of these states on the processing model of various
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="referrer-policy-attributes:concept-fetch"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetches</a> is defined in more detail
throughout this specification, in Fetch, and in Referrer Policy.
[\[FETCH\]](#refsFETCH) [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

<div class="note">

Several signals can contribute to which processing model is used for a
given <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="referrer-policy-attributes:concept-fetch-2"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a>; a
<a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
id="referrer-policy-attributes:referrer-policy-attribute">referrer
policy attribute</a> is only one of them. In general, the order in which
these signals are processed are:

1.  First, the presence of a [`noreferrer`](#link-type-noreferrer) link
    type;

2.  Then, the value of a <a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
    id="referrer-policy-attributes:referrer-policy-attribute-2">referrer
    policy attribute</a>;

3.  Then, the presence of any [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with
    [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute set to
    [`referrer`](#meta-referrer).

4.  Finally, the \`<a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-header-dfn"
    data-x-internal="http-referrer-policy"><code
    id="referrer-policy-attributes:http-referrer-policy">Referrer-Policy</code></a>\`
    HTTP header.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.6</span> Nonce attributes<a href="#nonce-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/nonce](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/nonce "The nonce global attribute is a content attribute defining a cryptographic nonce ("number used once") which can be used by Content Security Policy to determine whether or not a given fetch will be allowed to proceed for a given element.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox31+</span><span class="safari yes">SafariYes</span><span class="chrome yes">ChromeYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">EdgeYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

A <span id="attr-nonce" class="dfn" dfn-for="htmlsvg-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`nonce`</span> content attribute represents a
cryptographic nonce ("number used once") which can be used by Content
Security Policy to determine whether or not a given fetch will be
allowed to proceed. The value is text. [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

Elements that have a [`nonce`](#attr-nonce) content attribute ensure
that the cryptographic nonce is only exposed to script (and not to
side-channels like CSS attribute selectors) by taking the value from the
content attribute, moving it into an internal slot named
<span id="cryptographicnonce" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOrSVGElement"
dfn-type="attribute">\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]</span>, exposing it to
script via the [`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement) interface mixin,
and setting the content attribute to the empty string. Unless otherwise
specified, the slot's value is the empty string.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-noncedelement-nonce"
id="dom-htmlorsvgelement-nonce-dev"><code>nonce</code></a>  
Returns the value set for `element`'s cryptographic nonce. If the setter
was not used, this will be the value originally found in the
[`nonce`](#attr-nonce) content attribute.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-noncedelement-nonce"
id="nonce-attributes:dom-noncedelement-nonce"><code>nonce</code></a>` = ``value`  
Updates `element`'s cryptographic nonce value.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLElement/nonce](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/nonce "The nonce property of the HTMLElement interface returns the cryptographic number used once that is used by Content Security Policy to determine whether a given fetch will be allowed to proceed.")

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox75+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari<span title="Partial implementation.">🔰
10+</span></span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome61+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-noncedelement-nonce" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOrSVGElement" dfn-type="attribute">`nonce`</span> IDL
attribute must, on getting, return the value of this element's
<a href="#cryptographicnonce"
id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>; and
on setting, set this element's <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-2">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a> to
the given value.

</div>

<a href="#nonce-does-not-update-dom" class="self-link"></a>Note how the
setter for the [`nonce`](#dom-noncedelement-nonce) IDL attribute does
not update the corresponding content attribute. This, as well as the
below setting of the [`nonce`](#attr-nonce) content attribute to the
empty string when an element
<a href="#becomes-browsing-context-connected"
id="nonce-attributes:becomes-browsing-context-connected">becomes
browsing-context connected</a>, is meant to prevent exfiltration of the
nonce value through mechanisms that can easily read content attributes,
such as selectors. Learn more in [issue
\#2369](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2369), where this behavior
was introduced.

<div algorithm="">

The following <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
id="nonce-attributes:concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change-ext">attribute change
steps</a> are used for the [`nonce`](#attr-nonce) content attribute:

1.  If `element` does not
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include"
    id="nonce-attributes:include" data-x-internal="include">include</a>
    [`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement), then return.

2.  If `localName` is not [`nonce`](#attr-nonce) or `namespace` is not
    null, then return.

3.  If `value` is null, then set `element`'s
    <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
    id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-3">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>
    to the empty string.

4.  Otherwise, set `element`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
    id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-4">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>
    to `value`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an element <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include"
id="nonce-attributes:include-2" data-x-internal="include">including</a>
[`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement)
<a href="#becomes-browsing-context-connected"
id="nonce-attributes:becomes-browsing-context-connected-2">becomes
browsing-context connected</a>, the user agent must execute the
following steps on the `element`:

1.  Let `CSP list` be `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-root"
    id="nonce-attributes:shadow-including-root"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-root">shadow-including root</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-policy-container"
    id="nonce-attributes:concept-document-policy-container">policy
    container</a>'s <a href="#policy-container-csp-list"
    id="nonce-attributes:policy-container-csp-list">CSP list</a>.

2.  If `CSP list` <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#contains-a-header-delivered-content-security-policy"
    id="nonce-attributes:contains-a-header-delivered-content-security-policy"
    data-x-internal="contains-a-header-delivered-content-security-policy">contains
    a header-delivered Content Security Policy</a>, and `element` has a
    [`nonce`](#attr-nonce) content attribute whose value is not the
    empty string, then:

    1.  Let `nonce` be `element`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
        id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-5">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>.

    2.  <a
        href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value"
        id="nonce-attributes:concept-element-attributes-set-value"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-set-value">Set an attribute
        value</a> for `element` using "[`nonce`](#attr-nonce)" and the
        empty string.

    3.  Set `element`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
        id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-6">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>
        to `nonce`.

    If `element`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
    id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-7">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>
    were not restored it would be the empty string at this point.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone-ext"
id="nonce-attributes:concept-node-clone-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-ext">cloning steps</a> for elements
that <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include"
id="nonce-attributes:include-3" data-x-internal="include">include</a>
[`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement) given `node`, `copy`, and
`subtree` are to set `copy`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-8">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a> to
`node`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
id="nonce-attributes:cryptographicnonce-9">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.7</span> Lazy loading attributes<a href="#lazy-loading-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Lazy_loading](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Performance/Lazy_loading "Lazy loading is a strategy to identify resources as non-blocking (non-critical) and load these only when needed. It's a way to shorten the length of the critical rendering path, which translates into reduced page load times.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox75+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari15.4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome77+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

A <span id="lazy-loading-attribute" class="dfn">lazy loading
attribute</span> is an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-loading-lazy" class="dfn" dfn-for="img/loading,audio/loading,video/loading,iframe/loading" dfn-type="attr-value">`lazy`</span> | <span id="attr-loading-lazy-state" class="dfn">Lazy</span> | Used to defer fetching a resource until some conditions are met. |
| <span id="attr-loading-eager" class="dfn" dfn-for="img/loading,audio/loading,video/loading,iframe/loading" dfn-type="attr-value">`eager`</span> | <span id="attr-loading-eager-state" class="dfn">Eager</span> | Used to fetch a resource immediately; the default state. |

The attribute directs the user agent to fetch a resource immediately or
to defer fetching until some conditions associated with the element are
met, according to the attribute's current state.

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-loading-eager-state"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:attr-loading-eager-state">Eager</a> state.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="will-lazy-load-element-steps" class="dfn">will lazy load
element steps</span>, given an element `element`, are as follows:

1.  If <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:concept-n-noscript">scripting is
    disabled</a> for `element`, then return false.

    This is an anti-tracking measure, because if a user agent supported
    lazy loading when scripting is disabled, it would still be possible
    for a site to track a user's approximate scroll position throughout
    a session, by strategically placing images in a page's markup such
    that a server can track how many images are requested and when.

2.  If `element`'s <a href="#lazy-loading-attribute"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-loading-attribute">lazy loading
    attribute</a> is in the <a href="#attr-loading-lazy-state"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:attr-loading-lazy-state">Lazy</a> state,
    then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

Each [`img`](#the-img-element), [`audio`](#the-audio-element),
[`video`](#the-video-element), and [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
element has associated <span id="lazy-load-resumption-steps"
class="dfn">lazy load resumption steps</span>, initially null.

Each [`video`](#the-video-element) element also has associated
<span id="poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps" class="dfn">poster lazy
load resumption steps</span>, initially null.

For [`img`](#the-img-element), [`audio`](#the-audio-element),
[`video`](#the-video-element), and [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
elements that <a href="#will-lazy-load-element-steps"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:will-lazy-load-element-steps">will lazy
load</a>, these steps are run from the
<a href="#lazy-load-intersection-observer"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-intersection-observer">lazy load
intersection observer</a>'s callback or when their
<a href="#lazy-loading-attribute"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-loading-attribute-2">lazy loading
attribute</a> is set to the <a href="#attr-loading-eager-state"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:attr-loading-eager-state-2">Eager</a> state.
This causes the element to continue loading. For
[`video`](#the-video-element) elements,
<a href="#poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps">poster
lazy load resumption steps</a> are also run at the same time.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="lazy-load-intersection-observer" class="dfn">lazy load
intersection observer</span>, initially set to null but can be set to an
<a
href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver"
data-x-internal="intersectionobserver"><code
id="lazy-loading-attributes:intersectionobserver">IntersectionObserver</code></a>
instance.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="start-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element"
class="dfn">start intersection-observing a lazy loading element</span>
`element`, run these steps:

1.  Let `doc` be `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  If `doc`'s <a href="#lazy-load-intersection-observer"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-intersection-observer-2">lazy load
    intersection observer</a> is null, set it to a new <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver"
    data-x-internal="intersectionobserver"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:intersectionobserver-2">IntersectionObserver</code></a>
    instance, initialized as follows:

    The intention is to use the original value of the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver"
    data-x-internal="intersectionobserver"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:intersectionobserver-3">IntersectionObserver</code></a>
    constructor. However, we're forced to use the JavaScript-exposed
    constructor in this specification, until Intersection Observer
    exposes low-level hooks for use in specifications. See bug
    [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464)
    which tracks this.
    [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#refsINTERSECTIONOBSERVER)

    - The `callback` is these steps, with arguments `entries` and
      `observer`:

      1.  For each `entry` in `entries` <span class="XXX">using a method
          of iteration which does not trigger developer-modifiable array
          accessors or iteration hooks</span>:

          1.  Let `resumptionSteps` be null.

          2.  If `entry`.<a
              href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"
              data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"><code
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting">isIntersecting</code></a>
              is true, then set `resumptionSteps` to `entry`.<a
              href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"
              data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"><code
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-target">target</code></a>'s
              <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-resumption-steps">lazy load
              resumption steps</a>.

          3.  Let `posterResumptionSteps` be null.

              If `entry`.<a
              href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"
              data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"><code
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting-2">isIntersecting</code></a>
              is true and `entry`.<a
              href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"
              data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"><code
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-target-2">target</code></a>
              is a [`video`](#the-video-element) element, then set
              `posterResumptionSteps` to the
              [`video`](#the-video-element) element's
              <a href="#poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps"
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps-2">poster
              lazy load resumption steps</a>.

          4.  If `resumptionSteps` is null and `posterResumptionSteps`
              is null, then return.

          5.  <a href="#stop-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element"
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:stop-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element">Stop
              intersection-observing a lazy loading element</a> for
              `entry`.<a
              href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"
              data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"><code
              id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-target-3">target</code></a>.

          6.  If `resumptionSteps` is not null, then:

              1.  Set `entry`.<a
                  href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"
                  data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"><code
                  id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-target-4">target</code></a>'s
                  <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
                  id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-resumption-steps-2">lazy load
                  resumption steps</a> to null.

              2.  Invoke `resumptionSteps`.

          7.  If `posterResumptionSteps` is not null, then:

              1.  Set the [`video`](#the-video-element) element's
                  <a href="#poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps"
                  id="lazy-loading-attributes:poster-lazy-load-resumption-steps-3">poster
                  lazy load resumption steps</a> to null.

              2.  Invoke `posterResumptionSteps`.

          The intention is to use the original value of the <a
          href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"
          data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting"><code
          id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting-3">isIntersecting</code></a>
          and <a
          href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"
          data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserverentry-target"><code
          id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserverentry-target-5">target</code></a>
          getters. See
          [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464).
          [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#refsINTERSECTIONOBSERVER)

    - The `options` is an <a
      href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dictdef-intersectionobserverinit"
      data-x-internal="intersectionobserverinit"><code
      id="lazy-loading-attributes:intersectionobserverinit">IntersectionObserverInit</code></a>
      dictionary with the following dictionary members: «\[
      "`scrollMargin`" → <a href="#lazy-load-root-margin"
      id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-root-margin">lazy load scroll
      margin</a> \]»

      This allows for fetching the image during scrolling, when it does
      not yet — but is about to — intersect the viewport.

      The <a href="#lazy-load-root-margin"
      id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-root-margin-2">lazy load scroll
      margin</a> suggestions imply dynamic changes to the value, but the
      <a
      href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver"
      data-x-internal="intersectionobserver"><code
      id="lazy-loading-attributes:intersectionobserver-4">IntersectionObserver</code></a>
      API does not support changing the scroll margin. See issue
      [w3c/IntersectionObserver#428](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/428).

3.  Call `doc`'s <a href="#lazy-load-intersection-observer"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-intersection-observer-3">lazy load
    intersection observer</a>'s <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-observe"
    data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserver-observe"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserver-observe">observe</code></a>
    method with `element` as the argument.

    The intention is to use the original value of the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-observe"
    data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserver-observe"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserver-observe-2">observe</code></a>
    method. See
    [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464).
    [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#refsINTERSECTIONOBSERVER)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="stop-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element"
class="dfn">stop intersection-observing a lazy loading element</span>
`element`, run these steps:

1.  Let `doc` be `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `doc`'s <a href="#lazy-load-intersection-observer"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-intersection-observer-4">lazy load
    intersection observer</a> is not null.

3.  Call `doc`'s <a href="#lazy-load-intersection-observer"
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-intersection-observer-5">lazy load
    intersection observer</a>'s <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve"
    data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve">unobserve</code></a>
    method with `element` as the argument.

    The intention is to use the original value of the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve"
    data-x-internal="dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve"><code
    id="lazy-loading-attributes:dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve-2">unobserve</code></a>
    method. See
    [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464).
    [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#refsINTERSECTIONOBSERVER)

</div>

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> The
<span id="lazy-load-root-margin" class="dfn">lazy load scroll
margin</span> is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
value, but with the following suggestions to consider:

- Set a minimum value that most often results in the resources being
  loaded before they intersect the viewport under normal usage patterns
  for the given device.

- The typical scrolling speed: increase the value for devices with
  faster typical scrolling speeds.

- The current scrolling speed or momentum: the UA can attempt to predict
  where the scrolling will likely stop, and adjust the value
  accordingly.

- The network quality: increase the value for slow or high-latency
  connections.

- User preferences can influence the value.

It is important <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:tracking-vector-2"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector">for privacy</a> that the
<a href="#lazy-load-root-margin"
id="lazy-loading-attributes:lazy-load-root-margin-3">lazy load scroll
margin</a> not leak additional information. For example, the typical
scrolling speed on the current device could be imprecise so as to not
introduce a new fingerprinting vector.

#### <span class="secno">2.5.8</span> Blocking attributes<a href="#blocking-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="blocking-attribute" class="dfn">blocking attribute</span>
explicitly indicates that certain operations should be blocked on the
fetching of an external resource. The operations that can be blocked are
represented by <span id="possible-blocking-token" class="dfn">possible
blocking tokens</span>, which are strings listed by the following table:

| Possible blocking token | Description |
|----|----|
| "<span id="blocking-token-render" class="dfn">`render`</span>" | The element is <a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
id="blocking-attributes:potentially-render-blocking">potentially
render-blocking</a>. |

<a href="#future-blocking-tokens" class="self-link"></a>In the future,
there might be more <a href="#possible-blocking-token"
id="blocking-attributes:possible-blocking-token">possible blocking
tokens</a>.

A <a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="blocking-attributes:blocking-attribute">blocking attribute</a> must
have a value that is an
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="blocking-attributes:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a>, each of which are
<a href="#possible-blocking-token"
id="blocking-attributes:possible-blocking-token-2">possible blocking
tokens</a>. The
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="blocking-attributes:concept-supported-tokens"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> of a
<a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="blocking-attributes:blocking-attribute-2">blocking attribute</a> are
the <a href="#possible-blocking-token"
id="blocking-attributes:possible-blocking-token-3">possible blocking
tokens</a>. Any element can have at most one
<a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="blocking-attributes:blocking-attribute-3">blocking attribute</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="blocking-tokens-set" class="dfn">blocking tokens
set</span> for an element `el` are the result of the following steps:

1.  Let `value` be the value of `el`'s <a href="#blocking-attribute"
    id="blocking-attributes:blocking-attribute-4">blocking attribute</a>,
    or the empty string if no such attribute exists.

2.  Set `value` to `value`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="blocking-attributes:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

3.  Let `rawTokens` be the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-ascii-whitespace"
    id="blocking-attributes:split-a-string-on-spaces"
    data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-spaces">splitting <var>value</var> on
    ASCII whitespace</a>.

4.  Return a set containing the elements of `rawTokens` that are
    <a href="#possible-blocking-token"
    id="blocking-attributes:possible-blocking-token-4">possible blocking
    tokens</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An element is <span id="potentially-render-blocking"
class="dfn">potentially render-blocking</span> if its
<a href="#blocking-tokens-set"
id="blocking-attributes:blocking-tokens-set">blocking tokens set</a>
contains "[`render`](#blocking-token-render)", or if it is
<span id="implicitly-potentially-render-blocking" class="dfn">implicitly
potentially render-blocking</span>, which will be defined at the
individual elements. By default, an element is not
<a href="#implicitly-potentially-render-blocking"
id="blocking-attributes:implicitly-potentially-render-blocking">implicitly
potentially render-blocking</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.9</span> Fetch priority attributes<a href="#fetch-priority-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="fetch-priority-attribute" class="dfn">fetch priority
attribute</span> is an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-fetchpriority-high" class="dfn" dfn-for="img/fetchpriority,script/fetchpriority,link/fetchpriority" dfn-type="attr-value">`high`</span> | <span id="attr-fetchpriority-high-state" class="dfn">High</span> | Signals a high-priority <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-fetch"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> relative to other resources with the same <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-request-destination"
data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a>. |
| <span id="attr-fetchpriority-low" class="dfn" dfn-for="img/fetchpriority,script/fetchpriority,link/fetchpriority" dfn-type="attr-value">`low`</span> | <span id="attr-fetchpriority-low-state" class="dfn">Low</span> | Signals a low-priority <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-fetch-2"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> relative to other resources with the same <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-request-destination-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a>. |
| <span id="attr-fetchpriority-auto" class="dfn" dfn-for="img/fetchpriority,script/fetchpriority,link/fetchpriority" dfn-type="attr-value">`auto`</span> | <span id="attr-fetchpriority-auto-state" class="dfn">Auto</span> | Signals automatic determination of <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-fetch-3"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> priority relative to other resources with the same <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:concept-request-destination-3"
data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a>. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-fetchpriority-auto-state"
id="fetch-priority-attributes:attr-fetchpriority-auto-state">Auto</a>
state.

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.6</span> Common DOM interfaces<a href="#common-dom-interfaces" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">2.6.1</span> Reflecting content attributes in IDL attributes<a href="#reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes"
class="self-link"></a>

The building blocks for reflecting are as follows:

- A <span id="reflected-target" class="dfn">reflected target</span> is
  an element or [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object. It is
  typically clear from context and typically identical to the interface
  of the <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute">reflected
  IDL attribute</a>. It is always identical to that interface when it is
  an [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object.

- A <span id="reflected-idl-attribute" class="dfn">reflected IDL
  attribute</span> is an attribute interface member.

- A <span id="reflected-content-attribute-name" class="dfn">reflected
  content attribute name</span> is a string. When the
  <a href="#reflected-target"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target">reflected
  target</a> is an element, it represents the local name of a content
  attribute whose namespace is null. When the
  <a href="#reflected-target"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-2">reflected
  target</a> is an [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object, it
  represents a key of the <a href="#reflected-target"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-3">reflected
  target</a>'s <a href="#internals-target"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target">target
  element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map">internal
  content attribute map</a>.

A <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-2">reflected
IDL attribute</a> can be defined to <span id="reflect" class="dfn"
export="">reflect</span> a <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name">reflected
content attribute name</a> of a <a href="#reflected-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-4">reflected
target</a>. In general this means that the IDL attribute getter returns
the current value of the content attribute, and the setter changes the
value of the content attribute to the given value.

<a href="#reflected-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-5">Reflected
targets</a> have these associated algorithms:

- <span id="get-the-element" class="dfn">get the element</span>: takes
  no arguments; returns an element.
- <span id="get-the-content-attribute" class="dfn">get the content
  attribute</span>: takes no arguments; returns null or a string.
- <span id="set-the-content-attribute" class="dfn">set the content
  attribute</span>: takes a string `value`; returns nothing.
- <span id="delete-the-content-attribute" class="dfn">delete the content
  attribute</span>: takes no arguments; returns nothing.

<div var-scope="">

For a <a href="#reflected-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-6">reflected
target</a> that is an element `element`, these are defined as follows:

<a href="#get-the-element"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-element">get
the element</a>  
1.  Return `element`.

<a href="#get-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-content-attribute">get
the content attribute</a>  
1.  Let `attribute` be the result of <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-get-by-namespace"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:concept-element-attributes-get-by-namespace"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-get-by-namespace">getting an
    attribute by namespace and local name</a> given null, the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-2">reflected
    content attribute name</a>, and `element`.

2.  If `attribute` is null, then return null.

3.  Return `attribute`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-attribute-value"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:concept-attribute-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-attribute-value">value</a>.

<a href="#set-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:set-the-content-attribute">set
the content attribute</a> with a string `value`  
1.  <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:concept-element-attributes-set-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-set-value">Set an attribute
    value</a> given `element`, the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-3">reflected
    content attribute name</a>, and `value`.

<a href="#delete-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:delete-the-content-attribute">delete
the content attribute</a>  
1.  <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-remove-by-namespace"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:concept-element-attributes-remove-by-namespace"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-remove-by-namespace">Remove
    an attribute by namespace and local name</a> given null, the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-4">reflected
    content attribute name</a>, and `element`.

</div>

<div var-scope="">

For a <a href="#reflected-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-7">reflected
target</a> that is an [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object
`elementInternals`, they are defined as follows:

<a href="#get-the-element"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-element-2">get
the element</a>  
1.  Return `elementInternals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-2">target
    element</a>.

<a href="#get-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-content-attribute-2">get
the content attribute</a>  
1.  If `elementInternals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-3">target
    element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map-2">internal
    content attribute map</a>\[the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-5">reflected
    content attribute name</a>\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">does not exist</a>, then return null.

2.  Return `elementInternals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-4">target
    element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map-3">internal
    content attribute map</a>\[the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-6">reflected
    content attribute name</a>\].

<a href="#set-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:set-the-content-attribute-2">set
the content attribute</a> with a string `value`  
1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:map-set"
    data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> `elementInternals`'s
    <a href="#internals-target"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-5">target
    element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map-4">internal
    content attribute map</a>\[the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-7">reflected
    content attribute name</a>\] to `value`.

<a href="#delete-the-content-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:delete-the-content-attribute-2">delete
the content attribute</a>  
1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-remove"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:map-remove"
    data-x-internal="map-remove">Remove</a> `elementInternals`'s
    <a href="#internals-target"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-6">target
    element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map-5">internal
    content attribute map</a>\[the
    <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
    id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-8">reflected
    content attribute name</a>\].

</div>

This results in somewhat redundant data structures for
[`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) objects as their
<a href="#internals-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internals-target-7">target
element</a>'s <a href="#internal-content-attribute-map"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:internal-content-attribute-map-6">internal
content attribute map</a> cannot be directly manipulated and as such
reflection is only happening in a single direction. This approach was
nevertheless chosen to make it less error-prone to define IDL attributes
that are shared between <a href="#reflected-target"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-target-8">reflected
targets</a> and benefit from common API semantics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

IDL attributes of type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-domstring">DOMString</code></a>
or <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-domstring-2"
data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code>DOMString</code></a>`?` that
<a href="#reflect"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflect">reflect</a>
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:enumerated-attribute">enumerated</a>
content attributes can be <span id="limited-to-only-known-values"
class="dfn">limited to only known values</span>. Per the processing
models below, those will cause the getters for such IDL attributes to
only return keywords for those enumerated attributes, or the empty
string or null.

If a <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-3">reflected
IDL attribute</a> has the type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-domstring-3">DOMString</code></a>:

- <div algorithm="">

  The getter steps are:

  1.  Let `element` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#get-the-element"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-element-3">get
      the element</a>.

  2.  Let `contentAttributeValue` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-2"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
      <a href="#get-the-content-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-content-attribute-3">get
      the content attribute</a>.

  3.  Let `attributeDefinition` be the attribute definition of
      `element`'s content attribute whose namespace is null and local
      name is the <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-9">reflected
      content attribute name</a>.

  4.  If `attributeDefinition` indicates it is an
      <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:enumerated-attribute-2">enumerated
      attribute</a> and the <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-4">reflected
      IDL attribute</a> is defined to be
      <a href="#limited-to-only-known-values"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:limited-to-only-known-values">limited
      to only known values</a>:

      1.  If `contentAttributeValue` does not correspond to any state of
          `attributeDefinition` (e.g., it is null and there is no
          *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)*), or if it
          is in a state of `attributeDefinition` with no associated
          keyword value, then return the empty string.

      2.  Return the <a href="#canonical-keyword"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:canonical-keyword">canonical
          keyword</a> for the state of `attributeDefinition` that
          `contentAttributeValue` corresponds to.

  5.  If `contentAttributeValue` is null, then return the empty string.

  6.  Return `contentAttributeValue`.

  </div>

- <div algorithm="">

  The setter steps are to run
  <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-3"
  data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#set-the-content-attribute"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:set-the-content-attribute-3">set
  the content attribute</a> with the given value.

  </div>

If a <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-5">reflected
IDL attribute</a> has the type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-domstring-4"
data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code>DOMString</code></a>`?`:

- <div algorithm="">

  The getter steps are:

  1.  Let `element` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-4"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#get-the-element"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-element-4">get
      the element</a>.

  2.  Let `contentAttributeValue` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-5"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
      <a href="#get-the-content-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-content-attribute-4">get
      the content attribute</a>.

  3.  Let `attributeDefinition` be the attribute definition of
      `element`'s content attribute whose namespace is null and local
      name is the <a href="#reflected-content-attribute-name"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-content-attribute-name-10">reflected
      content attribute name</a>.

  4.  If `attributeDefinition` indicates it is an
      <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:enumerated-attribute-3">enumerated
      attribute</a>:

      1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:assert"
          data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: the
          <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-6">reflected
          IDL attribute</a> is <a href="#limited-to-only-known-values"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:limited-to-only-known-values-2">limited
          to only known values</a>.

      2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:assert-2"
          data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `contentAttributeValue`
          corresponds to a state of `attributeDefinition`.

      3.  If `contentAttributeValue` corresponds to a state of
          `attributeDefinition` with no associated keyword value, then
          return null.

      4.  Return the <a href="#canonical-keyword"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:canonical-keyword-2">canonical
          keyword</a> for the state of `attributeDefinition` that
          `contentAttributeValue` corresponds to.

  5.  Return `contentAttributeValue`.

- <div algorithm="">

  The setter steps are:

  1.  If the given value is null, then run
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-6"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
      <a href="#delete-the-content-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:delete-the-content-attribute-3">delete
      the content attribute</a>.

  2.  Otherwise, run <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-7"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
      <a href="#set-the-content-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:set-the-content-attribute-4">set
      the content attribute</a> with the given value.

  </div>

If a <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-7">reflected
IDL attribute</a> has the type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-USVString"
data-x-internal="idl-usvstring"><code
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-usvstring">USVString</code></a>,
optionally <span id="treated-as-a-url" class="dfn">treated as a
URL</span>:

- <div algorithm="">

  The getter steps are:

  1.  Let `element` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-8"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#get-the-element"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-element-5">get
      the element</a>.

  2.  Let `contentAttributeValue` be the result of running
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-9"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
      <a href="#get-the-content-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:get-the-content-attribute-5">get
      the content attribute</a>.

  3.  If the <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-8">reflected
      IDL attribute</a> is <a href="#treated-as-a-url"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:treated-as-a-url">treated
      as a URL</a>:

      1.  If `contentAttributeValue` is null, then return the empty
          string.

      2.  Let `urlString` be the result of
          <a href="#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url">encoding-parsing-and-serializing
          a URL</a> given `contentAttributeValue`, relative to
          `element`'s
          <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
          id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:node-document"
          data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

      3.  If `urlString` is not failure, then return `urlString`.

  4.  Return `contentAttributeValue`,
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string-convert"
      id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:convert"
      data-x-internal="convert">converted to a scalar value string</a>.

  </div>

- <div algorithm="">

  The setter steps are to run
  <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:this-10"
  data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#set-the-content-attribute"
  id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:set-the-content-attribute-5">set
  the content attribute</a> with the given value.

  </div>

If a <a href="#reflected-idl-attribute"
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:reflected-idl-attribute-9">reflected
IDL attribute</a> has the type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-boolean"
data-x-internal="idl-boolean"><code
id="reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-boolean">boolean</code></a>:

- <div algorithm="">

  The getter steps are:

  1.  Let `contentAttributeValue` be the result of running
