<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-radionodelist-value" class="dfn"
dfn-for="RadioNodeList" dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> IDL
attribute on the [`RadioNodeList`](#radionodelist) object, on getting,
must return the value returned by running the following steps:

1.  Let `element` be the first element in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:tree-order-4"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> represented by the
    [`RadioNodeList`](#radionodelist) object that is an
    [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
    <a href="#radio-button-state-(type=radio)"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:radio-button-state-(type=radio)">Radio
    Button</a> state and whose <a href="#concept-fe-checked"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:concept-fe-checked">checkedness</a>
    is true. Otherwise, let it be null.

2.  If `element` is null, return the empty string.

3.  If `element` is an element with no [`value`](#attr-input-value)
    attribute, return the string "`on`".

4.  Otherwise, return the value of `element`'s
    [`value`](#attr-input-value) attribute.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, the [`value`](#dom-radionodelist-value) IDL attribute must
run the following steps:

1.  If the new value is the string "`on`": let `element` be the first
    element in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:tree-order-5"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> represented by the
    [`RadioNodeList`](#radionodelist) object that is an
    [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
    <a href="#radio-button-state-(type=radio)"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:radio-button-state-(type=radio)-2">Radio
    Button</a> state and whose [`value`](#attr-input-value) content
    attribute is either absent, or present and equal to the new value,
    if any. If no such element exists, then instead let `element` be
    null.

    Otherwise: let `element` be the first element in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:tree-order-6"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> represented by the
    [`RadioNodeList`](#radionodelist) object that is an
    [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
    <a href="#radio-button-state-(type=radio)"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:radio-button-state-(type=radio)-3">Radio
    Button</a> state and whose [`value`](#attr-input-value) content
    attribute is present and equal to the new value, if any. If no such
    element exists, then instead let `element` be null.

2.  If `element` is not null, then set its <a href="#concept-fe-checked"
    id="the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface:concept-fe-checked-2">checkedness</a>
    to true.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">2.6.4.3</span> The [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) interface<a href="#the-htmloptionscollection-interface" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLOptionsCollection](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLOptionsCollection "The HTMLOptionsCollection interface represents a collection of <option> HTML elements (in document order) and offers methods and properties for selecting from the list as well as optionally altering its items. This object is returned only by the options property of select.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari3+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12.1+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer6+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS1+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android yes">WebView
Android37+</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) interface is used
for <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-collection"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:concept-collection"
data-x-internal="concept-collection">collections</a> of
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements. It is always rooted on a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element and has attributes and methods
that manipulate that element's descendants.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOptionsCollection : HTMLCollection {
  // inherits item(), namedItem()
  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long length; // shadows inherited length
  [CEReactions] setter undefined (unsigned long index, HTMLOptionElement? option);
  [CEReactions] undefined add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, optional (HTMLElement or long)? before = null);
  [CEReactions] undefined remove(long index);
  attribute long selectedIndex;
};
```

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-length"
id="dom-htmloptionscollection-length-dev"><code>length</code></a>  
Returns the number of elements in `collection`.

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-length"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:dom-htmloptionscollection-length-2"><code>length</code></a>` = ``value`  
When set to a smaller number than the existing length, truncates the
number of [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in the container
corresponding to `collection`.

When set to a greater number than the existing length, if that number is
less than or equal to 100000, adds new blank
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements to the container corresponding
to `collection`.

`element`` = ``collection``.`<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-htmlcollection-item"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:dom-htmlcollection-item-2"
data-x-internal="dom-htmlcollection-item"><code>item</code></a>`(``index``)`  
`element`` = ``collection``[``index``]`  
Returns the item at index `index` in `collection`. The items are sorted
in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:tree-order"
data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>.

`collection``[``index``] = ``element`  
When `index` is a greater number than the number of items in
`collection`, adds new blank [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in
the corresponding container.

When set to null, removes the item at index `index` from `collection`.

When set to an [`option`](#the-option-element) element, adds or replaces
it at index `index` in `collection`.

`element`` = ``collection``.`<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-htmlcollection-nameditem"
id="dom-htmlcollection-nameditem-dev"
data-x-internal="dom-htmlcollection-nameditem"><code>namedItem</code></a>`(``name``)`  
`element`` = ``collection``[``name``]`  
Returns the item with <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:concept-id"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> or [`name`](#attr-option-name)
`name` from `collection`.

If there are multiple matching items, then the first is returned.

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-add"
id="dom-htmloptionscollection-add-dev"><code>add</code></a>`(``element``[, ``before``])`  
Inserts `element` before the node given by `before`.

The `before` argument can be a number, in which case `element` is
inserted before the item with that number, or an element from
`collection`, in which case `element` is inserted before that element.

If `before` is omitted, null, or a number out of range, then `element`
will be added at the end of the list.

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:hierarchyrequesterror"
data-x-internal="hierarchyrequesterror">"<code>HierarchyRequestError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a>
if `element` is an ancestor of the element into which it is to be
inserted.

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-remove"
id="dom-htmloptionscollection-remove-dev"><code>remove</code></a>`(``index``)`  
Removes the item with index `index` from `collection`.

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex-2"><code>selectedIndex</code></a>  
Returns the index of the first selected item, if any, or −1 if there is
no selected item.

`collection``.`<a href="#dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex"
id="dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex-dev"><code>selectedIndex</code></a>` = ``index`  
Changes the selection to the [`option`](#the-option-element) element at
index `index` in `collection`.

<div algorithm="">

The object's
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:supported-property-indices"
data-x-internal="supported-property-indices">supported property
indices</a> are as defined for
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:htmlcollection-2">HTMLCollection</code></a>
objects.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-htmloptionscollection-length" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOptionsCollection" dfn-type="attribute">`length`</span>
getter steps are to return the number of nodes
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection"
data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
collection</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`length`](#dom-htmloptionscollection-length) setter steps are:

1.  Let `current` be the number of nodes
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection-2"
    data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
    collection</a>.

2.  If the given value is greater than `current`, then:

    1.  If the given value is greater than 100,000, then return.

    2.  Let `n` be `value` − `current`.

    3.  Append `n` new [`option`](#the-option-element) elements with no
        attributes and no child nodes to the
        [`select`](#the-select-element) element on which
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:this"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a> is rooted.

3.  If the given value is less than `current`, then:

    1.  Let `n` be `current` − `value`.

    2.  Remove the last `n` nodes in the collection from their parent
        nodes.

</div>

Setting [`length`](#dom-htmloptionscollection-length) never removes or
adds any [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) elements, and never adds
new children to existing [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) elements
(though it can remove children from them).

<div algorithm="">

The
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:supported-property-names"
data-x-internal="supported-property-names">supported property names</a>
consist of the non-empty values of all the [`id`](#the-id-attribute) and
[`name`](#attr-option-name) attributes of all the elements
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection-3"
data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
collection</a>, in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:tree-order-2"
data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>, ignoring later duplicates,
with the [`id`](#the-id-attribute) of an element preceding its
[`name`](#attr-option-name) if it contributes both, they differ from
each other, and neither is the duplicate of an earlier entry.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to <a
href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property"
data-x-internal="set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property">set the value
of a new indexed property</a> or <a
href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-an-existing-indexed-property"
id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:set-the-value-of-an-existing-indexed-property"
data-x-internal="set-the-value-of-an-existing-indexed-property">set the
value of an existing indexed property</a> for a given property index
`index` to a new value `value`, it must run the following algorithm:

1.  If `value` is null, invoke the steps for the
    [`remove`](#dom-htmloptionscollection-remove) method with `index` as
    the argument, and return.

2.  Let `length` be the number of nodes
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection-4"
    data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
    collection</a>.

3.  Let `delta` be `index` minus `length`.

4.  If `delta` is greater than zero, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:concept-node-append"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">append</a> a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:documentfragment">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    consisting of `delta` new [`option`](#the-option-element) elements
    with no attributes and no child nodes to the
    [`select`](#the-select-element) element on which the
    [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) is rooted.

5.  If `delta` is greater than or equal to zero,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:concept-node-append-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">append</a> `value` to the
    [`select`](#the-select-element) element. Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:concept-node-replace"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace">replace</a> the `index`th
    element in the collection by `value`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-htmloptionscollection-add" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOptionsCollection"
dfn-type="method">`add(``element``, ``before``)`</span> method must act
according to the following algorithm:

1.  If `element` is an ancestor of the [`select`](#the-select-element)
    element on which the
    [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) is rooted, then
    throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:hierarchyrequesterror-2"
    data-x-internal="hierarchyrequesterror">"<code>HierarchyRequestError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If `before` is an element, but that element isn't a descendant of
    the [`select`](#the-select-element) element on which the
    [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) is rooted, then
    throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notfounderror"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:notfounderror"
    data-x-internal="notfounderror">"<code>NotFoundError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  If `element` and `before` are the same element, then return.

4.  If `before` is a node, then let `reference` be that node. Otherwise,
    if `before` is an integer, and there is a `before`th node in the
    collection, let `reference` be that node. Otherwise, let `reference`
    be null.

5.  If `reference` is not null, let `parent` be the parent node of
    `reference`. Otherwise, let `parent` be the
    [`select`](#the-select-element) element on which the
    [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) is rooted.

6.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-pre-insert"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:pre-insert"
    data-x-internal="pre-insert">Pre-insert</a> `element` into `parent`
    node before `reference`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-htmloptionscollection-remove" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOptionsCollection"
dfn-type="method">`remove(``index``)`</span> method must act according
to the following algorithm:

1.  If the number of nodes
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection-5"
    data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
    collection</a> is zero, return.

2.  If `index` is not a number greater than or equal to 0 and less than
    the number of nodes
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
    id="the-htmloptionscollection-interface:represented-by-the-collection-6"
    data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented by the
    collection</a>, return.

3.  Let `element` be the `index`th element in the collection.

4.  Remove `element` from its parent node.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOptionsCollection"
dfn-type="attribute">`selectedIndex`</span> IDL attribute must act like
the identically named attribute on the [`select`](#the-select-element)
element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection)
is rooted

</div>

The [`DOMStringList`](#domstringlist) interface is a non-fashionable
retro way of representing a list of strings.

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface DOMStringList {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter DOMString? item(unsigned long index);
  boolean contains(DOMString string);
};
```

New APIs must use `sequence<DOMString>` or equivalent rather than
[`DOMStringList`](#domstringlist).

`strings``.`<a href="#dom-domstringlist-length"
id="dom-domstringlist-length-dev"><code>length</code></a>  
Returns the number of strings in `strings`.

`strings``[``index``]`  
`strings``.`<a href="#dom-domstringlist-item"
id="dom-domstringlist-item-dev"><code>item</code></a>`(``index``)`  
Returns the string with index `index` from `strings`.

`strings``.`<a href="#dom-domstringlist-contains"
id="dom-domstringlist-contains-dev"><code>contains</code></a>`(``string``)`  
Returns true if `strings` contains `string`, and false otherwise.

Each [`DOMStringList`](#domstringlist) object has an associated
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="the-domstringlist-interface:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The [`DOMStringList`](#domstringlist) interface
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="the-domstringlist-interface:supports-indexed-properties"
data-x-internal="supports-indexed-properties">supports indexed
properties</a>. The
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="the-domstringlist-interface:supported-property-indices"

indices</a> are the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-get-the-indices"

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-domstringlist-interface:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
associated list.

### <span class="secno">2.7</span> Safe passing of structured data<a href="#safe-passing-of-structured-data" class="self-link"></a>

<span id="structured-clone"></span>To support passing JavaScript
objects, including
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="safe-passing-of-structured-data:platform-object"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform objects</a>, across
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="safe-passing-of-structured-data:realm"
data-x-internal="realm">realm</a> boundaries, this specification defines
the following infrastructure for serializing and deserializing objects,
including in some cases transferring the underlying data instead of
copying it. Collectively this serialization/deserialization process is
known as "structured cloning", although most APIs perform separate
serialization and deserialization steps. (With the notable exception
being the [`structuredClone()`](#dom-structuredclone) method.)

This section uses the terminology and typographic conventions from the
JavaScript specification. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

#### <span class="secno">2.7.1</span> <span class="dfn">Serializable objects</span><a href="#serializable-objects" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#serializable-objects"
id="serializable-objects:serializable-objects">Serializable objects</a>
support being serialized, and later deserialized, in a way that is
independent of any given
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="serializable-objects:realm" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>. This
allows them to be stored on disk and later restored, or cloned across
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents"
id="serializable-objects:agent" data-x-internal="agent">agent</a> and
even <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="serializable-objects:agent-cluster"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> boundaries.

Not all objects are <a href="#serializable-objects"
id="serializable-objects:serializable-objects-2">serializable
objects</a>, and not all aspects of objects that are
<a href="#serializable-objects"
id="serializable-objects:serializable-objects-3">serializable
objects</a> are necessarily preserved when they are serialized.

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="serializable-objects:platform-object"
data-x-internal="platform-object">Platform objects</a> can be
<a href="#serializable-objects"
id="serializable-objects:serializable-objects-4">serializable
objects</a> if their
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
id="serializable-objects:primary-interface"
data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> is decorated
with the <span id="serializable" class="dfn"
dfn-type="extended-attribute" lt="Serializable">`[Serializable]`</span>
IDL <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute"
id="serializable-objects:extended-attribute"
data-x-internal="extended-attribute">extended attribute</a>. Such
interfaces must also define the following algorithms:

<span id="serialization-steps" class="dfn" export="">serialization steps</span>, taking a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="serializable-objects:platform-object-2"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> `value`, a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="serializable-objects:record" data-x-internal="record">Record</a> `serialized`, and a boolean `forStorage`  
A set of steps that serializes the data in `value` into fields of
`serialized`. The resulting data serialized into `serialized` must be
independent of any <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="serializable-objects:realm-2" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>.

These steps may throw an exception if serialization is not possible.

These steps may perform a <a href="#sub-serialization"
id="serializable-objects:sub-serialization">sub-serialization</a> to
serialize nested data structures. They should not call
<a href="#structuredserialize"
id="serializable-objects:structuredserialize">StructuredSerialize</a>
directly, as doing so will omit the important `memory` argument.

The introduction of these steps should omit mention of the `forStorage`
argument if it is not relevant to the algorithm.

<span id="deserialization-steps" class="dfn" export="">deserialization steps</span>, taking a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="serializable-objects:record-2" data-x-internal="record">Record</a> `serialized`, a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="serializable-objects:platform-object-3"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> `value`, and a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="serializable-objects:realm-3" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a> `targetRealm`  
A set of steps that deserializes the data in `serialized`, using it to
set up `value` as appropriate. `value` will be a newly-created instance
of the <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="serializable-objects:platform-object-4"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> type in question,
with none of its internal data set up; setting that up is the job of
these steps.

These steps may throw an exception if deserialization is not possible.

These steps may perform a <a href="#sub-deserialization"
id="serializable-objects:sub-deserialization">sub-deserialization</a> to
deserialize nested data structures. They should not call
<a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="serializable-objects:structureddeserialize">StructuredDeserialize</a>
directly, as doing so will omit the important `targetRealm` and `memory`
arguments.

It is up to the definition of individual platform objects to determine
what data is serialized and deserialized by these steps. Typically the
steps are very symmetric.

The [`[Serializable]`](#serializable) extended attribute must take no
arguments, and must only appear on an interface. It must not appear more
than once on an interface.

For a given
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="serializable-objects:platform-object-5"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a>, only the object's
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
id="serializable-objects:primary-interface-2"
data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> is considered
during the (de)serialization process. Thus, if inheritance is involved
in defining the interface, each
[`[Serializable]`](#serializable)-annotated interface in the inheritance
chain needs to define standalone <a href="#serialization-steps"
id="serializable-objects:serialization-steps">serialization steps</a>
and <a href="#deserialization-steps"
id="serializable-objects:deserialization-steps">deserialization
steps</a>, including taking into account any important data that might
come from inherited interfaces.

<div class="example">

Let's say we were defining a platform object `Person`, which had
associated with it two pieces of associated data:

- a name value, which is a string; and

- a best friend value, which is either another `Person` instance or
  null.

We could then define `Person` instances to be
<a href="#serializable-objects"
id="serializable-objects:serializable-objects-5">serializable
objects</a> by annotating the `Person` interface with the
[`[Serializable]`](#serializable)
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute"
id="serializable-objects:extended-attribute-2"
data-x-internal="extended-attribute">extended attribute</a>, and
defining the following accompanying algorithms:

<div algorithm="">

Their <a href="#serialization-steps"
id="serializable-objects:serialization-steps-2">serialization steps</a>,
given `value` and `serialized`:

1.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] to `value`'s associated name value.

2.  Let `serializedBestFriend` be the <a href="#sub-serialization"
    id="serializable-objects:sub-serialization-2">sub-serialization</a>
    of `value`'s associated best friend value.

3.  Set `serialized`.\[\[BestFriend\]\] to `serializedBestFriend`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Their <a href="#deserialization-steps"
id="serializable-objects:deserialization-steps-2">deserialization
steps</a>, given `serialized`, `value`, and `targetRealm`:

1.  Set `value`'s associated name value to `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\].

2.  Let `deserializedBestFriend` be the <a href="#sub-deserialization"
    id="serializable-objects:sub-deserialization-2">sub-deserialization</a>
    of `serialized`.\[\[BestFriend\]\].

3.  Set `value`'s associated best friend value to
    `deserializedBestFriend`.

</div>

</div>

Objects defined in the JavaScript specification are handled by the
<a href="#structuredserialize"
id="serializable-objects:structuredserialize-2">StructuredSerialize</a>
abstract operation directly.

<a href="#cloneable-objects" class="self-link"></a>Originally, this
specification defined the concept of "cloneable objects", which could be
cloned from one <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="serializable-objects:realm-4" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a> to
another. However, to better specify the behavior of certain more complex
situations, the model was updated to make the serialization and
deserialization explicit.

#### <span class="secno">2.7.2</span> <span class="dfn">Transferable objects</span><a href="#transferable-objects" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#transferable-objects"
id="transferable-objects:transferable-objects">Transferable objects</a>
support being transferred across
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents"
id="transferable-objects:agent" data-x-internal="agent">agents</a>.
Transferring is effectively recreating the object while sharing a
reference to the underlying data and then detaching the object being
transferred. This is useful to transfer ownership of expensive
resources. Not all objects are <a href="#transferable-objects"
id="transferable-objects:transferable-objects-2">transferable
objects</a> and not all aspects of objects that are
<a href="#transferable-objects"
id="transferable-objects:transferable-objects-3">transferable
objects</a> are necessarily preserved when transferred.

Transferring is an irreversible and non-idempotent operation. Once an
object has been transferred, it cannot be transferred, or indeed used,
again.

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object"
data-x-internal="platform-object">Platform objects</a> can be
<a href="#transferable-objects"
id="transferable-objects:transferable-objects-4">transferable
objects</a> if their
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
id="transferable-objects:primary-interface"
data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> is decorated
with the <span id="transferable" class="dfn"
dfn-type="extended-attribute" lt="Transferable">`[Transferable]`</span>
IDL <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute"
id="transferable-objects:extended-attribute"
data-x-internal="extended-attribute">extended attribute</a>. Such
interfaces must also define the following algorithms:

<span id="transfer-steps" class="dfn" export="">transfer steps</span>, taking a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object-2"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> `value` and a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="transferable-objects:record" data-x-internal="record">Record</a> `dataHolder`  
A set of steps that transfers the data in `value` into fields of
`dataHolder`. The resulting data held in `dataHolder` must be
independent of any <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="transferable-objects:realm" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>.

These steps may throw an exception if transferral is not possible.

<span id="transfer-receiving-steps" class="dfn" export="">transfer-receiving steps</span>, taking a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="transferable-objects:record-2" data-x-internal="record">Record</a> `dataHolder` and a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object-3"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> `value`  
A set of steps that receives the data in `dataHolder`, using it to set
up `value` as appropriate. `value` will be a newly-created instance of
the <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object-4"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> type in question,
with none of its internal data set up; setting that up is the job of
these steps.

These steps may throw an exception if it is not possible to receive the
transfer.

It is up to the definition of individual platform objects to determine
what data is transferred by these steps. Typically the steps are very
symmetric.

The [`[Transferable]`](#transferable) extended attribute must take no
arguments, and must only appear on an interface. It must not appear more
than once on an interface.

For a given
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object-5"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a>, only the object's
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
id="transferable-objects:primary-interface-2"
data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> is considered
during the transferring process. Thus, if inheritance is involved in
defining the interface, each [`[Transferable]`](#transferable)-annotated
interface in the inheritance chain needs to define standalone
<a href="#transfer-steps"
id="transferable-objects:transfer-steps">transfer steps</a> and
<a href="#transfer-receiving-steps"
id="transferable-objects:transfer-receiving-steps">transfer-receiving
steps</a>, including taking into account any important data that might
come from inherited interfaces.

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="transferable-objects:platform-object-6"
data-x-internal="platform-object">Platform objects</a> that are
<a href="#transferable-objects"
id="transferable-objects:transferable-objects-5">transferable
objects</a> have a <span id="detached" class="dfn"
dfn-for="platform object" dfn-type="attribute">\[\[Detached\]\]</span>
internal slot. This is used to ensure that once a platform object has
been transferred, it cannot be transferred again.

Objects defined in the JavaScript specification are handled by the
<a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
id="transferable-objects:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>
abstract operation directly.

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.3</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredSerializeInternal</span> ( `value`, `forStorage` \[ , `memory` \] )<a href="#structuredserializeinternal" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>
abstract operation takes as input a JavaScript value `value` and
serializes it to a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="structuredserializeinternal:realm" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>-independent
form, represented here as a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="structuredserializeinternal:record"
data-x-internal="record">Record</a>. This serialized form has all the
information necessary to later deserialize into a new JavaScript value
in a different realm.

This process can throw an exception, for example when trying to
serialize un-serializable objects.

1.  If `memory` was not supplied, let `memory` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:ordered-map"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a>.

    The purpose of the `memory` map is to avoid serializing objects
    twice. This ends up preserving cycles and the identity of duplicate
    objects in graphs.

2.  If `memory`\[`value`\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then return
    `memory`\[`value`\].

3.  Let `deep` be false.

4.  If `value` is undefined, null, <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-boolean-type"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:js-boolean"
    data-x-internal="js-boolean">a Boolean</a>, <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:js-number" data-x-internal="js-number">a
    Number</a>, <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-bigint-type"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:js-bigint" data-x-internal="js-bigint">a
    BigInt</a>, or <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:js-string" data-x-internal="js-string">a
    String</a>, then return { \[\[Type\]\]: "primitive", \[\[Value\]\]:
    `value` }.

5.  If `value` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-symbol-type"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:js-symbol"
    data-x-internal="js-symbol">is a Symbol</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

6.  Let `serialized` be an uninitialized value.

7.  If `value` has a \[\[BooleanData\]\] internal slot, then set
    `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Boolean", \[\[BooleanData\]\]:
    `value`.\[\[BooleanData\]\] }.

8.  Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[NumberData\]\] internal slot, then
    set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Number", \[\[NumberData\]\]:
    `value`.\[\[NumberData\]\] }.

9.  Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[BigIntData\]\] internal slot, then
    set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "BigInt", \[\[BigIntData\]\]:
    `value`.\[\[BigIntData\]\] }.

10. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[StringData\]\] internal slot, then
    set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "String", \[\[StringData\]\]:
    `value`.\[\[StringData\]\] }.

11. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[DateValue\]\] internal slot, then
    set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Date", \[\[DateValue\]\]:
    `value`.\[\[DateValue\]\] }.

12. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[RegExpMatcher\]\] internal slot,
    then set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "RegExp",
    \[\[RegExpMatcher\]\]: `value`.\[\[RegExpMatcher\]\],
    \[\[OriginalSource\]\]: `value`.\[\[OriginalSource\]\],
    \[\[OriginalFlags\]\]: `value`.\[\[OriginalFlags\]\] }.

13. Otherwise, if `value` has an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot,
    then:

    1.  If <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-issharedarraybuffer"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:issharedarraybuffer"
        data-x-internal="issharedarraybuffer">IsSharedArrayBuffer</a>(`value`)
        is true, then:

        1.  If the <a href="#current-settings-object"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:current-settings-object">current
            settings object</a>'s
            <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> is false, then throw a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-2"
            data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
            data-x-internal="domexception"><code
            id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

            This check is only needed when serializing (and not when
            deserializing) as the
            <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability-2">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> cannot change over time and a
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer-objects"
            data-x-internal="sharedarraybuffer"><code
            id="structuredserializeinternal:sharedarraybuffer">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>
            cannot leave an
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:agent-cluster"
            data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>.

        2.  If `forStorage` is true, then throw a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-3"
            data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
            data-x-internal="domexception"><code
            id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

        3.  If `value` has an \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] internal
            slot, then set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]:
            "GrowableSharedArrayBuffer", \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\],
            \[\[ArrayBufferByteLengthData\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLengthData\]\],
            \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\],
            \[\[AgentCluster\]\]: the
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:surrounding-agent"
            data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:agent-cluster-2"
            data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> }.

        4.  Otherwise, set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]:
            "SharedArrayBuffer", \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\],
            \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\], \[\[AgentCluster\]\]:
            the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:surrounding-agent-2"
            data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:agent-cluster-3"
            data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> }.

    2.  Otherwise:

        1.  If <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdetachedbuffer"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:isdetachedbuffer"
            data-x-internal="isdetachedbuffer">IsDetachedBuffer</a>(`value`)
            is true, then throw a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-4"
            data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
            data-x-internal="domexception"><code
            id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

        2.  Let `size` be `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

        3.  Let `dataCopy` be ?
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-createbytedatablock"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:createbytedatablock"
            data-x-internal="createbytedatablock">CreateByteDataBlock</a>(`size`).

            This can throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
            data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
            id="structuredserializeinternal:js-rangeerror">RangeError</code></a>
            exception upon allocation failure.

        4.  Perform
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-copydatablockbytes"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:copydatablockbytes"
            data-x-internal="copydatablockbytes">CopyDataBlockBytes</a>(`dataCopy`,
            0, `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\], 0, `size`).

        5.  If `value` has an \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] internal
            slot, then set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]:
            "ResizableArrayBuffer", \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\]: `dataCopy`,
            \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\]: `size`,
            \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\]:
            `value`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] }.

        6.  Otherwise, set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]:
            "ArrayBuffer", \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\]: `dataCopy`,
            \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\]: `size` }.

14. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot,
    then:

    1.  If
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isarraybufferviewoutofbounds"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:isarraybufferviewoutofbounds"
        data-x-internal="isarraybufferviewoutofbounds">IsArrayBufferViewOutOfBounds</a>(`value`)
        is true, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-5"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  Let `buffer` be the value of `value`'s \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\]
        internal slot.

    3.  Let `bufferSerialized` be ?
        <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-2">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`buffer`,
        `forStorage`, `memory`).

    4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:assert"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `bufferSerialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "ArrayBuffer",
        "ResizableArrayBuffer", "SharedArrayBuffer", or
        "GrowableSharedArrayBuffer".

    5.  If `value` has a \[\[DataView\]\] internal slot, then set
        `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "ArrayBufferView",
        \[\[Constructor\]\]: "DataView", \[\[ArrayBufferSerialized\]\]:
        `bufferSerialized`, \[\[ByteLength\]\]:
        `value`.\[\[ByteLength\]\], \[\[ByteOffset\]\]:
        `value`.\[\[ByteOffset\]\] }.

    6.  Otherwise:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:assert-2"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `value` has a
            \[\[TypedArrayName\]\] internal slot.

        2.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "ArrayBufferView",
            \[\[Constructor\]\]: `value`.\[\[TypedArrayName\]\],
            \[\[ArrayBufferSerialized\]\]: `bufferSerialized`,
            \[\[ByteLength\]\]: `value`.\[\[ByteLength\]\],
            \[\[ByteOffset\]\]: `value`.\[\[ByteOffset\]\],
            \[\[ArrayLength\]\]: `value`.\[\[ArrayLength\]\] }.

15. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[MapData\]\] internal slot, then:

    1.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Map", \[\[MapData\]\]: a
        new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list"
        data-x-internal="js-list">List</a> }.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

16. Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[SetData\]\] internal slot, then:

    1.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Set", \[\[SetData\]\]: a
        new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list-2"
        data-x-internal="js-list">List</a> }.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

17. Otherwise, if `value` has an \[\[ErrorData\]\] internal slot and
    `value` is not a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:platform-object"
    data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a>, then:

    1.  Let `name` be ? <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:js-get" data-x-internal="js-get">Get</a>(`value`,
        "name").

    2.  If `name` is not one of "Error", "EvalError", "RangeError",
        "ReferenceError", "SyntaxError", "TypeError", or "URIError",
        then set `name` to "Error".

    3.  Let `valueMessageDesc` be ?
        `value`.\[\[GetOwnProperty\]\]("`message`").

    4.  Let `message` be undefined if
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdatadescriptor"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:isdatadescriptor"
        data-x-internal="isdatadescriptor">IsDataDescriptor</a>(`valueMessageDesc`)
        is false, and ? <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:tostring"
        data-x-internal="tostring">ToString</a>(`valueMessageDesc`.\[\[Value\]\])
        otherwise.

    5.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Error", \[\[Name\]\]:
        `name`, \[\[Message\]\]: `message` }.

    6.  User agents should attach a serialized representation of any
        interesting accompanying data which are not yet specified,
        notably the `stack` property, to `serialized`.

        See the Error Stacks proposal for in-progress work on specifying
        this data. [\[JSERRORSTACKS\]](#refsJSERRORSTACKS)

18. Otherwise, if `value` is an Array exotic object, then:

    1.  Let `valueLenDescriptor` be ?
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarygetownproperty"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:ordinarygetownproperty"
        data-x-internal="ordinarygetownproperty">OrdinaryGetOwnProperty</a>(`value`,
        "`length`").

    2.  Let `valueLen` be `valueLenDescriptor`.\[\[Value\]\].

    3.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Array", \[\[Length\]\]:
        `valueLen`, \[\[Properties\]\]: a new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list-3"
        data-x-internal="js-list">List</a> }.

    4.  Set `deep` to true.

19. Otherwise, if `value` is a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:platform-object-2"
    data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> that is a
    <a href="#serializable-objects"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:serializable-objects">serializable
    object</a>:

    1.  If `value` has a <a href="#detached"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:detached">[[Detached]]</a>
        internal slot whose value is true, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-6"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  Let `typeString` be the identifier of the
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:primary-interface"
        data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> of
        `value`.

    3.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: `typeString` }.

    4.  Set `deep` to true.

20. Otherwise, if `value` is a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:platform-object-3"
    data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-7"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

21. Otherwise, if <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:iscallable"
    data-x-internal="iscallable">IsCallable</a>(`value`) is true, then
    throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-8"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

22. Otherwise, if `value` has any internal slot other than
    \[\[Prototype\]\], \[\[Extensible\]\], or \[\[PrivateElements\]\],
    then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-9"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-9">DOMException</code></a>.

    For instance, a \[\[PromiseState\]\] or \[\[WeakMapData\]\] internal
    slot.

23. Otherwise, if `value` is an exotic object and `value` is not the <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:object.prototype"
    data-x-internal="object.prototype">%Object.prototype%</a> intrinsic
    object associated with any
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:realm-2"
    data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:datacloneerror-10"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structuredserializeinternal:domexception-10">DOMException</code></a>.

    For instance, a proxy object.

24. Otherwise:

    1.  Set `serialized` to { \[\[Type\]\]: "Object",
        \[\[Properties\]\]: a new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list-4"
        data-x-internal="js-list">List</a> }.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:object.prototype-2"
    data-x-internal="object.prototype">%Object.prototype%</a> will end
    up being handled via this step and subsequent steps. The end result
    is that its exoticness is ignored, and after deserialization the
    result will be an empty object (not an
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#immutable-prototype-exotic-object"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:immutable-prototype-exotic-object"
    data-x-internal="immutable-prototype-exotic-object">immutable prototype
    exotic object</a>).

25. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set"
    id="structuredserializeinternal:map-set"
    data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> `memory`\[`value`\] to
    `serialized`.

26. If `deep` is true, then:

    1.  If `value` has a \[\[MapData\]\] internal slot, then:

        1.  Let `copiedList` be a new empty <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list-5"
            data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:list-iterate"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:record-2"
            data-x-internal="record">Record</a> { \[\[Key\]\],
            \[\[Value\]\] } `entry` of `value`.\[\[MapData\]\]:

            1.  Let `copiedEntry` be a new <a
                href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:record-3"
                data-x-internal="record">Record</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
                `entry`.\[\[Key\]\], \[\[Value\]\]:
                `entry`.\[\[Value\]\] }.

            2.  If `copiedEntry`.\[\[Key\]\] is not the special value
                *empty*,
                <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:list-append"
                data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> `copiedEntry`
                to `copiedList`.

        3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:list-iterate-2"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:record-4"
            data-x-internal="record">Record</a> { \[\[Key\]\],
            \[\[Value\]\] } `entry` of `copiedList`:

            1.  Let `serializedKey` be ?
                <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-3">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`entry`.\[\[Key\]\],
                `forStorage`, `memory`).

            2.  Let `serializedValue` be ?
                <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-4">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`entry`.\[\[Value\]\],
                `forStorage`, `memory`).

            3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:list-append-2"
                data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
                `serializedKey`, \[\[Value\]\]: `serializedValue` } to
                `serialized`.\[\[MapData\]\].

    2.  Otherwise, if `value` has a \[\[SetData\]\] internal slot, then:

        1.  Let `copiedList` be a new empty <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:js-list-6"
            data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:list-iterate-3"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `entry` of
            `value`.\[\[SetData\]\]:

            1.  If `entry` is not the special value *empty*,
                <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:list-append-3"
                data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> `entry` to
                `copiedList`.

        3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:list-iterate-4"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `entry` of
            `copiedList`:

            1.  Let `serializedEntry` be ?
                <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-5">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`entry`,
                `forStorage`, `memory`).

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:list-append-4"
                data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a>
                `serializedEntry` to `serialized`.\[\[SetData\]\].

    3.  Otherwise, if `value` is a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:platform-object-4"
        data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> that is a
        <a href="#serializable-objects"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:serializable-objects-2">serializable
        object</a>, then perform the <a href="#serialization-steps"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:serialization-steps">serialization
        steps</a> for `value`'s
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:primary-interface-2"
        data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a>, given
        `value`, `serialized`, and `forStorage`.

        The <a href="#serialization-steps"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:serialization-steps-2">serialization
        steps</a> may need to perform a <span id="sub-serialization"
        class="dfn" export="">sub-serialization</span>. This is an
        operation which takes as input a value `subValue`, and returns
        <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-6">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`subValue`,
        `forStorage`, `memory`). (In other words, a
        <a href="#sub-serialization"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:sub-serialization">sub-serialization</a>
        is a specialization of <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-7">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>
        to be consistent within this invocation.)

    4.  Otherwise, for each `key` in !
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-enumerableownproperties"
        id="structuredserializeinternal:enumerableownproperties"
        data-x-internal="enumerableownproperties">EnumerableOwnProperties</a>(`value`,
        key):

        1.  If ! <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hasownproperty"
            id="structuredserializeinternal:hasownproperty"
            data-x-internal="hasownproperty">HasOwnProperty</a>(`value`,
            `key`) is true, then:

            1.  Let `inputValue` be ? `value`.\[\[Get\]\](`key`,
                `value`).

            2.  Let `outputValue` be ?
                <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-8">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`inputValue`,
                `forStorage`, `memory`).

            3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structuredserializeinternal:list-append-5"
                data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
                `key`, \[\[Value\]\]: `outputValue` } to
                `serialized`.\[\[Properties\]\].

27. Return `serialized`.

</div>

<div class="example">

It's important to realize that the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="structuredserializeinternal:record-5"
data-x-internal="record">Records</a> produced by
<a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-9">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>
might contain "pointers" to other records that create circular
references. For example, when we pass the following JavaScript object
into <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
id="structuredserializeinternal:structuredserializeinternal-10">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>:

``` js
const o = {};
o.myself = o;
```

it produces the following result:

    {
      [[Type]]: "Object",
      [[Properties]]: «
        {
          [[Key]]: "myself",
          [[Value]]: <a pointer to this whole structure>
        }
      »
    }

</div>

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.4</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredSerialize</span> ( `value` )<a href="#structuredserialize" class="self-link"></a>

1.  Return ? <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
    id="structuredserialize:structuredserializeinternal">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`value`,
    false).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.5</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredSerializeForStorage</span> ( `value` )<a href="#structuredserializeforstorage" class="self-link"></a>

1.  Return ? <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
    id="structuredserializeforstorage:structuredserializeinternal">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`value`,
    true).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.6</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredDeserialize</span> ( `serialized`, `targetRealm` \[ , `memory` \] )<a href="#structureddeserialize" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize">StructuredDeserialize</a>
abstract operation takes as input a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
id="structureddeserialize:record" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
`serialized`, which was previously produced by
<a href="#structuredserialize"
id="structureddeserialize:structuredserialize">StructuredSerialize</a>
or <a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="structureddeserialize:structuredserializeforstorage">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>,
and deserializes it into a new JavaScript value, created in
`targetRealm`.

This process can throw an exception, for example when trying to allocate
memory for the new objects (especially `ArrayBuffer` objects).

1.  If `memory` was not supplied, let `memory` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="structureddeserialize:ordered-map"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a>.

    The purpose of the `memory` map is to avoid deserializing objects
    twice. This ends up preserving cycles and the identity of duplicate
    objects in graphs.

2.  If `memory`\[`serialized`\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="structureddeserialize:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then return
    `memory`\[`serialized`\].

3.  Let `deep` be false.

4.  Let `value` be an uninitialized value.

5.  If `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "primitive", then set `value` to
    `serialized`.\[\[Value\]\].

6.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Boolean", then set
    `value` to a new Boolean object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[BooleanData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[BooleanData\]\].

7.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Number", then set
    `value` to a new Number object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[NumberData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[NumberData\]\].

8.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "BigInt", then set
    `value` to a new BigInt object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[BigIntData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[BigIntData\]\].

9.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "String", then set
    `value` to a new String object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[StringData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[StringData\]\].

10. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Date", then set `value`
    to a new Date object in `targetRealm` whose \[\[DateValue\]\]
    internal slot value is `serialized`.\[\[DateValue\]\].

11. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "RegExp", then set
    `value` to a new RegExp object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[RegExpMatcher\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[RegExpMatcher\]\], whose \[\[OriginalSource\]\]
    internal slot value is `serialized`.\[\[OriginalSource\]\], and
    whose \[\[OriginalFlags\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[OriginalFlags\]\].

12. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "SharedArrayBuffer",
    then:

    1.  If `targetRealm`'s corresponding
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
        id="structureddeserialize:agent-cluster"
        data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> is not
        `serialized`.\[\[AgentCluster\]\], then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structureddeserialize:datacloneerror"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structureddeserialize:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  Otherwise, set `value` to a new SharedArrayBuffer object in
        `targetRealm` whose \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot value
        is `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] and whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

13. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is
    "GrowableSharedArrayBuffer", then:

    1.  If `targetRealm`'s corresponding
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
        id="structureddeserialize:agent-cluster-2"
        data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> is not
        `serialized`.\[\[AgentCluster\]\], then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structureddeserialize:datacloneerror-2"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structureddeserialize:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  Otherwise, set `value` to a new SharedArrayBuffer object in
        `targetRealm` whose \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot value
        is `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\], whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferByteLengthData\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLengthData\]\], and whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\].

14. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "ArrayBuffer", then set
    `value` to a new ArrayBuffer object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\], and whose
    \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

    If this throws an exception, catch it, and then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structureddeserialize:datacloneerror-3"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structureddeserialize:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

    This step might throw an exception if there is not enough memory
    available to create such an ArrayBuffer object.

15. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "ResizableArrayBuffer",
    then set `value` to a new ArrayBuffer object in `targetRealm` whose
    \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\], whose
    \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\], and whose
    \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
    `serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\].

    If this throws an exception, catch it, and then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="structureddeserialize:datacloneerror-4"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="structureddeserialize:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

    This step might throw an exception if there is not enough memory
    available to create such an ArrayBuffer object.

16. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "ArrayBufferView", then:

    1.  Let `deserializedArrayBuffer` be ?
        <a href="#structureddeserialize"
        id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-2">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`serialized`.\[\[ArrayBufferSerialized\]\],
        `targetRealm`, `memory`).

    2.  If `serialized`.\[\[Constructor\]\] is "DataView", then set
        `value` to a new DataView object in `targetRealm` whose
        \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot value is
        `deserializedArrayBuffer`, whose \[\[ByteLength\]\] internal
        slot value is `serialized`.\[\[ByteLength\]\], and whose
        \[\[ByteOffset\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ByteOffset\]\].

    3.  Otherwise, set `value` to a new typed array object in
        `targetRealm`, using the constructor given by
        `serialized`.\[\[Constructor\]\], whose
        \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot value is
        `deserializedArrayBuffer`, whose \[\[TypedArrayName\]\] internal
        slot value is `serialized`.\[\[Constructor\]\], whose
        \[\[ByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ByteLength\]\], whose \[\[ByteOffset\]\]
        internal slot value is `serialized`.\[\[ByteOffset\]\], and
        whose \[\[ArrayLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `serialized`.\[\[ArrayLength\]\].

17. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Map", then:

    1.  Set `value` to a new Map object in `targetRealm` whose
        \[\[MapData\]\] internal slot value is a new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structureddeserialize:js-list" data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

18. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Set", then:

    1.  Set `value` to a new Set object in `targetRealm` whose
        \[\[SetData\]\] internal slot value is a new empty <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
        id="structureddeserialize:js-list-2" data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

19. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Array", then:

    1.  Let `outputProto` be `targetRealm`.\[\[Intrinsics\]\].\[\[<a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-array-prototype-object"
        id="structureddeserialize:array.prototype"
        data-x-internal="array.prototype">%Array.prototype%</a>\]\].

    2.  Set `value` to !
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-arraycreate"
        id="structureddeserialize:arraycreate"
        data-x-internal="arraycreate">ArrayCreate</a>(`serialized`.\[\[Length\]\],
        `outputProto`).

    3.  Set `deep` to true.

20. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Object", then:

    1.  Set `value` to a new Object in `targetRealm`.

    2.  Set `deep` to true.

21. Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Error", then:

    1.  Let `prototype` be <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-error-prototype-object"
        id="structureddeserialize:error.prototype"
        data-x-internal="error.prototype">%Error.prototype%</a>.

    2.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "EvalError", then set
        `prototype` to <a href="#evalerror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:evalerror.prototype">%EvalError.prototype%</a>.

    3.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "RangeError", then set
        `prototype` to <a href="#rangeerror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:rangeerror.prototype">%RangeError.prototype%</a>.

    4.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "ReferenceError", then set
        `prototype` to <a href="#referenceerror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:referenceerror.prototype">%ReferenceError.prototype%</a>.

    5.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "SyntaxError", then set
        `prototype` to <a href="#syntaxerror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:syntaxerror.prototype">%SyntaxError.prototype%</a>.

    6.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "TypeError", then set
        `prototype` to <a href="#typeerror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:typeerror.prototype">%TypeError.prototype%</a>.

    7.  If `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] is "URIError", then set `prototype`
        to <a href="#urierror.prototype"
        id="structureddeserialize:urierror.prototype">%URIError.prototype%</a>.

    8.  Let `message` be `serialized`.\[\[Message\]\].

    9.  Set `value` to
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-objectcreate"
        id="structureddeserialize:ordinaryobjectcreate"
        data-x-internal="ordinaryobjectcreate">OrdinaryObjectCreate</a>(`prototype`,
        « \[\[ErrorData\]\] »).

    10. Let `messageDesc` be <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type"
        id="structureddeserialize:propertydescriptor"
        data-x-internal="propertydescriptor">PropertyDescriptor</a> {
        \[\[Value\]\]: `message`, \[\[Writable\]\]: true,
        \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.

    11. If `message` is not undefined, then perform !
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarydefineownproperty"
        id="structureddeserialize:ordinarydefineownproperty"
        data-x-internal="ordinarydefineownproperty">OrdinaryDefineOwnProperty</a>(`value`,
        "`message`", `messageDesc`).

    12. Any interesting accompanying data attached to `serialized`
        should be deserialized and attached to `value`.

22. Otherwise:

    1.  Let `interfaceName` be `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\].

    2.  If the interface identified by `interfaceName` is not
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-exposed"
        id="structureddeserialize:idl-exposed"
        data-x-internal="idl-exposed">exposed</a> in `targetRealm`, then
        throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structureddeserialize:datacloneerror-5"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structureddeserialize:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  Set `value` to a new instance of the interface identified by
        `interfaceName`, created in `targetRealm`.

    4.  Set `deep` to true.

23. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set"
    id="structureddeserialize:map-set" data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a>
    `memory`\[`serialized`\] to `value`.

24. If `deep` is true, then:

    1.  If `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Map", then:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structureddeserialize:list-iterate"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structureddeserialize:record-2" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
            { \[\[Key\]\], \[\[Value\]\] } `entry` of
            `serialized`.\[\[MapData\]\]:

            1.  Let `deserializedKey` be ?
                <a href="#structureddeserialize"
                id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-3">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`entry`.\[\[Key\]\],
                `targetRealm`, `memory`).

            2.  Let `deserializedValue` be ?
                <a href="#structureddeserialize"
                id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-4">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`entry`.\[\[Value\]\],
                `targetRealm`, `memory`).

            3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structureddeserialize:list-append"
                data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
                `deserializedKey`, \[\[Value\]\]: `deserializedValue` }
                to `value`.\[\[MapData\]\].

    2.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Set", then:
