        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structureddeserialize:list-iterate-2"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `entry` of
            `serialized`.\[\[SetData\]\]:

            1.  Let `deserializedEntry` be ?
                <a href="#structureddeserialize"
                id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-5">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`entry`,
                `targetRealm`, `memory`).

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="structureddeserialize:list-append-2"
                data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a>
                `deserializedEntry` to `value`.\[\[SetData\]\].

    3.  Otherwise, if `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\] is "Array" or "Object",
        then:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="structureddeserialize:list-iterate-3"
            data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structureddeserialize:record-3" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
            { \[\[Key\]\], \[\[Value\]\] } `entry` of
            `serialized`.\[\[Properties\]\]:

            1.  Let `deserializedValue` be ?
                <a href="#structureddeserialize"
                id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-6">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`entry`.\[\[Value\]\],
                `targetRealm`, `memory`).

            2.  Let `result` be !
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-createdataproperty"
                id="structureddeserialize:createdataproperty"
                data-x-internal="createdataproperty">CreateDataProperty</a>(`value`,
                `entry`.\[\[Key\]\], `deserializedValue`).

            3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
                id="structureddeserialize:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
                `result` is true.

    4.  Otherwise:

        1.  Perform the appropriate <a href="#deserialization-steps"
            id="structureddeserialize:deserialization-steps">deserialization
            steps</a> for the interface identified by
            `serialized`.\[\[Type\]\], given `serialized`, `value`, and
            `targetRealm`.

            The <a href="#deserialization-steps"
            id="structureddeserialize:deserialization-steps-2">deserialization
            steps</a> may need to perform a
            <span id="sub-deserialization" class="dfn"
            export="">sub-deserialization</span>. This is an operation
            which takes as input a previously-serialized <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="structureddeserialize:record-4" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
            `subSerialized`, and returns
            <a href="#structureddeserialize"
            id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-7">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`subSerialized`,
            `targetRealm`, `memory`). (In other words, a
            <a href="#sub-deserialization"
            id="structureddeserialize:sub-deserialization">sub-deserialization</a>
            is a specialization of <a href="#structureddeserialize"
            id="structureddeserialize:structureddeserialize-8">StructuredDeserialize</a>
            to be consistent within this invocation.)

25. Return `value`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.7</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</span> ( `value`, `transferList` )<a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer" class="self-link"></a>

1.  Let `memory` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:ordered-map"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a>.

    In addition to how it is used normally by
    <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:structuredserializeinternal">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>,
    in this algorithm `memory` is also used to ensure that
    <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:structuredserializeinternal-2">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>
    ignores items in `transferList`, and let us do our own handling
    instead.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `transferable` of
    `transferList`:

    1.  If `transferable` has neither an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\]
        internal slot nor a <a href="#detached"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:detached">[[Detached]]</a>
        internal slot, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  If `transferable` has an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot
        and <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-issharedarraybuffer"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:issharedarraybuffer"
        data-x-internal="issharedarraybuffer">IsSharedArrayBuffer</a>(`transferable`)
        is true, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror-2"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  If `memory`\[`transferable`\]
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:map-exists"
        data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror-3"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

    4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:map-set"
        data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> `memory`\[`transferable`\] to
        { \[\[Type\]\]: an uninitialized value }.

        `transferable` is not transferred yet as transferring has side
        effects and <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:structuredserializeinternal-3">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>
        needs to be able to throw first.

3.  Let `serialized` be ? <a href="#structuredserializeinternal"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:structuredserializeinternal-4">StructuredSerializeInternal</a>(`value`,
    false, `memory`).

4.  Let `transferDataHolders` be a new empty <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:js-list"
    data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="structuredserializewithtransfer:list-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `transferable` of
    `transferList`:

    1.  If `transferable` has an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot
        and <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdetachedbuffer"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:isdetachedbuffer"
        data-x-internal="isdetachedbuffer">IsDetachedBuffer</a>(`transferable`)
        is true, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror-4"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  If `transferable` has a <a href="#detached"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:detached-2">[[Detached]]</a>
        internal slot and `transferable`.<a href="#detached"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:detached-3">[[Detached]]</a>
        is true, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror-5"
        data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  Let `dataHolder` be `memory`\[`transferable`\].

    4.  If `transferable` has an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot,
        then:

        1.  If `transferable` has an \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\]
            internal slot, then:

            1.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\] to "ResizableArrayBuffer".

            2.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] to
                `transferable`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\].

            3.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] to
                `transferable`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

            4.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] to
                `transferable`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\].

        2.  Otherwise:

            1.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\] to "ArrayBuffer".

            2.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] to
                `transferable`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\].

            3.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] to
                `transferable`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

        3.  Perform ?
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-detacharraybuffer"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:detacharraybuffer"
            data-x-internal="detacharraybuffer">DetachArrayBuffer</a>(`transferable`).

            Specifications can use the \[\[ArrayBufferDetachKey\]\]
            internal slot to prevent
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
            data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:idl-arraybuffer">ArrayBuffer</code></a>s
            from being detached. This is used in WebAssembly JavaScript
            Interface, for example. [\[WASMJS\]](#refsWASMJS)

    5.  Otherwise:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:assert"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `transferable` is a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:platform-object"
            data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> that
            is a <a href="#transferable-objects"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:transferable-objects">transferable
            object</a>.

        2.  Let `interfaceName` be the identifier of the
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-primary-interface"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:primary-interface"
            data-x-internal="primary-interface">primary interface</a> of
            `transferable`.

        3.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\] to `interfaceName`.

        4.  Perform the appropriate <a href="#transfer-steps"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:transfer-steps">transfer steps</a>
            for the interface identified by `interfaceName`, given
            `transferable` and `dataHolder`.

        5.  Set `transferable`.<a href="#detached"
            id="structuredserializewithtransfer:detached-4">[[Detached]]</a>
            to true.

    6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="structuredserializewithtransfer:list-append"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `dataHolder` to
        `transferDataHolders`.

6.  Return { \[\[Serialized\]\]: `serialized`,
    \[\[TransferDataHolders\]\]: `transferDataHolders` }.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

#### <span class="secno">2.7.8</span> <span class="dfn">StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer</span> ( `serializeWithTransferResult`, `targetRealm` )<a href="#structureddeserializewithtransfer" class="self-link"></a>

1.  Let `memory` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:ordered-map"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a>.

    Analogous to <a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>,
    in addition to how it is used normally by
    <a href="#structureddeserialize"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:structureddeserialize">StructuredDeserialize</a>,
    in this algorithm `memory` is also used to ensure that
    <a href="#structureddeserialize"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:structureddeserialize-2">StructuredDeserialize</a>
    ignores items in
    `serializeWithTransferResult`.\[\[TransferDataHolders\]\], and let
    us do our own handling instead.

2.  Let `transferredValues` be a new empty <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:js-list"
    data-x-internal="js-list">List</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `transferDataHolder` of
    `serializeWithTransferResult`.\[\[TransferDataHolders\]\]:

    1.  Let `value` be an uninitialized value.

    2.  If `transferDataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\] is "ArrayBuffer", then set
        `value` to a new ArrayBuffer object in `targetRealm` whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal slot value is
        `transferDataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\], and whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `transferDataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\].

        In cases where the original memory occupied by
        \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] is accessible during the
        deserialization, this step is unlikely to throw an exception, as
        no new memory needs to be allocated: the memory occupied by
        \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] is instead just getting transferred into
        the new ArrayBuffer. This could be true, for example, when both
        the source and target realms are in the same process.

    3.  Otherwise, if `transferDataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\] is
        "ResizableArrayBuffer", then set `value` to a new ArrayBuffer
        object in `targetRealm` whose \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] internal
        slot value is `transferDataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferData\]\],
        whose \[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `transferDataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferByteLength\]\], and whose
        \[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\] internal slot value is
        `transferDataHolder`.\[\[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength\]\].

        For the same reason as the previous step, this step is also
        unlikely to throw an exception.

    4.  Otherwise:

        1.  Let `interfaceName` be `transferDataHolder`.\[\[Type\]\].

        2.  If the interface identified by `interfaceName` is not
            exposed in `targetRealm`, then throw a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
            id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:datacloneerror"
            data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
            data-x-internal="domexception"><code
            id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

        3.  Set `value` to a new instance of the interface identified by
            `interfaceName`, created in `targetRealm`.

        4.  Perform the appropriate <a href="#transfer-receiving-steps"
            id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:transfer-receiving-steps">transfer-receiving
            steps</a> for the interface identified by `interfaceName`
            given `transferDataHolder` and `value`.

    5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set"
        id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:map-set"
        data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a>
        `memory`\[`transferDataHolder`\] to `value`.

    6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:list-append"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `value` to
        `transferredValues`.

4.  Let `deserialized` be ? <a href="#structureddeserialize"
    id="structureddeserializewithtransfer:structureddeserialize-3">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`serializeWithTransferResult`.\[\[Serialized\]\],
    `targetRealm`, `memory`).

5.  Return { \[\[Deserialized\]\]: `deserialized`,
    \[\[TransferredValues\]\]: `transferredValues` }.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.7.9</span> Performing serialization and transferring from other specifications<a href="#performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications"
class="self-link"></a>

Other specifications may use the abstract operations defined here. The
following provides some guidance on when each abstract operation is
typically useful, with examples.

<a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>  
<a href="#structureddeserializewithtransfer"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structureddeserializewithtransfer">StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer</a>  
Cloning a value to another
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:realm"
data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>, with a transfer list, but where the
target realm is not known ahead of time. In this case the serialization
step can be performed immediately, with the deserialization step delayed
until the target realm becomes known.

[`messagePort.postMessage()`](#dom-messageport-postmessage) uses this
pair of abstract operations, as the destination realm is not known until
the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) <a href="#has-been-shipped"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:has-been-shipped">has
been shipped</a>.

<a href="#structuredserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserialize">StructuredSerialize</a>  
<a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializeforstorage">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>  
<a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structureddeserialize">StructuredDeserialize</a>  
Creating a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:realm-2"
data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>-independent snapshot of a given value
which can be saved for an indefinite amount of time, and then reified
back into a JavaScript value later, possibly multiple times.

<a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializeforstorage-2">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>
can be used for situations where the serialization is anticipated to be
stored in a persistent manner, instead of passed between realms. It
throws when attempting to serialize
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer-objects"
data-x-internal="sharedarraybuffer"><code
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:sharedarraybuffer">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>
objects, since storing shared memory does not make sense. Similarly, it
can throw or possibly have different behavior when given a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:platform-object"
data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a> with custom
<a href="#serialization-steps"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:serialization-steps">serialization
steps</a> when the `forStorage` argument is true.

[`history.pushState()`](#dom-history-pushstate) and
[`history.replaceState()`](#dom-history-replacestate) use
<a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializeforstorage-3">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>
on author-supplied state objects, storing them as
<a href="#serialized-state"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:serialized-state">serialized
state</a> in the appropriate <a href="#session-history-entry"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:session-history-entry">session
history entry</a>. Then, <a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structureddeserialize-2">StructuredDeserialize</a>
is used so that the [`history.state`](#dom-history-state) property can
return a clone of the originally-supplied state object.

[`broadcastChannel.postMessage()`](#dom-broadcastchannel-postmessage)
uses <a href="#structuredserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserialize-2">StructuredSerialize</a>
on its input, then uses <a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structureddeserialize-3">StructuredDeserialize</a>
multiple times on the result to produce a fresh clone for each
destination being broadcast to. Note that transferring does not make
sense in multi-destination situations.

Any API for persisting JavaScript values to the filesystem would also
use <a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializeforstorage-4">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>
on its input and <a href="#structureddeserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structureddeserialize-4">StructuredDeserialize</a>
on its output.

In general, call sites may pass in Web IDL values instead of JavaScript
values; this is to be understood to perform an implicit
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:concept-idl-convert"
data-x-internal="concept-idl-convert">conversion</a> to the JavaScript
value before invoking these algorithms.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Call sites that are not invoked as a result of author code synchronously
calling into a user agent method must take care to properly
<a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:prepare-to-run-script">prepare
to run script</a> and <a href="#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:prepare-to-run-a-callback">prepare
to run a callback</a> before invoking <a href="#structuredserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserialize-3">StructuredSerialize</a>,
<a href="#structuredserializeforstorage"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializeforstorage-5">StructuredSerializeForStorage</a>,
or <a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializewithtransfer-2">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>
abstract operations, if they are being performed on arbitrary objects.
This is necessary because the serialization process can invoke
author-defined accessors as part of its final deep-serialization steps,
and these accessors could call into operations that rely on the
<a href="#concept-entry-everything"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:concept-entry-everything">entry</a>
and <a href="#concept-incumbent-everything"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:concept-incumbent-everything">incumbent</a>
concepts being properly set up.

[`window.postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) performs
<a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserializewithtransfer-3">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>
on its arguments, but is careful to do so immediately, inside the
synchronous portion of its algorithm. Thus it is able to use the
algorithms without needing to <a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:prepare-to-run-script-2">prepare
to run script</a> and <a href="#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:prepare-to-run-a-callback-2">prepare
to run a callback</a>.

In contrast, a hypothetical API that used <a href="#structuredserialize"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:structuredserialize-4">StructuredSerialize</a>
to serialize some author-supplied object periodically, directly from a
<a href="#concept-task"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:concept-task">task</a>
on the <a href="#event-loop"
id="performing-structured-clones-from-other-specifications:event-loop">event
loop</a>, would need to ensure it performs the appropriate preparations
beforehand. As of this time, we know of no such APIs on the platform;
usually it is simpler to perform the serialization ahead of time, as a
synchronous consequence of author code.

#### <span class="secno">2.7.10</span> Structured cloning API<a href="#structured-cloning" class="self-link"></a>

`result`` = self.`<a href="#dom-structuredclone"
id="dom-structuredclone-dev"><code>structuredClone</code></a>`(``value``[, { `<a href="#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer"
id="structured-cloning:dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer"><code>transfer</code></a>` }])`  
Takes the input value and returns a deep copy by performing the
structured clone algorithm. <a href="#transferable-objects"
id="structured-cloning:transferable-objects">Transferable objects</a>
listed in the [`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)
array are transferred, not just cloned, meaning that they are no longer
usable in the input value.

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
id="structured-cloning:datacloneerror"
data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="structured-cloning:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if any part
of the input value is not <a href="#serializable-objects"
id="structured-cloning:serializable-objects">serializable</a>.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[structuredClone](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/structuredClone "The global structuredClone() method creates a deep clone of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.")

The <span id="dom-structuredclone" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`structuredClone(``value``, ``options``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  Let `serialized` be ? <a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
    id="structured-cloning:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>(`value`,
    `options`\["[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)"\]).

2.  Let `deserializeRecord` be ?
    <a href="#structureddeserializewithtransfer"
    id="structured-cloning:structureddeserializewithtransfer">StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer</a>(`serialized`,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="structured-cloning:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
    id="structured-cloning:concept-relevant-realm">relevant realm</a>).

3.  Return `deserializeRecord`.\[\[Deserialized\]\].

## <span class="secno">3</span> Semantics, structure, and APIs of HTML documents<a href="#dom" class="self-link"></a>

### <span class="secno">3.1</span> Documents<a href="#documents" class="self-link"></a>

Every XML and HTML document in an HTML UA is represented by a
[`Document`](#document) object. [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

The [`Document`](#document) object's <span id="the-document's-address"
class="dfn">[URL](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url)</span>
is defined in DOM. It is initially set when the [`Document`](#document)
object is created, but can change during the lifetime of the
[`Document`](#document) object; for example, it changes when the user
<a href="#navigate" id="documents:navigate">navigates</a> to a
<a href="#navigate-fragid" id="documents:navigate-fragid">fragment</a>
on the page and when the [`pushState()`](#dom-history-pushstate) method
is called with a new
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url" id="documents:url"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a>. [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

Interactive user agents typically expose the [`Document`](#document)
object's <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="documents:the-document&#39;s-address"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> in their user
interface. This is the primary mechanism by which a user can tell if a
site is attempting to impersonate another.

The [`Document`](#document) object's <span id="concept-document-origin"
class="dfn">[origin](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin)</span>
is defined in DOM. It is initially set when the [`Document`](#document)
object is created, and can change during the lifetime of the
[`Document`](#document) only upon setting
[`document.domain`](#dom-document-domain). A [`Document`](#document)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="documents:concept-document-origin"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> can differ from the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
id="documents:concept-url-origin"
data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a> of its
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="documents:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>; for example when a
<a href="#child-navigable" id="documents:child-navigable">child
navigable</a> is <a href="#create-a-new-child-navigable"
id="documents:create-a-new-child-navigable">created</a>, its
<a href="#nav-document" id="documents:nav-document">active document</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="documents:concept-document-origin-2"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is inherited from
its <a href="#nav-parent" id="documents:nav-parent">parent</a>'s
<a href="#nav-document" id="documents:nav-document-2">active
document</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="documents:concept-document-origin-3"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, even though its
<a href="#nav-document" id="documents:nav-document-3">active
document</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="documents:the-document&#39;s-address-3"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> is
[`about:blank`](#about:blank). [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

When a [`Document`](#document) is created by a
<a href="#concept-script" id="documents:concept-script">script</a> using
the <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domimplementation-createdocument"
data-x-internal="dom-domimplementation-createdocument"><code
id="documents:dom-domimplementation-createdocument">createDocument()</code></a>
or <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domimplementation-createhtmldocument"
data-x-internal="dom-domimplementation-createhtmldocument"><code
id="documents:dom-domimplementation-createhtmldocument">createHTMLDocument()</code></a>
methods, the [`Document`](#document) is
<a href="#ready-for-post-load-tasks"
id="documents:ready-for-post-load-tasks">ready for post-load tasks</a>
immediately.

<span id="the-document's-referrer" class="dfn" export="">The document's
referrer</span> is a string (representing a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url" id="documents:url-2"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a>) that can be set when the
[`Document`](#document) is created. If it is not explicitly set, then
its value is the empty string.

#### <span class="secno">3.1.1</span> The [`Document`](#document) object<a href="#the-document-object" class="self-link"></a>

Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome

DOM defines a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-document"
data-x-internal="dom-document"><code
id="the-document-object:dom-document">Document</code></a> interface,
which this specification extends significantly.

``` idl
enum DocumentReadyState { "loading", "interactive", "complete" };
enum DocumentVisibilityState { "visible", "hidden" };
typedef (HTMLScriptElement or SVGScriptElement) HTMLOrSVGScriptElement;

[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]
partial interface Document {
  static Document parseHTMLUnsafe((TrustedHTML or DOMString) html);

  // resource metadata management
  [PutForwards=href, LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute Location? location;
  attribute USVString domain;
  readonly attribute USVString referrer;
  attribute USVString cookie;
  readonly attribute DOMString lastModified;
  readonly attribute DocumentReadyState readyState;

  // DOM tree accessors
  getter object (DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString title;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString dir;
  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLElement? body;
  readonly attribute HTMLHeadElement? head;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection images;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection embeds;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection plugins;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection links;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection forms;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection scripts;
  NodeList getElementsByName(DOMString elementName);
  readonly attribute HTMLOrSVGScriptElement? currentScript; // classic scripts in a document tree only

  // dynamic markup insertion
  [CEReactions] Document open(optional DOMString unused1, optional DOMString unused2); // both arguments are ignored
  WindowProxy? open(USVString url, DOMString name, DOMString features);
  [CEReactions] undefined close();
  [CEReactions] undefined write((TrustedHTML or DOMString)... text);
  [CEReactions] undefined writeln((TrustedHTML or DOMString)... text);

  // user interaction
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? defaultView;
  boolean hasFocus();
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString designMode;
  [CEReactions] boolean execCommand(DOMString commandId, optional boolean showUI = false, optional DOMString value = "");
  boolean queryCommandEnabled(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandIndeterm(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandState(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandSupported(DOMString commandId);
  DOMString queryCommandValue(DOMString commandId);
  readonly attribute boolean hidden;
  readonly attribute DocumentVisibilityState visibilityState;

  // special event handler IDL attributes that only apply to Document objects
  [LegacyLenientThis] attribute EventHandler onreadystatechange;
  attribute EventHandler onvisibilitychange;

  // also has obsolete members
};
Document includes GlobalEventHandlers;
```

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="concept-document-policy-container" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">policy container</span> (a
<a href="#policy-container"
id="the-document-object:policy-container">policy container</a>),
initially a new policy container, which contains policies which apply to
the [`Document`](#document).

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="concept-document-permissions-policy" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">permissions policy</span>, which is a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#permissions-policy"
id="the-document-object:concept-permissions-policy"
data-x-internal="concept-permissions-policy">permissions policy</a>,
which is initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="concept-document-module-map" class="dfn">module map</span>,
which is a
<a href="#module-map" id="the-document-object:module-map">module map</a>,
initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="concept-document-coop"
class="dfn">opener policy</span>, which is an
<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="the-document-object:cross-origin-opener-policy">opener policy</a>,
initially a new opener policy.

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="is-initial-about:blank"
class="dfn">is initial `about:blank`</span>, which is a boolean,
initially false.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="concept-document-navigation-id" class="dfn">during-loading
navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi</span>, which is a
<a href="#navigation-id"
id="the-document-object:navigation-id">navigation ID</a> or null,
initially null.

As the name indicates, this is used for interfacing with the WebDriver
BiDi specification, which needs to be informed about certain occurrences
during the early parts of the [`Document`](#document)'s lifecycle, in a
way that ties them to the original <a href="#navigation-id"
id="the-document-object:navigation-id-2">navigation ID</a> used when the
navigation that created this [`Document`](#document) was the
<a href="#ongoing-navigation"
id="the-document-object:ongoing-navigation">ongoing navigation</a>. This
eventually gets set back to null, after WebDriver BiDi considers the
loading process to be finished. [\[BIDI\]](#refsBIDI)

Each [`Document`](#document) has an
<span id="concept-document-about-base-url" class="dfn">about base
URL</span>, which is a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-document-object:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> or null,
initially null.

This is only populated for "`about:`"-schemed [`Document`](#document)s.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="concept-document-bfcache-blocking-details" class="dfn">bfcache
blocking details</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="the-document-object:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
<a href="#nrr-details-struct"
id="the-document-object:nrr-details-struct">not restored reason
details</a>, initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="open-dialogs-list"
class="dfn">open dialogs list</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="the-document-object:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a> of
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements, initially empty.

#### <span class="secno">3.1.2</span> The [`DocumentOrShadowRoot`](#documentorshadowroot) interface<a href="#the-documentorshadowroot-interface" class="self-link"></a>

DOM defines the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#documentorshadowroot"
data-x-internal="dom-documentorshadowroot"><code
id="the-documentorshadowroot-interface:dom-documentorshadowroot">DocumentOrShadowRoot</code></a>
mixin, which this specification extends.

``` idl
partial interface mixin DocumentOrShadowRoot {
  readonly attribute Element? activeElement;
};
```

#### <span class="secno">3.1.3</span> Ancestor origins<a href="#ancestor-origins" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) object has an associated
<span id="concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
class="dfn" dfn-for="Document" export="">internal ancestor origin
objects list</span>, initially null.

The <span id="internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps"
class="dfn">internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps</span>
given a [`Document`](#document) object `document` and a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="ancestor-origins:referrer-policy"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> `referrerPolicy`
are:

1.  Let `output` be « ».

2.  Let `parentDoc` be `document`'s <a href="#doc-container-document"
    id="ancestor-origins:doc-container-document">container document</a>.

3.  If `parentDoc` is null, then return `output`.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="ancestor-origins:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `parentDoc` is
    <a href="#fully-active" id="ancestor-origins:fully-active">fully
    active</a>.

5.  Let `ancestorOrigins` be `parentDoc`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list">internal
    ancestor origin objects list</a>.

6.  Let `container` be `document`'s
    <a href="#node-navigable" id="ancestor-origins:node-navigable">node
    navigable</a>'s <a href="#nav-container"
    id="ancestor-origins:nav-container">container</a>.

7.  Let `masked` be false.

8.  If `referrerPolicy` is "`no-referrer`", then set `masked` to true.

9.  Otherwise, if `referrerPolicy` is "`same-origin`" and `parentDoc`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is not
    <a href="#same-origin" id="ancestor-origins:same-origin">same origin</a>
    with `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, then set
    `masked` to true.

    Since
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-mixed-content/#mixed-content"
    id="ancestor-origins:mixed-content"
    data-x-internal="mixed-content">mixed content</a> checks prevent
    <a href="#non-secure-context"
    id="ancestor-origins:non-secure-context">non-secure context</a>
    <a href="#environment"
    id="ancestor-origins:environment">environments</a> in
    <a href="#secure-context" id="ancestor-origins:secure-context">secure
    context</a> <a href="#environment"
    id="ancestor-origins:environment-2">environments</a>, there's no
    need to check for
    <a href="#secure-context" id="ancestor-origins:secure-context-2">secure
    contexts</a> for "`strict-origin`",
    "`strict-origin-when-cross-origin`", and
    "`no-referrer-when-downgrade`". The "`origin`" and
    "`origin-when-cross-origin`" values also don't need special
    treatment since we're at most exposing an
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> here.

10. If `masked` is true, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="ancestor-origins:list-append"
    data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> a new
    <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a> to
    `output`.

11. Otherwise, <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="ancestor-origins:list-append-2"
    data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> `parentDoc`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-4"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> to `output`.

12. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="ancestor-origins:list-iterate" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `ancestorOrigin` of `ancestorOrigins`:

    1.  If `masked` is true and `ancestorOrigin` is
        <a href="#same-origin" id="ancestor-origins:same-origin-2">same
        origin</a> with `parentDoc`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
        id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-5"
        data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ancestor-origins:list-append-3"
        data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> a new
        <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
        id="ancestor-origins:concept-origin-opaque-2">opaque origin</a>
        to `output` and
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="ancestor-origins:continue" data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ancestor-origins:list-append-4"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `ancestorOrigin` to
        `output` and set `masked` to false.

        Setting `masked` to false here doesn't imply that all further
        ancestors' origins are necessarily exposed. They might have been
        previously masked when an ancestor document ran these steps, and
        the resulting list is used as a starting point when a child
        document is created (see step 5 above).

13. Return `output`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) object has an associated
<span id="concept-document-ancestor-origins-list" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">ancestor origins list</span>, initially
null.

The <span id="ancestor-origins-list-creation-steps" class="dfn">ancestor
origins list creation steps</span> given a [`Document`](#document)
object `document` are:

1.  Let `ancestorOrigins` be `document`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
    id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-2">internal
    ancestor origin objects list</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="ancestor-origins:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `ancestorOrigins` is not null.

3.  Let `output` be « ».

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="ancestor-origins:list-iterate-2" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `origin` of `ancestorOrigins`:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ancestor-origins:list-append-5"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> the
        <a href="#ascii-serialisation-of-an-origin"
        id="ancestor-origins:ascii-serialisation-of-an-origin">serialization</a>
        of `origin` to `output`.

5.  Return a new [`DOMStringList`](#domstringlist) object whose
    associated list is `output`.

</div>

<div class="example">

Consider a <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="ancestor-origins:top-level-browsing-context">top-level browsing
context</a> document with the URL `https://a.example/top`:

``` html
<!doctype html>
<title>top</title>
<iframe referrerpolicy="no-referrer" src="https://a.example/child"></iframe>
```

The child document:

``` html
<!doctype html>
<title>child</title>
<iframe src="https://b.example/grandchild"></iframe>
<script>
 console.log([...location.ancestorOrigins]);
</script>
```

The grandchild document:

``` html
<!doctype html>
<title>grandchild</title>
<script>
 console.log([...location.ancestorOrigins]);
</script>
```

When the child's [`Document`](#document) object is created, its parent's
origin is masked because the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
[`referrerpolicy`](#attr-iframe-referrerpolicy) attribute's value is
"`no-referrer`", even though the documents are
<a href="#same-origin" id="ancestor-origins:same-origin-3">same
origin</a>. The value logged is « "`null`" ».

When the grandchild's [`Document`](#document) object is created, the
child's [`Document`](#document) object's
<a href="#concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-3">internal
ancestor origin objects list</a> (which contains a single
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-origin-opaque-3">opaque origin</a>) is used
as a starting point, and the child's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-6"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is added to the
list. The value logged is thus « "`https://a.example`", "`null`" ».

</div>

<div class="example">

If we consider the previous example but the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element in the top document has no
[`referrerpolicy`](#attr-iframe-referrerpolicy) attribute, and instead
the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element in the child document has
`referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`.

In this case, the top document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-7"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is added to the
child's [`Document`](#document) object's
<a href="#concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-4">internal
ancestor origin objects list</a>. The value logged is «
"`https://a.example`" ».

For the grandchild, the child's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-8"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is masked as an
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-origin-opaque-4">opaque origin</a>. Since
the top document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-9"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is
<a href="#same-origin" id="ancestor-origins:same-origin-4">same
origin</a> with the child document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-origin-10"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, it is also masked.
The value logged is thus « "`null`", "`null`" ».

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, we show that the top-level document's origin is not
masked even though there's a descendant same-origin document whose
origin *is* masked, since there's a cross-origin document in between.

- Top-level with URL `https://a.example/top`

  ``` html
  <iframe src="https://b.example/child"></iframe>
  ```

  The <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
  id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list">ancestor
  origins list</a> associated list is « ».

- Child with URL `https://b.example/child`

  ``` html
  <iframe src="https://a.example/grandchild"></iframe>
  ```

  The <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
  id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list-2">ancestor
  origins list</a> associated list is « "`https://a.example`" ».

- Grandchild with URL `https://a.example/grandchild`

  ``` html
  <iframe src="https://c.example/great-grandchild"
          referrerpolicy="no-referrer"></iframe>
  ```

  The <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
  id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list-3">ancestor
  origins list</a> associated list is « "`https://b.example`",
  "`https://a.example`" ».

- Great-grandchild with URL `https://c.example/great-grandchild`

  The <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
  id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list-4">ancestor
  origins list</a> associated list is « "`null`", "`https://b.example`",
  "`https://a.example`" ». The top-level origin is not masked.

</div>

<div class="example">

If we consider the previous example but the top-level document's
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) also has `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`,
then the resulting <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
id="ancestor-origins:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list-5">ancestor
origins list</a> associated list for each document would be:

- Top-level: « »

- Child: « "`null`" »

- Grandchild: « "`https://b.example`", "`null`" »

- Great-grandchild: « "`null`", "`https://b.example`", "`null`" ». The
  top-level origin is masked because it was masked when the child
  document ran the
  <a href="#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps"
  id="ancestor-origins:internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps">internal
  ancestor origin objects list creation steps</a>, and that result is
  passed on to the grandchild document's
  <a href="#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps"
  id="ancestor-origins:internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps-2">internal
  ancestor origin objects list creation steps</a>, and so on.

</div>

The <span id="dom-document-cookie" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
dfn-type="attribute">`cookie`</span> attribute represents the cookies of
the resource identified by the document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="resource-metadata-management:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>.

Using the synchronous [`document.cookie`](#dom-document-cookie) API can
be a source of performance issues. The Cookie Store API can be used
instead, as it provides an asynchronous way to handle cookies to avoid
performance issues. See the [Cookie Store API
introduction](https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#intro) for more
information. [\[COOKIESTORE\]](#refsCOOKIESTORE)

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) object that falls into one of the following
conditions is a <span id="cookie-averse-document-object"
class="dfn">cookie-averse `Document` object</span>:

- A [`Document`](#document) object whose <a href="#concept-document-bc"
  id="resource-metadata-management:concept-document-bc">browsing
  context</a> is null.
- A [`Document`](#document) whose
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
  id="resource-metadata-management:the-document&#39;s-address-3"
  data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>'s
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
  id="resource-metadata-management:concept-url-scheme"
  data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is not an
  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
  id="resource-metadata-management:http(s)-scheme"
  data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="resource-metadata-management:tracking-vector"
class="tracking-vector" data-x-internal="tracking-vector"

src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> On getting, if the document is

<code>Document</code> object</a>, then the user agent must return the

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="resource-metadata-management:concept-document-origin"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is an

id="resource-metadata-management:concept-origin-opaque">opaque
origin</a>, the user agent must throw a

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"

id="resource-metadata-management:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.
Otherwise, the user agent must return the
<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6265.html#sane-cookie-syntax"
id="resource-metadata-management:cookie-string"
data-x-internal="cookie-string">cookie-string</a> for the document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="resource-metadata-management:the-document&#39;s-address-4"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> for a "non-HTTP"
API, decoded using
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode-without-bom"
id="resource-metadata-management:utf-8-decode-without-bom"
data-x-internal="utf-8-decode-without-bom">UTF-8 decode without BOM</a>.
[\[COOKIES\]](#refsCOOKIES)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, if the document is a
<a href="#cookie-averse-document-object"
id="resource-metadata-management:cookie-averse-document-object-2">cookie-averse
<code>Document</code> object</a>, then the user agent must do nothing.
Otherwise, if the [`Document`](#document)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="resource-metadata-management:concept-document-origin-2"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is an

id="resource-metadata-management:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.
Otherwise, the user agent must act as it would when
<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6265.html#storage-model"
id="resource-metadata-management:receives-a-set-cookie-string"
data-x-internal="receives-a-set-cookie-string">receiving a
set-cookie-string</a> for the document's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="resource-metadata-management:the-document&#39;s-address-5"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> via a "non-HTTP"
API, consisting of the new value
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode"
id="resource-metadata-management:utf-8-encode"
data-x-internal="utf-8-encode">encoded as UTF-8</a>.
[\[COOKIES\]](#refsCOOKIES) [\[ENCODING\]](#refsENCODING)

</div>

Since the [`cookie`](#dom-document-cookie) attribute is accessible
across frames, the path restrictions on cookies are only a tool to help
manage which cookies are sent to which parts of the site, and are not in
any way a security feature.

The [`cookie`](#dom-document-cookie) attribute's getter and setter
synchronously access shared state. Since there is no locking mechanism,
other browsing contexts in a multiprocess user agent can modify cookies
while scripts are running. A site could, for instance, try to read a
cookie, increment its value, then write it back out, using the new value
of the cookie as a unique identifier for the session; if the site does
this twice in two different browser windows at the same time, it might
end up using the same "unique" identifier for both sessions, with
potentially disastrous effects.

Returns the date of the last modification to the document, as reported
by the server, in the form "`MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss`", in the user's local
time zone.

If the last modification date is not known, the current time is returned
instead.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-document-lastmodified" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
dfn-type="attribute">`lastModified`</span> attribute, on getting, must
return the date and time of the [`Document`](#document)'s source file's
last modification, in the user's local time zone, in the following
format:

1.  The month component of the date.

2.  A U+002F SOLIDUS character (/).

3.  The day component of the date.

4.  A U+002F SOLIDUS character (/).

5.  The year component of the date.

6.  A U+0020 SPACE character.

7.  The hours component of the time.

8.  A U+003A COLON character (:).

9.  The minutes component of the time.

10. A U+003A COLON character (:).

11. The seconds component of the time.

All the numeric components above, other than the year, must be given as
two <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
id="resource-metadata-management:ascii-digits"
data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a> representing the number
in base ten, zero-padded if necessary. The year must be given as the
shortest possible string of four or more
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
id="resource-metadata-management:ascii-digits-2"
data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a> representing the number
in base ten, zero-padded if necessary.

</div>

The [`Document`](#document)'s source file's last modification date and
time must be derived from relevant features of the networking protocols
used, e.g. from the value of the HTTP
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7232.html#header.last-modified"
data-x-internal="http-last-modified"><code
id="resource-metadata-management:http-last-modified">Last-Modified</code></a>\`
header of the document, or from metadata in the file system for local
files. If the last modification date and time are not known, the
attribute must return the current date and time in the above format.

#### <span class="secno">3.1.5</span> Reporting document loading status<a href="#reporting-document-loading-status" class="self-link"></a>

`document``.`<a href="#dom-document-readystate"
id="dom-document-readystate-dev"><code>readyState</code></a>  
Returns "`loading`" while the [`Document`](#document) is loading,
"`interactive`" once it is finished parsing but still loading
subresources, and "`complete`" once it has loaded.

The [`readystatechange`](#event-readystatechange) event fires on the
[`Document`](#document) object when this value changes.

The [`DOMContentLoaded`](#event-domcontentloaded) event fires after the
transition to "`interactive`" but before the transition to "`complete`",
at the point where all subresources apart from
[`async`](#attr-script-async) [`script`](#the-script-element) elements
have loaded.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

Each [`Document`](#document) has a <span id="current-document-readiness"
class="dfn">current document readiness</span>, a string, initially
"`complete`".

For [`Document`](#document) objects created via the
<a href="#initialise-the-document-object"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:initialise-the-document-object">create
and initialize a <code>Document</code> object</a> algorithm, this will
be immediately reset to "`loading`" before any script can observe the
value of [`document.readyState`](#dom-document-readystate). This default
applies to other cases such as <a href="#is-initial-about:blank"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:is-initial-about:blank">initial
<code>about:blank</code></a> [`Document`](#document)s or
[`Document`](#document)s without a <a href="#concept-document-bc"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:concept-document-bc">browsing
context</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-document-readystate" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
dfn-type="attribute">`readyState`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#current-document-readiness"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:current-document-readiness">current
document readiness</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="update-the-current-document-readiness" class="dfn">update
the current document readiness</span> for [`Document`](#document)
`document` to `readinessValue`:

1.  If `document`'s <a href="#current-document-readiness"
    id="reporting-document-loading-status:current-document-readiness-2">current
    document readiness</a> equals `readinessValue`, then return.

2.  Set `document`'s <a href="#current-document-readiness"
    id="reporting-document-loading-status:current-document-readiness-3">current
    document readiness</a> to `readinessValue`.

3.  If `document` is associated with an <a href="#html-parser"
    id="reporting-document-loading-status:html-parser">HTML parser</a>,
    then:

    1.  Let `now` be the <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:current-high-resolution-time"
        data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
        time</a> given `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:concept-relevant-global">relevant
        global object</a>.

    2.  If `readinessValue` is "`complete`", and `document`'s
        <a href="#load-timing-info"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:load-timing-info">load timing
        info</a>'s <a href="#dom-complete-time"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:dom-complete-time">DOM complete
        time</a> is 0, then set `document`'s <a href="#load-timing-info"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:load-timing-info-2">load timing
        info</a>'s <a href="#dom-complete-time"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:dom-complete-time-2">DOM complete
        time</a> to `now`.

    3.  Otherwise, if `readinessValue` is "`interactive`", and
        `document`'s <a href="#load-timing-info"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:load-timing-info-3">load timing
        info</a>'s <a href="#dom-interactive-time"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:dom-interactive-time">DOM
        interactive time</a> is 0, then set `document`'s
        <a href="#load-timing-info"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:load-timing-info-4">load timing
        info</a>'s <a href="#dom-interactive-time"
        id="reporting-document-loading-status:dom-interactive-time-2">DOM
        interactive time</a> to `now`.

4.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="reporting-document-loading-status:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`readystatechange`](#event-readystatechange) at `document`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) is said to have an <span id="active-parser"
class="dfn">active parser</span> if it is associated with an
<a href="#html-parser"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:html-parser-2">HTML parser</a> or
an <a href="#xml-parser"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:xml-parser">XML parser</a> that
has not yet been <a href="#stop-parsing"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:stop-parsing">stopped</a> or
<a href="#abort-a-parser"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:abort-a-parser">aborted</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A [`Document`](#document) has a <a href="#document-load-timing-info"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:document-load-timing-info">document
load timing info</a> <span id="load-timing-info" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">load timing info</span>.

A [`Document`](#document) has a <a href="#document-unload-timing-info"
id="reporting-document-loading-status:document-unload-timing-info">document
unload timing info</a> <span id="previous-document-unload-timing"
class="dfn" dfn-for="Document" export="">previous document unload
timing</span>.

A [`Document`](#document) has a boolean
<span id="was-created-via-cross-origin-redirects" class="dfn"
export="">was created via cross-origin redirects</span>, initially
false.

<span id="load-event-end-time" class="dfn" dfn-for="document load timing info" export="">load event end time</span> (default 0)

#### <span class="secno">3.1.6</span> <span class="dfn">Render-blocking mechanism</span><a href="#render-blocking-mechanism" class="self-link"></a>

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="render-blocking-element-set" class="dfn">render-blocking
element set</span>, a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
elements, initially the empty set.

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) `document`
<span id="allows-adding-render-blocking-elements" class="dfn">allows
adding render-blocking elements</span> if `document`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-content-type"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:concept-document-content-type"
data-x-internal="concept-document-content-type">content type</a> is
"[`text/html`](#text/html)" and <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:the-body-element-2">the body element</a>
of `document` is null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) `document` is <span id="render-blocked"
class="dfn">render-blocked</span> if both of the following are true:

- `document`'s <a href="#render-blocking-element-set"
  id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocking-element-set">render-blocking
  element set</a> is non-empty, or `document`
  <a href="#allows-adding-render-blocking-elements"
  id="render-blocking-mechanism:allows-adding-render-blocking-elements">allows
  adding render-blocking elements</a>.

- The <a
  href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
  id="render-blocking-mechanism:current-high-resolution-time"
  data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
  time</a> given `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
  id="render-blocking-mechanism:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
  object</a> has not exceeded an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
  id="render-blocking-mechanism:implementation-defined"
  data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
  timeout value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An element `el` is <span id="render-blocking"
class="dfn">render-blocking</span> if `el`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> `document` is
<a href="#render-blocked"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocked">render-blocked</a>, and
`el` is in `document`'s <a href="#render-blocking-element-set"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocking-element-set-2">render-blocking
element set</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="block-rendering" class="dfn">block rendering</span> on an
element `el`:

1.  Let `document` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  If `document` <a href="#allows-adding-render-blocking-elements"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:allows-adding-render-blocking-elements-2">allows
    adding render-blocking elements</a>, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:set-append"
    data-x-internal="set-append">append</a> `el` to `document`'s
    <a href="#render-blocking-element-set"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocking-element-set-3">render-blocking
    element set</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="unblock-rendering" class="dfn">unblock rendering</span> on
an element `el`:

1.  Let `document` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `el` from `document`'s
    <a href="#render-blocking-element-set"
    id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocking-element-set-4">render-blocking
    element set</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever a <a href="#render-blocking"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:render-blocking">render-blocking</a>
element `el` <a href="#becomes-browsing-context-disconnected"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:becomes-browsing-context-disconnected">becomes
browsing-context disconnected</a>, or `el`'s
<a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:blocking-attribute">blocking attribute</a>'s
value is changed so that `el` is no longer
<a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:potentially-render-blocking">potentially
render-blocking</a>, then <a href="#unblock-rendering"
id="render-blocking-mechanism:unblock-rendering">unblock rendering</a>
on `el`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.1.7</span> <span class="dfn">DOM tree accessors</span><a href="#dom-tree-accessors" class="self-link"></a>

data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>, if it's an
