<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-base-element:metadata-content-2">Metadata content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
In a [`head`](#the-head-element) element containing no other
[`base`](#the-base-element) elements.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-base-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
No <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-base-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-base-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`href`](#attr-base-href) — <a href="#document-base-url"
id="the-base-element:document-base-url">Document base URL</a>

[`target`](#attr-base-target) — Default
<a href="#navigable" id="the-base-element:navigable">navigable</a> for
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-base-element:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>
<a href="#navigate" id="the-base-element:navigate">navigation</a> and
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-base-element:form-submission-2">form submission</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-base).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-base).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-base-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLBaseElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute USVString href;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString target;
};
```

The [`base`](#the-base-element) element allows authors to specify the
<a href="#document-base-url"
id="the-base-element:document-base-url-2">document base URL</a> for the
purposes of parsing <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-base-element:url" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>, and the name
of the default
<a href="#navigable" id="the-base-element:navigable-2">navigable</a> for
the purposes of <a href="#following-hyperlinks-2"
id="the-base-element:following-hyperlinks-2">following hyperlinks</a>.
The element does not
<a href="#represents" id="the-base-element:represents">represent</a> any
content beyond this information.

There must be no more than one [`base`](#the-base-element) element per
document.

A [`base`](#the-base-element) element must have either an
[`href`](#attr-base-href) attribute, a [`target`](#attr-base-target)
attribute, or both.

The <span id="attr-base-href" class="dfn" dfn-for="base"
dfn-type="element-attr">`href`</span> content attribute, if specified,
must contain a <a href="#valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="the-base-element:valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>.

A [`base`](#the-base-element) element, if it has an
[`href`](#attr-base-href) attribute, must come before any other elements
in the tree that have attributes defined as taking
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-base-element:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>.

If there are multiple [`base`](#the-base-element) elements with
[`href`](#attr-base-href) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

The <span id="attr-base-target" class="dfn" dfn-for="base"
dfn-type="element-attr">`target`</span> attribute, if specified, must
contain a <a href="#valid-navigable-target-name-or-keyword"
id="the-base-element:valid-navigable-target-name-or-keyword">valid
navigable target name or keyword</a>, which specifies which
<a href="#navigable" id="the-base-element:navigable-3">navigable</a> is
to be used as the default when
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-base-element:hyperlink-2">hyperlinks</a>
and <a href="#the-form-element"
id="the-base-element:the-form-element">forms</a> in the
[`Document`](#document) cause
<a href="#navigate" id="the-base-element:navigate-2">navigation</a>.

A [`base`](#the-base-element) element, if it has a
[`target`](#attr-base-target) attribute, must come before any elements
in the tree that represent
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-base-element:hyperlink-3">hyperlinks</a>.

If there are multiple [`base`](#the-base-element) elements with
[`target`](#attr-base-target) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="get-an-element's-target" class="dfn">get an element's
target</span>, given an [`a`](#the-a-element),
[`area`](#the-area-element), or [`form`](#the-form-element) element
`element`, and an optional string-or-null `target` (default null), run
these steps:

1.  If `target` is null, then:

    1.  If `element` has a `target` attribute, then set `target` to that
        attribute's value.

    2.  Otherwise, if `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-base-element:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
        document</a> contains a [`base`](#the-base-element) element with
        a [`target`](#attr-base-target) attribute, set `target` to the
        value of the [`target`](#attr-base-target) attribute of the
        first such [`base`](#the-base-element) element.

2.  If `target` is not null, and contains an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-tab-or-newline"
    id="the-base-element:ascii-tab-or-newline"
    data-x-internal="ascii-tab-or-newline">ASCII tab or newline</a> and
    a U+003C (\<), then set `target` to "`_blank`".

3.  Return `target`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A [`base`](#the-base-element) element that is the first
[`base`](#the-base-element) element with an [`href`](#attr-base-href)
content attribute
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
id="the-base-element:in-a-document-tree"
data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a> has a
<span id="frozen-base-url" class="dfn">frozen base URL</span>. The
<a href="#frozen-base-url" id="the-base-element:frozen-base-url">frozen
base URL</a> must be
<a href="#immediately" id="the-base-element:immediately">immediately</a>
<a href="#set-the-frozen-base-url"
id="the-base-element:set-the-frozen-base-url">set</a> for an element
whenever any of the following situations occur:

- The [`base`](#the-base-element) element becomes the first
  [`base`](#the-base-element) element in
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
  id="the-base-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
  order</a> with an [`href`](#attr-base-href) content attribute in its
  [`Document`](#document).

- The [`base`](#the-base-element) element is the first
  [`base`](#the-base-element) element in
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
  id="the-base-element:tree-order-2" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
  order</a> with an [`href`](#attr-base-href) content attribute in its
  [`Document`](#document), and its [`href`](#attr-base-href) content
  attribute is changed.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="set-the-frozen-base-url" class="dfn" export="">set the
frozen base URL</span> for an element `element`:

1.  Let `document` be `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-base-element:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  Let `urlRecord` be the result of
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
    id="the-base-element:url-parser"
    data-x-internal="url-parser">parsing</a> the value of `element`'s
    [`href`](#attr-base-href) content attribute with `document`'s
    <a href="#fallback-base-url"
    id="the-base-element:fallback-base-url">fallback base URL</a>, and
    `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
    id="the-base-element:document&#39;s-character-encoding"
    data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">character
    encoding</a>. (Thus, the [`base`](#the-base-element) element isn't
    affected by itself.)

3.  If any of the following are true:

    - `urlRecord` is failure;

    - `urlRecord`'s
      <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
      id="the-base-element:concept-url-scheme"
      data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is "`data`" or
      "`javascript`"; or

    - running
      <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#allow-base-for-document"
      id="the-base-element:is-base-allowed-for-document"
      data-x-internal="is-base-allowed-for-document">Is base allowed for
      Document?</a> on `urlRecord` and `document` returns "`Blocked`",

    then set `element`'s <a href="#frozen-base-url"
    id="the-base-element:frozen-base-url-2">frozen base URL</a> to
    `document`'s <a href="#fallback-base-url"
    id="the-base-element:fallback-base-url-2">fallback base URL</a> and
    return.

4.  Set `element`'s <a href="#frozen-base-url"
    id="the-base-element:frozen-base-url-3">frozen base URL</a> to
    `urlRecord`.

5.  <a href="#respond-to-base-url-changes"
    id="the-base-element:respond-to-base-url-changes">Respond to base URL
    changes</a> given `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-base-href" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLBaseElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`href`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return the result of running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `document` be `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-base-element:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  Let `url` be the value of the [`href`](#attr-base-href) attribute of
    this element, if it has one, and the empty string otherwise.

3.  Let `urlRecord` be the result of
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
    id="the-base-element:url-parser-2"
    data-x-internal="url-parser">parsing</a> `url` with `document`'s
    <a href="#fallback-base-url"
    id="the-base-element:fallback-base-url-3">fallback base URL</a>, and
    `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
    id="the-base-element:document&#39;s-character-encoding-2"
    data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">character
    encoding</a>. (Thus, the [`base`](#the-base-element) element isn't
    affected by other [`base`](#the-base-element) elements or itself.)

4.  If `urlRecord` is failure, return `url`.

5.  Return the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="the-base-element:concept-url-serializer"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
    `urlRecord`.

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, a [`base`](#the-base-element) element is used to set
the <a href="#document-base-url"
id="the-base-element:document-base-url-3">document base URL</a>:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <title>This is an example for the &lt;base&gt; element</title>
        <base href="https://www.example.com/news/index.html">
    </head>
    <body>
        <p>Visit the <a href="archives.html">archives</a>.</p>
    </body>
</html>
```

The link in the above example would be a link to
"`https://www.example.com/news/archives.html`".

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-link-element:metadata-content-2">Metadata content</a>.

If the element is <a href="#allowed-in-the-body"
id="the-link-element:allowed-in-the-body">allowed in the body</a>:
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-link-element:flow-content-2">flow
content</a>.

If the element is <a href="#allowed-in-the-body"
id="the-link-element:allowed-in-the-body-2">allowed in the body</a>:
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-link-element:phrasing-content-2">phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-link-element:metadata-content-2-2">metadata content</a> is
expected.

In a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a
[`head`](#the-head-element) element.

If the element is <a href="#allowed-in-the-body"
id="the-link-element:allowed-in-the-body-3">allowed in the body</a>:
where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-link-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-link-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
No <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-link-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-link-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`href`](#attr-link-href) — Address of the
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>

[`crossorigin`](#attr-link-crossorigin) — How the element handles
crossorigin requests

[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) — Relationship between the document containing
the <a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-2">hyperlink</a>
and the destination resource

[`media`](#attr-link-media) — Applicable media

[`integrity`](#attr-link-integrity) — Integrity metadata used in
Subresource Integrity checks [\[SRI\]](#refsSRI)

[`hreflang`](#attr-link-hreflang) — Language of the linked resource

[`type`](#attr-link-type) — Hint for the type of the referenced resource

[`referrerpolicy`](#attr-link-referrerpolicy) — <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-link-element:referrer-policy"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">Referrer policy</a> for
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="the-link-element:concept-fetch"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetches</a> initiated by the element

[`sizes`](#attr-link-sizes) — Sizes of the icons (for
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="[`icon`](#rel-icon)")

[`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) — Images to use in different
situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc. (for
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="[`preload`](#link-type-preload)")

[`imagesizes`](#attr-link-imagesizes) — Image sizes for different page
layouts (for [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="[`preload`](#link-type-preload)")

[`as`](#attr-link-as) — Destination for a preload request (for
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="[`preload`](#link-type-preload)" and
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="[`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload)")

[`blocking`](#attr-link-blocking) — Whether the element is
<a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
id="the-link-element:potentially-render-blocking">potentially
render-blocking</a>

[`color`](#attr-link-color) — Color to use when customizing a site's
icon (for [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)="`mask-icon`")

[`disabled`](#attr-link-disabled) — Whether the link is disabled

[`fetchpriority`](#attr-link-fetchpriority) — Sets the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority"
id="the-link-element:concept-request-priority"
data-x-internal="concept-request-priority">priority</a> for
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="the-link-element:concept-fetch-2"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetches</a> initiated by the element

Also, the [`title`](#attr-link-title) attribute
<a href="#attr-link-title" id="the-link-element:attr-link-title-2">has
special semantics</a> on this element: Title of the link;
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name"
id="the-link-element:css-style-sheet-set-name"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set-name">CSS style sheet set name</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-link).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-link).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-link-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLinkElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString href;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? crossOrigin;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rel;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString as;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="rel"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString integrity;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString hreflang;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList sizes;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute USVString imageSrcset;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString imageSizes;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString referrerPolicy;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList blocking;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString fetchPriority;

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLLinkElement includes LinkStyle;
```

The [`link`](#the-link-element) element allows authors to link their
document to other resources.

The address of the link(s) is given by the <span id="attr-link-href"
class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`href`</span>
attribute. If the [`href`](#attr-link-href) attribute is present, then
its value must be a
<a href="#valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="the-link-element:valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>. One or both of the
[`href`](#attr-link-href) or [`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset)
attributes must be present.

If both the [`href`](#attr-link-href) and
[`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) attributes are absent, then the
element does not define a link.

The types of link indicated (the relationships) are given by the value
of the <span id="attr-link-rel" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`rel`</span> attribute, which, if present, must
have a value that is a
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="the-link-element:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a>. The [allowed keywords and
their meanings](#linkTypes) are defined in a later section. If the
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute is absent, has no keywords, or if none
of the keywords used are allowed according to the definitions in this
specification, then the element does not create any links.

[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="the-link-element:concept-supported-tokens"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> are the
keywords defined in [HTML link types](#linkTypes) which are allowed on
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements, impact the processing model, and
are supported by the user agent. The possible
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="the-link-element:concept-supported-tokens-2"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> are
[`alternate`](#rel-alternate),
[`dns-prefetch`](#link-type-dns-prefetch),
[`expect`](#link-type-expect), [`icon`](#rel-icon),
[`manifest`](#link-type-manifest),
[`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload), [`next`](#link-type-next),
[`pingback`](#link-type-pingback),
[`preconnect`](#link-type-preconnect),
[`prefetch`](#link-type-prefetch), [`preload`](#link-type-preload),
[`search`](#link-type-search), and
[`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet). [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="the-link-element:concept-supported-tokens-3"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> must
only include the tokens from this list that the user agent implements
the processing model for.

Theoretically a user agent could support the processing model for the
[`canonical`](#link-type-canonical) keyword — if it were a search engine
that executed JavaScript. But in practice that's quite unlikely. So in
most cases, [`canonical`](#link-type-canonical) ought not be included in
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="the-link-element:concept-supported-tokens-4"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a>.

A [`link`](#the-link-element) element must have either a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute or an
[`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute, but not both.

<div algorithm="">

If a [`link`](#the-link-element) element has an
[`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute, or has a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute that contains only keywords that are
<a href="#body-ok" id="the-link-element:body-ok">body-ok</a>, then the
element is said to be <span id="allowed-in-the-body" class="dfn">allowed
in the body</span>. This means that the element can be used where
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-link-element:phrasing-content-2-3">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

</div>

If the [`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute is used, the element can only
sometimes be used in the [`body`](#the-body-element) of the page. When
used with the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute,
the element can be used both in the [`head`](#the-head-element) element
and in the [`body`](#the-body-element) of the page, subject to the
constraints of the microdata model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two categories of links can be created using the
[`link`](#the-link-element) element: <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link">links to external
resources</a> and
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-3">hyperlinks</a>.
The [link types section](#linkTypes) defines whether a particular link
type is an external resource or a hyperlink. One
[`link`](#the-link-element) element can create multiple links (of which
some might be <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-2">external resource
links</a> and some might be
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-4">hyperlinks</a>);
exactly which and how many links are created depends on the keywords
given in the [`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute. User agents must process
the links on a per-link basis, not a per-element basis.

Each link created for a [`link`](#the-link-element) element is handled
separately. For instance, if there are two [`link`](#the-link-element)
elements with `rel="stylesheet"`, they each count as a separate external
resource, and each is affected by its own attributes independently.
Similarly, if a single [`link`](#the-link-element) element has a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute with the value `next stylesheet`, it
creates both a
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-5">hyperlink</a>
(for the [`next`](#link-type-next) keyword) and an
<a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-3">external resource
link</a> (for the [`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet) keyword), and
they are affected by other attributes (such as
[`media`](#attr-link-media) or [`title`](#attr-link-title)) differently.

<div class="example">

For example, the following [`link`](#the-link-element) element creates
two
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-6">hyperlinks</a>
(to the same page):

``` html
<link rel="author license" href="/about">
```

The two links created by this element are one whose semantic is that the
target page has information about the current page's author, and one
whose semantic is that the target page has information regarding the
license under which the current page is provided.

</div>

<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-7">Hyperlinks</a>
created with the [`link`](#the-link-element) element and its
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute apply to the whole document. This
contrasts with the [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute of
[`a`](#the-a-element) and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements, which
indicates the type of a link whose context is given by the link's
location within the document.

Unlike those created by [`a`](#the-a-element) and
[`area`](#the-area-element) elements,
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-link-element:hyperlink-8">hyperlinks</a>
created by [`link`](#the-link-element) elements are not displayed as
part of the document by default, in user agents that [support the
suggested default rendering](#renderingUA). And even if they are
force-displayed using CSS, they have no
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="the-link-element:activation-behaviour"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a>. Instead,
they primarily provide semantic information which might be used by the
page or by other software that consumes the page's contents.
Additionally, the user agent can [provide its own UI for following such
hyperlinks](#providing-users-with-a-means-to-follow-hyperlinks-created-using-the-link-element).

The exact behavior for <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-4">links to external
resources</a> depends on the exact relationship, as defined for the
relevant [link type](#linkTypes).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-crossorigin" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`crossorigin`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#cors-settings-attribute"
id="the-link-element:cors-settings-attribute">CORS settings
attribute</a>. It is intended for use with
<a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-5">external resource
links</a>.

The <span id="attr-link-media" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`media`</span> attribute says which media the
resource applies to. The value must be a
<a href="#valid-media-query-list"
id="the-link-element:valid-media-query-list">valid media query list</a>.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

It works by allowing you to provide a cryptographic hash that a fetched resource must match.")

The <span id="attr-link-integrity" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`integrity`</span> attribute represents the <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata"
id="the-link-element:concept-request-integrity-metadata"
data-x-internal="concept-request-integrity-metadata">integrity
metadata</a> for requests which this element is responsible for. The
value is text. The attribute must only be specified on
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)
attribute that contains the [`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet),
[`preload`](#link-type-preload), or
[`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload) keyword. [\[SRI\]](#refsSRI)

The <span id="attr-link-hreflang" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`hreflang`</span> attribute on the
[`link`](#the-link-element) element has the same semantics as the
<a href="#attr-hyperlink-hreflang"
id="the-link-element:attr-hyperlink-hreflang"><code>hreflang</code>
attribute on the <code>a</code> element</a>.

The <span id="attr-link-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute gives the
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="the-link-element:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
type</a> of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must
be a <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type"
id="the-link-element:valid-mime-type-string"
data-x-internal="valid-mime-type-string">valid MIME type string</a>.

For <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-6">external resource
links</a>, the [`type`](#attr-link-type) attribute is used as a hint to
user agents so that they can avoid fetching resources they do not
support.

The <span id="attr-link-referrerpolicy" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`referrerpolicy`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
id="the-link-element:referrer-policy-attribute">referrer policy
attribute</a>. It is intended for use with
<a href="#external-resource-link"
id="the-link-element:external-resource-link-7">external resource
links</a>, where it helps set the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-link-element:referrer-policy-2"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> used when
<a href="#fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource"
id="the-link-element:fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource">fetching and
processing the linked resource</a>.
[\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

The <span id="attr-link-title" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`title`</span> attribute gives the title of the
link. With one exception, it is purely advisory. The value is text. The
exception is for style sheet links that are
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
id="the-link-element:in-a-document-tree"
data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a>, for which
the [`title`](#attr-link-title) attribute defines
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set"
id="the-link-element:css-style-sheet-set"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set">CSS style sheet sets</a>.

The [`title`](#attr-link-title) attribute on [`link`](#the-link-element)
elements differs from the global [`title`](#attr-title) attribute of
most other elements in that a link without a title does not inherit the
title of the parent element: it merely has no title.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-imagesrcset" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`imagesrcset`</span> attribute may be present,
and is a <a href="#srcset-attribute"
id="the-link-element:srcset-attribute">srcset attribute</a>.

The [`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) and
[`href`](#attr-link-href) attributes (if
<a href="#width-descriptor" id="the-link-element:width-descriptor">width
descriptors</a> are not used) together contribute the
<a href="#image-source" id="the-link-element:image-source">image
sources</a> to the
<a href="#source-set" id="the-link-element:source-set">source set</a>.

If the [`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) attribute is present and
has any <a href="#image-candidate-string"
id="the-link-element:image-candidate-string">image candidate strings</a>
using a <a href="#width-descriptor"
id="the-link-element:width-descriptor-2">width descriptor</a>, the
<span id="attr-link-imagesizes" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`imagesizes`</span> attribute must also be
present, and is a
<a href="#sizes-attribute" id="the-link-element:sizes-attribute">sizes
attribute</a>. The [`imagesizes`](#attr-link-imagesizes) attribute
contributes the
<a href="#source-size-2" id="the-link-element:source-size-2">source
size</a> to the
<a href="#source-set" id="the-link-element:source-set-2">source set</a>.

The [`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) and
[`imagesizes`](#attr-link-imagesizes) attributes must only be specified
on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have both a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute that specifies the
[`preload`](#link-type-preload) keyword, as well as an
[`as`](#attr-link-as) attribute in the "`image`" state.

<div class="example">

These attributes allow preloading the appropriate resource that is later
used by an [`img`](#the-img-element) element that has the corresponding
values for its [`srcset`](#attr-img-srcset) and
[`sizes`](#attr-img-sizes) attributes:

``` html
<link rel="preload" as="image"
      imagesrcset="wolf_400px.jpg 400w, wolf_800px.jpg 800w, wolf_1600px.jpg 1600w"
      imagesizes="50vw">

<!-- ... later, or perhaps inserted dynamically ... -->
<img src="wolf.jpg" alt="A rad wolf"
     srcset="wolf_400px.jpg 400w, wolf_800px.jpg 800w, wolf_1600px.jpg 1600w"
     sizes="50vw">
```

Note how we omit the [`href`](#attr-link-href) attribute, as it would
only be relevant for browsers that do not support
[`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset), and in those cases it would
likely cause the incorrect image to be preloaded.

</div>

<div class="example">

The [`imagesrcset`](#attr-link-imagesrcset) attribute can be combined
with the [`media`](#attr-link-media) attribute to preload the
appropriate resource selected from a [`picture`](#the-picture-element)
element's sources, for
<a href="#art-direction" id="the-link-element:art-direction">art
direction</a>:

``` html
<link rel="preload" as="image"
      imagesrcset="dog-cropped-1x.jpg, dog-cropped-2x.jpg 2x"
      media="(max-width: 800px)">
<link rel="preload" as="image"
      imagesrcset="dog-wide-1x.jpg, dog-wide-2x.jpg 2x"
      media="(min-width: 801px)">

<!-- ... later, or perhaps inserted dynamically ... -->
<picture>
  <source srcset="dog-cropped-1x.jpg, dog-cropped-2x.jpg 2x"
          media="(max-width: 800px)">
  <img src="dog-wide-1x.jpg" srcset="dog-wide-2x.jpg 2x"
       alt="An awesome dog">
</picture>
```

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-sizes" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`sizes`</span> attribute gives the sizes of
icons for visual media. Its value, if present, is merely advisory. User
agents may use the value to decide which icon(s) to use if multiple
icons are available. If specified, the attribute must have a value that
is an <a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="the-link-element:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens-2">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a> which are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-link-element:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>.
Each value must be either an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-link-element:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "[`any`](#attr-link-sizes-any)", or a value that
consists of two <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-link-element:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integers</a> that do not have a leading U+0030 DIGIT ZERO (0) character
and that are separated by a single U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X or U+0058
LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character. The attribute must only be specified
on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute that specifies the [`icon`](#rel-icon)
keyword or the `apple-touch-icon` keyword.

The `apple-touch-icon` keyword is a registered
<a href="#concept-rel-extensions"
id="the-link-element:concept-rel-extensions">extension to the predefined
set of link types</a>, but user agents are not required to support it in
any way.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-as" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`as`</span> attribute specifies either a
<a href="#preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:preload-destination">preload destination</a> or a
<a href="#module-preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:module-preload-destination">module preload
destination</a> for a preload request for the resource given by the
[`href`](#attr-link-href) attribute. It is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-link-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>.
Each of the union of <a href="#preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:preload-destination-2">preload destinations</a> and
<a href="#module-preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:module-preload-destination-2">module preload
destinations</a> is a keyword for this attribute, mapping to a state of
the same name. The attribute must be specified on
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)
attribute that contains the [`preload`](#link-type-preload) keyword; in
such cases it must have a value which is a
<a href="#preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:preload-destination-3">preload destination</a>. It
may be specified on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have a
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute that contains the
[`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload) keyword; in such cases it
must have a value which is a <a href="#module-preload-destination"
id="the-link-element:module-preload-destination-3">module preload
destination</a>. For other [`link`](#the-link-element) elements, it must
not be specified.

The processing model for how the [`as`](#attr-link-as) attribute is used
is given in an individual link type's
<a href="#fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource"
id="the-link-element:fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource-2">fetch and
process the linked resource</a> algorithm.

The attribute does not have a *[missing value
default](#missing-value-default)* or *[invalid value
default](#invalid-value-default)*, meaning that invalid or missing
values for the attribute map to no state. This is accounted for in the
processing model. For [`preload`](#link-type-preload) links, both
conditions are an error; for [`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload)
links, a missing value will be treated as "`script`".

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-blocking" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`blocking`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="the-link-element:blocking-attribute">blocking attribute</a>. It is
used by link types [`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet) and
[`expect`](#link-type-expect), and it must only be specified on link
elements that have a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute containing those
keywords.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-link-color" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`color`</span> attribute is used with the
`mask-icon` link type. The attribute must only be specified on
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)
attribute that contains the `mask-icon` keyword. The value must be a
string that matches the CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#typedef-color"
id="the-link-element:color" data-x-internal="color">&lt;color&gt;</a>
production, defining a suggested color that user agents can use to
customize the display of the icon that the user sees when they pin your
site.

This specification does not have any user agent requirements for the
[`color`](#attr-link-color) attribute.

The `mask-icon` keyword is a registered
<a href="#concept-rel-extensions"
id="the-link-element:concept-rel-extensions-2">extension to the
predefined set of link types</a>, but user agents are not required to
support it in any way.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

[`link`](#the-link-element) elements have an associated
<span id="explicitly-enabled" class="dfn">explicitly enabled</span>
boolean. It is initially false.

The <span id="attr-link-disabled" class="dfn" dfn-for="link"
dfn-type="element-attr">`disabled`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-link-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a> that is
used with the [`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet) link type. The
attribute must only be specified on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements
that have a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute that contains the
[`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet) keyword.

<div algorithm="">

Whenever the [`disabled`](#attr-link-disabled) attribute is removed, set
the [`link`](#the-link-element) element's <a href="#explicitly-enabled"
id="the-link-element:explicitly-enabled">explicitly enabled</a>
attribute to true.

</div>

<div class="example">

Removing the [`disabled`](#attr-link-disabled) attribute dynamically,
e.g., using
`document.querySelector("link").removeAttribute("disabled")`, will fetch
and apply the style sheet:

``` html
<link disabled rel="alternate stylesheet" href="css/pooh">
```

</div>
