<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-meta-element:metadata-content-2">Metadata content</a>.

If the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is
present:
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-meta-element:flow-content-2">flow
content</a>.

If the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is
present: <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-meta-element:phrasing-content-2">phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
If the [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute is present, or if the
element's [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="the-meta-element:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type">Encoding
declaration state</a>: in a [`head`](#the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is present but
not in the <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="the-meta-element:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-2">Encoding
declaration state</a>: in a [`head`](#the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is present but
not in the <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="the-meta-element:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-3">Encoding
declaration state</a>: in a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element
that is a child of a [`head`](#the-head-element) element.

If the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute is present: where
<a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-meta-element:metadata-content-2-2">metadata content</a> is
expected.

If the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is
present: where <a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-meta-element:metadata-content-2-3">metadata content</a> is
expected.

If the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is
present: where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-meta-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-meta-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
No <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-meta-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-meta-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`name`](#attr-meta-name) — Metadata name

[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) — Pragma directive

[`content`](#attr-meta-content) — Value of the element

[`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) —
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="the-meta-element:character-encoding-declaration">Character encoding
declaration</a>

[`media`](#attr-meta-media) — Applicable media

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-meta).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-meta).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-meta-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMetaElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="http-equiv"] attribute DOMString httpEquiv;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString content;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-meta-element:represents">represents</a>
various kinds of metadata that cannot be expressed using the
[`title`](#the-title-element), [`base`](#the-base-element),
[`link`](#the-link-element), [`style`](#the-style-element), and
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements.

The [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element can represent document-level
metadata with the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute, pragma directives
with the [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute, and the file's
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="the-meta-element:character-encoding-declaration-2">character
encoding declaration</a> when an HTML document is serialized to string
form (e.g. for transmission over the network or for disk storage) with
the [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute.

Exactly one of the [`name`](#attr-meta-name),
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv), [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset),
and [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attributes must be
specified.

If either [`name`](#attr-meta-name),
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv), or
[`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) is specified, then the
[`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute must also be specified.
Otherwise, it must be omitted.

The <span id="attr-meta-charset" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta"
dfn-type="element-attr">`charset`</span> attribute specifies the
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding"
id="the-meta-element:encoding" data-x-internal="encoding">character
encoding</a> used by the document. This is a
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="the-meta-element:character-encoding-declaration-3">character
encoding declaration</a>. If the attribute is present, its value must be
an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-meta-element:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`utf-8`".

The [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute on the
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no effect in XML documents, but
is allowed in XML documents in order to facilitate migration to and from
XML.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with
a [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute per document.

The <span id="attr-meta-content" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta"
dfn-type="element-attr">`content`</span> attribute gives the value of
the document metadata or pragma directive when the element is used for
those purposes. The allowed values depend on the exact context, as
described in subsequent sections of this specification.

If a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has a <span id="attr-meta-name"
class="dfn" dfn-for="meta" dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span>
attribute, it sets document metadata. Document metadata is expressed in
terms of name-value pairs, the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute on
the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element giving the name, and the
[`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute on the same element giving the
value. The name specifies what aspect of metadata is being set; valid
names and the meaning of their values are described in the following
sections. If a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no
[`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute, then the value part of the
metadata name-value pair is the empty string.

The <span id="attr-meta-media" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta"
dfn-type="element-attr">`media`</span> attribute says which media the
metadata applies to. The value must be a
<a href="#valid-media-query-list"
id="the-meta-element:valid-media-query-list">valid media query list</a>.
Unless the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) is
[`theme-color`](#meta-theme-color), the [`media`](#attr-meta-media)
attribute has no effect on the processing model and must not be used by
authors.

##### <span class="secno">4.2.5.1</span> Standard metadata names<a href="#standard-metadata-names" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/meta/name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name "The <meta> element can be used to provide document metadata in terms of name-value pairs, with the name attribute giving the metadata name, and the content attribute giving the value.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12.1+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer6+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

This specification defines a few names for the [`name`](#attr-meta-name)
attribute of the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element.

Names are case-insensitive<span class="impl">, and must be compared in
an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
manner</span>.

<span id="meta-application-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`application-name`</span>

The value must be a short free-form string giving the name of the web
application that the page represents. If the page is not a web
application, the [`application-name`](#meta-application-name) metadata
name must not be used. Translations of the web application's name may be
given, using the [`lang`](#attr-lang) attribute to specify the language
of each name.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with
a given
<a href="#language" id="standard-metadata-names:language">language</a>
and where the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for [`application-name`](#meta-application-name) per document.

User agents may use the application name in UI in preference to the
page's [`title`](#the-title-element), since the title might include
status messages and the like relevant to the status of the page at a
particular moment in time instead of just being the name of the
application.

<div algorithm="">

To find the application name to use given an ordered list of languages
(e.g. British English, American English, and English), user agents must
run the following steps:

1.  Let `languages` be the list of languages.

2.  Let `default language` be the
    <a href="#language" id="standard-metadata-names:language-2">language</a>
    of the [`Document`](#document)'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="standard-metadata-names:document-element"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>, if any, and
    if that language is not unknown.

3.  If there is a `default language`, and if it is not the same language
    as any of the languages in `languages`, append it to `languages`.

4.  Let `winning language` be the first language in `languages` for
    which there is a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element in the
    [`Document`](#document) where the [`name`](#attr-meta-name)
    attribute value is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for [`application-name`](#meta-application-name) and whose
    <a href="#language" id="standard-metadata-names:language-3">language</a>
    is the language in question.

    If none of the languages have such a [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
    element, then return; there's no given application name.

5.  Return the value of the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute of
    the first [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element in the
    [`Document`](#document) in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="standard-metadata-names:tree-order"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> where the
    [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for [`application-name`](#meta-application-name) and whose
    <a href="#language" id="standard-metadata-names:language-4">language</a>
    is `winning language`.

</div>

This algorithm would be used by a browser when it needs a name for the
page, for instance, to label a bookmark. The languages it would provide
to the algorithm would be the user's preferred languages.

<span id="meta-author" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`author`</span>

The value must be a free-form string giving the name of one of the
page's authors.

<span id="meta-description" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`description`</span>

The value must be a free-form string that describes the page. The value
must be appropriate for use in a directory of pages, e.g. in a search
engine. There must not be more than one [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
element where the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-5"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for [`description`](#meta-description) per document.

<span id="meta-generator" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`generator`</span>

The value must be a free-form string that identifies one of the software
packages used to generate the document. This value must not be used on
pages whose markup is not generated by software, e.g. pages whose markup
was written by a user in a text editor.

<div class="example">

Here is what a tool called "Frontweaver" could include in its output, in
the page's [`head`](#the-head-element) element, to identify itself as
the tool used to generate the page:

``` html
<meta name=generator content="Frontweaver 8.2">
```

</div>

<span id="meta-keywords" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`keywords`</span>

The value must be a <a href="#set-of-comma-separated-tokens"
id="standard-metadata-names:set-of-comma-separated-tokens">set of
comma-separated tokens</a>, each of which is a keyword relevant to the
page.

<div class="example">

This page about typefaces on British motorways uses a
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) element to specify some keywords that users
might use to look for the page:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en-GB">
 <head>
  <title>Typefaces on UK motorways</title>
  <meta name="keywords" content="british,type face,font,fonts,highway,highways">
 </head>
 <body>
  ...
```

</div>

Many search engines do not consider such keywords, because this feature
has historically been used unreliably and even misleadingly as a way to
spam search engine results in a way that is not helpful for users.

<div algorithm="">

To obtain the list of keywords that the author has specified as
applicable to the page, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `keywords` be an empty list.

2.  For each [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with a
    [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute and a
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute and where the
    [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-6"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for [`keywords`](#meta-keywords):

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-commas"
        id="standard-metadata-names:split-a-string-on-commas"
        data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-commas">Split the value of the
        element's <code>content</code> attribute on commas</a>.

    2.  Add the resulting tokens, if any, to `keywords`.

3.  Remove any duplicates from `keywords`.

4.  Return `keywords`. This is the list of keywords that the author has
    specified as applicable to the page.

</div>

User agents should not use this information when there is insufficient
confidence in the reliability of the value.

For instance, it would be reasonable for a content management system to
use the keyword information of pages within the system to populate the
index of a site-specific search engine, but a large-scale content
aggregator that used this information would likely find that certain
users would try to game its ranking mechanism through the use of
inappropriate keywords.

<span id="meta-referrer" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`referrer`</span>

The value must be a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a>, which defines the
default <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy-2"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> for the
[`Document`](#document). [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

<div algorithm="">

If any [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element `element` is
<a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="standard-metadata-names:insert-an-element-into-a-document">inserted
into the document</a>, or has its [`name`](#attr-meta-name) or
[`content`](#attr-meta-content) attributes changed, user agents must run
the following algorithm:

1.  If `element` is not
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
    id="standard-metadata-names:in-a-document-tree"
    data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a>, then
    return.

2.  If `element` does not have a [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute
    whose value is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-7"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "[`referrer`](#meta-referrer)", then return.

3.  If `element` does not have a [`content`](#attr-meta-content)
    attribute, or that attribute's value is the empty string, then
    return.

4.  Let `value` be the value of `element`'s
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="standard-metadata-names:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

5.  If `value` is one of the values given in the first column of the
    following table, then set `value` to the value given in the second
    column:

    | Legacy value | Referrer policy |
    |----|----|
    | `never` | <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-no-referrer"
    data-x-internal="referrer-policy-no-referrer"><code
    id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy-no-referrer">no-referrer</code></a> |
    | `default` | the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#default-referrer-policy"
    id="standard-metadata-names:default-referrer-policy"
    data-x-internal="default-referrer-policy">default referrer policy</a> |
    | `always` | <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-unsafe-url"
    data-x-internal="referrer-policy-unsafe-url"><code
    id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy-unsafe-url">unsafe-url</code></a> |
    | `origin-when-crossorigin` | <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-origin-when-cross-origin"
    data-x-internal="referrer-policy-origin-when-cross-origin"><code
    id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy-origin-when-cross-origin">origin-when-cross-origin</code></a> |

6.  If `value` is a <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
    id="standard-metadata-names:referrer-policy-3"
    data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a>, then set
    `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="standard-metadata-names:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-policy-container"
    id="standard-metadata-names:concept-document-policy-container">policy
    container</a>'s <a href="#policy-container-referrer-policy"
    id="standard-metadata-names:policy-container-referrer-policy">referrer
    policy</a> to `policy`.

</div>

For historical reasons, unlike other standard metadata names, the
processing model for [`referrer`](#meta-referrer) is not responsive to
element removals, and does not use
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="standard-metadata-names:tree-order-2"
data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>. Only the
most-recently-inserted or most-recently-modified
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) element in this state has an effect.

<span id="meta-theme-color" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`theme-color`</span>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/meta/name/theme-color](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name/theme-color "The theme-color value for the name attribute of the <meta> element indicates a suggested color that user agents should use to customize the display of the page or of the surrounding user interface. If specified, the content attribute must contain a valid CSS <color>.")

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox no">FirefoxNo</span><span class="safari yes">Safari15+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome<span title="Partial implementation.">🔰
73+</span></span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera no">OperaNo</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge<span title="Partial implementation.">🔰
79+</span></span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android yes">Chrome
Android80+</span><span class="webview_android no">WebView
AndroidNo</span><span class="samsunginternet_android yes">Samsung
Internet6.2+</span><span class="opera_android no">Opera AndroidNo</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The value must be a string that matches the CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#typedef-color"
id="standard-metadata-names:color"
data-x-internal="color">&lt;color&gt;</a> production, defining a
suggested color that user agents should use to customize the display of
the page or of the surrounding user interface. For example, a browser
might color the page's title bar with the specified value, or use it as
a color highlight in a tab bar or task switcher.

Within an HTML document, the [`media`](#attr-meta-media) attribute value
must be unique amongst all the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements with
their [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value set to an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-8"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for [`theme-color`](#meta-theme-color).

<div class="example">

This standard itself uses "WHATWG green" as its theme color:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>HTML Standard</title>
<meta name="theme-color" content="#3c790a">
...
```

</div>

The [`media`](#attr-meta-media) attribute may be used to describe the
context in which the provided color should be used.

<div class="example">

If we only wanted to use "WHATWG green" as this standard's theme color
in dark mode, we could use the `prefers-color-scheme` media feature:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>HTML Standard</title>
<meta name="theme-color" content="#3c790a" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">
...
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To obtain a page's theme color, user agents must run the following
steps:

1.  Let `candidate elements` be the list of all
    [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements that meet the following
    criteria, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="standard-metadata-names:tree-order-3"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    - the element is
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
      id="standard-metadata-names:in-a-document-tree-2"
      data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a>;

    - the element has a [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute, whose value
      is an
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
      id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-9"
      data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
      match for [`theme-color`](#meta-theme-color); and

    - the element has a [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.

2.  For each `element` in `candidate elements`:

    1.  If `element` has a [`media`](#attr-link-media) attribute and the
        value of `element`'s [`media`](#attr-meta-media) attribute does
        not <a href="#matches-the-environment"
        id="standard-metadata-names:matches-the-environment">match the
        environment</a>, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="standard-metadata-names:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  Let `value` be the result of <a
        href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace"
        id="standard-metadata-names:strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace"
        data-x-internal="strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace">stripping
        leading and trailing ASCII whitespace</a> from the value of
        `element`'s [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.

    3.  Let `color` be the result of
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value"
        id="standard-metadata-names:parsed-as-a-css-color-value"
        data-x-internal="parsed-as-a-css-color-value">parsing</a>
        `value`.

    4.  If `color` is not failure, then return `color`.

3.  Return nothing (the page has no theme color).

</div>

If any [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements are
<a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="standard-metadata-names:insert-an-element-into-a-document-2">inserted
into the document</a> or <a href="#remove-an-element-from-a-document"
id="standard-metadata-names:remove-an-element-from-a-document">removed
from the document</a>, or existing [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements
have their [`name`](#attr-meta-name), [`content`](#attr-meta-content),
or [`media`](#attr-link-media) attributes changed, or if the environment
changes such that any [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element's
[`media`](#attr-link-media) attribute's value may now or may no longer
<a href="#matches-the-environment"
id="standard-metadata-names:matches-the-environment-2">match the
environment</a>, user agents must re-run the above algorithm and apply
the result to any affected UI.

When using the theme color in UI, user agents may adjust it in
implementation-specific ways to make it more suitable for the UI in
question. For example, if a user agent intends to use the theme color as
a background and display white text over it, it might use a darker
variant of the theme color in that part of the UI, to ensure adequate
contrast.

<span id="meta-color-scheme" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/name"
dfn-type="attr-value">`color-scheme`</span>

To aid user agents in rendering the page background with the desired
color scheme immediately (rather than waiting for all CSS in the page to
load), a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop"
id="standard-metadata-names:&#39;color-scheme&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;color-scheme&#39;">'color-scheme'</a> value can be
provided in a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element.

The value must be a string that matches the syntax for the CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop"
id="standard-metadata-names:&#39;color-scheme&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;color-scheme&#39;">'color-scheme'</a> property
value. It determines the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#pages-supported-color-schemes"
id="standard-metadata-names:page&#39;s-supported-color-schemes"
data-x-internal="page&#39;s-supported-color-schemes">page's supported
color-schemes</a>.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with
its [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute value set to an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-10"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for [`color-scheme`](#meta-color-scheme) per document.

<div class="example">

The following declaration indicates that the page is aware of and can
handle a color scheme with dark background colors and light foreground
colors:

``` html
<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To obtain a <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#pages-supported-color-schemes"
id="standard-metadata-names:page&#39;s-supported-color-schemes-2"
data-x-internal="page&#39;s-supported-color-schemes">page's supported
color-schemes</a>, user agents must run the following steps:

1.  Let `candidate elements` be the list of all
    [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements that meet the following
    criteria, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="standard-metadata-names:tree-order-4"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    - the element is
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
      id="standard-metadata-names:in-a-document-tree-3"
      data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a>;

    - the element has a [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute, whose value
      is an
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
      id="standard-metadata-names:ascii-case-insensitive-11"
      data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
      match for [`color-scheme`](#meta-color-scheme); and

    - the element has a [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.

2.  For each `element` in `candidate elements`:

    1.  Let `parsed` be the result of <a
        href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-a-list-of-component-values"
        id="standard-metadata-names:parse-a-list-of-component-values"
        data-x-internal="parse-a-list-of-component-values">parsing a list of
        component values</a> given the value of `element`'s
        [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.
    2.  If `parsed` is a valid CSS
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop"
        id="standard-metadata-names:&#39;color-scheme&#39;-3"
        data-x-internal="&#39;color-scheme&#39;">'color-scheme'</a>
        property value, then return `parsed`.

3.  Return null.

</div>

If any [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements are
<a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="standard-metadata-names:insert-an-element-into-a-document-3">inserted
into the document</a> or <a href="#remove-an-element-from-a-document"
id="standard-metadata-names:remove-an-element-from-a-document-2">removed
from the document</a>, or existing [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements
have their [`name`](#attr-meta-name) or [`content`](#attr-meta-content)
attributes changed, user agents must re-run the above algorithm.

Because these rules check successive elements until they find a match,
an author can provide multiple such values to handle fallback for legacy
user agents. Opposite to how CSS fallback works for properties, the
multiple meta elements needs to be arranged with the legacy values after
the newer values.

##### <span class="secno">4.2.5.2</span> Other metadata names<a href="#other-metadata-names" class="self-link"></a>

Anyone can create and use their own <span id="concept-meta-extensions"
class="dfn">extensions to the predefined set of metadata names</span>.
There is no requirement to register such extensions.

However, a new metadata name should not be created in any of the
following cases:

- If either the name is a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="other-metadata-names:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>, or the
  value of its accompanying [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute is
  a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="other-metadata-names:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>; in
  those cases, registering it as an <a href="#concept-rel-extensions"
  id="other-metadata-names:concept-rel-extensions">extension to the
  predefined set of link types</a> is encouraged (rather than creating a
  new metadata name).

- If the name is for something expected to have processing requirements
  in user agents; in that case it ought to be standardized.

Also, before creating and using a new metadata name, consulting the
[WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions
page](https://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/MetaExtensions) is encouraged — to
avoid choosing a metadata name that's already in use, and to avoid
duplicating the purpose of any metadata names that are already in use,
and to avoid new standardized names clashing with your chosen name.
[\[WHATWGWIKI\]](#refsWHATWGWIKI)

Anyone is free to edit the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page at any time
to add a metadata name. New metadata names can be specified with the
following information:

Keyword  
The actual name being defined. The name should not be confusingly
similar to any other defined name (e.g. differing only in case).

Brief description  
A short non-normative description of what the metadata name's meaning
is, including the format the value is required to be in.

Specification  
A link to a more detailed description of the metadata name's semantics
and requirements. It could be another page on the wiki, or a link to an
external page.

Synonyms  
A list of other names that have exactly the same processing
requirements. Authors should not use the names defined to be synonyms
(they are only intended to allow user agents to support legacy content).
Anyone may remove synonyms that are not used in practice; only names
that need to be processed as synonyms for compatibility with legacy
content are to be registered in this way.

Status  
One of the following:

Proposed  
The name has not received wide peer review and approval. Someone has
proposed it and is, or soon will be, using it.

Ratified  
The name has received wide peer review and approval. It has a
specification that unambiguously defines how to handle pages that use
the name, including when they use it in incorrect ways.

Discontinued  
The metadata name has received wide peer review and it has been found
wanting. Existing pages are using this metadata name, but new pages
should avoid it. The "brief description" and "specification" entries
will give details of what authors should use instead, if anything.

If a metadata name is found to be redundant with existing values, it
should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value.

If a metadata name is added in the "proposed" state for a period of a
month or more without being used or specified, then it may be removed
from the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page.

If a metadata name is added with the "proposed" status and found to be
redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a
synonym for the existing value. If a metadata name is added with the
"proposed" status and found to be harmful, then it should be changed to
"discontinued" status.

Anyone can change the status at any time, but should only do so in
accordance with the definitions above.

##### <span class="secno">4.2.5.3</span> Pragma directives<a href="#pragma-directives" class="self-link"></a>

When the <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta"
dfn-type="element-attr">`http-equiv`</span> attribute is specified on a
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) element, the element is a pragma directive.

<div id="warning-http-equiv-unrelated-to-http-headers" class="warning">

Despite the name [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv), pragma
directives are almost entirely unrelated to HTTP headers. Implementers
and web developers are best off thinking of them as entirely separate,
and the name as being a historical accident.

In more detail, although the [`refresh`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh)
keyword has the same processing model as the corresponding
\`[`Refresh`](#refresh)\` header, every other standardized pragma
directive has at least slightly different behavior than the
similarly-named header. (And usually dramatically-different behavior.)

Implementers or specification writers contemplating adding new
document-level pragmas or HTTP header-controlled switches should be
cautious about this mismatch, and avoid perpetuating the existing
confusion by adding the same or similar behavior to both an HTTP header
and an [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) pragma. Instead, consider
providing only an HTTP header, or if an in-document pragma is needed,
consider adding a new attribute to [`meta`](#the-meta-element) similar
to the model used by the [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute.
(Note that avoiding in-document pragmas is often the better choice,
since the DOM is mutable. Thus, even in the simple case where the
developer does not add, remove, or mutate [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
elements, the policy will go from un-applied to applied during parsing,
which can have complex implications.)

</div>

The [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="pragma-directives:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | Conforming | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-language" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`content-language`</span> | No | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language">Content
language</a> | Sets the <a href="#pragma-set-default-language"
id="pragma-directives:pragma-set-default-language">pragma-set default
language</a>. |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`content-type`</span> |  | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type">Encoding
declaration</a> | An alternative form of setting the [`charset`](#attr-meta-charset). |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-default-style" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`default-style`</span> |  | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style">Default
style</a> | Sets the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name"
id="pragma-directives:css-style-sheet-set-name"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set-name">name</a> of the default <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set"
id="pragma-directives:css-style-sheet-set"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set">CSS style sheet set</a>. |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-refresh" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`refresh`</span> |  | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh-2">Refresh</a> | Acts as a timed redirect. |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-set-cookie" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`set-cookie`</span> | No | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie">Set-Cookie</a> | Has no effect. |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-x-ua-compatible" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`x-ua-compatible`</span> |  | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-x-ua-compatible"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-x-ua-compatible">X-UA-Compatible</a> | In practice, encourages Internet Explorer to more closely follow the specifications. |
| <span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-security-policy" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta/http-equiv" dfn-type="attr-value">`content-security-policy`</span> |  | <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy">Content
security policy</a> | <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced"
id="pragma-directives:enforce-the-policy"
data-x-internal="enforce-the-policy">Enforces</a> a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy">Content Security Policy</a> on a [`Document`](#document). |

<div algorithm="">

When a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element is
<a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="pragma-directives:insert-an-element-into-a-document">inserted into
the document</a>, if its [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute
is present and represents one of the above states, then the user agent
must run the algorithm appropriate for that state, as described in the
following list:

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language" class="dfn">Content
language state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`content-language`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-language)`"`)

This feature is non-conforming. Authors are encouraged to use the
[`lang`](#attr-lang) attribute instead.

This pragma sets the <span id="pragma-set-default-language"
class="dfn">pragma-set default language</span>. Until such a pragma is
successfully processed, there is no
<a href="#pragma-set-default-language"
id="pragma-directives:pragma-set-default-language-2">pragma-set default
language</a>.

1.  If the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute, then return.

2.  If the element's [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute contains
    a U+002C COMMA character (,), then return.

3.  Let `input` be the value of the element's
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.

4.  Let `position` point at the first character of `input`.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
    id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace"
    data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
    within `input` given `position`.

6.  <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points"
    id="pragma-directives:collect-a-sequence-of-code-points"
    data-x-internal="collect-a-sequence-of-code-points">Collect a sequence
    of code points</a> that are not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="pragma-directives:space-characters"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> from `input`
    given `position`.

7.  Let `candidate` be the string that resulted from the previous step.

8.  If `candidate` is the empty string, return.

9.  Set the <a href="#pragma-set-default-language"
    id="pragma-directives:pragma-set-default-language-3">pragma-set default
    language</a> to `candidate`.

    If the value consists of multiple space-separated tokens, tokens
    after the first are ignored.

This pragma is almost, but not quite, entirely unlike the HTTP
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.content-language"
data-x-internal="http-content-language"><code
id="pragma-directives:http-content-language">Content-Language</code></a>\`
header of the same name. [\[HTTP\]](#refsHTTP)

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type" class="dfn">Encoding
declaration state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`content-type`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-type)`"`)

The <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-2">Encoding
declaration state</a> is just an alternative form of setting the
[`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute: it is a
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="pragma-directives:character-encoding-declaration">character encoding
declaration</a>. This state's user agent requirements are all handled by
the parsing section of the specification.

For [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements with an
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-3">Encoding
declaration state</a>, the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute
must have a value that is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="pragma-directives:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for a string that consists of: "`text/html;`", optionally followed
by any number of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
id="pragma-directives:space-characters-2"
data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>, followed by
"`charset=utf-8`".

A document must not contain both a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element
with an [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-4">Encoding
declaration state</a> and a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with the
[`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute present.

The <a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type-5">Encoding
declaration state</a> may be used in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="pragma-directives:html-documents"
data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML documents</a>, but elements with
an [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in that state must
not be used in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document"
id="pragma-directives:xml-documents" data-x-internal="xml-documents">XML
documents</a>.

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style" class="dfn">Default style
state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`default-style`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-default-style)`"`)

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

This pragma sets the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name"
id="pragma-directives:css-style-sheet-set-name-2"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set-name">name</a> of the default
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set"
id="pragma-directives:css-style-sheet-set-2"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set">CSS style sheet set</a>.

1.  If the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's
    value is the empty string, then return.

2.  <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#change-the-preferred-css-style-sheet-set-name"
    id="pragma-directives:change-the-preferred-css-style-sheet-set-name"
    data-x-internal="change-the-preferred-css-style-sheet-set-name">Change
    the preferred CSS style sheet set name</a> with the name being the
    value of the element's [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.
    [\[CSSOM\]](#refsCSSOM)

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh" class="dfn">Refresh state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`refresh`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-refresh)`"`)

This pragma acts as a timed redirect.

A [`Document`](#document) object has an associated
<span id="will-declaratively-refresh" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document">will declaratively refresh</span> (a boolean). It is
initially false.

1.  If the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's
    value is the empty string, then return.

2.  Let `input` be the value of the element's
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute.

3.  Run the <a href="#shared-declarative-refresh-steps"
    id="pragma-directives:shared-declarative-refresh-steps">shared
    declarative refresh steps</a> with the [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
    element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="pragma-directives:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, `input`, and the
    [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element.

The <span id="shared-declarative-refresh-steps" class="dfn">shared
declarative refresh steps</span>, given a [`Document`](#document) object
`document`, string `input`, and optionally a [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
element `meta`, are as follows:

1.  If `document`'s <a href="#will-declaratively-refresh"
    id="pragma-directives:will-declaratively-refresh">will declaratively
    refresh</a> is true, then return.

2.  Let `position` point at the first
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
    id="pragma-directives:code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code
    point</a> of `input`.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
    id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace-2"
    data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
    within `input` given `position`.

4.  Let `time` be 0.

5.  <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points"
    id="pragma-directives:collect-a-sequence-of-code-points-2"
    data-x-internal="collect-a-sequence-of-code-points">Collect a sequence
    of code points</a> that are
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="pragma-directives:ascii-digits" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII
    digits</a> from `input` given `position`, and let `timeString` be
    the result.

6.  If `timeString` is the empty string, then:

    1.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-2" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is not U+002E (.),
        then return.

7.  Otherwise, set `time` to the result of parsing `timeString` using
    the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
    id="pragma-directives:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules for
    parsing non-negative integers</a>.

8.  <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points"
    id="pragma-directives:collect-a-sequence-of-code-points-3"
    data-x-internal="collect-a-sequence-of-code-points">Collect a sequence
    of code points</a> that are
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="pragma-directives:ascii-digits-2"
    data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a> and U+002E FULL STOP
    characters (.) from `input` given `position`. Ignore any collected
    characters.

9.  Let `urlRecord` be `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="pragma-directives:the-document&#39;s-address"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>.

10. If `position` is not past the end of `input`, then:

    1.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-3" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is not U+003B (;),
        U+002C (,), or
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
        id="pragma-directives:space-characters-3"
        data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>, then
        return.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
        id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace-3"
        data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
        within `input` given `position`.

    3.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-4" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+003B (;) or
        U+002C (,), then advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-5" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>.

    4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
        id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace-4"
        data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
        within `input` given `position`.

11. If `position` is not past the end of `input`, then:

    1.  Let `urlString` be the substring of `input` from the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-6" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> at `position` to the end of the string.

    2.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-7" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+0055 (U) or
        U+0075 (u), then advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-8" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>. Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *skip quotes*.

    3.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-9" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+0052 (R) or
        U+0072 (r), then advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-10" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>. Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.

    4.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-11" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+004C (L) or
        U+006C (l), then advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-12" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>. Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.

    5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
        id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace-5"
        data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
        within `input` given `position`.

    6.  If the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-13" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+003D (=),
        then advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-14" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>. Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.

    7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace"
        id="pragma-directives:skip-ascii-whitespace-6"
        data-x-internal="skip-ascii-whitespace">Skip ASCII whitespace</a>
        within `input` given `position`.

    8.  *Skip quotes*: If the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-15" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `input` pointed to by `position` is U+0027 (') or
        U+0022 ("), then let `quote` be that
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-16" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>, and advance `position` to the next
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-17" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>. Otherwise, let `quote` be the empty string.

    9.  Set `urlString` to the substring of `input` from the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-18" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> at `position` to the end of the string.

    10. If `quote` is not the empty string, and there is a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-19" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a> in `urlString` equal to `quote`, then truncate
        `urlString` at that
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-20" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        point</a>, so that it and all subsequent
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
        id="pragma-directives:code-point-21" data-x-internal="code-point">code
        points</a> are removed.

    11. *Parse*: Set `urlRecord` to the result of
        <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
        id="pragma-directives:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a URL</a>
        given `urlString`, relative to `document`.

    12. If `urlRecord` is failure, then return.

    13. If `urlRecord`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
        id="pragma-directives:concept-url-scheme"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is
        "[`javascript`](#the-javascript:-url-special-case)", then
        return.

12. Set `document`'s <a href="#will-declaratively-refresh"
    id="pragma-directives:will-declaratively-refresh-2">will declaratively
    refresh</a> to true.

13. Perform one or more of the following steps:

    - After the refresh has come due (as defined below), if the user has
      not canceled the redirect and, if `meta` is given, `document`'s
      <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
      id="pragma-directives:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing flag
      set</a> does not have the
      <a href="#sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag"
      id="pragma-directives:sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
      automatic features browsing context flag</a> set, then
      <a href="#navigate" id="pragma-directives:navigate">navigate</a>
      `document`'s
      <a href="#node-navigable" id="pragma-directives:node-navigable">node
      navigable</a> to `urlRecord` using `document`, with
      *[historyHandling](#navigation-hh)* set to
      "[`replace`](#navigationhistorybehavior-replace)".

      For the purposes of the previous paragraph, a refresh is said to
      have come due as soon as the *later* of the following two
      conditions occurs:

      - At least `time` seconds have elapsed since `document`'s
        <a href="#completely-loaded-time"
        id="pragma-directives:completely-loaded-time">completely loaded time</a>,
        adjusted to take into account user or user agent preferences.
      - If `meta` is given, at least `time` seconds have elapsed since
        `meta` was <a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
        id="pragma-directives:insert-an-element-into-a-document-2">inserted into
        the document</a> `document`, adjusted to take into account user
        or user agent preferences.

      It is important to use `document` here, and not `meta`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
      id="pragma-directives:node-document-2"
      data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, as that might
      have changed between the initial set of steps and the refresh
      coming due and `meta` is not always given (in case of the HTTP
      \`[`Refresh`](#refresh)\` header).

    - Provide the user with an interface that, when selected,
      <a href="#navigate" id="pragma-directives:navigate-2">navigates</a>
      `document`'s
      <a href="#node-navigable" id="pragma-directives:node-navigable-2">node
      navigable</a> to `urlRecord` using `document`.

    - Do nothing.

    In addition, the user agent may, as with anything, inform the user
    of any and all aspects of its operation, including the state of any
    timers, the destinations of any timed redirects, and so forth.

For [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements with an
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh-3">Refresh state</a>,
the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute must have a value
consisting either of:

- just a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
  id="pragma-directives:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
  integer</a>, or
- a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
  id="pragma-directives:valid-non-negative-integer-2">valid non-negative
  integer</a>, followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), followed by
  one or more <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
  id="pragma-directives:space-characters-4"
  data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>, followed by a
  substring that is an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="pragma-directives:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for the string "`URL`", followed by a U+003D EQUALS SIGN
  character (=), followed by a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
  id="pragma-directives:valid-url-string"
  data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL string</a> that does not
  start with a literal U+0027 APOSTROPHE (') or U+0022 QUOTATION MARK
  (") character.

In the former case, the integer represents a number of seconds before
the page is to be reloaded; in the latter case the integer represents a
number of seconds before the page is to be replaced by the page at the
given <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="pragma-directives:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>.

<div class="example">

A news organization's front page could include the following markup in
the page's [`head`](#the-head-element) element, to ensure that the page
automatically reloads from the server every five minutes:

``` html
<meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="300">
```

</div>

<div class="example">

A sequence of pages could be used as an automated slide show by making
each page refresh to the next page in the sequence, using markup such as
the following:

``` html
<meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="20; URL=page4.html">
```

</div>

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie" class="dfn">Set-Cookie
state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`set-cookie`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-set-cookie)`"`)

This pragma is non-conforming and has no effect.

User agents are required to ignore this pragma.

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-x-ua-compatible"
class="dfn">X-UA-Compatible state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`x-ua-compatible`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-x-ua-compatible)`"`)

In practice, this pragma encourages Internet Explorer to more closely
follow the specifications.

For [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements with an
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-x-ua-compatible"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-x-ua-compatible-2">X-UA-Compatible
state</a>, the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute must have a
value that is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="pragma-directives:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`IE=edge`".

User agents are required to ignore this pragma.

<span id="attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy" class="dfn"
export="">Content security policy state</span>
(`http-equiv="`[`content-security-policy`](#attr-meta-http-equiv-keyword-content-security-policy)`"`)

This pragma <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced"
id="pragma-directives:enforce-the-policy-2"
data-x-internal="enforce-the-policy">enforces</a> a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-2"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy">Content Security Policy</a> on
a [`Document`](#document). [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

1.  If the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element is not a child of a
    [`head`](#the-head-element) element, return.

2.  If the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element has no
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's
    value is the empty string, then return.

3.  Let `policy` be the result of executing Content Security Policy's
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#parse-serialized-policy"
    id="pragma-directives:parse-a-serialized-content-security-policy"
    data-x-internal="parse-a-serialized-content-security-policy">parse a
    serialized Content Security Policy</a> algorithm on the
    [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element's
    [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute's value, with a source of
    "meta", and a disposition of "enforce".

4.  Remove all occurrences of the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-uri"
    data-x-internal="report-uri-directive"><code
    id="pragma-directives:report-uri-directive">report-uri</code></a>,
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors"
    data-x-internal="frame-ancestors-directive"><code
    id="pragma-directives:frame-ancestors-directive">frame-ancestors</code></a>,
    and <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#sandbox"
    data-x-internal="sandbox-directive"><code
    id="pragma-directives:sandbox-directive">sandbox</code></a>
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directives"
    id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-directive"
    data-x-internal="content-security-policy-directive">directives</a>
    from `policy`.

5.  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced"
    id="pragma-directives:enforce-the-policy-3"
    data-x-internal="enforce-the-policy">Enforce the policy</a>
    `policy`.

For [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements with an
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy-2">Content
security policy state</a>, the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute
must have a value consisting of a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#grammardef-serialized-policy"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-syntax"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy-syntax">valid Content Security
Policy</a>, but must not contain any
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-uri"
data-x-internal="report-uri-directive"><code
id="pragma-directives:report-uri-directive-2">report-uri</code></a>,
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors"
data-x-internal="frame-ancestors-directive"><code
id="pragma-directives:frame-ancestors-directive-2">frame-ancestors</code></a>,
or <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#sandbox"
data-x-internal="sandbox-directive"><code
id="pragma-directives:sandbox-directive-2">sandbox</code></a>
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directives"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-directive-2"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy-directive">directives</a>. The
<a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-3"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy">Content Security Policy</a>
given in the [`content`](#attr-meta-content) attribute will be
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced"
id="pragma-directives:enforce-the-policy-4"
data-x-internal="enforce-the-policy">enforced</a> upon the current
document. [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

At the time of inserting the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element to the
document, it is possible that some resources have already been fetched.
For example, images might be stored in the
<a href="#list-of-available-images"
id="pragma-directives:list-of-available-images">list of available
images</a> prior to dynamically inserting a [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
element with an [`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy"
id="pragma-directives:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy-3">Content
security policy state</a>. Resources that have already been fetched are
not guaranteed to be blocked by a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object"
id="pragma-directives:content-security-policy-4"
data-x-internal="content-security-policy">Content Security Policy</a>
that's <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced"
id="pragma-directives:enforce-the-policy-5"
data-x-internal="enforce-the-policy">enforced</a> late.

<div class="example">

A page might choose to mitigate the risk of cross-site scripting attacks
by preventing the execution of inline JavaScript, as well as blocking
all plugin content, using a policy such as the following:

``` html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'">
```

</div>

</div>

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with
any particular state in the document at a time.

##### <span class="secno">4.2.5.4</span> Specifying the document's character encoding<a href="#charset" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="character-encoding-declaration" class="dfn">character
encoding declaration</span> is a mechanism by which the
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding"
id="charset:encoding" data-x-internal="encoding">character encoding</a>
used to store or transmit a document is specified.

The Encoding standard requires use of the
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8" id="charset:utf-8"
data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a>
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding"
id="charset:encoding-2" data-x-internal="encoding">character
encoding</a> and requires use of the "`utf-8`"
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#label"
id="charset:encoding-label" data-x-internal="encoding-label">encoding
label</a> to identify it. Those requirements necessitate that the
document's <a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="charset:character-encoding-declaration">character encoding
declaration</a>, if it exists, specifies an
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#label"
id="charset:encoding-label-2" data-x-internal="encoding-label">encoding
label</a> using an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="charset:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for "`utf-8`". Regardless of whether a
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="charset:character-encoding-declaration-2">character encoding
declaration</a> is present or not, the actual
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
id="charset:document&#39;s-character-encoding"
data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">character
encoding</a> used to encode the document must be
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8" id="charset:utf-8-2"
data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a>. [\[ENCODING\]](#refsENCODING)

To enforce the above rules, authoring tools must default to using
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8" id="charset:utf-8-3"
data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a> for newly-created documents.

The following restrictions also apply:

- The character encoding declaration must be serialized without the use
  of <a href="#syntax-charref" id="charset:syntax-charref">character
  references</a> or character escapes of any kind.
- <span id="charset1024"><span id="charset512">The element containing
  the character encoding declaration must be serialized completely
  within the first 1024 bytes of the document.</span></span>

In addition, due to a number of restrictions on
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements, there can only be one
[`meta`](#the-meta-element)-based character encoding declaration per
document.

<div algorithm="">

If an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="charset:html-documents" data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML
document</a> does not start with a BOM, and its
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding"
id="charset:encoding-3" data-x-internal="encoding">encoding</a> is not
explicitly given by
<a href="#content-type" id="charset:content-type">Content-Type
metadata</a>, and the document is not
<a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
id="charset:an-iframe-srcdoc-document">an <code>iframe</code>
<code>srcdoc</code> document</a>, then the encoding must be specified
using a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with a
[`charset`](#attr-meta-charset) attribute or a
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with an
[`http-equiv`](#attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type"
id="charset:attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type">Encoding declaration
state</a>.

</div>

<div class="note">

A character encoding declaration is required (either in the
<a href="#content-type" id="charset:content-type-2">Content-Type
metadata</a> or explicitly in the file) even when all characters are in
the ASCII range, because a character encoding is needed to process
non-ASCII characters entered by the user in forms, in URLs generated by
scripts, and so forth.

Using non-UTF-8 encodings can have unexpected results on form submission
and URL encodings, which use the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
id="charset:document&#39;s-character-encoding-2"
data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">document's character
encoding</a> by default.

</div>

If the document is <a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
id="charset:an-iframe-srcdoc-document-2">an <code>iframe</code>
<code>srcdoc</code> document</a>, the document must not have a
<a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="charset:character-encoding-declaration-3">character encoding
declaration</a>. (In this case, the source is already decoded, since it
is part of the document that contained the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element).)

In XML, the XML declaration should be used for inline character encoding
information, if necessary.

<div class="example">

In HTML, to declare that the character encoding is
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8" id="charset:utf-8-4"
data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a>, the author could include the
following markup near the top of the document (in the
[`head`](#the-head-element) element):

``` html
<meta charset="utf-8">
```

In XML, the XML declaration would be used instead, at the very top of
the markup:

``` html
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
```

</div>

element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-style-element:metadata-content-2-2">metadata content</a> is
expected.

[`head`](#the-head-element) element.

id="the-style-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:

that gives a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#conform-classes"

data-x-internal="conformant-style-sheet">conformant style sheet</a>.

id="the-style-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

id="the-style-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-style-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`blocking`](#attr-style-blocking) — Whether the element is
<a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
id="the-style-element:potentially-render-blocking">potentially
render-blocking</a>

Also, the [`title`](#attr-style-title) attribute
<a href="#attr-style-title"
id="the-style-element:attr-style-title-2">has special semantics</a> on
this element:
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name"
id="the-style-element:css-style-sheet-set-name"
data-x-internal="css-style-sheet-set-name">CSS style sheet set name</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-style-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-style).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-style).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-style-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLStyleElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList blocking;

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLStyleElement includes LinkStyle;
```

The [`style`](#the-style-element) element allows authors to embed CSS
style sheets in their documents. The [`style`](#the-style-element)
element is one of several inputs to the styling processing model. The
element does not
<a href="#represents" id="the-style-element:represents">represent</a>
content for the user.
