<span class="firefox yes">Firefox4+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari5+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome5+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera11.1+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer9+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android11.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-footer-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-footer-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-footer-element:flow-content-2-2">flow
content</a> is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-footer-element:flow-content-2-3">Flow
content</a>, but with no [`header`](#the-header-element) or
[`footer`](#the-footer-element) element descendants.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-footer-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
If there is an ancestor <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-footer-element:sectioning-content-2">sectioning content</a>
element: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-footer); [for
implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-footer).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-footer);
[for
implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-footer-ancestorbody).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-footer-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`footer`](#the-footer-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-footer-element:represents">represents</a>
a footer for its nearest ancestor <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-footer-element:sectioning-content-2-2">sectioning content</a>
element, or for <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="the-footer-element:the-body-element-2">the body element</a> if there
is no such ancestor. A footer typically contains information about its
section such as who wrote it, links to related documents, copyright
data, and the like.

When the [`footer`](#the-footer-element) element contains entire
sections, they
<a href="#represents" id="the-footer-element:represents-2">represent</a>
appendices, indices, long colophons, verbose license agreements, and
other such content.

Contact information for the author or editor of a section belongs in an
[`address`](#the-address-element) element, possibly itself inside a
[`footer`](#the-footer-element). Bylines and other information that
could be suitable for both a [`header`](#the-header-element) or a
[`footer`](#the-footer-element) can be placed in either (or neither).
The primary purpose of these elements is merely to help the author write
self-explanatory markup that is easy to maintain and style; they are not
intended to impose specific structures on authors.

Footers don't necessarily have to appear at the *end* of a section,
though they usually do.

When there is no ancestor <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-footer-element:sectioning-content-2-3">sectioning content</a>
element, then it applies to the whole page.

The [`footer`](#the-footer-element) element is not itself
<a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-footer-element:sectioning-content-2-4">sectioning content</a>;
it doesn't introduce a new section.

<div class="example">

Here is a page with two footers, one at the top and one at the bottom,
with the same content:

``` html
<body>
 <footer><a href="../">Back to index...</a></footer>
 <hgroup>
  <h1>Lorem ipsum</h1>
  <p>The ipsum of all lorems</p>
 </hgroup>
 <p>A dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod
 tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
 veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex
 ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in
 voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla
 pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in
 culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.</p>
 <footer><a href="../">Back to index...</a></footer>
</body>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Here is an example which shows the [`footer`](#the-footer-element)
element being used both for a site-wide footer and for a section footer.

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<HTML LANG="en"><HEAD>
<TITLE>The Ramblings of a Scientist</TITLE>
<BODY>
<H1>The Ramblings of a Scientist</H1>
<ARTICLE>
 <H1>Episode 15</H1>
 <VIDEO SRC="/fm/015.ogv" CONTROLS PRELOAD>
  <P><A HREF="/fm/015.ogv">Download video</A>.</P>
 </VIDEO>
 <FOOTER> <!-- footer for article -->
  <P>Published <TIME DATETIME="2009-10-21T18:26-07:00">on 2009/10/21 at 6:26pm</TIME></P>
 </FOOTER>
</ARTICLE>
<ARTICLE>
 <H1>My Favorite Trains</H1>
 <P>I love my trains. My favorite train of all time is a Köf.</P>
 <P>It is fun to see them pull some coal cars because they look so
 dwarfed in comparison.</P>
 <FOOTER> <!-- footer for article -->
  <P>Published <TIME DATETIME="2009-09-15T14:54-07:00">on 2009/09/15 at 2:54pm</TIME></P>
 </FOOTER>
</ARTICLE>
<FOOTER> <!-- site wide footer -->
 <NAV>
  <P><A HREF="/credits.html">Credits</A> —
     <A HREF="/tos.html">Terms of Service</A> —
     <A HREF="/index.html">Blog Index</A></P>
 </NAV>
 <P>Copyright © 2009 Gordon Freeman</P>
</FOOTER>
</BODY>
</HTML>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Some site designs have what is sometimes referred to as "fat footers" —
footers that contain a lot of material, including images, links to other
articles, links to pages for sending feedback, special offers... in some
ways, a whole "front page" in the footer.

This fragment shows the bottom of a page on a site with a "fat footer":

``` html
...
 <footer>
  <nav>
   <section>
    <h1>Articles</h1>
    <p><img src="images/somersaults.jpeg" alt=""> Go to the gym with
    our somersaults class! Our teacher Jim takes you through the paces
    in this two-part article. <a href="articles/somersaults/1">Part
    1</a> · <a href="articles/somersaults/2">Part 2</a></p>
    <p><img src="images/kindplus.jpeg"> Tired of walking on the edge of
    a clif<!-- sic -->? Our guest writer Lara shows you how to bumble
    your way through the bars. <a href="articles/kindplus/1">Read
    more...</a></p>
    <p><img src="images/crisps.jpeg"> The chips are down, now all
    that's left is a potato. What can you do with it? <a
    href="articles/crisps/1">Read more...</a></p>
   </section>
   <ul>
    <li> <a href="/about">About us...</a>
    <li> <a href="/feedback">Send feedback!</a>
    <li> <a href="/sitemap">Sitemap</a>
   </ul>
  </nav>
  <p><small>Copyright © 2015 The Snacker —
  <a href="/tos">Terms of Service</a></small></p>
 </footer>
</body>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.3.10</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`address`</span> element<a href="#the-address-element" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/address](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/address "The <address> HTML element indicates that the enclosed HTML provides contact information for a person or people, or for an organization.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-address-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-address-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-address-element:flow-content-2-2">flow
content</a> is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-address-element:flow-content-2-3">Flow
content</a>, but with no <a href="#heading-content-2"
id="the-address-element:heading-content-2">heading content</a>
descendants, no <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-address-element:sectioning-content-2">sectioning content</a>
descendants, and no [`header`](#the-header-element),
[`footer`](#the-footer-element), or [`address`](#the-address-element)
element descendants.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-address-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-address).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-address).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-address-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`address`](#the-address-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-address-element:represents">represents</a>
the contact information for its nearest
[`article`](#the-article-element) or [`body`](#the-body-element) element
ancestor. If that is <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="the-address-element:the-body-element-2">the body element</a>, then
the contact information applies to the document as a whole.

<div class="example">

For example, a page at the W3C web site related to HTML might include
the following contact information:

``` html
<ADDRESS>
 <A href="../People/Raggett/">Dave Raggett</A>,
 <A href="../People/Arnaud/">Arnaud Le Hors</A>,
 contact persons for the <A href="Activity">W3C HTML Activity</A>
</ADDRESS>
```

</div>

The [`address`](#the-address-element) element must not be used to
represent arbitrary addresses (e.g. postal addresses), unless those
addresses are in fact the relevant contact information. (The
[`p`](#the-p-element) element is the appropriate element for marking up
postal addresses in general.)

The [`address`](#the-address-element) element must not contain
information other than contact information.

<div class="example">

For example, the following is non-conforming use of the
[`address`](#the-address-element) element:

``` bad
<ADDRESS>Last Modified: 1999/12/24 23:37:50</ADDRESS>
```

</div>

Typically, the [`address`](#the-address-element) element would be
included along with other information in a
[`footer`](#the-footer-element) element.

<div algorithm="">

The contact information for a node `node` is a collection of
[`address`](#the-address-element) elements defined by the first
applicable entry from the following list:

If `node` is an [`article`](#the-article-element) element  
If `node` is a [`body`](#the-body-element) element  
The contact information consists of all the
[`address`](#the-address-element) elements that have `node` as an
ancestor and do not have another [`body`](#the-body-element) or
[`article`](#the-article-element) element ancestor that is a descendant
of `node`.

If `node` has an ancestor element that is an [`article`](#the-article-element) element  
If `node` has an ancestor element that is a [`body`](#the-body-element) element  
The contact information of `node` is the same as the contact information
of the nearest [`article`](#the-article-element) or
[`body`](#the-body-element) element ancestor, whichever is nearest.

If `node`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-address-element:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> has <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="the-address-element:the-body-element-2-2">a body element</a>  
The contact information of `node` is the same as the contact information
of <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="the-address-element:the-body-element-2-3">the body element</a> of
the [`Document`](#document).

Otherwise  
There is no contact information for `node`.

</div>

User agents may expose the contact information of a node to the user, or
use it for other purposes, such as indexing sections based on the
sections' contact information.

<div class="example">

In this example the footer contains contact information and a copyright
notice.

``` html
<footer>
 <address>
  For more details, contact
  <a href="mailto:js@example.com">John Smith</a>.
 </address>
 <p><small>© copyright 2038 Example Corp.</small></p>
</footer>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.3.11</span> <span id="headings-and-outlines"></span><span id="outlines"></span>Headings and outlines<a href="#headings-and-outlines-2" class="self-link"></a>

[`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)
elements have a <span id="heading-level" class="dfn">heading
level</span>, which is given by
<a href="#get-an-element&#39;s-computed-heading-level"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:get-an-element&#39;s-computed-heading-level">getting
the element's computed heading level</a>.

These elements <a href="#represents"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:represents">represent</a>
<span id="concept-heading" class="dfn">headings</span>. The lower a
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading">heading</a>'s
<a href="#heading-level"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:heading-level">heading level</a> is, the
fewer ancestor sections the <a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-2">heading</a> has.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="outline" class="dfn">outline</span> is all
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-3">headings</a> in a
document, in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:tree-order"
data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>.

</div>

The <a href="#outline" id="headings-and-outlines-2:outline">outline</a>
should be used for generating document outlines, for example when
generating tables of contents. When creating an interactive table of
contents, entries should jump the user to the relevant
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-4">heading</a>.

If a document has one or more <a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-5">headings</a>, at least a
single <a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-6">heading</a> within the
<a href="#outline" id="headings-and-outlines-2:outline-2">outline</a>
should have a <a href="#heading-level"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:heading-level-2">heading level</a> of 1.

<div algorithm="">

Each <a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-7">heading</a> following
another <a href="#concept-heading"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:concept-heading-8">heading</a> `lead` in the
<a href="#outline" id="headings-and-outlines-2:outline-3">outline</a>
must have a <a href="#heading-level"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:heading-level-3">heading level</a> that is
less than, equal to, or 1 greater than `lead`'s <a href="#heading-level"
id="headings-and-outlines-2:heading-level-4">heading level</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following example is non-conforming:

``` bad
<body>
 <h1>Apples</h1>
 <p>Apples are fruit.</p>
 <section>
  <h3>Taste</h3>
  <p>They taste lovely.</p>
 </section>
</body>
```

It could be written as follows and then it would be conforming:

``` html
<body>
 <h1>Apples</h1>
 <p>Apples are fruit.</p>
 <section>
  <h2>Taste</h2>
  <p>They taste lovely.</p>
 </section>
</body>
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.3.11.1</span> Heading levels & offsets<a href="#heading-levels-&amp;-offsets" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="attr-headingoffset" class="dfn" dfn-for="global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`headingoffset`</span> content attribute allows
authors to offset heading levels for descendants.

If the [`headingoffset`](#attr-headingoffset) attribute is specified, it
must have a value that is a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:valid-non-negative-integer">valid
non-negative integer</a> between 0 and 8, inclusive.

The <span id="attr-headingreset" class="dfn" dfn-for="global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`headingreset`</span> content attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:boolean-attribute">boolean
attribute</a>. It allows authors to prevent a heading offset computation
from traversing beyond the element with the attribute.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="get-an-element's-computed-heading-level" class="dfn">get an
element's computed heading level</span>, given an element `element`:

1.  Let `level` be 0.

2.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 1.

3.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h2`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 2.

4.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h3`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 3.

5.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h4`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 4.

6.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h5`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 5.

7.  If `element`'s local name is
    [`h6`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), then set `level`
    to 6.

8.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:assert"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `level` is not 0.

9.  Increment `level` by the result of
    <a href="#get-an-element&#39;s-computed-heading-offset"
    id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:get-an-element&#39;s-computed-heading-offset">getting
    an element's computed heading offset</a> given `element`.

10. If `level` is greater than 9, then return 9.

11. Return `level`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="get-an-element's-computed-heading-offset" class="dfn">get
an element's computed heading offset</span>, given an element `element`,
perform the following steps. They return a non-negative integer.

1.  Let `offset` be 0.

2.  Let `inclusiveAncestor` be `element`.

3.  While `inclusiveAncestor` is not null:

    1.  Let `nextOffset` be 0.

    2.  If `inclusiveAncestor` is an <a href="#html-elements"
        id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:html-elements">HTML element</a>
        and has a [`headingoffset`](#attr-headingoffset) attribute, then
        parse its value using the
        <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
        id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
        for parsing non-negative integers</a>.

        If the result of parsing the value is not an error, then set
        `nextOffset` to that value.

    3.  Increment `offset` by `nextOffset`.

    4.  If `inclusiveAncestor` is an <a href="#html-elements"
        id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:html-elements-2">HTML element</a>
        and has a [`headingreset`](#attr-headingreset) attribute, then
        return `offset`.

    5.  Set `inclusiveAncestor` to the parent node of
        `inclusiveAncestor` within the
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
        id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:flat-tree"
        data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat tree</a>.

4.  Return `offset`.

</div>

<div class="example">

This example shows a combination of
[`headingoffset`](#attr-headingoffset),
[`headingreset`](#attr-headingreset), and
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-level"
data-x-internal="attr-aria-level"><code
id="heading-levels-&amp;-offsets:attr-aria-level">aria-level</code></a>
attributes with comments demonstrating the respective heading levels.
This example illustrates the various combinations and is not a best
practice example.

``` html
<body>
  <main>
   <h1>This is a heading level 1</h1>
   <article headingoffset="1">
    <h1>This is a heading level 2</h1>
    <section headingoffset="1">
     <h1>This is a heading level 3</h1>
     <dialog headingreset>
      <h1>This is a heading level 1</h1>
     </dialog>
    </section>
   </article>
   <h1 aria-level="2">This is a heading level 2</h1>
  </main>
</body>
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.3.11.2</span> Sample outlines<a href="#sample-outlines" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="example">

The following markup fragment:

``` html
<body>
  <hgroup id="document-title">
    <h1>HTML: Living Standard</h1>
    <p>Last Updated 12 August 2016</p>
  </hgroup>
  <p>Some intro to the document.</p>
  <h2>Table of contents</h2>
  <ol id=toc>...</ol>
  <h2>First section</h2>
  <p>Some intro to the first section.</p>
</body>
```

...results in 3 document headings:

1.  `<h1>HTML: Living Standard</h1>`

2.  `<h2>Table of contents</h2>`.

3.  `<h2>First section</h2>`.

A rendered view of the
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline">outline</a> might look
like:

<img src="/images/outline.svg" class="darkmode-aware" width="465"
height="120"
alt="Top-level section with the heading &quot;HTML: Living Standard&quot; and two subsections; &quot;Table of contents&quot; and &quot;First section&quot;." />

</div>

<div class="example">

First, here is a document, which is a book with very short chapters and
subsections:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang=en>
<title>The Tax Book (all in one page)</title>
<h1>The Tax Book</h1>
<h2>Earning money</h2>
<p>Earning money is good.</p>
<h3>Getting a job</h3>
<p>To earn money you typically need a job.</p>
<h2>Spending money</h2>
<p>Spending is what money is mainly used for.</p>
<h3>Cheap things</h3>
<p>Buying cheap things often not cost-effective.</p>
<h3>Expensive things</h3>
<p>The most expensive thing is often not the most cost-effective either.</p>
<h2>Investing money</h2>
<p>You can lend your money to other people.</p>
<h2>Losing money</h2>
<p>If you spend money or invest money, sooner or later you will lose money.
<h3>Poor judgement</h3>
<p>Usually if you lose money it's because you made a mistake.</p>
```

Its <a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-2">outline</a> could
be presented as follows:

1.  The Tax Book
    1.  Earning money
        1.  Getting a job
    2.  Spending money
        1.  Cheap things
        2.  Expensive things
    3.  Investing money
    4.  Losing money
        1.  Poor judgement

Notice that the [`title`](#the-title-element) element is not a
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="sample-outlines:concept-heading">heading</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

A document can contain multiple top-level headings:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang=en>
<title>Alphabetic Fruit</title>
<h1>Apples</h1>
<p>Pomaceous.</p>
<h1>Bananas</h1>
<p>Edible.</p>
<h1>Carambola</h1>
<p>Star.</p>
```

The document's
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-3">outline</a> could be
presented as follows:

1.  Apples
2.  Bananas
3.  Carambola

</div>

<div class="example">

[`header`](#the-header-element) elements do not influence the
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-4">outline</a> of a
document:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
<title>We're adopting a child! — Ray's blog</title>
<h1>Ray's blog</h1>
<article>
 <header>
  <nav>
   <a href="?t=-1d">Yesterday</a>;
   <a href="?t=-7d">Last week</a>;
   <a href="?t=-1m">Last month</a>
  </nav>
  <h2>We're adopting a child!</h2>
 </header>
 <p>As of today, Janine and I have signed the papers to become
 the proud parents of baby Diane! We've been looking forward to
 this day for weeks.</p>
</article>
</html>
```

The document's
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-5">outline</a> could be
presented as follows:

1.  Ray's blog
    1.  We're adopting a child!

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div class="example">

The following example is conforming, but not encouraged as it has no
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="sample-outlines:concept-heading-2">heading</a> whose
<a href="#heading-level" id="sample-outlines:heading-level">heading
level</a> is 1:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang=en>
<title>Alphabetic Fruit</title>
<section>
 <h2>Apples</h2>
 <p>Pomaceous.</p>
</section>
<section>
 <h2>Bananas</h2>
 <p>Edible.</p>
</section>
<section>
 <h2>Carambola</h2>
 <p>Star.</p>
</section>
```

The document's
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-6">outline</a> could be
presented as follows:

1.  1.  Apples
    2.  Bananas
    3.  Carambola

</div>

<div class="example">

The following example is conforming, but not encouraged as the first
<a href="#concept-heading"
id="sample-outlines:concept-heading-3">heading</a>'s
<a href="#heading-level" id="sample-outlines:heading-level-2">heading
level</a> is not 1:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang=en>
<title>Feathers on The Site of Encyclopedic Knowledge</title>
 <h2>A plea from our caretakers</h2>
 <p>Please, we beg of you, send help! We're stuck in the server room!</p>
<h1>Feathers</h1>
<p>Epidermal growths.</p>
```

The document's
<a href="#outline" id="sample-outlines:outline-7">outline</a> could be
presented as follows:

1.  1.  A plea from our caretakers
2.  Feathers

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.3.11.3</span> Exposing outlines to users<a href="#exposing-outlines-to-users" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are encouraged to expose page
<a href="#outline" id="exposing-outlines-to-users:outline">outlines</a>
to users to aid in navigation. This is especially true for non-visual
media, e.g. screen readers.

<div class="example">

For instance, a user agent could map the arrow keys as follows:

<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Shift</span> + <span class="kbd">← Left</span></span>  
Go to previous heading

<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Shift</span> + <span class="kbd">→ Right</span></span>  
Go to next heading

<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Shift</span> + <span class="kbd">↑ Up</span></span>  
Go to next heading whose <a href="#heading-level"
id="exposing-outlines-to-users:heading-level">level</a> is one less than
the current heading's level

<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Shift</span> + <span class="kbd">↓ Down</span></span>  
Go to next heading whose <a href="#heading-level"
id="exposing-outlines-to-users:heading-level-2">level</a> is the same as
the current heading's level

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.3.12</span> Usage summary<a href="#usage-summary-2" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<table class="vertical-summary-table">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th rowspan="2">Element</th>
<th>Purpose</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-body-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-body-element">body</code></a></td>
<td>The contents of the document.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;!DOCTYPE HTML&gt;
&lt;html lang=&quot;en&quot;&gt;
 &lt;head&gt; &lt;title&gt;Steve Hill&#39;s Home Page&lt;/title&gt; &lt;/head&gt;
 &lt;body&gt; &lt;p&gt;Hard Trance is My Life.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/body&gt;
&lt;/html&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-article-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-article-element">article</code></a></td>
<td>A complete, or self-contained, composition in a document, page,
application, or site and that is, in principle, independently
distributable or reusable, e.g. in syndication. This could be a forum
post, a magazine or newspaper article, a blog entry, a user-submitted
comment, an interactive widget or gadget, or any other independent item
of content.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;article&gt;
 &lt;img src=&quot;/tumblr_masqy2s5yn1rzfqbpo1_500.jpg&quot; alt=&quot;Yellow smiley face with the caption &#39;masif&#39;&quot;&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;My fave Masif tee so far!&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;footer&gt;Posted 2 days ago&lt;/footer&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;
&lt;article&gt;
 &lt;img src=&quot;/tumblr_m9tf6wSr6W1rzfqbpo1_500.jpg&quot; alt=&quot;&quot;&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;Happy 2nd birthday Masif Saturdays!!!&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;footer&gt;Posted 3 weeks ago&lt;/footer&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-section-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-section-element">section</code></a></td>
<td>A generic section of a document or application. A section, in this
context, is a thematic grouping of content, typically with a
heading.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;h1&gt;Biography&lt;/h1&gt;
&lt;section&gt;
 &lt;h1&gt;The facts&lt;/h1&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;1500+ shows, 14+ countries&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;
&lt;section&gt;
 &lt;h1&gt;2010/2011 figures per year&lt;/h1&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;100+ shows, 8+ countries&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-nav-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-nav-element">nav</code></a></td>
<td>A section of a page that links to other pages or to parts within the
page: a section with navigation links.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;nav&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&quot;/&quot;&gt;Home&lt;/a&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&quot;/biog.html&quot;&gt;Bio&lt;/a&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&quot;/discog.html&quot;&gt;Discog&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;/nav&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-aside-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-aside-element">aside</code></a></td>
<td>A section of a page that consists of content that is tangentially
related to the content around the <a href="#the-aside-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-aside-element-2">aside</code></a> element, and
which could be considered separate from that content. Such sections are
often represented as sidebars in printed typography.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;h1&gt;Music&lt;/h1&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As any burner can tell you, the event has a lot of trance.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;aside&gt;You can buy the music we played at our &lt;a href=&quot;buy.html&quot;&gt;playlist page&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/aside&gt;
&lt;p&gt;This year we played a kind of trance that originated in Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands in the mid-90s.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements">h1</code></a>–<a
href="#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements-2">h6</code></a></td>
<td>A heading</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;h1&gt;The Guide To Music On The Playa&lt;/h1&gt;
&lt;h2&gt;The Main Stage&lt;/h2&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If you want to play on a stage, you should bring one.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h2&gt;Amplified Music&lt;/h2&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Amplifiers up to 300W or 90dB are welcome.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-hgroup-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-hgroup-element">hgroup</code></a></td>
<td>A heading and related content. The element may be used to group an
<a href="#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements-3">h1</code></a>–<a
href="#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements-4">h6</code></a>
element with one or more <a href="#the-p-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-p-element">p</code></a> elements containing
content representing a subheading, alternative title, or tagline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;hgroup&gt;
 &lt;h1&gt;Burning Music&lt;/h1&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;The Guide To Music On The Playa&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/hgroup&gt;
&lt;section&gt;
 &lt;hgroup&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;Main Stage&lt;/h1&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;The Fiction Of A Music Festival&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;/hgroup&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;If you want to play on a stage, you should bring one.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;
&lt;section&gt;
 &lt;hgroup&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;Loudness!&lt;/h1&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Questions About Amplified Music&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;/hgroup&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;Amplifiers up to 300W or 90dB are welcome.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-header-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-header-element">header</code></a></td>
<td>A group of introductory or navigational aids.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;article&gt;
 &lt;header&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;Hard Trance is My Life&lt;/h1&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;By DJ Steve Hill and Technikal&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;/header&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;The album with the amusing punctuation has red artwork.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"><a href="#the-footer-element"><code
id="usage-summary-2:the-footer-element">footer</code></a></td>
<td>A footer for its nearest ancestor <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="usage-summary-2:sectioning-content-2">sectioning content</a>
element, or for <a href="#the-body-element-2"
id="usage-summary-2:the-body-element-2">the body element</a> if there is
no such ancestor. A footer typically contains information about its
section such as who wrote it, links to related documents, copyright
data, and the like.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><pre class="example"><code>&lt;article&gt;
 &lt;h1&gt;Hard Trance is My Life&lt;/h1&gt;
 &lt;p&gt;The album with the amusing punctuation has red artwork.&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;footer&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Artists: DJ Steve Hill and Technikal&lt;/p&gt;
 &lt;/footer&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;</code></pre></td>
</tr>
</tbody>

##### <span class="secno">4.3.12.1</span> Article or section?<a href="#article-or-section" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

A [`section`](#the-section-element) forms part of something else. An
[`article`](#the-article-element) is its own thing. But how does one
know which is which? Mostly the real answer is "it depends on author
intent".

For example, one could imagine a book with a "Granny Smith" chapter that
just said "These juicy, green apples make a great filling for apple
pies."; that would be a [`section`](#the-section-element) because
there'd be lots of other chapters on (maybe) other kinds of apples.

On the other hand, one could imagine a tweet or reddit comment or tumblr
post or newspaper classified ad that just said "Granny Smith. These
juicy, green apples make a great filling for apple pies."; it would then
be [`article`](#the-article-element)s because that was the whole thing.

A comment on an article is not part of the
[`article`](#the-article-element) on which it is commenting, therefore
it is its own [`article`](#the-article-element).

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-p-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-p).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-p).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-p-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLParagraphElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`p`](#the-p-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-p-element:represents">represents</a> a
<a href="#paragraph" id="the-p-element:paragraph">paragraph</a>.

While paragraphs are usually represented in visual media by blocks of
text that are physically separated from adjacent blocks through blank
lines, a style sheet or user agent would be equally justified in
presenting paragraph breaks in a different manner, for instance using
inline pilcrows (¶).

<div class="example">

The following examples are conforming HTML fragments:

``` html
<p>The little kitten gently seated herself on a piece of
carpet. Later in her life, this would be referred to as the time the
cat sat on the mat.</p>
```

``` html
<fieldset>
 <legend>Personal information</legend>
 <p>
   <label>Name: <input name="n"></label>
   <label><input name="anon" type="checkbox"> Hide from other users</label>
 </p>
 <p><label>Address: <textarea name="a"></textarea></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

``` html
<p>There was once an example from Femley,<br>
Whose markup was of dubious quality.<br>
The validator complained,<br>
So the author was pained,<br>
To move the error from the markup to the rhyming.</p>
```

</div>

The [`p`](#the-p-element) element should not be used when a more
specific element is more appropriate.

<div class="example">

The following example is technically correct:

``` html
<section>
 <!-- ... -->
 <p>Last modified: 2001-04-23</p>
 <p>Author: fred@example.com</p>
</section>
```

However, it would be better marked-up as:

``` html
<section>
 <!-- ... -->
 <footer>Last modified: 2001-04-23</footer>
 <address>Author: fred@example.com</address>
</section>
```

Or:

``` html
<section>
 <!-- ... -->
 <footer>
  <p>Last modified: 2001-04-23</p>
  <address>Author: fred@example.com</address>
 </footer>
</section>
```

</div>

<div class="note">

List elements (in particular, [`ol`](#the-ol-element) and
[`ul`](#the-ul-element) elements) cannot be children of
[`p`](#the-p-element) elements. When a sentence contains a bulleted
list, therefore, one might wonder how it should be marked up.

<div class="example">

For instance, this fantastic sentence has bullets relating to

- wizards,
- faster-than-light travel, and
- telepathy,

and is further discussed below.

</div>

The solution is to realize that a *[paragraph](#paragraph)*, in HTML
terms, is not a logical concept, but a structural one. In the fantastic
example above, there are actually *five*
<a href="#paragraph" id="the-p-element:paragraph-3">paragraphs</a> as
defined by this specification: one before the list, one for each bullet,
and one after the list.

<div class="example">

The markup for the above example could therefore be:

``` html
<p>For instance, this fantastic sentence has bullets relating to</p>
<ul>
 <li>wizards,
 <li>faster-than-light travel, and
 <li>telepathy,
</ul>
<p>and is further discussed below.</p>
```

</div>

Authors wishing to conveniently style such "logical" paragraphs
consisting of multiple "structural" paragraphs can use the
[`div`](#the-div-element) element instead of the [`p`](#the-p-element)
element.

<div class="example">

Thus for instance the above example could become the following:

``` html
<div>For instance, this fantastic sentence has bullets relating to
<ul>
 <li>wizards,
 <li>faster-than-light travel, and
 <li>telepathy,
</ul>
and is further discussed below.</div>
```

This example still has five structural paragraphs, but now the author
can style just the [`div`](#the-div-element) instead of having to
consider each part of the example separately.

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-hr-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLHRElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-hr-element:represents">represents</a> a
<a href="#paragraph" id="the-hr-element:paragraph">paragraph</a>-level
thematic break, e.g., a scene change in a story, or a transition to
another topic within a section of a reference book; alternatively, it
represents a separator between a set of options of a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element.

<div class="example">

The following fictional extract from a project manual shows two sections
that use the [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element to separate topics within
the section.

``` html
<section>
 <h1>Communication</h1>
 <p>There are various methods of communication. This section
 covers a few of the important ones used by the project.</p>
 <hr>
 <p>Communication stones seem to come in pairs and have mysterious
 properties:</p>
 <ul>
  <li>They can transfer thoughts in two directions once activated
  if used alone.</li>
  <li>If used with another device, they can transfer one's
  consciousness to another body.</li>
  <li>If both stones are used with another device, the
  consciousnesses switch bodies.</li>
 </ul>
 <hr>
 <p>Radios use the electromagnetic spectrum in the meter range and
 longer.</p>
 <hr>
 <p>Signal flares use the electromagnetic spectrum in the
 nanometer range.</p>
</section>
<section>
 <h1>Food</h1>
 <p>All food at the project is rationed:</p>
 <dl>
  <dt>Potatoes</dt>
  <dd>Two per day</dd>
  <dt>Soup</dt>
  <dd>One bowl per day</dd>
 </dl>
 <hr>
 <p>Cooking is done by the chefs on a set rotation.</p>
</section>
```

There is no need for an [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element between the
sections themselves, since the [`section`](#the-section-element)
elements and the [`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)
elements imply thematic changes themselves.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following extract from Pandora's Star by Peter F. Hamilton shows two
paragraphs that precede a scene change and the paragraph that follows
it. The scene change, represented in the printed book by a gap
containing a solitary centered star between the second and third
paragraphs, is here represented using the [`hr`](#the-hr-element)
element.

```
<p>Dudley was ninety-two, in his second life, and fast approaching
time for another rejuvenation. Despite his body having the physical
age of a standard fifty-year-old, the prospect of a long degrading
campaign within academia was one he regarded with dread. For a
supposedly advanced civilization, the Intersolar Commonwealth could be
appallingly backward at times, not to mention cruel.</p>
<p><i>Maybe it won't be that bad</i>, he told himself. The lie was
comforting enough to get him through the rest of the night's
shift.</p>
<hr>
<p>The Carlton AllLander drove Dudley home just after dawn. Like the
astronomer, the vehicle was old and worn, but perfectly capable of
doing its job. It had a cheap diesel engine, common enough on a
semi-frontier world like Gralmond, although its drive array was a
thoroughly modern photoneural processor. With its high suspension and
deep-tread tyres it could plough along the dirt track to the
observatory in all weather and seasons, including the metre-deep snow
of Gralmond's winters.</p>
```

</div>

The [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element does not affect the document's
<a href="#outline" id="the-hr-element:outline">outline</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-pre-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLPreElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`pre`](#the-pre-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-pre-element:represents">represents</a> a
block of preformatted text, in which structure is represented by
typographic conventions rather than by elements.

In <a href="#syntax" id="the-pre-element:syntax">the HTML syntax</a>, a
leading newline character immediately following the
[`pre`](#the-pre-element) element start tag is stripped.

Some examples of cases where the [`pre`](#the-pre-element) element could
be used:

- Including an email, with paragraphs indicated by blank lines, lists
  indicated by lines prefixed with a bullet, and so on.
- Including fragments of computer code, with structure indicated
  according to the conventions of that language.
- Displaying ASCII art.

Authors are encouraged to consider how preformatted text will be
experienced when the formatting is lost, as will be the case for users
of speech synthesizers, braille displays, and the like. For cases like
ASCII art, it is likely that an alternative presentation, such as a
textual description, would be more universally accessible to the readers
of the document.

To represent a block of computer code, the [`pre`](#the-pre-element)
element can be used with a [`code`](#the-code-element) element; to
represent a block of computer output the [`pre`](#the-pre-element)
element can be used with a [`samp`](#the-samp-element) element.
Similarly, the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element can be used within a
[`pre`](#the-pre-element) element to indicate text that the user is to
enter.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

<div class="example">

In the following snippet, a sample of computer code is presented.

``` html
<p>This is the <code>Panel</code> constructor:</p>
<pre><code>function Panel(element, canClose, closeHandler) {
  this.element = element;
  this.canClose = canClose;
  this.closeHandler = function () { if (closeHandler) closeHandler() };
}</code></pre>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following snippet, [`samp`](#the-samp-element) and
[`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) elements are mixed in the contents of a
[`pre`](#the-pre-element) element to show a session of Zork I.

``` html
<pre><samp>You are in an open field west of a big white house with a boarded
front door.
There is a small mailbox here.

></samp> <kbd>open mailbox</kbd>

<samp>Opening the mailbox reveals:
A leaflet.

></samp></pre>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The following shows a contemporary poem that uses the
[`pre`](#the-pre-element) element to preserve its unusual formatting,
which forms an intrinsic part of the poem itself.

``` html
<pre>                maxling

it is with a          heart
               heavy

that i admit loss of a feline
        so           loved

a friend lost to the
        unknown
                                (night)

~cdr 11dec07</pre>
```

</div>

A URL for the source of the quotation may be given using the cite attribute, while a text representation of the source can be given using the <cite> element.")

Android12.1+</span>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-blockquote-element:flow-content-2">Flow content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-blockquote-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-blockquote-element:flow-content-2-2">flow content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-blockquote-element:flow-content-2-3">Flow content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-blockquote-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`cite`](#attr-blockquote-cite) — Link to the source of the quotation or
more information about the edit

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-blockquote).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-blockquote).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-blockquote-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLQuoteElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString cite;
};
```

The [`HTMLQuoteElement`](#htmlquoteelement) interface is also used by
the [`q`](#the-q-element) element.

The [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) element
<a href="#represents"
id="the-blockquote-element:represents">represents</a> a section that is
quoted from another source.

Content inside a [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) must be quoted
from another source, whose address, if it has one, may be cited in the
<span id="attr-blockquote-cite" class="dfn" dfn-for="blockquote"
dfn-type="element-attr">`cite`</span> attribute.

If the [`cite`](#attr-blockquote-cite) attribute is present, it must be
a <a href="#valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="the-blockquote-element:valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>. To obtain the corresponding
citation link, the value of the attribute must be
<a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
id="the-blockquote-element:encoding-parsing-a-url">parsed</a> relative
to the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-blockquote-element:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>. User agents may allow
users to follow such citation links, but they are primarily intended for
private use (e.g., by server-side scripts collecting statistics about a
site's use of quotations), not for readers.

The content of a [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) may be
abbreviated or may have context added in the conventional manner for the
text's language.

<div class="example">

For example, in English this is traditionally done using square
brackets. Consider a page with the sentence "Jane ate the cracker. She
then said she liked apples and fish."; it could be quoted as follows:

``` html
<blockquote>
 <p>[Jane] then said she liked [...] fish.</p>
</blockquote>
```

</div>

Attribution for the quotation, if any, must be placed outside the
[`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) element.

<div class="example">

For example, here the attribution is given in a paragraph after the
quote:

``` html
<blockquote>
 <p>I contend that we are both atheists. I just believe in one fewer
 god than you do. When you understand why you dismiss all the other
 possible gods, you will understand why I dismiss yours.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>— Stephen Roberts</p>
```

The other examples below show other ways of showing attribution.

</div>

<div class="example">

Here a [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) element is used in
conjunction with a [`figure`](#the-figure-element) element and its
[`figcaption`](#the-figcaption-element) to clearly relate a quote to its
attribution (which is not part of the quote and therefore doesn't belong
inside the [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) itself):

``` html
<figure>
 <blockquote>
  <p>The truth may be puzzling. It may take some work to grapple with.
  It may be counterintuitive. It may contradict deeply held
  prejudices. It may not be consonant with what we desperately want to
  be true. But our preferences do not determine what's true. We have a
  method, and that method helps us to reach not absolute truth, only
  asymptotic approaches to the truth — never there, just closer
  and closer, always finding vast new oceans of undiscovered
  possibilities. Cleverly designed experiments are the key.</p>
 </blockquote>
 <figcaption>Carl Sagan, in "<cite>Wonder and Skepticism</cite>", from
 the <cite>Skeptical Inquirer</cite> Volume 19, Issue 1 (January-February
 1995)</figcaption>
</figure>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This next example shows the use of [`cite`](#the-cite-element) alongside
[`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element):

``` html
<p>His next piece was the aptly named <cite>Sonnet 130</cite>:</p>
<blockquote cite="https://quotes.example.org/s/sonnet130.html">
  <p>My mistress' eyes are nothing like the sun,<br>
  Coral is far more red, than her lips red,<br>
  ...
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This example shows how a forum post could use
[`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) to show what post a user is
replying to. The [`article`](#the-article-element) element is used for
each post, to mark up the threading.

``` html
<article>
 <h1><a href="https://bacon.example.com/?blog=109431">Bacon on a crowbar</a></h1>
 <article>
  <header><strong>t3yw</strong> 12 points 1 hour ago</header>
  <p>I bet a narwhal would love that.</p>
  <footer><a href="?pid=29578">permalink</a></footer>
  <article>
   <header><strong>greg</strong> 8 points 1 hour ago</header>
   <blockquote><p>I bet a narwhal would love that.</p></blockquote>
   <p>Dude narwhals don't eat bacon.</p>
   <footer><a href="?pid=29579">permalink</a></footer>
   <article>
    <header><strong>t3yw</strong> 15 points 1 hour ago</header>
    <blockquote>
     <blockquote><p>I bet a narwhal would love that.</p></blockquote>
     <p>Dude narwhals don't eat bacon.</p>
    </blockquote>
    <p>Next thing you'll be saying they don't get capes and wizard
    hats either!</p>
    <footer><a href="?pid=29580">permalink</a></footer>
    <article>
     <article>
      <header><strong>boing</strong> -5 points 1 hour ago</header>
      <p>narwhals are worse than ceiling cat</p>
      <footer><a href="?pid=29581">permalink</a></footer>
     </article>
    </article>
   </article>
  </article>
  <article>
   <header><strong>fred</strong> 1 points 23 minutes ago</header>
   <blockquote><p>I bet a narwhal would love that.</p></blockquote>
   <p>I bet they'd love to peel a banana too.</p>
   <footer><a href="?pid=29582">permalink</a></footer>
  </article>
 </article>
</article>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This example shows the use of a [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element)
for short snippets, demonstrating that one does not have to use
[`p`](#the-p-element) elements inside
[`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element) elements:

``` html
<p>He began his list of "lessons" with the following:</p>
<blockquote>One should never assume that his side of
the issue will be recognized, let alone that it will
be conceded to have merits.</blockquote>
<p>He continued with a number of similar points, ending with:</p>
<blockquote>Finally, one should be prepared for the threat
of breakdown in negotiations at any given moment and not
be cowed by the possibility.</blockquote>
<p>We shall now discuss these points...
```

</div>

[Examples of how to represent a conversation](#conversations) are shown
in a later section; it is not appropriate to use the
[`cite`](#the-cite-element) and [`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element)
elements for this purpose.

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-ol-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

If the element's children include at least one [`li`](#the-li-element)
element: <a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-ol-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-ol-element:flow-content-2-2">flow
content</a> is expected.

id="the-ol-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
Zero or more [`li`](#the-li-element) and
<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-ol-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-ol-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`reversed`](#attr-ol-reversed) — Number the list backwards

[`start`](#attr-ol-start) — <a href="#concept-ol-start"
id="the-ol-element:concept-ol-start">Starting value</a> of the list

[`type`](#attr-ol-type) — Kind of list marker

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-ol).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-ol).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-ol-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean reversed;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1] attribute long start;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`ol`](#the-ol-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-ol-element:represents">represents</a> a
list of items, where the items have been intentionally ordered, such
that changing the order would change the meaning of the document.

The items of the list are the [`li`](#the-li-element) element child
nodes of the [`ol`](#the-ol-element) element, in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-ol-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a>.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/ol#attr-reversed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/ol#attr-reversed "The <ol> HTML element represents an ordered list of items — typically rendered as a numbered list.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox18+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari6+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome18+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)≤79+</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-ol-reversed" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol"
dfn-type="element-attr">`reversed`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-ol-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>. If present,
it indicates that the list is a descending list (..., 3, 2, 1). If the
attribute is omitted, the list is an ascending list (1, 2, 3, ...).

The <span id="attr-ol-start" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol"
dfn-type="element-attr">`start`</span> attribute, if present, must be a
<a href="#valid-integer" id="the-ol-element:valid-integer">valid
integer</a>. It is used to determine the <a href="#concept-ol-start"
id="the-ol-element:concept-ol-start-2">starting value</a> of the list.

<div algorithm="">

An [`ol`](#the-ol-element) element has a <span id="concept-ol-start"
class="dfn">starting value</span>, which is an integer determined as
follows:

1.  If the [`ol`](#the-ol-element) element has a
    [`start`](#attr-ol-start) attribute, then:

    1.  Let `parsed` be the result of
        <a href="#rules-for-parsing-integers"
        id="the-ol-element:rules-for-parsing-integers">parsing the value of the
        attribute as an integer</a>.

    2.  If `parsed` is not an error, then return `parsed`.

2.  If the [`ol`](#the-ol-element) element has a
    [`reversed`](#attr-ol-reversed) attribute, then return the number of
    <a href="#list-owner" id="the-ol-element:list-owner">owned
    <code>li</code> elements</a>.

3.  Return 1.

</div>

The <span id="attr-ol-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute can be used to specify
the kind of marker to use in the list, in the cases where that matters
(e.g. because items are to be
<a href="#referenced" id="the-ol-element:referenced">referenced</a> by
their number/letter). The attribute, if specified, must have a value
that is <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
id="the-ol-element:identical-to"
data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> one of the characters
given in the first cell of one of the rows of the following table. The
[`type`](#attr-ol-type) attribute represents the state given in the cell
in the second column of the row whose first cell matches the attribute's
value; if none of the cells match, or if the attribute is omitted, then
the attribute represents the <a href="#attr-ol-type-state-decimal"
id="the-ol-element:attr-ol-type-state-decimal">decimal</a> state.

| Keyword | State | Description | Examples for values 1-3 and 3999-4001 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-ol-type-keyword-decimal" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`1`</span> (U+0031) | <span id="attr-ol-type-state-decimal" class="dfn">decimal</span> | Decimal numbers | `1.` | `2.` | `3.` | ... | `3999.` | `4000.` | `4001.` | ... |
| <span id="attr-ol-type-keyword-lower-alpha" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`a`</span> (U+0061) | <span id="attr-ol-type-state-lower-alpha" class="dfn">lower-alpha</span> | Lowercase latin alphabet | `a.` | `b.` | `c.` | ... | `ewu.` | `ewv.` | `eww.` | ... |
| <span id="attr-ol-type-keyword-upper-alpha" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`A`</span> (U+0041) | <span id="attr-ol-type-state-upper-alpha" class="dfn">upper-alpha</span> | Uppercase latin alphabet | `A.` | `B.` | `C.` | ... | `EWU.` | `EWV.` | `EWW.` | ... |
| <span id="attr-ol-type-keyword-lower-roman" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`i`</span> (U+0069) | <span id="attr-ol-type-state-lower-roman" class="dfn">lower-roman</span> | Lowercase roman numerals | `i.` | `ii.` | `iii.` | ... | `mmmcmxcix.` | `i̅v̅.` | `i̅v̅i.` | ... |
| <span id="attr-ol-type-keyword-upper-roman" class="dfn" dfn-for="ol/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`I`</span> (U+0049) | <span id="attr-ol-type-state-upper-roman" class="dfn">upper-roman</span> | Uppercase roman numerals | `I.` | `II.` | `III.` | ... | `MMMCMXCIX.` | `I̅V̅.` | `I̅V̅I.` | ... |

User agents should render the items of the list in a manner consistent
with the state of the [`type`](#attr-ol-type) attribute of the
[`ol`](#the-ol-element) element. Numbers less than or equal to zero
should always use the decimal system regardless of the
[`type`](#attr-ol-type) attribute.

For CSS user agents, a mapping for this attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists/#propdef-list-style-type"
id="the-ol-element:&#39;list-style-type&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;list-style-type&#39;">'list-style-type'</a> CSS
property is given [in the Rendering section](#decohints) (the mapping is
straightforward: the states above have the same names as their
corresponding CSS values).

It is possible to redefine the default CSS list styles used to implement
this attribute in CSS user agents; doing so will affect how list items
are rendered.

Due to <a href="#xattr-reflectdefault"
id="the-ol-element:xattr-reflectdefault-2">[ReflectDefault]</a> the
[`start`](#dom-ol-start) IDL attribute does not necessarily match the
list's <a href="#concept-ol-start"
id="the-ol-element:concept-ol-start-3">starting value</a>, in cases
where the [`start`](#attr-ol-start) content attribute is omitted and the
[`reversed`](#attr-ol-reversed) content attribute is specified.

<div class="example">

The following markup shows a list where the order matters, and where the
[`ol`](#the-ol-element) element is therefore appropriate. Compare this
list to the equivalent list in the [`ul`](#the-ul-element) section to
see an example of the same items using the [`ul`](#the-ul-element)
element.

``` html
<p>I have lived in the following countries (given in the order of when
I first lived there):</p>
<ol>
 <li>Switzerland
 <li>United Kingdom
 <li>United States
 <li>Norway
</ol>
```

Note how changing the order of the list changes the meaning of the
document. In the following example, changing the relative order of the
first two items has changed the birthplace of the author:

``` html
<p>I have lived in the following countries (given in the order of when
I first lived there):</p>
<ol>
 <li>United Kingdom
 <li>Switzerland
 <li>United States
 <li>Norway
</ol>
```

</div>

id="the-ul-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-ul-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

If the element's children include at least one [`li`](#the-li-element)
element: <a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-ul-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-ul-element:flow-content-2-2">flow
content</a> is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
Zero or more [`li`](#the-li-element) and
<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-ul-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-ul-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-ul).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-ul).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-ul-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLUListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`ul`](#the-ul-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-ul-element:represents">represents</a> a
list of items, where the order of the items is not important — that is,
where changing the order would not materially change the meaning of the
document.

The items of the list are the [`li`](#the-li-element) element child
nodes of the [`ul`](#the-ul-element) element.

<div class="example">

The following markup shows a list where the order does not matter, and
where the [`ul`](#the-ul-element) element is therefore appropriate.
Compare this list to the equivalent list in the [`ol`](#the-ol-element)
section to see an example of the same items using the
[`ol`](#the-ol-element) element.

``` html
<p>I have lived in the following countries:</p>
<ul>
 <li>Norway
 <li>Switzerland
 <li>United Kingdom
 <li>United States
</ul>
```

Note that changing the order of the list does not change the meaning of
the document. The items in the snippet above are given in alphabetical
order, but in the snippet below they are given in order of the size of
their current account balance in 2007, without changing the meaning of
the document whatsoever:

``` html
<p>I have lived in the following countries:</p>
<ul>
 <li>Switzerland
 <li>Norway
 <li>United Kingdom
 <li>United States
</ul>
```

</div>

<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-menu-element:flow-content-2-2">flow

id="the-menu-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:

<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-menu-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>

id="the-menu-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:

id="the-menu-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-menu-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-menu).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-menu).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-menu-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMenuElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`menu`](#the-menu-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-menu-element:represents">represents</a> a
toolbar consisting of its contents, in the form of an unordered list of
items (represented by [`li`](#the-li-element) elements), each of which
represents a command that the user can perform or activate.

The [`menu`](#the-menu-element) element is simply a semantic alternative
to [`ul`](#the-ul-element) to express an unordered list of commands (a
"toolbar").

<div class="example">

In this example, a text-editing application uses a
[`menu`](#the-menu-element) element to provide a series of editing
commands:

``` html
<menu>
 <li><button onclick="copy()"><img src="copy.svg" alt="Copy"></button></li>
 <li><button onclick="cut()"><img src="cut.svg" alt="Cut"></button></li>
 <li><button onclick="paste()"><img src="paste.svg" alt="Paste"></button></li>
</menu>
```

Note that the styling to make this look like a conventional toolbar menu
is up to the application.

</div>
