<a href="#represents" id="the-samp-element:represents">represents</a>
sample or quoted output from another program or computing system.

See the [`pre`](#the-pre-element) and [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) elements
for more details.

This element can be contrasted with the [`output`](#the-output-element)
element, which can be used to provide immediate output in a web
application.

<div class="example">

This example shows the [`samp`](#the-samp-element) element being used
inline:

``` html
<p>The computer said <samp>Too much cheese in tray
two</samp> but I didn't know what that meant.</p>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This second example shows a block of sample output from a console
program. Nested [`samp`](#the-samp-element) and
[`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) elements allow for the styling of specific
elements of the sample output using a style sheet. There's also a few
parts of the [`samp`](#the-samp-element) that are annotated with even
more detailed markup, to enable very precise styling. To achieve this,
[`span`](#the-span-element) elements are used.

``` html
<pre><samp><span class="prompt">jdoe@mowmow:~$</span> <kbd>ssh demo.example.com</kbd>
Last login: Tue Apr 12 09:10:17 2005 from mowmow.example.com on pts/1
Linux demo 2.6.10-grsec+gg3+e+fhs6b+nfs+gr0501+++p3+c4a+gr2b-reslog-v6.189 #1 SMP Tue Feb 1 11:22:36 PST 2005 i686 unknown

<span class="prompt">jdoe@demo:~$</span> <span class="cursor">_</span></samp></pre>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This third example shows a block of input and its respective output. The
example uses both [`code`](#the-code-element) and
[`samp`](#the-samp-element) elements.

``` html
<pre>
<code class="language-javascript">console.log(2.3 + 2.4)</code>
<samp>4.699999999999999</samp>
</pre>
```

</div>

id="the-kbd-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-kbd).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-kbd).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-kbd-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-kbd-element:represents">represents</a>
user input (typically keyboard input, although it may also be used to
represent other input, such as voice commands).

When the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element is nested inside a
[`samp`](#the-samp-element) element, it represents the input as it was
echoed by the system.

When the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element *contains* a
[`samp`](#the-samp-element) element, it represents input based on system
output, for example invoking a menu item.

When the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element is nested inside another
[`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element, it represents an actual key or other
single unit of input as appropriate for the input mechanism.

<div class="example">

Here the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element is used to indicate keys to
press:

``` html
<p>To make George eat an apple, press <kbd><kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>F3</kbd></kbd></p>
```

In this second example, the user is told to pick a particular menu item.
The outer [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element marks up a block of input,
with the inner [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) elements representing each
individual step of the input, and the [`samp`](#the-samp-element)
elements inside them indicating that the steps are input based on
something being displayed by the system, in this case menu labels:

``` html
<p>To make George eat an apple, select
    <kbd><kbd><samp>File</samp></kbd>|<kbd><samp>Eat Apple...</samp></kbd></kbd>
</p>
```

Such precision isn't necessary; the following is equally fine:

``` html
<p>To make George eat an apple, select <kbd>File | Eat Apple...</kbd></p>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.5.19</span> The <span id="the-sub-element" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`sub`</span> and <span id="the-sup-element" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`sup`</span> elements<a href="#the-sub-and-sup-elements" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

[Element/sub](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/sub "The <sub> HTML element specifies inline text which should be displayed as subscript for solely typographical reasons. Subscripts are typically rendered with a lowered baseline using smaller text.")

(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:flow-content-2">Flow content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a>
is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission
in text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
The [`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element: [for
authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-sub); [for
implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-sub).

The [`sup`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element: [for
authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-sup); [for
implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-sup).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Use [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`sup`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:represents">represents</a> a superscript
and the [`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-sub-and-sup-elements:represents-2">represents</a> a subscript.

These elements must be used only to mark up typographical conventions
with specific meanings, not for typographical presentation for
presentation's sake. For example, it would be inappropriate for the
[`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) and
[`sup`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) elements to be used in the name of
the LaTeX document preparation system. In general, authors should use
these elements only if the *absence* of those elements would change the
meaning of the content.

In certain languages, superscripts are part of the typographical
conventions for some abbreviations.

<div class="example">

``` html
<p>Their names are
<span lang="fr"><abbr>M<sup>lle</sup></abbr> Gwendoline</span> and
<span lang="fr"><abbr>M<sup>me</sup></abbr> Denise</span>.</p>
```

</div>

The [`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element can be used inside a
[`var`](#the-var-element) element, for variables that have subscripts.

<div class="example">

Here, the [`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) element is used to
represent the subscript that identifies the variable in a family of
variables:

``` html
<p>The coordinate of the <var>i</var>th point is
(<var>x<sub><var>i</var></sub></var>, <var>y<sub><var>i</var></sub></var>).
For example, the 10th point has coordinate
(<var>x<sub>10</sub></var>, <var>y<sub>10</sub></var>).</p>
```

</div>

Mathematical expressions often use subscripts and superscripts. Authors
are encouraged to use MathML for marking up mathematics, but authors may
opt to use [`sub`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) and
[`sup`](#the-sub-and-sup-elements) if detailed mathematical markup is
not desired. [\[MATHML\]](#refsMATHML)

<div class="example">

``` html
<var>E</var>=<var>m</var><var>c</var><sup>2</sup>
```

``` html
f(<var>x</var>, <var>n</var>) = log<sub>4</sub><var>x</var><sup><var>n</var></sup>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.5.20</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`i`</span> element<a href="#the-i-element" class="self-link"></a>

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/i](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/i "The <i> HTML element represents a range of text that is set off from the normal text for some reason, such as idiomatic text, technical terms, taxonomical designations, among others. Historically, these have been presented using italicized type, which is the original source of the <i> naming of this element.")

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-i-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-i-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-i-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-i-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-i-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes" id="the-i-element:global-attributes">Global
attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-i).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-i).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-i-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`i`](#the-i-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-i-element:represents">represents</a> a
span of text in an alternate voice or mood, or otherwise offset from the
normal prose in a manner indicating a different quality of text, such as
a taxonomic designation, a technical term, an idiomatic phrase from
another language, transliteration, a thought, or a ship name in Western
texts.

Terms in languages different from the main text should be annotated with
[`lang`](#attr-lang) attributes (or, in XML,
<a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag"
id="the-i-element:attr-xml-lang"
data-x-internal="attr-xml-lang"><code>lang</code> attributes in the
<span>XML namespace</span></a>).

<div class="example">

The examples below show uses of the [`i`](#the-i-element) element:

``` html
<p>The <i class="taxonomy">Felis silvestris catus</i> is cute.</p>
<p>The term <i>prose content</i> is defined above.</p>
<p>There is a certain <i lang="fr">je ne sais quoi</i> in the air.</p>
```

In the following example, a dream sequence is marked up using
[`i`](#the-i-element) elements.

``` html
<p>Raymond tried to sleep.</p>
<p><i>The ship sailed away on Thursday</i>, he
dreamt. <i>The ship had many people aboard, including a beautiful
princess called Carey. He watched her, day-in, day-out, hoping she
would notice him, but she never did.</i></p>
<p><i>Finally one night he picked up the courage to speak with
her—</i></p>
<p>Raymond woke with a start as the fire alarm rang out.</p>
```

</div>

Authors can use the [`class`](#classes) attribute on the
[`i`](#the-i-element) element to identify why the element is being used,
so that if the style of a particular use (e.g. dream sequences as
opposed to taxonomic terms) is to be changed at a later date, the author
doesn't have to go through the entire document (or series of related
documents) annotating each use.

Authors are encouraged to consider whether other elements might be more
applicable than the [`i`](#the-i-element) element, for instance the
[`em`](#the-em-element) element for marking up stress emphasis, or the
[`dfn`](#the-dfn-element) element to mark up the defining instance of a
term.

Style sheets can be used to format [`i`](#the-i-element) elements, just
like any other element can be restyled. Thus, it is not the case that
content in [`i`](#the-i-element) elements will necessarily be
italicized.

#### <span class="secno">4.5.21</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`b`</span> element<a href="#the-b-element" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/b](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/b "The <b> HTML element is used to draw the reader's attention to the element's contents, which are not otherwise granted special importance. This was formerly known as the Boldface element, and most browsers still draw the text in boldface. However, you should not use <b> for styling text or granting importance. If you wish to create boldface text, you should use the CSS font-weight property. If you wish to indicate an element is of special importance, you should use the <strong> element.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android yes">Firefox
Android4+</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-b-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-b-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-b-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-b-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-b-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes" id="the-b-element:global-attributes">Global
attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-b).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-b).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-b-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`b`](#the-b-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-b-element:represents">represents</a> a
span of text to which attention is being drawn for utilitarian purposes
without conveying any extra importance and with no implication of an
alternate voice or mood, such as key words in a document abstract,
product names in a review, actionable words in interactive text-driven
software, or an article lede.

<div class="example">

The following example shows a use of the [`b`](#the-b-element) element
to highlight key words without marking them up as important:

``` html
<p>The <b>frobonitor</b> and <b>barbinator</b> components are fried.</p>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following example, objects in a text adventure are highlighted as
being special by use of the [`b`](#the-b-element) element.

``` html
<p>You enter a small room. Your <b>sword</b> glows
brighter. A <b>rat</b> scurries past the corner wall.</p>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Another case where the [`b`](#the-b-element) element is appropriate is
in marking up the lede (or lead) sentence or paragraph. The following
example shows how a [BBC article about kittens adopting a rabbit as
their
own](http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/north_east/7101506.stm)
could be marked up:

``` html
<article>
 <h2>Kittens 'adopted' by pet rabbit</h2>
 <p><b class="lede">Six abandoned kittens have found an
 unexpected new mother figure — a pet rabbit.</b></p>
 <p>Veterinary nurse Melanie Humble took the three-week-old
 kittens to her Aberdeen home.</p>
[...]
```

</div>

As with the [`i`](#the-i-element) element, authors can use the
[`class`](#classes) attribute on the [`b`](#the-b-element) element to
identify why the element is being used, so that if the style of a
particular use is to be changed at a later date, the author doesn't have
to go through annotating each use.

The [`b`](#the-b-element) element should be used as a last resort when
no other element is more appropriate. In particular, headings should use
the [`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) to
[`h6`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements, stress
emphasis should use the [`em`](#the-em-element) element, importance
should be denoted with the [`strong`](#the-strong-element) element, and
text marked or highlighted should use the [`mark`](#the-mark-element)
element.

<div class="example">

The following would be *incorrect* usage:

``` bad
<p><b>WARNING!</b> Do not frob the barbinator!</p>
```

In the previous example, the correct element to use would have been
[`strong`](#the-strong-element), not [`b`](#the-b-element).

</div>

Style sheets can be used to format [`b`](#the-b-element) elements, just
like any other element can be restyled. Thus, it is not the case that
content in [`b`](#the-b-element) elements will necessarily be boldened.

#### <span class="secno">4.5.22</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`u`</span> element<a href="#the-u-element" class="self-link"></a>

This is rendered by default as a simple solid underline, but may be altered using CSS.")

iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-u-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-u-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-u-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-u-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-u-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes" id="the-u-element:global-attributes">Global
attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-u).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-u).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-u-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`u`](#the-u-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-u-element:represents">represents</a> a
span of text with an unarticulated, though explicitly rendered,
non-textual annotation, such as labeling the text as being a proper name
in Chinese text (a Chinese proper name mark), or labeling the text as
being misspelt.

In most cases, another element is likely to be more appropriate: for
marking stress emphasis, the [`em`](#the-em-element) element should be
used; for marking key words or phrases either the [`b`](#the-b-element)
element or the [`mark`](#the-mark-element) element should be used,
depending on the context; for marking book titles, the
[`cite`](#the-cite-element) element should be used; for labeling text
with explicit textual annotations, the [`ruby`](#the-ruby-element)
element should be used; for technical terms, taxonomic designation,
transliteration, a thought, or for labeling ship names in Western texts,
the [`i`](#the-i-element) element should be used.

The default rendering of the [`u`](#the-u-element) element in visual
presentations clashes with the conventional rendering of hyperlinks
(underlining). Authors are encouraged to avoid using the
[`u`](#the-u-element) element where it could be confused for a
hyperlink.

<div class="example">

In this example, a [`u`](#the-u-element) element is used to mark a word
as misspelt:

``` html
<p>The <u>see</u> is full of fish.</p>
```

</div>

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-mark-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-mark-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-mark-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-mark-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-mark-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-mark-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-mark).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-mark).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-mark-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`mark`](#the-mark-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-mark-element:represents">represents</a> a
run of text in one document marked or highlighted for
<a href="#referenced" id="the-mark-element:referenced">reference</a>
purposes, due to its relevance in another context. When used in a
quotation or other block of text referred to from the prose, it
indicates a highlight that was not originally present but which has been
added to bring the reader's attention to a part of the text that might
not have been considered important by the original author when the block
was originally written, but which is now under previously unexpected
scrutiny. When used in the main prose of a document, it indicates a part
of the document that has been highlighted due to its likely relevance to
the user's current activity.

<div class="example">

This example shows how the [`mark`](#the-mark-element) element can be
used to bring attention to a particular part of a quotation:

``` html
<p lang="en-US">Consider the following quote:</p>
<blockquote lang="en-GB">
 <p>Look around and you will find, no-one's really
 <mark>colour</mark> blind.</p>
</blockquote>
<p lang="en-US">As we can tell from the <em>spelling</em> of the word,
the person writing this quote is clearly not American.</p>
```

(If the goal was to mark the element as misspelt, however, the
[`u`](#the-u-element) element, possibly with a class, would be more
appropriate.)

</div>

<div class="example">

Another example of the [`mark`](#the-mark-element) element is
highlighting parts of a document that are matching some search string.
If someone looked at a document, and the server knew that the user was
searching for the word "kitten", then the server might return the
document with one paragraph modified as follows:

``` html
<p>I also have some <mark>kitten</mark>s who are visiting me
these days. They're really cute. I think they like my garden! Maybe I
should adopt a <mark>kitten</mark>.</p>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following snippet, a paragraph of text refers to a specific part
of a code fragment.

``` html
<p>The highlighted part below is where the error lies:</p>
<pre><code>var i: Integer;
begin
   i := <mark>1.1</mark>;
end.</code></pre>
```

This is separate from *syntax highlighting*, for which
[`span`](#the-span-element) is more appropriate. Combining both, one
would get:

``` html
<p>The highlighted part below is where the error lies:</p>
<pre><code><span class=keyword>var</span> <span class=ident>i</span>: <span class=type>Integer</span>;
<span class=keyword>begin</span>
   <span class=ident>i</span> := <span class=literal><mark>1.1</mark></span>;
<span class=keyword>end</span>.</code></pre>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

This is another example showing the use of [`mark`](#the-mark-element)
to highlight a part of quoted text that was originally not emphasized.
In this example, common typographic conventions have led the author to
explicitly style [`mark`](#the-mark-element) elements in quotes to
render in italics.

``` html
<style>
 blockquote mark, q mark {
   font: inherit; font-style: italic;
   text-decoration: none;
   background: transparent; color: inherit;
 }
 .bubble em {
   font: inherit; font-size: larger;
   text-decoration: underline;
 }
</style>
<article>
 <h1>She knew</h1>
 <p>Did you notice the subtle joke in the joke on panel 4?</p>
 <blockquote>
  <p class="bubble">I didn't <em>want</em> to believe. <mark>Of course
  on some level I realized it was a known-plaintext attack.</mark> But I
  couldn't admit it until I saw for myself.</p>
 </blockquote>
 <p>(Emphasis mine.) I thought that was great. It's so pedantic, yet it
 explains everything neatly.</p>
</article>
```

Note, incidentally, the distinction between the [`em`](#the-em-element)
element in this example, which is part of the original text being
quoted, and the [`mark`](#the-mark-element) element, which is
highlighting a part for comment.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following example shows the difference between denoting the
*importance* of a span of text ([`strong`](#the-strong-element)) as
opposed to denoting the *relevance* of a span of text
([`mark`](#the-mark-element)). It is an extract from a textbook, where
the extract has had the parts relevant to the exam highlighted. The
safety warnings, important though they may be, are apparently not
relevant to the exam.

``` html
<h3>Wormhole Physics Introduction</h3>

<p><mark>A wormhole in normal conditions can be held open for a
maximum of just under 39 minutes.</mark> Conditions that can increase
the time include a powerful energy source coupled to one or both of
the gates connecting the wormhole, and a large gravity well (such as a
black hole).</p>

<p><mark>Momentum is preserved across the wormhole. Electromagnetic
radiation can travel in both directions through a wormhole,
but matter cannot.</mark></p>

<p>When a wormhole is created, a vortex normally forms.
<strong>Warning: The vortex caused by the wormhole opening will
annihilate anything in its path.</strong> Vortexes can be avoided when
using sufficiently advanced dialing technology.</p>

<p><mark>An obstruction in a gate will prevent it from accepting a
wormhole connection.</mark></p>
```

</div>

It's particularly useful when a website dynamically inserts some text and doesn't know the directionality of the text being inserted.")

id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:

content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-bdi-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-bdi-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-bdi-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"

text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-bdi-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

Also, the [`dir`](#attr-dir) global attribute has special semantics on
this element.

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-bdi).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-bdi).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-bdi-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`bdi`](#the-bdi-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-bdi-element:represents">represents</a> a
span of text that is to be isolated from its surroundings for the
purposes of bidirectional text formatting. [\[BIDI\]](#refsBIDI)

The [`dir`](#attr-dir) global attribute defaults to
[`auto`](#attr-dir-auto) on this element (it never inherits from the
parent element like with other elements).

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

<div class="example">

This element is especially useful when embedding user-generated content
with an unknown directionality.

In this example, usernames are shown along with the number of posts that
the user has submitted. If the [`bdi`](#the-bdi-element) element were
not used, the username of the Arabic user would end up confusing the
text (the bidirectional algorithm would put the colon and the number "3"
next to the word "User" rather than next to the word "posts").

``` html
<ul>
 <li>User <bdi>jcranmer</bdi>: 12 posts.
 <li>User <bdi>hober</bdi>: 5 posts.
 <li>User <bdi>إيان</bdi>: 3 posts.
</ul>
```

<figure>
<img src="/images/sample-bdi.png" />
<figcaption>When using the <a href="#the-bdi-element"><code
id="the-bdi-element:the-bdi-element-3">bdi</code></a> element, the
username acts as expected.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<img src="/images/sample-not-bdi.png" />
<figcaption>If the <a href="#the-bdi-element"><code
id="the-bdi-element:the-bdi-element-4">bdi</code></a> element were to be
replaced by a <a href="#the-b-element"><code
id="the-bdi-element:the-b-element">b</code></a> element, the username
would confuse the bidirectional algorithm and the third bullet would end
up saying "User 3 :", followed by the Arabic name (right-to-left),
followed by "posts" and a period.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

Also, the [`dir`](#attr-dir) global attribute has special semantics on

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"

considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-bdo).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-bdo-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`bdo`](#the-bdo-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-bdo-element:represents">represents</a>
explicit text directionality formatting control for its children. It
allows authors to override the Unicode bidirectional algorithm by
explicitly specifying a direction override. [\[BIDI\]](#refsBIDI)

Authors must specify the [`dir`](#attr-dir) attribute on this element,
with the value [`ltr`](#attr-dir-ltr) to specify a left-to-right
override and with the value [`rtl`](#attr-dir-rtl) to specify a
right-to-left override. The [`auto`](#attr-dir-auto) value must not be
specified.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

id="the-span-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is

id="the-span-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:

Otherwise: <a href="#phrasing-content-2"

id="the-span-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in

id="the-span-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:

id="the-span-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-span).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-span).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-span-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSpanElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`span`](#the-span-element) element doesn't mean anything on its
own, but can be useful when used together with the
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-span-element:global-attributes-2">global attributes</a>, e.g.
[`class`](#classes), [`lang`](#attr-lang), or [`dir`](#attr-dir). It
<a href="#represents" id="the-span-element:represents">represents</a>
its children.

<div class="example">

In this example, a code fragment is marked up using
[`span`](#the-span-element) elements and [`class`](#classes) attributes
so that its keywords and identifiers can be color-coded from CSS:

``` html
<pre><code class="lang-c"><span class="keyword">for</span> (<span class="ident">j</span> = 0; <span class="ident">j</span> &lt; 256; <span class="ident">j</span>++) {
  <span class="ident">i_t3</span> = (<span class="ident">i_t3</span> & 0x1ffff) | (<span class="ident">j</span> &lt;&lt; 17);
  <span class="ident">i_t6</span> = (((((((<span class="ident">i_t3</span> >> 3) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 1) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 8) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 5) & 0xff;
  <span class="keyword">if</span> (<span class="ident">i_t6</span> == <span class="ident">i_t1</span>)
    <span class="keyword">break</span>;
}</code></pre>
```

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-br-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLBRElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`br`](#the-br-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-br-element:represents">represents</a> a
line break.

While line breaks are usually represented in visual media by physically
moving subsequent text to a new line, a style sheet or user agent would
be equally justified in causing line breaks to be rendered in a
different manner, for instance as green dots, or as extra spacing.

[`br`](#the-br-element) elements must be used only for line breaks that
are actually part of the content, as in poems or addresses.

<div class="example">

The following example is correct usage of the [`br`](#the-br-element)
element:

``` html
<p>P. Sherman<br>
42 Wallaby Way<br>
Sydney</p>
```

</div>

[`br`](#the-br-element) elements must not be used for separating
thematic groups in a paragraph.

<div class="example">

The following examples are non-conforming, as they abuse the
[`br`](#the-br-element) element:

``` html
<p><a ...>34 comments.</a><br>
<a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
```

``` html
<p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label><br>
<label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
```

Here are alternatives to the above, which are correct:

``` html
<p><a ...>34 comments.</a></p>
<p><a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
```

``` html
<p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label></p>
<p><label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
```

</div>

If a <a href="#paragraph" id="the-br-element:paragraph">paragraph</a>
consists of nothing but a single [`br`](#the-br-element) element, it
represents a placeholder blank line (e.g. as in a template). Such blank
lines must not be used for presentation purposes.

Any content inside [`br`](#the-br-element) elements must not be
considered part of the surrounding text.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

The [`wbr`](#the-wbr-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-wbr-element:represents">represents</a> a
line break opportunity.

<div class="example">

In the following example, someone is quoted as saying something which,
for effect, is written as one long word. However, to ensure that the
text can be wrapped in a readable fashion, the individual words in the
quote are separated using a [`wbr`](#the-wbr-element) element.

``` html
<p>So then she pointed at the tiger and screamed
"there<wbr>is<wbr>no<wbr>way<wbr>you<wbr>are<wbr>ever<wbr>going<wbr>to<wbr>catch<wbr>me"!</p>
```

</div>

Any content inside [`wbr`](#the-wbr-element) elements must not be
considered part of the surrounding text.

``` example
var wbr = document.createElement("wbr");
wbr.textContent = "This is wrong";
document.body.appendChild(wbr);
```

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

### <span class="secno">4.6</span> Links<a href="#links" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">4.6.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-2" class="self-link"></a>

Links are a conceptual construct, created by [`a`](#the-a-element),
[`area`](#the-area-element), [`form`](#the-form-element), and
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements, that
<a href="#represents" id="introduction-2:represents">represent</a> a
connection between two resources, one of which is the current
[`Document`](#document). There are three kinds of links in HTML:

<span id="external-resource-link" class="dfn" lt="external resource link" export="">Links to external resources</span>  
These are links to resources that are to be used to augment the current
document, generally automatically processed by the user agent. All
<a href="#external-resource-link"
id="introduction-2:external-resource-link">external resource links</a>
have a <a href="#fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource"
id="introduction-2:fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource">fetch and
process the linked resource</a> algorithm which describes how the
resource is obtained.

<span id="hyperlink" class="dfn" lt="hyperlink" export="">Hyperlinks</span>  
These are links to other resources that are generally exposed to the
user by the user agent so that the user can cause the user agent to
<a href="#navigate" id="introduction-2:navigate">navigate</a> to those
resources, e.g. to visit them in a browser or download them.

<span id="internal-resource-link" class="dfn" export="">Internal resource links</span>  
These are links to resources within the current document, used to give
those resources special meaning or behavior.

For [`link`](#the-link-element) elements with an
[`href`](#attr-link-href) attribute and a [`rel`](#attr-link-rel)
attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the
[`rel`](#attr-link-rel) attribute, as defined for those keywords in the
[link types](#linkTypes) section.

Similarly, for [`a`](#the-a-element) and [`area`](#the-area-element)
elements with an [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute and a
[`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute, links must be created for the
keywords of the [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute as defined for
those keywords in the [link types](#linkTypes) section. Unlike
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements, however, [`a`](#the-a-element) and
[`area`](#the-area-element) elements with an
[`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute that either do not have a
[`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute, or whose
[`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute has no keywords that are defined
as specifying
<a href="#hyperlink" id="introduction-2:hyperlink">hyperlinks</a>, must
also create a
<a href="#hyperlink" id="introduction-2:hyperlink-2">hyperlink</a>. This
implied hyperlink has no special meaning (it has no [link
type](#linkTypes)) beyond linking the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="introduction-2:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
document</a> to the resource given by the element's
[`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute.

Similarly, for [`form`](#the-form-element) elements with a
[`rel`](#attr-form-rel) attribute, links must be created for the
keywords of the [`rel`](#attr-form-rel) attribute as defined for those
keywords in the [link types](#linkTypes) section.
[`form`](#the-form-element) elements that do not have a
[`rel`](#attr-form-rel) attribute, or whose [`rel`](#attr-form-rel)
attribute has no keywords that are defined as specifying
<a href="#hyperlink" id="introduction-2:hyperlink-3">hyperlinks</a>,
must also create a
<a href="#hyperlink" id="introduction-2:hyperlink-4">hyperlink</a>.

A <a href="#hyperlink" id="introduction-2:hyperlink-5">hyperlink</a> can
have one or more <span id="hyperlink-annotation" class="dfn">hyperlink
annotations</span> that modify the processing semantics of that
hyperlink.

#### <span class="secno">4.6.2</span> Links created by [`a`](#the-a-element) and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements<a href="#links-created-by-a-and-area-elements" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-href" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`href`</span> attribute on [`a`](#the-a-element)
and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements must have a value that is a
<a href="#valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>.

The [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute on [`a`](#the-a-element)
and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements is not required; when those
elements do not have [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attributes they do
not create hyperlinks.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-target" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`target`</span> attribute, if present, must be a
<a href="#valid-navigable-target-name-or-keyword"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:valid-navigable-target-name-or-keyword">valid
navigable target name or keyword</a>. It gives the name of the
<a href="#navigable"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:navigable">navigable</a> that
will be used. User agents use this name when
<a href="#following-hyperlinks-2"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:following-hyperlinks-2">following
hyperlinks</a>.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-download" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`download`</span> attribute, if present,
indicates that the author intends the hyperlink to be used for
<a href="#downloading-hyperlinks"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:downloading-hyperlinks">downloading
a resource</a>. The attribute may have a value; the value, if any,
specifies the default filename that the author recommends for use in
labeling the resource in a local file system. There are no restrictions
on allowed values, but authors are cautioned that most file systems have
limitations with regard to what punctuation is supported in filenames,
and user agents are likely to adjust filenames accordingly.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

The <span id="ping" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`ping`</span> attribute, if present, gives the
URLs of the resources that are interested in being notified if the user
follows the hyperlink. The value must be a
<a href="#set-of-space-separated-tokens"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:set-of-space-separated-tokens">set
of space-separated tokens</a>, each of which must be a
<a href="#valid-non-empty-url"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:valid-non-empty-url">valid
non-empty URL</a> whose
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:concept-url-scheme"
data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is an
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:http(s)-scheme"
data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a>. The value is used
by the user agent for <a href="#hyperlink-auditing"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:hyperlink-auditing">hyperlink
auditing</a>.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-rel" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`rel`</span> attribute on [`a`](#the-a-element)
and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements controls what kinds of links
the elements create. The attribute's value must be an
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a>. The [allowed keywords and
their meanings](#linkTypes) are defined below.

[`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:concept-supported-tokens"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> are the
keywords defined in [HTML link types](#linkTypes) which are allowed on
[`a`](#the-a-element) and [`area`](#the-area-element) elements, impact
the processing model, and are supported by the user agent. The possible
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:concept-supported-tokens-2"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> are
[`noreferrer`](#link-type-noreferrer),
[`noopener`](#link-type-noopener), and [`opener`](#link-type-opener).
[`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:concept-supported-tokens-3"
data-x-internal="concept-supported-tokens">supported tokens</a> must
only include the tokens from this list that the user agent implements
the processing model for.

The [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute has no default value. If the
attribute is omitted or if none of the values in the attribute are
recognized by the user agent, then the document has no particular
relationship with the destination resource other than there being a
hyperlink between the two.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-hreflang" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`hreflang`</span> attribute on
[`a`](#the-a-element) elements that create <a href="#hyperlink"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:hyperlink">hyperlinks</a>, if
present, gives the language of the linked resource. It is purely
advisory. The value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag.
[\[BCP47\]](#refsBCP47) User agents must not consider this attribute
authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must use only
language information associated with the resource to determine its
language, not metadata included in the link to the resource.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="a,area"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute, if present, gives the
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:mime-type"
data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME type</a> of the linked resource. It is
purely advisory. The value must be a
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:valid-mime-type-string"
data-x-internal="valid-mime-type-string">valid MIME type string</a>.
User agents must not consider the [`type`](#attr-hyperlink-type)
attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must
not use metadata included in the link to the resource to determine its
type.

The <span id="attr-hyperlink-referrerpolicy" class="dfn"
dfn-for="a,area" dfn-type="element-attr">`referrerpolicy`</span>
attribute is a <a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:referrer-policy-attribute">referrer
policy attribute</a>. Its purpose is to set the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:referrer-policy"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> used when
<a href="#following-hyperlinks-2"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:following-hyperlinks-2-2">following
hyperlinks</a>. [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

When an [`a`](#the-a-element) or [`area`](#the-area-element) element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:activation-behaviour"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a> is
invoked, the user agent may allow the user to indicate a preference
regarding whether the hyperlink is to be used for <a href="#navigate"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:navigate">navigation</a> or
whether the resource it specifies is to be downloaded.

In the absence of a user preference, the default should be navigation if
the element has no [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute, and
should be to download the specified resource if it does.

<div algorithm="">

The
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:activation-behaviour-2"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a> of an
[`a`](#the-a-element) or [`area`](#the-area-element) element `element`
given an event `event` is:

1.  If `element` has no [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, then
    return.

2.  Let `hyperlinkSuffix` be null.

3.  If `element` is an [`a`](#the-a-element) element, and `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-target"
    id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:concept-event-target"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-target">target</a> is an
    [`img`](#the-img-element) with an [`ismap`](#attr-img-ismap)
    attribute specified, then:

    1.  Let `x` and `y` be 0.

    2.  If `event`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted"
        data-x-internal="dom-event-istrusted"><code
        id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:dom-event-istrusted">isTrusted</code></a>
        attribute is initialized to true, then set `x` to the distance
        in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
        id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:&#39;px&#39;"
        data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> from the left edge
        of the image to the location of the click, and set `y` to the
        distance in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
        id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:&#39;px&#39;-2"
        data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> from the top edge
        of the image to the location of the click.

    3.  If `x` is negative, set `x` to 0.

    4.  If `y` is negative, set `y` to 0.

    5.  Set `hyperlinkSuffix` to the concatenation of U+003F (?), the
        value of `x` expressed as a base-ten integer using
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
        id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:ascii-digits"
        data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a>, U+002C (,), and
        the value of `y` expressed as a base-ten integer using
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
        id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:ascii-digits-2"
        data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a>.

4.  Let `userInvolvement` be `event`'s <a href="#event-uni"
    id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:event-uni">user navigation
    involvement</a>.

5.  If the user has expressed a preference to download the hyperlink,
    then set `userInvolvement` to "[`browser UI`](#uni-browser-ui)".

    That is, if the user has expressed a specific preference for
    downloading, this no longer counts as merely
    "[`activation`](#uni-activation)".

6.  If `element` has a [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute,
    or if the user has expressed a preference to download the hyperlink,
    then <a href="#downloading-hyperlinks"
    id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:downloading-hyperlinks-2">download
    the hyperlink</a> created by `element` with
    *[hyperlinkSuffix](#downloading-hyperlinksuffix)* set to
    `hyperlinkSuffix` and
    *[userInvolvement](#downloading-userinvolvement)* set to
    `userInvolvement`.

7.  Otherwise, <a href="#following-hyperlinks-2"
    id="links-created-by-a-and-area-elements:following-hyperlinks-2-3">follow
    the hyperlink</a> created by `element` with
    *[hyperlinkSuffix](#following-hyperlinksuffix)* set to
    `hyperlinkSuffix` and
    *[userInvolvement](#following-userinvolvement)* set to
    `userInvolvement`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.6.3</span> API for hyperlink elements<a href="#api-for-hyperlink-elements" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
interface mixin HyperlinkElementUtils {
  readonly attribute USVString origin;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString protocol;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString username;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString password;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString host;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString hostname;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString port;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString pathname;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString search;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString hash;
};
```

An element implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin has an
associated <span id="concept-hyperlink-url" class="dfn">url</span> (null
or a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>). It
is initially null.

<div algorithm="">

An element implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin has the
following <a href="#extract-an-origin"
id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:extract-an-origin">extract an origin</a>
steps:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url">url</a> is
    null, then return null.

2.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-2">url</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a>.

</div>

An element implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin must have an
associated <span id="concept-hyperlink-url-set" class="dfn">set the
url</span> algorithm.

<div algorithm="">

When elements implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin are created, the
user agent must <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url-set"
id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-set">set the
url</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An element implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin has an
associated <span id="reinitialise-url" class="dfn">reinitialize
url</span> algorithm, which runs these steps:

1.  If the element's <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-3">url</a> is
    non-null, its
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-scheme"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is "`blob`", and it
    has an <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-opaque-path"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:opaque-path"
    data-x-internal="opaque-path">opaque path</a>, then terminate these
    steps.

2.  <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url-set"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-set-2">Set the
    url</a>.

</div>

An element implementing the
[`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#hyperlinkelementutils) mixin must have an
associated <span id="update-href" class="dfn">update `href`</span>
algorithm.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hyperlink-origin" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HyperlinkElementUtils" dfn-type="attribute">`origin`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-4">url</a> is
    null, return the empty string.

3.  Return the <a href="#ascii-serialisation-of-an-origin"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:ascii-serialisation-of-an-origin">serialization</a>
    of <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-5">url</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hyperlink-protocol" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HyperlinkElementUtils" dfn-type="attribute">`protocol`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-2">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-6">url</a> is
    null, return "`:`".

3.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-7">url</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-scheme-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a>, followed by "`:`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`protocol`](#dom-hyperlink-protocol) setter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-3">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-8">url</a> is
    null, then return.

3.  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:basic-url-parser"
    data-x-internal="basic-url-parser">Basic URL parse</a> the given
    value, followed by "`:`", with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-9">url</a> as
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:basic-url-parser-url"
    data-x-internal="basic-url-parser-url"><em>url</em></a> and
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-start-state"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:scheme-start-state"
    data-x-internal="scheme-start-state">scheme start state</a> as
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:basic-url-parser-state-override"
    data-x-internal="basic-url-parser-state-override"><em>state
    override</em></a>.

    Because the URL parser ignores multiple consecutive colons,
    providing a value of "`https:`" (or even "`https::::`") is the same
    as providing a value of "`https`".

4.  <a href="#update-href"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:update-href">Update <code>href</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hyperlink-username" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HyperlinkElementUtils" dfn-type="attribute">`username`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-4">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-10">url</a> is
    null, return the empty string.

3.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-10" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-11">url</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-username"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-username"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-username">username</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`username`](#dom-hyperlink-username) setter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-5">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  Let `url` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-11" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-12">url</a>.

3.  If `url` is null or `url` <a
    href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#cannot-have-a-username-password-port"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:cannot-have-a-username/password/port"
    data-x-internal="cannot-have-a-username/password/port">cannot have a
    username/password/port</a>, then return.

4.  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-username"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:set-the-username"
    data-x-internal="set-the-username">Set the username</a>, given `url`
    and the given value.

5.  <a href="#update-href"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:update-href-2">Update
    <code>href</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hyperlink-password" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HyperlinkElementUtils" dfn-type="attribute">`password`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-6">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  Let `url` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-12" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-13">url</a>.

3.  If `url` is null, then return the empty string.

4.  Return `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-password"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-password"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-password">password</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`password`](#dom-hyperlink-password) setter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-7">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  Let `url` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-13" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-14">url</a>.

3.  If `url` is null or `url` <a
    href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#cannot-have-a-username-password-port"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:cannot-have-a-username/password/port-2"
    data-x-internal="cannot-have-a-username/password/port">cannot have a
    username/password/port</a>, then return.

4.  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-password"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:set-the-password"
    data-x-internal="set-the-password">Set the password</a>, given `url`
    and the given value.

5.  <a href="#update-href"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:update-href-3">Update
    <code>href</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hyperlink-host" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HyperlinkElementUtils" dfn-type="attribute">`host`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-8">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  Let `url` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-14" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-15">url</a>.

3.  If `url` or `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-host"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-host">host</a> is null, return the

4.  If `url`'s <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-port"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-port">port</a> is null, return `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-host-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-host">host</a>,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:host-serializer"
    data-x-internal="host-serializer">serialized</a>.

5.  Return `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-host-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-host">host</a>,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:host-serializer-2"
    data-x-internal="host-serializer">serialized</a>, followed by "`:`"
    and `url`'s <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:concept-url-port-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-port">port</a>,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-an-integer"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:serialize-an-integer"
    data-x-internal="serialize-an-integer">serialized</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`host`](#dom-hyperlink-host) setter steps are:

1.  <a href="#reinitialise-url"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:reinitialise-url-9">Reinitialize url</a>.

2.  Let `url` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:this-15" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"

3.  If `url` is null or `url` has an

    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:opaque-path-2"

    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:basic-url-parser-url-2"

    id="api-for-hyperlink-elements:update-href-4">Update
    <code>href</code></a>.
