The <a href="#html-element-moving-steps"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:html-element-moving-steps">HTML element
moving steps</a> for [`a`](#the-a-element) and
[`area`](#the-area-element) elements, given `movedNode`, are:

1.  <a href="#consider-speculative-loads"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:consider-speculative-loads-3">Consider
    speculative loads</a> given `movedNode`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The following <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change-ext">attribute change
steps</a>, given `element`, `localName`, `oldValue`, `value`, and
`namespace`, are used for all [`a`](#the-a-element) and
[`area`](#the-area-element) elements:

1.  If `namespace` is not null, then return.

2.  If `oldValue` equals `value`, then return.

3.  If `localName` is [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href), then
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url-set"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-set">set the
    url</a> given `element`.

    This is only observable for
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#DefinitionOfScheme"
    data-x-internal="blob-protocol"><code
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:blob-protocol">blob:</code></a> URLs
    as <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:url-parser"
    data-x-internal="url-parser">parsing</a> them involves a
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#BlobURLStore"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:blob-url-store"
    data-x-internal="blob-url-store">Blob URL Store</a> lookup.

4.  If `localName` is [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href),
    [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-hyperlink-referrerpolicy), or
    [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel), then
    <a href="#consider-speculative-loads"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:consider-speculative-loads-4">consider
    speculative loads</a> given `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:node-document-4"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <a href="#update-href"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:update-href">update
<code>href</code></a> for an [`HTMLAnchorElement`](#htmlanchorelement)
or [`HTMLAreaElement`](#htmlareaelement) element, set the element's
[`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute's value to the
element's <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-2">url</a>,
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-url-serializer-2"
data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialized</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url-set"
id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-set-2">set the
url</a> algorithm for [`HTMLAnchorElement`](#htmlanchorelement) and
[`HTMLAreaElement`](#htmlareaelement) elements is as follows:

1.  Set this element's <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-3">url</a> to
    null.

2.  If this element's [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute
    is absent, then return.

3.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing
    a URL</a> given this element's [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href)
    content attribute's value, relative to this element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:node-document-5"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

4.  If `url` is not failure, then set this element's
    <a href="#concept-hyperlink-url"
    id="api-for-a-and-area-elements:concept-hyperlink-url-4">url</a> to
    `url`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.6.5</span> Following hyperlinks<a href="#following-hyperlinks" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

An element `element` <span id="cannot-navigate" class="dfn">cannot
navigate</span> if any of the following are true:

- `element`'s
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
  id="following-hyperlinks:node-document"
  data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is not
  <a href="#fully-active" id="following-hyperlinks:fully-active">fully
  active</a>; or

- `element` is not an [`a`](#the-a-element) element and is not
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
  id="following-hyperlinks:connected"
  data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>.

</div>

This is also used by <a href="#concept-form-submit"
id="following-hyperlinks:concept-form-submit">form submission</a> for
the [`form`](#the-form-element) element. The exception for
[`a`](#the-a-element) elements is for compatibility with web content.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="get-an-element's-noopener" class="dfn">get an element's
noopener</span>, given an [`a`](#the-a-element),
[`area`](#the-area-element), or [`form`](#the-form-element) element
`element`, a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="following-hyperlinks:url-record" data-x-internal="url-record">URL
record</a> `url`, and a string `target`, perform the following steps.
They return a boolean.

1.  If `element`'s [link types](#linkTypes) include the
    [`noopener`](#link-type-noopener) or
    [`noreferrer`](#link-type-noreferrer) keyword, then return true.

2.  <div id="opener-processing-model">

    If `element`'s [link types](#linkTypes) do not include the
    [`opener`](#link-type-opener) keyword and `target` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="following-hyperlinks:ascii-case-insensitive"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "`_blank`", then return true.

    </div>

3.  If `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry"
    id="following-hyperlinks:concept-url-blob-entry"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-blob-entry">blob URL entry</a> is not
    null:

    1.  Let `blobOrigin` be `url`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry"
        id="following-hyperlinks:concept-url-blob-entry-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-blob-entry">blob URL entry</a>'s
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-entry-environment"
        id="following-hyperlinks:blob-url-entry-environment"
        data-x-internal="blob-url-entry-environment">environment</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
        id="following-hyperlinks:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>.

    2.  Let `topLevelOrigin` be `element`'s
        <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="following-hyperlinks:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
        object</a>'s <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
        id="following-hyperlinks:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
        origin</a>.

    3.  If `blobOrigin` is not
        <a href="#same-site" id="following-hyperlinks:same-site">same site</a>
        with `topLevelOrigin`, then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="following-hyperlinks-2" class="dfn">follow the
hyperlink</span> created by an element `subject`, given an optional
<span id="following-hyperlinksuffix"
class="dfn">`hyperlinkSuffix`</span> (default null) and an optional
<span id="following-userinvolvement"
class="dfn">`userInvolvement`</span> (default "[`none`](#uni-none)"):

1.  If `subject` <a href="#cannot-navigate"
    id="following-hyperlinks:cannot-navigate">cannot navigate</a>, then
    return.

2.  Let `targetAttributeValue` be the empty string.

3.  If `subject` is an [`a`](#the-a-element) or
    [`area`](#the-area-element) element, then set `targetAttributeValue`
    to the result of <a href="#get-an-element&#39;s-target"
    id="following-hyperlinks:get-an-element&#39;s-target">getting an
    element's target</a> given `subject`.

4.  Let `urlRecord` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
    id="following-hyperlinks:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a
    URL</a> given `subject`'s [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
    value, relative to `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="following-hyperlinks:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

5.  If `urlRecord` is failure, then return.

6.  Let `noopener` be the result of
    <a href="#get-an-element&#39;s-noopener"
    id="following-hyperlinks:get-an-element&#39;s-noopener">getting an
    element's noopener</a> with `subject`, `urlRecord`, and
    `targetAttributeValue`.

7.  Let `targetNavigable` be the first return value of applying
    <a href="#the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable"
    id="following-hyperlinks:the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable">the rules
    for choosing a navigable</a> given `targetAttributeValue`,
    `subject`'s
    <a href="#node-navigable" id="following-hyperlinks:node-navigable">node
    navigable</a>, and `noopener`.

8.  If `targetNavigable` is null, then return.

9.  Let `urlString` be the result of applying the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="following-hyperlinks:concept-url-serializer"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">URL serializer</a> to
    `urlRecord`.

10. If `hyperlinkSuffix` is non-null, then append it to `urlString`.

11. <a href="#navigate" id="following-hyperlinks:navigate">Navigate</a>
    `targetNavigable` to `urlString` using `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="following-hyperlinks:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, with
    *[referrerPolicy](#navigation-referrer-policy)* set to `subject`'s
    <a href="#hyperlink-referrer-policy"
    id="following-hyperlinks:hyperlink-referrer-policy">hyperlink referrer
    policy</a>, *[userInvolvement](#navigation-user-involvement)* set to
    `userInvolvement`, and *[sourceElement](#navigation-source-element)*
    set to `subject`.

    Unlike many other types of navigations, following hyperlinks does
    not have special "[`replace`](#navigationhistorybehavior-replace)"
    behavior for when documents are not <a href="#completely-loaded"
    id="following-hyperlinks:completely-loaded">completely loaded</a>.
    This is true for both user-initiated instances of following
    hyperlinks, as well as script-triggered ones via, e.g.,
    `aElement.click()`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="hyperlink-referrer-policy" class="dfn">hyperlink referrer
policy</span> for an element `subject` is the value returned by the
following steps:

1.  <div id="noreferrer-a-area-processing-model">

    If `subject`'s [link types](#linkTypes) includes the
    [`noreferrer`](#link-type-noreferrer) keyword, then return
    "`no-referrer`".

    </div>

2.  Return the current state of `subject`'s
    [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-hyperlink-referrerpolicy) content
    attribute.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.6.6</span> Downloading resources<a href="#downloading-resources" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLAnchorElement/download](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLAnchorElement/download "The HTMLAnchorElement.download property is a string indicating that the linked resource is intended to be downloaded rather than displayed in the browser. The value, if any, specifies the default file name for use in labeling the resource in a local file system. If the name is not a valid file name in the underlying OS, the browser will adjust it.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox20+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari10.1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome15+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)13+</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

In some cases, resources are intended for later use rather than
immediate viewing. To indicate that a resource is intended to be
downloaded for use later, rather than immediately used, the
[`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute can be specified on the
[`a`](#the-a-element) or [`area`](#the-area-element) element that
creates the
<a href="#hyperlink" id="downloading-resources:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>
to that resource.

The attribute can furthermore be given a value, to specify the filename
that user agents are to use when storing the resource in a file system.
This value can be overridden by the
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html"
data-x-internal="http-content-disposition"><code
id="downloading-resources:http-content-disposition">Content-Disposition</code></a>\`
HTTP header's filename parameters. [\[RFC6266\]](#refsRFC6266)

In cross-origin situations, the [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download)
attribute has to be combined with the
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html"
data-x-internal="http-content-disposition"><code
id="downloading-resources:http-content-disposition-2">Content-Disposition</code></a>\`
HTTP header, specifically with the `attachment` disposition type, to
avoid the user being warned of possibly nefarious activity. (This is to
protect users from being made to download sensitive personal or
confidential information without their full understanding.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="downloading-hyperlinks" class="dfn" export="">download the
hyperlink</span> created by an element `subject`, given an optional
<span id="downloading-hyperlinksuffix"
class="dfn">`hyperlinkSuffix`</span> (default null) and an optional
<span id="downloading-userinvolvement"
class="dfn">`userInvolvement`</span> (default "[`none`](#uni-none)"):

1.  If `subject` <a href="#cannot-navigate"
    id="downloading-resources:cannot-navigate">cannot navigate</a>, then
    return.

2.  <div id="allowed-to-download">

    If `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="downloading-resources:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="downloading-resources:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing
    flag set</a> has the
    <a href="#sandboxed-downloads-browsing-context-flag"
    id="downloading-resources:sandboxed-downloads-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
    downloads browsing context flag</a> set, then return.

    </div>

3.  Let `urlString` be the result of
    <a href="#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
    id="downloading-resources:encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url">encoding-parsing-and-serializing
    a URL</a> given `subject`'s [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
    value, relative to `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="downloading-resources:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

4.  If `urlString` is failure, then return.

5.  If `hyperlinkSuffix` is non-null, then append it to `urlString`.

6.  If `userInvolvement` is not "[`browser UI`](#uni-browser-ui)", then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="downloading-resources:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `subject` has a [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download)
        attribute.

    2.  Let `navigation` be `subject`'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
        object</a>'s <a href="#window-navigation-api"
        id="downloading-resources:window-navigation-api">navigation API</a>.

    3.  Let `filename` be the value of `subject`'s
        [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute.

    4.  Let `continue` be the result of
        <a href="#fire-a-download-request-navigate-event"
        id="downloading-resources:fire-a-download-request-navigate-event">firing
        a download request <code>navigate</code> event</a> at
        `navigation` with
        *[destinationURL](#fire-navigate-download-destinationurl)* set
        to `urlString`,
        *[userInvolvement](#fire-navigate-download-userinvolvement)* set
        to `userInvolvement`,
        *[sourceElement](#fire-navigate-download-sourceelement)* set to
        `subject`, and *[filename](#fire-navigate-download-filename)*
        set to `filename`.

    5.  If `continue` is false, then return.

    6.  <a href="#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation"
        id="downloading-resources:inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation">Inform
        the navigation API about aborting navigation</a> given
        `subject`'s
        <a href="#node-navigable" id="downloading-resources:node-navigable">node
        navigable</a>.

7.  Run these steps
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="downloading-resources:in-parallel">in
    parallel</a>:

    1.  Optionally, the user agent may abort these steps, if it believes
        doing so would safeguard the user from a potentially hostile
        download.

    2.  Let `request` be a new
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-request"
        data-x-internal="concept-request">request</a> whose
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-request-url"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-url">URL</a> is `urlString`,
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-request-client"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-client">client</a> is
        <a href="#entry-settings-object"
        id="downloading-resources:entry-settings-object">entry settings
        object</a>,
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-request-initiator"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-initiator">initiator</a> is
        "`download`",
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-request-destination"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a> is
        the empty string, and whose
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#synchronous-flag"
        id="downloading-resources:synchronous-flag"
        data-x-internal="synchronous-flag">synchronous flag</a> and <a
        href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag"
        id="downloading-resources:use-url-credentials-flag"
        data-x-internal="use-url-credentials-flag">use-URL-credentials flag</a>
        are set.

    3.  Let `response` be the result of
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-fetch"
        data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetching</a> `request`.

    4.  <a href="#handle-as-a-download"
        id="downloading-resources:handle-as-a-download">Handle as a download</a>
        `response` with `subject`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
        id="downloading-resources:node-navigable-2">node navigable</a>
        and null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="handle-as-a-download" class="dfn">handle as a
download</span> a
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="downloading-resources:concept-response"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response` with a
<a href="#navigable" id="downloading-resources:navigable">navigable</a>
`navigable` and a <a href="#navigation-id"
id="downloading-resources:navigation-id">navigation ID</a> or null
`navigationId`:

1.  Let `suggestedFilename` be the result of
    <a href="#getting-the-suggested-filename"
    id="downloading-resources:getting-the-suggested-filename">getting the
    suggested filename</a> for `response`.

2.  Let `download behavior` be the result of <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-will-begin"
    id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-download-will-begin"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-download-will-begin">WebDriver BiDi
    download will begin</a> with `navigable` and a new <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status"
    id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-navigation-status"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigation-status">WebDriver BiDi
    navigation status</a> whose
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id"
    id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-id"
    data-x-internal="navigation-status-id">id</a> is `navigationId`,
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status"
    id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-status"
    data-x-internal="navigation-status-status">status</a> is "<a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-pending"
    data-x-internal="navigation-status-pending"><code
    id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-pending">pending</code></a>",
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url"
    id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-url"
    data-x-internal="navigation-status-url">url</a> is `response`'s
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-response-url"
    data-x-internal="concept-response-url">URL</a>, and <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-suggested-filename"
    id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-suggested-filename"
    data-x-internal="navigation-status-suggested-filename">suggestedFilename</a>
    is `suggestedFilename`.

3.  If `download behavior` is not null and `download behavior`'s <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#download-behavior-struct-allowed"
    id="downloading-resources:download-behavior-struct-allowed"
    data-x-internal="download-behavior-struct-allowed">allowed</a> is
    false:

    1.  Invoke <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end"
        id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-download-end"
        data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-download-end">WebDriver BiDi download
        end</a> with `navigable` and a new <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status"
        id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-navigation-status-2"
        data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigation-status">WebDriver BiDi
        navigation status</a> whose
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-id-2"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-id">id</a> is `navigationId`,
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-status-2"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-status">status</a> is "<a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-canceled"><code
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-canceled">canceled</code></a>",
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-url-2"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-url">url</a> is `response`'s
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-response-url-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-response-url">URL</a>.

    2.  Return.

4.  If `download behavior` is not null, let `destinationFolder` be
    `download behavior`'s <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#download-behavior-struct-destination-folder"
    id="downloading-resources:download-behavior-struct-destination-folder"
    data-x-internal="download-behavior-struct-destination-folder">destinationFolder</a>.

5.  Run these steps
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="downloading-resources:in-parallel-2">in
    parallel</a>:

    1.  Run
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
        id="downloading-resources:implementation-defined"
        data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
        steps to save `response` for later use. If `destinationFolder`
        is not null, the user agent should save the file to that path.
        If the user agent needs a filename, the user agent should use
        the `suggestedFilename`.

    2.  If any of the following are true:

        - the download is canceled by the user;

        - the download is canceled by the user agent;

        - an error occurs (for example, a network error, not enough
          storage, an unavailable destination folder);

        then:

        1.  Invoke <a
            href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end"
            id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-download-end-2"
            data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-download-end">WebDriver BiDi download
            end</a> with `navigable` and a new <a
            href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status"
            id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-navigation-status-3"
            data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigation-status">WebDriver BiDi
            navigation status</a> whose
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id"
            id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-id-3"
            data-x-internal="navigation-status-id">id</a> is
            `navigationId`,
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status"
            id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-status-3"
            data-x-internal="navigation-status-status">status</a> is "<a
            href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled"
            data-x-internal="navigation-status-canceled"><code
            id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-canceled-2">canceled</code></a>",
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url"
            id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-url-3"
            data-x-internal="navigation-status-url">url</a> is
            `response`'s
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
            id="downloading-resources:concept-response-url-3"
            data-x-internal="concept-response-url">URL</a>.

        2.  Return.

    3.  When the download completes successfully, invoke <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end"
        id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-download-end-3"
        data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-download-end">WebDriver BiDi download
        end</a> with `navigable` and a new <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status"
        id="downloading-resources:webdriver-bidi-navigation-status-4"
        data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigation-status">WebDriver BiDi
        navigation status</a> whose
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-id-4"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-id">id</a> is `navigationId`,
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-status-4"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-status">status</a> is "<a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-complete"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-complete"><code
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-complete">complete</code></a>",
        <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-downloaded-filepath"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-downloaded-filepath"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-downloaded-filepath">downloadedFilepath</a>
        is an absolute path of the downloaded file if available,
        otherwise null,
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url"
        id="downloading-resources:navigation-status-url-4"
        data-x-internal="navigation-status-url">url</a> is `response`'s
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
        id="downloading-resources:concept-response-url-4"
        data-x-internal="concept-response-url">URL</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="getting-the-suggested-filename" class="dfn">get the
suggested filename</span> for a
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="downloading-resources:concept-response-2"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response`:

This algorithm is intended to mitigate security dangers involved in
downloading files from untrusted sites, and user agents are strongly
urged to follow it.

1.  Let `filename` be the undefined value.

2.  If `response` has a
    \`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html"
    data-x-internal="http-content-disposition"><code
    id="downloading-resources:http-content-disposition-3">Content-Disposition</code></a>\`
    header, that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type, and
    the header includes filename information, then let `filename` have
    the value specified by the header, and jump to the step labeled
    *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#refsRFC6266)

3.  Let `interface origin` be the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> of the
    [`Document`](#document) in which the
    <a href="#downloading-hyperlinks"
    id="downloading-resources:downloading-hyperlinks">download</a> or
    <a href="#navigate" id="downloading-resources:navigate">navigate</a>
    action resulting in the download was initiated, if any.

4.  Let `response origin` be the <a href="#concept-origin"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-origin">origin</a> of the URL of
    `response`, unless that URL's
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-url-scheme"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> component is `data`,
    in which case let `response origin` be the same as the
    `interface origin`, if any.

5.  If there is no `interface origin`, then let `trusted operation` be
    true. Otherwise, let `trusted operation` be true if
    `response origin` is the
    <a href="#same-origin" id="downloading-resources:same-origin">same
    origin</a> as `interface origin`, and false otherwise.

6.  If `trusted operation` is true and `response` has a
    \`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html"
    data-x-internal="http-content-disposition"><code
    id="downloading-resources:http-content-disposition-4">Content-Disposition</code></a>\`
    header and that header includes filename information, then let
    `filename` have the value specified by the header, and jump to the
    step labeled *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#refsRFC6266)

7.  If the download was not initiated from a <a href="#hyperlink"
    id="downloading-resources:hyperlink-2">hyperlink</a> created by an
    [`a`](#the-a-element) or [`area`](#the-area-element) element, or if
    the element of the <a href="#hyperlink"
    id="downloading-resources:hyperlink-3">hyperlink</a> from which it
    was initiated did not have a [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download)
    attribute when the download was initiated, or if there was such an
    attribute but its value when the download was initiated was the
    empty string, then jump to the step labeled *no proposed filename*.

8.  Let `proposed filename` have the value of the
    [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute of the element of
    the <a href="#hyperlink"
    id="downloading-resources:hyperlink-4">hyperlink</a> that initiated
    the download at the time the download was initiated.

9.  If `trusted operation` is true, let `filename` have the value of
    `proposed filename`, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

10. If `response` has a
    \`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html"
    data-x-internal="http-content-disposition"><code
    id="downloading-resources:http-content-disposition-5">Content-Disposition</code></a>\`
    header and that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type,
    let `filename` have the value of `proposed filename`, and jump to
    the step labeled *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#refsRFC6266)

11. *No proposed filename*: If `trusted operation` is true, or if the
    user indicated a preference for having the response in question
    downloaded, let `filename` have a value derived from the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
    id="downloading-resources:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> of
    `response` in an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="downloading-resources:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    manner, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

12. Let `filename` be set to the user's preferred filename or to a
    filename selected by the user agent, and jump to the step labeled
    *sanitize* below.

    <div class="warning">

    If the algorithm reaches this step, then a download was begun from a
    different origin than `response`, and the origin did not mark the
    file as suitable for downloading, and the download was not initiated
    by the user. This could be because a
    [`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute was used to trigger
    the download, or because `response` is not of a type that the user
    agent supports.

    This could be dangerous, because, for instance, a hostile server
    could be trying to get a user to unknowingly download private
    information and then re-upload it to the hostile server, by tricking
    the user into thinking the data is from the hostile server.

    Thus, it is in the user's interests that the user be somehow
    notified that `response` comes from quite a different source, and to
    prevent confusion, any suggested filename from the potentially
    hostile `interface origin` should be ignored.

    </div>

13. *Sanitize*: Optionally, allow the user to influence `filename`. For
    example, a user agent could prompt the user for a filename,
    potentially providing the value of `filename` as determined above as
    a default value.

14. Adjust `filename` to be suitable for the local file system.

    For example, this could involve removing characters that are not
    legal in filenames, or trimming leading and trailing whitespace.

15. If the platform conventions do not in any way use
    <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension">extensions</a> to
    determine the types of file on the file system, then return
    `filename` as the filename.

16. Let `claimed type` be the type given by `response`'s
    <a href="#content-type"
    id="downloading-resources:content-type">Content-Type metadata</a>,
    if any is known. Let `named type` be the type given by `filename`'s
    <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension-2">extension</a>, if any
    is known. For the purposes of this step, a *type* is a mapping of a
    <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
    id="downloading-resources:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
    type</a> to an <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension-3">extension</a>.

17. If `named type` is consistent with the user's preferences (e.g.,
    because the value of `filename` was determined by prompting the
    user), then return `filename` as the filename.

18. If `claimed type` and `named type` are the same type (i.e., the type
    given by `response`'s <a href="#content-type"
    id="downloading-resources:content-type-2">Content-Type metadata</a>
    is consistent with the type given by `filename`'s
    <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension-4">extension</a>), then
    return `filename` as the filename.

19. If the `claimed type` is known, then alter `filename` to add an
    <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension-5">extension</a>
    corresponding to `claimed type`.

    Otherwise, if `named type` is known to be potentially dangerous
    (e.g. it will be treated by the platform conventions as a native
    executable, shell script, HTML application, or
    executable-macro-capable document), then optionally alter `filename`
    to add a known-safe <a href="#concept-extension"
    id="downloading-resources:concept-extension-6">extension</a> (e.g.
    "`.txt`").

    This last step would make it impossible to download executables,
    which might not be desirable. As always, implementers are forced to
    balance security and usability in this matter.

20. Return `filename` as the filename.

</div>

For the purposes of this algorithm, a file <span id="concept-extension"
class="dfn">extension</span> consists of any part of the filename that
platform conventions dictate will be used for identifying the type of
the file. For example, many operating systems use the part of the
filename following the last dot ("`.`") in the filename to determine the
type of the file, and from that the manner in which the file is to be
opened or executed.

User agents should ignore any directory or path information provided by
the response itself, its
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="downloading-resources:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>, and any
[`download`](#attr-hyperlink-download) attribute, in deciding where to
store the resulting file in the user's file system.

#### <span class="secno">4.6.7</span> <span class="dfn">Hyperlink auditing</span><a href="#hyperlink-auditing" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

If a
<a href="#hyperlink" id="hyperlink-auditing:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>
created by an [`a`](#the-a-element) or [`area`](#the-area-element)
element has a [`ping`](#ping) attribute, and the user follows the
hyperlink, and the value of the element's [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href)
attribute can be <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
id="hyperlink-auditing:encoding-parsing-a-url">parsed</a>, relative to
the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="hyperlink-auditing:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, without failure, then
the user agent must take the [`ping`](#ping) attribute's value,
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-ascii-whitespace"
id="hyperlink-auditing:split-a-string-on-spaces"
data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-spaces">split that string on ASCII
whitespace</a>, <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
id="hyperlink-auditing:encoding-parsing-a-url-2">parse</a> each
resulting token, relative to the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="hyperlink-auditing:node-document-2"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, and then run these
steps for each resulting
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="hyperlink-auditing:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `ping URL`,
ignoring when parsing returns failure:

1.  If `ping URL`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-url-scheme"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is not an
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:http(s)-scheme"
    data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a>, then return.

2.  Optionally, return. (For example, the user agent might wish to
    ignore any or all ping URLs in accordance with the user's expressed
    preferences.)

3.  Let `settingsObject` be the element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>.

4.  Let `request` be a new
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request"
    data-x-internal="concept-request">request</a> whose
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-url"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-url">URL</a> is `ping URL`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-method"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-method"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-method">method</a> is \``POST`\`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-header-list"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-header-list"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-header-list">header list</a> is «
    (\`[`Content-Type`](#content-type)\`, \`[`text/ping`](#text/ping)\`)
    », <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-body"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-body"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-body">body</a> is \``PING`\`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-client"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-client">client</a> is
    `settingsObject`,
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-destination"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a> is the
    empty string, <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-credentials-mode"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
    is "`include`",
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-referrer"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-referrer">referrer</a> is
    "`no-referrer`", and whose <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:use-url-credentials-flag"
    data-x-internal="use-url-credentials-flag">use-URL-credentials flag</a>
    is set, and whose
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-request-initiator-type"
    data-x-internal="concept-request-initiator-type">initiator type</a>
    is "`ping`".

5.  Let `target URL` be the result of
    <a href="#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url">encoding-parsing-and-serializing
    a URL</a> given the element's [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href)
    attribute's value, relative to the element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:node-document-4"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, and then:

    If the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:the-document&#39;s-address"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> of the [`Document`](#document) object containing the hyperlink being audited and `ping URL` have the <a href="#same-origin" id="hyperlink-auditing:same-origin">same
    origin</a>  
    If the origins are different, but the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-url-scheme-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> of the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> of the [`Document`](#document) containing the hyperlink being audited is not "`https`"  
    `request` must include a \`[`Ping-From`](#ping-from)\` header with,
    as its value, the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:the-document&#39;s-address-3"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> of the document
    containing the hyperlink, and a \`[`Ping-To`](#ping-to)\` HTTP
    header with, as its value, the `target URL`.

    Otherwise  
    `request` must include a \`[`Ping-To`](#ping-to)\` HTTP header with,
    as its value, `target URL`. <span class="note">`request` does not
    include a \`[`Ping-From`](#ping-from)\` header.</span>

6.  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
    id="hyperlink-auditing:concept-fetch"
    data-x-internal="concept-fetch">Fetch</a> `request`.

</div>

This may be done
<a href="#in-parallel" id="hyperlink-auditing:in-parallel">in
parallel</a> with the primary fetch, and is independent of the result of
that fetch.

User agents should allow the user to adjust this behavior, for example
in conjunction with a setting that disables the sending of HTTP
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.referer"
data-x-internal="http-referer"><code
id="hyperlink-auditing:http-referer">Referer</code></a>\` (sic) headers.
Based on the user's preferences, UAs may either
<a href="#ignore" id="hyperlink-auditing:ignore">ignore</a> the
[`ping`](#ping) attribute altogether, or selectively ignore URLs in the
list (e.g. ignoring any third-party URLs); this is explicitly accounted
for in the steps above.

User agents must ignore any entity bodies returned in the responses.
User agents may close the connection prematurely once they start
receiving a response body.

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="hyperlink-auditing:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> An [`a`](#the-a-element) or
[`area`](#the-area-element) element that creates a
<a href="#hyperlink" id="hyperlink-auditing:hyperlink-2">hyperlink</a>
and has the [`ping`](#ping) attribute is present, user agents may
indicate to the user that following the hyperlink will also cause
secondary requests to be sent in the background, possibly including
listing the actual target URLs.

For example, a visual user agent could include the hostnames of the
target ping URLs along with the hyperlink's actual URL in a status bar
or tooltip.

<div class="note">

The [`ping`](#ping) attribute is redundant with pre-existing
technologies like HTTP redirects and JavaScript in allowing web pages to
track which off-site links are most popular or allowing advertisers to
track click-through rates.

However, the [`ping`](#ping) attribute provides these advantages to the
user over those alternatives:

- It allows the user to see the final target URL unobscured.
- It allows the UA to inform the user about the out-of-band
  notifications.
- It allows the UA to optimize the use of available network bandwidth so
  that the target page loads faster.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.6.7.1</span> The \`[`Ping-From`](#ping-from)\` and \`[`Ping-To`](#ping-to)\` headers<a href="#the-ping-headers" class="self-link"></a>

The \`<span id="ping-from" class="dfn"
dfn-type="http-header">`Ping-From`</span>\` and \`<span id="ping-to"
class="dfn" dfn-type="http-header">`Ping-To`</span>\` HTTP request
headers are included in <a href="#hyperlink-auditing"
id="the-ping-headers:hyperlink-auditing">hyperlink auditing</a>
requests. Their value is a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-ping-headers:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>,
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
id="the-ping-headers:concept-url-serializer"
data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialized</a>.

</div>

</div>

The following table summarizes the link types that are defined by this
specification, by their corresponding keywords. This table is
non-normative; the actual definitions for the link types are given in
the next few sections.

In this section, the term *referenced document* refers to the resource
identified by the element representing the link, and the term *current
document* refers to the resource within which the element representing
the link finds itself.

To determine which link types apply to a [`link`](#the-link-element),
[`a`](#the-a-element), [`area`](#the-area-element), or
[`form`](#the-form-element) element, the element's `rel` attribute must
be <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-ascii-whitespace"
id="linkTypes:split-a-string-on-spaces"
data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-spaces">split on ASCII whitespace</a>.
The resulting tokens are the keywords for the link types that apply to
that element.

Except where otherwise specified, a keyword must not be specified more
than once per [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute.

Some of the sections that follow the table below list synonyms for
certain keywords. The indicated synonyms are to be handled as specified
by user agents, but must not be used in documents (for example, the
keyword "`copyright`").

Keywords are always
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="linkTypes:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>, and
must be compared as such.

Thus, `rel="next"` is the same as `rel="NEXT"`.

Keywords that are <span id="body-ok" class="dfn">body-ok</span> affect
whether [`link`](#the-link-element) elements are
<a href="#allowed-in-the-body"
id="linkTypes:allowed-in-the-body">allowed in the body</a>. The
<a href="#body-ok" id="linkTypes:body-ok">body-ok</a> keywords are
[`dns-prefetch`](#link-type-dns-prefetch),
[`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload),
[`pingback`](#link-type-pingback),
[`preconnect`](#link-type-preconnect),
[`prefetch`](#link-type-prefetch), [`preload`](#link-type-preload), and
[`stylesheet`](#link-type-stylesheet).

New link types that are to be implemented by web browsers are to be
added to this standard. The remainder can be
<a href="#concept-rel-extensions"
id="linkTypes:concept-rel-extensions">registered as extensions</a>.

| Link type | Effect on... |  |  | <a href="#body-ok" id="linkTypes:body-ok-2">body-ok</a> | Has \`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header"
data-x-internal="http-link"><code
id="linkTypes:http-link">Link</code></a>\` processing | Brief description |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | [`link`](#the-link-element) | [`a`](#the-a-element) and [`area`](#the-area-element) | [`form`](#the-form-element) |  |  |  |
| [`alternate`](#rel-alternate) | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink">Hyperlink</a> |  | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives alternate representations of the current document. |
| [`canonical`](#link-type-canonical) | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink-2">Hyperlink</a> | *not allowed* |  | · | · | Gives the preferred URL for the current document. |
| [`author`](#link-type-author) | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink-3">Hyperlink</a> |  | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives a link to the author of the current document or article. |
| [`bookmark`](#link-type-bookmark) | *not allowed* | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink-4">Hyperlink</a> | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives the permalink for the nearest ancestor section. |
| [`dns-prefetch`](#link-type-dns-prefetch) | <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="linkTypes:external-resource-link">External Resource</a> | *not allowed* |  | Yes | · | Specifies that the user agent should preemptively perform DNS resolution for the target resource's <a href="#concept-origin" id="linkTypes:concept-origin">origin</a>. |
| [`expect`](#link-type-expect) | <a href="#internal-resource-link"
id="linkTypes:internal-resource-link">Internal Resource</a> | *not allowed* |  | · | · | Expect an element with the target ID to appear in the current document. |
| [`external`](#link-type-external) | *not allowed* | <a href="#hyperlink-annotation"
id="linkTypes:hyperlink-annotation">Annotation</a> |  | · | · | Indicates that the referenced document is not part of the same site as the current document. |
| [`help`](#link-type-help) | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink-5">Hyperlink</a> |  |  | · | · | Provides a link to context-sensitive help. |
| [`icon`](#rel-icon) | <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="linkTypes:external-resource-link-2">External Resource</a> | *not allowed* |  | · | · | Imports an icon to represent the current document. |
| [`manifest`](#link-type-manifest) | <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="linkTypes:external-resource-link-3">External Resource</a> | *not allowed* |  | · | · | Imports or links to an <a href="https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-manifest"
id="linkTypes:application-manifest"

| [`modulepreload`](#link-type-modulepreload) | <a href="#external-resource-link"
id="linkTypes:external-resource-link-4">External Resource</a> | *not allowed* |  | Yes | · | Specifies that the user agent must preemptively <a href="#fetch-a-single-module-script"

id="linkTypes:concept-document-module-map">module map</a> for later evaluation. Optionally, the module's dependencies can be fetched as well. |
| [`license`](#link-type-license) | <a href="#hyperlink" id="linkTypes:hyperlink-6">Hyperlink</a> |  |  | · | · | Indicates that the main content of the current document is covered by the copyright license described by the referenced document. |

id="linkTypes:hyperlink-annotation-5">Annotation</a> |  | · | · | Creates an <a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
