The <span id="attr-iframe-srcdoc" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`srcdoc`</span> attribute gives the content of
the page that the element's <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-4">content navigable</a> is to
contain. The value of the attribute is used to
<a href="#create-navigation-params-from-a-srcdoc-resource"
id="the-iframe-element:create-navigation-params-from-a-srcdoc-resource">construct</a>
<span id="an-iframe-srcdoc-document" class="dfn" export="">an `iframe`
`srcdoc` document</span>, which is a [`Document`](#document) whose
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
id="the-iframe-element:the-document&#39;s-address"
data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>
<a href="#matches-about:srcdoc"
id="the-iframe-element:matches-about:srcdoc">matches
<code>about:srcdoc</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

The [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute, if present, must have a
value using
<a href="#syntax" id="the-iframe-element:syntax">the HTML syntax</a>
that consists of the following syntactic components, in the given order:

1.  Any number of <a href="#syntax-comments"
    id="the-iframe-element:syntax-comments">comments</a> and
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="the-iframe-element:space-characters"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>.
2.  Optionally, a <a href="#syntax-doctype"
    id="the-iframe-element:syntax-doctype">DOCTYPE</a>.
3.  Any number of <a href="#syntax-comments"
    id="the-iframe-element:syntax-comments-2">comments</a> and
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="the-iframe-element:space-characters-2"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>.
4.  The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="the-iframe-element:document-element"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>, in the form
    of an [`html`](#the-html-element) <a href="#syntax-elements"
    id="the-iframe-element:syntax-elements">element</a>.
5.  Any number of <a href="#syntax-comments"
    id="the-iframe-element:syntax-comments-3">comments</a> and
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="the-iframe-element:space-characters-3"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>.

</div>

The above requirements apply in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document"
id="the-iframe-element:xml-documents"
data-x-internal="xml-documents">XML documents</a> as well.

<div class="example">

Here a blog uses the [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute in
conjunction with the [`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute
described below to provide users of user agents that support this
feature with an extra layer of protection from script injection in the
blog post comments:

``` html
<article>
 <h1>I got my own magazine!</h1>
 <p>After much effort, I've finally found a publisher, and so now I
 have my own magazine! Isn't that awesome?! The first issue will come
 out in September, and we have articles about getting food, and about
 getting in boxes, it's going to be great!</p>
 <footer>
  <p>Written by <a href="/users/cap">cap</a>, 1 hour ago.
 </footer>
 <article>
  <footer> Thirteen minutes ago, <a href="/users/ch">ch</a> wrote: </footer>
  <iframe sandbox srcdoc="<p>did you get a cover picture yet?"></iframe>
 </article>
 <article>
  <footer> Nine minutes ago, <a href="/users/cap">cap</a> wrote: </footer>
  <iframe sandbox srcdoc="<p>Yeah, you can see it <a href=&quot;/gallery?mode=cover&amp;amp;page=1&quot;>in my gallery</a>."></iframe>
 </article>
 <article>
  <footer> Five minutes ago, <a href="/users/ch">ch</a> wrote: </footer>
  <iframe sandbox srcdoc="<p>hey that's earl's table.
<p>you should get earl&amp;amp;me on the next cover."></iframe>
 </article>
```

Notice the way that quotes have to be escaped (otherwise the
[`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute would end prematurely), and
the way raw ampersands (e.g. in URLs or in prose) mentioned in the
sandboxed content have to be *doubly* escaped — once so that the
ampersand is preserved when originally parsing the
[`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute, and once more to prevent the
ampersand from being misinterpreted when parsing the sandboxed content.

Furthermore, notice that since the <a href="#syntax-doctype"
id="the-iframe-element:syntax-doctype-2">DOCTYPE</a> is optional in
<a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
id="the-iframe-element:an-iframe-srcdoc-document"><code>iframe</code>
<code>srcdoc</code> documents</a>, and the [`html`](#the-html-element),
[`head`](#the-head-element), and [`body`](#the-body-element) elements
have <a href="#syntax-tag-omission"
id="the-iframe-element:syntax-tag-omission">optional start and end
tags</a>, and the [`title`](#the-title-element) element is also optional
in <a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
id="the-iframe-element:an-iframe-srcdoc-document-2"><code>iframe</code>
<code>srcdoc</code> documents</a>, the markup in a
[`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute can be relatively succinct
despite representing an entire document, since only the contents of the
[`body`](#the-body-element) element need appear literally in the syntax.
The other elements are still present, but only by implication.

</div>

In
<a href="#syntax" id="the-iframe-element:syntax-2">the HTML syntax</a>,
authors need only remember to use U+0022 QUOTATION MARK characters (")
to wrap the attribute contents and then to escape all U+0026 AMPERSAND
(&) and U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (") characters, and to specify the
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute, to ensure safe embedding of
content. (And remember to escape ampersands before quotation marks, to
ensure quotation marks become &quot; and not &amp;quot;.)

In XML the U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character (\<) needs to be escaped as
well. In order to prevent [attribute-value
normalization](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#AVNormalize), some of XML's
whitespace characters — specifically U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab),
U+000A LINE FEED (LF), and U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) — also need to be
escaped. [\[XML\]](#refsXML)

If the [`src`](#attr-iframe-src) attribute and the
[`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute are both specified together,
the [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute takes priority. This
allows authors to provide a fallback
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-iframe-element:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> for legacy
user agents that do not support the [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc)
attribute.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
<a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="the-iframe-element:html-element-post-connection-steps">HTML element
post-connection steps</a>, given `insertedNode`, are:

1.  <a href="#create-a-new-child-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:create-a-new-child-navigable">Create a new child
    navigable</a> for `insertedNode`.

2.  If `insertedNode` has a [`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute,
    then <a href="#parse-a-sandboxing-directive"
    id="the-iframe-element:parse-a-sandboxing-directive">parse the
    sandboxing directive</a> given the attribute's value and
    `insertedNode`'s <a href="#iframe-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="the-iframe-element:iframe-sandboxing-flag-set"><code>iframe</code>
    sandboxing flag set</a>.

3.  <a href="#process-the-iframe-attributes"
    id="the-iframe-element:process-the-iframe-attributes">Process the
    <code>iframe</code> attributes</a> for `insertedNode`, with
    *[initialInsertion](#process-iframe-initial-insertion)* set to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
<a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="the-iframe-element:html-element-removing-steps">HTML element
removing steps</a>, given `removedNode`, are to
<a href="#destroy-a-child-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:destroy-a-child-navigable">destroy a child
navigable</a> given `removedNode`.

</div>

This happens without any [`unload`](#event-unload) events firing (the
element's <a href="#concept-bcc-content-document"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-bcc-content-document">content
document</a> is *<a href="#destroy-a-child-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:destroy-a-child-navigable-2">destroyed</a>*, not
*<a href="#unload-a-document"
id="the-iframe-element:unload-a-document">unloaded</a>*).

Although [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)s are processed while in a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-iframe-element:shadow-tree" data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow
tree</a>, per the above, several other aspects of their behavior are not
well-defined with regards to shadow trees. See [issue
\#763](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/763) for more detail.

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element with a non-null
<a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-5">content navigable</a> has
its [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute set, changed, or removed,
the user agent must <a href="#process-the-iframe-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:process-the-iframe-attributes-2">process the
<code>iframe</code> attributes</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Similarly, whenever an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element with a
non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-6">content navigable</a> but
with no [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute specified has its
[`src`](#attr-iframe-src) attribute set, changed, or removed, the user
agent must <a href="#process-the-iframe-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:process-the-iframe-attributes-3">process the
<code>iframe</code> attributes</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="process-the-iframe-attributes" class="dfn">process the
`iframe` attributes</span> for an element `element`, with an optional
boolean <span id="process-iframe-initial-insertion"
class="dfn">`initialInsertion`</span> (default false):

1.  If `element`'s [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute is
    specified, then:

    1.  Set `element`'s <a href="#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded"
        id="the-iframe-element:current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded">current
        navigation was lazy loaded</a> boolean to false.

    2.  If the <a href="#will-lazy-load-element-steps"
        id="the-iframe-element:will-lazy-load-element-steps">will lazy load
        element steps</a> given `element` return true, then:

        1.  Set `element`'s <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
            id="the-iframe-element:lazy-load-resumption-steps">lazy load resumption
            steps</a> to the rest of this algorithm starting with the
            step labeled *navigate to the srcdoc resource*.

        2.  Set `element`'s
            <a href="#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded"
            id="the-iframe-element:current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded-2">current
            navigation was lazy loaded</a> boolean to true.

        3.  <a href="#start-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element"
            id="the-iframe-element:start-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element">Start
            intersection-observing a lazy loading element</a> for
            `element`.

        4.  Return.

    3.  *Navigate to the srcdoc resource*:
        <a href="#navigate-an-iframe-or-frame"
        id="the-iframe-element:navigate-an-iframe-or-frame">Navigate an
        <code>iframe</code> or <code>frame</code></a> given `element`,
        [`about:srcdoc`](#about:srcdoc), the empty string, and the value
        of `element`'s [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute.

        The resulting [`Document`](#document) must be considered
        <a href="#an-iframe-srcdoc-document"
        id="the-iframe-element:an-iframe-srcdoc-document-3">an
        <code>iframe</code> <code>srcdoc</code> document</a>.

2.  Otherwise:

    1.  Let `url` be the result of running the <a
        href="#shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements"
        id="the-iframe-element:shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements">shared
        attribute processing steps for <code>iframe</code> and
        <code>frame</code> elements</a> given `element` and
        `initialInsertion`.

    2.  If `url` is null, then return.

    3.  If `url` <a href="#matches-about:blank"
        id="the-iframe-element:matches-about:blank">matches
        <code>about:blank</code></a> and `initialInsertion` is true,
        then:

        1.  Run the <a href="#iframe-load-event-steps"
            id="the-iframe-element:iframe-load-event-steps">iframe load event
            steps</a> given `element`.

        2.  Return.

    4.  Let `referrerPolicy` be the current state of `element`'s
        [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-iframe-referrerpolicy) content
        attribute.

    5.  Set `element`'s <a href="#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded"
        id="the-iframe-element:current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded-3">current
        navigation was lazy loaded</a> boolean to false.

    6.  If the <a href="#will-lazy-load-element-steps"
        id="the-iframe-element:will-lazy-load-element-steps-2">will lazy load
        element steps</a> given `element` return true, then:

        1.  Set `element`'s <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
            id="the-iframe-element:lazy-load-resumption-steps-2">lazy load
            resumption steps</a> to the rest of this algorithm starting
            with the step labeled *navigate*.

        2.  Set `element`'s
            <a href="#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded"
            id="the-iframe-element:current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded-4">current
            navigation was lazy loaded</a> boolean to true.

        3.  <a href="#start-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element"
            id="the-iframe-element:start-intersection-observing-a-lazy-loading-element-2">Start
            intersection-observing a lazy loading element</a> for
            `element`.

        4.  Return.

    7.  *Navigate*: <a href="#navigate-an-iframe-or-frame"
        id="the-iframe-element:navigate-an-iframe-or-frame-2">Navigate an
        <code>iframe</code> or <code>frame</code></a> given `element`,
        `url`, and `referrerPolicy`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The
<span id="shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements"
class="dfn">shared attribute processing steps for `iframe` and `frame`
elements</span>, given an element `element` and a boolean
`initialInsertion`, are:

1.  Let `url` be the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
    id="the-iframe-element:url-record" data-x-internal="url-record">URL
    record</a> [`about:blank`](#about:blank).

2.  If `element` has a [`src`](#attr-iframe-src) attribute specified,
    and its value is not the empty string, then:

    1.  Let `maybeURL` be the result of
        <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
        id="the-iframe-element:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a
        URL</a> given that attribute's value, relative to `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-iframe-element:node-document"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

    2.  If `maybeURL` is not failure, then set `url` to `maybeURL`.

3.  If the <a href="#inclusive-ancestor-navigables"
    id="the-iframe-element:inclusive-ancestor-navigables">inclusive ancestor
    navigables</a> of `element`'s
    <a href="#node-navigable" id="the-iframe-element:node-navigable">node
    navigable</a> contains a
    <a href="#navigable" id="the-iframe-element:navigable">navigable</a>
    whose
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document">active
    document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="the-iframe-element:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals"
    id="the-iframe-element:concept-url-equals"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-equals">equals</a> `url` with
    *<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-equals-exclude-fragments"
    data-x-internal="url-equals-exclude-fragments">exclude fragments</a>*
    set to true, then return null.

4.  If `url` <a href="#matches-about:blank"
    id="the-iframe-element:matches-about:blank-2">matches
    <code>about:blank</code></a> and `initialInsertion` is true, then
    perform the <a href="#url-and-history-update-steps"
    id="the-iframe-element:url-and-history-update-steps">URL and history
    update steps</a> given `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-7">content navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-2">active
    document</a> and `url`.

    This is necessary in case `url` is something like `about:blank?foo`.
    If `url` is just plain `about:blank`, this will do nothing.

5.  Return `url`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="navigate-an-iframe-or-frame" class="dfn">navigate an
`iframe` or `frame`</span> given an element `element`, a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-iframe-element:url-3" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `url`, a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:referrer-policy-2"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> `referrerPolicy`,
an optional string-or-null `srcdocString` (default null), and an
optional boolean `initialInsertion` (default false):

1.  Let `historyHandling` be
    "[`auto`](#navigationhistorybehavior-auto)".

2.  If `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-8">content navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-3">active
    document</a> is not <a href="#completely-loaded"
    id="the-iframe-element:completely-loaded">completely loaded</a>,
    then set `historyHandling` to
    "[`replace`](#navigationhistorybehavior-replace)".

3.  If `element` is an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), then set
    `element`'s <a href="#iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time"
    id="the-iframe-element:iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time">pending
    resource-timing start time</a> to the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
    id="the-iframe-element:current-high-resolution-time"
    data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
    time</a> given `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-iframe-element:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-iframe-element:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>.

4.  <a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate">Navigate</a>
    `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-9">content navigable</a> to
    `url` using `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-iframe-element:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, with
    *[historyHandling](#navigation-hh)* set to `historyHandling`,
    *[referrerPolicy](#navigation-referrer-policy)* set to
    `referrerPolicy`, *[documentResource](#navigation-resource)* set to
    `srcdocString`, and
    *[initialInsertion](#navigation-initial-insertion)* set to
    `initialInsertion`.

</div>

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="iframe-load-in-progress"
class="dfn">iframe load in progress</span> flag and a
<span id="mute-iframe-load" class="dfn">mute iframe load</span> flag.
When a [`Document`](#document) is created, these flags must be unset for
that [`Document`](#document).

<div algorithm="">

To run the <span id="iframe-load-event-steps" class="dfn">iframe load
event steps</span>, given an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element
`element`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-iframe-element:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-10">content navigable</a>
    is not null.

2.  Let `childDocument` be `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-11">content navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-4">active
    document</a>.

3.  If `childDocument` has its <a href="#mute-iframe-load"
    id="the-iframe-element:mute-iframe-load">mute iframe load</a> flag
    set, then return.

4.  If `element`'s <a href="#iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time"
    id="the-iframe-element:iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time-2">pending
    resource-timing start time</a> is not null, then:

    1.  Let `global` be `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-iframe-element:node-document-4"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="the-iframe-element:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
        object</a>.

    2.  Let `fallbackTimingInfo` be a new
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-timing-info"
        id="the-iframe-element:fetch-timing-info"
        data-x-internal="fetch-timing-info">fetch timing info</a> whose
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-timing-info-start-time"
        id="the-iframe-element:fetch-timing-info-start-time"
        data-x-internal="fetch-timing-info-start-time">start time</a> is
        `element`'s <a href="#iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time"
        id="the-iframe-element:iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time-3">pending
        resource-timing start time</a> and whose
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-timing-info-end-time"
        id="the-iframe-element:fetch-timing-info-end-time"
        data-x-internal="fetch-timing-info-end-time">response end time</a>
        is the <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
        id="the-iframe-element:current-high-resolution-time-2"
        data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
        time</a> given `global`.

    3.  <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-mark-resource-timing"
        id="the-iframe-element:mark-resource-timing"
        data-x-internal="mark-resource-timing">Mark resource timing</a>
        given `fallbackTimingInfo`, `url`,
        "[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)", `global`, the empty string, a
        new <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#response-body-info"
        id="the-iframe-element:response-body-info"
        data-x-internal="response-body-info">response body info</a>, and
        0.

    4.  Set `element`'s
        <a href="#iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time"
        id="the-iframe-element:iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time-4">pending
        resource-timing start time</a> to null.

5.  Set `childDocument`'s <a href="#iframe-load-in-progress"
    id="the-iframe-element:iframe-load-in-progress">iframe load in
    progress</a> flag.

6.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-iframe-element:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`load`](#event-load) at `element`.

7.  Unset `childDocument`'s <a href="#iframe-load-in-progress"
    id="the-iframe-element:iframe-load-in-progress-2">iframe load in
    progress</a> flag.

</div>

This, in conjunction with scripting, can be used to probe the URL space
of the local network's HTTP servers. User agents may implement
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-origin">cross-origin</a> access control
policies that are stricter than those described above to mitigate this
attack, but unfortunately such policies are typically not compatible
with existing web content.

<div algorithm="">

If an element type <span id="potentially-delays-the-load-event"
class="dfn">potentially delays the load event</span>, then for each
element `element` of that type, the user agent must
<a href="#delay-the-load-event"
id="the-iframe-element:delay-the-load-event">delay the load event</a> of
`element`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-iframe-element:node-document-5"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> if `element`'s
<a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-12">content navigable</a> is
non-null and any of the following are true:

- `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
  id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-13">content navigable</a>'s
  <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-5">active
  document</a> is not <a href="#ready-for-post-load-tasks"
  id="the-iframe-element:ready-for-post-load-tasks">ready for post-load
  tasks</a>;

- `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
  id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-14">content navigable</a>'s
  <a href="#delaying-load-events-mode"
  id="the-iframe-element:delaying-load-events-mode">is delaying
  <code>load</code> events</a> is true; or

- anything is <a href="#delay-the-load-event"
  id="the-iframe-element:delay-the-load-event-2">delaying the load
  event</a> of `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
  id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-15">content navigable</a>'s
  <a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-6">active
  document</a>.

If, during the handling of the [`load`](#event-load) event, `element`'s
<a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-16">content navigable</a> is
again
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-2">navigated</a>,
that will further <a href="#delay-the-load-event"
id="the-iframe-element:delay-the-load-event-3">delay the load event</a>.

</div>

Each [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element has an associated
<span id="current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded" class="dfn">current
navigation was lazy loaded</span> boolean, initially false. It is set
and unset in the <a href="#process-the-iframe-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:process-the-iframe-attributes-4">process the
<code>iframe</code> attributes</a> algorithm.

An [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element whose
<a href="#current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded"
id="the-iframe-element:current-navigation-was-lazy-loaded-5">current
navigation was lazy loaded</a> boolean is false
<a href="#potentially-delays-the-load-event"
id="the-iframe-element:potentially-delays-the-load-event">potentially
delays the load event</a>.

Each [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element has an associated null or
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
id="the-iframe-element:domhighrestimestamp"
data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code>DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>
<span id="iframe-pending-resource-timing-start-time" class="dfn">pending
resource-timing start time</span>, initially set to null.

If, when the element is created, the [`srcdoc`](#attr-iframe-srcdoc)
attribute is not set, and the [`src`](#attr-iframe-src) attribute is
either also not set or set but its value cannot be
<a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
id="the-iframe-element:encoding-parsing-a-url-2">parsed</a>, the
element's <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-17">content navigable</a> will
remain at the <a href="#is-initial-about:blank"
id="the-iframe-element:is-initial-about:blank">initial
<code>about:blank</code></a> [`Document`](#document).

If the user
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-3">navigates</a>
away from this page, the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)'s
<a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-18">content navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-wp" id="the-iframe-element:nav-wp">active
<code>WindowProxy</code></a> object will proxy new [`Window`](#window)
objects for new [`Document`](#document) objects, but the
[`src`](#attr-iframe-src) attribute will not change.

The <span id="attr-iframe-sandbox" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`sandbox`</span> attribute, when specified,
enables a set of extra restrictions on any content hosted by the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element). Its value must be an
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="the-iframe-element:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a> that are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-iframe-element:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>. The
allowed values are:

- [`allow-downloads`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-downloads)
- [`allow-forms`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms)
- [`allow-modals`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-modals)
- [`allow-orientation-lock`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-orientation-lock)
- [`allow-pointer-lock`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock)
- [`allow-popups`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups)
- [`allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox)
- [`allow-presentation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-presentation)
- [`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin)
- [`allow-scripts`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts)
- [`allow-top-navigation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation)
- [`allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation)
- [`allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols)

When the attribute is set, the content is treated as being from a unique
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a>, forms,
scripts, and various potentially annoying APIs are disabled, and links
are prevented from targeting other
<a href="#navigable" id="the-iframe-element:navigable-2">navigables</a>.
The [`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin)
keyword causes the content to be treated as being from its real origin
instead of forcing it into an <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-origin-opaque-2">opaque origin</a>; the
[`allow-top-navigation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation)
keyword allows the content to
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-4">navigate</a> its
<a href="#nav-traversable"
id="the-iframe-element:nav-traversable">traversable navigable</a>; the
[`allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation)
keyword behaves similarly but allows such
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-5">navigation</a>
only when the browsing context's
<a href="#nav-window" id="the-iframe-element:nav-window">active
window</a> has <a href="#transient-activation"
id="the-iframe-element:transient-activation">transient activation</a>;
the
[`allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols)
reenables navigations toward non
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-scheme"
id="the-iframe-element:fetch-scheme"
data-x-internal="fetch-scheme">fetch scheme</a> to be
<a href="#hand-off-to-external-software"
id="the-iframe-element:hand-off-to-external-software">handed off to
external software</a>; and the
[`allow-forms`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms),
[`allow-modals`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-modals),
[`allow-orientation-lock`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-orientation-lock),
[`allow-pointer-lock`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock),
[`allow-popups`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups),
[`allow-presentation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-presentation),
[`allow-scripts`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts), and
[`allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox)
keywords re-enable forms, modal dialogs, screen orientation lock, the
pointer lock API, popups, the presentation API, scripts, and the
creation of unsandboxed <a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
id="the-iframe-element:auxiliary-browsing-context">auxiliary browsing
contexts</a> respectively. The
[`allow-downloads`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-downloads) keyword allows
content to perform downloads. [\[POINTERLOCK\]](#refsPOINTERLOCK)
[\[SCREENORIENTATION\]](#refsSCREENORIENTATION)
[\[PRESENTATION\]](#refsPRESENTATION)

The [`allow-top-navigation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation)
and
[`allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation)
keywords must not both be specified, as doing so is redundant; only
[`allow-top-navigation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation) will
have an effect in such non-conformant markup.

Similarly, the
[`allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols)
keyword must not be specified if either
[`allow-top-navigation`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation) or
[`allow-popups`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups) are specified, as
doing so is redundant.

To allow [`alert()`](#dom-alert), [`confirm()`](#dom-confirm), and
[`prompt()`](#dom-prompt) inside sandboxed content, both the
[`allow-modals`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-modals) and
[`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) keywords
need to be specified, and the loaded URL needs to be
<a href="#same-origin" id="the-iframe-element:same-origin">same
origin</a> with the <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
origin</a>. Without the
[`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) keyword,
the content is always treated as cross-origin, and cross-origin content
<a href="#cannot-show-simple-dialogs"
id="the-iframe-element:cannot-show-simple-dialogs">cannot show simple
dialogs</a>.

Setting both the [`allow-scripts`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts)
and [`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin)
keywords together when the embedded page has the
<a href="#same-origin" id="the-iframe-element:same-origin-2">same
origin</a> as the page containing the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
allows the embedded page to simply remove the
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute and then reload itself,
effectively breaking out of the sandbox altogether.

These flags only take effect when the <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-20">content navigable</a> of
the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element is
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-6">navigated</a>.
Removing them, or removing the entire [`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox)
attribute, has no effect on an already-loaded page.

Potentially hostile files should not be served from the same server as
the file containing the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element.
Sandboxing hostile content is of minimal help if an attacker can
convince the user to just visit the hostile content directly, rather
than in the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element). To limit the damage that
can be caused by hostile HTML content, it should be served from a
separate dedicated domain. Using a different domain ensures that scripts
in the files are unable to attack the site, even if the user is tricked
into visiting those pages directly, without the protection of the
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute.

<div algorithm="">

When an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is set or changed while it
has a non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-21">content navigable</a>, the
user agent must <a href="#parse-a-sandboxing-directive"
id="the-iframe-element:parse-a-sandboxing-directive-2">parse the
sandboxing directive</a> given the attribute's value and the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
<a href="#iframe-sandboxing-flag-set"
id="the-iframe-element:iframe-sandboxing-flag-set-2"><code>iframe</code>
sandboxing flag set</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is removed while it has a
non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-22">content navigable</a>, the
user agent must empty the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
<a href="#iframe-sandboxing-flag-set"
id="the-iframe-element:iframe-sandboxing-flag-set-3"><code>iframe</code>
sandboxing flag set</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, some completely-unknown, potentially hostile,
user-provided HTML content is embedded in a page. Because it is served
from a separate domain, it is affected by all the normal cross-site
restrictions. In addition, the embedded page has scripting disabled,
plugins disabled, forms disabled, and it cannot navigate any frames or
windows other than itself (or any frames or windows it itself embeds).

``` html
<p>We're not scared of you! Here is your content, unedited:</p>
<iframe sandbox src="https://usercontent.example.net/getusercontent.cgi?id=12193"></iframe>
```

It is important to use a separate domain so that if the attacker
convinces the user to visit that page directly, the page doesn't run in
the context of the site's origin, which would make the user vulnerable
to any attack found in the page.

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, a gadget from another site is embedded. The gadget has
scripting and forms enabled, and the origin sandbox restrictions are
lifted, allowing the gadget to communicate with its originating server.
The sandbox is still useful, however, as it disables plugins and popups,
thus reducing the risk of the user being exposed to malware and other
annoyances.

``` html
<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-scripts"
        src="https://maps.example.com/embedded.html"></iframe>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Suppose a file A contained the following fragment:

``` html
<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms" src=B></iframe>
```

Suppose that file B contained an iframe also:

``` html
<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src=C></iframe>
```

Further, suppose that file C contained a link:

``` html
<a href=D>Link</a>
```

For this example, suppose all the files were served as
[`text/html`](#text/html).

Page C in this scenario has all the sandboxing flags set. Scripts are
disabled, because the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in A has scripts
disabled, and this overrides the
[`allow-scripts`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts) keyword set on the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in B. Forms are also disabled, because
the inner [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) (in B) does not have the
[`allow-forms`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms) keyword set.

Suppose now that a script in A removes all the
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attributes in A and B. This would
change nothing immediately. If the user clicked the link in C, loading
page D into the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in B, page D would now
act as if the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in B had the
[`allow-same-origin`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) and
[`allow-forms`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms) keywords set, because
that was the state of the <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-23">content navigable</a> in
the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in A when page B was loaded.

Generally speaking, dynamically removing or changing the
[`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is ill-advised, because it
can make it quite hard to reason about what will be allowed and what
will not.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-iframe-allow" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`allow`</span> attribute, when specified,
determines the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#container-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-container-policy"
data-x-internal="concept-container-policy">container policy</a> that
will be used when the <a href="#concept-document-permissions-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-permissions-policy">permissions
policy</a> for a [`Document`](#document) in the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)'s <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-24">content navigable</a> is
initialized. Its value must be a <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#serialized-permissions-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-serialized-permissions-policy"
data-x-internal="concept-serialized-permissions-policy">serialized
permissions policy</a>. [\[PERMISSIONSPOLICY\]](#refsPERMISSIONSPOLICY)

<div class="example">

In this example, an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) is used to embed a
map from an online navigation service. The [`allow`](#attr-iframe-allow)
attribute is used to enable the Geolocation API within the nested
context.

``` html
<iframe src="https://maps.example.com/" allow="geolocation"></iframe>
```

</div>

The <span id="attr-iframe-allowfullscreen" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`allowfullscreen`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-iframe-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>. When
specified, it indicates that [`Document`](#document) objects in the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-25">content navigable</a> will
be initialized with a <a href="#concept-document-permissions-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-permissions-policy-2">permissions
policy</a> which allows the "`fullscreen`" feature to be used from any
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-origin-2">origin</a>. This is enforced by
the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#process-permissions-policy-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:process-permissions-policy-attributes"
data-x-internal="process-permissions-policy-attributes">process
permissions policy attributes</a> algorithm.
[\[PERMISSIONSPOLICY\]](#refsPERMISSIONSPOLICY)

<div class="example">

Here, an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) is used to embed a player from
a video site. The [`allowfullscreen`](#attr-iframe-allowfullscreen)
attribute is needed to enable the player to show its video fullscreen.

``` html
<article>
 <header>
  <p><img src="/usericons/1627591962735"> <b>Fred Flintstone</b></p>
  <p><a href="/posts/3095182851" rel=bookmark>12:44</a> — <a href="#acl-3095182851">Private Post</a></p>
 </header>
 <p>Check out my new ride!</p>
 <iframe src="https://video.example.com/embed?id=92469812" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</article>
```

</div>

Neither [`allow`](#attr-iframe-allow) nor
[`allowfullscreen`](#attr-iframe-allowfullscreen) can grant access to a
feature in an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element's
<a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-26">content navigable</a> if
the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-iframe-element:node-document-6"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is not already allowed
to use that feature.

<div algorithm="">

To determine whether a [`Document`](#document) object `document` is
<span id="allowed-to-use" class="dfn" export="">allowed to use</span>
the policy-controlled-feature `feature`, run these steps:

1.  If `document`'s <a href="#concept-document-bc"
    id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-bc">browsing context</a> is
    null, then return false.

2.  If `document` is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="the-iframe-element:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return false.

3.  If the result of running <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#is-feature-enabled"
    id="the-iframe-element:is-feature-enabled"
    data-x-internal="is-feature-enabled">is feature enabled in document for
    origin</a> on `feature`, `document`, and `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is "`Enabled`",
    then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

Because they only influence the
<a href="#concept-document-permissions-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-permissions-policy-3">permissions
policy</a> of the <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-27">content navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-document" id="the-iframe-element:nav-document-7">active
document</a>, the [`allow`](#attr-iframe-allow) and
[`allowfullscreen`](#attr-iframe-allowfullscreen) attributes only take
effect when the <a href="#content-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:content-navigable-28">content navigable</a> of
the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) is
<a href="#navigate" id="the-iframe-element:navigate-7">navigated</a>.
Adding or removing them has no effect on an already-loaded document.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element supports
<a href="#dimension-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:dimension-attributes">dimension attributes</a>
for cases where the embedded content has specific dimensions (e.g. ad
units have well-defined dimensions).

An [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element never has
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-iframe-element:fallback-content">fallback content</a>, as it
will always <a href="#create-a-new-child-navigable"
id="the-iframe-element:create-a-new-child-navigable-3">create a new
child navigable</a>, regardless of whether the specified initial
contents are successfully used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-iframe-referrerpolicy" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`referrerpolicy`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
id="the-iframe-element:referrer-policy-attribute">referrer policy
attribute</a>. Its purpose is to set the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-iframe-element:referrer-policy-3"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> used when
<a href="#process-the-iframe-attributes"
id="the-iframe-element:process-the-iframe-attributes-5">processing the
<code>iframe</code> attributes</a> as well as allowing masking of some
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="the-iframe-element:concept-document-origin-2"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origins</a> in the
<a href="#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps"
id="the-iframe-element:internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps">internal
ancestor origin objects list creation steps</a>.
[\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

The <span id="attr-iframe-loading" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe"
dfn-type="element-attr">`loading`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#lazy-loading-attribute"
id="the-iframe-element:lazy-loading-attribute">lazy loading
attribute</a>. Its purpose is to indicate the policy for loading
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) elements that are outside the viewport.

<div algorithm="">

When the [`loading`](#attr-iframe-loading) attribute's state is changed
to the <a href="#attr-loading-eager-state"
id="the-iframe-element:attr-loading-eager-state">Eager</a> state, the
user agent must run these steps:

1.  Let `resumptionSteps` be the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
    element's <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
    id="the-iframe-element:lazy-load-resumption-steps-3">lazy load
    resumption steps</a>.

2.  If `resumptionSteps` is null, then return.

3.  Set the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)'s
    <a href="#lazy-load-resumption-steps"
    id="the-iframe-element:lazy-load-resumption-steps-4">lazy load
    resumption steps</a> to null.

4.  Invoke `resumptionSteps`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Descendants of [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) elements represent
nothing. (In legacy user agents that do not support
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) elements, the contents would be parsed
as markup that could act as fallback content.)

The <a href="#html-parser" id="the-iframe-element:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> treats markup inside [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) elements
as text.

[`type`](#attr-embed-type) — Type of embedded resource

[`width`](#attr-dim-width) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#attr-dim-height) — Vertical dimension

Any other attribute that has no namespace (see prose).

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-embed-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-embed).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-embed).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-embed-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLEmbedElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString width;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString height;
  Document? getSVGDocument();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element provides an integration point
for an external application or interactive content.

The <span id="attr-embed-src" class="dfn" dfn-for="embed"
dfn-type="element-attr">`src`</span> attribute gives the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-embed-element:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> of the resource
being embedded. The attribute, if present, must contain a
<a href="#valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="the-embed-element:valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>.

If the [`itemprop`](#names:-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is
specified on an [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element, then the
[`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute must also be specified.

The <span id="attr-embed-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="embed"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute, if present, gives the
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="the-embed-element:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
type</a> by which the plugin to instantiate is selected. The value must
be a <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type"
id="the-embed-element:valid-mime-type-string"
data-x-internal="valid-mime-type-string">valid MIME type string</a>. If
both the [`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute and the
[`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute are present, then the
[`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute must specify the same type as the
<a href="#content-type" id="the-embed-element:content-type">explicit
Content-Type metadata</a> of the resource given by the
[`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute.

<div algorithm="">

While any of the following conditions are occurring, any
<a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin">plugin</a> instantiated
for the element must be removed, and the [`embed`](#the-embed-element)
element
<a href="#represents" id="the-embed-element:represents">represents</a>
nothing:

- The element has neither a [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute nor a
  [`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute.

- The element has a
  <a href="#media-element" id="the-embed-element:media-element">media
  element</a> ancestor.

- The element has an ancestor [`object`](#the-object-element) element
  that is *not* showing its <a href="#fallback-content"
  id="the-embed-element:fallback-content">fallback content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element is said to be
<span id="concept-embed-active" class="dfn">potentially active</span>
when the following conditions are all met simultaneously:

- The element is <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document"
  id="the-embed-element:in-a-document" data-x-internal="in-a-document">in
  a document</a> or was
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document"
  id="the-embed-element:in-a-document-2"
  data-x-internal="in-a-document">in a document</a> the last time the
  <a href="#event-loop" id="the-embed-element:event-loop">event loop</a>
  reached [step 1](#step1).

- The element's
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
  id="the-embed-element:node-document"
  data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is
  <a href="#fully-active" id="the-embed-element:fully-active">fully
  active</a>.

- The element has either a [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute set or a
  [`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute set (or both).

- The element's [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute is either absent or
  its value is not the empty string.

- The element is not a descendant of a
  <a href="#media-element" id="the-embed-element:media-element-2">media
  element</a>.

- The element is not a descendant of an [`object`](#the-object-element)
  element that is not showing its <a href="#fallback-content"
  id="the-embed-element:fallback-content-2">fallback content</a>.

- The element is
  <a href="#being-rendered" id="the-embed-element:being-rendered">being
  rendered</a>, or was
  <a href="#being-rendered" id="the-embed-element:being-rendered-2">being
  rendered</a> the last time the
  <a href="#event-loop" id="the-embed-element:event-loop-2">event loop</a>
  reached [step 1](#step1).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element that was not
<a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active">potentially active</a>
becomes <a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active-2">potentially active</a>,
and whenever a <a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active-3">potentially active</a>
[`embed`](#the-embed-element) element that is remaining
<a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active-4">potentially active</a> has
its [`src`](#attr-embed-type) attribute set, changed, or removed or its
[`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute set, changed, or removed, the user
agent must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="the-embed-element:queue-an-element-task">queue an element task</a>
on the <span id="embed-task-source" class="dfn">embed task source</span>
given the element to run <a href="#the-embed-element-setup-steps"
id="the-embed-element:the-embed-element-setup-steps">the
<code>embed</code> element setup steps</a> for that element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="the-embed-element-setup-steps" class="dfn">The `embed` element
setup steps</span> for a given [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element
`element` are as follows:

1.  If another
    <a href="#concept-task" id="the-embed-element:concept-task">task</a>
    has since been queued to run
    <a href="#the-embed-element-setup-steps"
    id="the-embed-element:the-embed-element-setup-steps-2">the
    <code>embed</code> element setup steps</a> for `element`, then
    return.

2.  If `element` has a [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute set, then:

    1.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
        id="the-embed-element:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a URL</a>
        given `element`'s [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute's value,
        relative to `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-embed-element:node-document-2"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

    2.  If `url` is failure, then return.

    3.  Let `request` be a new
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request"
        data-x-internal="concept-request">request</a> whose
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-url"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-url">URL</a> is `url`,
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-client"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-client">client</a> is
        `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-embed-element:node-document-3"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
        <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="the-embed-element:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
        object</a>,
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-destination"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a> is
        "`embed`", <a
        href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-credentials-mode"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
        is "`include`",
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-mode"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-mode">mode</a> is "`navigate`",
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-request-initiator-type"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-initiator-type">initiator type</a>
        is "`embed`", and whose <a
        href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag"
        id="the-embed-element:use-url-credentials-flag"
        data-x-internal="use-url-credentials-flag">use-URL-credentials flag</a>
        is set.

    4.  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-fetch"
        data-x-internal="concept-fetch">Fetch</a> `request`, with
        *<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response"
        data-x-internal="processresponse">processResponse</a>* set to
        the following steps given
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
        id="the-embed-element:concept-response"
        data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response`:

        1.  If another
            <a href="#concept-task" id="the-embed-element:concept-task-2">task</a>
            has since been queued to run
            <a href="#the-embed-element-setup-steps"
            id="the-embed-element:the-embed-element-setup-steps-3">the
            <code>embed</code> element setup steps</a> for `element`,
            then return.

        2.  If `response` is a
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error"
            id="the-embed-element:network-error"
            data-x-internal="network-error">network error</a>, then
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="the-embed-element:concept-event-fire"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
            [`load`](#event-load) at `element`, and return.

        3.  Let `type` be the result of determining the
            <a href="#concept-embed-type"
            id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-type">type of content</a>
            given `element` and `response`.

        4.  Switch on `type`:

            null  
            1.  <a href="#display-no-plugin"
                id="the-embed-element:display-no-plugin">Display no plugin</a>
                for `element`.

            Otherwise  
            1.  If `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
                id="the-embed-element:content-navigable">content navigable</a>
                is null, then <a href="#create-a-new-child-navigable"
                id="the-embed-element:create-a-new-child-navigable">create a new child
                navigable</a> for `element`.

            2.  <a href="#navigate" id="the-embed-element:navigate">Navigate</a>
                `element`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
                id="the-embed-element:content-navigable-2">content navigable</a>
                to `response`'s
                <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
                id="the-embed-element:concept-response-url"
                data-x-internal="concept-response-url">URL</a> using
                `element`'s
                <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
                id="the-embed-element:node-document-4"
                data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, with
                *[response](#navigation-response)* set to `response`,
                and *[historyHandling](#navigation-hh)* set to
                "[`replace`](#navigationhistorybehavior-replace)".

                `element`'s [`src`](#attr-embed-src) attribute does not
                get updated if the <a href="#content-navigable"
                id="the-embed-element:content-navigable-3">content navigable</a>
                gets further navigated to other locations.

            3.  `element` now
                <a href="#represents" id="the-embed-element:represents-2">represents</a>
                its <a href="#content-navigable"
                id="the-embed-element:content-navigable-4">content navigable</a>.

        Fetching the resource must <a href="#delay-the-load-event"
        id="the-embed-element:delay-the-load-event">delay the load event</a>
        of `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-embed-element:node-document-5"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

3.  Otherwise, <a href="#display-no-plugin"
    id="the-embed-element:display-no-plugin-2">display no plugin</a> for
    `element`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To determine the <span id="concept-embed-type" class="dfn">type of the
content</span> given an [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element `element`
and a <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="the-embed-element:concept-response-2"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response`, run the
following steps:

1.  If `element` has a [`type`](#attr-embed-type) attribute, and that
    attribute's value is a type that a
    <a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin-2">plugin</a>
    supports, then return the value of the [`type`](#attr-embed-type)
    attribute.

2.  If the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path"
    id="the-embed-element:concept-url-path"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-path">path</a> component of
    `response`'s
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
    id="the-embed-element:concept-response-url-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-response-url">url</a> matches a pattern
    that a <a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin-3">plugin</a>
    supports, then return the type that that plugin can handle.

    For example, a plugin might say that it can handle URLs with
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path"
    id="the-embed-element:concept-url-path-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-path">path</a> components that end with
    the four character string "`.swf`".

3.  If `response` has
    <a href="#content-type" id="the-embed-element:content-type-2">explicit
    Content-Type metadata</a>, and that value is a type that a
    <a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin-4">plugin</a>
    supports, then return that value.

4.  Return null.

It is intentional that the above algorithm allows `response` to have a
non-<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status"
id="the-embed-element:ok-status" data-x-internal="ok-status">ok
status</a>. This allows servers to return data for plugins even with
error responses (e.g., HTTP 500 Internal Server Error codes can still
contain plugin data).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="display-no-plugin" class="dfn">display no plugin</span> for
an [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element `element`:

1.  <a href="#destroy-a-child-navigable"
    id="the-embed-element:destroy-a-child-navigable">Destroy a child
    navigable</a> given `element`.

2.  Display an indication that no
    <a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin-5">plugin</a> could
    be found for `element`, as the contents of `element`.

3.  `element` now
    <a href="#represents" id="the-embed-element:represents-3">represents</a>
    nothing.

</div>

The [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element has no
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-embed-element:fallback-content-3">fallback content</a>; its
descendants are ignored.

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element that was
<a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active-5">potentially active</a>
stops being <a href="#concept-embed-active"
id="the-embed-element:concept-embed-active-6">potentially active</a>,
any <a href="#plugin" id="the-embed-element:plugin-6">plugin</a> that
had been instantiated for that element must be unloaded.

</div>

The [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element
<a href="#potentially-delays-the-load-event"
id="the-embed-element:potentially-delays-the-load-event">potentially
delays the load event</a>.

The [`embed`](#the-embed-element) element supports
<a href="#dimension-attributes"
id="the-embed-element:dimension-attributes">dimension attributes</a>.
