#### <span class="secno">4.8.17</span> <span class="dfn">Dimension attributes</span><a href="#dimension-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

**Author requirements**: The <span id="attr-dim-width" class="dfn"
dfn-for="img,iframe,embed,object,source,video"
dfn-type="element-attr">`width`</span> and <span id="attr-dim-height"
class="dfn" dfn-for="img,iframe,embed,object,source,video"
dfn-type="element-attr">`height`</span> attributes on
[`img`](#the-img-element), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element),
[`embed`](#the-embed-element), [`object`](#the-object-element),
[`video`](#the-video-element), [`source`](#the-source-element) when the
parent is a [`picture`](#the-picture-element) element and, when their
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="dimension-attributes:image-button-state-(type=image)">Image
Button</a> state, [`input`](#the-input-element) elements may be
specified to give the dimensions of the visual content of the element
(the width and height respectively, relative to the nominal direction of
the output medium), in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="dimension-attributes:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>. The attributes, if
specified, must have values that are
<a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="dimension-attributes:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integers</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The specified dimensions given may differ from the dimensions specified
in the resource itself, since the resource may have a resolution that
differs from the CSS pixel resolution. (On screens,
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="dimension-attributes:&#39;px&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> have a resolution of
96ppi, but in general the CSS pixel resolution depends on the reading
distance.) If both attributes are specified, then one of the following
statements must be true:

- `specified width` - 0.5 ≤ `specified height` \* `target ratio` ≤
  `specified width` + 0.5
- `specified height` - 0.5 ≤ `specified width` / `target ratio` ≤
  `specified height` + 0.5
- `specified height` = `specified width` = 0

The `target ratio` is the ratio of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
id="dimension-attributes:natural-width"
data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a> to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
id="dimension-attributes:natural-height"
data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a> in the resource. The
`specified width` and `specified height` are the values of the
[`width`](#attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#attr-dim-height) attributes
respectively.

</div>

The two attributes must be omitted if the resource in question does not
have both a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
id="dimension-attributes:natural-width-2"
data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a> and a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
id="dimension-attributes:natural-height-2"
data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a>.

If the two attributes are both 0, it indicates that the element is not
intended for the user (e.g. it might be a part of a service to count
page views).

The dimension attributes are not intended to be used to stretch the
image.

**User agent requirements**: User agents are expected to use these
attributes [as hints for the rendering](#dimRendering).

For [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#the-embed-element) and
[`object`](#the-object-element) the IDL attributes are
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code
id="dimension-attributes:idl-domstring">DOMString</code></a>; for
[`video`](#the-video-element) and [`source`](#the-source-element) the
IDL attributes are
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long"
data-x-internal="idl-unsigned-long"><code
id="dimension-attributes:idl-unsigned-long">unsigned long</code></a>.

The corresponding IDL attributes for [`img`](#dom-img-height) and
[`input`](#dom-input-height) elements are defined in those respective
elements' sections, as they are slightly more specific to those
elements' other behaviors.

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-table-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-table-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-table-element:flow-content-2-2">flow
content</a> is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
In this order: optionally a [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element,
followed by zero or more [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) elements,
followed optionally by a [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element, followed
by either zero or more [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) elements or one or
more [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements, followed optionally by a
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element, optionally intermixed with one or
more <a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-table-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting
elements</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-table-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-table).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-table).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-table-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableCaptionElement? caption;
  HTMLTableCaptionElement createCaption();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteCaption();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tHead;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTHead();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteTHead();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tFoot;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTFoot();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteTFoot();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection tBodies;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTBody();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLTableRowElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteRow(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`table`](#the-table-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-table-element:represents">represents</a>
data with more than one dimension, in the form of a
<a href="#concept-table" id="the-table-element:concept-table">table</a>.

The [`table`](#the-table-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-table-element:table-model">table
model</a>. Tables have rows, columns, and cells given by their
descendants. The rows and columns form a grid; a table's cells must
completely cover that grid without overlap.

Precise rules for determining whether this conformance requirement is
met are described in the description of the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-table-element:table-model-2">table
model</a>.

Authors are encouraged to provide information describing how to
interpret complex tables. Guidance on how to [provide such
information](#table-descriptions-techniques) is given below.

Tables must not be used as layout aids. Historically, some web authors
have misused tables in HTML as a way to control their page layout. This
usage is non-conforming, because tools attempting to extract tabular
data from such documents would obtain very confusing results. In
particular, users of accessibility tools like screen readers are likely
to find it very difficult to navigate pages with tables used for layout.

There are a variety of alternatives to using HTML tables for layout,
such as CSS grid layout, CSS flexible box layout ("flexbox"), CSS
multi-column layout, CSS positioning, and the CSS table model.
[\[CSS\]](#refsCSS)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tables can be complicated to understand and navigate. To help users with
this, user agents should clearly delineate cells in a table from each
other, unless the user agent has classified the table as a
(non-conforming) layout table.

Authors and implementers are encouraged to consider using some of the
[table design techniques](#table-layout-techniques) described below to
make tables easier to navigate for users.

User agents, especially those that do table analysis on arbitrary
content, are encouraged to find heuristics to determine which tables
actually contain data and which are merely being used for layout. This
specification does not define a precise heuristic, but the following are
suggested as possible indicators:

| Feature | Indication |
|----|----|
| The use of the [`role`](#attr-aria-role) attribute with the value <a href="https://w3c.github.io/aria/#presentation"
data-x-internal="attr-aria-role-presentation"><code
id="the-table-element:attr-aria-role-presentation">presentation</code></a> | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`border`](#attr-table-border) attribute with the non-conforming value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`cellspacing`](#attr-table-cellspacing) and [`cellpadding`](#attr-table-cellpadding) attributes with the value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of [`caption`](#the-caption-element), [`thead`](#the-thead-element), or [`th`](#the-th-element) elements | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) and [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attributes | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`border`](#attr-table-border) attribute with a value other than 0 | Probably a non-layout table |
| Explicit visible borders set using CSS | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`summary`](#attr-table-summary) attribute | Not a good indicator (both layout and non-layout tables have historically been given this attribute) |

It is quite possible that the above suggestions are wrong. Implementers
are urged to provide feedback elaborating on their experiences with
trying to create a layout table detection heuristic.

If a [`table`](#the-table-element) element has a (non-conforming)
[`summary`](#attr-table-summary) attribute, and the user agent has not
classified the table as a layout table, the user agent may report the
contents of that attribute to the user.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Creates a [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, along with a
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) if required, inserts them into the table
at the position given by the argument, and returns the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index −1, which
is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at
the end of the table.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of
rows, throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-table-element:indexsizeerror"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-table-element:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

Removes the [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element with the given position in
the table.

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index −1 is
equivalent to deleting the last row of the table.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the
last row, or if there are no rows, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-table-element:indexsizeerror-2"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-table-element:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

In all of the following attribute and method definitions, when an
element is to be <span id="table-created"
class="dfn">table-created</span>, that means to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
id="the-table-element:create-an-element"
data-x-internal="create-an-element">create an element</a> given the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-table-element:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, the given local name,
and the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
id="the-table-element:html-namespace-2"
data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-caption" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`caption`</span> IDL attribute must return, on
getting, the first [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element child of
the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On
setting, the first [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element child of
the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and
the new value, if not null, must be inserted as the first node of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-createcaption" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`createCaption()`</span>
method must return the first [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element
child of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a
new [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element must be
<a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created">table-created</a>, inserted as the
first node of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, and then
returned.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-deletecaption" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`deleteCaption()`</span>
method must remove the first [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element
child of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-thead" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`tHead`</span> IDL attribute must return, on
getting, the first [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element child of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On
setting, if the new value is null or a [`thead`](#the-thead-element)
element, the first [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element child of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and the
new value, if not null, must be inserted immediately before the first
element in the [`table`](#the-table-element) element that is neither a
[`caption`](#the-caption-element) element nor a
[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element, if any, or at the end of
the table if there are no such elements. If the new value is neither
null nor a [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element, then a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror"
id="the-table-element:hierarchyrequesterror-3"
data-x-internal="hierarchyrequesterror">"<code>HierarchyRequestError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-table-element:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a> must be
thrown instead.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-createthead" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`createTHead()`</span>
method must return the first [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element child
of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a new
[`thead`](#the-thead-element) element must be <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-2">table-created</a> and inserted
immediately before the first element in the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element that is neither a
[`caption`](#the-caption-element) element nor a
[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element, if any, or at the end of
the table if there are no such elements, and then that new element must
be returned.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-deletethead" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`deleteTHead()`</span>
method must remove the first [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element child
of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-tfoot" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`tFoot`</span> IDL attribute must return, on
getting, the first [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element child of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On
setting, if the new value is null or a [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
element, the first [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element child of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and the
new value, if not null, must be inserted at the end of the table. If the
new value is neither null nor a [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element,
then a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror"
id="the-table-element:hierarchyrequesterror-4"
data-x-internal="hierarchyrequesterror">"<code>HierarchyRequestError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-table-element:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a> must be
thrown instead.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-createtfoot" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`createTFoot()`</span>
method must return the first [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element child
of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a new
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element must be <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-3">table-created</a> and inserted at
the end of the table, and then that new element must be returned.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-deletetfoot" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`deleteTFoot()`</span>
method must remove the first [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element child
of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-tbodies" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`tBodies`</span> attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-table-element:htmlcollection-5">HTMLCollection</code></a> rooted
at the [`table`](#the-table-element) node, whose filter matches only
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) elements that are children of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-createtbody" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement" dfn-type="method">`createTBody()`</span>
method must <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-4">table-create</a> a new
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element, insert it immediately after the
last [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element child in the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if any, or at the end of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element if the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element has no
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element children, and then must return the
new [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-table-rows" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`rows`</span> attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-table-element:htmlcollection-6">HTMLCollection</code></a> rooted
at the [`table`](#the-table-element) node, whose filter matches only
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements that are either children of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, or children of
[`thead`](#the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), or
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) elements that are themselves children of
the [`table`](#the-table-element) element. The elements in the
collection must be ordered such that those elements whose parent is a
[`thead`](#the-thead-element) are included first, in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-table-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a>, followed by those elements whose parent is either a
[`table`](#the-table-element) or [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element,
again in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-table-element:tree-order-2" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a>, followed finally by those elements whose parent is a
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element, still in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-table-element:tree-order-3" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The behavior of the <span id="dom-table-insertrow" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="method">`insertRow(``index``)`</span> method depends on the
state of the table. When it is called, the method must act as required
by the first item in the following list of conditions that describes the
state of the table and the `index` argument:

If `index` is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection:  
The method must throw an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-table-element:indexsizeerror-3"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-table-element:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

If the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection has zero elements in it, and the [`table`](#the-table-element) has no [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) elements in it:  
The method must <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-5">table-create</a> a
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element, then <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-6">table-create</a> a
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, then append the [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
element to the [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element, then append the
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element to the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, and finally return the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

If the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection has zero elements in it:  
The method must <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-7">table-create</a> a
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, append it to the last
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element in the table, and return the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

If `index` is −1 or equal to the number of items in [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection:  
The method must <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-8">table-create</a> a
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, and append it to the parent of the last
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows)
collection. Then, the newly created [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element must
be returned.

Otherwise:  
The method must <a href="#table-created"
id="the-table-element:table-created-9">table-create</a> a
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, insert it immediately before the
`index`th [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element in the
[`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection, in the same parent, and finally
must return the newly created [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the <span id="dom-table-deleterow" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableElement"
dfn-type="method">`deleteRow(``index``)`</span> method is called, the
user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If `index` is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of
    elements in the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-table-element:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-table-element:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If `index` is −1, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-table-element:concept-node-remove"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the last element in
    the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection from its parent, or do
    nothing if the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection is empty.

3.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-table-element:concept-node-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the `index`th
    element in the [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection from its parent.

</div>

<div class="example">

Here is an example of a table being used to mark up a Sudoku puzzle.
Observe the lack of headers, which are not necessary in such a table.

``` html
<style>
 #sudoku { border-collapse: collapse; border: solid thick; }
 #sudoku colgroup, table#sudoku tbody { border: solid medium; }
 #sudoku td { border: solid thin; height: 1.4em; width: 1.4em; text-align: center; padding: 0; }
</style>
<h1>Today's Sudoku</h1>
<table id="sudoku">
 <colgroup><col><col><col>
 <colgroup><col><col><col>
 <colgroup><col><col><col>
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> 1 <td>   <td> 3 <td> 6 <td>   <td> 4 <td> 7 <td>   <td> 9
  <tr> <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 1 <td>
  <tr> <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 6
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> 2 <td>   <td> 4 <td>   <td> 3 <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 8
  <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
  <tr> <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td> 1
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> 6 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 2
  <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
  <tr> <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 8 <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 5
</table>
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.9.1.1</span> Techniques for describing tables<a href="#table-descriptions-techniques" class="self-link"></a>

For tables that consist of more than just a grid of cells with headers
in the first row and headers in the first column, and for any table in
general where the reader might have difficulty understanding the
content, authors should include explanatory information introducing the
table. This information is useful for all users, but is especially
useful for users who cannot see the table, e.g. users of screen readers.

Such explanatory information should introduce the purpose of the table,
outline its basic cell structure, highlight any trends or patterns, and
generally teach the user how to use the table.

For instance, the following table:

| Negative | Characteristic | Positive |
|----------|----------------|----------|
| Sad      | Mood           | Happy    |
| Failing  | Grade          | Passing  |

Characteristics with positive and negative sides

...might benefit from a description explaining the way the table is laid
out, something like "Characteristics are given in the second column,
with the negative side in the left column and the positive side in the
right column".

There are a variety of ways to include this information, such as:

In prose, surrounding the table  
<div class="example">

``` html
<p>In the following table, characteristics are given in the second
column, with the negative side in the left column and the positive
side in the right column.</p>
<table>
 <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th id="n"> Negative
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r1"> Sad
   <th id="r1"> Mood
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r2"> Failing
   <th id="r2"> Grade
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

</div>

In the table's [`caption`](#the-caption-element)  
<div class="example">

``` html
<table>
 <caption>
  <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides.</strong>
  <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
  negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
  column.</p>
 </caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th id="n"> Negative
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r1"> Sad
   <th id="r1"> Mood
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r2"> Failing
   <th id="r2"> Grade
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

</div>

In the table's [`caption`](#the-caption-element), in a [`details`](#the-details-element) element  
<div class="example">

``` html
<table>
 <caption>
  <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides.</strong>
  <details>
   <summary>Help</summary>
   <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
   negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
   column.</p>
  </details>
 </caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th id="n"> Negative
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r1"> Sad
   <th id="r1"> Mood
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r2"> Failing
   <th id="r2"> Grade
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

</div>

Next to the table, in the same [`figure`](#the-figure-element)  
<div class="example">

``` html
<figure>
 <figcaption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</figcaption>
 <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
 negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
 column.</p>
 <table>
  <thead>
   <tr>
    <th id="n"> Negative
    <th> Characteristic
    <th> Positive
  <tbody>
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
    <th id="r1"> Mood
    <td> Happy
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
    <th id="r2"> Grade
    <td> Passing
 </table>
</figure>
```

</div>

Next to the table, in a [`figure`](#the-figure-element)'s [`figcaption`](#the-figcaption-element)  
<div class="example">

``` html
<figure>
 <figcaption>
  <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</strong>
  <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
  negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
  column.</p>
 </figcaption>
 <table>
  <thead>
   <tr>
    <th id="n"> Negative
    <th> Characteristic
    <th> Positive
  <tbody>
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
    <th id="r1"> Mood
    <td> Happy
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
    <th id="r2"> Grade
    <td> Passing
 </table>
</figure>
```

</div>

Authors may also use other techniques, or combinations of the above
techniques, as appropriate.

The best option, of course, rather than writing a description explaining
the way the table is laid out, is to adjust the table such that no
explanation is needed.

<div class="example">

In the case of the table used in the examples above, a simple
rearrangement of the table so that the headers are on the top and left
sides removes the need for an explanation as well as removing the need
for the use of [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attributes:

``` html
<table>
 <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Negative
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <th> Mood
   <td> Sad
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <th> Grade
   <td> Failing
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.9.1.2</span> Techniques for table design<a href="#table-layout-techniques" class="self-link"></a>

Good table design is key to making tables more readable and usable.

In visual media, providing column and row borders and alternating row
backgrounds can be very effective to make complicated tables more
readable.

For tables with large volumes of numeric content, using monospaced fonts
can help users see patterns, especially in situations where a user agent
does not render the borders. (Unfortunately, for historical reasons, not
rendering borders on tables is a common default.)

In speech media, table cells can be distinguished by reporting the
corresponding headers before reading the cell's contents, and by
allowing users to navigate the table in a grid fashion, rather than
serializing the entire contents of the table in source order.

Authors are encouraged to use CSS to achieve these effects.

User agents are encouraged to render tables using these techniques
whenever the page does not use CSS and the table is not classified as a
layout table.

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
None.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As the first element child of a [`table`](#the-table-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-caption-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>, but with no descendant [`table`](#the-table-element)
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-caption-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a> can be omitted if the [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element
is not immediately followed by
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
id="the-caption-element:space-characters"
data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> or a
<a href="#syntax-comments"
id="the-caption-element:syntax-comments">comment</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-caption-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-caption).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-caption).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-caption-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableCaptionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-caption-element:represents">represents</a>
the title of the [`table`](#the-table-element) that is its parent, if it
has a parent and that is a [`table`](#the-table-element) element.

The [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-caption-element:table-model">table
model</a>.

When a [`table`](#the-table-element) element is the only content in a
[`figure`](#the-figure-element) element other than the
[`figcaption`](#the-figcaption-element), the
[`caption`](#the-caption-element) element should be omitted in favor of
the [`figcaption`](#the-figcaption-element).

A caption can introduce context for a table, making it significantly
easier to understand.

<div class="example">

Consider, for instance, the following table:

|     |     |     |     |     |     |     |
|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|
|     | 1   | 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   |
| 1   | 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   |
| 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   |
| 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   |
| 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  |
| 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  | 11  |
| 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  | 11  | 12  |

In the abstract, this table is not clear. However, with a caption giving
the table's number (for
<a href="#referenced" id="the-caption-element:referenced">reference</a>
in the main prose) and explaining its use, it makes more sense:

``` html
<caption>
<p>Table 1.
<p>This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two
six-sided dice. The first row represents the value of the first die,
the first column the value of the second die. The total is given in
the cell that corresponds to the values of the two dice.
</caption>
```

This provides the user with more context:

|     |     |     |     |     |     |     |
|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|
|     | 1   | 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   |
| 1   | 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   |
| 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   |
| 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   |
| 4   | 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  |
| 5   | 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  | 11  |
| 6   | 7   | 8   | 9   | 10  | 11  | 12  |

Table 1.  
This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two six-sided
dice. The first row represents the value of the first die, the first
column the value of the second die. The total is given in the cell that
corresponds to the values of the two dice.

</div>

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableColElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(1, 1000)] attribute unsigned long span;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-colgroup-element:represents">represents</a> a
<a href="#concept-column-group"
id="the-colgroup-element:concept-column-group">group</a> of one or more
<a href="#concept-column"
id="the-colgroup-element:concept-column">columns</a> in the
[`table`](#the-table-element) that is its parent, if it has a parent and
that is a [`table`](#the-table-element) element.

If the [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element contains no
[`col`](#the-col-element) elements, then the element may have a
<span id="attr-colgroup-span" class="dfn" dfn-for="colgroup"
dfn-type="element-attr">`span`</span> content attribute specified, whose
value must be a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-colgroup-element:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integer</a> greater than zero and less than or equal to 1000.

The [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element and its
[`span`](#attr-colgroup-span) attribute take part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-colgroup-element:table-model">table
model</a>.

id="the-col-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-col-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-col).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-col).

[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) elements.

If a [`col`](#the-col-element) element has a parent and that is a
[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element that itself has a parent
that is a [`table`](#the-table-element) element, then the
[`col`](#the-col-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-col-element:represents">represents</a> one
or more <a href="#concept-column"
id="the-col-element:concept-column">columns</a> in the
<a href="#concept-column-group"
id="the-col-element:concept-column-group">column group</a> represented
by that [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element).

The element may have a <span id="attr-col-span" class="dfn"
dfn-for="col" dfn-type="element-attr">`span`</span> content attribute
specified, whose value must be a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-col-element:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integer</a> greater than zero and less than or equal to 1000.

The [`col`](#the-col-element) element and its [`span`](#attr-col-span)
attribute take part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-col-element:table-model">table model</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
None.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As a child of a [`table`](#the-table-element) element, after any
[`caption`](#the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element),
and [`thead`](#the-thead-element) elements, but only if there are no
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements that are children of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
Zero or more [`tr`](#the-tr-element) and
<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-tbody-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element's <a href="#syntax-start-tag"
id="the-tbody-element:syntax-start-tag">start tag</a> can be omitted if
the first thing inside the [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element is a
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, and if the element is not immediately
preceded by a [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element),
[`thead`](#the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element
whose
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-tbody-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a> has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-tbody-element:syntax-end-tag-2">end
tag</a> can be omitted if the [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element is
immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) or
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element, or if there is no more content in
the parent element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-tbody-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-tbody).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-tbody).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableSectionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLTableRowElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteRow(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#htmltablesectionelement) interface is
also used for [`thead`](#the-thead-element) and
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) elements.

The [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-tbody-element:represents">represents</a> a
<a href="#concept-row-group"
id="the-tbody-element:concept-row-group">block</a> of
<a href="#concept-row" id="the-tbody-element:concept-row">rows</a> that
consist of a body of data for the parent [`table`](#the-table-element)
element, if the [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element has a parent and
it is a [`table`](#the-table-element).

The [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-tbody-element:table-model">table
model</a>.

`tbody``.`<a href="#dom-tbody-rows" id="dom-tbody-rows-dev"><code>rows</code></a>  
Returns an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-tbody-element:htmlcollection-2">HTMLCollection</code></a> of the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements of the table section.

`tr`` = ``tbody``.`<a href="#dom-tbody-insertrow"
id="dom-tbody-insertrow-dev"><code>insertRow</code></a>`([ ``index`` ])`  
Creates a [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, inserts it into the table
section at the position given by the argument, and returns the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index −1,
which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to
inserting at the end of the table section.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of
rows, throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-tbody-element:indexsizeerror"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-tbody-element:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

`tbody``.`<a href="#dom-tbody-deleterow"
id="dom-tbody-deleterow-dev"><code>deleteRow</code></a>`(``index``)`  
Removes the [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element with the given position in
the table section.

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index −1
is equivalent to deleting the last row of the table section.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the
last row, or if there are no rows, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-tbody-element:indexsizeerror-2"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-tbody-element:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tbody-rows" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableSectionElement" dfn-type="attribute">`rows`</span>
attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-tbody-element:htmlcollection-3">HTMLCollection</code></a> rooted
at this element, whose filter matches only [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
elements that are children of this element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tbody-insertrow" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableSectionElement"
dfn-type="method">`insertRow(``index``)`</span> method must act as
follows:

1.  If `index` is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in
    the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection, throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-tbody-element:indexsizeerror-3"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-tbody-element:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `table row` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-tbody-element:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    this element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-tbody-element:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, "`tr`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-tbody-element:html-namespace-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

3.  If `index` is −1 or equal to the number of items in the
    [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="the-tbody-element:concept-node-append"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">append</a> `table row` to this
    element.

4.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert"
    id="the-tbody-element:concept-node-insert"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert">insert</a> `table row` as a
    child of this element, immediately before the `index`th
    [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows)
    collection.

5.  Return `table row`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tbody-deleterow" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableSectionElement"
dfn-type="method">`deleteRow(``index``)`</span> method must, when
invoked, act as follows:

1.  If `index` is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of
    elements in the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-tbody-element:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-tbody-element:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If `index` is −1, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-tbody-element:concept-node-remove"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the last element in
    the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection from this element, or do
    nothing if the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection is empty.

3.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-tbody-element:concept-node-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the `index`th
    element in the [`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection from this
    element.

</div>

[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) elements and before any
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element), and
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements, but only if there are no other
[`thead`](#the-thead-element) elements that are children of the
[`table`](#the-table-element) element.

id="the-thead-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:

<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-thead-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-thead-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-thead-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a> can be omitted if the [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element is
immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) or
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-thead-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:

id="the-thead-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"

id="the-thead-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:

for [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) elements.

The [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-thead-element:represents">represents</a>
the <a href="#concept-row-group"
id="the-thead-element:concept-row-group">block</a> of
<a href="#concept-row" id="the-thead-element:concept-row">rows</a> that
consist of the column labels (headers) and any ancillary non-header
cells for the parent [`table`](#the-table-element) element, if the
[`thead`](#the-thead-element) element has a parent and it is a
[`table`](#the-table-element).

The [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-thead-element:table-model">table
model</a>.

<div class="example">

This example shows a [`thead`](#the-thead-element) element being used.
Notice the use of both [`th`](#the-th-element) and
[`td`](#the-td-element) elements in the [`thead`](#the-thead-element)
element: the first row is the headers, and the second row is an
explanation of how to fill in the table.

``` html
<table>
 <caption> School auction sign-up sheet </caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th><label for=e1>Name</label>
   <th><label for=e2>Product</label>
   <th><label for=e3>Picture</label>
   <th><label for=e4>Price</label>
  <tr>
   <td>Your name here
   <td>What are you selling?
   <td>Link to a picture
   <td>Your reserve price
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Ms Danus
   <td>Doughnuts
   <td><img src="https://example.com/mydoughnuts.png" title="Doughnuts from Ms Danus">
   <td>$45
  <tr>
   <td><input id=e1 type=text name=who required form=f>
   <td><input id=e2 type=text name=what required form=f>
   <td><input id=e3 type=url name=pic form=f>
   <td><input id=e4 type=number step=0.01 min=0 value=0 required form=f>
</table>
<form id=f action="/auction.cgi">
 <input type=button name=add value="Submit">
</form>
```

</div>

<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-tfoot-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-tfoot-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-tfoot-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a> can be omitted if there is no more content in the parent
element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-tfoot-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-tfoot-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-tfoot-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-tfoot).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-tfoot).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-tfoot-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#htmltablesectionelement), as defined
for [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) elements.

The [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-tfoot-element:represents">represents</a>
the <a href="#concept-row-group"
id="the-tfoot-element:concept-row-group">block</a> of
<a href="#concept-row" id="the-tfoot-element:concept-row">rows</a> that
consist of the column summaries (footers) for the parent
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, if the
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element has a parent and it is a
[`table`](#the-table-element).

The [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-tfoot-element:table-model">table
model</a>.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableRowElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute long rowIndex;
  readonly attribute long sectionRowIndex;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection cells;
  HTMLTableCellElement insertCell(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteCell(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

<a href="#concept-table" id="the-tr-element:concept-table">table</a>.

The [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element takes part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-tr-element:table-model">table model</a>.

list.

Returns −1 if the element isn't in a table.

`tr``.`<a href="#dom-tr-sectionrowindex"

Returns an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"

[HTMLTableRowElement/insertCell](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLTableRowElement/insertCell "The HTMLTableRowElement.insertCell() method inserts a new cell (<td>) into a table row (<tr>) and returns a reference to the cell.")

Creates a [`td`](#the-td-element) element, inserts it into the table row
at the position given by the argument, and returns the
[`td`](#the-td-element).

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index −1, which is
the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at
the end of the row.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of
cells, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-tr-element:indexsizeerror"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-tr-element:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

`tr``.`<a href="#dom-tr-deletecell"
id="dom-tr-deletecell-dev"><code>deleteCell</code></a>`(``index``)`

Removes the [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element) element
with the given position in the row.

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index −1 is
equivalent to deleting the last cell of the row.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the
last cell, or if there are no cells, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-tr-element:indexsizeerror-2"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-tr-element:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tr-rowindex" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableRowElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`rowIndex`</span> attribute must, if this element
has a parent [`table`](#the-table-element) element, or a parent
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#the-thead-element), or
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element and a *grandparent*
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, return the index of this
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element in that [`table`](#the-table-element)
element's [`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection. If there is no such
[`table`](#the-table-element) element, then the attribute must return
−1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tr-sectionrowindex" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableRowElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`sectionRowIndex`</span> attribute must, if this
element has a parent [`table`](#the-table-element),
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#the-thead-element), or
[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element, return the index of the
[`tr`](#the-tr-element) element in the parent element's `rows`
collection (for tables, that's [`HTMLTableElement`](#htmltableelement)'s
[`rows`](#dom-table-rows) collection; for table sections, that's
[`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#htmltablesectionelement)'s
[`rows`](#dom-tbody-rows) collection). If there is no such parent
element, then the attribute must return −1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tr-cells" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableRowElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`cells`</span> attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-tr-element:htmlcollection-3">HTMLCollection</code></a> rooted at
this [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, whose filter matches only
[`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements that are
children of the [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tr-insertcell" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableRowElement"
dfn-type="method">`insertCell(``index``)`</span> method must act as
follows:

1.  If `index` is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in
    the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-tr-element:indexsizeerror-3"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-tr-element:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `table cell` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-tr-element:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    this [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-tr-element:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
    document</a>, "`td`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-tr-element:html-namespace-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

3.  If `index` is equal to −1 or equal to the number of items in
    [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="the-tr-element:concept-node-append"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">append</a> `table cell` to
    this [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

4.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert"
    id="the-tr-element:concept-node-insert"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert">insert</a> `table cell` as a
    child of this [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element, immediately before
    the `index`th [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element)
    element in the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection.

5.  Return `table cell`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tr-deletecell" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableRowElement"
dfn-type="method">`deleteCell(``index``)`</span> method must act as
follows:

1.  If `index` is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of
    elements in the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-tr-element:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-tr-element:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If `index` is −1, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-tr-element:concept-node-remove"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the last element in
    the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection from its parent, or do
    nothing if the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection is empty.

3.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove"
    id="the-tr-element:concept-node-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-remove">remove</a> the `index`th
    element in the [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection from its parent.

</div>
