<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
None.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As a child of a [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-td-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`td`](#the-td-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-td-element:syntax-end-tag">end tag</a>
can be omitted if the [`td`](#the-td-element) element is immediately
followed by a [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element)
element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-td-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan) — Number of columns that the cell is to
span

[`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan) — Number of rows that the cell is to
span

[`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) — The header cells for this cell

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-td).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-td).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-td-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableCellElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(1, 1000)] attribute unsigned long colSpan;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(0, 65534)] attribute unsigned long rowSpan;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString headers;
  readonly attribute long cellIndex;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString scope; // only conforming for th elements
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString abbr;  // only conforming for th elements

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`HTMLTableCellElement`](#htmltablecellelement) interface is also
used for [`th`](#the-th-element) elements.

The [`td`](#the-td-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-td-element:represents">represents</a> a
data <a href="#concept-cell" id="the-td-element:concept-cell">cell</a>
in a table.

The [`td`](#the-td-element) element and its
[`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan), and
[`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attributes take part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-td-element:table-model">table model</a>.

User agents, especially in non-visual environments or where displaying
the table as a 2D grid is impractical, may give the user context for the
cell when rendering the contents of a cell; for instance, giving its
position in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-td-element:table-model-2">table model</a>,
or listing the cell's header cells (as determined by the
<a href="#algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells"
id="the-td-element:algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells">algorithm for
assigning header cells</a>). When a cell's header cells are being
listed, user agents may use the value of [`abbr`](#attr-th-abbr)
attributes on those header cells, if any, instead of the contents of the
header cells themselves.

<div class="example">

In this example, we see a snippet of a web application consisting of a
grid of editable cells (essentially a simple spreadsheet). One of the
cells has been configured to show the sum of the cells above it. Three
have been marked as headings, which use [`th`](#the-th-element) elements
instead of [`td`](#the-td-element) elements. A script would attach event
handlers to these elements to maintain the total.

``` html
<table>
 <tr>
  <th><input value="Name">
  <th><input value="Paid ($)">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Jeff">
  <td><input value="14">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Britta">
  <td><input value="9">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Abed">
  <td><input value="25">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Shirley">
  <td><input value="2">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Annie">
  <td><input value="5">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Troy">
  <td><input value="5">
 <tr>
  <td><input value="Pierce">
  <td><input value="1000">
 <tr>
  <th><input value="Total">
  <td><output value="1060">
</table>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.9.10</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`th`</span> element<a href="#the-th-element" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/th](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/th "The <th> HTML element defines a cell as the header of a group of table cells. The exact nature of this group is defined by the scope and headers attributes.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12.1+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
None.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As a child of a [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-th-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>, but with no [`header`](#the-header-element),
[`footer`](#the-footer-element), <a href="#sectioning-content-2"
id="the-th-element:sectioning-content-2">sectioning content</a>, or
<a href="#heading-content-2"
id="the-th-element:heading-content-2">heading content</a> descendants.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
A [`th`](#the-th-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-th-element:syntax-end-tag">end tag</a>
can be omitted if the [`th`](#the-th-element) element is immediately
followed by a [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element)
element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-th-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan) — Number of columns that the cell is to
span

[`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan) — Number of rows that the cell is to
span

[`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) — The header cells for this cell

[`scope`](#attr-th-scope) — Specifies which cells the header cell
applies to

[`abbr`](#attr-th-abbr) — Alternative label to use for the header cell
when referencing the cell in other contexts

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-th).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-th).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-th-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLTableCellElement`](#htmltablecellelement), as defined for
[`td`](#the-td-element) elements.

The [`th`](#the-th-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-th-element:represents">represents</a> a
header <a href="#concept-cell" id="the-th-element:concept-cell">cell</a>
in a table.

The [`th`](#the-th-element) element may have a <span id="attr-th-scope"
class="dfn" dfn-for="th" dfn-type="element-attr">`scope`</span> content
attribute specified.

The [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-th-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a> with
the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-th-scope-row" class="dfn" dfn-for="th/scope" dfn-type="attr-value">`row`</span> | <span id="attr-th-scope-row-state" class="dfn">Row</span> | The header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same row(s). |
| <span id="attr-th-scope-col" class="dfn" dfn-for="th/scope" dfn-type="attr-value">`col`</span> | <span id="attr-th-scope-column-state" class="dfn">Column</span> | The header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same column(s). |
| <span id="attr-th-scope-rowgroup" class="dfn" dfn-for="th/scope" dfn-type="attr-value">`rowgroup`</span> | <span id="attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state" class="dfn">Row Group</span> | The header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the row group. |
| <span id="attr-th-scope-colgroup" class="dfn" dfn-for="th/scope" dfn-type="attr-value">`colgroup`</span> | <span id="attr-th-scope-colgroup-state" class="dfn">Column Group</span> | The header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the column group. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-th-scope-auto-state" class="dfn">Auto</span> state. (In
this state the header cell applies to a set of cells selected based on
context.)

</div>

A [`th`](#the-th-element) element's [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute
must not be in the <a href="#attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state"
id="the-th-element:attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state">Row Group</a> state if
the element is not anchored in a
<a href="#concept-row-group" id="the-th-element:concept-row-group">row
group</a>, nor in the <a href="#attr-th-scope-colgroup-state"
id="the-th-element:attr-th-scope-colgroup-state">Column Group</a> state
if the element is not anchored in a <a href="#concept-column-group"
id="the-th-element:concept-column-group">column group</a>.

The [`th`](#the-th-element) element may have an <span id="attr-th-abbr"
class="dfn" dfn-for="th" dfn-type="element-attr">`abbr`</span> content
attribute specified. Its value must be an alternative label for the
header cell, to be used when referencing the cell in other contexts
(e.g. when describing the header cells that apply to a data cell). It is
typically an abbreviated form of the full header cell, but can also be
an expansion, or merely a different phrasing.

The [`th`](#the-th-element) element and its
[`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan),
[`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers), and [`scope`](#attr-th-scope)
attributes take part in the
<a href="#table-model" id="the-th-element:table-model">table model</a>.

<div class="example">

The following example shows how the [`scope`](#attr-th-scope)
attribute's [`rowgroup`](#attr-th-scope-rowgroup) value affects which
data cells a header cell applies to.

Here is a markup fragment showing a table:

``` html
<table>
 <thead>
  <tr> <th> ID <th> Measurement <th> Average <th> Maximum
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> Cats <td> <td>
  <tr> <td> 93 <th> Legs <td> 3.5 <td> 4
  <tr> <td> 10 <th> Tails <td> 1 <td> 1
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> English speakers <td> <td>
  <tr> <td> 32 <th> Legs <td> 2.67 <td> 4
  <tr> <td> 35 <th> Tails <td> 0.33 <td> 1
</table>
```

This would result in the following table:

| ID  | Measurement      | Average | Maximum |
|-----|------------------|---------|---------|
|     | Cats             |         |         |
| 93  | Legs             | 3.5     | 4       |
| 10  | Tails            | 1       | 1       |
|     | English speakers |         |         |
| 32  | Legs             | 2.67    | 4       |
| 35  | Tails            | 0.33    | 1       |

The headers in the first row all apply directly down to the rows in
their column.

The headers with a [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state"
id="the-th-element:attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state-2">Row Group</a> state
apply to all the cells in their row group other than the cells in the
first column.

The remaining headers apply just to the cells to the right of them.

<img src="/images/table-scope-diagram.png" width="459" height="256" />

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.9.11</span> Attributes common to [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements<a href="#attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements"
class="self-link"></a>

The [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements may
have a <span id="attr-tdth-colspan" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th"
dfn-type="element-attr">`colspan`</span> content attribute specified,
whose value must be a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:valid-non-negative-integer">valid
non-negative integer</a> greater than zero and less than or equal to
1000.

The [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements may
also have a <span id="attr-tdth-rowspan" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th"
dfn-type="element-attr">`rowspan`</span> content attribute specified,
whose value must be a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:valid-non-negative-integer-2">valid
non-negative integer</a> less than or equal to 65534. For this
attribute, the value zero means that the cell is to span all the
remaining rows in the row group.

These attributes give the number of columns and rows respectively that
the cell is to span. These attributes must not be used to overlap cells,
as described in the description of the <a href="#table-model"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:table-model">table model</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) element may have
a <span id="attr-tdth-headers" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th"
dfn-type="element-attr">`headers`</span> content attribute specified.
The [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attribute, if specified, must
contain a string consisting of an
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a>, none of which are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:identical-to"
data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> another token and each
of which must have the value of an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:concept-id"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> of a [`th`](#the-th-element) element
taking part in the same <a href="#concept-table"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:concept-table">table</a> as
the [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element) element (as
defined by the <a href="#table-model"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:table-model-2">table
model</a>).

<div algorithm="">

A [`th`](#the-th-element) element with
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:concept-id-2"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> `id` is said to be *directly
targeted* by all [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element)
elements in the same <a href="#concept-table"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:concept-table-2">table</a>
that have [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attributes whose values
include as one of their tokens the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:concept-id-3"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> `id`. A [`th`](#the-th-element)
element `A` is said to be *targeted* by a [`th`](#the-th-element) or
[`td`](#the-td-element) element `B` if either `A` is *directly targeted*
by `B` or if there exists an element `C` that is itself *targeted* by
the element `B` and `A` is *directly targeted* by `C`.

</div>

A [`th`](#the-th-element) element must not be *targeted* by itself.

The [`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan),
and [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attributes take part in the
<a href="#table-model"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:table-model-3">table
model</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

`cell``.`<a href="#dom-tdth-cellindex"
id="dom-tdth-cellindex-dev"><code>cellIndex</code></a>  
Returns the position of the cell in the row's [`cells`](#dom-tr-cells)
list. This does not necessarily correspond to the `x`-position of the
cell in the table, since earlier cells might cover multiple rows or
columns.

Returns −1 if the element isn't in a row.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tdth-cellindex" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTableCellElement" dfn-type="attribute">`cellIndex`</span>
IDL attribute must, if the element has a parent [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
element, return the index of the cell's element in the parent element's
[`cells`](#dom-tr-cells) collection. If there is no such parent element,
then the attribute must return −1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-th-scope" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLTableCellElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`scope`</span> IDL attribute must
<a href="#reflect"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:reflect">reflect</a> the
content attribute of the same name,
<a href="#limited-to-only-known-values"
id="attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements:limited-to-only-known-values">limited
to only known values</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.9.12</span> <span id="processing-model-2"></span>Processing model<a href="#table-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

The various table elements and their content attributes together define
the <span id="table-model" class="dfn">table model</span>.

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="concept-table" class="dfn">table</span> consists of cells
aligned on a two-dimensional grid of <span id="concept-slots"
class="dfn">slots</span> with coordinates (`x`, `y`). The grid is
finite, and is either empty or has one or more slots. If the grid has
one or more slots, then the `x` coordinates are always in the range
0 ≤ `x` \< `x`<sub>`width`</sub>, and the `y` coordinates are always in
the range 0 ≤ `y` \< `y`<sub>`height`</sub>. If one or both of
`x`<sub>`width`</sub> and `y`<sub>`height`</sub> are zero, then the
table is empty (has no slots). Tables correspond to
[`table`](#the-table-element) elements.

A <span id="concept-cell" class="dfn">cell</span> is a set of slots
anchored at a slot (`cell`<sub>`x`</sub>, `cell`<sub>`y`</sub>), and
with a particular `width` and `height` such that the cell covers all the
slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where
`cell`<sub>`x`</sub> ≤ `x` \< `cell`<sub>`x`</sub>+`width` and
`cell`<sub>`y`</sub> ≤ `y` \< `cell`<sub>`y`</sub>+`height`. Cells can
either be *data cells* or *header cells*. Data cells correspond to
[`td`](#the-td-element) elements, and header cells correspond to
[`th`](#the-th-element) elements. Cells of both types can have zero or
more associated header cells.

It is possible, in certain error cases, for two cells to occupy the same
slot.

A <span id="concept-row" class="dfn">row</span> is a complete set of
slots from `x`=0 to `x`=`x`<sub>`width`</sub>-1, for a particular value
of `y`. Rows usually correspond to [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements,
though a <a href="#concept-row-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-group">row group</a> can have
some implied
<a href="#concept-row" id="table-processing-model:concept-row">rows</a>
at the end in some cases involving <a href="#concept-cell"
id="table-processing-model:concept-cell">cells</a> spanning multiple
rows.

A <span id="concept-column" class="dfn">column</span> is a complete set
of slots from `y`=0 to `y`=`y`<sub>`height`</sub>-1, for a particular
value of `x`. Columns can correspond to [`col`](#the-col-element)
elements. In the absence of [`col`](#the-col-element) elements, columns
are implied.

A <span id="concept-row-group" class="dfn">row group</span> is a set of
<a href="#concept-row"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-2">rows</a> anchored at a slot
(0, `group`<sub>`y`</sub>) with a particular `height` such that the row
group covers all the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where
0 ≤ `x` \< `x`<sub>`width`</sub> and
`group`<sub>`y`</sub> ≤ `y` \< `group`<sub>`y`</sub>+`height`. Row
groups correspond to [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element),
[`thead`](#the-thead-element), and [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
elements. Not every row is necessarily in a row group.

A <span id="concept-column-group" class="dfn">column group</span> is a
set of <a href="#concept-column"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column">columns</a> anchored at a
slot (`group`<sub>`x`</sub>, 0) with a particular `width` such that the
column group covers all the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where
`group`<sub>`x`</sub> ≤ `x` \< `group`<sub>`x`</sub>+`width` and
0 ≤ `y` \< `y`<sub>`height`</sub>. Column groups correspond to
[`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) elements. Not every column is
necessarily in a column group.

</div>

<a href="#concept-row-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-group-2">Row groups</a> cannot
overlap each other. Similarly, <a href="#concept-column-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column-group">column groups</a>
cannot overlap each other.

A <a href="#concept-cell"
id="table-processing-model:concept-cell-2">cell</a> cannot cover slots
that are from two or more <a href="#concept-row-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-group-3">row groups</a>. It is,
however, possible for a cell to be in multiple
<a href="#concept-column-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column-group-2">column groups</a>.
All the slots that form part of one cell are part of zero or one
<a href="#concept-row-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-group-4">row groups</a> and zero
or more <a href="#concept-column-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column-group-3">column groups</a>.

In addition to <a href="#concept-cell"
id="table-processing-model:concept-cell-3">cells</a>,
<a href="#concept-column"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column-2">columns</a>,
<a href="#concept-row"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-3">rows</a>,
<a href="#concept-row-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-row-group-5">row groups</a>, and
<a href="#concept-column-group"
id="table-processing-model:concept-column-group-4">column groups</a>,
<a href="#concept-table"
id="table-processing-model:concept-table">tables</a> can have a
[`caption`](#the-caption-element) element associated with them. This
gives the table a heading, or legend.

A <span id="table-model-error" class="dfn">table model error</span> is
an error with the data represented by [`table`](#the-table-element)
elements and their descendants. Documents must not have table model
errors.

##### <span class="secno">4.9.12.1</span> Forming a table<a href="#forming-a-table" class="self-link"></a>

<div var-scope="">

<div algorithm="">

To determine which elements correspond to which slots in a
<a href="#concept-table" id="forming-a-table:concept-table">table</a>
associated with a [`table`](#the-table-element) element, to determine
the dimensions of the table (`x`<sub>`width`</sub> and
`y`<sub>`height`</sub>), and to determine if there are any
<a href="#table-model-error"
id="forming-a-table:table-model-error">table model errors</a>, user
agents must use the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x`<sub>`width`</sub> be 0.

2.  Let `y`<sub>`height`</sub> be 0.

3.  Let `pending `[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)` elements` be a list of
    [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) elements, initially empty.

4.  Let `the table` be the
    <a href="#concept-table" id="forming-a-table:concept-table-2">table</a>
    represented by the [`table`](#the-table-element) element. The
    `x`<sub>`width`</sub> and `y`<sub>`height`</sub> variables give
    `the table`'s dimensions. `The table` is initially empty.

5.  If the [`table`](#the-table-element) element has no children
    elements, then return `the table` (which will be empty).

6.  Associate the first [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element child
    of the [`table`](#the-table-element) element with `the table`. If
    there are no such children, then it has no associated
    [`caption`](#the-caption-element) element.

7.  Let the `current element` be the first element child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element) element.

    If a step in this algorithm ever requires the `current element` to
    be <span id="concept-table-advance" class="dfn">advanced to the next
    child of the `table`</span> when there is no such next child, then
    the user agent must jump to the step labeled *end*, near the end of
    this algorithm.

8.  While the `current element` is not one of the following elements,
    <a href="#concept-table-advance"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance">advance</a> the
    `current element` to the next child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element):

    - [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element)
    - [`thead`](#the-thead-element)
    - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
    - [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
    - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)

9.  If the `current element` is a [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element),
    follow these substeps:

    1.  *Column groups*: Process the `current element` according to the
        appropriate case below:

        If the `current element` has any [`col`](#the-col-element) element children  
        Follow these steps:

        1.  Let `x`<sub>`start`</sub> have the value of
            `x`<sub>`width`</sub>.

        2.  Let the `current column` be the first
            [`col`](#the-col-element) element child of the
            [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element.

        3.  *Columns*: If the `current column` [`col`](#the-col-element)
            element has a [`span`](#attr-col-span) attribute, then parse
            its value using the
            <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
            id="forming-a-table:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules for
            parsing non-negative integers</a>.

            If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero,
            then let `span` be that value.

            Otherwise, if the [`col`](#the-col-element) element has no
            [`span`](#attr-col-span) attribute, or if trying to parse
            the attribute's value resulted in an error or zero, then let
            `span` be 1.

            If `span` is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

        4.  Increase `x`<sub>`width`</sub> by `span`.

        5.  Let the last `span` <a href="#concept-column"
            id="forming-a-table:concept-column">columns</a> in
            `the table` correspond to the `current column`
            [`col`](#the-col-element) element.

        6.  If `current column` is not the last
            [`col`](#the-col-element) element child of the
            [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element, then let the
            `current column` be the next [`col`](#the-col-element)
            element child of the [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element)
            element, and return to the step labeled *columns*.

        7.  Let all the last <a href="#concept-column"
            id="forming-a-table:concept-column-2">columns</a> in
            `the table` from x=`x`<sub>`start`</sub> to
            x=`x`<sub>`width`</sub>-1 form a new
            <a href="#concept-column-group"
            id="forming-a-table:concept-column-group">column group</a>,
            anchored at the slot (`x`<sub>`start`</sub>, 0), with width
            `x`<sub>`width`</sub>-`x`<sub>`start`</sub>, corresponding
            to the [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element.

        If the `current element` has no [`col`](#the-col-element) element children  
        1.  If the [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element has a
            [`span`](#attr-colgroup-span) attribute, then parse its
            value using the
            <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
            id="forming-a-table:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-2">rules for
            parsing non-negative integers</a>.

            If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero,
            then let `span` be that value.

            Otherwise, if the [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element)
            element has no [`span`](#attr-colgroup-span) attribute, or
            if trying to parse the attribute's value resulted in an
            error or zero, then let `span` be 1.

            If `span` is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

        2.  Increase `x`<sub>`width`</sub> by `span`.

        3.  Let the last `span` <a href="#concept-column"
            id="forming-a-table:concept-column-3">columns</a> in
            `the table` form a new <a href="#concept-column-group"
            id="forming-a-table:concept-column-group-2">column group</a>,
            anchored at the slot (`x`<sub>`width`</sub>-`span`, 0), with
            width `span`, corresponding to the
            [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element.

    2.  <a href="#concept-table-advance"
        id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-2">Advance</a> the
        `current element` to the next child of the
        [`table`](#the-table-element).

    3.  While the `current element` is not one of the following
        elements, <a href="#concept-table-advance"
        id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-3">advance</a> the
        `current element` to the next child of the
        [`table`](#the-table-element):

        - [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element)
        - [`thead`](#the-thead-element)
        - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
        - [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
        - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)

    4.  If the `current element` is a
        [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element, jump to the step
        labeled *column groups* above.

10. Let `y`<sub>`current`</sub> be 0.

11. Let the `list of downward-growing cells` be an empty list.

12. *Rows*: While the `current element` is not one of the following
    elements, <a href="#concept-table-advance"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-4">advance</a> the
    `current element` to the next child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element):

    - [`thead`](#the-thead-element)
    - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
    - [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
    - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)

13. If the `current element` is a [`tr`](#the-tr-element), then run the
    <a href="#algorithm-for-processing-rows"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-processing-rows">algorithm for
    processing rows</a>, <a href="#concept-table-advance"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-5">advance</a> the
    `current element` to the next child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element), and return to the step labeled
    *rows*.

14. Run the <a href="#algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group">algorithm for
    ending a row group</a>.

15. If the `current element` is a [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element), then
    add that element to the list of
    `pending `[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)` elements`,
    <a href="#concept-table-advance"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-6">advance</a> the
    `current element` to the next child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element), and return to the step labeled
    *rows*.

16. The `current element` is either a [`thead`](#the-thead-element) or a
    [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element).

    Run the <a href="#algorithm-for-processing-row-groups"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-processing-row-groups">algorithm for
    processing row groups</a>.

17. <a href="#concept-table-advance"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-table-advance-7">Advance</a> the
    `current element` to the next child of the
    [`table`](#the-table-element).

18. Return to the step labeled *rows*.

19. *End*: For each [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element) element in the list of
    `pending `[`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)` elements`, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="forming-a-table:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>, run the <a href="#algorithm-for-processing-row-groups"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-processing-row-groups-2">algorithm for
    processing row groups</a>.

20. If there exists a
    <a href="#concept-row" id="forming-a-table:concept-row">row</a> or
    <a href="#concept-column"
    id="forming-a-table:concept-column-4">column</a> in `the table`
    containing only
    <a href="#concept-slots" id="forming-a-table:concept-slots">slots</a>
    that do not have a
    <a href="#concept-cell" id="forming-a-table:concept-cell">cell</a>
    anchored to them, then this is a <a href="#table-model-error"
    id="forming-a-table:table-model-error-2">table model error</a>.

21. Return `the table`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="algorithm-for-processing-row-groups" class="dfn">algorithm
for processing row groups</span>, which is invoked by the set of steps
above for processing [`thead`](#the-thead-element),
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), and [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element)
elements, is:

1.  Let `y`<sub>`start`</sub> have the value of `y`<sub>`height`</sub>.

2.  For each [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element that is a child of the
    element being processed, in tree order, run the
    <a href="#algorithm-for-processing-rows"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-processing-rows-2">algorithm for
    processing rows</a>.

3.  If `y`<sub>`height`</sub> \> `y`<sub>`start`</sub>, then let all the
    last
    <a href="#concept-row" id="forming-a-table:concept-row-2">rows</a>
    in `the table` from y=`y`<sub>`start`</sub> to
    y=`y`<sub>`height`</sub>-1 form a new
    <a href="#concept-row-group" id="forming-a-table:concept-row-group">row
    group</a>, anchored at the slot with coordinate (0,
    `y`<sub>`start`</sub>), with height
    `y`<sub>`height`</sub>-`y`<sub>`start`</sub>, corresponding to the
    element being processed.

4.  Run the <a href="#algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group-2">algorithm for
    ending a row group</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group" class="dfn">algorithm
for ending a row group</span>, which is invoked by the set of steps
above when starting and ending a block of rows, is:

1.  While `y`<sub>`current`</sub> is less than `y`<sub>`height`</sub>,
    follow these steps:

    1.  Run the <a href="#algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells"
        id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells">algorithm
        for growing downward-growing cells</a>.

    2.  Increase `y`<sub>`current`</sub> by 1.

2.  Empty the `list of downward-growing cells`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="algorithm-for-processing-rows" class="dfn">algorithm for
processing rows</span>, which is invoked by the set of steps above for
processing [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements, is:

1.  If `y`<sub>`height`</sub> is equal to `y`<sub>`current`</sub>, then
    increase `y`<sub>`height`</sub> by 1. (`y`<sub>`current`</sub> is
    never *greater* than `y`<sub>`height`</sub>.)

2.  Let `x`<sub>`current`</sub> be 0.

3.  Run the <a href="#algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells-2">algorithm
    for growing downward-growing cells</a>.

4.  If the [`tr`](#the-tr-element) element being processed has no
    [`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element) element children,
    then increase `y`<sub>`current`</sub> by 1, abort this set of steps,
    and return to the algorithm above.

5.  Let `current cell` be the first [`td`](#the-td-element) or
    [`th`](#the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
    element being processed.

6.  *Cells*: While `x`<sub>`current`</sub> is less than
    `x`<sub>`width`</sub> and the slot with coordinate
    (`x`<sub>`current`</sub>, `y`<sub>`current`</sub>) already has a
    cell assigned to it, increase `x`<sub>`current`</sub> by 1.

7.  If `x`<sub>`current`</sub> is equal to `x`<sub>`width`</sub>,
    increase `x`<sub>`width`</sub> by 1. (`x`<sub>`current`</sub> is
    never *greater* than `x`<sub>`width`</sub>.)

8.  If the `current cell` has a [`colspan`](#attr-tdth-colspan)
    attribute, then <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
    id="forming-a-table:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-3">parse
    that attribute's value</a>, and let `colspan` be the result.

    If parsing that value failed, or returned zero, or if the attribute
    is absent, then let `colspan` be 1, instead.

    If `colspan` is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

9.  If the `current cell` has a [`rowspan`](#attr-tdth-rowspan)
    attribute, then <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
    id="forming-a-table:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-4">parse
    that attribute's value</a>, and let `rowspan` be the result.

    If parsing that value failed or if the attribute is absent, then let
    `rowspan` be 1, instead.

    If `rowspan` is greater than 65534, let it be 65534 instead.

10. Let `cell grows downward` be false.

11. If `rowspan` is zero, then set `cell grows downward` to true and set
    `rowspan` to 1.

12. If `x`<sub>`width`</sub> \< `x`<sub>`current`</sub>+`colspan`, then
    let `x`<sub>`width`</sub> be `x`<sub>`current`</sub>+`colspan`.

13. If `y`<sub>`height`</sub> \< `y`<sub>`current`</sub>+`rowspan`, then
    let `y`<sub>`height`</sub> be `y`<sub>`current`</sub>+`rowspan`.

14. Let the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) such that
    `x`<sub>`current`</sub> ≤ `x` \< `x`<sub>`current`</sub>+`colspan`
    and
    `y`<sub>`current`</sub> ≤ `y` \< `y`<sub>`current`</sub>+`rowspan`
    be covered by a new
    <a href="#concept-cell" id="forming-a-table:concept-cell-2">cell</a>
    `c`, anchored at (`x`<sub>`current`</sub>, `y`<sub>`current`</sub>),
    which has width `colspan` and height `rowspan`, corresponding to the
    `current cell` element.

    If the `current cell` element is a [`th`](#the-th-element) element,
    let this new cell `c` be a header cell; otherwise, let it be a data
    cell.

    To establish which header cells apply to the `current cell` element,
    use the <a href="#algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells"
    id="forming-a-table:algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells">algorithm for
    assigning header cells</a> described in the next section.

    If any of the slots involved already had a
    <a href="#concept-cell" id="forming-a-table:concept-cell-3">cell</a>
    covering them, then this is a <a href="#table-model-error"
    id="forming-a-table:table-model-error-3">table model error</a>.
    Those slots now have two cells overlapping.

15. If `cell grows downward` is true, then add the tuple {`c`,
    `x`<sub>`current`</sub>, `colspan`} to the
    `list of downward-growing cells`.

16. Increase `x`<sub>`current`</sub> by `colspan`.

17. If `current cell` is the last [`td`](#the-td-element) or
    [`th`](#the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
    element being processed, then increase `y`<sub>`current`</sub> by 1,
    abort this set of steps, and return to the algorithm above.

18. Let `current cell` be the next [`td`](#the-td-element) or
    [`th`](#the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
    element being processed.

19. Return to the step labeled *cells*.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the algorithms above require the user agent to run the
<span id="algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells"
class="dfn">algorithm for growing downward-growing cells</span>, the
user agent must, for each {`cell`, `cell`<sub>`x`</sub>, `width`} tuple
in the `list of downward-growing cells`, if any, extend the
<a href="#concept-cell" id="forming-a-table:concept-cell-4">cell</a>
`cell` so that it also covers the slots with coordinates (`x`,
`y`<sub>`current`</sub>), where
`cell`<sub>`x`</sub> ≤ `x` \< `cell`<sub>`x`</sub>+`width`.

</div>

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.9.12.2</span> Forming relationships between data cells and header cells<a href="#header-and-data-cell-semantics" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

Each cell can be assigned zero or more header cells. The
<span id="algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells" class="dfn">algorithm
for assigning header cells</span> to a cell `principal cell` is as
follows.

1.  Let `header list` be an empty list of cells.

2.  Let (`principal`<sub>`x`</sub>, `principal`<sub>`y`</sub>) be the
    coordinate of the slot to which the `principal cell` is anchored.

3.  If the `principal cell` has a [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attribute specified  
    1.  Take the value of the `principal cell`'s
        [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attribute and
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-ascii-whitespace"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:split-a-string-on-spaces"
        data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-spaces">split it on ASCII
        whitespace</a>, letting `id list` be the list of tokens
        obtained.

    2.  For each token in the `id list`, if the first element in the
        [`Document`](#document) with an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:concept-id"
        data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> equal to the token is a cell
        in the same <a href="#concept-table"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:concept-table">table</a>, and
        that cell is not the `principal cell`, then add that cell to
        `header list`.

    If `principal cell` does not have a [`headers`](#attr-tdth-headers) attribute specified  
    1.  Let `principal`<sub>`width`</sub> be the width of the
        `principal cell`.

    2.  Let `principal`<sub>`height`</sub> be the height of the
        `principal cell`.

    3.  For each value of `y` from `principal`<sub>`y`</sub> to
        `principal`<sub>`y`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`height`</sub>-1, run
        the
        <a href="#internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells">internal
        algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells</a>, with the
        `principal cell`, the `header list`, the initial coordinate
        (`principal`<sub>`x`</sub>, `y`), and the increments Δ`x`=−1 and
        Δ`y`=0.

    4.  For each value of `x` from `principal`<sub>`x`</sub> to
        `principal`<sub>`x`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`width`</sub>-1, run
        the
        <a href="#internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells-2">internal
        algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells</a>, with the
        `principal cell`, the `header list`, the initial coordinate
        (`x`, `principal`<sub>`y`</sub>), and the increments Δ`x`=0 and
        Δ`y`=−1.

    5.  If the `principal cell` is anchored in a
        <a href="#concept-row-group"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:concept-row-group">row group</a>,
        then add all header cells that are <a href="#row-group-header"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:row-group-header">row group
        headers</a> and are anchored in the same row group with an
        `x`-coordinate less than or equal to
        `principal`<sub>`x`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`width`</sub>-1 and a
        `y`-coordinate less than or equal to
        `principal`<sub>`y`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`height`</sub>-1 to
        `header list`.

    6.  If the `principal cell` is anchored in a
        <a href="#concept-column-group"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:concept-column-group">column
        group</a>, then add all header cells that are
        <a href="#column-group-header"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:column-group-header">column group
        headers</a> and are anchored in the same column group with an
        `x`-coordinate less than or equal to
        `principal`<sub>`x`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`width`</sub>-1 and a
        `y`-coordinate less than or equal to
        `principal`<sub>`y`</sub>+`principal`<sub>`height`</sub>-1 to
        `header list`.

4.  Remove all the <a href="#empty-cell"
    id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:empty-cell">empty cells</a> from
    the `header list`.

5.  Remove any duplicates from the `header list`.

6.  Remove `principal cell` from the `header list` if it is there.

7.  Assign the headers in the `header list` to the `principal cell`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The
<span id="internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells"
class="dfn">internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header
cells</span>, given a `principal cell`, a `header list`, an initial
coordinate (`initial`<sub>`x`</sub>, `initial`<sub>`y`</sub>), and Δ`x`
and Δ`y` increments, is as follows:

1.  Let `x` equal `initial`<sub>`x`</sub>.

2.  Let `y` equal `initial`<sub>`y`</sub>.

3.  Let `opaque headers` be an empty list of cells.

4.  If `principal cell` is a header cell  
    Let `in header block` be true, and let
    `headers from current header block` be a list of cells containing
    just the `principal cell`.

    Otherwise  
    Let `in header block` be false and let
    `headers from current header block` be an empty list of cells.

5.  *Loop*: Increment `x` by Δ`x`; increment `y` by Δ`y`.

    For each invocation of this algorithm, one of Δ`x` and Δ`y` will be
    −1, and the other will be 0.

6.  If either `x` or `y` are less than 0, then abort this internal
    algorithm.

7.  If there is no cell covering slot (`x`, `y`), or if there is more
    than one cell covering slot (`x`, `y`), return to the substep
    labeled *loop*.

8.  Let `current cell` be the cell covering slot (`x`, `y`).

9.  If `current cell` is a header cell  
    1.  Set `in header block` to true.

    2.  Add `current cell` to `headers from current header block`.

    3.  Let `blocked` be false.

    4.  If Δ`x` is 0  
        If there are any cells in the `opaque headers` list anchored
        with the same `x`-coordinate as the `current cell`, and with the
        same width as `current cell`, then let `blocked` be true.

        If the `current cell` is not a <a href="#column-header"
        id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:column-header">column header</a>,
        then let `blocked` be true.

        If Δ`y` is 0  
        If there are any cells in the `opaque headers` list anchored
        with the same `y`-coordinate as the `current cell`, and with the
        same height as `current cell`, then let `blocked` be true.

        If the `current cell` is not a
        <a href="#row-header" id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:row-header">row
        header</a>, then let `blocked` be true.

    5.  If `blocked` is false, then add the `current cell` to the
        `header list`.

    If `current cell` is a data cell and `in header block` is true  
    Set `in header block` to false. Add all the cells in
    `headers from current header block` to the `opaque headers` list,
    and empty the `headers from current header block` list.

10. Return to the step labeled *loop*.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (`x`, `y`) with width
`width` and height `height` is said to be a <span id="column-header"
class="dfn">column header</span> if any of the following are true:

- the cell's [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-th-scope-column-state"
  id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-column-state">Column</a>
  state; or

- the cell's [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-th-scope-auto-state"
  id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-auto-state">Auto</a>
  state, and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots
  with `y`-coordinates `y` .. `y`+`height`-1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (`x`, `y`) with width
`width` and height `height` is said to be a <span id="row-header"
class="dfn">row header</span> if any of the following are true:

- the cell's [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-th-scope-row-state"
  id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-row-state">Row</a>
  state; or

- the cell's [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-th-scope-auto-state"
  id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-auto-state-2">Auto</a>
  state, the cell is not a <a href="#column-header"
  id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:column-header-2">column header</a>,
  and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots with
  `x`-coordinates `x` .. `x`+`width`-1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A header cell is said to be a <span id="column-group-header"
class="dfn">column group header</span> if its [`scope`](#attr-th-scope)
attribute is in the <a href="#attr-th-scope-colgroup-state"
id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-colgroup-state">Column
Group</a> state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A header cell is said to be a <span id="row-group-header"
class="dfn">row group header</span> if its [`scope`](#attr-th-scope)
attribute is in the <a href="#attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state"
id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:attr-th-scope-rowgroup-state">Row
Group</a> state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A cell is said to be an <span id="empty-cell" class="dfn">empty
cell</span> if it contains no elements and its
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:child-text-content"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>, if any,
consists only of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
id="header-and-data-cell-semantics:space-characters"
data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.9.13</span> Examples<a href="#table-examples" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

The following shows how one might mark up the bottom part of table 45 of
the Smithsonian physical tables, Volume 71:

``` html
<table>
 <caption>Specification values: <b>Steel</b>, <b>Castings</b>,
 Ann. A.S.T.M. A27-16, Class B;* P max. 0.06; S max. 0.05.</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th rowspan=2>Grade.</th>
   <th rowspan=2>Yield Point.</th>
   <th colspan=2>Ultimate tensile strength</th>
   <th rowspan=2>Per cent elong. 50.8&nbsp;mm or 2&nbsp;in.</th>
   <th rowspan=2>Per cent reduct. area.</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
   <th>kg/mm<sup>2</sup></th>
   <th>lb/in<sup>2</sup></th>
  </tr>
 </thead>
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Hard</td>
   <td>0.45 ultimate</td>
   <td>56.2</td>
   <td>80,000</td>
   <td>15</td>
   <td>20</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
   <td>Medium</td>
   <td>0.45 ultimate</td>
   <td>49.2</td>
   <td>70,000</td>
   <td>18</td>
   <td>25</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
   <td>Soft</td>
   <td>0.45 ultimate</td>
   <td>42.2</td>
   <td>60,000</td>
   <td>22</td>
   <td>30</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>
```

This table could look like this:

| Grade. | Yield Point. | Ultimate tensile strength |  | Per cent elong. 50.8 mm or 2 in. | Per cent reduct. area. |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | kg/mm<sup>2</sup> | lb/in<sup>2</sup> |  |  |
| Hard | 0.45 ultimate | 56.2 | 80,000 | 15 | 20 |
| Medium | 0.45 ultimate | 49.2 | 70,000 | 18 | 25 |
| Soft | 0.45 ultimate | 42.2 | 60,000 | 22 | 30 |

Specification values: **Steel**, **Castings**, Ann. A.S.T.M. A27-16,
Class B;\* P max. 0.06; S max. 0.05. {#table-example-1}
