</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-input-placeholder" class="dfn" dfn-for="input"
dfn-type="element-attr">`placeholder`</span> attribute represents a
*short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data
entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a
brief description of the expected format. The attribute, if specified,
must have a value that contains no U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D
CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters.

The [`placeholder`](#attr-input-placeholder) attribute should not be
used as an alternative to a [`label`](#the-label-element). For a longer
hint or other advisory text, the [`title`](#attr-title) attribute is
more appropriate.

These mechanisms are very similar but subtly different: the hint given
by the control's [`label`](#the-label-element) is shown at all times;
the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#attr-input-placeholder)
attribute is shown before the user enters a value; and the hint in the
[`title`](#attr-title) attribute is shown when the user requests further
help.

User agents should present this hint to the user, after having
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-newlines"
id="the-placeholder-attribute:strip-newlines"
data-x-internal="strip-newlines">stripped newlines</a> from it, when the
element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-placeholder-attribute:concept-fe-value">value</a> is the empty
string, especially if the control is not
<a href="#focused" id="the-placeholder-attribute:focused">focused</a>.

If a user agent normally doesn't show this hint to the user when the
control is
<a href="#focused" id="the-placeholder-attribute:focused-2">focused</a>,
then the user agent should nonetheless show the hint for the control if
it was focused as a result of the [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus)
attribute, since in that case the user will not have had an opportunity
to examine the control before focusing it.

<div class="example">

Here is an example of a mail configuration user interface that uses the
[`placeholder`](#attr-input-placeholder) attribute:

``` html
<fieldset>
 <legend>Mail Account</legend>
 <p><label>Name: <input type="text" name="fullname" placeholder="John Ratzenberger"></label></p>
 <p><label>Address: <input type="email" name="address" placeholder="john@example.net"></label></p>
 <p><label>Password: <input type="password" name="password"></label></p>
 <p><label>Description: <input type="text" name="desc" placeholder="My Email Account"></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In situations where the control's content has one directionality but the
placeholder needs to have a different directionality, Unicode's
bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters can be used in the
attribute value:

``` html
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 1 &#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 2 &#x202E;">
```

For slightly more clarity, here's the same example using numeric
character references instead of inline Arabic:

``` html
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 1&#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 2&#x202E;">
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.10.5.4</span> Common [`input`](#the-input-element) element APIs<a href="#common-input-element-apis" class="self-link"></a>

`input``.`<a href="#dom-input-value"
id="dom-input-value-dev"><code>value</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

Returns the current <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value">value</a> of the form
control.

the control is neither date- or time-based nor numeric, or if the

The <span id="dom-input-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> IDL attribute allows scripts to
manipulate the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-5">value</a> of an
[`input`](#the-input-element) element. The attribute is in one of the
following modes, which define its behavior:

<span id="dom-input-value-value" class="dfn">value</span>  
<div algorithm="">

On getting, return the current <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-6">value</a> of the
element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting:

1.  Let `oldValue` be the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-7">value</a>.

2.  Set the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-8">value</a> to the
    new value.

3.  Set the element's <a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-dirty">dirty value flag</a>
    to true.

4.  Invoke the <a href="#value-sanitization-algorithm"
    id="common-input-element-apis:value-sanitization-algorithm">value
    sanitization algorithm</a>, if the element's
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state defines one.

5.  If the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-9">value</a> (after
    applying the <a href="#value-sanitization-algorithm"
    id="common-input-element-apis:value-sanitization-algorithm-2">value
    sanitization algorithm</a>) is different from `oldValue`, and the
    element has a <a href="#concept-textarea/input-cursor"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-textarea/input-cursor">text entry
    cursor position</a>, move the
    <a href="#concept-textarea/input-cursor"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-textarea/input-cursor-2">text
    entry cursor position</a> to the end of the text control,
    unselecting any selected text and
    <a href="#set-the-selection-direction"
    id="common-input-element-apis:set-the-selection-direction">resetting the
    selection direction</a> to "`none`".

</div>

<span id="dom-input-value-default" class="dfn">default</span>  
<div algorithm="">

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#attr-input-value) content
attribute, return that attribute's value; otherwise, return the empty
string.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, set the value of the element's [`value`](#attr-input-value)
content attribute to the new value.

</div>

<span id="dom-input-value-default-on" class="dfn">default/on</span>  
<div algorithm="">

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#attr-input-value) content
attribute, return that attribute's value; otherwise, return the string
"`on`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, set the value of the element's [`value`](#attr-input-value)
content attribute to the new value.

</div>

<span id="dom-input-value-filename" class="dfn">filename</span>  
<div algorithm="">

On getting, return the string "`C:\fakepath\`" followed by the name of
the first file in the list of
<a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-3">selected
files</a>, if any, or the empty string if the list is empty.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, if the new value is the empty string, empty the list of
<a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-4">selected
files</a>; otherwise, throw an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-6"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

</div>

This "fakepath" requirement is a sad accident of history. See [the
example in the File Upload state section](#fakepath-srsly) for more
information.

Since <a href="#concept-input-file-path"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-file-path">path
components</a> are not permitted in filenames in the list of
<a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-5">selected
files</a>, the "\fakepath\\ cannot be mistaken for a path component.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-input-checked" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`checked`</span> IDL attribute allows scripts to
manipulate the <a href="#concept-fe-checked"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-checked-3">checkedness</a> of
an [`input`](#the-input-element) element. On getting, it must return the
current <a href="#concept-fe-checked"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-checked-4">checkedness</a> of
the element; and on setting, it must set the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-checked"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-checked-5">checkedness</a> to
the new value and set the element's
<a href="#concept-input-checked-dirty-flag"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-checked-dirty-flag">dirty
checkedness flag</a> to true.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="dom-input-files" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`files`</span> IDL attribute allows scripts to
access the element's <a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-6">selected
files</a>.

<div algorithm="">

On getting, if the IDL attribute <a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-apply">applies</a>, it must
return a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
data-x-internal="filelist"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:filelist-3">FileList</code></a> object
that represents the current <a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-7">selected
files</a>. The same object must be returned until the list of
<a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-8">selected
files</a> changes. If the IDL attribute
<a href="#do-not-apply" id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply">does
not apply</a>, then it must instead return null.
[\[FILEAPI\]](#refsFILEAPI)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, it must run these steps:

1.  If the IDL attribute <a href="#do-not-apply"
    id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-2">does not apply</a> or
    the given value is null, then return.

2.  Replace the element's <a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-type-file-selected-9">selected
    files</a> with the given value.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="dom-input-valueasdate" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLInputElement" dfn-type="attribute">`valueAsDate`</span> IDL
attribute represents the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-10">value</a> of the
element, interpreted as a date.

<div algorithm="">

On getting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#dom-input-valueasdate) attribute
<a href="#do-not-apply"
id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-3">does not apply</a>, as
defined for the [`input`](#the-input-element) element's
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then return null.
Otherwise, run the <a href="#concept-input-value-string-date"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-string-date">algorithm
to convert a string to a <code>Date</code> object</a> defined for that
state to the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-11">value</a>; if the
algorithm returned a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects"
data-x-internal="date"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:date-2">Date</code></a> object, then
return it, otherwise, return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#dom-input-valueasdate) attribute
<a href="#do-not-apply"
id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-4">does not apply</a>, as
defined for the [`input`](#the-input-element) element's
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-7"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-9">DOMException</code></a>;
otherwise, if the new value is not null and not a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects"
data-x-internal="date"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:date-3">Date</code></a> object throw a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:typeerror">TypeError</code></a> exception;
otherwise, if the new value is null or a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects"
data-x-internal="date"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:date-4">Date</code></a> object
representing the NaN time value, then set the
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-12">value</a> of the
element to the empty string; otherwise, run the
<a href="#concept-input-value-date-string"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-date-string">algorithm
to convert a <code>Date</code> object to a string</a>, as defined for
that state, on the new value, and set the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-13">value</a> of the
element to the resulting string.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="dom-input-valueasnumber" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLInputElement" dfn-type="attribute">`valueAsNumber`</span>
IDL attribute represents the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-14">value</a> of the
element, interpreted as a number.

<div algorithm="">

On getting, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#dom-input-valueasnumber) attribute
<a href="#do-not-apply"
id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-5">does not apply</a>, as
defined for the [`input`](#the-input-element) element's
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then return a
Not-a-Number (NaN) value. Otherwise, run the
<a href="#concept-input-value-string-number"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-string-number">algorithm
to convert a string to a number</a> defined for that state to the
element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-15">value</a>; if the
algorithm returned a number, then return it, otherwise, return a
Not-a-Number (NaN) value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On setting, if the new value is infinite, then throw a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:typeerror-2">TypeError</code></a>
exception. Otherwise, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#dom-input-valueasnumber)
attribute <a href="#do-not-apply"
id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-6">does not apply</a>, as
defined for the [`input`](#the-input-element) element's
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-8"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-10">DOMException</code></a>.
Otherwise, if the new value is a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then set the
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-16">value</a> of the
element to the empty string. Otherwise, run the
<a href="#concept-input-value-number-string"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-number-string">algorithm
to convert a number to a string</a>, as defined for that state, on the
new value, and set the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-17">value</a> of the
element to the resulting string.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-input-stepdown" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="method">`stepDown(``n``)`</span> and
<span id="dom-input-stepup" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="method">`stepUp(``n``)`</span> methods, when invoked, must run
the following algorithm:

1.  If the [`stepDown()`](#dom-input-stepdown) and
    [`stepUp()`](#dom-input-stepup) methods
    <a href="#do-not-apply" id="common-input-element-apis:do-not-apply-7">do
    not apply</a>, as defined for the [`input`](#the-input-element)
    element's [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then
    throw an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-9"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-11">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If the element has no <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step">allowed value step</a>,
    then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-10"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-12">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  If the element has a <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min">minimum</a> and a
    <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max">maximum</a> and the
    <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-2">minimum</a> is
    greater than the <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-2">maximum</a>, then
    return.

4.  If the element has a <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-3">minimum</a> and a
    <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-3">maximum</a> and
    there is no value greater than or equal to the element's
    <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-4">minimum</a> and
    less than or equal to the element's <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-4">maximum</a> that,
    when subtracted from the <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero">step base</a>,
    is an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-2">allowed value
    step</a>, then return.

5.  If applying the <a href="#concept-input-value-string-number"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-string-number-2">algorithm
    to convert a string to a number</a> to the string given by the
    element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-18">value</a> does
    not result in an error, then let `value` be the result of that
    algorithm. Otherwise, let `value` be zero.

6.  Let `valueBeforeStepping` be `value`.

7.  If `value` subtracted from the <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero-2">step base</a>
    is not an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-3">allowed value
    step</a>, then set `value` to the nearest value that, when
    subtracted from the <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero-3">step base</a>,
    is an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-4">allowed value
    step</a>, and that is less than `value` if the method invoked was
    the [`stepDown()`](#dom-input-stepdown) method, and more than
    `value` otherwise.

    Otherwise (`value` subtracted from the
    <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero-4">step base</a>
    is an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-5">allowed value
    step</a>):

    1.  Let `n` be the argument.

    2.  Let `delta` be the <a href="#concept-input-step"
        id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-6">allowed value
        step</a> multiplied by `n`.

    3.  If the method invoked was the
        [`stepDown()`](#dom-input-stepdown) method, negate `delta`.

    4.  Let `value` be the result of adding `delta` to `value`.

8.  If the element has a <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-5">minimum</a>, and
    `value` is less than that <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-6">minimum</a>, then
    set `value` to the smallest value that, when subtracted from the
    <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero-5">step base</a>,
    is an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-7">allowed value
    step</a>, and that is more than or equal to that
    <a href="#concept-input-min"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-7">minimum</a>.

9.  If the element has a <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-5">maximum</a>, and
    `value` is greater than that <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-6">maximum</a>, then
    set `value` to the largest value that, when subtracted from the
    <a href="#concept-input-min-zero"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-min-zero-6">step base</a>,
    is an integral multiple of the <a href="#concept-input-step"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-step-8">allowed value
    step</a>, and that is less than or equal to that
    <a href="#concept-input-max"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-max-7">maximum</a>.

10. If either the method invoked was the
    [`stepDown()`](#dom-input-stepdown) method and `value` is greater
    than `valueBeforeStepping`, or the method invoked was the
    [`stepUp()`](#dom-input-stepup) method and `value` is less than
    `valueBeforeStepping`, then return.

    <div class="example">

    This ensures that invoking the [`stepUp()`](#dom-input-stepup)
    method on the [`input`](#the-input-element) element in the following
    example does not change the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-19">value</a> of that
    element:

    ``` html
    <input type=number value=1 max=0>
    ```

    </div>

11. Let `value as string` be the result of running the
    <a href="#concept-input-value-number-string"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-value-number-string-2">algorithm
    to convert a number to a string</a>, as defined for the
    [`input`](#the-input-element) element's [`type`](#attr-input-type)
    attribute's current state, on `value`.

12. Set the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-20">value</a> of the
    element to `value as string`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-input-list" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`list`</span> IDL attribute must return the current
<a href="#concept-input-list"
id="common-input-element-apis:concept-input-list">suggestions source
element</a>, if any, or null otherwise.

<div algorithm="">

The [`HTMLInputElement`](#htmlinputelement)
<span id="dom-input-showpicker" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLInputElement"
dfn-type="method">`showPicker()`</span> and
[`HTMLSelectElement`](#htmlselectelement)
<span id="dom-select-showpicker" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="method">`showPicker()`</span> method steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    is not <a href="#concept-fe-mutable"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-mutable-2">mutable</a>,
    then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:invalidstateerror-11"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-13">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="common-input-element-apis:relevant-settings-object">relevant
    settings object</a>'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>
    is not
    <a href="#same-origin" id="common-input-element-apis:same-origin">same
    origin</a> with <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="common-input-element-apis:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant
    settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
    origin</a>, and <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element, or
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is not in the
    <a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
    id="common-input-element-apis:file-upload-state-(type=file)-2">File
    Upload</a> state or <a href="#color-state-(type=color)"
    id="common-input-element-apis:color-state-(type=color)-2">Color</a>
    state, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:securityerror-2"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-14">DOMException</code></a>.

    <a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
    id="common-input-element-apis:file-upload-state-(type=file)-3">File</a>
    and <a href="#color-state-(type=color)"
    id="common-input-element-apis:color-state-(type=color)-3">Color</a>
    inputs are exempted from this check for historical reason: their
    <a href="#input-activation-behavior"
    id="common-input-element-apis:input-activation-behavior">input
    activation behavior</a> also shows their pickers, and has never been
    guarded by an origin check.

3.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a> does not have <a href="#transient-activation"
    id="common-input-element-apis:transient-activation-2">transient
    activation</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notallowederror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:notallowederror-2"
    data-x-internal="notallowederror">"<code>NotAllowedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-15">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element, and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    is not <a href="#being-rendered"
    id="common-input-element-apis:being-rendered">being rendered</a>,
    then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="common-input-element-apis:notsupportederror"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:domexception-16">DOMException</code></a>.

5.  <a href="#show-the-picker,-if-applicable"
    id="common-input-element-apis:show-the-picker,-if-applicable">Show the
    picker, if applicable</a>, for
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="common-input-element-apis:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="show-the-picker,-if-applicable" class="dfn">show the
picker, if applicable</span> for an [`input`](#the-input-element) or
[`select`](#the-select-element) element `element`:

1.  If `element`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
    object</a> does not have <a href="#transient-activation"
    id="common-input-element-apis:transient-activation-3">transient
    activation</a>, then return.

2.  If `element` is not *[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)*, then return.

3.  <a href="#consume-user-activation"
    id="common-input-element-apis:consume-user-activation">Consume user
    activation</a> given `element`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-relevant-global-3">relevant global
    object</a>.

4.  If `element` does not <a href="#input-support-picker"
    id="common-input-element-apis:input-support-picker-2">support a
    picker</a>, then return.

5.  If `element` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element and
    `element`'s [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
    <a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
    id="common-input-element-apis:file-upload-state-(type=file)-4">File
    Upload</a> state, then run these steps
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="common-input-element-apis:in-parallel">in
    parallel</a>:

    1.  Optionally, wait until any prior execution of this algorithm has
        terminated.

    2.  Let `dismissed` be the result of <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-file-dialog-opened"
        id="common-input-element-apis:webdriver-bidi-file-dialog-opened"
        data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-file-dialog-opened">WebDriver BiDi file
        dialog opened</a> with `element`.

    3.  If `dismissed` is false:

        1.  Display a prompt to the user requesting that the user
            specify some files. If the
            [`multiple`](#attr-input-multiple) attribute is not set on
            `element`, there must be no more than one file selected;
            otherwise, any number may be selected. Files can be from the
            filesystem or created on the fly, e.g., a picture taken from
            a camera connected to the user's device.

        2.  Wait for the user to have made their selection.

    4.  If `dismissed` is true or if the user dismissed the prompt
        without changing their selection, then
        <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
        id="common-input-element-apis:queue-an-element-task">queue an element
        task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
        id="common-input-element-apis:user-interaction-task-source">user
        interaction task source</a> given `element` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="common-input-element-apis:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`cancel`](#event-cancel) at `element`, with the
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
        data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
        id="common-input-element-apis:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
        attribute initialized to true.

    5.  Otherwise, <a href="#update-the-file-selection"
        id="common-input-element-apis:update-the-file-selection">update the file
        selection</a> for `element`.

    As with all user interface specifications, user agents have a good
    deal of freedom in how they interpret these requirements. The above
    text implies that a user either dismisses the prompt or changes
    their selection; exactly one of these will be true. But the mapping
    of these possibilities to specific user interface elements is not
    mandated by the standard. For example, a user agent might interpret
    clicking the "Cancel" button when files were previously selected as
    a change of selection to select zero files, thus firing
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
    data-x-internal="event-input"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:event-input">input</code></a> and
    [`change`](#event-change). Or it might interpret such a click as a
    dismissal that leaves the selection unchanged, thus firing
    [`cancel`](#event-cancel). Similarly, it's up to the user agent
    whether re-selecting the same files as were previously selected
    counts as a dismissal, or as a change of selection.

6.  Otherwise, the user agent should show the relevant user interface
    for selecting a value for `element`, in the way it normally would
    when the user interacts with the control.

    When showing such a user interface, it must respect the requirements
    stated in the relevant parts of the specification for how `element`
    behaves given its [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute state. (For
    example, various sections describe restrictions on the resulting
    <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="common-input-element-apis:concept-fe-value-21">value</a>
    string.)

    This step can have side effects, such as closing other pickers that
    were previously shown by this algorithm. (If this closes a file
    selection picker, then per the above that will lead to firing either
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
    data-x-internal="event-input"><code
    id="common-input-element-apis:event-input-2">input</code></a> and
    [`change`](#event-change) events, or a [`cancel`](#event-cancel)
    event.)

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.10.5.5</span> Common event behaviors<a href="#common-input-element-events" class="self-link"></a>

When the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input">input</code></a> and
[`change`](#event-change) events <a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-input-apply">apply</a> (which is
the case for all [`input`](#the-input-element) controls other than
<a href="#concept-button"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-button">buttons</a> and those
with the [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#hidden-state-(type=hidden)"
id="common-input-element-events:hidden-state-(type=hidden)">Hidden</a>
state), the events are fired to indicate that the user has interacted
with the control. The
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-2">input</code></a> event
fires whenever the user has modified the data of the control. The
[`change`](#event-change) event fires when the value is committed, if
that makes sense for the control, or else when the control [loses
focus](#unfocus-causes-change-event). In all cases, the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-3">input</code></a> event
comes before the corresponding [`change`](#event-change) event (if any).

When an [`input`](#the-input-element) element has a defined
<a href="#input-activation-behavior"
id="common-input-element-events:input-activation-behavior">input
activation behavior</a>, the rules for dispatching these events, if they
<a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-input-apply-2">apply</a>, are
given in the section above that defines the [`type`](#attr-input-type)
attribute's state. (This is the case for all
[`input`](#the-input-element) controls with the
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)"
id="common-input-element-events:checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)">Checkbox</a>
state, the <a href="#radio-button-state-(type=radio)"
id="common-input-element-events:radio-button-state-(type=radio)">Radio
Button</a> state, or the <a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
id="common-input-element-events:file-upload-state-(type=file)">File
Upload</a> state.)

<div algorithm="">

For [`input`](#the-input-element) elements without a defined
<a href="#input-activation-behavior"
id="common-input-element-events:input-activation-behavior-2">input
activation behavior</a>, but to which these events
<a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-input-apply-3">apply</a>, and
for which the user interface involves both interactive manipulation and
an explicit commit action, then when the user changes the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value">value</a>, the user
agent must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task">queue an element
task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="common-input-element-events:user-interaction-task-source">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-4">input</code></a> at the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
and <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-composed">composed</code></a>
attributes initialized to true, and any time the user commits the
change, the user agent must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task-2">queue an
element task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="common-input-element-events:user-interaction-task-source-2">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to set its <a href="#user-validity"
id="common-input-element-events:user-validity">user validity</a> to true
and <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-2"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`change`](#event-change) at the [`input`](#the-input-element) element,
with the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-2">bubbles</code></a>
attribute initialized to true.

</div>

An example of a user interface involving both interactive manipulation
and a commit action would be a <a href="#range-state-(type=range)"
id="common-input-element-events:range-state-(type=range)">Range</a>
controls that use a slider, when manipulated using a pointing device.
While the user is dragging the control's knob,
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-5">input</code></a> events
would fire whenever the position changed, whereas the
[`change`](#event-change) event would only fire when the user let go of
the knob, committing to a specific value.

<div algorithm="">

For [`input`](#the-input-element) elements without a defined
<a href="#input-activation-behavior"
id="common-input-element-events:input-activation-behavior-3">input
activation behavior</a>, but to which these events
<a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-input-apply-4">apply</a>, and
for which the user interface involves an explicit commit action but no
intermediate manipulation, then any time the user commits a change to
the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-2">value</a>, the user
agent must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task-3">queue an
element task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="common-input-element-events:user-interaction-task-source-3">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to first
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-3"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-6">input</code></a> at the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-3">bubbles</code></a>
and <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-composed-2">composed</code></a>
attributes initialized to true, and then
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-4"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`change`](#event-change) at the [`input`](#the-input-element) element,
with the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-4">bubbles</code></a>
attribute initialized to true.

</div>

An example of a user interface with a commit action would be a
<a href="#color-state-(type=color)"
id="common-input-element-events:color-state-(type=color)">Color</a>
control that consists of a single button that brings up a color wheel:
if the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-3">value</a> only
changes when the dialog is closed, then that would be the explicit
commit action. On the other hand, if manipulating the control changes
the color interactively, then there might be no commit action.

Another example of a user interface with a commit action would be a
<a href="#date-state-(type=date)"
id="common-input-element-events:date-state-(type=date)">Date</a> control
that allows both text-based user input and user selection from a
drop-down calendar: while text input might not have an explicit commit
step, selecting a date from the drop down calendar and then dismissing
the drop down would be a commit action.

<div algorithm="">

For [`input`](#the-input-element) elements without a defined
<a href="#input-activation-behavior"
id="common-input-element-events:input-activation-behavior-4">input
activation behavior</a>, but to which these events
<a href="#concept-input-apply"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-input-apply-5">apply</a>, any
time the user causes the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-4">value</a> to change
without an explicit commit action, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task-4">queue an
element task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="common-input-element-events:user-interaction-task-source-4">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-5"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-7">input</code></a> at the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-5">bubbles</code></a>
and <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-composed-3">composed</code></a>
attributes initialized to true. The corresponding
[`change`](#event-change) event, if any, will be fired when the control
[loses focus](#unfocus-causes-change-event).

</div>

Examples of a user changing the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-5">value</a> would
include the user typing into a text control, pasting a new value into
the control, or undoing an edit in that control. Some user interactions
do not cause changes to the value, e.g., hitting the "delete" key in an
empty text control, or replacing some text in the control with text from
the clipboard that happens to be exactly the same text.

A <a href="#range-state-(type=range)"
id="common-input-element-events:range-state-(type=range)-2">Range</a>
control in the form of a slider that the user has
<a href="#focused" id="common-input-element-events:focused">focused</a>
and is interacting with using a keyboard would be another example of the
user changing the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-6">value</a> without a
commit step.

In the case of <a href="#concept-task"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-task">tasks</a> that just fire
an <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-8">input</code></a> event,
user agents may wait for a suitable break in the user's interaction
before <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task-5">queuing</a> the
tasks; for example, a user agent could wait for the user to have not hit
a key for 100ms, so as to only fire the event when the user pauses,
instead of continuously for each keystroke.

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to change an [`input`](#the-input-element)
element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-7">value</a> on behalf
of the user (e.g. as part of a form prefilling feature), the user agent
must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="common-input-element-events:queue-an-element-task-6">queue an
element task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="common-input-element-events:user-interaction-task-source-5">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to first update the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-fe-value-8">value</a>
accordingly, then
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-6"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="common-input-element-events:event-input-9">input</code></a> at the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-6">bubbles</code></a>
and <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-composed-4">composed</code></a>
attributes initialized to true, then
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="common-input-element-events:concept-event-fire-7"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`change`](#event-change) at the [`input`](#the-input-element) element,
with the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="common-input-element-events:dom-event-bubbles-7">bubbles</code></a>
attribute initialized to true.

</div>

These events are not fired in response to changes made to the values of
form controls by scripts. (This is to make it easier to update the
values of form controls in response to the user manipulating the
controls, without having to then filter out the script's own changes to
avoid an infinite loop.)

These events are also not fired when the browser changes the values of
form controls as part of <a href="#restore-persisted-state"
id="common-input-element-events:restore-persisted-state">state
restoration during navigation</a>.

#### <span class="secno">4.10.6</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`button`</span> element<a href="#the-button-element" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-button-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-button-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#interactive-content-2"
id="the-button-element:interactive-content-2">Interactive content</a>.

<a href="#category-listed"
id="the-button-element:category-listed">Listed</a>,
<a href="#category-label"
id="the-button-element:category-label">labelable</a>,
<a href="#category-submit"
id="the-button-element:category-submit">submittable</a>, and
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="the-button-element:category-autocapitalize">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting</a> <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="the-button-element:form-associated-element">form-associated
element</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-button-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-button-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

As the first child of a [`select`](#the-select-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-button-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>, but
there must be no <a href="#interactive-content-2"
id="the-button-element:interactive-content-2-2">interactive content</a>
descendant and no descendant with the [`tabindex`](#attr-tabindex)
attribute specified. If the element is the first child of a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element, then it may also have zero or
one descendant [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element)
element.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-button-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`command`](#attr-button-command) — Indicates to the targeted element
which action to take.

[`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) — Targets another element to be
invoked.

[`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#attr-fae-form) — Associates the element with a
[`form`](#the-form-element) element

[`formaction`](#attr-fs-formaction) —
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-button-element:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> to use for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2">form submission</a>

[`formenctype`](#attr-fs-formenctype) —
<a href="#entry-list" id="the-button-element:entry-list">Entry list</a>
encoding type to use for <a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-2">form submission</a>

[`formmethod`](#attr-fs-formmethod) — Variant to use for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-3">form submission</a>

[`formnovalidate`](#attr-fs-formnovalidate) — Bypass form control
validation for <a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-4">form submission</a>

[`formtarget`](#attr-fs-formtarget) —
<a href="#navigable" id="the-button-element:navigable">Navigable</a> for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-5">form submission</a>

[`name`](#attr-fe-name) — Name of the element to use for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-6">form submission</a> and in
the [`form.elements`](#dom-form-elements) API

[`popovertarget`](#attr-popovertarget) — Targets a popover element to
toggle, show, or hide

[`popovertargetaction`](#attr-popovertargetaction) — Indicates whether a
targeted popover element is to be toggled, shown, or hidden

[`type`](#attr-button-type) — Type of button

[`value`](#attr-button-value) — Value to be used for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-button-element:form-submission-2-7">form submission</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-button).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-button).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLButtonElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString command;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute Element? commandForElement;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute USVString formAction;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString formEnctype;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString formMethod;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean formNoValidate;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString formTarget;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
HTMLButtonElement includes PopoverTargetAttributes;
```

The [`button`](#the-button-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-button-element:represents">represents</a>
a button labeled by its contents.

The element is a <a href="#concept-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-button">button</a>.

The <span id="attr-button-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="button"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute controls the behavior of
the button when it is activated. It is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-button-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-button-type-submit" class="dfn" dfn-for="button/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`submit`</span> | <span id="attr-button-type-submit-state" class="dfn">Submit Button</span> | Submits the form. |
| <span id="attr-button-type-reset" class="dfn" dfn-for="button/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`reset`</span> | <span id="attr-button-type-reset-state" class="dfn">Reset Button</span> | Resets the form. |
| <span id="attr-button-type-button" class="dfn" dfn-for="button/type" dfn-type="attr-value">`button`</span> | <span id="attr-button-type-button-state" class="dfn">Button</span> | Does nothing. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-button-type-auto-state" class="dfn">Auto</span> state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`button`](#the-button-element) element is said to be a
<a href="#concept-submit-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-submit-button">submit button</a> if any
of the following are true:

- the [`type`](#attr-button-type) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-button-type-auto-state"
  id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-auto-state">Auto</a> state,
  both the [`command`](#attr-button-command) and
  [`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) content attributes are not
  present, and the
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-parent"
  id="the-button-element:parent" data-x-internal="parent">parent</a>
  node is not a [`select`](#the-select-element) element; or

- the [`type`](#attr-button-type) attribute is in the
  <a href="#attr-button-type-submit-state"
  id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-submit-state">Submit Button</a>
  state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

**Constraint validation**: If the element is not a
<a href="#concept-submit-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-submit-button-2">submit button</a>, the
element is <a href="#barred-from-constraint-validation"
id="the-button-element:barred-from-constraint-validation">barred from
constraint validation</a>.

</div>

If a [`button`](#the-button-element) element is the first
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
id="the-button-element:concept-tree-child"
data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">child</a> which is an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
id="the-button-element:element" data-x-internal="element">element</a> of
a [`select`](#the-select-element) element, then it is
<a href="#inert" id="the-button-element:inert">inert</a>.

If specified, the <span id="attr-button-commandfor" class="dfn"
dfn-for="button" dfn-type="element-attr">`commandfor`</span> attribute
value must be the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="the-button-element:concept-id" data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a>
of an element in the same
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="the-button-element:tree" data-x-internal="tree">tree</a> as the
<a href="#concept-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-button-2">button</a> with the
[`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) attribute.

The <span id="attr-button-command" class="dfn" dfn-for="button"
dfn-type="element-attr">`command`</span> attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-button-element:enumerated-attribute-2">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-button-command-toggle-popover" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`toggle-popover`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-toggle-popover-state" class="dfn">Toggle Popover</span> | Shows or hides the targeted [`popover`](#attr-popover) element. |
| <span id="attr-button-command-show-popover" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`show-popover`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-show-popover-state" class="dfn">Show Popover</span> | Shows the targeted [`popover`](#attr-popover) element. |
| <span id="attr-button-command-hide-popover" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`hide-popover`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-hide-popover-state" class="dfn">Hide Popover</span> | Hides the targeted [`popover`](#attr-popover) element. |
| <span id="attr-button-command-close" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`close`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-close-state" class="dfn">Close</span> | Closes the targeted [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element. |
| <span id="attr-button-command-request-close" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`request-close`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-request-close-state" class="dfn">Request Close</span> | Requests to close the targeted [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element. |
| <span id="attr-button-command-show-modal" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/command" dfn-type="attr-value">`show-modal`</span> | <span id="attr-button-command-show-modal-state" class="dfn">Show Modal</span> | Opens the targeted [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element as modal. |
| A <a href="#attr-button-command-custom"
id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-custom">custom command
keyword</a> | <span id="attr-button-command-custom-state" class="dfn">Custom</span> | Only dispatches the [`command`](#event-command) event on the targeted element. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-button-command-unknown-state" class="dfn">Unknown</span>
state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="attr-button-command-custom" class="dfn">custom command
keyword</span> is a string that
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-starts-with"
id="the-button-element:starts-with" data-x-internal="starts-with">starts
with</a> "`--`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="determine-if-command-is-valid" class="dfn">determine if a
command is valid for a target</span> given a
[`command`](#attr-button-command) attribute `command` and an element
`target`:

1.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-unknown-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-unknown-state">Unknown</a>
    state, then return false.

2.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-custom-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-custom-state">Custom</a>
    state, then return true.

3.  If `target` is not an
    <a href="#html-elements" id="the-button-element:html-elements">HTML
    element</a>, then return false.

4.  If `command` is in any of the following states:

    - <a href="#attr-button-command-toggle-popover-state"
      id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-toggle-popover-state">Toggle
      Popover</a>

    - <a href="#attr-button-command-show-popover-state"
      id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-show-popover-state">Show
      Popover</a>

    - <a href="#attr-button-command-hide-popover-state"
      id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-hide-popover-state">Hide
      Popover</a>

    then return true.

5.  If this standard does not define <a href="#is-valid-command-steps"
    id="the-button-element:is-valid-command-steps">is valid command
    steps</a> for `target`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
    id="the-button-element:concept-element-local-name"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a>, then
    return false.

6.  Otherwise, return the result of running `target`'s corresponding
    <a href="#is-valid-command-steps"
    id="the-button-element:is-valid-command-steps-2">is valid command
    steps</a> given `command`.

<div class="note">

The intent is to avoid dispatching a command event on an element type
that does not support that command.

However, element state is not considered. If an element can support a
particular command, the event is dispatched, even if that element is in
a state where it cannot execute that command.

This means, for example, that command events are dispatched for popover
commands on all
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-button-element:html-elements-2">HTML
elements</a>, even if they do not have a [`popover`](#attr-popover)
attribute.

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`button`](#the-button-element) element `element`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="the-button-element:activation-behaviour"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a> given
`event` is:

1.  If `element` is <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
    id="the-button-element:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a>, then
    return.

2.  If `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-button-element:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="the-button-element:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return.

3.  If `element` has a
    <a href="#form-owner" id="the-button-element:form-owner">form owner</a>:

    1.  If `element` is a <a href="#concept-submit-button"
        id="the-button-element:concept-submit-button-3">submit button</a>,
        then <a href="#concept-form-submit"
        id="the-button-element:concept-form-submit">submit</a>
        `element`'s
        <a href="#form-owner" id="the-button-element:form-owner-2">form
        owner</a> from `element` with
        *[userInvolvement](#submit-user-involvement)* set to `event`'s
        <a href="#event-uni" id="the-button-element:event-uni">user navigation
        involvement</a>, and return.

    2.  If `element`'s [`type`](#attr-button-type) attribute is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-type-reset-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-reset-state">Reset Button</a>
        state, then <a href="#concept-form-reset"
        id="the-button-element:concept-form-reset">reset</a> `element`'s
        <a href="#form-owner" id="the-button-element:form-owner-3">form
        owner</a>, and return.

    3.  If `element`'s [`type`](#attr-button-type) attribute is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-type-auto-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-auto-state-2">Auto</a>
        state, then return.

4.  Let `target` be the result of running `element`'s
    <a href="#attr-associated-element"
    id="the-button-element:attr-associated-element">get the
    <code>commandfor</code>-associated element</a>.

5.  If `target` is not null:

    1.  Let `command` be `element`'s [`command`](#attr-button-command)
        attribute.

    2.  If the result of <a href="#determine-if-command-is-valid"
        id="the-button-element:determine-if-command-is-valid">determining if a
        command is valid for a target</a> given `command` and `target`
        is false, then return.

    3.  Let `continue` be the result of
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="the-button-element:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">firing an event</a> named
        [`command`](#event-command) at `target`, using
        [`CommandEvent`](#commandevent), with its
        [`command`](#dom-commandevent-command) attribute initialized to
        `command`, its [`source`](#dom-commandevent-source) attribute
        initialized to `element`, and its
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
        data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
        id="the-button-element:dom-event-cancelable">cancelable</code></a>
        attribute initialized to true.

        [DOM standard issue
        \#1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328) tracks how to
        better standardize associated event data in a way which makes
        sense on Events. Currently an event attribute initialized to a
        value cannot also have a getter, and so an internal slot (or map
        of additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

    4.  If `continue` is false, then return.

    5.  If `target` is not
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
        id="the-button-element:connected"
        data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then return.

    6.  If `command` is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-command-custom-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-custom-state-2">Custom</a>
        state, then return.

    7.  If `command` is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-command-hide-popover-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-hide-popover-state-2">Hide
        Popover</a> state:

        1.  If the result of running <a href="#check-popover-validity"
            id="the-button-element:check-popover-validity">check popover
            validity</a> given `target`, true, false, and null is true,
            then run the <a href="#hide-popover-algorithm"
            id="the-button-element:hide-popover-algorithm">hide popover
            algorithm</a> given `target`, true, true, false, and
            `element`.

    8.  Otherwise, if `command` is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-command-toggle-popover-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-toggle-popover-state-2">Toggle
        Popover</a> state:

        1.  If the result of running <a href="#check-popover-validity"
            id="the-button-element:check-popover-validity-2">check popover
            validity</a> given `target`, false, false, and null is true,
            then run the
            <a href="#show-popover" id="the-button-element:show-popover">show
            popover algorithm</a> given `target`, false, and `element`.

        2.  Otherwise, if the result of running
            <a href="#check-popover-validity"
            id="the-button-element:check-popover-validity-3">check popover
            validity</a> given `target`, true, false, and null is true,
            then run the <a href="#hide-popover-algorithm"
            id="the-button-element:hide-popover-algorithm-2">hide popover
            algorithm</a> given `target`, true, true, false, and
            `element`.

    9.  Otherwise, if `command` is in the
        <a href="#attr-button-command-show-popover-state"
        id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-show-popover-state-2">Show
        Popover</a> state:

        1.  If the result of running <a href="#check-popover-validity"
            id="the-button-element:check-popover-validity-4">check popover
            validity</a> given `target`, false, false, and null is true,
            then run the
            <a href="#show-popover" id="the-button-element:show-popover-2">show
            popover algorithm</a> given `target`, false, and `element`.

    10. Otherwise, if this standard defines
        <a href="#command-steps" id="the-button-element:command-steps">command
        steps</a> for `target`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
        id="the-button-element:concept-element-local-name-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a>,
        then run the corresponding
        <a href="#command-steps" id="the-button-element:command-steps-2">command
        steps</a> given `target`, `element`, and `command`.

6.  Otherwise, run the
    <a href="#popover-target-attribute-activation-behavior"
    id="the-button-element:popover-target-attribute-activation-behavior">popover
    target attribute activation behavior</a> given `element` and
    `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-target"
    id="the-button-element:concept-event-target"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-target">target</a>.

</div>

An <a href="#html-elements" id="the-button-element:html-elements-3">HTML
element</a> can have specific <span id="is-valid-command-steps"
class="dfn">is valid command steps</span> and <span id="command-steps"
class="dfn">command steps</span> defined for the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
id="the-button-element:concept-element-local-name-3"
data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a>.

The [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate
the [`button`](#the-button-element) element with its
<a href="#form-owner" id="the-button-element:form-owner-4">form
owner</a>. The [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute represents the
element's name. The [`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to
make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being
submitted. The [`formaction`](#attr-fs-formaction),
[`formenctype`](#attr-fs-formenctype),
[`formmethod`](#attr-fs-formmethod),
[`formnovalidate`](#attr-fs-formnovalidate), and
[`formtarget`](#attr-fs-formtarget) attributes are
<a href="#attributes-for-form-submission"
id="the-button-element:attributes-for-form-submission">attributes for
form submission</a>.

The [`formnovalidate`](#attr-fs-formnovalidate) attribute can be used to
make submit buttons that do not trigger the constraint validation.

The [`formaction`](#attr-fs-formaction),
[`formenctype`](#attr-fs-formenctype),
[`formmethod`](#attr-fs-formmethod),
[`formnovalidate`](#attr-fs-formnovalidate), and
[`formtarget`](#attr-fs-formtarget) must not be specified if the element
is not a <a href="#concept-submit-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-submit-button-4">submit button</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-button-command" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLButtonElement" dfn-type="attribute">`command`</span> getter
steps are:

1.  Let `command` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-button-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`command`](#attr-button-command) attribute.

2.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-custom-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-custom-state-3">Custom</a>
    state, then return `command`'s value.

3.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-unknown-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-unknown-state-2">Unknown</a>
    state, then return the empty string.

4.  Return the keyword corresponding to the value of `command`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-button-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="button"
dfn-type="element-attr">`value`</span> attribute gives the element's
value for the purposes of form submission. The element's
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-button-element:concept-fe-value">value</a> is the value of the
element's [`value`](#attr-button-value) attribute, if there is one;
otherwise the empty string. The element's
<a href="#concept-fe-optional-value"
id="the-button-element:concept-fe-optional-value">optional value</a> is
the value of the element's [`value`](#attr-button-value) attribute, if
there is one; otherwise null.

</div>

A button (and its value) is only included in the form submission if the
button itself was used to initiate the form submission.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-button-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLButtonElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> getter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-button-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a> is a
    <a href="#concept-submit-button"
    id="the-button-element:concept-submit-button-5">submit button</a>,
    then return "`submit`".

2.  Let `state` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-button-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`type`](#attr-button-type) attribute.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-button-element:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `state` is not in the <a href="#attr-button-type-submit-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-submit-state-2">Submit
    Button</a> state.

4.  If `state` is in the <a href="#attr-button-type-auto-state"
    id="the-button-element:attr-button-type-auto-state-3">Auto</a>
    state, then return "`button`".

5.  Return the keyword value corresponding to `state`.

</div>

The [`willValidate`](#dom-cva-willvalidate),
[`validity`](#dom-cva-validity), and
[`validationMessage`](#dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and
the [`checkValidity()`](#dom-cva-checkvalidity),
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-cva-reportvalidity), and
[`setCustomValidity()`](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of
the <a href="#the-constraint-validation-api"
id="the-button-element:the-constraint-validation-api">constraint
validation API</a>. The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute
provides a list of the element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s. The
[`disabled`](#dom-button-disabled), [`form`](#dom-fae-form), and
[`name`](#dom-button-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's
forms API.

<div class="example">

The following button is labeled "Show hint" and pops up a dialog box
when activated:

``` html
<button type=button
        onclick="alert('This 15-20 minute piece was composed by George Gershwin.')">
 Show hint
</button>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The following shows how <a href="#concept-button"
id="the-button-element:concept-button-3">buttons</a> can use
[`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) to show and hide an element with
the [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute when activated:

``` html
<button type=button
        commandfor="the-popover"
        command="show-popover">
 Show menu
</button>
<div popover
     id="the-popover">
 <button commandfor="the-popover"
         command="hide-popover">
  Hide menu
 </button>
</div>
    
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The following shows how buttons can use
[`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) with a
<a href="#attr-button-command-custom"
id="the-button-element:attr-button-command-custom-2">custom command
keyword</a> on an element, demonstrating how one could use custom
commands for unspecified behavior:

``` html
<button type=button
        commandfor="the-image"
        command="--rotate-landscape">
 Rotate Left
</button>
<button type=button
        commandfor="the-image"
        command="--rotate-portrait">
 Rotate Right
</button>
<img id="the-image"
     src="photo.jpg">
<script>
  const image = document.getElementById("the-image");
  image.addEventListener("command", (event) => {
   if ( event.command == "--rotate-landscape" ) {
    event.target.style.rotate = "-90deg"
   } else if ( event.command == "--rotate-portrait" ) {
    event.target.style.rotate = "0deg"
   }
  });
</script>
    
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.10.7</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`select`</span> element<a href="#the-select-element" class="self-link"></a>
