<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-select-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-select-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#interactive-content-2"
id="the-select-element:interactive-content-2">Interactive content</a>.

<a href="#category-listed"
id="the-select-element:category-listed">Listed</a>,
<a href="#category-label"
id="the-select-element:category-label">labelable</a>,
<a href="#category-submit"
id="the-select-element:category-submit">submittable</a>,
<a href="#category-reset"
id="the-select-element:category-reset">resettable</a>, and
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="the-select-element:category-autocapitalize">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting</a> <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="the-select-element:form-associated-element">form-associated
element</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-select-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-select-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
Zero or one [`button`](#the-button-element) elements if the
[`select`](#the-select-element) is a
<a href="#drop-down-box" id="the-select-element:drop-down-box">drop-down
box</a>, followed by zero or more
<a href="#select-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-select-element:select-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>select</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-select-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`autocomplete`](#attr-fe-autocomplete) — Hint for form autofill feature

[`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#attr-fae-form) — Associates the element with a
[`form`](#the-form-element) element

[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) — Whether to allow multiple values

[`name`](#attr-fe-name) — Name of the element to use for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-select-element:form-submission-2">form submission</a> and in the
[`form.elements`](#dom-form-elements) API

[`required`](#attr-select-required) — Whether the control is required
for <a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-select-element:form-submission-2-2">form submission</a>

[`size`](#attr-select-size) — Size of the control

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
If the element has a [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute or a
[`size`](#attr-select-size) attribute with a value \> 1: [for
authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-select-multiple-or-size-greater-1);
[for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-select-listbox).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-select);
[for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-select-combobox).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-select-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSelectElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString autocomplete;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean multiple;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean required;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=0] attribute unsigned long size;
  

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLOptionsCollection options;
  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long length;
  getter HTMLOptionElement? item(unsigned long index);
  HTMLOptionElement? namedItem(DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] undefined add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, optional (HTMLElement or long)? before = null);
  [CEReactions] undefined remove(); // ChildNode overload
  [CEReactions] undefined remove(long index);
  [CEReactions] setter undefined (unsigned long index, HTMLOptionElement? option);

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection selectedOptions;
  attribute long selectedIndex;
  attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  undefined showPicker();

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`select`](#the-select-element) element represents a control for
selecting amongst a set of options.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/multiple](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/multiple "The Boolean multiple attribute, if set, means the form control accepts one or more values. Valid for the email and file input types and the <select>, the manner by which the user opts for multiple values depends on the form control.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

The <span id="attr-select-multiple" class="dfn" dfn-for="select"
dfn-type="element-attr">`multiple`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-select-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>. If the
attribute is present, then the [`select`](#the-select-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-select-element:represents">represents</a>
a control for selecting zero or more options from the
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list">list of options</a>.
If the attribute is absent, then the [`select`](#the-select-element)
element <a href="#represents"
id="the-select-element:represents-2">represents</a> a control for
selecting a single option from the <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-2">list of options</a>.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/size "The size attribute defines the width of the <input> and the height of the <select> element. For the input, if the type attribute is text or password then it's the number of characters. This must be an integer value of 0 or higher. If no size is specified, or an invalid value is specified, the input has no size declared, and the form control will be the default width based on the user agent. If CSS targets the element with properties impacting the width, CSS takes precedence.")

if specified, must have a value that is a

integer</a> greater than zero.

The <span id="attr-select-required" class="dfn" dfn-for="select"
dfn-type="element-attr">`required`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-select-element:boolean-attribute-2">boolean attribute</a>. When
specified, the user will be required to select a value before submitting
the form.

The [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate
the [`select`](#the-select-element) element with its
<a href="#form-owner" id="the-select-element:form-owner">form owner</a>.
The [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The
[`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control
non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The
[`autocomplete`](#attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute controls how the user
agent provides autofill behavior.

<div algorithm="">

If a [`select`](#the-select-element) element has a
[`required`](#attr-select-required) attribute specified, and has a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size">display size</a> of 1; and
if the <a href="#concept-option-value"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-value">value</a> of the first
[`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-3">list of options</a>
(if any) is the empty string, and that [`option`](#the-option-element)
element's parent node is the [`select`](#the-select-element) element
(and not an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element), then that
[`option`](#the-option-element) is the [`select`](#the-select-element)
element's <span id="placeholder-label-option" class="dfn">placeholder
label option</span>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If a [`select`](#the-select-element) element has a
[`required`](#attr-select-required) attribute specified, does not have a
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute specified, and has a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-2">display size</a> of 1,
then the [`select`](#the-select-element) element must have a
<a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-select-element:placeholder-label-option">placeholder label
option</a>.

</div>

In practice, the requirement stated in the paragraph above can only
apply when a [`select`](#the-select-element) element does not have a
[`size`](#attr-select-size) attribute with a value greater than 1.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its
[`required`](#attr-select-required) attribute specified, and either none
of the [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-4">list of options</a>
have their <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</a> set
to true, or the only [`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-5">list of options</a>
with its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-2">selectedness</a>
set to true is the <a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-select-element:placeholder-label-option-2">placeholder label
option</a>, then the element is <a href="#suffering-from-being-missing"
id="the-select-element:suffering-from-being-missing">suffering from
being missing</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-form-reset-control"
id="the-select-element:concept-form-reset-control">reset algorithm</a>
for a [`select`](#the-select-element) element `selectElement` is:

1.  Set `selectElement`'s
    <a href="#user-validity" id="the-select-element:user-validity">user
    validity</a> to false.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-select-element:list-iterate" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `optionElement` of `selectElement`'s
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-6">list of options</a>:

    1.  If `optionElement` has a [`selected`](#attr-option-selected)
        attribute, then set `optionElement`'s
        <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-3">selectedness</a>
        to true; otherwise set it to false.

    2.  Set `optionElement`'s <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness">dirtiness</a>
        to false.

3.  Run the <a href="#selectedness-setting-algorithm"
    id="the-select-element:selectedness-setting-algorithm">selectedness
    setting algorithm</a> given `selectElement`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element that is not
<a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
id="the-select-element:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a> is
*[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)*.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The user agent should allow the user to pick an
[`option`](#the-option-element) element from a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element in its
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-7">list of options</a>
(either through a click, or through unfocusing the element after
changing its value, or through a
<a href="#using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command"
id="the-select-element:using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command">menu
command</a>, or through any other mechanism) by running the
<a href="#concept-select-pick"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-pick">pick an option</a> algorithm
given the [`select`](#the-select-element) element, the
[`option`](#the-option-element) element, and if the
<a href="#select&#39;s-options-are-being-rendered-with-base-appearance"
id="the-select-element:select&#39;s-options-are-being-rendered-with-base-appearance"><code>select</code>'s
<code>option</code>s are being rendered with base appearance</a>, a
corresponding
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
id="the-select-element:event-keydown">keydown</code></a> or
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mouseup"
data-x-internal="event-mouseup"><code
id="the-select-element:event-mouseup">mouseup</code></a> event,
otherwise null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="concept-select-pick" class="dfn">pick an option</span>
given a [`select`](#the-select-element) element `select`, an
[`option`](#the-option-element) element `option`, and an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-event"
data-x-internal="event"><code
id="the-select-element:event">Event</code></a> or null `event`:

1.  If `select` has the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute or
    `select` is <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
    id="the-select-element:concept-fe-disabled-2">disabled</a>, then
    return.

2.  If `event` is not null and `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="the-select-element:canceled-flag"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a> is set, then
    return.

3.  If `event` is a
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent"><code
    id="the-select-element:mouseevent">MouseEvent</code></a> and
    `event`'s
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-button"
    data-x-internal="dom-mouseevent-button"><code
    id="the-select-element:dom-mouseevent-button">button</code></a>
    attribute is not 1, then return.

4.  Set `option`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-4">selectedness</a>
    to true.

5.  Set `option`'s <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness-2">dirtiness</a> to
    true.

6.  <a href="#send-select-update-notifications"
    id="the-select-element:send-select-update-notifications">Send
    <code>select</code> update notifications</a> given `select`.

7.  If `select` is being rendered as a <a href="#drop-down-box"
    id="the-select-element:drop-down-box-2">drop-down box</a> with
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
    id="the-select-element:base-appearance"
    data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, then run the
    <a href="#hide-popover-algorithm"
    id="the-select-element:hide-popover-algorithm">hide popover
    algorithm</a> given `select`'s
    <a href="#select-popover" id="the-select-element:select-popover">select
    popover</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, whenever
an [`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-8">list of options</a>
has its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-5">selectedness</a>
set to true, and whenever an [`option`](#the-option-element) element
with its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-6">selectedness</a>
set to true is added to the [`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-9">list of options</a>,
the user agent must set the <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-7">selectedness</a>
of all the other [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in its
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-10">list of
options</a> to false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent and the
element's <a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-3">display size</a> is
greater than 1, then the user agent should also allow the user to
request that the [`option`](#the-option-element) whose
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-8">selectedness</a>
is true, if any, be unselected. Upon this request being conveyed to the
user agent, and before the relevant user interaction event is queued
(e.g. before the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="the-select-element:event-click">click</code></a> event), the user
agent must set the <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-9">selectedness</a>
of that [`option`](#the-option-element) element to false, set its
<a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness-3">dirtiness</a> to
true, and then <a href="#send-select-update-notifications"
id="the-select-element:send-select-update-notifications-2">send
<code>select</code> update notifications</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the [`select`](#the-select-element) is being rendered as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element:drop-down-box-3">drop-down box</a> with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element:base-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, then the user
agent should allow the user to <span id="select-open-picker"
class="dfn">open the picker</span> given a corresponding
[`select`](#the-select-element) element `select` and a corresponding
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown"
data-x-internal="event-mousedown"><code
id="the-select-element:event-mousedown">mousedown</code></a> or
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
id="the-select-element:event-keydown-2">keydown</code></a> event
`event`:

1.  If `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="the-select-element:canceled-flag-2"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a> is set, then
    return.

2.  If `event`'s
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-button"
    data-x-internal="dom-mouseevent-button"><code
    id="the-select-element:dom-mouseevent-button-2">button</code></a>
    attribute is not 1, then return.

3.  Run the
    <a href="#show-popover" id="the-select-element:show-popover">show
    popover</a> algorithm given `select`'s <a href="#select-popover"
    id="the-select-element:select-popover-2">select popover</a>, false,
    and `select`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the [`select`](#the-select-element) is being rendered with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element:base-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, then the user
agent should allow the user to <span id="focus-another-option"
class="dfn">focus another option</span> given the new
[`option`](#the-option-element) element to focus `option` and a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
id="the-select-element:event-keydown-3">keydown</code></a> event
`event`:

1.  If `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="the-select-element:canceled-flag-3"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a> is set, then
    return.

2.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="the-select-element:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a> on
    `option`.

</div>

Implementations commonly allow the user to focus the next or previous
option via the arrow-up and arrow-down keys, focus the first or last
option via the Home or End keys, or focus the first or last option in
the viewport of the picker via the PageUp or PageDown keys.

Which particular keys of the keyboard cause these actions might differ
across implementations and platforms. The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide
has good
[recommendations](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/)
for this behavior.

If the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is present, and the
element is not <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
id="the-select-element:concept-fe-disabled-3">disabled</a>, then the
user agent should allow the user to <span id="concept-select-toggle"
class="dfn">toggle</span> the <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-10">selectedness</a>
of the [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in its
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-11">list of
options</a> that are themselves not <a href="#concept-option-disabled"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-disabled">disabled</a>. Upon such
an element being <a href="#concept-select-toggle"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-toggle">toggled</a> (either
through a click, or through a
<a href="#using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command"
id="the-select-element:using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command-2">menu
command</a>, or any other mechanism), and before the relevant user
interaction event is queued (e.g. before a related
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="the-select-element:event-click-2">click</code></a> event), the
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-11">selectedness</a>
of the [`option`](#the-option-element) element must be changed (from
true to false or false to true), the <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness-4">dirtiness</a> of the
element must be set to true, and the user agent must
<a href="#send-select-update-notifications"
id="the-select-element:send-select-update-notifications-3">send
<code>select</code> update notifications</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="concept-select-size" class="dfn">display size</span> of a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element is the result of applying the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-select-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> to the value of the element's
[`size`](#attr-select-size) attribute, if it has one and parsing it is
successful. If applying those rules to the attribute's value is not
successful, or if the [`size`](#attr-select-size) attribute is absent,
then the element's <a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-4">display size</a> is 4 if
the element's [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) content attribute is
present, and 1 otherwise.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To get the <span id="concept-select-option-list" class="dfn">list of
options</span> given a [`select`](#the-select-element) element `select`:

1.  Let `options` be « ».

2.  Let `node` be the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-first-child"
    id="the-select-element:first-child" data-x-internal="first-child">first
    child</a> of `select` in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-select-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-while"
    id="the-select-element:while" data-x-internal="while">While</a>
    `node` is not null:

    1.  If `node` is an [`option`](#the-option-element) element, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="the-select-element:list-append"
        data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> `node` to `options`.

    2.  If any of the following conditions are true:

        - `node` is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element;

        - `node` is an [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element;

        - `node` is an [`option`](#the-option-element) element;

        - `node` is a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element;

        - `node` is an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element and
          `node` has an
          <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor"
          id="the-select-element:ancestor" data-x-internal="ancestor">ancestor</a>
          [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) in between itself and
          `select`,

        then set `node` to the next
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
        id="the-select-element:descendant"
        data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a> of `select` in
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
        id="the-select-element:tree-order-2" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
        order</a>, excluding `node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
        id="the-select-element:descendant-2"
        data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a>, if any such node
        exists; otherwise null.

        Otherwise, set `node` to the next
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
        id="the-select-element:descendant-3"
        data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a> of `select` in
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
        id="the-select-element:tree-order-3" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
        order</a>, if any such node exists; otherwise null.

4.  Return `options`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If an [`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-12">list of
options</a> <span id="ask-for-a-reset" class="dfn">asks for a
reset</span>, then run that [`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#selectedness-setting-algorithm"
id="the-select-element:selectedness-setting-algorithm-2">selectedness
setting algorithm</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="selectedness-setting-algorithm" class="dfn">selectedness
setting algorithm</span>, given a [`select`](#the-select-element)
element `element`, is to run the following steps:

1.  If `element`'s [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is
    absent, and `element`'s <a href="#concept-select-size"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-5">display size</a> is 1,
    and no [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in the `element`'s
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-13">list of
    options</a> have their <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-12">selectedness</a>
    set to true, then set the <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-13">selectedness</a>
    of the first [`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-14">list of
    options</a> in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-select-element:tree-order-4" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a> that is not <a href="#concept-option-disabled"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-disabled-2">disabled</a>, if
    any, to true, and return.

2.  If `element`'s [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is
    absent, and two or more [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in
    `element`'s <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-15">list of
    options</a> have their <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-14">selectedness</a>
    set to true, then set the <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-15">selectedness</a>
    of all but the last [`option`](#the-option-element) element with its
    <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-16">selectedness</a>
    set to true in the <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-16">list of
    options</a> in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-select-element:tree-order-5" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a> to false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="send-select-update-notifications" class="dfn">send `select`
update notifications</span> for a [`select`](#the-select-element)
element `element`, <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="the-select-element:queue-an-element-task">queue an element task</a>
on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="the-select-element:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction
task source</a> given `element` to run these steps:

1.  Set `element`'s
    <a href="#user-validity" id="the-select-element:user-validity-2">user
    validity</a> to true.

2.  Run <a href="#update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent"
    id="the-select-element:update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent">update a
    <code>select</code>'s <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    `element`.

3.  Run <a href="#clone-selected-option-into-select-button"
    id="the-select-element:clone-selected-option-into-select-button">clone
    selected <code>option</code> into <code>select</code> button</a>
    given `element`.

4.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-select-element:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
    data-x-internal="event-input"><code
    id="the-select-element:event-input">input</code></a> at `element`,
    with the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="the-select-element:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a> and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
    id="the-select-element:dom-event-composed">composed</code></a>
    attributes initialized to true.

5.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-select-element:concept-event-fire-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`change`](#event-change) at `element`, with the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="the-select-element:dom-event-bubbles-2">bubbles</code></a>
    attribute initialized to true.

</div>

Inserts `element` before the node given by `before`.

The `before` argument can be a number, in which case `element` is
inserted before the item with that number, or an element from the
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-21">list of
options</a>, in which case `element` is inserted before that element.

If `before` is omitted, null, or a number out of range, then `element`
will be added at the end of the list.

This method will throw a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror"
id="the-select-element:hierarchyrequesterror"
data-x-internal="hierarchyrequesterror">"<code>HierarchyRequestError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-select-element:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if
`element` is an ancestor of the element into which it is to be inserted.

The <span id="dom-select-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return the string "`select-one`" if the
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, and the string
"`select-multiple`" if the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute
is present.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-options" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement" dfn-type="attribute">`options`</span> IDL
attribute must return an
[`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#htmloptionscollection) rooted at the
[`select`](#the-select-element) node, whose filter matches the elements
in the <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-23">list of
options</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`options`](#dom-select-options) collection is also mirrored on the
[`HTMLSelectElement`](#htmlselectelement) object. The
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="the-select-element:supported-property-indices"
data-x-internal="supported-property-indices">supported property
indices</a> at any instant are the indices supported by the object
returned by the [`options`](#dom-select-options) attribute at that
instant.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-length" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`length`</span> IDL attribute must return the
number of nodes
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#represented-by-the-collection"
id="the-select-element:represented-by-the-collection"
data-x-internal="represented-by-the-collection">represented</a> by the
[`options`](#dom-select-options) collection. On setting, it must act
like the attribute of the same name on the
[`options`](#dom-select-options) collection.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-item" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="method">`item(``index``)`</span> method must return the value
returned by
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-htmlcollection-item"
id="the-select-element:dom-htmlcollection-item"
data-x-internal="dom-htmlcollection-item">the method of the same
name</a> on the [`options`](#dom-select-options) collection, when

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-nameditem" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="method">`namedItem(``name``)`</span> method must return the
value returned by
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-htmlcollection-nameditem"
id="the-select-element:dom-htmlcollection-nameditem"
data-x-internal="dom-htmlcollection-nameditem">the method of the same
name</a> on the [`options`](#dom-select-options) collection, when

When the user agent is to <a
href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property"

id="the-select-element:childnode">ChildNode</code></a> interface
implemented by the [`HTMLSelectElement`](#htmlselectelement) ancestor
interface <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-select-element:element">Element</code></a> when it has no
arguments.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-selectedoptions" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`selectedOptions`</span> IDL attribute must return
an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-select-element:htmlcollection-3">HTMLCollection</code></a>
rooted at the [`select`](#the-select-element) node, whose filter matches
the elements in the <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-24">list of
options</a> that have their <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-17">selectedness</a>
set to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-selectedindex" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement" dfn-type="attribute">`selectedIndex`</span>
getter steps are to return the <a href="#concept-option-index"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-index">index</a> of the first
[`option`](#the-option-element) element in
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-select-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-25">list of
options</a> in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-select-element:tree-order-7" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a> that has its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-18">selectedness</a>
set to true, if any. If there isn't one, then return −1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`selectedIndex`](#dom-select-selectedindex) setter steps are:

1.  Let `firstMatchingOption` be null.

2.  For each `option` of <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-select-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-26">list of
    options</a>:

    1.  Set `option`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-19">selectedness</a>
        to false.

    2.  If `firstMatchingOption` is null and `option`'s
        <a href="#concept-option-index"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-index-2">index</a> is
        equal to the given value, then set `firstMatchingOption` to
        `option`.

3.  If `firstMatchingOption` is not null, then set
    `firstMatchingOption`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-20">selectedness</a>
    to true and set `firstMatchingOption`'s
    <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness-5">dirtiness</a> to
    true.

4.  Run <a href="#update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent"
    id="the-select-element:update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent-2">update a
    <code>select</code>'s <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-select-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

This can result in no element having a
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-21">selectedness</a>
set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#the-select-element)
element having no [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute and a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-6">display size</a> of 1.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-select-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSelectElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> getter steps are to return the
<a href="#concept-option-value"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-value-3">value</a> of the first
[`option`](#the-option-element) element in
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-select-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-27">list of
options</a> in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-select-element:tree-order-8" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a> that has its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-22">selectedness</a>
set to true, if any. If there isn't one, then return the empty string.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`value`](#dom-select-value) setter steps are:

1.  Let `firstMatchingOption` be null.

2.  For each `option` of <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-select-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-select-element:concept-select-option-list-28">list of
    options</a>:

    1.  Set `option`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-23">selectedness</a>
        to false.

    2.  If `firstMatchingOption` is null and `option`'s
        <a href="#concept-option-value"
        id="the-select-element:concept-option-value-4">value</a> is
        equal to the given value, then set `firstMatchingOption` to
        `option`.

3.  If `firstMatchingOption` is not null, then set
    `firstMatchingOption`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-24">selectedness</a>
    to true and set `firstMatchingOption`'s
    <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
    id="the-select-element:concept-option-dirtiness-6">dirtiness</a> to
    true.

4.  Run <a href="#update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent"
    id="the-select-element:update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent-3">update a
    <code>select</code>'s <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-select-element:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

This can result in no element having a
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element:concept-option-selectedness-25">selectedness</a>
set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#the-select-element)
element having no [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute and a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element:concept-select-size-7">display size</a> of 1.

For historical reasons, the default value of the
[`size`](#dom-select-size) IDL attribute does not return the actual size
used, which, in the absence of the [`size`](#attr-select-size) content
attribute, is either 1 or 4 depending on the presence of the
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute.

The [`willValidate`](#dom-cva-willvalidate),
[`validity`](#dom-cva-validity), and
[`validationMessage`](#dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and
the [`checkValidity()`](#dom-cva-checkvalidity),
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-cva-reportvalidity), and
[`setCustomValidity()`](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of
the <a href="#the-constraint-validation-api"
id="the-select-element:the-constraint-validation-api">constraint
validation API</a>. The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute
provides a list of the element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s. The
[`disabled`](#dom-select-disabled), [`form`](#dom-fae-form), and
[`name`](#dom-select-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's
forms API.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div class="example">

The following example shows how a [`select`](#the-select-element)
element can be used to offer the user with a set of options from which
the user can select a single option. The default option is preselected.

``` html
<p>
 <label for="unittype">Select unit type:</label>
 <select id="unittype" name="unittype">
  <option value="1"> Miner </option>
  <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
  <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
  <option value="4"> Max </option>
  <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
 </select>
</p>
```

When there is no default option, a placeholder can be used instead:

``` html
<select name="unittype" required>
 <option value=""> Select unit type </option>
 <option value="1"> Miner </option>
 <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
 <option value="3"> Snipey </option>
 <option value="4"> Max </option>
 <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
</select>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Here, the user is offered a set of options from which they can select
any number. By default, all five options are selected.

``` html
<p>
 <label for="allowedunits">Select unit types to enable on this map:</label>
 <select id="allowedunits" name="allowedunits" multiple>
  <option value="1" selected> Miner </option>
  <option value="2" selected> Puffer </option>
  <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
  <option value="4" selected> Max </option>
  <option value="5" selected> Firebot </option>
 </select>
</p>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Sometimes, a user has to select one or more items. This example shows
such an interface.

``` html
<label>
 Select the songs from that you would like on your Act II Mix Tape:
 <select multiple required name="act2">
  <option value="s1">It Sucks to Be Me (Reprise)
  <option value="s2">There is Life Outside Your Apartment
  <option value="s3">The More You Ruv Someone
  <option value="s4">Schadenfreude
  <option value="s5">I Wish I Could Go Back to College
  <option value="s6">The Money Song
  <option value="s7">School for Monsters
  <option value="s8">The Money Song (Reprise)
  <option value="s9">There's a Fine, Fine Line (Reprise)
  <option value="s10">What Do You Do With a B.A. in English? (Reprise)
  <option value="s11">For Now
 </select>
</label>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Occasionally it can be useful to have a separator:

``` html
<label>
 Select the song to play next:
 <select required name="next">
  <option value="sr">Random
  <hr>
  <option value="s1">It Sucks to Be Me (Reprise)
  <option value="s2">There is Life Outside Your Apartment
  …
```

</div>

<div id="example-customizable-select" class="example">

<a href="#example-customizable-select" class="self-link"></a>

Here is an example which uses [`div`](#the-div-element),
[`legend`](#the-legend-element), [`img`](#the-img-element),
[`button`](#the-button-element), and
[`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) elements:

``` html
<select>
  <button>
    <selectedcontent></selectedcontent>
  </button>
  <div class="border">
    <optgroup>
      <legend>WHATWG Specifications</legend>
      <option>
        <img src="html.jpg" alt="">
        HTML
      </option>
      <option>
        <img src="dom.jpg" alt="">
        DOM
      </option>
    </optgroup>
  </div>
  <div class="border">
    <optgroup>
      <legend>W3C Specifications</legend>
      <option>
        <img src="forms.jpg" alt="">
        CSS Form Control Styling
      </option>
      <option>
        <img src="pseudo.jpg" alt="">
        CSS Pseudo-Elements
      </option>
    <optgroup>
  </div>
</select>
```

</div>

<a href="#note-first-button-in-select-not-submit" class="self-link"></a>The
first child [`button`](#the-button-element) element as allowed by the
content model of [`select`](#the-select-element) is not a submit button.
It is used to replace the in-page rendering of the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element. Its form submission behavior is
prevented because it is
<a href="#inert" id="the-select-element:inert">inert</a>.

#### <span class="secno">4.10.8</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`datalist`</span> element<a href="#the-datalist-element" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-datalist-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-datalist-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-datalist-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
Either: <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-datalist-element:phrasing-content-2-3">phrasing content</a>.

Or: Zero or more [`option`](#the-option-element) and
<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-datalist-element:script-supporting-elements-2">script-supporting</a>
elements.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-datalist-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-datalist).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-datalist).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDataListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection options;
};
```

The [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element represents a set of
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements that represent predefined
options for other controls. In the rendering, the
[`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-datalist-element:represents">represents</a> nothing and it,
along with its children, should be hidden.

The [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element can be used in two ways.
In the simplest case, the [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element
has just [`option`](#the-option-element) element children.

<div class="example">

``` html
<label>
 Animal:
 <input name=animal list=animals>
 <datalist id=animals>
  <option value="Cat">
  <option value="Dog">
 </datalist>
</label>
```

</div>

In the more elaborate case, the [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element)
element can be given contents that are to be displayed for down-level
clients that don't support [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element). In this
case, the [`option`](#the-option-element) elements are provided inside a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element inside the
[`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element.

<div class="example">

``` html
<label>
 Animal:
 <input name=animal list=animals>
</label>
<datalist id=animals>
 <label>
  or select from the list:
  <select name=animal>
   <option value="">
   <option>Cat
   <option>Dog
  </select>
 </label>
</datalist>
```

</div>

The [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element is hooked up to an
[`input`](#the-input-element) element using the
[`list`](#attr-input-list) attribute on the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element.

Each [`option`](#the-option-element) element that is a descendant of the
[`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element, that is not
<a href="#concept-option-disabled"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-option-disabled">disabled</a>, and
whose <a href="#concept-option-value"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-option-value">value</a> is a string
that isn't the empty string, represents a suggestion. Each suggestion
has a <a href="#concept-option-value"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-option-value-2">value</a> and a
<a href="#concept-option-label"
id="the-datalist-element:concept-option-label">label</a>.

`datalist``.`<a href="#dom-datalist-options"
id="dom-datalist-options-dev"><code>options</code></a>  
Returns an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-datalist-element:htmlcollection-2">HTMLCollection</code></a> of
the [`option`](#the-option-element) elements of the
[`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datalist-options" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLDataListElement" dfn-type="attribute">`options`</span> IDL
attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-datalist-element:htmlcollection-3">HTMLCollection</code></a>
rooted at the [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) node, whose filter
matches [`option`](#the-option-element) elements.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a
[`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element ancestor, it is
<a href="#barred-from-constraint-validation"
id="the-datalist-element:barred-from-constraint-validation">barred from
constraint validation</a>.

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-optgroup-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:

id="the-optgroup-element:concept-element-content-model">Content

Zero or one [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element followed by zero or

<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-optgroup-element:syntax-end-tag">end

[`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element, if it is immediately

id="the-optgroup-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

disabled

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-optgroup-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-optgroup).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-optgroup).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-optgroup-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOptGroupElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString label;
};
```

The [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-optgroup-element:represents">represents</a> a
<a href="#optgroup-option-group"
id="the-optgroup-element:optgroup-option-group">group of
<code>option</code> elements</a> with a common label.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="optgroup-option-group" class="dfn">element's group of
`option` elements</span> consists of the [`option`](#the-option-element)
elements that are descendants of the [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)
element.

</div>

When showing [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in
[`select`](#the-select-element) elements, user agents should show the
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements of such groups as being related
to each other and separate from other [`option`](#the-option-element)
elements.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/disabled](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/disabled "The Boolean disabled attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, focusable, or even submitted with the form. The user can neither edit nor focus on the control, nor its form control descendants.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer8+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-optgroup-disabled" class="dfn" dfn-for="optgroup"
dfn-type="element-attr">`disabled`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-optgroup-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a> and
can be used to <a href="#concept-option-disabled"
id="the-optgroup-element:concept-option-disabled">disable</a> a
<a href="#optgroup-option-group"
id="the-optgroup-element:optgroup-option-group-2">group of
<code>option</code> elements</a> together.

The <span id="attr-optgroup-label" class="dfn" dfn-for="optgroup"
dfn-type="element-attr">`label`</span> attribute must be specified if
the [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) has no child
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) element.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="concept-optgroup-label" class="dfn">get an `optgroup`
element's label</span>, given an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)
`optgroup`:

1.  If `optgroup` has a child [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element,
    then return the result of <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace"
    id="the-optgroup-element:strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace"
    data-x-internal="strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace">stripping and
    collapsing ASCII whitespace</a> from the concatenation of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
    id="the-optgroup-element:concept-cd-data"
    data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a> of all the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="the-optgroup-element:text">Text</code></a> node descendants of
    `optgroup`'s first child [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-optgroup-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>, excluding any that are descendants of descendants of the
    [`legend`](#the-legend-element) that are themselves
    [`script`](#the-script-element) or
    <a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/interact.html#ScriptElement"
    id="the-optgroup-element:svg-script" data-x-internal="svg-script">SVG
    <code>script</code></a> elements.

2.  Otherwise, return the value of `optgroup`'s
    [`label`](#attr-optgroup-label) attribute.

</div>

The value of the <a href="#concept-optgroup-label"
id="the-optgroup-element:concept-optgroup-label"><code>optgroup</code>
label algorithm</a> gives the name of the group, for the purposes of the
user interface. User agents should use this attribute's value when
labeling the group of [`option`](#the-option-element) elements in a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element.

There is no way to select an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)
element. Only [`option`](#the-option-element) elements can be selected.
An [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element merely provides a label
for a group of [`option`](#the-option-element) elements.

<div class="example">

The following snippet shows how a set of lessons from three courses
could be offered in a [`select`](#the-select-element) drop-down widget:

``` html
<form action="courseselector.dll" method="get">
 <p>Which course would you like to watch today?
 <p><label>Course:
  <select name="c">
   <optgroup label="8.01 Physics I: Classical Mechanics">
    <option value="8.01.1">Lecture 01: Powers of Ten
    <option value="8.01.2">Lecture 02: 1D Kinematics
    <option value="8.01.3">Lecture 03: Vectors
   <optgroup label="8.02 Electricity and Magnetism">
    <option value="8.02.1">Lecture 01: What holds our world together?
    <option value="8.02.2">Lecture 02: Electric Field
    <option value="8.02.3">Lecture 03: Electric Flux
   <optgroup label="8.03 Physics III: Vibrations and Waves">
    <option value="8.03.1">Lecture 01: Periodic Phenomenon
    <option value="8.03.2">Lecture 02: Beats
    <option value="8.03.3">Lecture 03: Forced Oscillations with Damping
  </select>
 </label>
 <p><input type=submit value="▶ Play">
</form>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.10.10</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`option`</span> element<a href="#the-option-element" class="self-link"></a>

As such, <option> can represent menu items in popups and other lists of items in an HTML document.")
