<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#select-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-option-element:select-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>select</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

<a href="#optgroup-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-option-element:optgroup-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>optgroup</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As a descendant of a [`select`](#the-select-element) element.

As a descendant of a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element.

As a descendant of an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
If the element has a [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute and a
[`value`](#attr-option-value) attribute:
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-option-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a>.

If the element has a [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute but no
[`value`](#attr-option-value) attribute:
<a href="#text-content" id="the-option-element:text-content">Text</a>.

If the element has no [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute and is not
a descendant of a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element: Zero or
more <a href="#option-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-option-element:option-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>option</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

If the element has no [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute and is a
descendant of a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element:
<a href="#text-content" id="the-option-element:text-content-2">Text</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
An [`option`](#the-option-element) element's
<a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="the-option-element:syntax-end-tag">end
tag</a> can be omitted if the [`option`](#the-option-element) element is
immediately followed by another [`option`](#the-option-element) element,
if it is immediately followed by an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)
element, if it is immediately followed by an [`hr`](#the-hr-element)
element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-option-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`disabled`](#attr-option-disabled) — Whether the form control is
disabled

[`label`](#attr-option-label) — User-visible label

[`selected`](#attr-option-selected) — Whether the option is selected by
default

[`value`](#attr-option-value) — Value to be used for
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-option-element:form-submission-2">form submission</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-option).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-option).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-option-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyFactoryFunction=Option(optional DOMString text = "", optional DOMString value, optional boolean defaultSelected = false, optional boolean selected = false)]
interface HTMLOptionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString label;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="selected"] attribute boolean defaultSelected;
  attribute boolean selected;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString value;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString text;
  readonly attribute long index;
};
```

The [`option`](#the-option-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-option-element:represents">represents</a>
an option in a [`select`](#the-select-element) element or as part of a
list of suggestions in a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element) element.

In certain circumstances described in the definition of the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element, an
[`option`](#the-option-element) element can be a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element's
<a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-option-element:placeholder-label-option">placeholder label
option</a>. A <a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-option-element:placeholder-label-option-2">placeholder label
option</a> does not represent an actual option, but instead represents a
label for the [`select`](#the-select-element) control.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/disabled](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/disabled "The Boolean disabled attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, focusable, or even submitted with the form. The user can neither edit nor focus on the control, nor its form control descendants.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-option-disabled" class="dfn" dfn-for="option"
dfn-type="element-attr">`disabled`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-option-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>. An
[`option`](#the-option-element) element `option` is
<span id="concept-option-disabled" class="dfn">disabled</span> if the
following steps return true:

1.  If `option`'s [`disabled`](#attr-option-disabled) attribute is
    present, then return true.

2.  For each `ancestor` of `option`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor"
    id="the-option-element:ancestor"
    data-x-internal="ancestor">ancestors</a> in reverse
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-option-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` is a [`select`](#the-select-element),
        [`hr`](#the-hr-element), [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element), or
        [`option`](#the-option-element) element, then return false.

    2.  If `ancestor` is an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element,
        then return true if `ancestor`'s
        [`disabled`](#attr-optgroup-disabled) attribute is present;
        otherwise false.

3.  Return false.

</div>

An [`option`](#the-option-element) element that is
<a href="#attr-option-disabled"
id="the-option-element:attr-option-disabled-3">disabled</a> must prevent
any <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="the-option-element:event-click">click</code></a> events that are
<a href="#queue-a-task" id="the-option-element:queue-a-task">queued</a>
on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="the-option-element:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction
task source</a> from being dispatched on the element.

Being <a href="#concept-option-disabled"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-disabled">disabled</a> does not
prevent all modifications to the [`option`](#the-option-element)
element. For example, its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</a>
could be modified programmatically from JavaScript. Or, it could be
indirectly modified by user action, e.g., if other non-disabled
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element were modified.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-option-label" class="dfn" dfn-for="option"
dfn-type="element-attr">`label`</span> attribute provides a label for
element. The <span id="concept-option-label" class="dfn">label</span> of
an [`option`](#the-option-element) element is the value of the
[`label`](#attr-option-label) content attribute, if there is one and its
value is not the empty string, or, otherwise, the value of the element's
[`text`](#dom-option-text) IDL attribute.

</div>

The [`label`](#attr-option-label) content attribute, if specified, must
not be empty.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-option-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="option"
dfn-type="element-attr">`value`</span> attribute provides a value for
element. The <span id="concept-option-value" class="dfn">value</span> of
an [`option`](#the-option-element) element is the value of the
[`value`](#attr-option-value) content attribute, if there is one, or, if
there is not, the result of <a href="#collect-option-text"
id="the-option-element:collect-option-text">collect option text</a>
given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-option-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a> and false.

</div>

The <span id="attr-option-selected" class="dfn" dfn-for="option"
dfn-type="element-attr">`selected`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-option-element:boolean-attribute-2">boolean attribute</a>. It
represents the default <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-2">selectedness</a>
of the element.

The <span id="concept-option-dirtiness" class="dfn">dirtiness</span> of
an [`option`](#the-option-element) element is a boolean state, initially
false. It controls whether adding or removing the
[`selected`](#attr-option-selected) content attribute has any effect.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="concept-option-selectedness"
class="dfn">selectedness</span> of an [`option`](#the-option-element)
element is a boolean state, initially false. Except where otherwise
specified, when the element is created, its
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-3">selectedness</a>
must be set to true if the element has a
[`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute. Whenever an
[`option`](#the-option-element) element's
[`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute is added, if its
<a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-dirtiness">dirtiness</a> is false,
its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-4">selectedness</a>
must be set to true. Whenever an [`option`](#the-option-element)
element's [`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute is *removed*, if
its <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-dirtiness-2">dirtiness</a> is
false, its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-5">selectedness</a>
must be set to false.

</div>

The [`Option()`](#dom-option) constructor, when called with three or
fewer arguments, overrides the initial state of the
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-6">selectedness</a>
state to always be false even if the third argument is true (implying
that a [`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute is to be set). The
fourth argument can be used to explicitly set the initial
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-7">selectedness</a>
state when using the constructor.

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element whose
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is not specified must not
have more than one descendant [`option`](#the-option-element) element
with its [`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute set.

<div algorithm="">

An [`option`](#the-option-element) element's
<span id="concept-option-index" class="dfn">index</span> is the number
of [`option`](#the-option-element) elements that are in the same
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-option-element:concept-select-option-list">list of options</a>
but that come before it in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="the-option-element:tree-order-2" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a>. If the [`option`](#the-option-element) element is not in a
<a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-option-element:concept-select-option-list-2">list of options</a>,
then the [`option`](#the-option-element) element's
<a href="#concept-option-index"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-index">index</a> is zero.

</div>

Each [`option`](#the-option-element) element has a
<span id="cached-nearest-ancestor-select-element" class="dfn">cached
nearest ancestor `select` element</span>, which is a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element or null, initially set to null.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="update-an-option's-nearest-ancestor-select"
class="dfn">update an `option`'s nearest ancestor `select`</span>, given
an [`option`](#the-option-element) `option`:

1.  Let `oldSelect` be `option`'s
    <a href="#cached-nearest-ancestor-select-element"
    id="the-option-element:cached-nearest-ancestor-select-element">cached
    nearest ancestor <code>select</code> element</a>.

2.  Let `newSelect` be `option`'s
    <a href="#option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"
    id="the-option-element:option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"><code>option</code>
    element nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a>.

3.  If `oldSelect` is not `newSelect`:

    1.  If `oldSelect` is not null, then run the
        <a href="#selectedness-setting-algorithm"
        id="the-option-element:selectedness-setting-algorithm">selectedness
        setting algorithm</a> given `oldSelect`.

    2.  If `newSelect` is not null, then run the
        <a href="#selectedness-setting-algorithm"
        id="the-option-element:selectedness-setting-algorithm-2">selectedness
        setting algorithm</a> given `newSelect`.

4.  Set `option`'s <a href="#cached-nearest-ancestor-select-element"
    id="the-option-element:cached-nearest-ancestor-select-element-2">cached
    nearest ancestor <code>select</code> element</a> to `newSelect`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`option`](#the-option-element)
<a href="#html-element-insertion-steps"
id="the-option-element:html-element-insertion-steps">HTML element
insertion steps</a>, given `insertedOption`, are to run
<a href="#update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select"
id="the-option-element:update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select">update
an <code>option</code>'s nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a> given
`insertedOption`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`option`](#the-option-element)
<a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="the-option-element:html-element-removing-steps">HTML element
removing steps</a>, given `removedNode`, `isSubtreeRoot`, and
`oldAncestor` are to run
<a href="#update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select"
id="the-option-element:update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select-2">update
an <code>option</code>'s nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a> given
`removedNode`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`option`](#the-option-element) <a href="#html-element-moving-steps"
id="the-option-element:html-element-moving-steps">HTML element moving
steps</a>, given `movedNode`, `isSubtreeRoot`, and `oldAncestor` are to
run <a href="#update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select"
id="the-option-element:update-an-option&#39;s-nearest-ancestor-select-3">update
an <code>option</code>'s nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a> given
`movedNode`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To get the <span id="option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"
class="dfn">`option` element nearest ancestor `select`</span> given an
[`option`](#the-option-element) `option`, run these steps. They return a
[`select`](#the-select-element) or null.

1.  Let `ancestorOptgroup` be null.

2.  For each `ancestor` of `option`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor"
    id="the-option-element:ancestor-2"
    data-x-internal="ancestor">ancestors</a>, in reverse
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-option-element:tree-order-3" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` is a [`datalist`](#the-datalist-element),
        [`hr`](#the-hr-element), or [`option`](#the-option-element)
        element, then return null.

    2.  If `ancestor` is an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element:

        1.  If `ancestorOptgroup` is not null, then return null.

        2.  Set `ancestorOptgroup` to `ancestor`.

    3.  If `ancestor` is a [`select`](#the-select-element), then return
        `ancestor`.

3.  Return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="maybe-clone-an-option-into-selectedcontent"
class="dfn">maybe clone an `option` into `selectedcontent`</span>, given
an [`option`](#the-option-element) `option`:

1.  Let `select` be `option`'s
    <a href="#option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"
    id="the-option-element:option-element-nearest-ancestor-select-2"><code>option</code>
    element nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a>.

2.  If all of the following conditions are true:

    - `select` is not null;

    - `option`'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
      id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-8">selectedness</a>
      is true; and

    - `select`'s <a href="#select-enabled-selectedcontent"
      id="the-option-element:select-enabled-selectedcontent">enabled
      <code>selectedcontent</code></a> is not null,

    then run <a href="#clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent"
    id="the-option-element:clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent">clone an
    <code>option</code> into a <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    `option` and `select`'s <a href="#select-enabled-selectedcontent"
    id="the-option-element:select-enabled-selectedcontent-2">enabled
    <code>selectedcontent</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="clone-selected-option-into-select-button" class="dfn">clone
selected `option` into `select` button</span>, given a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element `select`:

1.  Let `option` be the first element of `select`'s
    <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-option-element:concept-select-option-list-3">option list</a>
    whose <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-9">selectedness</a>
    is set to true, if such an element exists; otherwise null.

2.  Let `text` be the empty string.

3.  If `option` is not null, then set `text` to `option`'s
    <a href="#dom-option-label"
    id="the-option-element:dom-option-label-2">label</a>.

4.  Set `select`'s <a href="#select-fallback-button-text"
    id="the-option-element:select-fallback-button-text">select fallback
    button text</a> to `text`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When an [`option`](#the-option-element) element is popped off the
<a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="the-option-element:stack-of-open-elements">stack of open
elements</a> of an
<a href="#html-parser" id="the-option-element:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> or
<a href="#xml-parser" id="the-option-element:xml-parser">XML parser</a>,
the user agent must run
<a href="#maybe-clone-an-option-into-selectedcontent"
id="the-option-element:maybe-clone-an-option-into-selectedcontent">maybe
clone an option into selectedcontent</a> given the
[`option`](#the-option-element) element.

</div>

`option``.`<a href="#dom-option-selected"
id="dom-option-selected-dev"><code>selected</code></a>

Returns true if the element is selected, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to override the current state of the element.

`option``.`<a href="#dom-option-index"
id="dom-option-index-dev"><code>index</code></a>

Returns the index of the element in its [`select`](#the-select-element)
element's [`options`](#dom-select-options) list.

`option``.`<a href="#dom-option-form"
id="dom-option-form-dev"><code>form</code></a>

Returns the element's [`form`](#the-form-element) element, if any, or
null otherwise.

`option``.`<a href="#dom-option-text"
id="dom-option-text-dev"><code>text</code></a>

Same as <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-textcontent"
data-x-internal="textcontent"><code
id="the-option-element:textcontent">textContent</code></a>, except that
spaces are collapsed and [`script`](#the-script-element) elements are
skipped.

`option`` = new `<a href="#dom-option" id="dom-option-dev"><code>Option</code></a>`([ ``text`` [, ``value`` [, ``defaultSelected`` [, ``selected`` ] ] ] ])`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLOptionElement/Option](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLOptionElement/Option "The Option() constructor creates a new HTMLOptionElement.")

Support in all current engines.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer5.5+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

Returns a new [`option`](#the-option-element) element.

The `text` argument sets the contents of the element.

The `value` argument sets the [`value`](#attr-option-value) attribute.

The `defaultSelected` argument sets the
[`selected`](#attr-option-selected) attribute.

The `selected` argument sets whether or not the element is selected. If
it is omitted, even if the `defaultSelected` argument is true, the
element is not selected.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-label" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`label`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `attribute` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-option-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute.

2.  If `attribute` is null, then return
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-option-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-option-label"
    id="the-option-element:concept-option-label">label</a>.

3.  Return `attribute`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-attribute-value"
    id="the-option-element:concept-attribute-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-attribute-value">value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-option-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-option-value"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-value">value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-selected" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement" dfn-type="attribute">`selected`</span> IDL
attribute, on getting, must return true if the element's
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-10">selectedness</a>
is true, and false otherwise. On setting, it must set the element's
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-11">selectedness</a>
to the new value, set its <a href="#concept-option-dirtiness"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-dirtiness-3">dirtiness</a> to
true, and then cause the element to
<a href="#ask-for-a-reset" id="the-option-element:ask-for-a-reset">ask
for a reset</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-index" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`index`</span> IDL attribute must return the
element's <a href="#concept-option-index"
id="the-option-element:concept-option-index-2">index</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-text" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`text`</span> getter steps are to return the result
of <a href="#collect-option-text"
id="the-option-element:collect-option-text-2">collect option text</a>
given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-option-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a> and
false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`text`](#dom-option-text) setter steps are to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#string-replace-all"
id="the-option-element:string-replace-all"
data-x-internal="string-replace-all">string replace all</a> with the
given value within <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-option-element:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-option-form" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`form`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `select` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-option-element:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"
    id="the-option-element:option-element-nearest-ancestor-select-3"><code>option</code>
    element nearest ancestor <code>select</code></a>.

2.  If `select` is null, then return null.

3.  Return `select`'s
    <a href="#form-owner" id="the-option-element:form-owner">form owner</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A legacy factory function is provided for creating
[`HTMLOptionElement`](#htmloptionelement) objects (in addition to the
factory methods from DOM such as
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement"
data-x-internal="dom-document-createelement"><code
id="the-option-element:dom-document-createelement">createElement()</code></a>):
<span id="dom-option" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOptionElement"
dfn-type="constructor">`Option(``text``, ``value``, ``defaultSelected``, ``selected``)`</span>.
When invoked, the legacy factory function must perform the following
steps:

1.  Let `document` be the <a href="#current-global-object"
    id="the-option-element:current-global-object">current global object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="the-option-element:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

2.  Let `option` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-option-element:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    `document`, "`option`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-option-element:html-namespace-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

3.  If `text` is not the empty string, then append to `option` a new
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="the-option-element:text">Text</code></a> node whose data is
    `text`.

4.  If `value` is given, then <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value"
    id="the-option-element:concept-element-attributes-set-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-set-value">set an attribute
    value</a> for `option` using "[`value`](#attr-option-value)" and
    `value`.

5.  If `defaultSelected` is true, then <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value"
    id="the-option-element:concept-element-attributes-set-value-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-set-value">set an attribute
    value</a> for `option` using "[`selected`](#attr-option-selected)"
    and the empty string.

6.  If `selected` is true, then set `option`'s
    <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-12">selectedness</a>
    to true; otherwise set its <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-option-element:concept-option-selectedness-13">selectedness</a>
    to false (even if `defaultSelected` is true).

7.  Return `option`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="collect-option-text" class="dfn">collect option
text</span>, given an [`option`](#the-option-element) element `option`
and a boolean `includeAltText`:

1.  Let `text` be the empty string.

2.  For each
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="the-option-element:descendant"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a> `descendant` of `option`
    in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-option-element:tree-order-4" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>:

    1.  If `descendant` is a [`script`](#the-script-element) or
        <a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/interact.html#ScriptElement"
        id="the-option-element:svg-script" data-x-internal="svg-script">SVG
        <code>script</code></a> element, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="the-option-element:continue" data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>
        skipping all
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
        id="the-option-element:descendant-2"
        data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a> of `descendant`.

    2.  If `descendant` is a
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="the-option-element:text-2">Text</code></a> node, then set
        `text` to the concatenation of `text` and `descendant`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
        id="the-option-element:concept-cd-data"
        data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a>.

    3.  If `descendant` is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element and
        `includeAltText` is true, then:

        1.  If the value of `descendant`'s [`alt`](#attr-img-alt)
            attribute is not empty, then set `text` to the concatenation
            of `text`, `" "`, the value of `descendant`'s
            [`alt`](#attr-img-alt) attribute, and `" "`.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="the-option-element:continue-2"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a> skipping all
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
            id="the-option-element:descendant-3"
            data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a> of
            `descendant`.

3.  Return the result of <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace"
    id="the-option-element:strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace"
    data-x-internal="strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace">strip and collapse
    ASCII whitespace</a> given `text`.

</div>

<a href="#note-option-no-value" class="self-link"></a>When no
[`value`](#attr-option-value) attribute is set on the
[`option`](#the-option-element) element, its text contents are used to
generate a submittable value. In the case that the
[`option`](#the-option-element) element has child elements, this can
lead to unexpected results such as [`option`](#the-option-element)
elements which render differently but have the same value. In order to
address this, setting the [`value`](#attr-option-value) attribute on
[`option`](#the-option-element) elements is recommended.

id="the-textarea-element:form-submission-2-3">form submission</a>

[`wrap`](#attr-textarea-wrap) — How the value of the form control is to

id="the-textarea-element:form-submission-2-4">form submission</a>

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTextAreaElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString autocomplete;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositiveWithFallback, ReflectDefault=20] attribute unsigned long cols;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString dirName;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectNonNegative] attribute long maxLength;
  [CEReactions, ReflectNonNegative] attribute long minLength;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString placeholder;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean readOnly;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean required;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositiveWithFallback, ReflectDefault=2] attribute unsigned long rows;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString wrap;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString value;
  readonly attribute unsigned long textLength;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  undefined select();
  attribute unsigned long selectionStart;
  attribute unsigned long selectionEnd;
  attribute DOMString selectionDirection;
  undefined setRangeText(DOMString replacement);
  undefined setRangeText(DOMString replacement, unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional SelectionMode selectionMode = "preserve");
  undefined setSelectionRange(unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional DOMString direction);
};
```

The [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-textarea-element:represents">represents</a> a multiline plain
text edit control for the element's
<span id="concept-textarea-raw-value" class="dfn">raw value</span>. The
contents of the control represent the control's default value.

The <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value">raw value</a> of a
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) control must be initially the empty
string.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional
algorithm](#bidireq).

The <span id="attr-textarea-readonly" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`readonly`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-textarea-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a> used
to control whether the text can be edited by the user or not.

<div class="example">

In this example, a text control is marked read-only because it
represents a read-only file:

``` html
Filename: <code>/etc/bash.bashrc</code>
<textarea name="buffer" readonly>
# System-wide .bashrc file for interactive bash(1) shells.

# To enable the settings / commands in this file for login shells as well,
# this file has to be sourced in /etc/profile.

# If not running interactively, don't do anything
[ -z "$PS1" ] &amp;&amp; return

...</textarea>
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#attr-textarea-readonly)
attribute is specified on a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element,
the element is <a href="#barred-from-constraint-validation"
id="the-textarea-element:barred-from-constraint-validation">barred from
constraint validation</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is
<a href="#concept-fe-mutable"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-mutable">mutable</a> if it is
neither <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a> nor has a
[`readonly`](#attr-textarea-readonly) attribute specified.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) is
<a href="#concept-fe-mutable"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-mutable-2">mutable</a>, its
<a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-2">raw value</a>
should be editable by the user: the user agent should allow the user to
edit, insert, and remove text, and to insert and remove line breaks in
the form of U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. Any time the user causes
the element's <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-3">raw value</a> to
change, the user agent must <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="the-textarea-element:queue-an-element-task">queue an element
task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="the-textarea-element:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction
task source</a> given the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
data-x-internal="event-input"><code
id="the-textarea-element:event-input">input</code></a> at the
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="the-textarea-element:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a> and
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
id="the-textarea-element:dom-event-composed">composed</code></a>
attributes initialized to true. User agents may wait for a suitable
break in the user's interaction before queuing the task; for example, a
user agent could wait for the user to have not hit a key for 100ms, so
as to only fire the event when the user pauses, instead of continuously
for each keystroke.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element's
<a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-dirty">dirty value flag</a> must be
set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that
changes the <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-4">raw value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone-ext"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-node-clone-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-ext">cloning steps</a> for
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements given `node`, `copy`, and
`subtree` are to propagate the <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-5">raw value</a> and
<a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-dirty-2">dirty value flag</a> from
`node` to `copy`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-children-changed-ext"
id="the-textarea-element:children-changed-steps"
data-x-internal="children-changed-steps">children changed steps</a> for
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements must, if the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-dirty-3">dirty value flag</a> is
false, set the element's <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-6">raw value</a> to
its <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="the-textarea-element:child-text-content"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-form-reset-control"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-form-reset-control">reset algorithm</a>
for [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements is to set the
<a href="#user-validity" id="the-textarea-element:user-validity">user
validity</a> to false, the <a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-dirty-4">dirty value flag</a> back
to false, and the <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-7">raw value</a> to
its <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="the-textarea-element:child-text-content-2"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is popped off the
<a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="the-textarea-element:stack-of-open-elements">stack of open
elements</a> of an
<a href="#html-parser" id="the-textarea-element:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> or
<a href="#xml-parser" id="the-textarea-element:xml-parser">XML
parser</a>, then the user agent must invoke the element's
<a href="#concept-form-reset-control"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-form-reset-control-2">reset
algorithm</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the element is <a href="#concept-fe-mutable"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-mutable-3">mutable</a>, the user
agent should allow the user to change the writing direction of the
element, setting it either to a left-to-right writing direction or a
right-to-left writing direction. If the user does so, the user agent
must then run the following steps:

1.  Set the element's [`dir`](#attr-dir) attribute to
    "[`ltr`](#attr-dir-ltr)" if the user selected a left-to-right
    writing direction, and "[`rtl`](#attr-dir-rtl)" if the user selected
    a right-to-left writing direction.

2.  <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
    id="the-textarea-element:queue-an-element-task-2">Queue an element
    task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
    id="the-textarea-element:user-interaction-task-source-2">user
    interaction task source</a> given the
    [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-event-fire-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input"
    data-x-internal="event-input"><code
    id="the-textarea-element:event-input-2">input</code></a> at the
    [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element, with the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="the-textarea-element:dom-event-bubbles-2">bubbles</code></a> and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-composed"><code
    id="the-textarea-element:dom-event-composed-2">composed</code></a>
    attributes initialized to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-textarea-cols" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`cols`</span> attribute specifies the expected
maximum number of characters per line. If the
[`cols`](#attr-textarea-cols) attribute is specified, its value must be
a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-textarea-element:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integer</a> greater than zero. If applying the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-textarea-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> to the attribute's value results
in a number greater than zero, then the element's
<span id="attr-textarea-cols-value" class="dfn">character width</span>
is that value; otherwise, it is 20.

</div>

The user agent may use the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element's
<a href="#attr-textarea-cols-value"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-cols-value">character width</a>
as a hint to the user as to how many characters the server prefers per
line (e.g. for visual user agents by making the width of the control be
that many characters). In visual renderings, the user agent should wrap
the user's input in the rendering so that each line is no wider than
this number of characters.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-textarea-rows" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`rows`</span> attribute specifies the number of
lines to show. If the [`rows`](#attr-textarea-rows) attribute is
specified, its value must be a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-textarea-element:valid-non-negative-integer-2">valid
non-negative integer</a> greater than zero. If applying the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-textarea-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-2">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> to the attribute's value results
in a number greater than zero, then the element's
<span id="attr-textarea-rows-value" class="dfn">character height</span>
is that value; otherwise, it is 2.

</div>

Visual user agents should set the height of the control to the number of
lines given by <a href="#attr-textarea-rows-value"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-rows-value">character height</a>.

The <span id="attr-textarea-wrap" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`wrap`</span> attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-textarea-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-textarea-wrap-soft" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea/wrap" dfn-type="attr-value">`soft`</span> | <span id="attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state" class="dfn">Soft</span> | Text is not to be wrapped when submitted (though can still be wrapped in the rendering). |
| <span id="attr-textarea-wrap-hard" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea/wrap" dfn-type="attr-value">`hard`</span> | <span id="attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state" class="dfn">Hard</span> | Text is to have newlines added by the user agent so that the text is wrapped when it is submitted. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state">Soft</a> state.

</div>

If the element's [`wrap`](#attr-textarea-wrap) attribute is in the
<a href="#attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state">Hard</a> state,
the [`cols`](#attr-textarea-cols) attribute must be specified.

For historical reasons, the element's value is normalized in three
different ways for three different purposes. The
<a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-8">raw value</a> is
the value as it was originally set. It is not normalized. The
<a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value">API value</a> is the
value used in the [`value`](#dom-textarea-value) IDL attribute,
[`textLength`](#dom-textarea-textlength) IDL attribute, and by the
[`maxlength`](#attr-fe-maxlength) and [`minlength`](#attr-fe-minlength)
content attributes. It is normalized so that line breaks use U+000A LINE
FEED (LF) characters. Finally, there is the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-value">value</a>, as used in form
submission and other processing models in this specification. It is
normalized as for the <a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-2">API value</a>, and in
addition, if necessary given the element's [`wrap`](#attr-textarea-wrap)
attribute, additional line breaks are inserted to wrap the text at the
given width.

<div algorithm="">

The algorithm for obtaining the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-3">API value</a> is to
return the element's <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-9">raw value</a>,
with <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines"
id="the-textarea-element:normalize-newlines"
data-x-internal="normalize-newlines">newlines normalized</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-value-2">value</a> is defined to be
the element's <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-10">API value</a>
with the <a href="#textarea-wrapping-transformation"
id="the-textarea-element:textarea-wrapping-transformation">textarea
wrapping transformation</a> applied. The
<span id="textarea-wrapping-transformation" class="dfn">textarea
wrapping transformation</span> is the following algorithm, as applied to
a string:

1.  If the element's [`wrap`](#attr-textarea-wrap) attribute is in the
    <a href="#attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state"
    id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state-2">Hard</a>
    state, insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters into the string using
    an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="the-textarea-element:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    algorithm so that each line has no more than
    <a href="#attr-textarea-cols-value"
    id="the-textarea-element:attr-textarea-cols-value-2">character width</a>
    characters. For the purposes of this requirement, lines are
    delimited by the start of the string, the end of the string, and
    U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.

</div>

The <span id="attr-textarea-maxlength" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`maxlength`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#attr-fe-maxlength"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-fe-maxlength-2">form control
<code>maxlength</code> attribute</a>.

If the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element has a
<a href="#maximum-allowed-value-length"
id="the-textarea-element:maximum-allowed-value-length">maximum allowed
value length</a>, then the element's children must be such that the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-length"
id="the-textarea-element:length-3" data-x-internal="length">length</a>
of the value of the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-descendant-text-content"
id="the-textarea-element:descendant-text-content"
data-x-internal="descendant-text-content">descendant text content</a>
with <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines"
id="the-textarea-element:normalize-newlines-2"
data-x-internal="normalize-newlines">newlines normalized</a> is less
than or equal to the element's <a href="#maximum-allowed-value-length"
id="the-textarea-element:maximum-allowed-value-length-2">maximum allowed
value length</a>.

The <span id="attr-textarea-minlength" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`minlength`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#attr-fe-minlength"
id="the-textarea-element:attr-fe-minlength-2">form control
<code>minlength</code> attribute</a>.

The <span id="attr-textarea-required" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`required`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-textarea-element:boolean-attribute-2">boolean attribute</a>.
When specified, the user will be required to enter a value before
submitting the form.

<div algorithm="">

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its
[`required`](#attr-textarea-required) attribute specified, and the
element is <a href="#concept-fe-mutable"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-mutable-4">mutable</a>, and the
element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-value-3">value</a> is the empty
string, then the element is <a href="#suffering-from-being-missing"
id="the-textarea-element:suffering-from-being-missing">suffering from
being missing</a>.

</div>

The <span id="attr-textarea-placeholder" class="dfn" dfn-for="textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`placeholder`</span> attribute represents a
*short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data
entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a
brief description of the expected format.

The [`placeholder`](#attr-textarea-placeholder) attribute should not be
used as an alternative to a [`label`](#the-label-element). For a longer
hint or other advisory text, the [`title`](#attr-title) attribute is
more appropriate.

These mechanisms are very similar but subtly different: the hint given
by the control's [`label`](#the-label-element) is shown at all times;
the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#attr-textarea-placeholder)
attribute is shown before the user enters a value; and the hint in the
[`title`](#attr-title) attribute is shown when the user requests further
help.

User agents should present this hint to the user when the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-value-4">value</a> is the empty
string and the control is not
<a href="#focused" id="the-textarea-element:focused">focused</a> (e.g.
by displaying it inside a blank unfocused control). All U+000D CARRIAGE
RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pairs (CRLF) in the hint, as well as
all other U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) and U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
characters in the hint, must be treated as line breaks when rendering
the hint.

If a user agent normally doesn't show this hint to the user when the
control is
<a href="#focused" id="the-textarea-element:focused-2">focused</a>, then
the user agent should nonetheless show the hint for the control if it
was focused as a result of the [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus)
attribute, since in that case the user will not have had an opportunity
to examine the control before focusing it.

The [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The
[`dirname`](#attr-fe-dirname) attribute controls how the element's
<a href="#the-directionality"
id="the-textarea-element:the-directionality-2">directionality</a> is
submitted. The [`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make
the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being
submitted. The [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly
associate the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element with its
<a href="#form-owner" id="the-textarea-element:form-owner">form
owner</a>. The [`autocomplete`](#attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute
controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

`textarea``.`<a href="#dom-textarea-type"
id="dom-textarea-type-dev"><code>type</code></a>  
Returns the string "`textarea`".

`textarea``.`<a href="#dom-textarea-value"
id="dom-textarea-value-dev"><code>value</code></a>  
Returns the current value of the element.

Can be set, to change the value.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-textarea-type" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTextAreaElement" dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> IDL
attribute must return the value "`textarea`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-textarea-defaultvalue" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTextAreaElement" dfn-type="attribute">`defaultValue`</span>
attribute's getter must return the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="the-textarea-element:child-text-content-3"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`defaultValue`](#dom-textarea-defaultvalue) attribute's setter must
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#string-replace-all"
id="the-textarea-element:string-replace-all"
data-x-internal="string-replace-all">string replace all</a> with the
given value within this element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-textarea-value" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTextAreaElement" dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> IDL
attribute must, on getting, return the element's
<a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-4">API value</a>. On
setting, it must perform the following steps:

1.  Let `oldAPIValue` be this element's <a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-5">API value</a>.

2.  Set this element's <a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea-raw-value-11">raw value</a>
    to the new value.

3.  Set this element's <a href="#concept-fe-dirty"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-dirty-5">dirty value flag</a> to
    true.

4.  If the new <a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-6">API value</a> is
    different from `oldAPIValue`, then move the
    <a href="#concept-textarea/input-cursor"
    id="the-textarea-element:concept-textarea/input-cursor">text entry
    cursor position</a> to the end of the text control, unselecting any
    selected text and <a href="#set-the-selection-direction"
    id="the-textarea-element:set-the-selection-direction">resetting the
    selection direction</a> to "`none`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-textarea-textlength" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTextAreaElement" dfn-type="attribute">`textLength`</span>
IDL attribute must return the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-length"
id="the-textarea-element:length-4" data-x-internal="length">length</a>
of the element's <a href="#concept-fe-api-value"
id="the-textarea-element:concept-fe-api-value-7">API value</a>.

</div>

The [`willValidate`](#dom-cva-willvalidate),
[`validity`](#dom-cva-validity), and
[`validationMessage`](#dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and
the [`checkValidity()`](#dom-cva-checkvalidity),
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-cva-reportvalidity), and
[`setCustomValidity()`](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of
the <a href="#the-constraint-validation-api"
id="the-textarea-element:the-constraint-validation-api">constraint
validation API</a>. The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute
provides a list of the element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s. The
[`select()`](#dom-textarea/input-select),
[`selectionStart`](#dom-textarea/input-selectionstart),
[`selectionEnd`](#dom-textarea/input-selectionend),
[`selectionDirection`](#dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection),
[`setRangeText()`](#dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and
[`setSelectionRange()`](#dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods
and IDL attributes expose the element's text selection. The
[`disabled`](#dom-textarea-disabled), [`form`](#dom-fae-form), and
[`name`](#dom-textarea-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's
forms API.

<div class="example">

Here is an example of a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) being used
for unrestricted free-form text input in a form:

``` html
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments></textarea></p>
```

To specify a maximum length for the comments, one can use the
[`maxlength`](#attr-textarea-maxlength) attribute:

``` html
<p>If you have any short comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments maxlength=200></textarea></p>
```

To give a default value, text can be included inside the element:

``` html
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments>You rock!</textarea></p>
```

You can also give a minimum length. Here, a letter needs to be filled
out by the user; a template (which is shorter than the minimum length)
is provided, but is insufficient to submit the form:

``` html
<textarea required minlength="500">Dear Madam Speaker,

Regarding your letter dated ...

...

Yours Sincerely,

...</textarea>
```

A placeholder can be given as well, to suggest the basic form to the
user, without providing an explicit template:

``` html
<textarea placeholder="Dear Francine,

They closed the parks this week, so we won't be able to
meet your there. Should we just have dinner?

Love,
Daddy"></textarea>
```

To have the browser submit <a href="#the-directionality"
id="the-textarea-element:the-directionality-3">the directionality</a> of
the element along with the value, the [`dirname`](#attr-fe-dirname)
attribute can be specified:

``` html
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know (you may use either English or Hebrew for your comments):
<textarea cols=80 name=comments dirname=comments.dir></textarea></p>
```

</div>

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOutputElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="for"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList htmlFor;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`output`](#the-output-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-output-element:represents">represents</a>
the result of a calculation performed by the application, or the result
of a user action.

This element can be contrasted with the [`samp`](#the-samp-element)
element, which is the appropriate element for quoting the output of
other programs run previously.

When used on an <output> element it allows for an explicit relationship between the elements that represent values which are used in the output.")

The <span id="attr-output-for" class="dfn" dfn-for="output"
dfn-type="element-attr">`for`</span> content attribute allows an
explicit relationship to be made between the result of a calculation and
the elements that represent the values that went into the calculation or
that otherwise influenced the calculation. The [`for`](#attr-output-for)
attribute, if specified, must contain a string consisting of an
<a href="#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="the-output-element:unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a>, none of which are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
id="the-output-element:identical-to"
data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> another token and each
of which must have the value of an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="the-output-element:concept-id" data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a>
of an element in the same
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="the-output-element:tree" data-x-internal="tree">tree</a>.

The [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate
the [`output`](#the-output-element) element with its
<a href="#form-owner" id="the-output-element:form-owner">form owner</a>.
The [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The
[`output`](#the-output-element) element is associated with a form so
that it can be easily
<a href="#referenced" id="the-output-element:referenced">referenced</a>
from the event handlers of form controls; the element's value itself is
not submitted when the form is submitted.

The element has a <span id="concept-output-default-value-override"
class="dfn">default value override</span> (null or a string). Initially
it must be null.

<div algorithm="">

The element's <span id="concept-output-default-value"
class="dfn">default value</span> is determined by the following steps:

1.  If this element's <a href="#concept-output-default-value-override"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-override">default
    value override</a> is non-null, then return it.

2.  Return this element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-descendant-text-content"
    id="the-output-element:descendant-text-content"
    data-x-internal="descendant-text-content">descendant text content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-form-reset-control"
id="the-output-element:concept-form-reset-control">reset algorithm</a>
for [`output`](#the-output-element) elements is to run these steps:

1.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#string-replace-all"
    id="the-output-element:string-replace-all"
    data-x-internal="string-replace-all">String replace all</a> with
    this element's <a href="#concept-output-default-value"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value">default value</a>
    within this element.

2.  Set this element's <a href="#concept-output-default-value-override"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-override-2">default
    value override</a> to null.

</div>

`output``.`<a href="#dom-output-value"
id="dom-output-value-dev"><code>value</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns the element's current value.

Can be set, to change the value.

`output``.`<a href="#dom-output-defaultvalue"
id="dom-output-defaultvalue-dev"><code>defaultValue</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns the element's current default value.

Can be set, to change the default value.

`output``.`<a href="#dom-output-type"
id="dom-output-type-dev"><code>type</code></a>  
Returns the string "`output`".

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-output-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOutputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-output-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-descendant-text-content"
id="the-output-element:descendant-text-content-2"
data-x-internal="descendant-text-content">descendant text content</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`value`](#dom-output-value) setter steps are:

1.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-output-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-output-default-value-override"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-override-3">default
    value override</a> to its <a href="#concept-output-default-value"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-2">default value</a>.

2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#string-replace-all"
    id="the-output-element:string-replace-all-2"
    data-x-internal="string-replace-all">String replace all</a> with the
    given value within <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-output-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-output-defaultvalue" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLOutputElement" dfn-type="attribute">`defaultValue`</span>
getter steps are to return the result of running
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-output-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-output-default-value"
id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-3">default value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`defaultValue`](#dom-output-defaultvalue) setter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-output-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-output-default-value-override"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-override-4">default
    value override</a> is null, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#string-replace-all"
    id="the-output-element:string-replace-all-3"
    data-x-internal="string-replace-all">string replace all</a> with the
    given value within <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-output-element:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a> and
    return.

2.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-output-element:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-output-default-value-override"
    id="the-output-element:concept-output-default-value-override-5">default
    value override</a> to the given value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-output-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOutputElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> getter steps are to return
"`output`".

</div>

The [`willValidate`](#dom-cva-willvalidate),
[`validity`](#dom-cva-validity), and
[`validationMessage`](#dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and
the [`checkValidity()`](#dom-cva-checkvalidity),
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-cva-reportvalidity), and
[`setCustomValidity()`](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of
the <a href="#the-constraint-validation-api"
id="the-output-element:the-constraint-validation-api">constraint
validation API</a>. The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute
provides a list of the element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s. The
[`form`](#dom-fae-form) and [`name`](#dom-output-name) IDL attributes
are part of the element's forms API.

<div class="example">

A simple calculator could use [`output`](#the-output-element) for its
display of calculated results:

``` html
<form onsubmit="return false" oninput="o.value = a.valueAsNumber + b.valueAsNumber">
 <input id=a type=number step=any> +
 <input id=b type=number step=any> =
 <output id=o for="a b"></output>
</form>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, an [`output`](#the-output-element) element is used to
report the results of a calculation performed by a remote server, as
they come in:

``` html
<output id="result"></output>
<script>
 var primeSource = new WebSocket('ws://primes.example.net/');
 primeSource.onmessage = function (event) {
   document.getElementById('result').value = event.data;
 }
</script>
```

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-progress-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-progress-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#category-label"
id="the-progress-element:category-label">Labelable element</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-progress-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-progress-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:
