id="the-progress-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>, but
there must be no [`progress`](#the-progress-element) element
descendants.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-progress-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`value`](#attr-progress-value) — Current value of the element

[`max`](#attr-progress-max) — Upper bound of range

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-progress).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-progress).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-progress-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLProgressElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double value;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositive, ReflectDefault=1.0] attribute double max;
  readonly attribute double position;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`progress`](#the-progress-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-progress-element:represents">represents</a> the completion
progress of a task. The progress is either indeterminate, indicating
that progress is being made but that it is not clear how much more work
remains to be done before the task is complete (e.g. because the task is
waiting for a remote host to respond), or the progress is a number in
the range zero to a maximum, giving the fraction of work that has so far
been completed.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/max](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/max "The max attribute defines the maximum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the value of the element is greater than this, the element fails validation. This value must be greater than or equal to the value of the min attribute. If the max attribute is present but is not specified or is invalid, no max value is applied. If the max attribute is valid and a non-empty value is greater than the maximum allowed by the max attribute, constraint validation will prevent form submission.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox6+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari6+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome6+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera11+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS7+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

There are two attributes that determine the current task completion
represented by the element. The <span id="attr-progress-value"
class="dfn" dfn-for="progress" dfn-type="element-attr">`value`</span>
attribute specifies how much of the task has been completed, and the
<span id="attr-progress-max" class="dfn" dfn-for="progress"
dfn-type="element-attr">`max`</span> attribute specifies how much work
the task requires in total. The units are arbitrary and not specified.

To make a determinate progress bar, add a
[`value`](#attr-progress-value) attribute with the current progress
(either a number from 0.0 to 1.0, or, if the [`max`](#attr-progress-max)
attribute is specified, a number from 0 to the value of the
[`max`](#attr-progress-max) attribute). To make an indeterminate
progress bar, remove the [`value`](#attr-progress-value) attribute.

Authors are encouraged to also include the current value and the maximum
value inline as text inside the element, so that the progress is made
available to users of legacy user agents.

<div class="example">

Here is a snippet of a web application that shows the progress of some
automated task:

``` html
<section>
 <h2>Task Progress</h2>
 <p>Progress: <progress id=p max=100><span>0</span>%</progress></p>
 <script>
  var progressBar = document.getElementById('p');
  function updateProgress(newValue) {
    progressBar.value = newValue;
    progressBar.getElementsByTagName('span')[0].textContent = newValue;
  }
 </script>
</section>
```

(The `updateProgress()` method in this example would be called by some
other code on the page to update the actual progress bar as the task
progressed.)

</div>

The [`value`](#attr-progress-value) and [`max`](#attr-progress-max)
attributes, when present, must have values that are
<a href="#valid-floating-point-number"
id="the-progress-element:valid-floating-point-number">valid
floating-point numbers</a>. The [`value`](#attr-progress-value)
attribute, if present, must have a value greater than or equal to zero,
and less than or equal to the value of the [`max`](#attr-progress-max)
attribute, if present, or 1.0, otherwise. The
[`max`](#attr-progress-max) attribute, if present, must have a value
greater than zero.

The [`progress`](#the-progress-element) element is the wrong element to
use for something that is just a gauge, as opposed to task progress. For
instance, indicating disk space usage using
[`progress`](#the-progress-element) would be inappropriate. Instead, the
[`meter`](#the-meter-element) element is available for such use cases.

<div algorithm="">

**User agent requirements**: If the [`value`](#attr-progress-value)
attribute is omitted, then the progress bar is an indeterminate progress
bar. Otherwise, it is a determinate progress bar.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar and the element has a
[`max`](#attr-progress-max) attribute, the user agent must parse the
[`max`](#attr-progress-max) attribute's value according to the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values"
id="the-progress-element:rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values">rules
for parsing floating-point number values</a>. If this does not result in
an error, and if the parsed value is greater than zero, then the
<span id="concept-progress-maximum" class="dfn">maximum value</span> of
the progress bar is that value. Otherwise, if the element has no
[`max`](#attr-progress-max) attribute, or if it has one but parsing it
resulted in an error, or if the parsed value was less than or equal to
zero, then the <a href="#concept-progress-maximum"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-maximum">maximum value</a> of
the progress bar is 1.0.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar, user agents must
parse the [`value`](#attr-progress-value) attribute's value according to
the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values"
id="the-progress-element:rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values-2">rules
for parsing floating-point number values</a>. If this does not result in
an error and the parsed value is greater than zero, then the
<span id="concept-progress-value" class="dfn">value</span> of the
progress bar is that parsed value. Otherwise, if parsing the
[`value`](#attr-progress-value) attribute's value resulted in an error
or a number less than or equal to zero, then the
<a href="#concept-progress-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-value">value</a> of the
progress bar is zero.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar, then the
<span id="concept-progress-current-value" class="dfn">current
value</span> is the <a href="#concept-progress-maximum"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-maximum-2">maximum value</a>,
if <a href="#concept-progress-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-value-2">value</a> is greater
than the <a href="#concept-progress-maximum"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-maximum-3">maximum value</a>,
and <a href="#concept-progress-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-value-3">value</a> otherwise.

</div>

**UA requirements for showing the progress bar**: When representing a
[`progress`](#the-progress-element) element to the user, the UA should
indicate whether it is a determinate or indeterminate progress bar, and
in the former case, should indicate the relative position of the
<a href="#concept-progress-current-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-current-value">current
value</a> relative to the <a href="#concept-progress-maximum"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-maximum-4">maximum value</a>.

`progress``.`<a href="#dom-progress-position"
id="dom-progress-position-dev"><code>position</code></a>  
For a determinate progress bar (one with known current and maximum
values), returns the result of dividing the current value by the maximum
value.

For an indeterminate progress bar, returns −1.

<div algorithm="">

If the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, then the
<span id="dom-progress-position" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLProgressElement" dfn-type="attribute">`position`</span> IDL
attribute must return −1. Otherwise, it must return the result of
dividing the <a href="#concept-progress-current-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-current-value-2">current
value</a> by the <a href="#concept-progress-maximum"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-maximum-5">maximum value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-progress-value" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLProgressElement" dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> getter
steps are to return 0 if <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-progress-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a> is an
indeterminate progress bar; otherwise
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-progress-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-progress-value"
id="the-progress-element:concept-progress-value-4">current value</a>.

</div>

Setting the [`value`](#dom-progress-value) IDL attribute to itself when
the corresponding content attribute is absent would change the progress
bar from an indeterminate progress bar to a determinate progress bar
with no progress.

The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the
element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s.

#### <span class="secno">4.10.14</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`meter`</span> element<a href="#the-meter-element" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-meter-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-meter-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#category-label"
id="the-meter-element:category-label">Labelable element</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-meter-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-meter-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-meter-element:phrasing-content-2-3">Phrasing content</a>, but
there must be no [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element descendants.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-attributes">Content attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-meter-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`value`](#attr-meter-value) — Current value of the element

[`min`](#attr-meter-min) — Lower bound of range

[`max`](#attr-meter-max) — Upper bound of range

[`low`](#attr-meter-low) — High limit of low range

[`high`](#attr-meter-high) — Low limit of high range

[`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum) — Optimum value in gauge

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-meter).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-meter).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-meter-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMeterElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double value;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double min;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double max;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double low;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double high;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double optimum;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-meter-element:represents">represents</a> a
scalar measurement within a known range, or a fractional value; for
example disk usage, the relevance of a query result, or the fraction of
a voting population to have selected a particular candidate.

This is also known as a gauge.

The [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element should not be used to indicate
progress (as in a progress bar). For that role, HTML provides a separate
[`progress`](#the-progress-element) element.

The [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element also does not represent a
scalar value of arbitrary range — for example, it would be wrong to use
this to report a weight, or height, unless there is a known maximum
value.

There are six attributes that determine the semantics of the gauge
represented by the element.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/max](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/max "The max attribute defines the maximum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the value of the element is greater than this, the element fails validation. This value must be greater than or equal to the value of the min attribute. If the max attribute is present but is not specified or is invalid, no max value is applied. If the max attribute is valid and a non-empty value is greater than the maximum allowed by the max attribute, constraint validation will prevent form submission.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS10.3+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android no">WebView
AndroidNo</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

<div class="feature">

[Attributes/min](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/min "The min attribute defines the minimum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the value of the element is less than this, the element fails validation. This value must be less than or equal to the value of the max attribute.")

Support in all current engines.

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox16+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari6+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome6+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)18</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS10.3+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android no">WebView
AndroidNo</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-meter-min" class="dfn" dfn-for="meter"
dfn-type="element-attr">`min`</span> attribute specifies the lower bound
of the range, and the <span id="attr-meter-max" class="dfn"
dfn-for="meter" dfn-type="element-attr">`max`</span> attribute specifies
the upper bound. The <span id="attr-meter-value" class="dfn"
dfn-for="meter" dfn-type="element-attr">`value`</span> attribute
specifies the value to have the gauge indicate as the "measured" value.

The other three attributes can be used to segment the gauge's range into
"low", "medium", and "high" parts, and to indicate which part of the
gauge is the "optimum" part. The <span id="attr-meter-low" class="dfn"
dfn-for="meter" dfn-type="element-attr">`low`</span> attribute specifies
the range that is considered to be the "low" part, and the
<span id="attr-meter-high" class="dfn" dfn-for="meter"
dfn-type="element-attr">`high`</span> attribute specifies the range that
is considered to be the "high" part. The <span id="attr-meter-optimum"
class="dfn" dfn-for="meter" dfn-type="element-attr">`optimum`</span>
attribute gives the position that is "optimum"; if that is higher than
the "high" value then this indicates that the higher the value, the
better; if it's lower than the "low" mark then it indicates that lower
values are better, and naturally if it is in between then it indicates
that neither high nor low values are good.

**Authoring requirements**: The [`value`](#attr-meter-value) attribute
must be specified. The [`value`](#attr-meter-value),
[`min`](#attr-meter-min), [`low`](#attr-meter-low),
[`high`](#attr-meter-high), [`max`](#attr-meter-max), and
[`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum) attributes, when present, must have
values that are <a href="#valid-floating-point-number"
id="the-meter-element:valid-floating-point-number">valid floating-point
numbers</a>.

<div algorithm="">

In addition, the attributes' values are further constrained:

Let `value` be the [`value`](#attr-meter-value) attribute's number.

If the [`min`](#attr-meter-min) attribute is specified, then let
`minimum` be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be 0.

If the [`max`](#attr-meter-max) attribute is specified, then let
`maximum` be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be 1.0.

The following inequalities must hold, as applicable:

- `minimum` ≤ `value` ≤ `maximum`

- `minimum` ≤ [`low`](#attr-meter-low) ≤ `maximum` (if
  [`low`](#attr-meter-low) is specified)

- `minimum` ≤ [`high`](#attr-meter-high) ≤ `maximum` (if
  [`high`](#attr-meter-high) is specified)

- `minimum` ≤ [`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum) ≤ `maximum` (if
  [`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum) is specified)

- [`low`](#attr-meter-low) ≤ [`high`](#attr-meter-high) (if both
  [`low`](#attr-meter-low) and [`high`](#attr-meter-high) are specified)

</div>

If no minimum or maximum is specified, then the range is assumed to be
0..1, and the value thus has to be within that range.

Authors are encouraged to include a textual representation of the
gauge's state in the element's contents, for users of user agents that
do not support the [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element.

When used with
<a href="#microdata" id="the-meter-element:microdata">microdata</a>, the
[`meter`](#the-meter-element) element's [`value`](#attr-meter-value)
attribute provides the element's machine-readable value.

<div class="example">

The following examples show three gauges that would all be
three-quarters full:

``` html
Storage space usage: <meter value=6 max=8>6 blocks used (out of 8 total)</meter>
```

``` html
Voter turnout: <meter value=0.75><img alt="75%" src="graph75.png"></meter>
```

``` html
Tickets sold: <meter min="0" max="100" value="75"></meter>
```

The following example is incorrect use of the element, because it
doesn't give a range (and since the default maximum is 1, both of the
gauges would end up looking maxed out):

``` bad
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of <meter value=12>12cm</meter>
and a height of <meter value=2>2cm</meter>.</p> <!-- BAD! -->
```

Instead, one would either not include the meter element, or use the
meter element with a defined range to give the dimensions in context
compared to other pies:

``` html
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of 12cm and a height of
2cm.</p>
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12>12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2>2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

</div>

There is no explicit way to specify units in the
[`meter`](#the-meter-element) element, but the units may be specified in
the [`title`](#attr-title) attribute in free-form text.

<div class="example">

The example above could be extended to mention the units:

``` html
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12 title="centimeters">12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2 title="centimeters">2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

**User agent requirements**: User agents must parse the
[`min`](#attr-meter-min), [`max`](#attr-meter-max),
[`value`](#attr-meter-value), [`low`](#attr-meter-low),
[`high`](#attr-meter-high), and [`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum)
attributes using the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values"
id="the-meter-element:rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values">rules
for parsing floating-point number values</a>.

User agents must then use all these numbers to obtain values for six
points on the gauge, as follows. (The order in which these are evaluated
is important, as some of the values refer to earlier ones.)

The <span id="concept-meter-minimum" class="dfn">minimum value</span>  
If the [`min`](#attr-meter-min) attribute is specified and a value could
be parsed out of it, then the minimum value is that value. Otherwise,
the minimum value is zero.

The <span id="concept-meter-maximum" class="dfn">maximum value</span>  
If the [`max`](#attr-meter-max) attribute is specified and a value could
be parsed out of it, then the candidate maximum value is that value.
Otherwise, the candidate maximum value is 1.0.

If the candidate maximum value is greater than or equal to the minimum
value, then the maximum value is the candidate maximum value. Otherwise,
the maximum value is the same as the minimum value.

The <span id="concept-meter-actual" class="dfn">actual value</span>  
If the [`value`](#attr-meter-value) attribute is specified and a value
could be parsed out of it, then that value is the candidate actual
value. Otherwise, the candidate actual value is zero.

If the candidate actual value is less than the minimum value, then the
actual value is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate actual value is greater than the maximum
value, then the actual value is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the actual value is the candidate actual value.

The <span id="concept-meter-low" class="dfn">low boundary</span>  
If the [`low`](#attr-meter-low) attribute is specified and a value could
be parsed out of it, then the candidate low boundary is that value.
Otherwise, the candidate low boundary is the same as the minimum value.

If the candidate low boundary is less than the minimum value, then the
low boundary is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate low boundary is greater than the maximum
value, then the low boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the low boundary is the candidate low boundary.

The <span id="concept-meter-high" class="dfn">high boundary</span>  
If the [`high`](#attr-meter-high) attribute is specified and a value
could be parsed out of it, then the candidate high boundary is that
value. Otherwise, the candidate high boundary is the same as the maximum
value.

If the candidate high boundary is less than the low boundary, then the
high boundary is the low boundary.

Otherwise, if the candidate high boundary is greater than the maximum
value, then the high boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the high boundary is the candidate high boundary.

The <span id="concept-meter-optimum" class="dfn">optimum point</span>  
If the [`optimum`](#attr-meter-optimum) attribute is specified and a
value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate optimum point is
that value. Otherwise, the candidate optimum point is the midpoint
between the minimum value and the maximum value.

If the candidate optimum point is less than the minimum value, then the
optimum point is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate optimum point is greater than the maximum
value, then the optimum point is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the optimum point is the candidate optimum point.

All of which will result in the following inequalities all being true:

- minimum value ≤ actual value ≤ maximum value

- minimum value ≤ low boundary ≤ high boundary ≤ maximum value

- minimum value ≤ optimum point ≤ maximum value

</div>

**UA requirements for regions of the gauge**: If the optimum point is
equal to the low boundary or the high boundary, or anywhere in between
them, then the region between the low and high boundaries of the gauge
must be treated as the optimum region, and the low and high parts, if
any, must be treated as suboptimal. Otherwise, if the optimum point is
less than the low boundary, then the region between the minimum value
and the low boundary must be treated as the optimum region, the region
from the low boundary up to the high boundary must be treated as a
suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated as an even
less good region. Finally, if the optimum point is higher than the high
boundary, then the situation is reversed; the region between the high
boundary and the maximum value must be treated as the optimum region,
the region from the high boundary down to the low boundary must be
treated as a suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated
as an even less good region.

**UA requirements for showing the gauge**: When representing a
[`meter`](#the-meter-element) element to the user, the UA should
indicate the relative position of the actual value to the minimum and
maximum values, and the relationship between the actual value and the
three regions of the gauge.

<div class="example">

The following markup:

``` html
<h3>Suggested groups</h3>
<menu>
 <li><a href="?cmd=hsg" onclick="hideSuggestedGroups()">Hide suggested groups</a></li>
</menu>
<ul>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/view">comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets</a> -
     <a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Layout/presentation on the WWW.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.5">Moderate activity,</meter> Usenet, 618 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/view">netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall</a> -
     <a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Mozilla XPInstall discussion.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 22 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/view">mozilla.dev.general</a> -
     <a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 66 subscribers</p>
 </li>
</ul>
```

Might be rendered as follows:

<img src="/images/sample-meter.png" width="332" height="178"
alt="With the &lt;meter&gt; elements rendered as inline green bars of varying lengths." />

</div>

User agents may combine the value of the [`title`](#attr-title)
attribute and the other attributes to provide context-sensitive help or
inline text detailing the actual values.

<div class="example">

For example, the following snippet:

``` html
<meter min=0 max=60 value=23.2 title=seconds></meter>
```

...might cause the user agent to display a gauge with a tooltip saying
"Value: 23.2 out of 60." on one line and "seconds" on a second line.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-value" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`value`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-actual"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-actual">actual value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-min" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`min`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-minimum"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-minimum">minimum value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-max" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`max`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-maximum"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-maximum">maximum value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-low" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`low`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-low"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-low">low boundary</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-high" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`high`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-high"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-high">high boundary</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-meter-optimum" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMeterElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`optimum`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-meter-element:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-meter-optimum"
id="the-meter-element:concept-meter-optimum">optimum value</a>.

</div>

The [`labels`](#dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the
element's [`label`](#the-label-element)s.

<div class="example">

The following example shows how a gauge could fall back to localized or
pretty-printed text.

``` html
<p>Disk usage: <meter min=0 value=170261928 max=233257824>170 261 928 bytes used
out of 233 257 824 bytes available</meter></p>
```

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-fieldset-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#category-listed"
id="the-fieldset-element:category-listed">Listed</a> and
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="the-fieldset-element:category-autocapitalize">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting</a> <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="the-fieldset-element:form-associated-element">form-associated
element</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-fieldset-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-fieldset-element:flow-content-2-2">flow content</a> is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
Optionally, a [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element, followed by
<a href="#flow-content-2"
id="the-fieldset-element:flow-content-2-3">flow content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-fieldset-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`disabled`](#attr-fieldset-disabled) — Whether the descendant form
controls, except any inside [`legend`](#the-legend-element), are
disabled

[`form`](#attr-fae-form) — Associates the element with a
[`form`](#the-form-element) element

[`name`](#attr-fe-name) — Name of the element to use in the
[`form.elements`](#dom-form-elements) API.

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-fieldset).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-fieldset).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFieldSetElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection elements;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);
};
```

The [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-fieldset-element:represents">represents</a> a set of form
controls (or other content) grouped together, optionally with a caption.
The caption is given by the first [`legend`](#the-legend-element)
element that is a child of the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)
element, if any. The remainder of the descendants form the group.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/fieldset#attr-disabled](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/fieldset#attr-disabled "The <fieldset> HTML element is used to group several controls as well as labels (<label>) within a web form.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox4+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari6+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome20+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android12+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="attr-fieldset-disabled" class="dfn" dfn-for="fieldset"
dfn-type="element-attr">`disabled`</span> attribute, when specified,
causes all the form control descendants of the
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element, excluding those that are
descendants of the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element's first
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) element child, if any, to be
<a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
id="the-fieldset-element:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element is a
<span id="concept-fieldset-disabled" class="dfn">disabled
fieldset</span> if it matches any of the following conditions:

- Its [`disabled`](#attr-fieldset-disabled) attribute is specified
- It is a descendant of another [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)
  element whose [`disabled`](#attr-fieldset-disabled) attribute is
  specified, and is *not* a descendant of that
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element's first
  [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element child, if any.

</div>

The [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate
the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element with its
<a href="#form-owner" id="the-fieldset-element:form-owner">form
owner</a>. The [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute represents the
element's name.

`fieldset``.`<a href="#dom-fieldset-type"
id="dom-fieldset-type-dev"><code>type</code></a>  
Returns the string "fieldset".

`fieldset``.`<a href="#dom-fieldset-elements"
id="dom-fieldset-elements-dev"><code>elements</code></a>  
Returns an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-fieldset-element:htmlcollection-2">HTMLCollection</code></a> of
the form controls in the element.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-fieldset-type" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLFieldSetElement" dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> IDL
attribute must return the string "`fieldset`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-fieldset-elements" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLFieldSetElement" dfn-type="attribute">`elements`</span> IDL
attribute must return an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection"
data-x-internal="htmlcollection"><code
id="the-fieldset-element:htmlcollection-3">HTMLCollection</code></a>
rooted at the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element, whose filter
matches <a href="#category-listed"
id="the-fieldset-element:category-listed-2">listed elements</a>.

</div>

The [`willValidate`](#dom-cva-willvalidate),
[`validity`](#dom-cva-validity), and
[`validationMessage`](#dom-cva-validationmessage) attributes, and the
[`checkValidity()`](#dom-cva-checkvalidity),
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-cva-reportvalidity), and
[`setCustomValidity()`](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of
the <a href="#the-constraint-validation-api"
id="the-fieldset-element:the-constraint-validation-api">constraint
validation API</a>. The [`form`](#dom-fae-form) and
[`name`](#dom-fieldset-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's
forms API.

<div class="example">

This example shows a [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element being
used to group a set of related controls:

``` html
<fieldset>
 <legend>Display</legend>
 <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=0 checked> Black on White</label>
 <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=1> White on Black</label>
 <p><label><input type=checkbox name=g> Use grayscale</label>
 <p><label>Enhance contrast <input type=range name=e list=contrast min=0 max=100 value=0 step=1></label>
 <datalist id=contrast>
  <option label=Normal value=0>
  <option label=Maximum value=100>
 </datalist>
</fieldset>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The following snippet shows a fieldset with a checkbox in the legend
that controls whether or not the fieldset is enabled. The contents of
the fieldset consist of two required text controls and an optional
year/month control.

``` html
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
 <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
 <p><label>Expiry date: <input name=clubexp type=month></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

You can also nest [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) elements. Here is
an example expanding on the previous one that does so:

``` html
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
 <fieldset name="numfields">
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio checked name=clubtype onchange="form.numfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has numbers on it
  </label> </legend>
  <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset name="letfields" disabled>
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio name=clubtype onchange="form.letfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has letters on it
  </label> </legend>
  <p><label>Card code: <input name=clublet required pattern="[A-Za-z]+"></label></p>
 </fieldset>
</fieldset>
```

In this example, if the outer "Use Club Card" checkbox is not checked,
everything inside the outer [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element),
including the two radio buttons in the legends of the two nested
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)s, will be disabled. However, if the
checkbox is checked, then the radio buttons will both be enabled and
will let you select which of the two inner
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)s is to be enabled.

</div>

<div class="example">

This example shows a grouping of controls where the
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) element both labels the grouping, and
the nested heading element surfaces the grouping in the document
outline:

``` html
<fieldset>
 <legend> <h2>
  How can we best reach you?
 </h2> </legend>
 <p> <label>
 <input type=radio checked name=contact_pref>
  Phone
 </label> </p>
 <p> <label>
  <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
  Text
 </label> </p>
 <p> <label>
  <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
  Email
 </label> </p>
</fieldset>
```

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
None.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
As the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-first-child"
id="the-legend-element:first-child" data-x-internal="first-child">first
child</a> of a [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element.

As the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-first-child"
id="the-legend-element:first-child-2"
data-x-internal="first-child">first child</a> of an
[`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
If the element is a child of an [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)
element: <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-legend-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>, but
there must be no <a href="#interactive-content-2"
id="the-legend-element:interactive-content-2">interactive content</a>
and no descendant with the [`tabindex`](#attr-tabindex) attribute.

Otherwise: <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-legend-element:phrasing-content-2-2">Phrasing content</a>,
optionally intermixed with <a href="#heading-content-2"
id="the-legend-element:heading-content-2">heading content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-legend-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-legend).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-legend).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-legend-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLegendElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-legend-element:represents">represents</a>
a caption for the rest of the contents of the
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) element's parent
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element, if any. Otherwise, if the
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) has a parent
[`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element, then the
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) represents the
[`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element)'s label.

`legend``.`<a href="#dom-legend-form"
id="dom-legend-form-dev"><code>form</code></a>  
Returns the element's [`form`](#the-form-element) element, if any, or
null otherwise.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-legend-form" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLLegendElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`form`</span> IDL attribute's behavior depends on
whether the [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element is in a
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element or not. If the
[`legend`](#the-legend-element) has a
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element as its parent, then the
[`form`](#dom-legend-form) IDL attribute must return the same value as
the [`form`](#dom-fae-form) IDL attribute on that
[`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element. Otherwise, it must return
null.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.10.17</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`selectedcontent`</span> element<a href="#the-selectedcontent-element" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in
which this element can be used</a>:  
As a descendant of a [`button`](#the-button-element) element which is a
child of a [`select`](#the-select-element) element.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag
omission in text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-selectedcontent).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-selectedcontent).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSelectedContentElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element reflects
the contents of a [`select`](#the-select-element) element's currently
selected [`option`](#the-option-element) element.
[`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) elements can be used
to declaratively show the selected [`option`](#the-option-element)
element's contents within the [`select`](#the-select-element) element's
first child [`button`](#the-button-element) element.

The [`option`](#the-option-element) element's
[`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute can be used to render a visible
label for the option, but the
[`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element will not
reflect the content of the [`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute.

Every [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element has a
boolean <span id="selectedcontent-disabled" class="dfn">disabled</span>,
which is initially false.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="update-a-select's-selectedcontent" class="dfn">update a
`select`'s `selectedcontent`</span> given a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element `select`:

1.  Let `selectedcontent` be the result of
    <a href="#select-enabled-selectedcontent"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:select-enabled-selectedcontent">get a
    <code>select</code>'s enabled <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    `select`.

2.  If `selectedcontent` is null, then return.

3.  Let `option` be the first [`option`](#the-option-element) in
    `select`'s <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-select-option-list">list of
    options</a> whose <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</a>
    is true, if any such [`option`](#the-option-element) exists,
    otherwise null.

4.  If `option` is null, then run <a href="#clear-a-selectedcontent"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:clear-a-selectedcontent">clear a
    <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given `selectedcontent`.

5.  Otherwise, run <a href="#clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent">clone
    an option into a <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given `option` and
    `selectedcontent`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="select-enabled-selectedcontent" class="dfn">get a
`select`'s enabled `selectedcontent`</span> given a
[`select`](#the-select-element) element `select`:

1.  If `select` has the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute,
    then return null.

2.  Let `selectedcontent` be the first
    [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:descendant"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a> of `select` in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:tree-order"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> if any such element
    exists; otherwise return null.

3.  If `selectedcontent`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled">disabled</a>
    is true, then return null.

4.  Return `selectedcontent`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent" class="dfn">clone
an `option` into a `selectedcontent`</span>, given an
[`option`](#the-option-element) element `option` and a
[`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element
`selectedcontent`:

1.  Let `documentFragment` be a new
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:documentfragment">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    whose <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is `option`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  For each `child` of `option`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-tree-child"
    data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a>:

    1.  Let `childClone` be the result of running
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-node-clone"
        data-x-internal="concept-node-clone">clone</a> given `child`
        with <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#clone-a-node-subtree"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-node-clone-subtree"
        data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-subtree">subtree</a> set to
        true.

    2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-node-append"
        data-x-internal="concept-node-append">Append</a> `childClone` to
        `documentFragment`.

3.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-node-replace-all"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace-all">Replace all</a> with
    `documentFragment` within `selectedcontent`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="clear-a-selectedcontent" class="dfn">clear a
`selectedcontent`</span> given a
[`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element
`selectedcontent`:

1.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:concept-node-replace-all-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace-all">Replace all</a> with null
    within `selectedcontent`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="clear-a-select's-non-primary-selectedcontent-elements"
class="dfn">clear a `select`'s non-primary `selectedcontent`
elements</span>, given a [`select`](#the-select-element) element
`select`:

1.  Let `passedFirstSelectedcontent` be false.

2.  For each `descendant` of `select`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:descendant-2"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a> in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:tree-order-2"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> that is a
    [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element:

    1.  If `passedFirstSelectedcontent` is false, then set
        `passedFirstSelectedcontent` to true.

    2.  Otherwise, run <a href="#clear-a-selectedcontent"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:clear-a-selectedcontent-2">clear a
        <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given `descendant`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element)
<a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:html-element-post-connection-steps">HTML
element post-connection steps</a>, given `selectedcontent`, are:

1.  Let `nearestSelectAncestor` be null.

2.  Set `selectedcontent`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled-2">disabled</a>
    to false.

3.  For each `ancestor` of `selectedcontent`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:ancestor"
    data-x-internal="ancestor">ancestors</a>, in reverse
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:tree-order-3"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element:

        1.  If `nearestSelectAncestor` is null, then set
            `nearestSelectAncestor` to `select` and
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="the-selectedcontent-element:continue"
            data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

        2.  Set `selectedcontent`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
            id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled-3">disabled</a>
            to true and
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break"
            id="the-selectedcontent-element:break" data-x-internal="break">break</a>.

    2.  If `ancestor` is an [`option`](#the-option-element) element or a
        [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element) element, then
        set `selectedcontent`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled-4">disabled</a>
        to true and
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:break-2"
        data-x-internal="break">break</a>.

4.  If `selectedcontent`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled-5">disabled</a>
    is true, `nearestSelectAncestor` is null, or `nearestSelectAncestor`
    has the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute, then return.

5.  Run <a href="#update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent">update
    a <code>select</code>'s <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
    `nearestSelectAncestor`.

6.  Run
    <a href="#clear-a-select&#39;s-non-primary-selectedcontent-elements"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:clear-a-select&#39;s-non-primary-selectedcontent-elements">clear
    a <code>select</code>'s non-primary <code>selectedcontent</code>
    elements</a> given `nearestSelectAncestor`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`selectedcontent`](#the-selectedcontent-element)
<a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="the-selectedcontent-element:html-element-removing-steps">HTML
element removing steps</a>, given `removedNode`, `isSubtreeRoot`, and
`oldAncestor` are:

1.  If `removedNode`'s <a href="#selectedcontent-disabled"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:selectedcontent-disabled-6">disabled</a>
    is true, then return.

2.  For each `ancestor` of `removedNode`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:ancestor-2"
    data-x-internal="ancestor">ancestors</a>, in reverse
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:tree-order-4"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element, then
        return.

3.  For each `ancestor` of `oldAncestor`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-inclusive-ancestor"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:inclusive-ancestor"
    data-x-internal="inclusive-ancestor">inclusive ancestors</a>, in
    reverse <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-selectedcontent-element:tree-order-5"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` is a [`select`](#the-select-element) element, then
        run <a href="#update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent"
        id="the-selectedcontent-element:update-a-select&#39;s-selectedcontent-2">update
        a <code>select</code>'s <code>selectedcontent</code></a> given
        `ancestor` and return.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.10.18</span> Form control infrastructure<a href="#form-control-infrastructure" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">4.10.18.1</span> A form control's value<a href="#a-form-control&#39;s-value" class="self-link"></a>

Most form controls have a <span id="concept-fe-value"
class="dfn">value</span> and a <span id="concept-fe-checked"
class="dfn">checkedness</span>. (The latter is only used by
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements.) These are used to describe how
the user interacts with the control.

A control's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value">value</a> is its
internal state. As such, it might not match the user's current input.

For instance, if a user enters the word "<span class="kbd">three</span>"
into <a href="#number-state-(type=number)"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:number-state-(type=number)">a numeric
field</a> that expects digits, the user's input would be the string
"three" but the control's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-2">value</a> would
remain unchanged. Or, if a user enters the email address
"<span class="kbd">  awesome@example.com</span>" (with leading
whitespace) into <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:email-state-(type=email)">an email
field</a>, the user's input would be the string "  awesome@example.com"
but the browser's UI for email fields might translate that into a
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-3">value</a> of
"`awesome@example.com`" (without the leading whitespace).

<span id="concept-textarea-dirty"></span>[`input`](#the-input-element)
and [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements have a
<span id="concept-fe-dirty" class="dfn">dirty value flag</span>. This is
used to track the interaction between the <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-4">value</a> and default
value. If it is false, <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-5">value</a> mirrors the
default value. If it is true, the default value is ignored.

Some form controls also have an <span id="concept-fe-optional-value"
class="dfn">optional value</span>. This largely mirrors the
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-6">value</a> but doesn't
normalize to an empty string. <span class="note">This ought to be used
sparingly, you generally want <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-7">value</a></span>.

[`input`](#the-input-element), [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), and
[`select`](#the-select-element) elements have a <span id="user-validity"
class="dfn">user validity</span> boolean. It is initially set to false.

To define the behavior of constraint validation in the face of the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element's
[`multiple`](#attr-input-multiple) attribute,
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements can also have separately defined
<span id="concept-fe-values" class="dfn">value*s*</span>.

To define the behavior of the [`maxlength`](#attr-fe-maxlength) and
[`minlength`](#attr-fe-minlength) attributes, as well as other APIs
specific to the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element, all form
control with a <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-8">value</a> also have
an algorithm for obtaining an
<span id="concept-textarea-api-value"></span><span id="concept-fe-api-value"
class="dfn">API value</span>. By default this algorithm is to simply
return the control's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-9">value</a>.

The [`select`](#the-select-element) element does not have a
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-fe-value-10">value</a>; the
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="a-form-control&#39;s-value:concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</a>
of its [`option`](#the-option-element) elements is what is used instead.

##### <span class="secno">4.10.18.2</span> Mutability<a href="#mutability" class="self-link"></a>

A form control can be designated as <span id="concept-fe-mutable"
class="dfn">*mutable*</span>.

This determines (by means of definitions and requirements in this
specification that rely on whether an element is so designated) whether
or not the user can modify the
<a href="#concept-fe-value" id="mutability:concept-fe-value">value</a>
or <a href="#concept-fe-checked"
id="mutability:concept-fe-checked">checkedness</a> of a form control, or
whether or not a control can be automatically prefilled.

##### <span class="secno">4.10.18.3</span> Association of controls and forms<a href="#association-of-controls-and-forms" class="self-link"></a>

A <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element">form-associated
element</a> can have a relationship with a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element, which is called the element's <span id="form-owner" class="dfn"
dfn-for="button,fieldset,input,object,output,select,textarea,img,form-associated custom element"
export="">form owner</span>. If a <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-2">form-associated
element</a> is not associated with a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element, its <a href="#form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner">form owner</a> is said
to be null.

A <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-3">form-associated
element</a> has an associated <span id="parser-inserted-flag"
class="dfn">parser inserted flag</span>.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

A <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-4">form-associated
element</a> is, by default, associated with its nearest ancestor
[`form`](#the-form-element) element (as described below), but, if it is
<a href="#category-listed"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed">listed</a>, may
have a <span id="attr-fae-form" class="dfn"
dfn-for="button,fieldset,input,object,output,select,textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`form`</span> attribute specified to override
this.

This feature allows authors to work around the lack of support for
nested [`form`](#the-form-element) elements.

<div algorithm="">

If a <a href="#category-listed"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-2">listed</a>
<a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-5">form-associated
element</a> has a [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute specified, then
that attribute's value must be the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-id"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> of a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element in the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree"
data-x-internal="tree">tree</a>.

</div>

The rules in this section are complicated by the fact that although
conforming documents or
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree-2"
data-x-internal="tree">trees</a> will never contain nested
[`form`](#the-form-element) elements, it is quite possible (e.g., using
a script that performs DOM manipulation) to generate
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree-3"
data-x-internal="tree">trees</a> that have such nested elements. They
are also complicated by rules in the HTML parser that, for historical
reasons, can result in a <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-6">form-associated
element</a> being associated with a [`form`](#the-form-element) element
that is not its ancestor.

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-7">form-associated
element</a> is created, its <a href="#form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-2">form owner</a> must
be initialized to null (no owner).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-8">form-associated
element</a> is to be <span id="concept-form-association"
class="dfn">associated</span> with a form, its <a href="#form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-3">form owner</a> must
be set to that form.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#category-listed"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-3">listed</a>
<a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-9">form-associated
element</a>'s [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute is set, changed, or
removed, then the user agent must <a href="#reset-the-form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:reset-the-form-owner">reset the
form owner</a> of that element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#category-listed"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-4">listed</a>
<a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-10">form-associated
element</a> has a [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute and the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-id-2"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> of any of the elements in the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree-4"
data-x-internal="tree">tree</a> changes, then the user agent must
<a href="#reset-the-form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:reset-the-form-owner-2">reset the
form owner</a> of that <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-11">form-associated
element</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#category-listed"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-5">listed</a>
<a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-12">form-associated
element</a> has a [`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute and an element with
an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-id-3"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> is
<a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:insert-an-element-into-a-document">inserted
into</a> or <a href="#remove-an-element-from-a-document"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:remove-an-element-from-a-document">removed
from</a> the [`Document`](#document), or its
<a href="#html-element-moving-steps"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:html-element-moving-steps">HTML
element moving steps</a> are run, then the user agent must
<a href="#reset-the-form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:reset-the-form-owner-3">reset the
form owner</a> of that <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-13">form-associated
element</a>.

</div>

The form owner is also reset by the
<a href="#html-element-insertion-steps"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:html-element-insertion-steps">HTML
element insertion steps</a>, <a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:html-element-removing-steps">HTML
element removing steps</a>, and <a href="#html-element-moving-steps"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:html-element-moving-steps-2">HTML
element moving steps</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="reset-the-form-owner" class="dfn">reset the form
owner</span> of a <a href="#form-associated-element"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-associated-element-14">form-associated
element</a> `element`:

1.  Unset `element`'s <a href="#parser-inserted-flag"
    id="association-of-controls-and-forms:parser-inserted-flag">parser
    inserted flag</a>.

2.  If all of the following are true:

    - `element`'s <a href="#form-owner"
      id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-4">form owner</a>
      is not null;

    - `element` is not <a href="#category-listed"
      id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-6">listed</a>
      or its [`form`](#attr-fae-form) content attribute is not present;
      and

    - `element`'s <a href="#form-owner"
      id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-5">form owner</a>
      is its nearest [`form`](#the-form-element) element ancestor after
      the change to the ancestor chain,

    then return.

3.  Set `element`'s <a href="#form-owner"
    id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-6">form owner</a>
    to null.

4.  If `element` is <a href="#category-listed"
    id="association-of-controls-and-forms:category-listed-7">listed</a>,
    has a [`form`](#attr-fae-form) content attribute, and is
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="association-of-controls-and-forms:connected"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then:

    1.  If the first element in `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
        id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree-5"
        data-x-internal="tree">tree</a>, in
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
        id="association-of-controls-and-forms:tree-order"
        data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>, to have an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
        id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-id-4"
        data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a> that is
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
        id="association-of-controls-and-forms:identical-to"
        data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> `element`'s
        [`form`](#attr-fae-form) content attribute's value, is a
        [`form`](#the-form-element) element, then
        <a href="#concept-form-association"
        id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-form-association">associate</a>
        the `element` with that [`form`](#the-form-element) element.

5.  Otherwise, if `element` has an ancestor [`form`](#the-form-element)
    element, then <a href="#concept-form-association"
    id="association-of-controls-and-forms:concept-form-association-2">associate</a>
    `element` with the nearest such ancestor [`form`](#the-form-element)
    element.

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following non-conforming snippet

``` bad
...
 <form id="a">
  <div id="b"></div>
 </form>
 <script>
  document.getElementById('b').innerHTML =
     '<table><tr><td></form><form id="c"><input id="d"></table>' +
     '<input id="e">';
 </script>
...
```

the <a href="#form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-7">form owner</a> of
"d" would be the inner nested form "c", while the <a href="#form-owner"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:form-owner-8">form owner</a> of
"e" would be the outer form "a".

This happens as follows: First, the "e" node gets associated with "c" in
the <a href="#html-parser"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:html-parser">HTML parser</a>.
Then, the [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) algorithm moves the
nodes from the temporary document to the "b" element. At this point, the
nodes see their ancestor chain change, and thus all the "magic"
associations done by the parser are reset to normal ancestor
associations.

This example is a non-conforming document, though, as it is a violation
of the content models to nest [`form`](#the-form-element) elements, and
there is a <a href="#parse-errors"
id="association-of-controls-and-forms:parse-errors">parse error</a> for
the `</form>` tag.

</div>

`element``.`<a href="#dom-fae-form" id="dom-fae-form-dev"><code>form</code></a>

#### <span class="secno">4.10.19</span> Attributes common to form controls<a href="#attributes-common-to-form-controls" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">4.10.19.1</span> Naming form controls: the [`name`](#attr-fe-name) attribute<a href="#naming-form-controls:-the-name-attribute"
class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Element/input#name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#name "The <input> HTML element is used to create interactive controls for web-based forms in order to accept data from the user; a wide variety of types of input data and control widgets are available, depending on the device and user agent. The <input> element is one of the most powerful and complex in all of HTML due to the sheer number of combinations of input types and attributes.")

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-fe-name" class="dfn"
dfn-for="button,fieldset,input,output,select,textarea"
dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> content attribute gives the name
of the form control, as used in <a href="#form-submission-2"
id="naming-form-controls:-the-name-attribute:form-submission-2">form
submission</a> and in the [`form`](#the-form-element) element's
[`elements`](#dom-form-elements) object. If the attribute is specified,
its value must not be the empty string or `isindex`.

A number of user agents historically implemented special support for
first-in-form text controls with the name `isindex`, and this
specification previously defined related user agent requirements for it.
However, some user agents subsequently dropped that special support, and
the related requirements were removed from this specification. So, to
avoid problematic reinterpretations in legacy user agents, the name
`isindex` is no longer allowed.

Other than `isindex`, any non-empty value for [`name`](#attr-form-name)
is allowed. An
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="naming-form-controls:-the-name-attribute:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the name <span id="attr-fe-name-charset"
class="dfn">`_charset_`</span> is special: if used as the name of a
<a href="#hidden-state-(type=hidden)"
id="naming-form-controls:-the-name-attribute:hidden-state-(type=hidden)">Hidden</a>
control with no [`value`](#attr-input-value) attribute, then during
submission the [`value`](#attr-input-value) attribute is automatically
given a value consisting of the submission character encoding.

<div class="note">

DOM clobbering is a common cause of security issues. Avoid using the
names of built-in form properties with the [`name`](#attr-fe-name)
content attribute.

In this example, the [`input`](#the-input-element) element overrides the
built-in [`method`](#attr-fs-method) property:

``` js
let form = document.createElement("form");
let input = document.createElement("input");
form.appendChild(input);

form.method;           // => "get"
input.name = "method"; // DOM clobbering occurs here
form.method === input; // => true
```

Since the input name takes precedence over built-in form properties, the
JavaScript reference `form.method` will point to the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element named "method" instead of the
built-in [`method`](#attr-fs-method) property.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.10.19.2</span> Submitting element directionality: the [`dirname`](#attr-fe-dirname) attribute<a href="#submitting-element-directionality:-the-dirname-attribute"
class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

[Element/input#dirname](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#dirname "The <input> HTML element is used to create interactive controls for web-based forms in order to accept data from the user; a wide variety of types of input data and control widgets are available, depending on the device and user agent. The <input> element is one of the most powerful and complex in all of HTML due to the sheer number of combinations of input types and attributes.")

------------------------------------------------------------------------
