    <a href="#inert" id="the-dialog-element:inert">inert</a> (unless
    that currently focused area is a <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-descendant"
    id="the-dialog-element:shadow-including-descendant"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-descendant">shadow-including
    descendant</a> of `subject`). In such cases, the
    <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:focused-area-of-the-document-2">focused area of
    the document</a> will soon be [reset](#focus-fixup-rule) to the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
    id="the-dialog-element:viewport" data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>.
    In a couple steps we will attempt to find a better candidate to
    focus.

15. If `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-7"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer"
    id="the-dialog-element:top-layer-2" data-x-internal="top-layer">top
    layer</a> does not already
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="the-dialog-element:list-contains-2"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contain</a> `subject`, then <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#add-an-element-to-the-top-layer"
    id="the-dialog-element:add-an-element-to-the-top-layer"
    data-x-internal="add-an-element-to-the-top-layer">add an element to the
    top layer</a> given `subject`.

16. Set `subject`'s <a href="#previously-focused-element"
    id="the-dialog-element:previously-focused-element-2">previously focused
    element</a> to the
    <a href="#focused" id="the-dialog-element:focused-4">focused</a>
    element.

17. Let `document` be `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-8"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

18. Let `hideUntil` be the result of running
    <a href="#topmost-popover-ancestor"
    id="the-dialog-element:topmost-popover-ancestor-3">topmost popover
    ancestor</a> given `subject`, `document`'s
    <a href="#showing-hint-popover-list"
    id="the-dialog-element:showing-hint-popover-list-2">showing hint popover
    list</a>, null, and false.

19. If `hideUntil` is null, then set `hideUntil` to the result of
    running <a href="#topmost-popover-ancestor"
    id="the-dialog-element:topmost-popover-ancestor-4">topmost popover
    ancestor</a> given `subject`, `document`'s
    <a href="#auto-popover-list"
    id="the-dialog-element:auto-popover-list-2">showing auto popover
    list</a>, null, and false.

20. If `hideUntil` is null, then set `hideUntil` to `document`.

21. Run <a href="#hide-all-popovers-until"
    id="the-dialog-element:hide-all-popovers-until-2">hide all popovers
    until</a> given `hideUntil`, false, and true.

22. Run the <a href="#dialog-focusing-steps"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-focusing-steps-6">dialog focusing
    steps</a> given `subject`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="set-the-dialog-close-watcher" class="dfn">set the dialog
close watcher</span>, given a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element
`dialog`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `dialog`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-4">close watcher</a> is
    null.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-3" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `dialog` has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute and `dialog`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-9"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is
    <a href="#fully-active" id="the-dialog-element:fully-active-4">fully
    active</a>.

3.  Set `dialog`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-5">close watcher</a> to
    the result of <a href="#establish-a-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:establish-a-close-watcher">establishing a close
    watcher</a> given `dialog`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>, with:

    - *[cancelAction](#create-close-watcher-cancelaction)* given
      `canPreventClose` being to return the result of
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
      id="the-dialog-element:concept-event-fire-3"
      data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">firing an event</a> named
      [`cancel`](#event-cancel) at `dialog`, with the
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
      data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
      id="the-dialog-element:dom-event-cancelable-3">cancelable</code></a>
      attribute initialized to `canPreventClose`.

    - *[closeAction](#create-close-watcher-closeaction)* being to
      <a href="#close-the-dialog"
      id="the-dialog-element:close-the-dialog-2">close the dialog</a>
      given `dialog`, `dialog`'s <a href="#request-close-return-value"
      id="the-dialog-element:request-close-return-value">request close return
      value</a>, and `dialog`'s <a href="#request-close-source-element"
      id="the-dialog-element:request-close-source-element">request close
      source element</a>.

    - *[getEnabledState](#create-close-watcher-getenabledstate)* being
      to return true if `dialog`'s
      <a href="#enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()"
      id="the-dialog-element:enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()-2">enable
      close watcher for request close</a> is true or `dialog`'s
      <a href="#computed-closed-by-state"
      id="the-dialog-element:computed-closed-by-state-3">computed closed-by
      state</a> is not <a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-none-state"
      id="the-dialog-element:attr-dialog-closedby-none-state-3">None</a>;
      otherwise false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#is-valid-command-steps"
id="the-dialog-element:is-valid-command-steps">is valid command
steps</a> for [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements, given a
[`command`](#attr-button-command) attribute `command`, are:

1.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-close-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-close-state">Close</a>
    state, the <a href="#attr-button-command-request-close-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-request-close-state">Request
    Close</a> state, or the
    <a href="#attr-button-command-show-modal-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-show-modal-state">Show
    Modal</a> state, then return true.

2.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The
<a href="#command-steps" id="the-dialog-element:command-steps">command
steps</a> for [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements, given an element
`element`, an element `source`, and a [`command`](#attr-button-command)
attribute `command`, are:

1.  If `element` is in the <a href="#popover-showing-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:popover-showing-state-3">popover showing</a>
    state, then return.

2.  If `command` is in the <a href="#attr-button-command-close-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-close-state-2">Close</a>
    state and `element` has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute,
    then <a href="#close-the-dialog"
    id="the-dialog-element:close-the-dialog-3">close the dialog</a>
    `element` with `source`'s <a href="#concept-fe-optional-value"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-fe-optional-value">optional value</a>
    and `source`.

3.  If `command` is in the
    <a href="#attr-button-command-request-close-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-request-close-state-2">Request
    Close</a> state and `element` has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open)
    attribute, then <a href="#dialog-request-close"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-request-close-3">request to close the
    dialog</a> `element` with `source`'s
    <a href="#concept-fe-optional-value"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-fe-optional-value-2">optional value</a>
    and `source`.

4.  If `command` is the <a href="#attr-button-command-show-modal-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-button-command-show-modal-state-2">Show
    Modal</a> state and `element` does not have an
    [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute, then
    <a href="#show-a-modal-dialog"
    id="the-dialog-element:show-a-modal-dialog-2">show a modal dialog</a>
    given `element` and `source`.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following buttons use [`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) to
open and close a "confirm" [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) as modal when
activated:

``` html
<button type=button
        commandfor="the-dialog"
        command="show-modal">
 Delete
</button>
<dialog id="the-dialog">
 <form action="/delete" method="POST">
  <button type="submit">
   Delete
  </button>
  <button commandfor="the-dialog"
          command="close">
   Cancel
  </button>
 </form>
</dialog>
    
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element `subject` is to be
<span id="close-the-dialog" class="dfn">closed</span>, with null or a
string `result` and an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-dialog-element:element-3">Element</code></a> or null `source`,
run these steps:

1.  If `subject` does not have an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute,
    then return.

2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-event-fire-4"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`beforetoggle`](#event-beforetoggle), using
    [`ToggleEvent`](#toggleevent), with the
    [`oldState`](#dom-toggleevent-oldstate) attribute initialized to
    "`open`", the [`newState`](#dom-toggleevent-newstate) attribute
    initialized to "`closed`", and the
    [`source`](#dom-toggleevent-source) attribute initialized to
    `source` at `subject`.

3.  If `subject` does not have an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute,
    then return.

4.  <a href="#queue-a-dialog-toggle-event-task"
    id="the-dialog-element:queue-a-dialog-toggle-event-task-3">Queue a
    dialog toggle event task</a> given `subject`, "`open`", "`closed`",
    and `source`.

5.  Remove `subject`'s [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute.

6.  If
    <a href="#is-modal" id="the-dialog-element:is-modal-5">is modal</a>
    of `subject` is true, then <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#request-an-element-to-be-removed-from-the-top-layer"
    id="the-dialog-element:request-an-element-to-be-removed-from-the-top-layer"
    data-x-internal="request-an-element-to-be-removed-from-the-top-layer">request
    an element to be removed from the top layer</a> given `subject`.

7.  Let `wasModal` be the value of `subject`'s
    <a href="#is-modal" id="the-dialog-element:is-modal-6">is modal</a>
    flag.

8.  Set
    <a href="#is-modal" id="the-dialog-element:is-modal-7">is modal</a>
    of `subject` to false.

9.  If `result` is not null, then set `subject`'s
    [`returnValue`](#dom-dialog-returnvalue) attribute to `result`.

10. Set `subject`'s <a href="#request-close-return-value"
    id="the-dialog-element:request-close-return-value-2">request close
    return value</a> to null.

11. Set `subject`'s <a href="#request-close-source-element"
    id="the-dialog-element:request-close-source-element-2">request close
    source element</a> to null.

12. If `subject`'s <a href="#previously-focused-element"
    id="the-dialog-element:previously-focused-element-3">previously focused
    element</a> is not null, then:

    1.  Let `element` be `subject`'s
        <a href="#previously-focused-element"
        id="the-dialog-element:previously-focused-element-4">previously focused
        element</a>.

    2.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#previously-focused-element"
        id="the-dialog-element:previously-focused-element-5">previously focused
        element</a> to null.

    3.  If `subject`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-dialog-element:node-document-10"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
        <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
        id="the-dialog-element:focused-area-of-the-document-3">focused area of
        the document</a>'s
        <a href="#dom-anchor" id="the-dialog-element:dom-anchor">DOM anchor</a>
        is a <a
        href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-descendant"
        id="the-dialog-element:shadow-including-inclusive-descendant"
        data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-descendant">shadow-including
        inclusive descendant</a> of `subject`, or `wasModal` is true,
        then run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
        id="the-dialog-element:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a> for
        `element`; the viewport should not be scrolled by doing this
        step.

13. <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
    id="the-dialog-element:queue-an-element-task">Queue an element task</a>
    on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
    id="the-dialog-element:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction
    task source</a> given the `subject` element to
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-event-fire-5"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    [`close`](#event-close) at `subject`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="dialog-request-close" class="dfn">request to close</span>
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element `subject`, given null or a
string `returnValue` and null or an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-dialog-element:element-4">Element</code></a> `source`:

1.  If `subject` does not have an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute,
    then return.

2.  If `subject` is not <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="the-dialog-element:connected-5"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a> or `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-11"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="the-dialog-element:fully-active-5">fully
    active</a>, then return.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-4" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `subject`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-6">close watcher</a> is
    not null.

4.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()"
    id="the-dialog-element:enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()-3">enable
    close watcher for request close</a> to true.

5.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#request-close-return-value"
    id="the-dialog-element:request-close-return-value-3">request close
    return value</a> to `returnValue`.

6.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#request-close-source-element"
    id="the-dialog-element:request-close-source-element-3">request close
    source element</a> to `source`.

7.  <a href="#close-watcher-request-close"
    id="the-dialog-element:close-watcher-request-close">Request to close</a>
    `subject`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-7">close watcher</a>
    with false.

8.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()"
    id="the-dialog-element:enable-close-watcher-for-requestclose()-4">enable
    close watcher for request close</a> to false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="queue-a-dialog-toggle-event-task" class="dfn">queue a
dialog toggle event task</span> given a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element)
element `element`, a string `oldState`, a string `newState`, and an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-dialog-element:element-5">Element</code></a> or null `source`:

1.  If `element`'s <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker">dialog toggle task
    tracker</a> is not null, then:

    1.  Set `oldState` to `element`'s
        <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker-2">dialog toggle task
        tracker</a>'s <a href="#toggle-task-old-state"
        id="the-dialog-element:toggle-task-old-state">old state</a>.

    2.  Remove `element`'s <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker-3">dialog toggle task
        tracker</a>'s <a href="#toggle-task-task"
        id="the-dialog-element:toggle-task-task">task</a> from its
        <a href="#task-queue" id="the-dialog-element:task-queue">task queue</a>.

    3.  Set `element`'s <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker-4">dialog toggle task
        tracker</a> to null.

2.  <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
    id="the-dialog-element:queue-an-element-task-2">Queue an element
    task</a> given the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
    id="the-dialog-element:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM manipulation
    task source</a> and `element` to run the following steps:

    1.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="the-dialog-element:concept-event-fire-6"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
        [`toggle`](#event-toggle) at `element`, using
        [`ToggleEvent`](#toggleevent), with the
        [`oldState`](#dom-toggleevent-oldstate) attribute initialized to
        `oldState`, the [`newState`](#dom-toggleevent-newstate)
        attribute initialized to `newState`, and the
        [`source`](#dom-toggleevent-source) attribute initialized to
        `source`.

    2.  Set `element`'s <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker-5">dialog toggle task
        tracker</a> to null.

3.  Set `element`'s <a href="#dialog-toggle-task-tracker"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-toggle-task-tracker-6">dialog toggle task
    tracker</a> to a struct with <a href="#toggle-task-task"
    id="the-dialog-element:toggle-task-task-2">task</a> set to the
    just-queued
    <a href="#concept-task" id="the-dialog-element:concept-task">task</a>
    and <a href="#toggle-task-old-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:toggle-task-old-state-2">old state</a> set to
    `oldState`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To retrieve a dialog's <span id="computed-closed-by-state"
class="dfn">computed closed-by state</span>, given a
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) `dialog`:

1.  If the state of `dialog`'s [`closedby`](#attr-dialog-closedby)
    attribute is <a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-auto-state"
    id="the-dialog-element:attr-dialog-closedby-auto-state-2">Auto</a>:

    1.  If `dialog`'s
        <a href="#is-modal" id="the-dialog-element:is-modal-8">is modal</a>
        is true, then return
        <a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-closerequest-state"
        id="the-dialog-element:attr-dialog-closedby-closerequest-state-2">Close
        Request</a>.

    2.  Return <a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-none-state"
        id="the-dialog-element:attr-dialog-closedby-none-state-4">None</a>.

2.  Return the state of `dialog`'s [`closedby`](#attr-dialog-closedby)
    attribute.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dialog-focusing-steps" class="dfn">dialog focusing
steps</span>, given a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element `subject`,
are as follows:

1.  If the <a href="#allow-focus-steps"
    id="the-dialog-element:allow-focus-steps">allow focus steps</a>
    given `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-12"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> return false, then
    return.

2.  Let `control` be null.

3.  If `subject` has the [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute,
    then set `control` to `subject`.

4.  If `control` is null, then set `control` to the
    <a href="#focus-delegate" id="the-dialog-element:focus-delegate">focus
    delegate</a> of `subject`.

5.  If `control` is null, then set `control` to `subject`.

6.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="the-dialog-element:focusing-steps-2">focusing steps</a> for
    `control`.

    If `control` is not
    <a href="#focusable" id="the-dialog-element:focusable">focusable</a>,
    this will do nothing. This would only happen if subject had no focus
    delegate, and the user agent decided that
    [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements were not generally
    focusable. In that case, any [earlier
    modifications](#note-dialog-plus-focus-fixup) to the
    <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:focused-area-of-the-document-4">focused area of
    the document</a> will apply.

7.  Let `topDocument` be `control`'s
    <a href="#node-navigable" id="the-dialog-element:node-navigable">node
    navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top" id="the-dialog-element:nav-top">top-level
    traversable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-dialog-element:nav-document">active
    document</a>.

8.  If `control`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-13"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is not the
    <a href="#same-origin" id="the-dialog-element:same-origin">same</a>
    as the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="the-dialog-element:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> of
    `topDocument`, then return.

9.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-empty"
    id="the-dialog-element:list-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-empty">Empty</a> `topDocument`'s
    <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
    id="the-dialog-element:autofocus-candidates">autofocus candidates</a>.

10. Set `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-processed-flag"
    id="the-dialog-element:autofocus-processed-flag">autofocus processed
    flag</a> to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dialog-setup-steps" class="dfn">dialog setup steps</span>,
given a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element `subject`, are as
follows:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-5" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `subject` has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-6" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `subject` is <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="the-dialog-element:connected-6"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-dialog-element:assert-7" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-14"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#open-dialogs-list"
    id="the-dialog-element:open-dialogs-list">open dialogs list</a> does
    not <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="the-dialog-element:list-contains-3"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contain</a> `subject`.

4.  Add `subject` to `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-15"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#open-dialogs-list"
    id="the-dialog-element:open-dialogs-list-2">open dialogs list</a>.

5.  <a href="#set-the-dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:set-the-dialog-close-watcher">Set the dialog
    close watcher</a> with `subject`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dialog-cleanup-steps" class="dfn">dialog cleanup
steps</span>, given a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element `subject`,
are as follows:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="the-dialog-element:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `subject` from `subject`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-dialog-element:node-document-16"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#open-dialogs-list"
    id="the-dialog-element:open-dialogs-list-3">open dialogs list</a>.

2.  If `subject`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
    id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-8">close watcher</a> is
    not null, then:

    1.  <a href="#close-watcher-destroy"
        id="the-dialog-element:close-watcher-destroy">Destroy</a>
        `subject`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-9">close watcher</a>.

    2.  Set `subject`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
        id="the-dialog-element:dialog-close-watcher-10">close watcher</a>
        to null.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.11.5</span> <span class="dfn">Dialog light dismiss</span><a href="#dialog-light-dismiss" class="self-link"></a>

"Light dismiss" means that clicking outside of a
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element whose
[`closedby`](#attr-dialog-closedby) attribute is in the
<a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-any-state"
id="dialog-light-dismiss:attr-dialog-closedby-any-state">Any</a> state
will close the [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element. This is in
addition to how such [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element)s respond to
<a href="#close-request" id="dialog-light-dismiss:close-request">close
requests</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="light-dismiss-open-dialogs" class="dfn">light dismiss open
dialogs</span>, given a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface"
data-x-internal="pointerevent"><code
id="dialog-light-dismiss:pointerevent">PointerEvent</code></a> `event`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-istrusted"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:dom-event-istrusted">isTrusted</code></a>
    attribute is true.

2.  Let `document` be `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-target"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:concept-event-target"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-target">target</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

3.  If `document`'s <a href="#open-dialogs-list"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:open-dialogs-list">open dialogs list</a> is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>, then return.

4.  Let `ancestor` be the result of running
    <a href="#nearest-clicked-dialog"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:nearest-clicked-dialog">nearest clicked
    dialog</a> given `event`.

5.  If `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:dom-event-type">type</code></a> is
    "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerdown-event"
    data-x-internal="event-pointerdown"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:event-pointerdown">pointerdown</code></a>",
    then set `document`'s <a href="#dialog-pointerdown-target"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:dialog-pointerdown-target">dialog pointerdown
    target</a> to `ancestor`.

6.  If `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:dom-event-type-2">type</code></a> is
    "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerup-event"
    data-x-internal="event-pointerup"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:event-pointerup">pointerup</code></a>",
    then:

    1.  Let `sameTarget` be true if `ancestor` is `document`'s
        <a href="#dialog-pointerdown-target"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:dialog-pointerdown-target-2">dialog pointerdown
        target</a>.

    2.  Set `document`'s <a href="#dialog-pointerdown-target"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:dialog-pointerdown-target-3">dialog pointerdown
        target</a> to null.

    3.  If `sameTarget` is false, then return.

    4.  Let `topmostDialog` be the last element of `document`'s
        <a href="#open-dialogs-list"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:open-dialogs-list-2">open dialogs list</a>.

    5.  If `ancestor` is `topmostDialog`, then return.

    6.  If `topmostDialog`'s <a href="#computed-closed-by-state"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:computed-closed-by-state">computed closed-by
        state</a> is not <a href="#attr-dialog-closedby-any-state"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:attr-dialog-closedby-any-state-2">Any</a>,
        then return.

    7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `topmostDialog`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:dialog-close-watcher">close watcher</a>
        is not null.

    8.  <a href="#close-watcher-request-close"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:close-watcher-request-close">Request to
        close</a> `topmostDialog`'s <a href="#dialog-close-watcher"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:dialog-close-watcher-2">close watcher</a>
        with false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="run-light-dismiss-activities" class="dfn">run light dismiss
activities</span>, given a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface"
data-x-internal="pointerevent"><code
id="dialog-light-dismiss:pointerevent-2">PointerEvent</code></a>
`event`:

1.  Run <a href="#light-dismiss-open-popovers"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:light-dismiss-open-popovers">light dismiss open
    popovers</a> with `event`.

2.  Run <a href="#light-dismiss-open-dialogs"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:light-dismiss-open-dialogs">light dismiss open
    dialogs</a> with `event`.

</div>

<a href="#run-light-dismiss-activities"
id="dialog-light-dismiss:run-light-dismiss-activities">Run light dismiss
activities</a> will be called by the [Pointer Events
spec](https://github.com/w3c/pointerevents/pull/460) when the user
clicks or touches anywhere on the page.

<div algorithm="">

To find the <span id="nearest-clicked-dialog" class="dfn">nearest
clicked dialog</span>, given a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface"
data-x-internal="pointerevent"><code
id="dialog-light-dismiss:pointerevent-3">PointerEvent</code></a>
`event`:

1.  Let `target` be `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-target"
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:concept-event-target-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-target">target</a>.

2.  If `target` is a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element, `target`
    has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute, `target`'s
    <a href="#is-modal" id="dialog-light-dismiss:is-modal">is modal</a>
    is true, and `event`'s
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clientx"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clientx"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:mouseevent-clientx">clientX</code></a> and
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clienty"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clienty"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:mouseevent-clienty">clientY</code></a> are
    outside the bounds of `target`, then return null.

    The check for
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clientx"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clientx"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:mouseevent-clientx-2">clientX</code></a>
    and
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clienty"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clienty"><code
    id="dialog-light-dismiss:mouseevent-clienty-2">clientY</code></a> is
    because a pointer event that hits the `::backdrop` pseudo element of
    a dialog will result in `event` having a target of the dialog
    element itself.

3.  Let `currentNode` be `target`.

4.  While `currentNode` is not null:

    1.  If `currentNode` is a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element
        and `currentNode` has an [`open`](#attr-dialog-open) attribute,
        then return `currentNode`.

    2.  Set `currentNode` to `currentNode`'s parent in the
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
        id="dialog-light-dismiss:flat-tree" data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat
        tree</a>.

5.  Return null.

</div>

### <span class="secno">4.12</span> Scripting<a href="#scripting-3" class="self-link"></a>

Scripts allow authors to add interactivity to their documents.

Authors are encouraged to use declarative alternatives to scripting
where possible, as declarative mechanisms are often more maintainable,
and many users disable scripting.

<div class="example">

For example, instead of using a script to show or hide a section to show
more details, the [`details`](#the-details-element) element could be
used.

</div>

Authors are also encouraged to make their applications degrade
gracefully in the absence of scripting support.

<div class="example">

For example, if an author provides a link in a table header to
dynamically resort the table, the link could also be made to function
without scripts by requesting the sorted table from the server.

</div>

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLScriptElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean defer;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList blocking;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? crossOrigin;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString referrerPolicy;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString integrity;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString fetchPriority;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString text;

  static boolean supports(DOMString type);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`script`](#the-script-element) element allows authors to include
dynamic script, instructions to the user agent, and data blocks in their
documents. The element does not
<a href="#represents" id="the-script-element:represents">represent</a>
content for the user.

The script element has two core attributes. The
<span id="attr-script-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> attribute allows customization of
the type of script represented:

- Omitting the attribute, setting it to the empty string, or setting it
  to a <a
  href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
  id="the-script-element:javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
  data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
  type essence match</a> means that the script is a
  <a href="#classic-script" id="the-script-element:classic-script">classic
  script</a>, to be interpreted according to the JavaScript
  *<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Script"
  data-x-internal="js-prod-script">Script</a>* top-level production.
  Authors should omit the [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute instead
  of redundantly setting it.

- Setting the attribute to an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="the-script-element:ascii-case-insensitive"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for "`module`" means that the script is a
  <a href="#javascript-module-script"
  id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script">JavaScript module
  script</a>, to be interpreted according to the JavaScript
  *<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Module"
  data-x-internal="js-prod-module">Module</a>* top-level production.

- Setting the attribute to an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="the-script-element:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for "`importmap`" means that the script is an
  <a href="#import-map" id="the-script-element:import-map">import map</a>,
  containing JSON that will be used to control the behavior of
  <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
  id="the-script-element:resolve-a-module-specifier">module specifier
  resolution</a>.

- Setting the attribute to an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="the-script-element:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for "`speculationrules`" means that the script defines a
  <a href="#speculation-rule-set"
  id="the-script-element:speculation-rule-set">speculation rule set</a>,
  containing JSON that will be used to describe [speculative
  loads](#speculative-loading).

- Setting the attribute to any other value means that the script is a
  <span id="data-block" class="dfn">data block</span>, which is not
  processed by the user agent, but instead by author script or other
  tools. Authors must use a
  <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type"
  id="the-script-element:valid-mime-type-string"
  data-x-internal="valid-mime-type-string">valid MIME type string</a>
  that is not a <a
  href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
  id="the-script-element:javascript-mime-type-essence-match-2"
  data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
  type essence match</a> to denote data blocks.

  The requirement that
  <a href="#data-block" id="the-script-element:data-block">data blocks</a>
  must be denoted using a
  <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type"
  id="the-script-element:valid-mime-type-string-2"
  data-x-internal="valid-mime-type-string">valid MIME type string</a> is
  in place to avoid potential future collisions. Values for the
  [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute that are not MIME types, like
  "`module`" or "`importmap`", are used by the standard to denote types
  of scripts which have special behavior in user agents. By using a
  valid MIME type string now, you ensure that your data block will not
  ever be reinterpreted as a different script type, even in future user
  agents.

The second core attribute is the <span id="attr-script-src" class="dfn"
dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`src`</span> attribute. It must
only be specified for <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-2">classic scripts</a> and
<a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-2">JavaScript module
scripts</a>, and denotes that instead of using the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="the-script-element:child-text-content"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> as the
script content, the script will be fetched from the specified
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-script-element:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>. If
[`src`](#attr-script-src) is specified, it must be a
<a href="#valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces"
id="the-script-element:valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid
non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces</a>.

Which other attributes may be specified on a given
[`script`](#the-script-element) element is determined by the following
table:

|  | [`nomodule`](#attr-script-nomodule) | [`async`](#attr-script-async) | [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) | [`blocking`](#attr-script-blocking) | [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) | [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-script-referrerpolicy) | [`integrity`](#attr-script-integrity) | [`fetchpriority`](#attr-script-fetchpriority) |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| External classic scripts | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Inline classic scripts | Yes | · | · | · | Yes\* | Yes\* | · | ·† |
| External module scripts | · | Yes | · | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Inline module scripts | · | Yes | · | · | Yes\* | Yes\* | · | ·† |
| Import maps | · | · | · | · | · | · | · | · |
| Speculation rules | · | · | · | · | · | · | · | · |
| Data blocks | · | · | · | · | · | · | · | · |

<span class="small">\* Although inline scripts have no initial fetches,
the [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) and
[`referrerpolicy`](#attr-script-referrerpolicy) attribute on inline
scripts affects the <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="the-script-element:concept-request-credentials-mode"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
and <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-script-element:referrer-policy-2"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> used by module
imports, including dynamic
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
data-x-internal="import()"><code
id="the-script-element:import()">import()</code></a>.</span>

<span class="small">† Unlike [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin)
and [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-script-referrerpolicy),
[`fetchpriority`](#attr-script-fetchpriority) does not affect module
imports. See some discussion in [issue
\#10276](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10276).</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The contents of inline [`script`](#the-script-element) elements, or the
external script resource, must conform with the requirements of the
JavaScript specification's
*<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Script"
data-x-internal="js-prod-script">Script</a>* or
*<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Module"
data-x-internal="js-prod-module">Module</a>* productions, for
<a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-3">classic scripts</a> and
<a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-3">JavaScript module
scripts</a> respectively. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

The contents of inline [`script`](#the-script-element) elements for
<a href="#import-map" id="the-script-element:import-map-2">import
maps</a> must conform with the
<a href="#import-map-authoring-requirements"
id="the-script-element:import-map-authoring-requirements">import map
authoring requirements</a>.

The contents of inline [`script`](#the-script-element) elements for
<a href="#speculation-rule-set"
id="the-script-element:speculation-rule-set-2">speculation rule sets</a>
must conform with the
<a href="#speculation-rule-set-authoring-requirements"
id="the-script-element:speculation-rule-set-authoring-requirements">speculation
rule set authoring requirements</a>.

When used to include
<a href="#data-block" id="the-script-element:data-block-2">data
blocks</a>, the data must be embedded inline, the format of the data
must be given using the [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute, and the
contents of the [`script`](#the-script-element) element must conform to
the requirements defined for the format used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-script-nomodule" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`nomodule`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-script-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a> that
prevents a script from being executed in user agents that support
<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-2">module

<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-3">module
scripts</a> in modern user agents and <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-4">classic scripts</a> in older
user agents, [as shown below](#script-nomodule-example).

The <span id="attr-script-async" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`async`</span> and <span id="attr-script-defer"
class="dfn" dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`defer`</span>
attributes are <a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-script-element:boolean-attribute-2">boolean attributes</a> that
indicate how the script should be evaluated. There are several possible
modes that can be selected using these attributes, depending on the
script's type.

For external <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-5">classic scripts</a>, if the
[`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute is present, then the classic
script will be fetched
<a href="#in-parallel" id="the-script-element:in-parallel">in
parallel</a> to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available
(potentially before parsing completes). If the
[`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute is not present but the
[`defer`](#attr-script-defer) attribute is present, then the classic
script will be fetched
<a href="#in-parallel" id="the-script-element:in-parallel-2">in
parallel</a> and evaluated when the page has finished parsing. If
neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and evaluated
immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete.

For
<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-4">module
scripts</a>, if the [`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute is present,
then the module script and all its dependencies will be fetched
<a href="#in-parallel" id="the-script-element:in-parallel-3">in
parallel</a> to parsing, and the module script will be evaluated as soon
as it is available (potentially before parsing completes). Otherwise,
the module script and its dependencies will be fetched
<a href="#in-parallel" id="the-script-element:in-parallel-4">in
parallel</a> to parsing and evaluated when the page has finished
parsing. (The [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) attribute has no effect on
module scripts.)

This is all summarized in the following schematic diagram:

<img src="/images/asyncdefer.svg" class="darkmode-aware"
style="width: 80%; min-width: 820px;"
alt="With &lt;script&gt;, parsing is interrupted by fetching and execution. With &lt;script defer&gt;, fetching is parallel to parsing and execution takes place after all parsing has finished. And with &lt;script async&gt;, fetching is parallel to parsing but once it finishes parsing is interrupted to execute the script. The story for &lt;script type=&quot;module&quot;&gt; is similar to &lt;script defer&gt;, but the dependencies will be fetched as well, and the story for &lt;script type=&quot;module&quot; async&gt; is similar to &lt;script async&gt; with the extra dependency fetching." />

The exact processing details for these attributes are, for mostly
historical reasons, somewhat non-trivial, involving a number of aspects
of HTML. The implementation requirements are therefore by necessity
scattered throughout the specification. The algorithms
[below](#script-processing-model) describe the core of this processing,
but these algorithms reference and are referenced by the parsing rules
for [`script`](#the-script-element) [start](#scriptTag) and
[end](#scriptEndTag) tags in HTML, [in foreign
content](#scriptForeignEndTag), and [in XML](#scriptTagXML), the rules
for the [`document.write()`](#dom-document-write) method, the handling
of [scripting](#scripting), etc.

When inserted using the [`document.write()`](#dom-document-write)
method, [`script`](#the-script-element) elements
[usually](#document-written-scripts-intervention) execute (typically
blocking further script execution or HTML parsing). When inserted using
the [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) and
[`outerHTML`](#dom-element-outerhtml) attributes, they do not execute at
all.

The [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) attribute may be specified even if the
[`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute is specified, to cause legacy
web browsers that only support [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) (and not
[`async`](#attr-script-async)) to fall back to the
[`defer`](#attr-script-defer) behavior instead of the blocking behavior
that is the default.

The <span id="attr-script-blocking" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`blocking`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#blocking-attribute"
id="the-script-element:blocking-attribute">blocking attribute</a>.

The <span id="attr-script-crossorigin" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`crossorigin`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#cors-settings-attribute"
id="the-script-element:cors-settings-attribute">CORS settings
attribute</a>. For external <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-6">classic scripts</a>, it
controls whether error information will be exposed, when the script is
obtained from other <a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-script-element:concept-origin">origins</a>. For external
<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-5">module
scripts</a>, it controls the <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="the-script-element:concept-request-credentials-mode-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
used for the initial fetch of the module source, if cross-origin. For
both <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-7">classic</a> and
<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-6">module
scripts</a>, it controls the <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode"
id="the-script-element:concept-request-credentials-mode-3"
data-x-internal="concept-request-credentials-mode">credentials mode</a>
used for cross-origin module imports.

Unlike <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-8">classic scripts</a>,
<a href="#module-script" id="the-script-element:module-script-7">module
scripts</a> require the use of the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-cors-protocol"
id="the-script-element:cors-protocol"
data-x-internal="cors-protocol">CORS protocol</a> for cross-origin
fetching.

The <span id="attr-script-referrerpolicy" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`referrerpolicy`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#referrer-policy-attribute"
id="the-script-element:referrer-policy-attribute">referrer policy
attribute</a>. Its sets the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy"
id="the-script-element:referrer-policy-3"
data-x-internal="referrer-policy">referrer policy</a> used for the
initial fetch of an external script, as well as the fetching of any
imported module scripts. [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#refsREFERRERPOLICY)

<div class="example">

An example of a [`script`](#the-script-element) element's referrer
policy being used when fetching imported scripts but not other
subresources:

``` html
<script referrerpolicy="origin">
  fetch('/api/data');    // not fetched with <script>'s referrer policy
  import('./utils.mjs'); // is fetched with <script>'s referrer policy ("origin" in this case)
</script>
```

</div>

The <span id="attr-script-integrity" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`integrity`</span> attribute sets the <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata"
id="the-script-element:concept-request-integrity-metadata"
data-x-internal="concept-request-integrity-metadata">integrity
metadata</a> used for the initial fetch of an external script. The value
must match <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#the-integrity-attribute"
id="the-script-element:the-requirements-of-the-integrity-attribute"
data-x-internal="the-requirements-of-the-integrity-attribute">the
requirements of the integrity attribute</a>. [\[SRI\]](#refsSRI)

The <span id="attr-script-fetchpriority" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
dfn-type="element-attr">`fetchpriority`</span> attribute is a
<a href="#fetch-priority-attribute"
id="the-script-element:fetch-priority-attribute">fetch priority
attribute</a>. Its sets the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority"
id="the-script-element:concept-request-priority-2"
data-x-internal="concept-request-priority">priority</a> used for the
initial fetch of an external script.

Changing any of these attributes dynamically has no direct effect; these
attributes are only used at specific times described in the [processing
model](#script-processing-model).

The <span id="dom-script-async" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLScriptElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`async`</span> getter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-script-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#script-force-async"
    id="the-script-element:script-force-async">force async</a> is true,
    then return true.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-script-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`async`](#attr-script-async) content attribute is present, then
    return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`async`](#dom-script-async) setter steps are:

1.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-script-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#script-force-async"
    id="the-script-element:script-force-async-2">force async</a> to
    false.

2.  If the given value is true, then set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-script-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`async`](#attr-script-async) content attribute to the empty string.

3.  Otherwise, remove <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-script-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`async`](#attr-script-async) content attribute.

</div>

`script``.`<a href="#dom-script-text"
id="dom-script-text-dev"><code>text</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"

element.

`script``.`<a href="#dom-script-text"

Replaces the element's children with the text given by `value`.

[`HTMLScriptElement`](#htmlscriptelement)`.`<a href="#dom-script-supports"
id="dom-script-supports-dev"><code>supports</code></a>`(``type``)`  
Returns true if the given `type` is a script type supported by the user
agent. The possible script types in this specification are "`classic`",
"`module`", and "`importmap`", but others might be added in the future.

The static <span id="dom-script-supports" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLScriptElement"
dfn-type="method">`supports(``type``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If `type` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="the-script-element:is" data-x-internal="is">is</a> "`classic`",
    then return true.

2.  If `type` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="the-script-element:is-2" data-x-internal="is">is</a> "`module`",
    then return true.

3.  If `type` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="the-script-element:is-3" data-x-internal="is">is</a>
    "`importmap`", then return true.

4.  If `type` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="the-script-element:is-4" data-x-internal="is">is</a>
    "`speculationrules`", then return true.

5.  Return false.

</div>

The `type` argument has to exactly match these values; we do not perform
an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-script-element:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match. This is different from how [`type`](#attr-script-type) content
attribute values are treated, and how
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-domtokenlist"
data-x-internal="domtokenlist"><code
id="the-script-element:domtokenlist-2">DOMTokenList</code></a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domtokenlist-supports"
data-x-internal="dom-domtokenlist-supports"><code
id="the-script-element:dom-domtokenlist-supports">supports()</code></a>
method works, but it aligns with the [`WorkerType`](#workertype)
enumeration used in the [`Worker()`](#dom-worker) constructor.
