<div class="example">

In this example, two [`script`](#the-script-element) elements are used.
One embeds an external <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-9">classic script</a>, and the
other includes some data as a
<a href="#data-block" id="the-script-element:data-block-3">data
block</a>.

``` html
<script src="game-engine.js"></script>
<script type="text/x-game-map">
........U.........e
o............A....e
.....A.....AAA....e
.A..AAA...AAAAA...e
</script>
```

The data in this case might be used by the script to generate the map of
a video game. The data doesn't have to be used that way, though; maybe
the map data is actually embedded in other parts of the page's markup,
and the data block here is just used by the site's search engine to help
users who are looking for particular features in their game maps.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following sample shows how a [`script`](#the-script-element) element
can be used to define a function that is then used by other parts of the
document, as part of a <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-10">classic script</a>. It also
shows how a [`script`](#the-script-element) element can be used to
invoke script while the document is being parsed, in this case to
initialize the form's output.

``` html
<script>
 function calculate(form) {
   var price = 52000;
   if (form.elements.brakes.checked)
     price += 1000;
   if (form.elements.radio.checked)
     price += 2500;
   if (form.elements.turbo.checked)
     price += 5000;
   if (form.elements.sticker.checked)
     price += 250;
   form.elements.result.value = price;
 }
</script>
<form name="pricecalc" onsubmit="return false" onchange="calculate(this)">
 <fieldset>
  <legend>Work out the price of your car</legend>
  <p>Base cost: £52000.</p>
  <p>Select additional options:</p>
  <ul>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=brakes> Ceramic brakes (£1000)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=radio> Satellite radio (£2500)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=turbo> Turbo charger (£5000)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=sticker> "XZ" sticker (£250)</label></li>
  </ul>
  <p>Total: £<output name=result></output></p>
 </fieldset>
 <script>
  calculate(document.forms.pricecalc);
 </script>
</form>
```

</div>

<div id="script-type-module-example-1" class="example">

<a href="#script-type-module-example-1" class="self-link"></a>

The following sample shows how a [`script`](#the-script-element) element
can be used to include an external <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-4">JavaScript module
script</a>.

``` html
<script type="module" src="app.mjs"></script>
```

This module, and all its dependencies (expressed through JavaScript
`import` statements in the source file), will be fetched. Once the
entire resulting module graph has been imported, and the document has
finished parsing, the contents of `app.mjs` will be evaluated.

Additionally, if code from another [`script`](#the-script-element)
element in the same [`Window`](#window) imports the module from
`app.mjs` (e.g. via `import "./app.mjs";`), then the same
<a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-5">JavaScript module
script</a> created by the former [`script`](#the-script-element) element
will be imported.

</div>

<div id="script-nomodule-example" class="example">

<a href="#script-nomodule-example" class="self-link"></a>

This example shows how to include a <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-6">JavaScript module
script</a> for modern user agents, and a <a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-11">classic script</a> for older
user agents:

``` html
<script type="module" src="app.mjs"></script>
<script nomodule defer src="classic-app-bundle.js"></script>
```

In modern user agents that support <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-7">JavaScript module
scripts</a>, the [`script`](#the-script-element) element with the
[`nomodule`](#attr-script-nomodule) attribute will be ignored, and the
[`script`](#the-script-element) element with a
[`type`](#attr-script-type) of "`module`" will be fetched and evaluated
(as a <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-8">JavaScript module
script</a>). Conversely, older user agents will ignore the
[`script`](#the-script-element) element with a
[`type`](#attr-script-type) of "`module`", as that is an unknown script
type for them — but they will have no problem fetching and evaluating
the other [`script`](#the-script-element) element (as a
<a href="#classic-script"
id="the-script-element:classic-script-12">classic script</a>), since
they do not implement the [`nomodule`](#attr-script-nomodule) attribute.

</div>

<div id="script-type-module-example-2" class="example">

<a href="#script-type-module-example-2" class="self-link"></a>

The following sample shows how a [`script`](#the-script-element) element
can be used to write an inline <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-9">JavaScript module
script</a> that performs a number of substitutions on the document's
text, in order to make for a more interesting reading experience (e.g.
on a news site): [\[XKCD1288\]](#refsXKCD1288)

``` html
<script type="module">
 import { walkAllTextNodeDescendants } from "./dom-utils.mjs";

 const substitutions = new Map([
   ["witnesses", "these dudes I know"]
   ["allegedly", "kinda probably"]
   ["new study", "Tumblr post"]
   ["rebuild", "avenge"]
   ["space", "spaaace"]
   ["Google glass", "Virtual Boy"]
   ["smartphone", "Pokédex"]
   ["electric", "atomic"]
   ["Senator", "Elf-Lord"]
   ["car", "cat"]
   ["election", "eating contest"]
   ["Congressional leaders", "river spirits"]
   ["homeland security", "Homestar Runner"]
   ["could not be reached for comment", "is guilty and everyone knows it"]
 ]);

 function substitute(textNode) {
   for (const [before, after] of substitutions.entries()) {
     textNode.data = textNode.data.replace(new RegExp(`\\b${before}\\b`, "ig"), after);
   }
 }

 walkAllTextNodeDescendants(document.body, substitute);
</script>
```

Some notable features gained by using a JavaScript module script include
the ability to import functions from other JavaScript modules, strict
mode by default, and how top-level declarations do not introduce new
properties onto the
<a href="#global-object" id="the-script-element:global-object">global
object</a>. Also note that no matter where this
[`script`](#the-script-element) element appears in the document, it will
not be evaluated until both document parsing has complete and its
dependency (`dom-utils.mjs`) has been fetched and evaluated.

</div>

<div id="json-module-script-example" class="example">

<a href="#json-module-script-example" class="self-link"></a>

The following sample shows how a <a href="#json-module-script"
id="the-script-element:json-module-script">JSON module script</a> can be
imported from inside a <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-10">JavaScript module
script</a>:

``` html
<script type="module">
 import peopleInSpace from "http://api.open-notify.org/astros.json" with { type: "json" };

 const list = document.querySelector("#people-in-space");
 for (const { craft, name } of peopleInSpace.people) {
   const li = document.createElement("li");
   li.textContent = `${name} / ${craft}`;
   list.append(li);
 }
</script>
```

MIME type checking for module scripts is strict. In order for the fetch
of the <a href="#json-module-script"
id="the-script-element:json-module-script-2">JSON module script</a> to
succeed, the HTTP response must have a
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type"
id="the-script-element:json-mime-type"
data-x-internal="json-mime-type">JSON MIME type</a>, for example
`Content-Type: text/json`. On the other hand, if the
`with { type: "json" }` part of the statement is omitted, it is assumed
that the intent is to import a <a href="#javascript-module-script"
id="the-script-element:javascript-module-script-11">JavaScript module
script</a>, and the fetch will fail if the HTTP response has a MIME type
that is not a
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type"
id="the-script-element:javascript-mime-type"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type">JavaScript MIME type</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.1.1</span> Processing model<a href="#script-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has several associated pieces
of state.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="parser-document" class="dfn">parser document</span>, which is
either null or a [`Document`](#document), initially null. It is set by
the <a href="#html-parser" id="script-processing-model:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> and the
<a href="#xml-parser" id="script-processing-model:xml-parser">XML
parser</a> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements they insert, and
affects the processing of those elements.
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements with non-null
<a href="#parser-document"
id="script-processing-model:parser-document">parser documents</a> are
known as <span id="parser-inserted" class="dfn" dfn-for="script"
export="">parser-inserted</span>.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="preparation-time-document" class="dfn">preparation-time
document</span>, which is either null or a [`Document`](#document),
initially null. It is used to prevent scripts that move between
documents during <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element">preparation</a>
from <a href="#execute-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:execute-the-script-element">executing</a>.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="script-force-async" class="dfn">force async</span> boolean,
initially true. It is set to false by the
<a href="#html-parser" id="script-processing-model:html-parser-2">HTML
parser</a> and the
<a href="#xml-parser" id="script-processing-model:xml-parser-2">XML
parser</a> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements they insert, and
when the element gets an [`async`](#attr-script-async) content attribute
added.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="concept-script-external" class="dfn">from an external
file</span> boolean, initially false. It is determined when the script
is <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-2">prepared</a>,
based on the [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute of the element at that
time.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="ready-to-be-parser-executed" class="dfn">ready to be
parser-executed</span> boolean, initially false. This is used only used
for elements that are also <a href="#parser-inserted"
id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted">parser-inserted</a>, to let
the parser know when to execute the script.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has an
<span id="already-started" class="dfn">already started</span> boolean,
initially false.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="concept-script-delay-load" class="dfn">delaying the load
event</span> boolean, initially false.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="concept-script-type" class="dfn">type</span>, which is either
null, "`classic`", "`module`", "`importmap`", or "`speculationrules`",
initially null. It is determined when the element is
<a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-3">prepared</a>,
based on the [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute of the element at
that time.

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has a
<span id="concept-script-result" class="dfn">result</span>, which is
either "`uninitialized`", null (representing an error), a
<a href="#concept-script"
id="script-processing-model:concept-script">script</a>, an
<a href="#import-map-parse-result"
id="script-processing-model:import-map-parse-result">import map parse
result</a>, or a <a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
id="script-processing-model:speculation-rules-parse-result">speculation
rules parse result</a>. It is initially "`uninitialized`".

<div algorithm="">

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element has
<span id="steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready" class="dfn">steps to
run when the result is ready</span>, which are a series of steps or
null, initially null. To <span id="mark-as-ready" class="dfn">mark as
ready</span> a [`script`](#the-script-element) element `el` given a
`result`:

1.  Set `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result">result</a> to
    `result`.

2.  If `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
    id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready">steps
    to run when the result is ready</a> are not null, then run them.

3.  Set `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
    id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready-2">steps
    to run when the result is ready</a> to null.

4.  Set `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-delay-load"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-delay-load">delaying the load
    event</a> to false.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`script`](#the-script-element) element `el` is
<a href="#implicitly-potentially-render-blocking"
id="script-processing-model:implicitly-potentially-render-blocking">implicitly
potentially render-blocking</a> if `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type">type</a> is
"`classic`", `el` is <a href="#parser-inserted"
id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted-2">parser-inserted</a>, and
`el` does not have an [`async`](#attr-script-async) or
[`defer`](#attr-script-defer) attribute.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone-ext"
id="script-processing-model:concept-node-clone-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-ext">cloning steps</a> for
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements given `node`, `copy`, and
`subtree` are to set `copy`'s <a href="#already-started"
id="script-processing-model:already-started">already started</a> to
`node`'s <a href="#already-started"
id="script-processing-model:already-started-2">already started</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When an [`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute is added to a
[`script`](#the-script-element) element `el`, the user agent must set
`el`'s <a href="#script-force-async"
id="script-processing-model:script-force-async">force async</a> to
false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever a [`script`](#the-script-element) element `el`'s
<a href="#concept-script-delay-load"
id="script-processing-model:concept-script-delay-load-2">delaying the
load event</a> is true, the user agent must
<a href="#delay-the-load-event"
id="script-processing-model:delay-the-load-event">delay the load
event</a> of `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document">preparation-time
document</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The [`script`](#the-script-element)
<a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps">HTML
element post-connection steps</a>, given `insertedNode`, are:

1.  If `insertedNode` is <a href="#parser-inserted"
    id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted-3">parser-inserted</a>,
    then return.

2.  <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
    id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-4">Prepare the
    script element</a> given `insertedNode`.

</div>

<div class="example">

The <a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-2">HTML
element post-connection steps</a> only run when the inserted element is
still <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
id="script-processing-model:connected"
data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, which protects against cases
where an earlier-inserted [`script`](#the-script-element) removes a
later-inserted [`script`](#the-script-element). For instance:

``` html
<script>
const script1 = document.createElement('script');
script1.innerText = `
  document.querySelector('#script2').remove();
`;

const script2 = document.createElement('script');
script2.id = 'script2';
script2.textContent = `console.log('script#2 running')`;

document.body.append(script1, script2);
</script>
```

Nothing is printed to the console in this example. By the time the
<a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-3">HTML
element post-connection steps</a> run for the first
[`script`](#the-script-element) that was atomically inserted by
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-append"
data-x-internal="dom-node-append"><code
id="script-processing-model:dom-node-append">append()</code></a>, it can
observe that the second [`script`](#the-script-element) is already
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
id="script-processing-model:connected-2"
data-x-internal="connected">connected</a> to the DOM, and it removes it
from the DOM. Because the second [`script`](#the-script-element) is no
longer <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
id="script-processing-model:connected-3"
data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, its
<a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-4">HTML
element post-connection steps</a> do not run, and it does not get
<a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-5">prepared</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`script`](#the-script-element)
<a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="script-processing-model:html-element-removing-steps">HTML element
removing steps</a> given `removedNode` are:

1.  If `removedNode`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-2">result</a> is a
    <a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
    id="script-processing-model:speculation-rules-parse-result-2">speculation
    rules parse result</a>, then:

    1.  <a href="#unregister-speculation-rules"
        id="script-processing-model:unregister-speculation-rules">Unregister
        speculation rules</a> given `removedNode`'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
        object</a> and `removedNode`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-3">result</a>.

    2.  Set `removedNode`'s <a href="#already-started"
        id="script-processing-model:already-started-3">already started</a>
        to false.

    3.  Set `removedNode`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-4">result</a>
        to null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`script`](#the-script-element)
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-children-changed-ext"
id="script-processing-model:children-changed-steps"
data-x-internal="children-changed-steps">children changed steps</a>
given `changedNode` are:

1.  If the [`script`](#the-script-element) element is not
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="script-processing-model:connected-4"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then return.

2.  Run the [`script`](#the-script-element)
    <a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
    id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-5">HTML
    element post-connection steps</a>, given `changedNode`.

</div>

<div class="example">

This has an interesting implication on the execution order of a
[`script`](#the-script-element) element and any newly-inserted child
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements. Consider the following
snippet:

``` html
<script id=outer-script></script>

<script>
  const outerScript = document.querySelector('#outer-script');

  const start = new Text('console.log(1);');
  const innerScript = document.createElement('script');
  innerScript.textContent = `console.log('inner script executing')`;
  const end = new Text('console.log(2);');

  outerScript.append(start, innerScript, end);

  // Logs:
  // 1
  // 2
  // inner script executing
</script>
```

By the time the second script block executes, the `outer-script` has
already been <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-6">prepared</a>,
but because it is empty, it did not execute and therefore is not marked
as <a href="#already-started"
id="script-processing-model:already-started-4">already started</a>. The
atomic insertion of the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="script-processing-model:text">Text</code></a> nodes and nested
[`script`](#the-script-element) element have the following effects:

1.  All three child nodes get atomically inserted as children of
    `outer-script`; all of their
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-node-insert-ext"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert-ext">insertion steps</a> run,
    which have no observable consequences in this case.

2.  The `outer-script`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-children-changed-ext"
    id="script-processing-model:children-changed-steps-2"
    data-x-internal="children-changed-steps">children changed steps</a>
    run, which <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
    id="script-processing-model:prepare-the-script-element-7">prepares</a>
    that script; because its body is now non-empty, this executes the
    contents of the two
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="script-processing-model:text-2">Text</code></a> nodes, in order.

3.  The [`script`](#the-script-element)
    <a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
    id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-6">HTML
    element post-connection steps</a> finally run for `innerScript`,
    causing its body to execute.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The following <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
id="script-processing-model:concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change-ext">attribute change
steps</a>, given `element`, `localName`, `oldValue`, `value`, and
`namespace`, are used for all [`script`](#the-script-element) elements:

1.  If `namespace` is not null, then return.

2.  If `localName` is [`src`](#attr-script-src), `value` is not null,
    and `element` is <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="script-processing-model:connected-5"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then run the
    [`script`](#the-script-element)
    <a href="#html-element-post-connection-steps"
    id="script-processing-model:html-element-post-connection-steps-7">HTML
    element post-connection steps</a>, given `element`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="prepare-the-script-element" class="dfn">prepare the script
element</span> given a [`script`](#the-script-element) element `el`:

1.  If `el`'s <a href="#already-started"
    id="script-processing-model:already-started-5">already started</a>
    is true, then return.

2.  Let `parser document` be `el`'s <a href="#parser-document"
    id="script-processing-model:parser-document-2">parser document</a>.

3.  Set `el`'s <a href="#parser-document"
    id="script-processing-model:parser-document-3">parser document</a>
    to null.

    This is done so that if parser-inserted
    [`script`](#the-script-element) elements fail to run when the parser
    tries to run them, e.g. because they are empty or specify an
    unsupported scripting language, another script can later mutate them
    and cause them to run again.

4.  If `parser document` is non-null and `el` does not have an
    [`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute, then set `el`'s
    <a href="#script-force-async"
    id="script-processing-model:script-force-async-2">force async</a> to
    true.

    This is done so that if a parser-inserted
    [`script`](#the-script-element) element fails to run when the parser
    tries to run it, but it is later executed after a script dynamically
    updates it, it will execute in an async fashion even if the
    [`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute isn't set.

5.  Let `source text` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
    id="script-processing-model:child-text-content"
    data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a>.

6.  <div id="script-processing-empty">

    If `el` has no [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute, and
    `source text` is the empty string, then return.

    </div>

7.  If `el` is not <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="script-processing-model:connected-6"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then return.

8.  <div id="script-processing-prepare">

    If any of the following are true:

    - `el` has a [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute whose value is
      the empty string;

    - `el` has no [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute but it has a
      [`language`](#attr-script-language) attribute and *that*
      attribute's value is the empty string; or

    - `el` has neither a [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute nor a
      [`language`](#attr-script-language) attribute,

    then let `the script block's type string` for this
    [`script`](#the-script-element) element be "`text/javascript`".

    Otherwise, if `el` has a [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute, then
    let `the script block's type string` be the value of that attribute
    with <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace"
    id="script-processing-model:strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace"
    data-x-internal="strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace">leading
    and trailing ASCII whitespace stripped</a>.

    Otherwise, `el` has a non-empty [`language`](#attr-script-language)
    attribute; let `the script block's type string` be the concatenation
    of "`text/`" and the value of `el`'s
    [`language`](#attr-script-language) attribute.

    The [`language`](#attr-script-language) attribute is never
    conforming, and is always ignored if there is a
    [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute present.

    </div>

9.  If `the script block's type string` is a <a
    href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
    id="script-processing-model:javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
    data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
    type essence match</a>, then set `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-2">type</a> to
    "`classic`".

10. Otherwise, if `the script block's type string` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="script-processing-model:ascii-case-insensitive"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for the string "`module`", then set `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-3">type</a> to
    "`module`".

11. Otherwise, if `the script block's type string` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="script-processing-model:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for the string "`importmap`", then set `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-4">type</a> to
    "`importmap`".

12. Otherwise, if `the script block's type string` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="script-processing-model:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for the string "`speculationrules`", then set `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-5">type</a> to
    "`speculationrules`".

13. Otherwise, return. (No script is executed, and `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-6">type</a> is left
    as null.)

14. If `parser document` is non-null, then set `el`'s
    <a href="#parser-document"
    id="script-processing-model:parser-document-4">parser document</a>
    back to `parser document` and set `el`'s
    <a href="#script-force-async"
    id="script-processing-model:script-force-async-3">force async</a> to
    false.

15. <div id="script-processing-start">

    Set `el`'s <a href="#already-started"
    id="script-processing-model:already-started-6">already started</a>
    to true.

    </div>

16. Set `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
    id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document-2">preparation-time
    document</a> to its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="script-processing-model:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

17. If `parser document` is non-null, and `parser document` is not equal
    to `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
    id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document-3">preparation-time
    document</a>, then return.

18. <div id="script-processing-noscript">

    If <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-n-noscript">scripting is
    disabled</a> for `el`, then return.

    The definition of <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-n-noscript-2">scripting is
    disabled</a> means that, amongst others, the following scripts will
    not execute: scripts in
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest"
    data-x-internal="xmlhttprequest"><code
    id="script-processing-model:xmlhttprequest">XMLHttpRequest</code></a>'s
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-xmlhttprequest-responsexml"
    data-x-internal="dom-xmlhttprequest-responsexml"><code
    id="script-processing-model:dom-xmlhttprequest-responsexml">responseXML</code></a>
    documents, scripts in [`DOMParser`](#domparser)-created documents,
    scripts in documents created by [`XSLTProcessor`](#xsltprocessor)'s
    [`transformToDocument`](#dom-xsltprocessor-transformtodocument)
    feature, and scripts that are first inserted by a script into a
    [`Document`](#document) that was created using the <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domimplementation-createdocument"
    data-x-internal="dom-domimplementation-createdocument"><code
    id="script-processing-model:dom-domimplementation-createdocument">createDocument()</code></a>
    API. [\[XHR\]](#refsXHR) [\[DOMPARSING\]](#refsDOMPARSING)
    [\[XSLTP\]](#refsXSLTP) [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

    </div>

19. If `el` has a [`nomodule`](#attr-script-nomodule) content attribute
    and its <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-7">type</a> is
    "`classic`", then return.

    This means specifying [`nomodule`](#attr-script-nomodule) on a
    <a href="#module-script"
    id="script-processing-model:module-script">module script</a> has no
    effect; the algorithm continues onward.

20. Let `cspType` be "`script speculationrules`" if `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-8">type</a> is
    "`speculationrules`"; otherwise, "`script`".

21. <div id="script-processing-csp">

    If `el` does not have a [`src`](#attr-script-src) content attribute,
    and the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline"
    id="script-processing-model:should-element&#39;s-inline-behavior-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy"
    data-x-internal="should-element&#39;s-inline-behavior-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy">Should
    element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?</a>
    algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when given `el`, `cspType`, and
    `source text`, then return. [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

    </div>

22. <div id="script-processing-for">

    If `el` has an [`event`](#attr-script-event) attribute and a
    [`for`](#attr-script-for) attribute, and `el`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-9">type</a> is
    "`classic`", then:

    1.  Let `for` be the value of `el`'s [`for`](#attr-script-for)
        attribute.

    2.  Let `event` be the value of `el`'s [`event`](#attr-script-event)
        attribute.

    3.  <a
        href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace"
        id="script-processing-model:strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace-2"
        data-x-internal="strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace">Strip
        leading and trailing ASCII whitespace</a> from `event` and
        `for`.

    4.  If `for` is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
        id="script-processing-model:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
        data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
        match for the string "`window`", then return.

    5.  If `event` is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
        id="script-processing-model:ascii-case-insensitive-5"
        data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
        match for either the string "`onload`" or the string
        "`onload()`", then return.

    </div>

23. <div id="script-processing-encoding">

    If `el` has a [`charset`](#attr-script-charset) attribute, then let
    `encoding` be the result of
    <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get"
    id="script-processing-model:getting-an-encoding"
    data-x-internal="getting-an-encoding">getting an encoding</a> from
    the value of the [`charset`](#attr-script-charset) attribute.

    If `el` does not have a [`charset`](#attr-script-charset) attribute,
    or if
    <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get"
    id="script-processing-model:getting-an-encoding-2"
    data-x-internal="getting-an-encoding">getting an encoding</a>
    failed, then let `encoding` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="script-processing-model:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
    id="script-processing-model:document&#39;s-character-encoding"
    data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">the encoding</a>.

    If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-10">type</a> is
    "`module`", this encoding will be ignored.

    </div>

24. Let `classic script CORS setting` be the current state of `el`'s
    [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) content attribute.

25. Let `module script credentials mode` be the
    <a href="#cors-settings-attribute-credentials-mode"
    id="script-processing-model:cors-settings-attribute-credentials-mode">CORS
    settings attribute credentials mode</a> for `el`'s
    [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) content attribute.

26. Let `cryptographic nonce` be `el`'s <a href="#cryptographicnonce"
    id="script-processing-model:cryptographicnonce">[[CryptographicNonce]]</a>
    internal slot's value.

27. If `el` has an [`integrity`](#attr-script-integrity) attribute, then
    let `integrity metadata` be that attribute's value.

    Otherwise, let `integrity metadata` be the empty string.

28. Let `referrer policy` be the current state of `el`'s
    [`referrerpolicy`](#attr-script-referrerpolicy) content attribute.

29. Let `fetch priority` be the current state of `el`'s
    [`fetchpriority`](#attr-script-fetchpriority) content attribute.

30. Let `parser metadata` be "`parser-inserted`" if `el` is
    <a href="#parser-inserted"
    id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted-4">parser-inserted</a>,
    and "`not-parser-inserted`" otherwise.

31. Let `options` be a <a href="#script-fetch-options"
    id="script-processing-model:script-fetch-options">script fetch
    options</a> whose <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-nonce"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-nonce">cryptographic
    nonce</a> is `cryptographic nonce`,
    <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-integrity"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-integrity">integrity
    metadata</a> is `integrity metadata`,
    <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-parser"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-parser">parser
    metadata</a> is `parser metadata`,
    <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-credentials"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-credentials">credentials
    mode</a> is `module script credentials mode`,
    <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy">referrer
    policy</a> is `referrer policy`, and
    <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-fetch-priority"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-fetch-priority">fetch
    priority</a> is `fetch priority`.

32. Let `settings object` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="script-processing-model:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="script-processing-model:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>.

33. <div id="script-processing-src-prepare">

    If `el` has a [`src`](#attr-script-src) content attribute, then:

    1.  If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-11">type</a> is
        "`importmap`" or "`speculationrules`", then
        <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
        id="script-processing-model:queue-an-element-task">queue an element
        task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="script-processing-model:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `el` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`error`](#event-error) at `el`, and return.

        External import maps and speculation rules are not currently
        supported. See [WICG/import-maps issue
        \#235](https://github.com/WICG/import-maps/issues/235) and
        [WICG/nav-speculation issue
        \#348](https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/issues/348) for
        discussions on adding support.

    2.  Let `src` be the value of `el`'s [`src`](#attr-script-src)
        attribute.

    3.  If `src` is the empty string, then
        <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
        id="script-processing-model:queue-an-element-task-2">queue an element
        task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="script-processing-model:dom-manipulation-task-source-2">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `el` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`error`](#event-error) at `el`, and return.

    4.  Set `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-external"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-external">from an external
        file</a> to true.

    5.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
        id="script-processing-model:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a
        URL</a> given `src`, relative to `el`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="script-processing-model:node-document-4"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

    6.  If `url` is failure, then <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
        id="script-processing-model:queue-an-element-task-3">queue an element
        task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="script-processing-model:dom-manipulation-task-source-3">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `el` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-event-fire-3"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`error`](#event-error) at `el`, and return.

    7.  If `el` is <a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
        id="script-processing-model:potentially-render-blocking">potentially
        render-blocking</a>, then <a href="#block-rendering"
        id="script-processing-model:block-rendering">block rendering</a>
        on `el`.

    8.  Set `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-delay-load"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-delay-load-3">delaying the
        load event</a> to true.

    9.  If `el` is currently <a href="#render-blocking"
        id="script-processing-model:render-blocking">render-blocking</a>,
        then set `options`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-render-blocking"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-render-blocking">render-blocking</a>
        to true.

    10. Let `onComplete` given `result` be the following steps:

        1.  <a href="#mark-as-ready" id="script-processing-model:mark-as-ready">Mark
            as ready</a> `el` given `result`.

    11. Switch on `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-12">type</a>:

        "`classic`"  
        <a href="#fetch-a-classic-script"
        id="script-processing-model:fetch-a-classic-script">Fetch a classic
        script</a> given `url`, `settings object`, `options`,
        `classic script CORS setting`, `encoding`, and `onComplete`.

        "`module`"  
        If `el` does not have an [`integrity`](#attr-script-integrity)
        attribute, then set `options`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-integrity"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-integrity-2">integrity
        metadata</a> to the result of
        <a href="#resolving-a-module-integrity-metadata"
        id="script-processing-model:resolving-a-module-integrity-metadata">resolving
        a module integrity metadata</a> with `url` and
        `settings object`.

        <a href="#fetch-a-module-script-tree"
        id="script-processing-model:fetch-a-module-script-tree">Fetch an
        external module script graph</a> given `url`, `settings object`,
        `options`, and `onComplete`.

        For performance reasons, user agents may start fetching the
        classic script or module graph (as defined above) as soon as the
        [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute is set, instead, in the hope
        that `el` will become connected (and that the
        [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) attribute won't change
        value in the meantime). Either way, once `el`
        <a href="#becomes-connected"
        id="script-processing-model:becomes-connected">becomes connected</a>,
        the load must have started as described in this step. If the UA
        performs such prefetching, but `el` never becomes connected, or
        the [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute is dynamically changed,
        or the [`crossorigin`](#attr-script-crossorigin) attribute is
        dynamically changed, then the user agent will not execute the
        script so obtained, and the fetching process will have been
        effectively wasted.

    </div>

34. <div id="establish-script-block-source">

    If `el` does not have a [`src`](#attr-script-src) content attribute:

    1.  Let `base URL` be `el`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="script-processing-model:node-document-5"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
        <a href="#document-base-url"
        id="script-processing-model:document-base-url">document base URL</a>.

    2.  Switch on `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-13">type</a>:

        "`classic`"  
        1.  Let `script` be the result of
            <a href="#creating-a-classic-script"
            id="script-processing-model:creating-a-classic-script">creating a
            classic script</a> using `source text`, `settings object`,
            `base URL`, and `options`.

        2.  <a href="#mark-as-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:mark-as-ready-2">Mark as ready</a>
            `el` given `script`.

        "`module`"  
        1.  Set `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-delay-load"
            id="script-processing-model:concept-script-delay-load-4">delaying the
            load event</a> to true.

        2.  If `el` is <a href="#potentially-render-blocking"
            id="script-processing-model:potentially-render-blocking-2">potentially
            render-blocking</a>, then:

            1.  <a href="#block-rendering"
                id="script-processing-model:block-rendering-2">Block rendering</a>
                on `el`.

            2.  Set `options`'s
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-render-blocking"
                id="script-processing-model:concept-script-fetch-options-render-blocking-2">render-blocking</a>
                to true.

        3.  <a href="#fetch-an-inline-module-script-graph"
            id="script-processing-model:fetch-an-inline-module-script-graph">Fetch
            an inline module script graph</a>, given `source text`,
            `base URL`, `settings object`, `options`, and with the
            following steps given `result`:

            1.  <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
                id="script-processing-model:queue-an-element-task-4">Queue an element
                task</a> on the <a href="#networking-task-source"
                id="script-processing-model:networking-task-source">networking task
                source</a> given `el` to perform the following steps:

                1.  <a href="#mark-as-ready"
                    id="script-processing-model:mark-as-ready-3">Mark as ready</a>
                    `el` given `result`.

                Queueing a task here means that, even if the inline
                module script has no dependencies or synchronously
                results in a parse error, we won't proceed to
                <a href="#execute-the-script-element"
                id="script-processing-model:execute-the-script-element-2">execute the
                script element</a> synchronously.

        "`importmap`"  
        1.  Let `result` be the result of
            <a href="#create-an-import-map-parse-result"
            id="script-processing-model:create-an-import-map-parse-result">creating
            an import map parse result</a> given `source text` and
            `base URL`.

        2.  <a href="#mark-as-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:mark-as-ready-4">Mark as ready</a>
            `el` given `result`.

        "`speculationrules`"  
        1.  Let `result` be the result of
            <a href="#create-a-speculation-rules-parse-result"
            id="script-processing-model:create-a-speculation-rules-parse-result">creating
            a speculation rules parse result</a> given `source text` and
            `el`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
            id="script-processing-model:node-document-6"
            data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

        2.  <a href="#mark-as-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:mark-as-ready-5">Mark as ready</a>
            `el` given `result`.

    </div>

35. If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-14">type</a> is
    "`classic`" and `el` has a [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute, or
    `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-15">type</a> is
    "`module`":

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="script-processing-model:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-5">result</a>
        is "`uninitialized`".

    2.  <div id="script-processing-src">

        If `el` has an [`async`](#attr-script-async) attribute or `el`'s
        <a href="#script-force-async"
        id="script-processing-model:script-force-async-4">force async</a>
        is true:

        1.  Let `scripts` be `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
            id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document-4">preparation-time
            document</a>'s
            <a href="#set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible"
            id="script-processing-model:set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible">set
            of scripts that will execute as soon as possible</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
            id="script-processing-model:set-append"
            data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a> `el` to `scripts`.

        3.  Set `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready-3">steps
            to run when the result is ready</a> to the following:

            1.  <a href="#execute-the-script-element"
                id="script-processing-model:execute-the-script-element-3">Execute the
                script element</a> `el`.

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
                id="script-processing-model:list-remove"
                data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `el` from
                `scripts`.

        </div>

    3.  <div id="script-processing-src-sync">

        Otherwise, if `el` is not <a href="#parser-inserted"
        id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted-5">parser-inserted</a>:

        1.  Let `scripts` be `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
            id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document-5">preparation-time
            document</a>'s <a
            href="#list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible"
            id="script-processing-model:list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible">list
            of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
            id="script-processing-model:list-append"
            data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `el` to `scripts`.

        3.  Set `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready-4">steps
            to run when the result is ready</a> to the following:

            1.  If `scripts`\[0\] is not `el`, then abort these steps.

            2.  While `scripts` is not empty, and `scripts`\[0\]'s
                <a href="#concept-script-result"
                id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-6">result</a>
                is not "`uninitialized`":

                1.  <a href="#execute-the-script-element"
                    id="script-processing-model:execute-the-script-element-4">Execute the
                    script element</a> `scripts`\[0\].

                2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
                    id="script-processing-model:list-remove-2"
                    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a>
                    `scripts`\[0\].

        </div>

    4.  <div id="script-processing-defer">

        Otherwise, if `el` has a [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) attribute
        or `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-16">type</a> is
        "`module`":

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
            id="script-processing-model:list-append-2"
            data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `el` to its
            <a href="#parser-document"
            id="script-processing-model:parser-document-5">parser document</a>'s
            <a
            href="#list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing"
            id="script-processing-model:list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing">list
            of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing</a>.

        2.  Set `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready-5">steps
            to run when the result is ready</a> to the following: set
            `el`'s <a href="#ready-to-be-parser-executed"
            id="script-processing-model:ready-to-be-parser-executed">ready to be
            parser-executed</a> to true. (The parser will handle
            executing the script.)

        </div>

    5.  <div id="script-processing-parser-inserted">

        Otherwise:

        1.  Set `el`'s <a href="#parser-document"
            id="script-processing-model:parser-document-6">parser document</a>'s
            <a href="#pending-parsing-blocking-script"
            id="script-processing-model:pending-parsing-blocking-script">pending
            parsing-blocking script</a> to `el`.

        2.  <a href="#block-rendering"
            id="script-processing-model:block-rendering-3">Block rendering</a>
            on `el`.

        3.  Set `el`'s <a href="#steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready"
            id="script-processing-model:steps-to-run-when-the-result-is-ready-6">steps
            to run when the result is ready</a> to the following: set
            `el`'s <a href="#ready-to-be-parser-executed"
            id="script-processing-model:ready-to-be-parser-executed-2">ready to be
            parser-executed</a> to true. (The parser will handle
            executing the script.)

        </div>

36. Otherwise:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="script-processing-model:assert-2"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `el`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-7">result</a>
        is *not* "`uninitialized`".

    2.  <div id="script-processing-style-delayed">

        If all of the following are true:

        - `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
          id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-17">type</a>
          is "`classic`";
        - `el` is <a href="#parser-inserted"
          id="script-processing-model:parser-inserted-6">parser-inserted</a>;
        - `el`'s <a href="#parser-document"
          id="script-processing-model:parser-document-7">parser document</a>
          <a href="#has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts"
          id="script-processing-model:has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts">has
          a style sheet that is blocking scripts</a>; and
        - either the parser that created `el` is an
          <a href="#xml-parser" id="script-processing-model:xml-parser-3">XML
          parser</a>, or it's an
          <a href="#html-parser" id="script-processing-model:html-parser-3">HTML
          parser</a> whose <a href="#script-nesting-level"
          id="script-processing-model:script-nesting-level">script nesting
          level</a> is not greater than one,

        then:

        1.  Set `el`'s <a href="#parser-document"
            id="script-processing-model:parser-document-8">parser document</a>'s
            <a href="#pending-parsing-blocking-script"
            id="script-processing-model:pending-parsing-blocking-script-2">pending
            parsing-blocking script</a> to `el`.

        2.  Set `el`'s <a href="#ready-to-be-parser-executed"
            id="script-processing-model:ready-to-be-parser-executed-3">ready to be
            parser-executed</a> to true. (The parser will handle
            executing the script.)

        </div>

    3.  <div id="script-processing-inline">

        Otherwise, <a href="#immediately"
        id="script-processing-model:immediately">immediately</a>
        <a href="#execute-the-script-element"
        id="script-processing-model:execute-the-script-element-5">execute the
        script element</a> `el`, even if other scripts are already
        executing.

        </div>

</div>

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="pending-parsing-blocking-script" class="dfn">pending
parsing-blocking script</span>, which is a
[`script`](#the-script-element) element or null, initially null.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible"
class="dfn">set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible</span>,
which is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="script-processing-model:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible"
class="dfn">list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as
possible</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="script-processing-model:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a> of
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing"
class="dfn">list of scripts that will execute when the document has
finished parsing</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="script-processing-model:list-2" data-x-internal="list">list</a> of
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

If a [`script`](#the-script-element) element that blocks a parser gets
moved to another [`Document`](#document) before it would normally have
stopped blocking that parser, it nonetheless continues blocking that
parser until the condition that causes it to be blocking the parser no
longer applies (e.g., if the script is a
<a href="#pending-parsing-blocking-script"
id="script-processing-model:pending-parsing-blocking-script-3">pending
parsing-blocking script</a> because the original [`Document`](#document)
<a href="#has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts"
id="script-processing-model:has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts-2">has
a style sheet that is blocking scripts</a> when it was parsed, but then
the script is moved to another [`Document`](#document) before the
blocking style sheet(s) loaded, the script still blocks the parser until
the style sheets are all loaded, at which time the script executes and
the parser is unblocked).

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="execute-the-script-element" class="dfn">execute the script
element</span> given a [`script`](#the-script-element) element `el`:

1.  Let `document` be `el`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="script-processing-model:node-document-7"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

2.  If `el`'s <a href="#preparation-time-document"
    id="script-processing-model:preparation-time-document-6">preparation-time
    document</a> is not equal to `document`, then return.

3.  <a href="#unblock-rendering"
    id="script-processing-model:unblock-rendering">Unblock rendering</a>
    on `el`.

4.  If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-8">result</a> is
    null, then <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-event-fire-4"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    [`error`](#event-error) at `el`, and return.

5.  If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-external"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-external-2">from an external
    file</a> is true, or `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-18">type</a> is
    "`module`", then increment `document`'s
    <a href="#ignore-destructive-writes-counter"
    id="script-processing-model:ignore-destructive-writes-counter">ignore-destructive-writes
    counter</a>.

6.  Switch on `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-type"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-type-19">type</a>:

    "`classic`"  
    1.  Let `oldCurrentScript` be the value to which `document`'s
        [`currentScript`](#dom-document-currentscript) object was most
        recently set.

    2.  If `el`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root"
        id="script-processing-model:root" data-x-internal="root">root</a>
        is *not* a
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root"
        id="script-processing-model:shadow-root"
        data-x-internal="shadow-root">shadow root</a>, then set
        `document`'s [`currentScript`](#dom-document-currentscript)
        attribute to `el`. Otherwise, set it to null.

        This does not use the
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
        id="script-processing-model:in-a-document-tree"
        data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a document tree</a>
        check, as `el` could have been removed from the document prior
        to execution, and in that scenario
        [`currentScript`](#dom-document-currentscript) still needs to
        point to it.

    3.  <a href="#run-a-classic-script"
        id="script-processing-model:run-a-classic-script">Run the classic
        script</a> given by `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-9">result</a>.

    4.  Set `document`'s [`currentScript`](#dom-document-currentscript)
        attribute to `oldCurrentScript`.

    "`module`"  
    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="script-processing-model:assert-3"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `document`'s
        [`currentScript`](#dom-document-currentscript) attribute is
        null.

    2.  <a href="#run-a-module-script"
        id="script-processing-model:run-a-module-script">Run the module
        script</a> given by `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-10">result</a>.

    "`importmap`"  
    1.  <a href="#register-an-import-map"
        id="script-processing-model:register-an-import-map">Register an import
        map</a> given `el`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
        object</a> and `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-11">result</a>.

    "`speculationrules`"  
    1.  <a href="#register-speculation-rules"
        id="script-processing-model:register-speculation-rules">Register
        speculation rules</a> given `el`'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-relevant-global-3">relevant global
        object</a> and `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-result"
        id="script-processing-model:concept-script-result-12">result</a>.

7.  Decrement the <a href="#ignore-destructive-writes-counter"
    id="script-processing-model:ignore-destructive-writes-counter-2">ignore-destructive-writes
    counter</a> of `document`, if it was incremented in the earlier
    step.

8.  If `el`'s <a href="#concept-script-external"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-script-external-3">from an external
    file</a> is true, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="script-processing-model:concept-event-fire-5"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    [`load`](#event-load) at `el`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.1.2</span> Scripting languages<a href="#scriptingLanguages" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are not required to support JavaScript. This standard needs
to be updated if a language other than JavaScript comes along and gets
similar wide adoption by web browsers. Until such a time, implementing
other languages is in conflict with this standard, given the processing
model defined for the [`script`](#the-script-element) element.

Servers should use [`text/javascript`](#text/javascript) for JavaScript
resources, in accordance with Updates to ECMAScript Media Types. Servers
should not use other
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type"
id="scriptingLanguages:javascript-mime-type"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type">JavaScript MIME types</a> for
JavaScript resources, and must not use
non-<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type"
id="scriptingLanguages:javascript-mime-type-2"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type">JavaScript MIME types</a>.
[\[RFC9239\]](#refsRFC9239)

For external JavaScript resources, MIME type parameters in
\`[`Content-Type`](#content-type)\` headers are generally ignored. (In
some cases the \``charset`\` parameter has an effect.) However, for the
[`script`](#the-script-element) element's [`type`](#attr-script-type)
attribute they are significant; it uses the <a
href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
id="scriptingLanguages:javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
type essence match</a> concept.

For example, scripts with their [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute
set to "`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`" will not be evaluated, even
though that is a valid
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type"
id="scriptingLanguages:javascript-mime-type-3"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type">JavaScript MIME type</a> when
parsed.

Furthermore, again for external JavaScript resources, special
considerations apply around \`[`Content-Type`](#content-type)\` header
processing as detailed in the <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
id="scriptingLanguages:prepare-the-script-element">prepare the script
element</a> algorithm and Fetch. [\[FETCH\]](#refsFETCH)

##### <span class="secno">4.12.1.3</span> <span class="dfn">Restrictions for contents of `script` elements</span><a href="#restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements"
class="self-link"></a>

The easiest and safest way to avoid the rather strange restrictions
described in this section is to always escape an ASCII case-insensitive
match for "`<!--`" as "`\x3C!--`", "`<script`" as "`\x3Cscript`", and
"`</script`" as "`\x3C/script`" when these sequences appear in literals
in scripts (e.g. in strings, regular expressions, or comments), and to
avoid writing code that uses such constructs in expressions. Doing so
avoids the pitfalls that the restrictions in this section are prone to
triggering: namely, that, for historical reasons, parsing of
[`script`](#the-script-element) blocks in HTML is a strange and exotic
practice that acts unintuitively in the face of these sequences.

The [`script`](#the-script-element) element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-descendant-text-content"
id="restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements:descendant-text-content"
data-x-internal="descendant-text-content">descendant text content</a>
must match the `script` production in the following ABNF, the character
set for which is Unicode. [\[ABNF\]](#refsABNF)

``` abnf
script        = outer *( comment-open inner comment-close outer )

outer         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-outer >
not-in-outer  = comment-open
inner         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-inner >
not-in-inner  = comment-close / script-open

comment-open  = "<!--"
comment-close = "-->"
script-open   = "<" s c r i p t tag-end

s             =  %x0053 ; U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S
s             =/ %x0073 ; U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S
c             =  %x0043 ; U+0043 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER C
c             =/ %x0063 ; U+0063 LATIN SMALL LETTER C
r             =  %x0052 ; U+0052 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER R
r             =/ %x0072 ; U+0072 LATIN SMALL LETTER R
i             =  %x0049 ; U+0049 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I
i             =/ %x0069 ; U+0069 LATIN SMALL LETTER I
p             =  %x0050 ; U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P
p             =/ %x0070 ; U+0070 LATIN SMALL LETTER P
t             =  %x0054 ; U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T
t             =/ %x0074 ; U+0074 LATIN SMALL LETTER T

tag-end       =  %x0009 ; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)
tag-end       =/ %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
tag-end       =/ %x000C ; U+000C FORM FEED (FF)
tag-end       =/ %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
tag-end       =/ %x002F ; U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
tag-end       =/ %x003E ; U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)
```

When a [`script`](#the-script-element) element contains
<a href="#inline-documentation-for-external-scripts"
id="restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements:inline-documentation-for-external-scripts">script
documentation</a>, there are further restrictions on the contents of the
element, as described in the section below.

<div class="example">

The following script illustrates this issue. Suppose you have a script
that contains a string, as in:

``` js
const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
console.log(example);
```

If one were to put this string directly in a
[`script`](#the-script-element) block, it would violate the restrictions
above:

``` html
<script>
  const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
```

The bigger problem, though, and the reason why it would violate those
restrictions, is that actually the script would get parsed weirdly: *the
script block above is not terminated*. That is, what looks like a
"`</script>`" end tag in this snippet is actually still part of the
[`script`](#the-script-element) block. The script doesn't execute (since
it's not terminated); if it somehow were to execute, as it might if the
markup looked as follows, it would fail because the script (highlighted
here) is not valid JavaScript:

``` html
<script>
  const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
<!-- despite appearances, this is actually part of the script still! -->
<script>
 ... // this is the same script block still...
</script>
```

What is going on here is that for legacy reasons, "`<!--`" and
"`<script`" strings in [`script`](#the-script-element) elements in HTML
need to be balanced in order for the parser to consider closing the
block.

By escaping the problematic strings as mentioned at the top of this
section, the problem is avoided entirely:

``` html
<script>
  // Note: `\x3C` is an escape sequence for `<`.
  const example = 'Consider this string: \x3C!-- \x3Cscript>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
<!-- this is just a comment between script blocks -->
<script>
 ... // this is a new script block
</script>
```

It is possible for these sequences to naturally occur in script
expressions, as in the following examples:

``` js
if (x<!--y) { ... }
if ( player<script ) { ... }
```

In such cases the characters cannot be escaped, but the expressions can
be rewritten so that the sequences don't occur, as in:

``` js
if (x < !--y) { ... }
if (!--y > x) { ... }
if (!(--y) > x) { ... }
if (player < script) { ... }
if (script > player) { ... }
```

Doing this also avoids a different pitfall as well: for related
historical reasons, the string "\<!--" in <a href="#classic-script"
id="restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements:classic-script">classic
scripts</a> is actually treated as a line comment start, just like "//".

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.1.4</span> <span class="dfn">Inline documentation for external scripts</span><a href="#inline-documentation-for-external-scripts"
class="self-link"></a>

If a [`script`](#the-script-element) element's [`src`](#attr-script-src)
attribute is specified, then the contents of the
[`script`](#the-script-element) element, if any, must be such that the
value of the [`text`](#dom-script-text) IDL attribute, which is derived
from the element's contents, matches the `documentation` production in
the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode.
[\[ABNF\]](#refsABNF)

``` abnf
documentation = *( *( space / tab / comment ) [ line-comment ] newline )
comment       = slash star *( not-star / star not-slash ) 1*star slash
line-comment  = slash slash *not-newline

; characters
tab           = %x0009 ; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)
newline       = %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
space         = %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
star          = %x002A ; U+002A ASTERISK (*)
slash         = %x002F ; U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
not-newline   = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
not-star      = %x0000-0029 / %x002B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+002A ASTERISK (*)
not-slash     = %x0000-002E / %x0030-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
```

This corresponds to putting the contents of the element in JavaScript
comments.

This requirement is in addition to the earlier restrictions on the
syntax of contents of [`script`](#the-script-element) elements.

<div class="example">

This allows authors to include documentation, such as license
information or API information, inside their documents while still
referring to external script files. The syntax is constrained so that
authors don't accidentally include what looks like valid script while
also providing a [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute.

``` html
<script src="cool-effects.js">
 // create new instances using:
 //    var e = new Effect();
 // start the effect using .play, stop using .stop:
 //    e.play();
 //    e.stop();
</script>
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.1.5</span> Interaction of [`script`](#the-script-element) elements and XSLT<a href="#scriptTagXSLT" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT interacts with the
[`script`](#the-script-element) element. However, in the absence of
another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines
for implementers, based on existing implementations:

- When an XSLT transformation program is triggered by an
  `<?xml-stylesheet?>` processing instruction and the browser implements
  a direct-to-DOM transformation, [`script`](#the-script-element)
  elements created by the XSLT processor need to have its
  <a href="#parser-document" id="scriptTagXSLT:parser-document">parser
  document</a> set correctly, and run in document order (modulo scripts
  marked [`defer`](#attr-script-defer) or
  [`async`](#attr-script-async)),
  <a href="#immediately" id="scriptTagXSLT:immediately">immediately</a>,
  as the transformation is occurring.

- The [`XSLTProcessor`](#xsltprocessor)
  [`transformToDocument()`](#dom-xsltprocessor-transformtodocument)
  method adds elements to a [`Document`](#document) object with a null
  <a href="#concept-document-bc"
  id="scriptTagXSLT:concept-document-bc">browsing context</a>, and,
  accordingly, any [`script`](#the-script-element) elements they create
  need to have their
  <a href="#already-started" id="scriptTagXSLT:already-started">already
  started</a> set to true in the <a href="#prepare-the-script-element"
  id="scriptTagXSLT:prepare-the-script-element">prepare the script
  element</a> algorithm and never get executed
  (<a href="#concept-environment-noscript"
  id="scriptTagXSLT:concept-environment-noscript">scripting is
  disabled</a>). Such [`script`](#the-script-element) elements still
  need to have their
  <a href="#parser-document" id="scriptTagXSLT:parser-document-2">parser
  document</a> set, though, such that their [`async`](#dom-script-async)
  IDL attribute will return false in the absence of an
  [`async`](#attr-script-async) content attribute.

- The [`XSLTProcessor`](#xsltprocessor)
  [`transformToFragment()`](#dom-xsltprocessor-transformtofragment)
  method needs to create a fragment that is equivalent to one built
  manually by creating the elements using
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelementns"
  data-x-internal="dom-document-createelementns"><code
  id="scriptTagXSLT:dom-document-createelementns">document.createElementNS()</code></a>.
  For instance, it needs to create [`script`](#the-script-element)
  elements with null
  <a href="#parser-document" id="scriptTagXSLT:parser-document-3">parser
  document</a> and with their
  <a href="#already-started" id="scriptTagXSLT:already-started-2">already
  started</a> set to false, so that they will execute when the fragment
  is inserted into a document.

The main distinction between the first two cases and the last case is
that the first two operate on [`Document`](#document)s and the last
operates on a fragment.

#### <span class="secno">4.12.2</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`noscript`</span> element<a href="#the-noscript-element" class="self-link"></a>
