<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-noscript-element:metadata-content-2">Metadata content</a>.

<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-noscript-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-noscript-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#select-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-noscript-element:select-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>select</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

<a href="#optgroup-element-inner-content-elements-2"
id="the-noscript-element:optgroup-element-inner-content-elements-2"><code>optgroup</code>
element inner content elements</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
In a [`head`](#the-head-element) element of an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="the-noscript-element:html-documents"
data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML document</a>, if there are no
ancestor [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) elements.

Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-noscript-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="the-noscript-element:html-documents-2"
data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML documents</a>, if there are no
ancestor [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) elements.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
When <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-noscript">scripting is disabled</a>,
in a [`head`](#the-head-element) element: in any order, zero or more
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements, zero or more
[`style`](#the-style-element) elements, and zero or more
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements.

When <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-noscript-2">scripting is disabled</a>,
not in a [`head`](#the-head-element) element: <a href="#transparent"
id="the-noscript-element:transparent">transparent</a>, but there must be
no [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element descendants.

Otherwise: text that conforms to the requirements given in the prose.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-noscript-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-noscript).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-noscript).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
Uses [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement).

The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-noscript-element:represents">represents</a> nothing if
<a href="#concept-n-script"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-script">scripting is enabled</a>, and
<a href="#represents"
id="the-noscript-element:represents-2">represents</a> its children if
<a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-noscript-3">scripting is disabled</a>.
It is used to present different markup to user agents that support
scripting and those that don't support scripting, by affecting how the
document is parsed.

When used in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="the-noscript-element:html-documents-3"
data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML documents</a>, the allowed content
model is as follows:

In a [`head`](#the-head-element) element, if <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-noscript-4">scripting is disabled</a> for the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element  
The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element must contain only
[`link`](#the-link-element), [`style`](#the-style-element), and
[`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements.

In a [`head`](#the-head-element) element, if <a href="#concept-n-script"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-script-2">scripting is enabled</a> for the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element  
The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element must contain only text,
except that invoking the <a href="#html-fragment-parsing-algorithm"
id="the-noscript-element:html-fragment-parsing-algorithm">HTML fragment
parsing algorithm</a> with the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element)
element as the [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context) element and the
text contents as the `input` must result in a list of nodes that
consists only of [`link`](#the-link-element),
[`style`](#the-style-element), and [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements
that would be conforming if they were children of the
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element, and no
<a href="#parse-errors" id="the-noscript-element:parse-errors">parse
errors</a>.

Outside of [`head`](#the-head-element) elements, if <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-noscript-5">scripting is disabled</a> for the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element  
The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element's content model is
<a href="#transparent"
id="the-noscript-element:transparent-2">transparent</a>, with the
additional restriction that a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element)
element must not have a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element as
an ancestor (that is, [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) can't be
nested).

Outside of [`head`](#the-head-element) elements, if <a href="#concept-n-script"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-script-3">scripting is enabled</a> for the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element  
The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element must contain only text,
except that the text must be such that running the following algorithm
results in a conforming document with no
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) elements and no
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements, and such that no step in the
algorithm throws an exception or causes an
<a href="#html-parser" id="the-noscript-element:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> to flag a
<a href="#parse-errors" id="the-noscript-element:parse-errors-2">parse
error</a>:

<div algorithm="">

1.  Remove every [`script`](#the-script-element) element from the
    document.
2.  Make a list of every [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element in
    the document. For every [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element
    in that list, perform the following steps:
    1.  Let `s` be the
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
        id="the-noscript-element:child-text-content"
        data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> of
        the [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element.
    2.  Set the [`outerHTML`](#dom-element-outerhtml) attribute of the
        [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element to the value of `s`.
        (This, as a side-effect, causes the
        [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element to be removed from
        the document.)

</div>

All these contortions are required because, for historical reasons, the
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element is handled differently by
the <a href="#html-parser" id="the-noscript-element:html-parser-2">HTML
parser</a> based on whether <a href="#scripting-mode"
id="the-noscript-element:scripting-mode">scripting mode</a> was
<a href="#scripting-mode-disabled"
id="the-noscript-element:scripting-mode-disabled">Disabled</a> when the
parser was invoked.

The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element must not be used in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document"
id="the-noscript-element:xml-documents"
data-x-internal="xml-documents">XML documents</a>.

The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element is only effective in
<a href="#syntax" id="the-noscript-element:syntax">the HTML syntax</a>,
it has no effect in <a href="#the-xhtml-syntax"
id="the-noscript-element:the-xhtml-syntax">the XML syntax</a>. This is
because the way it works is by essentially "turning off" the parser when
scripts are enabled, so that the contents of the element are treated as
pure text and not as real elements. XML does not define a mechanism by
which to do this.

The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element has no other
requirements. In particular, children of the
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element are not exempt from
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="the-noscript-element:form-submission-2">form submission</a>,
scripting, and so forth, even when <a href="#concept-n-script"
id="the-noscript-element:concept-n-script-4">scripting is enabled</a>
for the element.

<div class="example">

In the following example, a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element
is used to provide fallback for a script.

``` html
<form action="calcSquare.php">
 <p>
  <label for=x>Number</label>:
  <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
 </p>
 <script>
  var x = document.getElementById('x');
  var output = document.createElement('p');
  output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
  x.form.appendChild(output);
  x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
  x.oninput = function () {
    var v = x.valueAsNumber;
    output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
  };
 </script>
 <noscript>
  <input type=submit value="Calculate Square">
 </noscript>
</form>
```

When script is disabled, a button appears to do the calculation on the
server side. When script is enabled, the value is computed on-the-fly
instead.

The [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element is a blunt instrument.
Sometimes, scripts might be enabled, but for some reason the page's
script might fail. For this reason, it's generally better to avoid using
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element), and to instead design the script to
change the page from being a scriptless page to a scripted page on the
fly, as in the next example:

``` html
<form action="calcSquare.php">
 <p>
  <label for=x>Number</label>:
  <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
 </p>
 <input id="submit" type=submit value="Calculate Square">
 <script>
  var x = document.getElementById('x');
  var output = document.createElement('p');
  output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
  x.form.appendChild(output);
  x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
  x.oninput = function () {
    var v = x.valueAsNumber;
    output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
  };
  var submit = document.getElementById('submit');
  submit.parentNode.removeChild(submit);
 </script>
</form>
```

The above technique is also useful in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document"
id="the-noscript-element:xml-documents-2"
data-x-internal="xml-documents">XML documents</a>, since
[`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) is not allowed there.

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:

content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-template-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-template-element:script-supporting-elements-2">Script-supporting
element</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which
this element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#metadata-content-2"
id="the-template-element:metadata-content-2-2">metadata content</a> is
expected.

Where <a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-template-element:phrasing-content-2-2">phrasing content</a> is
expected.

Where <a href="#script-supporting-elements-2"
id="the-template-element:script-supporting-elements-2-2">script-supporting
elements</a> are expected.

As a child of a [`colgroup`](#the-colgroup-element) element that doesn't
have a [`span`](#attr-colgroup-span) attribute.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-content-model">Content
model</a>:  
<a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-template-element:concept-content-nothing">Nothing</a> (for
clarification, [see example](#template-example)).

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-template-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`shadowrootmode`](#attr-template-shadowrootmode) — Enables streaming
declarative shadow roots

[`shadowrootdelegatesfocus`](#attr-template-shadowrootdelegatesfocus) —
Sets <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
id="the-template-element:delegates-focus"
data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> on a declarative
shadow root

[`shadowrootclonable`](#attr-template-shadowrootclonable) — Sets
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-clonable"
id="the-template-element:clonable"
data-x-internal="clonable">clonable</a> on a declarative shadow root

[`shadowrootserializable`](#attr-template-shadowrootserializable) — Sets
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-serializable"
id="the-template-element:shadow-serializable"
data-x-internal="shadow-serializable">serializable</a> on a declarative
shadow root

[`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`](#attr-template-shadowrootcustomelementregistry)
— Enables declarative shadow roots to indicate they will use a custom
element registry

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-template).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-template).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-template-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTemplateElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute DocumentFragment content;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString shadowRootMode;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootDelegatesFocus;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootClonable;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootSerializable;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString shadowRootCustomElementRegistry;
};
```

The [`template`](#the-template-element) element is used to declare
fragments of HTML that can be cloned and inserted in the document by
script.

In a rendering, the [`template`](#the-template-element) element
<a href="#represents"
id="the-template-element:represents">represents</a> nothing.

The <span id="attr-template-shadowrootmode" class="dfn"
dfn-for="template" dfn-type="element-attr">`shadowrootmode`</span>
content attribute is an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-template-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-shadowrootmode-open" class="dfn" dfn-for="template/shadowrootmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`open`</span> | <span id="attr-shadowrootmode-open-state" class="dfn">Open</span> | The template element represents an open declarative shadow root. |
| <span id="attr-shadowrootmode-closed" class="dfn" dfn-for="template/shadowrootmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`closed`</span> | <span id="attr-shadowrootmode-closed-state" class="dfn">Closed</span> | The template element represents a closed declarative shadow root. |

The [`shadowrootmode`](#attr-template-shadowrootmode) attribute's
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* and *[missing value
default](#missing-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-shadowrootmode-none-state" class="dfn">None</span> state.

The <span id="attr-template-shadowrootdelegatesfocus" class="dfn"
dfn-for="template"
dfn-type="element-attr">`shadowrootdelegatesfocus`</span> content
attribute is a <a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-template-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>.

The <span id="attr-template-shadowrootclonable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="template" dfn-type="element-attr">`shadowrootclonable`</span>
content attribute is a <a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-template-element:boolean-attribute-2">boolean attribute</a>.

The <span id="attr-template-shadowrootserializable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="template"
dfn-type="element-attr">`shadowrootserializable`</span> content
attribute is a <a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-template-element:boolean-attribute-3">boolean attribute</a>.

The <span id="attr-template-shadowrootcustomelementregistry" class="dfn"
dfn-for="template"
dfn-type="element-attr">`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`</span> content
attribute is a <a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-template-element:boolean-attribute-4">boolean attribute</a>.

The <a href="#template-contents"
id="the-template-element:template-contents">template contents</a> of a
[`template`](#the-template-element) element [are not children of the
element itself](#template-syntax).

It is also possible, as a result of DOM manipulation, for a
[`template`](#the-template-element) element to contain
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="the-template-element:text">Text</code></a> nodes and element nodes;
however, having any is a violation of the
[`template`](#the-template-element) element's content model, since its
content model is defined as <a href="#concept-content-nothing"
id="the-template-element:concept-content-nothing-2">nothing</a>.

<div id="template-example" class="example">

<a href="#template-example" class="self-link"></a>

For example, consider the following document:

``` html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
 <head>
  <title>Homework</title>
 <body>
  <template id="template"><p>Smile!</p></template>
  <script>
   let num = 3;
   const fragment = document.getElementById('template').content.cloneNode(true);
   while (num-- > 1) {
     fragment.firstChild.before(fragment.firstChild.cloneNode(true));
     fragment.firstChild.textContent += fragment.lastChild.textContent;
   }
   document.body.appendChild(fragment);
  </script>
</html>
```

The [`p`](#the-p-element) element in the
[`template`](#the-template-element) is *not* a child of the
[`template`](#the-template-element) in the DOM; it is a child of the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
id="the-template-element:documentfragment-2">DocumentFragment</code></a>
returned by the [`template`](#the-template-element) element's
[`content`](#dom-template-content) IDL attribute.

If the script were to call
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-appendchild"
data-x-internal="dom-node-appendchild"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-node-appendchild">appendChild()</code></a>
on the [`template`](#the-template-element) element, that would add a
child to the [`template`](#the-template-element) element (as for any
other element); however, doing so is a violation of the
[`template`](#the-template-element) element's content model.

</div>

`template``.`<a href="#dom-template-content"
id="dom-template-content-dev"><code>content</code></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLTemplateElement/content](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLTemplateElement/content "The HTMLTemplateElement.content property returns a <template> element's template contents (a DocumentFragment).")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox22+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari8+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome26+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Returns the <a href="#template-contents"
id="the-template-element:template-contents-2">template contents</a> (a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
id="the-template-element:documentfragment-3">DocumentFragment</code></a>).

<div algorithm="">

Each [`template`](#the-template-element) element has an associated
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
id="the-template-element:documentfragment-4">DocumentFragment</code></a>
object that is its <span id="template-contents" class="dfn">template
contents</span>. The <a href="#template-contents"
id="the-template-element:template-contents-3">template contents</a> have
[no conformance requirements](#no-browsing-context). When a
[`template`](#the-template-element) element is created, the user agent
must run the following steps to establish the
<a href="#template-contents"
id="the-template-element:template-contents-4">template contents</a>:

1.  Let `document` be the [`template`](#the-template-element) element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#appropriate-template-contents-owner-document"
    id="the-template-element:appropriate-template-contents-owner-document">appropriate
    template contents owner document</a>.

2.  Create a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-template-element:documentfragment-5">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    object whose
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is `document` and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host"
    id="the-template-element:concept-documentfragment-host"
    data-x-internal="concept-documentfragment-host">host</a> is the
    [`template`](#the-template-element) element.

3.  Set the [`template`](#the-template-element) element's
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-5">template contents</a>
    to the newly created
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-template-element:documentfragment-6">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    object.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) `document`'s
<span id="appropriate-template-contents-owner-document"
class="dfn">appropriate template contents owner document</span> is the
[`Document`](#document) returned by the following algorithm:

1.  If `document` is not a [`Document`](#document) created by this
    algorithm:

    1.  If `document` does not yet have an
        <span id="associated-inert-template-document"
        class="dfn">associated inert template document</span>:

        1.  Let `newDocument` be a new [`Document`](#document) (whose
            <a href="#concept-document-bc"
            id="the-template-element:concept-document-bc">browsing context</a>
            is null). This is "a [`Document`](#document) created by this
            algorithm" for the purposes of the step above.

        2.  If `document` is an
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
            id="the-template-element:html-documents"
            data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML document</a>, then
            mark `newDocument` as an
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
            id="the-template-element:html-documents-2"
            data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML document</a> also.

        3.  Set `document`'s
            <a href="#associated-inert-template-document"
            id="the-template-element:associated-inert-template-document">associated
            inert template document</a> to `newDocument`.

    2.  Set `document` to `document`'s
        <a href="#associated-inert-template-document"
        id="the-template-element:associated-inert-template-document-2">associated
        inert template document</a>.

    Each [`Document`](#document) not created by this algorithm thus gets
    a single [`Document`](#document) to act as its proxy for owning the
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-6">template contents</a>
    of all its [`template`](#the-template-element) elements, so that
    they aren't in a <a href="#browsing-context"
    id="the-template-element:browsing-context">browsing context</a> and
    thus remain inert (e.g. scripts do not run). Meanwhile,
    [`template`](#the-template-element) elements inside
    [`Document`](#document) objects that *are* created by this algorithm
    just reuse the same [`Document`](#document) owner for their
    contents.

2.  Return `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt-ext"
id="the-template-element:concept-node-adopt-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-node-adopt-ext">adopting steps</a> (with `node`
and `oldDocument` as parameters) for [`template`](#the-template-element)
elements are the following:

1.  Let `document` be `node`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#appropriate-template-contents-owner-document"
    id="the-template-element:appropriate-template-contents-owner-document-2">appropriate
    template contents owner document</a>.

    `node`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:node-document-4"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is the
    [`Document`](#document) object that `node` was just adopted *into*.

2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt"
    id="the-template-element:concept-node-adopt"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-adopt">Adopt</a> `node`'s
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-7">template contents</a>
    (a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-template-element:documentfragment-7">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    object) into `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-template-content" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTemplateElement" dfn-type="attribute">`content`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="the-template-element:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-template-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-8">template contents</a>
    is not a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-shadowroot"
    data-x-internal="shadowroot"><code
    id="the-template-element:shadowroot">ShadowRoot</code></a> node.

2.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-template-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-9">template contents</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-template-shadowrootmode" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLTemplateElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`shadowRootMode`</span> IDL attribute must
<a href="#reflect" id="the-template-element:reflect">reflect</a> the
[`shadowrootmode`](#attr-template-shadowrootmode) content attribute,
<a href="#limited-to-only-known-values"
id="the-template-element:limited-to-only-known-values">limited to only
known values</a>.

</div>

The <a href="#dom-template-shadowrootcustomelementregistry"
id="the-template-element:dom-template-shadowrootcustomelementregistry">shadowRootCustomElementRegistry</a>
IDL attribute intentionally does not have a boolean type so it can be
extended.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone-ext"
id="the-template-element:concept-node-clone-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-ext">cloning steps</a> for
[`template`](#the-template-element) elements given `node`, `copy`, and
`subtree` are:

1.  If `subtree` is false, then return.

2.  For each `child` of `node`'s <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-10">template contents</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
    id="the-template-element:concept-tree-child"
    data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a>, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="the-template-element:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>: <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone"
    id="the-template-element:concept-node-clone"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-clone">clone a node</a> given `child`
    with <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#clone-a-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:concept-node-clone-document"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-document"><em>document</em></a>
    set to `copy`'s <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-11">template contents</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-template-element:node-document-5"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>,
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#clone-a-node-subtree"
    id="the-template-element:concept-node-clone-subtree"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-subtree"><em>subtree</em></a>
    set to true, and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#clone-a-node-parent"
    id="the-template-element:concept-node-clone-parent"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-clone-parent"><em>parent</em></a> set
    to `copy`'s <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-template-element:template-contents-12">template contents</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

In this example, a script populates a table four-column with data from a
data structure, using a [`template`](#the-template-element) to provide
the element structure instead of manually generating the structure from
markup.

``` html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang='en'>
<title>Cat data</title>
<script>
 // Data is hard-coded here, but could come from the server
 var data = [
   { name: 'Pillar', color: 'Ticked Tabby', sex: 'Female (neutered)', legs: 3 },
   { name: 'Hedral', color: 'Tuxedo', sex: 'Male (neutered)', legs: 4 },
 ];
</script>
<table>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th>Name <th>Color <th>Sex <th>Legs
 <tbody>
  <template id="row">
   <tr><td><td><td><td>
  </template>
</table>
<script>
 var template = document.querySelector('#row');
 for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i += 1) {
   var cat = data[i];
   var clone = template.content.cloneNode(true);
   var cells = clone.querySelectorAll('td');
   cells[0].textContent = cat.name;
   cells[1].textContent = cat.color;
   cells[2].textContent = cat.sex;
   cells[3].textContent = cat.legs;
   template.parentNode.appendChild(clone);
 }
</script>
```

This example uses
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-clonenode"
data-x-internal="dom-node-clonenode"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-node-clonenode">cloneNode()</code></a> on
the [`template`](#the-template-element)'s contents; it could
equivalently have used
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-importnode"
data-x-internal="dom-document-importnode"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-document-importnode">document.importNode()</code></a>,
which does the same thing. The only difference between these two APIs is
when the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="the-template-element:node-document-6"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is updated: with
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-clonenode"
data-x-internal="dom-node-clonenode"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-node-clonenode-2">cloneNode()</code></a> it
is updated when the nodes are appended with
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-appendchild"
data-x-internal="dom-node-appendchild"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-node-appendchild-2">appendChild()</code></a>,
with <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-importnode"
data-x-internal="dom-document-importnode"><code
id="the-template-element:dom-document-importnode-2">document.importNode()</code></a>
it is updated when the nodes are cloned.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.3.1</span> Interaction of [`template`](#the-template-element) elements with XSLT and XPath<a href="#template-XSLT-XPath" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT and XPath interact with the
[`template`](#the-template-element) element. However, in the absence of
another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines
for implementers, which are intended to be consistent with other
processing described in this specification:

- An XSLT processor based on an XML parser that acts
  <a href="#xml-parser" id="template-XSLT-XPath:xml-parser">as described
  in this specification</a> needs to act as if
  [`template`](#the-template-element) elements contain as descendants
  their <a href="#template-contents"
  id="template-XSLT-XPath:template-contents">template contents</a> for
  the purposes of the transform.

- An XSLT processor that outputs a DOM needs to ensure that nodes that
  would go into a [`template`](#the-template-element) element are
  instead placed into the element's <a href="#template-contents"
  id="template-XSLT-XPath:template-contents-2">template contents</a>.

- XPath evaluation using the XPath DOM API when applied to a
  [`Document`](#document) parsed using the
  <a href="#html-parser" id="template-XSLT-XPath:html-parser">HTML
  parser</a> or the
  <a href="#xml-parser" id="template-XSLT-XPath:xml-parser-2">XML
  parser</a> described in this specification needs to ignore
  <a href="#template-contents"
  id="template-XSLT-XPath:template-contents-3">template contents</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-slot-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-slot).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-slot-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSlotElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  sequence<Node> assignedNodes(optional AssignedNodesOptions options = {});
  sequence<Element> assignedElements(optional AssignedNodesOptions options = {});
  undefined assign((Element or Text)... nodes);
};

dictionary AssignedNodesOptions {
  boolean flatten = false;
};
```

The [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element defines a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-slot"
id="the-slot-element:concept-slot"
data-x-internal="concept-slot">slot</a>. It is typically used in a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-slot-element:shadow-tree" data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow
tree</a>. A [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-slot-element:represents">represents</a>
its <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes"
id="the-slot-element:assigned-nodes"
data-x-internal="assigned-nodes">assigned nodes</a>, if any, and its
contents otherwise.

The <span id="attr-slot-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="slot"
dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> content attribute may contain any
string value. It represents a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-slot"
id="the-slot-element:concept-slot-2"
data-x-internal="concept-slot">slot</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-name"
id="the-slot-element:slot-name" data-x-internal="slot-name">name</a>.

The [`name`](#attr-slot-name) attribute is used to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#assign-a-slot"
id="the-slot-element:assign-a-slot"
data-x-internal="assign-a-slot">assign slots</a> to other elements: a
[`slot`](#the-slot-element) element with a [`name`](#attr-slot-name)
attribute creates a named
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-slot"
id="the-slot-element:concept-slot-3"
data-x-internal="concept-slot">slot</a> to which any element is
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#assign-a-slot"
id="the-slot-element:assign-a-slot-2"
data-x-internal="assign-a-slot">assigned</a> if that element has a
[`slot`](#attr-slot) attribute whose value matches that
[`name`](#attr-slot-name) attribute's value, and the
[`slot`](#the-slot-element) element is a child of the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-slot-element:shadow-tree-2" data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow
tree</a> whose <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root"
id="the-slot-element:root" data-x-internal="root">root</a>'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host"
id="the-slot-element:concept-documentfragment-host"
data-x-internal="concept-documentfragment-host">host</a> has that
corresponding [`slot`](#attr-slot) attribute value.

`slot``.`<a href="#dom-slot-name" id="dom-slot-name-dev"><code>name</code></a>

Returns `slot`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes"
id="the-slot-element:assigned-nodes-3"
data-x-internal="assigned-nodes">assigned nodes</a>, if any, and
`slot`'s children otherwise, and does the same for any
[`slot`](#the-slot-element) elements encountered therein, recursively,
until there are no [`slot`](#the-slot-element) elements left.

`slot``.`<a href="#dom-slot-assign"
id="the-slot-element:dom-slot-assign-2"><code>assign</code></a>`(...``nodes``)`

Sets `slot`'s <a href="#manually-assigned-nodes"
id="the-slot-element:manually-assigned-nodes">manually assigned
nodes</a> to the given `nodes`.

The [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element has
<span id="manually-assigned-nodes" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSlotElement"
export="">manually assigned nodes</span>, which is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="the-slot-element:set" data-x-internal="set">ordered set</a> of
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-slotable"
id="the-slot-element:slottable"
data-x-internal="slottable">slottables</a> set by
[`assign()`](#dom-slot-assign). This set is initially empty.

The <a href="#manually-assigned-nodes"
id="the-slot-element:manually-assigned-nodes-2">manually assigned
nodes</a> set can be implemented using weak references to the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-slotable"
id="the-slot-element:slottable-2"
data-x-internal="slottable">slottables</a>, because this set is not
directly accessible from script.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-slot-assignednodes" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSlotElement"
dfn-type="method">`assignedNodes(``options``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If `options`\["[`flatten`](#dom-assignednodesoptions-flatten)"\] is
    false, then return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes"
    id="the-slot-element:assigned-nodes-5"
    data-x-internal="assigned-nodes">assigned nodes</a>.

2.  Return the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#find-flattened-slotables"
    id="the-slot-element:finding-flattened-slottables"
    data-x-internal="finding-flattened-slottables">finding flattened
    slottables</a> with <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-slot-assignedelements" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLSlotElement"
dfn-type="method">`assignedElements(``options``)`</span> method steps
are:

1.  If `options`\["[`flatten`](#dom-assignednodesoptions-flatten)"\] is
    false, then return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes"
    id="the-slot-element:assigned-nodes-6"
    data-x-internal="assigned-nodes">assigned nodes</a>, filtered to
    contain only
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
    data-x-internal="element"><code
    id="the-slot-element:element-2">Element</code></a> nodes.

2.  Return the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#find-flattened-slotables"
    id="the-slot-element:finding-flattened-slottables-2"
    data-x-internal="finding-flattened-slottables">finding flattened
    slottables</a> with <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    filtered to contain only
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
    data-x-internal="element"><code
    id="the-slot-element:element-3">Element</code></a> nodes.

</div>

The manually assigned nodes set is initially empty until nodes are assigned using assign().")

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView

Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-slot-assign" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLSlotElement"
dfn-type="method">`assign(...``nodes``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-slot-element:list-iterate" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `node` of <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#manually-assigned-nodes"
    id="the-slot-element:manually-assigned-nodes-3">manually assigned
    nodes</a>, set `node`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slottable-manual-slot-assignment"
    id="the-slot-element:manual-slot-assignment"
    data-x-internal="manual-slot-assignment">manual slot assignment</a>
    to null.

2.  Let `nodesSet` be a new
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="the-slot-element:set-2" data-x-internal="set">ordered set</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-slot-element:list-iterate-2" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `node` of `nodes`:

    1.  If `node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slottable-manual-slot-assignment"
        id="the-slot-element:manual-slot-assignment-2"
        data-x-internal="manual-slot-assignment">manual slot assignment</a>
        refers to a <a href="#the-slot-element"
        id="the-slot-element:the-slot-element-8">slot</a>, then remove
        `node` from that <a href="#the-slot-element"
        id="the-slot-element:the-slot-element-9">slot</a>'s
        <a href="#manually-assigned-nodes"
        id="the-slot-element:manually-assigned-nodes-4">manually assigned
        nodes</a>.

    2.  Set `node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slottable-manual-slot-assignment"
        id="the-slot-element:manual-slot-assignment-3"
        data-x-internal="manual-slot-assignment">manual slot assignment</a>
        to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="the-slot-element:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
        id="the-slot-element:set-append" data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a>
        `node` to `nodesSet`.

4.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#manually-assigned-nodes"
    id="the-slot-element:manually-assigned-nodes-5">manually assigned
    nodes</a> to `nodesSet`.

5.  Run
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#assign-slotables-for-a-tree"
    id="the-slot-element:assign-slottables-for-a-tree"
    data-x-internal="assign-slottables-for-a-tree">assign slottables for a
    tree</a> for <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-slot-element:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root"
    id="the-slot-element:root-2" data-x-internal="root">root</a>.

</div>

<a href="#concept-element-categories"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-categories">Categories</a>:  
<a href="#flow-content-2" id="the-canvas-element:flow-content-2">Flow
content</a>.

<a href="#phrasing-content-2"
id="the-canvas-element:phrasing-content-2">Phrasing content</a>.

<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category">Embedded content</a>.

<a href="#palpable-content-2"
id="the-canvas-element:palpable-content-2">Palpable content</a>.

<a href="#concept-element-contexts"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-contexts">Contexts in which this
element can be used</a>:  
Where <a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-2">embedded content</a>
is expected.

<a href="#concept-element-content-model"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-content-model">Content model</a>:  
<a href="#transparent"
id="the-canvas-element:transparent">Transparent</a>, but with no
<a href="#interactive-content-2"
id="the-canvas-element:interactive-content-2">interactive content</a>
descendants except for [`a`](#the-a-element) elements,
[`img`](#the-img-element) elements with
[`usemap`](#attr-hyperlink-usemap) attributes,
[`button`](#the-button-element) elements, [`input`](#the-input-element)
elements whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute are in the
<a href="#checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)"
id="the-canvas-element:checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)">Checkbox</a> or
<a href="#radio-button-state-(type=radio)"
id="the-canvas-element:radio-button-state-(type=radio)">Radio Button</a>
states, [`input`](#the-input-element) elements that are
<a href="#concept-button"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-button">buttons</a>, and
[`select`](#the-select-element) elements with a
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute or a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-select-size">display size</a> greater
than 1.

<a href="#concept-element-tag-omission"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-tag-omission">Tag omission in
text/html</a>:  
Neither tag is omissible.

<a href="#concept-element-attributes"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-attributes">Content
attributes</a>:  
<a href="#global-attributes"
id="the-canvas-element:global-attributes">Global attributes</a>

[`width`](#attr-canvas-width) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#attr-canvas-height) — Vertical dimension

<a href="#concept-element-accessibility-considerations"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-accessibility-considerations">Accessibility
considerations</a>:  
[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-canvas).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-canvas).

<a href="#concept-element-dom"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-element-dom">DOM interface</a>:  
``` idl
typedef (CanvasRenderingContext2D or ImageBitmapRenderingContext or WebGLRenderingContext or WebGL2RenderingContext or GPUCanvasContext) RenderingContext;

[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLCanvasElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long width;
  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long height;

  RenderingContext? getContext(DOMString contextId, optional any options = null);

  USVString toDataURL(optional DOMString type = "image/png", optional any quality);
  undefined toBlob(BlobCallback _callback, optional DOMString type = "image/png", optional any quality);
  OffscreenCanvas transferControlToOffscreen();
};

callback BlobCallback = undefined (Blob? blob);
```

The [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element provides scripts with a
resolution-dependent bitmap canvas, which can be used for rendering
graphs, game graphics, art, or other visual images on the fly.

Authors should not use the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element in a
document when a more suitable element is available. For example, it is
inappropriate to use a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element to render
a page heading: if the desired presentation of the heading is
graphically intense, it should be marked up using appropriate elements
(typically [`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)) and then
styled using CSS and supporting technologies such as
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-canvas-element:shadow-tree" data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow
trees</a>.

When authors use the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, they must
also provide content that, when presented to the user, conveys
essentially the same function or purpose as the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element)'s bitmap. This content may be placed as
content of the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element. The contents of
the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, if any, are the element's
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-canvas-element:fallback-content">fallback content</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

In interactive visual media, if <a href="#concept-n-script"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-n-script">scripting is enabled</a> for
the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, and if support for
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements has been enabled, then the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element
<a href="#represents" id="the-canvas-element:represents">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-3">embedded content</a>
consisting of a dynamically created image, the element's bitmap.

In non-interactive, static, visual media, if the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has been previously associated
with a rendering context (e.g. if the page was viewed in an interactive
visual medium and is now being printed, or if some script that ran
during the page layout process painted on the element), then the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-canvas-element:represents-2">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-4">embedded content</a>
with the element's current bitmap and size. Otherwise, the element
represents its <a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-canvas-element:fallback-content-2">fallback content</a> instead.

In non-visual media, and in visual media if
<a href="#concept-n-noscript"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-n-noscript">scripting is disabled</a> for
the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element or if support for
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements has been disabled, the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-canvas-element:represents-3">represents</a> its
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-canvas-element:fallback-content-3">fallback content</a> instead.

When a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element <a href="#represents"
id="the-canvas-element:represents-4">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-5">embedded content</a>,
the user can still focus descendants of the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element (in the
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-canvas-element:fallback-content-4">fallback content</a>). When
an element is
<a href="#focused" id="the-canvas-element:focused">focused</a>, it is
the target of keyboard interaction events (even though the element
itself is not visible). This allows authors to make an interactive
canvas keyboard-accessible: authors should have a one-to-one mapping of
interactive regions to *[focusable areas](#focusable-area)* in the
<a href="#fallback-content"
id="the-canvas-element:fallback-content-5">fallback content</a>. (Focus
has no effect on mouse interaction events.)
[\[UIEVENTS\]](#refsUIEVENTS)

<div algorithm="">

An element whose nearest [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element
ancestor is
<a href="#being-rendered" id="the-canvas-element:being-rendered">being
rendered</a> and <a href="#represents"
id="the-canvas-element:represents-5">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-6">embedded content</a>
is an element that is
<span id="being-used-as-relevant-canvas-fallback-content"
class="dfn">being used as relevant canvas fallback content</span>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has two attributes to
control the size of the element's bitmap: <span id="attr-canvas-width"
class="dfn" dfn-for="canvas" dfn-type="element-attr">`width`</span> and
<span id="attr-canvas-height" class="dfn" dfn-for="canvas"
dfn-type="element-attr">`height`</span>. These attributes, when
specified, must have values that are
<a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="the-canvas-element:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative
integers</a>. The <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-canvas-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> must be used to
<span id="obtain-numeric-values" class="dfn">obtain their numeric
values</span>. If an attribute is missing, or if parsing its value
returns an error, then the default value must be used instead. The
[`width`](#attr-canvas-width) attribute defaults to 300, and the
[`height`](#attr-canvas-height) attribute defaults to 150.

<div algorithm="">

When setting the value of the [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) or
[`height`](#attr-canvas-height) attribute, if the
<a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode">context mode</a> of
the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element is set to
<a href="#concept-canvas-placeholder"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-placeholder">placeholder</a>, the
user agent must throw an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="the-canvas-element:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-canvas-element:domexception">DOMException</code></a> and leave
the attribute's value unchanged.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
id="the-canvas-element:natural-dimensions"
data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a> of the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element when it <a href="#represents"
id="the-canvas-element:represents-6">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-7">embedded content</a>
are equal to the dimensions of the element's bitmap.

</div>

The user agent must use a square pixel density consisting of one pixel
of image data per coordinate space unit for the bitmaps of a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) and its rendering contexts.

A [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element can be sized arbitrarily by a
style sheet, its bitmap is then subject to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#the-object-fit"
id="the-canvas-element:&#39;object-fit&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;object-fit&#39;">'object-fit'</a> CSS property.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The bitmaps of [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements, the bitmaps of
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) objects, as well as some of the bitmaps of
rendering contexts, such as those described in the sections on the
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d),
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d),
and [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#imagebitmaprenderingcontext)
objects below, have an <span id="concept-canvas-origin-clean"
class="dfn">origin-clean</span> flag, which can be set to true or false.
Initially, when the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element or
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object is created, its bitmap's
<a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
flag must be set to true.

A [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element can have a rendering context
bound to it. Initially, it does not have a bound rendering context. To
keep track of whether it has a rendering context or not, and what kind
of rendering context it is, a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) also has a
<span id="concept-canvas-context-mode" class="dfn">canvas context
mode</span>, which is initially <span id="concept-canvas-none"
class="dfn">none</span> but can be changed to either
<span id="concept-canvas-placeholder" class="dfn">placeholder</span>,
<span id="concept-canvas-2d" class="dfn">2d</span>,
<span id="concept-canvas-bitmaprenderer"
class="dfn">bitmaprenderer</span>, <span id="concept-canvas-webgl"
class="dfn">webgl</span>, <span id="concept-canvas-webgl2"
class="dfn">webgl2</span>, or <span id="concept-canvas-webgpu"
class="dfn">webgpu</span> by algorithms defined in this specification.

When its <a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-2">canvas context
mode</a> is <a href="#concept-canvas-none"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-none">none</a>, a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has no rendering context, and
its bitmap must be
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="the-canvas-element:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a> with a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
id="the-canvas-element:natural-width"
data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a> equal to
<a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
id="the-canvas-element:obtain-numeric-values">the numeric value</a> of
the element's [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) attribute and a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
id="the-canvas-element:natural-height"
data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a> equal to
<a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
id="the-canvas-element:obtain-numeric-values-2">the numeric value</a> of
the element's [`height`](#attr-canvas-height) attribute, those values
being interpreted in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-canvas-element:&#39;px&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>, and being updated as the attributes are set, changed, or
removed.

When its <a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-3">canvas context
mode</a> is <a href="#concept-canvas-placeholder"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-placeholder-2">placeholder</a>, a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has no rendering context. It
serves as a placeholder for an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)
object, and the content of the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element
is updated by the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object's
rendering context.

When a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element represents
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="the-canvas-element:embedded-content-category-8">embedded content</a>,
it provides a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#paint-source"
id="the-canvas-element:paint-source"
data-x-internal="paint-source">paint source</a> whose width is the
element's <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
id="the-canvas-element:natural-width-2"
data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a>, whose height is the
element's <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
id="the-canvas-element:natural-height-2"
data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a>, and whose
appearance is the element's bitmap.

<div algorithm="">

Whenever the [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) and
[`height`](#attr-canvas-height) content attributes are set, removed,
changed, or redundantly set to the value they already have, then the
user agent must perform the action from the row of the following table
that corresponds to the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's
<a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-4">context mode</a>.

| <a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-5">Context Mode</a> | Action |
|----|----|
| <a href="#concept-canvas-2d"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-2d">2d</a> | Follow the steps to <a href="#concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions">set bitmap
dimensions</a> to <a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
id="the-canvas-element:obtain-numeric-values-3">the numeric values</a> of the [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) and [`height`](#attr-canvas-height) content attributes. |
| <a href="#concept-canvas-webgl"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-webgl">webgl</a> or <a href="#concept-canvas-webgl2"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-webgl2">webgl2</a> | Follow the behavior defined in the WebGL specifications. [\[WEBGL\]](#refsWEBGL) |
| <a href="#concept-canvas-webgpu"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-webgpu">webgpu</a> | Follow the behavior defined in WebGPU. [\[WEBGPU\]](#refsWEBGPU) |
| <a href="#concept-canvas-bitmaprenderer"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-bitmaprenderer">bitmaprenderer</a> | If the context's <a href="#concept-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-bitmap-mode"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-bitmap-mode">bitmap
mode</a> is set to <a href="#concept-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-blank"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-blank">blank</a>, run the steps to <a href="#set-an-imagebitmaprenderingcontext&#39;s-output-bitmap"
id="the-canvas-element:set-an-imagebitmaprenderingcontext&#39;s-output-bitmap">set
an <code>ImageBitmapRenderingContext</code>'s output bitmap</a>, passing the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's rendering context. |
| <a href="#concept-canvas-placeholder"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-placeholder-3">placeholder</a> | Do nothing. |
| <a href="#concept-canvas-none"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-none-2">none</a> | Do nothing. |

</div>

Returns an object that exposes an API for drawing on the canvas.
`contextId` specifies the desired API: "[`2d`](#canvas-context-2d)",
"[`bitmaprenderer`](#canvas-context-bitmaprenderer)",
"[`webgl`](#canvas-context-webgl)",
"[`webgl2`](#canvas-context-webgl2)", or
"[`webgpu`](#canvas-context-webgpu)". `options` is handled by that API.

This specification defines the "[`2d`](#canvas-context-2d)" and
"[`bitmaprenderer`](#canvas-context-bitmaprenderer)" contexts below. The
WebGL specifications define the "[`webgl`](#canvas-context-webgl)" and
"[`webgl2`](#canvas-context-webgl2)" contexts. WebGPU defines the
"[`webgpu`](#canvas-context-webgpu)" context. [\[WEBGL\]](#refsWEBGL)
[\[WEBGPU\]](#refsWEBGPU)

Returns null if `contextId` is not supported, or if the canvas has
already been initialized with another context type (e.g., trying to get
a "[`2d`](#canvas-context-2d)" context after getting a
"[`webgl`](#canvas-context-webgl)" context).

Returns a <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
id="the-canvas-element:data-protocol"
data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code>data:</code> URL</a> for the image
in the canvas.

The first argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be
returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is "[`image/png`](#image/png)";
that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The second
argument applies if the type is an image format that supports variable
quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#image/jpeg)"), and is a number in the
range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive indicating the desired quality level for the
resulting image.

When trying to use types other than "[`image/png`](#image/png)", authors
can check if the image was really returned in the requested format by
checking to see if the returned string starts with one of the exact
strings "`data:image/png,`" or "`data:image/png;`". If it does, the
image is PNG, and thus the requested type was not supported. (The one
exception to this is if the canvas has either no height or no width, in
which case the result might simply be "`data:,`".)

file containing the image in the canvas, and invokes a callback with a
handle to that object.

The second argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be
returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is "[`image/png`](#image/png)";
that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The third
argument applies if the type is an image format that supports variable
quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#image/jpeg)"), and is a number in the
range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive indicating the desired quality level for the
resulting image.

Returns a newly created [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object
that uses the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element as a placeholder.
Once the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has become a
placeholder for an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object, its
natural size can no longer be changed, and it cannot have a rendering
context. The content of the placeholder canvas is updated on the
[`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)'s <a href="#relevant-agent"
id="the-canvas-element:relevant-agent">relevant agent</a>'s
<a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="the-canvas-element:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>'s
<a href="#update-the-rendering"
id="the-canvas-element:update-the-rendering">update the rendering</a>
steps.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-canvas-todataurl" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLCanvasElement"
dfn-type="method">`toDataURL(``type``, ``quality``)`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-origin-clean-2">origin-clean</a>
    flag is set to false, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="the-canvas-element:securityerror"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-canvas-element:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has no
    pixels (i.e. either its horizontal dimension or its vertical
    dimension is zero), then return the string "`data:,`". (This is the
    shortest <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
    id="the-canvas-element:data-protocol-2"
    data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code>data:</code> URL</a>; it
    represents the empty string in a `text/plain` resource.)

3.  Let `file` be <a href="#a-serialisation-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file"
    id="the-canvas-element:a-serialisation-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file">a
    serialization of this <code>canvas</code> element's bitmap as a file</a>,
    passing `type` and `quality` if given.

4.  If `file` is null, then return "`data:,`".

5.  Return a <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
    id="the-canvas-element:data-protocol-3"
    data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code>data:</code> URL</a>
    representing `file`. [\[RFC2397\]](#refsRFC2397)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-canvas-toblob" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLCanvasElement"
dfn-type="method">`toBlob(``callback``, ``type``, ``quality``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-origin-clean-3">origin-clean</a>
    flag is set to false, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="the-canvas-element:securityerror-2"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-canvas-element:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `result` be null.

3.  If this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has pixels
    (i.e., neither its horizontal dimension nor its vertical dimension
    is zero), then set `result` to a copy of this
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap.

4.  Run these steps
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="the-canvas-element:in-parallel">in
    parallel</a>:

    1.  If `result` is non-null, then set `result` to
        <a href="#a-serialisation-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file"
        id="the-canvas-element:a-serialisation-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file-2">a
        serialization of <var>result</var> as a file</a> with `type` and
        `quality` if given.

    2.  <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
        id="the-canvas-element:queue-an-element-task">Queue an element task</a>
        on the <span id="canvas-blob-serialisation-task-source"
        class="dfn">canvas blob serialization task source</span> given
        the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element to run these steps:

        1.  If `result` is non-null, then set `result` to a new
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob"
            data-x-internal="blob"><code
            id="the-canvas-element:blob-3">Blob</code></a> object,
            created in the <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
            id="the-canvas-element:concept-relevant-realm">relevant realm</a>
            of this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element,
            representing `result`. [\[FILEAPI\]](#refsFILEAPI)

        2.  <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
            id="the-canvas-element:es-invoking-callback-functions"
            data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">Invoke</a>
            `callback` with « `result` » and "`report`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-canvas-transfercontroltooffscreen" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLCanvasElement"
dfn-type="method">`transferControlToOffscreen()`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's
    <a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-11">context mode</a>
    is not set to <a href="#concept-canvas-none"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-none-4">none</a>, throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="the-canvas-element:invalidstateerror-7"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-canvas-element:domexception-9">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `offscreenCanvas` be a new [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)
    object with its width and height equal to the values of the
    [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) and [`height`](#attr-canvas-height)
    content attributes of this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

3.  Set the `offscreenCanvas`'s <a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
    id="the-canvas-element:offscreencanvas-placeholder">placeholder
    <code>canvas</code> element</a> to a weak reference to this
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

4.  Set this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's
    <a href="#concept-canvas-context-mode"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-context-mode-12">context mode</a>
    to <a href="#concept-canvas-placeholder"
    id="the-canvas-element:concept-canvas-placeholder-5">placeholder</a>.

5.  Set the `offscreenCanvas`'s
    <a href="#offscreencanvas-inherited-lang"
    id="the-canvas-element:offscreencanvas-inherited-lang">inherited
    language</a> to the
    <a href="#language" id="the-canvas-element:language">language</a> of
    this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

6.  Set the `offscreenCanvas`'s
    <a href="#offscreencanvas-inherited-direction"
    id="the-canvas-element:offscreencanvas-inherited-direction">inherited
    direction</a> to the <a href="#the-directionality"
    id="the-canvas-element:the-directionality">directionality</a> of
    this [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

7.  Return `offscreenCanvas`.

</div>

};

enumerate methods defined in
[`CanvasUserInterface`](#canvasuserinterface) immediately after the
[`stroke()`](#dom-context-2d-stroke) method on
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) objects.

id="2dcontext:dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-alpha-2"><code>alpha</code></a>`: true ] [, `<a href="#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-desynchronized"
id="2dcontext:dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-desynchronized-2"><code>desynchronized</code></a>`: false ] [, `<a href="#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-colorspace"
id="2dcontext:dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-colorspace-2"><code>colorSpace</code></a>`: 'srgb'] [, `<a href="#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-willreadfrequently"
id="2dcontext:dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-willreadfrequently-2"><code>willReadFrequently</code></a>`: false ]} ])`

Returns a [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) object
that is permanently bound to a particular
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

If the [`alpha`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-alpha) member is
false, then the context is forced to always be opaque.

If the
[`desynchronized`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-desynchronized)
member is true, then the context might be
<a href="#concept-canvas-desynchronized"
id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-desynchronized">desynchronized</a>.

The [`colorSpace`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-colorspace)
member specifies the <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-color-space">color space</a> of the
rendering context.

The [`colorType`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-colortype)
member specifies the <a href="#concept-canvas-color-type"
id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-color-type">color type</a> of the rendering
context.

If the
[`willReadFrequently`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-willreadfrequently)
member is true, then the context is marked for
<a href="#concept-canvas-will-read-frequently"
id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-will-read-frequently">readback
optimization</a>.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-canvas"

  alpha component that is not 1.0; otherwise false.
- [`desynchronized`](#dom-canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings-desynchronized)
  member is true if the context can be
  <a href="#concept-canvas-desynchronized"
