<div algorithm="">

The [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) 2D rendering
context represents a flat linear Cartesian surface whose origin (0,0) is
at the top left corner, with the coordinate space having `x` values
increasing when going right, and `y` values increasing when going down.
The `x`-coordinate of the right-most edge is equal to the width of the
rendering context's
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap">output bitmap</a>
in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>; similarly, the `y`-coordinate of the bottom-most edge is
equal to the height of the rendering context's
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap-2">output
bitmap</a> in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-2" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>.

</div>

The size of the coordinate space does not necessarily represent the size
of the actual bitmaps that the user agent will use internally or during
rendering. On high-definition displays, for instance, the user agent may
internally use bitmaps with four device pixels per unit in the
coordinate space, so that the rendering remains at high quality
throughout. Anti-aliasing can similarly be implemented using
oversampling with bitmaps of a higher resolution than the final image on
the display.

<div class="example">

Using <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-3" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a> to describe the size of a rendering context's
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap-3">output
bitmap</a> does not mean that when rendered the canvas will cover an
equivalent area in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-4" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>. <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-5" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a> are reused for ease of integration with CSS features, such as
text layout.

In other words, the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element below's
rendering context has a 200x200
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap-4">output
bitmap</a> (which internally uses
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-6" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a> as a unit for ease of integration with CSS) and is rendered
as 100x100 <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="2dcontext:&#39;px&#39;-7" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>:

``` html
<canvas width=200 height=200 style=width:100px;height:100px>
```

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="2d-context-creation-algorithm" class="dfn">2D context
creation algorithm</span>, which is passed a `target` (a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element) and `options`, consists of
running these steps:

1.  Let `settings` be the result of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping"
    id="2dcontext:concept-idl-convert"
    data-x-internal="concept-idl-convert">converting</a> `options` to
    the dictionary type
    [`CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`](#canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings).
    (This can throw an exception.)

2.  Let `context` be a new
    [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) object.

3.  Initialize `context`'s [`canvas`](#dom-context-2d-canvas) attribute
    to point to `target`.

4.  Set `context`'s
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap-5">output
    bitmap</a> to the same bitmap as `target`'s bitmap (so that they are
    shared).

5.  <a href="#concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions"
    id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions">Set bitmap
    dimensions</a> to <a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
    id="2dcontext:obtain-numeric-values">the numeric values</a> of
    `target`'s [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) and
    [`height`](#attr-canvas-height) content attributes.

6.  Run the <a href="#canvas-setting-init-bitmap"
    id="2dcontext:canvas-setting-init-bitmap">canvas settings output bitmap
    initialization algorithm</a>, given `context` and `settings`.

7.  Return `context`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to
<span id="concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions" class="dfn">set bitmap
dimensions</span> to `width` and `height`, it must run these steps:

1.  <a href="#reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state"
    id="2dcontext:reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state-2">Reset
    the rendering context to its default state</a>.

2.  Resize the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="2dcontext:output-bitmap-6">output
    bitmap</a> to the new `width` and `height`.

3.  Let `canvas` be the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element to which
    the rendering context's [`canvas`](#dom-context-2d-canvas) attribute
    was initialized.

4.  If <a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
    id="2dcontext:obtain-numeric-values-2">the numeric value</a> of
    `canvas`'s [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) content attribute differs
    from `width`, then set `canvas`'s [`width`](#attr-canvas-width)
    content attribute to the shortest possible string representing
    `width` as a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
    id="2dcontext:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative integer</a>.

5.  If <a href="#obtain-numeric-values"
    id="2dcontext:obtain-numeric-values-3">the numeric value</a> of
    `canvas`'s [`height`](#attr-canvas-height) content attribute differs
    from `height`, then set `canvas`'s [`height`](#attr-canvas-height)
    content attribute to the shortest possible string representing
    `height` as a <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
    id="2dcontext:valid-non-negative-integer-2">valid non-negative
    integer</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

Only one square appears to be drawn in the following example:

``` js
// canvas is a reference to a <canvas> element
var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
context.fillRect(0,0,50,50);
canvas.setAttribute('width', '300'); // clears the canvas
context.fillRect(0,100,50,50);
canvas.width = canvas.width; // clears the canvas
context.fillRect(100,0,50,50); // only this square remains
```

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-canvas" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasRenderingContext2D" dfn-type="attribute">`canvas`</span>
attribute must return the value it was initialized to when the object
was created.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`CanvasColorType`](#canvascolortype) enumeration is used to specify
the <a href="#concept-canvas-color-type"
id="2dcontext:concept-canvas-color-type-3">color type</a> of the
canvas's backing store.

The "<span id="dom-canvascolortype-unorm8" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasColorType" dfn-type="enum-value">`unorm8`</span>" value
indicates that the type for all color components is 8-bit unsigned
normalized.

The "<span id="dom-canvascolortype-float16" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasColorType" dfn-type="enum-value">`float16`</span>" value
indicates that the type for all color components is 16-bit floating
point.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`CanvasFillRule`](#canvasfillrule) enumeration is used to select
the <span id="fill-rule" class="dfn">fill rule</span> algorithm by which
to determine if a point is inside or outside a path.

The "<span id="dom-context-2d-fillrule-nonzero" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillRule" dfn-type="enum-value">`nonzero`</span>" value
indicates the nonzero winding rule, wherein a point is considered to be
outside a shape if the number of times a half-infinite straight line
drawn from that point crosses the shape's path going in one direction is
equal to the number of times it crosses the path going in the other
direction.

The "<span id="dom-context-2d-fillrule-evenodd" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillRule" dfn-type="enum-value">`evenodd`</span>" value
indicates the even-odd rule, wherein a point is considered to be outside
a shape if the number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from
that point crosses the shape's path is even.

If a point is not outside a shape, it is inside the shape.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`ImageSmoothingQuality`](#imagesmoothingquality) enumeration is
used to express a preference for the interpolation quality to use when
smoothing images.

The "<span id="dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality-low" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ImageSmoothingQuality" dfn-type="enum-value">`low`</span>"
value indicates a preference for a low level of image interpolation
quality. Low-quality image interpolation may be more computationally
efficient than higher settings.

The "<span id="dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality-medium" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ImageSmoothingQuality" dfn-type="enum-value">`medium`</span>"
value indicates a preference for a medium level of image interpolation
quality.

The "<span id="dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality-high" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ImageSmoothingQuality" dfn-type="enum-value">`high`</span>"
value indicates a preference for a high level of image interpolation
quality. High-quality image interpolation may be more computationally
expensive than lower settings.

Bilinear scaling is an example of a relatively fast, lower-quality
image-smoothing algorithm. Bicubic or Lanczos scaling are examples of
image-smoothing algorithms that produce higher-quality output. This
specification does not mandate that specific interpolation algorithms be
used.

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.1</span> Implementation notes<a href="#implementation-notes" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

The
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="implementation-notes:output-bitmap">output
bitmap</a>, when it is not directly displayed by the user agent,
implementations can, instead of updating this bitmap, merely remember
the sequence of drawing operations that have been applied to it until
such time as the bitmap's actual data is needed (for example because of
a call to [`drawImage()`](#dom-context-2d-drawimage), or the
[`createImageBitmap()`](#dom-createimagebitmap) factory method). In many
cases, this will be more memory efficient.

The bitmap of a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element is the one
bitmap that's pretty much always going to be needed in practice. The
<a href="#output-bitmap"
id="implementation-notes:output-bitmap-2">output bitmap</a> of a
rendering context, when it has one, is always just an alias to a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap.

Additional bitmaps are sometimes needed, e.g. to enable fast drawing
when the canvas is being painted at a different size than its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
id="implementation-notes:natural-dimensions"
data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural size</a>, or to enable
double buffering so that graphics updates, like page scrolling for
example, can be processed concurrently while canvas draw commands are
being executed.

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.2</span> The canvas settings<a href="#the-canvas-settings" class="self-link"></a>

A [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object has an
<span id="output-bitmap" class="dfn">output bitmap</span> that is
initialized when the object is created.

The
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap">output
bitmap</a> has an <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
flag, which can be set to true or false. Initially, when one of these
bitmaps is created, its <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-origin-clean-2">origin-clean</a>
flag must be set to true.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object also has an
<span id="concept-canvas-alpha" class="dfn">alpha</span> boolean. When a
[`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object's
<a href="#concept-canvas-alpha"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-alpha">alpha</a> is false, then
its alpha component must be fixed to 1.0 (fully opaque) for all pixels,
and attempts to change the alpha component of any pixel must be silently
ignored.

Thus, the bitmap of such a context starts off as
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black"
id="the-canvas-settings:opaque-black"
data-x-internal="opaque-black">opaque black</a> instead of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="the-canvas-settings:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>;
[`clearRect()`](#dom-context-2d-clearrect) always results in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black"
id="the-canvas-settings:opaque-black-2"
data-x-internal="opaque-black">opaque black</a> pixels, every fourth
byte from [`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata) is always
255, the [`putImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-putimagedata) method
effectively ignores every fourth byte in its input, and so on. However,
the alpha component of styles and images drawn onto the canvas are still
honoured up to the point where they would impact the
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap-2">output
bitmap</a>'s alpha component; for instance, drawing a 50% transparent
white square on a freshly created
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap-3">output
bitmap</a> with its <a href="#concept-canvas-alpha"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-alpha-2">alpha</a> set to false
will result in a fully-opaque gray square.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object also has a
<span id="concept-canvas-desynchronized"
class="dfn">desynchronized</span> boolean. When a
[`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object's
<a href="#concept-canvas-desynchronized"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-desynchronized">desynchronized</a>
is true, then the user agent may optimize the rendering of the canvas to
reduce the latency, as measured from input events to rasterization, by
desynchronizing the canvas paint cycle from the event loop, bypassing
the ordinary user agent rendering algorithm, or both. Insofar as this
mode involves bypassing the usual paint mechanisms, rasterization, or
both, it might introduce visible tearing artifacts.

The user agent usually renders on a buffer which is not being displayed,
quickly swapping it and the one being scanned out for presentation; the
former buffer is called back buffer and the latter *front buffer*. A
popular technique for reducing latency is called front buffer rendering,
also known as *single buffer* rendering, where rendering happens in
parallel and racily with the scanning out process. This technique
reduces the latency at the price of potentially introducing tearing
artifacts and can be used to implement in total or part of the
<a href="#concept-canvas-desynchronized"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-desynchronized-2">desynchronized</a>
boolean. [\[MULTIPLEBUFFERING\]](#refsMULTIPLEBUFFERING)

The <a href="#concept-canvas-desynchronized"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-desynchronized-3">desynchronized</a>
boolean can be useful when implementing certain kinds of applications,
such as drawing applications, where the latency between input and
rasterization is critical.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object also has a
<span id="concept-canvas-will-read-frequently" class="dfn">will read
frequently</span> boolean. When a [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings)
object's <a href="#concept-canvas-will-read-frequently"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-will-read-frequently">will read
frequently</a> is true, the user agent may optimize the canvas for
readback operations.

On most devices the user agent needs to decide whether to store the
canvas's
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap-4">output
bitmap</a> on the GPU (this is also called "hardware accelerated"), or
on the CPU (also called "software"). Most rendering operations are more
performant for accelerated canvases, with the major exception being
readback with [`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata),
[`toDataURL()`](#dom-canvas-todataurl), or
[`toBlob()`](#dom-canvas-toblob). [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings)
objects with <a href="#concept-canvas-will-read-frequently"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-will-read-frequently-2">will read
frequently</a> equal to true tell the user agent that the webpage is
likely to perform many readback operations and that it is advantageous
to use a software canvas.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object also has a
<span id="concept-canvas-color-space" class="dfn">color space</span>
setting of type [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#predefinedcolorspace). The
[`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object's
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-color-space">color space</a>
indicates the color space for the
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap-5">output
bitmap</a>.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object also has a
<span id="concept-canvas-color-type" class="dfn">color type</span>
setting of type [`CanvasColorType`](#canvascolortype). The
[`CanvasSettings`](#canvassettings) object's
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-type"
id="the-canvas-settings:concept-canvas-color-type">color type</a>
indicates the data type of the color and alpha components of the pixels
of the
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="the-canvas-settings:output-bitmap-6">output
bitmap</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="canvas-setting-init-bitmap" class="dfn">initialize a
`CanvasSettings` output bitmap</span>, given a

1.  Set `context`'s <a href="#concept-canvas-alpha"

5.  Set `context`'s <a href="#concept-canvas-will-read-frequently"

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.3</span> The canvas state<a href="#the-canvas-state" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasState`](#canvasstate) interface
maintain a stack of drawing states. <span id="drawing-state"
class="dfn">Drawing states</span> consist of:

- The current <a href="#transformations"
  id="the-canvas-state:transformations">transformation matrix</a>.

- The current <a href="#clipping-region"
  id="the-canvas-state:clipping-region">clipping region</a>.

- The current <a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-letter-spacing"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-letter-spacing">letter
  spacing</a>, <a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-word-spacing"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-word-spacing">word
  spacing</a>, <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill
  style</a>, <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
  style</a>, <a href="#concept-canvas-current-filter"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvas-current-filter">filter</a>,
  <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global alpha</a>,
  <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
  id="the-canvas-state:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">compositing
  and blending operator</a>, and
  <a href="#concept-canvasshadowstyles-shadow-color"
  id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvasshadowstyles-shadow-color">shadow
  color</a>.

- The current values of the following attributes:
  [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth),
  [`lineCap`](#dom-context-2d-linecap),
  [`lineJoin`](#dom-context-2d-linejoin),
  [`miterLimit`](#dom-context-2d-miterlimit),
  [`lineDashOffset`](#dom-context-2d-linedashoffset),
  [`shadowOffsetX`](#dom-context-2d-shadowoffsetx),
  [`shadowOffsetY`](#dom-context-2d-shadowoffsety),
  [`shadowBlur`](#dom-context-2d-shadowblur),
  [`lang`](#dom-context-2d-lang), [`font`](#dom-context-2d-font),
  [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign),
  [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline),
  [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction),
  [`fontKerning`](#dom-context-2d-fontkerning),
  [`fontStretch`](#dom-context-2d-fontstretch),
  [`fontVariantCaps`](#dom-context-2d-fontvariantcaps),
  [`textRendering`](#dom-context-2d-textrendering),
  [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingenabled),
  [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality).

- The current
  <a href="#dash-list" id="the-canvas-state:dash-list">dash list</a>.

The rendering context's bitmaps are not part of the drawing state, as
they depend on whether and how the rendering context is bound to a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasState`](#canvasstate) mixin have a
<span id="concept-canvas-context-lost" class="dfn">context lost</span>
boolean, that is initialized to false when the object is created. The
<a href="#concept-canvas-context-lost"
id="the-canvas-state:concept-canvas-context-lost">context lost</a> value
is updated in the <a href="#context-lost-steps"
id="the-canvas-state:context-lost-steps">context lost steps</a>.

Resets the rendering context, which includes the backing buffer, the
drawing state stack, path, and styles.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-iscontextlost"
id="dom-context-2d-iscontextlost-dev"><code>isContextLost</code></a>`()`

Returns true if the rendering context was lost. Context loss can occur
due to driver crashes, running out of memory, etc. In these cases, the
canvas loses its backing storage and takes steps to
<a href="#reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state"
id="the-canvas-state:reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state">reset
the rendering context to its default state</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-save" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasState"
dfn-type="method">`save()`</span> method steps are to push a copy of the
current drawing state onto the drawing state stack.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-restore" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasState"
dfn-type="method">`restore()`</span> method steps are to pop the top
entry in the drawing state stack, and reset the drawing state it
describes. If there is no saved state, then the method must do nothing.

</div>

To <span id="reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state"
class="dfn">reset the rendering context to its default state</span>:

1.  Clear canvas's bitmap to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="the-canvas-state:transparent-black"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

2.  Empty the list of subpaths in context's
    <a href="#current-default-path"
    id="the-canvas-state:current-default-path">current default path</a>.

3.  Clear the context's drawing state stack.

4.  Reset everything that
    <a href="#drawing-state" id="the-canvas-state:drawing-state">drawing
    state</a> consists of to their initial values.

</div>

Objects that implement the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface have
attributes and methods (defined in this section) that control how lines
are treated by the object.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-linewidth" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`lineWidth`</span> attribute gives the width of
lines, in coordinate space units. On getting, it must return the current
value. On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN values must be
ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must change the
current value to the new value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth) attribute must
initially have the value 1.0.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="dom-context-2d-linecap" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles" dfn-type="attribute">`lineCap`</span>
attribute defines the type of endings that UAs will place on the end of
lines. The three valid values are "`butt`", "`round`", and "`square`".

<div algorithm="">

On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, the current
value must be changed to the new value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`lineCap`](#dom-context-2d-linecap) attribute must
initially have the value "`butt`".

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="dom-context-2d-linejoin" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles" dfn-type="attribute">`lineJoin`</span>
attribute defines the type of corners that UAs will place where two
lines meet. The three valid values are "`bevel`", "`round`", and
"`miter`".

<div algorithm="">

On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, the current
value must be changed to the new value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`lineJoin`](#dom-context-2d-linejoin) attribute must
initially have the value "`miter`".

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

When the [`lineJoin`](#dom-context-2d-linejoin) attribute has the value
"`miter`", strokes use the miter limit ratio to decide how to render
joins. The miter limit ratio can be explicitly set using the
<span id="dom-context-2d-miterlimit" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`miterLimit`</span> attribute. On getting, it must
return the current value. On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN
values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must
change the current value to the new value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`miterLimit`](#dom-context-2d-miterlimit) attribute must
initially have the value 10.0.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) object has a
<span id="dash-list" class="dfn">dash list</span>, which is either empty
or consists of an even number of non-negative numbers. Initially, the
<a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list">dash list</a> must be
empty.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-setlinedash" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="method">`setLineDash(``segments``)`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any value in `segments` is not finite (e.g. an Infinity or a NaN
    value), or if any value is negative (less than zero), then return
    (without throwing an exception; user agents could show a message on
    a developer console, though, as that would be helpful for
    debugging).

2.  If the number of elements in `segments` is odd, then let `segments`
    be the concatenation of two copies of `segments`.

3.  Set the object's
    <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-2">dash list</a> to
    `segments`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the <span id="dom-context-2d-getlinedash" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="method">`getLineDash()`</span> method is invoked, it must
return a sequence whose values are the values of the object's
<a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-3">dash list</a>, in the
same order.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

It is sometimes useful to change the "phase" of the dash pattern, e.g.
to achieve a "marching ants" effect. The phase can be set using the
<span id="dom-context-2d-linedashoffset" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPathDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`lineDashOffset`</span> attribute. On getting, it
must return the current value. On setting, infinite and NaN values must
be ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must change the
current value to the new value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`lineDashOffset`](#dom-context-2d-linedashoffset)
attribute must initially have the value 0.0.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="trace-a-path" class="dfn">trace a
path</span>, given an object `style` that implements the
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface, it must
run the following algorithm. This algorithm returns a new
<a href="#concept-path" id="line-styles:concept-path">path</a>.

1.  Let `path` be a copy of the path being traced.

2.  Prune all zero-length
    <a href="#line-segments" id="line-styles:line-segments">line
    segments</a> from `path`.

3.  Remove from `path` any subpaths containing no lines (i.e. subpaths
    with just one point).

4.  Replace each point in each subpath of `path` other than the first
    point and the last point of each subpath by a *join* that joins the
    line leading to that point to the line leading out of that point,
    such that the subpaths all consist of two points (a starting point
    with a line leading out of it, and an ending point with a line
    leading into it), one or more lines (connecting the points and the
    joins), and zero or more joins (each connecting one line to
    another), connected together such that each subpath is a series of
    one or more lines with a join between each one and a point on each
    end.

5.  Add a straight closing line to each closed subpath in `path`
    connecting the last point and the first point of that subpath;
    change the last point to a join (from the previously last line to
    the newly added closing line), and change the first point to a join
    (from the newly added closing line to the first line).

6.  If `style`'s
    <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-4">dash list</a> is
    empty, then jump to the step labeled *convert*.

7.  Let `pattern width` be the concatenation of all the entries of
    `style`'s
    <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-5">dash list</a>, in
    coordinate space units.

8.  For each subpath `subpath` in `path`, run the following substeps.
    These substeps mutate the subpaths in `path` *in vivo*.

    1.  Let `subpath width` be the length of all the lines of `subpath`,
        in coordinate space units.

    2.  Let `offset` be the value of `style`'s
        [`lineDashOffset`](#dom-context-2d-linedashoffset), in
        coordinate space units.

    3.  While `offset` is greater than `pattern width`, decrement it by
        `pattern width`.

        While `offset` is less than zero, increment it by
        `pattern width`.

    4.  Define `L` to be a linear coordinate line defined along all
        lines in `subpath`, such that the start of the first line in the
        subpath is defined as coordinate 0, and the end of the last line
        in the subpath is defined as coordinate `subpath width`.

    5.  Let `position` be 0 minus `offset`.

    6.  Let `index` be 0.

    7.  Let `current state` be *off* (the other states being *on* and
        *zero-on*).

    8.  *Dash on*: Let `segment length` be the value of `style`'s
        <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-6">dash list</a>'s
        `index`th entry.

    9.  Increment `position` by `segment length`.

    10. If `position` is greater than `subpath width`, then end these
        substeps for this subpath and start them again for the next
        subpath; if there are no more subpaths, then jump to the step
        labeled *convert* instead.

    11. If `segment length` is nonzero, then let `current state` be
        *on*.

    12. Increment `index` by one.

    13. *Dash off*: Let `segment length` be the value of `style`'s
        <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-7">dash list</a>'s
        `index`th entry.

    14. Let `start` be the offset `position` on `L`.

    15. Increment `position` by `segment length`.

    16. If `position` is less than zero, then jump to the step labeled
        *post-cut*.

    17. If `start` is less than zero, then let `start` be zero.

    18. If `position` is greater than `subpath width`, then let `end` be
        the offset `subpath width` on `L`. Otherwise, let `end` be the
        offset `position` on `L`.

    19. Jump to the first appropriate step:

        If `segment length` is zero and `current state` is *off*  
        Do nothing, just continue to the next step.

        If `current state` is *off*  
        Cut the line on which `end` finds itself short at `end` and
        place a point there, cutting in two the subpath that it was in;
        remove all line segments, joins, points, and subpaths that are
        between `start` and `end`; and finally place a single point at
        `start` with no lines connecting to it.

        The point has a *directionality* for the purposes of drawing
        line caps (see below). The directionality is the direction that
        the original line had at that point (i.e. when `L` was defined
        above).

        Otherwise  
        Cut the line on which `start` finds itself into two at `start`
        and place a point there, cutting in two the subpath that it was
        in, and similarly cut the line on which `end` finds itself short
        at `end` and place a point there, cutting in two the subpath
        that *it* was in, and then remove all line segments, joins,
        points, and subpaths that are between `start` and `end`.

        If `start` and `end` are the same point, then this results in
        just the line being cut in two and two points being inserted
        there, with nothing being removed, unless a join also happens to
        be at that point, in which case the join must be removed.

    20. *Post-cut*: If `position` is greater than `subpath width`, then
        jump to the step labeled *convert*.

    21. Increment `index` by one. If it is equal to the number of
        entries in `style`'s
        <a href="#dash-list" id="line-styles:dash-list-8">dash list</a>,
        then let `index` be 0.

    22. Return to the step labeled *dash on*.

9.  *Convert*: This is the step that converts the path to a new path
    that represents its stroke.

    Create a new
    <a href="#concept-path" id="line-styles:concept-path-2">path</a>
    that describes the edge of the areas that would be covered if a
    straight line of length equal to `style`'s
    [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth) was swept along each
    subpath in `path` while being kept at an angle such that the line is
    orthogonal to the path being swept, replacing each point with the
    end cap necessary to satisfy `style`'s
    [`lineCap`](#dom-context-2d-linecap) attribute as described
    previously and elaborated below, and replacing each join with the
    join necessary to satisfy `style`'s
    [`lineJoin`](#dom-context-2d-linejoin) type, as defined below.

    **Caps**: Each point has a flat edge perpendicular to the direction
    of the line coming out of it. This is then augmented according to
    the value of `style`'s [`lineCap`](#dom-context-2d-linecap). The
    "`butt`" value means that no additional line cap is added. The
    "`round`" value means that a semi-circle with the diameter equal to
    `style`'s [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth) width must
    additionally be placed on to the line coming out of each point. The
    "`square`" value means that a rectangle with the length of `style`'s
    [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth) width and the width of half
    `style`'s [`lineWidth`](#dom-context-2d-linewidth) width, placed
    flat against the edge perpendicular to the direction of the line
    coming out of the point, must be added at each point.

    Points with no lines coming out of them must have two caps placed
    back-to-back as if it was really two points connected to each other
    by an infinitesimally short straight line in the direction of the
    point's *directionality* (as defined above).

    **Joins**: In addition to the point where a join occurs, two
    additional points are relevant to each join, one for each line: the
    two corners found half the line width away from the join point, one
    perpendicular to each line, each on the side furthest from the other
    line.

    A triangle connecting these two opposite corners with a straight
    line, with the third point of the triangle being the join point,
    must be added at all joins. The
    [`lineJoin`](#dom-context-2d-linejoin) attribute controls whether
    anything else is rendered. The three aforementioned values have the
    following meanings:

    The "`bevel`" value means that this is all that is rendered at
    joins.

    The "`round`" value means that an arc connecting the two
    aforementioned corners of the join, abutting (and not overlapping)
    the aforementioned triangle, with the diameter equal to the line
    width and the origin at the point of the join, must be added at
    joins.

    The "`miter`" value means that a second triangle must (if it can
    given the miter length) be added at the join, with one line being
    the line between the two aforementioned corners, abutting the first
    triangle, and the other two being continuations of the outside edges
    of the two joining lines, as long as required to intersect without
    going over the miter length.

    The miter length is the distance from the point where the join
    occurs to the intersection of the line edges on the outside of the
    join. The miter limit ratio is the maximum allowed ratio of the
    miter length to half the line width. If the miter length would cause
    the miter limit ratio (as set by `style`'s
    [`miterLimit`](#dom-context-2d-miterlimit) attribute) to be
    exceeded, then this second triangle must not be added.

    The subpaths in the newly created path must be oriented such that
    for any point, the number of times a half-infinite straight line
    drawn from that point crosses a subpath is even if and only if the
    number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from that same
    point crosses a subpath going in one direction is equal to the
    number of times it crosses a subpath going in the other direction.

10. Return the newly created path.

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.5</span> Text styles<a href="#text-styles" class="self-link"></a>

when resolving fonts. "[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-lang-inherit)" takes
the language from the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
id="text-styles:document-element"
data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a> when there is no
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element.

The default is "[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-lang-inherit)".

`styles``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-textrendering"
id="text-styles:dom-context-2d-textrendering"><code>textRendering</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

Returns the current text rendering settings.

Can be set, to change the text rendering. The possible values and their
meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is
"[`auto`](#dom-context-2d-textrendering-auto)".

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-wordspacing"
id="dom-context-2d-wordspacing-dev"><code>wordSpacing</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

`styles``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-wordspacing"
id="text-styles:dom-context-2d-wordspacing"><code>wordSpacing</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

Returns the current spacing between words in the text.

Can be set, to change spacing between words. Values that cannot be
parsed as a CSS <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths"
id="text-styles:length-2-2"
data-x-internal="length-2">&lt;length&gt;</a> are ignored. The default
is "`0px`".

Objects that implement the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface have
attributes (defined in this section) that control how text is laid out
(rasterized or outlined) by the object. Such objects can also have a
<span id="font-style-source-object" class="dfn">font style source
object</span>. For
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) objects, this is
the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element given by the value of the
context's [`canvas`](#dom-context-2d-canvas) attribute. For
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)
objects, this is the <a href="#associated-offscreencanvas-object"
id="text-styles:associated-offscreencanvas-object">associated
<code>OffscreenCanvas</code> object</a>.

<div algorithm="">

Font resolution for the <a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object">font style source object</a>
requires a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-font-loading/#font-source"
id="text-styles:font-source" data-x-internal="font-source">font
source</a>. This is determined for a given `object` implementing
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) by the following
steps: [\[CSSFONTLOAD\]](#refsCSSFONTLOAD)

1.  If `object`'s <a href="#font-style-source-object"
    id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-2">font style source object</a>
    is a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, return the element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="text-styles:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
    document</a>.

2.  Otherwise, `object`'s <a href="#font-style-source-object"
    id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-3">font style source object</a>
    is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object:

    1.  Let `global` be `object`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="text-styles:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a>.

    2.  If `global` is a [`Window`](#window) object, then return
        `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
        id="text-styles:concept-document-window">associated
        <code>Document</code></a>.

    3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="text-styles:assert"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `global` implements
        [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope).

    4.  Return `global`.

</div>

<div class="example">

This is an example of font resolution with a regular
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element with ID `c1`.

``` js
const font = new FontFace("MyCanvasFont", "url(mycanvasfont.ttf)");
documents.fonts.add(font);

const context = document.getElementById("c1").getContext("2d");
document.fonts.ready.then(function() {
  context.font = "64px MyCanvasFont";
  context.fillText("hello", 0, 0);
});
```

In this example, the canvas will display text using `mycanvasfont.ttf`
as its font.

</div>

<div class="example">

This is an example of how font resolution can happen using
[`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas). Assuming a
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element with ID `c2` which is
transferred to a worker like so:

``` js
const offscreenCanvas = document.getElementById("c2").transferControlToOffscreen();
worker.postMessage(offscreenCanvas, [offscreenCanvas]);
```

Then, in the worker:

``` js
self.onmessage = function(ev) {
  const transferredCanvas = ev.data;
  const context = transferredCanvas.getContext("2d");
  const font = new FontFace("MyFont", "url(myfont.ttf)");
  self.fonts.add(font);
  self.fonts.ready.then(function() {
    context.font = "64px MyFont";
    context.fillText("hello", 0, 0);
  });
};
```

In this example, the canvas will display a text using `myfont.ttf`.
Notice that the font is only loaded inside the worker, and not in the
document context.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-font" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles" dfn-type="attribute">`font`</span> IDL
attribute, on setting, must be
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar"
id="text-styles:parse-something-according-to-a-css-grammar"
data-x-internal="parse-something-according-to-a-css-grammar">parsed as a
CSS &lt;'font'&gt; value</a> (but without supporting
property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit'), and the
resulting font must be assigned to the context, with the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height"
id="text-styles:&#39;line-height&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;line-height&#39;">'line-height'</a> component
forced to 'normal', with the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop"
id="text-styles:&#39;font-size&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;font-size&#39;">'font-size'</a> component
converted to <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="text-styles:&#39;px&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>, and with system fonts being computed to explicit values. If
the new value is syntactically incorrect (including using
property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit' or 'initial'),
then it must be ignored, without assigning a new font value.
[\[CSS\]](#refsCSS)

</div>

Font family names must be interpreted in the context of the
<a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-4">font style source object</a>
when the font is to be used; any fonts embedded using `@font-face` or
loaded using [`FontFace`](#fontface) objects that are visible to the
<a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-5">font style source object</a>
must therefore be available once they are loaded. (Each
<a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-6">font style source object</a>
has a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-font-loading/#font-source"
id="text-styles:font-source-2" data-x-internal="font-source">font
source</a>, which determines what fonts are available.) If a font is
used before it is fully loaded, or if the
<a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-7">font style source object</a>
does not have that font in scope at the time the font is to be used,
then it must be treated as if it was an unknown font, falling back to
another as described by the relevant CSS specifications.
[\[CSSFONTS\]](#refsCSSFONTS) [\[CSSFONTLOAD\]](#refsCSSFONTLOAD)

<div algorithm="">

On getting, the [`font`](#dom-context-2d-font) attribute must return the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value"
id="text-styles:serializing-a-css-value"
data-x-internal="serializing-a-css-value">serialized form</a> of the
current font of the context (with no
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height"
id="text-styles:&#39;line-height&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;line-height&#39;">'line-height'</a> component).
[\[CSSOM\]](#refsCSSOM)

</div>

<div class="example">

For example, after the following statement:

``` js
context.font = 'italic 400 12px/2 Unknown Font, sans-serif';
```

...the expression `context.font` would evaluate to the string
"`italic 12px "Unknown Font", sans-serif`". The "400" font-weight
doesn't appear because that is the default value. The line-height
doesn't appear because it is forced to "normal", the default value.

</div>

When the object implementing the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the font of the context must be set to 10px sans-serif. When
the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop"
id="text-styles:&#39;font-size&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;font-size&#39;">'font-size'</a> component is set
to lengths using percentages,
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#em"
id="text-styles:&#39;em&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;em&#39;">'em'</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#ex"
id="text-styles:&#39;ex&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;ex&#39;">'ex'</a>
units, or the 'larger' or 'smaller' keywords, these must be interpreted
relative to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="text-styles:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop"
id="text-styles:&#39;font-size&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;font-size&#39;">'font-size'</a> property of the
<a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-8">font style source object</a>
at the time that the attribute is set, if it is an element. When the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-weight-prop"
id="text-styles:&#39;font-weight&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;font-weight&#39;">'font-weight'</a> component is
set to the relative values 'bolder' and 'lighter', these must be
interpreted relative to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="text-styles:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-weight-prop"
id="text-styles:&#39;font-weight&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;font-weight&#39;">'font-weight'</a> property of
the <a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-9">font style source object</a>
at the time that the attribute is set, if it is an element. If the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="text-styles:computed-value-3"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed values</a> are undefined for a
particular case (e.g. because the <a href="#font-style-source-object"
id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-10">font style source
object</a> is not an element or is not
<a href="#being-rendered" id="text-styles:being-rendered">being
rendered</a>), then the relative keywords must be interpreted relative
to the normal-weight 10px sans-serif default.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-textalign" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`textAlign`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed
to the new value. When the object implementing the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) attribute must
initially have the value [`start`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-start).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`textBaseline`</span> IDL attribute, on getting,
must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be
changed to the new value. When the object implementing the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute
must initially have the value
[`alphabetic`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-alphabetic).

</div>

Objects that implement the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface have an
associated <span id="concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language"
class="dfn">language</span> value used to localize font rendering. Valid
values are a BCP 47 language tag, the empty string, or
"<span id="dom-context-2d-lang-inherit" class="dfn">inherit</span>"
where the language comes from the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element)
element's language, or the associated
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
id="text-styles:document-element-2"
data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a> when there is no
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element. Initially, the
<a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language"
id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language">language</a>
must be "[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-lang-inherit)".

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-lang" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles" dfn-type="attribute">`lang`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="text-styles:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language"
id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language-2">language</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`lang`](#dom-context-2d-lang) setter steps are to set
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="text-styles:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language"
id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language-3">language</a>
to the given value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-direction" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`direction`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed
to the new value. When the object implementing the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction) attribute must
initially have the value
"[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-direction-inherit)".

</div>

Objects that implement the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface have
attributes that control the spacing between letters and words. Such
objects have associated
<span id="concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-letter-spacing"
class="dfn">letter spacing</span> and
<span id="concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-word-spacing" class="dfn">word
spacing</span> values, which are CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths"
id="text-styles:length-2-3"
data-x-internal="length-2">&lt;length&gt;</a> values. Initially, both
must be the result of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar"
id="text-styles:parse-something-according-to-a-css-grammar-2"
data-x-internal="parse-something-according-to-a-css-grammar">parsing</a>
"`0px`" as a CSS <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths"
id="text-styles:length-2-4"
data-x-internal="length-2">&lt;length&gt;</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-textrendering" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTextDrawingStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`textRendering`</span> IDL attribute, on getting,
must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be
changed to the new value. When the object implementing the
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interface is
created, the [`textRendering`](#dom-context-2d-textrendering) attribute
must initially have the value
"[`auto`](#dom-context-2d-textrendering-auto)".

</div>

The [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) attribute's allowed
keywords are as follows:

<span id="dom-context-2d-textalign-start" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextAlign" dfn-type="enum-value">`start`</span>  
Align to the start edge of the text (left side in left-to-right text,
right side in right-to-left text).

<span id="dom-context-2d-textalign-end" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextAlign" dfn-type="enum-value">`end`</span>  
Align to the end edge of the text (right side in left-to-right text,
left side in right-to-left text).

<span id="dom-context-2d-textalign-left" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextAlign" dfn-type="enum-value">`left`</span>  
Align to the left.

<span id="dom-context-2d-textalign-right" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextAlign" dfn-type="enum-value">`right`</span>  
Align to the right.

<span id="dom-context-2d-textalign-center" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextAlign" dfn-type="enum-value">`center`</span>  
Align to the center.

The [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute's allowed
keywords correspond to alignment points in the font:

<img src="/images/baselines.png" width="738" height="300"
alt="The em-over baseline is roughly at the top of the glyphs in a font, the hanging baseline is where some glyphs like आ are anchored, the middle is half-way between the em-over and em-under baselines, the alphabetic baseline is where characters like Á, ÿ, f, and Ω are anchored, the ideographic-under baseline is where glyphs like 私 and 達 are anchored, and the em-under baseline is roughly at the bottom of the glyphs in a font. The top and bottom of the bounding box can be far from these baselines, due to glyphs extending far outside em-over and em-under baselines." />

The keywords map to these alignment points as follows:

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-top" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`top`</span>  
The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="text-styles:em-over-baseline"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a>

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-hanging" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`hanging`</span>  
The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline"
id="text-styles:hanging-baseline"
data-x-internal="hanging-baseline">hanging baseline</a>

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-middle" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`middle`</span>  
Halfway between the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="text-styles:em-over-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a> and the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="text-styles:em-under-baseline"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a>

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-alphabetic" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`alphabetic`</span>  
The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
id="text-styles:alphabetic-baseline"
data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a>

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-ideographic" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`ideographic`</span>  
The <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline"
id="text-styles:ideographic-under-baseline"
data-x-internal="ideographic-under-baseline">ideographic-under
baseline</a>

<span id="dom-context-2d-textbaseline-bottom" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasTextBaseline" dfn-type="enum-value">`bottom`</span>  
The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="text-styles:em-under-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a>

The [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction) attribute's allowed
keywords are as follows:

<span id="dom-context-2d-direction-ltr" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasDirection" dfn-type="enum-value">`ltr`</span>  
Treat input to the <a href="#text-preparation-algorithm"
id="text-styles:text-preparation-algorithm">text preparation
algorithm</a> as left-to-right text.

<span id="dom-context-2d-direction-rtl" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasDirection" dfn-type="enum-value">`rtl`</span>  
Treat input to the <a href="#text-preparation-algorithm"
id="text-styles:text-preparation-algorithm-2">text preparation
algorithm</a> as right-to-left text.

<span id="dom-context-2d-direction-inherit" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasDirection" dfn-type="enum-value">`inherit`</span>  
Use the process in the <a href="#text-preparation-algorithm"
id="text-styles:text-preparation-algorithm-3">text preparation
algorithm</a> to obtain the text direction from the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element,
<a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
id="text-styles:offscreencanvas-placeholder">placeholder
<code>canvas</code> element</a>, or
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
id="text-styles:document-element-3"
data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>.

The [`fontKerning`](#dom-context-2d-fontkerning) attribute's allowed
keywords are as follows:

<span id="dom-context-2d-fontkerning-auto" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasFontKerning" dfn-type="enum-value">`auto`</span>  
Kerning is applied at the discretion of the user agent.

<span id="dom-context-2d-fontkerning-normal" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasFontKerning" dfn-type="enum-value">`normal`</span>  
Kerning is applied.

<span id="dom-context-2d-fontkerning-none" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasFontKerning" dfn-type="enum-value">`none`</span>  
Kerning is not applied.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="text-preparation-algorithm" class="dfn">text preparation
algorithm</span> is as follows. It takes as input a string `text`, a
[`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) object `target`,
and an optional length `maxWidth`. It returns an array of glyph shapes,
each positioned on a common coordinate space, a `physical alignment`
whose value is one of *left*, *right*, and *center*, and an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="text-styles:inline-box" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>.
(Most callers of this algorithm ignore the `physical alignment` and the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="text-styles:inline-box-2" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
box</a>.)

1.  If `maxWidth` was provided but is less than or equal to zero or
    equal to NaN, then return an empty array.

2.  Replace all
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
    id="text-styles:space-characters"
    data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> in `text`
    with U+0020 SPACE characters.

3.  Let `font` be the current font of `target`, as given by that
    object's [`font`](#dom-context-2d-font) attribute.

4.  Let `language` be the `target`'s
    <a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language"
    id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-language-4">language</a>.

5.  If `language` is "[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-lang-inherit)":

    1.  Let `sourceObject` be `object`'s
        <a href="#font-style-source-object"
        id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-11">font style source
        object</a>.

    2.  If `sourceObject` is a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element,
        then set `language` to the `sourceObject`'s
        <a href="#language" id="text-styles:language">language</a>.

    3.  Otherwise:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="text-styles:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
            `sourceObject` is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)
            object.

        2.  Set `language` to the `sourceObject`'s
            <a href="#offscreencanvas-inherited-lang"
            id="text-styles:offscreencanvas-inherited-lang">inherited language</a>.

6.  If `language` is the empty string, then set `language` to
    <a href="#concept-explicitly-unknown"
    id="text-styles:concept-explicitly-unknown">explicitly unknown</a>.

7.  Apply the appropriate step from the following list to determine the
    value of `direction`:

    If the `target` object's [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction) attribute has the value "[`ltr`](#dom-context-2d-direction-ltr)"  
    Let `direction` be
    '<a href="#concept-ltr" id="text-styles:concept-ltr">ltr</a>'.

    If the `target` object's [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction) attribute has the value "[`rtl`](#dom-context-2d-direction-rtl)"  
    Let `direction` be
    '<a href="#concept-rtl" id="text-styles:concept-rtl">rtl</a>'.

    If the `target` object's [`direction`](#dom-context-2d-direction) attribute has the value "[`inherit`](#dom-context-2d-direction-inherit)"  
    1.  Let `sourceObject` be `object`'s
        <a href="#font-style-source-object"
        id="text-styles:font-style-source-object-12">font style source
        object</a>.

    2.  If `sourceObject` is a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element,
        then let `direction` be `sourceObject`'s
        <a href="#the-directionality"
        id="text-styles:the-directionality">directionality</a>.

    3.  Otherwise:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="text-styles:assert-3" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
            `sourceObject` is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)
            object.

        2.  Let `direction` be `sourceObject`'s
            <a href="#offscreencanvas-inherited-direction"
            id="text-styles:offscreencanvas-inherited-direction">inherited
            direction</a>.

8.  Form a hypothetical infinitely-wide CSS
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#line-box"
    id="text-styles:line-box" data-x-internal="line-box">line box</a>
    containing a single
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-3" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a> containing the text `text`, with the CSS
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#content-language"
    id="text-styles:content-language"
    data-x-internal="content-language">content language</a> set to
    `language`, and with its CSS properties set as follows:

    | Property | Source |
    |----|----|
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
    id="text-styles:&#39;direction&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> | `direction` |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-prop"
    id="text-styles:&#39;font&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;font&#39;">'font'</a> | `font` |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-kerning"
    id="text-styles:&#39;font-kerning&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;font-kerning&#39;">'font-kerning'</a> | `target`'s [`fontKerning`](#dom-context-2d-fontkerning) |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch"
    id="text-styles:&#39;font-stretch&#39;-9"
    data-x-internal="&#39;font-stretch&#39;">'font-stretch'</a> | `target`'s [`fontStretch`](#dom-context-2d-fontstretch) |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps"
    id="text-styles:&#39;font-variant-caps&#39;-7"
    data-x-internal="&#39;font-variant-caps&#39;">'font-variant-caps'</a> | `target`'s [`fontVariantCaps`](#dom-context-2d-fontvariantcaps) |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property"
    id="text-styles:&#39;letter-spacing&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;letter-spacing&#39;">'letter-spacing'</a> | `target`'s <a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-letter-spacing"
    id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-letter-spacing-3">letter
    spacing</a> |
    | <a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering"
    id="text-styles:svg-text-rendering-5"
    data-x-internal="svg-text-rendering">SVG text-rendering</a> | `target`'s [`textRendering`](#dom-context-2d-textrendering) |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
    id="text-styles:&#39;white-space&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> | 'pre' |
    | <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#propdef-word-spacing"
    id="text-styles:&#39;word-spacing&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;word-spacing&#39;">'word-spacing'</a> | `target`'s <a href="#concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-word-spacing"
    id="text-styles:concept-canvastextdrawingstyles-word-spacing-3">word
    spacing</a> |

    and with all other properties set to their initial values.

9.  If `maxWidth` was provided and the hypothetical width of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-4" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a> in the hypothetical
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#line-box"
    id="text-styles:line-box-2" data-x-internal="line-box">line box</a>
    is greater than `maxWidth`
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="text-styles:&#39;px&#39;-2" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
    pixels</a>, then change `font` to have a more condensed font (if one
    is available or if a reasonably readable one can be synthesized by
    applying a horizontal scale factor to the font) or a smaller font,
    and return to the previous step.

10. The `anchor point` is a point on the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-5" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>, and the `physical alignment` is one of the values *left*,
    *right*, and *center*. These variables are determined by the
    [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) and
    [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) values as follows:

    Horizontal position:

    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`left`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-left)  
    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`start`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-start) and `direction` is 'ltr'  
    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`end`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-end) and `direction` is 'rtl'  
    Set the `anchor point`'s horizontal position to the left edge of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-6" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>, and let `physical alignment` be *left*.

    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`right`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-right)  
    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`end`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-end) and `direction` is 'ltr'  
    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`start`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-start) and `direction` is 'rtl'  
    Set the `anchor point`'s horizontal position to the right edge of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-7" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>, and let `physical alignment` be *right*.

    If [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) is [`center`](#dom-context-2d-textalign-center)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s horizontal position to half way between the
    left and right edges of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-8" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>, and let `physical alignment` be *center*.

    Vertical position:

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`top`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-top)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to the top of the em box
    of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-9" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`hanging`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-hanging)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline"
    id="text-styles:hanging-baseline-2"
    data-x-internal="hanging-baseline">hanging baseline</a> of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font-2"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-10" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`middle`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-middle)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to half way between the
    bottom and the top of the em box of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font-3"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-11" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`alphabetic`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-alphabetic)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
    id="text-styles:alphabetic-baseline-2"
    data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a> of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font-4"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-12" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`ideographic`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-ideographic)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to the <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline"
    id="text-styles:ideographic-under-baseline-2"
    data-x-internal="ideographic-under-baseline">ideographic-under
    baseline</a> of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font-5"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-13" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

    If [`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) is [`bottom`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-bottom)  
    Set the `anchor point`'s vertical position to the bottom of the em
    box of the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
    id="text-styles:first-available-font-6"
    data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a> of
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-14" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>.

11. Let `result` be an array constructed by iterating over each glyph in
    the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-15" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a> from left to right (if any), adding to the array, for each
    glyph, the shape of the glyph as it is in the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
    id="text-styles:inline-box-16" data-x-internal="inline-box">inline
    box</a>, positioned on a coordinate space using
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="text-styles:&#39;px&#39;-3" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
    pixels</a> with its origin at the `anchor point`.

12. Return `result`, `physical alignment`, and the inline box.

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.6</span> Building paths<a href="#building-paths" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasPath`](#canvaspath) interface have a
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path">path</a>. A
<span id="concept-path" class="dfn">path</span> has a list of zero or
more subpaths. Each subpath consists of a list of one or more points,
connected by straight or curved <span id="line-segments"
class="dfn">line segments</span>, and a flag indicating whether the
subpath is closed or not. A closed subpath is one where the last point
of the subpath is connected to the first point of the subpath by a
straight line. Subpaths with only one point are ignored when painting
the path.

<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-2">Paths</a>
have a <span id="need-new-subpath" class="dfn">need new subpath</span>
flag. When this flag is set, certain APIs create a new subpath rather
than extending the previous one. When a
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-3">path</a> is
created, its
<a href="#need-new-subpath" id="building-paths:need-new-subpath">need
new subpath</a> flag must be set.

When an object implementing the [`CanvasPath`](#canvaspath) interface is
created, its
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-4">path</a> must
be initialized to zero subpaths.

`path``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-ellipse"
id="building-paths:dom-context-2d-ellipse"><code>ellipse</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``, ``radiusX``, ``radiusY``, ``rotation``, ``startAngle``, ``endAngle`` [, ``counterclockwise``])`

Adds points to the subpath such that the arc described by the
circumference of the ellipse described by the arguments, starting at the
given start angle and ending at the given end angle, going in the given
direction (defaulting to clockwise), is added to the path, connected to
the previous point by a straight line.

Throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="building-paths:indexsizeerror-3"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="building-paths:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a> if the given
radius is negative.
