`path``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-rect"
id="building-paths:dom-context-2d-rect"><code>rect</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`

Adds a new closed subpath to the path, representing the given rectangle.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-roundrect"
id="dom-context-2d-roundrect-dev"><code>roundRect</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``, ``radii``)`

`path``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-roundrect"
id="building-paths:dom-context-2d-roundrect"><code>roundRect</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``, ``radii``)`

Adds a new closed subpath to the path representing the given rounded
rectangle. `radii` is either a list of radii or a single radius
representing the corners of the rectangle in pixels. If a list is
provided, the number and order of these radii function in the same way
as the CSS <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-radius"
id="building-paths:&#39;border-radius&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-radius&#39;">'border-radius'</a> property.
A single radius behaves the same way as a list with a single element.

If `w` and `h` are both greater than or equal to 0, or if both are
smaller than 0, then the path is drawn clockwise. Otherwise, it is drawn
counterclockwise.

When `w` is negative, the rounded rectangle is flipped horizontally,
which means that the radius values that normally apply to the left
corners are used on the right and vice versa. Similarly, when `h` is
negative, the rounded rect is flipped vertically.

When a value `r` in `radii` is a number, the corresponding corner(s) are
drawn as circular arcs of radius `r`.

When a value `r` in `radii` is an object with `{ x, y }` properties, the
corresponding corner(s) are drawn as elliptical arcs whose `x` and `y`
radii are equal to `r.x` and `r.y`, respectively.

When the sum of the `radii` of two corners of the same edge is greater
than the length of the edge, all the `radii` of the rounded rectangle
are scaled by a factor of length / (`r1` + `r2`). If multiple edges have
this property, the scale factor of the edge with the smallest scale
factor is used. This is consistent with CSS behavior.

Throws a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
id="building-paths:js-rangeerror">RangeError</code></a> if `radii` is a
list whose size is not one, two, three, or four.

Throws a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
id="building-paths:js-rangeerror-2">RangeError</code></a> if a value in
`radii` is a negative number, or is an `{ x, y }` object whose `x` or
`y` properties are negative numbers.

The following methods allow authors to manipulate the
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-5">paths</a> of
objects implementing the [`CanvasPath`](#canvaspath) interface.

For objects implementing the [`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) and
[`CanvasTransform`](#canvastransform) interfaces, the points passed to
the methods, and the resulting lines added to
<a href="#current-default-path"
id="building-paths:current-default-path">current default path</a> by
these methods, must be transformed according to the
<a href="#transformations" id="building-paths:transformations">current
transformation matrix</a> before being added to the path.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-moveto" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`moveTo(``x``, ``y``)`</span> method, when invoked,
must run these steps:

1.  If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Create a new subpath with the specified point as its first (and
    only) point.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to <span id="ensure-there-is-a-subpath"
class="dfn">ensure there is a subpath</span> for a coordinate (`x`, `y`)
on a
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-6">path</a>, the
user agent must check to see if the
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-7">path</a> has
its
<a href="#need-new-subpath" id="building-paths:need-new-subpath-2">need
new subpath</a> flag set. If it does, then the user agent must create a
new subpath with the point (`x`, `y`) as its first (and only) point, as
if the [`moveTo()`](#dom-context-2d-moveto) method had been called, and
must then unset the
<a href="#concept-path" id="building-paths:concept-path-8">path</a>'s
<a href="#need-new-subpath" id="building-paths:need-new-subpath-3">need
new subpath</a> flag.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-closepath" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`closePath()`</span> method, when invoked, must do
nothing if the object's path has no subpaths. Otherwise, it must mark
the last subpath as closed, create a new subpath whose first point is
the same as the previous subpath's first point, and finally add this new
subpath to the path.

</div>

If the last subpath had more than one point in its list of points, then
this is equivalent to adding a straight line connecting the last point
back to the first point of the last subpath, thus "closing" the subpath.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

New points and the lines connecting them are added to subpaths using the
methods described below. In all cases, the methods only modify the last
subpath in the object's path.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-lineto" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`lineTo(``x``, ``y``)`</span> method, when invoked,
must run these steps:

1.  If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  If the object's path has no subpaths, then
    <a href="#ensure-there-is-a-subpath"
    id="building-paths:ensure-there-is-a-subpath">ensure there is a
    subpath</a> for (`x`, `y`).

3.  Otherwise, connect the last point in the subpath to the given point
    (`x`, `y`) using a straight line, and then add the given point (`x`,
    `y`) to the subpath.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-quadraticcurveto" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`quadraticCurveTo(``cpx``, ``cpy``, ``x``, ``y``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  <a href="#ensure-there-is-a-subpath"
    id="building-paths:ensure-there-is-a-subpath-2">Ensure there is a
    subpath</a> for (`cpx`, `cpy`).

3.  Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (`x`, `y`)
    using a quadratic Bézier curve with control point (`cpx`, `cpy`).
    [\[BEZIER\]](#refsBEZIER)

4.  Add the given point (`x`, `y`) to the subpath.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-beziercurveto" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`bezierCurveTo(``cp1x``, ``cp1y``, ``cp2x``, ``cp2y``, ``x``, ``y``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  <a href="#ensure-there-is-a-subpath"
    id="building-paths:ensure-there-is-a-subpath-3">Ensure there is a
    subpath</a> for (`cp1x`, `cp1y`).

3.  Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (`x`, `y`)
    using a cubic Bézier curve with control points (`cp1x`, `cp1y`) and
    (`cp2x`, `cp2y`). [\[BEZIER\]](#refsBEZIER)

4.  Add the point (`x`, `y`) to the subpath.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-arcto" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`arcTo(``x1``, ``y1``, ``x2``, ``y2``, ``radius``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  <a href="#ensure-there-is-a-subpath"
    id="building-paths:ensure-there-is-a-subpath-4">Ensure there is a
    subpath</a> for (`x1`, `y1`).

3.  If `radius` is negative, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="building-paths:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="building-paths:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  Let the point (`x0`, `y0`) be the last point in the subpath,
    transformed by the inverse of the
    <a href="#transformations" id="building-paths:transformations-2">current
    transformation matrix</a> (so that it is in the same coordinate
    system as the points passed to the method).

5.  If the point (`x0`, `y0`) is equal to the point (`x1`, `y1`), or if
    the point (`x1`, `y1`) is equal to the point (`x2`, `y2`), or if
    `radius` is zero, then add the point (`x1`, `y1`) to the subpath,
    and connect that point to the previous point (`x0`, `y0`) by a
    straight line.

6.  Otherwise, if the points (`x0`, `y0`), (`x1`, `y1`), and (`x2`,
    `y2`) all lie on a single straight line, then add the point (`x1`,
    `y1`) to the subpath, and connect that point to the previous point
    (`x0`, `y0`) by a straight line.

7.  Otherwise, let `The Arc` be the shortest arc given by circumference
    of the circle that has radius `radius`, and that has one point
    tangent to the half-infinite line that crosses the point (`x0`,
    `y0`) and ends at the point (`x1`, `y1`), and that has a different
    point tangent to the half-infinite line that ends at the point
    (`x1`, `y1`) and crosses the point (`x2`, `y2`). The points at which
    this circle touches these two lines are called the start and end
    tangent points respectively. Connect the point (`x0`, `y0`) to the
    start tangent point by a straight line, adding the start tangent
    point to the subpath, and then connect the start tangent point to
    the end tangent point by `The Arc`, adding the end tangent point to
    the subpath.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-arc" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`arc(``x``, ``y``, ``radius``, ``startAngle``, ``endAngle``, ``counterclockwise``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run the <a href="#ellipse-method-steps"
id="building-paths:ellipse-method-steps">ellipse method steps</a> with
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="building-paths:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `x`, `y`, `radius`, `radius`, 0,
`startAngle`, `endAngle`, and `counterclockwise`.

</div>

This makes it equivalent to [`ellipse()`](#dom-context-2d-ellipse)
except that both radii are equal and `rotation` is 0.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-ellipse" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`ellipse(``x``, ``y``, ``radiusX``, ``radiusY``, ``rotation``, ``startAngle``, ``endAngle``, ``counterclockwise``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run the <a href="#ellipse-method-steps"
id="building-paths:ellipse-method-steps-2">ellipse method steps</a> with
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="building-paths:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `x`, `y`,
`radiusX`, `radiusY`, `rotation`, `startAngle`, `endAngle`, and
`counterclockwise`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps"
class="dfn">determine the point on an ellipse steps</span>, given
`ellipse`, and `angle`, are:

1.  Let `eccentricCircle` be the circle that shares its origin with
    `ellipse`, with a radius equal to the semi-major axis of `ellipse`.

2.  Let `outerPoint` be the point on `eccentricCircle`'s circumference
    at `angle` measured in radians clockwise from `ellipse`'s semi-major
    axis.

3.  Let `chord` be the line perpendicular to `ellipse`'s major axis
    between this axis and `outerPoint`.

4.  Return the point on `chord` that crosses `ellipse`'s circumference.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="ellipse-method-steps" class="dfn">ellipse method
steps</span>, given `canvasPath`, `x`, `y`, `radiusX`, `radiusY`,
`rotation`, `startAngle`, `endAngle`, and `counterclockwise`, are:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  If either `radiusX` or `radiusY` are negative, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="building-paths:indexsizeerror-5"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="building-paths:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  If `canvasPath`'s path has any subpaths, then add a straight line
    from the last point in the subpath to the start point of the arc.

4.  Add the start and end points of the arc to the subpath, and connect
    them with an arc. The arc and its start and end points are defined
    as follows:

    Consider an ellipse that has its origin at (`x`, `y`), that has a
    major-axis radius `radiusX` and a minor-axis radius `radiusY`, and
    that is rotated about its origin such that its semi-major axis is
    inclined `rotation` radians clockwise from the x-axis.

    If `counterclockwise` is false and `endAngle` − `startAngle` is
    greater than or equal to 2π, or, if `counterclockwise` is *true* and
    `startAngle` − `endAngle` is greater than or equal to 2π, then the
    arc is the whole circumference of this ellipse, and both the start
    point and the end point are the result of running the
    <a href="#determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps"
    id="building-paths:determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps">determine
    the point on an ellipse steps</a> given this ellipse and
    `startAngle`.

    Otherwise, the start point is the result of running the
    <a href="#determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps"
    id="building-paths:determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps-2">determine
    the point on an ellipse steps</a> given this ellipse and
    `startAngle`, the end point is the result of running the
    <a href="#determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps"
    id="building-paths:determine-the-point-on-an-ellipse-steps-3">determine
    the point on an ellipse steps</a> given this ellipse and `endAngle`,
    and the arc is the path along the circumference of this ellipse from
    the start point to the end point, going counterclockwise if
    `counterclockwise` is true, and clockwise otherwise. Since the
    points are on the ellipse, as opposed to being simply angles from
    zero, the arc can never cover an angle greater than 2π radians.

    Even if the arc covers the entire circumference of the ellipse and
    there are no other points in the subpath, the path is not closed
    unless the [`closePath()`](#dom-context-2d-closepath) method is
    appropriately invoked.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-rect" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`rect(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Create a new subpath containing just the four points (`x`, `y`),
    (`x`+`w`, `y`), (`x`+`w`, `y`+`h`), (`x`, `y`+`h`), in that order,
    with those four points connected by straight lines.

3.  Mark the subpath as closed.

4.  Create a new subpath with the point (`x`, `y`) as the only point in
    the subpath.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-roundrect" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasPath"
dfn-type="method">`roundRect(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``, ``radii``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  If any of `x`, `y`, `w`, or `h` are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  If `radii` is an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unrestricted-double"
    data-x-internal="idl-unrestricted-double"><code
    id="building-paths:idl-unrestricted-double">unrestricted double</code></a>
    or <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dictdef-dompointinit"
    data-x-internal="dompointinit"><code
    id="building-paths:dompointinit">DOMPointInit</code></a>, then set
    `radii` to « `radii` ».

3.  If `radii` is not a list of size one, two, three, or four, then
    throw a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
    data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
    id="building-paths:js-rangeerror-3">RangeError</code></a>.

4.  Let `normalizedRadii` be an empty list.

5.  For each `radius` of `radii`:

    1.  If `radius` is a
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dictdef-dompointinit"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-2">DOMPointInit</code></a>:

        1.  If
            `radius`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-x">x</code></a>"\] or
            `radius`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-y">y</code></a>"\] is
            infinite or NaN, then return.

        2.  If
            `radius`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-2">x</code></a>"\] or
            `radius`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-2">y</code></a>"\] is
            negative, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
            data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
            id="building-paths:js-rangeerror-4">RangeError</code></a>.

        3.  Otherwise, append `radius` to `normalizedRadii`.

    2.  If `radius` is a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unrestricted-double"
        data-x-internal="idl-unrestricted-double"><code
        id="building-paths:idl-unrestricted-double-2">unrestricted double</code></a>:

        1.  If `radius` is infinite or NaN, then return.

        2.  If `radius` is negative, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
            data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
            id="building-paths:js-rangeerror-5">RangeError</code></a>.

        3.  Otherwise, append «\[
            "<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-3">x</code></a>" →
            `radius`,
            "<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
            data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
            id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-4">y</code></a>" →
            `radius` \]» to `normalizedRadii`.

6.  Let `upperLeft`, `upperRight`, `lowerRight`, and `lowerLeft` be
    null.

7.  If `normalizedRadii`'s size is 4, then set `upperLeft` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[0\], set `upperRight` to `normalizedRadii`\[1\],
    set `lowerRight` to `normalizedRadii`\[2\], and set `lowerLeft` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[3\].

8.  If `normalizedRadii`'s size is 3, then set `upperLeft` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[0\], set `upperRight` and `lowerLeft` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[1\], and set `lowerRight` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[2\].

9.  If `normalizedRadii`'s size is 2, then set `upperLeft` and
    `lowerRight` to `normalizedRadii`\[0\] and set `upperRight` and
    `lowerLeft` to `normalizedRadii`\[1\].

10. If `normalizedRadii`'s size is 1, then set `upperLeft`,
    `upperRight`, `lowerRight`, and `lowerLeft` to
    `normalizedRadii`\[0\].

11. Corner curves must not overlap. Scale all radii to prevent this:

    1.  Let `top` be
        `upperLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-5">x</code></a>"\] +
        `upperRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-6">x</code></a>"\].

    2.  Let `right` be
        `upperRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-3">y</code></a>"\] +
        `lowerRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-4">y</code></a>"\].

    3.  Let `bottom` be
        `lowerRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-7">x</code></a>"\] +
        `lowerLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-8">x</code></a>"\].

    4.  Let `left` be
        `upperLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-5">y</code></a>"\] +
        `lowerLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-6">y</code></a>"\].

    5.  Let `scale` be the minimum value of the ratios `w` / `top`, `h`
        / `right`, `w` / `bottom`, `h` / `left`.

    6.  If `scale` is less than 1, then set the
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-9">x</code></a> and
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-7">y</code></a> members of
        `upperLeft`, `upperRight`, `lowerLeft`, and `lowerRight` to
        their current values multiplied by `scale`.

12. Create a new subpath:

    1.  Move to the point (`x` +
        `upperLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-10">x</code></a>"\], `y`).

    2.  Draw a straight line to the point (`x` + `w` −
        `upperRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-11">x</code></a>"\], `y`).

    3.  Draw an arc to the point (`x` + `w`, `y` +
        `upperRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-8">y</code></a>"\]).

    4.  Draw a straight line to the point (`x` + `w`, `y` + `h` −
        `lowerRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-9">y</code></a>"\]).

    5.  Draw an arc to the point (`x` + `w` −
        `lowerRight`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-12">x</code></a>"\], `y` +
        `h`).

    6.  Draw a straight line to the point (`x` +
        `lowerLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-13">x</code></a>"\], `y` +
        `h`).

    7.  Draw an arc to the point (`x`, `y` + `h` −
        `lowerLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-10">y</code></a>"\]).

    8.  Draw a straight line to the point (`x`, `y` +
        `upperLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-y"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-y-11">y</code></a>"\]).

    9.  Draw an arc to the point (`x` +
        `upperLeft`\["<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x"
        data-x-internal="dompointinit-x"><code
        id="building-paths:dompointinit-x-14">x</code></a>"\], `y`).

13. Mark the subpath as closed.

14. Create a new subpath with the point (`x`, `y`) as the only point in
    the subpath.

</div>

This is designed to behave similarly to the CSS <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-radius"
id="building-paths:&#39;border-radius&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-radius&#39;">'border-radius'</a> property.

Adds to the path the path given by the argument.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-path2d" class="dfn" dfn-for="Path2D"
dfn-type="constructor">`Path2D(``path``)`</span> constructor, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  Let `output` be a new [`Path2D`](#path2d) object.

2.  If `path` is not given, then return `output`.

3.  If `path` is a [`Path2D`](#path2d) object, then add all subpaths of
    `path` to `output` and return `output`. (In other words, it returns
    a copy of the argument.)

4.  Let `svgPath` be the result of parsing and interpreting `path`
    according to SVG 2's rules for path data. [\[SVG\]](#refsSVG)

    The resulting path could be empty. SVG defines error handling rules
    for parsing and applying path data.

5.  Let (`x`, `y`) be the last point in `svgPath`.

6.  Add all the subpaths, if any, from `svgPath` to `output`.

7.  Create a new subpath in `output` with (`x`, `y`) as the only point
    in the subpath.

8.  Return `output`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-path2d-addpath" class="dfn" dfn-for="Path2D"
dfn-type="method">`addPath(``path``, ``transform``)`</span> method, when
invoked on a [`Path2D`](#path2d) object `a`, must run these steps:

1.  If the [`Path2D`](#path2d) object `path` has no subpaths, then
    return.

2.  Let `matrix` be the result of <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary"
    id="path2d-objects:create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary"
    data-x-internal="create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary">creating a
    <code>DOMMatrix</code> from the 2D dictionary</a> `transform`.

3.  If one or more of `matrix`'s
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m11-element" data-x-internal="m11-element">m11
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m12-element" data-x-internal="m12-element">m12
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m21-element" data-x-internal="m21-element">m21
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m22-element" data-x-internal="m22-element">m22
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m41-element" data-x-internal="m41-element">m41
    element</a>, or
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element"
    id="path2d-objects:m42-element" data-x-internal="m42-element">m42
    element</a> are infinite or NaN, then return.

4.  Create a copy of all the subpaths in `path`. Let `c` be this copy.

5.  Transform all the coordinates and lines in `c` by the transform
    matrix `matrix`.

6.  Let (`x`, `y`) be the last point in the last subpath of `c`.

7.  Add all the subpaths in `c` to `a`.

8.  Create a new subpath in `a` with (`x`, `y`) as the only point in the
    subpath.

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.8</span> <span class="dfn">Transformations</span><a href="#transformations" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasTransform`](#canvastransform)
interface have a <span id="current-transformation-matrix"
class="dfn">current transformation matrix</span>, as well as methods
(described in this section) to manipulate it. When an object
implementing the [`CanvasTransform`](#canvastransform) interface is
created, its transformation matrix must be initialized to the identity
matrix.

The <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix">current
transformation matrix</a> is applied to coordinates when creating the
<a href="#current-default-path"
id="transformations:current-default-path">current default path</a>, and
when painting text, shapes, and [`Path2D`](#path2d) objects, on objects
implementing the [`CanvasTransform`](#canvastransform) interface.

The transformations must be performed in reverse order.

For instance, if a scale transformation that doubles the width is
applied to the canvas, followed by a rotation transformation that
rotates drawing operations by a quarter turn, and a rectangle twice as
wide as it is tall is then drawn on the canvas, the actual result will
be a square.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-scale"
id="dom-context-2d-scale-dev"><code>scale</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``)`

Changes the <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-9">current
transformation matrix</a> to the identity matrix.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-scale" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform" dfn-type="method">`scale(``x``, ``y``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Add the scaling transformation described by the arguments to the
    <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-10">current
    transformation matrix</a>. The `x` argument represents the scale
    factor in the horizontal direction and the `y` argument represents
    the scale factor in the vertical direction. The factors are
    multiples.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-rotate" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform" dfn-type="method">`rotate(``angle``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If `angle` is infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Add the rotation transformation described by the argument to the
    <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-11">current
    transformation matrix</a>. The `angle` argument represents a
    clockwise rotation angle expressed in radians.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-translate" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform"
dfn-type="method">`translate(``x``, ``y``)`</span> method, when invoked,
must run these steps:

1.  If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Add the translation transformation described by the arguments to the
    <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-12">current
    transformation matrix</a>. The `x` argument represents the
    translation distance in the horizontal direction and the `y`
    argument represents the translation distance in the vertical
    direction. The arguments are in coordinate space units.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-transform" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform"
dfn-type="method">`transform(``a``, ``b``, ``c``, ``d``, ``e``, ``f``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Replace the <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-13">current
    transformation matrix</a> with the result of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-multiply"
    id="transformations:matrix-multiplication"
    data-x-internal="matrix-multiplication">multiplying</a> the
    <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-14">current
    transformation matrix</a> with the matrix described by:

    |     |     |     |
    |-----|-----|-----|
    | `a` | `c` | `e` |
    | `b` | `d` | `f` |
    | 0   | 0   | 1   |

</div>

The arguments `a`, `b`, `c`, `d`, `e`, and `f` are sometimes called
`m11`, `m12`, `m21`, `m22`, `dx`, and `dy` or `m11`, `m21`, `m12`,
`m22`, `dx`, and `dy`. Care ought to be taken in particular with the
order of the second and third arguments (`b` and `c`) as their order
varies from API to API and APIs sometimes use the notation `m12`/`m21`
and sometimes `m21`/`m12` for those positions.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-gettransform" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform" dfn-type="method">`getTransform()`</span>
method, when invoked, must return a newly created
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dommatrix"
data-x-internal="dommatrix"><code
id="transformations:dommatrix-2">DOMMatrix</code></a> representing a
copy of the <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-15">current
transformation matrix</a> matrix of the context.

</div>

This returned object is not live, so updating it will not affect the
<a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-16">current
transformation matrix</a>, and updating the
<a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-17">current
transformation matrix</a> will not affect an already returned
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dommatrix"
data-x-internal="dommatrix"><code
id="transformations:dommatrix-3">DOMMatrix</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-settransform" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform"
dfn-type="method">`setTransform(``a``, ``b``, ``c``, ``d``, ``e``, ``f``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Reset the <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-18">current
    transformation matrix</a> to the matrix described by:

    |     |     |     |
    |-----|-----|-----|
    | `a` | `c` | `e` |
    | `b` | `d` | `f` |
    | 0   | 0   | 1   |

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-settransform-matrix" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform"
dfn-type="method">`setTransform(``transform``)`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  Let `matrix` be the result of <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary"
    id="transformations:create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary"
    data-x-internal="create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary">creating a
    <code>DOMMatrix</code> from the 2D dictionary</a> `transform`.

2.  If one or more of `matrix`'s
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element"
    id="transformations:m11-element" data-x-internal="m11-element">m11
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element"
    id="transformations:m12-element" data-x-internal="m12-element">m12
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element"
    id="transformations:m21-element" data-x-internal="m21-element">m21
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element"
    id="transformations:m22-element" data-x-internal="m22-element">m22
    element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element"
    id="transformations:m41-element" data-x-internal="m41-element">m41
    element</a>, or
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element"
    id="transformations:m42-element" data-x-internal="m42-element">m42
    element</a> are infinite or NaN, then return.

3.  Reset the <a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
    id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-19">current
    transformation matrix</a> to `matrix`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-resettransform" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasTransform" dfn-type="method">`resetTransform()`</span>
method, when invoked, must reset the
<a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="transformations:current-transformation-matrix-20">current
transformation matrix</a> to the identity matrix.

</div>

<div class="note" var-scope="">

Given a matrix of the form created by the
[`transform()`](#dom-context-2d-transform) and
[`setTransform()`](#dom-context-2d-settransform) methods, i.e.,

|     |     |     |
|-----|-----|-----|
| `a` | `c` | `e` |
| `b` | `d` | `f` |
| 0   | 0   | 1   |

the resulting transformed coordinates after transform matrix
multiplication will be

`x`<sub>new</sub> = `a` `x` + `c` `y` + `e`  
`y`<sub>new</sub> = `b` `x` + `d` `y` + `f`

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.9</span> Image sources for 2D rendering contexts<a href="#image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts"
class="self-link"></a>

Some methods on the [`CanvasDrawImage`](#canvasdrawimage) and
[`CanvasFillStrokeStyles`](#canvasfillstrokestyles) interfaces take the
union type [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) as an argument.

This union type allows objects implementing any of the following
interfaces to be used as image sources:

- [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#htmlorsvgimageelement)
  ([`img`](#the-img-element) or
  <a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/embedded.html#ImageElement"
  id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:svg-image"
  data-x-internal="svg-image">SVG <code>image</code></a> elements)
- [`HTMLVideoElement`](#htmlvideoelement) ([`video`](#the-video-element)
  elements)
- [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#htmlcanvaselement)
  ([`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements)
- [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)
- [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap)
- <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface"
  data-x-internal="videoframe"><code
  id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:videoframe">VideoFrame</code></a>

Although not formally specified as such,
<a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/embedded.html#ImageElement"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:svg-image-2"
data-x-internal="svg-image">SVG <code>image</code></a> elements are
expected to be implemented nearly identical to [`img`](#the-img-element)
elements. That is,
<a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/embedded.html#ImageElement"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:svg-image-3"
data-x-internal="svg-image">SVG <code>image</code></a> elements share
the fundamental concepts and features of [`img`](#the-img-element)
elements.

The [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) interface can be created from a number
of other image-representing types, including [`ImageData`](#imagedata).

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument"
class="dfn">check the usability of the `image` argument</span>, where
`image` is a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object, run these
steps:

1.  Switch on `image`:

    [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#htmlorsvgimageelement)  
    If `image`'s <a href="#current-request"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:current-request">current
    request</a>'s <a href="#img-req-state"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:img-req-state">state</a>
    is <a href="#img-error"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:img-error">broken</a>,
    then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:invalidstateerror"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

    If `image` is not <a href="#img-good"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:img-good">fully
    decodable</a>, then return *bad*.

    If `image` has a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:natural-width"
    data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a> or
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:natural-height"
    data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a> (or both) equal
    to zero, then return *bad*.

    [`HTMLVideoElement`](#htmlvideoelement)  
    If `image`'s [`readyState`](#dom-media-readystate) attribute is
    either [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#dom-media-have_nothing) or
    [`HAVE_METADATA`](#dom-media-have_metadata), then return *bad*.

    [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#htmlcanvaselement)  
    [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)  
    If `image` has either a horizontal dimension or a vertical dimension
    equal to zero, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:invalidstateerror-2"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

    [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap)  
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface"
    data-x-internal="videoframe"><code
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:videoframe-2">VideoFrame</code></a>  
    If `image`'s <a href="#detached"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:detached">[[Detached]]</a>
    internal slot value is set to true, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:invalidstateerror-3"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Return *good*.

</div>

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
[`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#htmlorsvgimageelement), the element's image
must be used as the source image.

Specifically, when a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object
represents an animated image in an
[`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#htmlorsvgimageelement), the user agent must
use the default image of the animation (the one that the format defines
is to be used when animation is not supported or is disabled), or, if
there is no such image, the first frame of the animation, when rendering
the image for [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d)
APIs.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
[`HTMLVideoElement`](#htmlvideoelement), then the frame at the
<a href="#current-playback-position"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:current-playback-position">current
playback position</a> when the method with the argument is invoked must
be used as the source image when rendering the image for
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) APIs, and the
source image's dimensions must be the
<a href="#concept-video-intrinsic-width"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:concept-video-intrinsic-width">natural
width</a> and <a href="#concept-video-intrinsic-height"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:concept-video-intrinsic-height">natural
height</a> of the <a href="#media-resource"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:media-resource">media
resource</a> (i.e., after any aspect-ratio correction has been applied).

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
[`HTMLCanvasElement`](#htmlcanvaselement), the element's bitmap must be
used as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
element that is <a href="#being-rendered"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:being-rendered">being
rendered</a> and that element has been resized, the original image data
of the source image must be used, not the image as it is rendered (e.g.
[`width`](#attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#attr-dim-height) attributes
on the source element have no effect on how the object is interpreted
when rendering the image for
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) APIs).

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap), the object's bitmap image data must be
used as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents an
[`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas), the object's bitmap must be used
as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource) object represents a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface"
data-x-internal="videoframe"><code
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:videoframe-3">VideoFrame</code></a>,
the object's pixel data must be used as the source image, and the source
image's dimensions must be the object's <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-display-width-slot"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:display-width"
data-x-internal="display-width">[[display width]]</a> and <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-display-height-slot"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:display-height"
data-x-internal="display-height">[[display height]]</a>.

<div algorithm="">

An object `image` <span id="the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean"
class="dfn">is not origin-clean</span> if, switching on `image`'s type:

[`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#htmlorsvgimageelement)  
`image`'s <a href="#current-request"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:current-request-2">current
request</a>'s <a href="#img-req-data"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:img-req-data">image data</a>
is <a href="#cors-cross-origin"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:cors-cross-origin">CORS-cross-origin</a>.

[`HTMLVideoElement`](#htmlvideoelement)  
`image`'s <a href="#media-data"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:media-data">media data</a>
is <a href="#cors-cross-origin"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:cors-cross-origin-2">CORS-cross-origin</a>.

[`HTMLCanvasElement`](#htmlcanvaselement)  
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap)  
[`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas)  
`image`'s bitmap's <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
flag is false.

</div>

Returns the current style used for filling shapes.

Can be set, to change the
<a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill

The style can be either a string containing a CSS color, or a
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) or [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern)
object. Invalid values are ignored.

Returns the current style used for stroking shapes.

Can be set, to change the
<a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
style.</a>

The style can be either a string containing a CSS color, or a
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) or [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern)
object. Invalid values are ignored.

Objects that implement the
[`CanvasFillStrokeStyles`](#canvasfillstrokestyles) interface have
attributes and methods (defined in this section) that control how shapes
are treated by the object.

Such objects have associated
<span id="concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style" class="dfn">fill
style</span> and <span id="concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
class="dfn">stroke style</span> values, which are either CSS colors,
[`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern)s, or
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient)s. Initially, both must be the result
of <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:parsed-as-a-css-color-value"
data-x-internal="parsed-as-a-css-color-value">parsing</a> the string
"`#000000`".

When the value is a CSS color, it must not be affected by the
transformation matrix when used to draw on bitmaps.

When set to a [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern) or
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) object, changes made to the object
after the assignment do affect subsequent stroking or filling of shapes.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-fillstyle" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles" dfn-type="attribute">`fillStyle`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style-2">fill
    style</a> is a CSS color, then return the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:serialisation-of-a-color"
    data-x-internal="serialisation-of-a-color">serialization</a> of that
    color with <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:html-compatible-serialization-is-requested"
    data-x-internal="html-compatible-serialization-is-requested">HTML-compatible
    serialization requested</a>.

2.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style-3">fill
    style</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`fillStyle`](#dom-context-2d-fillstyle) setter steps are:

1.  If the given value is a string, then:

    1.  Let `context` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        [`canvas`](#dom-context-2d-canvas) attribute's value, if that is
        an element; otherwise null.

    2.  Let `parsedValue` be the result of
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:parsed-as-a-css-color-value-2"
        data-x-internal="parsed-as-a-css-color-value">parsing</a> the
        given value with `context` if non-null.

    3.  If `parsedValue` is failure, then return.

    4.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style-4">fill
        style</a> to `parsedValue`.

    5.  Return.

2.  If the given value is a [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern) object
    that is marked as <a href="#concept-canvas-pattern-not-origin-clean"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-pattern-not-origin-clean">not
    origin-clean</a>, then set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
    flag to false.

3.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style-5">fill
    style</a> to the given value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-strokestyle" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles"
dfn-type="attribute">`strokeStyle`</span> getter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style-2">stroke
    style</a> is a CSS color, then return the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:serialisation-of-a-color-2"
    data-x-internal="serialisation-of-a-color">serialization</a> of that
    color with <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:html-compatible-serialization-is-requested-2"
    data-x-internal="html-compatible-serialization-is-requested">HTML-compatible
    serialization requested</a>.

2.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style-3">stroke
    style</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`strokeStyle`](#dom-context-2d-strokestyle) setter steps are:

1.  If the given value is a string, then:

    1.  Let `context` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        [`canvas`](#dom-context-2d-canvas) attribute's value, if that is
        an element; otherwise null.

    2.  Let `parsedValue` be the result of
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:parsed-as-a-css-color-value-3"
        data-x-internal="parsed-as-a-css-color-value">parsing</a> the
        given value with `context` if non-null.

    3.  If `parsedValue` is failure, then return.

    4.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-10" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
        id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style-4">stroke
        style</a> to `parsedValue`.

    5.  Return.

2.  If the given value is a [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern) object
    that is marked as <a href="#concept-canvas-pattern-not-origin-clean"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-pattern-not-origin-clean-2">not
    origin-clean</a>, then set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-11" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-origin-clean-2">origin-clean</a>
    flag to false.

3.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:this-12" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style-5">stroke
    style</a> to the given value.

</div>

There are three types of gradients, linear gradients, radial gradients,
and conic gradients, represented by objects implementing the opaque
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) interface.

Once a gradient has been created (see below), stops are placed along it
to define how the colors are distributed along the gradient. The color
of the gradient at each stop is the color specified for that stop,
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:converting-colors"
data-x-internal="converting-colors">converted</a> to the
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-color-space">context's color
space</a>. Between each such stop, the colors and the alpha component
must be linearly interpolated in the
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:concept-canvas-color-space-2">context's color
space</a> without premultiplying the alpha value to find the color to
use at that offset. Before the first stop, the color must be the color
of the first stop. After the last stop, the color must be the color of
the last stop. When there are no stops, the gradient is
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

`gradient``.`<a href="#dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop"
id="dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop-dev"><code>addColorStop</code></a>`(``offset``, ``color``)`

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasGradient"
dfn-type="method">`addColorStop(``offset``, ``color``)`</span> method on
the [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient), when invoked, must run these
steps:

1.  If the `offset` is less than 0 or greater than 1, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:indexsizeerror-3"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `parsed color` be the result of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:parsed-as-a-css-color-value-4"
    data-x-internal="parsed-as-a-css-color-value">parsing</a> `color`.

    No element is passed to the parser because
    [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) objects are
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element)-neutral — a
    [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) object created by one
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) can be used by another, and there is
    therefore no way to know which is the "element in question" at the
    time that the color is specified.

3.  If `parsed color` is failure, throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:syntaxerror-2"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  Place a new stop on the gradient, at offset `offset` relative to the
    whole gradient, and with the color `parsed color`.

    If multiple stops are added at the same offset on a gradient, then
    they must be placed in the order added, with the first one closest
    to the start of the gradient, and each subsequent one
    infinitesimally further along towards the end point (in effect
    causing all but the first and last stop added at each point to be
    ignored).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createlineargradient" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles"
dfn-type="method">`createLinearGradient(``x0``, ``y0``, ``x1``, ``y1``)`</span>
method takes four arguments that represent the start point (`x0`, `y0`)
and end point (`x1`, `y1`) of the gradient. The method, when invoked,
must return a linear [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) initialized
with the specified line.

Linear gradients must be rendered such that all points on a line
perpendicular to the line that crosses the start and end points have the
color at the point where those two lines cross (with the colors coming
from the [interpolation and extrapolation](#interpolation) described
above). The points in the linear gradient must be transformed as
described by the <a href="#transformations"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transformations">current transformation
matrix</a> when rendering.

If `x0` = `x1` and `y0` = `y1`, then the linear gradient must paint
nothing.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createradialgradient" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles"
dfn-type="method">`createRadialGradient(``x0``, ``y0``, ``r0``, ``x1``, ``y1``, ``r1``)`</span>
method takes six arguments, the first three representing the start
circle with origin (`x0`, `y0`) and radius `r0`, and the last three
representing the end circle with origin (`x1`, `y1`) and radius `r1`.
The values are in coordinate space units. If either of `r0` or `r1` are
negative, then an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:indexsizeerror-4"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a> must
be thrown. Otherwise, the method, when invoked, must return a radial
[`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) initialized with the two specified
circles.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Radial gradients must be rendered by following these steps:

1.  If `x`<sub>`0`</sub> = `x`<sub>`1`</sub> and
    `y`<sub>`0`</sub> = `y`<sub>`1`</sub> and
    `r`<sub>`0`</sub> = `r`<sub>`1`</sub>, then the radial gradient must
    paint nothing. Return.

2.  Let
    x(`ω`) = (`x`<sub>`1`</sub>-`x`<sub>`0`</sub>)`ω` + `x`<sub>`0`</sub>.

    Let
    y(`ω`) = (`y`<sub>`1`</sub>-`y`<sub>`0`</sub>)`ω` + `y`<sub>`0`</sub>.

    Let
    r(`ω`) = (`r`<sub>`1`</sub>-`r`<sub>`0`</sub>)`ω` + `r`<sub>`0`</sub>.

    Let the color at `ω` be the color at that position on the gradient
    (with the colors coming from the [interpolation and
    extrapolation](#interpolation) described above).

3.  For all values of `ω` where r(`ω`) \> 0, starting with the value of
    `ω` nearest to positive infinity and ending with the value of `ω`
    nearest to negative infinity, draw the circumference of the circle
    with radius r(`ω`) at position (x(`ω`), y(`ω`)), with the color at
    `ω`, but only painting on the parts of the bitmap that have not yet
    been painted on by earlier circles in this step for this rendering
    of the gradient.

</div>

This effectively creates a cone, touched by the two circles defined in
the creation of the gradient, with the part of the cone before the start
circle (0.0) using the color of the first offset, the part of the cone
after the end circle (1.0) using the color of the last offset, and areas
outside the cone untouched by the gradient
(<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transparent-black-2"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>).

The resulting radial gradient must then be transformed as described by
the <a href="#transformations"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transformations-2">current transformation
matrix</a> when rendering.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createconicgradient" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles"
dfn-type="method">`createConicGradient(``startAngle``, ``x``, ``y``)`</span>
method takes three arguments, the first argument, `startAngle`,
represents the angle in radians at which the gradient begins, and the
last two arguments, (`x`, `y`), represent the center of the gradient in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>. The method, when invoked,
must return a conic [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) initialized with
the specified center and angle.

It follows the same rendering rule as CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#funcdef-conic-gradient"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:&#39;conic-gradient&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;conic-gradient&#39;">'conic-gradient'</a> and it
is equivalent to CSS 'conic-gradient(from `adjustedStartAngle`rad at
`x`px `y`px, `angularColorStopList`)'. Here:

- `adjustedStartAngle` is given by `startAngle` + π/2;

- `angularColorStopList` is given by the color stops that have been
  added to the [`CanvasGradient`](#canvasgradient) using
  [`addColorStop()`](#dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop), with the color
  stop offsets interpreted as percentages.

</div>

Gradients must be painted only where the relevant stroking or filling
effects requires that they be drawn.

image and repeats in the direction(s) given by the `repetition`
argument.

The allowed values for `repetition` are `repeat` (both directions),

`no-repeat` (neither). If the `repetition` argument is empty, the value

image is a canvas with no data, throws an

</div>

Sets the transformation matrix that will be used when rendering the
pattern during a fill or stroke painting operation.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createpattern" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasFillStrokeStyles"
dfn-type="method">`createPattern(``image``, ``repetition``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  Let `usability` be the result of
    <a href="#check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument">checking
    the usability of</a> `image`.

2.  If `usability` is *bad*, then return null.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `usability` is *good*.

4.  If `repetition` is the empty string, then set it to "`repeat`".

5.  If `repetition` is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:identical-to"
    data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> one of "`repeat`",
    "`repeat-x`", "`repeat-y`", or "`no-repeat`", then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:syntaxerror-3"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

6.  Let `pattern` be a new [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern) object with
    the image `image` and the repetition behavior given by `repetition`.

7.  If `image` <a href="#the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean">is
    not origin-clean</a>, then mark `pattern` as
    <span id="concept-canvas-pattern-not-origin-clean" class="dfn">not
    origin-clean</span>.

8.  Return `pattern`.

Modifying the `image` used when creating a
[`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern) object after calling the
[`createPattern()`](#dom-context-2d-createpattern) method must not
affect the pattern(s) rendered by the [`CanvasPattern`](#canvaspattern)
object.

</div>

Patterns have a transformation matrix, which controls how the pattern is
used when it is painted. Initially, a pattern's transformation matrix
must be the identity matrix.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-canvaspattern-settransform" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasPattern"
dfn-type="method">`setTransform(``transform``)`</span> method, when
invoked, must run these steps:

1.  Let `matrix` be the result of <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary"
    data-x-internal="create-a-dommatrix-from-a-2d-dictionary">creating a
    <code>DOMMatrix</code> from the 2D dictionary</a> `transform`.

2.  If one or more of `matrix`'s
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m11-element"
    data-x-internal="m11-element">m11 element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m12-element"
    data-x-internal="m12-element">m12 element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m21-element"
    data-x-internal="m21-element">m21 element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m22-element"
    data-x-internal="m22-element">m22 element</a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m41-element"
    data-x-internal="m41-element">m41 element</a>, or
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:m42-element"
    data-x-internal="m42-element">m42 element</a> are infinite or NaN,
    then return.

3.  Reset the pattern's transformation matrix to `matrix`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a pattern is to be rendered within an area, the user agent must run
the following steps to determine what is rendered:

1.  Create an infinite
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transparent-black-3"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a> bitmap.

2.  Place a copy of the image on the bitmap, anchored such that its top
    left corner is at the origin of the coordinate space, with one
    coordinate space unit per
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:&#39;px&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixel</a> of the image, then
    place repeated copies of this image horizontally to the left and
    right, if the repetition behavior is "`repeat-x`", or vertically up
    and down, if the repetition behavior is "`repeat-y`", or in all four
    directions all over the bitmap, if the repetition behavior is
    "`repeat`".

    If the original image data is a bitmap image, then the value painted
    at a point in the area of the repetitions is computed by filtering
    the original image data. When scaling up, if the
    [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingenabled)
    attribute is set to false, then the image must be rendered using
    nearest-neighbor interpolation. Otherwise, the user agent may use
    any filtering algorithm (for example bilinear interpolation or
    nearest-neighbor). User agents which support multiple filtering
    algorithms may use the value of the
    [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality)
    attribute to guide the choice of filtering algorithm. When such a
    filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the original
    image data, it must instead use the value from wrapping the pixel's
    coordinates to the original image's dimensions. (That is, the filter
    uses 'repeat' behavior, regardless of the value of the pattern's
    repetition behavior.)

3.  Transform the resulting bitmap according to the pattern's
    transformation matrix.

4.  Transform the resulting bitmap again, this time according to the
    <a href="#transformations"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transformations-3">current transformation
    matrix</a>.

5.  Replace any part of the image outside the area in which the pattern
    is to be rendered with
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transparent-black-4"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

6.  The resulting bitmap is what is to be rendered, with the same origin
    and same scale.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

If a radial gradient or repeated pattern is used when the transformation
matrix is singular, then the resulting style must be
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="fill-and-stroke-styles:transparent-black-5"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a> (otherwise the
gradient or pattern would be collapsed to a point or line, leaving the
other pixels undefined). Linear gradients and solid colors always define
all points even with singular transformation matrices.

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.11</span> Drawing rectangles to the bitmap<a href="#drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasRect`](#canvasrect) interface provide
the following methods for immediately drawing rectangles to the bitmap.
The methods each take four arguments; the first two give the `x` and `y`
coordinates of the top left of the rectangle, and the second two give
the width `w` and height `h` of the rectangle, respectively.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#transformations"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:transformations">current
transformation matrix</a> must be applied to the following four
coordinates, which form the path that must then be closed to get the
specified rectangle: (`x`, `y`), (`x`+`w`, `y`), (`x`+`w`, `y`+`h`),
(`x`, `y`+`h`).

</div>

Shapes are painted without affecting the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:current-default-path">current
default path</a>, and are subject to the <a href="#clipping-region"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:clipping-region">clipping
region</a>, and, with the exception of
[`clearRect()`](#dom-context-2d-clearrect), also
<a href="#shadows" id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:shadows">shadow
effects</a>, <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global
alpha</a>, and the <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
compositing and blending operator</a>.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-clearrect"
id="dom-context-2d-clearrect-dev"><code>clearRect</code></a>`(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

Paints the box that outlines the given rectangle onto the bitmap, using
the current stroke style.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-clearrect" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasRect"
dfn-type="method">`clearRect(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`</span> method,
when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Let `pixels` be the set of pixels in the specified rectangle that
    also intersect the current <a href="#clipping-region"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:clipping-region-2">clipping
    region</a>.

3.  Clear the pixels in `pixels` to a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:transparent-black-2"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>, erasing
    any previous image.

</div>

If either height or width are zero, this method has no effect, since the
set of pixels would be empty.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-fillrect" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasRect"
dfn-type="method">`fillRect(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`</span> method,
when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  If either `w` or `h` are zero, then return.

3.  Paint the specified rectangular area using
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill
    style</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-strokerect" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasRect"
dfn-type="method">`strokeRect(``x``, ``y``, ``w``, ``h``)`</span>
method, when invoked, must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Take the result of <a href="#trace-a-path"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:trace-a-path">tracing the path</a>
    described below, using the
    [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) interface's
    line styles, and fill it with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
    style</a>.

If both `w` and `h` are zero, the path has a single subpath with just
one point (`x`, `y`), and no lines, and this method thus has no effect
(the <a href="#trace-a-path"
id="drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap:trace-a-path-2">trace a path</a>
algorithm returns an empty path in that case).

If just one of either `w` or `h` is zero, then the path has a single
subpath consisting of two points, with coordinates (`x`, `y`) and
(`x`+`w`, `y`+`h`), in that order, connected by a single straight line.

Otherwise, the path has a single subpath consisting of four points, with
coordinates (`x`, `y`), (`x`+`w`, `y`), (`x`+`w`, `y`+`h`), and (`x`,
`y`+`h`), connected to each other in that order by straight lines.

</div>
