Returns the measurement described below.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasText`](#canvastext) interface provide
the following methods for rendering text.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-filltext" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasText"
dfn-type="method">`fillText(``text``, ``x``, ``y``, ``maxWidth``)`</span>
and <span id="dom-context-2d-stroketext" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasText"
dfn-type="method">`strokeText(``text``, ``x``, ``y``, ``maxWidth``)`</span>
methods render the given `text` at the given (`x`, `y`) coordinates
ensuring that the text isn't wider than `maxWidth` if specified, using
the current [`font`](#dom-context-2d-font),
[`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign), and
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) values. Specifically,
when the methods are invoked, the user agent must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Run the <a href="#text-preparation-algorithm"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:text-preparation-algorithm">text
    preparation algorithm</a>, passing it `text`, the object
    implementing the [`CanvasText`](#canvastext) interface, and, if the
    `maxWidth` argument was provided, that argument. Let `glyphs` be the
    result.

3.  Move all the shapes in `glyphs` to the right by `x`
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> and down by `y`
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>.

4.  Paint the shapes given in `glyphs`, as transformed by the
    <a href="#transformations"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:transformations">current transformation
    matrix</a>, with each
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-3"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixel</a> in the coordinate space
    of `glyphs` mapped to one coordinate space unit.

    For [`fillText()`](#dom-context-2d-filltext),
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill
    style</a> must be applied to the shapes and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
    style</a> must be ignored. For
    [`strokeText()`](#dom-context-2d-stroketext), the reverse holds:
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style-2">stroke
    style</a> must be applied to the result of <a href="#trace-a-path"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:trace-a-path">tracing</a> the shapes
    using the object implementing the [`CanvasText`](#canvastext)
    interface for the line styles, and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style-2">fill
    style</a> must be ignored.

    These shapes are painted without affecting the current path, and are
    subject to
    <a href="#shadows" id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:shadows">shadow
    effects</a>, <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global
    alpha</a>, the <a href="#clipping-region"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:clipping-region">clipping region</a>,
    and the <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
    id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
    compositing and blending operator</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> The
<span id="dom-context-2d-measuretext" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasText"
dfn-type="method">`measureText(``text``)`</span> method steps are to run
the <a href="#text-preparation-algorithm"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:text-preparation-algorithm-2">text
preparation algorithm</a>, passing it `text` and the object implementing
the [`CanvasText`](#canvastext) interface, and then using the returned
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a> return a new
[`TextMetrics`](#textmetrics) object with members behaving as described
in the following list: [\[CSS\]](#refsCSS)

</div>

<span id="dom-textmetrics-width" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`width`</span> attribute  
The width of that <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-2"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-4"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>. (The text's advance
width.)

<span id="dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxleft" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`actualBoundingBoxLeft`</span> attribute  
The distance parallel to the baseline from the alignment point given by
the [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) attribute to the left side
of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-5"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going left from the given alignment point.

The sum of this value and the next
([`actualBoundingBoxRight`](#dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxright))
can be wider than the width of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-3"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>
([`width`](#dom-textmetrics-width)), in particular with slanted fonts
where characters overhang their advance width.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxright" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`actualBoundingBoxRight`</span> attribute  
The distance parallel to the baseline from the alignment point given by
the [`textAlign`](#dom-context-2d-textalign) attribute to the right side
of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-6"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going right from the given alignment point.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-fontboundingboxascent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`fontBoundingBoxAscent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ascent-metric"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:ascent-metric"
data-x-internal="ascent-metric">ascent metric</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:first-available-font"
data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-7"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going up from the given baseline.

This value and the next are useful when rendering a background that have
to have a consistent height even if the exact text being rendered
changes. The
[`actualBoundingBoxAscent`](#dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxascent)
attribute (and its corresponding attribute for the descent) are useful
when drawing a bounding box around specific text.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-fontboundingboxdescent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`fontBoundingBoxDescent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#descent-metric"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:descent-metric"
data-x-internal="descent-metric">descent metric</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:first-available-font-2"
data-x-internal="first-available-font">first available font</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-8"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going down from the given baseline.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxascent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`actualBoundingBoxAscent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the top of
the bounding rectangle of the given text, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-9"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going up from the given baseline.

This number can vary greatly based on the input text, even if the first
font specified covers all the characters in the input. For example, the
[`actualBoundingBoxAscent`](#dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxascent) of
a lowercase "o" from an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:alphabetic-baseline"
data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a> would be
less than that of an uppercase "F". The value can easily be negative;
for example, the distance from the top of the em box
([`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) value
"[`top`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline-top)") to the top of the bounding
rectangle when the given text is just a single comma "`,`" would likely
(unless the font is quite unusual) be negative.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-actualboundingboxdescent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`actualBoundingBoxDescent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the bottom
of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-10"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating a distance going down from the given baseline.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-emheightascent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`emHeightAscent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-over-baseline"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a> in the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-4"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-11"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating that the given baseline is below the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-over-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a> (so this value
will usually be positive). Zero if the given baseline is the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-over-baseline-3"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a>; half the font
size if the given baseline is halfway between the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-over-baseline-4"
data-x-internal="em-over-baseline">em-over baseline</a> and the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-under-baseline"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a>.

<span id="dom-textmetrics-emheightdescent" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`emHeightDescent`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-under-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a> in the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-5"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-12"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating that the given baseline is above the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-under-baseline-3"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a>. (Zero if the
given baseline is the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:em-under-baseline-4"
data-x-internal="em-under-baseline">em-under baseline</a>.)

<span id="dom-textmetrics-hangingbaseline" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`hangingBaseline`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:hanging-baseline"
data-x-internal="hanging-baseline">hanging baseline</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-6"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-13"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating that the given baseline is below the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:hanging-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="hanging-baseline">hanging baseline</a>. (Zero if the
given baseline is the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:hanging-baseline-3"
data-x-internal="hanging-baseline">hanging baseline</a>.)

<span id="dom-textmetrics-alphabeticbaseline" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`alphabeticBaseline`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:alphabetic-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-7"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-14"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating that the given baseline is below the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:alphabetic-baseline-3"
data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a>. (Zero if
the given baseline is the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:alphabetic-baseline-4"
data-x-internal="alphabetic-baseline">alphabetic baseline</a>.)

<span id="dom-textmetrics-ideographicbaseline" class="dfn" dfn-for="TextMetrics" dfn-type="attribute">`ideographicBaseline`</span> attribute  
The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the
[`textBaseline`](#dom-context-2d-textbaseline) attribute to the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:ideographic-under-baseline"
data-x-internal="ideographic-under-baseline">ideographic-under
baseline</a> of the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:inline-box-8"
data-x-internal="inline-box">inline box</a>, in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:&#39;px&#39;-15"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>; positive numbers
indicating that the given baseline is below the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:ideographic-under-baseline-2"
data-x-internal="ideographic-under-baseline">ideographic-under
baseline</a>. (Zero if the given baseline is the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline"
id="drawing-text-to-the-bitmap:ideographic-under-baseline-3"
data-x-internal="ideographic-under-baseline">ideographic-under
baseline</a>.)

Glyphs rendered using [`fillText()`](#dom-context-2d-filltext) and
[`strokeText()`](#dom-context-2d-stroketext) can spill out of the box
given by the font size and the width returned by
[`measureText()`](#dom-context-2d-measuretext) (the text width). Authors
are encouraged to use the bounding box values described above if this is
an issue.

A future version of the 2D context API might provide a way to render
fragments of documents, rendered using CSS, straight to the canvas. This
would be provided in preference to a dedicated way of doing multiline
layout.

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.13</span> Drawing paths to the canvas<a href="#drawing-paths-to-the-canvas" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) interface
have a <span id="current-default-path" class="dfn">current default
path</span>. There is only one <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path">current default
path</a>, it is not part of the <a href="#drawing-state"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:drawing-state">drawing state</a>. The
<a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-2">current default
path</a> is a <a href="#concept-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:concept-path">path</a>, as described
above.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke"><code>isPointInStroke</code></a>`(``path``, ``x``, ``y``)`

Returns true if the given point would be in the region covered by the
stroke of the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-8">current default
path</a> or the given path, given the current stroke style.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-beginpath" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath" dfn-type="method">`beginPath()`</span> method
steps are to empty the list of subpaths in
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-9">current default
path</a> so that it once again has zero subpaths.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Where the following method definitions use the term
<span id="intended-path" class="dfn">intended path</span> for a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, it means `path` itself if it is a
[`Path2D`](#path2d) object, or the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-10">current default
path</a> otherwise.

</div>

When the <a href="#intended-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path">intended path</a> is a
[`Path2D`](#path2d) object, the coordinates and lines of its subpaths
must be transformed according to the <a href="#transformations"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:transformations">current transformation
matrix</a> on the object implementing the
[`CanvasTransform`](#canvastransform) interface when used by these
methods (without affecting the [`Path2D`](#path2d) object itself). When
the intended path is the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-11">current default
path</a>, it is not affected by the transform. (This is because
transformations already affect the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-12">current default
path</a> when it is constructed, so applying it when it is painted as
well would result in a double transformation.)

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-fill" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`fill(``fillRule``)`</span> method steps are to run
the
<a href="#fill-steps" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-steps">fill
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
null, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-fill-path" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`fill(``path``, ``fillRule``)`</span> method steps are
to run the
<a href="#fill-steps" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-steps-2">fill
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
`path`, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="fill-steps" class="dfn">fill steps</span>, given a
[`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) `context`, a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, and a
<a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule">fill
rule</a> `fillRule`, are to fill all the subpaths of the
<a href="#intended-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path-2">intended path</a> for
`path`, using `context`'s
<a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill
style</a>, and using the
<a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule-2">fill
rule</a> indicated by `fillRule`. Open subpaths must be implicitly
closed when being filled (without affecting the actual subpaths).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-stroke" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath" dfn-type="method">`stroke()`</span> method
steps are to run the <a href="#stroke-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:stroke-steps">stroke steps</a> given
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
and null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-stroke-path" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath" dfn-type="method">`stroke(``path``)`</span>
method steps are to run the <a href="#stroke-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:stroke-steps-2">stroke steps</a> given
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
and `path`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="stroke-steps" class="dfn">stroke steps</span>, given a
[`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) `context` and a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, are to <a href="#trace-a-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:trace-a-path">trace</a> the
<a href="#intended-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path-3">intended path</a> for
`path`, using `context`'s line styles as set by its
[`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) mixin, and then
fill the resulting path using `context`'s
<a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
style</a>, using the <a href="#dom-context-2d-fillrule-nonzero"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:dom-context-2d-fillrule-nonzero">nonzero
winding rule</a>.

</div>

As a result of how the algorithm to <a href="#trace-a-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:trace-a-path-2">trace a path</a> is
defined, overlapping parts of the paths in one stroke operation are
treated as if their union was what was painted.

The stroke *style* is affected by the transformation during painting,
even if the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-13">current default
path</a> is used.

Paths, when filled or stroked, must be painted without affecting the
<a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-default-path-14">current default
path</a> or any [`Path2D`](#path2d) objects, and must be subject to
<a href="#shadows" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:shadows">shadow
effects</a>, <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global
alpha</a>, the <a href="#clipping-region"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:clipping-region">clipping region</a>,
and the <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
compositing and blending operator</a>. (The effect of transformations is
described above and varies based on which path is being used.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-clip" class="dfn" dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`clip(``fillRule``)`</span> method steps are to run
the
<a href="#clip-steps" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:clip-steps">clip
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
null, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-clip-path" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`clip(``path``, ``fillRule``)`</span> method steps are
to run the
<a href="#clip-steps" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:clip-steps-2">clip
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
`path`, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="clip-steps" class="dfn">clip steps</span>, given a
[`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) `context`, a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, and a
<a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule-3">fill
rule</a> `fillRule`, are to create a new <span id="clipping-region"
class="dfn">clipping region</span> by calculating the intersection of
`context`'s current clipping region and the area described by the
<a href="#intended-path"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path-4">intended path</a> for
`path`, using the
<a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule-4">fill
rule</a> indicated by `fillRule`. Open subpaths must be implicitly
closed when computing the clipping region, without affecting the actual
subpaths. The new clipping region replaces the current clipping region.

</div>

When the context is initialized, its current clipping region must be set
to the largest infinite surface (i.e. by default, no clipping occurs).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-ispointinpath" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`isPointInPath(``x``, ``y``, ``fillRule``)`</span>
method steps are to return the result of the
<a href="#is-point-in-path-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:is-point-in-path-steps">is point in path
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
null, `x`, `y`, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-ispointinpath-path" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`isPointInPath(``path``, ``x``, ``y``, ``fillRule``)`</span>
method steps are to return the result of the
<a href="#is-point-in-path-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:is-point-in-path-steps-2">is point in
path steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
`path`, `x`, `y`, and `fillRule`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="is-point-in-path-steps" class="dfn">is point in path
steps</span>, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) `context`, a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, two numbers `x` and `y`, and a
<a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule-5">fill
rule</a> `fillRule`, are:

1.  If `x` or `y` are infinite or NaN, then return false.

2.  If the point given by the `x` and `y` coordinates, when treated as
    coordinates in the canvas coordinate space unaffected by the current
    transformation, is inside the <a href="#intended-path"
    id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path-5">intended path</a>
    for `path` as determined by the
    <a href="#fill-rule" id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:fill-rule-6">fill
    rule</a> indicated by `fillRule`, then return true. Open subpaths
    must be implicitly closed when computing the area inside the path,
    without affecting the actual subpaths. Points on the path itself
    must be considered to be inside the path.

3.  Return false.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`isPointInStroke(``x``, ``y``)`</span> method steps
are to return the result of the <a href="#is-point-in-stroke-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:is-point-in-stroke-steps">is point in
stroke steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-10" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
null, `x`, and `y`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke-path" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawPath"
dfn-type="method">`isPointInStroke(``path``, ``x``, ``y``)`</span>
method steps are to return the result of the
<a href="#is-point-in-stroke-steps"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:is-point-in-stroke-steps-2">is point in
stroke steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:this-11" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
`path`, `x`, and `y`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="is-point-in-stroke-steps" class="dfn">is point in stroke
steps</span>, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#canvasdrawpath) `context`, a
[`Path2D`](#path2d)-or-null `path`, and two numbers `x` and `y`, are:

1.  If `x` or `y` are infinite or NaN, then return false.

2.  If the point given by the `x` and `y` coordinates, when treated as
    coordinates in the canvas coordinate space unaffected by the current
    transformation, is inside the path that results from
    <a href="#trace-a-path"
    id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:trace-a-path-3">tracing</a> the
    <a href="#intended-path"
    id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:intended-path-6">intended path</a>
    for `path`, using the <a href="#dom-context-2d-fillrule-nonzero"
    id="drawing-paths-to-the-canvas:dom-context-2d-fillrule-nonzero-2">nonzero
    winding rule</a>, and using `context`'s line styles as set by its
    [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles) mixin, then
    return true. Points on the resulting path must be considered to be
    inside the path.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div id="drawCustomFocusRingExample" class="example">

<a href="#drawCustomFocusRingExample" class="self-link"></a>

This [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element has a couple of checkboxes.
The path-related commands are highlighted:

``` html
<canvas height=400 width=750>
 <label><input type=checkbox id=showA> Show As</label>
 <label><input type=checkbox id=showB> Show Bs</label>
 <!-- ... -->
</canvas>
<script>
 function drawCheckbox(context, element, x, y, paint) {
   context.save();
   context.font = '10px sans-serif';
   context.textAlign = 'left';
   context.textBaseline = 'middle';
   var metrics = context.measureText(element.labels[0].textContent);
   if (paint) {
     context.beginPath();
     context.strokeStyle = 'black';
     context.rect(x-5, y-5, 10, 10);
     context.stroke();
     if (element.checked) {
       context.fillStyle = 'black';
       context.fill();
     }
     context.fillText(element.labels[0].textContent, x+5, y);
   }
   context.beginPath();
   context.rect(x-7, y-7, 12 + metrics.width+2, 14);

   context.drawFocusIfNeeded(element);
   context.restore();
 }
 function drawBase() { /* ... */ }
 function drawAs() { /* ... */ }
 function drawBs() { /* ... */ }
 function redraw() {
   var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
   var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
   context.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
   drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showA'), 20, 40, true);
   drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showB'), 20, 60, true);
   drawBase();
   if (document.getElementById('showA').checked)
     drawAs();
   if (document.getElementById('showB').checked)
     drawBs();
 }
 function processClick(event) {
   var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
   var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
   var x = event.clientX;
   var y = event.clientY;
   var node = event.target;
   while (node) {
     x -= node.offsetLeft - node.scrollLeft;
     y -= node.offsetTop - node.scrollTop;
     node = node.offsetParent;
   }
   drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showA'), 20, 40, false);
   if (context.isPointInPath(x, y))
     document.getElementById('showA').checked = !(document.getElementById('showA').checked);
   drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showB'), 20, 60, false);
   if (context.isPointInPath(x, y))
     document.getElementById('showB').checked = !(document.getElementById('showB').checked);
   redraw();
 }
 document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('focus', redraw, true);
 document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('blur', redraw, true);
 document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('change', redraw, true);
 document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('click', processClick, false);
 redraw();
</script>
```

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.14</span> Drawing focus rings<a href="#drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view"
class="self-link"></a>

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded"
id="dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded-dev"><code>drawFocusIfNeeded</code></a>`(``element``)`

</div>

If `element` is <a href="#focused"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:focused">focused</a>,
draws a focus ring around the <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:current-default-path">current
default path</a>, following the platform conventions for focus rings.

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded-path-element"
id="dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded-path-element-dev"><code>drawFocusIfNeeded</code></a>`(``path``, ``element``)`

If `element` is <a href="#focused"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:focused-2">focused</a>,
draws a focus ring around `path`, following the platform conventions for
focus rings.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasUserInterface`](#canvasuserinterface)
interface provide the following methods to draw focus rings.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasUserInterface"
dfn-type="method">`drawFocusIfNeeded(``element``)`</span> method steps
are to <a href="#draw-focus-if-needed"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:draw-focus-if-needed">draw
focus if needed</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `element`, and
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#current-default-path"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:current-default-path-2">current
default path</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-drawfocusifneeded-path-element" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasUserInterface"
dfn-type="method">`drawFocusIfNeeded(``path``, ``element``)`</span>
method steps are to <a href="#draw-focus-if-needed"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:draw-focus-if-needed-2">draw
focus if needed</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:this-3"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `element`, and `path`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="draw-focus-if-needed" class="dfn">draw focus if
needed</span>, given an object implementing
[`CanvasUserInterface`](#canvasuserinterface) `context`, an element
`element`, and a <a href="#concept-path"
id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:concept-path">path</a>
`path`:

1.  If `element` is not <a href="#focused"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:focused-3">focused</a>
    or is not a descendant of `context`'s
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, then return.

2.  Draw a focus ring of the appropriate style along `path`, following
    platform conventions.

    Some platforms only draw focus rings around elements that have been
    focused from the keyboard, and not those focused from the mouse.
    Other platforms simply don't draw focus rings around some elements
    at all unless relevant accessibility features are enabled. This API
    is intended to follow these conventions. User agents that implement
    distinctions based on the manner in which the element was focused
    are encouraged to classify focus driven by the
    [`focus()`](#dom-focus) method based on the kind of user interaction
    event from which the call was triggered (if any).

    The focus ring should not be subject to the <a href="#shadows"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:shadows">shadow
    effects</a>, the <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global
    alpha</a>, the <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
    compositing and blending operator</a>, the
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-fill-style">fill
    style</a>, the
    <a href="#concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:concept-canvasfillstrokestyles-stroke-style">stroke
    style</a>, or any of the members in the
    [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#canvaspathdrawingstyles),
    [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#canvastextdrawingstyles) interfaces,
    but *should* be subject to the <a href="#clipping-region"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:clipping-region">clipping
    region</a>. (The effect of transformations is described above and
    varies based on which path is being used.)

3.  [Inform the user](#inform) that the focus is at the location given
    by the intended path. User agents may wait until the next time the
    <a href="#event-loop"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:event-loop">event
    loop</a> reaches its <a href="#update-the-rendering"
    id="drawing-focus-rings-and-scrolling-paths-into-view:update-the-rendering">update
    the rendering</a> step to optionally inform the user.

</div>

User agents should not implicitly close open subpaths in the intended
path when drawing the focus ring.

This might be a moot point, however. For example, if the focus ring is
drawn as an axis-aligned bounding rectangle around the points in the
intended path, then whether the subpaths are closed or not has no
effect. This specification intentionally does not specify precisely how
focus rings are to be drawn: user agents are expected to honor their
platform's native conventions.

"Inform the user", as used in this section, does not imply any
persistent state change. It could mean, for instance, calling a system
accessibility API to notify assistive technologies such as magnification
tools so that the user's magnifier moves to the given area of the
canvas. However, it does not associate the path with the element, or
provide a region for tactile feedback, etc.

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.15</span> Drawing images<a href="#drawing-images" class="self-link"></a>

Objects that implement the [`CanvasDrawImage`](#canvasdrawimage)
interface have the <span id="dom-context-2d-drawimage" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasDrawImage" dfn-type="method">`drawImage()`</span> method
to draw images.

This method can be invoked with three different sets of arguments:

- `drawImage(``image``, ``dx``, ``dy``)`
- `drawImage(``image``, ``dx``, ``dy``, ``dw``, ``dh``)`
- `drawImage(``image``, ``sx``, ``sy``, ``sw``, ``sh``, ``dx``, ``dy``, ``dw``, ``dh``)`

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-drawimage"
id="dom-context-2d-drawimage-dev"><code>drawImage</code></a>`(``image``, ``dx``, ``dy``)`

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-drawimage"
id="drawing-images:dom-context-2d-drawimage"><code>drawImage</code></a>`(``image``, ``dx``, ``dy``, ``dw``, ``dh``)`

`context``.`<a href="#dom-context-2d-drawimage"
id="drawing-images:dom-context-2d-drawimage-2"><code>drawImage</code></a>`(``image``, ``sx``, ``sy``, ``sw``, ``sh``, ``dx``, ``dy``, ``dw``, ``dh``)`

Draws the given image onto the canvas. The arguments are interpreted as
follows:

<img src="/images/drawImage.png" width="356" height="356"
alt="The sx and sy parameters give the x and y coordinates of the source rectangle; the sw and sh arguments give the width and height of the source rectangle; the dx and dy give the x and y coordinates of the destination rectangle; and the dw and dh arguments give the width and height of the destination rectangle." />

If the image isn't yet fully decoded, then nothing is drawn. If the
image is a canvas with no data, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="drawing-images:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="drawing-images:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

<div algorithm="">

When the [`drawImage()`](#dom-context-2d-drawimage) method is invoked,
the user agent must run these steps:

1.  If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.

2.  Let `usability` be the result of
    <a href="#check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument"
    id="drawing-images:check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument">checking
    the usability of <var>image</var></a>.

3.  If `usability` is *bad*, then return (without drawing anything).

4.  Establish the source and destination rectangles as follows:

    If not specified, the `dw` and `dh` arguments must default to the
    values of `sw` and `sh`, interpreted such that one
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="drawing-images:&#39;px&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
    pixel</a> in the image is treated as one unit in the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap">output
    bitmap</a>'s coordinate space. If the `sx`, `sy`, `sw`, and `sh`
    arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width"
    id="drawing-images:natural-width"
    data-x-internal="natural-width">natural width</a> in image pixels,
    and the image's
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
    id="drawing-images:natural-height"
    data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a> in image pixels,
    respectively. If the image has no
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
    id="drawing-images:natural-dimensions"
    data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a>, then
    the *concrete object size* must be used instead, as determined using
    the CSS "[Concrete Object Size
    Resolution](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing)"
    algorithm, with the *specified size* having neither a definite width
    nor height, nor any additional constraints, the object's natural
    properties being those of the `image` argument, and the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size"
    id="drawing-images:default-object-size"
    data-x-internal="default-object-size">default object size</a> being
    the size of the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap-2">output
    bitmap</a>. [\[CSSIMAGES\]](#refsCSSIMAGES)

    The source rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the four
    points (`sx`, `sy`), (`sx`+`sw`, `sy`), (`sx`+`sw`, `sy`+`sh`),
    (`sx`, `sy`+`sh`).

    The destination rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the
    four points (`dx`, `dy`), (`dx`+`dw`, `dy`), (`dx`+`dw`, `dy`+`dh`),
    (`dx`, `dy`+`dh`).

    When the source rectangle is outside the source image, the source
    rectangle must be clipped to the source image and the destination
    rectangle must be clipped in the same proportion.

    When the destination rectangle is outside the destination image (the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap-3">output
    bitmap</a>), the pixels that land outside the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap-4">output
    bitmap</a> are discarded, as if the destination was an infinite
    canvas whose rendering was clipped to the dimensions of the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap-5">output
    bitmap</a>.

5.  If one of the `sw` or `sh` arguments is zero, then return. Nothing
    is painted.

6.  Paint the region of the `image` argument specified by the source
    rectangle on the region of the rendering context's
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="drawing-images:output-bitmap-6">output
    bitmap</a> specified by the destination rectangle, after applying
    the
    <a href="#transformations" id="drawing-images:transformations">current
    transformation matrix</a> to the destination rectangle.

    The image data must be processed in the original direction, even if
    the dimensions given are negative.

    When scaling up, if the
    [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingenabled)
    attribute is set to true, the user agent should attempt to apply a
    smoothing algorithm to the image data when it is scaled. User agents
    which support multiple filtering algorithms may use the value of the
    [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingquality)
    attribute to guide the choice of filtering algorithm when the
    [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingenabled)
    attribute is set to true. Otherwise, the image must be rendered
    using nearest-neighbor interpolation.

    This specification does not define the precise algorithm to use when
    scaling an image down, or when scaling an image up when the
    [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#dom-context-2d-imagesmoothingenabled)
    attribute is set to true.

    When a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element is drawn onto itself,
    the
    <a href="#drawing-model" id="drawing-images:drawing-model">drawing
    model</a> requires the source to be copied before the image is
    drawn, so it is possible to copy parts of a
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element onto overlapping parts of
    itself.

    If the original image data is a bitmap image, then the value painted
    at a point in the destination rectangle is computed by filtering the
    original image data. The user agent may use any filtering algorithm
    (for example bilinear interpolation or nearest-neighbor). When the
    filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the original
    image data, it must instead use the value from the nearest edge
    pixel. (That is, the filter uses 'clamp-to-edge' behavior.) When the
    filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the source
    rectangle but inside the original image data, then the value from
    the original image data must be used.

    Thus, scaling an image in parts or in whole will have the same
    effect. This does mean that when sprites coming from a single sprite
    sheet are to be scaled, adjacent images in the sprite sheet can
    interfere. This can be avoided by ensuring each sprite in the sheet
    is surrounded by a border of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="drawing-images:transparent-black"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>, or by
    copying sprites to be scaled into temporary
    [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements and drawing the scaled
    sprites from there.

    Images are painted without affecting the current path, and are
    subject to
    <a href="#shadows" id="drawing-images:shadows">shadow effects</a>,
    <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
    id="drawing-images:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global alpha</a>,
    the
    <a href="#clipping-region" id="drawing-images:clipping-region">clipping
    region</a>, and the
    <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
    id="drawing-images:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
    compositing and blending operator</a>.

7.  If `image` <a href="#the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean"
    id="drawing-images:the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean">is not
    origin-clean</a>, then set the
    [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d)'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="drawing-images:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
    flag to false.

</div>

###### <span class="secno">4.12.5.1.16</span> <span class="dfn">Pixel manipulation</span><a href="#pixel-manipulation" class="self-link"></a>

Paints the data from the given [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object onto the
bitmap. If a dirty rectangle is provided, only the pixels from that
rectangle are painted.

The [`globalAlpha`](#dom-context-2d-globalalpha) and
[`globalCompositeOperation`](#dom-context-2d-globalcompositeoperation)
properties, as well as the
<a href="#shadows" id="pixel-manipulation:shadows">shadow attributes</a>,
are ignored for the purposes of this method call; pixels in the canvas
are replaced wholesale, with no composition, alpha blending, no shadows,
etc.

Throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="pixel-manipulation:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="pixel-manipulation:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a> if the
`imageData` object's [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute value's
\[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot is detached.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasImageData`](#canvasimagedata)
interface provide the following methods for reading and writing pixel
data to the bitmap.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createimagedata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasImageData"
dfn-type="method">`createImageData(``sw``, ``sh``, ``settings``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  If one or both of `sw` and `sh` are zero, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="pixel-manipulation:indexsizeerror-3"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="pixel-manipulation:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `newImageData` be a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
    id="pixel-manipulation:new" data-x-internal="new">new</a>
    [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object.

3.  <a href="#initialize-an-imagedata-object"
    id="pixel-manipulation:initialize-an-imagedata-object">Initialize</a>
    `newImageData` given the absolute magnitude of `sw`, the absolute
    magnitude of `sh`, `settings`, and
    *<a href="#initialize-imagedata-defaultcolorspace"
    id="pixel-manipulation:initialize-imagedata-defaultcolorspace">defaultColorSpace</a>*
    set to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-color-space-3">color space</a>.

4.  Initialize the image data of `newImageData` to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="pixel-manipulation:transparent-black-3"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

5.  Return `newImageData`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-createimagedata-imagedata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasImageData"
dfn-type="method">`createImageData(``imageData``)`</span> method steps
are:

1.  Let `newImageData` be a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
    id="pixel-manipulation:new-2" data-x-internal="new">new</a>
    [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object.

2.  Let `settings` be the [`ImageDataSettings`](#imagedatasettings)
    object «\[ "[`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedatasettings-colorspace)" →
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#dom-imagedata-colorspace"
    id="pixel-manipulation:dom-imagedata-colorspace">colorSpace</a>,
    "[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)" →
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#dom-imagedata-pixelformat"
    id="pixel-manipulation:dom-imagedata-pixelformat">pixelFormat</a>
    \]».

3.  <a href="#initialize-an-imagedata-object"
    id="pixel-manipulation:initialize-an-imagedata-object-2">Initialize</a>
    `newImageData` given the value of `imageData`'s
    [`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute, the value of
    `imageData`'s [`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute, and
    `settings`.

4.  Initialize the image data of `newImageData` to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="pixel-manipulation:transparent-black-4"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

5.  Return `newImageData`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-getimagedata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasImageData"
dfn-type="method">`getImageData(``sx``, ``sy``, ``sw``, ``sh``, ``settings``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  If either the `sw` or `sh` arguments are zero, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="pixel-manipulation:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="pixel-manipulation:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If the [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d)'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>
    flag is set to false, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="pixel-manipulation:securityerror"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="pixel-manipulation:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Let `imageData` be a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
    id="pixel-manipulation:new-3" data-x-internal="new">new</a>
    [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object.

4.  <a href="#initialize-an-imagedata-object"
    id="pixel-manipulation:initialize-an-imagedata-object-3">Initialize</a>
    `imageData` given `sw`, `sh`, `settings`, and
    *<a href="#initialize-imagedata-defaultcolorspace"
    id="pixel-manipulation:initialize-imagedata-defaultcolorspace-2">defaultColorSpace</a>*
    set to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-color-space-4">color space</a>.

5.  Let the source rectangle be the rectangle whose corners are the four
    points (`sx`, `sy`), (`sx`+`sw`, `sy`), (`sx`+`sw`, `sy`+`sh`),
    (`sx`, `sy`+`sh`).

6.  Set the pixel values of `imageData` to be the pixels of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="pixel-manipulation:output-bitmap">output
    bitmap</a> in the area specified by the source rectangle in the
    bitmap's coordinate space units, converted from
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="pixel-manipulation:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-color-space-5">color space</a>
    to `imageData`'s [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace) using <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric"
    id="pixel-manipulation:&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;">'relative-colorimetric'</a>
    rendering intent.

7.  Set the pixels values of `imageData` for areas of the source
    rectangle that are outside of the
    <a href="#output-bitmap" id="pixel-manipulation:output-bitmap-2">output
    bitmap</a> to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="pixel-manipulation:transparent-black-5"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

8.  Return `imageData`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-putimagedata-short" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasImageData"
dfn-type="method">`putImageData(``imageData``, ``dx``, ``dy``)`</span>
method steps are to <a href="#dom-context2d-putimagedata-common"
id="pixel-manipulation:dom-context2d-putimagedata-common">put pixels
from an <code>ImageData</code> onto a bitmap</a>, given `imageData`,
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="pixel-manipulation:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="pixel-manipulation:output-bitmap-3">output
bitmap</a>, `dx`, `dy`, 0, 0, `imageData`'s
[`width`](#dom-imagedata-width), and `imageData`'s
[`height`](#dom-imagedata-height).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-putimagedata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasImageData"
dfn-type="method">`putImageData(``imageData``, ``dx``, ``dy``, ``dirtyX``, ``dirtyY``, ``dirtyWidth``, ``dirtyHeight``)`</span>
method steps are to <a href="#dom-context2d-putimagedata-common"
id="pixel-manipulation:dom-context2d-putimagedata-common-2">put pixels
from an <code>ImageData</code> onto a bitmap</a>, given `imageData`,
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="pixel-manipulation:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="pixel-manipulation:output-bitmap-4">output
bitmap</a>, `dx`, `dy`, `dirtyX`, `dirtyY`, `dirtyWidth`, and
`dirtyHeight`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="dom-context2d-putimagedata-common" class="dfn">put pixels
from an `ImageData` onto a bitmap</span>, given an
[`ImageData`](#imagedata) `imageData`, an
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="pixel-manipulation:output-bitmap-5">output
bitmap</a> `bitmap`, and numbers `dx`, `dy`, `dirtyX`, `dirtyY`,
`dirtyWidth`, and `dirtyHeight`:

1.  Let `buffer` be `imageData`'s [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data)
    attribute value's \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot.

2.  If <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdetachedbuffer"
    id="pixel-manipulation:isdetachedbuffer"
    data-x-internal="isdetachedbuffer">IsDetachedBuffer</a>(`buffer`) is
    true, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="pixel-manipulation:invalidstateerror-2"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="pixel-manipulation:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  If `dirtyWidth` is negative, then let `dirtyX` be
    `dirtyX`+`dirtyWidth`, and let `dirtyWidth` be equal to the absolute
    magnitude of `dirtyWidth`.

    If `dirtyHeight` is negative, then let `dirtyY` be
    `dirtyY`+`dirtyHeight`, and let `dirtyHeight` be equal to the
    absolute magnitude of `dirtyHeight`.

4.  If `dirtyX` is negative, then let `dirtyWidth` be
    `dirtyWidth`+`dirtyX`, and let `dirtyX` be 0.

    If `dirtyY` is negative, then let `dirtyHeight` be
    `dirtyHeight`+`dirtyY`, and let `dirtyY` be 0.

5.  If `dirtyX`+`dirtyWidth` is greater than the
    [`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute of the `imageData`
    argument, then let `dirtyWidth` be the value of that
    [`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute, minus the value of
    `dirtyX`.

    If `dirtyY`+`dirtyHeight` is greater than the
    [`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute of the `imageData`
    argument, then let `dirtyHeight` be the value of that
    [`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute, minus the value of
    `dirtyY`.

6.  If, after those changes, either `dirtyWidth` or `dirtyHeight` are
    negative or zero, then return without affecting any bitmaps.

7.  For all integer values of `x` and `y` where
    `dirtyX` ≤ `x` \< `dirtyX`+`dirtyWidth` and
    `dirtyY` ≤ `y` \< `dirtyY`+`dirtyHeight`, set the pixel with
    coordinate (`dx`+`x`, `dy`+`y`) in `bitmap` to the color of the
    pixel at coordinate (`x`, `y`) in the `imageData` data structure's
    <a href="#concept-imagedata-bitmap-representation"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-imagedata-bitmap-representation">bitmap</a>,
    converted from `imageData`'s
    [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace) to the
    <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
    id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-color-space-6">color space</a>
    of `bitmap` using <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric"
    id="pixel-manipulation:&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;">'relative-colorimetric'</a>
    rendering intent.

</div>

Due to the lossy nature of converting between color spaces and
converting to and from <a href="#concept-premultiplied-alpha"
id="pixel-manipulation:concept-premultiplied-alpha">premultiplied
alpha</a> color values, pixels that have just been set using
[`putImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-putimagedata), and are not completely
opaque, might be returned to an equivalent
[`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata) as different values.

The current path, <a href="#transformations"
id="pixel-manipulation:transformations">transformation matrix</a>,
<a href="#shadows" id="pixel-manipulation:shadows-2">shadow
attributes</a>, <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="pixel-manipulation:concept-canvas-global-alpha">global alpha</a>,
the <a href="#clipping-region"
id="pixel-manipulation:clipping-region">clipping region</a>, and
<a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="pixel-manipulation:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
compositing and blending operator</a> must not affect the methods
described in this section.

<div class="example">

In the following example, the script generates an
[`ImageData`](#imagedata) object so that it can draw onto it.

``` js
// canvas is a reference to a <canvas> element
var context = canvas.getContext('2d');

// create a blank slate
var data = context.createImageData(canvas.width, canvas.height);

// create some plasma
FillPlasma(data, 'green'); // green plasma

// add a cloud to the plasma
AddCloud(data, data.width/2, data.height/2); // put a cloud in the middle

// paint the plasma+cloud on the canvas
context.putImageData(data, 0, 0);

// support methods
function FillPlasma(data, color) { ... }
function AddCloud(data, x, y) { ... }
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Here is an example of using
[`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata) and
[`putImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-putimagedata) to implement an edge
detection filter.

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
 <head>
  <title>Edge detection demo</title>
  <script>
   var image = new Image();
   function init() {
     image.onload = demo;
     image.src = "image.jpeg";
   }
   function demo() {
     var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
     var context = canvas.getContext('2d');

     // draw the image onto the canvas
     context.drawImage(image, 0, 0);

     // get the image data to manipulate
     var input = context.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

     // get an empty slate to put the data into
     var output = context.createImageData(canvas.width, canvas.height);

     // alias some variables for convenience
     // In this case input.width and input.height
     // match canvas.width and canvas.height
     // but we'll use the former to keep the code generic.
     var w = input.width, h = input.height;
     var inputData = input.data;
     var outputData = output.data;

     // edge detection
     for (var y = 1; y < h-1; y += 1) {
       for (var x = 1; x < w-1; x += 1) {
         for (var c = 0; c < 3; c += 1) {
           var i = (y*w + x)*4 + c;
           outputData[i] = 127 + -inputData[i - w*4 - 4] -   inputData[i - w*4] - inputData[i - w*4 + 4] +
                                 -inputData[i - 4]       + 8*inputData[i]       - inputData[i + 4] +
                                 -inputData[i + w*4 - 4] -   inputData[i + w*4] - inputData[i + w*4 + 4];
         }
         outputData[(y*w + x)*4 + 3] = 255; // alpha
       }
     }

     // put the image data back after manipulation
     context.putImageData(output, 0, 0);
   }
  </script>
 </head>
 <body onload="init()">
  <canvas></canvas>
 </body>
</html>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

Here is an example of color space conversion applied when drawing a
solid color and reading the result back using and
[`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata).

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
<title>Color space image data demo</title>

<canvas></canvas>

<script>
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');
const context = canvas.getContext('2d', {colorSpace:'display-p3'});

// Draw a red rectangle. Note that the hex color notation
// specifies sRGB colors.
context.fillStyle = "#FF0000";
context.fillRect(0, 0, 64, 64);

// Get the image data.
const pixels = context.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1);

// This will print 'display-p3', reflecting the default behavior
// of returning image data in the canvas's color space.
console.log(pixels.colorSpace);

// This will print the values 234, 51, and 35, reflecting the
// red fill color, converted to 'display-p3'.
console.log(pixels.data[0]);
console.log(pixels.data[1]);
console.log(pixels.data[2]);
</script>
```

</div>

Returns the <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="compositing:current-compositing-and-blending-operator">current
compositing and blending operator</a>, from the values defined in
Compositing and Blending. [\[COMPOSITE\]](#refsCOMPOSITE)

Can be set, to change the
<a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="compositing:current-compositing-and-blending-operator-2">current
compositing and blending operator</a>. Unknown values are ignored.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasCompositing`](#canvascompositing)
interface have a <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="compositing:concept-canvas-global-alpha-3">global alpha</a> value
and a <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="compositing:current-compositing-and-blending-operator-3">current
compositing and blending operator</a> value that both affect all the
drawing operations on this object.

The <span id="concept-canvas-global-alpha" class="dfn">global
alpha</span> value gives an alpha value that is applied to shapes and
images before they are composited onto the
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="compositing:output-bitmap">output
bitmap</a>. The value ranges from 0.0 (fully transparent) to 1.0 (no
additional transparency). It must initially have the value 1.0.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-globalalpha" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasCompositing" dfn-type="attribute">`globalAlpha`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="compositing:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="compositing:concept-canvas-global-alpha-4">global alpha</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`globalAlpha`](#dom-context-2d-globalalpha) setter steps are:

1.  If the given value is either infinite, NaN, or not in the range 0.0
    to 1.0, then return.

2.  Otherwise, set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="compositing:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
    id="compositing:concept-canvas-global-alpha-5">global alpha</a> to
    the given value.

</div>

The <span id="current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
class="dfn">current compositing and blending operator</span> value
controls how shapes and images are drawn onto the
<a href="#output-bitmap" id="compositing:output-bitmap-2">output
bitmap</a>, once they have had the
<a href="#concept-canvas-global-alpha"
id="compositing:concept-canvas-global-alpha-6">global alpha</a> and the
<a href="#current-transformation-matrix"
id="compositing:current-transformation-matrix">current transformation
matrix</a> applied. Initially, it must be set to "<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_srcover"
data-x-internal="gcop-source-over"><code
id="compositing:gcop-source-over">source-over</code></a>".

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-context-2d-globalcompositeoperation" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CanvasCompositing"
dfn-type="attribute">`globalCompositeOperation`</span> getter steps are
to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="compositing:this-3"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
id="compositing:current-compositing-and-blending-operator-4">current
compositing and blending operator</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The
[`globalCompositeOperation`](#dom-context-2d-globalcompositeoperation)
setter steps are:

1.  If the given value is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
    id="compositing:identical-to" data-x-internal="identical-to">identical
    to</a> any of the values that the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#ltblendmodegt"
    id="compositing:blend-mode"
    data-x-internal="blend-mode">&lt;blend-mode&gt;</a> or the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#compositemode"
    id="compositing:composite-mode"
    data-x-internal="composite-mode">&lt;composite-mode&gt;</a>
    properties are defined to take, then return.
    [\[COMPOSITE\]](#refsCOMPOSITE)

2.  Otherwise, set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="compositing:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#current-compositing-and-blending-operator"
    id="compositing:current-compositing-and-blending-operator-5">current
    compositing and blending operator</a> to the given value.

</div>
