------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D {
  readonly attribute OffscreenCanvas canvas;
};

OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasSettings;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasState;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTransform;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasCompositing;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageSmoothing;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFillStrokeStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasShadowStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFilters;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasRect;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawPath;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasText;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawImage;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageData;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPathDrawingStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTextDrawingStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPath;
```

The
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)
object is a rendering context for drawing to the
<a href="#offscreencanvas-bitmap"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:offscreencanvas-bitmap">bitmap</a>
of an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object. It is similar to the
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) object, with the
following differences:

- there is no support for <a href="#canvasuserinterface"
  id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:canvasuserinterface">user
  interface</a> features;

- its [`canvas`](#offscreencontext2d-canvas) attribute refers to an
  [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object rather than a
  [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element;

An
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)
object has an <span id="associated-offscreencanvas-object"
class="dfn">associated `OffscreenCanvas` object</span>, which is the
[`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object from which the
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)
object was created.

`offscreenCanvas`` = ``offscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D``.`<a href="#offscreencontext2d-canvas"
id="offscreencontext2d-canvas-dev"><code>canvas</code></a>  
Returns the <a href="#associated-offscreencanvas-object"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:associated-offscreencanvas-object">associated
<code>OffscreenCanvas</code> object</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="offscreen-2d-context-creation-algorithm"
class="dfn">offscreen 2D context creation algorithm</span>, which is
passed a `target` (an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) object) and
optionally some arguments, consists of running the following steps:

1.  If the algorithm was passed some arguments, let `arg` be the first
    such argument. Otherwise, let `arg` be undefined.

2.  Let `settings` be the result of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:concept-idl-convert"
    data-x-internal="concept-idl-convert">converting</a> `arg` to the
    dictionary type
    [`CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`](#canvasrenderingcontext2dsettings).
    (This can throw an exception.)

3.  Let `context` be a new
    [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)
    object.

4.  Set `context`'s <a href="#associated-offscreencanvas-object"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:associated-offscreencanvas-object-2">associated
    <code>OffscreenCanvas</code> object</a> to `target`.

5.  Run the <a href="#canvas-setting-init-bitmap"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:canvas-setting-init-bitmap">canvas
    settings output bitmap initialization algorithm</a>, given `context`
    and `settings`.

6.  Set `context`'s <a href="#output-bitmap"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:output-bitmap">output bitmap</a>
    to a newly created bitmap with the dimensions specified by the
    [`width`](#dom-offscreencanvas-width) and
    [`height`](#dom-offscreencanvas-height) attributes of `target`, and
    set `target`'s bitmap to the same bitmap (so that they are shared).

7.  If `context`'s <a href="#concept-canvas-alpha"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:concept-canvas-alpha">alpha</a>
    flag is set to true, initialize all the pixels of `context`'s
    <a href="#output-bitmap"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:output-bitmap-2">output
    bitmap</a> to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:transparent-black"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.
    Otherwise, initialize the pixels to
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black"
    id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:opaque-black"
    data-x-internal="opaque-black">opaque black</a>.

8.  Return `context`.

</div>

Implementations are encouraged to short-circuit the graphics update
steps of the <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:window-event-loop">window event
loop</a> for the purposes of updating the contents of a
<a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:offscreencanvas-placeholder">placeholder
<code>canvas</code> element</a> to the display. This could mean, for
example, that the bitmap contents are copied directly to a graphics
buffer that is mapped to the physical display location of the
<a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:offscreencanvas-placeholder-2">placeholder
<code>canvas</code> element</a>. This or similar short-circuiting
approaches can significantly reduce display latency, especially in cases
where the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) is updated from a
<a href="#worker-event-loop-2"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:worker-event-loop-2">worker event
loop</a> and the <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:window-event-loop-2">window event
loop</a> of the <a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:offscreencanvas-placeholder-3">placeholder
<code>canvas</code> element</a> is busy. However, such shortcuts cannot
have any script-observable side-effects. This means that the committed
bitmap still needs to be sent to the
<a href="#offscreencanvas-placeholder"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:offscreencanvas-placeholder-4">placeholder
<code>canvas</code> element</a>, in case the element is used as a
[`CanvasImageSource`](#canvasimagesource), as an
[`ImageBitmapSource`](#imagebitmapsource), or in case
[`toDataURL()`](#dom-canvas-todataurl) or
[`toBlob()`](#dom-canvas-toblob) are called on it.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="offscreencontext2d-canvas" class="dfn"
dfn-for="OffscreenCanvas" dfn-type="attribute">`canvas`</span>
attribute, on getting, must return this
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)'s
<a href="#associated-offscreencanvas-object"
id="the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context:associated-offscreencanvas-object-3">associated
<code>OffscreenCanvas</code> object</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.12.5.4</span> Color spaces and color space conversion<a href="#colour-spaces-and-colour-correction" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
enum PredefinedColorSpace { "srgb", "srgb-linear", "display-p3", "display-p3-linear" };
```

The [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#predefinedcolorspace) enumeration is used
to specify the <a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:concept-canvas-color-space">color
space</a> of the canvas's backing store.

The "<span id="dom-predefinedcolorspace-srgb" class="dfn"
dfn-for="PredefinedColorSpace" dfn-type="enum-value">`srgb`</span>"
value indicates the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:&#39;srgb&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;srgb&#39;">'srgb'</a> color space.

The "<span id="dom-predefinedcolorspace-srgb-linear" class="dfn"
dfn-for="PredefinedColorSpace"
dfn-type="enum-value">`srgb-linear`</span>" value indicates the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb-linear"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:&#39;srgb-linear&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;srgb-linear&#39;">'srgb-linear'</a> color space.

The "<span id="dom-predefinedcolorspace-display-p3" class="dfn"
dfn-for="PredefinedColorSpace"
dfn-type="enum-value">`display-p3`</span>" value indicates the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-display-p3"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:&#39;display-p3&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;display-p3&#39;">'display-p3'</a> color space.

The "<span id="dom-predefinedcolorspace-display-p3-linear" class="dfn"
dfn-for="PredefinedColorSpace"
dfn-type="enum-value">`display-p3-linear`</span>" value indicates the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#display-p3-linear-space"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:&#39;display-p3-linear&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;display-p3-linear&#39;">'display-p3-linear'</a>
color space.

<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:converting-colors"
data-x-internal="converting-colors">Color space conversion</a> must be
applied to the canvas's backing store when rendering the canvas to the
output device.

The algorithm for converting between color spaces can be found in the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:converting-colors-2"
data-x-internal="converting-colors">Converting Colors</a> section of CSS
Color. This color space conversion is identical to the color space
conversion that would be applied to an [`img`](#the-img-element) element
with a color profile that specifies the same
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-space"
id="colour-spaces-and-colour-correction:concept-canvas-color-space-2">color
space</a> as the canvas's backing store. [\[CSSCOLOR\]](#refsCSSCOLOR)

##### <span class="secno">4.12.5.5</span> Serializing bitmaps to a file<a href="#serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file" class="self-link"></a>

<div var-scope="">

When a user agent is to create
<span id="a-serialisation-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file" class="dfn">a
serialization of the bitmap as a file</span>, given a `type` and an
optional `quality`, it must create an image file in the format given by
`type`. If an error occurs during the creation of the image file (e.g.
an internal encoder error), then the result of the serialization is
null. [\[PNG\]](#refsPNG)

The image file's pixel data must be the bitmap's pixel data scaled to
one image pixel per coordinate space unit, and if the file format used
supports encoding resolution metadata, the resolution must be given as
96dpi (one image pixel per
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixel</a>).

If `type` is supplied, then it must be interpreted as a
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:mime-type"
data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME type</a> giving the format to use. If
the type has any parameters, then it must be treated as not supported.

For example, the value "[`image/png`](#image/png)" would mean to
generate a PNG image, the value "[`image/jpeg`](#image/jpeg)" would mean
to generate a JPEG image, and the value
"[`image/svg+xml`](#image/svg+xml)" would mean to generate an SVG image
(which would require that the user agent track how the bitmap was
generated, an unlikely, though potentially awesome, feature).

User agents must support PNG ("[`image/png`](#image/png)"). User agents
may support other types. If the user agent does not support the
requested type, then it must create the file using the PNG format.
[\[PNG\]](#refsPNG)

User agents must
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">convert the provided type
to ASCII lowercase</a> before establishing if they support that type.

For image types that do not support an alpha component, the serialized
image must be the bitmap image composited onto an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:opaque-black"
data-x-internal="opaque-black">opaque black</a> background using the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_srcover"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:gcop-source-over"
data-x-internal="gcop-source-over">source-over</a> compositing operator.

For image types that support color profiles, the serialized image must
include a color profile indicating the color space of the underlying
bitmap. For image types that do not support color profiles, the
serialized image must be
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:converting-colors"
data-x-internal="converting-colors">converted</a> to the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:&#39;srgb&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;srgb&#39;">'srgb'</a> color space using <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;relative-colorimetric&#39;">'relative-colorimetric'</a>
rendering intent.

Thus, in the 2D context, calling the
[`drawImage()`](#dom-context-2d-drawimage) method to render the output
of the [`toDataURL()`](#dom-canvas-todataurl) or
[`toBlob()`](#dom-canvas-toblob) method to the canvas, given the
appropriate dimensions, has no visible effect beyond, at most, clipping
colors of the canvas to a more narrow gamut.

For image types that support multiple bit depths, the serialized image
must use the bit depth that best preserves content of the underlying
bitmap.

For example, when serializing a 2D context that has
<a href="#concept-canvas-color-type"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:concept-canvas-color-type">color
type</a> of <a href="#dom-canvascolortype-float16"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:dom-canvascolortype-float16">float16</a>
to `type` "[`image/png`](#image/png)", the resulting image would have 16
bits per sample. This serialization will still lose significant detail
(all values less than 0.5/65535 would be clamped to 0, and all values
greater than 1 would be clamped to 1).

If `type` is an image format that supports variable quality (such as
"[`image/jpeg`](#image/jpeg)"), `quality` is given, and `type` is not
"[`image/png`](#image/png)", then, if `quality` <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
id="serialising-bitmaps-to-a-file:js-number"
data-x-internal="js-number">is a Number</a> in the range 0.0 to 1.0
inclusive, the user agent must treat `quality` as the desired quality
level. Otherwise, the user agent must use its default quality value, as
if the `quality` argument had not been given.

The use of type-testing here, instead of simply declaring `quality` as a
Web IDL `double`, is a historical artifact.

</div>

Different implementations can have slightly different interpretations of
"quality". When the quality is not specified, an implementation-specific
default is used that represents a reasonable compromise between
compression ratio, image quality, and encoding time.

##### <span class="secno">4.12.5.6</span> Security with [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements<a href="#security-with-canvas-elements" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

**Information leakage** can occur if scripts from one
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-origin">origin</a> can access
information (e.g. read pixels) from images from another origin (one that
isn't the <a href="#same-origin"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:same-origin">same</a>).

To mitigate this, bitmaps used with [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element)
elements, [`OffscreenCanvas`](#offscreencanvas) objects, and
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) objects are defined to have a flag
indicating whether they are <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</a>.
All bitmaps start with their <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-2">origin-clean</a>
set to true. The flag is set to false when cross-origin images are used.

The [`toDataURL()`](#dom-canvas-todataurl),
[`toBlob()`](#dom-canvas-toblob), and
[`getImageData()`](#dom-context-2d-getimagedata) methods check the flag
and will throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:securityerror"
data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="security-with-canvas-elements:domexception">DOMException</code></a>
rather than leak cross-origin data.

The value of the <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-3">origin-clean</a>
flag is propagated from a source's bitmap to a new
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object by
[`createImageBitmap()`](#dom-createimagebitmap). Conversely, a
destination [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element's bitmap will have
its <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-4">origin-clean</a>
flags set to false by [`drawImage`](#dom-context-2d-drawimage) if the
source image is an [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object whose bitmap has
its <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-5">origin-clean</a>
flag set to false.

The flag can be reset in certain situations; for example, when changing
the value of the [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) or the
[`height`](#attr-canvas-height) content attribute of the
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element to which a
[`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d) is bound, the
bitmap is cleared and its <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-6">origin-clean</a>
flag is reset.

When using an
[`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#imagebitmaprenderingcontext), the value
of the <a href="#concept-canvas-origin-clean"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:concept-canvas-origin-clean-7">origin-clean</a>
flag is propagated from [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) objects when they
are transferred to the [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) via
<a href="#dom-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-transferfromimagebitmap"
id="security-with-canvas-elements:dom-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-transferfromimagebitmap">transferFromImageBitmap()</a>.

##### <span class="secno">4.12.5.7</span> Premultiplied alpha and the 2D rendering context<a href="#premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context"
class="self-link"></a>

<span id="concept-premultiplied-alpha" class="dfn">Premultiplied
alpha</span> refers to one way of representing transparency in an image,
the other being non-premultiplied alpha.

Under non-premultiplied alpha, the red, green, and blue components of a
pixel represent that pixel's color, and its alpha component represents
that pixel's opacity.

Under premultiplied alpha, however, the red, green, and blue components
of a pixel represent the amounts of color that the pixel adds to the
image, and its alpha component represents the amount that the pixel
obscures whatever is behind it.

<div class="example">

For instance, assuming the color components range from 0 (off) to 255
(full intensity), these example colors are represented in the following
ways:

| CSS color representation | Premultiplied representation | Non-premultiplied representation | Description of color | Image of color blended above other content |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| rgba(255, 127, 0, 1) | 255, 127, 0, 255 | 255, 127, 0, 255 | Completely-opaque orange | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-1.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="An opaque orange circle sits atop a background" /> |
| rgba(255, 255, 0, 0.5) | 127, 127, 0, 127 | 255, 255, 0, 127 | Halfway-opaque yellow | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-2.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="A yellow circle, halfway transparent, sits atop a background" /> |
| Unrepresentable | 255, 127, 0, 127 | Unrepresentable | Additive halfway-opaque orange | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-3.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="An orange circle somewhat brightens the background that it sits atop" /> |
| Unrepresentable | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Unrepresentable | Additive fully-transparent orange | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-4.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="An orange circle completely brightens the background that it sits atop" /> |
| rgba(255, 127, 0, 0) | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Fully-transparent ("invisible") orange | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-5.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="An empty background with nothing atop it" /> |
| rgba(0, 127, 255, 0) | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Fully-transparent ("invisible") turquoise | <img src="images/premultiplied-example-5.png" width="96" height="96"
alt="An empty background with nothing atop it" /> |

</div>

<span id="convert-to-premultiplied" class="dfn">Converting a color value
from a non-premultiplied representation to a premultiplied one</span>
involves multiplying the color's red, green, and blue components by its
alpha component (remapping the range of the alpha component such that
"fully transparent" is 0, and "fully opaque" is 1).

<span id="convert-from-premultiplied" class="dfn">Converting a color
value from a premultiplied representation to a non-premultiplied
one</span> involves the inverse: dividing the color's red, green, and
blue components by its alpha component.

As certain colors can only be represented under premultiplied alpha (for
instance, additive colors), and others can only be represented under
non-premultiplied alpha (for instance, "invisible" colors which hold
certain red, green, and blue values even with no opacity); and division
and multiplication using finite precision entails a loss of accuracy,
converting between premultiplied and non-premultiplied alpha is a lossy
operation on colors that are not fully opaque.

A [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#canvasrenderingcontext2d)'s
<a href="#output-bitmap"
id="premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context:output-bitmap">output
bitmap</a> and an
[`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#offscreencanvasrenderingcontext2d)'s
<a href="#output-bitmap"
id="premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context:output-bitmap-2">output
bitmap</a> must use premultiplied alpha to represent transparent colors.

It is important for canvas bitmaps to represent colors using
premultiplied alpha because it affects the range of representable
colors. While additive colors cannot currently be drawn onto canvases
directly because CSS colors are non-premultiplied and cannot represent
them, it is still possible to, for instance, draw additive colors onto a
WebGL canvas and then draw that WebGL canvas onto a 2D canvas via
[`drawImage()`](#dom-context-2d-drawimage).

This article introduces the use of the Custom Elements API.")
