<div class="example">

The [`whenDefined()`](#dom-customelementregistry-whendefined) method can
be used to avoid performing an action until all appropriate
<a href="#custom-element"
id="custom-elements-api:custom-element-8">custom elements</a> are
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-defined"
id="custom-elements-api:concept-element-defined"
data-x-internal="concept-element-defined">defined</a>. In this example,
we combine it with the [`:defined`](#selector-defined) pseudo-class to
hide a dynamically-loaded article's contents until we're sure that all
of the <a href="#autonomous-custom-element"
id="custom-elements-api:autonomous-custom-element-2">autonomous custom
elements</a> it uses are defined.

``` js
articleContainer.hidden = true;

fetch(articleURL)
  .then(response => response.text())
  .then(text => {
    articleContainer.innerHTML = text;

    return Promise.all(
      [...articleContainer.querySelectorAll(":not(:defined)")]
        .map(el => customElements.whenDefined(el.localName))
    );
  })
  .then(() => {
    articleContainer.hidden = false;
  });
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-customelementregistry-upgrade" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CustomElementRegistry"
dfn-type="method">`upgrade(``root``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  For each <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-descendant"
    id="custom-elements-api:shadow-including-inclusive-descendant-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-descendant">shadow-including
    inclusive descendant</a> `candidate` of `root`, in <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order"
    id="custom-elements-api:shadow-including-tree-order-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-tree-order">shadow-including tree
    order</a>:

    1.  If `candidate` is not an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="custom-elements-api:element-2">Element</code></a> node, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="custom-elements-api:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  If `candidate`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
        id="custom-elements-api:element-custom-element-registry-3"
        data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
        registry</a> is not
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="custom-elements-api:this-25" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
        then <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="custom-elements-api:continue-2"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    3.  <a href="#concept-try-upgrade"
        id="custom-elements-api:concept-try-upgrade-2">Try to upgrade</a>
        `candidate`.

</div>

<div class="example">

The [`upgrade()`](#dom-customelementregistry-upgrade) method allows
upgrading of elements at will. Normally elements are automatically
upgraded when they become
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
id="custom-elements-api:connected-2"
data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, but this method can be used
if you need to upgrade before you're ready to connect the element.

``` js
const el = document.createElement("spider-man");

class SpiderMan extends HTMLElement {}
customElements.define("spider-man", SpiderMan);

console.assert(!(el instanceof SpiderMan)); // not yet upgraded

customElements.upgrade(el);
console.assert(el instanceof SpiderMan);    // upgraded!
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-customelementregistry-initialize" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CustomElementRegistry"
dfn-type="method">`initialize(``root``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-elements-api:this-26" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#is-scoped" id="custom-elements-api:is-scoped-4">is scoped</a>
    is false and either `root` is a [`Document`](#document) node or
    `root`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="custom-elements-api:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-custom-element-registry"
    id="custom-elements-api:document-custom-element-registry-5"
    data-x-internal="document-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a> is not <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-elements-api:this-27" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="custom-elements-api:notsupportederror-9"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="custom-elements-api:domexception-12">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If `root` is a [`Document`](#document) node whose
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-custom-element-registry"
    id="custom-elements-api:document-custom-element-registry-6"
    data-x-internal="document-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a> is null, then set `root`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-custom-element-registry"
    id="custom-elements-api:document-custom-element-registry-7"
    data-x-internal="document-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a> to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-elements-api:this-28" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

3.  Otherwise, if `root` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-shadowroot"
    data-x-internal="shadowroot"><code
    id="custom-elements-api:shadowroot-2">ShadowRoot</code></a> node
    whose <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-custom-element-registry"
    id="custom-elements-api:shadow-root-custom-element-registry-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-root-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a> is null, then set `root`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-custom-element-registry"
    id="custom-elements-api:shadow-root-custom-element-registry-3"
    data-x-internal="shadow-root-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a> to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-elements-api:this-29" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

4.  For each
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-inclusive-descendant"
    id="custom-elements-api:inclusive-descendant-2"
    data-x-internal="inclusive-descendant">inclusive descendant</a>
    `inclusiveDescendant` of `root`, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="custom-elements-api:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>:

    1.  If `inclusiveDescendant` is not an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="custom-elements-api:element-3">Element</code></a> node, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="custom-elements-api:continue-3"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  If `inclusiveDescendant`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
        id="custom-elements-api:element-custom-element-registry-4"
        data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
        registry</a> is null:

        1.  Set `inclusiveDescendant`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
            id="custom-elements-api:element-custom-element-registry-5"
            data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
            registry</a> to
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
            id="custom-elements-api:this-30" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

        2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
            id="custom-elements-api:this-31" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
            <a href="#is-scoped" id="custom-elements-api:is-scoped-5">is scoped</a>
            is true, then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
            id="custom-elements-api:set-append-2"
            data-x-internal="set-append">append</a>
            `inclusiveDescendant`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
            id="custom-elements-api:node-document-3"
            data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> to
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
            id="custom-elements-api:this-32" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
            <a href="#scoped-document-set"
            id="custom-elements-api:scoped-document-set-2">scoped document set</a>.

    3.  If `inclusiveDescendant`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
        id="custom-elements-api:element-custom-element-registry-6"
        data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
        registry</a> is not
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="custom-elements-api:this-33" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
        then <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="custom-elements-api:continue-4"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    4.  <a href="#concept-try-upgrade"
        id="custom-elements-api:concept-try-upgrade-3">Try to upgrade</a>
        `inclusiveDescendant`.

</div>

Once the custom element registry of a node is initialized to a
[`CustomElementRegistry`](#customelementregistry) object, it
intentionally cannot be changed any further. This simplifies reasoning
about code and allows implementations to optimize.

#### <span class="secno">4.13.5</span> <span class="dfn">Upgrades</span><a href="#upgrades" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="concept-upgrade-an-element" class="dfn" export="">upgrade
an element</span>, given as input a <a href="#custom-element-definition"
id="upgrades:custom-element-definition">custom element definition</a>
`definition` and an element `element`, run the following steps:

1.  <div id="concept-upgrade-an-element-early-exit">

    If `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
    id="upgrades:custom-element-state"
    data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a> is
    not "`undefined`" or "`uncustomized`", then return.

    <div class="example">

    One scenario where this can occur due to reentrant invocation of
    this algorithm, as in the following example:

    ``` html
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <x-foo id="a"></x-foo>
    <x-foo id="b"></x-foo>

    <script>
    // Defining enqueues upgrade reactions for both "a" and "b"
    customElements.define("x-foo", class extends HTMLElement {
      constructor() {
        super();

        const b = document.querySelector("#b");
        b.remove();

        // While this constructor is running for "a", "b" is still
        // undefined, and so inserting it into the document will enqueue a
        // second upgrade reaction for "b" in addition to the one enqueued
        // by defining x-foo.
        document.body.appendChild(b);
      }
    })
    </script>
    ```

    This step will thus bail out the algorithm early when
    <a href="#concept-upgrade-an-element"
    id="upgrades:concept-upgrade-an-element">upgrade an element</a> is
    invoked with "`b`" a second time.

    </div>

    </div>

2.  Set `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-definition"
    id="upgrades:concept-element-custom-element-definition"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-custom-element-definition">custom
    element definition</a> to `definition`.

3.  Set `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
    id="upgrades:custom-element-state-2"
    data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a> to
    "`failed`".

    It will be set to "`custom`" [after the upgrade
    succeeds](#concept-upgrade-an-element-set-state-to-custom). For now,
    we set it to "`failed`" so that any reentrant invocations will hit
    [the above early-exit step](#concept-upgrade-an-element-early-exit).

4.  For each `attribute` in `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attribute"
    id="upgrades:attribute-list" data-x-internal="attribute-list">attribute
    list</a>, in order,
    <a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
    id="upgrades:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction">enqueue a
    custom element callback reaction</a> with `element`, callback name
    "`attributeChangedCallback`", and « `attribute`'s local name, null,
    `attribute`'s value, `attribute`'s namespace ».

5.  If `element` is
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected" id="upgrades:connected"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then
    <a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
    id="upgrades:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction-2">enqueue a
    custom element callback reaction</a> with `element`, callback name
    "`connectedCallback`", and « ».

6.  Add `element` to the end of `definition`'s
    <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-construction-stack"
    id="upgrades:concept-custom-element-definition-construction-stack">construction
    stack</a>.

7.  Let `C` be `definition`'s
    <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-constructor"
    id="upgrades:concept-custom-element-definition-constructor">constructor</a>.

8.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set" id="upgrades:map-set"
    data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="upgrades:surrounding-agent"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
    <a href="#active-custom-element-constructor-map"
    id="upgrades:active-custom-element-constructor-map">active custom
    element constructor map</a>\[`C`\] to `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
    id="upgrades:element-custom-element-registry"
    data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a>.

9.  Run the following steps while catching any exceptions:

    1.  If `definition`'s
        <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-disable-shadow"
        id="upgrades:concept-custom-element-definition-disable-shadow">disable
        shadow</a> is true and `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
        id="upgrades:concept-element-shadow-root"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a> is
        non-null, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
        id="upgrades:notsupportederror"
        data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="upgrades:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

        This is needed as
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-element-attachshadow"
        data-x-internal="dom-element-attachshadow"><code
        id="upgrades:dom-element-attachshadow">attachShadow()</code></a>
        does not use <a href="#look-up-a-custom-element-definition"
        id="upgrades:look-up-a-custom-element-definition">look up a custom
        element definition</a> while
        [`attachInternals()`](#dom-attachinternals) does.

    2.  Set `element`'s <a
        href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
        id="upgrades:custom-element-state-3"
        data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a>
        to "`precustomized`".

    3.  Let `constructResult` be the result of
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#construct-a-callback-function"
        id="upgrades:es-constructing-callback-functions"
        data-x-internal="es-constructing-callback-functions">constructing</a>
        `C`, with no arguments.

        If `C` [non-conformantly](#custom-element-conformance) uses an
        API decorated with the [`[CEReactions]`](#cereactions) extended
        attribute, then the reactions enqueued at the beginning of this
        algorithm will execute during this step, before `C` finishes and
        control returns to this algorithm. Otherwise, they will execute
        after `C` and the rest of the upgrade process finishes.

    4.  If
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-samevalue" id="upgrades:samevalue"
        data-x-internal="samevalue">SameValue</a>(`constructResult`,
        `element`) is false, then throw a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="upgrades:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>.

        This can occur if `C` constructs another instance of the same
        custom element before calling `super()`, or if `C` uses
        JavaScript's `return`-override feature to return an arbitrary
        [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement) object from the constructor.

    Then, perform the following steps, regardless of whether the above
    steps threw an exception or not:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-remove"
        id="upgrades:map-remove" data-x-internal="map-remove">Remove</a>
        the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
        id="upgrades:surrounding-agent-2"
        data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
        <a href="#active-custom-element-constructor-map"
        id="upgrades:active-custom-element-constructor-map-2">active custom
        element constructor map</a>\[`C`\].

        This is a no-op if `C` immediately calls `super()` as it ought
        to do.

    2.  Remove the last entry from the end of `definition`'s
        <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-construction-stack"
        id="upgrades:concept-custom-element-definition-construction-stack-2">construction
        stack</a>.

        <div class="note">

        Assuming `C` calls `super()` (as it will if it is
        [conformant](#custom-element-conformance)), and that the call
        succeeds, this will be the
        <a href="#concept-already-constructed-marker"
        id="upgrades:concept-already-constructed-marker"><em>already
        constructed</em> marker</a> that replaced the `element` we
        pushed at the beginning of this algorithm. (The [HTML element
        constructor](#html-element-constructors) carries out this
        replacement.)

        If `C` does not call `super()` (i.e. it is not
        [conformant](#custom-element-conformance)), or if any step in
        the [HTML element constructor](#html-element-constructors)
        throws, then this entry will still be `element`.

        </div>

    Finally, if the above steps threw an exception, then:

    1.  Set `element`'s <a
        href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-definition"
        id="upgrades:concept-element-custom-element-definition-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-custom-element-definition">custom
        element definition</a> to null.

    2.  Empty `element`'s <a href="#custom-element-reaction-queue"
        id="upgrades:custom-element-reaction-queue">custom element reaction
        queue</a>.

    3.  Rethrow the exception (thus terminating this algorithm).

    If the above steps threw an exception, then `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
    id="upgrades:custom-element-state-4"
    data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a> will
    remain "`failed`" or "`precustomized`".

10. If `element` is a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
    id="upgrades:form-associated-custom-element">form-associated custom
    element</a>, then:

    1.  <a href="#reset-the-form-owner" id="upgrades:reset-the-form-owner">Reset
        the form owner</a> of `element`. If `element` is associated with
        a [`form`](#the-form-element) element, then
        <a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
        id="upgrades:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction-3">enqueue a
        custom element callback reaction</a> with `element`, callback
        name "`formAssociatedCallback`", and « the associated
        [`form`](#the-form-element) ».

    2.  If `element` is <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
        id="upgrades:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a>, then
        <a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
        id="upgrades:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction-4">enqueue a
        custom element callback reaction</a> with `element`, callback
        name "`formDisabledCallback`", and « true ».

11. <div id="concept-upgrade-an-element-set-state-to-custom">

    Set `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
    id="upgrades:custom-element-state-5"
    data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a> to
    "`custom`".

    </div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="concept-try-upgrade" class="dfn" export="">try to upgrade
an element</span> given an element `element`:

1.  Let `definition` be the result of
    <a href="#look-up-a-custom-element-definition"
    id="upgrades:look-up-a-custom-element-definition-2">looking up a custom
    element definition</a> given `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
    id="upgrades:element-custom-element-registry-2"
    data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a>, `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace"
    id="upgrades:concept-element-namespace"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-namespace">namespace</a>,
    `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
    id="upgrades:concept-element-local-name"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a>, and
    `element`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
    id="upgrades:concept-element-is-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>.

2.  If `definition` is not null, then
    <a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction"
    id="upgrades:enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction">enqueue a custom
    element upgrade reaction</a> given `element` and `definition`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.13.6</span> Custom element reactions<a href="#custom-element-reactions" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#custom-element"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element">custom element</a>
possesses the ability to respond to certain occurrences by running
author code:

- When
  <a href="#upgrades" id="custom-element-reactions:upgrades">upgraded</a>,
  its <a href="#custom-element-constructor"
  id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-constructor">constructor</a>
  is run, with no arguments.

- When it <a href="#becomes-connected"
  id="custom-element-reactions:becomes-connected">becomes connected</a>,
  its `connectedCallback` is called, with no arguments.

- When it <a href="#becomes-disconnected"
  id="custom-element-reactions:becomes-disconnected">becomes
  disconnected</a>, its `disconnectedCallback` is called, with no
  arguments.

- When it is
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-node-move-ext"
  data-x-internal="concept-node-move-ext">moved</a>, its
  `connectedMoveCallback` is called, with no arguments.

- When it is <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-adopt"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-node-adopt"
  data-x-internal="concept-node-adopt">adopted</a> into a new document,
  its `adoptedCallback` is called, given the old document and new
  document as arguments.

- When any of its attributes are
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-attributes-change"
  data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change">changed</a>,
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-append"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-attributes-append"
  data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-append">appended</a>,
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-remove"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-attributes-remove"
  data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-remove">removed</a>, or <a
  href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-replace"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-attributes-replace"
  data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-replace">replaced</a>, its
  `attributeChangedCallback` is called, given the attribute's local
  name, old value, new value, and namespace as arguments. (An
  attribute's old or new value is considered to be null when the
  attribute is added or removed, respectively.)

- When the user agent <a href="#reset-the-form-owner"
  id="custom-element-reactions:reset-the-form-owner">resets the form
  owner</a> of a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
  id="custom-element-reactions:form-associated-custom-element">form-associated
  custom element</a> and doing so changes the form owner, its
  `formAssociatedCallback` is called, given the new form owner (or null
  if no owner) as an argument.

- When the form owner of a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
  id="custom-element-reactions:form-associated-custom-element-2">form-associated
  custom element</a> is <a href="#concept-form-reset"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-form-reset">reset</a>, its
  `formResetCallback` is called.

- When the <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
  id="custom-element-reactions:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a> state
  of a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
  id="custom-element-reactions:form-associated-custom-element-3">form-associated
  custom element</a> is changed, its `formDisabledCallback` is called,
  given the new state as an argument.

- When the user agent updates a
  <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
  id="custom-element-reactions:form-associated-custom-element-4">form-associated
  custom element</a>'s value on behalf of a user or
  <a href="#restore-persisted-state"
  id="custom-element-reactions:restore-persisted-state">as part of
  navigation</a>, its `formStateRestoreCallback` is called, given the
  new state and a string indicating a reason, "`autocomplete`" or
  "`restore`", as arguments.

We call these reactions collectively
<span id="concept-custom-element-reaction" class="dfn">custom element
reactions</span>.

</div>

The way in which <a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction">custom
element reactions</a> are invoked is done with special care, to avoid
running author code during the middle of delicate operations.
Effectively, they are delayed until "just before returning to user
script". This means that for most purposes they appear to execute
synchronously, but in the case of complicated composite operations (like
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-node-clone"
data-x-internal="concept-node-clone">cloning</a>, or
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-range"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-range"
data-x-internal="concept-range">range</a> manipulation), they will
instead be delayed until after all the relevant user agent processing
steps have completed, and then run together as a batch.

Additionally, the precise ordering of these reactions is managed via a
somewhat-complicated stack-of-queues system, described below. The
intention behind this system is to guarantee that
<a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-2">custom
element reactions</a> always are invoked in the same order as their
triggering actions, at least within the local context of a single
<a href="#custom-element"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-2">custom element</a>.
(Because <a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-3">custom
element reaction</a> code can perform its own mutations, it is not
possible to give a global ordering guarantee across multiple elements.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each <a href="#similar-origin-window-agent"
id="custom-element-reactions:similar-origin-window-agent">similar-origin
window agent</a> has a <span id="custom-element-reactions-stack"
class="dfn">custom element reactions stack</span>, which is initially
empty. A <a href="#similar-origin-window-agent"
id="custom-element-reactions:similar-origin-window-agent-2">similar-origin
window agent</a>'s <span id="current-element-queue" class="dfn">current
element queue</span> is the <a href="#element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:element-queue">element queue</a> at the top
of its <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack">custom
element reactions stack</a>. Each item in the stack is an
<span id="element-queue" class="dfn">element queue</span>, which is
initially empty as well. Each item in an <a href="#element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:element-queue-2">element queue</a> is an
element. (The elements are not necessarily
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-custom"
data-x-internal="concept-element-custom">custom</a> yet, since this
queue is used for <a href="#upgrades"
id="custom-element-reactions:upgrades-2">upgrades</a> as well.)

Each <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack-2">custom
element reactions stack</a> has an associated
<span id="backup-element-queue" class="dfn">backup element queue</span>,
which is an initially-empty <a href="#element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:element-queue-3">element queue</a>.
Elements are pushed onto the <a href="#backup-element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:backup-element-queue">backup element
queue</a> during operations that affect the DOM without going through an
API decorated with [`[CEReactions]`](#cereactions), or through the
parser's <a href="#create-an-element-for-the-token"
id="custom-element-reactions:create-an-element-for-the-token">create an
element for the token</a> algorithm. An example of this is a
user-initiated editing operation which modifies the descendants or
attributes of an
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
id="custom-element-reactions:editable"
data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> element. To prevent reentrancy
when processing the <a href="#backup-element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:backup-element-queue-2">backup element
queue</a>, each <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack-3">custom
element reactions stack</a> also has a
<span id="processing-the-backup-element-queue" class="dfn">processing
the backup element queue</span> flag, initially unset.

All elements have an associated <span id="custom-element-reaction-queue"
class="dfn">custom element reaction queue</span>, initially empty. Each
item in the <a href="#custom-element-reaction-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reaction-queue">custom
element reaction queue</a> is of one of two types:

- An <span id="upgrade-reaction" class="dfn">upgrade reaction</span>,
  which will
  <a href="#upgrades" id="custom-element-reactions:upgrades-3">upgrade</a>
  the custom element and contains a <a href="#custom-element-definition"
  id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-definition">custom element
  definition</a>; or

- A <span id="callback-reaction" class="dfn">callback reaction</span>,
  which will call a lifecycle callback, and contains a callback function
  as well as a list of arguments.

This is all summarized in the following schematic diagram:

<img src="/images/custom-element-reactions.svg" class="darkmode-aware"
style="width: 80%; max-width: 580px;"
alt="A custom element reactions stack consists of a stack of element queues. Zooming in on a particular queue, we see that it contains a number of elements (in our example, &lt;x-a&gt;, then &lt;x-b&gt;, then &lt;x-c&gt;). Any particular element in the queue then has a custom element reaction queue. Zooming in on the custom element reaction queue, we see that it contains a variety of queued-up reactions (in our example, upgrade, then attribute changed, then another attribute changed, then connected)." />

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue"
class="dfn">enqueue an element on the appropriate element queue</span>,
given an element `element`, run the following steps:

1.  Let `reactionsStack` be `element`'s <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="custom-element-reactions:relevant-agent">relevant agent</a>'s
    <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack-4">custom
    element reactions stack</a>.

2.  If `reactionsStack` is empty, then:

    1.  Add `element` to `reactionsStack`'s
        <a href="#backup-element-queue"
        id="custom-element-reactions:backup-element-queue-3">backup element
        queue</a>.

    2.  If `reactionsStack`'s
        <a href="#processing-the-backup-element-queue"
        id="custom-element-reactions:processing-the-backup-element-queue">processing
        the backup element queue</a> flag is set, then return.

    3.  Set `reactionsStack`'s
        <a href="#processing-the-backup-element-queue"
        id="custom-element-reactions:processing-the-backup-element-queue-2">processing
        the backup element queue</a> flag.

    4.  <a href="#queue-a-microtask"
        id="custom-element-reactions:queue-a-microtask">Queue a microtask</a>
        to perform the following steps:

        1.  <a href="#invoke-custom-element-reactions"
            id="custom-element-reactions:invoke-custom-element-reactions">Invoke
            custom element reactions</a> in `reactionsStack`'s
            <a href="#backup-element-queue"
            id="custom-element-reactions:backup-element-queue-4">backup element
            queue</a>.

        2.  Unset `reactionsStack`'s
            <a href="#processing-the-backup-element-queue"
            id="custom-element-reactions:processing-the-backup-element-queue-3">processing
            the backup element queue</a> flag.

3.  Otherwise, add `element` to `element`'s <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="custom-element-reactions:relevant-agent-2">relevant agent</a>'s
    <a href="#current-element-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:current-element-queue">current element
    queue</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction" class="dfn"
export="">enqueue a custom element callback reaction</span>, given a
<a href="#custom-element"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-3">custom element</a>
`element`, a callback name `callbackName`, and a list of arguments
`args`, run the following steps:

1.  Let `definition` be `element`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-definition"
    id="custom-element-reactions:concept-element-custom-element-definition"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-custom-element-definition">custom
    element definition</a>.

2.  Let `callback` be the value of the entry in `definition`'s
    <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks"
    id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks">lifecycle
    callbacks</a> with key `callbackName`.

3.  If `callbackName` is "`connectedMoveCallback`" and `callback` is
    null:

    1.  Let `disconnectedCallback` be the value of the entry in
        `definition`'s
        <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks"
        id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks-2">lifecycle
        callbacks</a> with key "`disconnectedCallback`".

    2.  Let `connectedCallback` be the value of the entry in
        `definition`'s
        <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks"
        id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-definition-lifecycle-callbacks-3">lifecycle
        callbacks</a> with key "`connectedCallback`".

    3.  If `connectedCallback` and `disconnectedCallback` are null, then
        return.

    4.  Set `callback` to the following steps:

        1.  If `disconnectedCallback` is not null, then call
            `disconnectedCallback` with no arguments.

        2.  If `connectedCallback` is not null, then call
            `connectedCallback` with no arguments.

4.  If `callback` is null, then return.

5.  If `callbackName` is "`attributeChangedCallback`":

    1.  Let `attributeName` be the first element of `args`.

    2.  If `definition`'s
        <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-observed-attributes"
        id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-definition-observed-attributes">observed
        attributes</a> does not contain `attributeName`, then return.

6.  Add a new <a href="#callback-reaction"
    id="custom-element-reactions:callback-reaction">callback reaction</a>
    to `element`'s <a href="#custom-element-reaction-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reaction-queue-2">custom
    element reaction queue</a>, with callback function `callback` and
    arguments `args`.

7.  <a href="#enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue">Enqueue
    an element on the appropriate element queue</a> given `element`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction" class="dfn"
export="">enqueue a custom element upgrade reaction</span>, given an
element `element` and <a href="#custom-element-definition"
id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-definition-2">custom element
definition</a> `definition`, run the following steps:

1.  Add a new <a href="#upgrade-reaction"
    id="custom-element-reactions:upgrade-reaction">upgrade reaction</a>
    to `element`'s <a href="#custom-element-reaction-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reaction-queue-3">custom
    element reaction queue</a>, with
    <a href="#custom-element-definition"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-definition-3">custom element
    definition</a> `definition`.

2.  <a href="#enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue-2">Enqueue
    an element on the appropriate element queue</a> given `element`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="invoke-custom-element-reactions" class="dfn">invoke custom
element reactions</span> in an <a href="#element-queue"
id="custom-element-reactions:element-queue-4">element queue</a> `queue`,
run the following steps:

1.  While `queue` is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="custom-element-reactions:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>:

    1.  Let `element` be the result of
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-dequeue"
        id="custom-element-reactions:dequeue"
        data-x-internal="dequeue">dequeuing</a> from `queue`.

    2.  Let `reactions` be `element`'s
        <a href="#custom-element-reaction-queue"
        id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reaction-queue-4">custom
        element reaction queue</a>.

    3.  Repeat until `reactions` is empty:

        1.  Remove the first element of `reactions`, and let `reaction`
            be that element. Switch on `reaction`'s type:

            <a href="#upgrade-reaction"
            id="custom-element-reactions:upgrade-reaction-2">upgrade reaction</a>  
            <a href="#concept-upgrade-an-element"
            id="custom-element-reactions:concept-upgrade-an-element">Upgrade</a>
            `element` using `reaction`'s
            <a href="#custom-element-definition"
            id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-definition-4">custom element
            definition</a>.

            If this throws an exception, catch it, and
            <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="custom-element-reactions:report-an-exception">report</a>
            it for `reaction`'s <a href="#custom-element-definition"
            id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-definition-5">custom element
            definition</a>'s
            <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-constructor"
            id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-definition-constructor">constructor</a>'s
            corresponding JavaScript object's
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-associated-realm"
            id="custom-element-reactions:associated-realm"
            data-x-internal="associated-realm">associated realm</a>'s
            <a href="#concept-realm-global"
            id="custom-element-reactions:concept-realm-global">global object</a>.

            <a href="#callback-reaction"
            id="custom-element-reactions:callback-reaction-2">callback reaction</a>  
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
            id="custom-element-reactions:es-invoking-callback-functions"
            data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">Invoke</a>
            `reaction`'s callback function with `reaction`'s arguments
            and "`report`", and
            *<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value"
            data-x-internal="dfn-callback-this-value">callback this value</a>*
            set to `element`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

To ensure <a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-4">custom
element reactions</a> are triggered appropriately, we introduce the
<span id="cereactions" class="dfn" dfn-type="extended-attribute"
lt="CEReactions">`[CEReactions]`</span> IDL
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute"
id="custom-element-reactions:extended-attribute"
data-x-internal="extended-attribute">extended attribute</a>. It
indicates that the relevant algorithm is to be supplemented with
additional steps in order to appropriately track and invoke
<a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-5">custom
element reactions</a>.

The [`[CEReactions]`](#cereactions) extended attribute must take no
arguments, and must not appear on anything other than an operation,
attribute, setter, or deleter. Additionally, it must not appear on
readonly attributes.

<div algorithm="">

Operations, attributes, setters, or deleters annotated with the
[`[CEReactions]`](#cereactions) extended attribute must run the
following steps in place of the ones specified in their description:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#stack-push"
    id="custom-element-reactions:stack-push"
    data-x-internal="stack-push">Push</a> a new <a href="#element-queue"
    id="custom-element-reactions:element-queue-5">element queue</a> onto
    this object's <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="custom-element-reactions:relevant-agent-3">relevant agent</a>'s
    <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack-5">custom
    element reactions stack</a>.

2.  Run the originally-specified steps for this construct, catching any
    exceptions. If the steps return a value, let `value` be the returned
    value. If they throw an exception, let `exception` be the thrown
    exception.

3.  Let `queue` be the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#stack-pop"
    id="custom-element-reactions:stack-pop"
    data-x-internal="stack-pop">popping</a> from this object's
    <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="custom-element-reactions:relevant-agent-4">relevant agent</a>'s
    <a href="#custom-element-reactions-stack"
    id="custom-element-reactions:custom-element-reactions-stack-6">custom
    element reactions stack</a>.

4.  <a href="#invoke-custom-element-reactions"
    id="custom-element-reactions:invoke-custom-element-reactions-2">Invoke
    custom element reactions</a> in `queue`.

5.  If an exception `exception` was thrown by the original steps,
    rethrow `exception`.

6.  If a value `value` was returned from the original steps, return
    `value`.

</div>

<div class="note">

The intent behind this extended attribute is somewhat subtle. One way of
accomplishing its goals would be to say that every operation, attribute,
setter, and deleter on the platform must have these steps inserted, and
to allow implementers to optimize away unnecessary cases (where no DOM
mutation is possible that could cause
<a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-6">custom
element reactions</a> to occur).

However, in practice this imprecision could lead to non-interoperable
implementations of <a href="#concept-custom-element-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:concept-custom-element-reaction-7">custom
element reactions</a>, as some implementations might forget to invoke
these steps in some cases. Instead, we settled on the approach of
explicitly annotating all relevant IDL constructs, as a way of ensuring
interoperable behavior and helping implementations easily pinpoint all
cases where these steps are necessary.

</div>

Any nonstandard APIs introduced by the user agent that could modify the
DOM in such a way as to cause
<a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction">enqueuing
a custom element callback reaction</a> or
<a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction"
id="custom-element-reactions:enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction">enqueuing
a custom element upgrade reaction</a>, for example by modifying any
attributes or child elements, must also be decorated with the
[`[CEReactions]`](#cereactions) attribute.

<div class="note">

As of the time of this writing, the following nonstandard or
not-yet-standardized APIs are known to fall into this category:

- [`HTMLInputElement`](#htmlinputelement)'s `webkitdirectory` and
  `incremental` IDL attributes

- [`HTMLLinkElement`](#htmllinkelement)'s `scope` IDL attribute

</div>

#### <span class="secno">4.13.7</span> Element internals<a href="#element-internals" class="self-link"></a>

Certain capabilities are meant to be available to a custom element
author, but not to a custom element consumer. These are provided by the
[`element.attachInternals()`](#dom-attachinternals) method, which
returns an instance of [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals). The
properties and methods of [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) allow
control over internal features which the user agent provides to all
elements.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-attachinternals"
id="dom-attachinternals-dev"><code>attachInternals()</code></a>  
Returns an [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object targeting the
<a href="#custom-element" id="element-internals:custom-element">custom
element</a> `element`. Throws an exception if `element` is not a
<a href="#custom-element" id="element-internals:custom-element-2">custom
element</a>, if the "`internals`" feature was disabled as part of the
element definition, or if it is called twice on the same element.

Each [`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement) has an <span id="attached-internals"
class="dfn">attached internals</span> (null or an
[`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) object), initially null.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLElement/attachInternals](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/attachInternals "The HTMLElement.attachInternals() method returns an ElementInternals object. This method allows a custom element to participate in HTML forms. The ElementInternals interface provides utilities for working with these elements in the same way you would work with any standard HTML form element, and also exposes the Accessibility Object Model to the element.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox93+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari16.4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome77+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-attachinternals" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="method">`attachInternals()`</span> method steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
    id="element-internals:concept-element-is-value"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>
    is not null, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="element-internals:notsupportederror"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="element-internals:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `definition` be the result of
    <a href="#look-up-a-custom-element-definition"
    id="element-internals:look-up-a-custom-element-definition">looking up a
    custom element definition</a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
    id="element-internals:element-custom-element-registry"
    data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a>, <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace"
    id="element-internals:concept-element-namespace"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-namespace">namespace</a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
    id="element-internals:concept-element-local-name"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a>, and
    null.

3.  If `definition` is null, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="element-internals:notsupportederror-2"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="element-internals:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  If `definition`'s
    <a href="#concept-custom-element-definition-disable-internals"
    id="element-internals:concept-custom-element-definition-disable-internals">disable
    internals</a> is true, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="element-internals:notsupportederror-3"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="element-internals:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

5.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#attached-internals"
    id="element-internals:attached-internals">attached internals</a> is
    non-null, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="element-internals:notsupportederror-4"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="element-internals:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

6.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state"
    id="element-internals:custom-element-state"
    data-x-internal="custom-element-state">custom element state</a> is
    not "`precustomized`" or "`custom`", then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="element-internals:notsupportederror-5"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="element-internals:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

7.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#attached-internals"
    id="element-internals:attached-internals-2">attached internals</a>
    to a new [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) instance whose
    <a href="#internals-target"
    id="element-internals:internals-target">target element</a> is
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

8.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="element-internals:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#attached-internals"
    id="element-internals:attached-internals-3">attached internals</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.13.7.1</span> The [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) interface<a href="#the-elementinternals-interface" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[ElementInternals](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ElementInternals "The ElementInternals interface of the Document Object Model gives web developers a way to allow custom elements to fully participate in HTML forms. It provides utilities for working with these elements in the same way you would work with any standard HTML form element, and also exposes the Accessibility Object Model to the element.")

Support in all current engines.

iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera

The IDL for the [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) interface is as
follows, with the various operations and attributes defined in the
following sections:

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface ElementInternals {
  // Shadow root access
  readonly attribute ShadowRoot? shadowRoot;

  // Form-associated custom elements
  undefined setFormValue((File or USVString or FormData)? value,
                         optional (File or USVString or FormData)? state);

  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

  undefined setValidity(optional ValidityStateFlags flags = {},
                        optional DOMString message,
                        optional HTMLElement anchor);
  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  // Custom state pseudo-class
  [SameObject] readonly attribute CustomStateSet states;
};

// Accessibility semantics
ElementInternals includes ARIAMixin;

dictionary ValidityStateFlags {
  boolean valueMissing = false;
  boolean typeMismatch = false;
  boolean patternMismatch = false;
  boolean tooLong = false;
  boolean tooShort = false;
  boolean rangeUnderflow = false;
  boolean rangeOverflow = false;
  boolean stepMismatch = false;
  boolean badInput = false;
  boolean customError = false;
};
```

Each [`ElementInternals`](#elementinternals) has a
<span id="internals-target" class="dfn">target element</span>, which is
a <a href="#custom-element"
id="the-elementinternals-interface:custom-element">custom element</a>.

##### <span class="secno">4.13.7.2</span> Shadow root access<a href="#shadow-root-access" class="self-link"></a>

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-shadowroot"
id="shadow-root-access:dom-elementinternals-shadowroot"><code>shadowRoot</code></a>  
Returns the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-shadowroot"
data-x-internal="shadowroot"><code
id="shadow-root-access:shadowroot">ShadowRoot</code></a> for
`internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="shadow-root-access:internals-target">target element</a>, if the
<a href="#internals-target"
id="shadow-root-access:internals-target-2">target element</a> is a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
id="shadow-root-access:shadow-host" data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow
host</a>, or null otherwise.

The <span id="dom-elementinternals-shadowroot" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementInternals" dfn-type="attribute">`shadowRoot`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  Let `target` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="shadow-root-access:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#internals-target"
    id="shadow-root-access:internals-target-3">target element</a>.

2.  If `target` is not a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="shadow-root-access:shadow-host-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a>, then return null.

3.  Let `shadow` be `target`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
    id="shadow-root-access:concept-element-shadow-root"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>.

4.  If `shadow`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-available-to-element-internals"
    id="shadow-root-access:available-to-element-internals"
    data-x-internal="available-to-element-internals">available to element
    internals</a> is false, then return null.

5.  Return `shadow`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">4.13.7.3</span> Form-associated custom elements<a href="#form-associated-custom-elements" class="self-link"></a>

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-setformvalue"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-setformvalue"><code>setFormValue</code></a>`(``value``)`  
Sets both the <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state">state</a> and
<a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value">submission
value</a> of `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target">target element</a>
to `value`.

If `value` is null, the element won't participate in form submission.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-setformvalue"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-setformvalue-2"><code>setFormValue</code></a>`(``value``, ``state``)`  
Sets the <a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-2">submission
value</a> of `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-2">target
element</a> to `value`, and its <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-2">state</a> to `state`.

If `value` is null, the element won't participate in form submission.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-form"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-form"><code>form</code></a>  
Returns the <a href="#form-owner"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-owner">form owner</a> of
`internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-3">target
element</a>.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-setvalidity"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-setvalidity"><code>setValidity</code></a>`(``flags``, ``message`` [, ``anchor`` ])`  
Marks `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-4">target
element</a> as suffering from the constraints indicated by the `flags`
argument, and sets the element's validation message to `message`. If
`anchor` is specified, the user agent might use it to indicate problems
with the constraints of `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-5">target
element</a> when the <a href="#form-owner"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-owner-2">form owner</a> is
validated interactively or
[`reportValidity()`](#dom-elementinternals-reportvalidity) is called.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-setvalidity"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-setvalidity-2"><code>setValidity</code></a>`({})`  
Marks `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-6">target
element</a> as <a href="#concept-fv-valid"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:concept-fv-valid">satisfying its
constraints</a>.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-willvalidate"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-willvalidate"><code>willValidate</code></a>  
Returns true if `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-7">target
element</a> will be validated when the form is submitted; false
otherwise.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-validity"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-validity"><code>validity</code></a>  
Returns the [`ValidityState`](#validitystate) object for `internals`'s
<a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-8">target
element</a>.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-validationmessage"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-validationmessage"><code>validationMessage</code></a>  
Returns the error message that would be shown to the user if
`internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-9">target
element</a> was to be checked for validity.

`valid`` = ``internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-checkvalidity"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-checkvalidity"><code>checkValidity()</code></a>  
Returns true if `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-10">target
element</a> has no validity problems; false otherwise. Fires an
[`invalid`](#event-invalid) event at the element in the latter case.

`valid`` = ``internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-reportvalidity"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-reportvalidity-2"><code>reportValidity()</code></a>  
Returns true if `internals`'s <a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-11">target
element</a> has no validity problems; otherwise, returns false, fires an
[`invalid`](#event-invalid) event at the element, and (if the event
isn't canceled) reports the problem to the user.

`internals``.`<a href="#dom-elementinternals-labels"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:dom-elementinternals-labels"><code>labels</code></a>  
Returns a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-nodelist"
data-x-internal="nodelist"><code
id="form-associated-custom-elements:nodelist">NodeList</code></a> of all
the [`label`](#the-label-element) elements that `internals`'s
<a href="#internals-target"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-12">target
element</a> is associated with.

Each <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element">form-associated
custom element</a> has <span id="face-submission-value"
class="dfn">submission value</span>. It is used to provide one or more
<a href="#form-entry"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-entry">entries</a> on form
submission. The initial value of <a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-3">submission
value</a> is null, and <a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-4">submission
value</a> can be null, a string, a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code
id="form-associated-custom-elements:file">File</code></a>, or a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:list"
data-x-internal="list">list</a> of <a href="#form-entry"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-entry-2">entries</a>.

Each <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-2">form-associated
custom element</a> has <span id="face-state" class="dfn">state</span>.
It is information with which the user agent can restore a user's input
for the element. The initial value of <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-3">state</a> is null, and
<a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-4">state</a> can be null,
a string, a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code
id="form-associated-custom-elements:file-2">File</code></a>, or a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:list-2"
data-x-internal="list">list</a> of <a href="#form-entry"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-entry-3">entries</a>.

The [`setFormValue()`](#dom-elementinternals-setformvalue) method is
used by the custom element author to set the element's
<a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-5">submission
value</a> and <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-5">state</a>, thus
communicating these to the user agent.

When the user agent believes it is a good idea to restore a
<a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-3">form-associated
custom element</a>'s <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-6">state</a>, for example
<a href="#restore-persisted-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:restore-persisted-state">after
navigation</a> or restarting the user agent, they may
<a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction">enqueue
a custom element callback reaction</a> with that element, callback name
"`formStateRestoreCallback`", and « the state to be restored,
"`restore`" ».

If the user agent has a form-filling assist feature, then when the
feature is invoked, it may
<a href="#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction-2">enqueue
a custom element callback reaction</a> with a
<a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-4">form-associated
custom element</a>, callback name "`formStateRestoreCallback`", and «
the state value determined by history of state value and some
heuristics, "`autocomplete`" ».

In general, the <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-7">state</a> is
information specified by a user, and the
<a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-6">submission
value</a> is a value after canonicalization or sanitization, suitable
for submission to the server. The following examples makes this
concrete:

Suppose that we have a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-5">form-associated
custom element</a> which asks a user to specify a date. The user
specifies <span class="kbd">"3/15/2019"</span>, but the control wishes
to submit `"2019-03-15"` to the server.
<span class="kbd">"3/15/2019"</span> would be a <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-8">state</a> of the
element, and `"2019-03-15"` would be a <a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-7">submission
value</a>.

Suppose you develop a custom element emulating a the behavior of the
existing <a href="#checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)">checkbox</a>
[`input`](#the-input-element) type. Its <a href="#face-submission-value"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-8">submission
value</a> would be the value of its `value` content attribute, or the
string `"on"`. Its <a href="#face-state"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-9">state</a> would be one
of `"checked"`, `"unchecked"`, `"checked/indeterminate"`, or
`"unchecked/indeterminate"`.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-elementinternals-setformvalue" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementInternals"
dfn-type="method">`setFormValue(``value``, ``state``)`</span> method
steps are:

1.  Let `element` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-13">target
    element</a>.

2.  If `element` is not a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-6">form-associated
    custom element</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:notsupportederror"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Set `element`'s <a href="#face-submission-value"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-9">submission
    value</a> to `value` if `value` is not a
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata"
    data-x-internal="formdata"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:formdata">FormData</code></a>
    object, or to a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-clone"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:list-clone"
    data-x-internal="list-clone">clone</a> of `value`'s
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-formdata-entry-list"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:formdata-entry-list"
    data-x-internal="formdata-entry-list">entry list</a> otherwise.

4.  If the `state` argument of the function is omitted, set `element`'s
    <a href="#face-state"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-10">state</a> to its
    <a href="#face-submission-value"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-submission-value-10">submission
    value</a>.

5.  Otherwise, if `state` is a
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata"
    data-x-internal="formdata"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:formdata-2">FormData</code></a>
    object, set `element`'s <a href="#face-state"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-11">state</a> to a
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-clone"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:list-clone-2"
    data-x-internal="list-clone">clone</a> of `state`'s
    <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-formdata-entry-list"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:formdata-entry-list-2"
    data-x-internal="formdata-entry-list">entry list</a>.

6.  Otherwise, set `element`'s <a href="#face-state"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-state-12">state</a> to
    `state`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-7">form-associated
custom element</a> has validity flags named `valueMissing`,
`typeMismatch`, `patternMismatch`, `tooLong`, `tooShort`,
`rangeUnderflow`, `rangeOverflow`, `stepMismatch`, and `customError`.
They are false initially.

Each <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-8">form-associated
custom element</a> has a <span id="face-validation-message"
class="dfn">validation message</span> string. It is the empty string
initially.

Each <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-9">form-associated
custom element</a> has a <span id="face-validation-anchor"
class="dfn">validation anchor</span> element. It is null initially.

The <span id="dom-elementinternals-setvalidity" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementInternals"
dfn-type="method">`setValidity(``flags``, ``message``, ``anchor``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  Let `element` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-14">target
    element</a>.

2.  If `element` is not a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-10">form-associated
    custom element</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:notsupportederror-2"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  If `flags` contains one or more true values and `message` is not
    given or is the empty string, then throw a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>.

4.  For each entry `flag` → `value` of `flags`, set `element`'s validity
    flag with the name `flag` to `value`.

5.  Set `element`'s <a href="#face-validation-message"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-validation-message">validation
    message</a> to the empty string if `message` is not given or all of
    `element`'s validity flags are false, or to `message` otherwise.

6.  If `element`'s `customError` validity flag is true, then set
    `element`'s <a href="#custom-validity-error-message"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:custom-validity-error-message">custom
    validity error message</a> to `element`'s
    <a href="#face-validation-message"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-validation-message-2">validation
    message</a>. Otherwise, set `element`'s
    <a href="#custom-validity-error-message"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:custom-validity-error-message-2">custom
    validity error message</a> to the empty string.

7.  If `anchor` is not given, then set it to `element`.

8.  Otherwise, if `anchor` is not a <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-descendant"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:shadow-including-inclusive-descendant"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-descendant">shadow-including
    inclusive descendant</a> of `element`, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notfounderror"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:notfounderror"
    data-x-internal="notfounderror">"<code>NotFoundError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

9.  Set `element`'s <a href="#face-validation-anchor"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:face-validation-anchor">validation
    anchor</a> to `anchor`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-elementinternals-validationmessage" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementInternals"
dfn-type="attribute">`validationMessage`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `element` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#internals-target"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:internals-target-15">target

2.  If `element` is not a <a href="#form-associated-custom-element"
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:form-associated-custom-element-11">form-associated

    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"

    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="form-associated-custom-elements:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Return `element`'s <a href="#face-validation-message"
