present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vcard:concept-item-80">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard).

The <span id="kind-strings" class="dfn">kind strings</span> are:

<span id="md-vcard-kind-individual" class="dfn">`individual`</span>  
Indicates a single entity (e.g. a person).

<span id="md-vcard-kind-group" class="dfn">`group`</span>  
Indicates multiple entities (e.g. a mailing list).

<span id="md-vcard-kind-org" class="dfn">`org`</span>  
Indicates a single entity that is not a person (e.g. a company).

<span id="md-vcard-kind-location" class="dfn">`location`</span>  
Indicates a geographical place (e.g. an office building).

The <span id="address-type-strings" class="dfn">address type
strings</span> are:

<span id="md-vcard-type-adr-home" class="dfn">`home`</span>  
Indicates a delivery address for a residence.

<span id="md-vcard-type-adr-work" class="dfn">`work`</span>  
Indicates a delivery address for a place of work.

The <span id="telephone-type-strings" class="dfn">telephone type
strings</span> are:

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-home" class="dfn">`home`</span>  
Indicates a residential number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-work" class="dfn">`work`</span>  
Indicates a telephone number for a place of work.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-text" class="dfn">`text`</span>  
Indicates that the telephone number supports text messages (SMS).

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-voice" class="dfn">`voice`</span>  
Indicates a voice telephone number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-fax" class="dfn">`fax`</span>  
Indicates a facsimile telephone number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-cell" class="dfn">`cell`</span>  
Indicates a cellular telephone number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-video" class="dfn">`video`</span>  
Indicates a video conferencing telephone number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-pager" class="dfn">`pager`</span>  
Indicates a paging device telephone number.

<span id="md-vcard-type-tel-textphone" class="dfn">`textphone`</span>  
Indicates a telecommunication device for people with hearing or speech
difficulties.

The <span id="relationship-strings" class="dfn">relationship
strings</span> are:

<span id="md-vcard-rel-emergency" class="dfn">`emergency`</span>  
An emergency contact.

<span id="md-vcard-rel-agent" class="dfn">`agent`</span>  
Another entity that acts on behalf of this entity.

<span id="md-vcard-rel-contact" class="dfn">contact</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-acquaintance" class="dfn">acquaintance</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-friend" class="dfn">friend</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-met" class="dfn">met</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-co-worker" class="dfn">worker</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-colleague" class="dfn">colleague</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-co-resident" class="dfn">resident</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-neighbor" class="dfn">neighbor</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-child" class="dfn">child</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-parent" class="dfn">parent</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-sibling" class="dfn">sibling</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-spouse" class="dfn">spouse</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-kin" class="dfn">kin</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-muse" class="dfn">muse</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-crush" class="dfn">crush</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-date" class="dfn">date</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-sweetheart" class="dfn">sweetheart</span>  
<span id="md-vcard-rel-me" class="dfn">me</span>  
Has the meaning defined in XFN. [\[XFN\]](#refsXFN)

##### <span class="secno">5.3.1.1</span> Conversion to vCard<a href="#conversion-to-vcard" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

Given a list of nodes `nodes` in a [`Document`](#document), a user agent
must run the following algorithm to <span id="extracting-a-vcard"
class="dfn">extract any vCard data represented by those nodes</span>
(only the first vCard is returned):

1.  If none of the nodes in `nodes` are
    <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item">items</a>
    with the
    <a href="#item-types" id="conversion-to-vcard:item-types">item type</a>
    [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard), then there is
    no vCard. Abort the algorithm, returning nothing.

2.  Let `node` be the first node in `nodes` that is an
    <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-2">item</a>
    with the
    <a href="#item-types" id="conversion-to-vcard:item-types-2">item
    type</a> [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard).

3.  Let `output` be an empty string.

4.  <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line">Add a vCard line</a> with
    the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VCARD`" to `output`.

5.  <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-2">Add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`PROFILE`" and the value "`VCARD`" to `output`.

6.  <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-3">Add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`VERSION`" and the value "`4.0`" to `output`.

7.  <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-4">Add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`SOURCE`" and the result of
    <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string">escaping the
    vCard text string</a> that is the document's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:the-document&#39;s-address"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> as the value to
    `output`.

8.  If <a href="#the-title-element-2"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:the-title-element-2">the <code>title</code>
    element</a> is not null, <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-5">add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`NAME`" and with the result of
    <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string-2">escaping the
    vCard text string</a> obtained from <a href="#the-title-element-2"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:the-title-element-2-2">the <code>title</code>
    element</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-descendant-text-content"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:descendant-text-content"
    data-x-internal="descendant-text-content">descendant text content</a>
    as the value to `output`.

9.  Let `sex` be the empty string.

10. Let `gender-identity` be the empty string.

11. For each element `element` that is
    <a href="#the-properties-of-an-item"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:the-properties-of-an-item">a property of the
    item</a> `node`: for each name `name` in `element`'s
    <a href="#property-names"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:property-names">property names</a>, run the
    following substeps:

    1.  Let `parameters` be an empty set of name-value pairs.

    2.  Run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list. The
        steps will set a variable `value`, which is used in the next
        step.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-3">item</a> `subitem` and `name` is [`n`](#md-vcard-n)  
        1.  Let `value` be the empty string.

        2.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`family-name`](#md-vcard-n-family-name) in `subitem`.

        3.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        4.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-2">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`given-name`](#md-vcard-n-given-name) in `subitem`.

        5.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        6.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-3">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`additional-name`](#md-vcard-n-additional-name) in
            `subitem`.

        7.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        8.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-4">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`honorific-prefix`](#md-vcard-n-honorific-prefix) in
            `subitem`.

        9.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        10. Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-5">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`honorific-suffix`](#md-vcard-n-honorific-suffix) in
            `subitem`.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-2">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-4">item</a> `subitem` and `name` is [`adr`](#md-vcard-adr)  
        1.  Let `value` be the empty string.

        2.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-vcard-subproperties"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-vcard-subproperties">collecting vCard
            subproperties</a> named
            [`post-office-box`](#md-vcard-adr-post-office-box) in
            `subitem`.

        3.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        4.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-vcard-subproperties"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-vcard-subproperties-2">collecting
            vCard subproperties</a> named
            [`extended-address`](#md-vcard-adr-extended-address) in
            `subitem`.

        5.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        6.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-vcard-subproperties"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-vcard-subproperties-3">collecting
            vCard subproperties</a> named
            [`street-address`](#md-vcard-adr-street-address) in
            `subitem`.

        7.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        8.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-6">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`locality`](#md-vcard-adr-locality) in `subitem`.

        9.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        10. Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-7">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`region`](#md-vcard-adr-region) in `subitem`.

        11. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        12. Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-8">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`postal-code`](#md-vcard-adr-postal-code) in `subitem`.

        13. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

        14. Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-9">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`country-name`](#md-vcard-adr-country-name) in `subitem`.

        15. If there is a property named [`type`](#md-vcard-adr-type) in
            `subitem`, and the first such property has a
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-3">value</a>
            that is not an
            <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-5">item</a>
            and whose value consists only of
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:alphanumeric-ascii-characters"
            data-x-internal="alphanumeric-ascii-characters">ASCII alphanumerics</a>,
            then add a parameter named "`TYPE`" whose value is the
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-4">value</a>
            of that property to `parameters`.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-5">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-6">item</a> `subitem` and `name` is [`org`](#md-vcard-org)  
        1.  Let `value` be the empty string.

        2.  Append to `value` the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-10">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named
            [`organization-name`](#md-vcard-org-organization-name) in
            `subitem`.

        3.  For each property named
            [`organization-unit`](#md-vcard-org-organization-unit) in
            `subitem`, run the following steps:

            1.  If the <a href="#concept-property-value"
                id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-6">value</a>
                of the property is an
                <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-7">item</a>,
                then skip this property.

            2.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `value`.

            3.  Append the result of
                <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
                id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string-3">escaping the
                vCard text string</a> given by the
                <a href="#concept-property-value"
                id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-7">value</a>
                of the property to `value`.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-8">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-8">item</a> `subitem` with the <a href="#item-types" id="conversion-to-vcard:item-types-3">item
        type</a> [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard) and `name` is [`related`](#md-vcard-related)  
        1.  Let `value` be the empty string.

        2.  If there is a property named [`url`](#md-vcard-related-url)
            in `subitem`, and its element is a
            <a href="#url-property-elements"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:url-property-elements">URL property element</a>,
            then append the result of
            <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string-4">escaping the
            vCard text string</a> given by the
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-9">value</a>
            of the first such property to `value`, and add a parameter
            with the name "`VALUE`" and the value "`URI`" to
            `parameters`.

        3.  If there is a property named [`rel`](#md-vcard-related-rel)
            in `subitem`, and the first such property has a
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-10">value</a>
            that is not an
            <a href="#concept-item" id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-9">item</a>
            and whose value consists only of
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:alphanumeric-ascii-characters-2"
            data-x-internal="alphanumeric-ascii-characters">ASCII alphanumerics</a>,
            then add a parameter named "`RELATION`" whose value is the
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-11">value</a>
            of that property to `parameters`.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-12">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-10">item</a> and `name` is none of the above  
        1.  Let `value` be the result of
            <a href="#collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty-11">collecting
            the first vCard subproperty</a> named `value` in `subitem`.

        2.  If there is a property named `type` in `subitem`, and the
            first such property has a <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-13">value</a>
            that is not an <a href="#concept-item"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-11">item</a> and whose
            value consists only of
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:alphanumeric-ascii-characters-3"
            data-x-internal="alphanumeric-ascii-characters">ASCII alphanumerics</a>,
            then add a parameter named "`TYPE`" whose value is the
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-14">value</a>
            of that property to `parameters`.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-15">value</a> is not an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-12">item</a> and its `name` is [`sex`](#md-vcard-sex)  
        If this is the first such property to be found, set `sex` to the
        property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-16">value</a>.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-17">value</a> is not an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-13">item</a> and its `name` is [`gender-identity`](#md-vcard-gender-identity)  
        If this is the first such property to be found, set
        `gender-identity` to the property's
        <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-18">value</a>.

        Otherwise (the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-19">value</a> is not an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-14">item</a>)  
        1.  Let `value` be the property's
            <a href="#concept-property-value"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-20">value</a>.

        2.  If `element` is one of the <a href="#url-property-elements"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:url-property-elements-2">URL property
            elements</a>, add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and
            the value "`URI`" to `parameters`.

        3.  Otherwise, if `name` is [`bday`](#md-vcard-bday) or
            [`anniversary`](#md-vcard-anniversary) and the `value` is a
            <a href="#valid-date-string"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:valid-date-string">valid date string</a>,
            add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and the value
            "`DATE`" to `parameters`.

        4.  Otherwise, if `name` is [`rev`](#md-vcard-rev) and the
            `value` is a <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
            id="conversion-to-vcard:valid-global-date-and-time-string">valid global
            date and time string</a>, add a parameter with the name
            "`VALUE`" and the value "`DATE-TIME`" to `parameters`.

        5.  Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\ in `value`
            with another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

        6.  Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in `value` with a
            U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

        7.  Unless `name` is [`geo`](#md-vcard-geo), prefix every U+003B
            SEMICOLON character (;) in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE
            SOLIDUS character (\\.

        8.  Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED
            character pair (CRLF) in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE
            SOLIDUS character (\\ followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL
            LETTER N character (n).

        9.  Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or
            U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character in `value` with a U+005C
            REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\ followed by a U+006E LATIN
            SMALL LETTER N character (n).

    3.  <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-6">Add a vCard line</a>
        with the type `name`, the parameters `parameters`, and the value
        `value` to `output`.

12. If either `sex` or `gender-identity` has a value that is not the
    empty string, <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-7">add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`GENDER`" and the value consisting of the
    concatenation of `sex`, a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), and
    `gender-identity` to `output`.

13. <a href="#add-a-vcard-line"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:add-a-vcard-line-8">Add a vCard line</a>
    with the type "`END`" and the value "`VCARD`" to `output`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the above algorithm says that the user agent is to
<span id="add-a-vcard-line" class="dfn">add a vCard line</span>
consisting of a type `type`, optionally some parameters, and a value
`value` to a string `output`, it must run the following steps:

1.  Let `line` be an empty string.

2.  Append `type`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-uppercase"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:converted-to-ascii-uppercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-uppercase">converted to ASCII
    uppercase</a>, to `line`.

3.  If there are any parameters, then for each parameter, in the order
    that they were added, run these substeps:

    1.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `line`.

    2.  Append the parameter's name to `line`.

    3.  Append a U+003D EQUALS SIGN character (=) to `line`.

    4.  Append the parameter's value to `line`.

4.  Append a U+003A COLON character (:) to `line`.

5.  Append `value` to `line`.

6.  Let `maximum length` be 75.

7.  While `line`'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-code-point-length"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:code-point-length"
    data-x-internal="code-point-length">code point length</a> is greater
    than `maximum length`:

    1.  Append the first `maximum length` code points of `line` to
        `output`.

    2.  Remove the first `maximum length` code points from `line`.

    3.  Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to `output`.

    4.  Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to `output`.

    5.  Append a U+0020 SPACE character to `output`.

    6.  Let `maximum length` be 74.

8.  Append (what remains of) `line` to `output`.

9.  Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to `output`.

10. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to `output`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the steps above require the user agent to obtain the result of
<span id="collecting-vcard-subproperties" class="dfn">collecting vCard
subproperties</span> named `subname` in `subitem`, the user agent must
run the following steps:

1.  Let `value` be the empty string.

2.  For each property named `subname` in the item `subitem`, run the
    following substeps:

    1.  If the <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-21">value</a> of
        the property is itself an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-15">item</a>, then skip
        this property.

    2.  If this is not the first property named `subname` in `subitem`
        (ignoring any that were skipped by the previous step), then
        append a U+002C COMMA character (,) to `value`.

    3.  Append the result of <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string-5">escaping the
        vCard text string</a> given by the
        <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-22">value</a> of
        the property to `value`.

3.  Return `value`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the steps above require the user agent to obtain the result of
<span id="collecting-the-first-vcard-subproperty" class="dfn">collecting
the first vCard subproperty</span> named `subname` in `subitem`, the
user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If there are no properties named `subname` in `subitem`, then return
    the empty string.

2.  If the <a href="#concept-property-value"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-23">value</a> of the
    first property named `subname` in `subitem` is an
    <a href="#concept-item"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-item-16">item</a>, then return the
    empty string.

3.  Return the result of <a href="#escaping-the-vcard-text-string"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:escaping-the-vcard-text-string-6">escaping the
    vCard text string</a> given by the <a href="#concept-property-value"
    id="conversion-to-vcard:concept-property-value-24">value</a> of the
    first property named `subname` in `subitem`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the above algorithms say the user agent is to
<span id="escaping-the-vcard-text-string" class="dfn">escape the vCard
text string</span> `value`, the user agent must use the following steps:

1.  Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\ in `value` with
    another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

2.  Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in `value` with a U+005C
    REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

3.  Prefix every U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) in `value` with a U+005C
    REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

4.  Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair
    (CRLF) in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\
    followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).

5.  Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or U+000A LINE
    FEED (LF) character in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS
    character (\\ followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character
    (n).

6.  Return the mutated `value`.

</div>

This algorithm can generate invalid vCard output, if the input does not
conform to the rules described for the
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard)
<a href="#item-types" id="conversion-to-vcard:item-types-4">item
type</a> and <a href="#defined-property-name"
id="conversion-to-vcard:defined-property-name">defined property
names</a>.

##### <span class="secno">5.3.1.2</span> Examples<a href="#examples-2" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div class="example">

Here is a long example vCard for a fictional character called "Jack
Bauer":

``` html
<section id="jack" itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard">
 <h1 itemprop="fn">
  <span itemprop="n" itemscope>
   <span itemprop="given-name">Jack</span>
   <span itemprop="family-name">Bauer</span>
  </span>
 </h1>
 <img itemprop="photo" alt="" src="jack-bauer.jpg">
 <p itemprop="org" itemscope>
  <span itemprop="organization-name">Counter-Terrorist Unit</span>
  (<span itemprop="organization-unit">Los Angeles Division</span>)
 </p>
 <p>
  <span itemprop="adr" itemscope>
   <span itemprop="street-address">10201 W. Pico Blvd.</span><br>
   <span itemprop="locality">Los Angeles</span>,
   <span itemprop="region">CA</span>
   <span itemprop="postal-code">90064</span><br>
   <span itemprop="country-name">United States</span><br>
  </span>
  <span itemprop="geo">34.052339;-118.410623</span>
 </p>
 <h2>Assorted Contact Methods</h2>
 <ul>
  <li itemprop="tel" itemscope>
   <span itemprop="value">+1 (310) 597 3781</span> <span itemprop="type">work</span>
   <meta itemprop="type" content="voice">
  </li>
  <li><a itemprop="url" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Bauer">I'm on Wikipedia</a>
  so you can leave a message on my user talk page.</li>
  <li><a itemprop="url" href="http://www.jackbauerfacts.com/">Jack Bauer Facts</a></li>
  <li itemprop="email"><a href="mailto:j.bauer@la.ctu.gov.invalid">j.bauer@la.ctu.gov.invalid</a></li>
  <li itemprop="tel" itemscope>
   <span itemprop="value">+1 (310) 555 3781</span> <span>
   <meta itemprop="type" content="cell">mobile phone</span>
  </li>
 </ul>
 <ins datetime="2008-07-20 21:00:00+01:00">
  <meta itemprop="rev" content="2008-07-20 21:00:00+01:00">
  <p itemprop="tel" itemscope><strong>Update!</strong>
  My new <span itemprop="type">home</span> phone number is
  <span itemprop="value">01632 960 123</span>.</p>
 </ins>
</section>
```

The odd line wrapping is needed because newlines are meaningful in
microdata: newlines would be preserved in a conversion to, for example,
the vCard format.

</div>

<div class="example">

This example shows a site's contact details (using the
[`address`](#the-address-element) element) containing an address with
two street components:

``` html
<address itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard">
 <strong itemprop="fn"><span itemprop="n" itemscope><span itemprop="given-name">Alfred</span>
 <span itemprop="family-name">Person</span></span></strong> <br>
 <span itemprop="adr" itemscope>
  <span itemprop="street-address">1600 Amphitheatre Parkway</span> <br>
  <span itemprop="street-address">Building 43, Second Floor</span> <br>
  <span itemprop="locality">Mountain View</span>,
   <span itemprop="region">CA</span> <span itemprop="postal-code">94043</span>
 </span>
</address>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The vCard vocabulary can be used to just mark up people's names:

``` html
<span itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard"
><span itemprop=fn><span itemprop="n" itemscope><span itemprop="given-name"
>George</span> <span itemprop="family-name">Washington</span></span
></span></span>
```

This creates a single item with a two name-value pairs, one with the
name "fn" and the value "George Washington", and the other with the name
"n" and a second item as its value, the second item having the two
name-value pairs "given-name" and "family-name" with the values "George"
and "Washington" respectively. This is defined to map to the following
vCard:

    BEGIN:VCARD
    PROFILE:VCARD
    VERSION:4.0
    SOURCE:document's address
    FN:George Washington
    N:Washington;George;;;
    END:VCARD

</div>

#### <span class="secno">5.3.2</span> vEvent<a href="#vevent" class="self-link"></a>

An item with the
<a href="#item-types" id="vevent:item-types">item type</a>
<span id="md-vevent"
class="dfn">`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`</span>
represents an event.

This vocabulary does not <a href="#support-global-identifiers-for-items"
id="vevent:support-global-identifiers-for-items">support global
identifiers for items</a>.

The following are the type's <a href="#defined-property-name"
id="vevent:defined-property-name">defined property names</a>. They are
based on the vocabulary defined in Internet Calendaring and Scheduling
Core Object Specification (iCalendar), where more information on how to
interpret the values can be found. [\[RFC5545\]](#refsRFC5545)

Only the parts of the iCalendar vocabulary relating to events are used
here; this vocabulary cannot express a complete iCalendar instance.

<span id="md-vevent-attach" class="dfn">`attach`</span>  
Gives the address of an associated document for the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value">value</a> must be an
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="vevent:absolute-url" data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute URL</a>.

Any number of properties with the name [`attach`](#md-vevent-attach) may
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item">item</a> with the type
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-categories" class="dfn">`categories`</span>  
Gives the name of a category or tag that the event could be classified
as.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-2">value</a> must be text.

Any number of properties with the name
[`categories`](#md-vevent-categories) may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-2">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-class" class="dfn">`class`</span>  
Gives the access classification of the information regarding the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-3">value</a> must be text with one of
the following values:

- `public`
- `private`
- `confidential`

This is merely advisory and cannot be considered a confidentiality
measure.

A single property with the name [`class`](#md-vevent-class) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-3">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-comment" class="dfn">`comment`</span>  
Gives a comment regarding the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-4">value</a> must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`comment`](#md-vevent-comment)
may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-4">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-description" class="dfn">`description`</span>  
Gives a detailed description of the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-5">value</a> must be text.

A single property with the name [`description`](#md-vevent-description)
may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-5">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-geo" class="dfn">`geo`</span>  
Gives the geographical position of the event.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-6">value</a> must be text and must
match the following syntax:

1.  Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D
    HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
2.  One or more <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="vevent:ascii-digits" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a>.
3.  Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or
    more <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="vevent:ascii-digits-2" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII
    digits</a>.
4.  A U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).
5.  Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D
    HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
6.  One or more <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="vevent:ascii-digits-3" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII
    digits</a>.
7.  Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or
    more <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
    id="vevent:ascii-digits-4" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII
    digits</a>.

</div>

The optional components marked with an asterisk (\*) should be included,
and should have six digits each.

The value specifies latitude and longitude, in that order (i.e., "LAT
LON" ordering), in decimal degrees. The longitude represents the
location east and west of the prime meridian as a positive or negative
real number, respectively. The latitude represents the location north
and south of the equator as a positive or negative real number,
respectively.

A single property with the name [`geo`](#md-vevent-geo) may be present
within each <a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-6">item</a>
with the type
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-location" class="dfn">`location`</span>  
Gives the location of the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-7">value</a> must be text.

A single property with the name [`location`](#md-vevent-location) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-7">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-resources" class="dfn">`resources`</span>  
Gives a resource that will be needed for the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-8">value</a> must be text.

Any number of properties with the name
[`resources`](#md-vevent-resources) may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-8">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-status" class="dfn">`status`</span>  
Gives the confirmation status of the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-9">value</a> must be text with one of
the following values:

- `tentative`
- `confirmed`
- `canceled`

A single property with the name [`status`](#md-vevent-status) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-9">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-summary" class="dfn">`summary`</span>  
Gives a short summary of the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-10">value</a> must be text.

User agents should replace U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters in the
<a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-11">value</a> by U+0020 SPACE
characters when using the value.

A single property with the name [`summary`](#md-vevent-summary) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-10">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-dtend" class="dfn">`dtend`</span>  
Gives the date and time by which the event ends.

If the property with the name [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend) is present
within an <a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-11">item</a>
with the type
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent) that
has a property with the name [`dtstart`](#md-vevent-dtstart) whose value
is a
<a href="#valid-date-string" id="vevent:valid-date-string">valid date
string</a>, then the <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-12">value</a> of the property with the
name [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend) must be text that is a
<a href="#valid-date-string" id="vevent:valid-date-string-2">valid date
string</a> also. Otherwise, the <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-13">value</a> of the property must be
text that is a <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string">valid global date and time
string</a>.

In either case, the <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-14">value</a> be later in time than
the value of the [`dtstart`](#md-vevent-dtstart) property of the same
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-12">item</a>.

The time given by the [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend) property is not
inclusive. For day-long events, therefore, the
[`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend) property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-15">value</a> will be the day *after*
the end of the event.

A single property with the name [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-13">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent),
so long as that
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent) does
not have a property with the name [`duration`](#md-vevent-duration).

<span id="md-vevent-dtstart" class="dfn">`dtstart`</span>  
Gives the date and time at which the event starts.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-16">value</a> must be text that is
either a
<a href="#valid-date-string" id="vevent:valid-date-string-3">valid date
string</a> or a <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-2">valid global date and
time string</a>.

Exactly one property with the name [`dtstart`](#md-vevent-dtstart) must
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-14">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-duration" class="dfn">`duration`</span>  
Gives the duration of the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-17">value</a> must be text that is a
<a href="#valid-vevent-duration-string"
id="vevent:valid-vevent-duration-string">valid vevent duration
string</a>.

The duration represented is the sum of all the durations represented by
integers in the value.

A single property with the name [`duration`](#md-vevent-duration) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-15">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent),
so long as that
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent) does
not have a property with the name [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend).

<span id="md-vevent-transp" class="dfn">`transp`</span>  
Gives whether the event is to be considered as consuming time on a
calendar, for the purpose of free-busy time searches.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-18">value</a> must be text with one of
the following values:

- `opaque`
- `transparent`

A single property with the name [`transp`](#md-vevent-transp) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-16">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-contact" class="dfn">`contact`</span>  
Gives the contact information for the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-19">value</a> must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`contact`](#md-vevent-contact)
may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-17">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-url" class="dfn">`url`</span>  
Gives a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url" id="vevent:url"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a> for the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-20">value</a> must be an
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="vevent:absolute-url-2" data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute
URL</a>.

A single property with the name [`url`](#md-vevent-url) may be present
within each <a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-18">item</a>
with the type
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-uid" class="dfn">`uid`</span>  
Gives a globally unique identifier corresponding to the event.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-21">value</a> must be text.

A single property with the name [`uid`](#md-vevent-uid) may be present
within each <a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-19">item</a>
with the type
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-exdate" class="dfn">`exdate`</span>  
Gives a date and time at which the event does not occur despite the
recurrence rules.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-22">value</a> must be text that is
either a
<a href="#valid-date-string" id="vevent:valid-date-string-4">valid date
string</a> or a <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-3">valid global date and
time string</a>.

Any number of properties with the name [`exdate`](#md-vevent-exdate) may
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-20">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-rdate" class="dfn">`rdate`</span>  
Gives a date and time at which the event recurs.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-23">value</a> must be text that is one
of the following:

- A
  <a href="#valid-date-string" id="vevent:valid-date-string-5">valid date
  string</a>.
- A <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
  id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-4">valid global date and
  time string</a>.
- A <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
  id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-5">valid global date and
  time string</a> followed by a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/) followed by
  a second <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
  id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-6">valid global date and
  time string</a> representing a later time.
- A <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
  id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-7">valid global date and
  time string</a> followed by a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/) followed by
  a <a href="#valid-vevent-duration-string"
  id="vevent:valid-vevent-duration-string-2">valid vevent duration
  string</a>.

Any number of properties with the name [`rdate`](#md-vevent-rdate) may
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-21">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-rrule" class="dfn">`rrule`</span>  
Gives a rule for finding dates and times at which the event occurs.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-24">value</a> must be text that
matches the RECUR value type defined in iCalendar.
[\[RFC5545\]](#refsRFC5545)

A single property with the name [`rrule`](#md-vevent-rrule) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-22">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-created" class="dfn">`created`</span>  
Gives the date and time at which the event information was first created
in a calendaring system.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-25">value</a> must be text that is a
<a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-8">valid global date and
time string</a>.

A single property with the name [`created`](#md-vevent-created) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-23">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-last-modified" class="dfn">`last-modified`</span>  
Gives the date and time at which the event information was last modified
in a calendaring system.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-26">value</a> must be text that is a
<a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
id="vevent:valid-global-date-and-time-string-9">valid global date and
time string</a>.

A single property with the name
[`last-modified`](#md-vevent-last-modified) may be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-24">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<span id="md-vevent-sequence" class="dfn">`sequence`</span>  
Gives a revision number for the event information.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="vevent:concept-property-value-27">value</a> must be text that is a
<a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer">valid non-negative integer</a>.

A single property with the name [`sequence`](#md-vevent-sequence) may be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="vevent:concept-item-25">item</a> with the
type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent).

<div algorithm="">

A string is a <span id="valid-vevent-duration-string" class="dfn">valid
vevent duration string</span> if it matches the following pattern:

1.  A U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P character (P).

2.  One of the following:

    - A <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
      id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer-2">valid non-negative integer</a>
      followed by a U+0057 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W character (W). The
      integer represents a duration of that number of weeks.

    - At least one, and possible both in this order, of the following:

      1.  A <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
          id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer-3">valid non-negative integer</a>
          followed by a U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D character (D). The
          integer represents a duration of that number of days.

      2.  A U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character (T) followed by any
          one of the following, or the first and second of the following
          in that order, or the second and third of the following in
          that order, or all three of the following in this order:

          1.  A <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
              id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer-4">valid non-negative integer</a>
              followed by a U+0048 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER H character (H).
              The integer represents a duration of that number of hours.

          2.  A <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
              id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer-5">valid non-negative integer</a>
              followed by a U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character (M).
              The integer represents a duration of that number of
              minutes.

          3.  A <a href="#valid-non-negative-integer"
              id="vevent:valid-non-negative-integer-6">valid non-negative integer</a>
              followed by a U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character (S).
              The integer represents a duration of that number of
              seconds.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">5.3.2.1</span> Conversion to iCalendar<a href="#conversion-to-icalendar" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

Given a list of nodes `nodes` in a [`Document`](#document), a user agent
must run the following algorithm to <span id="extracting-vevent-data"
class="dfn">extract any vEvent data represented by those nodes</span>:

1.  If none of the nodes in `nodes` are <a href="#concept-item"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-item">items</a> with the type
    [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent),
    then there is no vEvent data. Abort the algorithm, returning
    nothing.

2.  Let `output` be an empty string.

3.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line">Add an iCalendar
    line</a> with the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VCALENDAR`" to
    `output`.

4.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-2">Add an iCalendar
    line</a> with the type "`PRODID`" and the value equal to a
    user-agent-specific string representing the user agent to `output`.

5.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-3">Add an iCalendar
    line</a> with the type "`VERSION`" and the value "`2.0`" to
    `output`.

6.  For each node `node` in `nodes` that is an <a href="#concept-item"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-item-2">item</a> with the type
    [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent),
    run the following steps:

    1.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-4">Add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VEVENT`" to
        `output`.

    2.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-5">Add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type "`DTSTAMP`" and a value consisting of an
        iCalendar DATE-TIME string representing the current date and
        time, with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE-TIME`", to `output`.
        [\[RFC5545\]](#refsRFC5545)

    3.  For each element `element` that is
        <a href="#the-properties-of-an-item"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:the-properties-of-an-item">a property of the
        item</a> `node`: for each name `name` in `element`'s
        <a href="#property-names"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:property-names">property names</a>,
        run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list:

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-property-value">value</a> is an <a href="#concept-item"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-item-3">item</a>  
        Skip the property.

        If the property is [`dtend`](#md-vevent-dtend)  
        If the property is [`dtstart`](#md-vevent-dtstart)  
        If the property is [`exdate`](#md-vevent-exdate)  
        If the property is [`rdate`](#md-vevent-rdate)  
        If the property is [`created`](#md-vevent-created)  
        If the property is [`last-modified`](#md-vevent-last-modified)  
        Let `value` be the result of stripping all U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS
        (-) and U+003A COLON (:) characters from the property's
        <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-property-value-2">value</a>.

        If the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-property-value-3">value</a>
        is a <a href="#valid-date-string"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:valid-date-string">valid date string</a>,
        then <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-6">add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type `name` and the value `value` to `output`,
        with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE`".

        Otherwise, if the property's <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-property-value-4">value</a>
        is a <a href="#valid-global-date-and-time-string"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:valid-global-date-and-time-string">valid
        global date and time string</a>, then
        <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-7">add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type `name` and the value `value` to `output`,
        with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE-TIME`".

        Otherwise, skip the property.

        Otherwise  
        <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-8">Add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type `name` and the property's
        <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:concept-property-value-5">value</a>
        to `output`.

    4.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
        id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-9">Add an iCalendar
        line</a> with the type "`END`" and the value "`VEVENT`" to
        `output`.

7.  <a href="#add-an-icalendar-line"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:add-an-icalendar-line-10">Add an iCalendar
    line</a> with the type "`END`" and the value "`VCALENDAR`" to
    `output`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the above algorithm says that the user agent is to
<span id="add-an-icalendar-line" class="dfn">add an iCalendar
line</span> consisting of a type `type`, a value `value`, and optionally
an annotation, to a string `output`, it must run the following steps:

1.  Let `line` be an empty string.

2.  Append `type`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-uppercase"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:converted-to-ascii-uppercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-uppercase">converted to ASCII
    uppercase</a>, to `line`.

3.  If there is an annotation:

    1.  Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to `line`.

    2.  Append the annotation to `line`.

4.  Append a U+003A COLON character (:) to `line`.

5.  Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\ in `value` with
    another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

6.  Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in `value` with a U+005C
    REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

7.  Prefix every U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) in `value` with a U+005C
    REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\.

8.  Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair
    (CRLF) in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\
    followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).

9.  Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or U+000A LINE
    FEED (LF) character in `value` with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS
    character (\\ followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character
    (n).

10. Append `value` to `line`.

11. Let `maximum length` be 75.

12. While `line`'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-code-point-length"
    id="conversion-to-icalendar:code-point-length"
    data-x-internal="code-point-length">code point length</a> is greater
    than `maximum length`:

    1.  Append the first `maximum length` code points of `line` to
        `output`.

    2.  Remove the first `maximum length` code points from `line`.

    3.  Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to `output`.

    4.  Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to `output`.

    5.  Append a U+0020 SPACE character to `output`.

    6.  Let `maximum length` be 74.

13. Append (what remains of) `line` to `output`.

14. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to `output`.

15. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to `output`.

</div>

This algorithm can generate invalid iCalendar output, if the input does
not conform to the rules described for the
[`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#md-vevent)
<a href="#item-types" id="conversion-to-icalendar:item-types">item
type</a> and <a href="#defined-property-name"
id="conversion-to-icalendar:defined-property-name">defined property
names</a>.

##### <span class="secno">5.3.2.2</span> Examples<a href="#examples-3" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div class="example">

Here is an example of a page that uses the vEvent vocabulary to mark up
an event:

``` html
<body itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent">
 ...
 <h1 itemprop="summary">Bluesday Tuesday: Money Road</h1>
 ...
 <time itemprop="dtstart" datetime="2009-05-05T19:00:00Z">May 5th @ 7pm</time>
 (until <time itemprop="dtend" datetime="2009-05-05T21:00:00Z">9pm</time>)
 ...
 <a href="http://livebrum.co.uk/2009/05/05/bluesday-tuesday-money-road"
    rel="bookmark" itemprop="url">Link to this page</a>
 ...
 <p>Location: <span itemprop="location">The RoadHouse</span></p>
 ...
 <p><input type=button value="Add to Calendar"
           onclick="location = getCalendar(this)"></p>
 ...
 <meta itemprop="description" content="via livebrum.co.uk">
</body>
```

The `getCalendar()` function is left as an exercise for the reader.

The same page could offer some markup, such as the following, for
copy-and-pasting into blogs:

``` html
<div itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent">
 <p>I'm going to
 <strong itemprop="summary">Bluesday Tuesday: Money Road</strong>,
 <time itemprop="dtstart" datetime="2009-05-05T19:00:00Z">May 5th at 7pm</time>
 to <time itemprop="dtend" datetime="2009-05-05T21:00:00Z">9pm</time>,
 at <span itemprop="location">The RoadHouse</span>!</p>
 <p><a href="http://livebrum.co.uk/2009/05/05/bluesday-tuesday-money-road"
       itemprop="url">See this event on livebrum.co.uk</a>.</p>
 <meta itemprop="description" content="via livebrum.co.uk">
</div>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">5.3.3</span> Licensing works<a href="#licensing-works" class="self-link"></a>

An item with the
<a href="#item-types" id="licensing-works:item-types">item type</a>
<span id="md-work" class="dfn">`http://n.whatwg.org/work`</span>
represents a work (e.g. an article, an image, a video, a song, etc.).
This type is primarily intended to allow authors to include licensing
information for works.

The following are the type's <a href="#defined-property-name"
id="licensing-works:defined-property-name">defined property names</a>.

<span id="md-work-work" class="dfn">`work`</span>  
Identifies the work being described.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="licensing-works:concept-property-value">value</a> must be an
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="licensing-works:absolute-url"
data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute URL</a>.

Exactly one property with the name [`work`](#md-work-work) must be
present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="licensing-works:concept-item">item</a> with
the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#md-work).

<span id="md-work-title" class="dfn">`title`</span>  
Gives the name of the work.

A single property with the name [`title`](#md-work-title) may be present
within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="licensing-works:concept-item-2">item</a>
with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#md-work).

<span id="md-work-author" class="dfn">`author`</span>  
Gives the name or contact information of one of the authors or creators
of the work.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="licensing-works:concept-property-value-2">value</a> must be either
an <a href="#concept-item" id="licensing-works:concept-item-3">item</a>
with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#md-vcard), or
text.

Any number of properties with the name [`author`](#md-work-author) may
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="licensing-works:concept-item-4">item</a>
with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#md-work).

<span id="md-work-license" class="dfn">`license`</span>  
Identifies one of the licenses under which the work is available.

The <a href="#concept-property-value"
id="licensing-works:concept-property-value-3">value</a> must be an
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="licensing-works:absolute-url-2"
data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute URL</a>.

Any number of properties with the name [`license`](#md-work-license) may
be present within each
<a href="#concept-item" id="licensing-works:concept-item-5">item</a>
with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#md-work).

##### <span class="secno">5.3.3.1</span> Examples<a href="#examples-4" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div class="example">

This example shows an embedded image entitled My Pond, licensed under
the Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International License
and the MIT license simultaneously.

``` html
<figure itemscope itemtype="http://n.whatwg.org/work">
 <img itemprop="work" src="mypond.jpeg">
 <figcaption>
  <p><cite itemprop="title">My Pond</cite></p>
  <p><small>Licensed under the <a itemprop="license"
  href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Creative
  Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International License</a>
  and the <a itemprop="license"
  href="http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php">MIT
  license</a>.</small>
 </figcaption>
</figure>
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">5.4</span> Converting HTML to other formats<a href="#converting-html-to-other-formats" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">5.4.1</span> JSON<a href="#json" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

Given a list of nodes `nodes` in a [`Document`](#document), a user agent
must run the following algorithm to <span id="extracting-json"
class="dfn">extract the microdata from those nodes into a JSON
form</span>:

1.  Let `result` be an empty object.

2.  Let `items` be an empty array.

3.  For each `node` in `nodes`, check if the element is a
    <a href="#top-level-microdata-items"
    id="json:top-level-microdata-items">top-level microdata item</a>,
    and if it is then
    <a href="#get-the-object" id="json:get-the-object">get the object</a>
    for that element and add it to `items`.

4.  Add an entry to `result` called "`items`" whose value is the array
    `items`.

5.  Return the result of serializing `result` to JSON in the shortest
    possible way (meaning no whitespace between tokens, no unnecessary
    zero digits in numbers, and only using Unicode escapes in strings
    for characters that do not have a dedicated escape sequence), and
    with a lowercase "`e`" used, when appropriate, in the representation
    of any numbers. [\[JSON\]](#refsJSON)

</div>

This algorithm returns an object with a single property that is an
array, instead of just returning an array, so that it is possible to
extend the algorithm in the future if necessary.

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to <span id="get-the-object" class="dfn">get the
object</span> for an item `item`, optionally with a list of elements
`memory`, it must run the following substeps:

1.  Let `result` be an empty object.

2.  If no `memory` was passed to the algorithm, let `memory` be an empty
    list.

3.  Add `item` to `memory`.

4.  If the `item` has any
    <a href="#item-types" id="json:item-types">item types</a>, add an
    entry to `result` called "`type`" whose value is an array listing
    the <a href="#item-types" id="json:item-types-2">item types</a> of
    `item`, in the order they were specified on the
    [`itemtype`](#attr-itemtype) attribute.

5.  If the `item` has a
    <a href="#global-identifier" id="json:global-identifier">global
    identifier</a>, add an entry to `result` called "`id`" whose value
    is the
    <a href="#global-identifier" id="json:global-identifier-2">global
    identifier</a> of `item`.

6.  Let `properties` be an empty object.

7.  For each element `element` that has one or more
    <a href="#property-names" id="json:property-names">property names</a>
    and is one of <a href="#the-properties-of-an-item"
    id="json:the-properties-of-an-item">the properties of the item</a>
    `item`, in the order those elements are given by the algorithm that
    returns <a href="#the-properties-of-an-item"
    id="json:the-properties-of-an-item-2">the properties of an item</a>,
    run the following substeps:

    1.  Let `value` be the <a href="#concept-property-value"
        id="json:concept-property-value">property value</a> of
        `element`.

    2.  If `value` is an
        <a href="#concept-item" id="json:concept-item">item</a>, then:
        If `value` is in `memory`, then let `value` be the string
        "`ERROR`". Otherwise,
        <a href="#get-the-object" id="json:get-the-object-2">get the object</a>
        for `value`, passing a copy of `memory`, and then replace
        `value` with the object returned from those steps.

    3.  For each name `name` in `element`'s
        <a href="#property-names" id="json:property-names-2">property names</a>,
        run the following substeps:

        1.  If there is no entry named `name` in `properties`, then add
            an entry named `name` to `properties` whose value is an
            empty array.

        2.  Append `value` to the entry named `name` in `properties`.

8.  Add an entry to `result` called "`properties`" whose value is the
    object `properties`.

9.  Return `result`.

</div>

<div class="example">

For example, take this markup:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
<title>My Blog</title>
<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
 <header>
  <h1 itemprop="headline">Progress report</h1>
  <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2013-08-29">today</time></p>
  <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
 </header>
 <p>All in all, he's doing well with his swim lessons. The biggest thing was he had trouble
 putting his head in, but we got it down.</p>
 <section>
  <h1>Comments</h1>
  <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c1">
   <link itemprop="url" href="#c1">
   <footer>
    <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
     <span itemprop="name">Greg</span>
    </span></p>
    <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2013-08-29">15 minutes ago</time></p>
   </footer>
   <p>Ha!</p>
  </article>
  <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c2">
   <link itemprop="url" href="#c2">
   <footer>
    <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
     <span itemprop="name">Charlotte</span>
    </span></p>
    <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2013-08-29">5 minutes ago</time></p>
   </footer>
   <p>When you say "we got it down"...</p>
  </article>
 </section>
</article>
```

It would be turned into the following JSON by the algorithm above
(supposing that the page's URL was
`https://blog.example.com/progress-report`):

``` json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": [ "http://schema.org/BlogPosting" ],
      "properties": {
        "headline": [ "Progress report" ],
        "datePublished": [ "2013-08-29" ],
        "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report?comments=0" ],
        "comment": [
          {
            "type": [ "http://schema.org/UserComments" ],
            "properties": {
              "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report#c1" ],
              "creator": [
                {
                  "type": [ "http://schema.org/Person" ],
                  "properties": {
                    "name": [ "Greg" ]
                  }
                }
              ],
              "commentTime": [ "2013-08-29" ]
            }
          },
          {
            "type": [ "http://schema.org/UserComments" ],
            "properties": {
              "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report#c2" ],
              "creator": [
                {
                  "type": [ "http://schema.org/Person" ],
                  "properties": {
                    "name": [ "Charlotte" ]
                  }
                }
              ],
              "commentTime": [ "2013-08-29" ]
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.1</span> The [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute<a href="#the-hidden-attribute" class="self-link"></a>
