All
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-hidden-attribute:html-elements">HTML
elements</a> may have the <span id="attr-hidden" class="dfn"
dfn-for="html-global" dfn-type="element-attr">`hidden`</span> content
attribute set. The [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-hidden-attribute:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-hidden-hidden" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/hidden" dfn-type="attr-value">`hidden`</span> | <span id="attr-hidden-hidden-state" class="dfn">Hidden</span> | Will not be rendered. |
| <span id="attr-hidden-until-found" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/hidden" dfn-type="attr-value">`until-found`</span> | <span id="attr-hidden-until-found-state" class="dfn">Hidden Until Found</span> | Will not be rendered, but content inside will be accessible to <a href="#find-in-page-2"
id="the-hidden-attribute:find-in-page-2">find-in-page</a> and <a href="#navigate-fragid"
id="the-hidden-attribute:navigate-fragid">fragment navigation</a>. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* is the
<span id="attr-hidden-not-hidden-state" class="dfn">Not Hidden</span>
state, and its *[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* and
*[empty value default](#empty-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state">Hidden</a> state.

</div>

When an element has the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-2">Hidden</a> state,
it indicates that the element is not yet, or is no longer, directly
relevant to the page's current state, or that it is being used to
declare content to be reused by other parts of the page as opposed to
being directly accessed by the user. User agents should not render
elements that are in the <a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-3">Hidden</a> state.

The requirement for user agents not to render elements that are in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-4">Hidden</a> state
can be implemented indirectly through the style layer. For example, a
web browser could implement these requirements [using the rules
suggested in the Rendering section](#hiddenCSS).

When an element has the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state">Hidden Until
Found</a> state, it indicates that the element is hidden like the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-5">Hidden</a> state
but the content inside the element will be accessible to
<a href="#find-in-page-2"
id="the-hidden-attribute:find-in-page-2-2">find-in-page</a> and
<a href="#navigate-fragid"
id="the-hidden-attribute:navigate-fragid-2">fragment navigation</a>.
When these features attempt to scroll to a target which is in the
element's subtree, the user agent will remove the
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in order to reveal the content before
scrolling to it by running the <a href="#ancestor-revealing-algorithm"
id="the-hidden-attribute:ancestor-revealing-algorithm">ancestor
revealing algorithm</a> on the target node.

Web browsers will use 'content-visibility: hidden' instead of 'display:
none' when the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute is in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-2">Hidden Until
Found</a> state, as specified in the [Rendering section](#hiddenCSS).

<div class="note">

Because this attribute is typically implemented using CSS, it's also
possible to override it using CSS. For instance, a rule that applies
'display: block' to all elements will cancel the effects of the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-6">Hidden</a> state.
Authors therefore have to take care when writing their style sheets to
make sure that the attribute is still styled as expected. In addition,
legacy user agents which don't support the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-3">Hidden Until
Found</a> state will have 'display: none' instead of
'content-visibility: hidden', so authors are encouraged to make sure
that their style sheets don't change the 'display' or
'content-visibility' properties of
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-4">Hidden Until
Found</a> elements.

Since elements with the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-5">Hidden Until
Found</a> state use 'content-visibility: hidden' instead of 'display:
none', there are two caveats of the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-6">Hidden Until
Found</a> state that make it different from the
<a href="#attr-hidden-hidden-state"
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-hidden-state-7">Hidden</a> state:

1.  The element needs to be affected by
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#containment-layout"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:layout-containment"
    data-x-internal="layout-containment">layout containment</a> in order
    to be revealed by find-in-page. This means that if the element in
    the <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-7">Hidden Until
    Found</a> state has a 'display' value of 'none', 'contents', or
    'inline', then the element will not be revealed by find-in-page.

2.  The element will still have a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-visibility"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:&#39;visibility&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;visibility&#39;">generated box</a> when in the
    <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-8">Hidden Until
    Found</a> state, which means that borders, margin, and padding will
    still be rendered around the element.

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following skeletal example, the attribute is used to hide the web
game's main screen until the user logs in:

``` html
  <h1>The Example Game</h1>
  <section id="login">
   <h2>Login</h2>
   <form>
    ...
    <!-- calls login() once the user's credentials have been checked -->
   </form>
   <script>
    function login() {
      // switch screens
      document.getElementById('login').hidden = true;
      document.getElementById('game').hidden = false;
    }
   </script>
  </section>
  <section id="game" hidden>
   ...
  </section>
```

</div>

The [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute must not be used to hide content
that could legitimately be shown in another presentation. For example,
it is incorrect to use [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) to hide panels in a
tabbed dialog, because the tabbed interface is merely a kind of overflow
presentation — one could equally well just show all the form controls in
one big page with a scrollbar. It is similarly incorrect to use this
attribute to hide content just from one presentation — if something is
marked [`hidden`](#attr-hidden), it is hidden from all presentations,
including, for instance, screen readers.

Elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) must not
<a href="#hyperlink" id="the-hidden-attribute:hyperlink">hyperlink</a>
to elements that are [`hidden`](#attr-hidden). The `for` attributes of
[`label`](#the-label-element) and [`output`](#the-output-element)
elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) must similarly
not refer to elements that are [`hidden`](#attr-hidden). In both cases,
such references would cause user confusion.

Elements and scripts may, however, refer to elements that are
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) in other contexts.

<div class="example">

For example, it would be incorrect to use the
[`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute to link to a section marked
with the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute. If the content is not
applicable or relevant, then there is no reason to link to it.

It would be fine, however, to use the ARIA
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-describedby"
data-x-internal="attr-aria-describedby"><code
id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-aria-describedby">aria-describedby</code></a>
attribute to refer to descriptions that are themselves
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden). While hiding the descriptions implies that
they are not useful alone, they could be written in such a way that they
are useful in the specific context of being referenced from the elements
that they describe.

Similarly, a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element with the
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute could be used by a scripted graphics
engine as an off-screen buffer, and a form control could refer to a
hidden [`form`](#the-form-element) element using its
[`form`](#attr-fae-form) attribute.

</div>

Elements in a section hidden by the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute
are still active, e.g. scripts and form controls in such sections still
execute and submit respectively. Only their presentation to the user
changes.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

[HTMLElement/hidden](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/hidden "The HTMLElement property hidden reflects the value of the element's hidden attribute.")

Support in all current engines.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-hidden" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`hidden`</span> getter steps are:

1.  If the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute is in the
    <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-9">Hidden Until
    Found</a> state, then return
    "[`until-found`](#attr-hidden-until-found)".

2.  If the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute is set, then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`hidden`](#dom-hidden) setter steps are:

1.  If the given value is a string that is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:ascii-case-insensitive"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "[`until-found`](#attr-hidden-until-found)", then set the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute to
    "[`until-found`](#attr-hidden-until-found)".

2.  Otherwise, if the given value is false, then remove the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute.

3.  Otherwise, if the given value is the empty string, then remove the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute.

4.  Otherwise, if the given value is null, then remove the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute.

5.  Otherwise, if the given value is 0, then remove the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute.

6.  Otherwise, if the given value is NaN, then remove the
    [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute.

7.  Otherwise, set the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute to the empty
    string.

</div>

An <span id="ancestor-reveal-pair" class="dfn">ancestor reveal
pair</span> is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple"
id="the-hidden-attribute:tuple" data-x-internal="tuple">tuple</a>
consisting of a <span id="ancestor-reveal-pair-node"
class="dfn">node</span> and a <span id="ancestor-reveal-pair-string"
class="dfn">string</span>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="ancestor-revealing-algorithm" class="dfn">ancestor
revealing algorithm</span> given a node `target` is:

1.  Let `ancestorsToReveal` be « ».

2.  Let `ancestor` be `target`.

3.  While `ancestor` has a parent node within the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
    id="the-hidden-attribute:flat-tree" data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat
    tree</a>:

    1.  If `ancestor` has a [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
        <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
        id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-10">Hidden Until
        Found</a> state, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="the-hidden-attribute:list-append"
        data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> (`ancestor`,
        "`until-found`") to `ancestorsToReveal`.

    2.  If `ancestor` is slotted into the second slot of a
        [`details`](#the-details-element) element which does not have an
        [`open`](#attr-details-open) attribute, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="the-hidden-attribute:list-append-2"
        data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> (`ancestor`'s parent
        node, "`details`") to `ancestorsToReveal`.

    3.  Set `ancestor` to the parent node of `ancestor` within the
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
        id="the-hidden-attribute:flat-tree-2" data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat
        tree</a>.

4.  For each (`ancestorToReveal`, `revealType`) of `ancestorsToReveal`:

    1.  If `ancestorToReveal` is not
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
        id="the-hidden-attribute:connected"
        data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then return.

    2.  If `revealType` is "`until-found`":

        1.  If `ancestorToReveal`'s [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute
            is not in the <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
            id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-11">Hidden Until
            Found</a> state, then return.

        2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="the-hidden-attribute:concept-event-fire"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
            [`beforematch`](#event-beforematch) at `ancestorToReveal`
            with the
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
            data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
            id="the-hidden-attribute:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
            attribute initialized to true.

        3.  If `ancestorToReveal` is not
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
            id="the-hidden-attribute:connected-2"
            data-x-internal="connected">connected</a>, then return.

        4.  If `ancestorToReveal`'s [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute
            is not in the <a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
            id="the-hidden-attribute:attr-hidden-until-found-state-12">Hidden Until
            Found</a> state, then return.

        5.  Remove the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute from
            `ancestorToReveal`.

    3.  Otherwise:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="the-hidden-attribute:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
            `revealType` is "`details`".

        2.  If `ancestorToReveal` has an [`open`](#attr-details-open)
            attribute, then return.

        3.  Set `ancestorToReveal`'s [`open`](#attr-details-open)
            attribute to the empty string.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.2</span> Page visibility<a href="#page-visibility" class="self-link"></a>

A <a href="#traversable-navigable"
id="page-visibility:traversable-navigable">traversable navigable</a>'s
<a href="#system-visibility-state"
id="page-visibility:system-visibility-state">system visibility state</a>,
including its initial value upon creation, is determined by the user
agent. It represents, for example, whether the browser window is
minimized, a browser tab is currently in the background, or a system
element such as a task switcher obscures the page.

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent determines that the <a href="#system-visibility-state"
id="page-visibility:system-visibility-state-2">system visibility
state</a> for <a href="#traversable-navigable"
id="page-visibility:traversable-navigable-2">traversable navigable</a>
`traversable` has changed to `newState`, it must run the following
steps:

1.  Let `navigables` be the <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
    id="page-visibility:inclusive-descendant-navigables">inclusive
    descendant navigables</a> of `traversable`'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="page-visibility:nav-document">active
    document</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="page-visibility:list-iterate" data-x-internal="list-iterate">For
    each</a> `navigable` of `navigables` <span class="XXX">in what
    order?</span>:

    1.  Let `document` be `navigable`'s
        <a href="#nav-document" id="page-visibility:nav-document-2">active
        document</a>.

    2.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
        id="page-visibility:queue-a-global-task">Queue a global task</a>
        on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
        id="page-visibility:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction task
        source</a> given `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="page-visibility:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a>
        to <a href="#update-the-visibility-state"
        id="page-visibility:update-the-visibility-state">update the visibility
        state</a> of `document` with `newState`.

</div>

A [`Document`](#document) has a <span id="visibility-state" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">visibility state</span>, which is either
"`hidden`" or "`visible`", initially set to "`hidden`".

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="update-the-visibility-state" class="dfn">update the
visibility state</span> of [`Document`](#document) `document` to
`visibilityState`:

1.  If `document`'s <a href="#visibility-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibility-state-3">visibility state</a> equals
    `visibilityState`, then return.

2.  Set `document`'s <a href="#visibility-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibility-state-4">visibility state</a> to
    `visibilityState`.

3.  <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry"
    id="page-visibility:queue-a-performance-entry"
    data-x-internal="queue-a-performance-entry">Queue</a> a new
    [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) whose
    <a href="#visibilitystateentry-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibilitystateentry-state">visibility state</a>
    is `visibilityState` and whose
    <a href="#visibilitystateentry-timestamp"
    id="page-visibility:visibilitystateentry-timestamp">timestamp</a> is
    the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
    id="page-visibility:current-high-resolution-time"
    data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
    time</a> given `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="page-visibility:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
    object</a>.

4.  Run the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/screen-orientation/#dfn-screen-orientation-change-steps"
    id="page-visibility:screen-orientation-change-steps"
    data-x-internal="screen-orientation-change-steps">screen orientation
    change steps</a> with `document`.
    [\[SCREENORIENTATION\]](#refsSCREENORIENTATION)

5.  Run the <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions/#view-transition-page-visibility-change-steps"
    id="page-visibility:view-transition-page-visibility-change-steps"
    data-x-internal="view-transition-page-visibility-change-steps">view
    transition page visibility change steps</a> with `document`.

6.  Run any <span id="page-visibility-change-steps" class="dfn"
    export="">page visibility change steps</span> which may be defined
    in other specifications, with <a href="#visibility-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibility-state-5">visibility state</a> and
    `document`.

    It would be better if specification authors sent a pull request to
    add calls from here into their specifications directly, instead of
    using the <a href="#page-visibility-change-steps"
    id="page-visibility:page-visibility-change-steps">page visibility change
    steps</a> hook, to ensure well-defined cross-specification call
    order. As of the time of this writing the following specifications
    are known to have <a href="#page-visibility-change-steps"
    id="page-visibility:page-visibility-change-steps-2">page visibility
    change steps</a>, which will be run in an unspecified order: Device
    Posture API and Web NFC. [\[DEVICEPOSTURE\]](#refsDEVICEPOSTURE)
    [\[WEBNFC\]](#refsWEBNFC)

7.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="page-visibility:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`visibilitychange`](#event-visibilitychange) at `document`, with
    its <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="page-visibility:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a> attribute
    initialized to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="set-the-initial-visibility-state" class="dfn">set the
initial visibility state</span> of [`Document`](#document) `document` to
`visibilityState`:

1.  Set `document`'s <a href="#visibility-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibility-state-6">visibility state</a> to
    `visibilityState`.

2.  <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry"
    id="page-visibility:queue-a-performance-entry-2"
    data-x-internal="queue-a-performance-entry">Queue</a> a new
    [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) whose
    <a href="#visibilitystateentry-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibilitystateentry-state-2">visibility state</a>
    is `document`'s <a href="#visibility-state"
    id="page-visibility:visibility-state-7">visibility state</a> and
    whose <a href="#visibilitystateentry-timestamp"
    id="page-visibility:visibilitystateentry-timestamp-2">timestamp</a>
    is 0.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.2.1</span> The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) interface<a href="#the-visibilitystateentry-interface" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**⚠**MDN

<div class="feature">

[VisibilityStateEntry](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/VisibilityStateEntry "The VisibilityStateEntry interface provides timings of page visibility state changes, i.e., when a tab changes from the foreground to the background or vice versa.")

Support in one engine only.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox no">FirefoxNo</span><span class="safari no">SafariNo</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome115+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge115+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) interface exposes
visibility changes to the document, from the moment the document becomes
active.

<div class="example">

For example, this allows JavaScript code in the page to examine
correlation between visibility changes and paint timing:

``` js
function wasHiddenBeforeFirstContentfulPaint() {
    const fcpEntry = performance.getEntriesByName("first-contentful-paint")[0];
    const visibilityStateEntries = performance.getEntriesByType("visibility-state");
    return visibilityStateEntries.some(e =>
                                            e.startTime < fcpEntry.startTime &&
                                            e.name === "hidden");
}
```

</div>

Since hiding a page can cause throttling of rendering and other
user-agent operations, it is common to use visibility changes as an
indication that such throttling has occurred. However, other things
could also cause throttling in different browsers, such as long periods
of inactivity.

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window)]
interface VisibilityStateEntry : PerformanceEntry {
  readonly attribute DOMString name;                 // shadows inherited name
  readonly attribute DOMString entryType;            // shadows inherited entryType
  readonly attribute DOMHighResTimeStamp startTime;  // shadows inherited startTime
  readonly attribute unsigned long duration;         // shadows inherited duration
};
```

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) has an associated
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
id="the-visibilitystateentry-interface:domhighrestimestamp"
data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code>DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>
<span id="visibilitystateentry-timestamp" class="dfn">timestamp</span>.

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#visibilitystateentry) has an associated
"`visible`" or "`hidden`" <span id="visibilitystateentry-state"
class="dfn">visibility state</span>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="visibilitystateentry-name" class="dfn"
dfn-for="VisibilityStateEntry" dfn-type="attribute">`name`</span> getter
steps are to return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-visibilitystateentry-interface:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#visibilitystateentry-state"
id="the-visibilitystateentry-interface:visibilitystateentry-state">visibility
state</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="visibilitystateentry-entrytype" class="dfn"
dfn-for="VisibilityStateEntry" dfn-type="attribute">`entryType`</span>
getter steps are to return "`visibility-state`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="visibilitystateentry-starttime" class="dfn"
dfn-for="VisibilityStateEntry" dfn-type="attribute">`startTime`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-visibilitystateentry-interface:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#visibilitystateentry-timestamp"
id="the-visibilitystateentry-interface:visibilitystateentry-timestamp">timestamp</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="visibilitystateentry-duration" class="dfn"
dfn-for="VisibilityStateEntry" dfn-type="attribute">`duration`</span>
getter steps are to return zero.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.3</span> Inert subtrees<a href="#inert-subtrees" class="self-link"></a>

See also [`inert`](#the-inert-attribute) for an explanation of the
attribute of the same name.

A node (in particular elements and text nodes) can be <span id="inert"
class="dfn">inert</span>. When a node is
<a href="#inert" id="inert-subtrees:inert">inert</a>:

- Hit-testing must act as if the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#pointer-events-control"
  id="inert-subtrees:&#39;pointer-events&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;pointer-events&#39;">'pointer-events'</a> CSS
  property were set to 'none'.

- Text selection functionality must act as if the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#content-selection"
  id="inert-subtrees:&#39;user-select&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;user-select&#39;">'user-select'</a> CSS property
  were set to 'none'.

- If it is
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
  id="inert-subtrees:editable" data-x-internal="editable">editable</a>,
  the node behaves as if it were non-editable.

- The user agent should ignore the node for the purposes of
  <a href="#find-in-page-2"
  id="inert-subtrees:find-in-page-2">find-in-page</a>.

Inert nodes generally cannot be focused, and user agents do not expose
the inert nodes to accessibility APIs or assistive technologies. Inert
nodes that are <a href="#concept-command"
id="inert-subtrees:concept-command">commands</a> will become inoperable
to users, in the manner described above.

User agents may allow the user to override the restrictions on
<a href="#find-in-page-2"
id="inert-subtrees:find-in-page-2-2">find-in-page</a> and text
selection, however.

By default, a node is not
<a href="#inert" id="inert-subtrees:inert-2">inert</a>.

#### <span class="secno">6.3.1</span> Modal dialogs and inert subtrees<a href="#modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) `document` is
<span id="blocked-by-a-modal-dialog" class="dfn">blocked by a modal
dialog</span> `subject` if `subject` is the topmost
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element in `document`'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:top-layer"
data-x-internal="top-layer">top layer</a>. While `document` is so
blocked, every node that is
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:connected"
data-x-internal="connected">connected</a> to `document`, with the
exception of the `subject` element and its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:flat-tree"
data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat tree</a> descendants, must become
<a href="#inert" id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:inert">inert</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

`subject` can additionally become
<a href="#inert" id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:inert-2">inert</a>
via the [`inert`](#the-inert-attribute) attribute, but only if specified
on `subject` itself (i.e., `subject` escapes inertness of ancestors);
`subject`'s <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:flat-tree-2"
data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat tree</a> descendants can become
<a href="#inert" id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:inert-3">inert</a>
in a similar fashion.

</div>

The [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element's
[`showModal()`](#dom-dialog-showmodal) method causes this mechanism to
trigger, by <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#add-an-element-to-the-top-layer"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:add-an-element-to-the-top-layer"
data-x-internal="add-an-element-to-the-top-layer">adding</a> the
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element to its
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer"
id="modal-dialogs-and-inert-subtrees:top-layer-2"
data-x-internal="top-layer">top layer</a>.

#### <span class="secno">6.3.2</span> The <span class="dfn">`inert`</span> attribute<a href="#the-inert-attribute" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/inert](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inert "The inert global attribute is a Boolean attribute indicating that the browser will ignore the element. With the inert attribute, all of the element's flat tree descendants (such as modal <dialog>s) that don't otherwise escape inertness are ignored. The inert attribute also makes the browser ignore input events sent by the user, including focus-related events and events from assistive technologies.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox112+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari15.5+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome102+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge102+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The [`inert`](#the-inert-attribute) attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-inert-attribute:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a> that
indicates, by its presence, that the element and all its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
id="the-inert-attribute:flat-tree" data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat
tree</a> descendants which don't otherwise escape inertness (such as
modal dialogs) are to be made
<a href="#inert" id="the-inert-attribute:inert">inert</a> by the user
agent.

An inert subtree should not contain any content or controls which are
critical to understanding or using aspects of the page which are not in
the inert state. Content in an inert subtree will not be perceivable by
all users, or interactive. Authors should not specify elements as inert
unless the content they represent are also visually obscured in some
way. In most cases, authors should not specify the [`inert`](#inert)
attribute on individual form controls. In these instances, the
[`disabled`](#attr-fe-disabled) attribute is probably more appropriate.

<div class="example">

The following example shows how to mark partially loaded content,
visually obscured by a "loading" message, as inert.

``` html
<section aria-labelledby=s1>
  <h3 id=s1>Population by City</h3>
  <div class=container>
    <div class=loading><p>Loading...</p></div>
    <div inert>
      <form>
        <fieldset>
          <legend>Date range</legend>
          <div>
            <label for=start>Start</label>
            <input type=date id=start>
          </div>
          <div>
            <label for=end>End</label>
            <input type=date id=end>
          </div>
          <div>
            <button>Apply</button>
          </div>
        </fieldset>
      </form>
      <table>
        <caption>From 20-- to 20--</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>City</th>
            <th>State</th>
            <th>20-- Population</th>
            <th>20-- Population</th>
            <th>Percentage change</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <!-- ... -->
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

<img src="/images/inert-example-loading-section.png" width="947"
height="243"
alt="Screenshot of Population by City content with an overlaid loading message which visually obscures the form controls and data table which have not fully rendered, and thus are in the inert state." />

The "loading" overlay obscures the inert content, making it visually
apparent that the inert content is not presently accessible. Notice that
the heading and "loading" text are not descendants of the element with
the [`inert`](#inert) attribute. This will ensure this text is
accessible to all users, while the inert content cannot be interacted
with by anyone.

</div>

<div class="note">

By default, there is no persistent visual indication of an element or
its subtree being inert. Appropriate visual styles for such content is
often context-dependent. For instance, an inert off-screen navigation
panel would not require a default style, as its off-screen position
visually obscures the content. Similarly, a modal
[`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element's backdrop will serve as the
means to visually obscure the inert content of the web page, rather than
styling the inert content specifically.

However, for many other situations authors are strongly encouraged to
clearly mark what parts of their document are active and which are
inert, to avoid user confusion. In particular, it is worth remembering
that not all users can see all parts of a page at once; for example,
users of screen readers, users on small devices or with magnifiers, and
even users using particularly small windows might not be able to see the
active part of a page and might get frustrated if inert sections are not
obviously inert.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.4</span> Tracking <span class="dfn" export="">user activation</span><a href="#tracking-user-activation" class="self-link"></a>

To prevent abuse of certain APIs that could be annoying to users (e.g.,
opening popups or vibrating phones), user agents allow these APIs only
when the user is actively interacting with the web page or has
interacted with the page at least once. This "active interaction" state
is maintained through the mechanisms defined in this section.

#### <span class="secno">6.4.1</span> Data model<a href="#user-activation-data-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div var-scope="">

For the purpose of tracking user activation, each [`Window`](#window)
`W` has two relevant values:

- A <span id="last-activation-timestamp" class="dfn">last activation
  timestamp</span>, which is either a
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
  data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code
  id="user-activation-data-model:domhighrestimestamp">DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>,
  positive infinity (indicating that `W` has never been activated), or
  negative infinity (indicating that the activation has been
  <a href="#consume-user-activation"
  id="user-activation-data-model:consume-user-activation">consumed</a>).
  Initially positive infinity.

- A <span id="last-history-action-activation-timestamp" class="dfn">last
  history-action activation timestamp</span>, which is either a
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
  data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code
  id="user-activation-data-model:domhighrestimestamp-2">DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>
  or positive infinity, initially positive infinity.

</div>

A user agent also defines a <span id="transient-activation-duration"
class="dfn">transient activation duration</span>, which is a constant
number indicating how long a user activation is available for certain
[user activation-gated APIs](#user-activation-gated-apis) (e.g., for
opening popups).

The <a href="#transient-activation-duration"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-duration">transient
activation duration</a> is expected be at most a few seconds, so that
the user can possibly perceive the link between an interaction with the
page and the page calling the activation-gated API.

<div var-scope="">

We then have the following boolean user activation states for `W`:

<span id="sticky-activation" class="dfn" export="">Sticky activation</span>  
<div algorithm="">

When the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
id="user-activation-data-model:current-high-resolution-time"
data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
time</a> given `W` is greater than or equal to the
<a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-activation-timestamp">last
activation timestamp</a> in `W`, `W` is said to have
<a href="#sticky-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:sticky-activation">sticky activation</a>.

</div>

This is `W`'s historical activation state, indicating whether the user
has ever interacted in `W`. It starts false, then changes to true (and
never changes back to false) when `W` gets the very first
<a href="#activation-notification"
id="user-activation-data-model:activation-notification">activation
notification</a>.

<span id="transient-activation" class="dfn" export="">Transient activation</span>  
<div algorithm="">

When the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
id="user-activation-data-model:current-high-resolution-time-2"
data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
time</a> given `W` is greater than or equal to the
<a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-activation-timestamp-2">last
activation timestamp</a> in `W`, and less than the
<a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-activation-timestamp-3">last
activation timestamp</a> in `W` plus the
<a href="#transient-activation-duration"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-duration-2">transient
activation duration</a>, then `W` is said to have
<a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation">transient
activation</a>.

</div>

This is `W`'s current activation state, indicating whether the user has
interacted in `W` recently. This starts with a false value, and remains
true for a limited time after every <a href="#activation-notification"
id="user-activation-data-model:activation-notification-2">activation
notification</a> `W` gets.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-2">transient
activation</a> state is considered <span id="activation-expiry"
class="dfn">expired</span> if it becomes false because the
<a href="#transient-activation-duration"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-duration-3">transient
activation duration</a> time has elapsed since the last user activation.
Note that it can become false even before the expiry time through an
<a href="#consume-user-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:consume-user-activation-2">activation
consumption</a>.

</div>

<span id="history-action-activation" class="dfn">History-action activation</span>  
<div algorithm="">

When the <a href="#last-history-action-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-history-action-activation-timestamp">last
history-action activation timestamp</a> of `W` is not equal to the
<a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-activation-timestamp-4">last
activation timestamp</a> of `W`, then `W` is said to have
<a href="#history-action-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:history-action-activation">history-action
activation</a>.

</div>

This is a special variant of user activation, used to allow access to
certain session history APIs which, if used too frequently, would make
it harder for the user to traverse back using [browser
UI](#nav-traversal-ui). It starts with a false value, and becomes true
whenever the user interacts with `W`, but is reset to false through
<a href="#consume-history-action-user-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:consume-history-action-user-activation">history-action
activation consumption</a>. This ensures such APIs cannot be used
multiple times in a row without an intervening user activation. But
unlike <a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-3">transient
activation</a>, there is no time limit within which such APIs must be
used.

</div>

The <a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-activation-timestamp-5">last
activation timestamp</a> and
<a href="#last-history-action-activation-timestamp"
id="user-activation-data-model:last-history-action-activation-timestamp-2">last
history-action activation timestamp</a> are retained even after the
[`Document`](#document) changes its <a href="#fully-active"
id="user-activation-data-model:fully-active">fully active</a> status
(e.g., after navigating away from a [`Document`](#document), or
navigating to a cached [`Document`](#document)). This means
<a href="#sticky-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:sticky-activation-2">sticky
activation</a> state spans multiple navigations as long as the same
[`Document`](#document) gets reused. For the transient activation state,
the original <a href="#activation-expiry"
id="user-activation-data-model:activation-expiry">expiry</a> time
remains unchanged (i.e., the state still expires within the
<a href="#transient-activation-duration"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-duration-4">transient
activation duration</a> limit from the original
<a href="#activation-triggering-input-event"
id="user-activation-data-model:activation-triggering-input-event">activation
triggering input event</a>). It is important to consider this when
deciding whether to base certain things off <a href="#sticky-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:sticky-activation-3">sticky
activation</a> or <a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-data-model:transient-activation-4">transient
activation</a>.

#### <span class="secno">6.4.2</span> Processing model<a href="#user-activation-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When a user interaction causes firing of an
<a href="#activation-triggering-input-event"
id="user-activation-processing-model:activation-triggering-input-event">activation
triggering input event</a> in a [`Document`](#document) `document`, the
user agent must perform the following <span id="activation-notification"
class="dfn">activation notification</span> steps *before*
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
id="user-activation-processing-model:concept-event-dispatch"
data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatching</a> the event:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:assert"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `document` is
    <a href="#fully-active"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:fully-active">fully active</a>.

2.  Let `windows` be « `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:concept-relevant-global">relevant
    global object</a> ».

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:list-extend"
    data-x-internal="list-extend">Extend</a> `windows` with the
    <a href="#nav-window"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-window">active window</a>
    of each of `document`'s <a href="#ancestor-navigables"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:ancestor-navigables">ancestor
    navigables</a>.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:list-extend-2"
    data-x-internal="list-extend">Extend</a> `windows` with the
    <a href="#nav-window"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-window-2">active window</a>
    of each of `document`'s <a href="#descendant-navigables"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:descendant-navigables">descendant
    navigables</a>, filtered to include only those <a href="#navigable"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:navigable">navigables</a> whose
    <a href="#nav-document"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-document">active document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is
    <a href="#same-origin"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:same-origin">same origin</a>
    with `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `window` in `windows`:

    1.  Set `window`'s <a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
        id="user-activation-processing-model:last-activation-timestamp">last
        activation timestamp</a> to the <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
        id="user-activation-processing-model:current-high-resolution-time"
        data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
        time</a>.

    2.  <a href="#notify-the-close-watcher-manager-about-user-activation"
        id="user-activation-processing-model:notify-the-close-watcher-manager-about-user-activation">Notify
        the close watcher manager about user activation</a> given
        `window`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An <span id="activation-triggering-input-event" class="dfn">activation
triggering input event</span> is any event whose
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted"
data-x-internal="dom-event-istrusted"><code
id="user-activation-processing-model:dom-event-istrusted">isTrusted</code></a>
attribute is true and whose
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
id="user-activation-processing-model:dom-event-type">type</code></a> is
one of:

- "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
  data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:event-keydown">keydown</code></a>",
  provided the key is neither the <span class="kbd">Esc</span> key nor a
  shortcut key reserved by the user agent;

- "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown"
  data-x-internal="event-mousedown"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:event-mousedown">mousedown</code></a>";

- "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerdown-event"
  data-x-internal="event-pointerdown"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:event-pointerdown">pointerdown</code></a>",
  provided the event's <a
  href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-pointerevent-pointertype"
  data-x-internal="pointertype"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:pointertype">pointerType</code></a>
  is "`mouse`";

- "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerup-event"
  data-x-internal="event-pointerup"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:event-pointerup">pointerup</code></a>",
  provided the event's <a
  href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-pointerevent-pointertype"
  data-x-internal="pointertype"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:pointertype-2">pointerType</code></a>
  is not "`mouse`"; or

- "<a href="https://w3c.github.io/touch-events/#event-touchend"
  data-x-internal="event-touchend"><code
  id="user-activation-processing-model:event-touchend">touchend</code></a>".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="#activation-consuming-api"
id="user-activation-processing-model:activation-consuming-api">Activation
consuming APIs</a> defined in this and other specifications can
<span id="consume-user-activation" class="dfn" export="">consume user
activation</span> by performing the following steps, given a
[`Window`](#window) `W`:

1.  If `W`'s <a href="#window-navigable"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:window-navigable">navigable</a>
    is null, then return.

2.  Let `top` be `W`'s <a href="#window-navigable"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:window-navigable-2">navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-top">top-level traversable</a>.

3.  Let `navigables` be the <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:inclusive-descendant-navigables">inclusive
    descendant navigables</a> of `top`'s <a href="#nav-document"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-document-2">active document</a>.

4.  Let `windows` be the list of [`Window`](#window) objects constructed
    by taking the <a href="#nav-window"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-window-3">active window</a>
    of each item in `navigables`.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:list-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `window` in `windows`,
    if `window`'s <a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:last-activation-timestamp-2">last
    activation timestamp</a> is not positive infinity, then set
    `window`'s <a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:last-activation-timestamp-3">last
    activation timestamp</a> to negative infinity.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="#history-action-activation-consuming-api"
id="user-activation-processing-model:history-action-activation-consuming-api">History-action
activation-consuming APIs</a> can
<span id="consume-history-action-user-activation" class="dfn">consume
history-action user activation</span> by performing the following steps,
given a [`Window`](#window) `W`:

1.  If `W`'s <a href="#window-navigable"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:window-navigable-3">navigable</a>
    is null, then return.

2.  Let `top` be `W`'s <a href="#window-navigable"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:window-navigable-4">navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-top-2">top-level
    traversable</a>.

3.  Let `navigables` be the <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:inclusive-descendant-navigables-2">inclusive
    descendant navigables</a> of `top`'s <a href="#nav-document"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-document-3">active document</a>.

4.  Let `windows` be the list of [`Window`](#window) objects constructed
    by taking the <a href="#nav-window"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:nav-window-4">active window</a>
    of each item in `navigables`.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:list-iterate-3"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `window` in `windows`,
    set `window`'s <a href="#last-history-action-activation-timestamp"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:last-history-action-activation-timestamp">last
    history-action activation timestamp</a> to `window`'s
    <a href="#last-activation-timestamp"
    id="user-activation-processing-model:last-activation-timestamp-4">last
    activation timestamp</a>.

</div>

Note the asymmetry in the sets of <a href="#browsing-context"
id="user-activation-processing-model:browsing-context">browsing
contexts</a> in the page that are affected by an
<a href="#activation-notification"
id="user-activation-processing-model:activation-notification">activation
notification</a> vs an <a href="#consume-user-activation"
id="user-activation-processing-model:consume-user-activation">activation
consumption</a>: an activation consumption changes (to false) the
<a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-processing-model:transient-activation">transient
activation</a> states for all browsing contexts in the page, but an
activation notification changes (to true) the states for a subset of
those browsing contexts. The exhaustive nature of consumption here is
deliberate: it prevents malicious sites from making multiple calls to an
<a href="#activation-consuming-api"
id="user-activation-processing-model:activation-consuming-api-2">activation
consuming API</a> from a single user activation (possibly by exploiting
a deep hierarchy of [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)s).

#### <span class="secno">6.4.3</span> APIs gated by user activation<a href="#user-activation-gated-apis" class="self-link"></a>

APIs that are dependent on user activation are classified into different
levels:

<span id="sticky-activation-gated-api" class="dfn" lt="sticky activation-gated API" export="">Sticky activation-gated APIs</span>  
These APIs require the <a href="#sticky-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:sticky-activation">sticky activation</a>
state to be true, so they are blocked until the very first user
activation.

<span id="transient-activation-gated-api" class="dfn" lt="transient activation-gated
   API" export="">Transient activation-gated APIs</span>  
These APIs require the <a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:transient-activation">transient
activation</a> state to be true, but they don't
<a href="#consume-user-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:consume-user-activation">consume</a> it,
so multiple calls are allowed per user activation until the transient
state <a href="#activation-expiry"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:activation-expiry">expires</a>.

<span id="activation-consuming-api" class="dfn" lt="transient activation-consuming API" export="">Transient activation-consuming APIs</span>  
These APIs require the <a href="#transient-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:transient-activation-2">transient
activation</a> state to be true, and they
<a href="#consume-user-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:consume-user-activation-2">consume user
activation</a> in each call to prevent multiple calls per user
activation.

<span id="history-action-activation-consuming-api" class="dfn" lt="history-action activation-consuming API" export="">History-action activation-consuming APIs</span>  
These APIs require the <a href="#history-action-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:history-action-activation">history-action
activation</a> state to be true, and they
<a href="#consume-history-action-user-activation"
id="user-activation-gated-apis:consume-history-action-user-activation">consume
history-action user activation</a> in each call to prevent multiple
calls per user activation.

#### <span class="secno">6.4.5</span> User agent automation<a href="#user-activation-user-agent-automation" class="self-link"></a>

For the purposes of user-agent automation and application testing, this
specification defines the following
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-extension-commands"
id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:extension-command"
data-x-internal="extension-command">extension command</a> for the Web
Driver specification. It is optional for a user agent to support the
following
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-extension-commands"
id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:extension-command-2"
data-x-internal="extension-command">extension command</a>.
[\[WEBDRIVER\]](#refsWEBDRIVER)

| HTTP Method | URI Template                                               |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| \``POST`\`  | `/session/{``session id``}/window/consume-user-activation` |

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-remote-end-steps"
id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:remote-end-steps"
data-x-internal="remote-end-steps">remote end steps</a> are:

1.  Let `window` be the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-current-browsing-context"
    id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:webdriver-current-browsing-context"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-current-browsing-context">current browsing
    context</a>'s <a href="#active-window"
    id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:active-window">active
    window</a>.

2.  Let `consume` be true if `window` has
    <a href="#transient-activation"
    id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:transient-activation">transient
    activation</a>; otherwise false.

3.  If `consume` is true, then <a href="#consume-user-activation"
    id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:consume-user-activation">consume
    user activation</a> of `window`.

4.  Return <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-success"
    id="user-activation-user-agent-automation:success-value"
    data-x-internal="success-value">success</a> with data `consume`.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.5</span> Activation behavior of elements<a href="#activation" class="self-link"></a>

Certain elements in HTML have an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="activation:activation-behaviour"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a>, which
means that the user can activate them. This is always caused by a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="activation:event-click">click</code></a> event.

The user agent should allow the user to manually trigger elements that
have an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="activation:activation-behaviour-2"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a>, for
instance using keyboard or voice input, or through mouse clicks. When
the user triggers an element with a defined
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
id="activation:activation-behaviour-3"
data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a> in a
manner other than clicking it, the default action of the interaction
event must be to
<a href="#fire-a-click-event" id="activation:fire-a-click-event">fire a
<code>click</code> event</a> at the element.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-click" id="dom-click-dev"><code>click</code></a>`()`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLElement/click](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/click "The HTMLElement.click() method simulates a mouse click on an element.")

Support in all current engines.

Acts as if the element was clicked.

Each element has an associated <span id="click-in-progress-flag"
class="dfn">click in progress flag</span>, which is initially unset.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-click" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="method">`click()`</span> method must run the following steps:

1.  If this element is a form control that is
    <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
    id="activation:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a>, then return.

2.  If this element's <a href="#click-in-progress-flag"
    id="activation:click-in-progress-flag">click in progress flag</a> is
    set, then return.

3.  Set this element's <a href="#click-in-progress-flag"
    id="activation:click-in-progress-flag-2">click in progress flag</a>.

4.  <a href="#fire-a-synthetic-pointer-event"
    id="activation:fire-a-synthetic-pointer-event">Fire a synthetic pointer
    event</a> named <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
    data-x-internal="event-click"><code
    id="activation:event-click-2">click</code></a> at this element, with
    the *not trusted flag* set.

5.  Unset this element's <a href="#click-in-progress-flag"
    id="activation:click-in-progress-flag-3">click in progress flag</a>.

</div>


`event``.`<a href="#dom-toggleevent-oldstate"
id="dom-toggleevent-oldstate-dev"><code>oldState</code></a>  
Set to "`closed`" when transitioning from closed to open, or set to
"`open`" when transitioning from open to closed.

`event``.`<a href="#dom-toggleevent-newstate"
id="dom-toggleevent-newstate-dev"><code>newState</code></a>  
Set to "`open`" when transitioning from closed to open, or set to
"`closed`" when transitioning from open to closed.

`event``.`<a href="#dom-toggleevent-source"
id="dom-toggleevent-source-dev"><code>source</code></a>  
Set to the element which initiated the toggle, which can be set up with
the [`popovertarget`](#attr-popovertarget) and
[`commandfor`](#attr-button-commandfor) attributes. If there is no
source element, then it is set to null.

[DOM standard issue \#1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328)
tracks how to better standardize associated event data in a way which
makes sense on Events. Currently an event attribute initialized to a
value cannot also have a getter, and so an internal slot (or map of
additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

A <span id="toggle-task-tracker" class="dfn">toggle task tracker</span>
is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="the-toggleevent-interface:struct"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> which has:

id="the-toggleevent-interface:concept-task">task</a> which fires a
[`ToggleEvent`](#toggleevent).

<span id="toggle-task-old-state" class="dfn">old state</span>  
A string which represents the <a href="#toggle-task-task"
id="the-toggleevent-interface:toggle-task-task">task</a>'s event's value
for the [`oldState`](#dom-toggleevent-oldstate) attribute.

#### <span class="secno">6.5.2</span> The [`CommandEvent`](#commandevent) interface<a href="#the-commandevent-interface" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CommandEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional CommandEventInit eventInitDict = {});
  readonly attribute Element? source;
  readonly attribute DOMString command;
};

dictionary CommandEventInit : EventInit {
  Element? source = null;
  DOMString command = "";
};
```

`event``.`<a href="#dom-commandevent-command"
id="dom-commandevent-command-dev"><code>command</code></a>  
Returns what action the element can take.

`event``.`<a href="#dom-commandevent-source"
id="dom-commandevent-source-dev"><code>source</code></a>  
Returns the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-commandevent-interface:element">Element</code></a> that was
interacted with in order to cause this event.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-commandevent-command" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CommandEvent" dfn-type="attribute">`command`</span> attribute
must return the value it was initialized to.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-commandevent-source" class="dfn"
dfn-for="CommandEvent" dfn-type="attribute">`source`</span> getter steps
are to return the result of
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#retarget"
id="the-commandevent-interface:dom-retarget"

data-x-internal="dom-event-currenttarget"><code
id="the-commandevent-interface:dom-event-currenttarget">currentTarget</code></a>.

</div>

[DOM standard issue \#1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328)
tracks how to better standardize associated event data in a way which
makes sense on Events. Currently an event attribute initialized to a

additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

### <span class="secno">6.6</span> Focus<a href="#focus" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">6.6.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-8" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

An HTML user interface typically consists of multiple interactive
widgets, such as form controls, scrollable regions, links, dialog boxes,
browser tabs, and so forth. These widgets form a hierarchy, with some
(e.g. browser tabs, dialog boxes) containing others (e.g. links, form
controls).

When interacting with an interface using a keyboard, key input is
channeled from the system, through the hierarchy of interactive widgets,
to an active widget, which is said to be
<a href="#focused" id="introduction-8:focused">focused</a>.

<div class="example">

Consider an HTML application running in a browser tab running in a
graphical environment. Suppose this application had a page with some
text controls and links, and was currently showing a modal dialog, which
itself had a text control and a button.

The hierarchy of focusable widgets, in this scenario, would include the
browser window, which would have, amongst its children, the browser tab
containing the HTML application. The tab itself would have as its
children the various links and text controls, as well as the dialog. The
dialog itself would have as its children the text control and the
button.

<img src="/images/focus-tree.png" width="800" height="450" />

If the widget with
<a href="#focused" id="introduction-8:focused-2">focus</a> in this
example was the text control in the dialog box, then key input would be
channeled from the graphical system to ① the web browser, then to ② the
tab, then to ③ the dialog, and finally to ④ the text control.

</div>

Keyboard *events* are always targeted at this
<a href="#focused" id="introduction-8:focused-3">focused</a> element.

#### <span class="secno">6.6.2</span> Data model<a href="#data-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="data-model:top-level-traversable">top-level traversable</a> has
<span id="system-focus" class="dfn" dfn-for="top-level
  traversable" export="">system focus</span> when it can receive
keyboard input channeled from the operating system, possibly targeted at
one of its
<a href="#nav-document" id="data-model:nav-document">active document</a>'s
<a href="#descendant-navigables"
id="data-model:descendant-navigables">descendant navigables</a>.

</div>

A <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="data-model:top-level-traversable-2">top-level traversable</a> has
<span id="user-attention" class="dfn"
dfn-for="top-level traversable">user attention</span> when its
<a href="#system-visibility-state"
id="data-model:system-visibility-state">system visibility state</a> is
"`visible`", and it either has
<a href="#system-focus" id="data-model:system-focus">system focus</a> or
user agent widgets directly related to it can receive keyboard input
channeled from the operating system.

User attention is lost when a browser window loses focus, whereas system
focus might also be lost to other system widgets in the browser window
such as a location bar.

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) `d` is a
<span id="fully-active-descendant-of-a-top-level-traversable-with-user-attention"
class="dfn" dfn-for="Document" export="">fully active descendant of a
top-level traversable with user attention</span> when `d` is
<a href="#fully-active" id="data-model:fully-active">fully active</a>
and `d`'s <a href="#node-navigable" id="data-model:node-navigable">node
navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-top" id="data-model:nav-top">top-level traversable</a> has
<a href="#user-attention" id="data-model:user-attention">user
attention</a>.

</div>

The term <span id="focusable-area" class="dfn">focusable area</span> is
used to refer to regions of the interface that can further become the
target of such keyboard input. Focusable areas can be elements, parts of
elements, or other regions managed by the user agent.

Each <a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area">focusable
area</a> has a <span id="dom-anchor" class="dfn">DOM anchor</span>,
which is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-node"
data-x-internal="node"><code id="data-model:node">Node</code></a> object
that represents the position of the
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-2">focusable
area</a> in the DOM. (When the
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-3">focusable
area</a> is itself a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-node"
data-x-internal="node"><code id="data-model:node-2">Node</code></a>, it
is its own
<a href="#dom-anchor" id="data-model:dom-anchor">DOM anchor</a>.) The
<a href="#dom-anchor" id="data-model:dom-anchor-2">DOM anchor</a> is
used in some APIs as a substitute for the
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-4">focusable
area</a> when there is no other DOM object to represent the
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-5">focusable
area</a>.

The following table describes what objects can be
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-6">focusable
areas</a>. The cells in the left column describe objects that can be
<a href="#focusable-area" id="data-model:focusable-area-7">focusable
areas</a>; the cells in the right column describe the
<a href="#dom-anchor" id="data-model:dom-anchor-3">DOM anchors</a> for
those elements. (The cells that span both columns are non-normative
examples.)
