<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-tabindex" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOrSVGElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`tabIndex`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `attribute` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-tabindex-attribute:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    [`tabindex`](#attr-tabindex) attribute.

2.  If `attribute` is not null:

    1.  Let `parsedValue` be the result of
        <a href="#rules-for-parsing-integers"
        id="the-tabindex-attribute:rules-for-parsing-integers-2">integer
        parsing</a> `attribute`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-attribute-value"
        id="the-tabindex-attribute:concept-attribute-value"
        data-x-internal="concept-attribute-value">value</a>.

    2.  If `parsedValue` is not an error and is within the
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long"
        data-x-internal="idl-long"><code
        id="the-tabindex-attribute:idl-long">long</code></a> range, then
        return `parsedValue`.

3.  Return 0 if <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-tabindex-attribute:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    is an [`a`](#the-a-element), [`area`](#the-area-element),
    [`button`](#the-button-element), [`frame`](#frame),
    [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), [`input`](#the-input-element),
    [`object`](#the-object-element), [`select`](#the-select-element),
    [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), or
    <a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/linking.html#AElement"
    id="the-tabindex-attribute:svg-a" data-x-internal="svg-a">SVG
    <code>a</code></a> element, or is a
    [`summary`](#the-summary-element) element that is a
    <a href="#summary-for-its-parent-details"
    id="the-tabindex-attribute:summary-for-its-parent-details">summary for
    its parent details</a>; otherwise −1.

</div>

The varying default value based on element type is a historical
artifact.

#### <span class="secno">6.6.4</span> <span id="processing-model-5"></span>Processing model<a href="#focus-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="get-the-focusable-area" class="dfn">get the focusable
area</span> for a `focus target` that is either an element that is not a
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area">focusable area</a>, or is a
<a href="#navigable" id="focus-processing-model:navigable">navigable</a>,
given an optional string `focus trigger` (default "`other`"), run the
first matching set of steps from the following list:

If `focus target` is an [`area`](#the-area-element) element with one or more shapes that are <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-2">focusable areas</a>  
Return the shape corresponding to the first [`img`](#the-img-element)
element in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="focus-processing-model:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
order</a> that uses the image map to which the
[`area`](#the-area-element) element belongs.

If `focus target` is an element with one or more scrollable regions that are <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-3">focusable areas</a>  
Return the element's first scrollable region, according to a pre-order,
depth-first traversal of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree"
id="focus-processing-model:flat-tree" data-x-internal="flat-tree">flat
tree</a>. [\[CSSSCOPING\]](#refsCSSSCOPING)

If `focus target` is the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
id="focus-processing-model:document-element"
data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a> of its [`Document`](#document)  
Return the [`Document`](#document)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="focus-processing-model:viewport"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>.

If `focus target` is a <a href="#navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-2">navigable</a>  
Return the <a href="#navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-3">navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-document" id="focus-processing-model:nav-document">active
document</a>.

If `focus target` is a <a href="#navigable-container"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-container">navigable container</a> with a non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable">content navigable</a>  
Return the <a href="#navigable-container"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-container-2">navigable
container</a>'s <a href="#content-navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable-2">content navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-document"
id="focus-processing-model:nav-document-2">active document</a>.

If `focus target` is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host"
data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a> whose <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
id="focus-processing-model:concept-element-shadow-root"
data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
id="focus-processing-model:delegates-focus"
data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> is true  
1.  Let `focusedElement` be the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>'s
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-processing-model:dom-anchor">DOM
    anchor</a>.

2.  If `focus target` is a <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor">shadow-including
    inclusive ancestor</a> of `focusedElement`, then return
    `focusedElement`.

3.  Return the <a href="#focus-delegate"
    id="focus-processing-model:focus-delegate">focus delegate</a> for
    `focus target` given `focus trigger`.

For <a href="#sequentially-focusable"
id="focus-processing-model:sequentially-focusable">sequential
focusability</a>, the handling of
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-2"
data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow hosts</a> and
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
id="focus-processing-model:delegates-focus-2"
data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> is done when
constructing the <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
id="focus-processing-model:sequential-focus-navigation-order">sequential
focus navigation order</a>. That is, the <a href="#focusing-steps"
id="focus-processing-model:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a> will never
be called on such
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-3"
data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow hosts</a> as part of sequential
focus navigation.

Otherwise  
Return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="focus-delegate" class="dfn">focus delegate</span> for a
`focusTarget`, given an optional string `focusTrigger` (default
"`other`"), is given by the following steps:

1.  If `focusTarget` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-4"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a> and its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
    id="focus-processing-model:concept-element-shadow-root-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
    id="focus-processing-model:delegates-focus-3"
    data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> is false, then
    return null.

2.  Let `whereToLook` be `focusTarget`.

3.  If `whereToLook` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-5"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a>, then set
    `whereToLook` to `whereToLook`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
    id="focus-processing-model:concept-element-shadow-root-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>.

4.  Let `autofocusDelegate` be the <a href="#autofocus-delegate"
    id="focus-processing-model:autofocus-delegate">autofocus delegate</a>
    for `whereToLook` given `focusTrigger`.

5.  If `autofocusDelegate` is not null, then return `autofocusDelegate`.

6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="focus-processing-model:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `descendant` of
    `whereToLook`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="focus-processing-model:descendant"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a>, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="focus-processing-model:tree-order-2"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    1.  Let `focusableArea` be null.

    2.  If `focusTarget` is a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element
        and `descendant` is <a href="#sequentially-focusable"
        id="focus-processing-model:sequentially-focusable-2">sequentially
        focusable</a>, then set `focusableArea` to `descendant`.

    3.  Otherwise, if `focusTarget` is not a
        [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) and `descendant` is a
        <a href="#focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-4">focusable area</a>,
        set `focusableArea` to `descendant`.

    4.  Otherwise, set `focusableArea` to the result of
        <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:get-the-focusable-area">getting the focusable
        area</a> for `descendant` given `focusTrigger`.

        This step can end up recursing, i.e., the
        <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:get-the-focusable-area-2">get the focusable
        area</a> steps might return the <a href="#focus-delegate"
        id="focus-processing-model:focus-delegate-2">focus delegate</a>
        of `descendant`.

    5.  If `focusableArea` is not null, then return `focusableArea`.

    It's important that we are *not* looking at the <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-descendant"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-including-descendant"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-descendant">shadow-including
    descendants</a> here, but instead only at the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="focus-processing-model:descendant-2"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a>.
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-6"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">Shadow hosts</a> are instead handled
    by the recursive case mentioned above.

7.  Return null.

The above algorithm essentially returns the first suitable
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-5">focusable area</a> where
the path between its
<a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-processing-model:dom-anchor-2">DOM
anchor</a> and `focusTarget` delegates focus at any shadow tree
boundaries.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="autofocus-delegate" class="dfn">autofocus delegate</span>
for a `focus target` given a `focus trigger` is given by the following
steps:

1.  For each
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="focus-processing-model:descendant-3"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendant</a> `descendant` of
    `focus target`, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="focus-processing-model:tree-order-3"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>:

    1.  If `descendant` does not have an
        [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) content attribute, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="focus-processing-model:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  Let `focusable area` be `descendant`, if `descendant` is a
        <a href="#focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-6">focusable area</a>;
        otherwise let `focusable area` be the result of
        <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:get-the-focusable-area-3">getting the
        focusable area</a> for `descendant` given `focus trigger`.

    3.  If `focusable area` is null, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="focus-processing-model:continue-2"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    4.  If `focusable area` is not <a href="#click-focusable"
        id="focus-processing-model:click-focusable">click focusable</a>
        and `focus trigger` is "`click`", then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="focus-processing-model:continue-3"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    5.  Return `focusable area`.

2.  Return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="focusing-steps" class="dfn" export="">focusing
steps</span> for an object `new focus target` that is either a
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-7">focusable area</a>, or an
element that is not a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-8">focusable area</a>, or a
<a href="#navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-4">navigable</a>, are as follows.
They can optionally be run with a `fallback target` and a string
`focus trigger`.

1.  If `new focus target` is not a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-9">focusable area</a>,
    then set `new focus target` to the result of
    <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
    id="focus-processing-model:get-the-focusable-area-4">getting the
    focusable area</a> for `new focus target`, given `focus trigger` if
    it was passed.

2.  If `new focus target` is null, then:

    1.  If no `fallback target` was specified, then return.

    2.  Otherwise, set `new focus target` to the `fallback target`.

3.  If `new focus target` is a <a href="#navigable-container"
    id="focus-processing-model:navigable-container-3">navigable
    container</a> with non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable-3">content navigable</a>,
    then set `new focus target` to the <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable-4">content navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document"
    id="focus-processing-model:nav-document-3">active document</a>.

4.  If `new focus target` is a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-10">focusable area</a> and
    its
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-processing-model:dom-anchor-3">DOM
    anchor</a> is
    <a href="#inert" id="focus-processing-model:inert">inert</a>, then
    return.

5.  If `new focus target` is the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-2">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>, then return.

6.  Let `old chain` be the
    <a href="#current-focus-chain-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:current-focus-chain-of-a-top-level-traversable">current
    focus chain of the top-level traversable</a> in which
    `new focus target` finds itself.

7.  Let `new chain` be the
    <a href="#focus-chain" id="focus-processing-model:focus-chain">focus
    chain</a> of `new focus target`.

8.  Run the <a href="#focus-update-steps"
    id="focus-processing-model:focus-update-steps">focus update steps</a>
    with `old chain`, `new chain`, and `new focus target` respectively.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

User agents must <a href="#immediately"
id="focus-processing-model:immediately">immediately</a> run the
<a href="#focusing-steps"
id="focus-processing-model:focusing-steps-2">focusing steps</a> for a
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-11">focusable area</a> or
<a href="#navigable"
id="focus-processing-model:navigable-5">navigable</a> `candidate`
whenever the user attempts to move the focus to `candidate`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="unfocusing-steps" class="dfn">unfocusing steps</span> for
an object `old focus target` that is either a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-12">focusable area</a> or an
element that is not a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-13">focusable area</a> are as
follows:

1.  If `old focus target` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-host-7"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a> whose
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
    id="focus-processing-model:concept-element-shadow-root-4"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
    id="focus-processing-model:delegates-focus-4"
    data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> is true, and
    `old focus target`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
    id="focus-processing-model:concept-element-shadow-root-5"
    data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a> is a
    <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor"
    id="focus-processing-model:shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor">shadow-including
    inclusive ancestor</a> of the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-3">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>'s
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-processing-model:dom-anchor-4">DOM
    anchor</a>, then set `old focus target` to that
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-4">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>.

2.  If `old focus target` is
    <a href="#inert" id="focus-processing-model:inert-2">inert</a>, then
    return.

3.  If `old focus target` is an [`area`](#the-area-element) element and
    one of its shapes is the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-5">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>, or, if
    `old focus target` is an element with one or more scrollable
    regions, and one of them is the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-6">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>, then let
    `old focus target` be that
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-7">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>.

4.  Let `old chain` be the
    <a href="#current-focus-chain-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:current-focus-chain-of-a-top-level-traversable-2">current
    focus chain of the top-level traversable</a> in which
    `old focus target` finds itself.

5.  If `old focus target` is not one of the entries in `old chain`, then
    return.

6.  If `old focus target` is not a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-14">focusable area</a>,
    then return.

7.  Let `topDocument` be `old chain`'s last entry.

8.  If `topDocument`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:node-navigable">node navigable</a> has
    <a href="#system-focus" id="focus-processing-model:system-focus">system
    focus</a>, then run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="focus-processing-model:focusing-steps-3">focusing steps</a> for
    `topDocument`'s <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
    id="focus-processing-model:viewport-2"
    data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>.

    Otherwise, apply any relevant platform-specific conventions for
    removing <a href="#system-focus"
    id="focus-processing-model:system-focus-2">system focus</a> from
    `topDocument`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:node-navigable-2">node navigable</a>, and
    run the <a href="#focus-update-steps"
    id="focus-processing-model:focus-update-steps-2">focus update steps</a>
    given `old chain`, an empty list, and null.

</div>

The <a href="#unfocusing-steps"
id="focus-processing-model:unfocusing-steps">unfocusing steps</a> do not
always result in the focus changing, even when applied to the
<a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-8">currently
focused area of a top-level traversable</a>. For example, if the
<a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-9">currently
focused area of a top-level traversable</a> is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="focus-processing-model:viewport-3"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>, then it will usually keep its
focus regardless until another <a href="#focusable-area"
id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-15">focusable area</a> is
explicitly focused with the <a href="#focusing-steps"
id="focus-processing-model:focusing-steps-4">focusing steps</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="focus-update-steps" class="dfn">focus update steps</span>,
given an `old chain`, a `new chain`, and a `new focus target`
respectively, are as follows:

1.  If the last entry in `old chain` and the last entry in `new chain`
    are the same, pop the last entry from `old chain` and the last entry
    from `new chain` and redo this step.

2.  For each entry `entry` in `old chain`, in order, run these substeps:

    1.  If `entry` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element, and the
        [`change`](#event-change) event <a href="#concept-input-apply"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-input-apply">applies</a> to
        the element, and the element does not have a defined
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior"
        id="focus-processing-model:activation-behaviour"
        data-x-internal="activation-behaviour">activation behavior</a>,
        and the user has changed the element's
        <a href="#concept-fe-value"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-fe-value">value</a> or its
        list of <a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-input-type-file-selected">selected
        files</a> while the control was focused without committing that
        change (such that it is different to what it was when the
        control was first focused), then:

        1.  Set `entry`'s
            <a href="#user-validity" id="focus-processing-model:user-validity">user
            validity</a> to true.

        2.  <div id="unfocus-causes-change-event">

            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="focus-processing-model:concept-event-fire"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
            [`change`](#event-change) at the element, with the
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
            data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
            id="focus-processing-model:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
            attribute initialized to true.

            </div>

    2.  If `entry` is an element, let `blur event target` be `entry`.

        If `entry` is a [`Document`](#document) object, let
        `blur event target` be that [`Document`](#document) object's
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
        object</a>.

        Otherwise, let `blur event target` be null.

    3.  If `entry` is the last entry in `old chain`, and `entry` is an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="focus-processing-model:element">Element</code></a>, and the
        last entry in `new chain` is also an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="focus-processing-model:element-2">Element</code></a>, then
        let `related blur target` be the last entry in `new chain`.
        Otherwise, let `related blur target` be null.

    4.  If `blur event target` is not null,
        <a href="#fire-a-focus-event"
        id="focus-processing-model:fire-a-focus-event">fire a focus event</a>
        named [`blur`](#event-blur) at `blur event target`, with
        `related blur target` as the related target.

        <a href="#note-sometimes-no-blur-event" class="self-link"></a>In
        some cases, e.g., if `entry` is an [`area`](#the-area-element)
        element's shape, a scrollable region, or a
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
        id="focus-processing-model:viewport-4"
        data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>, no event is fired.

3.  Apply any relevant platform-specific conventions for focusing
    `new focus target`. (For example, some platforms select the contents
    of a text control when that control is focused.)

4.  For each entry `entry` in `new chain`, in reverse order, run these
    substeps:

    1.  If `entry` is a <a href="#focusable-area"
        id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-16">focusable area</a>,
        and the <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
        id="focus-processing-model:focused-area-of-the-document">focused area of
        the document</a> is not `entry`:

        1.  Set `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
            id="focus-processing-model:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
            object</a>'s <a href="#window-navigation-api"
            id="focus-processing-model:window-navigation-api">navigation API</a>'s
            <a href="#focus-changed-during-ongoing-navigation"
            id="focus-processing-model:focus-changed-during-ongoing-navigation">focus
            changed during ongoing navigation</a> to true.

        2.  Designate `entry` as the
            <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
            id="focus-processing-model:focused-area-of-the-document-2">focused area
            of the document</a>.

    2.  If `entry` is an element, let `focus event target` be `entry`.

        If `entry` is a [`Document`](#document) object, let
        `focus event target` be that [`Document`](#document) object's
        <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-relevant-global-3">relevant global
        object</a>.

        Otherwise, let `focus event target` be null.

    3.  If `entry` is the last entry in `new chain`, and `entry` is an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="focus-processing-model:element-3">Element</code></a>, and
        the last entry in `old chain` is also an
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="focus-processing-model:element-4">Element</code></a>, then
        let `related focus target` be the last entry in `old chain`.
        Otherwise, let `related focus target` be null.

    4.  If `focus event target` is not null,
        <a href="#fire-a-focus-event"
        id="focus-processing-model:fire-a-focus-event-2">fire a focus event</a>
        named [`focus`](#event-focus) at `focus event target`, with
        `related focus target` as the related target.

        In some cases, e.g. if `entry` is an [`area`](#the-area-element)
        element's shape, a scrollable region, or a
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
        id="focus-processing-model:viewport-5"
        data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>, no event is fired.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="fire-a-focus-event" class="dfn">fire a focus event</span>
named `e` at an element `t` with a given related target `r`,
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="focus-processing-model:concept-event-fire-2"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named `e` at `t`,
using <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#focusevent"
data-x-internal="focusevent"><code
id="focus-processing-model:focusevent">FocusEvent</code></a>, with the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-focusevent-relatedtarget"
data-x-internal="dom-focusevent-relatedtarget"><code
id="focus-processing-model:dom-focusevent-relatedtarget">relatedTarget</code></a>
attribute initialized to `r`, the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view"
data-x-internal="dom-uievent-view"><code
id="focus-processing-model:dom-uievent-view">view</code></a> attribute
initialized to `t`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="focus-processing-model:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
<a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="focus-processing-model:concept-relevant-global-4">relevant global
object</a>, and the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#composed-flag"
id="focus-processing-model:composed-flag"
data-x-internal="composed-flag">composed flag</a> set.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

When a key event is to be routed in a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="focus-processing-model:top-level-traversable">top-level
traversable</a>, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `target area` be the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-10">currently
    focused area of the top-level traversable</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="focus-processing-model:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `target area` is not null, since key events are only routed to
    <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-processing-model:top-level-traversable-2">top-level
    traversables</a> that have <a href="#system-focus"
    id="focus-processing-model:system-focus-3">system focus</a>.
    Therefore, `target area` is a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="focus-processing-model:focusable-area-17">focusable area</a>.

3.  Let `target node` be `target area`'s
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-processing-model:dom-anchor-5">DOM
    anchor</a>.

4.  If `target node` is a [`Document`](#document) that has a
    <a href="#the-body-element-2"
    id="focus-processing-model:the-body-element-2">body element</a>,
    then let `target node` be <a href="#the-body-element-2"
    id="focus-processing-model:the-body-element-2-2">the body element</a>
    of that [`Document`](#document).

    Otherwise, if `target node` is a [`Document`](#document) object that
    has a non-null
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="focus-processing-model:document-element-2"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>, then let
    `target node` be that
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="focus-processing-model:document-element-3"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>.

5.  If `target node` is not
    <a href="#inert" id="focus-processing-model:inert-3">inert</a>,
    then:

    1.  Let `canHandle` be the result of
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
        id="focus-processing-model:concept-event-dispatch"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatching</a> the key
        event at `target node`.

    2.  If `canHandle` is true, then let `target area` handle the key
        event. This might include <a href="#fire-a-click-event"
        id="focus-processing-model:fire-a-click-event">firing a
        <code>click</code> event</a> at `target node`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="has-focus-steps" class="dfn" export="">has focus
steps</span>, given a [`Document`](#document) object `target`, are as
follows:

1.  If `target`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:node-navigable-3">node navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top" id="focus-processing-model:nav-top">top-level
    traversable</a> does not have <a href="#system-focus"
    id="focus-processing-model:system-focus-4">system focus</a>, then
    return false.

2.  Let `candidate` be `target`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="focus-processing-model:node-navigable-4">node navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top" id="focus-processing-model:nav-top-2">top-level
    traversable</a>'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="focus-processing-model:active-document">active document</a>.

3.  While true:

    1.  If `candidate` is `target`, then return true.

    2.  If the <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
        id="focus-processing-model:focused-area-of-the-document-3">focused
        area</a> of `candidate` is a <a href="#navigable-container"
        id="focus-processing-model:navigable-container-4">navigable
        container</a> with a non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable-5">content navigable</a>,
        then set `candidate` to the <a href="#nav-document"
        id="focus-processing-model:nav-document-4">active document</a>
        of that <a href="#navigable-container"
        id="focus-processing-model:navigable-container-5">navigable
        container</a>'s <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="focus-processing-model:content-navigable-6">content navigable</a>.

    3.  Otherwise, return false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.6.5</span> <span class="dfn">Sequential focus navigation</span><a href="#sequential-focus-navigation" class="self-link"></a>

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="sequential-focus-navigation-order" class="dfn">sequential
focus navigation order</span>, which orders some or all of the
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area">focusable areas</a> in
the [`Document`](#document) relative to each other. Its contents and
ordering are given by the
<a href="#flattened-tabindex-ordered-focus-navigation-scope"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:flattened-tabindex-ordered-focus-navigation-scope">flattened
tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope</a> of the
[`Document`](#document).

Per the rules defining the
<a href="#flattened-tabindex-ordered-focus-navigation-scope"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:flattened-tabindex-ordered-focus-navigation-scope-2">flattened
tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope</a>, the ordering is not
necessarily related to the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:tree-order"
data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a> of the
[`Document`](#document).

If a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-2">focusable area</a> is
omitted from the <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order">sequential
focus navigation order</a> of its [`Document`](#document), then it is
unreachable via <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation">sequential
focus navigation</a>.

There can also be a
<span id="sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point"
class="dfn">sequential focus navigation starting point</span>. It is
initially unset. The user agent may set it when the user indicates that
it should be moved.

For example, the user agent could set it to the position of the user's
click if the user clicks on the document contents.

User agents are required to set the
<a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point">sequential
focus navigation starting point</a> to the <a href="#target-element"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:target-element">target element</a> when
<a href="#navigate-fragid"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:navigate-fragid">navigating to a
fragment</a>.

A <span id="sequential-focus-direction" class="dfn">sequential focus
direction</span> is one of two possible values:
"<span id="sequential-focus-forward" class="dfn">`forward`</span>", or
"<span id="sequential-focus-backward" class="dfn">`backward`</span>".
They are used in the below algorithms to describe the direction in which
sequential focus travels at the user's request.

A <span id="selection-mechanism" class="dfn">selection mechanism</span>
is one of two possible values: "<span id="selection-mechanism-dom"
class="dfn">`DOM`</span>", or "<span id="selection-mechanism-sequential"
class="dfn">`sequential`</span>". They are used to describe how the
<a href="#sequential-navigation-search-algorithm"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-navigation-search-algorithm">sequential
navigation search algorithm</a> finds the <a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-3">focusable area</a> it
returns.

<div algorithm="">

When the user requests that focus move from the
<a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable">currently
focused area of a top-level traversable</a> to the next or previous
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-4">focusable area</a>
(e.g., as the default action of pressing the
<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">tab</span></span> key), or when the
user requests that focus sequentially move to a
<a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable">top-level
traversable</a> in the first place (e.g., from the browser's location
bar), the user agent must use the following algorithm:

1.  Let `starting point` be the
    <a href="#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable-2">currently
    focused area of a top-level traversable</a>, if the user requested
    to move focus sequentially from there, or else the
    <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable-2">top-level
    traversable</a> itself, if the user instead requested to move focus
    from outside the <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable-3">top-level
    traversable</a>.

2.  If there is a <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point-2">sequential
    focus navigation starting point</a> defined and it is inside
    `starting point`, then let `starting point` be the
    <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point-3">sequential
    focus navigation starting point</a> instead.

3.  Let `direction` be "[`forward`](#sequential-focus-forward)" if the
    user requested the next control, and
    "[`backward`](#sequential-focus-backward)" if the user requested the
    previous control.

    Typically, pressing
    <span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">tab</span></span> requests the
    next control, and pressing
    <span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">shift</span> +
    <span class="kbd">tab</span></span> requests the previous control.

4.  *Loop*: Let `selection mechanism` be
    "[`sequential`](#selection-mechanism-sequential)" if
    `starting point` is a <a href="#navigable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:navigable">navigable</a> or if
    `starting point` is in its [`Document`](#document)'s
    <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order-2">sequential
    focus navigation order</a>.

    Otherwise, `starting point` is not in its [`Document`](#document)'s
    <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order-3">sequential
    focus navigation order</a>; let `selection mechanism` be
    "[`DOM`](#selection-mechanism-dom)".

5.  Let `candidate` be the result of running the
    <a href="#sequential-navigation-search-algorithm"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-navigation-search-algorithm-2">sequential
    navigation search algorithm</a> with `starting point`, `direction`,
    and `selection mechanism`.

6.  If `candidate` is not null, then run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a>
    for `candidate` and return.

7.  Otherwise, unset the
    <a href="#sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point-4">sequential
    focus navigation starting point</a>.

8.  If `starting point` is a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable-4">top-level
    traversable</a>, or a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-5">focusable area</a>
    in the <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable-5">top-level
    traversable</a>, the user agent should transfer focus to its own
    controls appropriately (if any), honouring `direction`, and then
    return.

    For example, if `direction` is *backward*, then the last
    <a href="#sequentially-focusable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequentially-focusable">sequentially
    focusable</a> control before the browser's rendering area would be
    the control to focus.

    If the user agent has no <a href="#sequentially-focusable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequentially-focusable-2">sequentially
    focusable</a> controls — a kiosk-mode browser, for instance — then
    the user agent may instead restart these steps with the
    `starting point` being the <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:top-level-traversable-6">top-level
    traversable</a> itself.

9.  Otherwise, `starting point` is a <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-6">focusable area</a>
    in a <a href="#child-navigable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:child-navigable">child navigable</a>.
    Set `starting point` to that <a href="#child-navigable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:child-navigable-2">child navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-parent"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:nav-parent">parent</a> and return to
    the step labeled *loop*.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="sequential-navigation-search-algorithm"
class="dfn">sequential navigation search algorithm</span>, given a
<a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-7">focusable area</a>
`starting point`, <a href="#sequential-focus-direction"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-direction">sequential
focus direction</a> `direction`, and <a href="#selection-mechanism"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:selection-mechanism">selection
mechanism</a> `selection mechanism`, consists of the following steps.
They return a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-8">focusable area</a>-or-null.

1.  Pick the appropriate cell from the following table, and follow the
    instructions in that cell.

    The appropriate cell is the one that is from the column whose header
    describes `direction` and from the first row whose header describes
    `starting point` and `selection mechanism`.

    <table>
    <colgroup>
    <col style="width: 33%" />
    <col style="width: 33%" />
    <col style="width: 33%" />
    </colgroup>
    <thead>
    <tr>
    <th></th>
    <th><var>direction</var> is "<a href="#sequential-focus-forward"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-forward-2">forward</code></a>"</th>
    <th><var>direction</var> is "<a href="#sequential-focus-backward"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-backward-2">backward</code></a>"</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
    <th><var>starting point</var> is a <a href="#navigable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:navigable-2">navigable</a></th>
    <td>Let <var>candidate</var> be the first <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a> in <var>starting point</var>'s <a
    href="#nav-document"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:nav-document">active document</a>, if
    any; or else null</td>
    <td>Let <var>candidate</var> be the last <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-2">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a> in <var>starting point</var>'s <a
    href="#nav-document"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:nav-document-2">active document</a>, if
    any; or else null</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <th><var>selection mechanism</var> is "<a
    href="#selection-mechanism-dom"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:selection-mechanism-dom-2">DOM</code></a>"</th>
    <td><p>Let <var>candidate</var> be the <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-3">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a>, that appears nearest after
    <var>starting point</var> in <var>starting point</var>'s <a
    href="#document"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:document-8">Document</code></a>, in <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:shadow-including-tree-order"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-tree-order">shadow-including tree
    order</a>, if any; or else null</p>
    <p>In this case, <var>starting point</var> does not necessarily belong
    to its <a href="#document"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:document-9">Document</code></a>'s <a
    href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order-4">sequential
    focus navigation order</a>, so we'll select the <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-4">suitable</a>
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:list-item"
    data-x-internal="list-item">item</a> from that list that comes
    <em>after</em> <var>starting point</var> in <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:shadow-including-tree-order-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-tree-order">shadow-including tree
    order</a>.</p></td>
    <td>Let <var>candidate</var> be the <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-5">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a>, that appears nearest before
    <var>starting point</var> in <var>starting point</var>'s <a
    href="#document"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:document-10">Document</code></a>, in <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:shadow-including-tree-order-3"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-tree-order">shadow-including tree
    order</a>, if any; or else null</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <th><var>selection mechanism</var> is "<a
    href="#selection-mechanism-sequential"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:selection-mechanism-sequential-2">sequential</code></a>"</th>
    <td>Let <var>candidate</var> be the first <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-6">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a> after <var>starting point</var>, in
    <var>starting point</var>'s <a href="#document"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:document-11">Document</code></a>'s <a
    href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order-5">sequential
    focus navigation order</a>, if any; or else null</td>
    <td>Let <var>candidate</var> be the last <a
    href="#suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:suitable-sequentially-focusable-area-7">suitable
    sequentially focusable area</a> before <var>starting point</var>, in
    <var>starting point</var>'s <a href="#document"><code
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:document-12">Document</code></a>'s <a
    href="#sequential-focus-navigation-order"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-focus-navigation-order-6">sequential
    focus navigation order</a>, if any; or else null</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
    </table>

    A <span id="suitable-sequentially-focusable-area"
    class="dfn">suitable sequentially focusable area</span> is a
    <a href="#focusable-area"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:focusable-area-9">focusable area</a>
    whose
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="sequential-focus-navigation:dom-anchor">DOM
    anchor</a> is not
    <a href="#inert" id="sequential-focus-navigation:inert">inert</a>
    and is <a href="#sequentially-focusable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequentially-focusable-3">sequentially
    focusable</a>.

2.  If `candidate` is a <a href="#navigable-container"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:navigable-container">navigable
    container</a> with a non-null <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="sequential-focus-navigation:content-navigable">content navigable</a>,
    then:

    1.  Let `recursive candidate` be the result of running the
        <a href="#sequential-navigation-search-algorithm"
        id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-navigation-search-algorithm-3">sequential
        navigation search algorithm</a> with `candidate`'s
        <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="sequential-focus-navigation:content-navigable-2">content
        navigable</a>, `direction`, and
        "[`sequential`](#selection-mechanism-sequential)".

    2.  If `recursive candidate` is null, then return the result of
        running the <a href="#sequential-navigation-search-algorithm"
        id="sequential-focus-navigation:sequential-navigation-search-algorithm-4">sequential
        navigation search algorithm</a> with `candidate`, `direction`,
        and `selection mechanism`.

    3.  Otherwise, set `candidate` to `recursive candidate`.

3.  Return `candidate`.

</div>

Returns the deepest element in `documentOrShadowRoot` through which or
to which key events are being routed. This is, roughly speaking, the
focused element in the document.

For the purposes of this API, when a <a href="#child-navigable"
id="focus-management-apis:child-navigable">child navigable</a> is
focused, its <a href="#nav-container"
id="focus-management-apis:nav-container">container</a> is
[focused](#bc-focus-ergo-bcc-focus) within its
<a href="#nav-parent" id="focus-management-apis:nav-parent">parent</a>'s
<a href="#nav-document" id="focus-management-apis:nav-document">active
document</a>. For example, if the user moves the focus to a text control
in an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) is the element returned by the
[`activeElement`](#dom-documentorshadowroot-activeelement) API in the
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="focus-management-apis:node-document"
data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

Similarly, when the focused element is in a different
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-tree"
id="focus-management-apis:node-tree" data-x-internal="node-tree">node
tree</a> than `documentOrShadowRoot`, the element returned will be the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host"
id="focus-management-apis:concept-documentfragment-host"
data-x-internal="concept-documentfragment-host">host</a> that's located
in the same <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-tree"
id="focus-management-apis:node-tree-2" data-x-internal="node-tree">node
tree</a> as `documentOrShadowRoot` if `documentOrShadowRoot` is a <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor"
id="focus-management-apis:shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor"
data-x-internal="shadow-including-inclusive-ancestor">shadow-including
inclusive ancestor</a> of the focused element, and null if not.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-focus"
id="focus-management-apis:dom-focus"><code>focus</code></a>`({ `<a href="#dom-focusoptions-preventscroll"
id="focus-management-apis:dom-focusoptions-preventscroll-2"><code>preventScroll</code></a>`, `<a href="#dom-focusoptions-focusvisible"
id="focus-management-apis:dom-focusoptions-focusvisible-2"><code>focusVisible</code></a>` })`

Moves the focus to `element`.

If `element` is a <a href="#navigable-container"
id="focus-management-apis:navigable-container">navigable container</a>,
moves the focus to its <a href="#content-navigable"
id="focus-management-apis:content-navigable">content navigable</a>
instead.

By default, this method also scrolls `element` into view. Providing the
[`preventScroll`](#dom-focusoptions-preventscroll) option and setting it
to true prevents this behavior.

By default, user agents use
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="focus-management-apis:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
heuristics to determine whether to
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#indicate-focus"
id="focus-management-apis:indicate-focus"
data-x-internal="indicate-focus">indicate focus</a> via a focus ring.
Providing the [`focusVisible`](#dom-focusoptions-focusvisible) option
and setting it to true will ensure the focus ring is always visible.

</div>

Moves the focus to the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="focus-management-apis:viewport"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>. Use of this method is
discouraged; if you want to focus the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="focus-management-apis:viewport-2"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>, call the
[`focus()`](#dom-focus) method on the [`Document`](#document)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
id="focus-management-apis:document-element"
data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>.

Do not use this method to hide the focus ring if you find the focus ring
unsightly. Instead, use the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#the-focus-visible-pseudo"
data-x-internal=":focus-visible"><code
id="focus-management-apis::focus-visible">:focus-visible</code></a>
pseudo-class to override the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#outline"
id="focus-management-apis:&#39;outline&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;outline&#39;">'outline'</a> property, and provide
a different way to show what element is focused. Be aware that if an
alternative focusing style isn't made available, the page will be
significantly less usable for people who primarily navigate pages using
a keyboard, or those with reduced vision who use focus outlines to help
them navigate the page.

<div class="example">

For example, to hide the outline from
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements and instead use a yellow
background to indicate focus, you could use:

``` css
textarea:focus-visible { outline: none; background: yellow; color: black; }
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`DocumentOrShadowRoot`](#documentorshadowroot)
<span id="dom-documentorshadowroot-activeelement" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DocumentOrShadowRoot"
dfn-type="attribute">`activeElement`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `candidate` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="focus-management-apis:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
    id="focus-management-apis:focused-area-of-the-document">focused area</a>'s
    <a href="#dom-anchor" id="focus-management-apis:dom-anchor">DOM
    anchor</a>.

2.  Set `candidate` to the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#retarget"
    id="focus-management-apis:dom-retarget"
    data-x-internal="dom-retarget">retargeting</a> `candidate` against
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

3.  If `candidate`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root"
    id="focus-management-apis:root" data-x-internal="root">root</a> is
    not <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    then return null.

4.  If `candidate` is not a [`Document`](#document) object, then return
    `candidate`.

5.  If `candidate` has a <a href="#the-body-element-2"
    id="focus-management-apis:the-body-element-2">body element</a>, then
    return that <a href="#the-body-element-2"
    id="focus-management-apis:the-body-element-2-2">body element</a>.

6.  If `candidate`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="focus-management-apis:document-element-2"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a> is non-null,
    then return that
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
    id="focus-management-apis:document-element-3"
    data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>.

7.  Return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`Document`](#document) <span id="dom-document-hasfocus" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" dfn-type="method">`hasFocus()`</span> method steps
are to return the result of running the <a href="#has-focus-steps"
id="focus-management-apis:has-focus-steps">has focus steps</a> given
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="focus-management-apis:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The [`Window`](#window) <span id="dom-window-focus" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Window" dfn-type="method">`focus()`</span> method steps are:

1.  Let `current` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#window-navigable"
    id="focus-management-apis:window-navigable-2">navigable</a>.

2.  If `current` is null, then return.

3.  If the <a href="#allow-focus-steps"
    id="focus-management-apis:allow-focus-steps">allow focus steps</a>
    given `current`'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="focus-management-apis:nav-document-2">active
    document</a> return false, then return.

4.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="focus-management-apis:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a> with
    `current`.

5.  If `current` is a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="focus-management-apis:top-level-traversable">top-level
    traversable</a>, user agents are encouraged to trigger some sort of
    notification to indicate to the user that the page is attempting to
    gain focus.

</div>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Window/blur](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/blur "Shifts focus away from the window.")

Support in all current engines.

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer4+</span>
