<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`Window`](#window) <span id="dom-window-blur" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Window" dfn-type="method">`blur()`</span> method steps are to
do nothing.

</div>

Historically, the [`focus()`](#dom-window-focus) and
[`blur()`](#dom-window-blur) methods actually affected the system-level
focus of the system widget (e.g., tab or window) that contained the
<a href="#navigable" id="focus-management-apis:navigable">navigable</a>,
but hostile sites widely abuse this behavior to the user's detriment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The [`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement) <span id="dom-focus"
class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOrSVGElement"
dfn-type="method">`focus(``options``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If the <a href="#allow-focus-steps"
    id="focus-management-apis:allow-focus-steps-2">allow focus steps</a>
    given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="focus-management-apis:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> return false, then
    return.

2.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
    id="focus-management-apis:focusing-steps-2">focusing steps</a> for
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

3.  If `options`\["<span id="dom-focusoptions-focusvisible" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="FocusOptions"
    dfn-type="dict-member">`focusVisible`</span>"\] is true, or does not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="focus-management-apis:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exist</a> but in an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="focus-management-apis:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    way the user agent determines it would be best to do so, then
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#indicate-focus"
    id="focus-management-apis:indicate-focus-2"
    data-x-internal="indicate-focus">indicate focus</a>.

4.  If `options`\["<span id="dom-focusoptions-preventscroll" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="FocusOptions"
    dfn-type="dict-member">`preventScroll`</span>"\] is false, then
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#scroll-a-target-into-view"
    id="focus-management-apis:scroll-a-target-into-view"
    data-x-internal="scroll-a-target-into-view">scroll a target into
    view</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`auto`", "`center`", and "`center`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`HTMLOrSVGElement`](#htmlorsvgelement) <span id="dom-blur"
class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLOrSVGElement" dfn-type="method">`blur()`</span>
method steps are:

1.  The user agent should run the <a href="#unfocusing-steps"
    id="focus-management-apis:unfocusing-steps">unfocusing steps</a>
    given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="focus-management-apis:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    User agents may instead selectively or uniformly do nothing, for
    usability reasons.

</div>

For example, if the [`blur()`](#dom-blur) method is unwisely being used
to remove the focus ring for aesthetics reasons, the page would become
unusable by keyboard users. Ignoring calls to this method would thus
allow keyboard users to interact with the page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="allow-focus-steps" class="dfn" export="">allow focus
steps</span>, given a [`Document`](#document) object `target`, are:

1.  If `target` is <a href="#allowed-to-use"
    id="focus-management-apis:allowed-to-use">allowed to use</a> the
    "[`focus-without-user-activation`](#focus-without-user-activation-feature)"
    feature, then return true.

2.  If `target`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="focus-management-apis:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a> has <a href="#transient-activation"
    id="focus-management-apis:transient-activation">transient activation</a>,
    then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.6.7</span> <span id="autofocusing-a-form-control:-the-autofocus-attribute"></span>The [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute<a href="#the-autofocus-attribute" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="attr-fe-autofocus" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`autofocus`</span> content attribute allows the
author to indicate that an element is to be focused as soon as the page
is loaded, allowing the user to just start typing without having to
manually focus the main element.

When the [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute is specified on an
element inside [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements or
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-autofocus-attribute:html-elements">HTML
elements</a> whose [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is set, then it
will be focused when the dialog or popover becomes shown.

The [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To find the <span id="nearest-ancestor-autofocus-scoping-root-element"
class="dfn">nearest ancestor autofocus scoping root element</span> given
an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-autofocus-attribute:element">Element</code></a> `element`:

1.  If `element` is a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element, then
    return `element`.

2.  If `element`'s [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is not in the
    <a href="#attr-popover-none-state"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:attr-popover-none-state">No Popover</a>
    state, then return `element`.

3.  Let `ancestor` be `element`.

4.  While `ancestor` has a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#parent-element"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:parent-element"
    data-x-internal="parent-element">parent element</a>:

    1.  Set `ancestor` to `ancestor`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#parent-element"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:parent-element-2"
        data-x-internal="parent-element">parent element</a>.

    2.  If `ancestor` is a [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element, then
        return `ancestor`.

    3.  If `ancestor`'s [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is not in
        the <a href="#attr-popover-none-state"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:attr-popover-none-state-2">No Popover</a>
        state, then return `ancestor`.

5.  Return `ancestor`.

</div>

There must not be two elements with the same
<a href="#nearest-ancestor-autofocus-scoping-root-element"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:nearest-ancestor-autofocus-scoping-root-element">nearest
ancestor autofocus scoping root element</a> that both have the
[`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute specified.

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="autofocus-candidates"
class="dfn">autofocus candidates</span>
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a>,
initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#document) has an <span id="autofocus-processed-flag"
class="dfn">autofocus processed flag</span> boolean, initially false.

<div algorithm="">

When an element with the [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute
specified is <a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:insert-an-element-into-a-document">inserted
into a document</a>, run the following steps:

1.  If the user has indicated (for example, by starting to type in a
    form control) that they do not wish focus to be changed, then
    optionally return.

2.  Let `target` be the element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

3.  If `target` is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="the-autofocus-attribute:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return.

4.  If `target`'s <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active
    sandboxing flag set</a> has the
    <a href="#sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
    automatic features browsing context flag</a>, then return.

5.  If the <a href="#allow-focus-steps"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:allow-focus-steps">allow focus steps</a>
    given `target` return false, then return.

6.  Let `topDocument` be `target`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:node-navigable">node navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-top" id="the-autofocus-attribute:nav-top">top-level
    traversable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="the-autofocus-attribute:nav-document">active
    document</a>.

7.  If `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-processed-flag"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-processed-flag">autofocus
    processed flag</a> is false, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">remove</a> the element from
    `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates">autofocus
    candidates</a>, and
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-append"
    data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> the element to
    `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates-2">autofocus
    candidates</a>.

</div>

We do not check if an element is a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:focusable-area">focusable area</a> before
storing it in the <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates-3">autofocus
candidates</a> list, because even if it is not a focusable area when it
is inserted, it could become one by the time
<a href="#flush-autofocus-candidates"
id="the-autofocus-attribute:flush-autofocus-candidates">flush autofocus
candidates</a> sees it.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="flush-autofocus-candidates" class="dfn">flush autofocus
candidates</span> for a document `topDocument`, run these steps:

1.  If `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-processed-flag"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-processed-flag-2">autofocus
    processed flag</a> is true, then return.

2.  Let `candidates` be `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates-4">autofocus
    candidates</a>.

3.  If `candidates`
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">is empty</a>, then return.

4.  If `topDocument`'s <a href="#focused-area-of-the-document"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:focused-area-of-the-document">focused
    area</a> is not `topDocument` itself, or `topDocument` has non-null
    <a href="#target-element"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:target-element">target element</a>,
    then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-empty"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-empty"
        data-x-internal="list-empty">Empty</a> `candidates`.

    2.  Set `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-processed-flag"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-processed-flag-3">autofocus
        processed flag</a> to true.

    3.  Return.

5.  While `candidates` is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-is-empty-2"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>:

    1.  Let `element` be `candidates`\[0\].

    2.  Let `doc` be `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:node-document-2"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

    3.  If `doc` is not <a href="#fully-active"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:fully-active-2">fully active</a>,
        then <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-remove-2"
        data-x-internal="list-remove">remove</a> `element` from
        `candidates`, and
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    4.  If `doc`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:node-navigable-2">node navigable</a>'s
        <a href="#nav-top" id="the-autofocus-attribute:nav-top-2">top-level
        traversable</a> is not the same as `topDocument`'s
        <a href="#node-navigable"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:node-navigable-3">node navigable</a>,
        then <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-remove-3"
        data-x-internal="list-remove">remove</a> `element` from
        `candidates`, and
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:continue-2"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    5.  If `doc`'s <a href="#script-blocking-style-sheet-set"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:script-blocking-style-sheet-set">script-blocking
        style sheet set</a> is not
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-is-empty-3"
        data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>, then return.

        In this case, `element` is the currently-best candidate, but
        `doc` is not ready for autofocusing. We'll try again next time
        <a href="#flush-autofocus-candidates"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:flush-autofocus-candidates-2">flush
        autofocus candidates</a> is called.

    6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-remove-4"
        data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `element` from
        `candidates`.

    7.  Let `inclusiveAncestorDocuments` be a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-2" data-x-internal="list">list</a>
        consisting of the <a href="#nav-document"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:nav-document-2">active document</a>
        of `doc`'s <a href="#inclusive-ancestor-navigables"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:inclusive-ancestor-navigables">inclusive
        ancestor navigables</a>.

    8.  If any [`Document`](#document) in `inclusiveAncestorDocuments`
        has non-null <a href="#target-element"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:target-element-2">target element</a>,
        then <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:continue-3"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    9.  Let `target` be `element`.

    10. If `target` is not a <a href="#focusable-area"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:focusable-area-2">focusable area</a>,
        then set `target` to the result of
        <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:get-the-focusable-area">getting the
        focusable area</a> for `target`.

        <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates-5">Autofocus
        candidates</a> can
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-contains"
        data-x-internal="list-contains">contain</a> elements which are
        not <a href="#focusable-area"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:focusable-area-3">focusable areas</a>.
        In addition to the special cases handled in the
        <a href="#get-the-focusable-area"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:get-the-focusable-area-2">get the focusable
        area</a> algorithm, this can happen because a
        non-<a href="#focusable-area"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:focusable-area-4">focusable area</a>
        element with an [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute was
        <a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:insert-an-element-into-a-document-2">inserted
        into a document</a> and it never became focusable, or because
        the element was focusable but its status changed while it was
        stored in <a href="#autofocus-candidates"
        id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-candidates-6">autofocus
        candidates</a>.

    11. If `target` is not null, then:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-empty"
            id="the-autofocus-attribute:list-empty-2"
            data-x-internal="list-empty">Empty</a> `candidates`.

        2.  Set `topDocument`'s <a href="#autofocus-processed-flag"
            id="the-autofocus-attribute:autofocus-processed-flag-4">autofocus
            processed flag</a> to true.

        3.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
            id="the-autofocus-attribute:focusing-steps">focusing steps</a>
            for `target`.

</div>

This handles the automatic focusing during document load. The
[`show()`](#dom-dialog-show) and [`showModal()`](#dom-dialog-showmodal)
methods of [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) elements also processes the
[`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute.

Focusing the element does not imply that the user agent has to focus the
browser window if it has lost focus.

<div class="example">

In the following snippet, the text control would be focused when the
document was loaded.

``` html
<input maxlength="256" name="q" value="" autofocus>
<input type="submit" value="Search">
```

</div>

<div class="example">

The [`autofocus`](#attr-fe-autofocus) attribute applies to all elements,
not just to form controls. This allows examples such as the following:

``` html
<div contenteditable autofocus>Edit <strong>me!</strong><div>
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.7</span> Assigning keyboard shortcuts<a href="#assigning-keyboard-shortcuts" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">6.7.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-9" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

Each element that can be activated or focused can be assigned a single
key combination to activate it, using the
[`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

The exact shortcut is determined by the user agent, based on information
about the user's keyboard, what keyboard shortcuts already exist on the
platform, and what other shortcuts have been specified on the page,
using the information provided in the
[`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) attribute as a guide.

In order to ensure that a relevant keyboard shortcut is available on a
wide variety of input devices, the author can provide a number of
alternatives in the [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

Each alternative consists of a single character, such as a letter or
digit.

User agents can provide users with a list of the keyboard shortcuts, but
authors are encouraged to do so also. The
[`accessKeyLabel`](#dom-accesskeylabel) IDL attribute returns a string
representing the actual key combination assigned by the user agent.

<div class="example">

In this example, an author has provided a button that can be invoked
using a shortcut key. To support full keyboards, the author has provided
"C" as a possible key. To support devices equipped only with numeric
keypads, the author has provided "1" as another possible key.

``` html
<input type=button value=Collect onclick="collect()"
       accesskey="C 1" id=c>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

To tell the user what the shortcut key is, the author has here opted to
explicitly add the key combination to the button's label:

``` js
function addShortcutKeyLabel(button) {
  if (button.accessKeyLabel != '')
    button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
}
addShortcutKeyLabel(document.getElementById('c'));
```

Browsers on different platforms will show different labels, even for the
same key combination, based on the convention prevalent on that
platform. For example, if the key combination is the Control key, the
Shift key, and the letter C, a Windows browser might display
"`Ctrl+Shift+C`", whereas a Mac browser might display "`^⇧C`", while an
Emacs browser might just display "`C-C`". Similarly, if the key
combination is the Alt key and the Escape key, Windows might use
"`Alt+Esc`", Mac might use "`⌥⎋`", and an Emacs browser might use
"`M-ESC`" or "`ESC ESC`".

In general, therefore, it is unwise to attempt to parse the value
returned from the [`accessKeyLabel`](#dom-accesskeylabel) IDL attribute.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.7.2</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global" dfn-type="element-attr">`accesskey`</span> attribute<a href="#the-accesskey-attribute" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/accesskey](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/accesskey "The accesskey global attribute provides a hint for generating a keyboard shortcut for the current element. The attribute value must consist of a single printable character (which includes accented and other characters that can be generated by the keyboard).")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox1+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome1+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

All
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-accesskey-attribute:html-elements">HTML
elements</a> may have the [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute)
content attribute set. The [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute)
attribute's value is used by the user agent as a guide for creating a
keyboard shortcut that activates or focuses the element.

If specified, the value must be an
<a href="#ordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens"
id="the-accesskey-attribute:ordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">ordered
set of unique space-separated tokens</a> none of which are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
id="the-accesskey-attribute:identical-to"
data-x-internal="identical-to">identical to</a> another token and each
of which must be exactly one code point in length.

<div class="example">

In the following example, a variety of links are given with access keys
so that keyboard users familiar with the site can more quickly navigate
to the relevant pages:

``` html
<nav>
 <p>
  <a title="Consortium Activities" accesskey="A" href="/Consortium/activities">Activities</a> |
  <a title="Technical Reports and Recommendations" accesskey="T" href="/TR/">Technical Reports</a> |
  <a title="Alphabetical Site Index" accesskey="S" href="/Consortium/siteindex">Site Index</a> |
  <a title="About This Site" accesskey="B" href="/Consortium/">About Consortium</a> |
  <a title="Contact Consortium" accesskey="C" href="/Consortium/contact">Contact</a>
 </p>
</nav>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following example, the search field is given two possible access
keys, "s" and "0" (in that order). A user agent on a device with a full
keyboard might pick <span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Ctrl</span> +
<span class="kbd">Alt</span> + <span class="kbd">S</span></span> as the
shortcut key, while a user agent on a small device with just a numeric
keypad might pick just the plain unadorned key
<span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">0</span></span>:

``` html
<form action="/search">
 <label>Search: <input type="search" name="q" accesskey="s 0"></label>
 <input type="submit">
</form>
```

</div>

<div class="example">

In the following example, a button has possible access keys described. A
script then tries to update the button's label to advertise the key
combination the user agent selected.

``` html
<input type=submit accesskey="N @ 1" value="Compose">
...
<script>
 function labelButton(button) {
   if (button.accessKeyLabel)
     button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
 }
 var inputs = document.getElementsByTagName('input');
 for (var i = 0; i < inputs.length; i += 1) {
   if (inputs[i].type == "submit")
     labelButton(inputs[i]);
 }
</script>
```

On one user agent, the button's label might become "`Compose (⌘N)`". On
another, it might become "`Compose (Alt+⇧+1)`". If the user agent
doesn't assign a key, it will be just "`Compose`". The exact string
depends on what the <a href="#assigned-access-key"
id="the-accesskey-attribute:assigned-access-key">assigned access key</a>
is, and on how the user agent represents that key combination.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.7.3</span> <span id="processing-model-6"></span>Processing model<a href="#keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

An element's <span id="assigned-access-key" class="dfn">assigned access
key</span> is a key combination derived from the element's
[`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute. Initially, an
element must not have an <a href="#assigned-access-key"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key">assigned
access key</a>.

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an element's [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) attribute
is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must update the element's
<a href="#assigned-access-key"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-2">assigned
access key</a> by running the following steps:

1.  If the element has no [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute)
    attribute, then skip to the *fallback* step below.

2.  Otherwise,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-ascii-whitespace"
    id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:split-a-string-on-spaces"
    data-x-internal="split-a-string-on-spaces">split the attribute's value
    on ASCII whitespace</a>, and let `keys` be the resulting tokens.

3.  For each value in `keys` in turn, in the order the tokens appeared
    in the attribute's value, run the following substeps:

    1.  If the value is not a string exactly one code point in length,
        then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.

    2.  If the value does not correspond to a key on the system's
        keyboard, then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.

    3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
        id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:tracking-vector"
        class="tracking-vector" data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
        title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
        src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
        class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
        alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> If the user agent can
        find a mix of zero or more modifier keys that, combined with the
        key that corresponds to the value given in the attribute, can be
        used as the access key, then the user agent may assign that
        combination of keys as the element's
        <a href="#assigned-access-key"
        id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-3">assigned
        access key</a> and return.

4.  *Fallback*: Optionally, the user agent may assign a key combination
    of its choosing as the element's <a href="#assigned-access-key"
    id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-4">assigned
    access key</a> and then return.

5.  If this step is reached, the element has no
    <a href="#assigned-access-key"
    id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-5">assigned
    access key</a>.

</div>

Once a user agent has selected and assigned an access key for an
element, the user agent should not change the element's
<a href="#assigned-access-key"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-6">assigned
access key</a> unless the [`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute)
content attribute is changed or the element is moved to another
[`Document`](#document).

<div algorithm="">

When the user presses the key combination corresponding to the
<a href="#assigned-access-key"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:assigned-access-key-7">assigned
access key</a> for an element, if the element <a href="#concept-command"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:concept-command">defines a
command</a>, the command's <a href="#command-facet-hiddenstate"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:command-facet-hiddenstate">Hidden
State</a> facet is false (visible), the command's
<a href="#command-facet-disabledstate"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:command-facet-disabledstate">Disabled
State</a> facet is also false (enabled), the element is
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:in-a-document"
data-x-internal="in-a-document">in a document</a> that has a non-null
<a href="#concept-document-bc"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:concept-document-bc">browsing
context</a>, and neither the element nor any of its ancestors has a
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute specified, then the user agent must
trigger the <a href="#command-facet-action"
id="keyboard-shortcuts-processing-model:command-facet-action">Action</a>
of the command.

</div>

User agents [might expose](#expose-commands-in-ui) elements that have an
[`accesskey`](#the-accesskey-attribute) attribute in other ways as well,
e.g. in a menu displayed in response to a specific key combination.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

dfn-type="attribute">`accessKeyLabel`</span> IDL attribute must return a

### <span class="secno">6.8</span> Editing<a href="#editing-2" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.1</span> Making document regions editable: The [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable) content attribute<a href="#contenteditable" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

[HTMLElement/contentEditable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/contentEditable "The contentEditable property of the HTMLElement interface specifies whether or not the element is editable.")

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString contentEditable;

[Global_attributes/contenteditable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/contenteditable "The contenteditable global attribute is an enumerated attribute indicating if the element should be editable by the user. If so, the browser modifies its widget to allow editing.")

iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView

</div>

The <span id="attr-contenteditable" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`contenteditable`</span> content attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="contenteditable:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a> with
the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-contenteditable-true" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/contenteditable" dfn-type="attr-value">`true`</span> | <span id="attr-contenteditable-true-state" class="dfn">True</span> | The element is editable. |
| <span id="attr-contenteditable-false" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/contenteditable" dfn-type="attr-value">`false`</span> | <span id="attr-contenteditable-false-state" class="dfn">False</span> | The element is not editable. |
| <span id="attr-contenteditable-plaintextonly" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/contenteditable" dfn-type="attr-value">`plaintext-only`</span> | <span id="attr-contenteditable-plaintextonly-state" class="dfn">Plaintext-Only</span> | Only the element's raw text content is editable; rich formatting is disabled. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-contenteditable-inherit-state" class="dfn">Inherit</span>
state. The inherit state indicates that the element is editable (or not)
based on the parent element's state. The attribute's *[empty value
default](#empty-value-default)* is the
<a href="#attr-contenteditable-true-state"
id="contenteditable:attr-contenteditable-true-state">True</a> state.

</div>

<div class="example">

For example, consider a page that has a [`form`](#the-form-element) and
a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) to publish a new article, where
the user is expected to write the article using HTML:

``` html
<form method=POST>
 <fieldset>
  <legend>New article</legend>
  <textarea name=article>&lt;p>Hello world.&lt;/p></textarea>
 </fieldset>
 <p><button>Publish</button></p>
</form>
```

When scripting is enabled, the [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)
element could be replaced with a rich text control instead, using the
[`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable) attribute:

``` html
<form method=POST>
 <fieldset>
  <legend>New article</legend>
  <textarea id=textarea name=article>&lt;p>Hello world.&lt;/p></textarea>
  <div id=div style="white-space: pre-wrap" hidden><p>Hello world.</p></div>
  <script>
   let textarea = document.getElementById("textarea");
   let div = document.getElementById("div");
   textarea.hidden = true;
   div.hidden = false;
   div.contentEditable = "true";
   div.oninput = (e) => {
     textarea.value = div.innerHTML;
   };
  </script>
 </fieldset>
 <p><button>Publish</button></p>
</form>
```

Features to enable, e.g., inserting links, can be implemented using the
<a
href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#execcommand%28%29"
data-x-internal="execCommand"><code
id="contenteditable:execCommand">document.execCommand()</code></a> API,
or using
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#selection-interface"
data-x-internal="selection"><code
id="contenteditable:selection">Selection</code></a> APIs and other DOM
APIs. [\[EXECCOMMAND\]](#refsEXECCOMMAND)
[\[SELECTION\]](#refsSELECTION) [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

</div>

<div class="example">

The [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable) attribute can also be
used to great effect:

``` html
<!doctype html>
<html lang=en>
<title>Live CSS editing!</title>
<style style=white-space:pre contenteditable>
html { margin:.2em; font-size:2em; color:lime; background:purple }
head, title, style { display:block }
body { display:none }
</style>
```

</div>

`element``.`<a href="#dom-contenteditable"
id="dom-contenteditable-dev"><code>contentEditable</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

Returns "`true`", "`plaintext-only`", "`false`", or "`inherit`", based
on the state of the [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable)
attribute.

Can be set, to change that state.

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
id="contenteditable:syntaxerror"
data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="contenteditable:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if the new
value isn't one of those strings.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-iscontenteditable"
id="dom-iscontenteditable-dev"><code>isContentEditable</code></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLElement/isContentEditable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/isContentEditable "The HTMLElement.isContentEditable read-only property returns a boolean value that is true if the contents of the element are editable; otherwise it returns false.")

Support in all current engines.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer5.5+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS1+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android12.1+</span>

Returns true if the element is editable; otherwise, returns false.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-contenteditable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementContentEditable"
dfn-type="attribute">`contentEditable`</span> IDL attribute, on getting,
must return the string "`true`" if the content attribute is set to the
<a href="#attr-contenteditable-true-state"
id="contenteditable:attr-contenteditable-true-state-2">True</a> state,
"`plaintext-only`" if the content attribute is set to the
<a href="#attr-contenteditable-plaintextonly-state"
id="contenteditable:attr-contenteditable-plaintextonly-state">Plaintext-Only</a>
state, "`false`" if the content attribute is set to the
<a href="#attr-contenteditable-false-state"
id="contenteditable:attr-contenteditable-false-state">False</a> state,
and "`inherit`" otherwise. On setting, if the new value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="contenteditable:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`inherit`", then the content attribute must be
removed, if the new value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="contenteditable:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`true`", then the content attribute must be set to
the string "`true`", if the new value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="contenteditable:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`plaintext-only`", then the content attribute must
be set to the string "`plaintext-only`", if the new value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="contenteditable:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`false`", then the content attribute must be set
to the string "`false`", and otherwise the attribute setter must throw a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
id="contenteditable:syntaxerror-2"
data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="contenteditable:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-iscontenteditable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ElementContentEditable"
dfn-type="attribute">`isContentEditable`</span> IDL attribute, on
getting, must return true if the element is either an
<a href="#editing-host" id="contenteditable:editing-host">editing
host</a> or
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
id="contenteditable:editable" data-x-internal="editable">editable</a>,
and false otherwise.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.2</span> Making entire documents editable: the [`designMode`](#designMode) getter and setter<a

class="self-link"></a>

`document``.`<a href="#designMode"
id="dom-document-designmode-dev"><code>designMode</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

According to the specification, this property is meant to default to "off". Firefox follows this standard. The earlier versions of Chrome and IE default to "inherit". Starting in Chrome 43, the default is "off" and "inherit" is no longer supported. In IE6-10, the value is capitalized.")

(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer4+</span>

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView

Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android10.1+</span>

Returns "`on`" if the document is editable, and "`off`" if it isn't.

Can be set, to change the document's current state. This focuses the
document and resets the selection in that document.

[`Document`](#document) objects have an associated
<span id="design-mode-enabled" class="dfn">design mode enabled</span>,
which is a boolean. It is initially false.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="designMode" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
dfn-type="attribute">`designMode`</span> getter steps are to return
"`on`" if <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#design-mode-enabled"
id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:design-mode-enabled">design
mode enabled</a> is true; otherwise "`off`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`designMode`](#designMode) setter steps are:

1.  Let `value` be the given value,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

2.  If `value` is "`on`" and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#design-mode-enabled"
    id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:design-mode-enabled-2">design
    mode enabled</a> is false, then:

    1.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-3"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#design-mode-enabled"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:design-mode-enabled-3">design
        mode enabled</a> to true.

    2.  Reset <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-4"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:active-range"
        data-x-internal="active-range">active range</a>'s start and end
        boundary points to be at the start of
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-5"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    3.  Run the <a href="#focusing-steps"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:focusing-steps">focusing
        steps</a> for <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-6"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element"
        id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:document-element"
        data-x-internal="document-element">document element</a>, if
        non-null.

3.  If `value` is "`off`", then set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:this-7"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#design-mode-enabled"
    id="making-entire-documents-editable:-the-designmode-idl-attribute:design-mode-enabled-4">design
    mode enabled</a> to false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.3</span> Best practices for in-page editors<a href="#best-practices-for-in-page-editors" class="self-link"></a>

Authors are encouraged to set the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:&#39;white-space&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> property on
<a href="#editing-host"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:editing-host">editing hosts</a>
and on markup that was originally created through these editing
mechanisms to the value 'pre-wrap'. Default HTML whitespace handling is
not well suited to WYSIWYG editing, and line wrapping will not work
correctly in some corner cases if
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:&#39;white-space&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> is left at its
default value.

<div class="example">

As an example of problems that occur if the default 'normal' value is
used instead, consider the case of the user typing
"<span class="kbd">yellow␣␣ball</span>", with two spaces (here
represented by "␣") between the words. With the editing rules in place
for the default value of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:&#39;white-space&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> ('normal'),
the resulting markup will either consist of "`yellow&nbsp; ball`" or
"`yellow &nbsp;ball`"; i.e., there will be a non-breaking space between
the two words in addition to the regular space. This is necessary
because the 'normal' value for
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:&#39;white-space&#39;-4"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> requires
adjacent regular spaces to be collapsed together.

In the former case, "`yellow⍽`" might wrap to the next line ("⍽" being
used here to represent a non-breaking space) even though "`yellow`"
alone might fit at the end of the line; in the latter case, "`⍽ball`",
if wrapped to the start of the line, would have visible indentation from
the non-breaking space.

When <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="best-practices-for-in-page-editors:&#39;white-space&#39;-5"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> is set to
'pre-wrap', however, the editing rules will instead simply put two
regular spaces between the words, and should the two words be split at
the end of a line, the spaces would be neatly removed from the
rendering.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.4</span> Editing APIs<a href="#editing-apis" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

An <span id="editing-host" class="dfn" export="">editing host</span> is
either an <a href="#html-elements" id="editing-apis:html-elements">HTML
element</a> with its [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable)
attribute in the *true* state or *plaintext-only* state, or a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
id="editing-apis:concept-tree-child"
data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">child</a>
<a href="#html-elements" id="editing-apis:html-elements-2">HTML
element</a> of a [`Document`](#document) whose
<a href="#design-mode-enabled"
id="editing-apis:design-mode-enabled">design mode enabled</a> is true.

</div>

The definition of the terms <span id="active-range" class="dfn">[active
range](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range)</span>,
<span id="editing-host-of" class="dfn">[editing host
of](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editing-host-of)</span>,
and <span id="editable"
class="dfn">[editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable)</span>,
the user interface requirements of elements that are
<a href="#editing-host" id="editing-apis:editing-host">editing hosts</a>
or <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
id="editing-apis:editable" data-x-internal="editable">editable</a>, the
<span id="execCommand"
class="dfn">[`execCommand()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#execcommand%28%29)</span>,
<span id="dom-document-querycommandenabled"
class="dfn">[`queryCommandEnabled()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandenabled%28%29)</span>,
<span id="dom-document-querycommandindeterm"
class="dfn">[`queryCommandIndeterm()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandindeterm%28%29)</span>,
<span id="dom-document-querycommandstate"
class="dfn">[`queryCommandState()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandstate%28%29)</span>,
<span id="dom-document-querycommandsupported"
class="dfn">[`queryCommandSupported()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandsupported%28%29)</span>,
and <span id="dom-document-querycommandvalue"
class="dfn">[`queryCommandValue()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandvalue%28%29)</span>
methods, text selections, and the <span id="delete-the-selection"

#### <span class="secno">6.8.5</span> Spelling and grammar checking<a href="#spelling-and-grammar-checking" class="self-link"></a>

User agents can support the checking of spelling and grammar of editable
text, either in form controls (such as the value of
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an
<a href="#editing-host"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:editing-host">editing host</a> (e.g.
using [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable)).

For each element, user agents must establish a
<span id="concept-spellcheck-default" class="dfn">default
behavior</span>, either through defaults or through preferences
expressed by the user. There are three possible default behaviors for
each element:

<span id="concept-spellcheck-default-true" class="dfn">true-by-default</span>  
The element will be checked for spelling and grammar if its contents are
editable and spellchecking is not explicitly disabled through the
[`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) attribute.

<span id="concept-spellcheck-default-false" class="dfn">false-by-default</span>  
The element will never be checked for spelling and grammar unless
spellchecking is explicitly enabled through the
[`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) attribute.

<span id="concept-spellcheck-default-inherit" class="dfn">inherit-by-default</span>  
The element's default behavior is the same as its parent element's.
Elements that have no parent element cannot have this as their default
behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/spellcheck](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/spellcheck "The spellcheck global attribute is an enumerated attribute that defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">FirefoxYes</span><span class="safari yes">SafariYes</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome9+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">OperaYes</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer11</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android yes">Firefox
Android57+</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS9.3+</span><span class="chrome_android yes">Chrome
Android47+</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android37+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-spellcheck" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`spellcheck`</span> attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-spellcheck-true" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/spellcheck" dfn-type="attr-value">`true`</span> | <span id="attr-spellcheck-true-state" class="dfn">True</span> | Spelling and grammar will be checked. |
| <span id="attr-spellcheck-false" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/spellcheck" dfn-type="attr-value">`false`</span> | <span id="attr-spellcheck-false-state" class="dfn">False</span> | Spelling and grammar will not be checked. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-spellcheck-default-state" class="dfn">Default</span>
state. The default state indicates that the element is to act according
to a default behavior, possibly based on the parent element's own
[`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) state, as defined below. The
attribute's *[empty value default](#empty-value-default)* is the
<a href="#attr-spellcheck-true-state"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-true-state">True</a>
state.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

`element``.`<a href="#dom-spellcheck"
id="dom-spellcheck-dev"><code>spellcheck</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns true if the element is to have its spelling and grammar checked;
otherwise, returns false.

Can be set, to override the default and set the
[`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-spellcheck" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`spellcheck`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return true if the element's [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content
attribute is in the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-true-state"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-true-state-2">True</a>
state, or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content
attribute is in the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-default-state"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-default-state">Default</a>
state and the element's <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default">default
behavior</a> is <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default-true"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-true">true-by-default</a>,
or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute
is in the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-default-state"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-default-state-2">Default</a>
state and the element's <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-2">default
behavior</a> is <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default-inherit"
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-inherit">inherit-by-default</a>
and the element's parent element's [`spellcheck`](#dom-spellcheck) IDL
attribute would return true; otherwise, if none of those conditions
applies, then the attribute must instead return false.

</div>

The [`spellcheck`](#dom-spellcheck) IDL attribute is not affected by
user preferences that override the [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck)
content attribute, and therefore might not reflect the actual
spellchecking state.

<div algorithm="">

On setting, if the new value is true, then the element's
[`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute must be set to
"`true`", otherwise it must be set to "`false`".

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

User agents should only consider the following pieces of text as
checkable for the purposes of this feature:

- The <a href="#concept-fe-value"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-fe-value">value</a> of
  [`input`](#the-input-element) elements whose
  [`type`](#attr-input-type) attributes are in the
  <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">Text</a>,
  <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-2">Search</a>,
  <a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>, or
  <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a>
  states and that are *[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)* (i.e. that do not
  have the [`readonly`](#attr-input-readonly) attribute specified and
  that are not <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-fe-disabled">disabled</a>).
- The <a href="#concept-fe-value"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-fe-value-2">value</a> of
  [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements that do not have a
  [`readonly`](#attr-textarea-readonly) attribute and that are not
  <a href="#concept-fe-disabled"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-fe-disabled-2">disabled</a>.
- Text in <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
  data-x-internal="text"><code
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:text">Text</code></a> nodes that are
  children of <a href="#editing-host"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:editing-host-2">editing hosts</a> or
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:editable"
  data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> elements.
- Text in attributes of
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
  id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:editable-2"
  data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> elements.

For text that is part of a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:text-2">Text</code></a> node, the
element with which the text is associated is the element that is the
immediate parent of the first character of the word, sentence, or other
piece of text. For text in attributes, it is the attribute's element.
For the values of [`input`](#the-input-element) and
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements, it is the element itself.

<div algorithm="">

To determine if a word, sentence, or other piece of text in an
applicable element (as defined above) is to have spelling- and
grammar-checking enabled, the UA must use the following algorithm:

1.  If the user has disabled the checking for this text, then the
    checking is disabled.
2.  Otherwise, if the user has forced the checking for this text to
    always be enabled, then the checking is enabled.
3.  Otherwise, if the element with which the text is associated has a
    [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute, then: if that
    attribute is in the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-true-state"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-true-state-3">True</a>
    state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, if that attribute is in
    the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-false-state"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-false-state">False</a>
    state, then checking is disabled.
4.  Otherwise, if there is an ancestor element with a
    [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute that is not in
    the <a href="#attr-spellcheck-default-state"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-default-state-3">Default</a>
    state, then: if the nearest such ancestor's
    [`spellcheck`](#attr-spellcheck) content attribute is in the
    <a href="#attr-spellcheck-true-state"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:attr-spellcheck-true-state-4">True</a>
    state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, checking is disabled.
5.  Otherwise, if the element's <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-3">default
    behavior</a> is <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default-true"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-true-2">true-by-default</a>,
    then checking is enabled.
6.  Otherwise, if the element's <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-4">default
    behavior</a> is <a href="#concept-spellcheck-default-false"
    id="spelling-and-grammar-checking:concept-spellcheck-default-false">false-by-default</a>,
    then checking is disabled.
7.  Otherwise, if the element's parent element has *its* checking
    enabled, then checking is enabled.
8.  Otherwise, checking is disabled.

</div>

If the checking is enabled for a word/sentence/text, the user agent
should indicate spelling and grammar errors in that text. User agents
should take into account the other semantics given in the document when
suggesting spelling and grammar corrections. User agents may use the
language of the element to determine what spelling and grammar rules to
use, or may use the user's preferred language settings. UAs should use
[`input`](#the-input-element) element attributes such as
[`pattern`](#attr-input-pattern) to ensure that the resulting value is
valid, where possible.

If checking is disabled, the user agent should not indicate spelling or
grammar errors for that text.

<div class="example">

The element with ID "a" in the following example would be the one used
to determine if the word "Hello" is checked for spelling errors. In this
example, it would not be.

``` html
<div contenteditable="true">
 <span spellcheck="false" id="a">Hell</span><em>o!</em>
</div>
```

The element with ID "b" in the following example would have checking
enabled (the leading space character in the attribute's value on the
[`input`](#the-input-element) element causes the attribute to be
ignored, so the ancestor's value is used instead, regardless of the
default).

``` bad
<p spellcheck="true">
 <label>Name: <input spellcheck=" false" id="b"></label>
</p>
```

</div>

This specification does not define the user interface for spelling and
grammar checkers. A user agent could offer on-demand checking, could
perform continuous checking while the checking is enabled, or could use
other interfaces.

#### <span class="secno">6.8.6</span> Writing suggestions<a href="#writing-suggestions" class="self-link"></a>

User agents offer writing suggestions as users type into editable
regions, either in form controls (e.g., the
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element) or in elements in an
<a href="#editing-host" id="writing-suggestions:editing-host">editing
host</a>.

The <span id="attr-writingsuggestions" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`writingsuggestions`</span> content attribute is
an <a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="writing-suggestions:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-writingsuggestions-true" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/writingsuggestions" dfn-type="attr-value">`true`</span> | <span id="attr-writingsuggestions-true-state" class="dfn">True</span> | Writing suggestions should be offered on this element. |
| <span id="attr-writingsuggestions-false" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/writingsuggestions" dfn-type="attr-value">`false`</span> | <span id="attr-writingsuggestions-false-state" class="dfn">False</span> | Writing suggestions should not be offered on this element. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* is the
<span id="attr-writingsuggestions-default-state"
class="dfn">Default</span> state. The default state indicates that the
element is to act according to a default behavior, possibly based on the
parent element's own [`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions)
state, as defined below.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* and
*[empty value default](#empty-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-writingsuggestions-true-state"
id="writing-suggestions:attr-writingsuggestions-true-state">True</a>
state.

</div>

`element``.`<a href="#dom-writingsuggestions"
id="dom-writingsuggestions-dev"><code>writingSuggestions</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns "`true`" if the user agent is to offer writing suggestions under
the scope of the element; otherwise, returns "`false`".

Can be set, to override the default and set the
` `[`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions) content attribute.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="computed-writing-suggestions-value" class="dfn">computed
writing suggestions value</span> of a given `element` is determined by
running the following steps:

1.  If `element`'s [`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions)
    content attribute is in the
    <a href="#attr-writingsuggestions-false-state"
    id="writing-suggestions:attr-writingsuggestions-false-state">False</a>
    state, return "`false`".

2.  If `element`'s [`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions)
    content attribute is in the
    <a href="#attr-writingsuggestions-default-state"
    id="writing-suggestions:attr-writingsuggestions-default-state">Default</a>
    state, `element` has a parent element, and the
    <a href="#computed-writing-suggestions-value"
    id="writing-suggestions:computed-writing-suggestions-value">computed
    writing suggestions value</a> of `element`'s parent element is
    "`false`", then return "`false`".

3.  Return "`true`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-writingsuggestions" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`writingSuggestions`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="writing-suggestions:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#computed-writing-suggestions-value"
    id="writing-suggestions:computed-writing-suggestions-value-2">computed
    writing suggestions value</a>.

</div>

The [`writingSuggestions`](#dom-writingsuggestions) IDL attribute is not
affected by user preferences that override the
[`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions) content attribute, and
therefore might not reflect the actual writing suggestions state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

User agents should only offer suggestions within an element's scope if
the result of running the following algorithm given `element` returns
true:

1.  If the user has disabled writing suggestions, then return false.

2.  If none of the following conditions are true:

    - `element` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
      [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in either the
      <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
      id="writing-suggestions:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">Text</a>,
      <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
      id="writing-suggestions:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-2">Search</a>,
      <a href="#telephone-state-(type=tel)"
      id="writing-suggestions:telephone-state-(type=tel)">Telephone</a>,
      <a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
      id="writing-suggestions:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>, or
      <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
      id="writing-suggestions:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a> state
      and is *[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)*;

    - `element` is a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element that is
      *[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)*; or

    - `element` is an
      <a href="#editing-host" id="writing-suggestions:editing-host-2">editing
      host</a> or is
      <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
      id="writing-suggestions:editable"
      data-x-internal="editable">editable</a>,

    then return false.

3.  If `element` has an
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-inclusive-ancestor"
    id="writing-suggestions:inclusive-ancestor"
    data-x-internal="inclusive-ancestor">inclusive ancestor</a> with a
    [`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions) content attribute
    that's not in the <a href="#attr-writingsuggestions-default-state"
    id="writing-suggestions:attr-writingsuggestions-default-state-2">Default</a>
    and the nearest such ancestor's
    [`writingsuggestions`](#attr-writingsuggestions) content attribute
    is in the <a href="#attr-writingsuggestions-false-state"
    id="writing-suggestions:attr-writingsuggestions-false-state-2">False</a>
    state, then return false.

4.  Otherwise, return true.

</div>

This specification does not define the user interface for writing
suggestions. A user agent could offer on-demand suggestions, continuous
suggestions as the user types, inline suggestions, autofill-like
suggestions in a popup, or could use other interfaces.

#### <span class="secno">6.8.7</span> Autocapitalization<a href="#autocapitalization" class="self-link"></a>

Some methods of entering text, for example virtual keyboards on mobile
devices, and also voice input, often assist users by automatically
capitalizing the first letter of sentences (when composing text in a
language with this convention). A virtual keyboard that implements
autocapitalization might automatically switch to showing uppercase
letters (but allow the user to toggle it back to lowercase) when a
letter that should be autocapitalized is about to be typed. Other types
of input, for example voice input, may perform autocapitalization in a
way that does not give users an option to intervene first. The
[`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) attribute allows authors to
control such behavior.

The [`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) attribute, as typically
implemented, does not affect behavior when typing on a physical
keyboard. (For this reason, as well as the ability for users to override
the autocapitalization behavior in some cases or edit the text after
initial input, the attribute must not be relied on for any sort of input
validation.)

The [`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) attribute can be used on an
<a href="#editing-host" id="autocapitalization:editing-host">editing
host</a> to control autocapitalization behavior for the hosted editable
region, on an [`input`](#the-input-element) or
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to control the behavior for
inputting text into that element, or on a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element to control the default behavior for all
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="autocapitalization:category-autocapitalize">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting elements</a> associated with the [`form`](#the-form-element)
element.

The [`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) attribute never causes
autocapitalization to be enabled for [`input`](#the-input-element)
elements whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the
<a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
id="autocapitalization:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>,
<a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
id="autocapitalization:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a>, or
<a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
id="autocapitalization:password-state-(type=password)">Password</a>
states. (This behavior is included in the
<a href="#used-autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:used-autocapitalization-hint">used
autocapitalization hint</a> algorithm below.)

The autocapitalization processing model is based on selecting among five
<span id="autocapitalization-hint" class="dfn">autocapitalization
hints</span>, defined as follows:

<span id="autocap-hint-default" class="dfn">Default</span>  
The user agent and input method should make their own determination of
whether or not to enable autocapitalization.

<span id="autocap-hint-none" class="dfn">None</span>  
No autocapitalization should be applied (all letters should default to
lowercase).

<span id="autocap-hint-sentences" class="dfn">Sentences</span>  
The first letter of each sentence should default to a capital letter;
all other letters should default to lowercase.

<span id="autocap-hint-words" class="dfn">Words</span>  
The first letter of each word should default to a capital letter; all
other letters should default to lowercase.

<span id="autocap-hint-characters" class="dfn">Characters</span>  
All letters should default to uppercase.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/autocapitalize](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/autocapitalize "The autocapitalize global attribute is an enumerated attribute that controls whether and how text input is automatically capitalized as it is entered/edited by the user.")

Support in all current engines.
