</div>

</div>

</div>

The <span id="attr-autocapitalize" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`autocapitalize`</span> attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="autocapitalization:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
whose states are the possible <a href="#autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:autocapitalization-hint">autocapitalization
hints</a>. The <a href="#autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:autocapitalization-hint-2">autocapitalization
hint</a> specified by the attribute's state combines with other
considerations to form the <a href="#used-autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:used-autocapitalization-hint-2">used
autocapitalization hint</a>, which informs the behavior of the user
agent. The keywords for this attribute and their state mappings are as
follows:

| Keyword | State |
|----|----|
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-off" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`off`</span> | <a href="#autocap-hint-none"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-none">None</a> |
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-none" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`none`</span> |  |
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-on" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`on`</span> | <a href="#autocap-hint-sentences"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-sentences">Sentences</a> |
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-sentences" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`sentences`</span> |  |
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-words" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`words`</span> | <a href="#autocap-hint-words"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-words">Words</a> |
| <span id="attr-autocapitalize-characters" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocapitalize" dfn-type="attr-value">`characters`</span> | <a href="#autocap-hint-characters"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-characters">Characters</a> |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* is the
<a href="#autocap-hint-default"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-default">Default</a> state, and its
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* is the
<a href="#autocap-hint-sentences"
id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-sentences-2">Sentences</a> state.

</div>

`element``.`<a href="#dom-autocapitalize"
id="dom-autocapitalize-dev"><code>autocapitalize</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns the current autocapitalization state for the element, or an
empty string if it hasn't been set. Note that for
[`input`](#the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)
elements that inherit their state from a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element, this will return the autocapitalization state of the
[`form`](#the-form-element) element, but for an element in an editable
region, this will not return the autocapitalization state of the editing
host (unless this element is, in fact, the
<a href="#editing-host" id="autocapitalization:editing-host-2">editing
host</a>).

Can be set, to set the [`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) content
attribute (and thereby change the autocapitalization behavior for the
element).

<div algorithm="">

To compute the <span id="own-autocapitalization-hint" class="dfn">own
autocapitalization hint</span> of an element `element`, run the
following steps:

1.  If the [`autocapitalize`](#attr-autocapitalize) content attribute is
    present on `element`, and its value is not the empty string, return
    the state of the attribute.

2.  If `element` is an <a href="#category-autocapitalize"
    id="autocapitalization:category-autocapitalize-2">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
    inheriting element</a> and has a non-null
    <a href="#form-owner" id="autocapitalization:form-owner">form owner</a>,
    return the <a href="#own-autocapitalization-hint"
    id="autocapitalization:own-autocapitalization-hint">own
    autocapitalization hint</a> of `element`'s
    <a href="#form-owner" id="autocapitalization:form-owner-2">form
    owner</a>.

3.  Return <a href="#autocap-hint-default"
    id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-default-2">Default</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-autocapitalize" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`autocapitalize`</span> getter steps are to:

1.  Let `state` be the <a href="#own-autocapitalization-hint"
    id="autocapitalization:own-autocapitalization-hint-2">own
    autocapitalization hint</a> of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="autocapitalization:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

2.  If `state` is <a href="#autocap-hint-default"
    id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-default-3">Default</a>, then
    return the empty string.

3.  If `state` is <a href="#autocap-hint-none"
    id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-none-2">None</a>, then return
    "[`none`](#attr-autocapitalize-none)".

4.  If `state` is <a href="#autocap-hint-sentences"
    id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-sentences-3">Sentences</a>, then
    return "[`sentences`](#attr-autocapitalize-sentences)".

5.  Return the keyword value corresponding to `state`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

User agents that support customizable autocapitalization behavior for a
text input method and wish to allow web developers to control this
functionality should, during text input into an element, compute the
<span id="used-autocapitalization-hint" class="dfn">used
autocapitalization hint</span> for the element. This will be an
<a href="#autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:autocapitalization-hint-3">autocapitalization
hint</a> that describes the recommended autocapitalization behavior for
text input into the element.

User agents or input methods may choose to ignore or override the
<a href="#used-autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:used-autocapitalization-hint-3">used
autocapitalization hint</a> in certain circumstances.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#used-autocapitalization-hint"
id="autocapitalization:used-autocapitalization-hint-4">used
autocapitalization hint</a> for an element `element` is computed using
the following algorithm:

1.  If `element` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the
    <a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
    id="autocapitalization:url-state-(type=url)-2">URL</a>,
    <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
    id="autocapitalization:email-state-(type=email)-2">Email</a>, or
    <a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
    id="autocapitalization:password-state-(type=password)-2">Password</a>
    states, then return <a href="#autocap-hint-default"
    id="autocapitalization:autocap-hint-default-4">Default</a>.

2.  If `element` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element or a
    [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element, then return `element`'s
    <a href="#own-autocapitalization-hint"
    id="autocapitalization:own-autocapitalization-hint-3">own
    autocapitalization hint</a>.

3.  If `element` is an
    <a href="#editing-host" id="autocapitalization:editing-host-3">editing
    host</a> or an
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
    id="autocapitalization:editable" data-x-internal="editable">editable</a>
    element, then return the <a href="#own-autocapitalization-hint"
    id="autocapitalization:own-autocapitalization-hint-4">own
    autocapitalization hint</a> of the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editing-host-of"
    id="autocapitalization:editing-host-of"
    data-x-internal="editing-host-of">editing host of</a> `element`.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="autocapitalization:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    this step is never reached, since text input only occurs in elements
    that meet one of the above criteria.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.8</span> Autocorrection<a href="#autocorrection" class="self-link"></a>

Some methods of entering text assist users by automatically correcting
misspelled words while typing, a process also known as autocorrection.
User agents can support autocorrection of editable text, either in form
controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)
elements), or in elements in an
<a href="#editing-host" id="autocorrection:editing-host">editing
host</a> (e.g., using [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable)).
Autocorrection may be accompanied by user interfaces indicating that
text is about to be autocorrected or has been autocorrected, and is
commonly performed when inserting punctuation characters, spaces, or new
paragraphs after misspelled words. The
[`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) attribute allows authors to control
such behavior.

The [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) attribute can be used on an
editing host to control autocorrection behavior for the hosted editable
region, on an [`input`](#the-input-element) or
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to control the behavior when
inserting text into that element, or on a [`form`](#the-form-element)
element to control the default behavior for all
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="autocorrection:category-autocapitalize">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting elements</a> associated with the [`form`](#the-form-element)
element.

The [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) attribute never causes
autocorrection to be enabled for [`input`](#the-input-element) elements
whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the
<a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
id="autocorrection:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>,
<a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
id="autocorrection:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a>, or
<a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
id="autocorrection:password-state-(type=password)">Password</a> states.
(This behavior is included in the <a href="#used-autocorrection-state"
id="autocorrection:used-autocorrection-state">used autocorrection
state</a> algorithm below.)

The <span id="attr-autocorrect" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`autocorrect`</span> attribute is an enumerated
attribute with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-autocorrect-on" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocorrect" dfn-type="attr-value">`on`</span> | <span id="concept-autocorrection-on" class="dfn">On</span> | The user agent is permitted to automatically correct spelling errors while the user types. Whether spelling is automatically corrected while typing left is for the user agent to decide, and may depend on the element as well as the user's preferences. |
| <span id="attr-autocorrect-off" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/autocorrect" dfn-type="attr-value">`off`</span> | <span id="concept-autocorrection-off" class="dfn">Off</span> | The user agent is not allowed to automatically correct spelling while the user types. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)*,
*[missing value default](#missing-value-default)*, and *[empty value
default](#empty-value-default)* are all the
<a href="#concept-autocorrection-on"
id="autocorrection:concept-autocorrection-on">On</a> state.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-autocorrect" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`autocorrect`</span> getter steps are: return true
if the element's <a href="#used-autocorrection-state"
id="autocorrection:used-autocorrection-state-2">used autocorrection
state</a> is <a href="#concept-autocorrection-on"
id="autocorrection:concept-autocorrection-on-2">On</a> and false if the
element's <a href="#used-autocorrection-state"
id="autocorrection:used-autocorrection-state-3">used autocorrection
state</a> is <a href="#concept-autocorrection-off"
id="autocorrection:concept-autocorrection-off">Off</a>. The setter steps
are: if the given value is true, then the element's
[`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) attribute must be set to "`on`";
otherwise it must be set to "`off`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To compute the <span id="used-autocorrection-state" class="dfn">used
autocorrection state</span> of an element `element`, run these steps:

1.  If `element` is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
    [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the
    <a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
    id="autocorrection:url-state-(type=url)-2">URL</a>,
    <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
    id="autocorrection:email-state-(type=email)-2">Email</a>, or
    <a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
    id="autocorrection:password-state-(type=password)-2">Password</a>
    states, then return <a href="#concept-autocorrection-off"
    id="autocorrection:concept-autocorrection-off-2">Off</a>.

2.  If the [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) content attribute is
    present on `element`, then return the state of the attribute.

3.  If `element` is an <a href="#category-autocapitalize"
    id="autocorrection:category-autocapitalize-2">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
    inheriting element</a> and has a non-null
    <a href="#form-owner" id="autocorrection:form-owner">form owner</a>,
    then return the state of `element`'s
    <a href="#form-owner" id="autocorrection:form-owner-2">form owner</a>'s
    [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) attribute.

4.  Return <a href="#concept-autocorrection-on"
    id="autocorrection:concept-autocorrection-on-3">On</a>.

</div>

`element` . [`autocorrect`](#dom-autocorrect)  
Returns the autocorrection behavior of the element. Note that for
<a href="#category-autocapitalize"
id="autocorrection:category-autocapitalize-3">autocapitalize-and-autocorrect
inheriting elements</a> that inherit their state from a
[`form`](#the-form-element) element, this will return the autocorrection
behavior of the [`form`](#the-form-element) element, but for an element
in an editable region, this will not return the autocorrection behavior
of the
<a href="#editing-host" id="autocorrection:editing-host-2">editing
host</a> (unless this element is, in fact, the
<a href="#editing-host" id="autocorrection:editing-host-3">editing
host</a>).

`element` . [`autocorrect`](#dom-autocorrect) = `value`  
Updates the [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) content attribute (and
thereby changes the autocorrection behavior of the element).

<div class="example">

The [`input`](#the-input-element) element in the following example would
not allow autocorrection, since it does not have an
[`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) content attribute and therefore
inherits from the [`form`](#the-form-element) element, which has an
attribute of "[`off`](#attr-autocorrect-off)". However, the
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element would allow autocorrection,
since it has an [`autocorrect`](#attr-autocorrect) content attribute
with a value of "[`on`](#attr-autocorrect-on)".

``` html
<form autocorrect="off">
 <input type="search">
 <textarea autocorrect="on"></textarea>
</form>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.8.9</span> Input modalities: the [`inputmode`](#attr-inputmode) attribute<a href="#input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute"
class="self-link"></a>

form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)

id="input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute:editing-host">editing
host</a> (e.g., using [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable)).

The <span id="attr-inputmode" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`inputmode`</span> content attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> that specifies what kind of input mechanism would be most
helpful for users entering content.

| Keyword | Description |
|----|----|
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-none" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`none`</span> | The user agent should not display a virtual keyboard. This keyword is useful for content that renders its own keyboard control. |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-text" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`text`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale. |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-tel" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`tel`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of telephone number input. This should including keys for the digits 0 to 9, the "#" character, and the "\*" character. In some locales, this can also include alphabetic mnemonic labels (e.g., in the US, the key labeled "2" is historically also labeled with the letters A, B, and C). |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-url" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`url`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale, with keys for aiding in the input of <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute:url"
data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>, such as that for the "/" and "." characters and for quick input of strings commonly found in domain names such as "www." or ".com". |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-email" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`email`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale, with keys for aiding in the input of email addresses, such as that for the "@" character and the "." character. |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-numeric" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`numeric`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of numeric input. This keyword is useful for PIN entry. |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-decimal" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`decimal`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of fractional numeric input. Numeric keys and the format separator for the locale should be shown. |
| <span id="attr-inputmode-keyword-search" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/inputmode" dfn-type="attr-value">`search`</span> | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard optimized for search. |

The <span id="attr-enterkeyhint" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global"
dfn-type="element-attr">`enterkeyhint`</span> content attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="input-modalities:-the-enterkeyhint-attribute:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> that specifies what action label (or icon) to present for
the enter key on virtual keyboards. This allows authors to customize the
presentation of the enter key in order to make it more helpful for

| Keyword | Description |
|----|----|
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-enter" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`enter`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'enter', typically inserting a new line. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-done" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`done`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'done', typically meaning there is nothing more to input and the input method editor (IME) will be closed. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-go" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`go`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'go', typically meaning to take the user to the target of the text they typed. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-next" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`next`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'next', typically taking the user to the next field that will accept text. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-previous" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`previous`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'previous', typically taking the user to the previous field that will accept text. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-search" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`search`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'search', typically taking the user to the results of searching for the text they have typed. |
| <span id="attr-enterkeyhint-keyword-send" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/enterkeyhint" dfn-type="attr-value">`send`</span> | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'send', typically delivering the text to its target. |

### <span class="secno">6.9</span> Find-in-page<a href="#find-in-page" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">6.9.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-10" class="self-link"></a>

This section defines <span id="find-in-page-2"
class="dfn">find-in-page</span> — a common user-agent mechanism which
allows users to search through the contents of the page for particular
information.

Access to the <a href="#find-in-page-2"
id="introduction-10:find-in-page-2">find-in-page</a> feature is provided
via a <span id="find-in-page-interface" class="dfn">find-in-page
interface</span>. This is a user-agent provided user interface, which
allows the user to specify input and the parameters of the search. This
interface can appear as a result of a shortcut or a menu selection.

A combination of text input and settings in the
<a href="#find-in-page-interface"
id="introduction-10:find-in-page-interface">find-in-page interface</a>
represents the user <span id="fip-query" class="dfn">query</span>. This
typically includes the text that the user wants to search for, as well
as optional settings (e.g., the ability to restrict the search to whole
words only).

The user-agent processes page contents for a given
<a href="#fip-query" id="introduction-10:fip-query">query</a>, and
identifies zero or more <span id="fip-matches"
class="dfn">matches</span>, which are content ranges that satisfy the
user <a href="#fip-query" id="introduction-10:fip-query-2">query</a>.

One of the
<a href="#fip-matches" id="introduction-10:fip-matches">matches</a> is
identified to the user as the <span id="fip-active-match"
class="dfn">active match</span>. It is highlighted and scrolled into
view. The user can navigate through the
<a href="#fip-matches" id="introduction-10:fip-matches-2">matches</a> by
advancing the
<a href="#fip-active-match" id="introduction-10:fip-active-match">active
match</a> using the <a href="#find-in-page-interface"
id="introduction-10:find-in-page-interface-2">find-in-page interface</a>.

[Issue \#3539](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3539) tracks
standardizing how <a href="#find-in-page-2"
id="introduction-10:find-in-page-2-2">find-in-page</a> underlies the
currently-unspecified `window.find()` API.

#### <span class="secno">6.9.2</span> Interaction with [`details`](#the-details-element) and [`hidden=until-found`](#attr-hidden-until-found-state)<a href="#interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found"
class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When find-in-page begins searching for matches, all
[`details`](#the-details-element) elements in the page which do not have
their [`open`](#attr-details-open) attribute set should have the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#skips-its-contents"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:skips-its-contents"
data-x-internal="skips-its-contents">skipped contents</a> of their
second slot become accessible, without modifying the
[`open`](#attr-details-open) attribute, in order to make find-in-page
able to search through it. Similarly, all HTML elements with the
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:attr-hidden-until-found-state-2">Hidden
Until Found</a> state should have their
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#skips-its-contents"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:skips-its-contents-2"
data-x-internal="skips-its-contents">skipped contents</a> become
accessible without modifying the [`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in
order to make find-in-page able to search through them. After
find-in-page finishes searching for matches, the
[`details`](#the-details-element) elements and the elements with the
[`hidden`](#attr-hidden) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-hidden-until-found-state"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:attr-hidden-until-found-state-3">Hidden
Until Found</a> state should have their contents become skipped again.
This entire process must happen synchronously (and so is not observable
to users or to author code). [\[CSSCONTAIN\]](#refsCSSCONTAIN)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When find-in-page chooses a new <a href="#fip-active-match"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:fip-active-match">active
match</a>, perform the following steps:

1.  Let `node` be the first node in the <a href="#fip-active-match"
    id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:fip-active-match-2">active
    match</a>.

2.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:queue-a-global-task">Queue
    a global task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
    id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:user-interaction-task-source">user
    interaction task source</a> given `node`'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:concept-relevant-global">relevant
    global object</a> to run the <a href="#ancestor-revealing-algorithm"
    id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:ancestor-revealing-algorithm">ancestor
    revealing algorithm</a> on `node`.

</div>

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:tracking-vector"
class="tracking-vector" data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> When find-in-page auto-expands
a [`details`](#the-details-element) element like this, it will fire a
[`toggle`](#event-toggle) event. As with the separate
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#eventdef-document-scroll"
data-x-internal="event-scroll"><code
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:event-scroll">scroll</code></a>
event that find-in-page fires, this event could be used by the page to
discover what the user is typing into the find-in-page dialog. If the
page creates a tiny scrollable area with the current search term and
every possible next character the user could type separated by a gap,
and observes which one the browser scrolls to, it can add that character
to the search term and update the scrollable area to incrementally build
the search term. By wrapping each possible next match in a closed
[`details`](#the-details-element) element, the page could listen to
[`toggle`](#event-toggle) events instead of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#eventdef-document-scroll"
data-x-internal="event-scroll"><code
id="interaction-with-details-and-hidden=until-found:event-scroll-2">scroll</code></a>
events. This attack could be addressed for both events by not acting on
every character the user types into the find-in-page dialog.

#### <span class="secno">6.9.3</span> Interaction with selection<a href="#interaction-with-selection" class="self-link"></a>

The find-in-page process is invoked in the context of a document, and
may have an effect on the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dfn-selection"
id="interaction-with-selection:document-selection"
data-x-internal="document-selection">selection</a> of that document.
Specifically, the range that defines the <a href="#fip-active-match"
id="interaction-with-selection:fip-active-match">active match</a> can
dictate the current selection. These selection updates, however, can
happen at different times during the find-in-page process (e.g. upon the
<a href="#find-in-page-interface"
id="interaction-with-selection:find-in-page-interface">find-in-page
interface</a> dismissal or upon a change in the
<a href="#fip-active-match"
id="interaction-with-selection:fip-active-match-2">active match</a>
range).

### <span class="secno">6.10</span> Close requests and close watchers<a href="#close-requests-and-close-watchers" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">6.10.1</span> Close requests<a href="#close-requests" class="self-link"></a>

In an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="close-requests:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> (and
likely device-specific) manner, a user can send a
<span id="close-request" class="dfn" export="">close request</span> to
the user agent. This indicates that the user wishes to close something
that is currently being shown on the screen, such as a popover, menu,
dialog, picker, or display mode.

<div class="example">

Some example close requests are:

- The <span class="kbd">Esc</span> key on desktop platforms.

- The back button or gesture on certain mobile platforms such as
  Android.

- Any assistive technology's dismiss gesture, such as iOS VoiceOver's
  two-finger scrub "z" gesture.

- A game controller's canonical "back" button, such as the circle button
  on a DualShock gamepad.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever the user agent receives a potential close request targeted at a
[`Document`](#document) `document`, it must
<a href="#queue-a-global-task"
id="close-requests:queue-a-global-task">queue a global task</a> on the
<a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="close-requests:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction task
source</a> given `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="close-requests:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a>
to perform the following <span id="close-request-steps" class="dfn"
export="">close request steps</span>:

1.  If `document`'s
    <a href="https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#fullscreen-element"
    id="close-requests:fullscreen-element"
    data-x-internal="fullscreen-element">fullscreen element</a> is not
    null, then:

    1.  <a href="https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#fully-exit-fullscreen"
        id="close-requests:fully-exit-fullscreen"
        data-x-internal="fully-exit-fullscreen">Fully exit fullscreen</a>
        given `document`'s
        <a href="#node-navigable" id="close-requests:node-navigable">node
        navigable</a>'s
        <a href="#nav-top" id="close-requests:nav-top">top-level traversable</a>'s
        <a href="#nav-document" id="close-requests:nav-document">active
        document</a>.

    2.  Return.

    This does *not* fire any relevant event, such as
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
    data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
    id="close-requests:event-keydown">keydown</code></a>; it only causes
    <a
    href="https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#eventdef-document-fullscreenchange"
    data-x-internal="event-fullscreenchange"><code
    id="close-requests:event-fullscreenchange">fullscreenchange</code></a>
    to be eventually fired.

2.  Optionally, skip to the step labeled [alternative
    processing](#close-request-fallback).

    For example, if the user agent detects user frustration at repeated
    close request interception by the current web page, it might take
    this path.

3.  Fire any relevant events, per UI Events or other relevant
    specifications. [\[UIEVENTS\]](#refsUIEVENTS)

    An example of a relevant event in the UI Events model would be the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
    data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
    id="close-requests:event-keydown-2">keydown</code></a> event that UI
    Events
    [suggests](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#events-keyboard-event-order)
    firing when the user presses the <span class="kbd">Esc</span> key on
    their keyboard. On most platforms with keyboards, this is treated as
    a <a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request">close
    request</a>, and so would trigger these
    <a href="#close-request-steps"
    id="close-requests:close-request-steps">close request steps</a>.

    An example of relevant events that are outside of the model given in
    UI Events would be assistive technology synthesizing an
    <span class="kbd">Esc</span>
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
    data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
    id="close-requests:event-keydown-3">keydown</code></a> event when
    the user sends a
    <a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request-2">close
    request</a> by using a dismiss gesture.

4.  Let `event` be null if no such events are fired, or the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-event"
    data-x-internal="event"><code id="close-requests:event">Event</code></a>
    object representing one of the fired events otherwise. If multiple
    events are fired, which one is chosen is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="close-requests:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>.

5.  If `event` is not null, and its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="close-requests:canceled-flag"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a> is set, then
    return.

6.  If `document` is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="close-requests:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return.

    This step is necessary because, if `event` is not null, then an
    event listener might have caused `document` to no longer be
    <a href="#fully-active" id="close-requests:fully-active-2">fully
    active</a>.

7.  Let `closedSomething` be the result of
    <a href="#process-close-watchers"
    id="close-requests:process-close-watchers">processing close watchers</a>
    on `document`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="close-requests:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global object</a>.

8.  If `closedSomething` is true, then return.

9.  <div id="close-request-fallback">

    *Alternative processing*: Otherwise, there was nothing watching for
    a <a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request-3">close
    request</a>. The user agent may instead interpret this interaction
    as some other action, instead of interpreting it as a close request.

    </div>

</div>

On platforms where pressing the <span class="kbd">Esc</span> key is
interpreted as a
<a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request-4">close
request</a>, the user agent must interpret the key being pressed *down*
as the close request, instead of the key being released. Thus, in the
above algorithm, the "relevant events" that are fired must be the single
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
id="close-requests:event-keydown-4">keydown</code></a> event.

On platforms where <span class="kbd">Esc</span> is the
<a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request-5">close
request</a>, the user agent will first fire an appropriately-initialized
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown"
data-x-internal="event-keydown"><code
id="close-requests:event-keydown-5">keydown</code></a> event. If the web
developer cancels the event by calling
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-preventdefault"
data-x-internal="dom-event-preventdefault"><code
id="close-requests:dom-event-preventdefault">preventDefault()</code></a>,
then nothing further happens. But if the event fires without being
canceled, then the user agent proceeds to
<a href="#process-close-watchers"
id="close-requests:process-close-watchers-2">process close watchers</a>.

On platforms where a back button is a potential
<a href="#close-request" id="close-requests:close-request-6">close
request</a>, no event is involved, so when the back button is pressed,
the user agent proceeds directly to <a href="#process-close-watchers"
id="close-requests:process-close-watchers-3">process close watchers</a>.
If there is an <a href="#close-watcher-active"
id="close-requests:close-watcher-active">active</a>
<a href="#close-watcher" id="close-requests:close-watcher">close
watcher</a>, then that will get triggered. If there is not, then the
user agent can interpret the back button press in another way, for
example as a request to <a href="#traverse-the-history-by-a-delta"
id="close-requests:traverse-the-history-by-a-delta">traverse the history
by a delta</a> of −1.

#### <span class="secno">6.10.2</span> Close watcher infrastructure<a href="#close-watcher-infrastructure" class="self-link"></a>

Each [`Window`](#window) has a <span id="close-watcher-manager"
class="dfn">close watcher manager</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:struct"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> with the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:struct-item"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

- <span id="close-watcher-manager-groups" class="dfn">Groups</span>, a
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
  id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a>
  of <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
  id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-2"
  data-x-internal="list">lists</a> of <a href="#close-watcher"
  id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher">close watchers</a>,
  initially empty.

- <span id="close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
  class="dfn">Allowed number of groups</span>, a number, initially 1.

- <span id="close-watcher-manager-next" class="dfn">Next user
  interaction allows a new group</span>, a boolean, initially true.

Most of the complexity of the <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager">close watcher
manager</a> comes from anti-abuse protections designed to prevent
developers from disabling users' history traversal abilities, for
platforms where a <a href="#close-request"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-request">close request</a>'s
[fallback action](#close-request-fallback) is the main mechanism of
history traversal. In particular:

The grouping of <a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-2">close watchers</a> is
designed so that if multiple close watchers are created without
<a href="#history-action-activation"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:history-action-activation">history-action
activation</a>, they are grouped together, so that a user-triggered
<a href="#close-request"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-request-2">close request</a> will
close all of the close watchers in a group. This ensures that web
developers can't intercept an unlimited number of close requests by
creating close watchers; instead they can create a number equal to at
most 1 + the number of times the <a href="#tracking-user-activation"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:tracking-user-activation">user
activates the page</a>.

The <a href="#close-watcher-manager-next"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-next">next user
interaction allows a new group</a> boolean encourages web developers to
create <a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-3">close watchers</a> in
a way that is tied to individual <a href="#tracking-user-activation"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:tracking-user-activation-2">user
activations</a>. Without it, each user activation would increase the
<a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups">allowed
number of groups</a>, even if the web developer isn't "using" those user
activations to create close watchers. In short:

- Allowed: user interaction; create a close watcher in its own group;
  user interaction; create a close watcher in a second independent
  group.

- Disallowed: user interaction; user interaction; create a close watcher
  in its own group; create a close watcher in a second independent
  group.

- Allowed: user interaction; user interaction; create a close watcher in
  its own group; create a close watcher grouped with the previous one.

This protection is *not* important for upholding our desired invariant
of creating at most (1 + the number of times the
<a href="#tracking-user-activation"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:tracking-user-activation-3">user
activates the page</a>) groups. A determined abuser will just create one
close watcher per user interaction, "banking" them for future abuse. But
this system causes more predictable behavior for the normal case, and
encourages non-abusive developers to create close watchers directly in
response to user interactions.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="notify-the-close-watcher-manager-about-user-activation"
class="dfn">notify the close watcher manager about user
activation</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `window`:

1.  Let `manager` be `window`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-2">close watcher
    manager</a>.

2.  If `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-next"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-next-2">next user
    interaction allows a new group</a> is true, then increment
    `manager`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups-2">allowed
    number of groups</a>.

3.  Set `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-next"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-next-3">next user
    interaction allows a new group</a> to false.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A <span id="close-watcher" class="dfn" export="">close watcher</span> is
a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:struct-2"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> with the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:struct-item-2"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

- A <span id="close-watcher-window" class="dfn">window</span>, a
  [`Window`](#window).

- A <span id="close-watcher-cancel-action" class="dfn">cancel
  action</span>, an algorithm accepting a boolean argument and returning
  a boolean. The argument indicates whether or not the cancel action
  algorithm can prevent the close request from proceeding via the
  algorithm's return value. If the boolean argument is true, then the
  algorithm can return either true to indicate that the caller will
  proceed to the <a href="#close-watcher-close-action"
  id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-close-action">close
  action</a>, or false to indicate that the caller will bail out. If the
  argument is false, then the return value is always false. This
  algorithm can never throw an exception.

- A <span id="close-watcher-close-action" class="dfn">close
  action</span>, an algorithm accepting no arguments and returning
  nothing. This algorithm can never throw an exception.

- An <span id="close-watcher-is-running-cancel" class="dfn">is running
  cancel action</span> boolean.

- A <span id="close-watcher-get-enabled-state" class="dfn">get enabled
  state</span>, an algorithm accepting no arguments and returning a
  boolean. This algorithm can never throw an exception.

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-4">close watcher</a>
`closeWatcher` <span id="close-watcher-active" class="dfn">is
active</span> if `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-window"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-window">window</a>'s
<a href="#close-watcher-manager"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-3">close watcher
manager</a> <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-contains"
data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> any list which
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-contains-2"
data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> `closeWatcher`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="establish-a-close-watcher" class="dfn">establish a close
watcher</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `window`, a list of steps
<span id="create-close-watcher-cancelaction"
class="dfn">`cancelAction`</span>, a list of steps
<span id="create-close-watcher-closeaction"
class="dfn">`closeAction`</span>, and an algorithm that returns a
boolean <span id="create-close-watcher-getenabledstate"
class="dfn">`getEnabledState`</span>:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:assert"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `window`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> is <a href="#fully-active"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:fully-active">fully active</a>.

2.  Let `closeWatcher` be a new <a href="#close-watcher"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-5">close watcher</a>,
    with

    <a href="#close-watcher-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-window-2">window</a>  
    `window`

    <a href="#close-watcher-cancel-action"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-cancel-action">cancel
    action</a>  
    `cancelAction`

    <a href="#close-watcher-close-action"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-close-action-2">close
    action</a>  
    `closeAction`

    <a href="#close-watcher-is-running-cancel"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-is-running-cancel">is
    running cancel action</a>  
    false

    <a href="#close-watcher-get-enabled-state"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-get-enabled-state">get
    enabled state</a>  
    `getEnabledState`

3.  Let `manager` be `window`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-4">close watcher
    manager</a>.

4.  If `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups">groups</a>'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-size"
    data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is less than `manager`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups-3">allowed
    number of groups</a>, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-append"
    data-x-internal="list-append">append</a> « `closeWatcher` » to
    `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-2">groups</a>.

5.  Otherwise:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:assert-2"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `manager`'s
        <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-3">groups</a>'s
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-size-2"
        data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is at least 1 in this
        branch, since `manager`'s
        <a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups-4">allowed
        number of groups</a> is always at least 1.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-append-2"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `closeWatcher` to
        `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-4">groups</a>'s
        last <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-item"
        data-x-internal="list-item">item</a>.

6.  Set `manager`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-next"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-next-4">next user
    interaction allows a new group</a> to true.

7.  Return `closeWatcher`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="close-watcher-request-close" class="dfn">request to
close</span> a <a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-6">close watcher</a>
`closeWatcher` with boolean `requireHistoryActionActivation`:

1.  If `closeWatcher` <a href="#close-watcher-active"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-active">is not active</a>,
    then return true.

2.  If the result of running `closeWatcher`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-get-enabled-state"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-get-enabled-state-2">get
    enabled state</a> is false, then return true.

3.  If `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-is-running-cancel"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-is-running-cancel-2">is
    running cancel action</a> is true, then return true.

4.  Let `window` be `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-window-3">window</a>.

5.  If `window`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:concept-document-window-2">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> is not <a href="#fully-active"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:fully-active-2">fully active</a>,
    then return true.

6.  Let `canPreventClose` be true if `requireHistoryActionActivation` is
    false, or if `window`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-5">close watcher
    manager</a>'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-5">groups</a>'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-size-3"
    data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is less than `window`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-6">close watcher
    manager</a>'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups-5">allowed
    number of groups</a>, and `window` has
    <a href="#history-action-activation"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:history-action-activation-2">history-action
    activation</a>; otherwise false.

7.  Set `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-is-running-cancel"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-is-running-cancel-3">is
    running cancel action</a> to true.

8.  Let `shouldContinue` be the result of running `closeWatcher`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-cancel-action"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-cancel-action-2">cancel
    action</a> given `canPreventClose`.

9.  Set `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-is-running-cancel"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-is-running-cancel-4">is
    running cancel action</a> to false.

10. If `shouldContinue` is false, then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:assert-3"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `canPreventClose` is true.

    2.  <a href="#consume-history-action-user-activation"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:consume-history-action-user-activation">Consume
        history-action user activation</a> given `window`.

    3.  Return false.

    Note that since these substeps
    <a href="#consume-history-action-user-activation"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:consume-history-action-user-activation-2">consume
    history-action user activation</a>,
    <a href="#close-watcher-request-close"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-request-close">requesting
    to close</a> a <a href="#close-watcher"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-7">close watcher</a>
    twice without any intervening <a href="#tracking-user-activation"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:tracking-user-activation-4">user
    activation</a> will result in `canPreventClose` being false the
    second time.

11. <a href="#close-watcher-close"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-close">Close</a>
    `closeWatcher`.

12. Return true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="close-watcher-close" class="dfn">close</span> a
<a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-8">close watcher</a>
`closeWatcher`:

1.  If `closeWatcher` <a href="#close-watcher-active"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-active-2">is not
    active</a>, then return.

2.  If the result of running `closeWatcher`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-get-enabled-state"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-get-enabled-state-3">get
    enabled state</a> is false, then return.

3.  If `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-window-4">window</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:concept-document-window-3">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> is not <a href="#fully-active"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:fully-active-3">fully active</a>,
    then return.

4.  <a href="#close-watcher-destroy"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-destroy">Destroy</a>
    `closeWatcher`.

5.  Run `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-close-action"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-close-action-3">close
    action</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="close-watcher-destroy" class="dfn">destroy</span> a
<a href="#close-watcher"
id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-9">close watcher</a>
`closeWatcher`:

1.  Let `manager` be `closeWatcher`'s <a href="#close-watcher-window"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-window-5">window</a>'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-7">close watcher
    manager</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `group` of `manager`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-6">groups</a>:
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">remove</a> `closeWatcher` from
    `group`.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> any item from `manager`'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-7">groups</a>
    that <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">is empty</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="process-close-watchers" class="dfn">process close
watchers</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `window`:

1.  Let `processedACloseWatcher` be false.

2.  If `window`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-8">close watcher
    manager</a>'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-8">groups</a>
    is not empty:

    1.  Let `group` be the last
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-item-2"
        data-x-internal="list-item">item</a> in `window`'s
        <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-9">close watcher
        manager</a>'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager-groups"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-groups-9">groups</a>.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="close-watcher-infrastructure:list-iterate-2"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `closeWatcher` of
        `group`, in reverse order:

        1.  If the result of running `closeWatcher`'s
            <a href="#close-watcher-get-enabled-state"
            id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-get-enabled-state-4">get
            enabled state</a> is true, set `processedACloseWatcher` to
            true.

        2.  Let `shouldProceed` be the result of
            <a href="#close-watcher-request-close"
            id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-request-close-2">requesting
            to close</a> `closeWatcher` with true.

        3.  If `shouldProceed` is false, then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break"
            id="close-watcher-infrastructure:break"
            data-x-internal="break">break</a>.

3.  If `window`'s <a href="#close-watcher-manager"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-10">close watcher
    manager</a>'s
    <a href="#close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups"
    id="close-watcher-infrastructure:close-watcher-manager-allowed-number-of-groups-6">allowed
    number of groups</a> is greater than 1, decrement it by 1.

4.  Return `processedACloseWatcher`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.10.3</span> The [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) interface<a href="#the-closewatcher-interface" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CloseWatcher : EventTarget {
  constructor(optional CloseWatcherOptions options = {});

  undefined requestClose();
  undefined close();
  undefined destroy();

  attribute EventHandler oncancel;
  attribute EventHandler onclose;
};

dictionary CloseWatcherOptions {
  AbortSignal signal;
};
```

`watcher`` = new `<a href="#dom-closewatcher"
id="dom-closewatcher-dev"><code>CloseWatcher</code></a>`()`  
`watcher`` = new `<a href="#dom-closewatcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:dom-closewatcher-2"><code>CloseWatcher</code></a>`({ `<a href="#dom-closewatcheroptions-signal"
id="dom-closewatcheroptions-signal-dev"><code>signal</code></a>` })`  
Creates a new [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) instance.

If the [`signal`](#dom-closewatcheroptions-signal) option is provided,
then `watcher` can be destroyed (as if by
[`watcher.destroy()`](#dom-closewatcher-destroy)) by aborting the given
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#abortsignal"
data-x-internal="abortsignal"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:abortsignal-2">AbortSignal</code></a>.

If any <a href="#close-watcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-watcher">close watcher</a> is
already active, and the [`Window`](#window) does not have
<a href="#history-action-activation"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:history-action-activation">history-action
activation</a>, then the resulting [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) will
be closed together with that already-active <a href="#close-watcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-watcher-2">close watcher</a> in
response to any <a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request">close request</a>. (This
already-active <a href="#close-watcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-watcher-3">close watcher</a> does
not necessarily have to be a [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) object; it
could be a modal [`dialog`](#the-dialog-element) element, or a popover
generated by an element with the [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute.)

`watcher``.`<a href="#dom-closewatcher-requestclose"
id="dom-closewatcher-requestclose-dev"><code>requestClose</code></a>`()`  
Acts as if a <a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request-2">close request</a> was
sent targeting `watcher`, by first firing a [`cancel`](#event-cancel)
event, and if that event is not canceled with
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-preventdefault"
data-x-internal="dom-event-preventdefault"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:dom-event-preventdefault">preventDefault()</code></a>,
proceeding to fire a [`close`](#event-close) event before deactivating
the close watcher as if [`watcher.destroy()`](#dom-closewatcher-destroy)
was called.

This is a helper utility that can be used to consolidate cancelation and
closing logic into the [`cancel`](#event-cancel) and
[`close`](#event-close) event handlers, by having all
non-<a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request-3">close request</a>
closing affordances call this method.

`watcher``.`<a href="#dom-closewatcher-close"
id="dom-closewatcher-close-dev"><code>close</code></a>`()`  
Immediately fires the [`close`](#event-close) event, and then
deactivates the close watcher as if
[`watcher.destroy()`](#dom-closewatcher-destroy) was called.

This is a helper utility that can be used trigger the closing logic into
the [`close`](#event-close) event handler, skipping any logic in the
[`cancel`](#event-cancel) event handler.

`watcher``.`<a href="#dom-closewatcher-destroy"
id="dom-closewatcher-destroy-dev"><code>destroy</code></a>`()`  
Deactivates `watcher`, so that it will no longer receive
[`close`](#event-close) events and so that new independent
[`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) instances can be constructed.

This is intended to be called if the relevant UI element is torn down in
some other way than being closed.

Each [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) instance has an
<span id="internal-close-watcher" class="dfn">internal close
watcher</span>, which is a <a href="#close-watcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-watcher-4">close watcher</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-closewatcher"
class="dfn">`new CloseWatcher(``options``)`</span> constructor steps
are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> is not <a href="#fully-active"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:fully-active">fully active</a>, then
    throw an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:invalidstateerror"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  Let `closeWatcher` be the result of
    <a href="#establish-a-close-watcher"

    id="the-closewatcher-interface:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-closewatcher-interface:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant
    global object</a>, with:

    - *[cancelAction](#create-close-watcher-cancelaction)* given

      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
