The following are the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-handlers">event handlers</a> (and
their corresponding <a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-handler-event-type">event handler
event types</a>) that must be supported, as
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-handler-idl-attributes">event
handler IDL attributes</a>, by all objects implementing the
[`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) interface:

| <a href="#event-handlers"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-handlers-2">Event handler</a> | <a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-handler-event-type-2">Event handler
event type</a> |
|----|----|
| <span id="handler-closewatcher-oncancel" class="dfn" dfn-for="CloseWatcher" dfn-type="attribute">`oncancel`</span> | [`cancel`](#event-cancel) |
| <span id="handler-closewatcher-onclose" class="dfn" dfn-for="CloseWatcher" dfn-type="attribute">`onclose`</span> | [`close`](#event-close) |

<div id="example-CloseWatcher-basic" class="example">

<a href="#example-CloseWatcher-basic" class="self-link"></a>

If one wanted to implement a custom picker control, which closed itself
on a user-provided <a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request-4">close request</a> as
well as when a close button is pressed, the following code shows how one
would use the [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) API to process close
requests:

``` js
const watcher = new CloseWatcher();
const picker = setUpAndShowPickerDOMElement();

let chosenValue = null;

watcher.onclose = () => {
  chosenValue = picker.querySelector('input').value;
  picker.remove();
};

picker.querySelector('.close-button').onclick = () => watcher.requestClose();
```

Note how the logic to gather the chosen value is centralized in the
[`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) object's [`close`](#event-close) event
handler, with the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-click">click</code></a> event
handler for the close button delegating to that logic by calling
[`requestClose()`](#dom-closewatcher-requestclose).

</div>

<div id="example-CloseWatcher-cancel" class="example">

<a href="#example-CloseWatcher-cancel" class="self-link"></a>

The [`cancel`](#event-cancel) event on [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher)
objects can be used to prevent the [`close`](#event-close) event from
firing, and the [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) from being destroying. A
typical use case is as follows:

``` js
watcher.oncancel = async (e) => {
  if (hasUnsavedData && e.cancelable) {
    e.preventDefault();

    const userReallyWantsToClose = await askForConfirmation("Are you sure you want to close?");
    if (userReallyWantsToClose) {
      hasUnsavedData = false;
      watcher.close();
    }
  }
};
```

For abuse prevention purposes, this event is only
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:dom-event-cancelable-2">cancelable</code></a>
if the page has <a href="#history-action-activation"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:history-action-activation-2">history-action
activation</a>, which will be lost after any given
<a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request-5">close request</a>. This
ensures that if the user sends a close request twice in a row without
any intervening user activation, the request definitely succeeds; the
second request ignores any [`cancel`](#event-cancel) event handler's
attempt to call
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-preventdefault"
data-x-internal="dom-event-preventdefault"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:dom-event-preventdefault-2">preventDefault()</code></a>
and proceeds to close the [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher).

</div>

Combined, the above two examples show how
[`requestClose()`](#dom-closewatcher-requestclose) and
[`close()`](#dom-closewatcher-close) differ. Because we used
[`requestClose()`](#dom-closewatcher-requestclose) in the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="the-closewatcher-interface:event-click-2">click</code></a> event
handler for the close button, clicking that button will trigger the
[`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher)'s [`cancel`](#event-cancel) event, and
thus potentially ask the user for confirmation if there is unsaved data.
If we had used [`close()`](#dom-closewatcher-close), then this check
would be skipped. Sometimes that is appropriate, but usually
[`requestClose()`](#dom-closewatcher-requestclose) is the better option
for user-triggered close requests.

<div id="example-CloseWatcher-grouping" class="example">

<a href="#example-CloseWatcher-grouping" class="self-link"></a>

In addition to the <a href="#tracking-user-activation"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:tracking-user-activation">user
activation</a> restrictions for [`cancel`](#event-cancel) events, there
is a more subtle form of user activation gating for
[`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) construction. If one creates more than
one [`CloseWatcher`](#closewatcher) without user activation, then the
newly-created one will get grouped together with the
most-recently-created <a href="#close-watcher"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-watcher-5">close watcher</a>, so
that a single <a href="#close-request"
id="the-closewatcher-interface:close-request-6">close request</a> will
close them both:

``` js
window.onload = () => {
  // This will work as normal: it is the first close watcher created without user activation.
  (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
};

button1.onclick = () => {
  // This will work as normal: the button click counts as user activation.
  (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
};

button2.onclick = () => {
  // These will be grouped together, and both will close in response to a single close request.
  (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
  (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
};
```

This means that calling [`destroy()`](#dom-closewatcher-destroy),
[`close()`](#dom-closewatcher-close), or
[`requestClose()`](#dom-closewatcher-requestclose) properly is
important. Doing so is the only way to get back the "free" ungrouped
close watcher slot. Such close watchers created without user activation
are useful for cases like session inactivity timeout dialogs or urgent
notifications of server-triggered events, which are not generated in
response to user activation.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.11</span> <span class="dfn">Drag and drop</span><a href="#dnd" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTML_Drag_and_Drop_API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTML_Drag_and_Drop_API "HTML Drag and Drop interfaces enable applications to use drag-and-drop features in browsers.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox3.5+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari3.1+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome4+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)18</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer5.5+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android yes">Firefox
Android4+</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS2+</span><span class="chrome_android yes">Chrome
Android18+</span><span class="webview_android yes">WebView
Android4.4+</span><span class="samsunginternet_android yes">Samsung
Internet1.5+</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android14+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

This section defines an event-based drag-and-drop mechanism.

This specification does not define exactly what a *drag-and-drop
operation* actually is.

On a visual medium with a pointing device, a drag operation could be the
default action of a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown"
data-x-internal="event-mousedown"><code
id="dnd:event-mousedown">mousedown</code></a> event that is followed by
a series of <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousemove"
data-x-internal="event-mousemove"><code
id="dnd:event-mousemove">mousemove</code></a> events, and the drop could
be triggered by the mouse being released.

When using an input modality other than a pointing device, users would
probably have to explicitly indicate their intention to perform a
drag-and-drop operation, stating what they wish to drag and where they
wish to drop it, respectively.

However it is implemented, drag-and-drop operations must have a starting
point (e.g. where the mouse was clicked, or the start of the selection
or element that was selected for the drag), may have any number of
intermediate steps (elements that the mouse moves over during a drag, or
elements that the user picks as possible drop points as they cycle
through possibilities), and must either have an end point (the element
above which the mouse button was released, or the element that was
finally selected), or be canceled. The end point must be the last
element selected as a possible drop point before the drop occurs (so if
the operation is not canceled, there must be at least one element in the
middle step).

#### <span class="secno">6.11.1</span> Introduction<a href="#event-drag" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

To make an element draggable, give the element a
[`draggable`](#attr-draggable) attribute, and set an event listener for
[`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart) that stores the data being dragged.

The event handler typically needs to check that it's not a text
selection that is being dragged, and then needs to store data into the
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object and set the allowed effects
(copy, move, link, or some combination).

For example:

``` html
<p>What fruits do you like?</p>
<ol ondragstart="dragStartHandler(event)">
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-apple">Apples</li>
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-orange">Oranges</li>
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-pear">Pears</li>
</ol>
<script>
  var internalDNDType = 'text/x-example'; // set this to something specific to your site
  function dragStartHandler(event) {
    if (event.target instanceof HTMLLIElement) {
      // use the element's data-value="" attribute as the value to be moving:
      event.dataTransfer.setData(internalDNDType, event.target.dataset.value);
      event.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move'; // only allow moves
    } else {
      event.preventDefault(); // don't allow selection to be dragged
    }
  }
</script>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

To accept a drop, the drop target has to listen to the following events:

1.  The [`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) event handler reports
    whether or not the drop target is potentially willing to accept the
    drop, by canceling the event.
2.  The [`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) event handler specifies what
    feedback will be shown to the user, by setting the
    [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute of the
    [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) associated with the event. This
    event also needs to be canceled.
3.  The [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) event handler has a final chance to
    accept or reject the drop. If the drop is accepted, the event
    handler must perform the drop operation on the target. This event
    needs to be canceled, so that the
    [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute's value can
    be used by the source. Otherwise, the drop operation is rejected.

For example:

``` html
<p>Drop your favorite fruits below:</p>
<ol ondragenter="dragEnterHandler(event)" ondragover="dragOverHandler(event)"
    ondrop="dropHandler(event)">
</ol>
<script>
  var internalDNDType = 'text/x-example'; // set this to something specific to your site
  function dragEnterHandler(event) {
    var items = event.dataTransfer.items;
    for (var i = 0; i < items.length; ++i) {
      var item = items[i];
      if (item.kind == 'string' && item.type == internalDNDType) {
        event.preventDefault();
        return;
      }
    }
  }
  function dragOverHandler(event) {
    event.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move';
    event.preventDefault();
  }
  function dropHandler(event) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    var data = event.dataTransfer.getData(internalDNDType);
    if (data == 'fruit-apple') {
      li.textContent = 'Apples';
    } else if (data == 'fruit-orange') {
      li.textContent = 'Oranges';
    } else if (data == 'fruit-pear') {
      li.textContent = 'Pears';
    } else {
      li.textContent = 'Unknown Fruit';
    }
    event.target.appendChild(li);
  }
</script>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

To remove the original element (the one that was dragged) from the
display, the [`dragend`](#event-dnd-dragend) event can be used.

For our example here, that means updating the original markup to handle
that event:

``` html
<p>What fruits do you like?</p>
<ol ondragstart="dragStartHandler(event)" ondragend="dragEndHandler(event)">
 ...as before...
</ol>
<script>
  function dragStartHandler(event) {
    // ...as before...
  }
  function dragEndHandler(event) {
    if (event.dataTransfer.dropEffect == 'move') {
      // remove the dragged element
      event.target.parentNode.removeChild(event.target);
    }
  }
</script>
```

#### <span class="secno">6.11.2</span> The drag data store<a href="#the-drag-data-store" class="self-link"></a>

The data that underlies a drag-and-drop operation, known as the
<span id="drag-data-store" class="dfn">drag data store</span>, consists
of the following information:

- A <span id="drag-data-store-item-list" class="dfn">drag data store
  item list</span>, which is a list of items representing the dragged
  data, each consisting of the following information:

  <span id="the-drag-data-item-kind" class="dfn">The drag data item kind</span>  
  The kind of data:

  *Text*  
  Text.

  *File*  
  Binary data with a filename.

  <span id="the-drag-data-item-type-string" class="dfn">The drag data item type string</span>  
  A Unicode string giving the type or format of the data, generally
  given by a <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
  id="the-drag-data-store:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
  type</a>. Some values that are not
  <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
  id="the-drag-data-store:mime-type-2" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
  types</a> are special-cased for legacy reasons. The API does not
  enforce the use of
  <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
  id="the-drag-data-store:mime-type-3" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
  types</a>; other values can be used as well. In all cases, however,
  the values are all
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
  id="the-drag-data-store:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
  data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
  lowercase</a> by the API.

  There is a limit of one *text* item per
  <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
  id="the-drag-data-store:the-drag-data-item-type-string">item type
  string</a>.

  The actual data  
  A Unicode or binary string, in some cases with a filename (itself a
  Unicode string), as per <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
  id="the-drag-data-store:the-drag-data-item-kind">the drag data item
  kind</a>.

  The <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
  id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-item-list">drag data store item
  list</a> is ordered in the order that the items were added to the
  list; most recently added last.

- The following information, used to generate the UI feedback during the
  drag:

  - User-agent-defined default feedback information, known as the
    <span id="drag-data-store-default-feedback" class="dfn">drag data
    store default feedback</span>.
  - Optionally, a bitmap image and the coordinate of a point within that
    image, known as the <span id="drag-data-store-bitmap"
    class="dfn">drag data store bitmap</span> and
    <span id="drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate" class="dfn">drag data
    store hot spot coordinate</span>.

- A <span id="drag-data-store-mode" class="dfn">drag data store
  mode</span>, which is one of the following:

  <span id="concept-dnd-rw" class="dfn">Read/write mode</span>  
  For the [`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart) event. New data can be
  added to the
  <a href="#drag-data-store" id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store">drag
  data store</a>.

  <span id="concept-dnd-ro" class="dfn">Read-only mode</span>  
  For the [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) event. The list of items
  representing dragged data can be read, including the data. No new data
  can be added.

  <span id="concept-dnd-p" class="dfn">Protected mode</span>  
  For all other events. The formats and kinds in the
  <a href="#drag-data-store"
  id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-2">drag data store</a> list of
  items representing dragged data can be enumerated, but the data itself
  is unavailable and no new data can be added.

- A <span id="drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state" class="dfn">drag
  data store allowed effects state</span>, which is a string.

<div algorithm="">

When a <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-3">drag data store</a> is
<span id="create-a-drag-data-store" class="dfn">created</span>, it must
be initialized such that its <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-item-list-2">drag data store
item list</a> is empty, it has no
<a href="#drag-data-store-default-feedback"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-default-feedback">drag data
store default feedback</a>, it has no <a href="#drag-data-store-bitmap"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-bitmap">drag data store
bitmap</a> and <a href="#drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate">drag data
store hot spot coordinate</a>, its <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-mode">drag data store mode</a>
is <a href="#concept-dnd-p"
id="the-drag-data-store:concept-dnd-p">protected mode</a>, and its
<a href="#drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state"
id="the-drag-data-store:drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state">drag data
store allowed effects state</a> is the string
"[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)".

</div>

[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) objects are used to expose the
<a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store">drag data store</a> that
underlies a drag-and-drop operation.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DataTransfer {
  constructor();

  attribute DOMString dropEffect;
  attribute DOMString effectAllowed;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute DataTransferItemList items;

  undefined setDragImage(Element image, long x, long y);

  /* old interface */
  readonly attribute FrozenArray<DOMString> types;
  DOMString getData(DOMString format);
  undefined setData(DOMString format, DOMString data);
  undefined clearData(optional DOMString format);
  [SameObject] readonly attribute FileList files;
};
```

Returns a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
data-x-internal="filelist"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:filelist-2">FileList</code></a> of the
files being dragged, if any.

[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) objects that are created as part of
[drag-and-drop events](#dndevents) are only valid while those events are
being fired.

A [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated with a
<a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-3">drag data store</a>
while it is valid.

<div algorithm="">

A [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object has an associated
<span id="concept-datatransfer-types" class="dfn">types array</span>,
which is a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
data-x-internal="frozen-array"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:frozen-array-2">FrozenArray&lt;DOMString&gt;</code></a>,
initially empty. When the contents of the
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object's
<a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list">drag data
store item list</a> change, or when the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer)
object becomes no longer associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-4">drag data store</a>,
run the following steps:

1.  Let `L` be an empty sequence.

2.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is still associated
    with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-5">drag data store</a>,
    then:

    1.  For each item in the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object's
        <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
        id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-2">drag data
        store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
        id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind">kind</a>
        is *text*, add an entry to `L` consisting of the item's
        <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
        id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string">type
        string</a>.

    2.  If there are any items in the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer)
        object's <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
        id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-3">drag data
        store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
        id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-2">kind</a>
        is *File*, then add an entry to `L` consisting of the string
        "`Files`". (This value can be distinguished from the other
        values because it is not lowercase.)

3.  Set the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object's
    <a href="#concept-datatransfer-types"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-datatransfer-types">types
    array</a> to the result of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-create-frozen-array"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:creating-a-frozen-array"
    data-x-internal="creating-a-frozen-array">creating a frozen array</a>
    from `L`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer" class="dfn" dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="constructor">`DataTransfer()`</span> constructor, when
invoked, must return a newly created [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer)
object initialized as follows:

1.  Set the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-6">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-4">item
    list</a> to be an empty list.

2.  Set the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-7">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode">mode</a> to
    <a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-rw">read/write mode</a>.

3.  Set the [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) and
    [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) to "none".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-dropeffect" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer" dfn-type="attribute">`dropEffect`</span>
attribute controls the drag-and-drop feedback that the user is given
during a drag-and-drop operation. When the
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is created, the
[`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute is set to a
string value. On getting, it must return its current value. On setting,
if the new value is one of "<span id="dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-none"
class="dfn">`none`</span>", "<span id="dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy"
class="dfn">`copy`</span>", "<span id="dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link"
class="dfn">`link`</span>", or
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move" class="dfn">`move`</span>",
then the attribute's current value must be set to the new value. Other
values must be ignored.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer" dfn-type="attribute">`effectAllowed`</span>
attribute is used in the drag-and-drop processing model to initialize
the [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute during the
[`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) and
[`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) events. When the
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is created, the
[`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) attribute is set to a
string value. On getting, it must return its current value. On setting,
if the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-8">drag data store</a>'s
<a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-2">mode</a> is the
<a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-rw-2">read/write mode</a> and
the new value is one of "<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-none"
class="dfn">`none`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copy"
class="dfn">`copy`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copylink"
class="dfn">`copyLink`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copymove"
class="dfn">`copyMove`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-link"
class="dfn">`link`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-linkmove"
class="dfn">`linkMove`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-move"
class="dfn">`move`</span>",
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-all"
class="dfn">`all`</span>", or
"<span id="dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized"
class="dfn">`uninitialized`</span>", then the attribute's current value
must be set to the new value. Otherwise, it must be left unchanged.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-items" class="dfn" dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="attribute">`items`</span> attribute must return a
[`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object associated with
the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-setdragimage" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="method">`setDragImage(``image``, ``x``, ``y``)`</span> method
must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is no longer
    associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-9">drag data store</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

2.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-10">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-3">mode</a> is
    not the <a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-rw-3">read/write mode</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

3.  If `image` is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element, then set the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-bitmap"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-bitmap">drag data store
    bitmap</a> to the element's image (at its
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:natural-dimensions"
    data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural size</a>); otherwise,
    set the <a href="#drag-data-store-bitmap"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-bitmap-2">drag data store
    bitmap</a> to an image generated from the given element (the exact
    mechanism for doing so is not currently specified).

4.  Set the <a href="#drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate">drag
    data store hot spot coordinate</a> to the given `x`, `y` coordinate.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-types" class="dfn" dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="attribute">`types`</span> attribute must return this
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object's
<a href="#concept-datatransfer-types"
id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-datatransfer-types-2">types
array</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-getdata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer" dfn-type="method">`getData(``format``)`</span>
method must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is no longer
    associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-11">drag data store</a>,
    then return the empty string.

2.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-12">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-4">mode</a> is
    the <a href="#concept-dnd-p"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-p">protected mode</a>,
    then return the empty string.

3.  Let `format` be the first argument,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

4.  Let `convert-to-URL` be false.

5.  If `format` equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".

6.  If `format` equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`" and set
    `convert-to-URL` to true.

7.  If there is no item in the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-5">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-3">kind</a>
    is *text* and whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-2">type
    string</a> is equal to `format`, return the empty string.

8.  Let `result` be the data of the item in the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-6">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-4">kind</a>
    is *Plain Unicode string* and whose
    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-3">type
    string</a> is equal to `format`.

9.  If `convert-to-URL` is true, then parse `result` as appropriate for
    `text/uri-list` data, and then set `result` to the first URL from
    the list, if any, or the empty string otherwise.
    [\[RFC2483\]](#refsRFC2483)

10. Return `result`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-setdata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="method">`setData(``format``, ``data``)`</span> method must run
the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is no longer
    associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-13">drag data store</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

2.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-14">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-5">mode</a> is
    not the <a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-rw-4">read/write mode</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

3.  Let `format` be the first argument,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase-2"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

4.  If `format` equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".

    If `format` equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`".

5.  Remove the item in the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-7">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-5">kind</a>
    is *text* and whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-4">type
    string</a> is equal to `format`, if there is one.

6.  Add an item to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-8">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-6">kind</a>
    is *text*, whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-5">type
    string</a> is equal to `format`, and whose data is the string given
    by the method's second argument.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-cleardata" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransfer" dfn-type="method">`clearData(``format``)`</span>
method must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is no longer
    associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-15">drag data store</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

2.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-16">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-6">mode</a> is
    not the <a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-rw-5">read/write mode</a>,
    return. Nothing happens.

3.  If the method was called with no arguments, remove each item in the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-9">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-7">kind</a>
    is *Plain Unicode string*, and return.

4.  Set `format` to `format`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase-3"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

5.  If `format` equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".

    If `format` equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`".

6.  Remove the item in the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-10">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-8">kind</a>
    is *text* and whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-6">type
    string</a> is equal to `format`, if there is one.

</div>

The [`clearData()`](#dom-datatransfer-cleardata) method does not affect
whether any files were included in the drag, so the
[`types`](#dom-datatransfer-types) attribute's list might still not be
empty after calling [`clearData()`](#dom-datatransfer-cleardata) (it
would still contain the "`Files`" string if any files were included in
the drag).

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransfer-files" class="dfn" dfn-for="DataTransfer"
dfn-type="attribute">`files`</span> attribute must return a
<a href="#live" id="the-datatransfer-interface:live">live</a>
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
data-x-internal="filelist"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:filelist-3">FileList</code></a> sequence
consisting of <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:file">File</code></a> objects
representing the files found by the following steps. Furthermore, for a
given <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
data-x-internal="filelist"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:filelist-4">FileList</code></a> object
and a given underlying file, the same
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code
id="the-datatransfer-interface:file-2">File</code></a> object must be
used each time.

1.  Start with an empty list `L`.

2.  If the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is no longer
    associated with a <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-17">drag data store</a>,
    the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
    data-x-internal="filelist"><code
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:filelist-5">FileList</code></a> is
    empty. Return the empty list `L`.

3.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-18">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-mode-7">mode</a> is
    the <a href="#concept-dnd-p"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:concept-dnd-p-2">protected mode</a>,
    return the empty list `L`.

4.  For each item in the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-11">drag data
    store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-9">kind</a>
    is *File*, add the item's data (the file, in particular its name and
    contents, as well as its <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransfer-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-7">type</a>)
    to the list `L`.

5.  The files found by these steps are those in the list `L`.

</div>

This version of the API does not expose the types of the files during
the drag.

##### <span class="secno">6.11.3.1</span> The [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) interface<a href="#the-datatransferitemlist-interface" class="self-link"></a>

Each [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated with a
[`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DataTransferItemList {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter DataTransferItem (unsigned long index);
  DataTransferItem? add(DOMString data, DOMString type);
  DataTransferItem? add(File data);
  undefined remove(unsigned long index);
  undefined clear();
};
```

Adds a new entry for the given data to the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-5">drag data
store</a>. If the data is plain text then a `type` string has to be
provided also.

<div algorithm="">

While the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object's
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated with a
<a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-6">drag data
store</a>, the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object's
*mode* is the same as the <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-mode">drag data
store mode</a>. When the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist)
object's [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is *not* associated with
a <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-7">drag data
store</a>, the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object's
*mode* is the *disabled mode*. The <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-8">drag data
store</a> referenced in this section (which is used only when the
[`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object is not in the
*disabled mode*) is the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-9">drag data
store</a> with which the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist)
object's [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitemlist-length" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItemList" dfn-type="attribute">`length`</span>
attribute must return zero if the object is in the *disabled mode*;
otherwise it must return the number of items in the
<a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-item-list">drag
data store item list</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object is not in
the *disabled mode*, its
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:supported-property-indices"
data-x-internal="supported-property-indices">supported property
indices</a> are the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-get-the-indices"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:indices"
data-x-internal="indices">indices</a> of the
<a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-2">drag
data store item list</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <a
href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property"
data-x-internal="determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property">determine
the value of an indexed property</a> `i` of a
[`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object, the user agent
must return a [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object
representing the `i`th item in the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-10">drag data
store</a>. The same object must be returned each time a particular item
is obtained from this [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist)
object. The [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object must be
associated with the same [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object as the
[`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object when it is first
created.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitemlist-add" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItemList" dfn-type="method">`add()`</span> method
must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object is not
    in the *[read/write mode](#concept-dnd-rw)*, return null.

2.  Jump to the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

    If the first argument to the method is a string  
    If there is already an item in the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-3">drag
    data store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind">kind</a>
    is *text* and whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string">type
    string</a> is equal to the value of the method's second argument,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:notsupportederror"
    data-x-internal="notsupportederror">"<code>NotSupportedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

    Otherwise, add an item to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-4">drag
    data store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-2">kind</a>
    is *text*, whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-2">type
    string</a> is equal to the value of the method's second argument,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase-2"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>, and whose data is the string given by the method's
    first argument.

    If the first argument to the method is a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
    data-x-internal="file"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:file-2">File</code></a>  
    Add an item to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-5">drag
    data store item list</a> whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-3">kind</a>
    is *File*, whose <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-3">type
    string</a> is the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-blob-type"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:dom-blob-type">type</code></a>
    of the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
    data-x-internal="file"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:file-3">File</code></a>,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:converted-to-ascii-lowercase-3"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>, and whose data is the same as the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
    data-x-internal="file"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:file-4">File</code></a>'s
    data.

3.  [Determine the value of the indexed
    property](#dom-datatransferitemlist-item) corresponding to the newly
    added item, and return that value (a newly created
    [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitemlist-remove" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItemList"
dfn-type="method">`remove(``index``)`</span> method must run these
steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object is not
    in the *[read/write mode](#concept-dnd-rw)*, throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:invalidstateerror"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-11">drag data
    store</a> does not contain an `index`th item, then return.

3.  Remove the `index`th item from the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-12">drag data
    store</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitemlist-clear" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItemList" dfn-type="method">`clear()`</span>
method, if the [`DataTransferItemList`](#datatransferitemlist) object is
in the *[read/write mode](#concept-dnd-rw)*, must remove all the items
from the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitemlist-interface:drag-data-store-13">drag data
store</a>. Otherwise, it must do nothing.

</div>

Returns a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:file-2">File</code></a> object, if
<a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-3">the drag
data item kind</a> is *File*.

<div algorithm="">

While the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object's
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated with a
<a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store">drag data store</a>
and that <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-2">drag data
store</a>'s <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-item-list">drag data
store item list</a> still contains the item that the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object represents, the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object's *mode* is the same as
the <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-mode">drag data store
mode</a>. When the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object's
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is *not* associated with a
<a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-3">drag data
store</a>, or if the item that the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object represents has been
removed from the relevant <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-item-list-2">drag
data store item list</a>, the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem)
object's *mode* is the *disabled mode*. The <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-4">drag data
store</a> referenced in this section (which is used only when the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object is not in the *disabled
mode*) is the <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:drag-data-store-5">drag data
store</a> with which the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem)
object's [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object is associated.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitem-kind" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItem" dfn-type="attribute">`kind`</span> attribute
must return the empty string if the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object is in the *disabled
mode*; otherwise it must return the string given in the cell from the
second column of the following table from the row whose cell in the
first column contains <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-4">the drag
data item kind</a> of the item represented by the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object:

| Kind   | String     |
|--------|------------|
| *Text* | "`string`" |
| *File* | "`file`"   |

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitem-type" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItem" dfn-type="attribute">`type`</span> attribute
must return the empty string if the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object is in the *disabled
mode*; otherwise it must return
<a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
id="the-datatransferitem-interface:the-drag-data-item-type-string-2">the
drag data item type string</a> of the item represented by the
[`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitem-getasstring" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItem"
dfn-type="method">`getAsString(``callback``)`</span> method must run the
following steps:

1.  If the `callback` is null, return.

2.  If the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object is not in the
    *[read/write mode](#concept-dnd-rw)* or the *[read-only
    mode](#concept-dnd-ro)*, return. The callback is never invoked.

3.  If <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransferitem-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-5">the drag
    data item kind</a> is not *text*, then return. The callback is never
    invoked.

4.  Otherwise, <a href="#queue-a-task"
    id="the-datatransferitem-interface:queue-a-task">queue a task</a> to
    invoke `callback`, passing the actual data of the item represented
    by the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object as the
    argument.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-datatransferitem-getasfile" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DataTransferItem" dfn-type="method">`getAsFile()`</span> method
must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object is not in the
    *[read/write mode](#concept-dnd-rw)* or the *[read-only
    mode](#concept-dnd-ro)*, then return null.

2.  If <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="the-datatransferitem-interface:the-drag-data-item-kind-6">the drag
    data item kind</a> is not *File*, then return null.

3.  Return a new <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
    data-x-internal="file"><code
    id="the-datatransferitem-interface:file-3">File</code></a> object
    representing the actual data of the item represented by the
    [`DataTransferItem`](#datatransferitem) object.

</div>

The drag-and-drop processing model involves several events. They all use
the [`DragEvent`](#dragevent) interface.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DragEvent : MouseEvent {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional DragEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute DataTransfer? dataTransfer;
};

dictionary DragEventInit : MouseEventInit {
  DataTransfer? dataTransfer = null;
};
```

`event``.`<a href="#dom-dragevent-datatransfer"
id="dom-dragevent-datatransfer-dev"><code>dataTransfer</code></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[DragEvent/dataTransfer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DragEvent/dataTransfer "The DragEvent.dataTransfer property holds the drag operation's data (as a DataTransfer object).")
