Returns the [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object for the event.

Although, for consistency with other event interfaces, the
[`DragEvent`](#dragevent) interface has a constructor, it is not
particularly useful. In particular, there's no way to create a useful
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object from script, as
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) objects have a processing and security
model that is coordinated by the browser during drag-and-drops.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-dragevent-datatransfer" class="dfn"
dfn-for="DragEvent" dfn-type="attribute">`dataTransfer`</span> attribute
of the [`DragEvent`](#dragevent) interface must return the value it was
initialized to. It represents the context information for the event.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is required to <span id="fire-a-dnd-event"
class="dfn">fire a DND event</span> named `e` at an element, using a
particular <a href="#drag-data-store"
id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store">drag data store</a>, and
optionally with a specific `related target`, the user agent must run the
following steps:

1.  Let `dataDragStoreWasChanged` be false.

2.  If no specific `related target` was provided, set `related target`
    to null.

3.  Let `window` be the <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a> of the [`Document`](#document) object of the specified
    target element.

4.  If `e` is [`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart), then set the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-mode">drag data store
    mode</a> to the <a href="#concept-dnd-rw"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-dnd-rw">read/write mode</a> and
    set `dataDragStoreWasChanged` to true.

    If `e` is [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop), set the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-mode-2">drag data store
    mode</a> to the <a href="#concept-dnd-ro"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-dnd-ro">read-only mode</a>.

5.  Let `dataTransfer` be a newly created
    [`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object associated with the given
    <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-2">drag data store</a>.

6.  Set the [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) attribute
    to the <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-3">drag data store</a>'s
    <a href="#drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state">drag
    data store allowed effects state</a>.

7.  Set the [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute to
    "[`none`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-none)" if `e` is
    [`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart), [`drag`](#event-dnd-drag), or
    [`dragleave`](#event-dnd-dragleave); to the value corresponding to
    the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:current-drag-operation">current drag
    operation</a> if `e` is [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) or
    [`dragend`](#event-dnd-dragend); and to a value based on the
    [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) attribute's value
    and the drag-and-drop source, as given by the following table,
    otherwise (i.e. if `e` is [`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) or
    [`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover)):

    | [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) | [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) |
    |----|----|
    | "[`none`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-none)" | "[`none`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-none)" |
    | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copy)" | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)" |
    | "[`copyLink`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copylink)" | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override">if
    appropriate</a>, "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" |
    | "[`copyMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copymove)" | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-2">if
    appropriate</a>, "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | "[`all`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-all)" | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-3">if
    appropriate</a>, either "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" or "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-link)" | "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" |
    | "[`linkMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-linkmove)" | "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-4">if
    appropriate</a>, "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-move)" | "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)" when what is being dragged is a selection from a text control | "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-5">if
    appropriate</a>, either "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)" or "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" |
    | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)" when what is being dragged is a selection | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-6">if
    appropriate</a>, either "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" or "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)" when what is being dragged is an [`a`](#the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute | "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-7">if
    appropriate</a>, either "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)" or "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |
    | Any other case | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)", or, <a href="#concept-platform-dropeffect-override"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-platform-dropeffect-override-8">if
    appropriate</a>, either "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" or "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" |

    Where the table above provides
    <span id="concept-platform-dropeffect-override" class="dfn">possibly
    appropriate alternatives</span>, user agents may instead use the
    listed alternative values if platform conventions dictate that the
    user has requested those alternate effects.

    For example, Windows platform conventions are such that dragging
    while holding the "alt" key indicates a preference for linking the
    data, rather than moving or copying it. Therefore, on a Windows
    system, if "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" is an
    option according to the table above while the "alt" key is
    depressed, the user agent could select that instead of
    "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)" or
    "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)".

8.  Let `event` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-create"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:creating-an-event"
    data-x-internal="creating-an-event">creating an event</a> using
    [`DragEvent`](#dragevent).

9.  Initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:dom-event-type">type</code></a>
    attribute to `e`, its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
    attribute to true, its
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view"
    data-x-internal="dom-uievent-view"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:dom-uievent-view">view</code></a>
    attribute to `window`, its <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-relatedtarget"
    data-x-internal="dom-mouseevent-relatedtarget"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:dom-mouseevent-relatedtarget">relatedTarget</code></a>
    attribute to `related target`, and its
    [`dataTransfer`](#dom-dragevent-datatransfer) attribute to
    `dataTransfer`.

10. If `e` is not [`dragleave`](#event-dnd-dragleave) or
    [`dragend`](#event-dnd-dragend), then initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:dom-event-cancelable">cancelable</code></a>
    attribute to true.

11. Initialize `event`'s mouse and key attributes according to the state
    of the input devices as they would be for user interaction events.

    If there is no relevant pointing device, then initialize `event`'s
    `screenX`, `screenY`,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clientx"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clientx"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:mouseevent-clientx">clientX</code></a>,
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clienty"
    data-x-internal="mouseevent-clienty"><code
    id="the-dragevent-interface:mouseevent-clienty">clientY</code></a>,
    and `button` attributes to 0.

12. <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-event-dispatch"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">Dispatch</a> `event` at the
    specified target element.

13. Set the <a href="#drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-allowed-effects-state-2">drag
    data store allowed effects state</a> to the current value of
    `dataTransfer`'s [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed)
    attribute. (It can only have changed value if `e` is
    [`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart).)

14. If `dataDragStoreWasChanged` is true, then set the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-mode"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-mode-3">drag data store
    mode</a> back to the <a href="#concept-dnd-p"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:concept-dnd-p">protected mode</a>.

15. Break the association between `dataTransfer` and the
    <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="the-dragevent-interface:drag-data-store-4">drag data store</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.11.5</span> Processing model<a href="#drag-and-drop-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When the user attempts to begin a drag operation, the user agent must
run the following steps. User agents must act as if these steps were run
even if the drag actually started in another document or application and
the user agent was not aware that the drag was occurring until it
intersected with a document under the user agent's purview.

1.  Determine what is being dragged, as follows:

    If the drag operation was invoked on a selection, then it is the
    selection that is being dragged.

    Otherwise, if the drag operation was invoked on a
    [`Document`](#document), it is the first element, going up the
    ancestor chain, starting at the node that the user tried to drag,
    that has the IDL attribute [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) set to
    true. If there is no such element, then nothing is being dragged;
    return, the drag-and-drop operation is never started.

    Otherwise, the drag operation was invoked outside the user agent's
    purview. What is being dragged is defined by the document or
    application where the drag was started.

    [`img`](#the-img-element) elements and [`a`](#the-a-element)
    elements with an [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute have their
    [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) attribute set to true by default.

2.  <a href="#create-a-drag-data-store"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:create-a-drag-data-store">Create a
    drag data store</a>. All the DND events fired subsequently by the
    steps in this section must use this <a href="#drag-data-store"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store">drag data store</a>.

3.  Establish which DOM node is the <span id="source-node"
    class="dfn">source node</span>, as follows:

    If it is a selection that is being dragged, then the
    <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node">source node</a> is
    the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text">Text</code></a> node that
    the user started the drag on (typically the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-2">Text</code></a> node that
    the user originally clicked). If the user did not specify a
    particular node, for example if the user just told the user agent to
    begin a drag of "the selection", then the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-2">source node</a> is
    the first <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-3">Text</code></a> node
    containing a part of the selection.

    Otherwise, if it is an element that is being dragged, then the
    <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-3">source node</a> is
    the element that is being dragged.

    Otherwise, the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-4">source node</a> is
    part of another document or application. When this specification
    requires that an event be dispatched at the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-5">source node</a> in
    this case, the user agent must instead follow the platform-specific
    conventions relevant to that situation.

    Multiple events are fired on the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-6">source node</a>
    during the course of the drag-and-drop operation.

4.  Determine the <span id="list-of-dragged-nodes" class="dfn">list of
    dragged nodes</span>, as follows:

    If it is a selection that is being dragged, then the
    <a href="#list-of-dragged-nodes"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:list-of-dragged-nodes">list of
    dragged nodes</a> contains, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:tree-order"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>, every node that is
    partially or completely included in the selection (including all
    their ancestors).

    Otherwise, the <a href="#list-of-dragged-nodes"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:list-of-dragged-nodes-2">list of
    dragged nodes</a> contains only the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-7">source node</a>,
    if any.

5.  If it is a selection that is being dragged, then add an item to the
    <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list">drag data
    store item list</a>, with its properties set as follows:

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string">The
    drag data item type string</a>  
    "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
    data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text/plain">text/plain</code></a>"

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind">The drag
    data item kind</a>  
    *Text*

    The actual data  
    The text of the selection

    Otherwise, if any files are being dragged, then add one item per
    file to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-2">drag
    data store item list</a>, with their properties set as follows:

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-2">The
    drag data item type string</a>  
    The MIME type of the file, if known, or
    "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1"
    data-x-internal="application/octet-stream"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:application/octet-stream">application/octet-stream</code></a>"
    otherwise.

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-2">The drag
    data item kind</a>  
    *File*

    The actual data  
    The file's contents and name.

    Dragging files can currently only happen from outside a
    <a href="#navigable"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:navigable">navigable</a>, for
    example from a file system manager application.

    If the drag initiated outside of the application, the user agent
    must add items to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-3">drag
    data store item list</a> as appropriate for the data being dragged,
    honoring platform conventions where appropriate; however, if the
    platform conventions do not use
    <a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:mime-type"
    data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME types</a> to label dragged data,
    the user agent must make a best-effort attempt to map the types to
    MIME types, and, in any case, all the
    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-3">drag
    data item type strings</a> must be
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

    User agents may also add one or more items representing the
    selection or dragged element(s) in other forms, e.g. as HTML.

6.  If the <a href="#list-of-dragged-nodes"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:list-of-dragged-nodes-3">list of
    dragged nodes</a> is not empty, then <a href="#extracting-json"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:extracting-json">extract the
    microdata from those nodes into a JSON form</a>, and add one item to
    the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-4">drag
    data store item list</a>, with its properties set as follows:

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-4">The
    drag data item type string</a>  
    [`application/microdata+json`](#application/microdata+json)

    <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-3">The drag
    data item kind</a>  
    *Text*

    The actual data  
    The resulting JSON string.

7.  Run the following substeps:

    1.  Let `urls` be « ».

    2.  For each `node` in the <a href="#list-of-dragged-nodes"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:list-of-dragged-nodes-4">list of
        dragged nodes</a>:

        If the node is an [`a`](#the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute  
        Add to `urls` the result of
        <a href="#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url">encoding-parsing-and-serializing
        a URL</a> given the element's [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href)
        content attribute's value, relative to the element's
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:node-document"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

        If the node is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element with a [`src`](#attr-img-src) attribute  
        Add to `urls` the result of
        <a href="#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url-2">encoding-parsing-and-serializing
        a URL</a> given the element's [`src`](#attr-img-src) content
        attribute's value, relative to the element's
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:node-document-2"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

    3.  If `urls` is still empty, then return.

    4.  Let `url string` be the result of concatenating the strings in
        `urls`, in the order they were added, separated by a U+000D
        CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair (CRLF).

    5.  Add one item to the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-5">drag
        data store item list</a>, with its properties set as follows:

        <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-5">The
        drag data item type string</a>  
        [`text/uri-list`](#text/uri-list)

        <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-4">The drag
        data item kind</a>  
        *Text*

        The actual data  
        `url string`

8.  Update the <a href="#drag-data-store-default-feedback"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-default-feedback">drag
    data store default feedback</a> as appropriate for the user agent
    (if the user is dragging the selection, then the selection would
    likely be the basis for this feedback; if the user is dragging an
    element, then that element's rendering would be used; if the drag
    began outside the user agent, then the platform conventions for
    determining the drag feedback should be used).

9.  <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event">Fire a DND
    event</a> named [`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart) at the
    <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-8">source node</a>.

    If the event is canceled, then the drag-and-drop operation should
    not occur; return.

    Since events with no event listeners registered are, almost by
    definition, never canceled, drag-and-drop is always available to the
    user if the author does not specifically prevent it.

10. <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dfn-fire-a-pointer-event"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-pointer-event"
    data-x-internal="fire-a-pointer-event">Fire a pointer event</a> at
    the <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-9">source node</a>
    named
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointercancel-event"
    data-x-internal="event-pointercancel"><code
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:event-pointercancel">pointercancel</code></a>,
    and fire any other follow-up events as required by Pointer Events.
    [\[POINTEREVENTS\]](#refsPOINTEREVENTS)

11. <a href="#initiate-the-drag-and-drop-operation"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:initiate-the-drag-and-drop-operation">Initiate
    the drag-and-drop operation</a> in a manner consistent with platform
    conventions, and as described below.

    The drag-and-drop feedback must be generated from the first of the
    following sources that is available:

    1.  The <a href="#drag-data-store-bitmap"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-bitmap">drag data
        store bitmap</a>, if any. In this case, the
        <a href="#drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-hot-spot-coordinate">drag
        data store hot spot coordinate</a> should be used as hints for
        where to put the cursor relative to the resulting image. The
        values are expressed as distances in
        <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:&#39;px&#39;"
        data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> from the left side
        and from the top side of the image respectively.
        [\[CSS\]](#refsCSS)
    2.  The <a href="#drag-data-store-default-feedback"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-default-feedback-2">drag
        data store default feedback</a>.

</div>

From the moment that the user agent is to
<span id="initiate-the-drag-and-drop-operation" class="dfn">initiate the
drag-and-drop operation</span>, until the end of the drag-and-drop
operation, device input events (e.g. mouse and keyboard events) must be
suppressed.

During the drag operation, the element directly indicated by the user as
the drop target is called the <span id="immediate-user-selection"
class="dfn">immediate user selection</span>. (Only elements can be
selected by the user; other nodes must not be made available as drop
targets.) However, the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection">immediate
user selection</a> is not necessarily the
<span id="current-target-element" class="dfn">current target
element</span>, which is the element currently selected for the drop
part of the drag-and-drop operation.

The <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-2">immediate
user selection</a> changes as the user selects different elements
(either by pointing at them with a pointing device, or by selecting them
in some other way). The <a href="#current-target-element"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element">current
target element</a> changes when the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-3">immediate
user selection</a> changes, based on the results of event listeners in
the document, as described below.

Both the <a href="#current-target-element"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-2">current
target element</a> and the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-4">immediate
user selection</a> can be null, which means no target element is
selected. They can also both be elements in other (DOM-based) documents,
or other (non-web) programs altogether. (For example, a user could drag
text to a word-processor.) The <a href="#current-target-element"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-3">current
target element</a> is initially null.

In addition, there is also a <span id="current-drag-operation"
class="dfn">current drag operation</span>, which can take on the values
"<span id="concept-current-drag-operation-none"
class="dfn">`none`</span>",
"<span id="concept-current-drag-operation-copy"
class="dfn">`copy`</span>",
"<span id="concept-current-drag-operation-link"
class="dfn">`link`</span>", and
"<span id="concept-current-drag-operation-move"
class="dfn">`move`</span>". Initially, it has the value
"[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)". It is updated by the
user agent as described in the steps below.

<div algorithm="">

User agents must, as soon as the drag operation is
<a href="#initiate-the-drag-and-drop-operation"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:initiate-the-drag-and-drop-operation-2">initiated</a>
and every 350ms (±200ms) thereafter for as long as the drag operation is
ongoing, <a href="#queue-a-task"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:queue-a-task">queue a task</a> to
perform the following steps in sequence:

1.  If the user agent is still performing the previous iteration of the
    sequence (if any) when the next iteration becomes due, return for
    this iteration (effectively "skipping missed frames" of the
    drag-and-drop operation).

2.  <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-2">Fire a DND
    event</a> named [`drag`](#event-dnd-drag) at the
    <a href="#source-node"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-10">source node</a>.
    If this event is canceled, the user agent must set the
    <a href="#current-drag-operation"
    id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation">current drag
    operation</a> to "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)"
    (no drag operation).

3.  If the [`drag`](#event-dnd-drag) event was not canceled and the user
    has not ended the drag-and-drop operation, check the state of the
    drag-and-drop operation, as follows:

    1.  If the user is indicating a different
        <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-5">immediate
        user selection</a> than during the last iteration (or if this is
        the first iteration), and if this
        <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-6">immediate
        user selection</a> is not the same as the
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-4">current
        target element</a>, then update the
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-5">current
        target element</a> as follows:

        If the new <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-7">immediate
        user selection</a> is null  
        Set the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-6">current
        target element</a> to null also.

        If the new <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-8">immediate
        user selection</a> is in a non-DOM document or application  
        Set the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-7">current
        target element</a> to the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-9">immediate
        user selection</a>.

        Otherwise  
        <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-3">Fire a DND
        event</a> named [`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) at the
        <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-10">immediate
        user selection</a>.

        If the event is canceled, then set the
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-8">current
        target element</a> to the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-11">immediate
        user selection</a>.

        Otherwise, run the appropriate step from the following list:

        If the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-12">immediate
        user selection</a> is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">Text</a> state) or an <a href="#editing-host"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editing-host">editing host</a> or <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editable"
        data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> element, and the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-6">drag
        data store item list</a> has an item with <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-6">the
        drag data item type string</a> "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
        data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text/plain-2">text/plain</code></a>" and <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-5">the drag
        data item kind</a> *text*  
        Set the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-9">current
        target element</a> to the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-13">immediate
        user selection</a> anyway.

        If the <a href="#immediate-user-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:immediate-user-selection-14">immediate
        user selection</a> is <a href="#the-body-element-2"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-body-element-2">the body
        element</a>  
        Leave the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-10">current
        target element</a> unchanged.

        Otherwise  
        <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-4">Fire a DND
        event</a> named [`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) at
        <a href="#the-body-element-2"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-body-element-2-2">the body
        element</a>, if there is one, or at the [`Document`](#document)
        object, if not. Then, set the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-11">current
        target element</a> to <a href="#the-body-element-2"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-body-element-2-3">the body
        element</a>, regardless of whether that event was canceled or
        not.

    2.  If the previous step caused the
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-12">current
        target element</a> to change, and if the previous target element
        was not null or a part of a non-DOM document, then
        <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-5">fire a DND
        event</a> named [`dragleave`](#event-dnd-dragleave) at the
        previous target element, with the new
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-13">current
        target element</a> as the specific *related target*.

    3.  If the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-14">current
        target element</a> is a DOM element, then
        <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-6">fire a DND
        event</a> named [`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) at this
        <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-15">current
        target element</a>.

        If the [`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) event is not canceled,
        run the appropriate step from the following list:

        If the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-16">current
        target element</a> is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-2">Text</a> state) or an <a href="#editing-host"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editing-host-2">editing host</a> or <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editable-2"
        data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> element, and the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-7">drag
        data store item list</a> has an item with <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-7">the
        drag data item type string</a> "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
        data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text/plain-3">text/plain</code></a>" and <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-6">the drag
        data item kind</a> *text*  
        Set the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-2">current
        drag operation</a> to either
        "[`copy`](#concept-current-drag-operation-copy)" or
        "[`move`](#concept-current-drag-operation-move)", as appropriate
        given the platform conventions.

        Otherwise  
        Reset the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-3">current
        drag operation</a> to
        "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)".

        Otherwise (if the [`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) event *is*
        canceled), set the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-4">current
        drag operation</a> based on the values of the
        [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) and
        [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attributes of the
        [`DragEvent`](#dragevent) object's
        [`dataTransfer`](#dom-dragevent-datatransfer) object as they
        stood after the event
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:concept-event-dispatch"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatch</a> finished,
        as per the following table:

        | [`effectAllowed`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed) | [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) | Drag operation |
        |----|----|----|
        | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)", "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copy)", "[`copyLink`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copylink)", "[`copyMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copymove)", or "[`all`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-all)" | "[`copy`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-copy)" | "[`copy`](#concept-current-drag-operation-copy)" |
        | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)", "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-link)", "[`copyLink`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copylink)", "[`linkMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-linkmove)", or "[`all`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-all)" | "[`link`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-link)" | "[`link`](#concept-current-drag-operation-link)" |
        | "[`uninitialized`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-uninitialized)", "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-move)", "[`copyMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-copymove)", "[`linkMove`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-linkmove)", or "[`all`](#dom-datatransfer-effectallowed-all)" | "[`move`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect-move)" | "[`move`](#concept-current-drag-operation-move)" |
        | Any other case |  | "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)" |

    4.  Otherwise, if the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-17">current
        target element</a> is not a DOM element, use platform-specific
        mechanisms to determine what drag operation is being performed
        (none, copy, link, or move), and set the
        <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-5">current
        drag operation</a> accordingly.

    5.  Update the drag feedback (e.g. the mouse cursor) to match the
        <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-6">current
        drag operation</a>, as follows:

        | Drag operation | Feedback |
        |----|----|
        | "[`copy`](#concept-current-drag-operation-copy)" | Data will be copied if dropped here. |
        | "[`link`](#concept-current-drag-operation-link)" | Data will be linked if dropped here. |
        | "[`move`](#concept-current-drag-operation-move)" | Data will be moved if dropped here. |
        | "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)" | No operation allowed, dropping here will cancel the drag-and-drop operation. |

4.  Otherwise, if the user ended the drag-and-drop operation (e.g. by
    releasing the mouse button in a mouse-driven drag-and-drop
    interface), or if the [`drag`](#event-dnd-drag) event was canceled,
    then this will be the last iteration. Run the following steps, then
    stop the drag-and-drop operation:

    1.  If the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-7">current
        drag operation</a> is
        "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)" (no drag
        operation), or if the user ended the drag-and-drop operation by
        canceling it (e.g. by hitting the
        <span class="kbd"><span class="kbd">Escape</span></span> key),
        or if the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-18">current
        target element</a> is null, then the drag operation failed. Run
        these substeps:

        1.  Let `dropped` be false.

        2.  If the <a href="#current-target-element"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-19">current
            target element</a> is a DOM element,
            <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-7">fire a DND
            event</a> named [`dragleave`](#event-dnd-dragleave) at it;
            otherwise, if it is not null, use platform-specific
            conventions for drag cancelation.

        3.  Set the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-8">current
            drag operation</a> to
            "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)".

        Otherwise, the drag operation might be a success; run these
        substeps:

        1.  Let `dropped` be true.

        2.  If the <a href="#current-target-element"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-20">current
            target element</a> is a DOM element,
            <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-8">fire a DND
            event</a> named [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) at it; otherwise,
            use platform-specific conventions for indicating a drop.

        3.  If the event is canceled, set the
            <a href="#current-drag-operation"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-9">current
            drag operation</a> to the value of the
            [`dropEffect`](#dom-datatransfer-dropeffect) attribute of
            the [`DragEvent`](#dragevent) object's
            [`dataTransfer`](#dom-dragevent-datatransfer) object as it
            stood after the event
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:concept-event-dispatch-2"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatch</a>
            finished.

            Otherwise, the event is not canceled; perform the event's
            default action, which depends on the exact target as
            follows:

            If the <a href="#current-target-element"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-21">current
            target element</a> is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-3">Text</a> state) or an <a href="#editing-host"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editing-host-3">editing host</a> or <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editable-3"
            data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> element, and the <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-8">drag
            data store item list</a> has an item with <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-8">the
            drag data item type string</a> "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
            data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text/plain-4">text/plain</code></a>" and <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-7">the drag
            data item kind</a> *text*  
            Insert the actual data of the first item in the
            <a href="#drag-data-store-item-list"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:drag-data-store-item-list-9">drag
            data store item list</a> to have
            <a href="#the-drag-data-item-type-string"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-type-string-9">a
            drag data item type string</a> of
            "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
            data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text/plain-5">text/plain</code></a>"
            and <a href="#the-drag-data-item-kind"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:the-drag-data-item-kind-8">a drag
            data item kind</a> that is *text* into the text control or
            <a href="#editing-host"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editing-host-4">editing host</a>
            or
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editable-4"
            data-x-internal="editable">editable</a> element in a manner
            consistent with platform-specific conventions (e.g.
            inserting it at the current mouse cursor position, or
            inserting it at the end of the field).

            Otherwise  
            Reset the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
            id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-10">current
            drag operation</a> to
            "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)".

    2.  <a href="#fire-a-dnd-event"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:fire-a-dnd-event-9">Fire a DND
        event</a> named [`dragend`](#event-dnd-dragend) at the
        <a href="#source-node"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:source-node-11">source node</a>.

    3.  Run the appropriate steps from the following list as the default
        action of the [`dragend`](#event-dnd-dragend) event:

        If `dropped` is true, the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-22">current
        target element</a> is a *text control* (see below), the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-11">current
        drag operation</a> is "[`move`](#concept-current-drag-operation-move)", and the source of the drag-and-drop operation is a selection in the DOM that is entirely contained within an <a href="#editing-host"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:editing-host-5">editing host</a>  
        <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#delete-the-selection"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:delete-the-selection"
        data-x-internal="delete-the-selection">Delete the selection</a>.

        If `dropped` is true, the <a href="#current-target-element"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-target-element-23">current
        target element</a> is a *text control* (see below), the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-12">current
        drag operation</a> is "[`move`](#concept-current-drag-operation-move)", and the source of the drag-and-drop operation is a selection in a text control  
        The user agent should delete the dragged selection from the
        relevant text control.

        If `dropped` is false or if the <a href="#current-drag-operation"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:current-drag-operation-13">current
        drag operation</a> is "[`none`](#concept-current-drag-operation-none)"  
        The drag was canceled. If the platform conventions dictate that
        this be represented to the user (e.g. by animating the dragged
        selection going back to the source of the drag-and-drop
        operation), then do so.

        Otherwise  
        The event has no default action.

        For the purposes of this step, a *text control* is a
        [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element or an
        [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
        [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the
        <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-4">Text</a>,
        <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-5">Search</a>,
        <a href="#telephone-state-(type=tel)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:telephone-state-(type=tel)">Tel</a>,
        <a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>,
        <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a>,
        <a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:password-state-(type=password)">Password</a>,
        or <a href="#number-state-(type=number)"
        id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:number-state-(type=number)">Number</a>
        states.

</div>

User agents are encouraged to consider how to react to drags near the
edge of scrollable regions. For example, if a user drags a link to the
bottom of the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="drag-and-drop-processing-model:viewport"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a> on a long page, it might make
sense to scroll the page so that the user can drop the link lower on the
page.

This model is independent of which [`Document`](#document) object the
nodes involved are from; the events are fired as described above and the
rest of the processing model runs as described above, irrespective of
how many documents are involved in the operation.

#### <span class="secno">6.11.7</span> The [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) attribute<a href="#the-draggable-attribute" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Global_attributes/draggable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/draggable "The draggable global attribute is an enumerated attribute that indicates whether the element can be dragged, either with native browser behavior or the HTML Drag and Drop API.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox2+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari5+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome4+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera12+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet ExplorerYes</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

All
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-draggable-attribute:html-elements">HTML
elements</a> may have the <span id="attr-draggable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="html-global" dfn-type="element-attr">`draggable`</span> content
attribute set. The [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-draggable-attribute:enumerated-attribute">enumerated
attribute</a> with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-draggable-true" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/draggable" dfn-type="attr-value">`true`</span> | <span id="attr-draggable-true-state" class="dfn">True</span> | The element will be draggable. |
| <span id="attr-draggable-false" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/draggable" dfn-type="attr-value">`false`</span> | <span id="attr-draggable-false-state" class="dfn">False</span> | The element will not be draggable. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<span id="attr-draggable-auto-state" class="dfn">Auto</span> state. The
auto state uses the default behavior of the user agent.

</div>

An element with a [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) attribute should also
have a [`title`](#attr-title) attribute that names the element for the
purpose of non-visual interactions.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-draggable"
id="dom-draggable-dev"><code>draggable</code></a>` [ = ``value`` ]`  
Returns true if the element is draggable; otherwise, returns false.

Can be set, to override the default and set the
[`draggable`](#attr-draggable) content attribute.

The <span id="dom-draggable" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`draggable`</span> IDL attribute, whose value
depends on the content attribute's in the way described below, controls
whether or not the element is draggable. Generally, only text selections
are draggable, but elements whose [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL
attribute is true become draggable as well.

<div algorithm="">

If an element's [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) content attribute has the
state <a href="#attr-draggable-true-state"
id="the-draggable-attribute:attr-draggable-true-state">True</a>, the
[`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL attribute must return true.

Otherwise, if the element's [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) content
attribute has the state <a href="#attr-draggable-false-state"
id="the-draggable-attribute:attr-draggable-false-state">False</a>, the
[`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL attribute must return false.

Otherwise, the element's [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) content
attribute has the state <a href="#attr-draggable-auto-state"
id="the-draggable-attribute:attr-draggable-auto-state">Auto</a>. If the
element is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element, an
[`object`](#the-object-element) element that <a href="#represents"
id="the-draggable-attribute:represents">represents</a> an image, or an
[`a`](#the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href)
content attribute, the [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL attribute must
return true; otherwise, the [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL attribute
must return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If the [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL attribute is set to the value
false, the [`draggable`](#attr-draggable) content attribute must be set
to the literal value "`false`". If the [`draggable`](#dom-draggable) IDL
attribute is set to the value true, the [`draggable`](#attr-draggable)
content attribute must be set to the literal value "`true`".

</div>

#### <span class="secno">6.11.8</span> Security risks in the drag-and-drop model<a href="#security-risks-in-the-drag-and-drop-model"
class="self-link"></a>

User agents must not make the data added to the
[`DataTransfer`](#datatransfer) object during the
[`dragstart`](#event-dnd-dragstart) event available to scripts until the
[`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) event, because otherwise, if a user were to
drag sensitive information from one document to a second document,
crossing a hostile third document in the process, the hostile document
could intercept the data.

For the same reason, user agents must consider a drop to be successful
only if the user specifically ended the drag operation — if any scripts
end the drag operation, it must be considered unsuccessful (canceled)
and the [`drop`](#event-dnd-drop) event must not be fired.

User agents should take care to not start drag-and-drop operations in
response to script actions. For example, in a mouse-and-window
environment, if a script moves a window while the user has their mouse
button depressed, the UA would not consider that to start a drag. This
is important because otherwise UAs could cause data to be dragged from
sensitive sources and dropped into hostile documents without the user's
consent.

User agents should filter potentially active (scripted) content (e.g.
HTML) when it is dragged and when it is dropped, using a safelist of
known-safe features. Similarly,
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-relative"
id="security-risks-in-the-drag-and-drop-model:relative-url"
data-x-internal="relative-url">relative URLs</a> should be turned into
absolute URLs to avoid references changing in unexpected ways. This
specification does not specify how this is performed.

<div class="example">

Consider a hostile page providing some content and getting the user to
select and drag and drop (or indeed, copy and paste) that content to a
victim page's [`contenteditable`](#attr-contenteditable) region. If the
browser does not ensure that only safe content is dragged, potentially
unsafe content such as scripts and event handlers in the selection, once
dropped (or pasted) into the victim site, get the privileges of the
victim site. This would thus enable a cross-site scripting attack.

</div>

### <span class="secno">6.12</span> The [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute<a href="#the-popover-attribute" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

[Global_attributes/popover](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/popover "The popover global attribute is used to designate an element as a popover element.")

All
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements">HTML
elements</a> may have the <span id="attr-popover" class="dfn"
dfn-for="html-global" dfn-type="element-attr">`popover`</span> content
attribute set. When specified, the element won't be rendered until it
becomes shown, at which point it will be rendered on top of other page
content.

<div class="example">

The [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is a global attribute that
allows authors flexibility to ensure popover functionality can be
applied to elements with the most relevant semantics.

The following demonstrates how one might create a popover sub-navigation
list of links, within the global navigation for a website.

``` html
<ul>
  <li>
    <a href=...>All Products</a>
    <button popovertarget=sub-nav>
     <img src=down-arrow.png alt="Product pages">
    </button>
    <ul popover id=sub-nav>
     <li><a href=...>Shirts</a>
     <li><a href=...>Shoes</a>
     <li><a href=...>Hats etc.</a>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <!-- other list items and links here -->
</ul>
```

</div>

When using [`popover`](#attr-popover) on elements without accessibility
semantics, for instance the [`div`](#the-div-element) element, authors
should use the appropriate ARIA attributes to ensure the popover is
accessible.

<div class="example">

The following shows the baseline markup to create a custom menu popover,
where the first menuitem will receive keyboard focus when the popover is
invoked due to the use of the `autofocus` attribute. Navigating the
menuitems with arrow keys and activation behaviors would still need
author scripting. Additional requirements for building custom menus
widgets are defined in the [WAI-ARIA
specification](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#menu).

``` html
<button popovertarget=m>Actions</button>
<div role=menu id=m popover>
  <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1 autofocus>Edit</button>
  <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1>Hide</button>
  <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1>Delete</button>
</div>
```

A popover can be useful for rendering a status message, confirming the
action performed by the user. The following demonstrates how one could
reveal a popover in an [`output`](#the-output-element) element.

``` html
<button id=submit>Submit</button>
<p><output><span popover=manual></span></output></p>

<script>
 const sBtn = document.getElementById("submit");
 const outSpan = document.querySelector("output [popover=manual]");
 let successMessage;
 let errorMessage;

 /* define logic for determining success of action
  and determining the appropriate success or error
  messages to use */

 sBtn.addEventListener("click", ()=> {
  if ( success ) {
   outSpan.textContent = successMessage;
  }
  else {
   outSpan.textContent = errorMessage;
  }
  outSpan.showPopover();

  setTimeout(function () {
   outSpan.hidePopover();
  }, 10000);
 });
</script>
```

</div>

Inserting a popover element into an [`output`](#the-output-element)
element will generally cause screen readers to announce the content when
it becomes visible. Depending on the complexity or frequency of the
content, this could be either useful or annoying to users of these
assistive technologies. Keep this in mind when using the
[`output`](#the-output-element) element or other ARIA live regions to
ensure the best user experience.

The [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-popover-attribute:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
|----|----|----|
| <span id="attr-popover-auto" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/popover" dfn-type="attr-value">`auto`</span> | <span id="attr-popover-auto-state" class="dfn">Auto</span> | Closes other popovers when opened; has <a href="#popover-light-dismiss"
id="the-popover-attribute:popover-light-dismiss">light dismiss</a> and responds to <a href="#close-request" id="the-popover-attribute:close-request">close
requests</a>. |
| <span id="attr-popover-manual" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/popover" dfn-type="attr-value">`manual`</span> | <span id="attr-popover-manual-state" class="dfn">Manual</span> | Does not close other popovers; does not <a href="#popover-light-dismiss"
id="the-popover-attribute:popover-light-dismiss-2">light dismiss</a> or respond to <a href="#close-request"
id="the-popover-attribute:close-request-2">close requests</a>. |
| <span id="attr-popover-hint" class="dfn" dfn-for="html-global/popover" dfn-type="attr-value">`hint`</span> | <span id="attr-popover-hint-state" class="dfn">Hint</span> | Closes other hint popovers when opened, but not other auto popovers; has <a href="#popover-light-dismiss"
id="the-popover-attribute:popover-light-dismiss-3">light dismiss</a> and responds to <a href="#close-request"
id="the-popover-attribute:close-request-3">close requests</a>. |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* is the
<span id="attr-popover-none-state" class="dfn">No Popover</span> state,
its *[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* is the
<a href="#attr-popover-manual-state"
id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-manual-state">Manual</a> state,
and its *[empty value default](#empty-value-default)* is the
<a href="#attr-popover-auto-state"
id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-auto-state">Auto</a> state.

</div>

The <span id="dom-popover" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`popover`</span> IDL attribute must
<a href="#reflect" id="the-popover-attribute:reflect">reflect</a> the
<a href="#attr-popover"
id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-5">popover</a> attribute,
<a href="#limited-to-only-known-values"
id="the-popover-attribute:limited-to-only-known-values">limited to only

</div>

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-2">HTML
element</a> has a <span id="popover-visibility-state" class="dfn"
export="">popover visibility state</span>, initially
<a href="#popover-hidden-state"
id="the-popover-attribute:popover-hidden-state">hidden</a>, with these
potential values:

- <span id="popover-hidden-state" class="dfn"
  dfn-for="popover visibility state" export="">hidden</span>

- <span id="popover-showing-state" class="dfn"
  dfn-for="popover visibility state" export="">showing</span>

Every [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="popover-pointerdown-target" class="dfn">popover pointerdown
target</span>, which is an
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-3">HTML
element</a> or null, initially null.

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-4">HTML
element</a> has a <span id="popover-trigger" class="dfn">popover
trigger</span>, which is an
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-5">HTML
element</a> or null, initially set to null.

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-6">HTML
element</a> has a <span id="popover-showing-or-hiding"
class="dfn">popover showing or hiding</span>, which is a boolean,
initially set to false.

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-7">HTML
element</a> <span id="popover-toggle-task-tracker" class="dfn">popover
toggle task tracker</span>, which is a <a href="#toggle-task-tracker"
id="the-popover-attribute:toggle-task-tracker">toggle task tracker</a>
or null, initially null.

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-8">HTML
element</a> has a <span id="popover-close-watcher" class="dfn">popover
close watcher</span>, which is a
<a href="#close-watcher" id="the-popover-attribute:close-watcher">close
watcher</a> or null, initially null.

Every
<a href="#html-elements" id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-9">HTML
element</a> has an <span id="opened-in-popover-mode" class="dfn">opened
in popover mode</span>, which is a string or null, initially null.

<div algorithm="">

The following <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
id="the-popover-attribute:concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change-ext">attribute change
steps</a>, given `element`, `localName`, `oldValue`, `value`, and
`namespace`, are used for all <a href="#html-elements"
id="the-popover-attribute:html-elements-10">HTML elements</a>:

1.  If `namespace` is not null, then return.

2.  If `localName` is not [`popover`](#attr-popover), then return.

3.  If `element`'s <a href="#popover-visibility-state"
    id="the-popover-attribute:popover-visibility-state">popover visibility
    state</a> is in the <a href="#popover-showing-state"
    id="the-popover-attribute:popover-showing-state">showing state</a>
    and `oldValue` and `value` are in different <a href="#attr-popover"
    id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-7">states</a>, then run the
    <a href="#hide-popover-algorithm"
    id="the-popover-attribute:hide-popover-algorithm">hide popover
    algorithm</a> given `element`, true, true, false, and null.

</div>

`element``.`<a href="#dom-showpopover"
id="dom-showpopover-dev"><code>showPopover</code></a>`()`  
Shows the popover `element` by adding it to the top layer. If
`element`'s [`popover`](#attr-popover) attribute is in the
<a href="#attr-popover-auto-state"
id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-auto-state-2">Auto</a> state,
then this will also close all other <a href="#attr-popover-auto-state"
id="the-popover-attribute:attr-popover-auto-state-3">Auto</a> popovers
unless they are an ancestor of `element` according to the
<a href="#topmost-popover-ancestor"
id="the-popover-attribute:topmost-popover-ancestor">topmost popover
ancestor</a> algorithm.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-hidepopover"
id="dom-hidepopover-dev"><code>hidePopover</code></a>`()`  
Hides the popover `element` by removing it from the top layer and
applying `display: none` to it.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-togglepopover"
id="dom-togglepopover-dev"><code>togglePopover</code></a>`()`  
If the popover `element` is not showing, then this method shows it.
Otherwise, this method hides it. This method returns true if the popover
is open after calling it, otherwise false.

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[HTMLElement/showPopover](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/showPopover "The showPopover() method of the HTMLElement interface shows a popover element (i.e. one that has a valid popover attribute) by adding it to the top layer.")
