| ("`https`", "`example.org`", 314, "`example.org`") | ("`https`", "`example.org`", 420, "`example.org`") | ❌ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`example.org`", null, null) | ("`https`", "`example.org`", null, "`example.org`") | ✅ | ❌ |
| ("`https`", "`example.org`", null, "`example.org`") | ("`http`", "`example.org`", null, "`example.org`") | ❌ | ❌ |

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.1.1.1</span> Sites<a href="#sites" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="scheme-and-host" class="dfn">scheme-and-host</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="sites:tuple"
data-x-internal="tuple">tuple</a> of a
<span id="concept-scheme-and-host-scheme" class="dfn">scheme</span> (an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-string"
id="sites:ascii-string" data-x-internal="ascii-string">ASCII string</a>)
and a <span id="concept-scheme-and-host-host" class="dfn">host</span> (a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host"
id="sites:concept-host" data-x-internal="concept-host">host</a>).

A <span id="site" class="dfn" export="">site</span> is an
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque" id="sites:concept-origin-opaque">opaque
origin</a> or a <a href="#scheme-and-host"
id="sites:scheme-and-host">scheme-and-host</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="obtain-a-site" class="dfn" export="">obtain a site</span>,
given an origin `origin`, run these steps:

1.  If `origin` is an <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="sites:concept-origin-opaque-2">opaque origin</a>, then return
    `origin`.

2.  If `origin`'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-host" id="sites:concept-origin-host">host</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-registrable-domain"
    id="sites:registrable-domain"
    data-x-internal="registrable-domain">registrable domain</a> is null,
    then return (`origin`'s <a href="#concept-origin-scheme"
    id="sites:concept-origin-scheme">scheme</a>, `origin`'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-host" id="sites:concept-origin-host-2">host</a>).

3.  Return (`origin`'s <a href="#concept-origin-scheme"
    id="sites:concept-origin-scheme-2">scheme</a>, `origin`'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-host" id="sites:concept-origin-host-3">host</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-registrable-domain"
    id="sites:registrable-domain-2"
    data-x-internal="registrable-domain">registrable domain</a>).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Two <a href="#site" id="sites:site">sites</a>, `A` and `B`, are said to
be <span id="concept-site-same-site" class="dfn" dfn-for="site"
export="">same site</span> if the following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `A` and `B` are the same <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="sites:concept-origin-opaque-3">opaque origin</a>, then return
    true.

2.  If `A` or `B` is an <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="sites:concept-origin-opaque-4">opaque origin</a>, then return
    false.

3.  If `A`'s and `B`'s <a href="#concept-scheme-and-host-scheme"
    id="sites:concept-scheme-and-host-scheme">scheme</a> values are
    different, then return false.

4.  If `A`'s and `B`'s <a href="#concept-scheme-and-host-host"
    id="sites:concept-scheme-and-host-host">host</a> values are not
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-equals"
    id="sites:host-equals" data-x-internal="host-equals">equal</a>, then
    return false.

5.  Return true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="serialization-of-a-site" class="dfn"
export="">serialization of a site</span> is the string obtained by
applying the following algorithm to the given
<a href="#site" id="sites:site-2">site</a> `site`:

1.  If `site` is an <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="sites:concept-origin-opaque-5">opaque origin</a>, then return
    "`null`".

2.  Let `result` be `site`\[0\].

3.  Append "`://`" to `result`.

4.  Append `site`\[1\],
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer"
    id="sites:host-serializer"
    data-x-internal="host-serializer">serialized</a>, to `result`.

5.  Return `result`.

</div>

It needs to be clear from context that the serialized value is a site,
not an origin, as there is not necessarily a syntactic difference
between the two. For example, the origin ("`https`", "`shop.example`",
null, null) and the site ("`https`", "`shop.example`") have the same
serialization: "`https://shop.example`".

<div algorithm="">

Two <a href="#concept-origin" id="sites:concept-origin">origins</a>, `A`
and `B`, are said to be <span id="schemelessly-same-site" class="dfn"
export="">schemelessly same site</span> if the following algorithm
returns true:

1.  If `A` and `B` are the same <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="sites:concept-origin-opaque-6">opaque origin</a>, then return
    true.

2.  If `A` and `B` are both
    <a href="#concept-origin-tuple" id="sites:concept-origin-tuple">tuple
    origins</a>, then:

    1.  Let `hostA` be `A`'s
        <a href="#concept-origin-host" id="sites:concept-origin-host-4">host</a>,
        and let `hostB` be `B`'s
        <a href="#concept-origin-host" id="sites:concept-origin-host-5">host</a>.

    2.  If `hostA`
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-equals"
        id="sites:host-equals-2" data-x-internal="host-equals">equals</a>
        `hostB` and `hostA`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-registrable-domain"
        id="sites:registrable-domain-3"
        data-x-internal="registrable-domain">registrable domain</a> is
        null, then return true.

    3.  If `hostA`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-registrable-domain"
        id="sites:registrable-domain-4"
        data-x-internal="registrable-domain">registrable domain</a>
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-equals"
        id="sites:host-equals-3" data-x-internal="host-equals">equals</a>
        `hostB`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-registrable-domain"
        id="sites:registrable-domain-5"
        data-x-internal="registrable-domain">registrable domain</a> and
        is non-null, then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Two <a href="#concept-origin" id="sites:concept-origin-2">origins</a>,
`A` and `B`, are said to be <span id="same-site" class="dfn"
export="">same site</span> if the following algorithm returns true:

1.  Let `siteA` be the result of
    <a href="#obtain-a-site" id="sites:obtain-a-site">obtaining a site</a>
    given `A`.

2.  Let `siteB` be the result of
    <a href="#obtain-a-site" id="sites:obtain-a-site-2">obtaining a site</a>
    given `B`.

3.  If `siteA` is
    <a href="#concept-site-same-site" id="sites:concept-site-same-site">same
    site</a> with `siteB`, then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

Unlike the <a href="#same-origin" id="sites:same-origin">same origin</a>
and <a href="#same-origin-domain" id="sites:same-origin-domain">same
origin-domain</a> concepts, for <a href="#schemelessly-same-site"
id="sites:schemelessly-same-site">schemelessly same site</a> and
<a href="#same-site" id="sites:same-site">same site</a>, the
<a href="#concept-origin-port" id="sites:concept-origin-port">port</a>
and <a href="#concept-origin-domain"
id="sites:concept-origin-domain">domain</a> components are ignored.

For the reasons [explained in
URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#warning-avoid-psl), the
<a href="#same-site" id="sites:same-site-2">same site</a> and
<a href="#schemelessly-same-site"
id="sites:schemelessly-same-site-2">schemelessly same site</a> concepts
should be avoided when possible, in favor of
<a href="#same-origin" id="sites:same-origin-2">same origin</a> checks.

<div id="example-same-site" class="example">

<a href="#example-same-site" class="self-link"></a>

Given that `wildlife.museum`, `museum`, and `com` are
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-public-suffix"
id="sites:public-suffix" data-x-internal="public-suffix">public
suffixes</a> and that `example.com` is not:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
| `A` | `B` | <a href="#schemelessly-same-site"
id="sites:schemelessly-same-site-3">schemelessly same site</a> | <a href="#same-site" id="sites:same-site-3">same site</a> |
| ("`https`", "`example.com`") | ("`https`", "`sub.example.com`") | ✅ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`example.com`") | ("`https`", "`sub.other.example.com`") | ✅ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`example.com`") | ("`http`", "`non-secure.example.com`") | ✅ | ❌ |
| ("`https`", "`r.wildlife.museum`") | ("`https`", "`sub.r.wildlife.museum`") | ✅ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`r.wildlife.museum`") | ("`https`", "`sub.other.r.wildlife.museum`") | ✅ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`r.wildlife.museum`") | ("`https`", "`other.wildlife.museum`") | ❌ | ❌ |
| ("`https`", "`r.wildlife.museum`") | ("`https`", "`wildlife.museum`") | ❌ | ❌ |
| ("`https`", "`wildlife.museum`") | ("`https`", "`wildlife.museum`") | ✅ | ✅ |
| ("`https`", "`example.com`") | ("`https`", "`example.com.`") | ❌ | ❌ |

(Here we have omitted the
<a href="#concept-origin-port" id="sites:concept-origin-port-2">port</a>
and <a href="#concept-origin-domain"
id="sites:concept-origin-domain-2">domain</a> components since they are
not considered.)

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.1.1.2</span> Relaxing the same-origin restriction<a href="#relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction" class="self-link"></a>

`document``.`<a href="#dom-document-domain"
id="dom-document-domain-dev"><code>domain</code></a>` [ = ``domain`` ]`  
Returns the current domain used for security checks.

Can be set to a value that removes subdomains, to change the
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin">origin</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-domain"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin-domain">domain</a>
to allow pages on other subdomains of the same domain (if they do the
same thing) to access each other. This enables pages on different hosts
of a domain to synchronously access each other's DOMs.

In sandboxed [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)s, [`Document`](#document)s
with <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin-opaque">opaque
origins</a>, and [`Document`](#document)s without a
<a href="#concept-document-bc"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-document-bc">browsing
context</a>, the setter will throw a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:securityerror"
data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
exception. In cases where
[`crossOriginIsolated`](#dom-crossoriginisolated) or
[`originAgentCluster`](#dom-originagentcluster) return true, the setter
will do nothing.

<div class="critical">

Avoid using the [`document.domain`](#dom-document-domain) setter. It
undermines the security protections provided by the same-origin policy.
This is especially acute when using shared hosting; for example, if an
untrusted third party is able to host an HTTP server at the same IP
address but on a different port, then the same-origin protection that
normally protects two different sites on the same host will fail, as the
ports are ignored when comparing origins after the
[`document.domain`](#dom-document-domain) setter has been used.

Because of these security pitfalls, this feature is in the process of
being removed from the web platform. (This is a long process that takes
many years.)

Instead, use [`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) or
[`MessageChannel`](#messagechannel) objects to communicate across
origins in a safe manner.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-document-domain" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
dfn-type="attribute">`domain`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `effectiveDomain` be
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-effective-domain"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin-effective-domain">effective
    domain</a>.

2.  If `effectiveDomain` is null, then return the empty string.

3.  Return `effectiveDomain`,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:host-serializer"
    data-x-internal="host-serializer">serialized</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`domain`](#dom-document-domain) setter steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-document-bc"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-document-bc-2">browsing
    context</a> is null, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:securityerror-2"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active
    sandboxing flag set</a> has its
    <a href="#sandboxed-document.domain-browsing-context-flag"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:sandboxed-document.domain-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
    <code>document.domain</code> browsing context flag</a> set, then
    throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:securityerror-3"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Let `effectiveDomain` be
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-effective-domain"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin-effective-domain-2">effective
    domain</a>.

4.  If `effectiveDomain` is null, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:securityerror-4"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

5.  If the given value
    <a href="#is-a-registrable-domain-suffix-of-or-is-equal-to"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:is-a-registrable-domain-suffix-of-or-is-equal-to">is
    not a registrable domain suffix of and is not equal to</a>
    `effectiveDomain`, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:securityerror-5"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

6.  If the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:surrounding-agent"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:agent-cluster"
    data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>'s
    <a href="#is-origin-keyed"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:is-origin-keyed">is
    origin-keyed</a> is true, then return.

7.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:this-5"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-document-origin-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-origin-domain"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-origin-domain-2">domain</a>
    to the result of
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-parser"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:host-parser"
    data-x-internal="host-parser">parsing</a> the given value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To determine if a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value-string"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:scalar-value-string"
data-x-internal="scalar-value-string">scalar value string</a>
`hostSuffixString`
<span id="is-a-registrable-domain-suffix-of-or-is-equal-to" class="dfn"
lt="is a registrable domain suffix of or is equal to|is not a registrable domain suffix of
  and is not equal to" export="">is a registrable domain suffix of or is
equal to</span> a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-host"
data-x-internal="concept-host">host</a> `originalHost`:

1.  If `hostSuffixString` is the empty string, then return false.

2.  Let `hostSuffix` be the result of
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-parser"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:host-parser-2"
    data-x-internal="host-parser">parsing</a> `hostSuffixString`.

3.  If `hostSuffix` is failure, then return false.

4.  If `hostSuffix` does not
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-equals"
    id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:host-equals"
    data-x-internal="host-equals">equal</a> `originalHost`, then:

    1.  If `hostSuffix` or `originalHost` is not a
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-domain"
        id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-domain"
        data-x-internal="concept-domain">domain</a>, then return false.

        This excludes
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host"
        id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:concept-host-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-host">hosts</a> that are
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ip-address"
        id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:ip-address"
        data-x-internal="ip-address">IP addresses</a>.

    2.  If `hostSuffix`, prefixed by U+002E (.), does not match the end
        of `originalHost`, then return false.

    3.  If any of the following are true:

        - `hostSuffix`
          <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-equals"
          id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:host-equals-2"
          data-x-internal="host-equals">equals</a> `hostSuffix`'s
          <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-public-suffix"
          id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:public-suffix"
          data-x-internal="public-suffix">public suffix</a>; or

        - `hostSuffix`, prefixed by U+002E (.), matches the end of
          `originalHost`'s
          <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-public-suffix"
          id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:public-suffix-2"
          data-x-internal="public-suffix">public suffix</a>,

        then return false. [\[URL\]](#refsURL)

    4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:assert"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `originalHost`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-public-suffix"
        id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:public-suffix-3"
        data-x-internal="public-suffix">public suffix</a>, prefixed by
        U+002E (.), matches the end of `hostSuffix`.

5.  Return true.

</div>

<div id="example-registrable-domain-suffix" class="example">

<a href="#example-registrable-domain-suffix" class="self-link"></a>

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
| `hostSuffixString` | `originalHost` | Outcome of <a href="#is-a-registrable-domain-suffix-of-or-is-equal-to"
id="relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction:is-a-registrable-domain-suffix-of-or-is-equal-to-2">is
a registrable domain suffix of or is equal to</a> | Notes |
| "`0.0.0.0`" | `0.0.0.0` | ✅ |  |
| "`0x10203`" | `0.1.2.3` | ✅ |  |
| "`[0::1]`" | `::1` | ✅ |  |
| "`example.com`" | `example.com` | ✅ |  |
| "`example.com`" | `example.com.` | ❌ | Trailing dot is significant. |
| "`example.com.`" | `example.com` | ❌ |  |
| "`example.com`" | `www.example.com` | ✅ |  |
| "`com`" | `example.com` | ❌ | At the time of writing, `com` is a public suffix. |
| "`example`" | `example` | ✅ |  |
| "`compute.amazonaws.com`" | `example.compute.amazonaws.com` | ❌ | At the time of writing, `*``.compute.amazonaws.com` is a public suffix. |
| "`example.compute.amazonaws.com`" | `www.example.compute.amazonaws.com` | ❌ |  |
| "`amazonaws.com`" | `www.example.compute.amazonaws.com` | ❌ |  |
| "`amazonaws.com`" | `test.amazonaws.com` | ✅ | At the time of writing, `amazonaws.com` is a registrable domain. |

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.1.1.3</span> The [`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) interface<a href="#the-origin-interface" class="self-link"></a>

The [`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) interface represents an
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin">origin</a>, allowing robust
<a href="#same-origin" id="the-origin-interface:same-origin">same
origin</a> and
<a href="#same-site" id="the-origin-interface:same-site">same site</a>
comparisons.

``` idl
[Exposed=*]
interface Origin {
  constructor();

  static Origin from(any value);

  readonly attribute boolean opaque;

  boolean isSameOrigin(Origin other);
  boolean isSameSite(Origin other);
};
```

[`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) objects have an associated
<span id="concept-origin-origin" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Origin">origin</span>, which holds an <a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-2">origin</a>.

<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
id="the-origin-interface:platform-object"
data-x-internal="platform-object">Platform objects</a> have an
<span id="extract-an-origin" class="dfn" dfn-for="platform object"
export="">extract an origin</span> operation, which returns null unless
otherwise specified.

<div algorithm="">

Objects implementing the [`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) interface's
<a href="#extract-an-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:extract-an-origin">extract an origin</a> steps
are to return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-origin-interface:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin">origin</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-origin-constructor" class="dfn" dfn-for="Origin"
dfn-type="constructor">`new Origin()`</span> constructor steps are to
set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-origin-interface:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-2">origin</a> to a unique
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The static <span id="dom-origin-from" class="dfn" dfn-for="Origin"
dfn-type="method">`from(``value``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If `value` is a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object"
    id="the-origin-interface:platform-object-2"
    data-x-internal="platform-object">platform object</a>:

    1.  Let `origin` be the result of executing `value`'s
        <a href="#extract-an-origin"
        id="the-origin-interface:extract-an-origin-2">extract an origin</a>
        operation.

    2.  If `origin` is not null, then return a new
        [`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) object whose
        <a href="#concept-origin-origin"
        id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-3">origin</a> is
        `origin`.

2.  If `value` is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
    id="the-origin-interface:string" data-x-internal="string">string</a>:

    1.  Let `parsedURL` be the result of
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser"
        id="the-origin-interface:basic-url-parser"
        data-x-internal="basic-url-parser">basic URL parsing</a>
        `value`.

    2.  If `parsedURL` is not failure, then return a new
        [`Origin`](#dom-origin-interface) object whose
        <a href="#concept-origin-origin"
        id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-4">origin</a> is
        set to `parsedURL`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
        id="the-origin-interface:concept-url-origin"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a>.

3.  Throw a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
    id="the-origin-interface:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-origin-opaque" class="dfn" dfn-for="Origin"
dfn-type="attribute">`opaque`</span> getter steps are to return true if
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-origin-interface:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-5">origin</a> is an
<a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-opaque-2">opaque origin</a>;
otherwise false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-origin-issameorigin" class="dfn" dfn-for="Origin"
dfn-type="method">`isSameOrigin(``other``)`</span> method steps are to
return true if <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-origin-interface:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-6">origin</a> is
<a href="#same-origin" id="the-origin-interface:same-origin-2">same
origin</a> with `other`'s <a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-7">origin</a>; otherwise
false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-origin-issamesite" class="dfn" dfn-for="Origin"
dfn-type="method">`isSameSite(``other``)`</span> method steps are to
return true if <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-origin-interface:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-8">origin</a> is
<a href="#same-site" id="the-origin-interface:same-site-2">same site</a>
with `other`'s <a href="#concept-origin-origin"
id="the-origin-interface:concept-origin-origin-9">origin</a>; otherwise
false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">7.1.2</span> <span id="origin-isolation"></span>Origin-keyed agent clusters<a href="#origin-keyed-agent-clusters" class="self-link"></a>

`window.`<a href="#dom-originagentcluster"
id="dom-originagentcluster-dev"><code>originAgentCluster</code></a>  
Returns true if this [`Window`](#window) belongs to an
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a> which is
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:concept-origin">origin</a>-<a href="#agent-cluster-key"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-key">keyed</a>, in the
manner described in this section.

A [`Document`](#document) delivered over a <a href="#secure-context"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:secure-context">secure context</a> can
request that it be placed in an <a href="#concept-origin"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:concept-origin-2">origin</a>-<a href="#agent-cluster-key"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-key-2">keyed</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-2"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>, by using the
\`<span id="origin-agent-cluster" class="dfn"
dfn-type="http-header">`Origin-Agent-Cluster`</span>\` HTTP response
header. This header is a <a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:http-structured-header"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header">structured header</a> whose
value must be a <a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#boolean"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:http-structured-header-boolean"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-boolean">boolean</a>.
[\[STRUCTURED-FIELDS\]](#refsSTRUCTURED-FIELDS)

Per the processing model in the
<a href="#initialise-the-document-object"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:initialise-the-document-object">create
and initialize a new <code>Document</code> object</a>, values that are
not the <a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#boolean"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:http-structured-header-boolean-2"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-boolean">structured header
boolean</a> true value (i.e., \``?1`\`) will be ignored.

The consequences of using this header are that the resulting
[`Document`](#document)'s <a href="#agent-cluster-key"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-key-3">agent cluster
key</a> is its
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:concept-document-origin"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, instead of the
<a href="#obtain-a-site"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:obtain-a-site">corresponding site</a>.
In terms of observable effects, this means that attempting to [relax the
same-origin restriction](#relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) using
[`document.domain`](#dom-document-domain) will instead do nothing, and
it will not be possible to send
<a href="https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#module"
data-x-internal="webassembly.module"><code
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:webassembly.module">WebAssembly.Module</code></a>
objects to cross-origin [`Document`](#document)s (even if they are
<a href="#same-site" id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:same-site">same
site</a>). Behind the scenes, this isolation can allow user agents to
allocate implementation-specific resources corresponding to
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-3"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent clusters</a>, such as processes or
threads, more efficiently.

Note that within a <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:browsing-context-group">browsing context
group</a>, the \`[`Origin-Agent-Cluster`](#origin-agent-cluster)\`
header can never cause same-origin [`Document`](#document) objects to
end up in different
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-4"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent clusters</a>, even if one sends
the header and the other doesn't. This is prevented by means of the
<a href="#historical-agent-cluster-key-map"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:historical-agent-cluster-key-map">historical
agent cluster key map</a>.

This means that the [`originAgentCluster`](#dom-originagentcluster)
getter can return false, even if the header is set, if the header was
omitted on a previously-loaded same-origin page in the same
<a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:browsing-context-group-2">browsing
context group</a>. Similarly, it can return true even when the header is
not set.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-originagentcluster" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="attribute">`originAgentCluster`</span> getter steps are to
return the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:surrounding-agent"
data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-5"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>'s
<a href="#is-origin-keyed"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:is-origin-keyed">is origin-keyed</a>.

</div>

[`Document`](#document)s with an <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a>
can be considered unconditionally origin-keyed; for them the header has
no effect, and the [`originAgentCluster`](#dom-originagentcluster)
getter will always return true.

Similarly, [`Document`](#document)s whose
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-6"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>'s
<a href="#agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation"
id="origin-keyed-agent-clusters:agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation">cross-origin
isolation mode</a> is not "[`none`](#cross-origin-isolation-none)" are
automatically origin-keyed. The
\`[`Origin-Agent-Cluster`](#origin-agent-cluster)\` header might be
useful as an additional hint to implementations about resource
allocation, since the
\`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`](#cross-origin-opener-policy-2)\` and
\`[`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`](#cross-origin-embedder-policy)\`
headers used to achieve cross-origin isolation are more about ensuring
that everything in the same address space opts in to being there. But
adding it would have no additional observable effects on author code.

#### <span class="secno">7.1.3</span> Cross-origin opener policies<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policies" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="cross-origin-opener-policy-value" class="dfn">opener policy
value</span> allows a document which is navigated to in a
<a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context">top-level
browsing context</a> to force the creation of a new
<a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context-2">top-level
browsing context</a>, and a corresponding <a href="#tlbc-group"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:tlbc-group">group</a>. The possible
values are:

"<span id="coop-unsafe-none" class="dfn">`unsafe-none`</span>"  
This is the (current) default and means that the document will occupy
the same <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context-3">top-level
browsing context</a> as its predecessor, unless that document specified
a different <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy">opener
policy</a>.

"<span id="coop-same-origin-allow-popups" class="dfn">`same-origin-allow-popups`</span>"  
This forces the creation of a new <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context-4">top-level
browsing context</a> for the document, unless its predecessor specified
the same <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-2">opener
policy</a> and they are <a href="#same-origin"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:same-origin">same origin</a>.

"<span id="coop-same-origin" class="dfn">`same-origin`</span>"  
This behaves the same as
"[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)", with the
addition that any <a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:auxiliary-browsing-context">auxiliary
browsing context</a> created needs to contain <a href="#same-origin"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:same-origin-2">same origin</a>
documents that also have the same <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-3">opener
policy</a> or it will appear closed to the opener.

"<span id="coop-same-origin-plus-coep" class="dfn">`same-origin-plus-COEP`</span>"  
This behaves the same as "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)", with the
addition that it sets the (new) <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context-5">top-level
browsing context</a>'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:tlbc-group-2">group</a>'s
<a href="#bcg-cross-origin-isolation"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:bcg-cross-origin-isolation">cross-origin
isolation mode</a> to one of
"[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" or
"[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)".

"[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)" cannot be
directly set via the
\`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`](#cross-origin-opener-policy-2)\`
header, but results from a combination of setting both
\`<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-2"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-2-3"><code>Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy</code></a>`: `<a href="#coop-same-origin"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:coop-same-origin-2"><code>same-origin</code></a>\`
and a
\`[`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`](#cross-origin-embedder-policy)\`
header whose value is <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation">compatible
with cross-origin isolation</a> together.

"<span id="coop-noopener-allow-popups" class="dfn">`noopener-allow-popups`</span>"  
This forces the creation of a new <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:top-level-browsing-context-6">top-level
browsing context</a> for the document, regardless of its predecessor.

<div class="note">

While including a [`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)
value severs the opener relationship between the document on which it is
applied and its opener, it does not create a robust security boundary
between those same-origin documents.

Other risks from same-origin applications include:

- Same-origin requests fetching the document's content — could be
  mitigated through Fetch Metadata filtering.
  [\[FETCHMETADATA\]](#refsFETCHMETADATA)

- Same-origin framing - could be mitigated through
  [`X-Frame-Options`](#x-frame-options) or CSP
  <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors"
  data-x-internal="frame-ancestors-directive"><code
  id="cross-origin-opener-policies:frame-ancestors-directive">frame-ancestors</code></a>.

- JavaScript accessible cookies - can be mitigated by ensuring all
  cookies are `httponly`.

- [`localStorage`](#dom-localstorage) access to sensitive data.

- Service worker installation.

- [Cache API](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#cache) manipulation
  or access to sensitive data. [\[SW\]](#refsSW)

- `postMessage` or [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) messaging
  that exposes sensitive information.

- Autofill which may not require user interaction for same-origin
  documents.

Developers using [`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)
need to make sure that their sensitive applications don't rely on
client-side features accessible to other same-origin documents, e.g.,
[`localStorage`](#dom-localstorage) and other client-side storage APIs,
[`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) and related same-origin
communication mechanisms. They also need to make sure that their
server-side endpoints don't return sensitive data to non-navigation
requests, whose response content is accessible to same-origin documents.

</div>

An <span id="cross-origin-opener-policy" class="dfn">opener
policy</span> consists of:

- A <span id="coop-struct-value" class="dfn">value</span>, which is an
  <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-value"
  id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-value">opener
  policy value</a>, initially "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)".

- A <span id="coop-struct-report-endpoint" class="dfn">reporting
  endpoint</span>, which is string or null, initially null.

- A <span id="coop-struct-report-only-value" class="dfn">report-only
  value</span>, which is an <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-value"
  id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-value-2">opener
  policy value</a>, initially "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)".

- A <span id="coop-struct-report-only-endpoint" class="dfn">report-only
  reporting endpoint</span>, which is a string or null, initially null.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="matching-coop" class="dfn">match opener policy
values</span>, given an <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-value"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-value-3">opener
policy value</a> `documentCOOP`, an <a href="#concept-origin"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:concept-origin">origin</a>
`documentOrigin`, an <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-value"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:cross-origin-opener-policy-value-4">opener
policy value</a> `responseCOOP`, and an <a href="#concept-origin"
id="cross-origin-opener-policies:concept-origin-2">origin</a>
`responseOrigin`:

1.  If `documentCOOP` is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)" and
    `responseCOOP` is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)", then return
    true.

2.  If `documentCOOP` is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)" or
    `responseCOOP` is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)", then return
    false.

3.  If `documentCOOP` is `responseCOOP` and `documentOrigin` is
    <a href="#same-origin"
    id="cross-origin-opener-policies:same-origin-3">same origin</a> with
    `responseOrigin`, then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.1.3.1</span> The headers<a href="#the-coop-headers" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "The HTTP Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) response header allows you to ensure a top-level document does not share a browsing context group with cross-origin documents.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox79+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari15.2+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome83+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera no">OperaNo</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge83+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android no">WebView
AndroidNo</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android no">Opera AndroidNo</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

A [`Document`](#document)'s <a href="#concept-document-coop"
id="the-coop-headers:concept-document-coop">cross-origin opener
policy</a> is derived from the \`<span id="cross-origin-opener-policy-2"
class="dfn" dfn-type="http-header">`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`</span>\`
and \`<span id="cross-origin-opener-policy-report-only" class="dfn"
dfn-type="http-header">`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only`</span>\`
HTTP response headers. These headers are
<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html"
id="the-coop-headers:http-structured-header"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header">structured headers</a> whose
value must be a <a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#token"
id="the-coop-headers:http-structured-header-token"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-token">token</a>.
[\[STRUCTURED-FIELDS\]](#refsSTRUCTURED-FIELDS)

The valid <a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#token"
id="the-coop-headers:http-structured-header-token-2"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-token">token</a> values are the
<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-value"
id="the-coop-headers:cross-origin-opener-policy-value">opener policy
values</a>. The token may also have attached
<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#param"
id="the-coop-headers:http-structured-header-parameters"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-parameters">parameters</a>; of
these, the "<span id="coop-report-to" class="dfn">`report-to`</span>"
parameter can have a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
id="the-coop-headers:valid-url-string"
data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL string</a> identifying an
appropriate reporting endpoint. [\[REPORTING\]](#refsREPORTING)

Per the processing model described below, user agents will ignore this
header if it contains an invalid value. Likewise, user agents will
ignore this header if the value cannot be parsed as a
<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#token"
id="the-coop-headers:http-structured-header-token-3"
data-x-internal="http-structured-header-token">token</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="obtain-coop" class="dfn">obtain an opener policy</span>
given a <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
id="the-coop-headers:concept-response"
data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response` and an
<a href="#environment" id="the-coop-headers:environment">environment</a>
`reservedEnvironment`:

1.  Let `policy` be a new <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
    id="the-coop-headers:cross-origin-opener-policy">opener policy</a>.

2.  If `reservedEnvironment` is a <a href="#non-secure-context"
    id="the-coop-headers:non-secure-context">non-secure context</a>,
    then return `policy`.

3.  Let `parsedItem` be the result of <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-structured-header"
    id="the-coop-headers:getting-a-structured-field-value"
    data-x-internal="getting-a-structured-field-value">getting a structured
    field value</a> given
    \`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`](#cross-origin-opener-policy-2)\`
    and "`item`" from `response`'s
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list"
    id="the-coop-headers:concept-response-header-list"
    data-x-internal="concept-response-header-list">header list</a>.

4.  If `parsedItem` is not null, then:

    1.  If `parsedItem`\[0\] is "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)",
        then:

        1.  Let `coep` be the result of
            <a href="#obtain-an-embedder-policy"
            id="the-coop-headers:obtain-an-embedder-policy">obtaining a cross-origin
            embedder policy</a> from `response` and
            `reservedEnvironment`.

        2.  If `coep`'s <a href="#embedder-policy-value-2"
            id="the-coop-headers:embedder-policy-value-2">value</a> is
            <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="the-coop-headers:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation">compatible
            with cross-origin isolation</a>, then set `policy`'s
            <a href="#coop-struct-value"
            id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-value">value</a> to
            "[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)".

        3.  Otherwise, set `policy`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
            id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-value-2">value</a> to
            "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)".

    2.  If `parsedItem`\[0\] is
        "[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)",
        then set `policy`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
        id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-value-3">value</a> to
        "[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)".

    3.  If `parsedItem`\[0\] is
        "[`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)", then
        set `policy`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
        id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-value-4">value</a> to
        "[`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)".

    4.  If `parsedItem`\[1\]\["[`report-to`](#coop-report-to)"\]
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="the-coop-headers:map-exists" data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>
        and it is a string, then set `policy`'s
        <a href="#coop-struct-report-endpoint"
        id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-report-endpoint">reporting endpoint</a>
        to `parsedItem`\[1\]\["[`report-to`](#coop-report-to)"\].

5.  Set `parsedItem` to the result of <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-structured-header"
    id="the-coop-headers:getting-a-structured-field-value-2"
    data-x-internal="getting-a-structured-field-value">getting a structured
    field value</a> given
    \`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only`](#cross-origin-opener-policy-report-only)\`
    and "`item`" from `response`'s
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list"
    id="the-coop-headers:concept-response-header-list-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-response-header-list">header list</a>.

6.  If `parsedItem` is not null, then:

    1.  If `parsedItem`\[0\] is "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)",
        then:

        1.  Let `coep` be the result of
            <a href="#obtain-an-embedder-policy"
            id="the-coop-headers:obtain-an-embedder-policy-2">obtaining a
            cross-origin embedder policy</a> from `response` and
            `reservedEnvironment`.

        2.  If `coep`'s <a href="#embedder-policy-value-2"
            id="the-coop-headers:embedder-policy-value-2-2">value</a> is
            <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="the-coop-headers:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation-2">compatible
            with cross-origin isolation</a> or `coep`'s
            <a href="#embedder-policy-report-only-value"
            id="the-coop-headers:embedder-policy-report-only-value">report-only
            value</a> is
            <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="the-coop-headers:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation-3">compatible
            with cross-origin isolation</a>, then set `policy`'s
            <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
            id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-report-only-value">report-only
            value</a> to
            "[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)".

            Report only COOP also considers report-only COEP to assign
            the special
            "[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)"
            value. This allows developers more freedom in the order of
            deployment of COOP and COEP.

        3.  Otherwise, set `policy`'s
            <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
            id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-report-only-value-2">report-only
            value</a> to "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)".

    2.  If `parsedItem`\[0\] is
        "[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)",
        then set `policy`'s <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
        id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-report-only-value-3">report-only
        value</a> to
        "[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)".

    3.  If `parsedItem`\[1\]\["[`report-to`](#coop-report-to)"\]
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="the-coop-headers:map-exists-2"
        data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a> and it is a string, then
        set `policy`'s <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-endpoint"
        id="the-coop-headers:coop-struct-report-only-endpoint">report-only
        reporting endpoint</a> to
        `parsedItem`\[1\]\["[`report-to`](#coop-report-to)"\].

7.  Return `policy`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.1.3.2</span> Browsing context group switches due to opener policy<a
href="#browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy"
class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-popup"
class="dfn">check if popup COOP values require a browsing context group
switch</span>, given two <a href="#concept-origin"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin">origins</a>
`responseOrigin` and `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, and two
<a href="#coop-struct-value"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value">opener
policy values</a> `responseCOOPValue` and `activeDocumentCOOPValue`:

1.  If `responseCOOPValue` is
    "[`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)", then
    return true.

2.  If all of the following are true:

    - `activeDocumentCOOPValue`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
      id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-2">value</a>
      is "[`same-origin-allow-popups`](#coop-same-origin-allow-popups)"
      or "[`noopener-allow-popups`](#coop-noopener-allow-popups)"; and

    - `responseCOOPValue` is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)",

    then return false.

3.  If the result of <a href="#matching-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:matching-coop">matching</a>
    `activeDocumentCOOPValue`, `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`,
    `responseCOOPValue`, and `responseOrigin` is true, then return
    false.

4.  Return true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value"
class="dfn">check if COOP values require a browsing context group
switch</span>, given a boolean `isInitialAboutBlank`, two
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin-2">origins</a>
`responseOrigin` and `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, and two
<a href="#coop-struct-value"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-3">opener
policy values</a> `responseCOOPValue` and `activeDocumentCOOPValue`:

1.  If `isInitialAboutBlank` is true, then return the result of
    <a href="#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-popup"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-popup">checking
    if popup COOP values requires a browsing context group switch</a>
    with `responseOrigin`, `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`,
    `responseCOOPValue`, and `activeDocumentCOOPValue`.

2.  Here we are dealing with a non-popup navigation.

    If the result of <a href="#matching-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:matching-coop-2">matching</a>
    `activeDocumentCOOPValue`, `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`,
    `responseCOOPValue`, and `responseOrigin` is true, then return
    false.

3.  Return true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="check-bcg-switch-navigation-report-only" class="dfn">check
if enforcing report-only COOP would require a browsing context group
switch</span>, given a boolean `isInitialAboutBlank`, two
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin-3">origins</a>
`responseOrigin`, `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, and two
<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:cross-origin-opener-policy">opener
policies</a> `responseCOOP` and `activeDocumentCOOP`:

1.  If the result of
    <a href="#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value">checking
    if COOP values require a browsing context group switch</a> given
    `isInitialAboutBlank`, `responseOrigin`,
    `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, `responseCOOP`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-report-only-value">report-only
    value</a>, and `activeDocumentCOOPReportOnly`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-report-only-value-2">report-only
    value</a> is false, then return false.

    Matching report-only policies allows a website to specify the same
    report-only opener policy on all its pages and not receive violation
    reports for navigations between these pages.

2.  If the result of
    <a href="#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-2">checking
    if COOP values require a browsing context group switch</a> given
    `isInitialAboutBlank`, `responseOrigin`,
    `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, `responseCOOP`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-4">value</a>,
    and `activeDocumentCOOPReportOnly`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-report-only-value-3">report-only
    value</a> is true, then return true.

3.  If the result of
    <a href="#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-3">checking
    if COOP values require a browsing context group switch</a> given
    `isInitialAboutBlank`, `responseOrigin`,
    `activeDocumentNavigationOrigin`, `responseCOOP`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-report-only-value-4">report-only
    value</a>, and `activeDocumentCOOPReportOnly`'s
    <a href="#coop-struct-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-5">value</a>
    is true, then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

An <span id="coop-enforcement-result" class="dfn">opener policy
enforcement result</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:struct"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> with the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:struct-item"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

- A boolean <span id="coop-enforcement-bcg-switch" class="dfn">needs a
  browsing context group switch</span>, initially false.

- A boolean <span id="coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only"
  class="dfn">would need a browsing context group switch due to
  report-only</span>, initially false.

- A <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:url"
  data-x-internal="url">URL</a> <span id="coop-enforcement-url"
  class="dfn">url</span>.

- An <a href="#concept-origin"
  id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin-4">origin</a>
  <span id="coop-enforcement-origin" class="dfn">origin</span>.

- An <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
  id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:cross-origin-opener-policy-2">opener
  policy</a> <span id="coop-enforcement-coop" class="dfn">opener
  policy</span>.

- A boolean <span id="coop-enforcement-source" class="dfn">current
  context is navigation source</span>, initially false.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="coop-enforce" class="dfn">enforce a response's opener
policy</span>, given a <a href="#browsing-context"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context">browsing
context</a> `browsingContext`, a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:url-2"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `responseURL`, an
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin-5">origin</a>
`responseOrigin`, an <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:cross-origin-opener-policy-3">opener
policy</a> `responseCOOP`, an <a href="#coop-enforcement-result"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-result">opener
policy enforcement result</a> `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`, and a
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-request-referrer"
data-x-internal="concept-request-referrer">referrer</a> `referrer`:

1.  Let `newCOOPEnforcementResult` be a new
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-result"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-result-2">opener
    policy enforcement result</a> with

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch">needs
    a browsing context group switch</a>  
    `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-2">needs
    a browsing context group switch</a>

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only">would
    need a browsing context group switch due to report-only</a>  
    `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only-2">would
    need a browsing context group switch due to report-only</a>

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-url"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-url">url</a>  
    `responseURL`

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin">origin</a>  
    `responseOrigin`

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-coop">opener
    policy</a>  
    `responseCOOP`

    <a href="#coop-enforcement-source"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-source">current
    context is navigation source</a>  
    true

2.  Let `isInitialAboutBlank` be `browsingContext`'s
    <a href="#active-document"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:active-document">active
    document</a>'s <a href="#is-initial-about:blank"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:is-initial-about:blank">is
    initial <code>about:blank</code></a>.

3.  If `isInitialAboutBlank` is true and `browsingContext`'s
    <a href="#browsing-context-initial-url"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context-initial-url">initial
    URL</a> is null, set `browsingContext`'s
    <a href="#browsing-context-initial-url"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context-initial-url-2">initial
    URL</a> to `responseURL`.

4.  If the result of
    <a href="#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value-4">checking
    if COOP values require a browsing context group switch</a> given
    `isInitialAboutBlank`, `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-coop-2">opener
    policy</a>'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-6">value</a>,
    `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-2">origin</a>,
    `responseCOOP`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-7">value</a>,
    and `responseOrigin` is true, then:

    1.  Set `newCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
        <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-3">needs
        a browsing context group switch</a> to true.

    2.  If `browsingContext`'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:tlbc-group">group</a>'s
        <a href="#browsing-context-set"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context-set">browsing
        context set</a>'s
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:list-size"
        data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is greater than 1, then:

        1.  <a href="#coop-violation-navigation-to"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-violation-navigation-to">Queue
            a violation report for browsing context group switch when navigating to
            a COOP response</a> with `responseCOOP`, "`enforce`",
            `responseURL`, `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-url"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-url-2">url</a>,
            `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-3">origin</a>,
            `responseOrigin`, and `referrer`.

        2.  <a href="#coop-violation-navigation-from"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-violation-navigation-from">Queue
            a violation report for browsing context group switch when navigating
            away from a COOP response</a> with
            `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-coop"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-coop-3">opener
            policy</a>, "`enforce`", `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-url"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-url-3">url</a>,
            `responseURL`, `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-4">origin</a>,
            `responseOrigin`, and `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-source"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-source-2">current
            context is navigation source</a>.

5.  If the result of <a href="#check-bcg-switch-navigation-report-only"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:check-bcg-switch-navigation-report-only">checking
    if enforcing report-only COOP would require a browsing context group
    switch</a> given `isInitialAboutBlank`, `responseOrigin`,
    `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-5">origin</a>,
    `responseCOOP`, and `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-coop-4">opener
    policy</a>, is true, then:

    1.  Set `newCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
        <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only-3">would
        need a browsing context group switch due to report-only</a> to
        true.

    2.  If `browsingContext`'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:tlbc-group-2">group</a>'s
        <a href="#browsing-context-set"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context-set-2">browsing
        context set</a>'s
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:list-size-2"
        data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is greater than 1, then:

        1.  <a href="#coop-violation-navigation-to"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-violation-navigation-to-2">Queue
            a violation report for browsing context group switch when navigating to
            a COOP response</a> with `responseCOOP`, "`reporting`",
            `responseURL`, `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-url"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-url-4">url</a>,
            `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-6">origin</a>,
            `responseOrigin`, and `referrer`.

        2.  <a href="#coop-violation-navigation-from"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-violation-navigation-from-2">Queue
            a violation report for browsing context group switch when navigating
            away from a COOP response</a> with
            `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-coop"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-coop-5">opener
            policy</a>, "`reporting`", `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-url"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-url-5">url</a>,
            `responseURL`, `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-origin"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-origin-7">origin</a>,
            `responseOrigin`, and `currentCOOPEnforcementResult`'s
            <a href="#coop-enforcement-source"
            id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-source-3">current
            context is navigation source</a>.

6.  Return `newCOOPEnforcementResult`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="obtain-browsing-context-navigation" class="dfn">obtain a
browsing context to use for a navigation response</span>, given
<a href="#navigation-params"
id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params">navigation
params</a> `navigationParams`:

1.  Let `browsingContext` be `navigationParams`'s
    <a href="#navigation-params-navigable"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-navigable">navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-bc"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:nav-bc">active
    browsing context</a>.

2.  If `browsingContext` is not a <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:top-level-browsing-context">top-level
    browsing context</a>, then return `browsingContext`.

3.  Let `coopEnforcementResult` be `navigationParams`'s
    <a href="#navigation-params-coop-enforcement-result"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-coop-enforcement-result">COOP
    enforcement result</a>.

4.  Let `swapGroup` be `coopEnforcementResult`'s
    <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-4">needs
    a browsing context group switch</a>.

5.  Let `sourceOrigin` be `browsingContext`'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:active-document-2">active
    document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>.

6.  Let `destinationOrigin` be `navigationParams`'s
    <a href="#navigation-params-origin"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-origin">origin</a>.

7.  If `sourceOrigin` is not <a href="#same-site"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:same-site">same
    site</a> with `destinationOrigin`:

    1.  If either of `sourceOrigin` or `destinationOrigin` have a
        <a href="#concept-origin-scheme"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-origin-scheme">scheme</a>
        that is not an
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:http(s)-scheme"
        data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a> and the user
        agent considers it necessary for `sourceOrigin` and
        `destinationOrigin` to be isolated from each other (for
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:implementation-defined"
        data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
        reasons), optionally set `swapGroup` to true.

        For example, if a user navigates from `about:settings` to
        `https://example.com`, the user agent could force a swap.

        [Issue \#10842](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10842)
        tracks settling on an interoperable behavior here, instead of
        letting this be optional.

    2.  If `navigationParams`'s
        <a href="#navigation-params-user-involvement"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-user-involvement">user
        involvement</a> is "[`browser UI`](#uni-browser-ui)", optionally
        set `swapGroup` to true.

        [Issue \#6356](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6356)
        tracks settling on an interoperable behavior here, instead of
        letting this be optional.

8.  If `browsingContext`'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:tlbc-group-3">group</a>'s
    <a href="#browsing-context-set"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:browsing-context-set-3">browsing
    context set</a>'s <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:list-size-3"
    data-x-internal="list-size">size</a> is 1, optionally set
    `swapGroup` to true.

    Some implementations swap browsing context groups here for
    performance reasons.

    The check for other contexts that could script this one is not
    sufficient to prevent differences in behavior that could affect a
    web page. Even if there are currently no other contexts, the
    destination page could open a window, then if the user navigates
    back, the previous page could expect to be able to script the opened
    window. Doing a swap here would break that use case.

9.  If `swapGroup` is false, then:

    1.  If `coopEnforcementResult`'s
        <a href="#coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-enforcement-bcg-switch-report-only-4">would
        need a browsing context group switch due to report-only</a> is
        true, set `browsingContext`'s
        <a href="#virtual-browsing-context-group-id"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:virtual-browsing-context-group-id">virtual
        browsing context group ID</a> to a new unique identifier.

    2.  Return `browsingContext`.

10. Let `newBrowsingContext` be the first return value of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-top-level-browsing-context"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:creating-a-new-top-level-browsing-context">creating
    a new top-level browsing context and document</a>.

    In this case we are going to perform a browsing context group swap.
    `browsingContext` will not be used by the new
    [`Document`](#document) that we are about to
    <a href="#initialise-the-document-object"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:initialise-the-document-object">create</a>.
    If it is not used by other [`Document`](#document)s either (such as
    ones in the back/forward cache), then the user agent might [destroy
    it](#a-browsing-context-is-discarded) at this point.

11. Let `navigationCOOP` be `navigationParams`'s
    <a href="#navigation-params-coop"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-coop">cross-origin
    opener policy</a>.

12. If `navigationCOOP`'s <a href="#coop-struct-value"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-8">value</a>
    is "[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)", then
    set `newBrowsingContext`'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:tlbc-group-4">group</a>'s
    <a href="#bcg-cross-origin-isolation"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:bcg-cross-origin-isolation">cross-origin
    isolation mode</a> to either
    "[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" or
    "[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)". The choice of
    which is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>.

    It is difficult on some platforms to provide the security properties
    required by the
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
    isolated capability</a>.
    "[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)" grants access to it
    and "[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" does not.

13. Let `sandboxFlags` be a
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-clone"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:list-clone"
    data-x-internal="list-clone">clone</a> of `navigationParams`'s
    <a href="#navigation-params-sandboxing"
    id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:navigation-params-sandboxing">final
    sandboxing flag set</a>.

14. If `sandboxFlags` is not empty, then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:assert"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `navigationCOOP`'s
        <a href="#coop-struct-value"
        id="browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy:coop-struct-value-9">value</a>
        is "[`unsafe-none`](#coop-unsafe-none)".

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
