id="jake-diagrams:tn-current-session-history-step-2">current session
history step</a> of the traversable, and all cells with bold-italic URLs
represent the <a href="#nav-current-history-entry"
id="jake-diagrams:nav-current-history-entry">current session history
entry</a> for that row's navigable.

Thus, the above Jake diagram depicts the following sequence of events:

0.  A <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="jake-diagrams:top-level-traversable-2">top-level traversable</a>
    is created, starting at the URL `/t-a`, with two
    <a href="#child-navigable" id="jake-diagrams:child-navigable-2">child
    navigables</a> starting at `/i-0-a` and `/i-1-a` respectively.

1.  The first child navigable is
    <a href="#navigate" id="jake-diagrams:navigate">navigated</a> to
    another document, with URL `/i-0-b`.

2.  The second child navigable is
    <a href="#navigate" id="jake-diagrams:navigate-2">navigated</a> to
    another document, with URL `/i-1-b`.

3.  The top-level traversable is
    <a href="#navigate" id="jake-diagrams:navigate-3">navigated</a> to
    the *same* document, updating its URL to `/t-a#foo`.

4.  The top-level traversable is
    <a href="#navigate" id="jake-diagrams:navigate-4">navigated</a> to
    another document, with URL `/t-b`. (Notice how this document, of
    course, does not carry over the old document's child navigables.)

5.  The traversable was <a href="#traverse-the-history-by-a-delta"
    id="jake-diagrams:traverse-the-history-by-a-delta">traversed by a
    delta</a> of −3, back to step 1.

<a href="#jake-diagram" id="jake-diagrams:jake-diagram">Jake
diagrams</a> are a powerful tool for visualizing the interactions of
multiple navigables, navigations, and traversals. They cannot capture
every possible interaction — for example, they only work with a single
level of nesting — but we will have ocassion to use them to illustrate
several complex situations throughout this standard.

<a href="#jake-diagram" id="jake-diagrams:jake-diagram-2">Jake
diagrams</a> are named after their creator, the inimitable Jake
Archibald.

##### <span class="secno">7.3.1.5</span> Related navigable collections<a href="#related-navigable-collections" class="self-link"></a>

It is often helpful in this standard's algorithms to look at collections
of <a href="#navigable"
id="related-navigable-collections:navigable">navigables</a> starting at
a given [`Document`](#document). This section contains a curated set of
algorithms for collecting those navigables.

The return values of these algorithms are ordered so that parents
appears before their children. Callers rely on this ordering.

Starting with a [`Document`](#document), rather than a
<a href="#navigable"
id="related-navigable-collections:navigable-2">navigable</a>, is
generally better because it makes the caller cognizant of whether they
are starting with a <a href="#fully-active"
id="related-navigable-collections:fully-active">fully active</a>
[`Document`](#document) or not. Although non-<a href="#fully-active"
id="related-navigable-collections:fully-active-2">fully active</a>
[`Document`](#document)s do have ancestor and descendant navigables,
they often behave as if they don't (e.g., in the
[`window.parent`](#dom-parent) getter).

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="ancestor-navigables" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
export="">ancestor navigables</span> of a [`Document`](#document)
`document` are given by these steps:

1.  Let `navigable` be `document`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="related-navigable-collections:node-navigable">node navigable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-parent"
    id="related-navigable-collections:nav-parent">parent</a>.

2.  Let `ancestors` be an empty list.

3.  While `navigable` is not null:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-prepend"
        id="related-navigable-collections:list-prepend"
        data-x-internal="list-prepend">Prepend</a> `navigable` to
        `ancestors`.

    2.  Set `navigable` to `navigable`'s <a href="#nav-parent"
        id="related-navigable-collections:nav-parent-2">parent</a>.

4.  Return `ancestors`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="inclusive-ancestor-navigables" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">inclusive ancestor navigables</span> of a
[`Document`](#document) `document` are given by these steps:

1.  Let `navigables` be `document`'s <a href="#ancestor-navigables"
    id="related-navigable-collections:ancestor-navigables">ancestor
    navigables</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-append"
    data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `document`'s
    <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="related-navigable-collections:node-navigable-2">node navigable</a>
    to `navigables`.

3.  Return `navigables`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="descendant-navigables" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
export="">descendant navigables</span> of a [`Document`](#document)
`document` are given by these steps:

1.  Let `navigables` be new
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list" data-x-internal="list">list</a>.

2.  Let `navigableContainers` be a
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-2"
    data-x-internal="list">list</a> of all <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-descendant"
    id="related-navigable-collections:shadow-including-descendant"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-descendant">shadow-including
    descendants</a> of `document` that are
    <a href="#navigable-container"
    id="related-navigable-collections:navigable-container">navigable
    containers</a>, in <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order"
    id="related-navigable-collections:shadow-including-tree-order"
    data-x-internal="shadow-including-tree-order">shadow-including tree
    order</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `navigableContainer` of
    `navigableContainers`:

    1.  If `navigableContainer`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="related-navigable-collections:content-navigable">content
        navigable</a> is null, then continue.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend"
        id="related-navigable-collections:list-extend"
        data-x-internal="list-extend">Extend</a> `navigables` with
        `navigableContainer`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="related-navigable-collections:content-navigable-2">content
        navigable</a>'s <a href="#nav-document"
        id="related-navigable-collections:nav-document">active document</a>'s
        <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
        id="related-navigable-collections:inclusive-descendant-navigables">inclusive
        descendant navigables</a>.

4.  Return `navigables`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="inclusive-descendant-navigables" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Document" export="">inclusive descendant navigables</span> of a
[`Document`](#document) `document` are given by these steps:

1.  Let `navigables` be « `document`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="related-navigable-collections:node-navigable-3">node navigable</a>
    ».

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-extend-2"
    data-x-internal="list-extend">Extend</a> `navigables` with
    `document`'s <a href="#descendant-navigables"
    id="related-navigable-collections:descendant-navigables">descendant
    navigables</a>.

3.  Return `navigables`.

</div>

These descendant-collecting algorithms are described as looking at the
DOM tree of descendant [`Document`](#document) objects. In reality, this
is often not feasible since the DOM tree can be in another process from
the caller of the algorithm. Instead, implementations generally
replicate the appropriate trees across processes.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="document-tree-child-navigables" class="dfn">document-tree
child navigables</span> of a [`Document`](#document) `document` are
given by these steps:

1.  If `document`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="related-navigable-collections:node-navigable-4">node navigable</a>
    is null, then return the empty list.

2.  Let `navigables` be new
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-3"
    data-x-internal="list">list</a>.

3.  Let `navigableContainers` be a
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-4"
    data-x-internal="list">list</a> of all
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant"
    id="related-navigable-collections:descendant"
    data-x-internal="descendant">descendants</a> of `document` that are
    <a href="#navigable-container"
    id="related-navigable-collections:navigable-container-2">navigable
    containers</a>, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="related-navigable-collections:tree-order"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="related-navigable-collections:list-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `navigableContainer` of
    `navigableContainers`:

    1.  If `navigableContainer`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="related-navigable-collections:content-navigable-3">content
        navigable</a> is null, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="related-navigable-collections:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="related-navigable-collections:list-append-2"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `navigableContainer`'s
        <a href="#content-navigable"
        id="related-navigable-collections:content-navigable-4">content
        navigable</a> to `navigables`.

5.  Return `navigables`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.3.1.6</span> Navigable destruction<a href="#garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts"
class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="destroy-a-child-navigable" class="dfn">destroy a child
navigable</span> given a <a href="#navigable-container"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:navigable-container">navigable
container</a> `container`:

1.  Let `navigable` be `container`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:content-navigable">content
    navigable</a>.

2.  If `navigable` is null, then return.

3.  Set `container`'s <a href="#content-navigable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:content-navigable-2">content
    navigable</a> to null.

4.  <a href="#inform-the-navigation-api-about-child-navigable-destruction"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:inform-the-navigation-api-about-child-navigable-destruction">Inform
    the navigation API about child navigable destruction</a> given
    `navigable`.

5.  <a href="#destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants">Destroy
    a document and its descendants</a> given `navigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-document"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-document">active
    document</a>.

6.  Let `parentDocState` be `container`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:node-navigable">node
    navigable</a>'s <a href="#nav-active-history-entry"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-active-history-entry">active
    session history entry</a>'s <a href="#she-document-state"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:she-document-state">document
    state</a>.

7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> the
    <a href="#nested-history"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nested-history">nested
    history</a> from `parentDocState`'s
    <a href="#document-state-nested-histories"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:document-state-nested-histories">nested
    histories</a> whose <a href="#nested-history-id"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nested-history-id">id</a>
    equals `navigable`'s <a href="#nav-id"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-id">id</a>.

8.  Let `traversable` be `container`'s <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:node-navigable-2">node
    navigable</a>'s <a href="#nav-traversable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-traversable">traversable
    navigable</a>.

9.  <a href="#tn-append-session-history-traversal-steps"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:tn-append-session-history-traversal-steps">Append
    the following session history traversal steps</a> to `traversable`:

    1.  <a href="#update-for-navigable-creation/destruction"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:update-for-navigable-creation/destruction">Update
        for navigable creation/destruction</a> given `traversable`.

10. Invoke <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed">WebDriver BiDi
    navigable destroyed</a> with `navigable`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="destroy-a-top-level-traversable" class="dfn">destroy</span>
a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:top-level-traversable">top-level
traversable</a> `traversable`:

1.  Let `browsingContext` be `traversable`'s <a href="#nav-bc"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-bc">active browsing
    context</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `historyEntry` in
    `traversable`'s <a href="#tn-session-history-entries"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:tn-session-history-entries">session
    history entries</a> <span class="XXX">in what order?</span>:

    1.  Let `document` be `historyEntry`'s <a href="#she-document"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:she-document">document</a>.

    2.  If `document` is not null, then
        <a href="#destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants-2">destroy
        a document and its descendants</a> given `document`.

3.  <a href="#bcg-remove"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:bcg-remove">Remove</a>
    `browsingContext`.

4.  Remove `traversable` from the user interface (e.g., close or hide
    its tab in a tabbed browser).

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:list-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `traversable` from the user
    agent's <a href="#top-level-traversable-set"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:top-level-traversable-set">top-level
    traversable set</a>.

6.  Invoke <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-navigable-destroyed">WebDriver BiDi
    navigable destroyed</a> with `traversable`.

</div>

User agents may <a href="#destroy-a-top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:destroy-a-top-level-traversable">destroy
a top-level traversable</a> at any time (typically, [in response to user
requests](#nav-traversal-ui)).

<div algorithm="">

<span id="close-a-browsing-context"></span>To
<span id="close-a-top-level-traversable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="top-level traversable" export="">close</span> a
<a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:top-level-traversable-2">top-level
traversable</a> `traversable`:

1.  If `traversable`'s <a href="#is-closing"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:is-closing">is closing</a>
    is true, then return.

2.  <a href="#definitely-close-a-top-level-traversable"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:definitely-close-a-top-level-traversable">Definitely
    close</a> `traversable`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="definitely-close-a-top-level-traversable"
class="dfn">definitely close</span> a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:top-level-traversable-3">top-level
traversable</a> `traversable`:

1.  Let `toUnload` be `traversable`'s <a href="#nav-document"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-document-2">active
    document</a>'s <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:inclusive-descendant-navigables">inclusive
    descendant navigables</a>.

2.  If the result of <a href="#checking-if-unloading-is-canceled"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:checking-if-unloading-is-canceled">checking
    if unloading is canceled</a> for `toUnload` is not "`continue`",
    then return.

3.  <a href="#tn-append-session-history-traversal-steps"
    id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:tn-append-session-history-traversal-steps-2">Append
    the following session history traversal steps</a> to `traversable`:

    1.  Let `afterAllUnloads` be an algorithm step which
        <a href="#destroy-a-top-level-traversable"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:destroy-a-top-level-traversable-2">destroys</a>
        `traversable`.

    2.  <a href="#unload-a-document-and-its-descendants"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:unload-a-document-and-its-descendants">Unload
        a document and its descendants</a> given `traversable`'s
        <a href="#nav-document"
        id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:nav-document-3">active
        document</a>, null, and `afterAllUnloads`.

</div>

The <a href="#close-a-top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:close-a-top-level-traversable">close</a>
vs. <a href="#definitely-close-a-top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:definitely-close-a-top-level-traversable-2">definitely
close</a> separation allows other specifications to call
<a href="#close-a-top-level-traversable"
id="garbage-collection-and-browsing-contexts:close-a-top-level-traversable-2">close</a>
and have it be a no-op if the top-level traversable is already closing
due to JavaScript code calling [`window.close()`](#dom-window-close).

##### <span class="secno">7.3.1.7</span> <span id="browsing-context-names"></span>Navigable target names<a href="#navigable-target-names" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable">Navigables</a> can be given
<a href="#nav-target" id="navigable-target-names:nav-target">target
names</a>, which are strings allowing certain APIs (such as
[`window.open()`](#dom-open) or the [`a`](#the-a-element) element's
[`target`](#attr-hyperlink-target) attribute) to target
<a href="#navigate" id="navigable-target-names:navigate">navigations</a>
at that navigable.

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="valid-navigable-target-name" class="dfn">valid navigable
target name</span> is any string with at least one character that does
not contain both an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-tab-or-newline"
id="navigable-target-names:ascii-tab-or-newline"
data-x-internal="ascii-tab-or-newline">ASCII tab or newline</a> and a
U+003C (\<), and it does not start with a U+005F (\_). (Names starting
with a U+005F (\_) are reserved for special keywords.)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="valid-navigable-target-name-or-keyword" class="dfn">valid
navigable target name or keyword</span> is any string that is either a
<a href="#valid-navigable-target-name"
id="navigable-target-names:valid-navigable-target-name">valid navigable
target name</a> or that is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for one of: `_blank`, `_self`, `_parent`, or `_top`.

</div>

These values have different meanings based on whether the page is
sandboxed or not, as summarized in the following (non-normative) table.
In this table, "current" means the <a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable-2">navigable</a> that the link or
script is in, "parent" means the
<a href="#nav-parent" id="navigable-target-names:nav-parent">parent</a>
of the <a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable-3">navigable</a> that the link or
script is in, "top" means the
<a href="#nav-top" id="navigable-target-names:nav-top">top-level
traversable</a> of the <a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable-4">navigable</a> that the link or
script is in, "new" means a new <a href="#traversable-navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:traversable-navigable">traversable
navigable</a> with a null <a href="#nav-parent"
id="navigable-target-names:nav-parent-2">parent</a> (which may use an
<a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
id="navigable-target-names:auxiliary-browsing-context">auxiliary
browsing context</a>, subject to various user preferences and user agent
policies), "none" means that nothing will happen, and "maybe new" means
the same as "new" if the
"[`allow-popups`](#attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups)" keyword is also
specified on the [`sandbox`](#attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute (or if the
user overrode the sandboxing), and the same as "none" otherwise.

| Keyword | Ordinary effect | Effect in an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) with... |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | `sandbox=""` | `sandbox="allow-top-navigation"` |
| none specified, for links and form submissions | current | current | current |
| empty string | current | current | current |
| `_blank` | new | maybe new | maybe new |
| `_self` | current | current | current |
| `_parent` if there isn't a parent | current | current | current |
| `_parent` if parent is also top | parent/top | none | parent/top |
| `_parent` if there is one and it's not top | parent | none | none |
| `_top` if top is current | current | current | current |
| `_top` if top is not current | top | none | top |
| name that doesn't exist | new | maybe new | maybe new |
| name that exists and is a descendant | specified descendant | specified descendant | specified descendant |
| name that exists and is current | current | current | current |
| name that exists and is an ancestor that is top | specified ancestor | none | specified ancestor/top |
| name that exists and is an ancestor that is not top | specified ancestor | none | none |
| other name that exists with common top | specified | none | none |
| name that exists with different top, if <a href="#familiar-with"
id="navigable-target-names:familiar-with">familiar</a> and <a href="#one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator"
id="navigable-target-names:one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator">one
permitted sandboxed navigator</a> | specified | specified | specified |
| name that exists with different top, if <a href="#familiar-with"
id="navigable-target-names:familiar-with-2">familiar</a> but not <a href="#one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator"
id="navigable-target-names:one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator-2">one
permitted sandboxed navigator</a> | specified | none | none |
| name that exists with different top, not <a href="#familiar-with"
id="navigable-target-names:familiar-with-3">familiar</a> | new | maybe new | maybe new |

<span class="small">Most of the restrictions on sandboxed browsing
contexts are applied by other algorithms, e.g. the <a href="#navigate"
id="navigable-target-names:navigate-2">navigation</a> algorithm, not
<a href="#the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable">the rules
for choosing a navigable</a> given below.</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="find-a-navigable-by-target-name" class="dfn">find a
navigable by target name</span> given a string `name` and a
<a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable-5">navigable</a>
`currentNavigable`:

1.  Let `currentDocument` be `currentNavigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-document" id="navigable-target-names:nav-document">active
    document</a>.

2.  Let `sourceSnapshotParams` be the result of
    <a href="#snapshotting-source-snapshot-params"
    id="navigable-target-names:snapshotting-source-snapshot-params">snapshotting
    source snapshot params</a> given `currentDocument`.

3.  Let `subtreesToSearch` be an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="navigable-target-names:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    choice of one of the following:

    - « `currentNavigable`'s <a href="#nav-traversable"
      id="navigable-target-names:nav-traversable">traversable navigable</a>,
      `currentNavigable` »

    - the <a href="#inclusive-ancestor-navigables"
      id="navigable-target-names:inclusive-ancestor-navigables">inclusive
      ancestor navigables</a> of `currentDocument`

    [Issue \#10848](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10848) tracks
    settling on one of these two possibilities, to achieve
    interoperability.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="navigable-target-names:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `subtreeToSearch` of
    `subtreesToSearch`, in reverse order:

    1.  Let `documentToSearch` be `subtreeToSearch`'s
        <a href="#nav-document"
        id="navigable-target-names:nav-document-2">active document</a>.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="navigable-target-names:list-iterate-2"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `navigable` of the
        <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
        id="navigable-target-names:inclusive-descendant-navigables">inclusive
        descendant navigables</a> of `documentToSearch`:

        1.  If `currentNavigable` is not <a href="#allowed-to-navigate"
            id="navigable-target-names:allowed-to-navigate">allowed by sandboxing to
            navigate</a> `navigable` given `sourceSnapshotParams`, then
            optionally
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="navigable-target-names:continue"
            data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

            [Issue \#10849](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10849)
            tracks making this check required, to achieve
            interoperability.

        2.  If `navigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-target" id="navigable-target-names:nav-target-2">target
            name</a> is `name`, then return `navigable`.

5.  Let `currentTopLevelBrowsingContext` be `currentNavigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc">active browsing
    context</a>'s
    <a href="#bc-tlbc" id="navigable-target-names:bc-tlbc">top-level
    browsing context</a>.

6.  Let `group` be `currentTopLevelBrowsingContext`'s
    <a href="#tlbc-group" id="navigable-target-names:tlbc-group">group</a>.

7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="navigable-target-names:list-iterate-3"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a>
    `topLevelBrowsingContext` of `group`'s
    <a href="#browsing-context-set"
    id="navigable-target-names:browsing-context-set">browsing context
    set</a>, in an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="navigable-target-names:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    order (the user agent should pick a consistent ordering, such as the
    most recently opened, most recently focused, or more closely
    related):

    [Issue \#10850](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10850) tracks
    picking a specific ordering, to achieve interoperability.

    1.  If `currentTopLevelBrowsingContext` is
        `topLevelBrowsingContext`, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="navigable-target-names:continue-2"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    2.  Let `documentToSearch` be `topLevelBrowsingContext`'s
        <a href="#active-document"
        id="navigable-target-names:active-document">active document</a>.

    3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="navigable-target-names:list-iterate-4"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `navigable` of the
        <a href="#inclusive-descendant-navigables"
        id="navigable-target-names:inclusive-descendant-navigables-2">inclusive
        descendant navigables</a> of `documentToSearch`:

        1.  If `currentNavigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-2">active browsing
            context</a> is not <a href="#familiar-with"
            id="navigable-target-names:familiar-with-4">familiar with</a>
            `navigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-3">active browsing
            context</a>, then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="navigable-target-names:continue-3"
            data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

        2.  If `currentNavigable` is not <a href="#allowed-to-navigate"
            id="navigable-target-names:allowed-to-navigate-2">allowed by sandboxing
            to navigate</a> `navigable` given `sourceSnapshotParams`,
            then optionally
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="navigable-target-names:continue-4"
            data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

            [Issue \#10849](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10849)
            tracks making this check required, to achieve
            interoperability.

        3.  If `navigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-target" id="navigable-target-names:nav-target-3">target
            name</a> is `name`, then return `navigable`.

8.  Return null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="the-rules-for-choosing-a-navigable" class="dfn">The rules for
choosing a navigable</span>, given a string `name`, a
<a href="#navigable"
id="navigable-target-names:navigable-6">navigable</a>
`currentNavigable`, and a boolean `noopener` are as follows:

1.  Let `chosen` be null.

2.  Let `windowType` be "`existing or none`".

3.  Let `sandboxingFlagSet` be `currentNavigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-document"
    id="navigable-target-names:nav-document-3">active document</a>'s
    <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="navigable-target-names:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing
    flag set</a>.

4.  If `name` is the empty string or an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "`_self`", then set `chosen` to `currentNavigable`.

5.  Otherwise, if `name` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "`_parent`", set `chosen` to `currentNavigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-parent"
    id="navigable-target-names:nav-parent-3">parent</a>, if any, and
    `currentNavigable` otherwise.

6.  Otherwise, if `name` is an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "`_top`", set `chosen` to `currentNavigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-traversable"
    id="navigable-target-names:nav-traversable-2">traversable navigable</a>.

7.  Otherwise, if `name` is not an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive-5"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
    match for "`_blank`" and `noopener` is false, then set `chosen` to
    the result of <a href="#find-a-navigable-by-target-name"
    id="navigable-target-names:find-a-navigable-by-target-name">finding a
    navigable by target name</a> given `name` and `currentNavigable`.

8.  If `chosen` is null, then a new <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="navigable-target-names:top-level-traversable">top-level
    traversable</a> is being requested, and what happens depends on the
    user agent's configuration and abilities — it is determined by the
    rules given for the first applicable option from the following list:

    If `currentNavigable`'s <a href="#nav-window" id="navigable-target-names:nav-window">active
    window</a> does not have <a href="#transient-activation"
    id="navigable-target-names:transient-activation">transient
    activation</a> and the user agent has been configured to not show popups (i.e., the user agent has a "popup blocker" enabled)  
    The user agent may inform the user that a popup has been blocked.

    If `sandboxingFlagSet` has the <a href="#sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag"
    id="navigable-target-names:sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
    auxiliary navigation browsing context flag</a> set  
    The user agent may report to a developer console that a popup has
    been blocked.

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will create a new <a href="#top-level-traversable"
    id="navigable-target-names:top-level-traversable-2">top-level
    traversable</a>  
    1.  <a href="#consume-user-activation"
        id="navigable-target-names:consume-user-activation">Consume user
        activation</a> of `currentNavigable`'s
        <a href="#nav-window" id="navigable-target-names:nav-window-2">active
        window</a>.

    2.  Set `windowType` to "`new and unrestricted`".

    3.  Let `currentDocument` be `currentNavigable`'s
        <a href="#nav-document"
        id="navigable-target-names:nav-document-4">active document</a>.

    4.  If `currentDocument`'s <a href="#concept-document-coop"
        id="navigable-target-names:concept-document-coop">opener policy</a>'s
        <a href="#coop-struct-value"
        id="navigable-target-names:coop-struct-value">value</a> is
        "[`same-origin`](#coop-same-origin)" or
        "[`same-origin-plus-COEP`](#coop-same-origin-plus-coep)", and
        `currentDocument`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
        id="navigable-target-names:concept-document-origin"
        data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is not
        <a href="#same-origin" id="navigable-target-names:same-origin">same
        origin</a> with `currentDocument`'s
        <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="navigable-target-names:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
        object</a>'s <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
        id="navigable-target-names:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
        origin</a>, then:

        1.  Set `noopener` to true.

        2.  Set `name` to "`_blank`".

        3.  Set `windowType` to "`new with no opener`".

        In the presence of an <a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy"
        id="navigable-target-names:cross-origin-opener-policy">opener policy</a>,
        nested documents that are cross-origin with their top-level
        browsing context's active document always set `noopener` to
        true.

    5.  Let `targetName` be the empty string.

    6.  If `name` is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
        id="navigable-target-names:ascii-case-insensitive-6"
        data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
        match for "`_blank`", then set `targetName` to `name`.

    7.  <div id="noopener">

        If `noopener` is true, then set `chosen` to the result of
        <a href="#creating-a-new-top-level-traversable"
        id="navigable-target-names:creating-a-new-top-level-traversable">creating
        a new top-level traversable</a> given null, `targetName`, and
        `currentNavigable`.

        </div>

    8.  Otherwise:

        1.  Set `chosen` to the result of
            <a href="#creating-a-new-top-level-traversable"
            id="navigable-target-names:creating-a-new-top-level-traversable-2">creating
            a new top-level traversable</a> given `currentNavigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-4">active browsing
            context</a>, `targetName`, and `currentNavigable`.

        2.  If `sandboxingFlagSet`'s
            <a href="#sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag"
            id="navigable-target-names:sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
            navigation browsing context flag</a> is set, then set
            `chosen`'s
            <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-5">active browsing
            context</a>'s <a href="#one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator"
            id="navigable-target-names:one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator-3">one
            permitted sandboxed navigator</a> to `currentNavigable`'s
            <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-6">active browsing
            context</a>.

    9.  If `sandboxingFlagSet`'s
        <a href="#sandbox-propagates-to-auxiliary-browsing-contexts-flag"
        id="navigable-target-names:sandbox-propagates-to-auxiliary-browsing-contexts-flag">sandbox
        propagates to auxiliary browsing contexts flag</a> is set, then
        all the flags that are set in `sandboxingFlagSet` must be set in
        `chosen`'s
        <a href="#nav-bc" id="navigable-target-names:nav-bc-7">active browsing
        context</a>'s <a href="#popup-sandboxing-flag-set"
        id="navigable-target-names:popup-sandboxing-flag-set">popup sandboxing
        flag set</a>.

    10. Set `chosen`'s <a href="#is-created-by-web-content"
        id="navigable-target-names:is-created-by-web-content">is created by web
        content</a> to true.

    If the newly created <a href="#navigable"
    id="navigable-target-names:navigable-7">navigable</a> `chosen` is
    immediately
    <a href="#navigate" id="navigable-target-names:navigate-3">navigated</a>,
    then the navigation will be done as a
    "[`replace`](#navigationhistorybehavior-replace)" navigation.

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will choose `currentNavigable`  
    Set `chosen` to `currentNavigable`.

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will not find a navigable  
    Do nothing.

    User agents are encouraged to provide a way for users to configure
    the user agent to always choose `currentNavigable`.

9.  Return `chosen` and `windowType`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">7.3.2</span> Browsing contexts<a href="#windows" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="browsing-context" class="dfn" export="">browsing
context</span> is a programmatic representation of a series of
documents, multiple of which can live within a single
<a href="#navigable" id="windows:navigable">navigable</a>. Each
<a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context">browsing
context</a> has a corresponding [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) object, as
well as the following:

- An <span id="opener-browsing-context" class="dfn" export="">opener
  browsing context</span>, a
  <a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-2">browsing
  context</a> or null, initially null.

- An <span id="opener-origin-at-creation" class="dfn">opener origin at
  creation</span>, an
  <a href="#concept-origin" id="windows:concept-origin">origin</a> or
  null, initially null.

- An <span id="is-popup" class="dfn">is popup</span> boolean, initially
  false.

  The only mandatory impact in this specification of
  <a href="#is-popup" id="windows:is-popup">is popup</a> is on the
  [`visible`](#dom-barprop-visible) getter of the relevant
  [`BarProp`](#barprop) objects. However, user agents might also use it
  for [user interface considerations](#nav-traversal-ui).

- An <span id="is-auxiliary" class="dfn">is auxiliary</span> boolean,
  initially false.

- An <span id="browsing-context-initial-url" class="dfn">initial
  URL</span>, a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url" id="windows:url"
  data-x-internal="url">URL</a> or null, initially null.

- A <span id="virtual-browsing-context-group-id" class="dfn">virtual
  browsing context group ID</span> integer, initially 0. This is used by
  <a href="#coop-struct-report-only-value"
  id="windows:coop-struct-report-only-value">opener policy reporting</a>,
  to keep track of the browsing context group switches that would have
  happened if the report-only policy had been enforced.

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-3">browsing
context</a>'s <span id="active-window" class="dfn">active window</span>
is its [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) object's
<a href="#concept-windowproxy-window"
id="windows:concept-windowproxy-window">[[Window]]</a> internal slot
value. A
<a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-4">browsing
context</a>'s <span id="active-document" class="dfn">active
document</span> is its
<a href="#active-window" id="windows:active-window">active window</a>'s
<a href="#concept-document-window"
id="windows:concept-document-window">associated
<code>Document</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-5">browsing
context</a>'s <span id="bc-traversable" class="dfn"
dfn-for="browsing context" export="">top-level traversable</span> is its
<a href="#active-document" id="windows:active-document">active
document</a>'s
<a href="#node-navigable" id="windows:node-navigable">node navigable</a>'s
<a href="#nav-top" id="windows:nav-top">top-level traversable</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-6">browsing
context</a> whose
<a href="#is-auxiliary" id="windows:is-auxiliary">is auxiliary</a> is
true is known as an <span id="auxiliary-browsing-context" class="dfn"
export="">auxiliary browsing context</span>. Auxiliary browsing contexts
are always <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="windows:top-level-browsing-context">top-level browsing contexts</a>.

</div>

It's unclear whether a separate
<a href="#is-auxiliary" id="windows:is-auxiliary-2">is auxiliary</a>
concept is necessary. In [issue
\#5680](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5680), it is indicated
that we may be able to simplify this by using whether or not the
<a href="#opener-browsing-context"
id="windows:opener-browsing-context">opener browsing context</a> is
null.

Modern specifications should avoid using the
<a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-7">browsing
context</a> concept in most cases, unless they are dealing with the
subtleties of [browsing context group
switches](#browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-cross-origin-opener-policy)
and <a href="#agent-cluster-map" id="windows:agent-cluster-map">agent
cluster allocation</a>. Instead, the [`Document`](#document) and
<a href="#navigable" id="windows:navigable-2">navigable</a> concepts are
usually more appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A <span id="concept-document-bc" class="dfn" dfn-for="Document"
lt="browsing context" export="">`Document`'s browsing context</span> is
a <a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-8">browsing
context</a> or null, initially null.

A [`Document`](#document) does not necessarily have a non-null
<a href="#concept-document-bc" id="windows:concept-document-bc">browsing
context</a>. In particular, data mining tools are likely to never
instantiate browsing contexts. A [`Document`](#document) created using
an API such as <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domimplementation-createdocument"
data-x-internal="dom-domimplementation-createdocument"><code
id="windows:dom-domimplementation-createdocument">createDocument()</code></a>
never has a non-null <a href="#concept-document-bc"
id="windows:concept-document-bc-2">browsing context</a>. And the
[`Document`](#document) originally created for an
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element, which has since been
<a href="#remove-an-element-from-a-document"
id="windows:remove-an-element-from-a-document">removed from the
document</a>, has no associated browsing context, since that browsing
context was
<a href="#destroy-a-document" id="windows:destroy-a-document">nulled
out</a>.

In general, there is a 1-to-1 mapping from the [`Window`](#window)
object to the [`Document`](#document) object, as long as the
[`Document`](#document) object has a non-null
<a href="#concept-document-bc"
id="windows:concept-document-bc-3">browsing context</a>. There is one
exception. A [`Window`](#window) can be reused for the presentation of a
second [`Document`](#document) in the same
<a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-9">browsing
context</a>, such that the mapping is then 1-to-2. This occurs when a
<a href="#browsing-context" id="windows:browsing-context-10">browsing
context</a> is <a href="#navigate" id="windows:navigate">navigated</a>
from the <a href="#is-initial-about:blank"
id="windows:is-initial-about:blank">initial <code>about:blank</code></a>
[`Document`](#document) to another, which will be done with
<a href="#navigationhistorybehavior-replace"
id="windows:navigationhistorybehavior-replace">replacement</a>.

##### <span class="secno">7.3.2.1</span> Creating browsing contexts<a href="#creating-browsing-contexts" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-new-browsing-context" class="dfn">create a new
browsing context and document</span>, given null or a
[`Document`](#document) object `creator`, null or an element `embedder`,
and a <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group">browsing context
group</a> `group`:

1.  Let `browsingContext` be a new <a href="#browsing-context"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:browsing-context">browsing context</a>.

2.  Let `unsafeContextCreationTime` be the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:unsafe-shared-current-time"
    data-x-internal="unsafe-shared-current-time">unsafe shared current
    time</a>.

3.  Let `creatorOrigin` be null.

4.  Let `creatorBaseURL` be null.

5.  <div id="creator-browsing-context">

    If `creator` is non-null, then:

    1.  Set `creatorOrigin` to `creator`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin"
        data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>.

    2.  Set `creatorBaseURL` to `creator`'s <a href="#document-base-url"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:document-base-url">document base URL</a>.

    3.  Set `browsingContext`'s
        <a href="#virtual-browsing-context-group-id"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:virtual-browsing-context-group-id">virtual
        browsing context group ID</a> to `creator`'s
        <a href="#concept-document-bc"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-bc">browsing context</a>'s
        <a href="#bc-tlbc" id="creating-browsing-contexts:bc-tlbc">top-level
        browsing context</a>'s
        <a href="#virtual-browsing-context-group-id"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:virtual-browsing-context-group-id-2">virtual
        browsing context group ID</a>.

    </div>

6.  Let `sandboxFlags` be the result of
    <a href="#determining-the-creation-sandboxing-flags"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:determining-the-creation-sandboxing-flags">determining
    the creation sandboxing flags</a> given `browsingContext` and
    `embedder`.

7.  <div id="about-blank-origin">

    Let `origin` be the result of <a href="#determining-the-origin"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:determining-the-origin">determining the
    origin</a> given [`about:blank`](#about:blank), `sandboxFlags`, and
    `creatorOrigin`.

    </div>

8.  Let `permissionsPolicy` be the result of <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#create-for-navigable"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:creating-a-permissions-policy"
    data-x-internal="creating-a-permissions-policy">creating a permissions
    policy</a> given `embedder` and `origin`.
    [\[PERMISSIONSPOLICY\]](#refsPERMISSIONSPOLICY)

9.  Let `agent` be the result of
    <a href="#obtain-similar-origin-window-agent"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:obtain-similar-origin-window-agent">obtaining
    a similar-origin window agent</a> given `origin`, `group`, and
    false.

10. Let `realm execution context` be the result of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-javascript-realm"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:creating-a-new-javascript-realm">creating
    a new realm</a> given `agent` and the following customizations:

    - For the global object, create a new [`Window`](#window) object.

    - For the global **this** binding, use `browsingContext`'s
      [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) object.

11. Let `topLevelCreationURL` be [`about:blank`](#about:blank) if
    `embedder` is null; otherwise `embedder`'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object">relevant
    settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-creation-url"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-environment-top-level-creation-url">top-level
    creation URL</a>.

12. Let `topLevelOrigin` be `origin` if `embedder` is null; otherwise
    `embedder`'s <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant
    settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
    origin</a>.

13. <a href="#set-up-a-window-environment-settings-object"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:set-up-a-window-environment-settings-object">Set
    up a window environment settings object</a> with
    [`about:blank`](#about:blank), `realm execution context`, null,
    `topLevelCreationURL`, and `topLevelOrigin`.

14. Let `loadTimingInfo` be a new <a href="#document-load-timing-info"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:document-load-timing-info">document load
    timing info</a> with its <a href="#navigation-start-time"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:navigation-start-time">navigation start
    time</a> set to the result of calling
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:coarsen-time"
    data-x-internal="coarsen-time">coarsen time</a> with
    `unsafeContextCreationTime` and the new
    <a href="#environment-settings-object"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:environment-settings-object">environment
    settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
    isolated capability</a>.

15. Let `document` be a new [`Document`](#document), with:

    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-type"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-type"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-type">type</a>  
    "`html`"

    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-content-type"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-content-type"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-content-type">content type</a>  
    "[`text/html`](#text/html)"

    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-mode"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-mode"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-mode">mode</a>  
    "`quirks`"

    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>  
    `origin`

    <a href="#concept-document-bc"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-bc-2">browsing
    context</a>  
    `browsingContext`

    <a href="#concept-document-permissions-policy"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-permissions-policy">permissions
    policy</a>  
    `permissionsPolicy`

    <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active
    sandboxing flag set</a>  
    `sandboxFlags`

    <a href="#load-timing-info"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:load-timing-info">load timing info</a>  
    `loadTimingInfo`

    <a href="#is-initial-about:blank"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:is-initial-about:blank">is initial
    <code>about:blank</code></a>  
    true

    <a href="#concept-document-about-base-url"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-about-base-url">about
    base URL</a>  
    `creatorBaseURL`

    <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots">allow
    declarative shadow roots</a>  
    true

    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-custom-element-registry"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:document-custom-element-registry"
    data-x-internal="document-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a>  
    a new [`CustomElementRegistry`](#customelementregistry) object

16. Let `iframeReferrerPolicy` be the result of
    <a href="#determining-the-iframe-element-referrer-policy"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:determining-the-iframe-element-referrer-policy">determining
    the <code>iframe</code> element referrer policy</a> given
    `embedder`.

17. Set `document`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list">internal
    ancestor origin objects list</a> to the result of running the
    <a href="#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps">internal
    ancestor origin objects list creation steps</a> given `document` and
    `iframeReferrerPolicy`.

18. Set `document`'s <a href="#concept-document-ancestor-origins-list"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-ancestor-origins-list">ancestor
    origins list</a> to the result of running the
    <a href="#ancestor-origins-list-creation-steps"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:ancestor-origins-list-creation-steps">ancestor
    origins list creation steps</a> given `document`.

19. If `creator` is non-null, then:

    1.  Set `document`'s <a href="#the-document&#39;s-referrer"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:the-document&#39;s-referrer">referrer</a>
        to the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-url-serializer"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
        `creator`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:the-document&#39;s-address"
        data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a>.

    2.  Set `document`'s <a href="#concept-document-policy-container"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-policy-container">policy
        container</a> to a <a href="#clone-a-policy-container"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:clone-a-policy-container">clone</a>
        of `creator`'s <a href="#concept-document-policy-container"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-policy-container-2">policy
        container</a>.

    3.  If `creator`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-3"
        data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is
        <a href="#same-origin" id="creating-browsing-contexts:same-origin">same
        origin</a> with `creator`'s <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object-3">relevant
        settings object</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-environment-top-level-origin-2">top-level
        origin</a>, then set `document`'s
        <a href="#concept-document-coop"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-coop">opener policy</a>
        to `creator`'s <a href="#concept-document-bc"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-bc-3">browsing
        context</a>'s
        <a href="#bc-tlbc" id="creating-browsing-contexts:bc-tlbc-2">top-level
        browsing context</a>'s <a href="#active-document"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:active-document">active document</a>'s
        <a href="#concept-document-coop"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-coop-2">opener
        policy</a>.

20. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:assert"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-url"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:the-document&#39;s-address-2"
    data-x-internal="the-document&#39;s-address">URL</a> and
    `document`'s <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object-4">relevant
    settings object</a>'s <a href="#concept-environment-creation-url"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-environment-creation-url">creation
    URL</a> are [`about:blank`](#about:blank).

21. Mark `document` as <a href="#ready-for-post-load-tasks"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:ready-for-post-load-tasks">ready for
    post-load tasks</a>.

22. <a href="#populate-with-html/head/body"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:populate-with-html/head/body">Populate
    with <code>html</code>/<code>head</code>/<code>body</code></a> given
    `document`.

23. <a href="#make-active" id="creating-browsing-contexts:make-active">Make
    active</a> `document`.

24. <a href="#completely-finish-loading"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:completely-finish-loading">Completely
    finish loading</a> `document`.

25. Return `browsingContext` and `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-new-top-level-browsing-context"
class="dfn">create a new top-level browsing context and document</span>:

1.  Let `group` and `document` be the result of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-browsing-context-group-and-document"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:creating-a-new-browsing-context-group-and-document">creating
    a new browsing context group and document</a>.

2.  Return `group`'s <a href="#browsing-context-set"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-set">browsing context
    set</a>\[0\] and `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-new-auxiliary-browsing-context"
class="dfn">create a new auxiliary browsing context and document</span>,
given a <a href="#browsing-context"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-2">browsing context</a>
`opener`:

1.  Let `openerTopLevelBrowsingContext` be `opener`'s
    <a href="#bc-traversable"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:bc-traversable">top-level traversable</a>'s
    <a href="#nav-bc" id="creating-browsing-contexts:nav-bc">active browsing
    context</a>.

2.  Let `group` be `openerTopLevelBrowsingContext`'s
    <a href="#tlbc-group"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:tlbc-group">group</a>.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:assert-2"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `group` is non-null, as
    <a href="#navigate"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:navigate">navigating</a> invokes this
    directly.

4.  Let `browsingContext` and `document` be the result of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-browsing-context"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:creating-a-new-browsing-context">creating
    a new browsing context and document</a> with `opener`'s
    <a href="#nav-document"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:nav-document">active document</a>,
    null, and `group`.

5.  Set `browsingContext`'s
    <a href="#is-auxiliary" id="creating-browsing-contexts:is-auxiliary">is
    auxiliary</a> to true.

6.  <a href="#bcg-append"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:bcg-append">Append</a>
    `browsingContext` to `group`.

7.  Set `browsingContext`'s <a href="#opener-browsing-context"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:opener-browsing-context">opener browsing
    context</a> to `opener`.

8.  Set `browsingContext`'s <a href="#virtual-browsing-context-group-id"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:virtual-browsing-context-group-id-3">virtual
    browsing context group ID</a> to `openerTopLevelBrowsingContext`'s
    <a href="#virtual-browsing-context-group-id"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:virtual-browsing-context-group-id-4">virtual
    browsing context group ID</a>.

9.  Set `browsingContext`'s <a href="#opener-origin-at-creation"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:opener-origin-at-creation">opener origin
    at creation</a> to `opener`'s <a href="#nav-document"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:nav-document-2">active document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-4"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>.

10. Return `browsingContext` and `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="determining-the-origin" class="dfn">determine the
origin</span>, given a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `url`,
a <a href="#sandboxing-flag-set"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:sandboxing-flag-set">sandboxing flag
set</a> `sandboxFlags`, and an <a href="#concept-origin"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-origin">origin</a>-or-null
`sourceOrigin`:

1.  <div id="sandboxOrigin">

    If `sandboxFlags` has its
    <a href="#sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
    origin browsing context flag</a> set, then return a new
    <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a>.

    </div>

2.  If `url` is null, then return a new <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-origin-opaque-2">opaque
    origin</a>.

3.  If `url` is [`about:srcdoc`](#about:srcdoc), then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="creating-browsing-contexts:assert-3"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `sourceOrigin` is non-null.

    2.  Return `sourceOrigin`.

4.  If `url` <a href="#matches-about:blank"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:matches-about:blank">matches
    <code>about:blank</code></a> and `sourceOrigin` is non-null, then
    return `sourceOrigin`.

5.  Return `url`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
    id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-url-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a>.

The cases that return `sourceOrigin` result in two
[`Document`](#document)s that end up with the same underlying
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
id="creating-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-5"
data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, meaning that
[`document.domain`](#dom-document-domain) affects both.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.3.2.2</span> Related browsing contexts<a href="#nested-browsing-contexts" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context">browsing context</a>
`potentialDescendant` is said to be an
<span id="ancestor-browsing-context" class="dfn">ancestor</span> of a
browsing context `potentialAncestor` if the following algorithm returns
true:

1.  Let `potentialDescendantDocument` be `potentialDescendant`'s
    <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document">active document</a>.

2.  If `potentialDescendantDocument` is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="nested-browsing-contexts:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return false.

3.  Let `ancestorBCs` be the list obtained by taking the
    <a href="#concept-document-bc"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:concept-document-bc">browsing context</a>
    of the <a href="#nav-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-document">active document</a> of
    each member of `potentialDescendantDocument`'s
    <a href="#ancestor-navigables"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:ancestor-navigables">ancestor
    navigables</a>.

4.  If `ancestorBCs`
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:list-contains"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> `potentialAncestor`,
    then return true.

5.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="top-level-browsing-context" class="dfn" export="">top-level
browsing context</span> is a <a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-2">browsing context</a>
whose <a href="#active-document"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-2">active document</a>'s
<a href="#node-navigable"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:node-navigable">node navigable</a> is a
<a href="#traversable-navigable"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:traversable-navigable">traversable
navigable</a>.

</div>

It is *not* required to be a <a href="#top-level-traversable"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:top-level-traversable">top-level
traversable</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="bc-tlbc" class="dfn">top-level browsing context</span> of
a <a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-3">browsing context</a>
`start` is the result of the following algorithm:

1.  If `start`'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-3">active document</a>
    is not <a href="#fully-active"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:fully-active-2">fully active</a>, then
    return null.

2.  Let `navigable` be `start`'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-4">active document</a>'s
    <a href="#node-navigable"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:node-navigable-2">node navigable</a>.

3.  While `navigable`'s <a href="#nav-parent"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-parent">parent</a> is not null, set
    `navigable` to `navigable`'s <a href="#nav-parent"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-parent-2">parent</a>.

4.  Return `navigable`'s
    <a href="#nav-bc" id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-bc">active browsing
    context</a>.

</div>

<div id="warning-avoid-related-bc-terms" class="warning">

The terms <a href="#ancestor-browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:ancestor-browsing-context">ancestor
browsing context</a> and <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context">top-level
browsing context</a> are rarely useful, since
<a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-4">browsing contexts</a>
in general are [usually the inappropriate specification concept to
use](#warning-avoid-using-bcs). Note in particular that when a
<a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-5">browsing context</a>'s
<a href="#active-document"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-5">active document</a> is
not <a href="#fully-active"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:fully-active-3">fully active</a>, it never
counts as an ancestor or top-level browsing context, and as such these
concepts are not useful when [bfcache](#note-bfcache) is in play.

Instead, use concepts such as the <a href="#ancestor-navigables"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:ancestor-navigables-2">ancestor
navigables</a> collection, the
<a href="#nav-parent" id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-parent-3">parent
navigable</a>, or a navigable's <a href="#nav-traversable"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:nav-traversable">top-level traversable</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

<span id="security-nav"></span>A <a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-6">browsing context</a>
`A` is <span id="familiar-with" class="dfn">familiar with</span> a
second <a href="#browsing-context"
id="nested-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-7">browsing context</a>
`B` if the following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `A`'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-6">active document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is
    <a href="#same-origin" id="nested-browsing-contexts:same-origin">same
    origin</a> with `B`'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-7">active document</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a>, then return
    true.

2.  If `A`'s
    <a href="#bc-tlbc" id="nested-browsing-contexts:bc-tlbc">top-level
    browsing context</a> is `B`, then return true.

3.  If `B` is an <a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:auxiliary-browsing-context">auxiliary
    browsing context</a> and `A` is <a href="#familiar-with"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:familiar-with">familiar with</a> `B`'s
    <a href="#opener-browsing-context"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:opener-browsing-context">opener browsing
    context</a>, then return true.

4.  If there exists an <a href="#ancestor-browsing-context"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:ancestor-browsing-context-2">ancestor
    browsing context</a> of `B` whose <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-8">active document</a>
    has the <a href="#same-origin"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:same-origin-2">same</a>
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:concept-document-origin-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> as the
    <a href="#active-document"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:active-document-9">active document</a>
    of `A`, then return true.

    This includes the case where `A` is an
    <a href="#ancestor-browsing-context"
    id="nested-browsing-contexts:ancestor-browsing-context-3">ancestor
    browsing context</a> of `B`.

5.  Return false.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">7.3.2.3</span> Groupings of browsing contexts<a href="#groupings-of-browsing-contexts" class="self-link"></a>

A <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context">top-level
browsing context</a> has an associated <span id="tlbc-group"
class="dfn">group</span> (null or a <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group">browsing
context group</a>). It is initially null.

A user agent holds a <span id="browsing-context-group-set"
class="dfn">browsing context group set</span> (a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
<a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-2">browsing
context groups</a>).

A <span id="browsing-context-group" class="dfn">browsing context
group</span> holds a <span id="browsing-context-set"
class="dfn">browsing context set</span> (a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:set-2" data-x-internal="set">set</a>
of <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context-2">top-level
browsing contexts</a>).

A <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context-3">top-level
browsing context</a> is added to the <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-3">group</a>
when the group is
<a href="#creating-a-new-browsing-context-group-and-document"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:creating-a-new-browsing-context-group-and-document">created</a>.
All subsequent <a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context-4">top-level
browsing contexts</a> added to the <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-4">group</a>
will be <a href="#auxiliary-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:auxiliary-browsing-context">auxiliary
browsing contexts</a>.

A <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-5">browsing
context group</a> has an associated <span id="agent-cluster-map"
class="dfn">agent cluster map</span> (a weak
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:ordered-map"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a> of <a href="#agent-cluster-key"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:agent-cluster-key">agent cluster
keys</a> to <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:agent-cluster"
data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent clusters</a>). User agents are
responsible for collecting agent clusters when it is deemed that nothing
can access them anymore.

A <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-6">browsing
context group</a> has an associated
<span id="historical-agent-cluster-key-map" class="dfn">historical agent
cluster key map</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:ordered-map-2"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a> of <a href="#concept-origin"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:concept-origin">origins</a> to
<a href="#agent-cluster-key"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:agent-cluster-key-2">agent cluster
keys</a>. This map is used to ensure the consistency of the
[origin-keyed agent clusters](#origin-keyed-agent-clusters) feature by
recording what agent cluster keys were previously used for a given
origin.

The <a href="#historical-agent-cluster-key-map"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:historical-agent-cluster-key-map">historical
agent cluster key map</a> only ever gains entries over the lifetime of
the browsing context group.

A <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-7">browsing
context group</a> has a <span id="bcg-cross-origin-isolation"
class="dfn">cross-origin isolation mode</span>, which is a
<a href="#cross-origin-isolation-mode"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:cross-origin-isolation-mode">cross-origin
isolation mode</a>. It is initially
"[`none`](#cross-origin-isolation-none)".

A <span id="cross-origin-isolation-mode" class="dfn">cross-origin
isolation mode</span> is one of three possible values:
"<span id="cross-origin-isolation-none" class="dfn">`none`</span>",
"<span id="cross-origin-isolation-logical"
class="dfn">`logical`</span>", or
"<span id="cross-origin-isolation-concrete"
class="dfn">`concrete`</span>".

<div class="note">

"[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" and
"[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)" are similar. They are
both used for <a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-8">browsing
context groups</a> where:

- every top-level [`Document`](#document) has
  \`<a href="#cross-origin-opener-policy-2"
  id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:cross-origin-opener-policy-2"><code>Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy</code></a>`: `<a href="#coop-same-origin"
  id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:coop-same-origin"><code>same-origin</code></a>\`,
  and

- every [`Document`](#document) has a
  \`[`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`](#cross-origin-embedder-policy)\`
  header whose value is
  <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
  id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation">compatible
  with cross-origin isolation</a>.

On some platforms, it is difficult to provide the security properties
required to grant safe access to the APIs gated by the
<a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
isolated capability</a>. As a result, only
"[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)" can grant access that
capability. "[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" is used on
platform not supporting this capability, where various restrictions
imposed by cross-origin isolation will still apply, but the capability
is not granted.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-new-browsing-context-group-and-document"
class="dfn">create a new browsing context group and document</span>:

1.  Let `group` be a new <a href="#browsing-context-group"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-9">browsing
    context group</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:set-append"
    data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a> `group` to the user agent's
    <a href="#browsing-context-group-set"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-set">browsing
    context group set</a>.

3.  Let `browsingContext` and `document` be the result of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-browsing-context"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:creating-a-new-browsing-context">creating
    a new browsing context and document</a> with null, null, and
    `group`.

4.  <a href="#bcg-append"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:bcg-append">Append</a>
    `browsingContext` to `group`.

5.  Return `group` and `document`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="bcg-append" class="dfn">append</span> a
<a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context-5">top-level
browsing context</a> `browsingContext` to a
<a href="#browsing-context-group"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-group-10">browsing
context group</a> `group`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:set-append-2"
    data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a> `browsingContext` to
    `group`'s <a href="#browsing-context-set"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:browsing-context-set">browsing
    context set</a>.

2.  Set `browsingContext`'s <a href="#tlbc-group"
    id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:tlbc-group">group</a> to `group`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="bcg-remove" class="dfn">remove</span> a
<a href="#top-level-browsing-context"
id="groupings-of-browsing-contexts:top-level-browsing-context-6">top-level
browsing context</a> `browsingContext`:
