    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet"
    id="creating-scripts:synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet"
    data-x-internal="synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet">synchronously
    replace the rules of a <code>CSSStyleSheet</code></a> on `sheet`
    given `source`.

    If this throws an exception, catch it, and set `script`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-parse-error"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-parse-error-8">parse error</a>
    to that exception, and return `script`.

    The steps to <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet"
    id="creating-scripts:synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet-2"
    data-x-internal="synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet">synchronously
    replace the rules of a <code>CSSStyleSheet</code></a> will throw if
    `source` contains any `@import` rules. This is by-design for now
    because there is not yet an agreement on how to handle these for CSS
    module scripts; therefore they are blocked altogether until a
    consensus is reached.

7.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-record"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-record-4">record</a> to the
    result of <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-create-default-export-synthetic-module"
    id="creating-scripts:createdefaultexportsyntheticmodule"
    data-x-internal="createdefaultexportsyntheticmodule">CreateDefaultExportSyntheticModule</a>(`sheet`).

8.  Return `script`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-json-module-script" class="dfn">create a JSON
module script</span>, given a string `source` and an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="creating-scripts:environment-settings-object-5">environment settings
object</a> `settings`:

1.  Let `script` be a new
    <a href="#module-script" id="creating-scripts:module-script-4">module
    script</a> that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.

2.  Set `script`'s <a href="#settings-object"
    id="creating-scripts:settings-object-5">settings object</a> to
    `settings`.

3.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-base-url-5">base URL</a> and
    <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-script-fetch-options-5">fetch
    options</a> to null.

4.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-parse-error"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-parse-error-9">parse error</a>
    and <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow-6">error to
    rethrow</a> to null.

5.  Let `result` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parse-json-module"
    id="creating-scripts:parsejsonmodule"

    If this throws an exception, catch it, and set `script`'s

    to that exception, and return `script`.

6.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-record"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-record-5">record</a> to
    `result`.

7.  Return `script`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="creating-a-text-module-script" class="dfn">create a text
module script</span>, given a string `text` and an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="creating-scripts:environment-settings-object-6">environment settings
object</a> `settings`:

1.  Let `script` be a new
    <a href="#module-script" id="creating-scripts:module-script-5">module
    script</a> that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.

2.  Set `script`'s <a href="#settings-object"
    id="creating-scripts:settings-object-6">settings object</a> to
    `settings`.

3.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-base-url-6">base URL</a> and
    <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-script-fetch-options-6">fetch
    options</a> to null.

4.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-parse-error"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-parse-error-11">parse error</a>
    and <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow-7">error to
    rethrow</a> to null.

5.  Let `result` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/proposal-import-text/#sec-create-text-module"
    id="creating-scripts:createtextmodule"
    data-x-internal="createtextmodule">CreateTextModule</a>(`text`).

6.  Set `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-record"
    id="creating-scripts:concept-script-record-6">record</a> to

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="module-type-from-module-request" class="dfn">module type
from module request</span> steps, given a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record"
id="creating-scripts:modulerequest-record"
data-x-internal="modulerequest-record">ModuleRequest Record</a>
`moduleRequest`, are as follows:

1.  Let `moduleType` be "`javascript-or-wasm`".

2.  If `moduleRequest`.\[\[Attributes\]\] has a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
    id="creating-scripts:record" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
    `entry` such that `entry`.\[\[Key\]\] is "`type`", then:

    1.  If `entry`.\[\[Value\]\] is "`javascript-or-wasm`", then set
        `moduleType` to null.

        This specification uses the "`javascript-or-wasm`" module type
        internally for <a href="#javascript-module-script"
        id="creating-scripts:javascript-module-script">JavaScript module
        scripts</a> or <a href="#webassembly-module-script"
        id="creating-scripts:webassembly-module-script">WebAssembly module
        scripts</a>, so this step is needed to prevent modules from
        being imported using a "`javascript-or-wasm`" type attribute (a
        null `moduleType` will cause the <a href="#module-type-allowed"
        id="creating-scripts:module-type-allowed">module type allowed</a>
        check to fail).

    2.  Otherwise, set `moduleType` to `entry`.\[\[Value\]\].

3.  Return `moduleType`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="module-type-allowed" class="dfn">module type
allowed</span> steps, given a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="creating-scripts:string-3" data-x-internal="string">string</a>
`moduleType` and an <a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="creating-scripts:environment-settings-object-7">environment settings
object</a> `settings`, are as follows:

1.  If `moduleType` is not "`javascript-or-wasm`", "`css`", "`json`", or
    "`text`", then return false.

2.  If `moduleType` is "`css`" and the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#the-cssstylesheet-interface"
    data-x-internal="cssstylesheet"><code
    id="creating-scripts:cssstylesheet">CSSStyleSheet</code></a>
    interface is not
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-exposed"
    id="creating-scripts:idl-exposed"
    data-x-internal="idl-exposed">exposed</a> in `settings`'s
    <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
    id="creating-scripts:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm-4">realm</a>,
    then return false.

3.  Return true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="fetch-destination-from-module-type" class="dfn">fetch
destination from module type</span> steps, given a
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination"
id="creating-scripts:concept-request-destination"
data-x-internal="concept-request-destination">destination</a>
`defaultDestination` and a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="creating-scripts:string-4" data-x-internal="string">string</a>
`moduleType`, are as follows:

1.  If `moduleType` is "`json`", then return "`json`".
2.  If `moduleType` is "`css`", then return "`style`".
3.  If `moduleType` is "`text`", then return "`text`".
4.  Return `defaultDestination`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.4</span> Calling scripts<a href="#calling-scripts" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="run-a-classic-script" class="dfn" export="">run a classic
script</span> given a
<a href="#classic-script" id="calling-scripts:classic-script">classic
script</a> `script` and an optional boolean `rethrow errors` (default
false):

1.  Let `settings` be the
    <a href="#settings-object" id="calling-scripts:settings-object">settings
    object</a> of `script`.

2.  <a href="#check-if-we-can-run-script"
    id="calling-scripts:check-if-we-can-run-script">Check if we can run
    script</a> with `settings`. If this returns "do not run", then
    return <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion"
    id="calling-scripts:normalcompletion"
    data-x-internal="normalcompletion">NormalCompletion</a>(empty).

3.  <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-classic-script-execution-start-time"
    id="calling-scripts:record-classic-script-execution-start-time"
    data-x-internal="record-classic-script-execution-start-time">Record
    classic script execution start time</a> given `script`.

4.  <a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
    id="calling-scripts:prepare-to-run-script">Prepare to run script</a>
    given `settings`.

5.  Let `evaluationStatus` be null.

6.  If `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow">error to
    rethrow</a> is not null, then set `evaluationStatus` to
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
    id="calling-scripts:throwcompletion"
    data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`script`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow-2">error to
    rethrow</a>).

7.  Otherwise, set `evaluationStatus` to <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation"
    id="calling-scripts:js-scriptevaluation"
    data-x-internal="js-scriptevaluation">ScriptEvaluation</a>(`script`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-record"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-script-record">record</a>).

    If <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation"
    id="calling-scripts:js-scriptevaluation-2"
    data-x-internal="js-scriptevaluation">ScriptEvaluation</a> does not
    complete because the user agent has
    <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
    id="calling-scripts:abort-a-running-script">aborted the running
    script</a>, leave `evaluationStatus` as null.

8.  If `evaluationStatus` is an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="calling-scripts:completion-record"
    data-x-internal="completion-record">abrupt completion</a>, then:

    1.  If `rethrow errors` is true and `script`'s
        <a href="#muted-errors" id="calling-scripts:muted-errors">muted
        errors</a> is false, then:

        1.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
            id="calling-scripts:clean-up-after-running-script">Clean up after
            running script</a> with `settings`.

        2.  Rethrow `evaluationStatus`.\[\[Value\]\].

    2.  If `rethrow errors` is true and `script`'s
        <a href="#muted-errors" id="calling-scripts:muted-errors-2">muted
        errors</a> is true, then:

        1.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
            id="calling-scripts:clean-up-after-running-script-2">Clean up after
            running script</a> with `settings`.

        2.  Throw a
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#networkerror"
            id="calling-scripts:networkerror"
            data-x-internal="networkerror">"<code>NetworkError</code>"</a>
            <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
            data-x-internal="domexception"><code
            id="calling-scripts:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  Otherwise, `rethrow errors` is false. Perform the following
        steps:

        1.  <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="calling-scripts:report-an-exception">Report an exception</a>
            given by `evaluationStatus`.\[\[Value\]\] for `script`'s
            <a href="#settings-object"
            id="calling-scripts:settings-object-2">settings object</a>'s
            <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
            id="calling-scripts:concept-settings-object-global">global object</a>.

        2.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
            id="calling-scripts:clean-up-after-running-script-3">Clean up after
            running script</a> with `settings`.

        3.  Return `evaluationStatus`.

9.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
    id="calling-scripts:clean-up-after-running-script-4">Clean up after
    running script</a> with `settings`.

10. If `evaluationStatus` is a normal completion, then return
    `evaluationStatus`.

11. If we've reached this point, `evaluationStatus` was left as null
    because the script was <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
    id="calling-scripts:abort-a-running-script-2">aborted prematurely</a>
    during evaluation. Return
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
    id="calling-scripts:throwcompletion-2"
    data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(a new
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror"
    data-x-internal="quotaexceedederror"><code
    id="calling-scripts:quotaexceedederror">QuotaExceededError</code></a>).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="run-a-module-script" class="dfn" export="">run a module
script</span> given a
<a href="#module-script" id="calling-scripts:module-script">module
script</a> `script` and an optional boolean `preventErrorReporting`
(default false):

1.  Let `settings` be the <a href="#settings-object"
    id="calling-scripts:settings-object-3">settings object</a> of
    `script`.

2.  <a href="#check-if-we-can-run-script"
    id="calling-scripts:check-if-we-can-run-script-2">Check if we can run
    script</a> with `settings`. If this returns "do not run", then
    return
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-resolved-with"
    id="calling-scripts:a-promise-resolved-with"
    data-x-internal="a-promise-resolved-with">a promise resolved with</a>
    undefined.

3.  <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-module-script-execution-start-time"
    id="calling-scripts:record-module-script-execution-start-time"
    data-x-internal="record-module-script-execution-start-time">Record
    module script execution start time</a> given `script`.

4.  <a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
    id="calling-scripts:prepare-to-run-script-2">Prepare to run script</a>
    given `settings`.

5.  Let `evaluationPromise` be null.

6.  If `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow-3">error to
    rethrow</a> is not null, then set `evaluationPromise` to
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with"
    id="calling-scripts:a-promise-rejected-with"
    data-x-internal="a-promise-rejected-with">a promise rejected with</a>
    `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-script-error-to-rethrow-4">error to
    rethrow</a>.

7.  Otherwise:

    1.  Let `record` be `script`'s <a href="#concept-script-record"
        id="calling-scripts:concept-script-record-2">record</a>.

    2.  Set `evaluationPromise` to
        `record`.<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation"
        id="calling-scripts:js-evaluate"
        data-x-internal="js-evaluate">Evaluate</a>().

        This step will recursively evaluate all of the module's
        dependencies.

        If <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation"
        id="calling-scripts:js-evaluate-2"
        data-x-internal="js-evaluate">Evaluate</a> fails to complete as
        a result of the user agent <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
        id="calling-scripts:abort-a-running-script-3">aborting the running
        script</a>, then set `evaluationPromise` to
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with"
        id="calling-scripts:a-promise-rejected-with-2"
        data-x-internal="a-promise-rejected-with">a promise rejected with</a>
        a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror"
        data-x-internal="quotaexceedederror"><code
        id="calling-scripts:quotaexceedederror-2">QuotaExceededError</code></a>.

8.  If `preventErrorReporting` is false, then
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-rejection"
    id="calling-scripts:upon-rejection"
    data-x-internal="upon-rejection">upon rejection</a> of
    `evaluationPromise` with `reason`, <a href="#report-an-exception"
    id="calling-scripts:report-an-exception-2">report an exception</a>
    given by `reason` for `script`'s <a href="#settings-object"
    id="calling-scripts:settings-object-4">settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-settings-object-global-2">global object</a>.

9.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
    id="calling-scripts:clean-up-after-running-script-5">Clean up after
    running script</a> with `settings`.

10. Return `evaluationPromise`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The steps to <span id="check-if-we-can-run-script" class="dfn">check if
we can run script</span> with an <a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="calling-scripts:environment-settings-object">environment settings
object</a> `settings` are as follows. They return either "run" or "do
not run".

1.  If the <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-settings-object-global-3">global object</a>
    specified by `settings` is a [`Window`](#window) object whose
    [`Document`](#document) object is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="calling-scripts:fully-active">fully
    active</a>, then return "do not run".

2.  If <a href="#concept-environment-noscript"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-environment-noscript">scripting is
    disabled</a> for `settings`, then return "do not run".

3.  Return "run".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The steps to <span id="prepare-to-run-script" class="dfn"
export="">prepare to run script</span> with an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="calling-scripts:environment-settings-object-2">environment settings
object</a> `settings` are as follows:

1.  Push `settings`'s <a href="#realm-execution-context"
    id="calling-scripts:realm-execution-context">realm execution context</a>
    onto the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
    id="calling-scripts:javascript-execution-context-stack"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
    execution context stack</a>; it is now the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context"
    id="calling-scripts:running-javascript-execution-context"
    data-x-internal="running-javascript-execution-context">running
    JavaScript execution context</a>.

2.  Add `settings` to the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="calling-scripts:surrounding-agent"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="calling-scripts:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>'s
    <a href="#currently-running-task"
    id="calling-scripts:currently-running-task">currently running task</a>'s
    <a href="#script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set"
    id="calling-scripts:script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set">script
    evaluation environment settings object set</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The steps to <span id="clean-up-after-running-script" class="dfn"
export="">clean up after running script</span> with an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="calling-scripts:environment-settings-object-3">environment settings
object</a> `settings` are as follows:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="calling-scripts:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `settings`'s <a href="#realm-execution-context"
    id="calling-scripts:realm-execution-context-2">realm execution
    context</a> is the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context"
    id="calling-scripts:running-javascript-execution-context-2"
    data-x-internal="running-javascript-execution-context">running
    JavaScript execution context</a>.

2.  Remove `settings`'s <a href="#realm-execution-context"
    id="calling-scripts:realm-execution-context-3">realm execution
    context</a> from the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
    id="calling-scripts:javascript-execution-context-stack-2"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
    execution context stack</a>.

3.  If the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
    id="calling-scripts:javascript-execution-context-stack-3"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
    execution context stack</a> is now empty,
    <a href="#perform-a-microtask-checkpoint"
    id="calling-scripts:perform-a-microtask-checkpoint">perform a microtask
    checkpoint</a>. (If this runs scripts, these algorithms will be
    invoked reentrantly.)

</div>

These algorithms are not invoked by one script directly calling another,
but they can be invoked reentrantly in an indirect manner, e.g. if a
script dispatches an event which has event listeners registered.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="running-script" class="dfn">running script</span> is the
<a href="#concept-script" id="calling-scripts:concept-script">script</a>
in the \[\[HostDefined\]\] field in the ScriptOrModule component of the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context"
id="calling-scripts:running-javascript-execution-context-3"
data-x-internal="running-javascript-execution-context">running
JavaScript execution context</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.5</span> Killing scripts<a href="#killing-scripts" class="self-link"></a>

Although the JavaScript specification does not account for this
possibility, it's sometimes necessary to
<span id="abort-a-running-script" class="dfn"
lt="abort a running script|abort the running script" export="">abort a
running script</span>. This causes any <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation"
id="killing-scripts:js-scriptevaluation"
data-x-internal="js-scriptevaluation">ScriptEvaluation</a> or
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-source-text-module-records"
id="killing-scripts:source-text-module-record"
data-x-internal="source-text-module-record">Source Text Module
Record</a> <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation"
id="killing-scripts:js-evaluate"
data-x-internal="js-evaluate">Evaluate</a> invocations to cease
immediately, emptying the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
id="killing-scripts:javascript-execution-context-stack"
data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
execution context stack</a> without triggering any of the normal
mechanisms like `finally` blocks. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

User agents may impose resource limitations on scripts, for example CPU
quotas, memory limits, total execution time limits, or bandwidth
limitations. When a script exceeds a limit, the user agent may either
throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror"
data-x-internal="quotaexceedederror"><code
id="killing-scripts:quotaexceedederror">QuotaExceededError</code></a>,
<a href="#abort-a-running-script"
id="killing-scripts:abort-a-running-script">abort the script</a> without
an exception, prompt the user, or throttle script execution.

<div class="example">

For example, the following script never terminates. A user agent could,
after waiting for a few seconds, prompt the user to either terminate the
script or let it continue.

``` html
<script>
 while (true) { /* loop */ }
</script>
```

</div>

User agents are encouraged to allow users to disable scripting whenever
the user is prompted either by a script (e.g. using the
[`window.alert()`](#dom-alert) API) or because of a script's actions
(e.g. because it has exceeded a time limit).

If scripting is disabled while a script is executing, the script should
be terminated immediately.

User agents may allow users to specifically disable scripts just for the
purposes of closing a <a href="#browsing-context"
id="killing-scripts:browsing-context">browsing context</a>.

For example, the prompt mentioned in the example above could also offer
the user with a mechanism to just close the page entirely, without
running any [`unload`](#event-unload) event handlers.

##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.6</span> Runtime script errors<a href="#runtime-script-errors" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[reportError](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/reportError "The reportError() global method may be used to report errors to the console or global event handlers, emulating an uncaught JavaScript exception.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox93+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari15.4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome95+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge95+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

`self.`<a href="#dom-reporterror"
id="dom-reporterror-dev"><code>reportError</code></a>`(``e``)`  
Dispatches an [`error`](#event-error) event at the global object for the
given value `e`, in the same fashion as an unhandled exception.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="extract-error" class="dfn">extract error information</span>
from a JavaScript value `exception`:

1.  Let `attributes` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="runtime-script-errors:ordered-map"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a> keyed by IDL attributes.

2.  Set `attributes`\[[`error`](#dom-errorevent-error)\] to `exception`.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
    id="runtime-script-errors:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
    data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
    title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
    src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
    class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
    alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> Set
    `attributes`\[[`message`](#dom-errorevent-message)\],
    `attributes`\[[`filename`](#dom-errorevent-filename)\],
    `attributes`\[[`lineno`](#dom-errorevent-lineno)\], and
    `attributes`\[[`colno`](#dom-errorevent-colno)\] to
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="runtime-script-errors:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    values derived from `exception`.

    Browsers implement behavior not specified here or in the JavaScript
    specification to gather values which are helpful, including in
    unusual cases (e.g., `eval`). In the future, this might be specified
    in greater detail.

4.  Return `attributes`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="report-the-error"></span>To <span id="report-an-exception"
class="dfn" export="">report an exception</span> `exception` which is a
JavaScript value, for a particular
<a href="#global-object" id="runtime-script-errors:global-object">global
object</a> `global` and optional boolean
<span id="report-exception-omiterror" class="dfn">`omitError`</span>
(default false):

1.  Let `notHandled` be true.

2.  Let `errorInfo` be the result of <a href="#extract-error"
    id="runtime-script-errors:extract-error">extracting error
    information</a> from `exception`.

3.  Let `script` be a <a href="#concept-script"
    id="runtime-script-errors:concept-script">script</a> found in an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="runtime-script-errors:implementation-defined-2"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    way, or null. This should usually be the <a href="#running-script"
    id="runtime-script-errors:running-script">running script</a> (most
    notably during <a href="#run-a-classic-script"
    id="runtime-script-errors:run-a-classic-script">run a classic script</a>).

    Implementations have not yet settled on interoperable behavior for
    which script is used to determine whether errors are muted in less
    common cases.

4.  If `script` is a <a href="#classic-script"
    id="runtime-script-errors:classic-script">classic script</a> and
    `script`'s
    <a href="#muted-errors" id="runtime-script-errors:muted-errors">muted
    errors</a> is true, then set
    `errorInfo`\[[`error`](#dom-errorevent-error)\] to null,
    `errorInfo`\[[`message`](#dom-errorevent-message)\] to
    "`Script error.`",
    `errorInfo`\[[`filename`](#dom-errorevent-filename)\] to the empty
    string, `errorInfo`\[[`lineno`](#dom-errorevent-lineno)\] to 0, and
    `errorInfo`\[[`colno`](#dom-errorevent-colno)\] to 0.

5.  If `omitError` is true, then set
    `errorInfo`\[[`error`](#dom-errorevent-error)\] to null.

6.  If `global` is not <a href="#in-error-reporting-mode"
    id="runtime-script-errors:in-error-reporting-mode">in error reporting
    mode</a>, then:

    1.  Set `global`'s <a href="#in-error-reporting-mode"
        id="runtime-script-errors:in-error-reporting-mode-2">in error reporting
        mode</a> to true.

    2.  If `global` implements
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
        data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
        id="runtime-script-errors:eventtarget">EventTarget</code></a>,
        then set `notHandled` to the result of
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="runtime-script-errors:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">firing an event</a> named
        [`error`](#event-error) at `global`, using
        [`ErrorEvent`](#errorevent), with the
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
        data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
        id="runtime-script-errors:dom-event-cancelable">cancelable</code></a>
        attribute initialized to true, and additional attributes
        initialized according to `errorInfo`.

        Returning true in an event handler cancels the event per
        <a href="#the-event-handler-processing-algorithm"
        id="runtime-script-errors:the-event-handler-processing-algorithm">the
        event handler processing algorithm</a>.

    3.  Set `global`'s <a href="#in-error-reporting-mode"
        id="runtime-script-errors:in-error-reporting-mode-3">in error reporting
        mode</a> to false.

7.  If `notHandled` is true, then:

    1.  Set `errorInfo`\[[`error`](#dom-errorevent-error)\] to null.

    2.  If `global` implements
        [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#dedicatedworkerglobalscope),
        <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
        id="runtime-script-errors:queue-a-global-task">queue a global task</a>
        on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="runtime-script-errors:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM manipulation
        task source</a> with the `global`'s associated
        [`Worker`](#worker)'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
        id="runtime-script-errors:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
        object</a> to run these steps:

        1.  Let `workerObject` be the [`Worker`](#worker) object
            associated with `global`.

        2.  Set `notHandled` to the result of
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="runtime-script-errors:concept-event-fire-2"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">firing an event</a>
            named [`error`](#event-error) at `workerObject`, using
            [`ErrorEvent`](#errorevent), with the
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
            data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
            id="runtime-script-errors:dom-event-cancelable-2">cancelable</code></a>
            attribute initialized to true, and additional attributes
            initialized according to `errorInfo`.

        3.  If `notHandled` is true, then <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="runtime-script-errors:report-an-exception">report</a>
            `exception` for `workerObject`'s
            <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
            id="runtime-script-errors:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
            object</a> with <a href="#report-exception-omiterror"
            id="runtime-script-errors:report-exception-omiterror"><var>omitError</var></a>
            set to true.

            The actual `exception` value will not be available in the
            owner realm, but the user agent still carries through enough
            information to set the message, filename, and other
            attributes, as well as potentially report to a developer
            console.

    3.  Otherwise, the user agent may report `exception` to a developer
        console.

</div>

If the implicit port connecting a worker to its [`Worker`](#worker)
object has been disentangled (i.e. if the parent worker has been
terminated), then the user agent must act as if the [`Worker`](#worker)
object had no [`error`](#event-error) event handler and as if that
worker's [`onerror`](#handler-workerglobalscope-onerror) attribute was
null, but must otherwise act as described above.

Thus, error reports propagate up to the chain of dedicated workers up to
the original [`Document`](#document), even if some of the workers along
this chain have been terminated and garbage collected.

Previous revisions of this standard defined an algorithm to
<span id="report-the-exception" class="dfn" lt="report the exception"
export="">report the exception</span>. As part of [issue
\#958](https://github.com/whatwg/html), this has been superseded by
<a href="#report-an-exception"
id="runtime-script-errors:report-an-exception-2">report an exception</a>
which behaves differently and takes different inputs. [Issue
\#10516](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10516) tracks updating
the specification ecosystem.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-reporterror" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`reportError(``e``)`</span> method steps are to
<a href="#report-an-exception"
id="runtime-script-errors:report-an-exception-3">report an exception</a>
`e` for <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="runtime-script-errors:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

It is unclear whether <a href="#muted-errors"
id="runtime-script-errors:muted-errors-2">muting</a> is applicable here.
In Chrome and Safari it is muted, but in Firefox it is not. See also
[issue \#958](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/958).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[ErrorEvent](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ErrorEvent "The ErrorEvent interface represents events providing information related to errors in scripts or in files.")

Support in all current engines.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The [`ErrorEvent`](#errorevent) interface is defined as follows:

``` idl
[Exposed=*]
interface ErrorEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional ErrorEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute DOMString message;
  readonly attribute USVString filename;
  readonly attribute unsigned long lineno;
  readonly attribute unsigned long colno;
  readonly attribute any error;
};

dictionary ErrorEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString message = "";
  USVString filename = "";
  unsigned long lineno = 0;
  unsigned long colno = 0;
  any error;
};
```

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-errorevent-message" class="dfn" dfn-for="ErrorEvent"
dfn-type="attribute">`message`</span> attribute must return the value it
was initialized to. It represents the error message.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-errorevent-filename" class="dfn" dfn-for="ErrorEvent"
dfn-type="attribute">`filename`</span> attribute must return the value
it was initialized to. It represents the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="runtime-script-errors:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> of the
script in which the error originally occurred.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-errorevent-lineno" class="dfn" dfn-for="ErrorEvent"
dfn-type="attribute">`lineno`</span> attribute must return the value it
was initialized to. It represents the line number where the error
occurred in the script.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-errorevent-colno" class="dfn" dfn-for="ErrorEvent"
dfn-type="attribute">`colno`</span> attribute must return the value it
was initialized to. It represents the column number where the error
occurred in the script.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-errorevent-error" class="dfn" dfn-for="ErrorEvent"
dfn-type="attribute">`error`</span> attribute must return the value it
was initialized to. It must initially be initialized to undefined. Where
appropriate, it is set to the object representing the error (e.g., the
exception object in the case of an uncaught exception).

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.7</span> Unhandled promise rejections<a href="#unhandled-promise-rejections" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Window/rejectionhandled_event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/rejectionhandled_event "The rejectionhandled event is sent to the script's global scope (usually window but also Worker) whenever a rejected JavaScript Promise is handled late, i.e. when a handler is attached to the promise after its rejection had caused an unhandledrejection event.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox69+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari11+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome49+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS11.3+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

In addition to synchronous [runtime script
errors](#runtime-script-errors), scripts may experience asynchronous
promise rejections, tracked via the
[`unhandledrejection`](#event-unhandledrejection) and
[`rejectionhandled`](#event-rejectionhandled) events. Tracking these
rejections is done via the
<a href="#the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation"
id="unhandled-promise-rejections:the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation">HostPromiseRejectionTracker</a>
abstract operation, but reporting them is defined here.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="notify-about-rejected-promises" class="dfn">notify about
rejected promises</span> given a <a href="#global-object"
id="unhandled-promise-rejections:global-object">global object</a>
`global`:

1.  Let `list` be a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-clone"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:list-clone"
    data-x-internal="list-clone">clone</a> of `global`'s
    <a href="#about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list">about-to-be-notified
    rejected promises list</a>.

2.  If `list` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">is empty</a>, then return.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-empty"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:list-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-empty">Empty</a> `global`'s
    <a href="#about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list-2">about-to-be-notified
    rejected promises list</a>.

4.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:queue-a-global-task">Queue a global
    task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
    id="unhandled-promise-rejections:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
    manipulation task source</a> given `global` to run the following
    step:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="unhandled-promise-rejections:list-iterate"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> promise `p` of
        `list`:

        1.  If `p`.\[\[PromiseIsHandled\]\] is true, then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="unhandled-promise-rejections:continue"
            data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

        2.  Let `notCanceled` be the result of
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="unhandled-promise-rejections:concept-event-fire"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">firing an event</a>
            named [`unhandledrejection`](#event-unhandledrejection) at
            `global`, using
            [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#promiserejectionevent), with the
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
            data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
            id="unhandled-promise-rejections:dom-event-cancelable">cancelable</code></a>
            attribute initialized to true, the
            [`promise`](#dom-promiserejectionevent-promise) attribute
            initialized to `p`, and the
            [`reason`](#dom-promiserejectionevent-reason) attribute
            initialized to `p`.\[\[PromiseResult\]\].

        3.  <div id="concept-promise-rejection-handled">

            If `notCanceled` is true, then the user agent may report
            `p`.\[\[PromiseResult\]\] to a developer console.

            </div>

        4.  If `p`.\[\[PromiseIsHandled\]\] is false, then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
            id="unhandled-promise-rejections:set-append"
            data-x-internal="set-append">append</a> `p` to `global`'s
            <a href="#outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set"
            id="unhandled-promise-rejections:outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set">outstanding
            rejected promises weak set</a>.

</div>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[PromiseRejectionEvent](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PromiseRejectionEvent "The PromiseRejectionEvent interface represents events which are sent to the global script context when JavaScript Promises are rejected. These events are particularly useful for telemetry and debugging purposes.")

Support in all current engines.

(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS11.3+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome

The [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#promiserejectionevent) interface is
defined as follows:

``` idl
[Exposed=*]
interface PromiseRejectionEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, PromiseRejectionEventInit eventInitDict);

  readonly attribute object promise;
  readonly attribute any reason;
};

dictionary PromiseRejectionEventInit : EventInit {
  required object promise;
  any reason;
};
```
