##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.8</span> Import map parse results<a href="#import-map-parse-results" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="import-map-parse-result" class="dfn">import map parse
result</span> is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="import-map-parse-results:struct" data-x-internal="struct">struct</a>
that is similar to a <a href="#concept-script"
id="import-map-parse-results:concept-script">script</a>, and also can be
stored in a [`script`](#the-script-element) element's
<a href="#concept-script-result"
id="import-map-parse-results:concept-script-result">result</a>, but is
not counted as a <a href="#concept-script"
id="import-map-parse-results:concept-script-2">script</a> for other
purposes. It has the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="import-map-parse-results:struct-item"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

An <span id="impr-import-map" class="dfn">import map</span>  
An <a href="#import-map" id="import-map-parse-results:import-map">import
map</a> or null.

An <span id="impr-error-to-rethrow" class="dfn">error to rethrow</span>  
A JavaScript value representing an error that will prevent using this
import map, when non-null.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="create-an-import-map-parse-result" class="dfn">create an
import map parse result</span> given a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-parse-results:string" data-x-internal="string">string</a>
`input` and a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-parse-results:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  Let `result` be an <a href="#import-map-parse-result"
    id="import-map-parse-results:import-map-parse-result">import map parse
    result</a> whose <a href="#impr-import-map"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-import-map">import map</a> is null
    and whose <a href="#impr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-error-to-rethrow">error to rethrow</a>
    is null.

2.  <a href="#parse-an-import-map-string"
    id="import-map-parse-results:parse-an-import-map-string">Parse an import
    map string</a> given `input` and `baseURL`, catching any exceptions.
    If this threw an exception, then set `result`'s
    <a href="#impr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-error-to-rethrow-2">error to
    rethrow</a> to that exception. Otherwise, set `result`'s
    <a href="#impr-import-map"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-import-map-2">import map</a> to
    the return value.

3.  Return `result`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="register-an-import-map" class="dfn">register an import
map</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `global` and an
<a href="#import-map-parse-result"
id="import-map-parse-results:import-map-parse-result-2">import map parse
result</a> `result`:

1.  If `result`'s <a href="#impr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-error-to-rethrow-3">error to
    rethrow</a> is not null, then <a href="#report-an-exception"
    id="import-map-parse-results:report-an-exception">report an
    exception</a> given by `result`'s <a href="#impr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-error-to-rethrow-4">error to
    rethrow</a> for `global` and return.

2.  <a href="#merge-existing-and-new-import-maps"
    id="import-map-parse-results:merge-existing-and-new-import-maps">Merge
    existing and new import maps</a>, given `global` and `result`'s
    <a href="#impr-import-map"
    id="import-map-parse-results:impr-import-map-3">import map</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.4.9</span> Speculation rules parse results<a href="#speculation-rules-parse-results" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="speculation-rules-parse-result" class="dfn">speculation
rules parse result</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:struct"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> that is similar to a
<a href="#concept-script"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-script">script</a>, and also
can be stored in a [`script`](#the-script-element) element's
<a href="#concept-script-result"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-script-result">result</a>,
but is not counted as a <a href="#concept-script"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-script-2">script</a> for
other purposes. It has the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:struct-item"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

A <span id="srpr-sr-set" class="dfn">speculation rule set</span>  
A <a href="#speculation-rule-set"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rule-set">speculation
rule set</a> or null.

An <span id="srpr-error-to-rethrow" class="dfn">error to rethrow</span>  
A JavaScript value representing an error that will prevent using these
speculation rules, when non-null.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="create-a-speculation-rules-parse-result" class="dfn">create
a speculation rules parse result</span> given a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:string"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `input` and a
[`Document`](#document) `document`:

1.  Let `result` be a <a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rules-parse-result">speculation
    rules parse result</a> whose <a href="#srpr-sr-set"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-sr-set">import map</a> is
    null and whose <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow">error to
    rethrow</a> is null.

2.  <a href="#parse-a-speculation-rule-set-string"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:parse-a-speculation-rule-set-string">Parse
    a speculation rule set string</a> given `input`, `document`, and
    `document`'s <a href="#document-base-url"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:document-base-url">document base
    URL</a>, catching any exceptions. If this threw an exception, then
    set `result`'s <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow-2">error to
    rethrow</a> to that exception. Otherwise, set `result`'s
    <a href="#srpr-sr-set"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-sr-set-2">speculation rule
    set</a> to the return value.

3.  Return `result`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="register-speculation-rules" class="dfn">register
speculation rules</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `global`, a
<a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rules-parse-result-2">speculation
rules parse result</a> `result`, and an optional boolean `queueErrors`
(default false):

1.  If `result`'s <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow-3">error to
    rethrow</a> is not null, then:

    1.  If `queueErrors` is true, then <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
        id="speculation-rules-parse-results:queue-a-global-task">queue a global
        task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="speculation-rules-parse-results:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `global` to perform the
        following step:

        1.  <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="speculation-rules-parse-results:report-an-exception">Report an
            exception</a> given by `result`'s
            <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
            id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow-4">error to
            rethrow</a> for `global`.

    2.  Otherwise, <a href="#report-an-exception"
        id="speculation-rules-parse-results:report-an-exception-2">report an
        exception</a> given by `result`'s
        <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
        id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow-5">error to
        rethrow</a> for `global`.

    3.  Return.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:list-append"
    data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `result`'s
    <a href="#srpr-sr-set"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-sr-set-3">speculation rule
    set</a> to `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>'s <a href="#document-sr-sets"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:document-sr-sets">speculation rule
    sets</a>.

3.  <a href="#consider-speculative-loads"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:consider-speculative-loads">Consider
    speculative loads</a> for `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-document-window-2">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="unregister-speculation-rules" class="dfn">unregister
speculation rules</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `global` and a
<a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rules-parse-result-3">speculation
rules parse result</a> `result`:

1.  If `result`'s <a href="#srpr-error-to-rethrow"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-error-to-rethrow-6">error to
    rethrow</a> is not null, then return.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:list-remove"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `result`'s
    <a href="#srpr-sr-set"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-sr-set-4">speculation rule
    set</a> from `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-document-window-3">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>'s <a href="#document-sr-sets"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:document-sr-sets-2">speculation rule
    sets</a>.

3.  <a href="#consider-speculative-loads"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:consider-speculative-loads-2">Consider
    speculative loads</a> for `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-document-window-4">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="update-speculation-rules" class="dfn">update speculation
rules</span> given a [`Window`](#window) `global`, a
<a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rules-parse-result-4">speculation
rules parse result</a> `oldResult`, and a
<a href="#speculation-rules-parse-result"
id="speculation-rules-parse-results:speculation-rules-parse-result-5">speculation
rules parse result</a> `newResult`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:list-remove-2"
    data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `oldResult`'s
    <a href="#srpr-sr-set"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:srpr-sr-set-5">speculation rule
    set</a> from `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:concept-document-window-5">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>'s <a href="#document-sr-sets"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:document-sr-sets-3">speculation rule
    sets</a>.

2.  <a href="#register-speculation-rules"
    id="speculation-rules-parse-results:register-speculation-rules">Register
    speculation rules</a> given `global`, `newResult`, and true.

    <a href="#note-update-speculation-rules-queue-errors"
    class="self-link"></a>When updating speculation rules, as opposed to
    registering them for the first time, we ensure that any
    [`error`](#event-error) events are queued as tasks, instead of
    synchronously fired. Although synchronously executing
    [`error`](#event-error) event handlers is OK when inserting
    [`script`](#the-script-element) elements, it's best if other
    modifications do not cause such synchronous script execution.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.1.5</span> Module specifier resolution<a href="#module-specifier-resolution" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.5.1</span> The resolution algorithm<a href="#the-resolution-algorithm" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier">resolve a
module specifier</a> algorithm is the primary entry point for converting
module specifier strings into
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:url" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>. When
no <a href="#import-map" id="the-resolution-algorithm:import-map">import
maps</a> are involved, it is relatively straightforward, and reduces to
<a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier">resolving
a URL-like module specifier</a>.

When there is a non-empty
<a href="#import-map" id="the-resolution-algorithm:import-map-2">import
map</a> present, the behavior is more complex. It checks candidate
entries from all applicable <a href="#module-specifier-map"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:module-specifier-map">module specifier
maps</a>, from most-specific to least-specific
<a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-import-map-scopes">scopes</a>
(falling back to the top-level unscoped
<a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-import-map-imports">imports</a>),
and from most-specific to least-specific prefixes. For each candidate,
the <a href="#resolving-an-imports-match"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolving-an-imports-match">resolve an
imports match</a> algorithm will give one of the following results:

- Successful resolution of the specifier to a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>.
  Then the <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
  id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-2">resolve a
  module specifier</a> algorithm will return that URL.

- Throwing an exception. Then the <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
  id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-3">resolve a
  module specifier</a> algorithm will rethrow that exception, without
  any further fallbacks.

- Failing to resolve, without an error. In this case the outer
  <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
  id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-4">resolve a
  module specifier</a> algorithm will move on to the next candidate.

In the end, if no successful resolution is found via any of the
candidate <a href="#module-specifier-map"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:module-specifier-map-2">module specifier
maps</a>, <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-5">resolve a
module specifier</a> will throw an exception. Thus the result is always
either a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-3" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> or a
thrown exception.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="resolve-a-module-specifier" class="dfn">resolve a module
specifier</span> given a <a href="#the-script-element"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:the-script-element">script</a>-or-null
`referringScript` and a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:string" data-x-internal="string">string</a>
`specifier`:

1.  Let `settingsObject` and `baseURL` be null.

2.  If `referringScript` is not null, then:

    1.  Set `settingsObject` to `referringScript`'s
        <a href="#settings-object"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:settings-object">settings object</a>.

    2.  Set `baseURL` to `referringScript`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>.

3.  Otherwise:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        there is a <a href="#current-settings-object"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:current-settings-object">current settings
        object</a>.

    2.  Set `settingsObject` to the <a href="#current-settings-object"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:current-settings-object-2">current settings
        object</a>.

    3.  Set `baseURL` to `settingsObject`'s
        <a href="#api-base-url" id="the-resolution-algorithm:api-base-url">API
        base URL</a>.

4.  Let `importMap` be an <a href="#empty-import-map"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:empty-import-map">empty import map</a>.

5.  If `settingsObject`'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-settings-object-global">global
    object</a> implements [`Window`](#window), then set `importMap` to
    `settingsObject`'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-settings-object-global-2">global
    object</a>'s <a href="#concept-global-import-map"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-global-import-map">import map</a>.

6.  Let `serializedBaseURL` be `baseURL`,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-serializer"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialized</a>.

7.  Let `asURL` be the result of
    <a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier-2">resolving
    a URL-like module specifier</a> given `specifier` and `baseURL`.

8.  Let `normalizedSpecifier` be the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-serializer-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
    `asURL`, if `asURL` is non-null; otherwise, `specifier`.

9.  Let `result` be a <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-4" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>-or-null,
    initially null.

10. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `scopePrefix` →
    `scopeImports` of `importMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-import-map-scopes-2">scopes</a>:

    1.  If `scopePrefix` is `serializedBaseURL`, or if `scopePrefix`
        ends with U+002F (/) and `scopePrefix` is a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-prefix"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:code-unit-prefix"
        data-x-internal="code-unit-prefix">code unit prefix</a> of
        `serializedBaseURL`, then:

        1.  Let `scopeImportsMatch` be the result of
            <a href="#resolving-an-imports-match"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolving-an-imports-match-2">resolving an
            imports match</a> given `normalizedSpecifier`, `asURL`, and
            `scopeImports`.

        2.  If `scopeImportsMatch` is not null, then set `result` to
            `scopeImportsMatch`, and
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:break" data-x-internal="break">break</a>.

11. If `result` is null, set `result` to the result of
    <a href="#resolving-an-imports-match"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolving-an-imports-match-3">resolving an
    imports match</a> given `normalizedSpecifier`, `asURL`, and
    `importMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-import-map-imports-2">imports</a>.

12. If `result` is null, set it to `asURL`.

    By this point, if `result` was null, `specifier` wasn't remapped to
    anything by `importMap`, but it might have been able to be turned
    into a URL.

13. If `result` is not null, then:

    1.  <a href="#add-module-to-resolved-module-set"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:add-module-to-resolved-module-set">Add
        module to resolved module set</a> given `settingsObject`,
        `serializedBaseURL`, `normalizedSpecifier`, and `asURL`.

    2.  Return `result`.

14. Throw a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>
    indicating that `specifier` was a bare specifier, but was not
    remapped to anything by `importMap`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="resolving-an-imports-match" class="dfn">resolve an imports
match</span>, given a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:string-2"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `normalizedSpecifier`, a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-5" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>-or-null
`asURL`, and a <a href="#module-specifier-map"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:module-specifier-map-3">module specifier
map</a> `specifierMap`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:list-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `specifierKey` →
    `resolutionResult` of `specifierMap`:

    1.  If `specifierKey` is `normalizedSpecifier`, then:

        1.  If `resolutionResult` is null, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
            data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:typeerror-2">TypeError</code></a>
            indicating that resolution of `specifierKey` was blocked by
            a null entry.

            This will terminate the entire
            <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-6">resolve a
            module specifier</a> algorithm, without any further
            fallbacks.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:assert-2"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `resolutionResult` is a
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-6" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>.

        3.  Return `resolutionResult`.

    2.  If all of the following are true:

        - `specifierKey` ends with U+002F (/);

        - `specifierKey` is a
          <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-prefix"
          id="the-resolution-algorithm:code-unit-prefix-2"
          data-x-internal="code-unit-prefix">code unit prefix</a> of
          `normalizedSpecifier`; and

        - either `asURL` is null, or `asURL`
          <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special"
          id="the-resolution-algorithm:is-special" data-x-internal="is-special">is
          special</a>,

        then:

        1.  If `resolutionResult` is null, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
            data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:typeerror-3">TypeError</code></a>
            indicating that the resolution of `specifierKey` was blocked
            by a null entry.

            This will terminate the entire
            <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-7">resolve a
            module specifier</a> algorithm, without any further
            fallbacks.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:assert-3"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `resolutionResult` is a
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-7" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>.

        3.  Let `afterPrefix` be the portion of `normalizedSpecifier`
            after the initial `specifierKey` prefix.

        4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:assert-4"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `resolutionResult`,
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-serializer-3"
            data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialized</a>,
            ends with U+002F (/), as enforced during
            <a href="#parse-an-import-map-string"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:parse-an-import-map-string">parsing</a>.

        5.  Let `url` be the result of
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-parser"
            data-x-internal="url-parser">URL parsing</a> `afterPrefix`
            with `resolutionResult`.

        6.  If `url` is failure, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
            data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:typeerror-4">TypeError</code></a>
            indicating that resolution of `normalizedSpecifier` was
            blocked since the `afterPrefix` portion could not be
            URL-parsed relative to the `resolutionResult` mapped to by
            the `specifierKey` prefix.

            This will terminate the entire
            <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-8">resolve a
            module specifier</a> algorithm, without any further
            fallbacks.

        7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:assert-5"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `url` is a
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-8" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>.

        8.  If the
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-serializer-4"
            data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a>
            of `resolutionResult` is not a
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-prefix"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:code-unit-prefix-3"
            data-x-internal="code-unit-prefix">code unit prefix</a> of
            the
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-serializer-5"
            data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a>
            of `url`, then throw a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
            data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:typeerror-5">TypeError</code></a>
            indicating that the resolution of `normalizedSpecifier` was
            blocked due to it backtracking above its prefix
            `specifierKey`.

            This will terminate the entire
            <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
            id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-9">resolve a
            module specifier</a> algorithm, without any further
            fallbacks.

        9.  Return `url`.

2.  Return null.

    The <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:resolve-a-module-specifier-10">resolve a
    module specifier</a> algorithm will fall back to a less-specific
    scope, or to "`imports`", if possible.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier" class="dfn">resolve
a URL-like module specifier</span>, given a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:string-3"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `specifier` and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-9" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  If `specifier`
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-starts-with"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:starts-with"
    data-x-internal="starts-with">starts with</a> "`/`", "`./`", or
    "`../`", then:

    1.  Let `url` be the result of
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-parser-2"
        data-x-internal="url-parser">URL parsing</a> `specifier` with
        `baseURL`.

    2.  If `url` is failure, then return null.

        One way this could happen is if `specifier` is "`../foo`" and
        `baseURL` is a
        <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
        data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code
        id="the-resolution-algorithm:data-protocol">data:</code></a>
        URL.

    3.  Return `url`.

    This includes cases where `specifier`
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-starts-with"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:starts-with-2"
    data-x-internal="starts-with">starts with</a> "`//`", i.e.,
    scheme-relative URLs. Thus, `url` might end up with a different
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:concept-url-host"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-host">host</a> than `baseURL`.

2.  Let `url` be the result of
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
    id="the-resolution-algorithm:url-parser-3"
    data-x-internal="url-parser">URL parsing</a> `specifier` (with no
    base URL).

3.  If `url` is failure, then return null.

4.  Return `url`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.5.2</span> Import maps<a href="#import-maps" class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#import-map" id="import-map-dev">import map</a> allows
control over module specifier resolution. Import maps are delivered via
inline [`script`](#the-script-element) elements with their
[`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute set to "`importmap`", and with
their <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="import-maps:child-text-content"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> containing a
JSON representation of the import map.

A [`Document`](#document) can have multiple import maps processed, which
can happen either before or after any modules have been imported, e.g.,
via <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
data-x-internal="import()"><code
id="import-maps:import()">import()</code></a> expressions or
[`script`](#the-script-element) elements with their
[`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute set to "`module`". The
<a href="#merge-existing-and-new-import-maps"
id="import-maps:merge-existing-and-new-import-maps">merge existing and
new import maps</a> algorithm ensures that new import maps cannot define
the module resolution for modules that were already defined by past
import maps, or for ones that were already resolved.

<div id="example-import-map-bare-specifier" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-bare-specifier" class="self-link"></a>

The simplest use of import maps is to globally remap a bare module
specifier:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js"
  }
}
```

This enables statements like `import moment from "moment";` to work,
fetching and evaluating the JavaScript module at the
`/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js` URL.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-trailing-slashes" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-trailing-slashes" class="self-link"></a>

An import map can remap a class of module specifiers into a class of
URLs by using trailing slashes, like so:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "moment/": "/node_modules/moment/src/"
  }
}
```

This enables statements like
`import localeData from "moment/locale/zh-cn.js";` to work, fetching and
evaluating the JavaScript module at the
`/node_modules/moment/src/locale/zh-cn.js` URL. Such trailing-slash
mappings are often combined with bare-specifier mappings, e.g.

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js",
    "moment/": "/node_modules/moment/src/"
  }
}
```

so that both the "main module" specified by "`moment`" and the
"submodules" specified by paths such as "`moment/locale/zh-cn.js`" are
available.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-url-like-specifier" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-url-like-specifier" class="self-link"></a>

Bare specifiers are not the only type of module specifiers which import
maps can remap. "URL-like" specifiers, i.e., those that are either
parseable as absolute URLs or start with "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`", can
be remapped as well:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "https://cdn.example.com/vue/dist/vue.runtime.esm.js": "/node_modules/vue/dist/vue.runtime.esm.js",
    "/js/app.mjs": "/js/app-8e0d62a03.mjs",
    "../helpers/": "https://cdn.example/helpers/"
  }
}
```

Note how the URL to be remapped, as well as the URL being mapped to, can
be specified either as absolute URLs, or as relative URLs starting with
"`/`", "`./`", or "`../`". (They cannot be specified as relative URLs
without those starting sigils, as those help distinguish from bare
module specifiers.) Also note how the [trailing slash
mapping](#example-import-map-trailing-slashes) works in this context as
well.

Such remappings operate on the post-canonicalization URL, and do not
require a match between the literal strings supplied in the import map
key and the imported module specifier. So for example, if this import
map was included on `https://example.com/app.html`, then not only would
`import "/js/app.mjs"` be remapped, but so would `import "./js/app.mjs"`
and `import "./foo/../js/app.mjs"`.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-scopes" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-scopes" class="self-link"></a>

All previous examples have globally remapped module specifiers, by using
the top-level "`imports`" key in the import map. The top-level
"`scopes`" key can be used to provide localized remappings, which only
apply when the referring module matches a specific URL prefix. For
example:

``` json
{
  "scopes": {
    "/a/" : {
      "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js"
    },
    "/b/" : {
      "moment": "https://cdn.example.com/moment/src/moment.js"
    }
  }
}
```

With this import map, the statement `import "moment"` will have
different meanings depending on which referrer script contains the
statement:

- Inside scripts located under `/a/`, this will import
  `/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js`.

- Inside scripts located under `/b/`, this will import
  `https://cdn.example.com/moment/src/moment.js`.

- Inside scripts located under `/c/`, this will fail to resolve and thus
  throw an exception.

A typical usage of scopes is to allow multiple versions of the "same"
module to exist in a web application, with some parts of the module
graph importing one version, and other parts importing another version.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-scopes-overlapping" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-scopes-overlapping" class="self-link"></a>

Scopes can overlap each other, and overlap the global "`imports`"
specifier map. At resolution time, scopes are consulted in order of
most- to least-specific, where specificity is measured by sorting the
scopes using the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-less-than"
id="import-maps:code-unit-less-than"
data-x-internal="code-unit-less-than">code unit less than</a> operation.
So, for example, "`/scope2/scope3/`" is treated as more specific than
"`/scope2/`", which is treated as more specific than the top-level
(unscoped) mappings.

The following import map illustrates this:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "a": "/a-1.mjs",
    "b": "/b-1.mjs",
    "c": "/c-1.mjs"
  },
  "scopes": {
    "/scope2/": {
      "a": "/a-2.mjs"
    },
    "/scope2/scope3/": {
      "b": "/b-3.mjs"
    }
  }
}
```

This results in the following resolutions (using relative URLs for
brevity):

|          |                        | Specifier  |            |            |
|----------|------------------------|------------|------------|------------|
|          |                        | "`a`"      | "`b`"      | "`c`"      |
| Referrer | `/scope1/r.mjs`        | `/a-1.mjs` | `/b-1.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |
|          | `/scope2/r.mjs`        | `/a-2.mjs` | `/b-1.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |
|          | `/scope2/scope3/r.mjs` | `/a-2.mjs` | `/b-3.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-integrity" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-integrity" class="self-link"></a>

Import maps can also be used to provide modules with integrity metadata
to be used in Subresource Integrity checks. [\[SRI\]](#refsSRI)

The following import map illustrates this:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "a": "/a-1.mjs",
    "b": "/b-1.mjs",
    "c": "/c-1.mjs"
  },
  "integrity": {
    "/a-1.mjs": "sha384-Li9vy3DqF8tnTXuiaAJuML3ky+er10rcgNR/VqsVpcw+ThHmYcwiB1pbOxEbzJr7",
    "/d-1.mjs": "sha384-MBO5IDfYaE6c6Aao94oZrIOiC6CGiSN2n4QUbHNPhzk5Xhm0djZLQqTpL0HzTUxk"
  }
}
```

The above example provides integrity metadata to be enforced on the
modules `/a-1.mjs` and `/d-1.mjs`, even if the latter is not defined as
an import in the map.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="import-maps:child-text-content-2"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> of a
[`script`](#the-script-element) element representing an
<a href="#import-map" id="import-maps:import-map">import map</a> must
match the following <span id="import-map-authoring-requirements"
class="dfn">import map authoring requirements</span>:

- It must be valid JSON. [\[JSON\]](#refsJSON)

- The JSON must represent a JSON object, with at most the three keys
  "`imports`", "`scopes`", and "`integrity`".

- The values corresponding to the "`imports`", "`scopes`", and
  "`integrity`" keys, if present, must themselves be JSON objects.

- The value corresponding to the "`imports`" key, if present, must be a
  <a href="#valid-module-specifier-map"
  id="import-maps:valid-module-specifier-map">valid module specifier
  map</a>.

- The value corresponding to the "`scopes`" key, if present, must be a
  JSON object, whose keys are
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
  id="import-maps:valid-url-string"
  data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL strings</a> and whose
  values are <a href="#valid-module-specifier-map"
  id="import-maps:valid-module-specifier-map-2">valid module specifier
  maps</a>.

- The value corresponding to the "`integrity`" key, if present, must be
  a JSON object, whose keys are
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
  id="import-maps:valid-url-string-2"
  data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL strings</a> and whose
  values fit <a
  href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#the-integrity-attribute"
  id="import-maps:the-requirements-of-the-integrity-attribute"
  data-x-internal="the-requirements-of-the-integrity-attribute">the
  requirements of the integrity attribute</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="valid-module-specifier-map" class="dfn">valid module
specifier map</span> is a JSON object that meets the following
requirements:

- All of its keys must be nonempty.

- All of its values must be strings.

- Each value must be either a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
  id="import-maps:absolute-url" data-x-internal="absolute-url">valid
  absolute URL</a> or a
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
  id="import-maps:valid-url-string-3"
  data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL string</a> that
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-starts-with"
  id="import-maps:starts-with" data-x-internal="starts-with">starts
  with</a> "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`".

- If a given key
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-ends-with"
  id="import-maps:ends-with" data-x-internal="ends-with">ends with</a>
  "`/`", then the corresponding value must also.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.5.3</span> Import map processing model<a href="#import-map-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

Formally, an <span id="import-map" class="dfn">import map</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="import-map-processing-model:struct"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> with three
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="import-map-processing-model:struct-item"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

- <span id="concept-import-map-imports" class="dfn">imports</span>, a
  <a href="#module-specifier-map"
  id="import-map-processing-model:module-specifier-map">module specifier
  map</a>;

- <span id="concept-import-map-scopes" class="dfn">scopes</span>, an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
  id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map"
  data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> of
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="import-map-processing-model:url" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a> to
  <a href="#module-specifier-map"
  id="import-map-processing-model:module-specifier-map-2">module specifier
  maps</a>; and

- <span id="concept-import-map-integrity" class="dfn">integrity</span>,
  a <a href="#module-integrity-map"
  id="import-map-processing-model:module-integrity-map">module integrity
  map</a>.

A <span id="module-specifier-map" class="dfn">module specifier
map</span> is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-2"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
id="import-map-processing-model:map-key"
data-x-internal="map-key">keys</a> are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string"
data-x-internal="string">strings</a> and whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-value"
id="import-map-processing-model:map-value"
data-x-internal="map-value">values</a> are either
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-2" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a> or
nulls.

A <span id="module-integrity-map" class="dfn">module integrity
map</span> is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-3"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-2"
data-x-internal="map-key">keys</a> are
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-3" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>
and whose <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-value"
id="import-map-processing-model:map-value-2"
data-x-internal="map-value">values</a> are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-2"
data-x-internal="string">strings</a> that will be used as <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-request-integrity-metadata"
data-x-internal="concept-request-integrity-metadata">integrity
metadata</a>.

An <span id="empty-import-map" class="dfn">empty import map</span> is an
<a href="#import-map" id="import-map-processing-model:import-map">import
map</a> with its <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports">imports</a>
and <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes">scopes</a>
both being empty maps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A <span id="specifier-resolution-record" class="dfn">specifier
resolution record</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="import-map-processing-model:struct-2"
data-x-internal="struct">struct</a>. It has the following
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="import-map-processing-model:struct-item-2"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a>:

A <span id="specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url" class="dfn">serialized base URL</span>  
A <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-3"
data-x-internal="string">string</a>-or-null that represents the base URL
of the specifier, when one exists.

A <span id="specifier-resolution-record-specifier" class="dfn">specifier</span>  
A <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-4"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> representing the specifier.

A <span id="specifier-resolution-record-as-url" class="dfn">specifier as a URL</span>  
A <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-4" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>-or-null
that represents the URL in case of a URL-like module specifier.

Implementations can replace
<a href="#specifier-resolution-record-as-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-as-url">specifier
as a URL</a> with a boolean that indicates that the specifier is either
bare or URL-like that <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special"
id="import-map-processing-model:is-special"
data-x-internal="is-special">is special</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="add-module-to-resolved-module-set" class="dfn">add module
to resolved module set</span> given an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="import-map-processing-model:environment-settings-object">environment
settings object</a> `settingsObject`, a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-5"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `serializedBaseURL`, a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-6"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `normalizedSpecifier`, and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-5" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>-or-null
`asURL`:

1.  Let `global` be `settingsObject`'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-settings-object-global">global
    object</a>.

2.  If `global` does not implement [`Window`](#window), then return.

3.  Let `record` be a new <a href="#specifier-resolution-record"
    id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record">specifier
    resolution record</a>, with
    <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url"
    id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url">serialized
    base URL</a> set to `serializedBaseURL`,
    <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-specifier"
    id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-specifier">specifier</a>
    set to `normalizedSpecifier`, and
    <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-as-url"
    id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-as-url-2">specifier
    as a URL</a> set to `asURL`.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="import-map-processing-model:set-append"
    data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a> `record` to `global`'s
    <a href="#resolved-module-set"
    id="import-map-processing-model:resolved-module-set">resolved module
    set</a>.

</div>
