<div algorithm="">

To <span id="parse-an-import-map-string" class="dfn">parse an import map
string</span>, given a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-7"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `input` and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-6" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  Let `parsed` be the result of <a
    href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#parse-a-json-string-to-an-infra-value"
    id="import-map-processing-model:parse-a-json-string-to-an-infra-value"
    data-x-internal="parse-a-json-string-to-an-infra-value">parsing a JSON
    string to an Infra value</a> given `input`.

2.  If `parsed` is not an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-4"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>, then throw a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
    id="import-map-processing-model:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>
    indicating that the top-level value needs to be a JSON object.

3.  Let `sortedAndNormalizedImports` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-5"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

4.  If `parsed`\["`imports`"\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then:

    1.  If `parsed`\["`imports`"\] is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-6"
        data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>, then throw a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="import-map-processing-model:typeerror-2">TypeError</code></a>
        indicating that the value for the "`imports`" top-level key
        needs to be a JSON object.

    2.  Set `sortedAndNormalizedImports` to the result of
        <a href="#sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map">sorting
        and normalizing a module specifier map</a> given
        `parsed`\["`imports`"\] and `baseURL`.

5.  Let `sortedAndNormalizedScopes` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-7"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

6.  If `parsed`\["`scopes`"\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists-2"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then:

    1.  If `parsed`\["`scopes`"\] is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-8"
        data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>, then throw a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="import-map-processing-model:typeerror-3">TypeError</code></a>
        indicating that the value for the "`scopes`" top-level key needs
        to be a JSON object.

    2.  Set `sortedAndNormalizedScopes` to the result of
        <a href="#sorting-and-normalizing-scopes"
        id="import-map-processing-model:sorting-and-normalizing-scopes">sorting
        and normalizing scopes</a> given `parsed`\["`scopes`"\] and
        `baseURL`.

7.  Let `normalizedIntegrity` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-9"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

8.  If `parsed`\["`integrity`"\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists-3"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then:

    1.  If `parsed`\["`integrity`"\] is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-10"
        data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>, then throw a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="import-map-processing-model:typeerror-4">TypeError</code></a>
        indicating that the value for the "`integrity`" top-level key
        needs to be a JSON object.

    2.  Set `normalizedIntegrity` to the result of
        <a href="#normalizing-a-module-integrity-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:normalizing-a-module-integrity-map">normalizing
        a module integrity map</a> given `parsed`\["`integrity`"\] and
        `baseURL`.

9.  If `parsed`'s <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-3"
    data-x-internal="map-key">keys</a>
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="import-map-processing-model:list-contains"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> any items besides
    "`imports`", "`scopes`", or "`integrity`", then the user agent
    should <a
    href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
    id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console"
    data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
    the console</a> indicating that an invalid top-level key was present
    in the import map.

    This can help detect typos. It is not an error, because that would
    prevent any future extensions from being added backward-compatibly.

10. Return an <a href="#import-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:import-map-2">import map</a> whose
    <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports-2">imports</a>
    are `sortedAndNormalizedImports`, whose
    <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-2">scopes</a>
    are `sortedAndNormalizedScopes`, and whose
    <a href="#concept-import-map-integrity"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-integrity">integrity</a>
    are `normalizedIntegrity`.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-normalization" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-normalization" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#import-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:import-map-3">import map</a> that
results from this parsing algorithm is highly normalized. For example,
given a base URL of `https://example.com/base/page.html`, the input

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "node_modules/helper/index.mjs",
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

will generate an <a href="#import-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:import-map-4">import map</a> with
<a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports-3">imports</a>
of

    «[
      "https://example.com/app/helper" → https://example.com/base/node_modules/helper/index.mjs
      "lodash" → https://example.com/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js
    ]»

and (despite nothing being present in the input string) an empty
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-11"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> for its
<a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-3">scopes</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="merge-module-specifier-maps" class="dfn">merge module
specifier maps</span>, given a <a href="#module-specifier-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:module-specifier-map-3">module specifier
map</a> `newMap` and a <a href="#module-specifier-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:module-specifier-map-4">module specifier
map</a> `oldMap`:

1.  Let `mergedMap` be a deep copy of `oldMap`.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-iterate"
    data-x-internal="map-iterate">For each</a> `specifier` → `url` of
    `newMap`:

    1.  If `specifier`
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists-4"
        data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a> in `oldMap`, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-2"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating the ignored rule. They may choose
            to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing
            one.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    2.  Set `mergedMap`\[`specifier`\] to `url`.

3.  Return `mergedMap`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="merge-existing-and-new-import-maps" class="dfn">merge
existing and new import maps</span>, given a
<a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
id="import-map-processing-model:concept-settings-object-global-2">global
object</a> `global` and an <a href="#import-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:import-map-5">import map</a>
`newImportMap`:

1.  Let `newImportMapScopes` be a deep copy of `newImportMap`'s
    <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-4">scopes</a>.

    We're mutating these copies and removing items from them when they
    are used to ignore scope-specific rules. This is true for
    `newImportMapScopes`, as well as to `newImportMapImports` below.

2.  Let `oldImportMap` be `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-global-import-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-global-import-map">import
    map</a>.

3.  Let `newImportMapImports` be a deep copy of `newImportMap`'s
    <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports-4">imports</a>.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="map-iterate">For each</a> `scopePrefix` →
    `scopeImports` of `newImportMapScopes`:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `record` of
        `global`'s <a href="#resolved-module-set"
        id="import-map-processing-model:resolved-module-set-2">resolved module
        set</a>:

        1.  If `scopePrefix` is `record`'s
            <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url"
            id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url-2">serialized
            base URL</a>, or if `scopePrefix` ends with U+002F (/) and
            `scopePrefix` is a
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-prefix"
            id="import-map-processing-model:code-unit-prefix"
            data-x-internal="code-unit-prefix">code unit prefix</a> of
            `record`'s
            <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url"
            id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-serialized-base-url-3">serialized
            base URL</a>, then:

            1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
                id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-2"
                data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a>
                `specifierKey` → `resolutionResult` of `scopeImports`:

                1.  If `specifierKey` is `record`'s
                    <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-specifier"
                    id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-specifier-2">specifier</a>,
                    or if all of the following conditions are true:

                    - `specifierKey` ends with U+002F (/);

                    - `specifierKey` is a
                      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-prefix"
                      id="import-map-processing-model:code-unit-prefix-2"
                      data-x-internal="code-unit-prefix">code unit prefix</a>
                      of `record`'s
                      <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-specifier"
                      id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-specifier-3">specifier</a>;

                    - either `record`'s
                      <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-as-url"
                      id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-as-url-3">specifier
                      as a URL</a> is null or
                      <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special"
                      id="import-map-processing-model:is-special-2"
                      data-x-internal="is-special">is special</a>,

                    then:

                    1.  The user agent may <a
                        href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
                        id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-3"
                        data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
                        the console</a> indicating the ignored rule.
                        They may choose to avoid reporting if the rule
                        is identical to an existing one.

                    2.  Remove `scopeImports`\[`specifierKey`\].

        Implementers are encouraged to implement a more efficient
        matching algorithm when working with the
        <a href="#resolved-module-set"
        id="import-map-processing-model:resolved-module-set-3">resolved module
        set</a>. As guidance, the number of resolved/mapped modules in a
        large application can be on the order of thousands.

    2.  If `scopePrefix`
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists-5"
        data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a> in `oldImportMap`'s
        <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-5">scopes</a>,
        then set `oldImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-6">scopes</a>\[`scopePrefix`\]
        to the result of <a href="#merge-module-specifier-maps"
        id="import-map-processing-model:merge-module-specifier-maps">merging
        module specifier maps</a>, given `scopeImports` and
        `oldImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-7">scopes</a>\[`scopePrefix`\].

    3.  Otherwise, set `oldImportMap`'s
        <a href="#concept-import-map-scopes"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-scopes-8">scopes</a>\[`scopePrefix`\]
        to `scopeImports`.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-iterate-3"
    data-x-internal="map-iterate">For each</a> `url` → `integrity` of
    `newImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-integrity"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-integrity-2">integrity</a>:

    1.  If `url` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="import-map-processing-model:map-exists-6"
        data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a> in `oldImportMap`'s
        <a href="#concept-import-map-integrity"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-integrity-3">integrity</a>,
        then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-4"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating the ignored rule. They may choose
            to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing
            one.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-2"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    2.  Set `oldImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-integrity"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-integrity-4">integrity</a>\[`url`\]
        to `integrity`.

6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-3"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `record` of `global`'s
    <a href="#resolved-module-set"
    id="import-map-processing-model:resolved-module-set-4">resolved module
    set</a>:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-4"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `specifier` → `url`
        of `newImportMapImports`:

        1.  If `specifier`
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-starts-with"
            id="import-map-processing-model:starts-with"
            data-x-internal="starts-with">starts with</a> `record`'s
            <a href="#specifier-resolution-record-specifier"
            id="import-map-processing-model:specifier-resolution-record-specifier-4">specifier</a>,
            then:

            1.  The user agent may <a
                href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
                id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-5"
                data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
                the console</a> indicating the ignored rule. They may
                choose to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an
                existing one.

            2.  Remove `newImportMapImports`\[`specifier`\].

7.  Set `oldImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports-5">imports</a>
    to the result of <a href="#merge-module-specifier-maps"
    id="import-map-processing-model:merge-module-specifier-maps-2">merge
    module specifier maps</a>, given `newImportMapImports` and
    `oldImportMap`'s <a href="#concept-import-map-imports"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-import-map-imports-6">imports</a>.

</div>

The above algorithm merges a new import map into the given
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="import-map-processing-model:environment-settings-object-2">environment
settings object</a>'s <a href="#global-object"
id="import-map-processing-model:global-object">global object</a>'s
<a href="#import-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:import-map-6">import map</a>. Let's
examine a few examples:

<div id="example-import-map-merge-unrelated" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-merge-unrelated" class="self-link"></a>

There are two cases when rules of the new import map don't get merged
into the existing one.

1.  The new import map rule has the exact same scope and specifier as a
    rule in the existing import map. We'll call that "conflicting rule".

2.  The new import map rule may impact the resolution of an already
    resolved module. We'll call that "impacted already resolved module".

When the new import map has no conflicting rules, and there are no
impacted resolved modules, the resulting map would be a combination of
the new and existing maps. Rules that would have individually impacted
similar modules (e.g. "/app/" and "/app/helper") but are not an exact
match are not conflicting, and all make it to the merged map.

So, the following existing and new import maps:

``` json
{
   "imports": {
    "/app/": "./original-app/",
  }
}
```

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
  },
  "scopes": {
    "/js": {
      "/app/": "./js-app/"
    }
  }
}
```

Would be equivalent to the following single import map:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "/app/": "./original-app/",
    "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
  },
  "scopes": {
    "/js": {
      "/app/": "./js-app/"
    }
  }
}
```

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-merge-conflict-imports" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-merge-conflict-imports"
class="self-link"></a>

When the new import map impacts an already resolved module, that rule
gets dropped from the import map.

So, if the <a href="#resolved-module-set"
id="import-map-processing-model:resolved-module-set-5">resolved module
set</a> already contains the "`/app/helper`", the following new import
map:

``` json
{
   "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

Would be equivalent to the following one:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-merge-conflict-scopes" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-merge-conflict-scopes"
class="self-link"></a>

The same is true for rules that impact already resolved modules defined
in specific scopes. If we already resolved "`/app/helper`" from
"`/app/main.mjs`" the following new import map:

``` json
{
  "scopes": {
    "/app/": {
      "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
    }
  },
   "imports": {
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

Would similarly be equivalent to:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-merge-conflict-imports-and-scopes"
class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-merge-conflict-imports-and-scopes"
class="self-link"></a>

We could also have cases where a single already-resolved module
specifier has multiple rules for its resolution, depending on the
referring script. In such cases, only the relevant rules would not be
added to the map.

For example, if we already resolved "`/app/helper`" from
"`/app/vendor/main.mjs`", the following new import map:

``` json
{
  "scopes": {
    "/app/": {
      "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
    },
    "/app/vendor/": {
      "/app/": "./vendor_helper/"
    },
    "/vendor/": {
      "/app/helper": "./helper/vendor_index.mjs"
    }
  },
   "imports": {
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
    "/app/": "./general_app_path/"
    "/app/helper": "./other_path/helper/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

Would be equivalent to:

``` json
{
  "scopes": {
    "/vendor/": {
      "/app/helper": "./helper/vendor_index.mjs"
    }
  },
  "imports": {
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

This is achieved by the fact that the merge algorithm tracks already
resolved modules and removes rules affecting them from new import maps
before they are merged into the existing one.

</div>

<div id="example-import-map-merge-two-map-conflict" class="example">

<a href="#example-import-map-merge-two-map-conflict"
class="self-link"></a>

When the new import map has conflicting rules to the existing import
map, with no impacted already resolved modules, the existing import map
rules persist.

For example, the following existing and new import maps:

``` json
{
   "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
  }
}
```

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "./main/helper/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

Would be equivalent to the following single import map:

``` json
{
  "imports": {
    "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
    "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js",
  }
}
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map"
class="dfn">sort and normalize a module specifier map</span>, given an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-12"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> `originalMap` and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-7" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  Let `normalized` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-13"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-5"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `specifierKey` → `value`
    of `originalMap`:

    1.  Let `normalizedSpecifierKey` be the result of
        <a href="#normalizing-a-specifier-key"
        id="import-map-processing-model:normalizing-a-specifier-key">normalizing
        a specifier key</a> given `specifierKey` and `baseURL`.

    2.  If `normalizedSpecifierKey` is null, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="import-map-processing-model:continue-3"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a>.

    3.  If `value` is not a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
        id="import-map-processing-model:string-8"
        data-x-internal="string">string</a>, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-6"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating that addresses need to be
            strings.

        2.  Set `normalized`\[`normalizedSpecifierKey`\] to null.

        3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-4"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    4.  Let `addressURL` be the result of
        <a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
        id="import-map-processing-model:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier">resolving
        a URL-like module specifier</a> given `value` and `baseURL`.

    5.  If `addressURL` is null, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-7"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating that the address was invalid.

        2.  Set `normalized`\[`normalizedSpecifierKey`\] to null.

        3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-5"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    6.  If `specifierKey` ends with U+002F (/), and the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-url-serializer"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
        `addressURL` does not end with U+002F (/), then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-8"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating that an invalid address was given
            for the specifier key `specifierKey`; since `specifierKey`
            ends with a slash, the address needs to as well.

        2.  Set `normalized`\[`normalizedSpecifierKey`\] to null.

        3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-6"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    7.  Set `normalized`\[`normalizedSpecifierKey`\] to `addressURL`.

3.  Return the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-sort-in-descending-order"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-sort-descending"
    data-x-internal="map-sort-descending">sorting in descending order</a>
    `normalized`, with an entry `a` being less than an entry `b` if
    `a`'s <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-4"
    data-x-internal="map-key">key</a> is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-less-than"
    id="import-map-processing-model:code-unit-less-than"
    data-x-internal="code-unit-less-than">code unit less than</a> `b`'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-5"
    data-x-internal="map-key">key</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="sorting-and-normalizing-scopes" class="dfn">sort and
normalize scopes</span>, given an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-14"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> `originalMap` and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-8" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  Let `normalized` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-15"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-6"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `scopePrefix` →
    `potentialSpecifierMap` of `originalMap`:

    1.  If `potentialSpecifierMap` is not an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-16"
        data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>, then throw a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="import-map-processing-model:typeerror-5">TypeError</code></a>
        indicating that the value of the scope with prefix `scopePrefix`
        needs to be a JSON object.

    2.  Let `scopePrefixURL` be the result of
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
        id="import-map-processing-model:url-parser"
        data-x-internal="url-parser">URL parsing</a> `scopePrefix` with
        `baseURL`.

    3.  If `scopePrefixURL` is failure, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-9"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> that the scope prefix URL was not parseable.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-7"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    4.  Let `normalizedScopePrefix` be the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
        id="import-map-processing-model:concept-url-serializer-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
        `scopePrefixURL`.

    5.  Set `normalized`\[`normalizedScopePrefix`\] to the result of
        <a href="#sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map"
        id="import-map-processing-model:sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map-2">sorting
        and normalizing a module specifier map</a> given
        `potentialSpecifierMap` and `baseURL`.

3.  Return the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-sort-in-descending-order"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-sort-descending-2"
    data-x-internal="map-sort-descending">sorting in descending order</a>
    `normalized`, with an entry `a` being less than an entry `b` if
    `a`'s <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-6"
    data-x-internal="map-key">key</a> is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-less-than"
    id="import-map-processing-model:code-unit-less-than-2"
    data-x-internal="code-unit-less-than">code unit less than</a> `b`'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key"
    id="import-map-processing-model:map-key-7"
    data-x-internal="map-key">key</a>.

</div>

In the above two algorithms, sorting keys and scopes in descending order
has the effect of putting "`foo/bar/`" before "`foo/`". This in turn
gives "`foo/bar/`" a higher priority than "`foo/`" during
<a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
id="import-map-processing-model:resolve-a-module-specifier">module
specifier resolution</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="normalizing-a-module-integrity-map" class="dfn">normalize a
module integrity map</span>, given an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-17"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a> `originalMap`:

1.  Let `normalized` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="import-map-processing-model:ordered-map-18"
    data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="import-map-processing-model:list-iterate-7"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `key` → `value` of
    `originalMap`:

    1.  Let `resolvedURL` be the result of
        <a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
        id="import-map-processing-model:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier-2">resolving
        a URL-like module specifier</a> given `key` and `baseURL`.

        Unlike "`imports`", keys of the integrity map are treated as
        URLs, not module specifiers. However, we use the
        <a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
        id="import-map-processing-model:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier-3">resolve
        a URL-like module specifier</a> algorithm to prohibit "bare"
        relative URLs like `foo`, which could be mistaken for module
        specifiers.

    2.  If `resolvedURL` is null, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-10"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating that the key failed to resolve.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-8"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    3.  If `value` is not a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
        id="import-map-processing-model:string-9"
        data-x-internal="string">string</a>, then:

        1.  The user agent may <a
            href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
            id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-11"
            data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
            the console</a> indicating that <a
            href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata"
            id="import-map-processing-model:concept-request-integrity-metadata-2"
            data-x-internal="concept-request-integrity-metadata">integrity
            metadata</a> values need to be
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
            id="import-map-processing-model:string-10"
            data-x-internal="string">strings</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
            id="import-map-processing-model:continue-9"
            data-x-internal="continue">Continue</a>.

    4.  Set `normalized`\[`resolvedURL`\] to `value`.

3.  Return `normalized`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="normalizing-a-specifier-key" class="dfn">normalize a
specifier key</span>, given a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="import-map-processing-model:string-11"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> `specifierKey` and a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="import-map-processing-model:url-9" data-x-internal="url">URL</a>
`baseURL`:

1.  If `specifierKey` is the empty string, then:

    1.  The user agent may <a
        href="https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console"
        id="import-map-processing-model:report-a-warning-to-the-console-12"
        data-x-internal="report-a-warning-to-the-console">report a warning to
        the console</a> indicating that specifier keys may not be the
        empty string.

    2.  Return null.

2.  Let `url` be the result of
    <a href="#resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier"
    id="import-map-processing-model:resolving-a-url-like-module-specifier-4">resolving
    a URL-like module specifier</a>, given `specifierKey` and `baseURL`.

3.  If `url` is not null, then return the
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="import-map-processing-model:concept-url-serializer-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of `url`.

4.  Return `specifierKey`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.1.6</span> JavaScript specification host hooks<a href="#javascript-specification-host-hooks" class="self-link"></a>

The JavaScript specification contains a number of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="javascript-specification-host-hooks:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
abstract operations, that vary depending on the host environment. This
section defines them for user agent hosts.

<div algorithm="">

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.1</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnsureCanAddPrivateElement</span>(`O`)<a href="#the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation"
class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostensurecanaddprivateelement"
id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:js-hostensurecanaddprivateelement"
data-x-internal="js-hostensurecanaddprivateelement">HostEnsureCanAddPrivateElement</a>(`O`)
abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  If `O` is a [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) object, or
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements"
    id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:implements"
    data-x-internal="implements">implements</a> [`Location`](#location),
    then return <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
    id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:throwcompletion"
    data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(a new <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
    id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>).

2.  Return <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion"
    id="the-hostensurecanaddprivateelement-implementation:normalcompletion"
    data-x-internal="normalcompletion">NormalCompletion</a>(unused).

</div>

JavaScript private fields can be applied to arbitrary objects. Since
this can dramatically complicate implementation for particularly-exotic
host objects, the JavaScript language specification provides this hook
to allow hosts to reject private fields on objects meeting a
host-defined criteria. In the case of HTML,
[`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) and [`Location`](#location) have
complicated semantics — particularly around navigation and security —
that make implementation of private field semantics challenging, so our
implementation simply rejects those objects.

<div algorithm="">

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.2</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnsureCanCompileStrings</span>(`realm`, `parameterStrings`, `bodyString`, `codeString`, `compilationType`, `parameterArgs`, `bodyArg`)<a
href="#hostensurecancompilestrings(realm,-parameterstrings,-bodystring,-codestring,-compilationtype,-parameterargs,-bodyarg)"
class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostensurecancompilestrings(realm,-parameterstrings,-bodystring,-codestring,-compilationtype,-parameterargs,-bodyarg):implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> <a
href="https://tc39.es/proposal-dynamic-code-brand-checks/#sec-hostensurecancompilestrings"
id="hostensurecancompilestrings(realm,-parameterstrings,-bodystring,-codestring,-compilationtype,-parameterargs,-bodyarg):js-hostensurecancompilestrings"
data-x-internal="js-hostensurecancompilestrings">HostEnsureCanCompileStrings</a>
abstract operation, redefined by the Dynamic Code Brand Checks proposal.
User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)
[\[JSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS\]](#refsJSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS)

1.  Perform ?
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#can-compile-strings"
    id="hostensurecancompilestrings(realm,-parameterstrings,-bodystring,-codestring,-compilationtype,-parameterargs,-bodyarg):csp-ensurecspdoesnotblockstringcompilation"
    data-x-internal="csp-ensurecspdoesnotblockstringcompilation">EnsureCSPDoesNotBlockStringCompilation</a>(`realm`,
    `parameterStrings`, `bodyString`, `codeString`, `compilationType`,
    `parameterArgs`, `bodyArg`). [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.3</span> <span class="dfn">HostGetCodeForEval</span>(`argument`)<a href="#hostgetcodeforeval(argument)" class="self-link"></a>

The Dynamic Code Brand Checks proposal contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostgetcodeforeval(argument):implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> <a
href="https://tc39.es/proposal-dynamic-code-brand-checks/#sec-hostgetcodeforeval"
id="hostgetcodeforeval(argument):js-hostgetcodeforeval"
data-x-internal="js-hostgetcodeforeval">HostGetCodeForEval</a>(`argument`)
abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS\]](#refsJSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS)

1.  If `argument` is a
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-script"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedscript"><code
    id="hostgetcodeforeval(argument):tt-trustedscript">TrustedScript</code></a>
    object, then return `argument`'s <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript-data"
    id="hostgetcodeforeval(argument):tt-trustedscript-data"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedscript-data">data</a>.

2.  Otherwise, return no-code.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.4</span> <span class="dfn">HostPromiseRejectionTracker</span>(`promise`, `operation`)<a href="#the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation"
class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-host-promise-rejection-tracker"
id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:js-hostpromiserejectiontracker"
data-x-internal="js-hostpromiserejectiontracker">HostPromiseRejectionTracker</a>(`promise`,
`operation`) abstract operation. User agents must use the following
implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `script` be the <a href="#running-script"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:running-script">running
    script</a>.

2.  If `script` is a <a href="#classic-script"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:classic-script">classic
    script</a> and `script`'s <a href="#muted-errors"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:muted-errors">muted
    errors</a> is true, then return.

3.  Let `settingsObject` be the <a href="#current-settings-object"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:current-settings-object">current
    settings object</a>.

4.  If `script` is not null, then set `settingsObject` to `script`'s
    <a href="#settings-object"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:settings-object">settings
    object</a>.

5.  Let `global` be `settingsObject`'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:concept-settings-object-global">global
    object</a>.

6.  If `operation` is "`reject`", then:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:list-append"
        data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a> `promise` to `global`'s
        <a href="#about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list">about-to-be-notified
        rejected promises list</a>.

7.  If `operation` is "`handle`", then:

    1.  If `global`'s
        <a href="#about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:about-to-be-notified-rejected-promises-list-2">about-to-be-notified
        rejected promises list</a>
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:list-contains"
        data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> `promise`, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:list-remove"
        data-x-internal="list-remove">remove</a> `promise` from that
        list and return.

    2.  If `global`'s <a href="#outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set">outstanding
        rejected promises weak set</a> does not
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:list-contains-2"
        data-x-internal="list-contains">contain</a> `promise`, then
        return.

    3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:list-remove-2"
        data-x-internal="list-remove">Remove</a> `promise` from
        `global`'s <a href="#outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:outstanding-rejected-promises-weak-set-2">outstanding
        rejected promises weak set</a>.

    4.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:queue-a-global-task">Queue
        a global task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `global` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="the-hostpromiserejectiontracker-implementation:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`rejectionhandled`](#event-rejectionhandled) at `global`, using
        [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#promiserejectionevent), with the
        [`promise`](#dom-promiserejectionevent-promise) attribute
        initialized to `promise`, and the
        [`reason`](#dom-promiserejectionevent-reason) attribute
        initialized to `promise`.\[\[PromiseResult\]\].

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.5</span> <span class="dfn">HostSystemUTCEpochNanoseconds</span>(`global`)<a href="#hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds" class="self-link"></a>

The Temporal proposal contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> <a
href="https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#sec-hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds"
id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:js-hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds"
data-x-internal="js-hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds">HostSystemUTCEpochNanoseconds</a>
abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JSTEMPORAL\]](#refsJSTEMPORAL)

1.  Let `settingsObject` be `global`'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:relevant-settings-object">relevant
    settings object</a>.

2.  Let `time` be `settingsObject`'s
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-wall-time"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:current-wall-time"
    data-x-internal="current-wall-time">current wall time</a>.

3.  Let `ns` be the number of nanoseconds from the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unix-epoch"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:unix-epoch"
    data-x-internal="unix-epoch">Unix epoch</a> to `time`, rounded to
    the nearest integer.

4.  Return the result of <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#clamping"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:clamping"
    data-x-internal="clamping">clamping</a> `ns` between
    <a href="https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#eqn-nsMinInstant"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:nsmininstant"
    data-x-internal="nsmininstant">nsMinInstant</a> and
    <a href="https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#eqn-nsMaxInstant"
    id="hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds:nsmaxinstant"
    data-x-internal="nsmaxinstant">nsMaxInstant</a>.
