##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6</span> Job-related host hooks<a href="#integration-with-javascript-jobs" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**⚠**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Reference/Global_Objects/Promise#Incumbent_settings_object_tracking](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise#Incumbent_settings_object_tracking "The Promise object represents the eventual completion (or failure) of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value.")

Support in one engine only.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox50+</span><span class="safari no">SafariNo</span><span class="chrome no">ChromeNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera unknown">Opera?</span><span class="edge_blink no">EdgeNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge unknown">Edge
(Legacy)?</span><span class="ie no">Internet ExplorerNo</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android unknown">Opera
Android?</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

The JavaScript specification defines Jobs to be scheduled and run later
by the host, as well as
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:jobcallback-record"
data-x-internal="jobcallback-record">JobCallback Records</a> which
encapsulate JavaScript functions that are called as part of jobs. The
JavaScript specification contains a number of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
abstract operations that lets the host define how jobs are scheduled and
how JobCallbacks are handled. HTML uses these abstract operations to
<span id="incumbent-settings-object-tracking-in-promises">track the
<a href="#incumbent-settings-object"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:incumbent-settings-object">incumbent
settings object</a> in promises and
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects"
data-x-internal="finalizationregistry"><code
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:finalizationregistry">FinalizationRegistry</code></a>
callbacks</span> by saving and restoring the
<a href="#incumbent-settings-object"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:incumbent-settings-object-2">incumbent
settings object</a> and a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:javascript-execution-context"
data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context">JavaScript execution
context</a> for the <a href="#active-script"
id="integration-with-javascript-jobs:active-script">active script</a> in
JobCallbacks. This section defines them for user agent hosts.

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.1</span> <span class="dfn">HostCallJobCallback</span>(`callback`, `V`, `argumentsList`)<a href="#hostcalljobcallback" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostcalljobcallback:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostcalljobcallback"
id="hostcalljobcallback:js-hostcalljobcallback"
data-x-internal="js-hostcalljobcallback">HostCallJobCallback</a>(`callback`,
`V`, `argumentsList`) abstract operation to let hosts restore state when
invoking JavaScript callbacks from inside tasks. User agents must use
the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `incumbent settings` be
    `callback`.\[\[HostDefined\]\].\[\[IncumbentSettings\]\].

2.  Let `script execution context` be
    `callback`.\[\[HostDefined\]\].\[\[ActiveScriptContext\]\].

3.  <a href="#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:prepare-to-run-a-callback">Prepare to run a
    callback</a> with `incumbent settings`.

    This affects the <a href="#concept-incumbent-everything"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:concept-incumbent-everything">incumbent</a>
    concept while the callback runs.

4.  If `script execution context` is not null, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#stack-push"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:stack-push"
    data-x-internal="stack-push">push</a> `script execution context`
    onto the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:javascript-execution-context-stack"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
    execution context stack</a>.

    This affects the
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostcalljobcallback:active-script">active
    script</a> while the callback runs.

5.  Let `result` be <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-call"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:call" data-x-internal="call">Call</a>(`callback`.\[\[Callback\]\],
    `V`, `argumentsList`).

6.  If `script execution context` is not null, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#stack-pop"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:stack-pop" data-x-internal="stack-pop">pop</a>
    `script execution context` from the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:javascript-execution-context-stack-2"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
    execution context stack</a>.

7.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-a-callback"
    id="hostcalljobcallback:clean-up-after-running-a-callback">Clean up
    after running a callback</a> with `incumbent settings`.

8.  Return `result`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.2</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob</span>(`finalizationRegistry`)<a href="#hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob"
class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript has the ability to register objects with
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects"
data-x-internal="finalizationregistry"><code
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:finalizationregistry">FinalizationRegistry</code></a>
objects, in order to schedule a cleanup action if they are found to be
garbage collected. The JavaScript specification contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-host-cleanup-finalization-registry"
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:js-hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob"
data-x-internal="js-hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob">HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob</a>(`finalizationRegistry`)
abstract operation to schedule the cleanup action.

The timing and occurrence of cleanup work is
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:implementation-defined-2"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> in
the JavaScript specification. User agents might differ in when and
whether an object is garbage collected, affecting both whether the
return value of the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-weak-ref.prototype.deref"
data-x-internal="weakref.prototype.deref()"><code
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:weakref.prototype.deref()">WeakRef.prototype.deref()</code></a>
method is undefined, and whether
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects"
data-x-internal="finalizationregistry"><code
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:finalizationregistry-2">FinalizationRegistry</code></a>
cleanup callbacks occur. There are well-known cases in popular web
browsers where objects are not accessible to JavaScript, but they remain
retained by the garbage collector indefinitely. HTML clears kept-alive
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-weak-ref-objects"
data-x-internal="weakref"><code
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:weakref">WeakRef</code></a>
objects in the <a href="#perform-a-microtask-checkpoint"
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:perform-a-microtask-checkpoint">perform
a microtask checkpoint</a> algorithm. Authors would be best off not
depending on the timing details of garbage collection implementations.

Cleanup actions do not take place interspersed with synchronous
JavaScript execution, but rather happen in queued
<a href="#concept-task"
id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:concept-task">tasks</a>.
User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `global` be `finalizationRegistry`.\[\[Realm\]\]'s
    <a href="#global-object"
    id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:global-object">global
    object</a>.

2.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:queue-a-global-task">Queue
    a global task</a> on the <span id="javascript-engine-task-source"
    class="dfn">JavaScript engine task source</span> given `global` to
    perform the following steps:

    1.  Let `entry` be
        `finalizationRegistry`.\[\[CleanupCallback\]\].\[\[Callback\]\].\[\[Realm\]\]'s
        <a href="#concept-realm-settings-object"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:concept-realm-settings-object">environment
        settings object</a>.

    2.  <a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:prepare-to-run-script">Prepare
        to run script</a> with `entry`.

        This affects the <a href="#concept-entry-everything"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:concept-entry-everything">entry</a>
        concept while the cleanup callback runs.

    3.  Let `result` be the result of performing
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cleanup-finalization-registry"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:cleanupfinalizationregistry"
        data-x-internal="cleanupfinalizationregistry">CleanupFinalizationRegistry</a>(`finalizationRegistry`).

    4.  <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:clean-up-after-running-script">Clean
        up after running script</a> with `entry`.

    5.  If `result` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:completion-record"
        data-x-internal="completion-record">abrupt completion</a>, then
        <a href="#report-an-exception"
        id="hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjob:report-an-exception">report
        an exception</a> given by `result`.\[\[Value\]\] for `global`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.3</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnqueueGenericJob</span>(`job`, `realm`)<a href="#hostenqueuegenericjob" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostenqueuegenericjob:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuegenericjob"
id="hostenqueuegenericjob:js-hostenqueuegenericjob"
data-x-internal="js-hostenqueuegenericjob">HostEnqueueGenericJob</a>(`job`,
`realm`) abstract operation to perform generic jobs in a particular
realm (e.g., resolve promises resulting from
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-atomics.waitasync"
data-x-internal="atomics.waitasync"><code
id="hostenqueuegenericjob:atomics.waitasync">Atomics.waitAsync</code></a>).
User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `global` be `realm`'s <a href="#concept-realm-global"
    id="hostenqueuegenericjob:concept-realm-global">global object</a>.

2.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="hostenqueuegenericjob:queue-a-global-task">Queue a global task</a>
    on the <a href="#javascript-engine-task-source"
    id="hostenqueuegenericjob:javascript-engine-task-source">JavaScript
    engine task source</a> given `global` to perform `job`().

</div>

<span id="integration-with-the-javascript-job-queue"></span>
<span id="enqueuejob(queuename,-job,-arguments)"></span>

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.4</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnqueuePromiseJob</span>(`job`, `realm`)<a href="#hostenqueuepromisejob" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostenqueuepromisejob:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuepromisejob"
id="hostenqueuepromisejob:js-hostenqueuepromisejob"
data-x-internal="js-hostenqueuepromisejob">HostEnqueuePromiseJob</a>(`job`,
`realm`) abstract operation to schedule Promise-related operations. HTML
schedules these operations in the microtask queue. User agents must use
the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  If `realm` is not null, then let `job settings` be the
    <a href="#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="hostenqueuepromisejob:concept-realm-settings-object">settings
    object</a> for `realm`. Otherwise, let `job settings` be null.

    <div class="note">

    If `realm` is not null, it is the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
    id="hostenqueuepromisejob:realm" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>
    of the author code that will run. When `job` is returned by
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob"
    id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromisereactionjob"
    data-x-internal="newpromisereactionjob">NewPromiseReactionJob</a>,
    it is the realm of the promise's handler function. When `job` is
    returned by
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob"
    id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromiseresolvethenablejob"
    data-x-internal="newpromiseresolvethenablejob">NewPromiseResolveThenableJob</a>,
    it is the realm of the `then` function.

    If `realm` is null, either no author code will run or author code is
    guaranteed to throw. For the former, the author may not have passed
    in code to run, such as in `promise.then(null, null)`. For the
    latter, it is because a revoked Proxy was passed. In both cases, all
    the steps below that would otherwise use `job settings` get skipped.

    [NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob)
    and
    [NewPromiseReactionJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob)
    both seem to provide non-null realms (the current Realm Record) in
    the case of a revoked proxy. The previous text could be updated to
    reflect that.

    </div>

2.  <a href="#queue-a-microtask"
    id="hostenqueuepromisejob:queue-a-microtask">Queue a microtask</a>
    to perform the following steps:

    1.  If `job settings` is not null, then
        <a href="#prepare-to-run-script"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:prepare-to-run-script">prepare to run
        script</a> with `job settings`.

        This affects the <a href="#concept-entry-everything"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:concept-entry-everything">entry</a>
        concept while the job runs.

    2.  Let `result` be `job`().

        `job` is an
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-abstract-closure"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:abstract-closure"
        data-x-internal="abstract-closure">abstract closure</a> returned
        by <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromisereactionjob-2"
        data-x-internal="newpromisereactionjob">NewPromiseReactionJob</a>
        or
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromiseresolvethenablejob-2"
        data-x-internal="newpromiseresolvethenablejob">NewPromiseResolveThenableJob</a>.
        The promise's handler function when `job` is returned by
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromisereactionjob-3"
        data-x-internal="newpromisereactionjob">NewPromiseReactionJob</a>,
        and the `then` function when `job` is returned by
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:newpromiseresolvethenablejob-3"
        data-x-internal="newpromiseresolvethenablejob">NewPromiseResolveThenableJob</a>,
        are wrapped in
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:jobcallback-record"
        data-x-internal="jobcallback-record">JobCallback Records</a>.
        HTML saves the <a href="#incumbent-settings-object"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:incumbent-settings-object">incumbent settings
        object</a> and a
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:javascript-execution-context"
        data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context">JavaScript execution
        context</a> for to the
        <a href="#active-script" id="hostenqueuepromisejob:active-script">active
        script</a> in <a href="#hostmakejobcallback"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:hostmakejobcallback">HostMakeJobCallback</a>
        and restores them in <a href="#hostcalljobcallback"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:hostcalljobcallback">HostCallJobCallback</a>.

    3.  If `job settings` is not null, then
        <a href="#clean-up-after-running-script"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:clean-up-after-running-script">clean up after
        running script</a> with `job settings`.

    4.  If `result` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:completion-record"
        data-x-internal="completion-record">abrupt completion</a>, then
        <a href="#report-an-exception"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:report-an-exception">report an exception</a>
        given by `result`.\[\[Value\]\] for `realm`'s
        <a href="#concept-realm-global"
        id="hostenqueuepromisejob:concept-realm-global">global object</a>.

        There is a very gnarly case where HostEnqueuePromiseJob is
        called with a null realm (e.g., because Promise.prototype.then
        was called with null handlers) but also the job returns abruptly
        (because the promise capability's resolve or reject handler
        threw, possibly because this is a subclass of Promise that takes
        the supplied functions and wraps them in throwing functions
        before passing them on to the function passed to the Promise
        superclass constructor). Which global is to be used then,
        considering that the current realm could be different at each of
        those steps, by using a Promise constructor or
        Promise.prototype.then from another realm? See [issue
        \#10526](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10526).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.5</span> <span class="dfn">HostEnqueueTimeoutJob</span>(`job`, `realm`, `milliseconds`)<a href="#hostenqueuetimeoutjob" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuetimeoutjob"
id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:js-hostenqueuetimeoutjob"
data-x-internal="js-hostenqueuetimeoutjob">HostEnqueueTimeoutJob</a>(`job`,
`milliseconds`) abstract operation to schedule an operation to be
performed after a timeout. HTML schedules these operations using
<a href="#run-steps-after-a-timeout"
id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:run-steps-after-a-timeout">run steps after a
timeout</a>. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `global` be `realm`'s <a href="#concept-realm-global"
    id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:concept-realm-global">global object</a>.

2.  Let `timeoutStep` be an algorithm step which
    <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:queue-a-global-task">queues a global task</a>
    on the <a href="#javascript-engine-task-source"
    id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:javascript-engine-task-source">JavaScript
    engine task source</a> given `global` to perform `job`().

3.  <a href="#run-steps-after-a-timeout"
    id="hostenqueuetimeoutjob:run-steps-after-a-timeout-2">Run steps after a
    timeout</a> given `global`, "`JavaScript`", `milliseconds`, and
    `timeoutStep`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.6.6</span> <span class="dfn">HostMakeJobCallback</span>(`callable`)<a href="#hostmakejobcallback" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostmakejobcallback:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostmakejobcallback"
id="hostmakejobcallback:js-hostmakejobcallback"
data-x-internal="js-hostmakejobcallback">HostMakeJobCallback</a>(`callable`)
abstract operation to let hosts attach state to JavaScript callbacks
that are called from inside
<a href="#concept-task" id="hostmakejobcallback:concept-task">task</a>s.
User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `incumbent settings` be the <a href="#incumbent-settings-object"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:incumbent-settings-object">incumbent settings
    object</a>.

2.  Let `active script` be the
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostmakejobcallback:active-script">active
    script</a>.

3.  Let `script execution context` be null.

4.  If `active script` is not null, set `script execution context` to a
    new <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:javascript-execution-context"
    data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context">JavaScript execution
    context</a>, with its Function field set to null, its Realm field
    set to `active script`'s <a href="#settings-object"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:settings-object">settings object</a>'s
    <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm">realm</a>,
    and its ScriptOrModule set to `active script`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-record"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:concept-script-record">record</a>.

    As seen below, this is used in order to propagate the current
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostmakejobcallback:active-script-2">active
    script</a> forward to the time when the job callback is invoked.

    <div class="example">

    A case where `active script` is non-null, and saving it in this way
    is useful, is the following:

    ``` js
    Promise.resolve('import(`./example.mjs`)').then(eval);
    ```

    Without this step (and the steps that use it in
    <a href="#hostcalljobcallback"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:hostcalljobcallback">HostCallJobCallback</a>),
    there would be no
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostmakejobcallback:active-script-3">active
    script</a> when the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
    data-x-internal="import()"><code
    id="hostmakejobcallback:import()">import()</code></a> expression is
    evaluated, since <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-eval-x"
    data-x-internal="eval()"><code
    id="hostmakejobcallback:eval()">eval()</code></a> is a built-in
    function that does not originate from any particular
    <a href="#concept-script"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:concept-script">script</a>.

    With this step in place, the active script is propagated from the
    above code into the job, allowing
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
    data-x-internal="import()"><code
    id="hostmakejobcallback:import()-2">import()</code></a> to use the
    original script's <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>
    appropriately.

    </div>

    <div class="example">

    `active script` can be null if the user clicks on the following
    button:

    ``` html
    <button onclick="Promise.resolve('import(`./example.mjs`)').then(eval)">Click me</button>
    ```

    In this case, the JavaScript function for the
    <a href="#event-handlers" id="hostmakejobcallback:event-handlers">event
    handler</a> will be created by the
    <a href="#getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler">get
    the current value of the event handler</a> algorithm, which creates
    a function with null \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] value. Thus, when the
    promise machinery calls <a href="#hostmakejobcallback"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:hostmakejobcallback">HostMakeJobCallback</a>,
    there will be no
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostmakejobcallback:active-script-4">active
    script</a> to pass along.

    As a consequence, this means that when the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
    data-x-internal="import()"><code
    id="hostmakejobcallback:import()-3">import()</code></a> expression
    is evaluated, there will still be no
    <a href="#active-script" id="hostmakejobcallback:active-script-5">active
    script</a>. Fortunately that is handled by our implementation of
    <a href="#hostloadimportedmodule"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:hostloadimportedmodule">HostLoadImportedModule</a>
    by falling back to using the <a href="#current-settings-object"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:current-settings-object">current settings
    object</a>'s
    <a href="#api-base-url" id="hostmakejobcallback:api-base-url">API base
    URL</a>.

    </div>

5.  Return the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records"
    id="hostmakejobcallback:jobcallback-record"
    data-x-internal="jobcallback-record">JobCallback Record</a> {
    \[\[Callback\]\]: `callable`, \[\[HostDefined\]\]: {
    \[\[IncumbentSettings\]\]: `incumbent settings`,
    \[\[ActiveScriptContext\]\]: `script execution context` } }.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.6.7</span> Module-related host hooks<a href="#integration-with-the-javascript-module-system"
class="self-link"></a>

The JavaScript specification defines a syntax for modules, as well as
some host-agnostic parts of their processing model. This specification
defines the rest of their processing model: how the module system is
bootstrapped, via the [`script`](#the-script-element) element with
[`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute set to "`module`", and how modules
are fetched, resolved, and executed. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

Although the JavaScript specification speaks in terms of "scripts"
versus "modules", in general this specification speaks in terms of
<a href="#classic-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:classic-script">classic
scripts</a> versus <a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script">module
scripts</a>, since both of them use the [`script`](#the-script-element)
element.

`modulePromise`` = `<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import()"
data-x-internal="import()"><code>import(</code><var>specifier</var><code>)</code></a>  
Returns a promise for the module namespace object for the
<a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script-2">module
script</a> identified by `specifier`. This allows dynamic importing of
module scripts at runtime, instead of statically using the `import`
statement form. The specifier will be
<a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:resolve-a-module-specifier">resolved</a>
relative to the <a href="#active-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:active-script">active
script</a>.

The returned promise will be rejected if an invalid specifier is given,
or if a failure is encountered while <a href="#hostloadimportedmodule"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:hostloadimportedmodule">fetching</a>
or evaluating the resulting module graph.

This syntax can be used inside both <a href="#classic-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:classic-script-2">classic</a>
and <a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script-3">module
scripts</a>. It thus provides a bridge into the module-script world,
from the classic-script world.

`url`` = `<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-meta-properties"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import.meta"
data-x-internal="import.meta"><code>import.meta</code></a>`.`<a href="#import-meta-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import-meta-url"><code>url</code></a>  
Returns the <a href="#active-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:active-script-2">active
module script</a>'s <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:concept-script-base-url">base
URL</a>.

This syntax can only be used inside <a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script-4">module
scripts</a>.

`url`` = `<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-meta-properties"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import.meta-2"
data-x-internal="import.meta"><code>import.meta</code></a>`.`<a href="#import-meta-resolve"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import-meta-resolve"><code>resolve</code></a>`(``specifier``)`  
Returns `specifier`, <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:resolve-a-module-specifier-2">resolved</a>
relative to the <a href="#active-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:active-script-3">active
script</a>. That is, this returns the URL that would be imported by
using <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
data-x-internal="import()"><code
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import()-2">import(</code><var>specifier</var><code
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:import()-2">)</code></a>.

Throws a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>
exception if an invalid specifier is given.

This syntax can only be used inside <a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script-5">module
scripts</a>.

A <span id="module-map" class="dfn">module map</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:ordered-map"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a> keyed by
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:tuple"
data-x-internal="tuple">tuples</a> consisting of a
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:url-record"
data-x-internal="url-record">URL record</a> and a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:string"
data-x-internal="string">string</a>. The
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:url-record-2"
data-x-internal="url-record">URL record</a> is the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:concept-request-url"
data-x-internal="concept-request-url">request URL</a> at which the
module was fetched, and the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:string-2"
data-x-internal="string">string</a> indicates the type of the module
(e.g. "`javascript-or-wasm`"). The <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map">module
map</a>'s values are either a <a href="#module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-script-6">module
script</a>, null (used to represent failed fetches), or a placeholder
value "`fetching`". <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-2">Module
maps</a> are used to ensure that imported module scripts are only
fetched, parsed, and evaluated once per [`Document`](#document) or
[worker](#workers).

<div class="example">

Since <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-3">module
maps</a> are keyed by (URL, module type), the following code will create
three separate entries in the <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-4">module
map</a>, since it results in three different (URL, module type)
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:tuple-2"
data-x-internal="tuple">tuples</a> (all with "`javascript-or-wasm`"
type):

``` js
import "https://example.com/module.mjs";
import "https://example.com/module.mjs#map-buster";
import "https://example.com/module.mjs?debug=true";
```

That is, URL <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:concept-url-query"
data-x-internal="concept-url-query">queries</a> and
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:concept-url-fragment"
data-x-internal="concept-url-fragment">fragments</a> can be varied to
create distinct entries in the <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-5">module
map</a>; they are not ignored. Thus, three separate fetches and three
separate module evaluations will be performed.

In contrast, the following code would only create a single entry in the
<a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-6">module
map</a>, since after applying the
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:url-parser"
data-x-internal="url-parser">URL parser</a> to these inputs, the
resulting <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:url-record-3"
data-x-internal="url-record">URL records</a> are equal:

``` js
import "https://example.com/module2.mjs";
import "https:example.com/module2.mjs";
import "https://///example.com\\module2.mjs";
import "https://example.com/foo/../module2.mjs";
```

So in this second example, only one fetch and one module evaluation will
occur.

Note that this behavior is the same as how <a href="#sharedworker"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:sharedworker">shared
workers</a> are keyed by their parsed
<a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url">constructor
URL</a>.

</div>

<div class="example">

Since module type is also part of the <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-7">module
map</a> key, the following code will create two separate entries in the
<a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-8">module
map</a> (the type is "`javascript-or-wasm`" for the first, and "`css`"
for the second):

``` html
<script type=module>
  import "https://example.com/module";
</script>
<script type=module>
  import "https://example.com/module" with { type: "css" };
</script>
```

This can result in two separate fetches and two separate module
evaluations being performed.

In practice, due to the as-yet-unspecified memory cache (see issue
[\#6110](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6110)) the resource may
only be fetched once in WebKit and Blink-based browsers. Additionally,
as long as all module types are mutually exclusive, the module type
check in <a href="#fetch-a-single-module-script"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:fetch-a-single-module-script">fetch
a single module script</a> will fail for at least one of the imports, so
at most one module evaluation will occur.

The purpose of including the type in the <a href="#module-map"
id="integration-with-the-javascript-module-system:module-map-9">module
map</a> key is so that an import with the wrong type attribute does not
prevent a different import of the same specifier but with the correct
type from succeeding.

</div>

<div class="example">

JavaScript module scripts are the default import type when importing
from another JavaScript module; that is, when an `import` statement
lacks a `type` import attribute the imported module script's type will
be JavaScript. Attempting to import a JavaScript resource using an
`import` statement with a `type` import attribute will fail:

``` html
<script type="module">
    // All of the following will fail, assuming that the imported .mjs files are served with a
    // JavaScript MIME type. JavaScript module scripts are the default and cannot be imported with
    // any import type attribute.
    import foo from "./foo.mjs" with { type: "javascript" };
    import foo2 from "./foo2.mjs" with { type: "js" };
    import foo3 from "./foo3.mjs" with { type: "" };
    await import("./foo4.mjs", { with: { type: null } });
    await import("./foo5.mjs", { with: { type: undefined } });
</script>
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostgetimportmetaproperties"
id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:js-hostgetimportmetaproperties"
data-x-internal="js-hostgetimportmetaproperties">HostGetImportMetaProperties</a>
abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `moduleScript` be `moduleRecord`.\[\[HostDefined\]\].

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:assert"
    data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `moduleScript`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>
    is not null, as `moduleScript` is a
    <a href="#javascript-module-script"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:javascript-module-script">JavaScript
    module script</a>.

3.  Let `urlString` be `moduleScript`'s
    <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:concept-script-base-url-2">base URL</a>,
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:concept-url-serializer"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialized</a>.

4.  Let `steps` be the following steps, given the argument `specifier`:

    1.  Set `specifier` to ?
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring"
        id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:tostring"
        data-x-internal="tostring">ToString</a>(`specifier`).

    2.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
        id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:resolve-a-module-specifier">resolving a
        module specifier</a> given `moduleScript` and `specifier`.

    3.  Return the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
        id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:concept-url-serializer-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
        `url`.

5.  Let `resolveFunction` be !
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-createbuiltinfunction"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:createbuiltinfunction"
    data-x-internal="createbuiltinfunction">CreateBuiltinFunction</a>(`steps`,
    1, "`resolve`", « »).

6.  Return « <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:record"
    data-x-internal="record">Record</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
    "<span id="import-meta-url" class="dfn">`url`</span>",
    \[\[Value\]\]: `urlString` }, <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
    id="hostgetimportmetaproperties:record-2"
    data-x-internal="record">Record</a> { \[\[Key\]\]:
    "<span id="import-meta-resolve" class="dfn">`resolve`</span>",
    \[\[Value\]\]: `resolveFunction` } ».

###### <span class="secno">8.1.6.7.3</span> <span class="dfn">HostLoadImportedModule</span>(`referrer`, `moduleRequest`, `loadState`, `payload`)<a href="#hostloadimportedmodule" class="self-link"></a>

JavaScript contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="hostloadimportedmodule:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-HostLoadImportedModule"
id="hostloadimportedmodule:js-hostloadimportedmodule"
data-x-internal="js-hostloadimportedmodule">HostLoadImportedModule</a>
abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation:
[\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#refsJAVASCRIPT)

1.  Let `settingsObject` be the <a href="#current-settings-object"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:current-settings-object">current settings
    object</a>.

2.  If `settingsObject`'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-settings-object-global">global
    object</a> implements [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#workletglobalscope) or
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkerglobalscope"
    data-x-internal="serviceworkerglobalscope"><code
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:serviceworkerglobalscope">ServiceWorkerGlobalScope</code></a>
    and `loadState` is undefined, then:

    `loadState` is undefined when the current fetching process has been
    initiated by a dynamic
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
    data-x-internal="import()"><code
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:import()">import()</code></a> call,
    either directly or when loading the transitive dependencies of the
    dynamically imported module.

    1.  Perform
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule"
        data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
        `moduleRequest`, `payload`,
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion"
        data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(a new <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:typeerror">TypeError</code></a>)).

    2.  Return.

3.  Let `referencingScript` be null.

4.  Let `originalFetchOptions` be the
    <a href="#default-script-fetch-options"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:default-script-fetch-options">default script
    fetch options</a>.

5.  Let `fetchReferrer` be "`client`".

6.  If `referrer` is a
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-script-records"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:script-record"
    data-x-internal="script-record">Script Record</a> or a
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:cyclic-module-record"
    data-x-internal="cyclic-module-record">Cyclic Module Record</a>,
    then:

    1.  Set `referencingScript` to `referrer`.\[\[HostDefined\]\].

    2.  Set `settingsObject` to `referencingScript`'s
        <a href="#settings-object"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:settings-object">settings object</a>.

    3.  Set `fetchReferrer` to `referencingScript`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>.

    4.  Set `originalFetchOptions` to `referencingScript`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-script-script-fetch-options">fetch
        options</a>.

    <div class="example">

    `referrer` is usually a
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-script-records"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:script-record-2"
    data-x-internal="script-record">Script Record</a> or a
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:cyclic-module-record-2"
    data-x-internal="cyclic-module-record">Cyclic Module Record</a>, but
    it will not be so for event handlers per the
    <a href="#getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler">get
    the current value of the event handler</a> algorithm. For example,
    given:

    ``` html
    <button onclick="import('./foo.mjs')">Click me</button>
    ```

    If a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
    data-x-internal="event-click"><code
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:event-click">click</code></a> event
    occurs, then at the time the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
    data-x-internal="import()"><code
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:import()-2">import()</code></a>
    expression runs,
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getactivescriptormodule"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:getactivescriptormodule"
    data-x-internal="getactivescriptormodule">GetActiveScriptOrModule</a>
    will return null, and this operation will receive the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:current-realm"
    data-x-internal="current-realm">current realm</a> as a fallback
    `referrer`.

    </div>

7.  If `referrer` is a
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:cyclic-module-record-3"
    data-x-internal="cyclic-module-record">Cyclic Module Record</a> and
    `moduleRequest` is equal to the first element of
    `referrer`.\[\[RequestedModules\]\], then:

    1.  <div id="validate-requested-module-specifiers">

        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:list-iterate"
        data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a>
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:modulerequest-record"
        data-x-internal="modulerequest-record">ModuleRequest record</a>
        `requested` of `referrer`.\[\[RequestedModules\]\]:

        1.  If `requested`.\[\[Attributes\]\] contains a <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:record" data-x-internal="record">Record</a>
            `entry` such that `entry`.\[\[Key\]\] is not "`type`", then:

            1.  Let `error` be a new <a
                href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
                data-x-internal="syntaxerror-2"><code
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:syntaxerror-2">SyntaxError</code></a>
                exception.

            2.  If `loadState` is not undefined and
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to `error`.

            3.  Perform
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule-2"
                data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
                `moduleRequest`, `payload`,
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-2"
                data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`error`)).

            4.  Return.

            The JavaScript specification re-performs this validation but
            it is duplicated here to avoid unnecessarily loading any of
            the dependencies on validation failure.

        2.  <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:resolve-a-module-specifier">Resolve a module
            specifier</a> given `referencingScript` and
            `requested`.\[\[Specifier\]\], catching any exceptions. If
            they throw an exception, let `resolutionError` be the thrown
            exception.

        3.  If the previous step threw an exception, then:

            1.  If `loadState` is not undefined and
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to `resolutionError`.

            2.  Perform
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule-3"
                data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
                `moduleRequest`, `payload`,
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-3"
                data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`resolutionError`)).

            3.  Return.

        4.  Let `moduleType` be the result of running the
            <a href="#module-type-from-module-request"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:module-type-from-module-request">module type
            from module request</a> steps given `requested`.

        5.  If the result of running the <a href="#module-type-allowed"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:module-type-allowed">module type allowed</a>
            steps given `moduleType` and `settingsObject` is false,
            then:

            1.  Let `error` be a new <a
                href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
                data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:typeerror-2">TypeError</code></a>
                exception.

            2.  If `loadState` is not undefined and
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set
                `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to `error`.

            3.  Perform
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule-4"
                data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
                `moduleRequest`, `payload`,
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
                id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-4"
                data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`error`)).

            4.  Return.

        This step is essentially validating all of the requested module
        specifiers and type attributes when the first call to
        <a href="#hostloadimportedmodule"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:hostloadimportedmodule">HostLoadImportedModule</a>
        for a static module dependency list is made, to avoid further
        loading operations in the case any one of the dependencies has a
        static error. We treat a module with unresolvable module
        specifiers or unsupported type attributes the same as one that
        cannot be parsed; in both cases, a syntactic issue makes it
        impossible to ever contemplate linking the module later.

        </div>

8.  Let `url` be the result of <a href="#resolve-a-module-specifier"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:resolve-a-module-specifier-2">resolving a
    module specifier</a> given `referencingScript` and
    `moduleRequest`.\[\[Specifier\]\], catching any exceptions. If they
    throw an exception, let `resolutionError` be the thrown exception.

9.  If the previous step threw an exception, then:

    1.  If `loadState` is not undefined and
        `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set
        `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to `resolutionError`.

    2.  Perform
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule-5"
        data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
        `moduleRequest`, `payload`,
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-5"
        data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`resolutionError`)).

    3.  Return.

10. Let `fetchOptions` be the result of
    <a href="#get-the-descendant-script-fetch-options"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:get-the-descendant-script-fetch-options">getting
    the descendant script fetch options</a> given
    `originalFetchOptions`, `url`, and `settingsObject`.

11. Let `destination` be `"script"`.

12. Let `fetchClient` be `settingsObject`.

13. If `loadState` is not undefined, then:

    1.  Set `destination` to `loadState`.\[\[Destination\]\].

    2.  Set `fetchClient` to `loadState`.\[\[FetchClient\]\].

14. <a href="#fetch-a-single-imported-module-script"
    id="hostloadimportedmodule:fetch-a-single-imported-module-script">Fetch
    a single imported module script</a> given `url`, `fetchClient`,
    `destination`, `fetchOptions`, `settingsObject`, `fetchReferrer`,
    `moduleRequest`, and `onSingleFetchComplete` as defined below. If
    `loadState` is not undefined and `loadState`.\[\[PerformFetch\]\] is
    not null, pass `loadState`.\[\[PerformFetch\]\] along as well.

    `onSingleFetchComplete` given `moduleScript` is the following
    algorithm:

    1.  Let `completion` be null.

    2.  If `moduleScript` is null, then set `completion` to
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-6"
        data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(a new <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-x-internal="typeerror"><code
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:typeerror-3">TypeError</code></a>).

    3.  Otherwise, if `moduleScript`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-parse-error"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-script-parse-error">parse error</a>
        is not null, then:

        1.  Let `parseError` be `moduleScript`'s
            <a href="#concept-script-parse-error"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-script-parse-error-2">parse error</a>.

        2.  Set `completion` to
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion"
            id="hostloadimportedmodule:throwcompletion-7"
            data-x-internal="throwcompletion">ThrowCompletion</a>(`parseError`).

        3.  If `loadState` is not undefined and
            `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set
            `loadState`.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to `parseError`.

    4.  Otherwise, set `completion` to
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:normalcompletion"
        data-x-internal="normalcompletion">NormalCompletion</a>(`moduleScript`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-record"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:concept-script-record">record</a>).

    5.  Perform
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule"
        id="hostloadimportedmodule:finishloadingimportedmodule-6"
        data-x-internal="finishloadingimportedmodule">FinishLoadingImportedModule</a>(`referrer`,
        `moduleRequest`, `payload`, `completion`).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.1.7</span> Event loops<a href="#event-loops" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.7.1</span> Definitions<a href="#definitions-3" class="self-link"></a>

To coordinate events, user interaction, scripts, rendering, networking,
and so forth, user agents must use <span id="event-loop" class="dfn"
lt="event loop" export="">event loops</span> as described in this
section. Each
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents" id="definitions-3:agent"
data-x-internal="agent">agent</a> has an associated
<span id="concept-agent-event-loop" class="dfn" dfn-for="agent"
export="">event loop</span>, which is unique to that agent.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a> of a
<a href="#similar-origin-window-agent"
id="definitions-3:similar-origin-window-agent">similar-origin window
agent</a> is known as a <span id="window-event-loop" class="dfn">window
event loop</span>. The <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:concept-agent-event-loop-2">event loop</a> of a
<a href="#dedicated-worker-agent"
id="definitions-3:dedicated-worker-agent">dedicated worker agent</a>,
<a href="#shared-worker-agent"
id="definitions-3:shared-worker-agent">shared worker agent</a>, or
<a href="#service-worker-agent"
id="definitions-3:service-worker-agent">service worker agent</a> is
known as a <span id="worker-event-loop-2" class="dfn">worker event
loop</span>. And the <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:concept-agent-event-loop-3">event loop</a> of a
<a href="#worklet-agent" id="definitions-3:worklet-agent">worklet
agent</a> is known as a <span id="worklet-event-loop"
class="dfn">worklet event loop</span>.

</div>

<div class="note">

<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop">Event loops</a> do
not necessarily correspond to implementation threads. For example,
multiple
<a href="#window-event-loop" id="definitions-3:window-event-loop">window
event loops</a> could be cooperatively scheduled in a single thread.

However, for the various worker
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents" id="definitions-3:agent-2"
data-x-internal="agent">agents</a> that are allocated with
\[\[CanBlock\]\] set to true, the JavaScript specification does place
requirements on them regarding
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-forward-progress"
id="definitions-3:forward-progress"
data-x-internal="forward-progress">forward progress</a>, which
effectively amount to requiring dedicated per-agent threads in those
cases.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-2">event loop</a>
has one or more <span id="task-queue" class="dfn">task queues</span>. A
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue">task queue</a> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="definitions-3:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
<a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task">tasks</a>.

<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-2">Task queues</a>
are <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="definitions-3:set-2" data-x-internal="set">sets</a>, not
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue" id="definitions-3:queue"
data-x-internal="queue">queues</a>, because the [event loop processing
model](#event-loop-processing-model) grabs the first
<a href="#concept-task-runnable"
id="definitions-3:concept-task-runnable"><em>runnable</em></a>
<a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task-2">task</a> from
the chosen queue, instead of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-dequeue"
id="definitions-3:dequeue" data-x-internal="dequeue">dequeuing</a> the
first task.

The
<a href="#microtask-queue" id="definitions-3:microtask-queue">microtask
queue</a> is not a
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-3">task queue</a>.

Tasks encapsulate algorithms that are responsible for such work as:

Events  
Dispatching an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-event"
data-x-internal="event"><code id="definitions-3:event">Event</code></a>
object at a particular
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="definitions-3:eventtarget">EventTarget</code></a> object is often
done by a dedicated task.

Not all events are dispatched using the
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-4">task queue</a>;
many are dispatched during other tasks.

Parsing  
The
<a href="#html-parser" id="definitions-3:html-parser">HTML parser</a>
tokenizing one or more bytes, and then processing any resulting tokens,
is typically a task.

Callbacks  
Calling a callback is often done by a dedicated task.

Using a resource  
When an algorithm <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="definitions-3:concept-fetch"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetches</a> a resource, if the fetching
occurs in a non-blocking fashion then the processing of the resource
once some or all of the resource is available is performed by a task.

Reacting to DOM manipulation  
Some elements have tasks that trigger in response to DOM manipulation,
e.g. when that element is <a href="#insert-an-element-into-a-document"
id="definitions-3:insert-an-element-into-a-document">inserted into the
document</a>.

Formally, a <span id="concept-task" class="dfn" lt="task"
export="">task</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct"
id="definitions-3:struct" data-x-internal="struct">struct</a> which has:

<span id="concept-task-steps" class="dfn">Steps</span>  
A series of steps specifying the work to be done by the task.

A <span id="concept-task-source" class="dfn">source</span>  
One of the
<a href="#task-source" id="definitions-3:task-source">task sources</a>,
used to group and serialize related tasks.

A <span id="concept-task-document" class="dfn">document</span>  
A [`Document`](#document) associated with the task, or null for tasks
that are not in a <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:window-event-loop-2">window event loop</a>.

A <span id="script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set" class="dfn" export="">script evaluation environment settings object set</span>  
A <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="definitions-3:set-3" data-x-internal="set">set</a> of
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="definitions-3:environment-settings-object">environment settings
objects</a> used for tracking script evaluation during the task.

<div algorithm="">

A <a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task-3">task</a> is
<span id="concept-task-runnable" class="dfn">runnable</span> if its
<a href="#concept-task-document"
id="definitions-3:concept-task-document">document</a> is either null or
<a href="#fully-active" id="definitions-3:fully-active">fully active</a>.

</div>

Per its <a href="#concept-task-source"
id="definitions-3:concept-task-source">source</a> field, each
<a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task-4">task</a> is
defined as coming from a specific <span id="task-source" class="dfn"
export="">task source</span>. For each
<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-3">event loop</a>,
every
<a href="#task-source" id="definitions-3:task-source-2">task source</a>
must be associated with a specific
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-5">task queue</a>.

Essentially,
<a href="#task-source" id="definitions-3:task-source-3">task sources</a>
are used within standards to separate logically-different types of
tasks, which a user agent might wish to distinguish between.
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-6">Task queues</a>
are used by user agents to coalesce task sources within a given
<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-4">event loop</a>.

For example, a user agent could have one
<a href="#task-queue" id="definitions-3:task-queue-7">task queue</a> for
mouse and key events (to which the
<a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="definitions-3:user-interaction-task-source">user interaction task
source</a> is associated), and another to which all other
<a href="#task-source" id="definitions-3:task-source-4">task sources</a>
are associated. Then, using the freedom granted in the initial step of
the [event loop processing model](#event-loop-processing-model), it
could give keyboard and mouse events preference over other tasks
three-quarters of the time, keeping the interface responsive but not
starving other task queues. Note that in this setup, the processing
model still enforces that the user agent would never process events from
any one
<a href="#task-source" id="definitions-3:task-source-5">task source</a>
out of order.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each
<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-5">event loop</a> has
a <span id="currently-running-task" class="dfn">currently running
task</span>, which is either a
<a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task-5">task</a> or
null. Initially, this is null. It is used to handle reentrancy.

Each
<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-6">event loop</a> has
a <span id="microtask-queue" class="dfn">microtask queue</span>, which
is a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue"
id="definitions-3:queue-2" data-x-internal="queue">queue</a> of
<a href="#microtask" id="definitions-3:microtask">microtasks</a>,
initially empty. A <span id="microtask" class="dfn"
export="">microtask</span> is a colloquial way of referring to a
<a href="#concept-task" id="definitions-3:concept-task-6">task</a> that
was created via the
<a href="#queue-a-microtask" id="definitions-3:queue-a-microtask">queue
a microtask</a> algorithm.

Each
<a href="#event-loop" id="definitions-3:event-loop-7">event loop</a> has
a <span id="performing-a-microtask-checkpoint" class="dfn">performing a
microtask checkpoint</span> boolean, which is initially false. It is
used to prevent reentrant invocation of the
<a href="#perform-a-microtask-checkpoint"
id="definitions-3:perform-a-microtask-checkpoint">perform a microtask
checkpoint</a> algorithm.

Each <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:window-event-loop-3">window event loop</a> has a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code
id="definitions-3:domhighrestimestamp">DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>
<span id="last-render-opportunity-time" class="dfn">last render
opportunity time</span>, initially set to zero.

Each <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:window-event-loop-4">window event loop</a> has a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code
id="definitions-3:domhighrestimestamp-2">DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>
<span id="last-idle-period-start-time" class="dfn">last idle period
start time</span>, initially set to zero.

<div algorithm="">

To get the <span id="same-loop-windows" class="dfn">same-loop
windows</span> for a <a href="#window-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:window-event-loop-5">window event loop</a> `loop`,
return all [`Window`](#window) objects whose
<a href="#relevant-agent" id="definitions-3:relevant-agent">relevant
agent</a>'s <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="definitions-3:concept-agent-event-loop-4">event loop</a> is `loop`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.7.2</span> Queuing tasks<a href="#queuing-tasks" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="queue-a-task" class="dfn" export="">queue a task</span> on
a <a href="#task-source" id="queuing-tasks:task-source">task source</a>
`source`, which performs a series of steps `steps`, optionally given an
event loop `event loop` and a document `document`:

1.  If `event loop` was not given, set `event loop` to the
    <a href="#implied-event-loop"
    id="queuing-tasks:implied-event-loop">implied event loop</a>.

2.  If `document` was not given, set `document` to the
    <a href="#implied-document" id="queuing-tasks:implied-document">implied
    document</a>.

3.  Let `task` be a new
    <a href="#concept-task" id="queuing-tasks:concept-task">task</a>.

4.  Set `task`'s <a href="#concept-task-steps"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-steps">steps</a> to `steps`.

5.  Set `task`'s <a href="#concept-task-source"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-source">source</a> to `source`.

6.  Set `task`'s <a href="#concept-task-document"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-document">document</a> to the
    `document`.

7.  Set `task`'s
    <a href="#script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set"
    id="queuing-tasks:script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set">script
    evaluation environment settings object set</a> to an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="queuing-tasks:set" data-x-internal="set">set</a>.

8.  Let `queue` be the
    <a href="#task-queue" id="queuing-tasks:task-queue">task queue</a>
    to which `source` is associated on `event loop`.

9.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="queuing-tasks:list-append" data-x-internal="list-append">Append</a>
    `task` to `queue`.

</div>

Failing to pass an event loop and document to
<a href="#queue-a-task" id="queuing-tasks:queue-a-task">queue a task</a>
means relying on the ambiguous and poorly-specified
<a href="#implied-event-loop"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-event-loop-2">implied event loop</a> and
<a href="#implied-document"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-document-2">implied document</a> concepts.
Specification authors should either always pass these values, or use the
wrapper algorithms <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
id="queuing-tasks:queue-a-global-task">queue a global task</a> or
<a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="queuing-tasks:queue-an-element-task">queue an element task</a>
instead. Using the wrapper algorithms is recommended.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="queue-a-global-task" class="dfn" export="">queue a global
task</span> on a
<a href="#task-source" id="queuing-tasks:task-source-2">task source</a>
`source`, with a
<a href="#global-object" id="queuing-tasks:global-object">global
object</a> `global` and a series of steps `steps`:

1.  Let `event loop` be `global`'s
    <a href="#relevant-agent" id="queuing-tasks:relevant-agent">relevant
    agent</a>'s <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>.

2.  Let `document` be `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>, if `global` is a [`Window`](#window)
    object; otherwise null.

3.  <a href="#queue-a-task" id="queuing-tasks:queue-a-task-2">Queue a
    task</a> given `source`, `event loop`, `document`, and `steps`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="queue-an-element-task" class="dfn" export="">queue an
element task</span> on a
<a href="#task-source" id="queuing-tasks:task-source-3">task source</a>
`source`, with an element `element` and a series of steps `steps`:

1.  Let `global` be `element`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a>.

2.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="queuing-tasks:queue-a-global-task-2">Queue a global task</a>
    given `source`, `global`, and `steps`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="queue-a-microtask" class="dfn" export="">queue a
microtask</span> which performs a series of steps `steps`, optionally
given a document `document`:

1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="queuing-tasks:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: there
    is a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="queuing-tasks:surrounding-agent"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>. I.e.,
    this algorithm is not called while
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="queuing-tasks:in-parallel">in parallel</a>.

2.  Let `eventLoop` be the
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="queuing-tasks:surrounding-agent-2"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-agent-event-loop-2">event loop</a>.

3.  If `document` was not given, set `document` to the
    <a href="#implied-document"
    id="queuing-tasks:implied-document-3">implied document</a>.

4.  Let `microtask` be a new
    <a href="#concept-task" id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-2">task</a>.

5.  Set `microtask`'s <a href="#concept-task-steps"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-steps-2">steps</a> to `steps`.

6.  Set `microtask`'s <a href="#concept-task-source"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-source-2">source</a> to the
    <span id="microtask-task-source" class="dfn">microtask task
    source</span>.

7.  Set `microtask`'s <a href="#concept-task-document"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-document-2">document</a> to
    `document`.

8.  Set `microtask`'s
    <a href="#script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set"
    id="queuing-tasks:script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set-2">script
    evaluation environment settings object set</a> to an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="queuing-tasks:set-2" data-x-internal="set">set</a>.

9.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-enqueue"
    id="queuing-tasks:enqueue" data-x-internal="enqueue">Enqueue</a>
    `microtask` on `eventLoop`'s
    <a href="#microtask-queue" id="queuing-tasks:microtask-queue">microtask
    queue</a>.

</div>

It is possible for a
<a href="#microtask" id="queuing-tasks:microtask">microtask</a> to be
moved to a regular
<a href="#task-queue" id="queuing-tasks:task-queue-2">task queue</a>,
if, during its initial execution, it <a href="#spin-the-event-loop"
id="queuing-tasks:spin-the-event-loop">spins the event loop</a>. This is
the only case in which the <a href="#concept-task-source"
id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-source-3">source</a>,
<a href="#concept-task-document"
id="queuing-tasks:concept-task-document-3">document</a>, and
<a href="#script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set"
id="queuing-tasks:script-evaluation-environment-settings-object-set-3">script
evaluation environment settings object set</a> of the microtask are
consulted; they are ignored by the
<a href="#perform-a-microtask-checkpoint"
id="queuing-tasks:perform-a-microtask-checkpoint">perform a microtask
checkpoint</a> algorithm.

The <span id="implied-event-loop" class="dfn">implied event loop</span>
when queuing a task is the one that can deduced from the context of the
calling algorithm. This is generally unambiguous, as most specification
algorithms only ever involve a single
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents" id="queuing-tasks:agent"
data-x-internal="agent">agent</a> (and thus a single
<a href="#event-loop" id="queuing-tasks:event-loop">event loop</a>). The
exception is algorithms involving or specifying cross-agent
communication (e.g., between a window and a worker); for those cases,
the <a href="#implied-event-loop"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-event-loop-3">implied event loop</a> concept
must not be relied upon and specifications must explicitly provide an
<a href="#event-loop" id="queuing-tasks:event-loop-2">event loop</a>
when <a href="#queue-a-task" id="queuing-tasks:queue-a-task-3">queuing a
task</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="implied-document" class="dfn">implied document</span> when
queuing a task on an
<a href="#event-loop" id="queuing-tasks:event-loop-3">event loop</a>
`event loop` is determined as follows:

1.  If `event loop` is not a
    <a href="#window-event-loop" id="queuing-tasks:window-event-loop">window
    event loop</a>, then return null.

2.  If the task is being queued in the context of an element, then
    return the element's
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="queuing-tasks:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
    document</a>.

3.  If the task is being queued in the context of a
    <a href="#browsing-context" id="queuing-tasks:browsing-context">browsing
    context</a>, then return the browsing context's
    <a href="#active-document" id="queuing-tasks:active-document">active
    document</a>.

4.  If the task is being queued by or for a
    <a href="#concept-script" id="queuing-tasks:concept-script">script</a>,
    then return the script's
    <a href="#settings-object" id="queuing-tasks:settings-object">settings
    object</a>'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-settings-object-global">global object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="queuing-tasks:concept-document-window-2">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="queuing-tasks:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    this step is never reached, because one of the previous conditions
    is true. <span class="XXX">Really?</span>

</div>

Both <a href="#implied-event-loop"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-event-loop-4">implied event loop</a> and
<a href="#implied-document"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-document-4">implied document</a> are
vaguely-defined and have a lot of action-at-a-distance. The hope is to
remove these, especially <a href="#implied-document"
id="queuing-tasks:implied-document-5">implied document</a>. See [issue
\#4980](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4980).

##### <span class="secno">8.1.7.3</span> <span id="processing-model-8"></span>Processing model<a href="#event-loop-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

An
<a href="#event-loop" id="event-loop-processing-model:event-loop">event
loop</a> must continually run through the following steps for as long as
it exists:

1.  Let `oldestTask` and `taskStartTime` be null.

2.  If the <a href="#event-loop"
    id="event-loop-processing-model:event-loop-2">event loop</a> has a
    <a href="#task-queue" id="event-loop-processing-model:task-queue">task
    queue</a> with at least one <a href="#concept-task-runnable"
    id="event-loop-processing-model:concept-task-runnable">runnable</a>
    <a href="#concept-task"
    id="event-loop-processing-model:concept-task">task</a>, then:

    1.  Let `taskQueue` be one such
        <a href="#task-queue" id="event-loop-processing-model:task-queue-2">task
        queue</a>, chosen in an
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:implementation-defined"
        data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
        manner.

        Remember that the <a href="#microtask-queue"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:microtask-queue">microtask queue</a>
        is not a
        <a href="#task-queue" id="event-loop-processing-model:task-queue-3">task
        queue</a>, so it will not be chosen in this step. However, a
        <a href="#task-queue" id="event-loop-processing-model:task-queue-4">task
        queue</a> to which the <a href="#microtask-task-source"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:microtask-task-source">microtask task
        source</a> is associated might be chosen in this step. In that
        case, the <a href="#concept-task"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:concept-task-2">task</a> chosen
        in the next step was originally a <a href="#microtask"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:microtask">microtask</a>, but it
        got moved as part of <a href="#spin-the-event-loop"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:spin-the-event-loop">spinning the event
        loop</a>.

    2.  Set `taskStartTime` to the
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time"
        id="event-loop-processing-model:unsafe-shared-current-time"
        data-x-internal="unsafe-shared-current-time">unsafe shared current
        time</a>.
