  event handler processing algorithm</a>. Initially, an
  <a href="#event-handlers"
  id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-3">event handler</a>'s
  <a href="#event-handler-listener"
  id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener">listener</a> must
  be set to null.

Event handlers are exposed in two ways.

The first way, common to all event handlers, is as an
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-idl-attributes">event handler
IDL attribute</a>.

The second way is as an <a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-content-attributes">event
handler content attribute</a>. Event handlers on
<a href="#html-elements"
id="event-handler-attributes:html-elements">HTML elements</a> and some
of the event handlers on [`Window`](#window) objects are exposed in this
way.

For both of these two ways, the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-4">event handler</a> is
exposed through a <span id="event-handler-name" class="dfn">name</span>,
which is a string that always starts with "`on`" and is followed by the
name of the event for which the handler is intended.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Most of the time, the object that exposes an <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-5">event handler</a> is the
same as the object on which the corresponding
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-listener-3"
data-x-internal="event-listener">event listener</a> is added. However,
the [`body`](#the-body-element) and [`frameset`](#frameset) elements
expose several <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-6">event handlers</a> that
act upon the element's [`Window`](#window) object, if one exists. In
either case, we call the object an <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-7">event handler</a> acts
upon the <span id="event-handler-target" class="dfn">target</span> of
that <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-8">event handler</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler"
class="dfn">determine the target of an event handler</span>, given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget">EventTarget</code></a> object
`eventTarget` on which the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-9">event handler</a> is
exposed, and an <a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name">event handler name</a>
`name`, the following steps are taken:

1.  If `eventTarget` is not a [`body`](#the-body-element) element or a
    [`frameset`](#frameset) element, then return `eventTarget`.

2.  If `name` is not the name of an attribute member of the
    [`WindowEventHandlers`](#windoweventhandlers) interface mixin and
    the <a href="#window-reflecting-body-element-event-handler-set"
    id="event-handler-attributes:window-reflecting-body-element-event-handler-set"><code>Window</code>-reflecting
    body element event handler set</a> does not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="event-handler-attributes:list-contains"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contain</a> `name`, then return
    `eventTarget`.

3.  If `eventTarget`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="event-handler-attributes:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is not an
    <a href="#active-document"
    id="event-handler-attributes:active-document">active document</a>,
    then return null.

    This could happen if this object is a [`body`](#the-body-element)
    element without a corresponding [`Window`](#window) object, for
    example.

    This check does not necessarily prevent [`body`](#the-body-element)
    and [`frameset`](#frameset) elements that are not
    <a href="#the-body-element-2"
    id="event-handler-attributes:the-body-element-2-2">the body element</a>
    of their
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="event-handler-attributes:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> from reaching the
    next step. In particular, a [`body`](#the-body-element) element
    created in an <a href="#active-document"
    id="event-handler-attributes:active-document-2">active document</a>
    (perhaps with
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement"
    data-x-internal="dom-document-createelement"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-document-createelement">document.createElement()</code></a>)
    but not <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected"
    id="event-handler-attributes:connected"
    data-x-internal="connected">connected</a> will also have its
    corresponding [`Window`](#window) object as the
    <a href="#event-handler-target"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-target">target</a> of
    several <a href="#event-handlers"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-10">event handlers</a>
    exposed through it.

4.  Return `eventTarget`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="event-handler-attributes:node-document-3"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="event-handler-attributes:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-2">EventTarget</code></a>
object that has one or more <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-11">event handlers</a>
specified has an associated <span id="event-handler-map" class="dfn"
dfn-for="EventTarget" export="">event handler map</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="event-handler-attributes:ordered-map"
data-x-internal="ordered-map">map</a> of strings representing
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-2">names</a> of
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-12">event handlers</a> to
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-13">event handlers</a>.

<div algorithm="">

When an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-3">EventTarget</code></a>
object that has one or more <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-14">event handlers</a>
specified is created, its <a href="#event-handler-map"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map">event handler map</a>
must be initialized such that it contains an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="event-handler-attributes:map-entry"
data-x-internal="map-entry">entry</a> for each <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-15">event handler</a> that
has that object as <a href="#event-handler-target"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-target-2">target</a>, with
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="event-handler-attributes:struct-item-2"
data-x-internal="struct-item">items</a> in those
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-16">event handlers</a> set
to their initial values.

</div>

The order of the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="event-handler-attributes:map-entry-2"
data-x-internal="map-entry">entries</a> of <a href="#event-handler-map"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-2">event handler map</a>
could be arbitrary. It is not observable through any algorithms that
operate on the map.

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="event-handler-attributes:map-entry-3"
data-x-internal="map-entry">Entries</a> are not created in the
<a href="#event-handler-map"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-3">event handler map</a>
of an object for <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-17">event handlers</a> that
are merely exposed on that object, but have some other object as their
<a href="#event-handler-target"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-target-3">targets</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <span id="event-handler-idl-attributes" class="dfn" export="">event
handler IDL attribute</span> is an IDL attribute for a specific
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-18">event handler</a>. The
name of the IDL attribute is the same as the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-3">name</a> of the
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-19">event handler</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The getter of an <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-idl-attributes-2">event
handler IDL attribute</a> with name `name`, when called, must run these
steps:

1.  Let `eventTarget` be the result of
    <a href="#determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler">determining
    the target of an event handler</a> given this object and `name`.

2.  If `eventTarget` is null, then return null.

3.  Return the result of
    <a href="#getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler">getting
    the current value of the event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and
    `name`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The setter of an <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-idl-attributes-3">event
handler IDL attribute</a> with name `name`, when called, must run these
steps:

1.  Let `eventTarget` be the result of
    <a href="#determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler-2">determining
    the target of an event handler</a> given this object and `name`.

2.  If `eventTarget` is null, then return.

3.  If the given value is null, then
    <a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler">deactivate an
    event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and `name`.

4.  Otherwise:

    1.  Let `handlerMap` be `eventTarget`'s <a href="#event-handler-map"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-4">event handler map</a>.

    2.  Let `eventHandler` be `handlerMap`\[`name`\].

    3.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-2">value</a> to
        the given value.

    4.  <a href="#activate-an-event-handler"
        id="event-handler-attributes:activate-an-event-handler">Activate an
        event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and `name`.

</div>

Certain <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-idl-attributes-4">event
handler IDL attributes</a> have additional requirements, in particular
the [`onmessage`](#handler-messageeventtarget-onmessage) attribute of
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <span id="event-handler-content-attributes" class="dfn"
export="">event handler content attribute</span> is a content attribute
for a specific <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-20">event handler</a>. The
name of the content attribute is the same as the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-4">name</a> of the
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-21">event handler</a>.

<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-content-attributes-2">Event
handler content attributes</a>, when specified, must contain valid
JavaScript code which, when parsed, would match the
*<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-FunctionBody"
data-x-internal="js-prod-functionbody">FunctionBody</a>* production
after
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-automatic-semicolon-insertion"
id="event-handler-attributes:automatic-semicolon-insertion"
data-x-internal="automatic-semicolon-insertion">automatic semicolon
insertion</a>.

<div algorithm="">

The following <a
href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
id="event-handler-attributes:concept-element-attributes-change-ext"
data-x-internal="concept-element-attributes-change-ext">attribute change
steps</a> are used to synchronize between
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-content-attributes-3">event
handler content attributes</a> and <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-22">event handlers</a>:
[\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

1.  If `namespace` is not null, or `localName` is not the name of an
    <a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-content-attributes-4">event
    handler content attribute</a> on `element`, then return.

2.  Let `eventTarget` be the result of
    <a href="#determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:determining-the-target-of-an-event-handler-3">determining
    the target of an event handler</a> given `element` and `localName`.

3.  If `eventTarget` is null, then return.

4.  If `value` is null, then <a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler-2">deactivate
    an event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and `localName`.

5.  Otherwise:

    1.  If the
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline"
        id="event-handler-attributes:should-element&#39;s-inline-behavior-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy"
        data-x-internal="should-element&#39;s-inline-behavior-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy">Should
        element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?</a>
        algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when executed upon `element`,
        "`script attribute`", and `value`, then return.
        [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

    2.  Let `handlerMap` be `eventTarget`'s <a href="#event-handler-map"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-5">event handler map</a>.

    3.  Let `eventHandler` be `handlerMap`\[`localName`\].

    4.  Let `location` be the script location that triggered the
        execution of these steps.

    5.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-3">value</a> to
        the <a href="#internal-raw-uncompiled-handler"
        id="event-handler-attributes:internal-raw-uncompiled-handler-2">internal
        raw uncompiled handler</a> `value`/`location`.

    6.  <a href="#activate-an-event-handler"
        id="event-handler-attributes:activate-an-event-handler-2">Activate an
        event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and `localName`.

Per the DOM Standard, these steps are run even if `oldValue` and `value`
are identical (setting an attribute to its current value), but *not* if
`oldValue` and `value` are both null (removing an attribute that doesn't
currently exist). [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="deactivate-an-event-handler" class="dfn">deactivate an
event handler</span> given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-4">EventTarget</code></a>
object `eventTarget` and a string `name` that is the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-5">name</a> of an
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-23">event handler</a>, run
these steps:

1.  Let `handlerMap` be `eventTarget`'s <a href="#event-handler-map"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-6">event handler map</a>.

2.  Let `eventHandler` be `handlerMap`\[`name`\].

3.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-4">value</a> to
    null.

4.  Let `listener` be `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener-2">listener</a>.

5.  If `listener` is not null, then
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#remove-an-event-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:remove-an-event-listener"
    data-x-internal="remove-an-event-listener">remove an event listener</a>
    with `eventTarget` and `listener`.

6.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener-3">listener</a>
    to null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="erase-all-event-listeners-and-handlers" class="dfn">erase
all event listeners and handlers</span> given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-5">EventTarget</code></a>
object `eventTarget`, run these steps:

1.  If `eventTarget` has an associated <a href="#event-handler-map"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-7">event handler map</a>,
    then for each `name` → `eventHandler` of `eventTarget`'s associated
    <a href="#event-handler-map"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-8">event handler map</a>,
    <a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler-3">deactivate
    an event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and `name`.

2.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#remove-all-event-listeners"
    id="event-handler-attributes:remove-all-event-listeners"
    data-x-internal="remove-all-event-listeners">Remove all event
    listeners</a> given `eventTarget`.

</div>

This algorithm is used to define
[`document.open()`](#dom-document-open).

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="activate-an-event-handler" class="dfn">activate an event
handler</span> given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-6">EventTarget</code></a>
object `eventTarget` and a string `name` that is the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-6">name</a> of an
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-24">event handler</a>, run
these steps:

1.  Let `handlerMap` be `eventTarget`'s <a href="#event-handler-map"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-9">event handler map</a>.

2.  Let `eventHandler` be `handlerMap`\[`name`\].

3.  If `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener-4">listener</a>
    is not null, then return.

4.  Let `callback` be the result of creating a Web IDL
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#callbackdef-eventlistener"
    data-x-internal="dom-eventlistener"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-eventlistener">EventListener</code></a>
    instance representing a reference to a function of one argument that
    executes the steps of
    <a href="#the-event-handler-processing-algorithm"
    id="event-handler-attributes:the-event-handler-processing-algorithm-2">the
    event handler processing algorithm</a>, given `eventTarget`, `name`,
    and its argument.

    The <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#callbackdef-eventlistener"
    data-x-internal="dom-eventlistener"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-eventlistener-2">EventListener</code></a>'s
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context"
    id="event-handler-attributes:callback-context"
    data-x-internal="callback-context">callback context</a> can be
    arbitrary; it does not impact the steps of
    <a href="#the-event-handler-processing-algorithm"
    id="event-handler-attributes:the-event-handler-processing-algorithm-3">the
    event handler processing algorithm</a>. [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

    The callback is emphatically *not* the <a href="#event-handlers"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-25">event handler</a>
    itself. Every event handler ends up registering the same callback,
    the algorithm defined below, which takes care of invoking the right
    code, and processing the code's return value.

5.  Let `listener` be a new
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-listener-4"
    data-x-internal="event-listener">event listener</a> whose
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-listener-type"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-listener-type"
    data-x-internal="event-listener-type">type</a> is the
    <span id="event-handler-event-type" class="dfn" export="">event
    handler event type</span> corresponding to `eventHandler` and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-listener-callback"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-listener-callback"
    data-x-internal="event-listener-callback">callback</a> is
    `callback`.

    To be clear, an
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-listener-5"
    data-x-internal="event-listener">event listener</a> is different
    from an
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#callbackdef-eventlistener"
    data-x-internal="dom-eventlistener"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-eventlistener-3">EventListener</code></a>.

6.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#add-an-event-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:add-an-event-listener"
    data-x-internal="add-an-event-listener">Add an event listener</a>
    with `eventTarget` and `listener`.

7.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-listener"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener-5">listener</a>
    to `listener`.

</div>

<div class="note">

The event listener registration happens only if the
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-26">event handler</a>'s
<a href="#event-handler-value"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-5">value</a> is being
set to non-null, and the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-27">event handler</a> is not
already activated. Since listeners are called in the order they were
registered, assuming no <a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler-4">deactivation</a>
occurred, the order of event listeners for a particular event type will
always be:

1.  the event listeners registered with
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"
    data-x-internal="dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener">addEventListener()</code></a>
    before the first time the <a href="#event-handlers"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-28">event handler</a>'s
    <a href="#event-handler-value"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-6">value</a> was
    set to non-null

2.  then the callback to which it is currently set, if any

3.  and finally the event listeners registered with
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"
    data-x-internal="dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener-2">addEventListener()</code></a>
    *after* the first time the <a href="#event-handlers"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-29">event handler</a>'s
    <a href="#event-handler-value"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-7">value</a> was
    set to non-null.

</div>

<div class="example">

This example demonstrates the order in which event listeners are
invoked. If the button in this example is clicked by the user, the page
will show four alerts, with the text "ONE", "TWO", "THREE", and "FOUR"
respectively.

``` html
<button id="test">Start Demo</button>
<script>
 var button = document.getElementById('test');
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('ONE') }, false);
 button.setAttribute('onclick', "alert('NOT CALLED')"); // event handler listener is registered here
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('THREE') }, false);
 button.onclick = function () { alert('TWO'); };
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('FOUR') }, false);
</script>
```

However, in the following example, the event handler is
<a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler-5">deactivated</a>
after its initial activation (and its event listener is removed), before
being reactivated at a later time. The page will show five alerts with
"ONE", "TWO", "THREE", "FOUR", and "FIVE" respectively, in order.

``` html
<button id="test">Start Demo</button>
<script>
 var button = document.getElementById('test');
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('ONE') }, false);
 button.setAttribute('onclick', "alert('NOT CALLED')"); // event handler is activated here
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('TWO') }, false);
 button.onclick = null;                                 // but deactivated here
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('THREE') }, false);
 button.onclick = function () { alert('FOUR'); };       // and re-activated here
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('FIVE') }, false);
</script>
```

</div>

The interfaces implemented by the event object do not influence whether
an <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-30">event handler</a> is
triggered or not.

<div algorithm="">

<span id="the-event-handler-processing-algorithm" class="dfn">The event
handler processing algorithm</span> for an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-7">EventTarget</code></a>
object `eventTarget`, a string `name` representing the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-7">name</a> of an
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-31">event handler</a>, and
an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-event"
data-x-internal="event"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:event">Event</code></a> object `event` is
as follows:

1.  If <a href="#concept-n-noscript"
    id="event-handler-attributes:concept-n-noscript">scripting is
    disabled</a> for `eventTarget`, then return.

2.  Let `callback` be the result of
    <a href="#getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler-2">getting
    the current value of the event handler</a> given `eventTarget` and
    `name`.

3.  If `callback` is null, then return.

4.  Let `special error event handling` be true if `event` is an
    [`ErrorEvent`](#errorevent) object, `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-type">type</code></a> is
    "[`error`](#event-error)", and `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-currenttarget"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-currenttarget"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-currenttarget">currentTarget</code></a>
    implements the
    [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin.
    Otherwise, let `special error event handling` be false.

5.  Process the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-event"
    data-x-internal="event"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-2">Event</code></a> object
    `event` as follows:

    If `special error event handling` is true  
    Let `return value` be the result of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
    id="event-handler-attributes:es-invoking-callback-functions"
    data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">invoking</a>
    `callback` with « `event`'s [`message`](#dom-errorevent-message),
    `event`'s [`filename`](#dom-errorevent-filename), `event`'s
    [`lineno`](#dom-errorevent-lineno), `event`'s
    [`colno`](#dom-errorevent-colno), `event`'s
    [`error`](#dom-errorevent-error) », "`rethrow`", and with
    *<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value"
    data-x-internal="dfn-callback-this-value">callback this value</a>*
    set to `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-currenttarget"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-currenttarget"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-currenttarget-2">currentTarget</code></a>.

    Otherwise  
    Let `return value` be the result of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
    id="event-handler-attributes:es-invoking-callback-functions-2"
    data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">invoking</a>
    `callback` with « `event` », "`rethrow`", and with
    *<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value"
    data-x-internal="dfn-callback-this-value">callback this value</a>*
    set to `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-currenttarget"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-currenttarget"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-currenttarget-3">currentTarget</code></a>.

    If an exception gets thrown by the callback, it will be rethrown,
    ending these steps. The exception will propagate to the
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
    id="event-handler-attributes:concept-event-dispatch"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">DOM event dispatch logic</a>,
    which will then <a href="#report-an-exception"
    id="event-handler-attributes:report-an-exception">report</a> it.

6.  Process `return value` as follows:

    If `event` is a [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#beforeunloadevent) object and `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-type-2">type</code></a> is "[`beforeunload`](#event-beforeunload)"  
    In this case, the <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-idl-attributes-5">event
    handler IDL attribute</a>'s type will be
    [`OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler`](#onbeforeunloadeventhandler), so
    `return value` will have been coerced into either null or a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
    data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:idl-domstring">DOMString</code></a>.

    If `return value` is not null, then:

    1.  Set `event`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
        id="event-handler-attributes:canceled-flag"
        data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a>.

    2.  If `event`'s [`returnValue`](#dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue)
        attribute's value is the empty string, then set `event`'s
        [`returnValue`](#dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) attribute's
        value to `return value`.

    If `special error event handling` is true  
    If `return value` is true, then set `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="event-handler-attributes:canceled-flag-2"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a>.

    Otherwise  
    If `return value` is false, then set `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#canceled-flag"
    id="event-handler-attributes:canceled-flag-3"
    data-x-internal="canceled-flag">canceled flag</a>.

    If we've gotten to this "Otherwise" clause because `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:dom-event-type-3">type</code></a> is
    "[`beforeunload`](#event-beforeunload)" but `event` is *not* a
    [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#beforeunloadevent) object, then
    `return value` will never be false, since in such cases
    `return value` will have been coerced into either null or a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString"
    data-x-internal="idl-domstring"><code
    id="event-handler-attributes:idl-domstring-2">DOMString</code></a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [`EventHandler`](#eventhandler) callback function type represents a
callback used for event handlers. It is represented in Web IDL as
follows:

``` idl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback EventHandlerNonNull = any (Event event);
typedef EventHandlerNonNull? EventHandler;
```

In JavaScript, any
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function"
data-x-internal="idl-function"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:idl-function">Function</code></a> object
implements this interface.

<div class="example">

For example, the following document fragment:

``` html
<body onload="alert(this)" onclick="alert(this)">
```

...leads to an alert saying "`[object Window]`" when the document is
loaded, and an alert saying "`[object HTMLBodyElement]`" whenever the
user clicks something in the page.

</div>

<div class="note">

The return value of the function affects whether the event is canceled
or not: as described above, if the return value is false, the event is
canceled.

There are two exceptions in the platform, for historical reasons:

- The [`onerror`](#handler-onerror) handlers on global objects, where
  returning *true* cancels the event.

- The [`onbeforeunload`](#handler-window-onbeforeunload) handler, where
  returning any non-null and non-undefined value will cancel the event.

</div>

For historical reasons, the [`onerror`](#handler-onerror) handler has
different arguments:

``` idl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull = any ((Event or DOMString) event, optional DOMString source, optional unsigned long lineno, optional unsigned long colno, optional any error);
typedef OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull? OnErrorEventHandler;
```

<div class="example">

``` js
window.onerror = (message, source, lineno, colno, error) => { … };
```

</div>

Similarly, the [`onbeforeunload`](#handler-window-onbeforeunload)
handler has a different return value:

``` idl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull = DOMString? (Event event);
typedef OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull? OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler;
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <span id="internal-raw-uncompiled-handler" class="dfn">internal raw
uncompiled handler</span> is a tuple with the following information:

- An uncompiled script body

- A location where the script body originated, in case an error needs to
  be reported

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to
<span id="getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler"
class="dfn">get the current value of the event handler</span> given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget"
data-x-internal="eventtarget"><code
id="event-handler-attributes:eventtarget-8">EventTarget</code></a>
object `eventTarget` and a string `name` that is the
<a href="#event-handler-name"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-name-8">name</a> of an
<a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-32">event handler</a>, it
must run these steps:

1.  Let `handlerMap` be `eventTarget`'s <a href="#event-handler-map"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-map-10">event handler map</a>.

2.  Let `eventHandler` be `handlerMap`\[`name`\].

3.  If `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-8">value</a> is an
    <a href="#internal-raw-uncompiled-handler"
    id="event-handler-attributes:internal-raw-uncompiled-handler-3">internal
    raw uncompiled handler</a>, then:

    1.  If `eventTarget` is an element, then let `element` be
        `eventTarget`, and `document` be `element`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
        id="event-handler-attributes:node-document-4"
        data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>. Otherwise,
        `eventTarget` is a [`Window`](#window) object, let `element` be
        null, and `document` be `eventTarget`'s
        <a href="#concept-document-window"
        id="event-handler-attributes:concept-document-window">associated
        <code>Document</code></a>.

    2.  If `document`'s <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
        id="event-handler-attributes:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active
        sandboxing flag set</a> has its
        <a href="#sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag"
        id="event-handler-attributes:sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed
        scripts browsing context flag</a> set, then return null.

    3.  Let `body` be the uncompiled script body in `eventHandler`'s
        <a href="#event-handler-value"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-9">value</a>.

    4.  Let `location` be the location where the script body originated,
        as given by `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-10">value</a>.

    5.  If `element` is not null and `element` has a
        <a href="#form-owner" id="event-handler-attributes:form-owner">form
        owner</a>, let `form owner` be that
        <a href="#form-owner" id="event-handler-attributes:form-owner-2">form
        owner</a>. Otherwise, let `form owner` be null.

    6.  Let `settings object` be the <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="event-handler-attributes:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
        object</a> of `document`.

    7.  If `body` is not parsable as
        *<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-FunctionBody"
        data-x-internal="js-prod-functionbody">FunctionBody</a>* or if
        parsing detects an
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#early-error-rule"
        id="event-handler-attributes:early-error"
        data-x-internal="early-error">early error</a>, then follow these
        substeps:

        1.  Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
            id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-11">value</a>
            to null.

            This does not <a href="#deactivate-an-event-handler"
            id="event-handler-attributes:deactivate-an-event-handler-6">deactivate</a>
            the event handler, which additionally
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#remove-an-event-listener"
            id="event-handler-attributes:remove-an-event-listener-2"
            data-x-internal="remove-an-event-listener">removes</a> the
            event handler's <a href="#event-handler-listener"
            id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-listener-6">listener</a>
            (if present).

        2.  Let `syntaxError` be a new <a
            href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
            data-x-internal="syntaxerror-2"><code
            id="event-handler-attributes:syntaxerror-2">SyntaxError</code></a>
            exception associated with `settings object`'s
            <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
            id="event-handler-attributes:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm">realm</a>
            which describes the error while parsing. It should be based
            on `location`, where the script body originated.

        3.  <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="event-handler-attributes:report-an-exception-2">Report an
            exception</a> with `syntaxError` for `settings object`'s
            <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
            id="event-handler-attributes:concept-settings-object-global">global
            object</a>.

        4.  Return null.

    8.  Push `settings object`'s <a href="#realm-execution-context"
        id="event-handler-attributes:realm-execution-context">realm execution
        context</a> onto the
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
        id="event-handler-attributes:javascript-execution-context-stack"
        data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
        execution context stack</a>; it is now the
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context"
        id="event-handler-attributes:running-javascript-execution-context"
        data-x-internal="running-javascript-execution-context">running
        JavaScript execution context</a>.

        This is necessary so the subsequent invocation of
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinaryfunctioncreate"
        id="event-handler-attributes:js-ordinaryfunctioncreate"
        data-x-internal="js-ordinaryfunctioncreate">OrdinaryFunctionCreate</a>
        takes place in the correct
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms"
        id="event-handler-attributes:realm" data-x-internal="realm">realm</a>.

    9.  Let `function` be the result of calling
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinaryfunctioncreate"
        id="event-handler-attributes:js-ordinaryfunctioncreate-2"
        data-x-internal="js-ordinaryfunctioncreate">OrdinaryFunctionCreate</a>,
        with arguments:

        *functionPrototype*  
        <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-function-prototype-object"
        id="event-handler-attributes:function.prototype"
        data-x-internal="function.prototype">%Function.prototype%</a>

        *sourceText*  
        If `name` is [`onerror`](#handler-onerror) and `eventTarget` is a [`Window`](#window) object  
        The string formed by concatenating "`function `", `name`,
        "`(event, source, lineno, colno, error) {`", U+000A LF, `body`,
        U+000A LF, and "`}`".

        Otherwise  
        The string formed by concatenating "`function `", `name`,
        "`(event) {`", U+000A LF, `body`, U+000A LF, and "`}`".

        *ParameterList*  
        If `name` is [`onerror`](#handler-onerror) and `eventTarget` is a [`Window`](#window) object  
        Let the function have five arguments, named `event`, `source`,
        `lineno`, `colno`, and `error`.

        Otherwise  
        Let the function have a single argument called `event`.

        *body*  
        The result of parsing `body` above.

        *thisMode*  
        non-lexical-this

        *scope*  
        1.  Let `realm` be `settings object`'s
            <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
            id="event-handler-attributes:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm-2">realm</a>.

        2.  Let `scope` be `realm`.\[\[GlobalEnv\]\].

        3.  If `eventHandler` is an element's <a href="#event-handlers"
            id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-33">event handler</a>,
            then set `scope` to
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment"
            id="event-handler-attributes:js-newobjectenvironment"
            data-x-internal="js-newobjectenvironment">NewObjectEnvironment</a>(`document`,
            true, `scope`).

            (Otherwise, `eventHandler` is a [`Window`](#window) object's
            <a href="#event-handlers"
            id="event-handler-attributes:event-handlers-34">event handler</a>.)

        4.  If `form owner` is not null, then set `scope` to
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment"
            id="event-handler-attributes:js-newobjectenvironment-2"
            data-x-internal="js-newobjectenvironment">NewObjectEnvironment</a>(`form owner`,
            true, `scope`).

        5.  If `element` is not null, then set `scope` to
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment"
            id="event-handler-attributes:js-newobjectenvironment-3"
            data-x-internal="js-newobjectenvironment">NewObjectEnvironment</a>(`element`,
            true, `scope`).

        6.  Return `scope`.

    10. Remove `settings object`'s <a href="#realm-execution-context"
        id="event-handler-attributes:realm-execution-context-2">realm execution
        context</a> from the
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
        id="event-handler-attributes:javascript-execution-context-stack-2"
        data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
        execution context stack</a>.

    11. Set `function`.\[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] to null.

        <div class="note">

        This is done because the default behavior, of associating the
        created function with the nearest <a href="#concept-script"
        id="event-handler-attributes:concept-script">script</a> on the
        stack, can lead to path-dependent results. For example, an event
        handler which is first invoked by user interaction would end up
        with null \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] (since then this algorithm
        would be first invoked when the <a href="#active-script"
        id="event-handler-attributes:active-script">active script</a> is
        null), whereas one that is first invoked by dispatching an event
        from script would have its \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] set to that
        script.

        Instead, we just always set \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] to null. This
        is more intuitive anyway; the idea that the first script which
        dispatches an event is somehow responsible for the event handler
        code is dubious.

        In practice, this only affects the resolution of relative URLs
        via <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
        data-x-internal="import()"><code
        id="event-handler-attributes:import()">import()</code></a>,
        which consult the <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
        id="event-handler-attributes:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>
        of the associated script. Nulling out \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\]
        means that <a href="#hostloadimportedmodule"
        id="event-handler-attributes:hostloadimportedmodule">HostLoadImportedModule</a>
        will fall back to the <a href="#current-settings-object"
        id="event-handler-attributes:current-settings-object">current settings
        object</a>'s
        <a href="#api-base-url" id="event-handler-attributes:api-base-url">API
        base URL</a>.

        </div>

    12. Set `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
        id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-12">value</a>
        to the result of creating a Web IDL
        [`EventHandler`](#eventhandler) callback function object whose
        object reference is `function` and whose
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context"
        id="event-handler-attributes:callback-context-2"
        data-x-internal="callback-context">callback context</a> is
        `settings object`.

4.  Return `eventHandler`'s <a href="#event-handler-value"
    id="event-handler-attributes:event-handler-value-13">value</a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.1.8.2</span> Event handlers on elements, [`Document`](#document) objects, and [`Window`](#window) objects<a
href="#event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects"
class="self-link"></a>

The following are the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handlers">event
handlers</a> (and their corresponding
<a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-event-type">event

<a href="#html-elements"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:html-elements">HTML
elements</a>, as both <a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-content-attributes">event

<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes">event
handler IDL attributes</a>; and that must be supported by all
[`Document`](#document) and [`Window`](#window) objects, as

id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes-2">event

The following are the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handlers-3">event
handlers</a> (and their corresponding
<a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-event-type-3">event
handler event types</a>) that must be supported by all
<a href="#html-elements"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:html-elements-2">HTML
elements</a> other than [`body`](#the-body-element) and
[`frameset`](#frameset) elements, as both
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-content-attributes-2">event
handler content attributes</a> and
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes-3">event
handler IDL attributes</a>; that must be supported by all
[`Document`](#document) objects, as
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes-4">event
handler IDL attributes</a>; and that must be supported by all
[`Window`](#window) objects, as <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes-5">event
handler IDL attributes</a> on the [`Window`](#window) objects
themselves, and with corresponding
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-content-attributes-3">event
handler content attributes</a> and
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-idl-attributes-6">event
handler IDL attributes</a> exposed on all [`body`](#the-body-element)
and [`frameset`](#frameset) elements that are owned by that
[`Window`](#window) object's <a href="#concept-document-window"
id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:concept-document-window">associated
<code>Document</code></a>:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>

id="event-handlers-on-elements,-document-objects,-and-window-objects:event-handler-event-type-4">Event
handler event type</a></th>
</tr>

class="dfn">`Window`-reflecting body element event handler set</span>.

objects, as <a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"

###### <span class="secno">8.1.8.2.1</span> IDL definitions<a href="#idl-definitions" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
interface mixin GlobalEventHandlers {
  attribute EventHandler onabort;
  attribute EventHandler onauxclick;
  attribute EventHandler onbeforeinput;
  attribute EventHandler onbeforematch;
  attribute EventHandler onbeforetoggle;
  attribute EventHandler onblur;
  attribute EventHandler oncancel;
  attribute EventHandler oncanplay;
  attribute EventHandler oncanplaythrough;
```

##### <span class="secno">8.1.8.3</span> Event firing<a href="#event-firing" class="self-link"></a>

Certain operations and methods are defined as firing events on elements.
For example, the [`click()`](#dom-click) method on the
[`HTMLElement`](#htmlelement) interface is defined as firing a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click"
data-x-internal="event-click"><code
id="event-firing:event-click">click</code></a> event on the element.
[\[POINTEREVENTS\]](#refsPOINTEREVENTS)

<div algorithm="">

<span id="fire-a-synthetic-pointer-event" class="dfn">Firing a synthetic
pointer event named `e`</span> at `target`, with an optional
`not trusted flag`, means running these steps:

1.  Let `event` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-create"
    id="event-firing:creating-an-event"
    data-x-internal="creating-an-event">creating an event</a> using
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface"
    data-x-internal="pointerevent"><code
    id="event-firing:pointerevent">PointerEvent</code></a>.

2.  Initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="event-firing:dom-event-type">type</code></a> attribute to `e`.

3.  Initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
    id="event-firing:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a> and
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-cancelable"><code
    id="event-firing:dom-event-cancelable">cancelable</code></a>
    attributes to true.

4.  Set `event`'s <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#composed-flag"
    id="event-firing:composed-flag" data-x-internal="composed-flag">composed
    flag</a>.

5.  If the `not trusted flag` is set, initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-istrusted"><code
    id="event-firing:dom-event-istrusted">isTrusted</code></a> attribute
    to false.

6.  Initialize `event`'s `ctrlKey`, `shiftKey`, `altKey`, and `metaKey`
    attributes according to the current state of the key input device,
    if any (false for any keys that are not available).

7.  Initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view"
    data-x-internal="dom-uievent-view"><code
    id="event-firing:dom-uievent-view">view</code></a> attribute to
    `target`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="event-firing:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
    document</a>'s [`Window`](#window) object, if any, and null
    otherwise.

8.  `event`'s `getModifierState()` method is to return values
    appropriately describing the current state of the key input device.

9.  Return the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
    id="event-firing:concept-event-dispatch"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatching</a> `event` at
    `target`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="fire-a-click-event" class="dfn">Firing a `click` event</span>
at `target` means <a href="#fire-a-synthetic-pointer-event"
id="event-firing:fire-a-synthetic-pointer-event">firing a synthetic
pointer event named <code>click</code></a> at `target`.

</div>

### <span class="secno">8.2</span> The [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin<a href="#windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin" class="self-link"></a>

The [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin is
for use of APIs that are to be exposed on [`Window`](#window) and
[`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) objects.

Other standards are encouraged to further extend it using
`partial interface mixin `<a href="#windoworworkerglobalscope"
id="windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin:windoworworkerglobalscope-3"><code>WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope</code></a>` { … };`
along with an appropriate reference.

``` idl
typedef (DOMString or Function or TrustedScript) TimerHandler;

interface mixin WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope {
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute USVString origin;
  readonly attribute boolean isSecureContext;
  readonly attribute boolean crossOriginIsolated;

  undefined reportError(any e);

  // base64 utility methods
  DOMString btoa(DOMString data);
  ByteString atob(DOMString data);

  // timers
  long setTimeout(TimerHandler handler, optional long timeout = 0, any... arguments);
  undefined clearTimeout(optional long id = 0);
  long setInterval(TimerHandler handler, optional long timeout = 0, any... arguments);
  undefined clearInterval(optional long id = 0);

  // microtask queuing
  undefined queueMicrotask(VoidFunction callback);

  // ImageBitmap
  Promise<ImageBitmap> createImageBitmap(ImageBitmapSource image, optional ImageBitmapOptions options = {});
  Promise<ImageBitmap> createImageBitmap(ImageBitmapSource image, long sx, long sy, long sw, long sh, optional ImageBitmapOptions options = {});

  // structured cloning
  any structuredClone(any value, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});
};
Window includes WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope;
WorkerGlobalScope includes WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope;
```

Returns whether scripts running in this global are allowed to use APIs
that require cross-origin isolation. This depends on the
\`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`](#cross-origin-opener-policy-2)\` and
\`[`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`](#cross-origin-embedder-policy)\` HTTP
response headers and the
"[`cross-origin-isolated`](#cross-origin-isolated-feature)" feature.

<div class="example">

Developers are strongly encouraged to use `self.origin` over
`location.origin`. The former returns the <a href="#concept-origin"
id="windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin:concept-origin-2">origin</a> of the
environment, the latter of the URL of the environment. Imagine the
following script executing in a document on `https://stargate.example/`:

``` js
var frame = document.createElement("iframe")
frame.onload = function() {
  var frameWin = frame.contentWindow
  console.log(frameWin.location.origin) // "null"
  console.log(frameWin.origin) // "https://stargate.example"
}
document.body.appendChild(frame)
```

`self.origin` is a more reliable security indicator.

</div>

### <span class="secno">8.3</span> Base64 utility methods<a href="#atob" class="self-link"></a>

The [`atob()`](#dom-atob) and [`btoa()`](#dom-btoa) methods allow
developers to transform content to and from the base64 encoding.

In these APIs, for mnemonic purposes, the "b" can be considered to stand
for "binary", and the "a" for "ASCII". In practice, though, for
primarily historical reasons, both the input and output of these
functions are Unicode strings.

`result`` = self.`<a href="#dom-btoa" id="dom-btoa-dev"><code>btoa</code></a>`(``data``)`
