<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-shadowroot"
data-x-internal="shadowroot"><code
id="the-innerhtml-property:shadowroot">ShadowRoot</code></a>'s
<span id="dom-shadowroot-innerhtml" class="dfn" dfn-for="ShadowRoot"
dfn-type="attribute">`innerHTML`</span> getter steps are to return the
result of running <a href="#fragment-serializing-algorithm-steps"
id="the-innerhtml-property:fragment-serializing-algorithm-steps-2">fragment
serializing algorithm steps</a> with
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-innerhtml-property:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a> and
true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-innerhtml-property:element-4">Element</code></a>'s
[`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) setter steps are:

1.  Let `compliantString` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:tt-getcompliantstring"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedhtml"><code
    id="the-innerhtml-property:tt-trustedhtml">TrustedHTML</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>, the given value, "`Element innerHTML`", and "`script`".

2.  Let `context` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

3.  Let `fragment` be the result of invoking the
    <a href="#fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps">fragment
    parsing algorithm steps</a> with `context` and `compliantString`.

4.  If `context` is a [`template`](#the-template-element) element, then
    set `context` to the [`template`](#the-template-element) element's
    <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:template-contents">template contents</a>
    (a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-innerhtml-property:documentfragment-3">DocumentFragment</code></a>).

    Setting [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) on a
    [`template`](#the-template-element) element will replace all the
    nodes in its <a href="#template-contents"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:template-contents-2">template contents</a>
    rather than its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-tree-child"
    data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a>.

5.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-node-replace-all"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace-all">Replace all</a> with
    `fragment` within `context`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-shadowroot"
data-x-internal="shadowroot"><code
id="the-innerhtml-property:shadowroot-2">ShadowRoot</code></a>'s
[`innerHTML`](#dom-shadowroot-innerhtml) setter steps are:

1.  Let `compliantString` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:tt-getcompliantstring-2"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedhtml"><code
    id="the-innerhtml-property:tt-trustedhtml-2">TrustedHTML</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global
    object</a>, the given value, "`ShadowRoot innerHTML`", and
    "`script`".

2.  Let `context` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-documentfragment-host"
    data-x-internal="concept-documentfragment-host">host</a>.

3.  Let `fragment` be the result of invoking the
    <a href="#fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps-2">fragment
    parsing algorithm steps</a> with `context` and `compliantString`.

4.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:concept-node-replace-all-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace-all">Replace all</a> with
    `fragment` within <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-innerhtml-property:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.5.5</span> The [`outerHTML`](#dom-element-outerhtml) property<a href="#the-outerhtml-property" class="self-link"></a>

The [`outerHTML`](#dom-element-outerhtml) property has a number of
outstanding issues in the DOM Parsing and Serialization [issue
tracker](https://github.com/w3c/DOM-Parsing/issues), documenting various
problems with its specification.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-element-outerhtml"
id="dom-element-outerhtml-dev"><code>outerHTML</code></a>  
Returns a fragment of HTML or XML that represents the element and its
contents.

In the case of an XML document, throws an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="the-outerhtml-property:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-outerhtml-property:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if the
element cannot be serialized to XML.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-element-outerhtml"
id="the-outerhtml-property:dom-element-outerhtml-3"><code>outerHTML</code></a>` = ``value`  
Replaces the element with nodes parsed from the given string.

In the case of an XML document, throws a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
id="the-outerhtml-property:syntaxerror"
data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-outerhtml-property:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a> if
the given string is not well-formed.

Throws a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#nomodificationallowederror"
id="the-outerhtml-property:nomodificationallowederror"
data-x-internal="nomodificationallowederror">"<code>NoModificationAllowedError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-outerhtml-property:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a> if
the parent of the element is a <a href="#document"
id="the-outerhtml-property:document"><code>Document</code></a>.

This property's setter performs no sanitization to remove
potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like
[`script`](#the-script-element) or
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="the-outerhtml-property:event-handler-content-attributes">event
handler content attributes</a>.

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-outerhtml-property:element">Element</code></a>'s
<span id="dom-element-outerhtml" class="dfn" dfn-for="Element"
dfn-type="attribute">`outerHTML`</span> getter steps are:

1.  Let `element` be a fictional node whose only child is
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

2.  Return the result of running
    <a href="#fragment-serializing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:fragment-serializing-algorithm-steps">fragment
    serializing algorithm steps</a> with `element` and true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-outerhtml-property:element-2">Element</code></a>'s
[`outerHTML`](#dom-element-outerhtml) setter steps are:

1.  Let `compliantString` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:tt-getcompliantstring"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedhtml"><code
    id="the-outerhtml-property:tt-trustedhtml">TrustedHTML</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
    object</a>, the given value, "`Element outerHTML`", and "`script`".

2.  Let `parent` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-parent"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:parent" data-x-internal="parent">parent</a>.

3.  If `parent` is null, return. There would be no way to obtain a
    reference to the nodes created even if the remaining steps were run.

4.  If `parent` is a [`Document`](#document), throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#nomodificationallowederror"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:nomodificationallowederror-2"
    data-x-internal="nomodificationallowederror">"<code>NoModificationAllowedError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-outerhtml-property:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

5.  If `parent` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="the-outerhtml-property:documentfragment">DocumentFragment</code></a>,
    set `parent` to the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, "`body`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:html-namespace-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

6.  Let `fragment` be the result of invoking the
    <a href="#fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps">fragment
    parsing algorithm steps</a> given `parent` and `compliantString`.

7.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:concept-node-replace"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-replace">Replace</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    with `fragment` within
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-parent"
    id="the-outerhtml-property:parent-2" data-x-internal="parent">parent</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.5.6</span> The [`insertAdjacentHTML()`](#dom-element-insertadjacenthtml) method<a href="#the-insertadjacenthtml()-method" class="self-link"></a>

The [`insertAdjacentHTML()`](#dom-element-insertadjacenthtml) method has
a number of outstanding issues in the DOM Parsing and Serialization
[issue tracker](https://github.com/w3c/DOM-Parsing/issues), documenting
various problems with its specification.

`element``.`<a href="#dom-element-insertadjacenthtml"
id="dom-element-insertadjacenthtml-dev"><code>insertAdjacentHTML</code></a>`(``position``, ``string``)`  
Parses `string` as HTML or XML and inserts the resulting nodes into the
tree in the position given by the `position` argument, as follows:

"`beforebegin`"  
Before the element itself (i.e., after `element`'s previous sibling)

"`afterbegin`"  
Just inside the element, before its first child.

"`beforeend`"  
Just inside the element, after its last child.

"`afterend`"  
After the element itself (i.e., before `element`'s next sibling)

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:syntaxerror"
data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:domexception">DOMException</code></a>
if the arguments have invalid values (e.g., in the case of an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:xml-documents"
data-x-internal="xml-documents">XML document</a>, if the given string is
not well-formed).

Throws a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#nomodificationallowederror"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:nomodificationallowederror"
data-x-internal="nomodificationallowederror">"<code>NoModificationAllowedError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>
if the given position isn't possible (e.g. inserting elements after the
root element of a [`Document`](#document)).

This method performs no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous
elements and attributes like [`script`](#the-script-element) or
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:event-handler-content-attributes">event
handler content attributes</a>.

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:element">Element</code></a>'s
<span id="dom-element-insertadjacenthtml" class="dfn" dfn-for="Element"
dfn-type="method">`insertAdjacentHTML(``position``, ``string``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  Let `compliantString` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:tt-getcompliantstring"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedhtml"><code
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:tt-trustedhtml">TrustedHTML</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-relevant-global">relevant
    global object</a>, `string`, "`Element insertAdjacentHTML`", and
    "`script`".

2.  Let `context` be null.

3.  Use the first matching item from this list:

    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`beforebegin`"  
    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`afterend`"  
    1.  Set `context` to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
        id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-2"
        data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#dom-parent"
        id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:dom-parent">parent</a>.

    2.  If `context` is null or a [`Document`](#document), throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#nomodificationallowederror"
        id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:nomodificationallowederror-2"
        data-x-internal="nomodificationallowederror">"<code>NoModificationAllowedError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`afterbegin`"  
    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`beforeend`"  
    Set `context` to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    Otherwise  
    Throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:syntaxerror-2"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  If `context` is not an
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
    data-x-internal="element"><code
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:element-2">Element</code></a> or
    all of the following are true:

    - `context`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
      id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:node-document"
      data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is an HTML
      document;

    - `context`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
      id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-element-local-name"
      data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a> is
      "[`html`](#the-html-element)"; and

    - `context`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace"
      id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-element-namespace"
      data-x-internal="concept-element-namespace">namespace</a> is the
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
      id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:html-namespace-2"
      data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>,

    then set `context` to the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, "`body`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:html-namespace-2-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

5.  Let `fragment` be the result of invoking the
    <a href="#fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps">fragment
    parsing algorithm steps</a> with `context` and `compliantString`.

6.  Use the first matching item from this list:
    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-5"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`beforebegin`"  
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-node-insert"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert">Insert</a> `fragment` into
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-5"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#dom-parent"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:dom-parent-2">parent</a> before
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-6"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-6"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`afterbegin`"  
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-node-insert-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert">Insert</a> `fragment` into
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-7"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a> before its
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-first-child"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:first-child"
    data-x-internal="first-child">first child</a>.

    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-7"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`beforeend`"  
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-node-append"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">Append</a> `fragment` to
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-8"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

    If `position` is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:ascii-case-insensitive-8"
    data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a> match for the string "`afterend`"  
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:concept-node-insert-3"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-insert">Insert</a> `fragment` into
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-9"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#dom-parent"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:dom-parent-3">parent</a> before
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:this-10"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-next-sibling"
    id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:next-sibling"
    data-x-internal="next-sibling">next sibling</a>.

</div>

As with other direct
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-node"
data-x-internal="node"><code
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:node">Node</code></a>-manipulation
APIs (and unlike [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml)),
[`insertAdjacentHTML()`](#dom-element-insertadjacenthtml) does not
include any special handling for [`template`](#the-template-element)
elements. In most cases you will want to use
`templateEl.`<a href="#dom-template-content"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:dom-template-content"><code>content</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-element-insertadjacenthtml"
id="the-insertadjacenthtml()-method:dom-element-insertadjacenthtml-4"><code>insertAdjacentHTML()</code></a>
instead of directly manipulating the child nodes of a
[`template`](#the-template-element) element.

#### <span class="secno">8.5.7</span> The [`createContextualFragment()`](#dom-range-createcontextualfragment) method<a href="#the-createcontextualfragment()-method" class="self-link"></a>

The [`createContextualFragment()`](#dom-range-createcontextualfragment)
method has a number of outstanding issues in the DOM Parsing and
Serialization [issue
tracker](https://github.com/w3c/DOM-Parsing/issues), documenting various
problems with its specification.

`docFragment`` = ``range``.`<a href="#dom-range-createcontextualfragment"
id="dom-range-createcontextualfragment-dev"><code>createContextualFragment</code></a>`(``string``)`  
Returns a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:documentfragment">DocumentFragment</code></a>
created from the markup string `string` using `range`'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-range-start-node"
id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:concept-range-start-node"
data-x-internal="concept-range-start-node">start node</a> as the context
in which `fragment` is parsed.

This method performs no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous
elements and attributes like [`script`](#the-script-element) or
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:event-handler-content-attributes">event
handler content attributes</a>.

``` idl
partial interface Range {
  [CEReactions, NewObject] DocumentFragment createContextualFragment((TrustedHTML or DOMString) string);
};
```

<div algorithm="">

<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-range"
data-x-internal="range"><code
id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:range">Range</code></a>'s
<span id="dom-range-createcontextualfragment" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Range"
dfn-type="method">`createContextualFragment(``string``)`</span> method
steps are:

1.  Let `compliantString` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:tt-getcompliantstring"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedhtml"><code
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:tt-trustedhtml-2">TrustedHTML</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:concept-relevant-global">relevant
    global object</a>, `string`, "`Range createContextualFragment`", and
    "`script`".

2.  Let `node` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-range-start-node"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:concept-range-start-node-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-range-start-node">start node</a>.

3.  Let `element` be null.

4.  If `node` <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:implements"
    data-x-internal="implements">implements</a>
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
    data-x-internal="element"><code
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:element">Element</code></a>,
    set `element` to `node`.

5.  Otherwise, if `node`
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:implements-2"
    data-x-internal="implements">implements</a>
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
    data-x-internal="text"><code
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:text">Text</code></a> or
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-comment"
    data-x-internal="comment-2"><code
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:comment-2">Comment</code></a>,
    set `element` to `node`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#parent-element"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:parent-element"
    data-x-internal="parent-element">parent element</a>.

6.  If `element` is null or all of the following are true:

    - `element`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
      id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:node-document"
      data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is an HTML
      document;

    - `element`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name"
      id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:concept-element-local-name"
      data-x-internal="concept-element-local-name">local name</a> is
      "[`html`](#the-html-element)"; and

    - `element`'s
      <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace"
      id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:concept-element-namespace"
      data-x-internal="concept-element-namespace">namespace</a> is the
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
      id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:html-namespace-2"
      data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>,

    then set `element` to the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>, "`body`", and the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:html-namespace-2-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>.

7.  Return the result of invoking the
    <a href="#fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:fragment-parsing-algorithm-steps">fragment
    parsing algorithm steps</a> with `element`, `compliantString`, and
    <a href="#scripting-mode-fragment"
    id="the-createcontextualfragment()-method:scripting-mode-fragment">Fragment</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.5.8</span> The [`XMLSerializer`](#xmlserializer) interface<a href="#the-xmlserializer-interface" class="self-link"></a>

The [`XMLSerializer`](#xmlserializer) interface has a number of
outstanding issues in the DOM Parsing and Serialization [issue
tracker](https://github.com/w3c/DOM-Parsing/issues), documenting various
problems with its specification. The remainder of DOM Parsing and
Serialization will be gradually upstreamed to this specification.

`xmlSerializer`` = new `<a href="#dom-xmlserializer-constructor"
id="dom-xmlserializer-constructor-dev"><code>XMLSerializer</code></a>`()`  
Constructs a new [`XMLSerializer`](#xmlserializer) object.

`string`` = ``xmlSerializer``.`<a href="#dom-xmlserializer-serializetostring"
id="dom-xmlserializer-serializetostring-dev"><code>serializeToString</code></a>`(``root``)`  
Returns the result of serializing `root` to XML.

Throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="the-xmlserializer-interface:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-xmlserializer-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if
`root` cannot be serialized to XML.

The design of [`XMLSerializer`](#xmlserializer), as a class that needs
to be constructed and then have its
[`serializeToString()`](#dom-xmlserializer-serializetostring) method
called, is an unfortunate historical artifact. If we were designing this
functionality today it would be a standalone function.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface XMLSerializer {
  constructor();

  DOMString serializeToString(Node root);
};
```

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-xmlserializer-constructor"
class="dfn">`new XMLSerializer()`</span> constructor steps are to do
nothing.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-xmlserializer-serializetostring" class="dfn"
dfn-for="XMLSerializer"
dfn-type="method">`serializeToString(``root``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  Return the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#dfn-xml-serialization"
    id="the-xmlserializer-interface:xml-serialization"
    data-x-internal="xml-serialization">XML serialization</a> of `root`
    given false.

</div>

Cancels the timeout set with [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval) or
[`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout) identified by `id`.

Timers can be nested; after five such nested timers, however, the
interval is forced to be at least four milliseconds.

This API does not guarantee that timers will run exactly on schedule.
Delays due to CPU load, other tasks, etc, are to be expected.

Objects that implement the
[`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin have a
<span id="map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope" export="">map of setTimeout and
setInterval IDs</span>, which is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="timers:ordered-map" data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>,
initially empty. Each
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key" id="timers:map-key"
data-x-internal="map-key">key</a> in this map is a positive integer,
corresponding to the return value of a [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout)
or [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval) call. Each
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-value" id="timers:map-value"
data-x-internal="map-value">value</a> is a
<a href="#unique-internal-value"
id="timers:unique-internal-value">unique internal value</a>,
corresponding to a key in the object's
<a href="#map-of-active-timers" id="timers:map-of-active-timers">map of
active timers</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-settimeout" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`setTimeout(``handler``, ``timeout``, ...``arguments``)`</span>
method steps are to return the result of running the
<a href="#timer-initialisation-steps"
id="timers:timer-initialisation-steps">timer initialization steps</a>
given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="timers:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `handler`, `timeout`, `arguments`, and
false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-setinterval" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`setInterval(``handler``, ``timeout``, ...``arguments``)`</span>
method steps are to return the result of running the
<a href="#timer-initialisation-steps"
id="timers:timer-initialisation-steps-2">timer initialization steps</a>
given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="timers:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `handler`, `timeout`, `arguments`, and
true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-cleartimeout" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`clearTimeout(``id``)`</span> and
<span id="dom-clearinterval" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`clearInterval(``id``)`</span> method steps are to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-remove"
id="timers:map-remove" data-x-internal="map-remove">remove</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="timers:this-3"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids">map of setTimeout and
setInterval IDs</a>\[`id`\].

</div>

Because [`clearTimeout()`](#dom-cleartimeout) and
[`clearInterval()`](#dom-clearinterval) clear entries from the same map,
either method can be used to clear timers created by
[`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout) or
[`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To perform the <span id="timer-initialisation-steps" class="dfn">timer
initialization steps</span>, given a
[`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) `global`, a
string or <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function"
data-x-internal="idl-function"><code
id="timers:idl-function">Function</code></a> or
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-script"
data-x-internal="tt-trustedscript"><code
id="timers:tt-trustedscript">TrustedScript</code></a> `handler`, a
number `timeout`, a list `arguments`, a boolean `repeat`, and optionally
(and only if `repeat` is true) a number `previousId`, perform the
following steps. They return a number.

1.  Let `thisArg` be `global` if that is a
    [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object; otherwise let
    `thisArg` be the [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) that corresponds to
    `global`.

2.  If `previousId` was given, let `id` be `previousId`; otherwise, let
    `id` be an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="timers:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    integer that is greater than zero and does not already
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="timers:map-exists" data-x-internal="map-exists">exist</a> in
    `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
    id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-2">map of setTimeout
    and setInterval IDs</a>.

3.  If the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent"
    id="timers:surrounding-agent"
    data-x-internal="surrounding-agent">surrounding agent</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="timers:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>'s
    <a href="#currently-running-task"
    id="timers:currently-running-task">currently running task</a> is a
    task that was created by this algorithm, then let `nesting level` be
    the <a href="#concept-task" id="timers:concept-task">task</a>'s
    <a href="#timer-nesting-level" id="timers:timer-nesting-level">timer
    nesting level</a>. Otherwise, let `nesting level` be 0.

    The task's
    <a href="#timer-nesting-level" id="timers:timer-nesting-level-2">timer
    nesting level</a> is used both for nested calls to
    [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout), and for the repeating timers
    created by [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval). (Or, indeed, for any
    combination of the two.) In other words, it represents nested
    invocations of this algorithm, not of a particular method.

4.  If `timeout` is less than 0, then set `timeout` to 0.

5.  If `nesting level` is greater than 5, and `timeout` is less than 4,
    then set `timeout` to 4.

6.  Let `realm` be `global`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
    id="timers:concept-relevant-realm">relevant realm</a>.

7.  Let `initiating script` be the
    <a href="#active-script" id="timers:active-script">active script</a>.

8.  Let `uniqueHandle` be null.

9.  Let `task` be a
    <a href="#concept-task" id="timers:concept-task-2">task</a> that
    runs the following substeps:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="timers:assert"
        data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `uniqueHandle` is a
        <a href="#unique-internal-value"
        id="timers:unique-internal-value-2">unique internal value</a>,
        not null.

    2.  If `id` does not
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="timers:map-exists-2" data-x-internal="map-exists">exist</a>
        in `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
        id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-3">map of setTimeout
        and setInterval IDs</a>, then abort these steps.

    3.  If `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
        id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-4">map of setTimeout
        and setInterval IDs</a>\[`id`\] does not equal `uniqueHandle`,
        then abort these steps.

        This accommodates for the ID having been cleared by a
        [`clearTimeout()`](#dom-cleartimeout) or
        [`clearInterval()`](#dom-clearinterval) call, and being reused
        by a subsequent [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout) or
        [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval) call.

    4.  Let `settings object` be `global`'s
        <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="timers:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings object</a>.

    5.  If <a href="#concept-environment-noscript"
        id="timers:concept-environment-noscript">scripting is disabled</a>
        for `settings object`, then abort these steps.

    6.  <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-timing-info-for-timer-handler"
        id="timers:record-timing-info-for-timer-handler"
        data-x-internal="record-timing-info-for-timer-handler">Record timing
        info for timer handler</a> given `handler`, `settings object`,
        and `repeat`.

    7.  If `handler` is a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function"
        data-x-internal="idl-function"><code
        id="timers:idl-function-2">Function</code></a>, then
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
        id="timers:es-invoking-callback-functions"
        data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">invoke</a>
        `handler` given `arguments` and "`report`", and with
        *<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value"
        data-x-internal="dfn-callback-this-value">callback this value</a>*
        set to `thisArg`.

    8.  Otherwise:

        1.  If `previousId` was not given:

            1.  Let `globalName` be "`Window`" if `global` is a
                [`Window`](#window) object; "`WorkerGlobalScope`"
                otherwise.

            2.  Let `methodName` be "`setInterval`" if `repeat` is true;
                "`setTimeout`" otherwise.

            3.  Let `sink` be a concatenation of `globalName`, U+0020
                SPACE, and `methodName`.

            4.  Set `handler` to the result of invoking the <a
                href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
                id="timers:tt-getcompliantstring"
                data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
                string</a> algorithm with
                <a href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-script"
                data-x-internal="tt-trustedscript"><code
                id="timers:tt-trustedscript-2">TrustedScript</code></a>,
                `global`, `handler`, `sink`, and "`script`".

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="timers:assert-2"
            data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>: `handler` is a string.

        3.  Perform
            <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#can-compile-strings"
            id="timers:csp-ensurecspdoesnotblockstringcompilation"
            data-x-internal="csp-ensurecspdoesnotblockstringcompilation">EnsureCSPDoesNotBlockStringCompilation</a>(`realm`,
            « », `handler`, `handler`, timer, « », `handler`). If this
            throws an exception, catch it,
            <a href="#report-an-exception"
            id="timers:report-an-exception">report</a> it for `global`,
            and abort these steps.

        4.  Let `fetch options` be the
            <a href="#default-script-fetch-options"
            id="timers:default-script-fetch-options">default script fetch
            options</a>.

        5.  Let `base URL` be `settings object`'s
            <a href="#api-base-url" id="timers:api-base-url">API base URL</a>.

        6.  If `initiating script` is not null, then:

            1.  Set `fetch options` to a
                <a href="#script-fetch-options" id="timers:script-fetch-options">script
                fetch options</a> whose
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-nonce"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-nonce">cryptographic nonce</a>
                is `initiating script`'s
                <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
                id="timers:concept-script-script-fetch-options">fetch options</a>'s
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-nonce"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-nonce-2">cryptographic nonce</a>,
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-integrity"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-integrity">integrity
                metadata</a> is the empty string,
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-parser"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-parser">parser metadata</a>
                is "`not-parser-inserted`",
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-credentials"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-credentials">credentials
                mode</a> is `initiating script`'s
                <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
                id="timers:concept-script-script-fetch-options-2">fetch options</a>'s
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-credentials"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-credentials-2">credentials
                mode</a>,
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy">referrer
                policy</a> is `initiating script`'s
                <a href="#concept-script-script-fetch-options"
                id="timers:concept-script-script-fetch-options-3">fetch options</a>'s
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-referrer-policy-2">referrer
                policy</a>, and
                <a href="#concept-script-fetch-options-fetch-priority"
                id="timers:concept-script-fetch-options-fetch-priority">fetch
                priority</a> is "`auto`".

            2.  Set `base URL` to `initiating script`'s
                <a href="#concept-script-base-url"
                id="timers:concept-script-base-url">base URL</a>.

            The effect of these steps ensures that the string
            compilation done by [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout) and
            [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval) behaves equivalently to
            that done by <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-eval-x"
            data-x-internal="eval()"><code id="timers:eval()">eval()</code></a>.
            That is,
            <a href="#module-script" id="timers:module-script">module script</a>
            fetches via
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls"
            data-x-internal="import()"><code
            id="timers:import()">import()</code></a> will behave the
            same in both contexts.

        7.  Let `script` be the result of
            <a href="#creating-a-classic-script"
            id="timers:creating-a-classic-script">creating a classic script</a>
            given `handler`, `settings object`, `base URL`, and
            `fetch options`.

        8.  <a href="#run-a-classic-script" id="timers:run-a-classic-script">Run the
            classic script</a> `script`.

    9.  If `id` does not
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
        id="timers:map-exists-3" data-x-internal="map-exists">exist</a>
        in `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
        id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-5">map of setTimeout
        and setInterval IDs</a>, then abort these steps.

    10. If `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
        id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-6">map of setTimeout
        and setInterval IDs</a>\[`id`\] does not equal `uniqueHandle`,
        then abort these steps.

        The ID might have been removed via the author code in `handler`
        calling [`clearTimeout()`](#dom-cleartimeout) or
        [`clearInterval()`](#dom-clearinterval). Checking that
        uniqueHandle isn't different accounts for the possibility of the
        ID, after having been cleared, being reused by a subsequent
        [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout) or
        [`setInterval()`](#dom-setinterval) call.

    11. If `repeat` is true, then perform the
        <a href="#timer-initialisation-steps"
        id="timers:timer-initialisation-steps-3">timer initialization steps</a>
        again, given `global`, `handler`, `timeout`, `arguments`, true,
        and `id`.

    12. Otherwise, <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-remove"
        id="timers:map-remove-2" data-x-internal="map-remove">remove</a>
        `global`'s <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
        id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-7">map of setTimeout
        and setInterval IDs</a>\[`id`\].

10. Increment `nesting level` by one.

11. Set `task`'s <span id="timer-nesting-level" class="dfn">timer
    nesting level</span> to `nesting level`.

12. Let `completionStep` be an algorithm step which
    <a href="#queue-a-global-task" id="timers:queue-a-global-task">queues a
    global task</a> on the <span id="timer-task-source" class="dfn"
    export="">timer task source</span> given `global` to run `task`.

13. Set `uniqueHandle` to the result of
    <a href="#run-steps-after-a-timeout"
    id="timers:run-steps-after-a-timeout">running steps after a timeout</a>
    given `global`, "`setTimeout/setInterval`", `timeout`, and
    `completionStep`.

14. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set" id="timers:map-set"
    data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> `global`'s
    <a href="#map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids"
    id="timers:map-of-settimeout-and-setinterval-ids-8">map of setTimeout
    and setInterval IDs</a>\[`id`\] to `uniqueHandle`.

15. Return `id`.

</div>

Argument conversion as defined by Web IDL (for example, invoking
`toString()` methods on objects passed as the first argument) happens in
the algorithms defined in Web IDL, before this algorithm is invoked.

<div class="example">

So for example, the following rather silly code will result in the log
containing "`ONE TWO `":

``` js
var log = '';
function logger(s) { log += s + ' '; }

setTimeout({ toString: function () {
  setTimeout("logger('ONE')", 100);
  return "logger('TWO')";
} }, 100);
```

</div>

<div class="example">

To run tasks of several milliseconds back to back without any delay,
while still yielding back to the browser to avoid starving the user
interface (and to avoid the browser killing the script for hogging the
CPU), simply queue the next timer before performing work:

``` js
function doExpensiveWork() {
  var done = false;
  // ...
  // this part of the function takes up to five milliseconds
  // set done to true if we're done
  // ...
  return done;
}

function rescheduleWork() {
  var id = setTimeout(rescheduleWork, 0); // preschedule next iteration
  if (doExpensiveWork())
    clearTimeout(id); // clear the timeout if we don't need it
}

function scheduleWork() {
  setTimeout(rescheduleWork, 0);
}

scheduleWork(); // queues a task to do lots of work
```

</div>

Objects that implement the
[`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin have a
<span id="map-of-active-timers" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope" export="">map of active
timers</span>, which is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="timers:ordered-map-2" data-x-internal="ordered-map">ordered map</a>,
initially empty. Each
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-key" id="timers:map-key-2"
data-x-internal="map-key">key</a> in this map is a
<a href="#unique-internal-value"
id="timers:unique-internal-value-3">unique internal value</a> that
represents a timer, and each
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-value"
id="timers:map-value-2" data-x-internal="map-value">value</a> is a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp"
data-x-internal="domhighrestimestamp"><code
id="timers:domhighrestimestamp">DOMHighResTimeStamp</code></a>,
representing the expiry time for that timer.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="run-steps-after-a-timeout" class="dfn" export="">run steps
after a timeout</span>, given a
[`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) `global`, a
string `orderingIdentifier`, a number `milliseconds`, and a set of steps
`completionSteps`, perform the following steps. They return a
<a href="#unique-internal-value"
id="timers:unique-internal-value-4">unique internal value</a>.

1.  Let `timerKey` be a new <a href="#unique-internal-value"
    id="timers:unique-internal-value-5">unique internal value</a>.

2.  Let `startTime` be the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time"
    id="timers:current-high-resolution-time"
    data-x-internal="current-high-resolution-time">current high resolution
    time</a> given `global`.

3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set" id="timers:map-set-2"
    data-x-internal="map-set">Set</a> `global`'s
    <a href="#map-of-active-timers" id="timers:map-of-active-timers-2">map
    of active timers</a>\[`timerKey`\] to `startTime` plus
    `milliseconds`.

4.  Run the following steps
    <a href="#in-parallel" id="timers:in-parallel">in parallel</a>:

    1.  If `global` is a [`Window`](#window) object, wait until
        `global`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
        id="timers:concept-document-window">associated <code>Document</code></a>
        has been
        <a href="#fully-active" id="timers:fully-active">fully active</a>
        for a further `milliseconds` milliseconds (not necessarily
        consecutively).

        Otherwise, `global` is a
        [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object; wait until
        `milliseconds` milliseconds have passed with the worker not
        suspended (not necessarily consecutively).

    2.  Wait until any invocations of this algorithm that had the same
        `global` and `orderingIdentifier`, that started before this one,
        and whose `milliseconds` is less than or equal to this one's,
        have completed.

    3.  Optionally, wait a further
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
        id="timers:implementation-defined-2"
        data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
        length of time.

        This is intended to allow user agents to pad timeouts as needed
        to optimize the power usage of the device. For example, some
        processors have a low-power mode where the granularity of timers
        is reduced; on such platforms, user agents can slow timers down
        to fit this schedule instead of requiring the processor to use
        the more accurate mode with its associated higher power usage.

    4.  Perform `completionSteps`.

    5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-remove"
        id="timers:map-remove-3" data-x-internal="map-remove">Remove</a>
        `global`'s
        <a href="#map-of-active-timers" id="timers:map-of-active-timers-3">map
        of active timers</a>\[`timerKey`\].

5.  Return `timerKey`.

<a href="#run-steps-after-a-timeout"
id="timers:run-steps-after-a-timeout-2">Run steps after a timeout</a> is
meant to be used by other specifications that want to execute
developer-supplied code after a developer-supplied timeout, in a similar
manner to [`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout). (Note, however, it does not
have the nesting and clamping behavior of
[`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout).) Such specifications can choose an
`orderingIdentifier` to ensure ordering within their specification's
timeouts, while not constraining ordering with respect to other
specification's timeouts.

</div>

### <span class="secno">8.7</span> Microtask queuing<a href="#microtask-queuing" class="self-link"></a>

</div>

`self``.`<a href="#dom-queuemicrotask"
id="dom-queuemicrotask-dev"><code>queueMicrotask</code></a>`(``callback``)`  
<a href="#queue-a-microtask"
id="microtask-queuing:queue-a-microtask">Queues</a> a
<a href="#microtask" id="microtask-queuing:microtask">microtask</a> to
run the given `callback`.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-queuemicrotask" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope"
dfn-type="method">`queueMicrotask(``callback``)`</span> method must
<a href="#queue-a-microtask"
id="microtask-queuing:queue-a-microtask-2">queue a microtask</a> to
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function"
id="microtask-queuing:es-invoking-callback-functions"
data-x-internal="es-invoking-callback-functions">invoke</a> `callback`
with « » and "`report`".

</div>

The [`queueMicrotask()`](#dom-queuemicrotask) method allows authors to
schedule a callback on the <a href="#microtask-queue"
id="microtask-queuing:microtask-queue">microtask queue</a>. This allows
their code to run once the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
id="microtask-queuing:javascript-execution-context-stack"
data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
execution context stack</a> is next empty, which happens once all
currently executing synchronous JavaScript has run to completion. This
doesn't yield control back to the
<a href="#event-loop" id="microtask-queuing:event-loop">event loop</a>,
as would be the case when using, for example,
[`setTimeout(``f``, 0)`](#dom-settimeout).

Authors ought to be aware that scheduling a lot of microtasks has the
same performance downsides as running a lot of synchronous code. Both
will prevent the browser from doing its own work, such as rendering. In
many cases,
[`requestAnimationFrame()`](#dom-animationframeprovider-requestanimationframe)
or <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#the-requestidlecallback-method"
data-x-internal="requestidlecallback()"><code
id="microtask-queuing:requestidlecallback()">requestIdleCallback()</code></a>
is a better choice. In particular, if the goal is to run code before the
next rendering cycle, that is the purpose of
[`requestAnimationFrame()`](#dom-animationframeprovider-requestanimationframe).

As can be seen from the following examples, the best way of thinking
about [`queueMicrotask()`](#dom-queuemicrotask) is as a mechanism for
rearranging synchronous code, effectively placing the queued code
immediately after the currently executing synchronous JavaScript has run
to completion.

<div class="example">

The most common reason for using
[`queueMicrotask()`](#dom-queuemicrotask) is to create consistent
ordering, even in the cases where information is available
synchronously, without introducing undue delay.

For example, consider a custom element firing a `load` event, that also
maintains an internal cache of previously-loaded data. A naïve
implementation might look like:

``` js
MyElement.prototype.loadData = function (url) {
  if (this._cache[url]) {
    this._setData(this._cache[url]);
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));
  } else {
    fetch(url).then(res => res.arrayBuffer()).then(data => {
      this._cache[url] = data;
      this._setData(data);
      this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));
    });
  }
};
```

This naïve implementation is problematic, however, in that it causes its
users to experience inconsistent behavior. For example, code such as

``` js
element.addEventListener("load", () => console.log("loaded"));
console.log("1");
element.loadData();
console.log("2");
```

will sometimes log "1, 2, loaded" (if the data needs to be fetched), and
sometimes log "1, loaded, 2" (if the data is already cached). Similarly,
after the call to `loadData()`, it will be inconsistent whether or not
the data is set on the element.

To get a consistent ordering, [`queueMicrotask()`](#dom-queuemicrotask)
can be used:

``` js
MyElement.prototype.loadData = function (url) {
  if (this._cache[url]) {
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      this._setData(this._cache[url]);
      this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));
    });
  } else {
    fetch(url).then(res => res.arrayBuffer()).then(data => {
      this._cache[url] = data;
      this._setData(data);
      this.dispatchEvent(new Event("load"));
    });
  }
};
```

By essentially rearranging the queued code to be after the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack"
id="microtask-queuing:javascript-execution-context-stack-2"
data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context-stack">JavaScript
execution context stack</a> empties, this ensures a consistent ordering
and update of the element's state.

</div>

<div class="example">

Another interesting use of [`queueMicrotask()`](#dom-queuemicrotask) is
to allow uncoordinated "batching" of work by multiple callers. For
example, consider a library function that wants to send data somewhere
as soon as possible, but doesn't want to make multiple network requests
if doing so is easily avoidable. One way to balance this would be like
so:

``` js
const queuedToSend = [];

function sendData(data) {
  queuedToSend.push(data);

  if (queuedToSend.length === 1) {
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      const stringToSend = JSON.stringify(queuedToSend);
      queuedToSend.length = 0;

      fetch("/endpoint", stringToSend);
    });
  }
}
```

With this architecture, multiple subsequent calls to `sendData()` within
the currently executing synchronous JavaScript will be batched together
into one <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-global-fetch"
data-x-internal="fetch()"><code
id="microtask-queuing:fetch()">fetch()</code></a> call, but with no
intervening event loop tasks preempting the fetch (as would have
happened with similar code that instead used
[`setTimeout()`](#dom-settimeout)).

</div>

Displays a modal text control prompt with the given message, waits for
the user to dismiss it, and returns the value that the user entered. If
the user cancels the prompt, then returns null instead. If the second
argument is present, then the given value is used as a default.

Logic that depends on
<a href="#concept-task" id="simple-dialogs:concept-task">tasks</a> or
<a href="#microtask" id="simple-dialogs:microtask">microtasks</a>, such
as <a href="#media-element" id="simple-dialogs:media-element">media
elements</a> loading their
<a href="#media-data" id="simple-dialogs:media-data">media data</a>, are
stalled when these methods are invoked.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-alert-noargs" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`alert()`</span> and <span id="dom-alert" class="dfn"
dfn-for="Window" dfn-type="method">`alert(``message``)`</span> method
steps are:

1.  If we <a href="#cannot-show-simple-dialogs"
    id="simple-dialogs:cannot-show-simple-dialogs">cannot show simple
    dialogs</a> for
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="simple-dialogs:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>, then return.

2.  If the method was invoked with no arguments, then let `message` be
    the empty string; otherwise, let `message` be the method's first
    argument.

3.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines"
    id="simple-dialogs:normalize-newlines"
    data-x-internal="normalize-newlines">normalizing newlines</a> given
    `message`.

4.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="#optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string"
    id="simple-dialogs:optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string">optionally
    truncating</a> `message`.

5.  Let `userPromptHandler` be <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt opened</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`alert`", and `message`.

6.  If `userPromptHandler` is "`none`", then:

    1.  Show `message` to the user, treating U+000A LF as a line break.

    2.  Optionally, <a href="#pause" id="simple-dialogs:pause">pause</a>
        while waiting for the user to acknowledge the message.

7.  Invoke <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt closed</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`alert`", and true.

</div>

This method is defined using two overloads, instead of using an optional
argument, for historical reasons. The practical impact of this is that
`alert(undefined)` is treated as `alert("undefined")`, but `alert()` is
treated as `alert("")`.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-confirm" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`confirm(``message``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If we <a href="#cannot-show-simple-dialogs"
    id="simple-dialogs:cannot-show-simple-dialogs-2">cannot show simple
    dialogs</a> for <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>, then
    return false.

2.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines"
    id="simple-dialogs:normalize-newlines-2"
    data-x-internal="normalize-newlines">normalizing newlines</a> given
    `message`.

3.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="#optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string"
    id="simple-dialogs:optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string-2">optionally
    truncating</a> `message`.

4.  Show `message` to the user, treating U+000A LF as a line break, and
    ask the user to respond with a positive or negative response.

5.  Let `userPromptHandler` be <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt opened</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-5" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`confirm`", and `message`.

6.  Let `accepted` be false.

7.  If `userPromptHandler` is "`none`", then:

    1.  <a href="#pause" id="simple-dialogs:pause-2">Pause</a> until the
        user responds either positively or negatively.

    2.  If the user responded positively, then set `accepted` to true.

8.  If `userPromptHandler` is "`accept`", then set `accepted` to true.

9.  Invoke <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt closed</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-6" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`confirm`", and `accepted`.

10. Return `accepted`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-prompt" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`prompt(``message``, ``default``)`</span> method steps
are:

1.  If we <a href="#cannot-show-simple-dialogs"
    id="simple-dialogs:cannot-show-simple-dialogs-3">cannot show simple
    dialogs</a> for <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-7" data-x-internal="this">this</a>, then
    return null.

2.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-newlines"
    id="simple-dialogs:normalize-newlines-3"
    data-x-internal="normalize-newlines">normalizing newlines</a> given
    `message`.

3.  Set `message` to the result of
    <a href="#optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string"
    id="simple-dialogs:optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string-3">optionally
    truncating</a> `message`.

4.  Set `default` to the result of
    <a href="#optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string"
    id="simple-dialogs:optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string-4">optionally
    truncating</a> `default`.

5.  Show `message` to the user, treating U+000A LF as a line break, and
    ask the user to either respond with a string value or abort. The
    response must be defaulted to the value given by `default`.

6.  Let `userPromptHandler` be <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened-3"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-opened">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt opened</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-8" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`prompt`", and `message`.

7.  Let `result` be null.

8.  If `userPromptHandler` is "`none`", then:

    1.  <a href="#pause" id="simple-dialogs:pause-3">Pause</a> while
        waiting for the user's response.

    2.  If the user did not abort, then set `result` to the string that
        the user responded with.

9.  Otherwise, if `userPromptHandler` is "`accept`", then set `result`
    to the empty string.

10. Invoke <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed"
    id="simple-dialogs:webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed-3"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-user-prompt-closed">WebDriver BiDi user
    prompt closed</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="simple-dialogs:this-9" data-x-internal="this">this</a>,
    "`prompt`", false if `result` is null or true otherwise, and
    `result`.

11. Return `result`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="optionally-truncate-a-simple-dialog-string"
class="dfn">optionally truncate a simple dialog string</span> `s`,
return either `s` itself or some string derived from `s` that is
shorter. User agents should not provide UI for displaying the elided
portion of `s`, as this makes it too easy for abusers to create dialogs
of the form "Important security alert! Click 'Show More' for full
details!".

</div>

For example, a user agent might want to only display the first 100
characters of a message. Or, a user agent might replace the middle of
the string with "…". These types of modifications can be useful in
limiting the abuse potential of unnaturally large, trustworthy-looking
system dialogs.

<div algorithm="">

We <span id="cannot-show-simple-dialogs" class="dfn">cannot show simple
dialogs</span> for a [`Window`](#window) `window` when the following
algorithm returns true:

1.  If the <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="simple-dialogs:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing flag
    set</a> of `window`'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="simple-dialogs:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> has the <a href="#sandboxed-modals-flag"
    id="simple-dialogs:sandboxed-modals-flag">sandboxed modals flag</a>
    set, then return true.

2.  If `window`'s <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="simple-dialogs:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="simple-dialogs:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a> and
    `window`'s <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="simple-dialogs:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant settings
    object</a>'s <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="simple-dialogs:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
    origin</a> are not <a href="#same-origin-domain"
    id="simple-dialogs:same-origin-domain">same origin-domain</a>, then
    return true.

3.  If `window`'s
    <a href="#relevant-agent" id="simple-dialogs:relevant-agent">relevant
    agent</a>'s <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="simple-dialogs:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>'s
    <a href="#termination-nesting-level"
    id="simple-dialogs:termination-nesting-level">termination nesting
    level</a> is nonzero, then optionally return true.

4.  Optionally, return true. (For example, the user agent might give the
    user the option to ignore all modal dialogs, and would thus abort at
    this step whenever the method was invoked.)

5.  Return false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.8.2</span> Printing<a href="#printing" class="self-link"></a>

Android114+</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome

Android10.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

`window``.`<a href="#dom-print" id="dom-print-dev"><code>print</code></a>`()`  
Prompts the user to print the page.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-print" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`print()`</span> method steps are:

1.  Let `document` be
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="printing:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="printing:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

2.  If `document` is not
    <a href="#fully-active" id="printing:fully-active">fully active</a>,
    then return.

3.  If `document`'s
    <a href="#unload-counter" id="printing:unload-counter">unload
    counter</a> is greater than 0, then return.

4.  If `document` is <a href="#ready-for-post-load-tasks"
    id="printing:ready-for-post-load-tasks">ready for post-load tasks</a>,
    then run the
    <a href="#printing-steps" id="printing:printing-steps">printing
    steps</a> for `document`.

5.  Otherwise, set `document`'s <span id="print-when-loaded"
    class="dfn">print when loaded</span> flag.

</div>

User agents should also run the
<a href="#printing-steps" id="printing:printing-steps-2">printing
steps</a> whenever the user asks for the opportunity to
<a href="#obtain-a-physical-form"
id="printing:obtain-a-physical-form">obtain a physical form</a> (e.g.
printed copy), or the representation of a physical form (e.g. PDF copy),
of a document.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="printing-steps" class="dfn">printing steps</span> for a
[`Document`](#document) `document` are:

1.  The user agent may display a message to the user or return (or
    both).

    For instance, a kiosk browser could silently ignore any invocations
    of the [`print()`](#dom-print) method.

    For instance, a browser on a mobile device could detect that there
    are no printers in the vicinity and display a message saying so
    before continuing to offer a "save to PDF" option.

2.  If the <a href="#active-sandboxing-flag-set"
    id="printing:active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing flag set</a>
    of `document` has the <a href="#sandboxed-modals-flag"
    id="printing:sandboxed-modals-flag">sandboxed modals flag</a> set,
    then return.

    If the printing dialog is blocked by a [`Document`](#document)'s
    sandbox, then neither the [`beforeprint`](#event-beforeprint) nor
    [`afterprint`](#event-afterprint) events will be fired.

3.  The user agent must
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="printing:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    [`beforeprint`](#event-beforeprint) at the
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="printing:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a> of
    `document`, as well as any
    <a href="#child-navigable" id="printing:child-navigable">child
    navigable</a> in it.

    Firing in children only doesn't seem right here, and some tasks
    likely need to be queued. See [issue
    \#5096](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5096).

    The [`beforeprint`](#event-beforeprint) event can be used to
    annotate the printed copy, for instance adding the time at which the
    document was printed.

4.  The user agent should offer the user the opportunity to
    <a href="#obtain-a-physical-form"
    id="printing:obtain-a-physical-form-2">obtain a physical form</a>
    (or the representation of a physical form) of `document`. The user
    agent may wait for the user to either accept or decline before
    returning; if so, the user agent must
    <a href="#pause" id="printing:pause">pause</a> while the method is
    waiting. Even if the user agent doesn't wait at this point, the user
    agent must use the state of the relevant documents as they are at
    this point in the algorithm if and when it eventually creates the
    alternate form.

5.  The user agent must
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="printing:concept-event-fire-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
    [`afterprint`](#event-afterprint) at the
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="printing:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global object</a>
    of `document`, as well as any
    <a href="#child-navigable" id="printing:child-navigable-2">child
    navigables</a> in it.

    Firing in children only doesn't seem right here, and some tasks
    likely need to be queued. See [issue
    \#5096](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5096).

    The [`afterprint`](#event-afterprint) event can be used to revert
    annotations added in the earlier event, as well as showing
    post-printing UI. For instance, if a page is walking the user
    through the steps of applying for a home loan, the script could
    automatically advance to the next step after having printed a form
    or other.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">8.9.1</span> The [`Navigator`](#navigator) object<a href="#the-navigator-object" class="self-link"></a>

Instances of [`Navigator`](#navigator) represent the identity and state
of the user agent (the client). It has also been used as a generic
global under which various APIs are located, but this is not precedent
to build upon. Instead use the
[`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#windoworworkerglobalscope) mixin or
equivalent.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface Navigator {
  // objects implementing this interface also implement the interfaces given below
};
Navigator includes NavigatorID;
Navigator includes NavigatorLanguage;
Navigator includes NavigatorOnLine;
Navigator includes NavigatorContentUtils;
Navigator includes NavigatorCookies;
Navigator includes NavigatorPlugins;
Navigator includes NavigatorConcurrentHardware;
```

These interface mixins are defined separately so that
[`WorkerNavigator`](#workernavigator) can reuse parts of the
[`Navigator`](#navigator) interface.

<div algorithm="">

Each [`Window`](#window) has an <span id="associated-navigator"
class="dfn">associated `Navigator`</span>, which is a
[`Navigator`](#navigator) object. Upon creation of the
[`Window`](#window) object, its <a href="#associated-navigator"
id="the-navigator-object:associated-navigator">associated
<code>Navigator</code></a> must be set to a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
id="the-navigator-object:new" data-x-internal="new">new</a>
[`Navigator`](#navigator) object created in the [`Window`](#window)
object's <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
id="the-navigator-object:concept-relevant-realm">relevant realm</a>.

</div>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">
