The <span id="dom-navigator" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="attribute">`navigator`</span> and
<span id="dom-clientinformation" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="attribute">`clientInformation`</span> getter steps are to
return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="the-navigator-object:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#associated-navigator"
id="the-navigator-object:associated-navigator-2">associated
<code>Navigator</code></a>.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.9.1.1</span> Client identification<a href="#client-identification" class="self-link"></a>

``` idl
interface mixin NavigatorID {
  readonly attribute DOMString appCodeName; // constant "Mozilla"
  readonly attribute DOMString appName; // constant "Netscape"
  readonly attribute DOMString appVersion;
  readonly attribute DOMString platform;
  readonly attribute DOMString product; // constant "Gecko"
  [Exposed=Window] readonly attribute DOMString productSub;
  readonly attribute DOMString userAgent;
  [Exposed=Window] readonly attribute DOMString vendor;
  [Exposed=Window] readonly attribute DOMString vendorSub; // constant ""
};
```

In certain cases, despite the best efforts of the entire industry, web
browsers have bugs and limitations that web authors are forced to work
around.

This section defines a collection of attributes that can be used to
determine, from script, the kind of user agent in use, in order to work
around these issues.

The user agent has a <span id="concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
class="dfn">navigator compatibility mode</span>, which is either
*Chrome*, *Gecko*, or *WebKit*.

The <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode">navigator
compatibility mode</a> constrains the [`NavigatorID`](#navigatorid)
mixin to the combinations of attribute values and presence of
[`taintEnabled()`](#dom-navigator-taintenabled) and
[`oscpu`](#dom-navigator-oscpu) that are known to be compatible with
existing web content.

Client detection should always be limited to detecting known current
versions; future versions and unknown versions should always be assumed
to be fully compliant.

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-appcodename"
id="dom-navigator-appcodename-dev"><code>appCodeName</code></a>

Returns the string "`Mozilla`".

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator-2"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-appname"
id="dom-navigator-appname-dev"><code>appName</code></a>

Returns the string "`Netscape`".

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator-3"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-appversion"
id="dom-navigator-appversion-dev"><code>appVersion</code></a>

Returns the version of the browser.

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator-4"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-platform"
id="dom-navigator-platform-dev"><code>platform</code></a>

Returns the name of the platform.

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator-5"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-product"
id="dom-navigator-product-dev"><code>product</code></a>

Returns the string "`Gecko`".

id="client-identification:dom-navigator-6"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-productsub"
id="dom-navigator-productsub-dev"><code>productSub</code></a>

Returns either the string "`20030107`", or the string "`20100101`".

`self``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="client-identification:dom-navigator-7"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-useragent"
id="dom-navigator-useragent-dev"><code>userAgent</code></a>

id="client-identification:dom-navigator-9"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-vendorsub"
id="dom-navigator-vendorsub-dev"><code>vendorSub</code></a>

Returns the empty string.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-appcodename" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorID" dfn-type="attribute">`appCodeName`</span> getter
steps are to return "`Mozilla`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-appname" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`appName`</span> getter steps are to return
"`Netscape`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-appversion" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorID" dfn-type="attribute">`appVersion`</span> getter
steps are:

1.  Let `userAgent` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="client-identification:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="client-identification:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>'s <a
    href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#environment-default-user-agent-value"
    id="client-identification:environment-default-user-agent-value"
    data-x-internal="environment-default-user-agent-value">environment
    default `<code>User-Agent</code>` value</a>.

2.  If `userAgent` does not start with \``Mozilla/5.0 (`\`, then return
    the empty string.

3.  Let `trail` be the substring of `userAgent`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#isomorphic-decode"
    id="client-identification:isomorphic-decode"
    data-x-internal="isomorphic-decode">isomorphic decoded</a>, that
    follows the "`Mozilla/`" prefix.

4.  If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
    id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-2">navigator
    compatibility mode</a> is *Chrome* or *WebKit*  
    Return `trail`.

    If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
    id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-3">navigator
    compatibility mode</a> is *Gecko*  
    If `trail` starts with "`5.0 (Windows`", then return
    "`5.0 (Windows)`".

    Otherwise, return the prefix of `trail` up to but not including the
    first U+003B (;), concatenated with the character U+0029 RIGHT
    PARENTHESIS. For example, "`5.0 (Macintosh)`", "`5.0 (Android 10)`",
    or "`5.0 (X11)`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-platform" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`platform`</span> getter steps are to return a
string representing the platform on which the browser is executing (e.g.
"`MacIntel`", "`Win32`", "`Linux x86_64`", "`Linux armv81`") or, for
privacy and compatibility, a string that is commonly returned on another
platform.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-product" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`product`</span> getter steps are to return
"`Gecko`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-productsub" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorID" dfn-type="attribute">`productSub`</span> getter
steps are to return the appropriate string from the following list:

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-4">navigator
compatibility mode</a> is *Chrome* or *WebKit*  
The string "`20030107`".

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-5">navigator
compatibility mode</a> is *Gecko*  
The string "`20100101`".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-useragent" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`userAgent`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="client-identification:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#relevant-settings-object"
id="client-identification:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant settings
object</a>'s <a
href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#environment-default-user-agent-value"
id="client-identification:environment-default-user-agent-value-2"
data-x-internal="environment-default-user-agent-value">environment
default `<code>User-Agent</code>` value</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-vendor" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`vendor`</span> getter steps are to return the
appropriate string from the following list:

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-6">navigator
compatibility mode</a> is *Chrome*  
The string "`Google Inc.`".

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-7">navigator
compatibility mode</a> is *Gecko*  
The empty string.

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-8">navigator
compatibility mode</a> is *WebKit*

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-vendorsub" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`vendorSub`</span> getter steps are to return the

If the <a href="#concept-navigator-compatibility-mode"
id="client-identification:concept-navigator-compatibility-mode-9">navigator

``` idl
};
```

dfn-for="NavigatorID" dfn-type="method">`taintEnabled()`</span> method
must return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-oscpu" class="dfn" dfn-for="NavigatorID"
dfn-type="attribute">`oscpu`</span> attribute's getter must return

the browser is executing, e.g. "`Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64`",
"`Linux x86_64`".

</div>

class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> Any information in this API
that varies from user to user can be used to profile the user. In fact,

to include as little information in this API as possible.

Returns an array of language tags representing the user's preferred
languages, with the most preferred language first.

The most preferred language is the one returned by
[`navigator.language`](#dom-navigator-language).

A [`languagechange`](#event-languagechange) event is fired at the
[`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object
when the user agent's understanding of what the user's preferred
languages are changes.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-language" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorLanguage" dfn-type="attribute">`language`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  Let `emulatedLanguage` be the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-emulated-language"
    id="language-preferences:webdriver-bidi-emulated-language"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-emulated-language">WebDriver BiDi
    emulated language</a> for
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="language-preferences:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="language-preferences:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>.
2.  If `emulatedLanguage` is not null, return `emulatedLanguage`.
3.  Return a valid BCP 47 language tag representing either
    <a href="#a-plausible-language"
    id="language-preferences:a-plausible-language">a plausible language</a>
    or the user's most preferred language. [\[BCP47\]](#refsBCP47)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-languages" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorLanguage" dfn-type="attribute">`languages`</span>
getter steps are:

1.  Let `emulatedLanguage` be the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-emulated-language"
    id="language-preferences:webdriver-bidi-emulated-language-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-bidi-emulated-language">WebDriver BiDi
    emulated language</a> for
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="language-preferences:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="language-preferences:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant settings
    object</a>.
2.  If `emulatedLanguage` is not null, return a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
    id="language-preferences:frozen-array"
    data-x-internal="frozen-array">frozen array</a> containing
    `emulatedLanguage`.
3.  Return a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
    id="language-preferences:frozen-array-2"
    data-x-internal="frozen-array">frozen array</a> of valid BCP 47
    language tags representing either one or more
    <a href="#a-plausible-language"
    id="language-preferences:a-plausible-language-2">plausible languages</a>,
    or the user's preferred languages, ordered by preference with the
    most preferred language first. [\[BCP47\]](#refsBCP47)

The same object must be returned until the user agent needs to return
different values, or values in a different order, or `emulatedLanguage`
is updated.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever the user agent needs to make the
[`navigator.languages`](#dom-navigator-languages) attribute of a
[`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object
`global` return a new set of language tags, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-a-global-task"
id="language-preferences:queue-a-global-task">queue a global task</a> on
the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
id="language-preferences:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM manipulation
task source</a> given `global` to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="language-preferences:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`languagechange`](#event-languagechange) at `global`, and wait until
that task begins to be executed before actually returning a new value.

</div>

To determine <span id="a-plausible-language" class="dfn">a plausible
language</span>, the user agent should bear in mind the following:

- <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
  id="language-preferences:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
  data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
  title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
  src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
  class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
  alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> Any information in this API
  that varies from user to user can be used to profile or identify the
  user.
- If the user is not using a service that obfuscates the user's point of
  origin (e.g. the Tor anonymity network), then the value that is least
  likely to distinguish the user from other users with similar origins
  (e.g. from the same IP address block) is the language used by the
  majority of such users. [\[TOR\]](#refsTOR)
- If the user is using an anonymizing service, then the value "`en-US`"
  is suggested; if all users of the service use that same value, that
  reduces the possibility of distinguishing the users from each other.

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="language-preferences:tracking-vector-2" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> To avoid introducing any more
fingerprinting vectors, user agents should use the same list for the
APIs defined in this function as for the HTTP
\`<a href="https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.accept-language"
data-x-internal="http-accept-language"><code
id="language-preferences:http-accept-language">Accept-Language</code></a>\`
header.

Returns false if the user agent is definitely offline (disconnected from
the network). Returns true if the user agent might be online.

The events [`online`](#event-online) and [`offline`](#event-offline) are
fired when the value of this attribute changes.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-navigator-online" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorOnLine" dfn-type="attribute">`onLine`</span> getter
steps are to return true if
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="navigator.online:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#relevant-settings-object"
id="navigator.online:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
object</a> <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#is-offline"
id="navigator.online:is-offline" data-x-internal="is-offline">is
offline</a> is false; otherwise false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the value that would be returned by the
[`navigator.onLine`](#dom-navigator-online) attribute of a
[`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope)
`global` changes from true to false, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-a-global-task"
id="navigator.online:queue-a-global-task">queue a global task</a> on the
<a href="#networking-task-source"
id="navigator.online:networking-task-source">networking task source</a>
given `global` to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="navigator.online:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`offline`](#event-offline) at `global`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

On the other hand, when the value that would be returned by the
[`navigator.onLine`](#dom-navigator-online) attribute of a
[`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope)
`global` changes from false to true, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-a-global-task"
id="navigator.online:queue-a-global-task-2">queue a global task</a> on
the <a href="#networking-task-source"
id="navigator.online:networking-task-source-2">networking task
source</a> given `global` to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="navigator.online:concept-event-fire-2"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`online`](#event-online) at the [`Window`](#window) or
[`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object.

</div>

This attribute is inherently unreliable. A computer can be connected to
a network without having Internet access.

<div class="example">

In this example, an indicator is updated as the browser goes online and
offline.

``` html
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
 <head>
  <title>Online status</title>
  <script>
   function updateIndicator() {
     document.getElementById('indicator').textContent = navigator.onLine ? 'online' : 'offline';
   }
  </script>
 </head>
 <body onload="updateIndicator()" ononline="updateIndicator()" onoffline="updateIndicator()">
  <p>The network is: <span id="indicator">(state unknown)</span>
 </body>
</html>
```

</div>

``` idl
interface mixin NavigatorContentUtils {
  [SecureContext] undefined registerProtocolHandler(DOMString scheme, USVString url);
  [SecureContext] undefined unregisterProtocolHandler(DOMString scheme, USVString url);
};
```

`window``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="custom-handlers:dom-navigator"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler"
id="dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler-dev"><code>registerProtocolHandler</code></a>`(``scheme``, ``url``)`

Registers a handler for `scheme` at `url`. For example, an online
telephone messaging service could register itself as a handler of the
<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5724#section-2"
data-x-internal="sms-protocol"><code
id="custom-handlers:sms-protocol">sms:</code></a> scheme, so that if the
user clicks on such a link, they are given the opportunity to use that
web site. [\[SMS\]](#refsSMS)

The string "`%s`" in `url` is used as a placeholder for where to put the
URL of the content to be handled.

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
id="custom-handlers:securityerror"
data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="custom-handlers:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if the user
agent blocks the registration (this might happen if trying to register
as a handler for "`http`", for instance).

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
id="custom-handlers:syntaxerror"
data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="custom-handlers:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a> if the
"`%s`" string is missing in `url`.

`window``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="custom-handlers:dom-navigator-2"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-unregisterprotocolhandler"

The <span id="dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorContentUtils"
dfn-type="method">`registerProtocolHandler(``scheme``, ``url``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  Let (`normalizedScheme`, `normalizedURLString`) be the result of
    running <a href="#normalize-protocol-handler-parameters"
    id="custom-handlers:normalize-protocol-handler-parameters">normalize
    protocol handler parameters</a> with `scheme`, `url`, and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="custom-handlers:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="custom-handlers:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
    object</a>.

2.  <a href="#in-parallel" id="custom-handlers:in-parallel">In parallel</a>:
    <span id="protocol-handler-registration" class="dfn"
    export="">register a protocol handler</span> for `normalizedScheme`
    and `normalizedURLString`. User agents may, within the constraints
    described, do whatever they like. A user agent could, for instance,
    prompt the user and offer the user the opportunity to add the site
    to a shortlist of handlers, or make the handlers their default, or
    cancel the request. User agents could also silently collect the
    information, providing it only when relevant to the user.

    User agents should keep track of which sites have registered
    handlers (even if the user has declined such registrations) so that
    the user is not repeatedly prompted with the same request.

    If the <a href="#registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"
    id="custom-handlers:registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"><code>registerProtocolHandler()</code>
    automation mode</a> of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-handlers:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-document-window">associated
    <code>Document</code></a> is not
    "<span id="rph-automation-mode-none" class="dfn">`none`</span>", the
    user agent should first verify that it is in an automation context
    (see <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#security"
    id="custom-handlers:webdriver&#39;s-security-considerations"
    data-x-internal="webdriver&#39;s-security-considerations">WebDriver's
    security considerations</a>). The user agent should then bypass the
    above communication of information and gathering of user consent,
    and instead do the following based on the value of the
    <a href="#registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"
    id="custom-handlers:registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode-2"><code>registerProtocolHandler()</code>
    automation mode</a>:

    "<span id="rph-automation-mode-auto-accept" class="dfn">`autoAccept`</span>"  
    Act as if the user has seen the registration details and accepted
    the request.

    "<span id="rph-automation-mode-auto-reject" class="dfn">`autoReject`</span>"  
    Act as if the user has seen the registration details and rejected
    the request.

    When the <span id="protocol-handler-invocation" class="dfn"
    lt="invoke a protocol
        handler" export="">user agent uses this handler</span> for a
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
    id="custom-handlers:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `inputURL`:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
        id="custom-handlers:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
        `inputURL`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
        id="custom-handlers:concept-url-scheme"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is
        `normalizedScheme`.

    2.  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-username"
        id="custom-handlers:set-the-username"
        data-x-internal="set-the-username">Set the username</a> given
        `inputURL` and the empty string.

    3.  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-password"
        id="custom-handlers:set-the-password"
        data-x-internal="set-the-password">Set the password</a> given
        `inputURL` and the empty string.

    4.  Let `inputURLString` be the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
        id="custom-handlers:concept-url-serializer"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
        `inputURL`.

    5.  Let `encodedURL` be the result of running
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#string-utf-8-percent-encode"
        id="custom-handlers:utf-8-percent-encode"
        data-x-internal="utf-8-percent-encode">UTF-8 percent-encode</a>
        on `inputURLString` using the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#component-percent-encode-set"
        id="custom-handlers:component-percent-encode-set"
        data-x-internal="component-percent-encode-set">component percent-encode
        set</a>.

    6.  Let `handlerURLString` be `normalizedURLString`.

    7.  Replace the first instance of "`%s`" in `handlerURLString` with
        `encodedURL`.

    8.  Let `resultURL` be the result of
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
        id="custom-handlers:url-parser" data-x-internal="url-parser">parsing</a>
        `handlerURLString`.

    9.  <a href="#navigate" id="custom-handlers:navigate">Navigate</a>
        an appropriate
        <a href="#navigable" id="custom-handlers:navigable">navigable</a>
        to `resultURL`.

    <div class="example">

    If the user had visited a site at `https://example.com/` that made
    the following call:

    ``` js
    navigator.registerProtocolHandler('web+soup', 'soup?url=%s')
    ```

    ...and then, much later, while visiting `https://www.example.net/`,
    clicked on a link such as:

    ``` html
    <a href="web+soup:chicken-kïwi">Download our Chicken Kïwi soup!</a>
    ```

    ...then the UA might navigate to the following URL:

        https://example.com/soup?url=web+soup:chicken-k%C3%AFwi

    This site could then do whatever it is that it does with soup
    (synthesize it and ship it to the user, or whatever).

    </div>

    This does not define when the handler is used. To some extent, the
    <a href="#navigate" id="custom-handlers:navigate-2">processing model for
    navigating across documents</a> defines some cases where it is
    relevant, but in general user agents may use this information
    wherever they would otherwise consider handing schemes to native
    plugins or helper applications.

</div>

The <span id="dom-navigator-unregisterprotocolhandler" class="dfn"
dfn-for="NavigatorContentUtils"
dfn-type="method">`unregisterProtocolHandler(``scheme``, ``url``)`</span>
method steps are:

1.  Let (`normalizedScheme`, `normalizedURLString`) be the result of
    running <a href="#normalize-protocol-handler-parameters"
    id="custom-handlers:normalize-protocol-handler-parameters-2">normalize
    protocol handler parameters</a> with `scheme`, `url`, and
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="custom-handlers:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="custom-handlers:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant settings
    object</a>.

2.  <a href="#in-parallel" id="custom-handlers:in-parallel-2">In
    parallel</a>: unregister the handler described by `normalizedScheme`
    and `normalizedURLString`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="normalize-protocol-handler-parameters" class="dfn"
export="">normalize protocol handler parameters</span>, given a string
`scheme`, a string `url`, and an <a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="custom-handlers:environment-settings-object">environment settings
object</a> `environment`, run these steps:

1.  Set `scheme` to `scheme`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase"
    id="custom-handlers:converted-to-ascii-lowercase"
    data-x-internal="converted-to-ascii-lowercase">converted to ASCII
    lowercase</a>.

2.  If `scheme` is neither a <a href="#safelisted-scheme"
    id="custom-handlers:safelisted-scheme">safelisted scheme</a> nor a
    string starting with "`web+`" followed by one or more
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lower-alpha"
    id="custom-handlers:lowercase-ascii-letters"
    data-x-internal="lowercase-ascii-letters">ASCII lower alphas</a>,
    then throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="custom-handlers:securityerror-3"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="custom-handlers:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

    This means that including a colon in `scheme` (as in "`mailto:`")
    will throw.

    The following schemes are the <span id="safelisted-scheme"
    class="dfn" export="">safelisted schemes</span>:

    - `bitcoin`
    - `ftp`
    - `ftps`
    - `geo`
    - `im`
    - `irc`
    - `ircs`
    - `magnet`
    - `mailto`
    - `matrix`
    - `mms`
    - `news`
    - `nntp`
    - `openpgp4fpr`
    - `sftp`
    - `sip`
    - `sms`
    - `smsto`
    - `ssh`
    - `tel`
    - `urn`
    - `webcal`
    - `wtai`
    - `xmpp`

    This list can be changed. If there are schemes that ought to be
    added, please send feedback.

3.  If `url` does not contain "`%s`", then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="custom-handlers:syntaxerror-3"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="custom-handlers:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  Let `urlRecord` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
    id="custom-handlers:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing a URL</a>
    given `url`, relative to `environment`.

5.  If `urlRecord` is failure, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="custom-handlers:syntaxerror-4"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="custom-handlers:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

    This is forcibly the case if the `%s` placeholder is in the host or
    port of the URL.

6.  If `urlRecord`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-url-scheme-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is not an
    <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
    id="custom-handlers:http(s)-scheme"
    data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a> or `urlRecord`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-url-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a> is not
    <a href="#same-origin" id="custom-handlers:same-origin">same origin</a>
    with `environment`'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>, then
    throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
    id="custom-handlers:securityerror-4"
    data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="custom-handlers:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="custom-handlers:assert-2" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    the result of <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-secure-contexts/#potentially-trustworthy-url"
    id="custom-handlers:is-url-potentially-trustworthy"
    data-x-internal="is-url-potentially-trustworthy">Is url potentially
    trustworthy?</a> given `urlRecord` is "`Potentially Trustworthy`".

    Because <a href="#normalize-protocol-handler-parameters"
    id="custom-handlers:normalize-protocol-handler-parameters-3">normalize
    protocol handler parameters</a> is run within a
    <a href="#secure-context" id="custom-handlers:secure-context">secure
    context</a>, this is implied by the
    <a href="#same-origin" id="custom-handlers:same-origin-2">same
    origin</a> condition.

8.  Return (`scheme`, `urlRecord`).

    The <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer"
    id="custom-handlers:concept-url-serializer-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-serializer">serialization</a> of
    `urlRecord` will by definition not be a
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string"
    id="custom-handlers:valid-url-string"
    data-x-internal="valid-url-string">valid URL string</a> as it
    includes the string "`%s`" which is not a valid component in a URL.

</div>

###### <span class="secno">8.9.1.4.1</span> Security and privacy<a href="#security-and-privacy" class="self-link"></a>

Custom scheme handlers can introduce a number of concerns, in particular
privacy concerns.

**Hijacking all web usage.** User agents should not allow schemes that
are key to its normal operation, such as an
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme"
id="security-and-privacy:http(s)-scheme"
data-x-internal="http(s)-scheme">HTTP(S) scheme</a>, to be rerouted
through third-party sites. This would allow a user's activities to be
trivially tracked, and would allow user information, even in secure
connections, to be collected.

**Hijacking defaults.** User agents are strongly urged to not
automatically change any defaults, as this could lead the user to send
data to remote hosts that the user is not expecting. New handlers
registering themselves should never automatically cause those sites to
be used.

**Registration spamming.** User agents should consider the possibility
that a site will attempt to register a large number of handlers,
possibly from multiple domains (e.g., by redirecting through a series of
pages each on a different domain, and each registering a handler for
`web+spam:` — analogous practices abusing other web browser features
have been used by pornography web sites for many years). User agents
should gracefully handle such hostile attempts, protecting the user.

**Hostile handler metadata.** User agents should protect against typical
attacks against strings embedded in their interface, for example
ensuring that markup or escape characters in such strings are not
executed, that null bytes are properly handled, that over-long strings
do not cause crashes or buffer overruns, and so forth.

**Leaking private data.** Web page authors may reference a custom scheme
handler using URL data considered private. They might do so with the
expectation that the user's choice of handler points to a page inside
the organization, ensuring that sensitive data will not be exposed to
third parties. However, a user may have registered a handler pointing to
an external site, resulting in a data leak to that third party.
Implementers might wish to consider allowing administrators to disable
custom handlers on certain subdomains, content types, or schemes.

**Interface interference.** User agents should be prepared to handle
intentionally long arguments to the methods. For example, if the user
interface exposed consists of an "accept" button and a "deny" button,
with the "accept" binding containing the name of the handler, it's
important that a long name not cause the "deny" button to be pushed off
the screen.

###### <span class="secno">8.9.1.4.2</span> <span id="rph-user-agent-automation" class="dfn">User agent automation</span><a href="#user-agent-automation" class="self-link"></a>

Each [`Document`](#document) has a
<span id="registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"
class="dfn">`registerProtocolHandler()` automation mode</span>. It
defaults to "[`none`](#rph-automation-mode-none)", but it also can be
either "[`autoAccept`](#rph-automation-mode-auto-accept)" or
"[`autoReject`](#rph-automation-mode-auto-reject)".

For the purposes of user agent automation and website testing, this
standard defines <span id="set-rph-registration-mode" class="dfn">Set
RPH Registration Mode</span> WebDriver
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-extension-commands"
id="user-agent-automation:extension-command"
data-x-internal="extension-command">extension command</a>. It instructs
the user agent to place a [`Document`](#document) into a mode where it
will automatically simulate a user either accepting or rejecting and
registration confirmation prompt dialog.

| HTTP Method | URI Template                                     |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| \``POST`\`  | `/session/{session id}/custom-handlers/set-mode` |

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-remote-end-steps"
id="user-agent-automation:remote-end-steps"
data-x-internal="remote-end-steps">remote end steps</a> are:

1.  If `parameters` is not a JSON Object, return a
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-errors"
    id="user-agent-automation:webdriver-error"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-error">WebDriver error</a> with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-error-code"
    id="user-agent-automation:webdriver-error-code"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-error-code">WebDriver error code</a>
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-invalid-argument"
    id="user-agent-automation:invalid-argument"
    data-x-internal="invalid-argument">invalid argument</a>.

2.  Let `mode` be the result of
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-getting-properties"
    id="user-agent-automation:getting-a-property"
    data-x-internal="getting-a-property">getting a property</a> named
    "`mode`" from `parameters`.

3.  If `mode` is not "[`autoAccept`](#rph-automation-mode-auto-accept)",
    "[`autoReject`](#rph-automation-mode-auto-reject)", or
    "[`none`](#rph-automation-mode-none)", return a
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-errors"
    id="user-agent-automation:webdriver-error-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-error">WebDriver error</a> with
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-error-code"
    id="user-agent-automation:webdriver-error-code-2"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-error-code">WebDriver error code</a>
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-invalid-argument"
    id="user-agent-automation:invalid-argument-2"
    data-x-internal="invalid-argument">invalid argument</a>.

4.  Let `document` be the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-current-browsing-context"
    id="user-agent-automation:webdriver-current-browsing-context"
    data-x-internal="webdriver-current-browsing-context">current browsing
    context</a>'s <a href="#active-document"
    id="user-agent-automation:active-document">active document</a>.

5.  Set `document`'s
    <a href="#registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"
    id="user-agent-automation:registerprotocolhandler()-automation-mode"><code>registerProtocolHandler()</code>
    automation mode</a> to `mode`.

6.  Return <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-success"
    id="user-agent-automation:success-value"
    data-x-internal="success-value">success</a> with data null.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">8.9.1.6</span> PDF viewing support<a href="#pdf-viewing-support" class="self-link"></a>

`window``.`<a href="#dom-navigator"
id="pdf-viewing-support:dom-navigator"><code>navigator</code></a>`.`<a href="#dom-navigator-pdfviewerenabled"
id="dom-navigator-pdfviewerenabled-dev"><code>pdfViewerEnabled</code></a>  
Returns true if the user agent supports inline viewing of PDF files when
<a href="#navigate" id="pdf-viewing-support:navigate">navigating</a> to
them, or false otherwise. In the latter case, PDF files will be handled
by <a href="#hand-off-to-external-software"
id="pdf-viewing-support:hand-off-to-external-software">external
software</a>.

``` idl
interface mixin NavigatorPlugins {
  [SameObject] readonly attribute PluginArray plugins;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute MimeTypeArray mimeTypes;
  boolean javaEnabled();
  readonly attribute boolean pdfViewerEnabled;
};

[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]
interface PluginArray {
  undefined refresh();
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter Plugin? item(unsigned long index);
  getter Plugin? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]
interface MimeTypeArray {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter MimeType? item(unsigned long index);
  getter MimeType? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]
interface Plugin {
  readonly attribute DOMString name;
  readonly attribute DOMString description;
  readonly attribute DOMString filename;
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter MimeType? item(unsigned long index);
  getter MimeType? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface MimeType {
  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  readonly attribute DOMString description;
  readonly attribute DOMString suffixes;
  readonly attribute Plugin enabledPlugin;
};
```

Although these days detecting PDF viewer support can be done via
[`navigator.pdfViewerEnabled`](#dom-navigator-pdfviewerenabled), for
historical reasons, there are a number of complex and intertwined
interfaces that provide the same capability, which legacy code relies
on. This section specifies both the simple modern variant and the
complicated historical one.

<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="pdf-viewing-support:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> Each user agent has a
<span id="pdf-viewer-supported" class="dfn">PDF viewer supported</span>
boolean, whose value is
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="pdf-viewing-support:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> (and
might vary according to user preferences).

This value also impacts the
<a href="#navigate" id="pdf-viewing-support:navigate-2">navigation</a>
processing model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each [`Window`](#window) object has a
<span id="pdf-viewer-plugin-objects" class="dfn">PDF viewer plugin
objects</span> list. If the user agent's <a href="#pdf-viewer-supported"
id="pdf-viewing-support:pdf-viewer-supported">PDF viewer supported</a>
is false, then it is the empty list. Otherwise, it is a list containing
five [`Plugin`](#dom-plugin) objects, whose
<a href="#concept-plugin-name"
id="pdf-viewing-support:concept-plugin-name">names</a> are,
respectively:

0.  "`PDF Viewer`"
1.  "`Chrome PDF Viewer`"
2.  "`Chromium PDF Viewer`"
3.  "`Microsoft Edge PDF Viewer`"
4.  "`WebKit built-in PDF`"

The values of the above list form the <span id="pdf-viewer-plugin-names"
class="dfn">PDF viewer plugin names</span> list.

These names were chosen based on evidence of what websites historically
search for, and thus what is necessary for user agents to expose in
order to maintain compatibility with existing content. They are ordered
alphabetically. The "`PDF Viewer`" name was then inserted in the 0th
position so that the [`enabledPlugin`](#dom-mimetype-enabledplugin)
getter could point to a generic plugin name.

Each [`Window`](#window) object has a
<span id="pdf-viewer-mime-type-objects" class="dfn">PDF viewer mime type
objects</span> list. If the user agent's <a href="#pdf-viewer-supported"
id="pdf-viewing-support:pdf-viewer-supported-2">PDF viewer supported</a>
is false, then it is the empty list. Otherwise, it is a list containing
two [`MimeType`](#mimetype) objects, whose
<a href="#concept-mimetype-type"
id="pdf-viewing-support:concept-mimetype-type">types</a> are,
respectively:

0.  "`application/pdf`"
1.  "`text/pdf`"

The values of the above list form the <span id="pdf-viewer-mime-types"
class="dfn">PDF viewer mime types</span> list.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each [`NavigatorPlugins`](#navigatorplugins) object has a
<span id="plugins-array" class="dfn">plugins array</span>, which is a
new [`PluginArray`](#pluginarray), and a <span id="mime-types-array"
class="dfn">mime types array</span>, which is a new
[`MimeTypeArray`](#mimetypearray).

``` idl
typedef (Uint8ClampedArray or Float16Array) ImageDataArray;

enum ImageDataPixelFormat { "rgba-unorm8", "rgba-float16" };

dictionary ImageDataSettings {
  PredefinedColorSpace colorSpace;
  ImageDataPixelFormat pixelFormat = "rgba-unorm8";
};

[Exposed=(Window,Worker),
 Serializable]
interface ImageData {
  constructor(unsigned long sw, unsigned long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});
  constructor(ImageDataArray data, unsigned long sw, optional unsigned long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});

  readonly attribute unsigned long width;
  readonly attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute ImageDataArray data;
  readonly attribute ImageDataPixelFormat pixelFormat;
  readonly attribute PredefinedColorSpace colorSpace;
};
```

An [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object
<span id="concept-imagedata-bitmap-representation" class="dfn">
represents a rectanglar bitmap</span> with width equal to the
` `[`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute and height equal to the
[`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute. The pixel values of this
bitmap are stored in the ` `[`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute in
left-to-right order, row by row from top to bottom, starting with 0 for
the top left pixel, with the order and numerical representation of the
color components of each pixel determined by the
[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedata-pixelformat) attribute. The color space
of the pixel values of the bitmap is determined by the
[`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace) attribute.

id="dom-imagedata-dev"><code>ImageData</code></a>`(``sw``, ``sh`` [, ``settings``])`

and the color space indicated by `settings`. All the pixels in the
returned object are

`imageData`` = new `<a href="#dom-imagedata-with-data"
id="dom-imagedata-with-data-dev"><code>ImageData</code></a>`(``data``, ``sw`` [, ``sh`` [, ``settings`` ] ])`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object using the data provided in
the [`ImageDataArray`](#imagedataarray) argument, interpreted using the
given dimensions and the color space indicated by `settings`.

The byte length of the data needs to be a multiple of the number of
bytes per pixel times the given width. If the height is provided as
well, then the length needs to be exactly the number of bytes per pixel
times the width times the height.

Throws an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
id="the-imagedata-interface:indexsizeerror-2"
data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a> if
the given data and dimensions can't be interpreted consistently, or if
either dimension is zero.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-imagedata" class="dfn" dfn-for="ImageData"
dfn-type="constructor">`new ImageData(``sw``, ``sh``, ``settings``)`</span>
constructor steps are:

1.  If one or both of `sw` and `sh` are zero, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:indexsizeerror-3"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-3">DOMException</code></a>.

2.  <a href="#initialize-an-imagedata-object"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:initialize-an-imagedata-object">Initialize</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    given `sw`, `sh`, and `settings`.

3.  Initialize the image data of
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    to <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:transparent-black-2"
    data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-imagedata-with-data" class="dfn" dfn-for="ImageData"
dfn-type="constructor">`new ImageData(``data``, ``sw``, ``sh``, ``settings``)`</span>
constructor steps are:

1.  Let `bytesPerPixel` be 4 if
    `settings`\["[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)"\]
    is "<a href="#dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8-3">rgba-unorm8</a>";
    otherwise 8.

2.  Let `length` be the
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#buffersource-byte-length"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:buffer-source-byte-length"
    data-x-internal="buffer-source-byte-length">buffer source byte
    length</a> of `data`.

3.  If `length` is not a nonzero integral multiple of `bytesPerPixel`,
    then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:invalidstateerror"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-4">DOMException</code></a>.

4.  Let `length` be `length` divided by `bytesPerPixel`.

5.  If `length` is not an integral multiple of `sw`, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:indexsizeerror-4"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-5">DOMException</code></a>.

    At this step, the length is guaranteed to be greater than zero
    (otherwise the second step above would have aborted the steps), so
    if `sw` is zero, this step will throw the exception and return.

6.  Let `height` be `length` divided by `sw`.

7.  If `sh` was given and its value is not equal to `height`, then throw
    an <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:indexsizeerror-5"
    data-x-internal="indexsizeerror">"<code>IndexSizeError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-6">DOMException</code></a>.

8.  <a href="#initialize-an-imagedata-object"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:initialize-an-imagedata-object-2">Initialize</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:this-3" data-x-internal="this">this</a>
    given `sw`, `sh`, `settings`, and
    *<a href="#initialize-imagedata-source"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:initialize-imagedata-source">source</a>*
    set to `data`.

    This step does not set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:this-4" data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    data to a copy of `data`. It sets it to the actual
    [`ImageDataArray`](#imagedataarray) object passed as `data`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="initialize-an-imagedata-object" class="dfn">initialize an
`ImageData` object</span> `imageData`, given a positive integer number
of pixels per row `pixelsPerRow`, a positive integer number of rows
`rows`, an [`ImageDataSettings`](#imagedatasettings) `settings`, an
optional [`ImageDataArray`](#imagedataarray)
<span id="initialize-imagedata-source" class="dfn">`source`</span>, and
an optional [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#predefinedcolorspace)
<span id="initialize-imagedata-defaultcolorspace"
class="dfn">`defaultColorSpace`</span>:

1.  If `source` was given:

    1.  If
        `settings`\["[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)"\]
        equals "<a href="#dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8-4">rgba-unorm8</a>"
        and `source` is not a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray"
        data-x-internal="idl-uint8clampedarray"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-uint8clampedarray-2">Uint8ClampedArray</code></a>,
        then throw an
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:invalidstateerror-2"
        data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-7">DOMException</code></a>.

    2.  If
        `settings`\["[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)"\]
        is "<a href="#dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-float16"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-float16-2">rgba-float16</a>"
        and `source` is not a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array"
        data-x-internal="idl-float16array"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-float16array-2">Float16Array</code></a>,
        then throw an
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:invalidstateerror-3"
        data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:domexception-8">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  Initialize the <span id="dom-imagedata-data" class="dfn"
        dfn-for="ImageData" dfn-type="attribute">`data`</span> attribute
        of `imageData` to `source`.

2.  Otherwise (`source` was not given):

    1.  If
        `settings`\["[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)"\]
        is "<a href="#dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8-5">rgba-unorm8</a>",
        then initialize the [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute of
        `imageData` to a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray"
        data-x-internal="idl-uint8clampedarray"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-uint8clampedarray-3">Uint8ClampedArray</code></a>
        object. The
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray"
        data-x-internal="idl-uint8clampedarray"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-uint8clampedarray-4">Uint8ClampedArray</code></a>
        object must use a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
        data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-arraybuffer">ArrayBuffer</code></a>
        for its storage, and must have a zero byte offset and byte
        length equal to the length of its storage, in bytes. The storage
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
        data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-arraybuffer-2">ArrayBuffer</code></a>
        must have a length of 4 × `rows` × `pixelsPerRow` bytes.

    2.  Otherwise, if
        `settings`\["[`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat)"\]
        is "<a href="#dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8"
        id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8-6">rgba-float16</a>",
        then initialize the [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute of
        `imageData` to a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array"
        data-x-internal="idl-float16array"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-float16array-3">Float16Array</code></a>
        object. The
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array"
        data-x-internal="idl-float16array"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-float16array-4">Float16Array</code></a>
        object must use a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
        data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-arraybuffer-3">ArrayBuffer</code></a>
        for its storage, and must have a zero byte offset and byte
        length equal to the length of its storage, in bytes. The storage
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
        data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-arraybuffer-4">ArrayBuffer</code></a>
        must have a length of 8 × `rows` × `pixelsPerRow` bytes.

    3.  If the storage
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
        data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-arraybuffer-5">ArrayBuffer</code></a>
        could not be allocated, then rethrow the <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror"
        data-x-internal="js-rangeerror"><code
        id="the-imagedata-interface:js-rangeerror">RangeError</code></a>
        thrown by JavaScript, and return.

3.  Initialize the <span id="dom-imagedata-width" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="ImageData" dfn-type="attribute">`width`</span> attribute of
    `imageData` to `pixelsPerRow`.

4.  Initialize the <span id="dom-imagedata-height" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="ImageData" dfn-type="attribute">`height`</span> attribute
    of `imageData` to `rows`.

5.  Initialize the <span id="dom-imagedata-pixelformat" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="ImageData" dfn-type="attribute">`pixelFormat`</span>
    attribute of `imageData` to
    `settings`\["<span id="dom-imagedatasettings-pixelformat"
    class="dfn" dfn-for="ImageDataSettings"
    dfn-type="dict-member">`pixelFormat`</span>"\].

6.  If `settings`\["[`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedatasettings-colorspace)"\]
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:map-exists"
    data-x-internal="map-exists">exists</a>, then initialize the
    <span id="dom-imagedata-colorspace" class="dfn" dfn-for="ImageData"
    dfn-type="attribute">`colorSpace`</span> attribute of `imageData` to
    `settings`\["<span id="dom-imagedatasettings-colorspace" class="dfn"
    dfn-for="ImageDataSettings"
    dfn-type="dict-member">`colorSpace`</span>"\].

7.  Otherwise, if `defaultColorSpace` was given, then initialize the
    [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace) attribute of `imageData`
    to `defaultColorSpace`.

8.  Otherwise, initialize the [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace)
    attribute of `imageData` to
    "<a href="#dom-predefinedcolorspace-srgb"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:dom-predefinedcolorspace-srgb-2">srgb</a>".

</div>

<div algorithm="">

[`ImageData`](#imagedata) objects are <a href="#serializable-objects"
id="the-imagedata-interface:serializable-objects">serializable
objects</a>. Their <a href="#serialization-steps"
id="the-imagedata-interface:serialization-steps">serialization steps</a>,
given `value` and `serialized`, are:

1.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Data\]\] to the <a href="#sub-serialization"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:sub-serialization">sub-serialization</a>
    of the value of `value`'s [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute.

2.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Width\]\] to the value of `value`'s
    [`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute.

3.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Height\]\] to the value of `value`'s
    [`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute.

4.  Set `serialized`.\[\[ColorSpace\]\] to the value of `value`'s
    [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace) attribute.

5.  Set `serialized`.\[\[PixelFormat\]\] to the value of `value`'s
    [`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedata-pixelformat) attribute.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Their <a href="#deserialization-steps"
id="the-imagedata-interface:deserialization-steps">deserialization
steps</a>, given `serialized`, `value`, and `targetRealm`, are:

1.  Initialize `value`'s [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute to the
    <a href="#sub-deserialization"
    id="the-imagedata-interface:sub-deserialization">sub-deserialization</a>
    of `serialized`.\[\[Data\]\].

2.  Initialize `value`'s [`width`](#dom-imagedata-width) attribute to
    `serialized`.\[\[Width\]\].

3.  Initialize `value`'s [`height`](#dom-imagedata-height) attribute to
    `serialized`.\[\[Height\]\].

4.  Initialize `value`'s [`colorSpace`](#dom-imagedata-colorspace)
    attribute to `serialized`.\[\[ColorSpace\]\].

5.  Initialize `value`'s [`pixelFormat`](#dom-imagedata-pixelformat)
    attribute to `serialized`.\[\[PixelFormat\]\].

</div>

The [`ImageDataPixelFormat`](#imagedatapixelformat) enumeration is used
to specify type of the [`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute of an
[`ImageData`](#imagedata) and the arrangement and numerical
representation of the color components for each pixel.

The "<span id="dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-unorm8" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ImageDataPixelFormat"
dfn-type="enum-value">`rgba-unorm8`</span>" value indicates that the
[`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute of an [`ImageData`](#imagedata)
must be of type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray"
id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-uint8clampedarray-5"
data-x-internal="idl-uint8clampedarray">Uint8ClampedArray</a>. The color
components of each pixel must be stored in four sequential elements in
the order of red, green, blue, and then alpha. Each element represents
the 8-bit unsigned normalized value for that component.

The "<span id="dom-imagedatapixelformat-rgba-float16" class="dfn"
dfn-for="ImageDataPixelFormat"
dfn-type="enum-value">`rgba-float16`</span>" value indicates that the
[`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute of an [`ImageData`](#imagedata)
must be of type
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array"
id="the-imagedata-interface:idl-float16array-5"
data-x-internal="idl-float16array">Float16Array</a>. The color
components of each pixel must be stored in four sequential elements in
the order of red, green, blue, and then alpha. Each element represents
the value for that component.

#### <span class="secno">8.10.2</span> The [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) interface<a href="#the-imagebitmap-interface" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

[ImageBitmap](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ImageBitmap "The ImageBitmap interface represents a bitmap image which can be drawn to a <canvas> without undue latency. It can be created from a variety of source objects using the createImageBitmap() factory method. ImageBitmap provides an asynchronous and resource efficient pathway to prepare textures for rendering in WebGL.")

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker), Serializable, Transferable]
interface ImageBitmap {
  readonly attribute unsigned long width;
  readonly attribute unsigned long height;
  undefined close();
};

typedef (CanvasImageSource or
         Blob or
         ImageData) ImageBitmapSource;

enum ImageOrientation { "from-image", "flipY" };
enum PremultiplyAlpha { "none", "premultiply", "default" };
enum ColorSpaceConversion { "none", "default" };
enum ResizeQuality { "pixelated", "low", "medium", "high" };

dictionary ImageBitmapOptions {
  ImageOrientation imageOrientation = "from-image";
  PremultiplyAlpha premultiplyAlpha = "default";
  ColorSpaceConversion colorSpaceConversion = "default";
  [EnforceRange] unsigned long resizeWidth;
  [EnforceRange] unsigned long resizeHeight;
  ResizeQuality resizeQuality = "low";
};
```

An [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object represents a bitmap image that
can be painted to a canvas without undue latency.

The exact judgement of what is undue latency of this is left up to the
implementer, but in general if making use of the bitmap requires network
I/O, or even local disk I/O, then the latency is probably undue; whereas
if it only requires a blocking read from a GPU or system RAM, the
latency is probably acceptable.

`promise`` = self.`<a href="#dom-createimagebitmap"
id="dom-createimagebitmap-dev"><code>createImageBitmap</code></a>`(``image`` [, ``options`` ])`

The method exists on the global scope in both windows and workers. It accepts a variety of different image sources, and returns a Promise which resolves to an ImageBitmap.")

`promise`` = self.`<a href="#dom-createimagebitmap"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:dom-createimagebitmap"><code>createImageBitmap</code></a>`(``image``, ``sx``, ``sy``, ``sw``, ``sh`` [, ``options`` ])`

Takes `image`, which can be an [`img`](#the-img-element) element, an
<a href="https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/embedded.html#ImageElement"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:svg-image" data-x-internal="svg-image">SVG
<code>image</code></a> element, a [`video`](#the-video-element) element,
a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element, a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob"
data-x-internal="blob"><code
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:blob-2">Blob</code></a> object, an
[`ImageData`](#imagedata) object, or another
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object, and returns a promise that is
resolved when a new [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) is created.

If no [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object can be constructed, for
example because the provided `image` data is not actually an image, then
the promise is rejected instead.

If `sx`, `sy`, `sw`, and `sh` arguments are provided, the source image
is cropped to the given pixels, with any pixels missing in the original
replaced by
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>. These
coordinates are in the source image's pixel coordinate space, *not* in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>.

If `options` is provided, the [`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object's
bitmap data is modified according to `options`. For example, if the
[`premultiplyAlpha`](#dom-imagebitmapoptions-premultiplyalpha) option is
set to "[`premultiply`](#dom-premultiplyalpha-premultiply)", the
<a href="#concept-imagebitmap-bitmap-data"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:concept-imagebitmap-bitmap-data">bitmap
data</a>'s non-alpha color components are
<a href="#concept-premultiplied-alpha"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:concept-premultiplied-alpha">premultiplied
by the alpha component</a>.

Rejects the promise with an
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:invalidstateerror"
data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if
the source image is not in a valid state (e.g., an
[`img`](#the-img-element) element that hasn't loaded successfully, an
[`ImageBitmap`](#imagebitmap) object whose <a href="#detached"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:detached">[[Detached]]</a> internal slot
value is true, an [`ImageData`](#imagedata) object whose
[`data`](#dom-imagedata-data) attribute value's
\[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot is detached, or a
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob"
data-x-internal="blob"><code
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:blob-3">Blob</code></a> whose data cannot
be interpreted as a bitmap image).

Rejects the promise with a
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:securityerror"
data-x-internal="securityerror">"<code>SecurityError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a> if
the script is not allowed to access the image data of the source image
(e.g. a [`video`](#the-video-element) that is
<a href="#cors-cross-origin"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:cors-cross-origin">CORS-cross-origin</a>,
or a [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) being drawn on by a script in a
worker from another <a href="#concept-origin"
id="the-imagebitmap-interface:concept-origin">origin</a>).

`imageBitmap``.`<a href="#dom-imagebitmap-close"
