#### <span class="secno">9.2.3</span> <span id="processing-model-9"></span>Processing model<a href="#sse-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="announce-the-connection"
class="dfn">announce the connection</span>, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-a-task" id="sse-processing-model:queue-a-task">queue a
task</a> which, if the [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate)
attribute is set to a value other than
[`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed), sets the
[`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute to
[`OPEN`](#dom-eventsource-open) and
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fires an event</a> named
[`open`](#event-open) at the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="reestablish-the-connection"
class="dfn">reestablish the connection</span>, the user agent must run
the following steps. These steps are run
<a href="#in-parallel" id="sse-processing-model:in-parallel">in
parallel</a>, not as part of a
<a href="#concept-task" id="sse-processing-model:concept-task">task</a>.
(The tasks that it queues, of course, are run like normal tasks and not
themselves
<a href="#in-parallel" id="sse-processing-model:in-parallel-2">in
parallel</a>.)

1.  <a href="#queue-a-task" id="sse-processing-model:queue-a-task-2">Queue a
    task</a> to run the following steps:

    1.  If the [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute is
        set to [`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed), abort the task.

    2.  Set the [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute to
        [`CONNECTING`](#dom-eventsource-connecting).

    3.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
        [`error`](#event-error) at the [`EventSource`](#eventsource)
        object.

2.  Wait a delay equal to the reconnection time of the event source.

3.  Optionally, wait some more. In particular, if the previous attempt
    failed, then user agents might introduce an exponential backoff
    delay to avoid overloading a potentially already overloaded server.
    Alternatively, if the operating system has reported that there is no
    network connectivity, user agents might wait for the operating
    system to announce that the network connection has returned before
    retrying.

4.  Wait until the aforementioned task has run, if it has not yet run.

5.  <a href="#queue-a-task" id="sse-processing-model:queue-a-task-3">Queue a
    task</a> to run the following steps:

    1.  If the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
        [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute is not set
        to [`CONNECTING`](#dom-eventsource-connecting), then return.

    2.  Let `request` be the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
        <a href="#concept-event-stream-request"
        id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-stream-request">request</a>.

    3.  If the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
        <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
        id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-stream-last-event-id">last event
        ID string</a> is not the empty string, then:

        1.  Let `lastEventIDValue` be the [`EventSource`](#eventsource)
            object's <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
            id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-stream-last-event-id-2">last
            event ID string</a>,
            <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode"
            id="sse-processing-model:utf-8-encode"
            data-x-internal="utf-8-encode">encoded as UTF-8</a>.

        2.  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-set"
            id="sse-processing-model:concept-header-list-set"
            data-x-internal="concept-header-list-set">Set</a>
            (\`[`Last-Event-ID`](#last-event-id)\`, `lastEventIDValue`)
            in `request`'s
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-header-list"
            id="sse-processing-model:concept-request-header-list"
            data-x-internal="concept-request-header-list">header list</a>.

    4.  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
        id="sse-processing-model:concept-fetch"
        data-x-internal="concept-fetch">Fetch</a> `request` and process
        the response obtained in this fashion, if any, as described
        earlier in this section.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="fail-the-connection" class="dfn">fail
the connection</span>, the user agent must
<a href="#queue-a-task" id="sse-processing-model:queue-a-task-4">queue a
task</a> which, if the [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate)
attribute is set to a value other than
[`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed), sets the
[`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute to
[`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed) and
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="sse-processing-model:concept-event-fire-3"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fires an event</a> named
[`error`](#event-error) at the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object.
**Once the user agent has <a href="#fail-the-connection"
id="sse-processing-model:fail-the-connection">failed the connection</a>,
it does *not* attempt to reconnect.**

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <a href="#task-source" id="sse-processing-model:task-source">task
source</a> for any <a href="#concept-task"
id="sse-processing-model:concept-task-2">tasks</a> that are
<a href="#queue-a-task"
id="sse-processing-model:queue-a-task-5">queued</a> by
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) objects is the
<span id="remote-event-task-source" class="dfn">remote event task
source</span>.

#### <span class="secno">9.2.4</span> The \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#last-event-id)\` header<a href="#the-last-event-id-header" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="last-event-id" class="dfn"
dfn-type="http-header">`Last-Event-ID`</span>\` HTTP request header
reports an [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
<a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
id="the-last-event-id-header:concept-event-stream-last-event-id">last
event ID string</a> to the server when the user agent is to
<a href="#reestablish-the-connection"
id="the-last-event-id-header:reestablish-the-connection">reestablish the
connection</a>.

See [whatwg/html issue
\#7363](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7363) to define the value
space better. It is essentially any UTF-8 encoded string, that does not
contain U+0000 NULL, U+000A LF, or U+000D CR.

#### <span class="secno">9.2.5</span> Parsing an event stream<a href="#parsing-an-event-stream" class="self-link"></a>

This event stream format's
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="parsing-an-event-stream:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
type</a> is [`text/event-stream`](#text/event-stream).

The event stream format is as described by the `stream` production of
the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode.
[\[ABNF\]](#refsABNF)

``` abnf
stream        = [ bom ] *event
event         = *( comment / field ) end-of-line
comment       = colon *any-char end-of-line
field         = 1*name-char [ colon [ space ] *any-char ] end-of-line
end-of-line   = ( cr lf / cr / lf )

; characters
lf            = %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
cr            = %x000D ; U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)
space         = %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
colon         = %x003A ; U+003A COLON (:)
bom           = %xFEFF ; U+FEFF BYTE ORDER MARK
name-char     = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-000C / %x000E-0039 / %x003B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+003A COLON (:)
any-char      = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-000C / %x000E-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)
```

Event streams in this format must always be encoded as UTF-8.
[\[ENCODING\]](#refsENCODING)

Lines must be separated by either a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE
FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or
a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character.

Since connections established to remote servers for such resources are
expected to be long-lived, UAs should ensure that appropriate buffering
is used. In particular, while line buffering with lines are defined to
end with a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character is safe, block
buffering or line buffering with different expected line endings can
cause delays in event dispatch.

#### <span class="secno">9.2.6</span> Interpreting an event stream<a href="#event-stream-interpretation" class="self-link"></a>

Streams must be decoded using the
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode"
id="event-stream-interpretation:utf-8-decode"
data-x-internal="utf-8-decode">UTF-8 decode</a> algorithm.

The <a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode"
id="event-stream-interpretation:utf-8-decode-2"
data-x-internal="utf-8-decode">UTF-8 decode</a> algorithm strips one
leading UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), if any.

The stream must then be parsed by reading everything line by line, with
a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a
single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character not preceded by a U+000D CARRIAGE
RETURN (CR) character, and a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)
character not followed by a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character being the
ways in which a line can end.

<div var-scope="">

When a stream is parsed, a `data` buffer, an `event type` buffer, and a
`last event ID` buffer must be associated with it. They must be
initialized to the empty string.

<div algorithm="">

Lines must be processed, in the order they are received, as follows:

If the line is empty (a blank line)  
<a href="#dispatchMessage"
id="event-stream-interpretation:dispatchMessage">Dispatch the event</a>,
as defined below.

If the line starts with a U+003A COLON character (:)  
Ignore the line.

If the line contains a U+003A COLON character (:)  
Collect the characters on the line before the first U+003A COLON
character (:), and let `field` be that string.

Collect the characters on the line after the first U+003A COLON
character (:), and let `value` be that string. If `value` starts with a
U+0020 SPACE character, remove it from `value`.

[Process the field](#processField) using the steps described below,
using `field` as the field name and `value` as the field value.

Otherwise, the string is not empty but does not contain a U+003A COLON character (:)  
[Process the field](#processField) using the steps described below,
using the whole line as the field name, and the empty string as the
field value.

</div>

Once the end of the file is reached, any pending data must be discarded.
(If the file ends in the middle of an event, before the final empty
line, the incomplete event is not dispatched.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The steps to <span class="dfn">process the field</span> given a field
name and a field value depend on the field name, as given in the
following list. Field names must be compared literally, with no case
folding performed.

If the field name is "event"  
Set the `event type` buffer to the field value.

If the field name is "data"  
Append the field value to the `data` buffer, then append a single U+000A
LINE FEED (LF) character to the `data` buffer.

If the field name is "id"  
If the field value does not contain U+0000 NULL, then set the
`last event ID` buffer to the field value. Otherwise, ignore the field.

If the field name is "retry"  
If the field value consists of only
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit"
id="event-stream-interpretation:ascii-digits"
data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a>, then interpret the
field value as an integer in base ten, and set the event stream's
<a href="#concept-event-stream-reconnection-time"
id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-stream-reconnection-time">reconnection
time</a> to that integer. Otherwise, ignore the field.

Otherwise  
The field is ignored.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is required to <span id="dispatchMessage"
class="dfn">dispatch the event</span>, the user agent must process the
`data` buffer, the `event type` buffer, and the `last event ID` buffer
using steps appropriate for the user agent.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

For web browsers, the appropriate steps to <a href="#dispatchMessage"
id="event-stream-interpretation:dispatchMessage-2">dispatch the
event</a> are as follows:

1.  Set the <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-stream-last-event-id">last
    event ID string</a> of the event source to the value of the
    `last event ID` buffer. The buffer does not get reset, so the
    <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-stream-last-event-id-2">last
    event ID string</a> of the event source remains set to this value
    until the next time it is set by the server.

2.  If the `data` buffer is an empty string, set the `data` buffer and
    the `event type` buffer to the empty string and return.

3.  If the `data` buffer's last character is a U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
    character, then remove the last character from the `data` buffer.

4.  Let `event` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-create"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:creating-an-event"
    data-x-internal="creating-an-event">creating an event</a> using
    [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), in the
    <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-relevant-realm">relevant
    realm</a> of the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object.

5.  Initialize `event`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    data-x-internal="dom-event-type"><code
    id="event-stream-interpretation:dom-event-type">type</code></a>
    attribute to "[`message`](#event-message)", its
    [`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute to `data`, its
    <a href="#concept-messageevent-origin"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-messageevent-origin">origin</a>
    to the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-url-origin"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a> of the event
    stream's final URL (i.e., the URL after redirects), and its
    [`lastEventId`](#dom-messageevent-lasteventid) attribute to the
    <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-stream-last-event-id-3">last
    event ID string</a> of the event source.

6.  If the `event type` buffer has a value other than the empty string,
    change the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-type"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-type"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-type">type</a> of the newly created
    event to equal the value of the `event type` buffer.

7.  Set the `data` buffer and the `event type` buffer to the empty
    string.

8.  <a href="#queue-a-task"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:queue-a-task">Queue a task</a>
    which, if the [`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute
    is set to a value other than [`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed),
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch"
    id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-dispatch"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-dispatch">dispatches</a> the newly
    created event at the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object.

If an event doesn't have an "id" field, but an earlier event did set the
event source's <a href="#concept-event-stream-last-event-id"
id="event-stream-interpretation:concept-event-stream-last-event-id-4">last
event ID string</a>, then the event's
[`lastEventId`](#dom-messageevent-lasteventid) field will be set to the
value of whatever the last seen "id" field was.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

For other user agents, the appropriate steps to
<a href="#dispatchMessage"
id="event-stream-interpretation:dispatchMessage-3">dispatch the
event</a> are implementation dependent, but at a minimum they must set
the `data` and `event type` buffers to the empty string before
returning.

</div>

</div>

<div class="example">

The following event stream, once followed by a blank line:

    data: YHOO
    data: +2
    data: 10

...would cause an event [`message`](#event-message) with the interface
[`MessageEvent`](#messageevent) to be dispatched on the
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) object. The event's
[`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute would contain the string
"`YHOO\n+2\n10`" (where "`\n`" represents a newline).

This could be used as follows:

``` js
var stocks = new EventSource("https://stocks.example.com/ticker.php");
stocks.onmessage = function (event) {
  var data = event.data.split('\n');
  updateStocks(data[0], data[1], data[2]);
};
```

...where `updateStocks()` is a function defined as:

``` js
function updateStocks(symbol, delta, value) { ... }
```

...or some such.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following stream contains four blocks. The first block has just a
comment, and will fire nothing. The second block has two fields with
names "data" and "id" respectively; an event will be fired for this
block, with the data "first event", and will then set the last event ID
to "1" so that if the connection died between this block and the next,
the server would be sent a \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#last-event-id)\` header
with the value \``1`\`. The third block fires an event with data "second
event", and also has an "id" field, this time with no value, which
resets the last event ID to the empty string (meaning no
\`[`Last-Event-ID`](#last-event-id)\` header will now be sent in the
event of a reconnection being attempted). Finally, the last block just
fires an event with the data " third event" (with a single leading space
character). Note that the last still has to end with a blank line, the
end of the stream is not enough to trigger the dispatch of the last
event.

    : test stream

    data: first event
    id: 1

    data:second event
    id

    data:  third event

</div>

<div class="example">

The following stream fires two events:

    data

    data
    data

    data:

The first block fires events with the data set to the empty string, as
would the last block if it was followed by a blank line. The middle
block fires an event with the data set to a single newline character.
The last block is discarded because it is not followed by a blank line.

</div>

<div class="example">

The following stream fires two identical events:

    data:test

    data: test

This is because the space after the colon is ignored if present.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">9.2.7</span> Authoring notes<a href="#authoring-notes" class="self-link"></a>

Legacy proxy servers are known to, in certain cases, drop HTTP
connections after a short timeout. To protect against such proxy
servers, authors can include a comment line (one starting with a ':'
character) every 15 seconds or so.

Authors wishing to relate event source connections to each other or to
specific documents previously served might find that relying on IP
addresses doesn't work, as individual clients can have multiple IP
addresses (due to having multiple proxy servers) and individual IP
addresses can have multiple clients (due to sharing a proxy server). It
is better to include a unique identifier in the document when it is
served and then pass that identifier as part of the URL when the
connection is established.

Authors are also cautioned that HTTP chunking can have unexpected
negative effects on the reliability of this protocol, in particular if
the chunking is done by a different layer unaware of the timing
requirements. If this is a problem, chunking can be disabled for serving
event streams.

Clients that support HTTP's per-server connection limitation might run
into trouble when opening multiple pages from a site if each page has an
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) to the same domain. Authors can avoid this
using the relatively complex mechanism of using unique domain names per
connection, or by allowing the user to enable or disable the
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) functionality on a per-page basis, or by
sharing a single [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object using a
<a href="#sharedworkerglobalscope"
id="authoring-notes:sharedworkerglobalscope">shared worker</a>.

#### <span class="secno">9.2.8</span> Connectionless push and other features<a href="#eventsource-push" class="self-link"></a>

User agents running in controlled environments, e.g. browsers on mobile
handsets tied to specific carriers, may offload the management of the
connection to a proxy on the network. In such a situation, the user
agent for the purposes of conformance is considered to include both the
handset software and the network proxy.

<div class="example">

For example, a browser on a mobile device, after having established a
connection, might detect that it is on a supporting network and request
that a proxy server on the network take over the management of the
connection. The timeline for such a situation might be as follows:

1.  Browser connects to a remote HTTP server and requests the resource
    specified by the author in the [`EventSource`](#dom-eventsource)
    constructor.
2.  The server sends occasional messages.
3.  In between two messages, the browser detects that it is idle except
    for the network activity involved in keeping the TCP connection
    alive, and decides to switch to sleep mode to save power.
4.  The browser disconnects from the server.
5.  The browser contacts a service on the network, and requests that the
    service, a "push proxy", maintain the connection instead.
6.  The "push proxy" service contacts the remote HTTP server and
    requests the resource specified by the author in the
    [`EventSource`](#dom-eventsource) constructor (possibly including a
    \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#last-event-id)\` HTTP header, etc.).
7.  The browser allows the mobile device to go to sleep.
8.  The server sends another message.
9.  The "push proxy" service uses a technology such as OMA push to
    convey the event to the mobile device, which wakes only enough to
    process the event and then returns to sleep.

</div>

This can reduce the total data usage, and can therefore result in
considerable power savings.

As well as implementing the existing API and
[`text/event-stream`](#text/event-stream) wire format as defined by this
specification and in more distributed ways as described above, formats
of event framing defined by <a href="#other-applicable-specifications"
id="eventsource-push:other-applicable-specifications">other applicable
specifications</a> may be supported. This specification does not define
how they are to be parsed or processed.

#### <span class="secno">9.2.9</span> Garbage collection<a href="#garbage-collection" class="self-link"></a>

While an [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
[`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) is
[`CONNECTING`](#dom-eventsource-connecting), and the object has one or
more event listeners registered for [`open`](#event-open),
[`message`](#event-message), or [`error`](#event-error) events, there
must be a strong reference from the [`Window`](#window) or
[`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object that the
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's constructor was invoked from to
the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object itself.

While an [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's
[`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) is
[`OPEN`](#dom-eventsource-open), and the object has one or more event
listeners registered for [`message`](#event-message) or
[`error`](#event-error) events, there must be a strong reference from
the [`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope)
object that the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's constructor was
invoked from to the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object itself.

While there is a task queued by an [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object
on the <a href="#remote-event-task-source"
id="garbage-collection:remote-event-task-source">remote event task
source</a>, there must be a strong reference from the
[`Window`](#window) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object
that the [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object's constructor was invoked
from to that [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object.

<div algorithm="">

If a user agent is to <span id="concept-eventsource-forcibly-close"
class="dfn">forcibly close</span> an [`EventSource`](#eventsource)
object (this happens when a [`Document`](#document) object goes away
permanently), the user agent must abort any instances of the
<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="garbage-collection:concept-fetch"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> algorithm started for this
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) object, and must set the
[`readyState`](#dom-eventsource-readystate) attribute to
[`CLOSED`](#dom-eventsource-closed).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

If an [`EventSource`](#eventsource) object is garbage collected while
its connection is still open, the user agent must abort any instance of
the <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
id="garbage-collection:concept-fetch-2"
data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> algorithm opened by this
[`EventSource`](#eventsource).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">9.2.10</span> Implementation advice<a href="#implementation-advice" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

User agents are strongly urged to provide detailed diagnostic
information about [`EventSource`](#eventsource) objects and their
related network connections in their development consoles, to aid
authors in debugging code using this API.

For example, a user agent could have a panel displaying all the
[`EventSource`](#eventsource) objects a page has created, each listing
the constructor's arguments, whether there was a network error, what the
CORS status of the connection is and what headers were sent by the
client and received from the server to lead to that status, the messages
that were received and how they were parsed, and so forth.

Implementations are especially encouraged to report detailed information
to their development consoles whenever an [`error`](#event-error) event
is fired, since little to no information can be made available in the
events themselves.

### <span class="secno">9.3</span> <span id="crossDocumentMessages" class="dfn">Cross-document messaging</span><a href="#web-messaging" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Window/postMessage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage "The window.postMessage() method safely enables cross-origin communication between Window objects; e.g., between a page and a pop-up that it spawned, or between a page and an iframe embedded within it.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox3+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome2+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera9.5+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android yes">WebView
Android≤37+</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android10.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

Web browsers, for security and privacy reasons, prevent documents in
different domains from affecting each other; that is, cross-site
scripting is disallowed.

While this is an important security feature, it prevents pages from
different domains from communicating even when those pages are not
hostile. This section introduces a messaging system that allows
documents to communicate with each other regardless of their source
domain, in a way designed to not enable cross-site scripting attacks.

<a href="#fingerprint-postMessage" class="self-link"></a>
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="web-messaging:tracking-vector" class="tracking-vector"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector"
title="There is a tracking vector here."><img
src="https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg"
class="darkmode-aware" crossorigin="" width="46" height="64"
alt="(This is a tracking vector.)" /></a> The
[`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) API can be used as a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector"
id="web-messaging:tracking-vector-2"
data-x-internal="tracking-vector">tracking vector</a>.

#### <span class="secno">9.3.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-12" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div class="example">

For example, if document A contains an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
element that contains document B, and script in document A calls
[`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) on the [`Window`](#window)
object of document B, then a message event will be fired on that object,
marked as originating from the [`Window`](#window) of document A. The
script in document A might look like:

``` js
var o = document.getElementsByTagName('iframe')[0];
o.contentWindow.postMessage('Hello world', 'https://b.example.org/');
```

To register an event handler for incoming events, the script would use
`addEventListener()` (or similar mechanisms). For example, the script in
document B might look like:

``` js
window.addEventListener('message', receiver, false);
function receiver(e) {
  if (e.origin == 'https://example.com') {
    if (e.data == 'Hello world') {
      e.source.postMessage('Hello', e.origin);
    } else {
      alert(e.data);
    }
  }
}
```

This script first checks the domain is the expected domain, and then
looks at the message, which it either displays to the user, or responds
to by sending a message back to the document which sent the message in
the first place.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">9.3.2</span> Security<a href="#security-postmsg" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">9.3.2.1</span> Authors<a href="#authors" class="self-link"></a>

Use of this API requires extra care to protect users from hostile
entities abusing a site for their own purposes.

Authors should check the [`origin`](#dom-messageevent-origin) attribute
to ensure that messages are only accepted from domains that they expect
to receive messages from. Otherwise, bugs in the author's message
handling code could be exploited by hostile sites.

Furthermore, even after checking the
[`origin`](#dom-messageevent-origin) attribute, authors should also
check that the data in question is of the expected format. Otherwise, if
the source of the event has been attacked using a cross-site scripting
flaw, further unchecked processing of information sent using the
[`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) method could result in the
attack being propagated into the receiver.

Authors should not use the wildcard keyword (\*) in the `targetOrigin`
argument in messages that contain any confidential information, as
otherwise there is no way to guarantee that the message is only
delivered to the recipient to which it was intended.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Authors who accept messages from any origin are encouraged to consider
the risks of a denial-of-service attack. An attacker could send a high
volume of messages; if the receiving page performs expensive computation
or causes network traffic to be sent for each such message, the
attacker's message could be multiplied into a denial-of-service attack.
Authors are encouraged to employ rate limiting (only accepting a certain
number of messages per minute) to make such attacks impractical.

##### <span class="secno">9.3.2.2</span> User agents<a href="#user-agents" class="self-link"></a>

The integrity of this API is based on the inability for scripts of one
<a href="#concept-origin" id="user-agents:concept-origin">origin</a> to
post arbitrary events (using `dispatchEvent()` or otherwise) to objects
in other origins (those that are not the
<a href="#same-origin" id="user-agents:same-origin">same</a>).

Implementers are urged to take extra care in the implementation of this
feature. It allows authors to transmit information from one domain to
another domain, which is normally disallowed for security reasons. It
also requires that UAs be careful to allow access to certain properties
but not others.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

User agents are also encouraged to consider rate-limiting message
traffic between different
<a href="#concept-origin" id="user-agents:concept-origin-2">origins</a>,
to protect naïve sites from denial-of-service attacks.

#### <span class="secno">9.3.3</span> Posting messages<a href="#posting-messages" class="self-link"></a>

`window``.`<a href="#dom-window-postmessage-options"
id="dom-window-postmessage-options-dev"><code>postMessage</code></a>`(``message`` [, ``options`` ])`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Window/postMessage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage "The window.postMessage() method safely enables cross-origin communication between Window objects; e.g., between a page and a pop-up that it spawned, or between a page and an iframe embedded within it.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox3+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari4+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome2+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android yes">WebView
Android37+</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera
Android10.1+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

Posts a message to the given window. Messages can be structured objects,
e.g. nested objects and arrays, can contain JavaScript values (strings,
numbers, <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects"
data-x-internal="date"><code id="posting-messages:date">Date</code></a>
objects, etc.), and can contain certain data objects such as
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file"
data-x-internal="file"><code id="posting-messages:file">File</code></a>
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob"
data-x-internal="blob"><code id="posting-messages:blob">Blob</code></a>,
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section"
data-x-internal="filelist"><code
id="posting-messages:filelist">FileList</code></a>, and
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer"
data-x-internal="idl-arraybuffer"><code
id="posting-messages:idl-arraybuffer">ArrayBuffer</code></a> objects.

Objects listed in the
[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer) member of
`options` are transferred, not just cloned, meaning that they are no
longer usable on the sending side.

A target origin can be specified using the
[`targetOrigin`](#dom-windowpostmessageoptions-targetorigin) member of
`options`. If not provided, it defaults to "`/`". This default restricts
the message to same-origin targets only.

If the origin of the target window doesn't match the given target
origin, the message is discarded, to avoid information leakage. To send
the message to the target regardless of origin, set the target origin to
"`*`".

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
id="posting-messages:datacloneerror"
data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="posting-messages:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if `transfer`
array contains duplicate objects or if `message` could not be cloned.

`window``.`<a href="#dom-window-postmessage"
id="posting-messages:dom-window-postmessage"><code>postMessage</code></a>`(``message``, ``targetOrigin`` [, ``transfer`` ])`

This is an alternate version of
[`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage-options) where the target
origin is specified as a parameter. Calling
`window.postMessage(message, target, transfer)` is equivalent to
`window.postMessage(message, {targetOrigin, transfer})`.

When posting a message to a [`Window`](#window) of a
<a href="#browsing-context"
id="posting-messages:browsing-context">browsing context</a> that has
just been navigated to a new [`Document`](#document) is likely to result
in the message not receiving its intended recipient: the scripts in the
target <a href="#browsing-context"
id="posting-messages:browsing-context-2">browsing context</a> have to
have had time to set up listeners for the messages. Thus, for instance,
in situations where a message is to be sent to the [`Window`](#window)
of newly created child [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), authors are
advised to have the child [`Document`](#document) post a message to
their parent announcing their readiness to receive messages, and for the
parent to wait for this message before beginning posting messages.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="window-post-message-steps" class="dfn">window post message
steps</span>, given a `targetWindow`, `message`, and `options`, are as
follows:

1.  Let `targetRealm` be `targetWindow`'s
    <a href="#concept-global-object-realm"
    id="posting-messages:concept-global-object-realm">realm</a>.

2.  Let `incumbentSettings` be the <a href="#incumbent-settings-object"
    id="posting-messages:incumbent-settings-object">incumbent settings
    object</a>.

3.  Let `targetOrigin` be
    `options`\["[`targetOrigin`](#dom-windowpostmessageoptions-targetorigin)"\].

4.  If `targetOrigin` is a single U+002F SOLIDUS character (/), then set
    `targetOrigin` to `incumbentSettings`'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="posting-messages:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>.

5.  Otherwise, if `targetOrigin` is not a single U+002A ASTERISK
    character (\*), then:

    1.  Let `parsedURL` be the result of running the
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser"
        id="posting-messages:url-parser" data-x-internal="url-parser">URL
        parser</a> on `targetOrigin`.

    2.  If `parsedURL` is failure, then throw a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
        id="posting-messages:syntaxerror"
        data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
        data-x-internal="domexception"><code
        id="posting-messages:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

    3.  Set `targetOrigin` to `parsedURL`'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin"
        id="posting-messages:concept-url-origin"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-origin">origin</a>.

6.  Let `transfer` be
    `options`\["[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)"\].

7.  Let `serializeWithTransferResult` be
    <a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
    id="posting-messages:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>(`message`,
    `transfer`). Rethrow any exceptions.

8.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="posting-messages:queue-a-global-task">Queue a global task</a> on
    the <span id="posted-message-task-source" class="dfn">posted message
    task source</span> given `targetWindow` to run the following steps:

    1.  If the `targetOrigin` argument is not a single literal U+002A
        ASTERISK character (\*) and `targetWindow`'s
        <a href="#concept-document-window"
        id="posting-messages:concept-document-window">associated
        <code>Document</code></a>'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin"
        id="posting-messages:concept-document-origin"
        data-x-internal="concept-document-origin">origin</a> is not
        <a href="#same-origin" id="posting-messages:same-origin">same origin</a>
        with `targetOrigin`, then return.

    2.  Let `origin` be `incumbentSettings`'s
        <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
        id="posting-messages:concept-settings-object-origin-2">origin</a>.

    3.  Let `source` be the [`WindowProxy`](#windowproxy) object
        corresponding to `incumbentSettings`'s
        <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
        id="posting-messages:concept-settings-object-global">global object</a>
        (a [`Window`](#window) object).

    4.  Let `deserializeRecord` be
        <a href="#structureddeserializewithtransfer"
        id="posting-messages:structureddeserializewithtransfer">StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer</a>(`serializeWithTransferResult`,
        `targetRealm`).

        If this throws an exception, catch it,
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="posting-messages:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror) at `targetWindow`, using
        [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), with its
        <a href="#concept-messageevent-origin"
        id="posting-messages:concept-messageevent-origin">origin</a>
        initialized to `origin` and the
        [`source`](#dom-messageevent-source) attribute initialized to
        `source`, and then return.

    5.  Let `messageClone` be `deserializeRecord`.\[\[Deserialized\]\].

    6.  Let `newPorts` be a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
        id="posting-messages:frozen-array" data-x-internal="frozen-array">frozen
        array</a> consisting of all [`MessagePort`](#messageport)
        objects in `deserializeRecord`.\[\[TransferredValues\]\], if
        any, maintaining their relative order.

    7.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="posting-messages:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
        [`message`](#event-message) at `targetWindow`, using
        [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), with its
        <a href="#concept-messageevent-origin"
        id="posting-messages:concept-messageevent-origin-2">origin</a>
        initialized to `origin`, the
        [`source`](#dom-messageevent-source) attribute initialized to
        `source`, the [`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute
        initialized to `messageClone`, and the
        [`ports`](#dom-messageevent-ports) attribute initialized to
        `newPorts`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`Window`](#window) interface's
<span id="dom-window-postmessage-options" class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``options``)`</span> method
steps are to run the <a href="#window-post-message-steps"
id="posting-messages:window-post-message-steps">window post message
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="posting-messages:this" data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `message`,
and `options`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`Window`](#window) interface's <span id="dom-window-postmessage"
class="dfn" dfn-for="Window"
dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``targetOrigin``, ``transfer``)`</span>
method steps are to run the <a href="#window-post-message-steps"
id="posting-messages:window-post-message-steps-2">window post message
steps</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="posting-messages:this-2" data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `message`,
and «\[ "[`targetOrigin`](#dom-windowpostmessageoptions-targetorigin)" →
`targetOrigin`, "[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)"
→ `transfer` \]».

</div>

#### <span class="secno">9.4.1</span> Introduction<a href="#introduction-13" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

To enable independent pieces of code (e.g. running in different
<a href="#browsing-context"
id="introduction-13:browsing-context">browsing contexts</a>) to
communicate directly, authors can use <a href="#channel-messaging"
id="introduction-13:channel-messaging">channel messaging</a>.

Communication channels in this mechanism are implemented as two-ways
pipes, with a port at each end. Messages sent in one port are delivered
at the other port, and vice-versa. Messages are delivered as DOM events,
without interrupting or blocking running
<a href="#concept-task" id="introduction-13:concept-task">tasks</a>.

To create a connection (two "entangled" ports), the `MessageChannel()`
constructor is called:

``` js
var channel = new MessageChannel();
```

One of the ports is kept as the local port, and the other port is sent
to the remote code, e.g. using
[`postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage):

``` js
otherWindow.postMessage('hello', 'https://example.com', [channel.port2]);
```

To send messages, the [`postMessage()`](#dom-messageport-postmessage)
method on the port is used:

``` js
channel.port1.postMessage('hello');
```

To receive messages, one listens to [`message`](#event-message) events:

``` js
channel.port1.onmessage = handleMessage;
function handleMessage(event) {
  // message is in event.data
  // ...
}
```

Data sent on a port can be structured data; for example here an array of
strings is passed on a [`MessagePort`](#messageport):

``` js
port1.postMessage(['hello', 'world']);
```

##### <span class="secno">9.4.1.1</span> Examples<a href="#examples-5" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div class="example">

In this example, two JavaScript libraries are connected to each other
using [`MessagePort`](#messageport)s. This allows the libraries to later
be hosted in different frames, or in [`Worker`](#worker) objects,
without any change to the APIs.

``` html
<script src="contacts.js"></script> <!-- exposes a contacts object -->
<script src="compose-mail.js"></script> <!-- exposes a composer object -->
<script>
 var channel = new MessageChannel();
 composer.addContactsProvider(channel.port1);
 contacts.registerConsumer(channel.port2);
</script>
```

Here's what the "addContactsProvider()" function's implementation could
look like:

``` js
function addContactsProvider(port) {
  port.onmessage = function (event) {
    switch (event.data.messageType) {
      case 'search-result': handleSearchResult(event.data.results); break;
      case 'search-done': handleSearchDone(); break;
      case 'search-error': handleSearchError(event.data.message); break;
      // ...
    }
  };
};
```

Alternatively, it could be implemented as follows:

``` js
function addContactsProvider(port) {
  port.addEventListener('message', function (event) {
    if (event.data.messageType == 'search-result')
      handleSearchResult(event.data.results);
  });
  port.addEventListener('message', function (event) {
    if (event.data.messageType == 'search-done')
      handleSearchDone();
  });
  port.addEventListener('message', function (event) {
    if (event.data.messageType == 'search-error')
      handleSearchError(event.data.message);
  });
  // ...
  port.start();
};
```

The key difference is that when using
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"
data-x-internal="dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener"><code
id="examples-5:dom-eventtarget-addeventlistener">addEventListener()</code></a>,
the [`start()`](#dom-messageport-start) method must also be invoked.
When using [`onmessage`](#handler-messageeventtarget-onmessage), the
call to [`start()`](#dom-messageport-start) is implied.

The [`start()`](#dom-messageport-start) method, whether called
explicitly or implicitly (by setting
[`onmessage`](#handler-messageeventtarget-onmessage)), starts the flow
of messages: messages posted on message ports are initially paused, so
that they don't get dropped on the floor before the script has had a
chance to set up its handlers.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">9.4.1.2</span> Ports as the basis of an object-capability model on the web<a href="#ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web"
class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

<div var-scope="">

Ports can be viewed as a way to expose limited capabilities (in the
object-capability model sense) to other actors in the system. This can
either be a weak capability system, where the ports are merely used as a
convenient model within a particular origin, or as a strong capability
model, where they are provided by one origin `provider` as the only
mechanism by which another origin `consumer` can effect change in or
obtain information from `provider`.

</div>

For example, consider a situation in which a social web site embeds in
one [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) the user's email contacts provider
(an address book site, from a second origin), and in a second
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) a game (from a third origin). The outer
social site and the game in the second [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
cannot access anything inside the first [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element);
together they can only:

- <a href="#navigate"
  id="ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web:navigate">Navigate</a>
  the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) to a new
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web:url"
  data-x-internal="url">URL</a>, such as the same
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
  id="ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web:url-2"
  data-x-internal="url">URL</a> but with a different
  <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment"
  id="ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web:concept-url-fragment"
  data-x-internal="concept-url-fragment">fragment</a>, causing the
  [`Window`](#window) in the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) to receive
  a [`hashchange`](#event-hashchange) event.

- Resize the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), causing the
  [`Window`](#window) in the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) to receive
  a
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#eventdef-window-resize"
  data-x-internal="event-resize"><code
  id="ports-as-the-basis-of-an-object-capability-model-on-the-web:event-resize">resize</code></a>
  event.

- Send a [`message`](#event-message) event to the [`Window`](#window) in
  the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) using the
  [`window.postMessage()`](#dom-window-postmessage) API.

The contacts provider can use these methods, most particularly the third
one, to provide an API that can be accessed by other origins to
manipulate the user's address book. For example, it could respond to a
message "`add-contact Guillaume Tell <tell@pomme.example.net>`" by
adding the given person and email address to the user's address book.

To avoid any site on the web being able to manipulate the user's
contacts, the contacts provider might only allow certain trusted sites,
such as the social site, to do this.

Now suppose the game wanted to add a contact to the user's address book,
and that the social site was willing to allow it to do so on its behalf,
essentially "sharing" the trust that the contacts provider had with the
social site. There are several ways it could do this; most simply, it
could just proxy messages between the game site and the contacts site.
However, this solution has a number of difficulties: it requires the
social site to either completely trust the game site not to abuse the
privilege, or it requires that the social site verify each request to
make sure it's not a request that it doesn't want to allow (such as
adding multiple contacts, reading the contacts, or deleting them); it
also requires some additional complexity if there's ever the possibility
of multiple games simultaneously trying to interact with the contacts
provider.

Using message channels and [`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects,
however, all of these problems can go away. When the game tells the
social site that it wants to add a contact, the social site can ask the
contacts provider not for it to add a contact, but for the *capability*
to add a single contact. The contacts provider then creates a pair of
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects, and sends one of them back to the
social site, who forwards it on to the game. The game and the contacts
provider then have a direct connection, and the contacts provider knows
to only honor a single "add contact" request, nothing else. In other
words, the game has been granted the capability to add a single contact.

##### <span class="secno">9.4.1.3</span> Ports as the basis of abstracting out service implementations<a href="#ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations"
class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

Continuing the example from the previous section, consider the contacts
provider in particular. While an initial implementation might have
simply used <a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest"
data-x-internal="xmlhttprequest"><code
id="ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations:xmlhttprequest">XMLHttpRequest</code></a>
objects in the service's [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), an evolution
of the service might instead want to use a <a href="#sharedworker"
id="ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations:sharedworker">shared
worker</a> with a single
<a href="https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket"
data-x-internal="websocket-2"><code
id="ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations:websocket-2">WebSocket</code></a>
connection.

If the initial design used [`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects to
grant capabilities, or even just to allow multiple simultaneous
independent sessions, the service implementation can switch from the
<a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest"
data-x-internal="xmlhttprequest"><code
id="ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations:xmlhttprequest-2">XMLHttpRequest</code></a>s-in-each-[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)
model to the
shared-<a href="https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket"
data-x-internal="websocket-2"><code
id="ports-as-the-basis-of-abstracting-out-service-implementations:websocket-2-2">WebSocket</code></a>
model without changing the API at all: the ports on the service provider
side can all be forwarded to the shared worker without it affecting the
users of the API in the slightest.

#### <span class="secno">9.4.4</span> Message ports<a href="#message-ports" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[MessagePort](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MessagePort "The MessagePort interface of the Channel Messaging API represents one of the two ports of a MessageChannel, allowing messages to be sent from one port and listening out for them arriving at the other.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox41+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari5+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome2+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="opera yes">Opera10.6+</span><span class="edge_blink yes">Edge79+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="edge yes">Edge
(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

Each channel has two message ports. Data sent through one port is
received by the other port, and vice versa.

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker,AudioWorklet), Transferable]
interface MessagePort : EventTarget {
  undefined postMessage(any message, sequence<object> transfer);
  undefined postMessage(any message, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});
  undefined start();
  undefined close();

  // event handlers
  attribute EventHandler onclose;
};

MessagePort includes MessageEventTarget;

dictionary StructuredSerializeOptions {
  sequence<object> transfer = [];
};
```

`port``.`<a href="#dom-messageport-postmessage"
id="dom-messageport-postmessage-dev"><code>postMessage</code></a>`(``message`` [, ``transfer``])`

`port``.`<a href="#dom-messageport-postmessage-options"
id="dom-messageport-postmessage-options-dev"><code>postMessage</code></a>`(``message`` [, { ``transfer`` }])`

Posts a message through the channel. Objects listed in `transfer` are
transferred, not just cloned, meaning that they are no longer usable on
the sending side.

Throws a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
id="message-ports:datacloneerror"
data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
data-x-internal="domexception"><code
id="message-ports:domexception">DOMException</code></a> if `transfer`
contains duplicate objects or `port`, or if `message` could not be
cloned.

`port``.`<a href="#dom-messageport-start"
id="dom-messageport-start-dev"><code>start</code></a>`()`

[MessagePort/start](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MessagePort/start "The start() method of the MessagePort interface starts the sending of messages queued on the port. This method is only needed when using EventTarget.addEventListener; it is implied when using onmessage.")

Begins dispatching messages received on the port.

`port``.`<a href="#dom-messageport-close"
id="dom-messageport-close-dev"><code>close</code></a>`()`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[MessagePort/close](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MessagePort/close "The close() method of the MessagePort interface disconnects the port, so it is no longer active. This stops the flow of messages to that port.")

Support in all current engines.

<div class="support">

<span class="firefox yes">Firefox41+</span><span class="safari yes">Safari5+</span><span class="chrome yes">Chrome2+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------
