(Legacy)12+</span><span class="ie yes">Internet Explorer10+</span>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<span class="firefox_android unknown">Firefox
Android?</span><span class="safari_ios unknown">Safari
iOS?</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

Disconnects the port, so that it is no longer active.

Each [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object has a
<span id="message-event-target" class="dfn">message event target</span>
(a [`MessageEventTarget`](#messageeventtarget)), to which the
[`message`](#event-message) and [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror)
events are dispatched. Unless otherwise specified, it defaults to the
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) object itself.

Each [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object can be entangled with another
(a symmetric relationship). Each [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object
also has a
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source">task source</a>
called the <span id="port-message-queue" class="dfn">port message
queue</span>, initially empty. A
<a href="#port-message-queue" id="message-ports:port-message-queue">port
message queue</a> can be enabled or disabled, and is initially disabled.
Once enabled, a port can never be disabled again (though messages in the
queue can get moved to another queue or removed altogether, which has
much the same effect). A [`MessagePort`](#messageport) also has a
<span id="has-been-shipped" class="dfn">has been shipped</span> flag,
which must initially be false.

<div algorithm="">

When a port's <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-2">port message queue</a> is
enabled, the
<a href="#event-loop" id="message-ports:event-loop">event loop</a> must
use it as one of its
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source-2">task sources</a>.
When a port's <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="message-ports:concept-relevant-global">relevant global object</a> is
a [`Window`](#window), all
<a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task">tasks</a>
<a href="#queue-a-task" id="message-ports:queue-a-task">queued</a> on
its <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-3">port message queue</a> must be
associated with the port's <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="message-ports:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant global object</a>'s
<a href="#concept-document-window"
id="message-ports:concept-document-window">associated
<code>Document</code></a>.

</div>

If the document is
<a href="#fully-active" id="message-ports:fully-active">fully active</a>,
but the event listeners were all created in the context of documents
that are *not*
<a href="#fully-active" id="message-ports:fully-active-2">fully
active</a>, then the messages will not be received unless and until the
documents become
<a href="#fully-active" id="message-ports:fully-active-3">fully
active</a> again.

<div algorithm="">

Each
<a href="#event-loop" id="message-ports:event-loop-2">event loop</a> has
a
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source-3">task source</a>
called the <span id="unshipped-port-message-queue" class="dfn">unshipped
port message queue</span>. This is a virtual
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source-4">task source</a>:
it must act as if it contained the
<a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task-2">tasks</a> of
each <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-4">port message queue</a> of each
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) whose
<a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped">has been
shipped</a> flag is false, whose <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-5">port message queue</a> is
enabled, and whose
<a href="#relevant-agent" id="message-ports:relevant-agent">relevant
agent</a>'s <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
id="message-ports:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a> is that
<a href="#event-loop" id="message-ports:event-loop-3">event loop</a>, in
the order in which they were added to their respective
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source-5">task source</a>.
When a
<a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task-3">task</a> would
be removed from the <a href="#unshipped-port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:unshipped-port-message-queue">unshipped port message
queue</a>, it must instead be removed from its
<a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-6">port message queue</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`MessagePort`](#messageport)'s
<a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-2">has
been shipped</a> flag is false, its <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-7">port message queue</a> must be
ignored for the purposes of the
<a href="#event-loop" id="message-ports:event-loop-4">event loop</a>.
(The <a href="#unshipped-port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:unshipped-port-message-queue-2">unshipped port message
queue</a> is used instead.)

</div>

The
<a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-3">has
been shipped</a> flag is set to true when a port, its twin, or the
object it was cloned from, is or has been transferred. When a
[`MessagePort`](#messageport)'s
<a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-4">has
been shipped</a> flag is true, its <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-8">port message queue</a> acts as a
first-class
<a href="#task-source" id="message-ports:task-source-6">task source</a>,
unaffected to any <a href="#unshipped-port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:unshipped-port-message-queue-3">unshipped port message
queue</a>.

<div algorithm="">

When the user agent is to <span id="entangle"
class="dfn">entangle</span> two [`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects,
it must run the following steps:

1.  If one of the ports is already entangled, then disentangle it and
    the port that it was entangled with.

    If those two previously entangled ports were the two ports of a
    [`MessageChannel`](#messagechannel) object, then that
    [`MessageChannel`](#messagechannel) object no longer represents an
    actual channel: the two ports in that object are no longer
    entangled.

2.  Associate the two ports to be entangled, so that they form the two
    parts of a new channel. (There is no
    [`MessageChannel`](#messagechannel) object that represents this
    channel.)

    Two ports `A` and `B` that have gone through this step are now said
    to be entangled; one is entangled to the other, and vice versa.

    While this specification describes this process as instantaneous,
    implementations are more likely to implement it via message passing.
    As with all algorithms, the key is "merely" that the end result be
    indistinguishable, in a black-box sense, from the specification.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="disentangle" class="dfn">disentangle</span> steps, given a
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) `initiatorPort` which initiates
disentangling, are as follows:

1.  Let `otherPort` be the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) which
    `initiatorPort` was entangled with.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert"
    id="message-ports:assert" data-x-internal="assert">Assert</a>:
    `otherPort` exists.

3.  Disentangle `initiatorPort` and `otherPort`, so that they are no
    longer entangled or associated with each other.

4.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
    id="message-ports:concept-event-fire"
    data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
    [`close`](#event-close) at `otherPort`.

<div class="note">

The [`close`](#event-close) event will be fired even if the port is not
explicitly closed. The cases where this event is dispatched are:

- the [`close()`](#dom-messageport-close) method was called;
- the [`Document`](#document) was <a href="#destroy-a-document"
  id="message-ports:destroy-a-document">destroyed</a>; or
- the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) was [garbage
  collected](#ports-and-garbage-collection).

We only dispatch the event on `otherPort` because `initiatorPort`
explicitly triggered the close, its [`Document`](#document) no longer
exists, or it was already garbage collected, as described above.

</div>

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

[`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects are
<a href="#transferable-objects"
id="message-ports:transferable-objects">transferable objects</a>. Their
<a href="#transfer-steps" id="message-ports:transfer-steps">transfer
steps</a>, given `value` and `dataHolder`, are:

1.  Set `value`'s
    <a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-5">has
    been shipped</a> flag to true.

2.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[PortMessageQueue\]\] to `value`'s
    <a href="#port-message-queue"
    id="message-ports:port-message-queue-9">port message queue</a>.

3.  If `value` is entangled with another port `remotePort`, then:

    1.  Set `remotePort`'s
        <a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-6">has
        been shipped</a> flag to true.

    2.  Set `dataHolder`.\[\[RemotePort\]\] to `remotePort`.

4.  Otherwise, set `dataHolder`.\[\[RemotePort\]\] to null.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Their <a href="#transfer-receiving-steps"
id="message-ports:transfer-receiving-steps">transfer-receiving steps</a>,
given `dataHolder` and `value`, are:

1.  Set `value`'s
    <a href="#has-been-shipped" id="message-ports:has-been-shipped-7">has
    been shipped</a> flag to true.

2.  Move all the
    <a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task-4">tasks</a>
    that are to fire [`message`](#event-message) events in
    `dataHolder`.\[\[PortMessageQueue\]\] to the
    <a href="#port-message-queue"
    id="message-ports:port-message-queue-10">port message queue</a> of
    `value`, if any, leaving `value`'s <a href="#port-message-queue"
    id="message-ports:port-message-queue-11">port message queue</a> in
    its initial disabled state, and, if `value`'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="message-ports:concept-relevant-global-3">relevant global object</a>
    is a [`Window`](#window), associating the moved
    <a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task-5">tasks</a>
    with `value`'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="message-ports:concept-relevant-global-4">relevant global object</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-window"
    id="message-ports:concept-document-window-2">associated
    <code>Document</code></a>.

3.  If `dataHolder`.\[\[RemotePort\]\] is not null, then
    <a href="#entangle" id="message-ports:entangle">entangle</a>
    `dataHolder`.\[\[RemotePort\]\] and `value`. (This will disentangle
    `dataHolder`.\[\[RemotePort\]\] from the original port that was
    transferred.)

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="message-port-post-message-steps" class="dfn">message port
post message steps</span>, given `sourcePort`, `targetPort`, `message`,
and `options` are as follows:

1.  Let `transfer` be
    `options`\["[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)"\].

2.  If `transfer` <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="message-ports:list-contains"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> `sourcePort`, then
    throw a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror"
    id="message-ports:datacloneerror-2"
    data-x-internal="datacloneerror">"<code>DataCloneError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="message-ports:domexception-2">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Let `doomed` be false.

4.  If `targetPort` is not null and `transfer`
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain"
    id="message-ports:list-contains-2"
    data-x-internal="list-contains">contains</a> `targetPort`, then set
    `doomed` to true and optionally report to a developer console that
    the target port was posted to itself, causing the communication
    channel to be lost.

5.  Let `serializeWithTransferResult` be
    <a href="#structuredserializewithtransfer"
    id="message-ports:structuredserializewithtransfer">StructuredSerializeWithTransfer</a>(`message`,
    `transfer`). Rethrow any exceptions.

6.  If `targetPort` is null, or if `doomed` is true, then return.

7.  Add a
    <a href="#concept-task" id="message-ports:concept-task-6">task</a>
    that runs the following steps to the <a href="#port-message-queue"
    id="message-ports:port-message-queue-12">port message queue</a> of
    `targetPort`:

    1.  Let `finalTargetPort` be the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) in
        whose <a href="#port-message-queue"
        id="message-ports:port-message-queue-13">port message queue</a>
        the task now finds itself.

        This can be different from `targetPort`, if `targetPort` itself
        was transferred and thus all its tasks moved along with it.

    2.  Let `messageEventTarget` be `finalTargetPort`'s
        <a href="#message-event-target"
        id="message-ports:message-event-target">message event target</a>.

    3.  Let `targetRealm` be `finalTargetPort`'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
        id="message-ports:concept-relevant-realm">relevant realm</a>.

    4.  Let `deserializeRecord` be
        <a href="#structureddeserializewithtransfer"
        id="message-ports:structureddeserializewithtransfer">StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer</a>(`serializeWithTransferResult`,
        `targetRealm`).

        If this throws an exception, catch it,
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="message-ports:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror) at `messageEventTarget`,
        using [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), and then return.

    5.  Let `messageClone` be `deserializeRecord`.\[\[Deserialized\]\].

    6.  Let `newPorts` be a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
        id="message-ports:frozen-array" data-x-internal="frozen-array">frozen
        array</a> consisting of all [`MessagePort`](#messageport)
        objects in `deserializeRecord`.\[\[TransferredValues\]\], if
        any, maintaining their relative order.

    7.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="message-ports:concept-event-fire-3"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
        [`message`](#event-message) at `messageEventTarget`, using
        [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), with the
        [`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute initialized to
        `messageClone` and the [`ports`](#dom-messageevent-ports)
        attribute initialized to `newPorts`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-messageport-postmessage-options" class="dfn"
dfn-for="MessagePort"
dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``options``)`</span> method
steps are:

1.  Let `targetPort` be the port with which
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a> is entangled, if any; otherwise let
    it be null.

2.  Run the <a href="#message-port-post-message-steps"
    id="message-ports:message-port-post-message-steps">message port post
    message steps</a> providing
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `targetPort`, `message` and
    `options`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-messageport-postmessage" class="dfn"
dfn-for="MessagePort"
dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``transfer``)`</span> method
steps are:

1.  Let `targetPort` be the port with which
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a> is entangled, if any; otherwise let
    it be null.

2.  Let `options` be «\[
    "[`transfer`](#dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer)" →
    `transfer` \]».

3.  Run the <a href="#message-port-post-message-steps"
    id="message-ports:message-port-post-message-steps-2">message port post
    message steps</a> providing
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>, `targetPort`, `message` and
    `options`.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-messageport-start" class="dfn" dfn-for="MessagePort"
dfn-type="method">`start()`</span> method steps are to enable
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-5"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-14">port message queue</a>, if it
is not already enabled.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-messageport-close" class="dfn" dfn-for="MessagePort"
dfn-type="method">`close()`</span> method steps are:

1.  Set
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-6"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#detached" id="message-ports:detached">[[Detached]]</a>
    internal slot value to true.

2.  If
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="message-ports:this-7"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a> is entangled,
    <a href="#disentangle" id="message-ports:disentangle">disentangle</a>
    it.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following are the
<a href="#event-handlers" id="message-ports:event-handlers">event
handlers</a> (and their corresponding
<a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="message-ports:event-handler-event-type">event handler event
types</a>) that must be supported, as
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="message-ports:event-handler-idl-attributes">event handler IDL
attributes</a>, by all objects implementing the
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) interface:

| <a href="#event-handlers" id="message-ports:event-handlers-2">Event
handler</a> | <a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="message-ports:event-handler-event-type-2">Event handler event
type</a> |
|----|----|
| <span id="handler-messageport-onclose" class="dfn" dfn-for="MessagePort" dfn-type="attribute">`onclose`</span> | [`close`](#event-close) |

<div algorithm="">

The first time a [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object's
[`onmessage`](#handler-messageeventtarget-onmessage) IDL attribute is
set, the port's <a href="#port-message-queue"
id="message-ports:port-message-queue-15">port message queue</a> must be
enabled, as if the [`start()`](#dom-messageport-start) method had been
called.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">9.4.5</span> Ports and garbage collection<a href="#ports-and-garbage-collection" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object `o` is garbage collected, if
`o` is entangled, then the user agent must <a href="#disentangle"
id="ports-and-garbage-collection:disentangle">disentangle</a> `o`.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When a [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object `o` is entangled and
[`message`](#event-message) or [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror)
event listener is registered, user agents must act as if `o`'s entangled
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) object has a strong reference to `o`.

</div>

Furthermore, a [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object must not be garbage
collected while there exists an event referenced by a
<a href="#concept-task"
id="ports-and-garbage-collection:concept-task">task</a> in a
<a href="#task-queue" id="ports-and-garbage-collection:task-queue">task
queue</a> that is to be dispatched on that [`MessagePort`](#messageport)
object, or while the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object's
<a href="#port-message-queue"
id="ports-and-garbage-collection:port-message-queue">port message
queue</a> is enabled and not empty.

<div class="note">

Thus, a message port can be received, given an event listener, and then
forgotten, and so long as that event listener could receive a message,
the channel will be maintained.

Of course, if this was to occur on both sides of the channel, then both
ports could be garbage collected, since they would not be reachable from
live code, despite having a strong reference to each other. However, if
a message port has a pending message, it is not garbage collected.

</div>

Authors are strongly encouraged to explicitly close
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects to disentangle them, so that their
resources can be recollected. Creating many
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects and discarding them without
closing them can lead to high transient memory usage since garbage
collection is not necessarily performed promptly, especially for
[`MessagePort`](#messageport)s where garbage collection can involve
cross-process coordination.

### <span class="secno">9.5</span> <span class="dfn">Broadcasting to other browsing contexts</span><a href="#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts"

It allows communication between different documents (in different windows, tabs, frames or iframes) of the same origin. Messages are broadcasted via a message event fired at all BroadcastChannel objects listening to the channel, except the object that sent the message.")

Pages on a single <a href="#concept-origin"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-origin">origin</a>
opened by the same user in the same user agent but in different
unrelated <a href="#browsing-context"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:browsing-context">browsing
contexts</a> sometimes need to send notifications to each other, for
example "hey, the user logged in over here, check your credentials
again".

For elaborate cases, e.g. to manage locking of shared state, to manage
synchronization of resources between a server and multiple local
clients, to share a
<a href="https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket"
data-x-internal="websocket-2"><code
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:websocket-2">WebSocket</code></a>
connection with a remote host, and so forth, <a href="#sharedworker"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:sharedworker">shared
workers</a> are the most appropriate solution.

For simple cases, though, where a shared worker would be an unreasonable
overhead, authors can use the simple channel-based broadcast mechanism
described in this section.

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface BroadcastChannel : EventTarget {
  constructor(DOMString name);

  readonly attribute DOMString name;
  undefined postMessage(any message);
  undefined close();
  attribute EventHandler onmessage;
  attribute EventHandler onmessageerror;
};
```

`broadcastChannel`` = new `<a href="#dom-broadcastchannel"
id="dom-broadcastchannel-dev"><code>BroadcastChannel</code></a>`(``name``)`

A [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) object has a
<span id="channel-name" class="dfn">channel name</span> and a
<span id="concept-broadcastchannel-closed" class="dfn">closed
flag</span>.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-broadcastchannel"
class="dfn">`new BroadcastChannel(``name``)`</span> constructor steps
are:

1.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#channel-name"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:channel-name">channel
    name</a> to `name`.

2.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-2"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-broadcastchannel-closed"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-broadcastchannel-closed">closed
    flag</a> to false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-broadcastchannel-name" class="dfn"
dfn-for="BroadcastChannel" dfn-type="attribute">`name`</span> getter
steps are to return <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-3"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#channel-name"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:channel-name-2">channel
name</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) object is said to be
<span id="eligible-for-messaging" class="dfn">eligible for
messaging</span> when its <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-relevant-global">relevant
global object</a> is either:

- a [`Window`](#window) object whose <a href="#concept-document-window"
  id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-document-window">associated
  <code>Document</code></a> is <a href="#fully-active"
  id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:fully-active">fully
  active</a>, or

- a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object whose
  <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
  id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:dom-workerglobalscope-closing">closing</a>
  flag is false and is not <a href="#suspendable-worker"
  id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:suspendable-worker">suspendable</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-broadcastchannel-postmessage" class="dfn"
dfn-for="BroadcastChannel"
dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``)`</span> method steps are:

1.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a> is not
    <a href="#eligible-for-messaging"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:eligible-for-messaging">eligible
    for messaging</a>, then return.

2.  If <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-5"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-broadcastchannel-closed"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-broadcastchannel-closed-2">closed
    flag</a> is true, then throw an
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:invalidstateerror"
    data-x-internal="invalidstateerror">"<code>InvalidStateError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

3.  Let `serialized` be <a href="#structuredserialize"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:structuredserialize">StructuredSerialize</a>(`message`).
    Rethrow any exceptions.

4.  Let `sourceOrigin` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-6"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object">relevant
    settings object</a>'s <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>.

5.  Let `sourceStorageKey` be the result of running <a
    href="https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes"
    data-x-internal="obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes">obtain a
    storage key for non-storage purposes</a> with
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-7"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object-2">relevant
    settings object</a>.

6.  Let `destinations` be a list of
    [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) objects that match the
    following criteria:

    - They are <a href="#eligible-for-messaging"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:eligible-for-messaging-2">eligible
      for messaging</a>.

    - The result of running <a
      href="https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes-2"
      data-x-internal="obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes">obtain a
      storage key for non-storage purposes</a> with their
      <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:relevant-settings-object-3">relevant
      settings object</a>
      <a href="https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key-equal"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:storage-key-equal"
      data-x-internal="storage-key-equal">equals</a> `sourceStorageKey`.

    - Their <a href="#channel-name"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:channel-name-3">channel
      name</a> <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:is"
      data-x-internal="is">is</a>
      <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-8"
      data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#channel-name"
      id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:channel-name-4">channel
      name</a>.

7.  Remove `source` from `destinations`.

8.  Sort `destinations` such that all
    [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) objects whose
    <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:relevant-agent">relevant
    agents</a> are the same are sorted in creation order, oldest first.
    (This does not define a complete ordering. Within this constraint,
    user agents may sort the list in any
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    manner.)

9.  For each `destination` in `destinations`,
    <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:queue-a-global-task">queue a
    global task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
    manipulation task source</a> given `destination`'s
    <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-relevant-global-2">relevant
    global object</a> to perform the following steps:

    1.  If `destination`'s <a href="#concept-broadcastchannel-closed"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-broadcastchannel-closed-3">closed
        flag</a> is true, then abort these steps.

    2.  Let `targetRealm` be `destination`'s
        <a href="#concept-relevant-realm"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-relevant-realm">relevant
        realm</a>.

    3.  Let `data` be <a href="#structureddeserialize"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:structureddeserialize">StructuredDeserialize</a>(`serialized`,
        `targetRealm`).

        If this throws an exception, catch it,
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-event-fire"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror) at `destination`, using
        [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), with its
        <a href="#concept-messageevent-origin"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-messageevent-origin">origin</a>
        initialized to `sourceOrigin`, and then abort these steps.

    4.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire an event</a> named
        [`message`](#event-message) at `destination`, using
        [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent), with the
        [`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute initialized to `data`
        and its <a href="#concept-messageevent-origin"
        id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-messageevent-origin-2">origin</a>
        initialized to `sourceOrigin`.

</div>

While a [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) object whose
<a href="#concept-broadcastchannel-closed"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-broadcastchannel-closed-4">closed
flag</a> is false has an event listener registered for
[`message`](#event-message) or [`messageerror`](#event-messageerror)
events, there must be a strong reference from the
[`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) object's
<a href="#concept-relevant-global"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-relevant-global-3">relevant
global object</a> to the [`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) object
itself.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-broadcastchannel-close" class="dfn"
dfn-for="BroadcastChannel" dfn-type="method">`close()`</span> method
steps are to set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:this-9"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-broadcastchannel-closed"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:concept-broadcastchannel-closed-5">closed
flag</a> to true.

</div>

Authors are strongly encouraged to explicitly close
[`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) objects when they are no longer
needed, so that they can be garbage collected. Creating many
[`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) objects and discarding them
while leaving them with an event listener and without closing them can
lead to an apparent memory leak, since the objects will continue to live
for as long as they have an event listener (or until their page or
worker is closed).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following are the <a href="#event-handlers"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:event-handlers">event
handlers</a> (and their corresponding
<a href="#event-handler-event-type"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:event-handler-event-type">event
handler event types</a>) that must be supported, as
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts:event-handler-idl-attributes">event
handler IDL attributes</a>, by all objects implementing the
[`BroadcastChannel`](#broadcastchannel) interface:

<div class="example">

Suppose a page wants to know when the user logs out, even when the user
does so from another tab at the same site:

``` js
var authChannel = new BroadcastChannel('auth');
authChannel.onmessage = function (event) {
  if (event.data == 'logout')
    showLogout();
}

function logoutRequested() {
  // called when the user asks us to log them out
  doLogout();
  showLogout();
  authChannel.postMessage('logout');
}

function doLogout() {
  // actually log the user out (e.g. clearing cookies)
  // ...
}

function showLogout() {
  // update the UI to indicate we're logged out
  // ...
}
```

## <span class="secno">10</span> Web workers<a href="#workers" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Web_Workers_API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API "Web Workers makes it possible to run a script operation in a background thread separate from the main execution thread of a web application. The advantage of this is that laborious processing can be performed in a separate thread, allowing the main (usually the UI) thread to run without being blocked/slowed down.")

Support in all current engines.
