#### <span class="secno">10.2.2</span> The event loop<a href="#worker-event-loop" class="self-link"></a>

A <a href="#worker-event-loop-2"
id="worker-event-loop:worker-event-loop-2">worker event loop</a>'s
<a href="#task-queue" id="worker-event-loop:task-queue">task queues</a>
only have events, callbacks, and networking activity as
<a href="#concept-task" id="worker-event-loop:concept-task">tasks</a>.
These <a href="#worker-event-loop-2"
id="worker-event-loop:worker-event-loop-2-2">worker event loops</a> are
created by the
<a href="#run-a-worker" id="worker-event-loop:run-a-worker">run a
worker</a> algorithm.

Each [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object has a
<span id="dom-workerglobalscope-closing" class="dfn"
dfn-for="WorkerGlobalScope" export="">closing</span> flag, which must be
initially false, but which can get set to true by the algorithms in the
processing model section below.

<div algorithm="">

Once the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope)'s
<a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
id="worker-event-loop:dom-workerglobalscope-closing">closing</a> flag is
set to true, the
<a href="#event-loop" id="worker-event-loop:event-loop">event loop</a>'s
<a href="#task-queue" id="worker-event-loop:task-queue-2">task
queues</a> must discard any further
<a href="#concept-task" id="worker-event-loop:concept-task-2">tasks</a>
that would be added to them (tasks already on the queue are unaffected
except where otherwise specified). Effectively, once the
<a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
id="worker-event-loop:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-2">closing</a> flag
is true, timers stop firing, notifications for all pending background
operations are dropped, etc.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">10.2.3</span> The worker's lifetime<a href="#the-worker&#39;s-lifetime" class="self-link"></a>

Workers communicate with other workers and with [`Window`](#window)s
through <a href="#channel-messaging"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:channel-messaging">message channels</a>
and their [`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects.

<div algorithm="">

Each [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object
`worker global scope` has a list of <span id="the-worker's-ports"
class="dfn" export="">the worker's ports</span>, which consists of all
the [`MessagePort`](#messageport) objects that are entangled with
another port and that have one (but only one) port owned by
`worker global scope`. This list includes the implicit
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) in the case of
<a href="#dedicatedworkerglobalscope"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:dedicatedworkerglobalscope">dedicated
workers</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

Given an <a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:environment-settings-object">environment
settings object</a> `o` when creating or obtaining a worker, the
<span id="relevant-owner-to-add" class="dfn">relevant owner to
add</span> depends on the type of
<a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-settings-object-global">global
object</a> specified by `o`. If `o`'s
<a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-settings-object-global-2">global
object</a> is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object (i.e.,
if we are creating a nested dedicated worker), then the relevant owner
is that global object. Otherwise, `o`'s
<a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-settings-object-global-3">global
object</a> is a [`Window`](#window) object, and the relevant owner is
that [`Window`](#window)'s <a href="#concept-document-window"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-document-window">associated
<code>Document</code></a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A user agent has an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
value, the <span id="between-loads-shared-worker-timeout"
class="dfn">between-loads shared worker timeout</span>, which is some
small amount of time. This represents how long the user agent allows
shared workers to survive while a page is loading, in case that page is
going to contact the shared worker again. Setting this value to greater
than zero lets user agents avoid the cost of restarting a shared worker
used by a site when the user is navigating from page to page within that
site.

A typical value for the <a href="#between-loads-shared-worker-timeout"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:between-loads-shared-worker-timeout">between-loads
shared worker timeout</a> might be 5 seconds.

A user agent has an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:implementation-defined-2"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
value, the <span id="extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout"
class="dfn">extended lifetime shared worker timeout</span>, which is
some amount of time. This represents how long the user agent allows
shared workers which the web developer has requested be given an
extended lifetime, to survive and perform work after all of their
<a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set">owners</a>
have disappeared. User agents should choose a value that is equal to the
longest lifetime that a service worker can stay alive without any
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-service-worker-client"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:service-worker-client"
data-x-internal="service-worker-client">clients</a>, and must not choose
a value that is longer than that amount of time.

A typical value for the
<a href="#extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout">extended
lifetime shared worker timeout</a> could be anywhere from 10 seconds to
5 minutes, depending on the implementation's individual policies
regarding background work being performed by an origin without a
user-visible representation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) `global` is
<span id="in-extended-lifetime-worker" class="dfn">in extended
lifetime</span> if the following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `global` is not a
    [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope), then return
    false.

2.  If `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-extended-lifetime"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-extended-lifetime">extended
    lifetime</a> is false, then return false.

3.  If `global`'s <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-2">owner
    set</a> <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-is-empty"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">is empty</a>, but has been empty for
    less than the user agent's
    <a href="#extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout-2">extended
    lifetime shared worker timeout</a>, then return true.

4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-iterate"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `owner` of `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-3">owner
    set</a>:

    1.  If `owner` is a [`Document`](#document) that is
        <a href="#fully-active"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:fully-active">fully active</a>,
        then return false.

        In this case `global` will be <a href="#active-needed-worker"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker">actively needed</a>,
        but it's not in extended lifetime.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-iterate-2"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `owner` of `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-4">owner
    set</a>:

    1.  If `owner` is a [`Document`](#document) and the amount of time
        that `owner` that has been non-<a href="#fully-active"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:fully-active-2">fully active</a>
        is less than the user agent's
        <a href="#extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout-3">extended
        lifetime shared worker timeout</a>, then return true.

    2.  If `owner` is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) that
        is <a href="#in-extended-lifetime-worker"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:in-extended-lifetime-worker">in extended
        lifetime</a>, then return true.

6.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) `global` is
<span id="active-needed-worker" class="dfn">actively needed</span> if
the following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `global` is <a href="#in-extended-lifetime-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:in-extended-lifetime-worker-2">in extended
    lifetime</a>, then return true.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-iterate-3"
    data-x-internal="list-iterate">For each</a> `owner` of `global`'s
    <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-5">owner
    set</a>:

    1.  If `owner` is a [`Document`](#document), and `owner` is
        <a href="#fully-active"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:fully-active-3">fully active</a>,
        then return true.

    2.  If `owner` is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) that
        is <a href="#active-needed-worker"
        id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-2">actively
        needed</a>, then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) `global` is
<span id="protected-worker" class="dfn">protected</span> if the
following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `global` is not <a href="#active-needed-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-3">actively
    needed</a>, then return false.

2.  If `global` is <a href="#in-extended-lifetime-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:in-extended-lifetime-worker-3">in extended
    lifetime</a>, then return true.

3.  If `global` is a
    [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope), then return
    true.

4.  If `global`'s <a href="#the-worker&#39;s-ports"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:the-worker&#39;s-ports">the worker's
    ports</a> is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-is-empty-2"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>, then return true.

5.  If `global` has outstanding timers, database transactions, or
    network connections, then return true.

6.  Return false.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) `global` is
<span id="permissible-worker" class="dfn">permissible</span> if the
following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `global`'s <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-6">owner
    set</a> is not
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-is-empty-3"
    data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a>, then return true.

2.  If `global` is <a href="#in-extended-lifetime-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:in-extended-lifetime-worker-4">in extended
    lifetime</a>, then return true.

3.  If all of the following are true:

    - `global` is a
      [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope);

    - `global`'s <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-7">owner
      set</a> has been
      <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:list-is-empty-4"
      data-x-internal="list-is-empty">empty</a> for no more than the
      user agent's <a href="#between-loads-shared-worker-timeout"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:between-loads-shared-worker-timeout-2">between-loads
      shared worker timeout</a>; and

    - the user agent has a <a href="#navigable"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:navigable">navigable</a> whose
      <a href="#nav-document"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:nav-document">active document</a> is
      not <a href="#completely-loaded"
      id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:completely-loaded">completely loaded</a>,

    then return true.

4.  Return false.

</div>

<div id="note-worker-lifetime-terminology-relationships" class="note">

<a href="#note-worker-lifetime-terminology-relationships"
class="self-link"></a>

The following relationships hold between these terms:

- Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) that is
  <a href="#in-extended-lifetime-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:in-extended-lifetime-worker-5">in extended
  lifetime</a> is <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-4">actively
  needed</a>, <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker">protected</a>, and
  <a href="#permissible-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker">permissible</a>.

- Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) that is
  <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-5">actively
  needed</a> or <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-2">protected</a> is
  <a href="#permissible-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker-2">permissible</a>.

- Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) that is
  <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-3">protected</a> is
  <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-6">actively
  needed</a>.

However, the converses do not always hold:

- A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) can be
  <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-7">actively
  needed</a> but not <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-4">protected</a>, if
  it's a dedicated worker with no outstanding async work that is still
  performing computation on behalf of a fully active owner, but whose
  corresponding [`Worker`](#worker) object has been garbage collected.
  [Because of the garbage collection](#ports-and-garbage-collection),
  the <a href="#the-worker&#39;s-ports"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:the-worker&#39;s-ports-2">ports</a>
  collection is empty, so it is no longer protected. However, its event
  loop has not yet yielded to [empty its owner
  set](#step-empty-worker-global-scope-owner-set), so it is still
  actively needed.

- A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) can be
  <a href="#permissible-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker-3">permissible</a>
  but not <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-5">protected</a> or
  <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-8">actively
  needed</a>, if all the [`Document`](#document)s in its transitive set
  of owners are in [bfcache](#note-bfcache), or if it's a
  [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope) with no current
  owners being kept alive for the duration of the
  <a href="#between-loads-shared-worker-timeout"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:between-loads-shared-worker-timeout-3">between-loads
  shared worker timeout</a>.

</div>

<div id="note-between-loads-shared-worker-timeout-lifetime"
class="note">

<a href="#note-between-loads-shared-worker-timeout-lifetime"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#between-loads-shared-worker-timeout"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:between-loads-shared-worker-timeout-4">between-loads
shared worker timeout</a> only influences the definition of
<a href="#permissible-worker"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker-4">permissible</a>, not
<a href="#protected-worker"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-6">protected</a>, and so
implementations are not required to keep shared workers alive for that
duration. Rather, they are required to close shared workers after the
timeout is reached.

In contrast, the <a href="#extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:extended-lifetime-shared-worker-timeout-4">extended
lifetime shared worker timeout</a> does influence the definition of
<a href="#protected-worker"
id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-7">protected</a>, so
implementations are required to keep shared workers alive (and not
suspended) for that duration.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) `global` is
<span id="suspendable-worker" class="dfn">suspendable</span> if the
following algorithm returns true:

1.  If `global` is <a href="#active-needed-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-9">actively
    needed</a>, then return false.

2.  If `global` is <a href="#permissible-worker"
    id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker-5">permissible</a>,
    then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

<div id="note-worker-lifetime-terminology" class="note">

<a href="#note-worker-lifetime-terminology" class="self-link"></a>

These concepts are used elsewhere in the specification's normative
requirements as follows:

- Workers get [closed as orphans](#step-closing-orphan-workers) between
  when they stop being <a href="#protected-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:protected-worker-8">protected</a> and
  when they stop being <a href="#permissible-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:permissible-worker-6">permissible</a>.

- Workers that have been closed, but keep executing, [can be
  terminated](#terminate-rampant-workers) at the user agent's
  discretion, once they stop being <a href="#active-needed-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:active-needed-worker-10">actively
  needed</a>.

- Workers get [suspended or un-suspended](#step-suspending-workers)
  based on whether they are <a href="#suspendable-worker"
  id="the-worker&#39;s-lifetime:suspendable-worker">suspendable</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">10.2.4</span> <span id="processing-model-10"></span>Processing model<a href="#worker-processing-model" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="run-a-worker" class="dfn"
export="">run a worker</span> for a script with [`Worker`](#worker) or
[`SharedWorker`](#sharedworker) object `worker`,
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="worker-processing-model:url" data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `url`,
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="worker-processing-model:environment-settings-object">environment
settings object</a> `outside settings`, [`MessagePort`](#messageport)
`outside port`, and a [`WorkerOptions`](#workeroptions) dictionary
`options`, it must run the following steps.

1.  Let `is shared` be true if `worker` is a
    [`SharedWorker`](#sharedworker) object, and false otherwise.

2.  Let `owner` be the <a href="#relevant-owner-to-add"
    id="worker-processing-model:relevant-owner-to-add">relevant owner to
    add</a> given `outside settings`.

3.  Let `unsafeWorkerCreationTime` be the
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time"
    id="worker-processing-model:unsafe-shared-current-time"
    data-x-internal="unsafe-shared-current-time">unsafe shared current
    time</a>.

4.  Let `agent` be the result of
    <a href="#obtain-a-dedicated/shared-worker-agent"
    id="worker-processing-model:obtain-a-dedicated/shared-worker-agent">obtaining
    a dedicated/shared worker agent</a> given `outside settings` and
    `is shared`. Run the rest of these steps in that agent.

5.  Let `realm execution context` be the result of
    <a href="#creating-a-new-javascript-realm"
    id="worker-processing-model:creating-a-new-javascript-realm">creating a
    new realm</a> given `agent` and the following customizations:

    - For the global object, if `is shared` is true, create a new
      [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope) object.
      Otherwise, create a new
      [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#dedicatedworkerglobalscope)
      object.

6.  Let `worker global scope` be the <a href="#concept-realm-global"
    id="worker-processing-model:concept-realm-global">global object</a>
    of `realm execution context`'s Realm component.

    This is the
    [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#dedicatedworkerglobalscope) or
    [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#sharedworkerglobalscope) object created
    in the previous step.

7.  <a href="#set-up-a-worker-environment-settings-object"
    id="worker-processing-model:set-up-a-worker-environment-settings-object">Set
    up a worker environment settings object</a> with
    `realm execution context`, `outside settings`, and
    `unsafeWorkerCreationTime`, and let `inside settings` be the result.

8.  Set `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-name"
    id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-name">name</a>
    to `options`\["[`name`](#dom-workeroptions-name)"\].

9.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="worker-processing-model:set-append"
    data-x-internal="set-append">Append</a> `owner` to
    `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
    id="worker-processing-model:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set">owner
    set</a>.

10. If `is shared` is true, then:

    1.  Set `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-origin"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-origin">constructor
        origin</a> to `outside settings`'s
        <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>.

    2.  Set `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url">constructor
        URL</a> to `url`.

    3.  Set `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-type"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-type">type</a>
        to `options`\["[`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type)"\].

    4.  Set `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-credentials"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-credentials">credentials</a>
        to
        `options`\["[`credentials`](#dom-workeroptions-credentials)"\].

    5.  Set `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-extended-lifetime"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-extended-lifetime">extended
        lifetime</a> to
        `options`\["[`extendedLifetime`](#dom-sharedworkeroptions-extendedlifetime)"\].

11. Let `destination` be "`sharedworker`" if `is shared` is true, and
    "`worker`" otherwise.

12. Obtain `script` by switching on
    `options`\["[`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type)"\]:

    "`classic`"  
    <a href="#fetch-a-classic-worker-script"
    id="worker-processing-model:fetch-a-classic-worker-script">Fetch a
    classic worker script</a> given `url`, `outside settings`,
    `destination`, `inside settings`, and with `onComplete` and
    `performFetch` as defined below.

    "`module`"  
    <a href="#fetch-a-module-worker-script-tree"
    id="worker-processing-model:fetch-a-module-worker-script-tree">Fetch a
    module worker script graph</a> given `url`, `outside settings`,
    `destination`, the value of the `credentials` member of `options`,
    `inside settings`, and with `onComplete` and `performFetch` as
    defined below.

    In both cases, let `performFetch` be the following
    <a href="#fetching-scripts-perform-fetch"
    id="worker-processing-model:fetching-scripts-perform-fetch">perform the
    fetch hook</a> given `request`,
    [`isTopLevel`](#fetching-scripts-is-top-level), and
    [`processCustomFetchResponse`](#fetching-scripts-processcustomfetchresponse):

    1.  If `isTopLevel` is false,
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-fetch"
        data-x-internal="concept-fetch">fetch</a> `request` with
        *<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body"
        data-x-internal="processresponseconsumebody">processResponseConsumeBody</a>*
        set to `processCustomFetchResponse`, and abort these steps.

    2.  Set `request`'s
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reserved-client"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-request-reserved-client"
        data-x-internal="concept-request-reserved-client">reserved client</a>
        to `inside settings`.

    3.  <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-fetch-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-fetch">Fetch</a> `request` with
        *<a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body"
        data-x-internal="processresponseconsumebody">processResponseConsumeBody</a>*
        set to the following steps given
        <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-response"
        data-x-internal="concept-response">response</a> `response` and
        null, failure, or a
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-sequence"
        id="worker-processing-model:byte-sequence"
        data-x-internal="byte-sequence">byte sequence</a> `bodyBytes`:

        1.  Set `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-url"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-url">url</a>
            to `response`'s
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-response-url"
            data-x-internal="concept-response-url">url</a>.

        2.  Set `inside settings`'s
            <a href="#concept-environment-creation-url"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-environment-creation-url">creation
            URL</a> to `response`'s
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-response-url-2"
            data-x-internal="concept-response-url">url</a>.

        3.  <a href="#initialize-worker-policy-container"
            id="worker-processing-model:initialize-worker-policy-container">Initialize
            worker global scope's policy container</a> given
            `worker global scope`, `response`, and `inside settings`.

        4.  If the <a
            href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#run-global-object-csp-initialization"
            id="worker-processing-model:run-csp-initialization-for-a-global-object"
            data-x-internal="run-csp-initialization-for-a-global-object">Run CSP
            initialization for a global object</a> algorithm returns
            "`Blocked`" when executed upon `worker global scope`, set
            `response` to a
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error"
            id="worker-processing-model:network-error"
            data-x-internal="network-error">network error</a>.
            [\[CSP\]](#refsCSP)

        5.  If `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-embedder-policy"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-embedder-policy">embedder
            policy</a>'s <a href="#embedder-policy-value-2"
            id="worker-processing-model:embedder-policy-value-2">value</a>
            is <a href="#compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="worker-processing-model:compatible-with-cross-origin-isolation">compatible
            with cross-origin isolation</a> and `is shared` is true,
            then set `agent`'s
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
            id="worker-processing-model:agent-cluster"
            data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>'s
            <a href="#agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="worker-processing-model:agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation">cross-origin
            isolation mode</a> to
            "[`logical`](#cross-origin-isolation-logical)" or
            "[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)". The one
            chosen is
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
            id="worker-processing-model:implementation-defined"
            data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>.

            This really ought to be set when the agent cluster is
            created, which requires a redesign of this section.

        6.  If the result of
            <a href="#check-a-global-object&#39;s-embedder-policy"
            id="worker-processing-model:check-a-global-object&#39;s-embedder-policy">checking
            a global object's embedder policy</a> with
            `worker global scope`, `outside settings`, and `response` is
            false, then set `response` to a
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error"
            id="worker-processing-model:network-error-2"
            data-x-internal="network-error">network error</a>.

        7.  Set `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> to true if `agent`'s
            <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters"
            id="worker-processing-model:agent-cluster-2"
            data-x-internal="agent-cluster">agent cluster</a>'s
            <a href="#agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation"
            id="worker-processing-model:agent-cluster-cross-origin-isolation-2">cross-origin
            isolation mode</a> is
            "[`concrete`](#cross-origin-isolation-concrete)".

        8.  If `is shared` is false and `owner`'s
            <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> is false, then set
            `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability-2">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> to false.

        9.  If `is shared` is false and `response`'s
            <a href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-response-url-3"
            data-x-internal="concept-response-url">url</a>'s
            <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-url-scheme"
            data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is "`data`",
            then set `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability-3">cross-origin
            isolated capability</a> to false.

            This is a conservative default for now, while we figure out
            how workers in general, and
            <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
            data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code
            id="worker-processing-model:data-protocol">data:</code></a>
            URL workers in particular (which are cross-origin from their
            owner), will be treated in the context of permissions
            policies. See [w3c/webappsec-permissions-policy issue
            \#207](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-permissions-policy/issues/207)
            for more details.

        10. Run `processCustomFetchResponse` with `response` and
            `bodyBytes`.

    In both cases, let `onComplete` given `script` be the following
    steps:

    1.  If `script` is null or if `script`'s
        <a href="#concept-script-error-to-rethrow"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-script-error-to-rethrow">error to
        rethrow</a> is non-null, then:

        1.  <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
            id="worker-processing-model:queue-a-global-task">Queue a global task</a>
            on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
            id="worker-processing-model:dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM
            manipulation task source</a> given `worker`'s
            <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-relevant-global">relevant global
            object</a> to
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
            id="worker-processing-model:concept-event-fire"
            data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
            [`error`](#event-error) at `worker`.

        2.  Run the <a href="#environment-discarding-steps"
            id="worker-processing-model:environment-discarding-steps">environment
            discarding steps</a> for `inside settings`.

        3.  Abort these steps.

    2.  Associate `worker` with `worker global scope`.

    3.  Let `inside port` be a
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
        id="worker-processing-model:new" data-x-internal="new">new</a>
        [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object in `inside settings`'s
        <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
        id="worker-processing-model:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm">realm</a>.

    4.  If `is shared` is false, then:

        1.  Set `inside port`'s <a href="#message-event-target"
            id="worker-processing-model:message-event-target">message event
            target</a> to `worker global scope`.

        2.  Set `worker global scope`'s
            <a href="#inside-port" id="worker-processing-model:inside-port">inside
            port</a> to `inside port`.

    5.  <a href="#entangle" id="worker-processing-model:entangle">Entangle</a>
        `outside port` and `inside port`.

    6.  Create a new [`WorkerLocation`](#workerlocation) object and
        associate it with `worker global scope`.

    7.  <div id="step-closing-orphan-workers">

        *Closing orphan workers*: Start monitoring `worker global scope`
        such that no sooner than it stops being
        <a href="#protected-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:protected-worker">protected</a>, and
        no later than it stops being <a href="#permissible-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:permissible-worker">permissible</a>,
        `worker global scope`'s <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
        id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing">closing</a>
        flag is set to true.

        </div>

    8.  <div id="step-suspending-workers">

        *Suspending workers*: Start monitoring `worker global scope`,
        such that whenever `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
        id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-2">closing</a>
        flag is false and it is <a href="#suspendable-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:suspendable-worker">suspendable</a>,
        the user agent suspends execution of script in
        `worker global scope` until such time as either the
        <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
        id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-3">closing</a>
        flag switches to true or `worker global scope` stops being
        <a href="#suspendable-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:suspendable-worker-2">suspendable</a>.

        </div>

    9.  Set `inside settings`'s
        <a href="#concept-environment-execution-ready-flag"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-environment-execution-ready-flag">execution
        ready flag</a>.

    10. If `script` is a <a href="#classic-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:classic-script">classic script</a>,
        then <a href="#run-a-classic-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:run-a-classic-script">run the classic
        script</a> `script`. Otherwise, it is a <a href="#module-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:module-script">module script</a>;
        <a href="#run-a-module-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:run-a-module-script">run the module
        script</a> `script`.

        In addition to the usual possibilities of returning a value or
        failing due to an exception, this could be
        <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:abort-a-running-script">prematurely
        aborted</a> by the <a href="#terminate-a-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:terminate-a-worker">terminate a worker</a>
        algorithm defined below.

    11. Enable `outside port`'s <a href="#port-message-queue"
        id="worker-processing-model:port-message-queue">port message queue</a>.

    12. If `is shared` is false, enable the
        <a href="#port-message-queue"
        id="worker-processing-model:port-message-queue-2">port message queue</a>
        of the worker's implicit port.

    13. If `is shared` is true, then <a href="#queue-a-global-task"
        id="worker-processing-model:queue-a-global-task-2">queue a global
        task</a> on the <a href="#dom-manipulation-task-source"
        id="worker-processing-model:dom-manipulation-task-source-2">DOM
        manipulation task source</a> given `worker global scope` to
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-event-fire-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
        [`connect`](#event-workerglobalscope-connect) at
        `worker global scope`, using [`MessageEvent`](#messageevent),
        with the [`data`](#dom-messageevent-data) attribute initialized
        to the empty string, the [`ports`](#dom-messageevent-ports)
        attribute initialized to a new
        <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type"
        id="worker-processing-model:frozen-array"
        data-x-internal="frozen-array">frozen array</a> containing
        `inside port`, and the [`source`](#dom-messageevent-source)
        attribute initialized to `inside port`.

    14. Enable the
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-client-message-queue"
        id="worker-processing-model:dfn-client-message-queue"
        data-x-internal="dfn-client-message-queue">client message queue</a>
        of the
        <a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer"
        data-x-internal="serviceworkercontainer"><code
        id="worker-processing-model:serviceworkercontainer">ServiceWorkerContainer</code></a>
        object whose associated <a
        href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer-service-worker-client"
        id="worker-processing-model:serviceworkercontainer-service-worker-client"
        data-x-internal="serviceworkercontainer-service-worker-client">service
        worker client</a> is `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
        id="worker-processing-model:relevant-settings-object">relevant settings
        object</a>.

    15. *Event loop*: Run the <a href="#responsible-event-loop"
        id="worker-processing-model:responsible-event-loop">responsible event
        loop</a> specified by `inside settings` until it is destroyed.

        The handling of events or the execution of callbacks by
        <a href="#concept-task"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-task">tasks</a> run by the
        <a href="#event-loop" id="worker-processing-model:event-loop">event
        loop</a> might get <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
        id="worker-processing-model:abort-a-running-script-2">prematurely
        aborted</a> by the <a href="#terminate-a-worker"
        id="worker-processing-model:terminate-a-worker-2">terminate a worker</a>
        algorithm defined below.

        The worker processing model remains on this step until the event
        loop is destroyed, which happens after the
        <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
        id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-4">closing</a>
        flag is set to true, as described in the
        <a href="#event-loop" id="worker-processing-model:event-loop-2">event
        loop</a> processing model.

    16. <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-clear"
        id="worker-processing-model:map-clear"
        data-x-internal="map-clear">Clear</a> the
        `worker global scope`'s <a href="#map-of-active-timers"
        id="worker-processing-model:map-of-active-timers">map of active
        timers</a>.

    17. Disentangle all the ports in the list of
        <a href="#the-worker&#39;s-ports"
        id="worker-processing-model:the-worker&#39;s-ports">the worker's
        ports</a>.

    18. <div id="step-empty-worker-global-scope-owner-set">

        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-empty"
        id="worker-processing-model:list-empty"
        data-x-internal="list-empty">Empty</a> `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
        id="worker-processing-model:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-2">owner
        set</a>.

        </div>

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="terminate-a-worker" class="dfn"
export="">terminate a worker</span>, it must run the following steps
<a href="#in-parallel" id="worker-processing-model:in-parallel">in
parallel</a> with the worker's main loop (the
"<a href="#run-a-worker" id="worker-processing-model:run-a-worker">run a
worker</a>" processing model defined above):

1.  Set the worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object's
    <a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
    id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-5">closing</a>
    flag to true.

2.  If there are any <a href="#concept-task"
    id="worker-processing-model:concept-task-2">tasks</a> queued in the
    [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object's
    <a href="#relevant-agent"
    id="worker-processing-model:relevant-agent">relevant agent</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-agent-event-loop"
    id="worker-processing-model:concept-agent-event-loop">event loop</a>'s
    <a href="#task-queue" id="worker-processing-model:task-queue">task
    queues</a>, discard them without processing them.

3.  <a href="#abort-a-running-script"
    id="worker-processing-model:abort-a-running-script-3">Abort the
    script</a> currently running in the worker.

4.  If the worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object is
    actually a
    [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#dedicatedworkerglobalscope) object
    (i.e. the worker is a dedicated worker), then empty the
    <a href="#port-message-queue"
    id="worker-processing-model:port-message-queue-3">port message queue</a>
    of the port that the worker's implicit port is entangled with.

</div>

User agents may invoke the <a href="#terminate-a-worker"
id="worker-processing-model:terminate-a-worker-3">terminate a worker</a>
algorithm when a worker stops being <a href="#active-needed-worker"
id="worker-processing-model:active-needed-worker">actively needed</a>
and the worker continues executing even after its
<a href="#dom-workerglobalscope-closing"
id="worker-processing-model:dom-workerglobalscope-closing-6">closing</a>
flag was set to true.

#### <span class="secno">10.2.5</span> Runtime script errors<a href="#runtime-script-errors-2" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

Whenever an uncaught runtime script error occurs in one of the worker's
scripts, if the error did not occur while handling a previous script
error, the user agent will <a href="#report-an-exception"
id="runtime-script-errors-2:report-an-exception">report</a> it for the
worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#workerglobalscope) object.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">10.2.6</span> Creating workers<a href="#creating-workers" class="self-link"></a>

##### <span class="secno">10.2.6.2</span> Script settings for workers<a href="#script-settings-for-workers" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="set-up-a-worker-environment-settings-object"
class="dfn">set up a worker environment settings object</span>, given a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts"
id="script-settings-for-workers:javascript-execution-context"
data-x-internal="javascript-execution-context">JavaScript execution
context</a> `execution context`, an
<a href="#environment-settings-object"
id="script-settings-for-workers:environment-settings-object">environment
settings object</a> `outside settings`, and a number
`unsafeWorkerCreationTime`:

1.  Let `realm` be the value of `execution context`'s Realm component.

2.  Let `worker global scope` be `realm`'s
    <a href="#concept-realm-global"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-realm-global">global object</a>.

3.  Let `origin` be a unique <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-origin-opaque">opaque origin</a>
    if `worker global scope`'s <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-url">url</a>'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-url-scheme"
    data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is "`data`";
    otherwise `outside settings`'s
    <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-origin">origin</a>.

4.  Let `settings object` be a new
    <a href="#environment-settings-object"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:environment-settings-object-2">environment
    settings object</a> whose algorithms are defined as follows:

    The <a href="#realm-execution-context"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:realm-execution-context">realm execution
    context</a>  
    Return `execution context`.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-module-map"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-module-map">module
    map</a>  
    Return `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-module-map"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-module-map">module
    map</a>.

    The <a href="#api-base-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:api-base-url">API base URL</a>  
    Return `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-url-2">url</a>.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-origin-2">origin</a>  
    Return `origin`.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-has-cross-site-ancestor"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-has-cross-site-ancestor">has
    cross-site ancestry</a>  
    1.  If `outside settings`'s
        <a href="#concept-settings-object-has-cross-site-ancestor"
        id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-has-cross-site-ancestor-2">has
        cross-site ancestor</a> is true, then return true.

    2.  If `worker global scope`'s
        <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-url"
        id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-url-3">url</a>'s
        <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme"
        id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-url-scheme-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-url-scheme">scheme</a> is "`data`",
        then return true.

    3.  Return false.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-policy-container"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-policy-container">policy
    container</a>  
    Return `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-policy-container"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-policy-container">policy
    container</a>.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
    isolated capability</a>  
    Return `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability">cross-origin
    isolated capability</a>.

    The <a href="#concept-settings-object-time-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-settings-object-time-origin">time
    origin</a>  
    Return the result of
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:coarsen-time"
    data-x-internal="coarsen-time">coarsening</a>
    `unsafeWorkerCreationTime` with `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-workerglobalscope-cross-origin-isolated-capability-2">cross-origin
    isolated capability</a>.

5.  Set `settings object`'s <a href="#concept-environment-id"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-id">id</a> to a
    new unique opaque string,
    <a href="#concept-environment-creation-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-creation-url">creation
    URL</a> to `worker global scope`'s
    <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:url" data-x-internal="url">url</a>,
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-creation-url"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-top-level-creation-url">top-level
    creation URL</a> to null,
    <a href="#concept-environment-target-browsing-context"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-target-browsing-context">target
    browsing context</a> to null, and
    <a href="#concept-environment-active-service-worker"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-active-service-worker">active
    service worker</a> to null.

6.  If `worker global scope` is a
    [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#dedicatedworkerglobalscope) object,
    then set `settings object`'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-top-level-origin">top-level
    origin</a> to `outside settings`'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-top-level-origin-2">top-level
    origin</a>.

7.  Otherwise, set `settings object`'s
    <a href="#concept-environment-top-level-origin"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:concept-environment-top-level-origin-3">top-level
    origin</a> to an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="script-settings-for-workers:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    value.

    See [Client-Side Storage
    Partitioning](https://privacycg.github.io/storage-partitioning/) for
    the latest on properly defining this.

8.  Set `realm`'s \[\[HostDefined\]\] field to `settings object`.

9.  Return `settings object`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">10.2.6.3</span> Dedicated workers and the [`Worker`](#worker) interface<a href="#dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface"
class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

**✔**MDN

<div class="feature">

[Worker](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Worker "The Worker interface of the Web Workers API represents a background task that can be created via script, which can send messages back to its creator.")

Support in all current engines.

Android?</span><span class="safari_ios yes">Safari
iOS5+</span><span class="chrome_android unknown">Chrome
Android?</span><span class="webview_android unknown">WebView
Android?</span><span class="samsunginternet_android unknown">Samsung
Internet?</span><span class="opera_android yes">Opera Android11+</span>

</div>

</div>

</div>

``` idl
[Exposed=(Window,DedicatedWorker,SharedWorker)]
interface Worker : EventTarget {
  constructor((TrustedScriptURL or USVString) scriptURL, optional WorkerOptions options = {});

  undefined terminate();

  undefined postMessage(any message, sequence<object> transfer);
  undefined postMessage(any message, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});
};

dictionary WorkerOptions {
  DOMString name = "";
  WorkerType type = "classic";
  RequestCredentials credentials = "same-origin"; // credentials is only used if type is "module"
};

enum WorkerType { "classic", "module" };

Worker includes AbstractWorker;
Worker includes MessageEventTarget;
```

`worker`` = new `<a href="#dom-worker" id="dom-worker-dev"><code>Worker</code></a>`(``scriptURL`` [, ``options`` ])`

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped before">

**✔**MDN

`options` can contain the following values:

- [`name`](#dom-workeroptions-name) can be used to define the
  <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-name"

  of that global environment, primarily for debugging purposes.

- [`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type) can be used to load the new global
  environment from `scriptURL` as a JavaScript module, by setting it to
  the value "`module`".

- [`credentials`](#dom-workeroptions-credentials) can be used to specify
  how `scriptURL` is fetched, but only if
  [`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type) is set to "`module`".

id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:dom-structuredserializeoptions-transfer"><code>transfer</code></a>` } ])`

Clones `message` and transmits it to `worker`'s global environment.
`transfer` can be passed as a list of objects that are to be transferred
rather than cloned.

Each [`Worker`](#worker) object has an associated
<span id="outside-port" class="dfn" dfn-for="Worker">outside port</span>
(a [`MessagePort`](#messageport)). This port is part of a channel that
is set up when the worker is created, but it is not exposed. This object
must never be garbage collected before the [`Worker`](#worker) object.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-worker-terminate" class="dfn" dfn-for="Worker"
dfn-type="method">`terminate()`</span> method steps are to
<a href="#terminate-a-worker"
id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:terminate-a-worker">terminate
a worker</a> given <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s worker.

dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``transfer``)`</span> and

dfn-type="method">`postMessage(``message``, ``options``)`</span> methods
on [`Worker`](#worker) objects act as if, when invoked, they immediately
invoked the respective
[`postMessage(``message``, ``transfer``)`](#dom-messageport-postmessage)
and
[`postMessage(``message``, ``options``)`](#dom-messageport-postmessage-options)
on <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#outside-port"
id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:outside-port">outside
port</a>, with the same arguments, and returned the same return value.

</div>

<div class="example">

The [`postMessage()`](#dom-worker-postmessage) method's first argument
can be structured data:

``` js
worker.postMessage({opcode: 'activate', device: 1938, parameters: [23, 102]});
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-worker" class="dfn" dfn-for="Worker"
dfn-type="constructor">`new Worker(``scriptURL``, ``options``)`</span>
constructor steps are:

1.  Let `compliantScriptURL` be the result of invoking the <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:tt-getcompliantstring"
    data-x-internal="tt-getcompliantstring">get trusted type compliant
    string</a> algorithm with <a
    href="https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscripturl"
    data-x-internal="tt-trustedscripturl"><code
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:tt-trustedscripturl-2">TrustedScriptURL</code></a>,
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-3"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#concept-relevant-global"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:concept-relevant-global">relevant
    global object</a>, `scriptURL`, "`Worker constructor`", and
    "`script`".

2.  Let `outsideSettings` be
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-4"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
    <a href="#relevant-settings-object"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:relevant-settings-object">relevant
    settings object</a>.

3.  Let `workerURL` be the result of <a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:encoding-parsing-a-url">encoding-parsing
    a URL</a> given `compliantScriptURL`, relative to `outsideSettings`.

    Any <a href="#same-origin"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:same-origin">same-origin</a>
    URL (including
    <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#DefinitionOfScheme"
    data-x-internal="blob-protocol"><code
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:blob-protocol">blob:</code></a>
    URLs) can be used.
    <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2"
    data-x-internal="data-protocol"><code
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:data-protocol">data:</code></a>
    URLs can also be used, but they create a worker with an
    <a href="#concept-origin-opaque"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:concept-origin-opaque">opaque
    origin</a>.

4.  If `workerURL` is failure, then throw a
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:syntaxerror"
    data-x-internal="syntaxerror">"<code>SyntaxError</code>"</a>
    <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException"
    data-x-internal="domexception"><code
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:domexception">DOMException</code></a>.

5.  Let `outsidePort` be a <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:new"
    data-x-internal="new">new</a> [`MessagePort`](#messageport) in
    `outsideSettings`'s
    <a href="#environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:environment-settings-object&#39;s-realm">realm</a>.

6.  Set `outsidePort`'s <a href="#message-event-target"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:message-event-target">message
    event target</a> to <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-5"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

7.  Set <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-6"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s <a href="#outside-port"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:outside-port-2">outside
    port</a> to `outsidePort`.

8.  Let `worker` be <a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:this-7"
    data-x-internal="this">this</a>.

9.  Run this step <a href="#in-parallel"
    id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:in-parallel">in
    parallel</a>:

    1.  <a href="#run-a-worker"
        id="dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface:run-a-worker">Run a
        worker</a> given `worker`, `workerURL`, `outsideSettings`,
        `outsidePort`, and `options`.

</div>

Returns a new [`SharedWorker`](#sharedworker) object. `scriptURL` will
be fetched and executed in the background, creating a new global
environment for which `sharedWorker` represents the communication
channel. `name` can be used to define the
<a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-name"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-workerglobalscope-name">name</a>
of that global environment.

`sharedWorker`` = new `<a href="#dom-sharedworker"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:dom-sharedworker-2"><code>SharedWorker</code></a>`(``scriptURL`` [, ``options`` ])`

Returns a new [`SharedWorker`](#sharedworker) object. `scriptURL` will
be fetched and executed in the background, creating a new global
environment for which `sharedWorker` represents the communication
channel.

`options` can contain the following values:

- [`name`](#dom-workeroptions-name) can be used to define the
  <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-name"
  id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-workerglobalscope-name-2">name</a>
  of that global environment.

- [`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type) can be used to load the new global
  environment from `scriptURL` as a JavaScript module, by setting it to
  the value "`module`".

- [`credentials`](#dom-workeroptions-credentials) can be used to specify
  how `scriptURL` is fetched, but only if
  [`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type) is set to "`module`".

- [`extendedLifetime`](#dom-sharedworkeroptions-extendedlifetime) can be
  set to request that the newly-created global environment be given
  extra time to perform its operations even after all of its
  <a href="#concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set"
  id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set">owners</a>
  have disappeared. This can be useful, for example, for performing
  asynchronous work after page unload.

Note that attempting to construct a shared worker with `options` whose
[`type`](#dom-workeroptions-type),
[`credentials`](#dom-workeroptions-credentials), or
[`extendedLifetime`](#dom-sharedworkeroptions-extendedlifetime) values
mismatch those of an existing shared worker with the same
<a href="#concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-sharedworkerglobalscope-constructor-url">constructor
URL</a> and <a href="#concept-workerglobalscope-name"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-workerglobalscope-name-3">name</a>,
will cause the returned `sharedWorker` to fire an
[`error`](#event-error) event and not connect to the existing shared
worker.

Returns `sharedWorker`'s [`MessagePort`](#messageport) object which can
be used to communicate with the global environment.

A user agent has an associated <span id="shared-worker-manager"
class="dfn">shared worker manager</span> which is the result of
<a href="#starting-a-new-parallel-queue"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:starting-a-new-parallel-queue">starting
a new parallel queue</a>.

Each user agent has a single <a href="#shared-worker-manager"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:shared-worker-manager">shared
worker manager</a> for simplicity. Implementations could use one per
<a href="#concept-origin"
id="shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface:concept-origin">origin</a>;
that would not be observably different and enables more concurrency.

<span id="concept-sharedworker-port" class="dfn">port</span>, a
[`MessagePort`](#messageport) set when the object is created.

dfn-type="attribute">`port`</span> getter steps are to return
