id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:list-of-active-formatting-elements-3">list
of active formatting elements</a> (it also switches to the
"<a href="#parsing-main-intd"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intd">in cell</a>"
<a href="#insertion-mode"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:insertion-mode-3">insertion mode</a>).

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#the-td-element)

The <a href="#concept-parser-marker"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:concept-parser-marker-2">marker</a>
means that when the "aaa" character tokens are seen, no
[`b`](#the-b-element) element is created to hold the resulting
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text">Text</code></a> node:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#the-td-element)
            - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
              data-x-internal="text"><code
              id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-2">#text</code></a>:
              aaa

The end tags are handled in a straight-forward manner; after handling
them, the <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:stack-of-open-elements-3">stack of open
elements</a> has on it the elements [`html`](#the-html-element),
[`body`](#the-body-element), [`table`](#the-table-element), and
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element); the
<a href="#list-of-active-formatting-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:list-of-active-formatting-elements-4">list
of active formatting elements</a> still has the [`b`](#the-b-element)
element in it (the <a href="#concept-parser-marker"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:concept-parser-marker-3">marker</a>
having been removed by the "td" end tag token); and the
<a href="#insertion-mode"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:insertion-mode-4">insertion mode</a> is
"<a href="#parsing-main-intbody"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intbody-2">in table
body</a>".

Thus it is that the "bbb" character tokens are found. These trigger the
"<a href="#parsing-main-intabletext"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intabletext">in table
text</a>" insertion mode to be used (with the
<a href="#original-insertion-mode"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:original-insertion-mode">original
insertion mode</a> set to "<a href="#parsing-main-intbody"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intbody-3">in table
body</a>"). The character tokens are collected, and when the next token
(the [`table`](#the-table-element) element end tag) is seen, they are
processed as a group. Since they are not all spaces, they are handled as
per the "anything else" rules in the "<a href="#parsing-main-intable"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intable-2">in table</a>"
insertion mode, which defer to the "<a href="#parsing-main-inbody"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-inbody">in body</a>"
insertion mode but with <a href="#foster-parent"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:foster-parent-2">foster parenting</a>.

When <a href="#reconstruct-the-active-formatting-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:reconstruct-the-active-formatting-elements">the
active formatting elements are reconstructed</a>, a
[`b`](#the-b-element) element is created and <a href="#foster-parent"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:foster-parent-3">foster parented</a>,
and then the "bbb" <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-3">Text</code></a> node is appended
to it:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-4">#text</code></a>: bbb
    - [`table`](#the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#the-td-element)
            - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
              data-x-internal="text"><code
              id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-5">#text</code></a>:
              aaa

The <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:stack-of-open-elements-4">stack of open
elements</a> has on it the elements [`html`](#the-html-element),
[`body`](#the-body-element), [`table`](#the-table-element),
[`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), and the new [`b`](#the-b-element) (again,
note that this doesn't match the resulting tree!); the
<a href="#list-of-active-formatting-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:list-of-active-formatting-elements-5">list
of active formatting elements</a> has the new [`b`](#the-b-element)
element in it; and the <a href="#insertion-mode"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:insertion-mode-5">insertion mode</a> is
still "<a href="#parsing-main-intbody"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:parsing-main-intbody-4">in table
body</a>".

Had the character tokens been only
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:space-characters"
data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> instead of
"bbb", then that
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:space-characters-2"
data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a> would just be
appended to the [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element) element.

Finally, the [`table`](#the-table-element) is closed by a "table" end
tag. This pops all the nodes from the <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:stack-of-open-elements-5">stack of open
elements</a> up to and including the [`table`](#the-table-element)
element, but it doesn't affect the
<a href="#list-of-active-formatting-elements"
id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:list-of-active-formatting-elements-6">list
of active formatting elements</a>, so the "ccc" character tokens after
the table result in yet another [`b`](#the-b-element) element being
created, this time after the table:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-6">#text</code></a>: bbb
    - [`table`](#the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#the-td-element)
            - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
              data-x-internal="text"><code
              id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-7">#text</code></a>:
              aaa
    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="unexpected-markup-in-tables:text-8">#text</code></a>: ccc

##### <span class="secno">13.2.10.4</span> Scripts that modify the page as it is being parsed<a href="#scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed"
class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

Consider the following markup, which for this example we will assume is
the document with <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:url"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `https://example.com/inner`, being
rendered as the content of an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) in another
document with the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:url-2"
data-x-internal="url">URL</a> `https://example.com/outer`:

``` html
<div id=a>
 <script>
  var div = document.getElementById('a');
  parent.document.body.appendChild(div);
 </script>
 <script>
  alert(document.URL);
 </script>
</div>
<script>
 alert(document.URL);
</script>
```

Up to the first "script" end tag, before the script is parsed, the
result is relatively straightforward:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`div`](#the-div-element)
      <span class="t2">[`id`](#the-id-attribute)="`a`"</span>
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:text">#text</code></a>:
      - [`script`](#the-script-element)
        - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
          data-x-internal="text"><code
          id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:text-2">#text</code></a>:
          var div = document.getElementById('a'); ⏎
          parent.document.body.appendChild(div);

After the script is parsed, though, the [`div`](#the-div-element)
element and its child [`script`](#the-script-element) element are gone:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)

They are, at this point, in the [`Document`](#document) of the
aforementioned outer <a href="#browsing-context"
id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:browsing-context">browsing
context</a>. However, the <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:stack-of-open-elements">stack
of open elements</a> *still contains the [`div`](#the-div-element)
element*.

Thus, when the second [`script`](#the-script-element) element is parsed,
it is inserted *into the outer [`Document`](#document) object*.

Those parsed into different [`Document`](#document)s than the one the
parser was created for do not execute, so the first alert does not show.

Once the [`div`](#the-div-element) element's end tag is parsed, the
[`div`](#the-div-element) element is popped off the stack, and so the
next [`script`](#the-script-element) element is in the inner
[`Document`](#document):

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`script`](#the-script-element)
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="scripts-that-modify-the-page-as-it-is-being-parsed:text-3">#text</code></a>:
        alert(document.URL);

This script does execute, resulting in an alert that says
"https://example.com/inner".

##### <span class="secno">13.2.10.5</span> The execution of scripts that are moving across multiple documents<a
href="#the-execution-of-scripts-that-are-moving-across-multiple-documents"
class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

Elaborating on the example in the previous section, consider the case
where the second [`script`](#the-script-element) element is an external
script (i.e. one with a [`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute). Since the
element was not in the parser's [`Document`](#document) when it was
created, that external script is not even downloaded.

In a case where a [`script`](#the-script-element) element with a
[`src`](#attr-script-src) attribute is parsed normally into its parser's
[`Document`](#document), but while the external script is being
downloaded, the element is moved to another document, the script
continues to download, but does not execute.

In general, moving [`script`](#the-script-element) elements between
[`Document`](#document)s is considered a bad practice.

##### <span class="secno">13.2.10.6</span> Unclosed formatting elements<a href="#unclosed-formatting-elements" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is non-normative.*

The following markup shows how nested formatting elements (such as
[`b`](#the-b-element)) get collected and continue to be applied even as
the elements they are contained in are closed, but that excessive
duplicates are thrown away.

``` html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<p><b class=x><b class=x><b><b class=x><b class=x><b>X
<p>X
<p><b><b class=x><b>X
<p></b></b></b></b></b></b>X
```

The resulting DOM tree is as follows:

- DOCTYPE: `html`
- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`p`](#the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#the-b-element)
        <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
        - [`b`](#the-b-element)
          <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
          - [`b`](#the-b-element)
            - [`b`](#the-b-element)
              <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
              - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
                - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                  - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
                    data-x-internal="text"><code
                    id="unclosed-formatting-elements:text">#text</code></a>:
                    X⏎
    - [`p`](#the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#the-b-element)
        <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
        - [`b`](#the-b-element)
          - [`b`](#the-b-element)
            <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
            - [`b`](#the-b-element)
              <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
              - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
                  data-x-internal="text"><code
                  id="unclosed-formatting-elements:text-2">#text</code></a>:
                  X⏎
    - [`p`](#the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#the-b-element)
        <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
        - [`b`](#the-b-element)
          - [`b`](#the-b-element)
            <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
            - [`b`](#the-b-element)
              <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
              - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                  - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                    <span class="t2">[`class`](#classes)="`x`"</span>
                    - [`b`](#the-b-element)
                      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
                        data-x-internal="text"><code
                        id="unclosed-formatting-elements:text-3">#text</code></a>:
                        X⏎
    - [`p`](#the-p-element)
      - <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="unclosed-formatting-elements:text-4">#text</code></a>: X⏎

Note how the second [`p`](#the-p-element) element in the markup has no
explicit [`b`](#the-b-element) elements, but in the resulting DOM, up to
three of each kind of formatting element (in this case three
[`b`](#the-b-element) elements with the class attribute, and two
unadorned [`b`](#the-b-element) elements) get reconstructed before the
element's "X".

Also note how this means that in the final paragraph only six
[`b`](#the-b-element) end tags are needed to completely clear the
<a href="#list-of-active-formatting-elements"
id="unclosed-formatting-elements:list-of-active-formatting-elements">list
of active formatting elements</a>, even though nine
[`b`](#the-b-element) start tags have been seen up to this point.

### <span class="secno">13.3</span> Serializing HTML fragments<a href="#serialising-html-fragments" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

For the purposes of the following algorithm, an element
<span id="serializes-as-void" class="dfn">serializes as void</span> if
its element type is one of the <a href="#void-elements"
id="serialising-html-fragments:void-elements">void elements</a>, or is
[`basefont`](#basefont), [`bgsound`](#bgsound), [`frame`](#frame),
[`keygen`](#keygen), or [`param`](#param).

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The following steps form the
<span id="html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm" class="dfn"
export="">HTML fragment serialization algorithm</span>. The algorithm
takes as input a DOM
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="serialising-html-fragments:element">Element</code></a>,
[`Document`](#document), or
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
id="serialising-html-fragments:documentfragment">DocumentFragment</code></a>
referred to as `the node`, a boolean `serializableShadowRoots`, and a
`sequence<ShadowRoot>` `shadowRoots`, and returns a string.

This algorithm serializes the *children* of the node being serialized,
not the node itself.

1.  If `the node` <a href="#serializes-as-void"
    id="serialising-html-fragments:serializes-as-void">serializes as
    void</a>, then return the empty string.

2.  Let `s` be a string, and initialize it to the empty string.

3.  If `the node` is a [`template`](#the-template-element) element, then
    let `the node` instead be the [`template`](#the-template-element)
    element's <a href="#template-contents"
    id="serialising-html-fragments:template-contents">template contents</a>
    (a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documentfragment"
    data-x-internal="documentfragment"><code
    id="serialising-html-fragments:documentfragment-2">DocumentFragment</code></a>
    node).

4.  If `current node` is a
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-shadow-host"
    id="serialising-html-fragments:shadow-host"
    data-x-internal="shadow-host">shadow host</a>, then:

    1.  Let `shadow` be `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-shadow-root"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-shadow-root"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-shadow-root">shadow root</a>.

    2.  If one of the following is true:

        - `serializableShadowRoots` is true and `shadow`'s
          <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-serializable"
          id="serialising-html-fragments:shadow-serializable"
          data-x-internal="shadow-serializable">serializable</a> is
          true; or

        - `shadowRoots` contains `shadow`,

        then:

        1.  Append "`<template shadowrootmode="`".

        2.  If `shadow`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-mode"
            id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-shadow-root-mode"
            data-x-internal="concept-shadow-root-mode">mode</a> is
            "`open`", then append "`open`". Otherwise, append
            "`closed`".

        3.  Append "`"`".

        4.  If `shadow`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-delegates-focus"
            id="serialising-html-fragments:delegates-focus"
            data-x-internal="delegates-focus">delegates focus</a> is
            set, then append "` shadowrootdelegatesfocus=""`".

        5.  If `shadow`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-serializable"
            id="serialising-html-fragments:shadow-serializable-2"
            data-x-internal="shadow-serializable">serializable</a> is
            set, then append "` shadowrootserializable=""`".

        6.  If `shadow`'s
            <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-clonable"
            id="serialising-html-fragments:clonable"
            data-x-internal="clonable">clonable</a> is set, then append
            "` shadowrootclonable=""`".

        7.  Let `shouldAppendRegistryAttribute` be the result of running
            these steps:

            1.  Let `documentRegistry` be `shadow`'s
                <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
                id="serialising-html-fragments:node-document"
                data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>'s
                <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-custom-element-registry"
                id="serialising-html-fragments:document-custom-element-registry"
                data-x-internal="document-custom-element-registry">custom element
                registry</a>.

            2.  Let `shadowRegistry` be `shadow`'s <a
                href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadowroot-custom-element-registry"
                id="serialising-html-fragments:shadow-root-custom-element-registry"
                data-x-internal="shadow-root-custom-element-registry">custom element
                registry</a>.

            3.  If `documentRegistry` is null and `shadowRegistry` is
                null, then return false.

            4.  If `documentRegistry` <a
                href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#is-a-global-custom-element-registry"
                id="serialising-html-fragments:is-a-global-custom-element-registry"
                data-x-internal="is-a-global-custom-element-registry">is a global custom
                element registry</a> and `shadowRegistry` <a
                href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#is-a-global-custom-element-registry"
                id="serialising-html-fragments:is-a-global-custom-element-registry-2"
                data-x-internal="is-a-global-custom-element-registry">is a global custom
                element registry</a>, then return false.

            5.  Return true.

        8.  If `shouldAppendRegistryAttribute` is true, then append
            "` shadowrootcustomelementregistry=""`".

        9.  Append "`>`".

        10. Append the value of running the
            <a href="#html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm"
            id="serialising-html-fragments:html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm">HTML
            fragment serialization algorithm</a> with `shadow`,
            `serializableShadowRoots`, and `shadowRoots` (thus recursing
            into this algorithm for that element).

        11. Append "`</template>`".

5.  For each child node of `the node`, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="serialising-html-fragments:tree-order"
    data-x-internal="tree-order">tree order</a>, run the following
    steps:

    1.  Let `current node` be the child node being processed.

    2.  Append the appropriate string from the following list to `s`:

        If `current node` is an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
        data-x-internal="element"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:element-2">Element</code></a>  
        If `current node` is an element in the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:html-namespace-2"
        data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>, the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#mathml-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:mathml-namespace"
        data-x-internal="mathml-namespace">MathML namespace</a>, or the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#svg-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:svg-namespace"
        data-x-internal="svg-namespace">SVG namespace</a>, then let
        `tagname` be `current node`'s local name. Otherwise, let
        `tagname` be `current node`'s qualified name.

        Append a U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character (\<), followed by
        `tagname`.

        For <a href="#html-elements"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:html-elements">HTML elements</a>
        created by the
        <a href="#html-parser" id="serialising-html-fragments:html-parser">HTML
        parser</a> or
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement"
        data-x-internal="dom-document-createelement"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:dom-document-createelement">createElement()</code></a>,
        `tagname` will be lowercase.

        If `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>
        is not null, and the element does not have an [`is`](#attr-is)
        attribute in its attribute list, then append "` is="`", followed
        by `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>
        <a href="#escapingString"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:escapingString">escaped as described
        below</a> in *attribute mode*, followed by a U+0022 QUOTATION
        MARK character (").

        For each attribute that the element has, append a U+0020 SPACE
        character, the <a href="#attribute&#39;s-serialised-name"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:attribute&#39;s-serialised-name">attribute's
        serialized name as described below</a>, a U+003D EQUALS SIGN
        character (=), a U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character ("), the
        attribute's value, <a href="#escapingString"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:escapingString-2">escaped as described
        below</a> in *attribute mode*, and a second U+0022 QUOTATION
        MARK character (").

        An <span id="attribute's-serialised-name"
        class="dfn">attribute's serialized name</span> for the purposes
        of the previous paragraph must be determined as follows:

        If the attribute has no namespace  
        The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's local name.

        For attributes on <a href="#html-elements"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:html-elements-2">HTML elements</a>
        set by the <a href="#html-parser"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:html-parser-2">HTML parser</a> or
        by
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-element-setattribute"
        data-x-internal="dom-element-setattribute"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:dom-element-setattribute">setAttribute()</code></a>,
        the local name will be lowercase.

        If the attribute is in the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:xml-namespace"
        data-x-internal="xml-namespace">XML namespace</a>  
        The attribute's serialized name is "`xml:`" followed by the
        attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlns-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:xmlns-namespace"
        data-x-internal="xmlns-namespace">XMLNS namespace</a> and the attribute's local name is `xmlns`  
        The attribute's serialized name is "`xmlns`".

        If the attribute is in the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlns-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:xmlns-namespace-2"
        data-x-internal="xmlns-namespace">XMLNS namespace</a> and the attribute's local name is not `xmlns`  
        The attribute's serialized name is "`xmlns:`" followed by the
        attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#xlink-namespace"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:xlink-namespace"
        data-x-internal="xlink-namespace">XLink namespace</a>  
        The attribute's serialized name is "`xlink:`" followed by the
        attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in some other namespace  
        The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's qualified
        name.

        While the exact order of attributes is
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:implementation-defined"
        data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>,
        and may depend on factors such as the order that the attributes
        were given in the original markup, the sort order must be
        stable, such that consecutive invocations of this algorithm
        serialize an element's attributes in the same order.

        Append a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (\>).

        If `current node` <a href="#serializes-as-void"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:serializes-as-void-2">serializes as
        void</a>, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:continue"
        data-x-internal="continue">continue</a> on to the next child
        node at this point.

        Append the value of running the
        <a href="#html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm-2">HTML
        fragment serialization algorithm</a> with `current node`,
        `serializableShadowRoots`, and `shadowRoots` (thus recursing
        into this algorithm for that node), followed by a U+003C
        LESS-THAN SIGN character (\<), a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/),
        `tagname` again, and finally a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN
        character (\>).

        If `current node` is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
        data-x-internal="text"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:text">Text</code></a> node  
        If the parent of `current node` is a
        [`style`](#the-style-element), [`script`](#the-script-element),
        [`xmp`](#xmp), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element),
        [`noembed`](#noembed), [`noframes`](#noframes), or
        [`plaintext`](#plaintext) element, or if the parent of
        `current node` is a [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element) element
        and <a href="#concept-n-script"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-n-script">scripting is
        enabled</a> for the node, then append the value of
        `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-cd-data"
        data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a> literally.

        Otherwise, append the value of `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-cd-data-2"
        data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a>,
        <a href="#escapingString"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:escapingString-3">escaped as described
        below</a>.

        If `current node` is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-comment"
        data-x-internal="comment-2"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:comment-2">Comment</code></a>  
        Append "`<!--`" (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+0021 EXCLAMATION MARK,
        U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS), followed by the value
        of `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-cd-data-3"
        data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a>, followed by the
        literal string "`-->`" (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D
        HYPHEN-MINUS, U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN).

        If `current node` is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-processinginstruction"
        data-x-internal="processinginstruction"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:processinginstruction">ProcessingInstruction</code></a>  
        Append "`<?`" (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+003F QUESTION MARK),
        followed by the value of `current node`'s `target` IDL
        attribute, followed by a single U+0020 SPACE character, followed
        by the value of `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-cd-data-4"
        data-x-internal="concept-cd-data">data</a>, followed by a single
        U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (\>).

        If `current node` is a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-documenttype"
        data-x-internal="documenttype"><code
        id="serialising-html-fragments:documenttype">DocumentType</code></a>  
        Append "`<!DOCTYPE`" (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+0021 EXCLAMATION
        MARK, U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D, U+004F LATIN CAPITAL LETTER
        O, U+0043 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER C, U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T,
        U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y, U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P,
        U+0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E), followed by a space (U+0020
        SPACE), followed by the value of `current node`'s
        <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-doctype-name"
        id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-doctype-name"
        data-x-internal="concept-doctype-name">name</a>, followed by
        "`>`" (U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN).

6.  Return `s`.

</div>

It is possible that the output of this algorithm, if parsed with an
<a href="#html-parser"
id="serialising-html-fragments:html-parser-3">HTML parser</a>, will not
return the original tree structure. Tree structures that do not
roundtrip a serialize and reparse step can also be produced by the
<a href="#html-parser"
id="serialising-html-fragments:html-parser-4">HTML parser</a> itself,
although such cases are typically non-conforming.

<div id="example-html-serializer-roundtrip-comments-and-script"
class="example">

<a href="#example-html-serializer-roundtrip-comments-and-script"
class="self-link"></a>

For instance, if a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to which
a `Comment` node has been appended is serialized and the output is then
reparsed, the comment will end up being displayed in the text control.
Similarly, if, as a result of DOM manipulation, an element contains a
comment that contains "`-->`", then when the result of serializing the
element is parsed, the comment will be truncated at that point and the
rest of the comment will be interpreted as markup. More examples would
be making a [`script`](#the-script-element) element contain a
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text"
data-x-internal="text"><code
id="serialising-html-fragments:text-2">Text</code></a> node with the
text string "`</script>`", or having a [`p`](#the-p-element) element
that contains a [`ul`](#the-ul-element) element (as the
[`ul`](#the-ul-element) element's <a href="#syntax-start-tag"
id="serialising-html-fragments:syntax-start-tag">start tag</a> would
imply the end tag for the [`p`](#the-p-element)).

This can enable cross-site scripting attacks. An example of this would
be a page that lets the user enter some font family names that are then
inserted into a CSS [`style`](#the-style-element) block via the DOM and
which then uses the [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) IDL attribute
to get the HTML serialization of that [`style`](#the-style-element)
element: if the user enters "`</style><script>attack</script>`" as a
font family name, [`innerHTML`](#dom-element-innerhtml) will return
markup that, if parsed in a different context, would contain a
[`script`](#the-script-element) node, even though no
[`script`](#the-script-element) node existed in the original DOM.

</div>

<div id="example-html-serializer-roundtrip-nested-form" class="example">

<a href="#example-html-serializer-roundtrip-nested-form"
class="self-link"></a>

For example, consider the following markup:

``` html
<form id="outer"><div></form><form id="inner"><input>
```

This will be parsed into:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`form`](#the-form-element)
      <span class="t2">[`id`](#the-id-attribute)="`outer`"</span>
      - [`div`](#the-div-element)
        - [`form`](#the-form-element)
          <span class="t2">[`id`](#the-id-attribute)="`inner`"</span>
          - [`input`](#the-input-element)

The [`input`](#the-input-element) element will be associated with the
inner [`form`](#the-form-element) element. Now, if this tree structure
is serialized and reparsed, the `<form id="inner">` start tag will be
ignored, and so the [`input`](#the-input-element) element will be
associated with the outer [`form`](#the-form-element) element instead.

``` html
<html><head></head><body><form id="outer"><div><form id="inner"><input></form></div></form></body></html>
```

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`form`](#the-form-element)
      <span class="t2">[`id`](#the-id-attribute)="`outer`"</span>
      - [`div`](#the-div-element)
        - [`input`](#the-input-element)

</div>

<div id="example-html-serializer-roundtrip-foster-parenting"
class="example">

<a href="#example-html-serializer-roundtrip-foster-parenting"
class="self-link"></a>

As another example, consider the following markup:

``` html
<a><table><a>
```

This will be parsed into:

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`a`](#the-a-element)
      - [`a`](#the-a-element)
      - [`table`](#the-table-element)

That is, the [`a`](#the-a-element) elements are nested, because the
second [`a`](#the-a-element) element is <a href="#foster-parent"
id="serialising-html-fragments:foster-parent">foster parented</a>. After
a serialize-reparse roundtrip, the [`a`](#the-a-element) elements and
the [`table`](#the-table-element) element would all be siblings, because
the second `<a>` start tag implicitly closes the first
[`a`](#the-a-element) element.

``` html
<html><head></head><body><a><a></a><table></table></a></body></html>
```

- [`html`](#the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#the-body-element)
    - [`a`](#the-a-element)
    - [`a`](#the-a-element)
    - [`table`](#the-table-element)

</div>

For historical reasons, this algorithm does not round-trip an initial
U+000A (LF) character in [`pre`](#the-pre-element),
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element), or [`listing`](#listing) elements,
even though (in the first two cases) the markup being round-tripped can
be conforming. The <a href="#html-parser"
id="serialising-html-fragments:html-parser-5">HTML parser</a> will drop
such a character during parsing, but this algorithm does *not* serialize
an extra U+000A (LF) character.

<div id="example-html-serializer-roundtrip-linefeed" class="example">

<a href="#example-html-serializer-roundtrip-linefeed"
class="self-link"></a>

For example, consider the following markup:

``` html
<pre>

Hello.</pre>
```

When this document is first parsed, the [`pre`](#the-pre-element)
element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="serialising-html-fragments:child-text-content"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> starts with
a single newline character. After a serialize-reparse roundtrip, the
[`pre`](#the-pre-element) element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-child-text-content"
id="serialising-html-fragments:child-text-content-2"
data-x-internal="child-text-content">child text content</a> is simply
"`Hello.`".

</div>

Because of the special role of the [`is`](#attr-is) attribute in
signaling the creation of <a href="#customized-built-in-element"
id="serialising-html-fragments:customized-built-in-element">customized
built-in elements</a>, in that it provides a mechanism for parsed HTML
to set the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value-3"
data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>, we
special-case its handling during serialization. This ensures that an
element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value-4"
data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a> is
preserved through serialize-parse roundtrips.

<div id="example-html-serializer-roundtrip-is-attribute"
class="example">

<a href="#example-html-serializer-roundtrip-is-attribute"
class="self-link"></a>

When creating a <a href="#customized-built-in-element"
id="serialising-html-fragments:customized-built-in-element-2">customized
built-in element</a> via the parser, a developer uses the
[`is`](#attr-is) attribute directly; in such cases serialize-parse
roundtrips work fine.

``` html
<script>
window.SuperP = class extends HTMLParagraphElement {};
customElements.define("super-p", SuperP, { extends: "p" });
</script>

<div id="container"><p is="super-p">Superb!</p></div>

<script>
console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
container.innerHTML = container.innerHTML;
console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
console.assert(container.firstChild instanceof SuperP);
</script>
```

But when creating a customized built-in element via its
<a href="#custom-element-constructor"
id="serialising-html-fragments:custom-element-constructor">constructor</a>
or via <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement"
data-x-internal="dom-document-createelement"><code
id="serialising-html-fragments:dom-document-createelement-2">createElement()</code></a>,
the [`is`](#attr-is) attribute is not added. Instead, the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value-5"
data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a>
(which is what the custom elements machinery uses) is set without
intermediating through an attribute.

``` html
<script>
container.innerHTML = "";
const p = document.createElement("p", { is: "super-p" });
container.appendChild(p);

// The is attribute is not present in the DOM:
console.assert(!p.hasAttribute("is"));

// But the element is still a super-p:
console.assert(p instanceof SuperP);
</script>
```

To ensure that serialize-parse roundtrips still work, the serialization
process explicitly writes out the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value"
id="serialising-html-fragments:concept-element-is-value-6"
data-x-internal="concept-element-is-value"><code>is</code> value</a> as
an [`is`](#attr-is) attribute:

``` html
<script>
console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
container.innerHTML = container.innerHTML;
console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
console.assert(container.firstChild instanceof SuperP);
</script>
```

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="escapingString" class="dfn">Escaping a string</span> (for the
purposes of the algorithm above) consists of running the following
steps:

1.  Replace any occurrence of "`&`" character by "`&amp;`".

2.  Replace any occurrences of the U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE character by
    "`&nbsp;`".

3.  Replace any occurrences of the "`<`" character by "`&lt;`".

4.  Replace any occurrences of the "`>`" character by "`&gt;`".

5.  If the algorithm was invoked in the *attribute mode*, then replace
    any occurrences of the "`"`" character by "`&quot;`".

</div>

### <span class="secno">13.4</span> Parsing HTML fragments<a href="#parsing-html-fragments" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="html-fragment-parsing-algorithm" class="dfn">HTML fragment
parsing algorithm</span>, given an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element"
data-x-internal="element"><code
id="parsing-html-fragments:element">Element</code></a> node
<span id="concept-frag-parse-context" class="dfn">`context`</span>,
string `input`, an optional boolean `allowDeclarativeShadowRoots`
(default false), and an optional
<a href="#fragment-parser-scripting-mode"
id="parsing-html-fragments:fragment-parser-scripting-mode">fragment
parser scripting mode</a> `scriptingMode` (default
<a href="#scripting-mode-inert"
id="parsing-html-fragments:scripting-mode-inert">Inert</a>) is the
following steps. They return a list of zero or more nodes.

Parts marked <span id="fragment-case" class="dfn">fragment case</span>
in algorithms in the
<a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser">HTML
parser</a> section are parts that only occur if the parser was created
for the purposes of this algorithm. The algorithms have been annotated
with such markings for informational purposes only; such markings have
no normative weight. If it is possible for a condition described as a
<a href="#fragment-case"
id="parsing-html-fragments:fragment-case">fragment case</a> to occur
even when the parser wasn't created for the purposes of handling this
algorithm, then that is an error in the specification.

1.  Let `document` be a [`Document`](#document) node whose
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-type"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-document-type"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-type">type</a> is "`html`".

2.  Let `contextDocument` be [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context)'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:node-document"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a>.

3.  If `contextDocument` is in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:quirks-mode"
    data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>, then set `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-mode"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-document-mode"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-mode">mode</a> to "`quirks`".

4.  Otherwise, if [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context)'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:node-document-2"
    data-x-internal="node-document">node document</a> is in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-limited-quirks"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:limited-quirks-mode"
    data-x-internal="limited-quirks-mode">limited-quirks mode</a>, then
    set `document`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-mode"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-document-mode-2"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-mode">mode</a> to
    "`limited-quirks`".

5.  If `allowDeclarativeShadowRoots` is true, then set `document`'s <a
    href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots"
    data-x-internal="concept-document-allow-declarative-shadow-roots">allow
    declarative shadow roots</a> to true.

6.  Create a new
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-2">HTML
    parser</a>, and associate it with `document`.

7.  If `contextDocument`'s <a href="#concept-n-script"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-n-script">scripting is disabled</a>,
    then set `scriptingMode` to <a href="#scripting-mode-disabled"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:scripting-mode-disabled">Disabled</a>.

8.  Set the parser's <a href="#scripting-mode"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:scripting-mode">scripting mode</a> to
    `scriptingMode`.

9.  Set the state of the
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-3">HTML
    parser</a>'s <a href="#tokenization"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:tokenization">tokenization</a> stage as
    follows, switching on the [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context)
    element:

    [`title`](#the-title-element)  
    [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)  
    Switch the tokenizer to the
    <a href="#rcdata-state" id="parsing-html-fragments:rcdata-state">RCDATA
    state</a>.

    [`style`](#the-style-element)  
    [`xmp`](#xmp)  
    [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element)  
    [`noembed`](#noembed)  
    [`noframes`](#noframes)  
    Switch the tokenizer to the <a href="#rawtext-state"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:rawtext-state">RAWTEXT state</a>.

    [`script`](#the-script-element)  
    Switch the tokenizer to the <a href="#script-data-state"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:script-data-state">script data state</a>.

    [`noscript`](#the-noscript-element)  
    If <a href="#scripting-mode"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:scripting-mode-2">scripting mode</a> is
    not <a href="#scripting-mode-disabled"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:scripting-mode-disabled-2">Disabled</a>,
    switch the tokenizer to the <a href="#rawtext-state"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:rawtext-state-2">RAWTEXT state</a>.
    Otherwise, leave the tokenizer in the
    <a href="#data-state" id="parsing-html-fragments:data-state">data
    state</a>.

    [`plaintext`](#plaintext)  
    Switch the tokenizer to the <a href="#plaintext-state"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:plaintext-state">PLAINTEXT state</a>.

    Any other element  
    Leave the tokenizer in the
    <a href="#data-state" id="parsing-html-fragments:data-state-2">data
    state</a>.

    For performance reasons, an implementation that does not report
    errors and that uses the actual state machine described in this
    specification directly could use the PLAINTEXT state instead of the
    RAWTEXT and script data states where those are mentioned in the list
    above. Except for rules regarding parse errors, they are equivalent,
    since there is no <a href="#appropriate-end-tag-token"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:appropriate-end-tag-token">appropriate end
    tag token</a> in the fragment case, yet they involve far fewer state
    transitions.

10. Let `root` be the result of
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:create-an-element"
    data-x-internal="create-an-element">creating an element</a> given
    `document`, "`html`", the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:html-namespace-2"
    data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>, null, null,
    false, and `context`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#element-custom-element-registry"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:element-custom-element-registry"
    data-x-internal="element-custom-element-registry">custom element
    registry</a>.

11. <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-node-append"
    data-x-internal="concept-node-append">Append</a> `root` to
    `document`.

12. Set up the
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-4">HTML
    parser</a>'s <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:stack-of-open-elements">stack of open
    elements</a> so that it contains just the single element `root`.

13. If [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context) is a
    [`template`](#the-template-element) element, then push
    "<a href="#parsing-main-intemplate"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:parsing-main-intemplate">in template</a>"
    onto the <a href="#stack-of-template-insertion-modes"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:stack-of-template-insertion-modes">stack of
    template insertion modes</a> so that it is the new
    <a href="#current-template-insertion-mode"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:current-template-insertion-mode">current
    template insertion mode</a>.

14. Create a start tag token whose name is the local name of
    [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context) and whose attributes are
    the attributes of [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context).

    Let this start tag token be the start tag token of
    [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context); e.g. for the purposes of
    determining if it is an <a href="#html-integration-point"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:html-integration-point">HTML integration
    point</a>.

15. <a href="#reset-the-insertion-mode-appropriately"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:reset-the-insertion-mode-appropriately">Reset
    the parser's insertion mode appropriately</a>.

    The parser will reference the
    [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context) element as part of that
    algorithm.

16. Set the
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-5">HTML
    parser</a>'s <a href="#form-element-pointer"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:form-element-pointer"><code>form</code>
    element pointer</a> to the nearest node to
    [`context`](#concept-frag-parse-context) that is a
    [`form`](#the-form-element) element (going straight up the ancestor
    chain, and including the element itself, if it is a
    [`form`](#the-form-element) element), if any. (If there is no such
    [`form`](#the-form-element) element, the
    <a href="#form-element-pointer"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:form-element-pointer-2"><code>form</code>
    element pointer</a> keeps its initial value, null.)

17. Place the `input` into the
    <a href="#input-stream" id="parsing-html-fragments:input-stream">input
    stream</a> for the
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-6">HTML
    parser</a> just created. The encoding
    <a href="#concept-encoding-confidence"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-encoding-confidence">confidence</a>
    is *irrelevant*.

18. Start the
    <a href="#html-parser" id="parsing-html-fragments:html-parser-7">HTML
    parser</a> and let it run until it has consumed all the characters
    just inserted into the input stream.

19. Return `root`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:concept-tree-child"
    data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a>, in
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order"
    id="parsing-html-fragments:tree-order" data-x-internal="tree-order">tree
    order</a>.

</div>

### <span class="secno">13.5</span> <span class="dfn">Named character references</span><a href="#named-character-references" class="self-link"></a>

id="named-character-references:syntax-charref">character reference</a>
names that are supported by HTML, and the code points to which they
refer. It is referenced by the previous sections.

It is intentional, for legacy compatibility, that many code points have
multiple character reference names. For example, some appear both with
and without the trailing semicolon, or with different capitalizations.

## <span class="secno">14</span> <span id="xhtml" class="dfn">The XML syntax</span><a href="#the-xhtml-syntax" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="mdn-anno wrapped">

This section only describes the rules for XML resources. Rules for
[`text/html`](#text/html) resources are discussed in the section above
entitled
"<a href="#syntax" id="the-xhtml-syntax:syntax">The HTML syntax</a>".

Using the XML syntax is not recommended, for reasons which include the
fact that there is no specification which defines the rules for how an
XML parser must map a string of bytes or characters into a
[`Document`](#document) object, as well as the fact that the XML syntax
is essentially unmaintained — in that, it’s not expected that any
further features will ever be added to the XML syntax (even when such
features have been added to the
<a href="#syntax" id="the-xhtml-syntax:syntax-2">HTML syntax</a>).

### <span class="secno">14.1</span> Writing documents in the XML syntax<a href="#writing-xhtml-documents" class="self-link"></a>

The XML syntax for HTML was formerly referred to as "XHTML", but this
specification does not use that term (among other reasons, because no
such term is used for the HTML syntaxes of MathML and SVG).

The syntax for XML is defined in XML and Namespaces in XML.
[\[XML\]](#refsXML) [\[XMLNS\]](#refsXMLNS)

This specification does not define any syntax-level requirements beyond
those defined for XML proper.

XML documents may contain a `DOCTYPE` if desired, but this is not
required to conform to this specification. This specification does not
define a public or system identifier, nor provide a formal DTD.

According to XML, XML processors are not guaranteed to process the
external DTD subset referenced in the DOCTYPE. This means, for example,
that using [entity references](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#dt-entref) for
characters in XML documents is unsafe if they are defined in an external
file (except for `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`, `&quot;`, and `&apos;`).

### <span class="secno">14.2</span> Parsing XML documents<a href="#parsing-xhtml-documents" class="self-link"></a>

This section describes the relationship between XML and the DOM, with a
particular emphasis on how this interacts with HTML.

An <span id="xml-parser" class="dfn" export="">XML parser</span>, for
the purposes of this specification, is a construct that follows the
rules given in XML to map a string of bytes or characters into a
[`Document`](#document) object.

At the time of writing, no such rules actually exist.

An <a href="#xml-parser" id="parsing-xhtml-documents:xml-parser">XML
parser</a> is either associated with a [`Document`](#document) object
when it is created, or creates one implicitly.

This [`Document`](#document) must then be populated with DOM nodes that
represent the tree structure of the input passed to the parser, as
defined by XML, Namespaces in XML, and DOM. When creating DOM nodes
representing elements, the <a href="#create-an-element-for-the-token"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:create-an-element-for-the-token">create an
element for a token</a> algorithm or some equivalent that operates on
appropriate XML data structures must be used, to ensure the proper
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-interface"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:element-interface"
data-x-internal="element-interface">element interfaces</a> are created
and that <a href="#custom-element"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:custom-element">custom elements</a> are set
up correctly.

For the operations that the
<a href="#xml-parser" id="parsing-xhtml-documents:xml-parser-2">XML
parser</a> performs on the [`Document`](#document)'s tree, the user
agent must act as if elements and attributes were individually appended
and set respectively so as to trigger rules in this specification
regarding what happens when an element is inserted into a document or
has its attributes set, and DOM's requirements regarding
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#mutation-observers"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:mutation-observers"
data-x-internal="mutation-observers">mutation observers</a> mean that
mutation observers *are* fired. [\[XML\]](#refsXML)
[\[XMLNS\]](#refsXMLNS) [\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)
[\[UIEVENTS\]](#refsUIEVENTS)

Between the time an element's start tag is parsed and the time either
the element's end tag is parsed or the parser detects a well-formedness
error, the user agent must act as if the element was in a
<a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:stack-of-open-elements">stack of open
elements</a>.

This is used by various elements to only start certain processes once
they are popped off of the <a href="#stack-of-open-elements"
id="parsing-xhtml-documents:stack-of-open-elements-2">stack of open
elements</a>.

This specification provides the following additional information that
user agents should use when retrieving an external entity: the public
identifiers given in the following list all correspond to [the URL given
by this
