id="margin-collapsing-quirks:concept-tree-child-4"
data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">child</a> of a
[`td`](#the-td-element) or [`th`](#the-th-element) element and has no
<a href="#concept-rendering-substantial"
id="margin-collapsing-quirks:concept-rendering-substantial-5">substantial</a>
following siblings, is <a href="#expected"
id="margin-collapsing-quirks:expected-4">expected</a> to have a
user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-block-end"
id="margin-collapsing-quirks:&#39;margin-block-end&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-block-end&#39;">'margin-block-end'</a>
property to zero.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">15.3.10</span> Form controls<a href="#form-controls" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

input, button, textarea {
  letter-spacing: initial;
  word-spacing: initial;
  line-height: initial;
}

input, select, button, textarea {
  text-transform: initial;
  text-indent: initial;
  text-shadow: initial;
  appearance: auto;
}

input:not([type=image i], [type=range i], [type=checkbox i], [type=radio i]) {
  overflow: clip !important;
  overflow-clip-margin: 0 !important;
}

input, select, textarea {
  text-align: initial;
}

:autofill {
  field-sizing: fixed !important;
}

input:is([type=reset i], [type=button i], [type=submit i]), button {
  text-align: center;
}

input, button {
  display: inline-block;
}

input[type=hidden i], input[type=file i], input[type=image i] {
  appearance: none;
}

input:is([type=radio i], [type=checkbox i], [type=reset i], [type=button i],
[type=submit i], [type=color i], [type=search i]), select, button {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

textarea { white-space: pre-wrap; }
```

In <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks"
id="form-controls:quirks-mode" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks
mode</a>, the following rules are also
<a href="#expected" id="form-controls:expected">expected</a> to apply:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

input:not([type=image i]), textarea { box-sizing: border-box; }
```

Each kind of form control is also described in the [Widgets](#widgets)
section, which describes the look and feel of the control.

For [`input`](#the-input-element) elements where the
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is not in the
<a href="#hidden-state-(type=hidden)"
id="form-controls:hidden-state-(type=hidden)">Hidden</a> state or the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="form-controls:image-button-state-(type=image)">Image Button</a>
state, and that are
<a href="#being-rendered" id="form-controls:being-rendered">being
rendered</a>, are
<a href="#expected" id="form-controls:expected-2">expected</a> to act as
follows:

- The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#inner-display-type"
  id="form-controls:inner-display-type"
  data-x-internal="inner-display-type">inner display type</a> is always
  'flow-root'.

#### <span class="secno">15.3.11</span> The [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element<a href="#the-hr-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

hr {
  color: gray;
  border-style: inset;
  border-width: 1px;
  margin-block: 0.5em;
  margin-inline: auto;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

The following rules are also
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
apply, as <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-hr-element-2:presentational-hints">presentational hints</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

hr[align=left i] { margin-left: 0; margin-right: auto; }
hr[align=right i] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: 0; }
hr[align=center i] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; }
hr[color], hr[noshade] { border-style: solid; }
```

<div algorithm="">

If an [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element has either a
[`color`](#attr-hr-color) attribute or a [`noshade`](#attr-hr-noshade)
attribute, and furthermore also has a [`size`](#attr-hr-size) attribute,
and parsing that attribute's value using the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-hr-element-2:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules for
parsing non-negative integers</a> doesn't generate an error, then the
user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected-2">expected</a> to use
the parsed value divided by two as a pixel length for
<a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-hr-element-2:presentational-hints-2">presentational hints</a>
for the properties <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;border-top-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-top-width&#39;">'border-top-width'</a>, <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;border-right-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-right-width&#39;">'border-right-width'</a>,
<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;">'border-bottom-width'</a>,
and <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;border-left-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-left-width&#39;">'border-left-width'</a> on
the element.

Otherwise, if an [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element has neither a
[`color`](#attr-hr-color) attribute nor a [`noshade`](#attr-hr-noshade)
attribute, but does have a [`size`](#attr-hr-size) attribute, and
parsing that attribute's value using the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-hr-element-2:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-2">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> doesn't generate an error, then:
if the parsed value is one, then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected-3">expected</a> to use
the attribute as a <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-hr-element-2:presentational-hints-3">presentational hint</a>
setting the element's <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;">'border-bottom-width'</a>
to 0; otherwise, if the parsed value is greater than one, then the user
agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected-4">expected</a> to use
the parsed value minus two as a pixel length for
<a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-hr-element-2:presentational-hints-4">presentational hints</a>
for the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;height&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;height&#39;">'height'</a> property on the element.

</div>

The [`width`](#attr-hr-width) attribute on an [`hr`](#the-hr-element)
element <a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="the-hr-element-2:maps-to-the-dimension-property">maps to the
dimension property</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;width&#39;">'width'</a> on the element.

When an [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element has a [`color`](#attr-hr-color)
attribute, its value is
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected-5">expected</a> to be
parsed using the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value"
id="the-hr-element-2:rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value">rules for
parsing a legacy color value</a>, and if that does not return failure,
the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-hr-element-2:expected-6">expected</a> to
treat the attribute as a <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-hr-element-2:presentational-hints-5">presentational hint</a>
setting the element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property"
id="the-hr-element-2:&#39;color&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;color&#39;">'color'</a> property to the resulting
color.

#### <span class="secno">15.3.12</span> The [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) and [`legend`](#the-legend-element) elements<a href="#the-fieldset-and-legend-elements" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

fieldset {
  display: block;
  margin-inline: 2px;
  border: groove 2px ThreeDFace;
  padding-block: 0.35em 0.625em;
  padding-inline: 0.75em;
  min-inline-size: min-content;
}

legend {
  padding-inline: 2px;
}

legend[align=left i] {
  justify-self: left;
}

legend[align=center i] {
  justify-self: center;
}

legend[align=right i] {
  justify-self: right;
}
```

<div algorithm="">

The [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element, when it generates a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box"
id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:css-box"
data-x-internal="css-box">CSS box</a>, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected">expected</a> to act as
follows:

- The element is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-2">expected</a> to
  establish a new
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-formatting-context"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:block-formatting-context"
  data-x-internal="block-formatting-context">block formatting context</a>.

- The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> property is
  <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-3">expected</a> to act
  as follows:

  - If the computed value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> is a value such
    that the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#outer-display-type"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:outer-display-type"
    data-x-internal="outer-display-type">outer display type</a> is
    'inline', then behave as 'inline-block'.

  - Otherwise, behave as 'flow-root'.

  This does not change the computed value.

- If the element's box has a child box that matches the conditions in
  the list below, then the first such child box is the 'fieldset'
  element's <span id="rendered-legend" class="dfn">rendered
  legend</span>:

  - The child is a [`legend`](#the-legend-element) element.
  - The child's used value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#float-position"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;float&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;float&#39;">'float'</a> is 'none'.
  - The child's used value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position/#position-property"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;position&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;position&#39;">'position'</a> is not
    'absolute' or 'fixed'.

- If the element has a <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend">rendered
  legend</a>, then the border is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-4">expected</a> to not
  be painted behind the rectangle defined as follows, using the writing
  mode of the fieldset:

  1.  The block-start edge of the rectangle is the smaller of the
      block-start edge of the <a href="#rendered-legend"
      id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-2">rendered
      legend</a>'s margin rectangle at its static position (ignoring
      transforms), and the block-start outer edge of the
      [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s border.

  2.  The block-end edge of the rectangle is the larger of the block-end
      edge of the <a href="#rendered-legend"
      id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-3">rendered
      legend</a>'s margin rectangle at its static position (ignoring
      transforms), and the block-end outer edge of the
      [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s border.

  3.  The inline-start edge of the rectangle is the smaller of the
      inline-start edge of the <a href="#rendered-legend"
      id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-4">rendered
      legend</a>'s border rectangle at its static position (ignoring
      transforms), and the inline-start outer edge of the
      [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s border.

  4.  The inline-end edge of the rectangle is the larger of the
      inline-end edge of the <a href="#rendered-legend"
      id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-5">rendered
      legend</a>'s border rectangle at its static position (ignoring
      transforms), and the inline-end outer edge of the
      [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s border.

- The space allocated for the element's border on the block-start side
  is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-5">expected</a> to be
  the element's <a
  href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-border-block-start-width"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;border-block-start-width&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;border-block-start-width&#39;">'border-block-start-width'</a>
  or the <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-6">rendered
  legend</a>'s margin box size in the
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s block-flow direction, whichever
  is greater.

- For the purpose of calculating the used
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;block-size&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;block-size&#39;">'block-size'</a>, if the
  computed
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;block-size&#39;-2"
  data-x-internal="&#39;block-size&#39;">'block-size'</a> is not 'auto',
  the space allocated for the <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-7">rendered
  legend</a>'s margin box that spills out past the border, if any, is
  <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-6">expected</a> to be
  subtracted from the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;block-size&#39;-3"
  data-x-internal="&#39;block-size&#39;">'block-size'</a>. If the
  content box's block-size would be negative, then let the content box's
  block-size be 0 instead.

- If the element has a <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-8">rendered
  legend</a>, then that element is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-7">expected</a> to be
  the first child box.

- The <a href="#anonymous-fieldset-content-box"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:anonymous-fieldset-content-box">anonymous
  fieldset content box</a> is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-8">expected</a> to
  appear after the <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-9">rendered
  legend</a> and is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-9">expected</a> to
  contain the content (including the '::before' and '::after'
  pseudo-elements) of the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element
  except for the <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-10">rendered
  legend</a>, if there is one.

- The used value of the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-top"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;padding-top&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;padding-top&#39;">'padding-top'</a>,
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-right"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;padding-right&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;padding-right&#39;">'padding-right'</a>,
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-bottom"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;padding-bottom&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;padding-bottom&#39;">'padding-bottom'</a>, and
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-left"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;padding-left&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;padding-left&#39;">'padding-left'</a> properties
  are <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-10">expected</a> to be
  zero.

- For the purpose of calculating the min-content inline size, use the
  greater of the min-content inline size of the
  <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-11">rendered
  legend</a> and the min-content inline size of the
  <a href="#anonymous-fieldset-content-box"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:anonymous-fieldset-content-box-2">anonymous
  fieldset content box</a>.

- For the purpose of calculating the max-content inline size, use the
  greater of the max-content inline size of the
  <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-12">rendered
  legend</a> and the max-content inline size of the
  <a href="#anonymous-fieldset-content-box"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:anonymous-fieldset-content-box-3">anonymous
  fieldset content box</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element's
<a href="#rendered-legend"
id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-13">rendered
legend</a>, if any, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-11">expected</a> to act as
follows:

- The element is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-12">expected</a> to
  establish a new
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:formatting-context"
  data-x-internal="formatting-context">formatting context</a> for its
  contents. The type of this
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:formatting-context-2"
  data-x-internal="formatting-context">formatting context</a> is
  determined by its
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-3"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> value, as usual.

- The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-4"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> property is
  <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-13">expected</a> to
  behave as if its computed value was blockified.

  This does not change the computed value.

- If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:computed-value"
  data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;inline-size&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;inline-size&#39;">'inline-size'</a> is 'auto',
  then the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:used-value"
  data-x-internal="used-value">used value</a> is the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#fit-content-inline-size"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:fit-content-inline-size"
  data-x-internal="fit-content-inline-size">fit-content inline size</a>.

- The element is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-14">expected</a> to be
  positioned in the inline direction as is normal for blocks (e.g.,
  taking into account margins and the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-self"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;justify-self&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;justify-self&#39;">'justify-self'</a> property).

- The element's box is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-15">expected</a> to be
  constrained in the inline direction by the inline content size of the
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) as if it had used its computed
  inline padding.

  <div class="example">

  For example, if the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) has a
  specified padding of 50px, then the <a href="#rendered-legend"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:rendered-legend-14">rendered
  legend</a> will be positioned 50px in from the
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element)'s border. The padding will further
  apply to the <a href="#anonymous-fieldset-content-box"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:anonymous-fieldset-content-box-4">anonymous
  fieldset content box</a> instead of the
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element itself.

  </div>

- The element is <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-16">expected</a> to be
  positioned in the block-flow direction such that its border box is
  centered over the border on the block-start side of the
  [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element's
<span id="anonymous-fieldset-content-box" class="dfn">anonymous fieldset
content box</span> is <a href="#expected"
id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-17">expected</a> to act as
follows:

- The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-5"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> property is
  <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-18">expected</a> to act
  as follows:

  - If the computed value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-6"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> on the
    [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element is 'grid' or
    'inline-grid', then set the used value to 'grid'.

  - If the computed value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;display&#39;-7"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> on the
    [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element is 'flex' or
    'inline-flex', then set the used value to 'flex'.

  - Otherwise, set the used value to 'flow-root'.

- The following properties are <a href="#expected"
  id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:expected-19">expected</a> to
  inherit from the [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element) element:

  - <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-content"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;align-content&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;align-content&#39;">'align-content'</a>
  - <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-items"
    id="the-fieldset-and-legend-elements:&#39;align-items&#39;"

### <span class="secno">15.4</span> Replaced elements<a href="#replaced-elements" class="self-link"></a>

The following elements can be
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="replaced-elements:replaced-element"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced elements</a>:
[`audio`](#the-audio-element), [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element),
[`embed`](#the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element),
[`img`](#the-img-element), [`input`](#the-input-element),
[`object`](#the-object-element), and [`video`](#the-video-element).

#### <span class="secno">15.4.1</span> Embedded content<a href="#embedded-content-rendering-rules" class="self-link"></a>

The [`embed`](#the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), and
[`video`](#the-video-element) elements are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected">expected</a> to be
treated as
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:replaced-element"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced elements</a>.

A [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) element that <a href="#represents"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:represents">represents</a>
<a href="#embedded-content-category"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:embedded-content-category">embedded
content</a> is <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-2">expected</a> to be
treated as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:replaced-element-2"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a>; the contents of
such elements are the element's bitmap, if any, or else a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a> bitmap with
the same
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:natural-dimensions"
data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a> as the
element. Other [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements are
<a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-3">expected</a> to be
treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

An [`object`](#the-object-element) element that <a href="#represents"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:represents-2">represents</a> an
image, plugin, or its <a href="#content-navigable"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:content-navigable">content
navigable</a> is <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-4">expected</a> to be
treated as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:replaced-element-3"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a>. Other
[`object`](#the-object-element) elements are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-5">expected</a> to be
treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

The [`audio`](#the-audio-element) element, when it is
<a href="#expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user">exposing
a user interface</a>, is <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-6">expected</a> to be
treated as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:replaced-element-4"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> about one line
high, as wide as is necessary to expose the user agent's user interface
features. When an [`audio`](#the-audio-element) element is not
<a href="#expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user-2">exposing
a user interface</a>, the user agent is <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-7">expected</a> to force
its <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:&#39;display&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> property to compute to
'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

Whether a [`video`](#the-video-element) element is
<a href="#expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user-3">exposing
a user interface</a> is not <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-8">expected</a> to affect
the size of the rendering; controls are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-9">expected</a> to be
overlaid above the page content without causing any layout changes, and
are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-10">expected</a> to
disappear when the user does not need them.

When a [`video`](#the-video-element) element represents a poster frame
or frame of video, the poster frame or frame of video is
<a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-11">expected</a> to be
rendered at the largest size that maintains the aspect ratio of that
poster frame or frame of video without being taller or wider than the
[`video`](#the-video-element) element itself, and is <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-12">expected</a> to be
centered in the [`video`](#the-video-element) element.

Any subtitles or captions are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-13">expected</a> to be
overlaid directly on top of their [`video`](#the-video-element) element,
as defined by the relevant rendering rules; for WebVTT, those are the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks"
data-x-internal="rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks">rules
for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks</a>.
[\[WEBVTT\]](#refsWEBVTT)

When the user agent starts
<a href="#expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user-4">exposing
a user interface</a> for a [`video`](#the-video-element) element, the
user agent should run the
<a href="#rules-for-updating-the-text-track-rendering"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:rules-for-updating-the-text-track-rendering">rules
for updating the text track rendering</a> of each of the
<a href="#text-track"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:text-track">text tracks</a> in the
[`video`](#the-video-element) element's <a href="#list-of-text-tracks"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:list-of-text-tracks">list of text
tracks</a> that are <a href="#text-track-showing"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:text-track-showing">showing</a> and
whose <a href="#text-track-kind"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:text-track-kind">text track
kind</a> is one of [`subtitles`](#dom-texttrack-kind-subtitles) or
[`captions`](#dom-texttrack-kind-captions) (e.g., for
<a href="#text-track"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:text-track-2">text tracks</a> based
on WebVTT, the <a
href="https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks-2"
data-x-internal="rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks">rules
for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks</a>).
[\[WEBVTT\]](#refsWEBVTT)

Resizing [`video`](#the-video-element) and
[`canvas`](#the-canvas-element) elements does not interrupt video
playback or clear the canvas.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following CSS rules are <a href="#expected"
id="embedded-content-rendering-rules:expected-14">expected</a> to apply:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

iframe { border: 2px inset; }
video { object-fit: contain; }
```

#### <span class="secno">15.4.2</span> Images<a href="#images-3" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are <a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected">expected</a>
to render [`img`](#the-img-element) elements and
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#attr-input-type)
attributes are in the <a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="images-3:image-button-state-(type=image)">Image Button</a> state,
according to the first applicable rules from the following list:

If the element
<a href="#represents" id="images-3:represents">represents</a> an image

The user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-2">expected</a> to treat the
element as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="images-3:replaced-element"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> and render the
image according to the rules for doing so defined in CSS.

If the element does not
<a href="#represents" id="images-3:represents-2">represent</a> an image
and either:

- the user agent has reason to believe that the image will become
  *[available](#img-available)* and be rendered in due course, or
- the element has no `alt` attribute, or
- the [`Document`](#document) is in
  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks"
  id="images-3:quirks-mode" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>,
  and the element already has
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
  id="images-3:natural-dimensions"
  data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a> (e.g.,
  from the <a href="#dimension-attributes"
  id="images-3:dimension-attributes">dimension attributes</a> or CSS
  rules)

The user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-3">expected</a> to treat the
element as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="images-3:replaced-element-2"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> whose content is
the text that the element represents, if any, optionally alongside an
icon indicating that the image is being obtained (if applicable). For
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements, the element is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-4">expected</a> to appear
button-like to indicate that the element is a
<a href="#concept-button" id="images-3:concept-button">button</a>.

If the element is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element that
<a href="#represents" id="images-3:represents-3">represents</a> some
text and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-5">expected</a> to treat the
element as a non-replaced phrasing element whose content is the text,
optionally with an icon indicating that an image is missing, so that the
user can request the image be displayed or investigate why it is not
rendering. In non-graphical contexts, such an icon should be omitted.

If the element is an [`img`](#the-img-element) element that
<a href="#represents" id="images-3:represents-4">represents</a> nothing
and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-6">expected</a> to treat the
element as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="images-3:replaced-element-3"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> whose
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
id="images-3:natural-dimensions-2"
data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a> are 0. (In
the absence of further styles, this will cause the element to
essentially not be rendered.)

If the element is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element that does not
<a href="#represents" id="images-3:represents-5">represent</a> an image
and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-7">expected</a> to treat the
element as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="images-3:replaced-element-4"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> consisting of a
button whose content is the element's alternative text. The
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions"
id="images-3:natural-dimensions-3"
data-x-internal="natural-dimensions">natural dimensions</a> of the
button are <a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-8">expected</a> to
be about one line in height and whatever width is necessary to render
the text on one line.

The icons mentioned above are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-9">expected</a> to be
relatively small so as not to disrupt most text but be easily clickable.
In a visual environment, for instance, icons could be 16 pixels by 16
pixels square, or 1em by 1em if the images are scalable. In an audio
environment, the icon could be a short bleep. The icons are intended to
indicate to the user that they can be used to get to whatever options
the UA provides for images, and, where appropriate, are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-10">expected</a> to provide
access to the context menu that would have come up if the user
interacted with the actual image.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

All animated images with the same
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="images-3:absolute-url" data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute
URL</a> and the same image data are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-11">expected</a> to be
rendered synchronized to the same timeline as a group, with the timeline
starting at the time of the least recent addition to the group.

In other words, when a second image with the same
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="images-3:absolute-url-2" data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute
URL</a> and animated image data is inserted into a document, it jumps to
the point in the animation cycle that is currently being displayed by
the first image.

<div algorithm="">

When a user agent is to <span id="restart-the-animation"
class="dfn">restart the animation</span> for an
[`img`](#the-img-element) element showing an animated image, all
animated images with the same
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute"
id="images-3:absolute-url-3" data-x-internal="absolute-url">absolute
URL</a> and the same image data in that [`img`](#the-img-element)
element's <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document"
id="images-3:node-document" data-x-internal="node-document">node
document</a> are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-12">expected</a> to restart
their animation from the beginning.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following CSS rules are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-13">expected</a> to apply:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

img:is([sizes="auto" i], [sizes^="auto," i]) {
  contain: size !important;
  contain-intrinsic-size: 300px 150px;
}
```

The following CSS rules are
<a href="#expected" id="images-3:expected-14">expected</a> to apply when
the [`Document`](#document) is in
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks"
id="images-3:quirks-mode-2" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks
mode</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

img[align=left i] { margin-right: 3px; }
img[align=right i] { margin-left: 3px; }
```

#### <span class="secno">15.4.3</span> Attributes for embedded content and images<a href="#attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images"
class="self-link"></a>

The following CSS rules are <a href="#expected"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:expected">expected</a> to
apply as <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:presentational-hints">presentational
hints</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

embed[align=left i], iframe[align=left i], img[align=left i],
input[type=image i][align=left i], object[align=left i] {
  float: left;
}

embed[align=right i], iframe[align=right i], img[align=right i],
input[type=image i][align=right i], object[align=right i] {
  float: right;
}

embed[align=top i], iframe[align=top i], img[align=top i],
input[type=image i][align=top i], object[align=top i] {
  vertical-align: top;
}

embed[align=baseline i], iframe[align=baseline i], img[align=baseline i],
input[type=image i][align=baseline i], object[align=baseline i] {
  vertical-align: baseline;
}

embed[align=texttop i], iframe[align=texttop i], img[align=texttop i],
input[type=image i][align=texttop i], object[align=texttop i] {
  vertical-align: text-top;
}

embed[align=absmiddle i], iframe[align=absmiddle i], img[align=absmiddle i],
input[type=image i][align=absmiddle i], object[align=absmiddle i],
embed[align=abscenter i], iframe[align=abscenter i], img[align=abscenter i],
input[type=image i][align=abscenter i], object[align=abscenter i] {
  vertical-align: middle;
}

embed[align=bottom i], iframe[align=bottom i], img[align=bottom i],
input[type=image i][align=bottom i], object[align=bottom i] {
  vertical-align: bottom;
}
```

When an [`embed`](#the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element),
[`img`](#the-img-element), or [`object`](#the-object-element) element,
or an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)">Image
Button</a> state, has an `align` attribute whose value is an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", the user agent
is <a href="#expected"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:expected-2">expected</a>
to act as if the element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;vertical-align&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;vertical-align&#39;">'vertical-align'</a> property
was set to a value that aligns the vertical middle of the element with
the parent element's baseline.

The `hspace` attribute of [`embed`](#the-embed-element),
[`img`](#the-img-element), or [`object`](#the-object-element) elements,
and [`input`](#the-input-element) elements with a
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)-2">Image
Button</a> state, <a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:maps-to-the-dimension-property">maps
to the dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-left"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;margin-left&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-left&#39;">'margin-left'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-right"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;margin-right&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-right&#39;">'margin-right'</a> on the
element.

The `vspace` attribute of [`embed`](#the-embed-element),
[`img`](#the-img-element), or [`object`](#the-object-element) elements,
and [`input`](#the-input-element) elements with a
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)-3">Image
Button</a> state, <a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:maps-to-the-dimension-property-2">maps
to the dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-top"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;margin-top&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-top&#39;">'margin-top'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-bottom"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;margin-bottom&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-bottom&#39;">'margin-bottom'</a> on the
element.

When an [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element has a
[`frameborder`](#attr-iframe-frameborder) attribute whose value, when
parsed using the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-integers"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:rules-for-parsing-integers">rules
for parsing integers</a>, is zero or an error, the user agent is
<a href="#expected"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:expected-3">expected</a>
to have <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:presentational-hints-2">presentational
hints</a> setting the element's <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-top-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-top-width&#39;">'border-top-width'</a>, <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-right-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-right-width&#39;">'border-right-width'</a>,
<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;">'border-bottom-width'</a>,
and <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-left-width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-left-width&#39;">'border-left-width'</a>
properties to zero.

When an [`img`](#the-img-element) element,
[`object`](#the-object-element) element, or
[`input`](#the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#attr-input-type)
attribute in the <a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)-4">Image
Button</a> state has a `border` attribute whose value, when parsed using
the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a>, is found to be a number greater
than zero, the user agent is <a href="#expected"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:expected-4">expected</a>
to use the parsed value for eight <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:presentational-hints-3">presentational
hints</a>: four setting the parsed value as a pixel length for the
element's <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-top-width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-top-width&#39;">'border-top-width'</a>, <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-right-width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-right-width&#39;">'border-right-width'</a>,
<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-bottom-width&#39;">'border-bottom-width'</a>,
and <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-left-width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-left-width&#39;">'border-left-width'</a>
properties, and four setting the element's <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-style"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-top-style&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-top-style&#39;">'border-top-style'</a>, <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-style"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-right-style&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-right-style&#39;">'border-right-style'</a>,
<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-style"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-bottom-style&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-bottom-style&#39;">'border-bottom-style'</a>,
and <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-style"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;border-left-style&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;border-left-style&#39;">'border-left-style'</a>
properties to the value 'solid'.

The [`width`](#attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#attr-dim-height)
attributes on an [`img`](#the-img-element) element's
<a href="#concept-img-dimension-attribute-source"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:concept-img-dimension-attribute-source">dimension
attribute source</a> <a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:maps-to-the-dimension-property-3">map
to the dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;width&#39;">'width'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;height&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;height&#39;">'height'</a> on the
[`img`](#the-img-element) element respectively. They similarly
<a href="#map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property-(using-dimension-rules)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property-(using-dimension-rules)">map
to the aspect-ratio property (using dimension rules)</a> of the
[`img`](#the-img-element) element.

The [`width`](#attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#attr-dim-height)
attributes on [`embed`](#the-embed-element),
[`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), [`object`](#the-object-element), and
[`video`](#the-video-element) elements, and
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#attr-input-type)
attribute in the <a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)-5">Image
Button</a> state and that either represents an image or that the user
expects will eventually represent an image,
<a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:maps-to-the-dimension-property-4">map
to the dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;width&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;width&#39;">'width'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:&#39;height&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;height&#39;">'height'</a> on the element
respectively.

The [`width`](#attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#attr-dim-height)
attributes
<a href="#map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property-(using-dimension-rules)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property-(using-dimension-rules)-2">map
to the aspect-ratio property (using dimension rules)</a> on
[`img`](#the-img-element) and [`video`](#the-video-element) elements,
and [`input`](#the-input-element) elements with a
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:image-button-state-(type=image)-6">Image
Button</a> state.

The [`width`](#attr-canvas-width) and [`height`](#attr-canvas-height)
attributes <a href="#map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property"
id="attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images:map-to-the-aspect-ratio-property">map
to the aspect-ratio property</a> on [`canvas`](#the-canvas-element)
elements.

#### <span class="secno">15.4.4</span> Image maps<a href="#image-maps-2" class="self-link"></a>

Shapes on an
<a href="#image-map" id="image-maps-2:image-map">image map</a> are
<a href="#expected" id="image-maps-2:expected">expected</a> to act, for
the purpose of the CSS cascade, as elements independent of the original
[`area`](#the-area-element) element that happen to match the same style
rules but inherit from the [`img`](#the-img-element) or
[`object`](#the-object-element) element.

For the purposes of the rendering, only the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor"
id="image-maps-2:&#39;cursor&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;cursor&#39;">'cursor'</a> property is
<a href="#expected" id="image-maps-2:expected-2">expected</a> to have
any effect on the shape.

Thus, for example, if an [`area`](#the-area-element) element has a
[`style`](#attr-style) attribute that sets the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor"
id="image-maps-2:&#39;cursor&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;cursor&#39;">'cursor'</a> property to 'help', then
when the user designates that shape, the cursor would change to a Help
cursor.

Similarly, if an [`area`](#the-area-element) element had a CSS rule that
set its <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor"
id="image-maps-2:&#39;cursor&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;cursor&#39;">'cursor'</a> property to 'inherit'
(or if no rule setting the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor"
id="image-maps-2:&#39;cursor&#39;-4"
data-x-internal="&#39;cursor&#39;">'cursor'</a> property matched the
element at all), the shape's cursor would be inherited from the
[`img`](#the-img-element) or [`object`](#the-object-element) element of
the <a href="#image-map" id="image-maps-2:image-map-2">image map</a>,
not from the parent of the [`area`](#the-area-element) element.

### <span class="secno">15.5</span> <span id="bindings"></span>Widgets<a href="#widgets" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">15.5.1</span> Native appearance<a href="#native-appearance-2" class="self-link"></a>

The CSS Basic User Interface specification calls elements that can have
a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="native-appearance-2:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#widget"
id="native-appearance-2:widget" data-x-internal="widget">widgets</a>,
and defines whether to use that
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="native-appearance-2:native-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> depending on
the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching"
id="native-appearance-2:&#39;appearance&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;appearance&#39;">'appearance'</a> property. That
logic, in turn, depends on whether each the element is classified as a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="native-appearance-2:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable"
id="native-appearance-2:non-devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="non-devolvable-widget">non-devolvable widget</a>. This
section defines which elements match these concepts for HTML, what their
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="native-appearance-2:native-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is, and any
particularity of their
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolved"
id="native-appearance-2:devolved-widget"
data-x-internal="devolved-widget">devolved</a> state or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="native-appearance-2:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.
[\[CSSUI\]](#refsCSSUI)

The following elements can have a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="native-appearance-2:native-appearance-4"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> for the
purpose of the CSS
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching"
id="native-appearance-2:&#39;appearance&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;appearance&#39;">'appearance'</a> property.

- [`button`](#the-button-element)
- [`input`](#the-input-element)
- [`meter`](#the-meter-element)
- [`progress`](#the-progress-element)
- [`select`](#the-select-element)
- [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element)

#### <span class="secno">15.5.2</span> Writing mode<a href="#writing-mode" class="self-link"></a>

Several widgets have their rendering controlled by the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode"
id="writing-mode:&#39;writing-mode&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;writing-mode&#39;">'writing-mode'</a> CSS
property. For the purposes of those widgets, we have the following
definitions.

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="horizontal-writing-mode" class="dfn">horizontal writing
mode</span> is when resolving the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode"
id="writing-mode:&#39;writing-mode&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;writing-mode&#39;">'writing-mode'</a> property of
the control results in a computed value of 'horizontal-tb'.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

A <span id="vertical-writing-mode" class="dfn">vertical writing
mode</span> is when resolving the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode"
id="writing-mode:&#39;writing-mode&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;writing-mode&#39;">'writing-mode'</a> property of
the control results in a computed value of either 'vertical-rl',
'vertical-lr', 'sideways-rl' or 'sideways-lr'.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">15.5.3</span> Button layout<a href="#button-layout" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

When an element uses
<a href="#button-layout-2" id="button-layout:button-layout-2">button
layout</a>, it is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="button-layout:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>, and its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="button-layout:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is that of a
button.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

<span id="button-layout-2" class="dfn">Button layout</span> is as
follows:

- If the element is a [`button`](#the-button-element) element, then the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> property is
  <a href="#expected" id="button-layout:expected">expected</a> to act as
  follows:

  - If the computed value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> is 'inline-grid',
    'grid', 'inline-flex', 'flex', 'none', or 'contents', then behave as
    the computed value.

  - Otherwise, if the computed value of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;-3"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> is a value such
    that the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#outer-display-type"
    id="button-layout:outer-display-type"
    data-x-internal="outer-display-type">outer display type</a> is
    'inline', then behave as 'inline-block'.

  - Otherwise, behave as 'flow-root'.

- The element is
  <a href="#expected" id="button-layout:expected-2">expected</a> to
  establish a new
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context"
  id="button-layout:formatting-context"
  data-x-internal="formatting-context">formatting context</a> for its
  contents. The type of this formatting context is determined by its
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;-4"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> value, as usual.

- If the element is
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position/#absolute-position"
  id="button-layout:absolutely-positioned"
  data-x-internal="absolutely-positioned">absolutely-positioned</a>,
  then for the purpose of the [CSS visual formatting
  model](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#visuren), act as if the element
  is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
  id="button-layout:replaced-element"
  data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a>.
  [\[CSS\]](#refsCSS)

- If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
  id="button-layout:computed-value"
  data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size"
  id="button-layout:&#39;inline-size&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;inline-size&#39;">'inline-size'</a> is 'auto',
  then the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value"
  id="button-layout:used-value" data-x-internal="used-value">used
  value</a> is the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#fit-content-inline-size"
  id="button-layout:fit-content-inline-size"
  data-x-internal="fit-content-inline-size">fit-content inline size</a>.

- For the purpose of the 'normal' keyword of the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-self"
  id="button-layout:&#39;align-self&#39;"
  data-x-internal="&#39;align-self&#39;">'align-self'</a> property, act
  as if the element is a replaced element.

- If the element is an [`input`](#the-input-element) element, or if it
  is a [`button`](#the-button-element) element and its computed value
  for <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
  id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;-5"
  data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> is not
  'inline-grid', 'grid', 'inline-flex', or 'flex', then the element's
  box has a child <span id="anonymous-button-content-box"
  class="dfn">anonymous button content box</span> with the following
  behaviors:

  - The box is a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-level"
    id="button-layout:block-level"
    data-x-internal="block-level">block-level</a>
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-container"
    id="button-layout:block-container"
    data-x-internal="block-container">block container</a> that
    establishes a new
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-formatting-context"
    id="button-layout:block-formatting-context"
    data-x-internal="block-formatting-context">block formatting context</a>
    (i.e., <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop"
    id="button-layout:&#39;display&#39;-6"
    data-x-internal="&#39;display&#39;">'display'</a> is 'flow-root').

  - If the box does not overflow in the horizontal axis, then it is
    centered horizontally.

  - If the box does not overflow in the vertical axis, then it is
    centered vertically.

  Otherwise, there is no <a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
  id="button-layout:anonymous-button-content-box">anonymous button content
  box</a>.

</div>

Need to define the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="button-layout:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.4</span> The [`button`](#the-button-element) element<a href="#the-button-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

The [`button`](#the-button-element) element, when it generates a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box"
id="the-button-element-2:css-box" data-x-internal="css-box">CSS box</a>,
is <a href="#expected" id="the-button-element-2:expected">expected</a>
to depict a button and to use <a href="#button-layout-2"
id="the-button-element-2:button-layout-2">button layout</a> whose
<a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
id="the-button-element-2:anonymous-button-content-box">anonymous button
content box</a>'s contents (if there is an
<a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
id="the-button-element-2:anonymous-button-content-box-2">anonymous
button content box</a>) are the child boxes the element's box would
otherwise have.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.5</span> The [`details`](#the-details-element) and [`summary`](#the-summary-element) elements<a href="#the-details-and-summary-elements" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

details, summary {
  display: block;
}
details > summary:first-of-type {
  display: list-item;
  counter-increment: list-item 0;
  list-style: disclosure-closed inside;
}
details[open] > summary:first-of-type {
  list-style-type: disclosure-open;
}
```

The [`details`](#the-details-element) element is <a href="#expected"
id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected">expected</a> to have an
internal <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-details-and-summary-elements:shadow-tree"
data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow tree</a> with three child elements:

1.  The first child element is a [`slot`](#the-slot-element) that is
    <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-2">expected</a> to
    take the [`details`](#the-details-element) element's first
    [`summary`](#the-summary-element) element child, if any. This
    element has a single child [`summary`](#the-summary-element) element
    called the <span id="default-summary" class="dfn">default
    summary</span> which has text content that is
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:implementation-defined"
    data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a>
    (and probably locale-specific).

    The [`summary`](#the-summary-element) element that this slot
    <a href="#represents"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:represents">represents</a> is
    <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-3">expected</a> to
    allow the user to request the details be shown or hidden.

2.  The second child element is a [`slot`](#the-slot-element) that is
    <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-4">expected</a> to
    take the [`details`](#the-details-element) element's remaining
    descendants, if any. This element has no contents.

    This element is <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-5">expected</a> to
    match the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#details-content-pseudo"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:&#39;::details-content&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;::details-content&#39;">'::details-content'</a>
    pseudo-element.

    <div algorithm="">

    This element is <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-6">expected</a> to
    have its [`style`](#attr-style) attribute set to
    "`display: block; content-visibility: hidden;`" when the
    [`details`](#the-details-element) element does not have an
    [`open`](#attr-details-open) attribute. When it does have the
    [`open`](#attr-details-open) attribute, the [`style`](#attr-style)
    attribute is <a href="#expected"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:expected-7">expected</a> to be
    set to "`display: block;`".

    </div>

    Because the slots are hidden inside a shadow tree, this
    [`style`](#attr-style) attribute is not directly visible to author
    code. Its impacts, however, are visible. Notably, the choice of
    `content-visibility: hidden` instead of, e.g., `display: none`,
    impacts the results of various APIs that query layout information.

3.  The third child element is either a [`link`](#the-link-element) or
    [`style`](#the-style-element) element with the following styles for
    the <a href="#default-summary"
    id="the-details-and-summary-elements:default-summary">default
    summary</a>:

    ``` css
    :host summary {
      display: list-item;
      counter-increment: list-item 0;
      list-style: disclosure-closed inside;
    }
    :host([open]) summary {
      list-style-type: disclosure-open;
    }
    ```

    The position of this child element relative to the other two is not
    observable. This means that implementations might have it in a
    different order relative to its siblings. Implementations might even
    associate the style with the shadow tree using a mechanism that is
    not an element.

The structure of this shadow tree is observable through the ways that
the children of the [`details`](#the-details-element) element and the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#details-content-pseudo"
id="the-details-and-summary-elements:&#39;::details-content&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;::details-content&#39;">'::details-content'</a>
pseudo-element respond to CSS styles.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.6</span> The [`input`](#the-input-element) element as a text entry widget<a href="#the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget"
class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">Text</a>,
<a href="#telephone-state-(type=tel)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:telephone-state-(type=tel)">Telephone</a>,
<a href="#url-state-(type=url)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:url-state-(type=url)">URL</a>,
or <a href="#email-state-(type=email)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:email-state-(type=email)">Email</a>
state, is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
depicting a one-line text control.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)-2">Search</a>
state is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:devolvable-widget-2"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:native-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-2">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;inline-block&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
depicting a one-line text control. If the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of the element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;appearance&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;appearance&#39;">'appearance'</a> property is not
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-appearance-textfield"
data-x-internal="&#39;textfield&#39;"><code
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;textfield&#39;">'textfield'</code></a>,
it may have a distinct style indicating that it is a search field.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#password-state-(type=password)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:password-state-(type=password)">Password</a>
state is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:devolvable-widget-3"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:native-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-3">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;inline-block&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
depicting a one-line text control that obscures data entry.

</div>

For [`input`](#the-input-element) elements whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the above states, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:used-value"
data-x-internal="used-value">used value</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;line-height&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;line-height&#39;">'line-height'</a> property must
be a length value that is no smaller than what the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:used-value-2"
data-x-internal="used-value">used value</a> would be for 'line-height:
normal'.

The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:used-value-3"
data-x-internal="used-value">used value</a> will not be the actual
keyword 'normal'. Also, this rule does not affect the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a>.

<div algorithm="">

If these text controls provide a text selection, then, when the user
changes the current selection, the user agent is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-4">expected</a> to
<a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:queue-an-element-task">queue
an element task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:user-interaction-task-source">user
interaction task source</a> given the [`input`](#the-input-element)
element to <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`select`](#event-select) at the element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
attribute initialized to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the above states is an
<a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#element-with-default-preferred-size"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:element-with-default-preferred-size"
data-x-internal="element-with-default-preferred-size">element with
default preferred size</a>, and user agents are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-5">expected</a> to
apply the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;field-sizing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> CSS property
to the element. User agents are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-6">expected</a> to
determine the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:inline-size"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:intrinsic-size"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> by the following
steps:

1.  If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property
    on the element has a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:computed-value-3"
    data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:field-sizing-content"
    data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:inline-size-2"
    data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> is determined by the
    text which the element shows. The text is either a
    <a href="#concept-fe-value"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:concept-fe-value">value</a>
    or a short hint specified by the
    [`placeholder`](#attr-input-placeholder) attribute. User agents may
    take the text caret size into account in the
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:inline-size-3"
    data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a>.

2.  If the element has a [`size`](#attr-input-size) attribute, and
    parsing that attribute's value using the
    <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
    for parsing non-negative integers</a> doesn't generate an error,
    return the value obtained from applying the
    <a href="#converting-a-character-width-to-pixels"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:converting-a-character-width-to-pixels">converting
    a character width to pixels</a> algorithm to the value of the
    attribute.

3.  Otherwise, return the value obtained from applying the
    <a href="#converting-a-character-width-to-pixels"
    id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:converting-a-character-width-to-pixels-2">converting
    a character width to pixels</a> algorithm to the number 20.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="converting-a-character-width-to-pixels"
class="dfn">converting a character width to pixels</span> algorithm
returns (`size`-1)×`avg` + `max`, where `size` is the character width to
convert, `avg` is the average character width of the primary font for
the element for which the algorithm is being run, in pixels, and `max`
is the maximum character width of that same font, also in pixels. (The
element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:&#39;letter-spacing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;letter-spacing&#39;">'letter-spacing'</a> property
does not affect the result.)

</div>

These text controls are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:expected-7">expected</a> to
be <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#scroll-container"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:scroll-container"
data-x-internal="scroll-container">scroll containers</a> and support
scrolling in the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-axis"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:inline-axis"
data-x-internal="inline-axis">inline axis</a>, but not the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#block-axis"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:block-axis"
data-x-internal="block-axis">block axis</a>.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:native-appearance-4"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

<a href="#number-state-(type=number)"

state is an <a
