id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:intrinsic-size"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is about one line
high. If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property on
the element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:field-sizing-content"
data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:inline-size"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:intrinsic-size-2"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:expected-8">expected</a>
to be about as wide as necessary to show the current
<a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:concept-fe-value">value</a>.
Otherwise, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:inline-size-2"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:intrinsic-size-3"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:expected-9">expected</a>
to be about as wide as necessary to show the widest possible value.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#date-state-(type=date)"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:date-state-(type=date)-2">Date</a>,
<a href="#month-state-(type=month)"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:month-state-(type=month)-2">Month</a>,
<a href="#week-state-(type=week)"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:week-state-(type=week)-2">Week</a>,
<a href="#time-state-(type=time)"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:time-state-(type=time)-2">Time</a>,
or <a href="#local-date-and-time-state-(type=datetime-local)"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:local-date-and-time-state-(type=datetime-local)-2">Local
Date and Time</a> state, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-domain-specific-widgets:expected-10">expected</a>
to be about one line high, and about as wide as necessary to show the
widest possible value.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">15.5.8</span> The [`input`](#the-input-element) element as a range control<a href="#the-input-element-as-a-range-control" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#range-state-(type=range)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:range-state-(type=range)">Range</a>
state is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:non-devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="non-devolvable-widget">non-devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
depicting a slider control.

</div>

When this control has a <a href="#horizontal-writing-mode"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:horizontal-writing-mode">horizontal
writing mode</a>, the control is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:expected-2">expected</a> to be
a horizontal slider. Its lowest value is on the right if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:&#39;direction&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and on the
left otherwise. When this control has a <a href="#vertical-writing-mode"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:vertical-writing-mode">vertical
writing mode</a>, it is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:expected-3">expected</a> to be
a vertical slider. Its lowest value is on the bottom if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:&#39;direction&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and on the
top otherwise.

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#attr-input-list)
attribute) are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:expected-4">expected</a> to be
shown as tick marks on the slider, which the slider can snap to.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-range-control:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.9</span> The [`input`](#the-input-element) element as a color well<a href="#the-input-element-as-a-colour-well" class="self-link"></a>

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#color-state-(type=color)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:color-state-(type=color)">Color</a>
state is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:expected">expected</a> to depict
a color well, which, when activated, provides the user with a color
picker (e.g. a color wheel or color palette) from which the color can be
changed. The element, when it generates a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:css-box"
data-x-internal="css-box">CSS box</a>, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:expected-2">expected</a> to use
<a href="#button-layout-2"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:button-layout-2">button
layout</a>, that has no child boxes of the
<a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:anonymous-button-content-box">anonymous
button content box</a>. The <a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:anonymous-button-content-box-2">anonymous
button content box</a> is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:expected-3">expected</a> to have
a <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:presentational-hints">presentational
hint</a> setting the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:&#39;background-color&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;background-color&#39;">'background-color'</a>
property to the element's <a href="#concept-fe-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:concept-fe-value">value</a>.

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#attr-input-list)
attribute) are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:expected-4">expected</a> to be
shown in the color picker interface, not on the color well itself.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-input-element-as-a-colour-well:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.11</span> The [`input`](#the-input-element) element as a file upload control<a href="#the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control"
class="self-link"></a>

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:file-upload-state-(type=file)">File
Upload</a> state, when it generates a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:css-box"
data-x-internal="css-box">CSS box</a>, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
containing a span of text giving the filename(s) of the
<a href="#concept-input-type-file-selected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:concept-input-type-file-selected">selected
files</a>, if any, followed by a button that, when activated, provides
the user with a file picker from which the selection can be changed. The
button is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:expected-2">expected</a>
to use <a href="#button-layout-2"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:button-layout-2">button
layout</a> and match the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#file-selector-button-pseudo"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:&#39;::file-selector-button&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;::file-selector-button&#39;">'::file-selector-button'</a>
pseudo-element. The contents of its
<a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:anonymous-button-content-box">anonymous
button content box</a> are <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:expected-3">expected</a>
to be <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> (and
possibly locale-specific) text, for example "Choose file".

User agents may handle an [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#file-upload-state-(type=file)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:file-upload-state-(type=file)-2">File
Upload</a> state as an <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#element-with-default-preferred-size"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:element-with-default-preferred-size"
data-x-internal="element-with-default-preferred-size">element with
default preferred size</a>, and user agents may apply the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:&#39;field-sizing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> CSS property
to the element. If the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property on
the element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:field-sizing-content"
data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:intrinsic-size"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> of the element is
<a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:expected-4">expected</a>
to depend on its content such as the <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#file-selector-button-pseudo"
id="the-input-element-as-a-file-upload-control:&#39;::file-selector-button&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;::file-selector-button&#39;">'::file-selector-button'</a>
pseudo-element and chosen file names.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.12</span> The [`input`](#the-input-element) element as a button<a href="#the-input-element-as-a-button" class="self-link"></a>

An [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute is in the
<a href="#submit-button-state-(type=submit)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:submit-button-state-(type=submit)">Submit
Button</a>, <a href="#reset-button-state-(type=reset)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:reset-button-state-(type=reset)">Reset
Button</a>, or <a href="#button-state-(type=button)"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:button-state-(type=button)">Button</a>
state, when it generates a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:css-box" data-x-internal="css-box">CSS
box</a>, is <a href="#expected"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:expected">expected</a> to depict a
button and use <a href="#button-layout-2"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:button-layout-2">button layout</a> and
the contents of the <a href="#anonymous-button-content-box"

an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
id="the-input-element-as-a-button:implementation-defined"
data-x-internal="implementation-defined">implementation-defined</a> (and
probably locale-specific) fashion, if not.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.13</span> The [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element<a href="#the-marquee-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

marquee {
  display: inline-block;
  text-align: initial;
  overflow: hidden !important;
}
```

<div algorithm="">

The [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element, while
<a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element-2:concept-marquee-on">turned on</a>, is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
render in an animated fashion according to its attributes as follows:

If the element's [`behavior`](#attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the <a href="#attr-marquee-behavior-scroll"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-behavior-scroll">scroll</a> state  
Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the
[`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such
that it begins off the start side of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the inner end
side.

For example, if the [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute is
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-left"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-left">left</a> (the
default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are
off the side of the right edge of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>, and the contents would
then slide up to the point where the left edge of the contents are flush
with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area-2"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-2">expected</a>
to <a href="#increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index"
id="the-marquee-element-2:increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index">increment
the marquee current loop index</a>. If the element is still
<a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element-2:concept-marquee-on-2">turned on</a> after
this, then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-3">expected</a>
to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the <a href="#attr-marquee-behavior-slide"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-behavior-slide">slide</a> state  
Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the
[`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such
that it begins off the start side of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), and ends off the end side of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element).

For example, if the [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute is
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-left"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-left-2">left</a> (the
default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are
off the side of the right edge of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area-3"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>, and the contents would
then slide up to the point where the *right* edge of the contents are
flush with the left inner edge of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area-4"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-4">expected</a>
to <a href="#increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index"
id="the-marquee-element-2:increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index-2">increment
the marquee current loop index</a>. If the element is still
<a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element-2:concept-marquee-on-3">turned on</a> after
this, then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-5">expected</a>
to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the <a href="#attr-marquee-behavior-alternate"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-behavior-alternate">alternate</a> state  
When the <a href="#marquee-current-loop-index"
id="the-marquee-element-2:marquee-current-loop-index">marquee current
loop index</a> is even (or zero), slide the contents of the element in
the direction described by the [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction)
attribute as defined below, such that it begins flush with the start
side of the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the
end side of the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element).

When the <a href="#marquee-current-loop-index"
id="the-marquee-element-2:marquee-current-loop-index-2">marquee current
loop index</a> is odd, slide the contents of the element in the opposite
direction than that described by the
[`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such
that it begins flush with the end side of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the start side of
the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element).

For example, if the [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute is
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-left"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-left-3">left</a> (the
default), then the contents would with their right edge flush with the
right inner edge of the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area-5"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>, and the contents would
then slide up to the point where the *left* edge of the contents are
flush with the left inner edge of the
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)'s
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area"
id="the-marquee-element-2:content-area-6"
data-x-internal="content-area">content area</a>.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-6">expected</a>
to <a href="#increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index"
id="the-marquee-element-2:increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index-3">increment
the marquee current loop index</a>. If the element is still
<a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element-2:concept-marquee-on-4">turned on</a> after
this, then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-7">expected</a>
to continue the animation.

</div>

The [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute has the meanings
described in the following table:

| [`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute state | Direction of animation | Start edge | End edge | Opposite direction |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| <a href="#attr-marquee-direction-left"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-left-4">left</a> | ← Right to left | Right | Left | → Left to Right |
| <a href="#attr-marquee-direction-right"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-right">right</a> | → Left to Right | Left | Right | ← Right to left |
| <a href="#attr-marquee-direction-up"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-up">up</a> | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) | Bottom | Top | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) |
| <a href="#attr-marquee-direction-down"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-down">down</a> | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) | Top | Bottom | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) |

In any case, the animation should proceed such that there is a delay
given by the <a href="#marquee-scroll-interval"
id="the-marquee-element-2:marquee-scroll-interval">marquee scroll
interval</a> between each frame, and such that the content moves at most
the distance given by the <a href="#marquee-scroll-distance"
id="the-marquee-element-2:marquee-scroll-distance">marquee scroll
distance</a> with each frame.

<div algorithm="">

When a [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element has a `bgcolor`
attribute set, the value is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-8">expected</a>
to be parsed using the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value"
id="the-marquee-element-2:rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value">rules
for parsing a legacy color value</a>, and if that does not return
failure, the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-marquee-element-2:expected-9">expected</a>
to treat the attribute as a <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-marquee-element-2:presentational-hints">presentational hint</a>
setting the element's <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;background-color&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;background-color&#39;">'background-color'</a>
property to the resulting color.

</div>

The `width` and `height` attributes on a
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element
<a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="the-marquee-element-2:maps-to-the-dimension-property">map to the
dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;width&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;width&#39;">'width'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;height&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;height&#39;">'height'</a> on the element
respectively.

<div algorithm="">

The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height"
id="the-marquee-element-2:natural-height"
data-x-internal="natural-height">natural height</a> of a
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element with its
[`direction`](#attr-marquee-direction) attribute in the
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-up"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-up-2">up</a> or
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-down"
id="the-marquee-element-2:attr-marquee-direction-down-2">down</a> states
is 200 <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>.

</div>

The `vspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element
<a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="the-marquee-element-2:maps-to-the-dimension-property-2">maps to the
dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-top"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;margin-top&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-top&#39;">'margin-top'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-bottom"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;margin-bottom&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-bottom&#39;">'margin-bottom'</a> on the
element. The `hspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)
element <a href="#maps-to-the-dimension-property"
id="the-marquee-element-2:maps-to-the-dimension-property-3">maps to the
dimension properties</a>
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-left"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;margin-left&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-left&#39;">'margin-left'</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-right"
id="the-marquee-element-2:&#39;margin-right&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;margin-right&#39;">'margin-right'</a> on the
element.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.14</span> The [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element<a href="#the-meter-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

meter { appearance: auto; }
```

<div algorithm="">

The [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-meter-element-2:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-meter-element-2:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected" id="the-meter-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box with a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;block-size&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;block-size&#39;">'block-size'</a> of '1em' and an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;inline-size&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-size&#39;">'inline-size'</a> of '5em', a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;vertical-align&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;vertical-align&#39;">'vertical-align'</a> of
'-0.2em', and with its contents depicting a gauge.

</div>

When this element has a <a href="#horizontal-writing-mode"
id="the-meter-element-2:horizontal-writing-mode">horizontal writing
mode</a>, the depiction is
<a href="#expected" id="the-meter-element-2:expected-2">expected</a> to
be of a horizontal gauge. Its minimum value is on the right if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;direction&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-meter-element-2:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and on the
left otherwise. When this element has a <a href="#vertical-writing-mode"
id="the-meter-element-2:vertical-writing-mode">vertical writing mode</a>,
it is
<a href="#expected" id="the-meter-element-2:expected-3">expected</a> to
depict a vertical gauge. Its minimum value is on the bottom if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-meter-element-2:&#39;direction&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-meter-element-2:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and on the
top otherwise.

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-meter-element-2:expected-4">expected</a> to
use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for gauges, if
any.

Requirements for what must be depicted in the gauge are included in the
definition of the [`meter`](#the-meter-element) element.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-meter-element-2:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.15</span> The [`progress`](#the-progress-element) element<a href="#the-progress-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

progress { appearance: auto; }
```

<div algorithm="">

The [`progress`](#the-progress-element) element is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-progress-element-2:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-progress-element-2:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> is
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box with a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;block-size&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;block-size&#39;">'block-size'</a> of '1em' and an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;inline-size&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-size&#39;">'inline-size'</a> of '10em', and
a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;vertical-align&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;vertical-align&#39;">'vertical-align'</a> of
'-0.2em'.

</div>

<img src="/images/sample-progress.png" class="extra" width="276"
height="115" /> When this element has a
<a href="#horizontal-writing-mode"
id="the-progress-element-2:horizontal-writing-mode">horizontal writing
mode</a>, the element is
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected-2">expected</a>
to be depicted as a horizontal progress bar. The start is on the right
and the end is on the left if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;direction&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property on this
element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-progress-element-2:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and with
the start on the left and the end on the right otherwise. When this
element has a <a href="#vertical-writing-mode"
id="the-progress-element-2:vertical-writing-mode">vertical writing
mode</a>, it is
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected-3">expected</a>
to be depicted as a vertical progress bar. The start is on the bottom
and the end is on the top if the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction"
id="the-progress-element-2:&#39;direction&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;direction&#39;">'direction'</a> property on this
element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-progress-element-2:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of 'rtl', and with
the start on the top and the end on the bottom otherwise.

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected-4">expected</a>
to use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for progress
bars. In particular, user agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected-5">expected</a>
to use different presentations for determinate and indeterminate
progress bars. User agents are also
<a href="#expected" id="the-progress-element-2:expected-6">expected</a>
to vary the presentation based on the dimensions of the element.

Requirements for how to determine if the progress bar is determinate or
indeterminate, and what progress a determinate progress bar is to show,
are included in the definition of the
[`progress`](#the-progress-element) element.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-progress-element-2:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

#### <span class="secno">15.5.16</span> The [`select`](#the-select-element) element<a href="#the-select-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

The [`select`](#the-select-element) element is an <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#element-with-default-preferred-size"
id="the-select-element-2:element-with-default-preferred-size"
data-x-internal="element-with-default-preferred-size">element with
default preferred size</a>, and user agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
apply the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;field-sizing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> CSS property
to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements.

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element is either a
<span id="list-box" class="dfn" dfn-for="select" export="">list
box</span> or a <span id="drop-down-box" class="dfn" dfn-for="select"
export="">drop-down box</span>, depending on its attributes.

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element whose
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is present is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-2">expected</a> to
render as a multi-select
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box">list box</a> if
its <a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-size">display size</a> is
greater than 1. If the [`select`](#the-select-element) element has the
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute and a
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-size-2">display size</a> of 1,
then it may render as a multi-select <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box">drop-down box</a> if the
platform supports it; otherwise as a multi-select
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-2">list box</a>.

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element whose
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-3">expected</a> to
render as a single-select <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-2">drop-down box</a> if its
<a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-size-3">display size</a> is 1,
or as a single-select
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-3">list box</a> if
its <a href="#concept-select-size"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-size-4">display size</a> is
greater than 1.

<div algorithm="">

When the element renders as a
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-4">list box</a>,
it is a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-select-element-2:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-4">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box. The
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-select-element-2:inline-size"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-select-element-2:intrinsic-size"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is the
<a href="#width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels"
id="the-select-element-2:width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels">width of the
<code>select</code>'s labels</a> plus the width of a scrollbar. The
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#block-size"
id="the-select-element-2:block-size" data-x-internal="block-size">block
size</a> of its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-select-element-2:intrinsic-size-2"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is determined by the
following steps:

1.  If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
    id="the-select-element-2:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property
    on the element has a
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
    id="the-select-element-2:computed-value"
    data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
    id="the-select-element-2:field-sizing-content"
    data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, return the
    height necessary to contain all rows for items.

2.  If the [`size`](#attr-select-size) attribute is absent or it has no
    valid value, return the height necessary to contain four rows.

3.  Otherwise, return the height necessary to contain as many rows for
    items as given by the element's <a href="#concept-select-size"
    id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-size-5">display size</a>.

</div>

A [`select`](#the-select-element) element which is being rendered as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-3">drop-down box</a> is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-5">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;inline-block&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box. The
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-select-element-2:inline-size-2"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-select-element-2:intrinsic-size-3"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is the
<a href="#width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels"
id="the-select-element-2:width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels-2">width of
the <code>select</code>'s labels</a>. If the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property on
the element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-select-element-2:computed-value-2"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
id="the-select-element-2:field-sizing-content-2"
data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size"
id="the-select-element-2:inline-size-3"
data-x-internal="inline-size">inline size</a> of the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-select-element-2:intrinsic-size-4"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> depends on the shown
text. The shown text is typically the label of an
[`option`](#the-option-element) of which
<a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</a>
is set to true.

<div algorithm="">

When the element renders as a <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-4">drop-down box</a>, it is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-select-element-2:devolvable-widget-2"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>. Its
appearance in the devolved state, as well as its appearance when the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-select-element-2:computed-value-3"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of the element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;appearance&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;appearance&#39;">'appearance'</a> property is <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-appearance-menulist-button"
data-x-internal="&#39;menulist-button&#39;"><code
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;menulist-button&#39;">'menulist-button'</code></a>,
is that of a drop-down box, including a "drop-down button", but not
necessarily rendered using a native control of the host operating
system. In such a state, CSS properties such as
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;color&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;color&#39;">'color'</a>, <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;background-color&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;background-color&#39;">'background-color'</a>, and
'border' should not be disregarded (as is generally permissible when
rendering an element according to its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a>).

</div>

In either case
(<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-5">list box</a>
or <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-5">drop-down box</a>), the
element's items are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-6">expected</a> to
be the element's <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-option-list">list of options</a>,
with the element's [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-tree-child"
data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a> providing headers for
groups of options where applicable.

[`select`](#the-select-element) elements which render as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-6">drop-down box</a> support a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> in addition to
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

[`select`](#the-select-element) elements which render as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-7">drop-down box</a> without the
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute or as a
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-6">list box</a>
support a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> in addition to
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-2"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

The [`select`](#the-select-element) element's <a href="#select-popover"
id="the-select-element-2:select-popover">select popover</a> supports a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> and a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-4"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a>. The
<a href="#select-popover"
id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-2">select popover</a> can only
be rendered with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-4"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> if its associated
[`select`](#the-select-element) is being rendered with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-5"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>.

<div algorithm="">

When a [`select`](#the-select-element) is being rendered as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-8">drop-down box</a> with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-6"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, it is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-7">expected</a> to
render with a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-select-element-2:shadow-tree"
data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow tree</a> that contains the
following elements:

1.  A <span id="select-button-slot" class="dfn">select button
    slot</span>, which is a [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element. It is
    appended to the [`select`](#the-select-element)'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root"
    id="the-select-element-2:shadow-root"
    data-x-internal="shadow-root">shadow root</a> as the first child. It
    is
    <a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-8">expected</a>
    to take the first child element of the
    [`select`](#the-select-element) if the first child element is a
    [`button`](#the-button-element).

2.  A <span id="select-fallback-button-text" class="dfn">select fallback
    button text</span>, which is a [`div`](#the-div-element) element. It
    is appended to the <a href="#select-button-slot"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-button-slot">select button slot</a>.

3.  A <span id="select-popover" class="dfn">select popover</span>, which
    is a [`div`](#the-div-element) element. It is appended to the
    [`select`](#the-select-element)'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root"
    id="the-select-element-2:shadow-root-2"
    data-x-internal="shadow-root">shadow root</a> as the second child,
    after the <a href="#select-button-slot"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-button-slot-2">select button slot</a>.
    The [`select`](#the-select-element) element's
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo"
    id="the-select-element-2:&#39;::picker&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;::picker&#39;">'::picker'</a> pseudo-element
    is the <a href="#select-popover"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-3">select popover</a> if the
    <a
    href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#typedef-picker-form-control-identifier"
    id="the-select-element-2:picker-form-control-identifier"
    data-x-internal="picker-form-control-identifier">provided argument</a>
    is `select`.

4.  A <span id="select-popover-slot" class="dfn">select popover
    slot</span>, which is a [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element. It is
    appended to the <a href="#select-popover"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-4">select popover</a>. It is
    <a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-9">expected</a>
    to take all child nodes of the [`select`](#the-select-element)
    except for the first child [`button`](#the-button-element), which is
    taken by the <a href="#select-button-slot"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-button-slot-3">select button slot</a>.

</div>

Since <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-7"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> is determined by
computing style, it isn't possible to swap this DOM structure when
switching appearance. Implementations can always include the DOM
structure for <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-8"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> when the
[`select`](#the-select-element) is rendered as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-9">drop-down box</a> and then
choose to include or exclude it from the layout tree in order to control
whether it gets rendered or not.

The <a href="#select-popover"
id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-5">select popover</a> is only
rendered when it is opted in to
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-9"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a> separately from
the [`select`](#the-select-element) element. Otherwise, a native picker
is used.

When a [`select`](#the-select-element) is being rendered as a
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-7">list box</a>
with <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-10"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, it is expected to
render with a <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree"
id="the-select-element-2:shadow-tree-2"
data-x-internal="shadow-tree">shadow tree</a> that contains a
<span id="select-list-box-slot" class="dfn">select list box slot</span>,
which is a [`slot`](#the-slot-element) element. The
<a href="#select-list-box-slot"
id="the-select-element-2:select-list-box-slot">select list box slot</a>
is appended to the [`select`](#the-select-element)'s
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root"
id="the-select-element-2:shadow-root-3"
data-x-internal="shadow-root">shadow root</a> as the first child. The
<a href="#select-list-box-slot"
id="the-select-element-2:select-list-box-slot-2">select list box
slot</a> is expected to take all children of the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element.

The <a href="#select-popover"
id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-6">select popover</a>'s <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position/#implicit-anchor-element"
id="the-select-element-2:implicit-anchor-element"
data-x-internal="implicit-anchor-element">implicit anchor element</a> is
its associated [`select`](#the-select-element) element.

When a [`select`](#the-select-element) element is being rendered with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-5"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-3"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>, or the
[`select`](#the-select-element) element is being rendered as a
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-8">list box</a>,
the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;::picker&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;::picker&#39;">'::picker'</a> pseudo-element and
the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#selectordef-picker-icon"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;::picker-icon&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;::picker-icon&#39;">'::picker-icon'</a>
pseudo-element do not apply.

The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;::picker&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;::picker&#39;">'::picker'</a> pseudo-element is
not rendered when it has
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-6"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-4"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

The <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#checkmark"
id="the-select-element-2:&#39;::checkmark&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;::checkmark&#39;">'::checkmark'</a> pseudo-element
only applies to [`option`](#the-option-element) elements which are
<a href="#option-base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:option-base-appearance">being rendered with
base appearance</a>.

An [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-10">expected</a>
to be rendered by displaying the element's
[`label`](#attr-optgroup-label) attribute.

<div algorithm="">

To determine if a
<span id="select's-options-are-being-rendered-with-base-appearance"
class="dfn">`select`'s `option`s are being rendered with base
appearance</span>, given a [`select`](#the-select-element) element
`select`:

1.  If `select` is being rendered as a
    <a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-9">list box</a>
    with <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
    id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-11"
    data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, then return
    true.

2.  If `select` is being rendered as a <a href="#drop-down-box"
    id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-10">drop-down box</a> with
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
    id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-12"
    data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, and its
    <a href="#select-popover"
    id="the-select-element-2:select-popover-7">select popover</a> is
    being rendered with
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
    id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-13"
    data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>, and `select`
    does not have the [`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute set,
    then return true.

3.  Return false.

</div>

An [`option`](#the-option-element) element is
<span id="option-base-appearance" class="dfn">rendered with base
appearance</span> if it has a
<a href="#option-element-nearest-ancestor-select"
id="the-select-element-2:option-element-nearest-ancestor-select">nearest
ancestor <code>select</code></a> and the
<a href="#select&#39;s-options-are-being-rendered-with-base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:select&#39;s-options-are-being-rendered-with-base-appearance"><code>select</code>'s
<code>option</code>s are being rendered with base appearance</a>.

An [`option`](#the-option-element) element is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-11">expected</a>
to be rendered by displaying the result of
<a href="#collect-option-text"
id="the-select-element-2:collect-option-text">collect option text</a>
given the [`option`](#the-option-element) and true, indented under its
[`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element) element if it has one. If the
[`option`](#the-option-element) <a href="#option-base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:option-base-appearance-2">is being rendered
with base appearance</a> and the [`option`](#the-option-element)'s
[`label`](#attr-option-label) attribute is not set, then the
[`option`](#the-option-element) is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-12">expected</a>
to render all of its children rather than by displaying its
<a href="#concept-option-label"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-option-label">label</a>.

Each sequence of one or more child [`hr`](#the-hr-element) element
siblings may be rendered as a single separator.

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="width-of-the-select's-labels" class="dfn">width of the
`select`'s labels</span> is the wider of the width necessary to render
the widest [`optgroup`](#the-optgroup-element), and the width necessary
to render the widest [`option`](#the-option-element) element in the
element's <a href="#concept-select-option-list"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-select-option-list-2">list of
options</a> (including its indent, if any). If the
[`select`](#the-select-element) has the
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) attribute and is being rendered as a
<a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-11">drop-down box</a>, then the
width should also be wide enough to accomodate the text rendered in the
[`select`](#the-select-element) with any combination of
[`option`](#the-option-element)s selected.

The <a href="#width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels"
id="the-select-element-2:width-of-the-select&#39;s-labels-3">width of
the <code>select</code>'s labels</a> has an accomodation for
[`multiple`](#attr-select-multiple) because some implementations use
special text to represent multiple options being selected, such as "2
selected." In this case, the select needs to be wide enough to render "2
selected" in addition to the individual
[`option`](#the-option-element)s.

</div>

If a [`select`](#the-select-element) element contains a
<a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-select-element-2:placeholder-label-option">placeholder label
option</a>, the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-13">expected</a>
to render that [`option`](#the-option-element) in a manner that conveys
that it is a label, rather than a valid option of the control. This can
include preventing the <a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-select-element-2:placeholder-label-option-2">placeholder label
option</a> from being explicitly selected by the user. When the
<a href="#placeholder-label-option"
id="the-select-element-2:placeholder-label-option-3">placeholder label
option</a>'s <a href="#concept-option-selectedness"
id="the-select-element-2:concept-option-selectedness-2">selectedness</a>
is true, the control is
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-14">expected</a>
to be displayed in a fashion that indicates that no valid option is
currently selected.

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-15">expected</a>
to render the labels in a [`select`](#the-select-element) in such a
manner that any alignment remains consistent whether the label is being
displayed as part of the page or in a menu control.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-7"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-5"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

The following styles are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-16">expected</a>
to apply to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements when they are being
rendered with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-8"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-6"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  letter-spacing: initial;
  word-spacing: initial;
  line-height: initial;
}
```

The following styles are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-17">expected</a>
to apply to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements when they are being
rendered as a <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-12">drop-down box</a> with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:native-appearance-9"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> or
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:primitive-appearance-7"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  display: inline-block;
}
```

The following styles are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-18">expected</a>
to apply to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements when they are being
rendered with <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-14"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  background-color: transparent;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  user-select: none;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

select option:enabled:hover {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 10%, transparent);
}
select option:enabled:active {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 20%, transparent);
}
select option:disabled {
  color: color-mix(currentColor 50%, transparent);
}

select option {
  min-inline-size: 24px;
  min-block-size: max(24px, 1lh);
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  padding-block-end: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5em;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

select option::checkmark {
  content: '\2713' / '';
}
select option:not(:checked)::checkmark {
  visibility: hidden;
}

select optgroup {
  display: block;
  font-weight: bolder;
}

select optgroup option {
  font-weight: normal;
}

select optgroup legend {
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  min-block-size: 1lh;
}
```

The following styles are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-19">expected</a>
to apply to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements when they are being
rendered as a <a href="#drop-down-box"
id="the-select-element-2:drop-down-box-13">drop-down box</a> with
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-15"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  border-radius: 0.5em;
  padding-block: 0.25em;
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  min-block-size: calc-size(auto, max(size, 24px, 1lh));
  min-inline-size: calc-size(auto, max(size, 24px));
  display: inline-flex;
  gap: 0.5em;
  border-radius: 0.5em;
  field-sizing: content !important;
}

select > button:first-child {
  all: unset;
  display: contents;
}

select:enabled:hover {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 10%, transparent);
}
select:enabled:active {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 20%, transparent);
}
select:disabled {
  color: color-mix(currentColor 50%, transparent);
}

::picker(select) {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  border: 1px solid;
  padding: 0;
  color: CanvasText;
  background-color: Canvas;
  margin: 0;
  inset: auto;
  min-inline-size: anchor-size(self-inline);
  max-block-size: stretch;
  overflow: auto;
  position-area: block-end span-inline-end;
  position-try-order: most-block-size;
  position-try-fallbacks:
    block-start span-inline-end,
    block-end span-inline-start,
    block-start span-inline-start;
}

select::picker-icon {
  content: counter(fake-counter-name, disclosure-open);
  display: block;
  margin-inline-start: auto;
}
```

The following styles are
<a href="#expected" id="the-select-element-2:expected-20">expected</a>
to apply to [`select`](#the-select-element) elements when they are being
rendered as a
<a href="#list-box" id="the-select-element-2:list-box-10">list box</a>
with <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance"
id="the-select-element-2:base-appearance-16"
data-x-internal="base-appearance">base appearance</a>:

``` css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  overflow: auto;
  display: inline-block;
  block-size: calc(max(24px, 1lh) * attr(size type(<integer>), 4));
}
```

#### <span class="secno">15.5.17</span> The [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element<a href="#the-textarea-element-2" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

The [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable"
id="the-textarea-element-2:devolvable-widget"
data-x-internal="devolvable-widget">devolvable widget</a>
<a href="#expected" id="the-textarea-element-2:expected">expected</a> to
render as an
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;inline-block&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;inline-block&#39;">'inline-block'</a> box
depicting a multiline text control. If this multiline text control
provides a selection, then, when the user changes the current selection,
the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-textarea-element-2:expected-2">expected</a>
to <a href="#queue-an-element-task"
id="the-textarea-element-2:queue-an-element-task">queue an element
task</a> on the <a href="#user-interaction-task-source"
id="the-textarea-element-2:user-interaction-task-source">user
interaction task source</a> given the
[`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element to
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
id="the-textarea-element-2:concept-event-fire"
data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">fire an event</a> named
[`select`](#event-select) at the element, with the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles"
data-x-internal="dom-event-bubbles"><code
id="the-textarea-element-2:dom-event-bubbles">bubbles</code></a>
attribute initialized to true.

</div>

The [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is an <a
href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#element-with-default-preferred-size"
id="the-textarea-element-2:element-with-default-preferred-size"
data-x-internal="element-with-default-preferred-size">element with
default preferred size</a>, and user agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-textarea-element-2:expected-3">expected</a>
to apply the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;field-sizing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> CSS property
to [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements.

If the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;field-sizing&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;field-sizing&#39;">'field-sizing'</a> property on
the element has a
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value"
id="the-textarea-element-2:computed-value"
data-x-internal="computed-value">computed value</a> of
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content"
id="the-textarea-element-2:field-sizing-content"
data-x-internal="field-sizing-content">'content'</a>, the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-textarea-element-2:intrinsic-size"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is determined from
the text which the element shows. The text is either a
<a href="#concept-textarea-raw-value"
id="the-textarea-element-2:concept-textarea-raw-value">raw value</a> or
a short hint specified by the
[`placeholder`](#attr-textarea-placeholder) attribute. User agents may
take the text caret size into account in the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-textarea-element-2:intrinsic-size-2"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a>. Otherwise, its
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size"
id="the-textarea-element-2:intrinsic-size-3"
data-x-internal="intrinsic-size">intrinsic size</a> is computed from
<a href="#textarea-effective-width"
id="the-textarea-element-2:textarea-effective-width">textarea effective
width</a> and <a href="#textarea-effective-height"
id="the-textarea-element-2:textarea-effective-height">textarea effective
height</a> (as defined below).

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="textarea-effective-width" class="dfn">textarea effective
width</span> of a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is
`size`×`avg` + `sbw`, where `size` is the element's
<a href="#attr-textarea-cols-value"
id="the-textarea-element-2:attr-textarea-cols-value">character width</a>,
`avg` is the average character width of the primary font of the element,
in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;px&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>, and `sbw` is the width of
a scrollbar, in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;px&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>. (The element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;letter-spacing&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;letter-spacing&#39;">'letter-spacing'</a> property
does not affect the result.)

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="textarea-effective-height" class="dfn">textarea effective
height</span> of a [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) element is the
height in <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;px&#39;-3"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> of the number of lines
given by the element's <a href="#attr-textarea-rows-value"
id="the-textarea-element-2:attr-textarea-rows-value">character
height</a>, plus the height of a scrollbar in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;px&#39;-4"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>.

</div>

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-textarea-element-2:expected-4">expected</a>
to apply the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;white-space&#39;"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> CSS property
to [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements. For historical reasons,
if the element has a [`wrap`](#attr-textarea-wrap) attribute whose value
is an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="the-textarea-element-2:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`off`", then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-textarea-element-2:expected-5">expected</a>
to treat the attribute as a <a href="#presentational-hints"
id="the-textarea-element-2:presentational-hints">presentational hint</a>
setting the element's
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property"
id="the-textarea-element-2:&#39;white-space&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;white-space&#39;">'white-space'</a> property to
'pre'.

Need to detail the
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance"
id="the-textarea-element-2:native-appearance"
data-x-internal="native-appearance">native appearance</a> and
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance"
id="the-textarea-element-2:primitive-appearance"
data-x-internal="primitive-appearance">primitive appearance</a>.

### <span class="secno">15.6</span> Frames and framesets<a href="#frames-and-framesets" class="self-link"></a>

<div algorithm="">

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected">expected</a> to
render [`frameset`](#frameset) elements as a box with the height and
width of the <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="frames-and-framesets:viewport"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>, with a surface rendered
according to the following layout algorithm:

1.  The `cols` and `rows` variables are lists of zero or more pairs
    consisting of a number and a unit, the unit being one of
    *percentage*, *relative*, and *absolute*.

    Use the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions"
    id="frames-and-framesets:rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions">rules
    for parsing a list of dimensions</a> to parse the value of the
    element's `cols` attribute, if there is one. Let `cols` be the
    result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

    Use the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions"
    id="frames-and-framesets:rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions-2">rules
    for parsing a list of dimensions</a> to parse the value of the
    element's `rows` attribute, if there is one. Let `rows` be the
    result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

2.  For any of the entries in `cols` or `rows` that have the number zero
    and the unit *relative*, change the entry's number to one.

3.  If `cols` has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the
    value 1 and the unit *relative* to `cols`.

    If `rows` has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the
    value 1 and the unit *relative* to `rows`.

4.  Invoke the algorithm defined below to
    <a href="#convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values"
    id="frames-and-framesets:convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values">convert
    a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values</a> using `cols` as
    the input list, and the width of the surface that the
    [`frameset`](#frameset) is being rendered into, in
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="frames-and-framesets:&#39;px&#39;"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>, as the input
    dimension. Let `sized cols` be the resulting list.

    Invoke the algorithm defined below to
    <a href="#convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values"
    id="frames-and-framesets:convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values-2">convert
    a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values</a> using `rows` as
    the input list, and the height of the surface that the
    [`frameset`](#frameset) is being rendered into, in
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="frames-and-framesets:&#39;px&#39;-2"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>, as the input
    dimension. Let `sized rows` be the resulting list.

5.  Split the surface into a grid of `w`×`h` rectangles, where `w` is
    the number of entries in `sized cols` and `h` is the number of
    entries in `sized rows`.

    Size the columns so that each column in the grid is as many
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="frames-and-framesets:&#39;px&#39;-3"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> wide as the
    corresponding entry in the `sized cols` list.

    Size the rows so that each row in the grid is as many
    <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
    id="frames-and-framesets:&#39;px&#39;-4"
    data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a> high as the
    corresponding entry in the `sized rows` list.

6.  Let `children` be the list of [`frame`](#frame) and
    [`frameset`](#frameset) elements that are
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child"
    id="frames-and-framesets:concept-tree-child"
    data-x-internal="concept-tree-child">children</a> of the
    [`frameset`](#frameset) element for which the algorithm was invoked.

7.  For each row of the grid of rectangles created in the previous step,
    from top to bottom, run these substeps:

    1.  For each rectangle in the row, from left to right, run these
        substeps:

        1.  If there are any elements left in `children`, take the first
            element in the list, and assign it to the rectangle.

            If this is a [`frameset`](#frameset) element, then recurse
            the entire [`frameset`](#frameset) layout algorithm for that
            [`frameset`](#frameset) element, with the rectangle as the
            surface.

            Otherwise, it is a [`frame`](#frame) element; render its
            <a href="#content-navigable"
            id="frames-and-framesets:content-navigable">content navigable</a>,
            positioned and sized to fit the rectangle.

        2.  If there are any elements left in `children`, remove the
            first element from `children`.

8.  If the [`frameset`](#frameset) element
    <a href="#has-a-border" id="frames-and-framesets:has-a-border">has a
    border</a>, draw an outer set of borders around the rectangles,
    using the element's <a href="#frame-border-colour"
    id="frames-and-framesets:frame-border-colour">frame border color</a>.

    For each rectangle, if there is an element assigned to that
    rectangle, and that element
    <a href="#has-a-border" id="frames-and-framesets:has-a-border-2">has a
    border</a>, draw an inner set of borders around that rectangle,
    using the element's <a href="#frame-border-colour"
    id="frames-and-framesets:frame-border-colour-2">frame border color</a>.

    For each (visible) border that does not abut a rectangle that is
    assigned a [`frame`](#frame) element with a `noresize` attribute
    (including rectangles in further nested [`frameset`](#frameset)
    elements), the user agent is
    <a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected-2">expected</a>
    to allow the user to move the border, resizing the rectangles
    within, keeping the proportions of any nested
    [`frameset`](#frameset) grids.

    A [`frameset`](#frameset) or [`frame`](#frame) element
    <span id="has-a-border" class="dfn">has a border</span> if the
    following algorithm returns true:

    1.  If the element has a `frameborder` attribute whose value is not
        the empty string and whose first character is either a U+0031
        DIGIT ONE (1) character, a U+0079 LATIN SMALL LETTER Y character
        (y), or a U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y character (Y), then
        return true.

    2.  Otherwise, if the element has a `frameborder` attribute, return
        false.

    3.  Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a
        [`frameset`](#frameset) element, then return true if *that*
        element
        <a href="#has-a-border" id="frames-and-framesets:has-a-border-3">has a
        border</a>, and false if it does not.

    4.  Otherwise, return true.

    The <span id="frame-border-colour" class="dfn">frame border
    color</span> of a [`frameset`](#frameset) or [`frame`](#frame)
    element is the color obtained from the following algorithm:

    1.  If the element has a `bordercolor` attribute, and applying the
        <a href="#rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value"
        id="frames-and-framesets:rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-colour-value">rules
        for parsing a legacy color value</a> to that attribute's value
        does not return failure, then return the color so obtained.

    2.  Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a
        [`frameset`](#frameset) element, then return the
        <a href="#frame-border-colour"
        id="frames-and-framesets:frame-border-colour-3">frame border color</a>
        of that element.

    3.  Otherwise, return gray.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The algorithm to
<span id="convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values"
class="dfn">convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel
values</span> consists of the following steps:

1.  Let `input list` be the list of numbers and units passed to the
    algorithm.

    Let `output list` be a list of numbers the same length as
    `input list`, all zero.

    Entries in `output list` correspond to the entries in `input list`
    that have the same position.

2.  Let `input dimension` be the size passed to the algorithm.

3.  Let `total percentage` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list`
    whose unit is *percentage*.

    Let `total relative` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list`
    whose unit is *relative*.

    Let `total absolute` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list`
    whose unit is *absolute*.

    Let `remaining space` be the value of `input dimension`.

4.  If `total absolute` is greater than `remaining space`, then for each
    entry in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*, set the
    corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in
    `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by
    `total absolute`. Then, set `remaining space` to zero.

    Otherwise, for each entry in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*,
    set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the
    entry in `input list`. Then, decrement `remaining space` by
    `total absolute`.

5.  If `total percentage` multiplied by the `input dimension` and
    divided by 100 is greater than `remaining space`, then for each
    entry in `input list` whose unit is *percentage*, set the
    corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in
    `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by
    `total percentage`. Then, set `remaining space` to zero.

    Otherwise, for each entry in `input list` whose unit is
    *percentage*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the
    number of the entry in `input list` multiplied by the
    `input dimension` and divided by 100. Then, decrement
    `remaining space` by `total percentage` multiplied by the
    `input dimension` and divided by 100.

6.  For each entry in `input list` whose unit is *relative*, set the
