    corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in
    `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by
    `total relative`.

7.  Return `output list`.

</div>

User agents working with integer values for frame widths (as opposed to
user agents that can lay frames out with subpixel accuracy) are
<a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected-3">expected</a> to
distribute the remainder first to the last entry whose unit is
*relative*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit
is *percentage*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose
unit is *absolute*, and finally, failing all else, to the last entry.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The contents of a [`frame`](#frame) element that does not have a
[`frameset`](#frameset) parent are
<a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected-4">expected</a> to
be rendered as
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black"
id="frames-and-framesets:transparent-black"
data-x-internal="transparent-black">transparent black</a>; the user
agent is
<a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected-5">expected</a> to
not render its <a href="#content-navigable"
id="frames-and-framesets:content-navigable-2">content navigable</a> in
this case, and its <a href="#content-navigable"
id="frames-and-framesets:content-navigable-3">content navigable</a> is
<a href="#expected" id="frames-and-framesets:expected-6">expected</a> to
have a <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
id="frames-and-framesets:viewport-2"
data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a> with zero width and zero height.

### <span class="secno">15.7</span> Interactive media<a href="#interactive-media" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">15.7.1</span> Links, forms, and navigation<a href="#links,-forms,-and-navigation" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are <a href="#expected"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:expected">expected</a> to allow the
user to control aspects of <a href="#hyperlink"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:hyperlink">hyperlink</a> activation and
<a href="#form-submission-2"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:form-submission-2">form submission</a>,
such as which <a href="#navigable"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:navigable">navigable</a> is to be used
for the subsequent <a href="#navigate"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:navigate">navigation</a>.

User agents are <a href="#expected"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:expected-2">expected</a> to allow users
to discover the destination of <a href="#hyperlink"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:hyperlink-2">hyperlinks</a> and of
<a href="#the-form-element"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:the-form-element">forms</a> before
triggering their <a href="#navigate"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:navigate-2">navigation</a>.

User agents are <a href="#expected"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:expected-3">expected</a> to inform the
user of whether a <a href="#hyperlink"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:hyperlink-3">hyperlink</a> includes
<a href="#hyperlink-auditing"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:hyperlink-auditing">hyperlink
auditing</a>, and to let them know at a minimum which domains will be
contacted as part of such auditing.

User agents may allow users to <a href="#navigate"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:navigate-3">navigate</a>
<a href="#navigable"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:navigable-2">navigables</a> to the URLs
<a href="#encoding-parsing-a-url"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:encoding-parsing-a-url">indicated</a>
by the `cite` attributes on [`q`](#the-q-element),
[`blockquote`](#the-blockquote-element), [`ins`](#the-ins-element), and
[`del`](#the-del-element) elements.

User agents may surface <a href="#hyperlink"
id="links,-forms,-and-navigation:hyperlink-4">hyperlinks</a> created by
[`link`](#the-link-element) elements in their user interface, as
discussed
[previously](#providing-users-with-a-means-to-follow-hyperlinks-created-using-the-link-element).

#### <span class="secno">15.7.2</span> The [`title`](#attr-title) attribute<a href="#the-title-attribute-2" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="the-title-attribute-2:expected">expected</a> to
expose the <a href="#advisory-information"
id="the-title-attribute-2:advisory-information">advisory information</a>
of elements upon user request, and to make the user aware of the
presence of such information.

On interactive graphical systems where the user can use a pointing
device, this could take the form of a tooltip. When the user is unable
to use a pointing device, then the user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="the-title-attribute-2:expected-2">expected</a>
to make the content available in some other fashion, e.g. by making the
element a <a href="#focusable-area"
id="the-title-attribute-2:focusable-area">focusable area</a> and always
displaying the <a href="#advisory-information"
id="the-title-attribute-2:advisory-information-2">advisory
information</a> of the currently
<a href="#focused" id="the-title-attribute-2:focused">focused</a>
element, or by showing the <a href="#advisory-information"
id="the-title-attribute-2:advisory-information-3">advisory
information</a> of the elements under the user's finger on a touch
device as the user pans around the screen.

U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters are
<a href="#expected" id="the-title-attribute-2:expected-3">expected</a>
to cause line breaks in the tooltip; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)
characters are
<a href="#expected" id="the-title-attribute-2:expected-4">expected</a>
to render as a nonzero horizontal shift that lines up the next glyph
with the next tab stop, with tab stops occurring at points that are
multiples of 8 times the width of a U+0020 SPACE character.

<div class="example">

For example, a visual user agent could make elements with a
[`title`](#attr-title) attribute
<a href="#focusable" id="the-title-attribute-2:focusable">focusable</a>,
and could make any
<a href="#focused" id="the-title-attribute-2:focused-2">focused</a>
element with a [`title`](#attr-title) attribute show its tooltip under
the element while the element has focus. This would allow a user to tab
around the document to find all the advisory text.

</div>

<div class="example">

As another example, a screen reader could provide an audio cue when
reading an element with a tooltip, with an associated key to read the
last tooltip for which a cue was played.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">15.7.3</span> Editing hosts<a href="#editing-hosts" class="self-link"></a>

The current text editing caret (i.e. the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range"
id="editing-hosts:active-range" data-x-internal="active-range">active
range</a>, if it is empty and in an
<a href="#editing-host" id="editing-hosts:editing-host">editing host</a>),
if any, is <a href="#expected" id="editing-hosts:expected">expected</a>
to act like an inline
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element"
id="editing-hosts:replaced-element"
data-x-internal="replaced-element">replaced element</a> with the
vertical dimensions of the caret and with zero width for the purposes of
the CSS rendering model.

This means that even an empty block can have the caret inside it, and
that when the caret is in such an element, it prevents
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#collapsing-margins"
id="editing-hosts:collapsing-margins"
data-x-internal="collapsing-margins">margins from collapsing</a> through
the element.

#### <span class="secno">15.7.4</span> Text rendered in native user interfaces<a href="#text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces"
class="self-link"></a>

User agents are <a href="#expected"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:expected">expected</a> to
honor the Unicode semantics of text that is exposed in user interfaces,
for example supporting the bidirectional algorithm in text shown in
dialogs, title bars, popup menus, and tooltips. Text from the contents
of elements is <a href="#expected"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:expected-2">expected</a> to
be rendered in a manner that honors <a href="#the-directionality"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:the-directionality">the
directionality</a> of the element from which the text was obtained. Text
from attributes is <a href="#expected"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:expected-3">expected</a> to
be rendered in a manner that honours the
<a href="#directionality-of-the-attribute"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:directionality-of-the-attribute">directionality
of the attribute</a>.

<div class="example">

Consider the following markup, which has Hebrew text asking for a
programming language, the languages being text for which a left-to-right
direction is important given the punctuation in some of their names:

``` html
<p dir="rtl" lang="he">
 <label>
  בחר שפת תכנות:
  <select>
   <option dir="ltr">C++</option>
   <option dir="ltr">C#</option>
   <option dir="ltr">FreePascal</option>
   <option dir="ltr">F#</option>
  </select>
 </label>
</p>
```

If the [`select`](#the-select-element) element was rendered as a drop
down box, a correct rendering would ensure that the punctuation was the
same both in the drop down, and in the box showing the current
selection.

<img src="/images/bidiselect.png" width="206" height="105" />

</div>

<div class="example">

The directionality of attributes depends on the attribute and on the
element's [`dir`](#attr-dir) attribute, as the following example
demonstrates. Consider this markup:

``` html
<table>
 <tr>
  <th abbr="(א" dir=ltr>A
  <th abbr="(א" dir=rtl>A
  <th abbr="(א" dir=auto>A
</table>
```

If the [`abbr`](#attr-th-abbr) attributes are rendered, e.g. in a
tooltip or other user interface, the first will have a left parenthesis
(because the direction is 'ltr'), the second will have a right
parenthesis (because the direction is 'rtl'), and the third will have a
right parenthesis (because the direction is determined *from the
attribute value* to be 'rtl').

However, if instead the attribute was not a
<a href="#directionality-capable-attribute"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:directionality-capable-attribute">directionality-capable
attribute</a>, the results would be different:

``` html
<table>
 <tr>
  <th data-abbr="(א" dir=ltr>A
  <th data-abbr="(א" dir=rtl>A
  <th data-abbr="(א" dir=auto>A
</table>
```

In this case, if the user agent were to expose the `data-abbr` attribute
in the user interface (e.g. in a debugging environment), the last case
would be rendered with a *left* parenthesis, because the direction would
be determined from the element's contents.

</div>

A string provided by a script (e.g. the argument to
[`window.alert()`](#dom-alert)) is <a href="#expected"
id="text-rendered-in-native-user-interfaces:expected-4">expected</a> to
be treated as an independent set of one or more bidirectional algorithm
paragraphs when displayed, as defined by the bidirectional algorithm,
including, for instance, supporting the paragraph-breaking behavior of
U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. For the purposes of determining the
paragraph level of such text in the bidirectional algorithm, this
specification does *not* provide a higher-level override of rules P2 and
P3. [\[BIDI\]](#refsBIDI)

When necessary, authors can enforce a particular direction for a given
paragraph by starting it with the Unicode U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK or
U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK characters.

<div class="example">

Thus, the following script:

``` js
alert('\u05DC\u05DE\u05D3 HTML \u05D4\u05D9\u05D5\u05DD!')
```

...would always result in a message reading
"<span dir="rtl">למד LMTH היום!</span>" (not
"<span dir="ltr">דמל HTML םויה!</span>"), regardless of the language of
the user agent interface or the direction of the page or any of its
elements.

</div>

<div class="example">

For a more complex example, consider the following script:

``` bad
/* Warning: this script does not handle right-to-left scripts correctly */
var s;
if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
  alert(s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
}
```

When the user enters "<span class="kbd">Kitty</span>", the user agent
would alert "`Kitty! Ok, Fred, Kitty, and Wilma will get the car.`".
However, if the user enters "<span class="kbd" dir="rtl"
lang="ar">لا أفهم</span>", then the bidirectional algorithm will
determine that the direction of the paragraph is right-to-left, and so
the output will be the following unintended mess:
"<span dir="rtl">`لا أفهم! derF ,kO, لا أفهم, rac eht teg lliw amliW dna.`</span>"

To force an alert that starts with user-provided text (or other text of
unknown directionality) to render left-to-right, the string can be
prefixed with a U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK character:

``` js
var s;
if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
  alert('\u200E' + s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
}
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">15.8</span> Print media<a href="#print-media" class="self-link"></a>

User agents are
<a href="#expected" id="print-media:expected">expected</a> to allow the
user to request the opportunity to <span id="obtain-a-physical-form"
class="dfn">obtain a physical form</span> (or a representation of a
physical form) of a [`Document`](#document). For example, selecting the
option to print a page or convert it to PDF format. [\[PDF\]](#refsPDF)

When the user actually <a href="#obtain-a-physical-form"
id="print-media:obtain-a-physical-form">obtains a physical form</a> (or
a representation of a physical form) of a [`Document`](#document), the
user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="print-media:expected-2">expected</a> to create a
new rendering of the [`Document`](#document) for the print media.

### <span class="secno">15.9</span> Unstyled XML documents<a href="#unstyled-xml-documents" class="self-link"></a>

HTML user agents may, in certain circumstances, find themselves
rendering non-HTML documents that use vocabularies for which they lack
any built-in knowledge. This section provides for a way for user agents
to handle such documents in a somewhat useful manner.

While a [`Document`](#document) is an <a href="#unstyled-document"
id="unstyled-xml-documents:unstyled-document">unstyled document</a>, the
user agent is
<a href="#expected" id="unstyled-xml-documents:expected">expected</a> to
render <a href="#an-unstyled-document-view"
id="unstyled-xml-documents:an-unstyled-document-view">an unstyled
document view</a>.

<div algorithm="">

A [`Document`](#document) is an <span id="unstyled-document"
class="dfn">unstyled document</span> while it matches the following
conditions:

- The [`Document`](#document) has no author style sheets (whether
  referenced by HTTP headers, processing instructions, elements like
  [`link`](#the-link-element), inline elements like
  [`style`](#the-style-element), or any other mechanism).
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#document) have any
  <a href="#presentational-hints"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:presentational-hints">presentational
  hints</a>.
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#document) have any
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:css-styling-attribute"
  data-x-internal="css-styling-attribute">style attributes</a>.
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#document) are in any of the
  following namespaces:
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:html-namespace-2"
  data-x-internal="html-namespace-2">HTML namespace</a>,
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#svg-namespace"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:svg-namespace"
  data-x-internal="svg-namespace">SVG namespace</a>,
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#mathml-namespace"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:mathml-namespace"
  data-x-internal="mathml-namespace">MathML namespace</a>
- The [`Document`](#document) has no <a href="#focusable-area"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:focusable-area">focusable area</a> (e.g.
  from XLink) other than the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:viewport"
  data-x-internal="viewport">viewport</a>.
- The [`Document`](#document) has no <a href="#hyperlink"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:hyperlink">hyperlinks</a> (e.g. from
  XLink).
- There exists no <a href="#concept-script"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:concept-script">script</a> whose
  <a href="#settings-object"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:settings-object">settings object</a>'s
  <a href="#concept-settings-object-global"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:concept-settings-object-global">global
  object</a> is a [`Window`](#window) object with this
  [`Document`](#document) as its <a href="#concept-document-window"
  id="unstyled-xml-documents:concept-document-window">associated
  <code>Document</code></a>.
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#document) have any
  registered event listeners.

</div>

<span id="an-unstyled-document-view" class="dfn">An unstyled document
view</span> is one where the DOM is not rendered according to CSS (which
would, since there are no applicable styles in this context, just result
in a wall of text), but is instead rendered in a manner that is useful
for a developer. This could consist of just showing the
[`Document`](#document) object's source, maybe with syntax highlighting,
or it could consist of displaying just the DOM tree, or simply a message
saying that the page is not a styled document.

If a [`Document`](#document) stops being an <a href="#unstyled-document"
id="unstyled-xml-documents:unstyled-document-2">unstyled document</a>,
then the conditions above stop applying, and thus a user agent following
these requirements will switch to using the regular CSS rendering.

## <span class="secno">16</span> Obsolete features<a href="#obsolete" class="self-link"></a>

### <span class="secno">16.1</span> Obsolete but conforming features<a href="#obsolete-but-conforming-features" class="self-link"></a>

Features listed in this section will trigger warnings in conformance
checkers.

Authors should not specify a [`border`](#attr-img-border) attribute on
an [`img`](#the-img-element) element. If the attribute is present, its
value must be the string "`0`". CSS should be used instead.

Authors should not specify a [`charset`](#attr-script-charset) attribute
on a [`script`](#the-script-element) element. If the attribute is
present, its value must be an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for "`utf-8`". (This has no effect in a document that conforms to
the requirements elsewhere in this standard of being encoded as
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:utf-8"
data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a>.)

Authors should not specify a [`language`](#attr-script-language)
attribute on a [`script`](#the-script-element) element. If the attribute
is present, its value must be an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`JavaScript`" and either the
[`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute must be omitted or its value must
be an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`text/javascript`". The attribute should be
entirely omitted instead (with the value "`JavaScript`", it has no
effect), or replaced with use of the [`type`](#attr-script-type)
attribute.

Authors should not specify a value for the [`type`](#attr-script-type)
attribute on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements that is the empty
string or a <a
href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
type essence match</a>. Instead, they should omit the attribute, which
has the same effect.

Authors should not specify a [`type`](#attr-style-type) attribute on a
[`style`](#the-style-element) element. If the attribute is present, its
value must be an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for "[`text/css`](#text/css)".

Authors should not specify the [`name`](#attr-a-name) attribute on
[`a`](#the-a-element) elements. If the attribute is present, its value
must not be the empty string and must neither be equal to the value of
any of the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:concept-id"
data-x-internal="concept-id">IDs</a> in the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:tree"
data-x-internal="tree">tree</a> other than the element's own
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:concept-id-2"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a>, if any, nor be equal to the value
of any of the other [`name`](#attr-a-name) attributes on
[`a`](#the-a-element) elements in the element's
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:tree-2"
data-x-internal="tree">tree</a>. If this attribute is present and the
element has an <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:concept-id-3"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a>, then the attribute's value must be
equal to the element's <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:concept-id-4"
data-x-internal="concept-id">ID</a>. In earlier versions of the
language, this attribute was intended as a way to specify possible
targets for <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:concept-url-fragment"
data-x-internal="concept-url-fragment">fragments</a> in
<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:url" data-x-internal="url">URLs</a>.
The [`id`](#the-id-attribute) attribute should be used instead.

Authors should not, but may despite requirements to the contrary
elsewhere in this specification, specify the
[`maxlength`](#attr-input-maxlength) and [`size`](#attr-input-size)
attributes on [`input`](#the-input-element) elements whose
[`type`](#attr-input-type) attributes are in the
<a href="#number-state-(type=number)"
id="obsolete-but-conforming-features:number-state-(type=number)">Number</a>
state. One valid reason for using these attributes regardless is to help
legacy user agents that do not support [`input`](#the-input-element)
elements with `type="number"` to still render the text control with a
useful width.

#### <span class="secno">16.1.1</span> Warnings for obsolete but conforming features<a href="#warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features"
class="self-link"></a>

To ease the transition from HTML4 Transitional documents to the language
defined in *this* specification, and to discourage certain features that
are only allowed in very few circumstances, conformance checkers must
warn the user when the following features are used in a document. These
are generally old obsolete features that have no effect, and are allowed
only to distinguish between likely mistakes (regular conformance errors)
and mere vestigial markup or unusual and discouraged practices (these
warnings).

The following features must be categorized as described above:

- The presence of a [`border`](#attr-img-border) attribute on an
  [`img`](#the-img-element) element if its value is the string "`0`".

- The presence of a [`charset`](#attr-script-charset) attribute on a
  [`script`](#the-script-element) element if its value is an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for "`utf-8`".

- The presence of a [`language`](#attr-script-language) attribute on a
  [`script`](#the-script-element) element if its value is an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-2"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for the string "`JavaScript`" and if there is no
  [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute or there is and its value is an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-3"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for the string "`text/javascript`".

- The presence of a [`type`](#attr-style-type) attribute on a
  [`script`](#the-script-element) element if its value is a <a
  href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:javascript-mime-type-essence-match"
  data-x-internal="javascript-mime-type-essence-match">JavaScript MIME
  type essence match</a>.

- The presence of a [`type`](#attr-style-type) attribute on a
  [`style`](#the-style-element) element if its value is an
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:ascii-case-insensitive-4"
  data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
  match for "[`text/css`](#text/css)".

- The presence of a [`name`](#attr-a-name) attribute on an
  [`a`](#the-a-element) element, if its value is not the empty string.

- The presence of a [`maxlength`](#attr-input-maxlength) attribute on an
  [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#attr-input-type)
  attribute is in the <a href="#number-state-(type=number)"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:number-state-(type=number)">Number</a>
  state.

- The presence of a [`size`](#attr-input-size) attribute on an
  [`input`](#the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#attr-input-type)
  attribute is in the <a href="#number-state-(type=number)"
  id="warnings-for-obsolete-but-conforming-features:number-state-(type=number)-2">Number</a>
  state.

Conformance checkers must distinguish between pages that have no
conformance errors and have none of these obsolete features, and pages
that have no conformance errors but do have some of these obsolete
features.

For example, a validator could report some pages as "Valid HTML" and
others as "Valid HTML with warnings".

### <span class="secno">16.2</span> Non-conforming features<a href="#non-conforming-features" class="self-link"></a>

Elements in the following list are entirely obsolete, and must not be
used by authors:

<span id="applet" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`applet`</span>  
Use [`embed`](#the-embed-element) or [`object`](#the-object-element)
instead.

<span id="acronym" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`acronym`</span>  
Use [`abbr`](#the-abbr-element) instead.

<span id="bgsound" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`bgsound`</span>  
Use [`audio`](#the-audio-element) instead.

<span id="dir" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`dir`</span>  
Use [`ul`](#the-ul-element) instead.

[`frame`](#frame)  
[`frameset`](#frameset)  
<span id="noframes" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`noframes`</span>  
Either use [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) and CSS instead, or use
server-side includes to generate complete pages with the various
invariant parts merged in.

<span id="isindex" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`isindex`</span>  
Use an explicit [`form`](#the-form-element) and
<a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)"
id="non-conforming-features:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">text
control</a> combination instead.

<span id="keygen" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`keygen`</span>  
For enterprise device management use cases, use native on-device
management capabilities.

For certificate enrollment use cases, use the Web Cryptography API to
generate a keypair for the certificate, and then export the certificate
and key to allow the user to install them manually.
[\[WEBCRYPTO\]](#refsWEBCRYPTO)

<span id="listing" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`listing`</span>  
Use [`pre`](#the-pre-element) and [`code`](#the-code-element) instead.

<span id="menuitem" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`menuitem`</span>  
To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu"
data-x-internal="event-contextmenu"><code
id="non-conforming-features:event-contextmenu">contextmenu</code></a>
event.

<span id="nextid" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`nextid`</span>  
Use GUIDs instead.

<span id="noembed" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`noembed`</span>  
Use [`object`](#the-object-element) instead of
[`embed`](#the-embed-element) when fallback is necessary.

<span id="param" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`param`</span>  
Use the [`data`](#attr-object-data) attribute of the
[`object`](#the-object-element) element to set the URL of the external
resource.

<span id="plaintext" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`plaintext`</span>  
Use the "<a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3"
data-x-internal="text/plain"><code
id="non-conforming-features:text/plain">text/plain</code></a>"
<a href="https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type"
id="non-conforming-features:mime-type" data-x-internal="mime-type">MIME
type</a> instead.

<span id="rb" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`rb`</span>  
<span id="rtc" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`rtc`</span>  
Providing the ruby base directly inside the [`ruby`](#the-ruby-element)
element or using nested [`ruby`](#the-ruby-element) elements is
sufficient.

<span id="strike" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`strike`</span>  
Use [`del`](#the-del-element) instead if the element is marking an edit,
otherwise use [`s`](#the-s-element) instead.

<span id="xmp" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`xmp`</span>  
Use [`pre`](#the-pre-element) and [`code`](#the-code-element) instead,
and escape "`<`" and "`&`" characters as "`&lt;`" and "`&amp;`"
respectively.

<span id="basefont" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`basefont`</span>  
<span id="big" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`big`</span>  
<span id="blink" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`blink`</span>  
<span id="center" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`center`</span>  
<span id="font" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`font`</span>  
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element)  
<span id="multicol" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`multicol`</span>  
<span id="nobr" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`nobr`</span>  
<span id="spacer" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`spacer`</span>  
<span id="tt" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`tt`</span>  
Use appropriate elements or CSS instead.

Where the [`tt`](#tt) element would have been used for marking up
keyboard input, consider the [`kbd`](#the-kbd-element) element; for
variables, consider the [`var`](#the-var-element) element; for computer
code, consider the [`code`](#the-code-element) element; and for computer
output, consider the [`samp`](#the-samp-element) element.

Similarly, if the [`big`](#big) element is being used to denote a
heading, consider using the
[`h1`](#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element; if it is being
used for marking up important passages, consider the
[`strong`](#the-strong-element) element; and if it is being used for
highlighting text for reference purposes, consider the
[`mark`](#the-mark-element) element.

See also the [text-level semantics usage summary](#usage-summary) for
more suggestions with examples.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following attributes are obsolete (though the elements are still
part of the language), and must not be used by authors:

<span id="attr-a-charset" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`charset`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
<span id="attr-link-charset" class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`charset`</span> on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements  
Use an HTTP \`[`Content-Type`](#content-type)\` header on the linked
resource instead.

<span id="attr-script-charset" class="dfn" dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`charset`</span> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)  
Omit the attribute. Both documents and scripts are required to use
<a href="https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8"
id="non-conforming-features:utf-8" data-x-internal="utf-8">UTF-8</a>, so
it is redundant to specify it on the [`script`](#the-script-element)
element since it inherits from the document.

<span id="attr-a-coords" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`coords`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
<span id="attr-a-shape" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`shape`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
Use [`area`](#the-area-element) instead of [`a`](#the-a-element) for
image maps.

<span id="attr-a-methods" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`methods`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
<span id="attr-link-methods" class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`methods`</span> on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements  
Use the HTTP OPTIONS feature instead.

<span id="attr-a-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)  
<span id="attr-embed-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="embed" dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> on [`embed`](#the-embed-element) elements  
<span id="attr-img-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="img" dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> on [`img`](#the-img-element) elements  
<span id="attr-option-name" class="dfn" dfn-for="option" dfn-type="element-attr">`name`</span> on [`option`](#the-option-element) elements  
Use the [`id`](#the-id-attribute) attribute instead.

<span id="attr-a-rev" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`rev`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
<span id="attr-link-rev" class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`rev`</span> on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements  
Use the [`rel`](#attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute instead, with an opposite
term. (For example, instead of `rev="made"`, use `rel="author"`.)

<span id="attr-a-urn" class="dfn" dfn-for="a" dfn-type="element-attr">`urn`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element) elements  
<span id="attr-link-urn" class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`urn`</span> on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements  
Specify the preferred persistent identifier using the
[`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute instead.

<span id="attr-form-accept" class="dfn" dfn-for="form" dfn-type="element-attr">`accept`</span> on [`form`](#the-form-element) elements  
Use the [`accept`](#attr-input-accept) attribute directly on the
[`input`](#the-input-element) elements instead.

<span id="attr-area-hreflang" class="dfn" dfn-for="area" dfn-type="element-attr">`hreflang`</span> on [`area`](#the-area-element) elements  
<span id="attr-area-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="area" dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> on [`area`](#the-area-element) elements  
These attributes do not do anything useful, and for historical reasons
there are no corresponding IDL attributes on [`area`](#the-area-element)
elements. Omit them altogether.

<span id="attr-area-nohref" class="dfn" dfn-for="area" dfn-type="element-attr">`nohref`</span> on [`area`](#the-area-element) elements  
Omitting the [`href`](#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute is sufficient; the
[`nohref`](#attr-area-nohref) attribute is unnecessary. Omit it
altogether.

<span id="attr-head-profile" class="dfn" dfn-for="head" dfn-type="element-attr">`profile`</span> on [`head`](#the-head-element) elements  
Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<span id="attr-html-manifest" class="dfn" dfn-for="html" dfn-type="element-attr">`manifest`</span> on [`html`](#the-html-element) elements  
Use service workers instead. [\[SW\]](#refsSW)

<span id="attr-html-version" class="dfn" dfn-for="html" dfn-type="element-attr">`version`</span> on [`html`](#the-html-element) elements  
Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<span id="attr-input-ismap" class="dfn" dfn-for="input" dfn-type="element-attr">`ismap`</span> on [`input`](#the-input-element) elements  
Unnecessary. Omit it altogether. All [`input`](#the-input-element)
elements with a [`type`](#attr-input-type) attribute in the
<a href="#image-button-state-(type=image)"
id="non-conforming-features:image-button-state-(type=image)">Image
Button</a> state are processed as server-side image maps.

<span id="attr-input-usemap" class="dfn" dfn-for="input" dfn-type="element-attr">`usemap`</span> on [`input`](#the-input-element) elements  
<span id="attr-object-usemap" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`usemap`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
Use the [`img`](#the-img-element) element for image maps.

<span id="attr-iframe-longdesc" class="dfn" dfn-for="iframe" dfn-type="element-attr">`longdesc`</span> on [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) elements  
<span id="attr-img-longdesc" class="dfn" dfn-for="img" dfn-type="element-attr">`longdesc`</span> on [`img`](#the-img-element) elements  
Use a regular [`a`](#the-a-element) element to link to the description,
or (in the case of images) use an
<a href="#image-map" id="non-conforming-features:image-map">image
map</a> to provide a link from the image to the image's description.

<span id="attr-img-lowsrc" class="dfn" dfn-for="img" dfn-type="element-attr">`lowsrc`</span> on [`img`](#the-img-element) elements  
Use a progressive JPEG image (given in the [`src`](#attr-img-src)
attribute), instead of using two separate images.

<span id="attr-link-target" class="dfn" dfn-for="link" dfn-type="element-attr">`target`</span> on [`link`](#the-link-element) elements  
Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<span id="attr-menu-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="menu" dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> on [`menu`](#the-menu-element) elements  
To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu"
data-x-internal="event-contextmenu"><code
id="non-conforming-features:event-contextmenu-2">contextmenu</code></a>
event. For toolbar menus, omit the attribute.

<span id="attr-menu-label" class="dfn" dfn-for="menu" dfn-type="element-attr">`label`</span> on [`menu`](#the-menu-element) elements  
<span id="attr-contextmenu" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`contextmenu`</span> on all elements  
<span id="handler-onshow" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`onshow`</span> on all elements  
To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the
<a href="https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu"
data-x-internal="event-contextmenu"><code
id="non-conforming-features:event-contextmenu-3">contextmenu</code></a>
event.

<span id="attr-meta-scheme" class="dfn" dfn-for="meta" dfn-type="element-attr">`scheme`</span> on [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements  
Use only one scheme per field, or make the scheme declaration part of
the value.

<span id="attr-object-archive" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`archive`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
<span id="attr-object-classid" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`classid`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
<span id="attr-object-code" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`code`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
<span id="attr-object-codebase" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`codebase`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
<span id="attr-object-codetype" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`codetype`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
Use the [`data`](#attr-object-data) and [`type`](#attr-object-type)
attributes to invoke
<a href="#plugin" id="non-conforming-features:plugin">plugins</a>.

<span id="attr-object-declare" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`declare`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
Repeat the [`object`](#the-object-element) element completely each time
the resource is to be reused.

<span id="attr-object-standby" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`standby`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
Optimize the linked resource so that it loads quickly or, at least,
incrementally.

<span id="attr-object-typemustmatch" class="dfn" dfn-for="object" dfn-type="element-attr">`typemustmatch`</span> on [`object`](#the-object-element) elements  
Avoid using [`object`](#the-object-element) elements with untrusted
resources.

<span id="attr-script-language" class="dfn" dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`language`</span> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)  
Omit the attribute for JavaScript; for
<a href="#data-block" id="non-conforming-features:data-block">data
blocks</a>, use the [`type`](#attr-script-type) attribute instead.

<span id="attr-script-event" class="dfn" dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`event`</span> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements  
<span id="attr-script-for" class="dfn" dfn-for="script" dfn-type="element-attr">`for`</span> on [`script`](#the-script-element) elements  
Use DOM events mechanisms to register event listeners.
[\[DOM\]](#refsDOM)

<span id="attr-style-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="style" dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> on [`style`](#the-style-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)  
Omit the attribute for CSS; for
<a href="#data-block" id="non-conforming-features:data-block-2">data
blocks</a>, use [`script`](#the-script-element) as the container instead
of [`style`](#the-style-element).

<span id="attr-table-datapagesize" class="dfn" dfn-for="table" dfn-type="element-attr">`datapagesize`</span> on [`table`](#the-table-element) elements  
Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<span id="attr-table-summary" class="dfn" dfn-for="table" dfn-type="element-attr">`summary`</span> on [`table`](#the-table-element) elements  
Use one of the [techniques for describing
tables](#table-descriptions-techniques) given in the
[`table`](#the-table-element) section instead.

<span id="attr-td-abbr" class="dfn" dfn-for="td" dfn-type="element-attr">`abbr`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) elements  
Use text that begins in an unambiguous and terse manner, and include any
more elaborate text after that. The [`title`](#attr-title) attribute can
also be useful in including more detailed text, so that the cell's
contents can be made terse. If it's a heading, use
[`th`](#the-th-element) (which has an [`abbr`](#attr-th-abbr)
attribute).

<span id="attr-tdth-axis" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`axis`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
Use the [`scope`](#attr-th-scope) attribute on the relevant
[`th`](#the-th-element).

<span id="attr-td-scope" class="dfn" dfn-for="td" dfn-type="element-attr">`scope`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) elements  
Use [`th`](#the-th-element) elements for heading cells.

<span id="attr-datasrc" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`datasrc`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element), [`button`](#the-button-element), [`div`](#the-div-element), [`frame`](#frame), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), [`img`](#the-img-element), [`input`](#the-input-element), [`label`](#the-label-element), [`legend`](#the-legend-element), [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), [`object`](#the-object-element), [`option`](#the-option-element), [`select`](#the-select-element), [`span`](#the-span-element), [`table`](#the-table-element), and [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements  
<span id="attr-datafld" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`datafld`</span> on [`a`](#the-a-element), [`button`](#the-button-element), [`div`](#the-div-element), [`fieldset`](#the-fieldset-element), [`frame`](#frame), [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element), [`img`](#the-img-element), [`input`](#the-input-element), [`label`](#the-label-element), [`legend`](#the-legend-element), [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), [`object`](#the-object-element), [`select`](#the-select-element), [`span`](#the-span-element), and [`textarea`](#the-textarea-element) elements  
<span id="attr-dataformatas" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`dataformatas`</span> on [`button`](#the-button-element), [`div`](#the-div-element), [`input`](#the-input-element), [`label`](#the-label-element), [`legend`](#the-legend-element), [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element), [`object`](#the-object-element), [`option`](#the-option-element), [`select`](#the-select-element), [`span`](#the-span-element), and [`table`](#the-table-element) elements  
Use script and a mechanism such as
<a href="https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest"
data-x-internal="xmlhttprequest"><code
id="non-conforming-features:xmlhttprequest">XMLHttpRequest</code></a> to
populate the page dynamically. [\[XHR\]](#refsXHR)

<span id="attr-dropzone" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`dropzone`</span> on all elements  
Use script to handle the [`dragenter`](#event-dnd-dragenter) and
[`dragover`](#event-dnd-dragover) events instead.

<span id="attr-tdth-align" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`align`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-bgcolor" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`bgcolor`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-char" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`char`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-charoff" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`charoff`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-height" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`height`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-nowrap" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`nowrap`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-valign" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`valign`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tdth-width" class="dfn" dfn-for="td,th" dfn-type="element-attr">`width`</span> on [`td`](#the-td-element) and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-align" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`align`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-bgcolor" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`bgcolor`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-char" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`char`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-charoff" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`charoff`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-height" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`height`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-tr-valign" class="dfn" dfn-for="tr" dfn-type="element-attr">`valign`</span> on [`tr`](#the-tr-element) elements  
<span id="attr-ul-compact" class="dfn" dfn-for="ul" dfn-type="element-attr">`compact`</span> on [`ul`](#the-ul-element) elements  
<span id="attr-ul-type" class="dfn" dfn-for="ul" dfn-type="element-attr">`type`</span> on [`ul`](#the-ul-element) elements  
<span id="attr-background" class="dfn" dfn-type="element-attr">`background`</span> on [`body`](#the-body-element), [`table`](#the-table-element), [`thead`](#the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#the-tr-element), [`td`](#the-td-element), and [`th`](#the-th-element) elements  
Use CSS instead.

### <span class="secno">16.3</span> Requirements for implementations<a href="#requirements-for-implementations" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">16.3.1</span> The <span class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`marquee`</span> element<a href="#the-marquee-element" class="self-link"></a>

The [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element is a presentational
element that animates content. CSS transitions and animations are a more
appropriate mechanism. [\[CSSANIMATIONS\]](#refsCSSANIMATIONS)
[\[CSSTRANSITIONS\]](#refsCSSTRANSITIONS)

The [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element must implement the
[`HTMLMarqueeElement`](#htmlmarqueeelement) interface.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMarqueeElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString behavior;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString bgColor;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString direction;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString height;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long hspace;
  [CEReactions] attribute long loop;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=6] attribute unsigned long scrollAmount;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=85] attribute unsigned long scrollDelay;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean trueSpeed;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long vspace;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString width;

  undefined start();
  undefined stop();
};
```

A [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element can be
<span id="concept-marquee-on" class="dfn">turned on</span> or
<span id="concept-marquee-off" class="dfn">turned off</span>. When it is
created, it is <a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element:concept-marquee-on">turned on</a>.

<div algorithm="">

When the <span id="dom-marquee-start" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLMarqueeElement" dfn-type="method">`start()`</span> method
is called, the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element must be
<a href="#concept-marquee-on"
id="the-marquee-element:concept-marquee-on-2">turned on</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

When the <span id="dom-marquee-stop" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLMarqueeElement" dfn-type="method">`stop()`</span> method is
called, the [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element must be
<a href="#concept-marquee-off"
id="the-marquee-element:concept-marquee-off">turned off</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-marquee-behavior" class="dfn" dfn-for="marquee"
dfn-type="element-attr">`behavior`</span> content attribute on
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) elements is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-marquee-element:enumerated-attribute">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State |
|----|----|
| `scroll` | <span id="attr-marquee-behavior-scroll" class="dfn">scroll</span> |
| `slide` | <span id="attr-marquee-behavior-slide" class="dfn">slide</span> |
| `alternate` | <span id="attr-marquee-behavior-alternate" class="dfn">alternate</span> |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-marquee-behavior-scroll"
id="the-marquee-element:attr-marquee-behavior-scroll">scroll</a> state.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-marquee-direction" class="dfn" dfn-for="marquee"
dfn-type="element-attr">`direction`</span> content attribute on
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) elements is an
<a href="#enumerated-attribute"
id="the-marquee-element:enumerated-attribute-2">enumerated attribute</a>
with the following keywords and states (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State                                                            |
|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `left`  | <span id="attr-marquee-direction-left" class="dfn">left</span>   |
| `right` | <span id="attr-marquee-direction-right" class="dfn">right</span> |
| `up`    | <span id="attr-marquee-direction-up" class="dfn">up</span>       |
| `down`  | <span id="attr-marquee-direction-down" class="dfn">down</span>   |

<div algorithm="">

The attribute's *[missing value default](#missing-value-default)* and
*[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)* are both the
<a href="#attr-marquee-direction-left"
id="the-marquee-element:attr-marquee-direction-left">left</a> state.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="attr-marquee-truespeed" class="dfn" dfn-for="marquee"
dfn-type="element-attr">`truespeed`</span> content attribute on
[`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) elements is a
<a href="#boolean-attribute"
id="the-marquee-element:boolean-attribute">boolean attribute</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element has a
<span id="marquee-scroll-interval" class="dfn">marquee scroll
interval</span>, which is obtained as follows:

1.  If the element has a `scrolldelay` attribute, and parsing its value
    using the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
    id="the-marquee-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers">rules
    for parsing non-negative integers</a> does not return an error, then
    let `delay` be the parsed value. Otherwise, let `delay` be 85.

2.  If the element does not have a
    [`truespeed`](#attr-marquee-truespeed) attribute, and the `delay`
    value is less than 60, then let `delay` be 60 instead.

3.  The <a href="#marquee-scroll-interval"
    id="the-marquee-element:marquee-scroll-interval">marquee scroll
    interval</a> is `delay`, interpreted in milliseconds.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element has a
<span id="marquee-scroll-distance" class="dfn">marquee scroll
distance</span>, which, if the element has a `scrollamount` attribute,
and parsing its value using the
<a href="#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers"
id="the-marquee-element:rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers-2">rules
for parsing non-negative integers</a> does not return an error, is the
parsed value interpreted in
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-marquee-element:&#39;px&#39;" data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS
pixels</a>, and otherwise is 6
<a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px"
id="the-marquee-element:&#39;px&#39;-2"
data-x-internal="&#39;px&#39;">CSS pixels</a>.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<div algorithm="">

A [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element has a
<span id="marquee-loop-count" class="dfn">marquee loop count</span>,
which, if the element has a <span id="attr-marquee-loop" class="dfn"
dfn-for="marquee" dfn-type="element-attr">`loop`</span> attribute, and
parsing its value using the <a href="#rules-for-parsing-integers"
id="the-marquee-element:rules-for-parsing-integers">rules for parsing
integers</a> does not return an error or a number less than 1, is the
parsed value, and otherwise is −1.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-marquee-loop" class="dfn" dfn-for="HTMLMarqueeElement"
dfn-type="attribute">`loop`</span> IDL attribute, on getting, must
return the element's <a href="#marquee-loop-count"
id="the-marquee-element:marquee-loop-count">marquee loop count</a>; and
on setting, if the new value is different than the element's
<a href="#marquee-loop-count"
id="the-marquee-element:marquee-loop-count-2">marquee loop count</a> and
either greater than zero or equal to −1, must set the element's
[`loop`](#attr-marquee-loop) content attribute (adding it if necessary)
to the
<a href="#valid-integer" id="the-marquee-element:valid-integer">valid
integer</a> that represents the new value. (Other values are ignored.)

</div>

A [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element also has a
<span id="marquee-current-loop-index" class="dfn">marquee current loop
index</span>, which is zero when the element is created.

<div algorithm="">

The rendering layer will occasionally
<span id="increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index"
class="dfn">increment the marquee current loop index</span>, which must
cause the following steps to be run:

1.  If the <a href="#marquee-loop-count"
    id="the-marquee-element:marquee-loop-count-3">marquee loop count</a>
    is −1, then return.

2.  Increment the <a href="#marquee-current-loop-index"
    id="the-marquee-element:marquee-current-loop-index">marquee current loop
    index</a> by one.

3.  If the <a href="#marquee-current-loop-index"
    id="the-marquee-element:marquee-current-loop-index-2">marquee current
    loop index</a> is now greater than or equal to the element's
    <a href="#marquee-loop-count"
    id="the-marquee-element:marquee-loop-count-4">marquee loop count</a>,
    <a href="#concept-marquee-off"
    id="the-marquee-element:concept-marquee-off-2">turn off</a> the
    [`marquee`](#the-marquee-element) element.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### <span class="secno">16.3.2</span> Frames<a href="#frames" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="frameset" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`frameset`</span>
element acts as
<a href="#the-body-element-2" id="frames:the-body-element-2">the body
element</a> in documents that use frames.

The [`frameset`](#frameset) element must implement the
[`HTMLFrameSetElement`](#htmlframesetelement) interface.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFrameSetElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString cols;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rows;
};
HTMLFrameSetElement includes WindowEventHandlers;
```

The [`frameset`](#frameset) element exposes as
<a href="#event-handler-content-attributes"
id="frames:event-handler-content-attributes">event handler content
attributes</a> a number of the
<a href="#event-handlers" id="frames:event-handlers">event handlers</a>
of the [`Window`](#window) object. It also mirrors their
<a href="#event-handler-idl-attributes"
id="frames:event-handler-idl-attributes">event handler IDL
attributes</a>.

The <a href="#event-handlers" id="frames:event-handlers-2">event
handlers</a> of the [`Window`](#window) object named by the
<a href="#window-reflecting-body-element-event-handler-set"
id="frames:window-reflecting-body-element-event-handler-set"><code>Window</code>-reflecting
body element event handler set</a>, exposed on the
[`frameset`](#frameset) element, replace the generic
<a href="#event-handlers" id="frames:event-handlers-3">event
handlers</a> with the same names normally supported by
<a href="#html-elements" id="frames:html-elements">HTML elements</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <span id="frame" class="dfn" dfn-type="element">`frame`</span>
element has a
<a href="#content-navigable" id="frames:content-navigable">content
navigable</a> similar to the [`iframe`](#the-iframe-element) element,
but rendered within a [`frameset`](#frameset) element.

<div algorithm="">

The [`frame`](#frame) <a href="#html-element-insertion-steps"
id="frames:html-element-insertion-steps">HTML element insertion
steps</a>, given `insertedNode`, are:

1.  If `insertedNode` is not
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree"
    id="frames:in-a-document-tree" data-x-internal="in-a-document-tree">in a
    document tree</a>, then return.

2.  If `insertedNode`'s
    <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root"
    id="frames:root" data-x-internal="root">root</a>'s
    <a href="#concept-document-bc" id="frames:concept-document-bc">browsing
    context</a> is null, then return.

3.  <a href="#create-a-new-child-navigable"
    id="frames:create-a-new-child-navigable">Create a new child
    navigable</a> for `insertedNode`.

4.  <a href="#process-the-frame-attributes"
    id="frames:process-the-frame-attributes">Process the <code>frame</code>
    attributes</a> for `insertedNode`, with
    *[initialInsertion](#process-frame-initial-insertion)* set to true.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The [`frame`](#frame) <a href="#html-element-removing-steps"
id="frames:html-element-removing-steps">HTML element removing steps</a>,
given `removedNode`, are to <a href="#destroy-a-child-navigable"
id="frames:destroy-a-child-navigable">destroy a child navigable</a>
given `removedNode`.

</div>

Whenever a [`frame`](#frame) element with a non-null
<a href="#content-navigable" id="frames:content-navigable-2">content
navigable</a> has its `src` attribute set, changed, or removed, the user
agent must <a href="#process-the-frame-attributes"
id="frames:process-the-frame-attributes-2">process the
<code>frame</code> attributes</a>.

<div algorithm="">

To <span id="process-the-frame-attributes" class="dfn">process the
`frame` attributes</span> for an element `element`, with an optional
boolean <span id="process-frame-initial-insertion"
class="dfn">`initialInsertion`</span>:

1.  Let `url` be the result of running the <a
    href="#shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements"
    id="frames:shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements">shared
    attribute processing steps for <code>iframe</code> and
    <code>frame</code> elements</a> given `element` and
    `initialInsertion`.

2.  If `url` is null, then return.

3.  If `url`
    <a href="#matches-about:blank" id="frames:matches-about:blank">matches
    <code>about:blank</code></a> and `initialInsertion` is true, then:

    1.  <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire"
        id="frames:concept-event-fire" data-x-internal="concept-event-fire">Fire
        an event</a> named [`load`](#event-load) at `element`.

    2.  Return.

4.  <a href="#navigate-an-iframe-or-frame"
    id="frames:navigate-an-iframe-or-frame">Navigate an <code>iframe</code>
    or <code>frame</code></a> given `element`, `url`, the empty string,
    and `initialInsertion`.

</div>

The [`frame`](#frame) element
<a href="#potentially-delays-the-load-event"
id="frames:potentially-delays-the-load-event">potentially delays the
load event</a>.

The [`frame`](#frame) element must implement the
[`HTMLFrameElement`](#htmlframeelement) interface.

``` idl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFrameElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString scrolling;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString frameBorder;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString longDesc;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean noResize;
  readonly attribute Document? contentDocument;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? contentWindow;

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString marginHeight;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString marginWidth;
};
```

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-frame-contentdocument" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLFrameElement" dfn-type="attribute">`contentDocument`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="frames:this"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#concept-bcc-content-document"
id="frames:concept-bcc-content-document">content document</a>.

</div>

<div algorithm="">

The <span id="dom-frame-contentwindow" class="dfn"
dfn-for="HTMLFrameElement" dfn-type="attribute">`contentWindow`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this" id="frames:this-2"
data-x-internal="this">this</a>'s
<a href="#content-window" id="frames:content-window">content window</a>.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">16.3.3</span> Other elements, attributes and APIs<a href="#other-elements,-attributes-and-apis" class="self-link"></a>

equivalent to [`abbr`](#the-abbr-element) elements in terms of semantics
and for purposes of rendering.

};

``` idl
partial interface HTMLMetaElement {
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString scheme;
};
```

User agents may treat the [`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme) content
attribute on the [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element as an extension of
the element's [`name`](#attr-meta-name) content attribute when
processing a [`meta`](#the-meta-element) element with a
[`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute whose value is one that the user
agent recognizes as supporting the [`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme)
attribute.

User agents are encouraged to ignore the [`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme)
attribute and instead process the value given to the metadata name as if
it had been specified for each expected value of the
[`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme) attribute.

<div class="example">

For example, if the user agent acts on [`meta`](#the-meta-element)
elements with [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attributes having the value
"eGMS.subject.keyword", and knows that the [`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme)
attribute is used with this metadata name, then it could take the
[`scheme`](#attr-meta-scheme) attribute into account, acting as if it
was an extension of the [`name`](#attr-meta-name) attribute. Thus the
following two [`meta`](#the-meta-element) elements could be treated as
two elements giving values for two different metadata names, one
consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and "LGCL", and
the other consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and
"ORLY":

``` bad
<!-- this markup is invalid -->
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="LGCL" content="Abandoned vehicles">
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="ORLY" content="Mah car: kthxbye">
```

The suggested processing of this markup, however, would be equivalent to
the following:

``` html
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" content="Abandoned vehicles">
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" content="Mah car: kthxbye">
```

</div>

## <span class="secno">17</span> IANA considerations<a href="#iana" class="self-link"></a>

### <span class="secno">17.1</span> <span class="dfn">`text/html`</span><a href="#text/html" class="self-link"></a>

This registration is for community review and will be submitted to the
IESG for review, approval, and registration with IANA.

Type name:  
text

Subtype name:  
html

Required parameters:  
No required parameters

Optional parameters:  
`charset`  
The `charset` parameter may be provided to specify the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding"
id="text/html:document&#39;s-character-encoding"
data-x-internal="document&#39;s-character-encoding">document's character
encoding</a>, overriding any <a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="text/html:character-encoding-declaration">character encoding
declarations</a> in the document other than a Byte Order Mark (BOM). The
parameter's value must be an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive"
id="text/html:ascii-case-insensitive"
data-x-internal="ascii-case-insensitive">ASCII case-insensitive</a>
match for the string "`utf-8`". [\[ENCODING\]](#refsENCODING)

Encoding considerations:  
8bit (see the section on <a href="#character-encoding-declaration"
id="text/html:character-encoding-declaration-2">character encoding
declarations</a>)

Security considerations:  
Entire novels have been written about the security considerations that
apply to HTML documents. Many are listed in this document, to which the
reader is referred for more details. Some general concerns bear
mentioning here, however:

HTML is scripted language, and has a large number of APIs (some of which
are described in this document). Script can expose the user to potential
risks of information leakage, credential leakage, cross-site scripting
attacks, cross-site request forgeries, and a host of other problems.
While the designs in this specification are intended to be safe if
implemented correctly, a full implementation is a massive undertaking
and, as with any software, user agents are likely to have security bugs.

Even without scripting, there are specific features in HTML which, for
historical reasons, are required for broad compatibility with legacy
content but that expose the user to unfortunate security problems. In
particular, the [`img`](#the-img-element) element can be used in
conjunction with some other features as a way to effect a port scan from
the user's location on the Internet. This can expose local network
topologies that the attacker would otherwise not be able to determine.

HTML relies on a compartmentalization scheme sometimes known as the
*same-origin policy*. An
<a href="#concept-origin" id="text/html:concept-origin">origin</a> in
most cases consists of all the pages served from the same host, on the
same port, using the same protocol.

It is critical, therefore, to ensure that any untrusted content that
forms part of a site be hosted on a different
<a href="#concept-origin" id="text/html:concept-origin-2">origin</a>
than any sensitive content on that site. Untrusted content can easily
spoof any other page on the same origin, read data from that origin,
cause scripts in that origin to execute, submit forms to and from that
origin even if they are protected from cross-site request forgery
attacks by unique tokens, and make use of any third-party resources
exposed to or rights granted to that origin.

Interoperability considerations:  
Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are
defined in this specification.

Published specification:  
This document is the relevant specification. Labeling a resource with
the [`text/html`](#text/html) type asserts that the resource is an
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document"
id="text/html:html-documents" data-x-internal="html-documents">HTML
document</a> using
<a href="#syntax" id="text/html:syntax">the HTML syntax</a>.

Applications that use this media type:  
Web browsers, tools for processing web content, HTML authoring tools,
search engines, validators.

Additional information:  
Magic number(s):  
No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify an HTML document. More
information on detecting HTML documents is available in MIME Sniffing.
[\[MIMESNIFF\]](#refsMIMESNIFF)

File extension(s):  
"`html`" and "`htm`" are commonly, but certainly not exclusively, used
as the extension for HTML documents.

Macintosh file type code(s):  
`TEXT`

Person & email address to contact for further information:  
Ian Hickson \<ian@hixie.ch\>

Intended usage:  
Common

Restrictions on usage:  
No restrictions apply.

Author:  
Ian Hickson \<ian@hixie.ch\>

Change controller:  
W3C

<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment"
id="text/html:concept-url-fragment"
data-x-internal="concept-url-fragment">Fragments</a> used with
[`text/html`](#text/html) resources either refer to the
<a href="#the-indicated-part-of-the-document"
id="text/html:the-indicated-part-of-the-document">indicated part</a> of
the corresponding [`Document`](#document), or provide state information
for in-page scripts.

### <span class="secno">17.2</span> <span class="dfn">`multipart/x-mixed-replace`</span><a href="#multipart/x-mixed-replace" class="self-link"></a>

This registration is for community review and will be submitted to the
IESG for review, approval, and registration with IANA.

Type name:  
multipart

Subtype name:  
x-mixed-replace

Required parameters:  
- `boundary` (defined in RFC2046) [\[RFC2046\]](#refsRFC2046)

Optional parameters:  
No optional parameters.

Encoding considerations:  
binary

Security considerations:  
Subresources of a
[`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#multipart/x-mixed-replace) resource can
be of any type, including types with non-trivial security implications
such as [`text/html`](#text/html).

Interoperability considerations:  
None.

Published specification:  
This specification describes processing rules for web browsers.
Conformance requirements for generating resources with this type are the
same as for [`multipart/mixed`](#multipart/mixed).
[\[RFC2046\]](#refsRFC2046)

Applications that use this media type:  
This type is intended to be used in resources generated by web servers,
for consumption by web browsers.

Additional information:  
Magic number(s):  
No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify a
[`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#multipart/x-mixed-replace) resource.

File extension(s):  
No specific file extensions are recommended for this type.

Macintosh file type code(s):  
No specific Macintosh file type codes are recommended for this type.

Person & email address to contact for further information:  
Ian Hickson \<ian@hixie.ch\>

Intended usage:  
Common

Restrictions on usage:  
No restrictions apply.

Author:  
Ian Hickson \<ian@hixie.ch\>

Change controller:  
W3C

<a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment"
id="multipart/x-mixed-replace:concept-url-fragment"
data-x-internal="concept-url-fragment">Fragments</a> used with
[`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#multipart/x-mixed-replace) resources
apply to each body part as defined by the type used by that body part.

### <span class="secno">17.3</span> <span class="dfn">`application/xhtml+xml`</span><a href="#application/xhtml+xml" class="self-link"></a>

[\[RFC7303\]](#refsRFC7303)

Interoperability considerations:
